Each week we read 5 or 6 selections and wrote a 5 or 6 page double spaced paper. Grading was very reasonable, but the effort to read and write that much is substantial. Consider voice recognition software for papers.
One of the best teachers in the Business School. Amazing class structure.
So boring almost fell asleep in every single lecture. Definitely wasn't enjoyable or interesting but if you have to do it, study the practice homework and try leave a good impression on Okao.
DO NOT TAKE

Easily one of the worst professors I've had. Lectures are disorganized and unclear, exams don't reflect what's taught, and expectations are never explained. Grading feels arbitrary and asking questions rarely helps because he laughs at you. Do yourself a favor and avoid this class  and professor AT ALL COSTS in anything even on hallways .

reviews.comment: I don't like this old fart. He's a confusing, horrible teacher and total piece of work. Typically when one says "have a nice break" when turning in a final exam, professors respond similarly. This guy didn't even glance at me and just said okay. He makes you feel stupid for asking any question and is not helpful, especially in offce hours.

Professor Okao is a walking encyclopedia with a deep knowledge of many subjects not limited to Economics. He is engaging and is passionate about teaching. Seek him out and you will realize that the negative comments must be taken with a grain of salt as I do not find any of it valid based on my experience. He is also funny. 100% would take again.
Refused to work with me while serious life stuff was happening for my family and I had to keep traveling during the week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No point in attending class, even though it is required. All tests/homework through Macmillan. Utilize the practice homework's, the exams are word for word the same. Lecture's were basically him repeating the text books. Also worth 4 credits typically- just take this basic class elsewhere. It's practically all online work anyways.

Professor Okao's lectures are very boring, but if you take notes and pay attention you will be fine. The tests are exactly like the homework. If you show up to class there is some extra credit he adds in at the end for attendance. He is also very strict on deadlines.

Lectures are BORING. Doesn't grade on attendance and don't bother going because you will not learn anything. Tests are exactly like homework. Read the book and you're good. About one assignment every 2 weeks.

Very bad at communicating and unforgiving. Lectures are long and extremely slow/boring. Test are around 100 questions despite horrible lectures and lack of material given to you to learn the information. I would never take a class with this professor again, he complains about all the work he has to do but all work is auto-graded electronically.

Just be in class and take notes to get a good grade. Also, his online textbook has practice problems that are literally in the test. Professor Okao tests you on what he teaches you. If you are unable to turn in an assignment, email him a day or so before the due date.

Make sure to take notes in class, as the exams are based on your lecture notes, and homework questions. The material is fairly easy and has real world use cases, unlike other classes. He also takes attendance for extra credit. He knows his stuff and he doesn't mind staying after class to explain stuff.

Incredibly boring. I learned faster and more from just reading the chapters in the textbook. He often goes off on long tangents about stuff that's hardly even related to what we're learning about. I stopped going to discussion because it was awful. There's about 1 assignment a week, 3ish tests over the semester, and extra credit. Easy A

I took honors econ (econ 143) hoping that I would have a better, more engaging professor than non-honors econ. I was wrong. Dr. Okao goes over material straight from the book at a snail's pace. Interrupts students when they try to answer questions. Incredibly vague on due dates and how much assignments would be worth.

Dr. Okao is an influential instructor... He helped me find my passion for environmental economics. I took his Environmental Econ course and he was absolutely perfect! He excels in sticking to the structure of the course through book material and provides examples that match reality in different cases.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I personally think Mr. Okao is a great teacher. I learned a lot of information from going to his lectures, I find them especially interesting if you interact with him. answer and ask questions if you can, he is likely to round your letter grade up to the next letter grade if he believes you are a good student who asks questions and attends classes.

The lectures aren't required but he will take attendance and could curve your grade based on how often you go. His lectures are extremely boring and are pretty much a copy-paste of the textbook. He also goes over topics very slowly and leaves a lot to be done in discussions and reading. I recommend reading the textbook.

class was held in the morning, and was a boring lecturer, which made attending class incredibly difficult because of low motivation. Said that attendance wouldn't be counted but then made us check in on a sheet for every lecture we were present. Genuinely would never like to take another econ class, especially with a professor like him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredibly boring lectures, so it was a pro for me that attendance was extra credit. 4-5 tests throughout the semester, homework was a breeze and tests weren't too much harder than the homeworks. Only class I've taken at KU that I would say is an "easy A."

Is Professor Okao's class lecture heavy? Yes, but with the discussion it isn't that much of an issue. In my opinion, as long as you actually go to class and complete the assignments the class isn't too difficult. He gives a good amount of extra credit, you could have probably increased by an entire letter grade if you took advantage of it.

He gave zero effort in teaching. All he did was post the quizzes and tests. His video lectures were impossible to understand. Every time a student emailed him he would reply very rudely. Not a good professor only reason he is still there is because of tenure.

While attendance is not mandatory for this course, he strongly advises against skipping. You can read from the textbook but he has small details that you need to focus on that he doesnt make announcements about outside of class or on blackboard. Overall tough grader, laughed at me when I answered his non-rhetorical rhetorical questions. Unpleasant
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Makes tests due early on Saturdays. No forgiveness when requesting assistance. Does not actually teach the class, yet has a bad attitude about how hard work is for him (all he does is just post the quizzes and worksheets and then complains about his students needing help during covid).

I found his lectures to be a bit on the boring side, and he could use some help organizing his lecture notes. He's not high-energy, but he knows his stuff. I have a feeling if I didn't already have a deep interest in macro, I probably would've hated the class. He's got a funky accent though, so that's cool.

Laughs at students when they contribute. Very dull approach to lectures. Not helpful when you ask questions. NO partial credit. One error and you get 0 pts. Memorize the study guides multiple choice, and find all homework answers online and you'll do fine. Would recommend sitting through the lectures as he'll curve your grade if you attend class.

Professor Okao has great lectures and will always answer questions. He may seem standoff-ish at first, but he once let our class change the due date for a homework assignment because we all had prior commitments. He gives SOME extra credit towards the end of the semester. Review the study guides for tests and ask questions. He wants you to do well!

must attend class. very hard to pay attention too, however all the info you need is in the textbook which he copies too the board the entire lecture very slowly. you'll miss important dates and info if you don't attend class, and professor is unwilling to help students outside of class. test format was different everytime and he grades how he wants
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is an engaging teacher that wants to push his students. He strives for critical thinking often waiting until a studnet will answer, even incorrectly, before teaching a subject. Attendance is counted but not graded, rather used to sway a borderline grade. He is one of the greatest people I have ever learned from.
Hard to understand, does not cover formula's that he test you on from the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class wasn't that hard honestly. In the beginning of the semester I would have rated her 1/5 but now that I have gotten the hang of her teaching style I hate it less. For people planning on taking this class: you can probably skip every YouTube video she links on the module PDF. If she didn't record herself, it probably won't be on the exam.

Truly not as bad as people say. Group work isn't great, but every other aspect of this course is extremely manageable and a small amount of effort can get you a decent grade. The TA's are amazing and Dr. Archibald seriously cares... if you care to ask. Can be a lot of work, but follow a schedule and it's fine!

Dr. Archibald is overly hated. Students with absolutely no initiative just love to complain about things when they are slightly difficult. The course is flipped and many people dislike that but the flipped nature of this course is NOT poorly executed. There are so many resources for students in BIOL152, if you need them, USE THEM!!!!!!

I really liked this course. I understand a lot of people dislike flipped courses because (for the most part) they're done poorly. This is NOT one of those poorly done flipped courses. I felt engaged, and she does teach during class, it's just much more active. I would 1000% take this class again.

Genuinely the worst teaching methods I have ever experienced. Group work is the worst idea of all time, exam questions are worded so horribly, every day I went to class I considered switching to business. A dude in my group spent more time on his gpa calculator than work. For how easy the content was I had to spend way too much time to get an A.

Very module-heavy. Content is not taught in class, and you are expected to know everything before attending. Professor is nice, however, IClickers, Worksheets, Mini-Exams, and Exams are all worded weirdly and made very confusing. This class should not be a flipped course; there is too much information given for exams to be cumulative, but they are

I dread going to this class every day. I am taking this class as a sophomore and I would rather taken ochem 2 a dozen times before taking this class again. She makes the class so boring and the modules take several hours to complete. I would never take this class again.

Bio 152 is a flipped course. Basically you're teaching yourself accept you are still required to be in class. She will never fully answer questions. Her grading is known to be unfair at times. Exams are all somewhat cumulative and the questions are worded very different and confusing. No retakes, lots of out of class work, not much teaching.
mid ahh class. I

This class should not be a flipped class. You have to teach yourself everything, and each lecture is filled with iClickers that are worded to trick you and don't help you at all! The TA sessions are the same thing, so unless you want to meet with her each module to get additional help, you are on your own! Take it online or somewhere else!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: i dread going to this class every day. this should NOT be a flipped course at all because she does not teach ANYTHING and expects you to know EVERYTHING before class starts. this is crowned the winner for the worst class ive taken at KU thus far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Has confusing questions. Does not word things clearly. I HATE GROUP PROJECTS. Group tests take up 20% of your total test grade!! Lectures are boring. Expensive textbook required. Lots of reading (textbook and module)
The class really isn't that bad if you pay attention to the modules and take notes, lectures can be a little boring and there is a decent amount of reading but it's not that bad if you lock in
The other reviews are pretty harsh; Archibald was a decent professor. It's pretty easy as long as you do the flipped modules on time and take advantage of all the extra credit!

The tests in this class were unnecessarily confusing, considering it was only a 100-level class. They weren't the most difficult tests ever, but each question was so nitpicky in terms of the content being asked. The lectures themself weren't as terrible as I had heard, but Archibald can be quite condescending when being asked for help.

When I looked at Dr. Archibald's rating before taking her class I was concerned, but she is not as bad as her overall rating and reviews give the impression of. BIOL 152 is a flipped course, so it has the side effect of making the lectures a bit boring and repetitive, but helpful for review. Tests are weighted in a manner that can only help you.

reviews.comment: Be prepared to spend most of your time studying for her class. Her exams and iclickers are confusing. I wouldn't take her class again.

reviews.comment: Super easy class and a GREAT lecturer. She's really great at in-depth explanations and giving examples. Super helpful and interactive. Exam 2 is the hardest out of 3 exams but they were all pretty tame. She does do trick questions a lot, but by the time you finish the semester, you're already trained to spot the trick questions easily on the exams.

Very kind and caring, she is a great person and genuinely is interested in what she teaches.. This class was enjoyable and interesting. Amazing TA's as well. Biggest downfall are the online modules, they can be very unclear at times. Along with that, exams and mini-exams can be misleading. Personally, I really liked working in groups during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Archibald is easily one of the most kind, understanding professors I've met. She genuinely is interested in the class and wants to help everyone succeed. As for the class itself, it is not as difficult as everyone makes it out to be. Just make sure you have effective studying methods and this class with be both easy and fascinating for you.
Not personable at all. Tests are weighted very heavy and she uses wording on the tests that you will have never seen before. She purposely tries to trick you on these tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Archibald was a good professor and was willing to answer questions. The TA's I had and their sessions were also helpful and you can get extra credit just by going. Soft-spoken, but passionate about biology. She's sweet and cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The worst class I've ever taken.

I cannot believe this. I need to study for modules BEFORE and AFTER every class, and class is FLIPPED COURSE?????? She is just yapping at class, and giving unnecessary informations. Iclickers terrible. Modules terrible. She just destroyed my 4.0 GPA. Even tho I had genetics and bicohemistry before her. This is just a nightmare.

Many of her iClicker and exam questions try to trick you with odd phrasing, but as long as you keep that in mind this is an otherwise very easy biology class. People like to be dramatic how bad it is but really it's a matter of showing up and studying effectively.

Uses trick questions and strange phrasing on exams, expecting students to decipher them. TA's tried to help and were often wrong because of how confusing she was. My biggest advice is to work hard at the beginning of the semester, go to sessions and grasp the info. If you do well on the 1st exam, you're set up for the rest of the course.
Dr. Archibald is such a great teacher. I don't get the hate, genuinely not as bad as everyone says. She lets you use a note card on exams and is so nice and understanding.

Prof. Archibald is represented terribly on this rate my professor. It was an easy class; all you have to do is show up and participate/complete the group work assignments, and you will get an A. She also has extra credit available if you are low on points, your lowest exam grade will be worth only half of the points (dropped from final grade.)

Honestly everyone is being dramatic. The class really isn't that hard. I didn't even pay attention to the lectures and just studied the PLUS packets and got a high A. Literally just show up for class and do the groupworks and do the extra credit and you'll get an A. She's actually nice. Wanted to give her 5 bc people are too mean.
No lecture slideshow except for course gallery. I despise reverse lecture style.

This class was really fun and rewarding and Dr. Archibald did a great job teaching about plant systematics and made me much more interested in the subject. I hate this class it was so unhelpful and the modules didnt do jack. She also didnt really explain things well and my biggest issue was how reliant she is on iclicker. Class isnt that bad. Attendance is mandatory (iclickers and groupwork). Get close with you groupmates, they help alot! Go to plus session they will save you. Tests are cumulative - yes EVERY test is cumulative. Lectures are boring, notes take forever. Just work hard and you'll pass with a high grade.
don't take this class if you want to remain sane

terrible teacher and not helpful. modules are long and dreadful and what is discussed in class has nothing to do with any of it. exams are cumulative and very hard. doesnt read the room when it comes to confused students. doesnt see the issue when the class average is a 65%.

The only thing is that she isn't the most engaging; but she's a good professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't take this class.

There is a module to do every week and they typically took me a few hours to complete. In class we'd go over the material in the module which sometime felt repetitive, but also would clear up difficult concepts. However, it also felt like she was throwing so many topics at us each lecture and could be confusing.

I love biology, and this class made me start to hate it. All exams are cumulative, with no study guides, no real study material, and lots of information, and it's all crammed into a flipped-style classroom, which only adds to the stress. Lectures are pointless except for the group work, questions worded difficult for no reason, overall 2/10 class.

reviews.comment: I think the class was decent and I did enjoy the lectures. However, the in-class participation was a bit much and team collaboration was not always successful. This class wasn't too hard but there were a LOT of terms to memorize, and a lot of chapters covered each test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The flipped format can be difficult but the modules she put together were really comprehensive while still being understandable, and if you read her questions carefully it's easy to figure out what she's asking. I think some people are put off because her affect is a bit flat, but I don't think it's fair to judge her on that.

She doesn't teach very well. A lot of the questions on tests and quizzes are very complexly worded. Made me hate biology as a bio major. She's nice but just repeats things from the modules instead of teaching and answering questions. Told me that non-disjunction (in meiosis) is not real and does not happen.
She's very nice but doesn't do a lot of teaching. Flipped classroom style.

reviews.comment:
This professor would rather spend her time wording the questions to be as confusing as humanly possible, than teach.

I legitimately hated taking this class, this professor is not doing her job properly. The teacher only lectures once a week. Worst of all, legitimately no proper study guides were given in a class which is so insanely test heavy.
I used to love biology, and this professor was so awful it made me switch majors.
She honestly made me consider switching schools just so I could take BIOL 152 with a different professor.

This class was difficult not because of content but because she makes it difficult. reviews.comment: She does everything she can to prepare you for exams. She even provides detailed explanations under every quiz, worksheet, and groupwork question. Not only that but she is a great communicator and she genuinely cares for success for her students. She even provides much extra credit. The exams can get difficult but biology itself is just tough.

This class is genuinely the worst class I have ever taken. The workload is insane. You can spend hours studying, and still be completely lost.On top of that, there are so many trick questions. If it isn't a trick question, it's a question over a specific, small topic mentioned once. If you can avoid taking this class, please do.

I am extremely disappointed with the set-up of this class and the lack of support I feel. As a 100-level class, the difficulty is way beyond what it should be, test questions are very tricky and worded badly, you learn all of the content by yourself, and tests are 80% individual and 20% group. My best advice is to pick a different professor.

Tricking students when assessing them with wording and confusing questioning is absolutely unethical.  Students are here to learn and all that is being taught is that this professor is power hungry and wants students to feel inept. Her TA doesn't know what she means by questions and is unable to help. The professor shows little empathy for students

I did not like Dr. Archibald. She loves to trick you on exams. The exams will make or break your grade and there is no real way to study for them. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Archibald is a wonderful professor who lets you know actually what you need to know for the course and how she will grade. However, YOU HAVE TO DO THE HOMEWORK. It's not hard as long as you do the modules and go to class. Lots of extra credit and opportunities to meet with her or the TAs.

I loved having professor Archibald! She made her expectations very clear and taught me a lot. As long as you do the homework and show up to lecture, it is very a very easy class. I definitely recommend!

The class is flipped schedule, but she reviews the information inside class as well. She offers up to 7 points of extra credit, but her tests are set up to get points back as you redo the test with a group. She also allows notecards on tests. Overall the class is fairly easy as long as you learn the information outside of class as well.

Gives absolutely zero f about students and grades like satan himself. No review packets for tests. No extra credit. Oh wait correction. EXTRA CREDIT IS DILUTED TO WORTH NOTHING. Trick questions causing you to lose lots of points. Worst teacher in college. She should resign in disgrace.

I actually hate Jenny so much! I would not recommend her to any student ever. I recommend that you take the class with her husband BIOL 153. The flipped classroom actually make me want to die. She is a tricky person. She changes words up to make it impossible to understand what you are trying to learn. Everything is cumulative so good luck!

I would never take this teacher pick someone else and you will thank me later. She is the worst teacher I have ever had in my whole life. She tricks you and her test are very hard and the test are cumulative. Sometimes the TA's in the class don't even know the answer to her questions.

This class is flipped, and the actual class time is useless, but group work is important so you have to go. The worst part of being in class is that you can't listen to her talk on 3x speed like you can with the lecture videos. Every iclicker and test question she writes is worded in the most confusing way possible, like she's trying to trick you.

Every test/quiz question was designed to trick you. Hybrid class that shouldn't be hybrid and every lecture isn't spent lecturing it is iClicker and group work. Actually worst class I've ever taken. It is basically a teach yourself class about PLANT BIOLOGY. would not recommend. try to get into honors (with her husband) he gives out A's.

Quizzes and tests are written in the most unclear language possible, on top of making test grades inclusive of group exams. Flipped format course so you do 95% of the teaching yourself from 8-10 pdfs filled with videos 3-15min made in 2020.

reviews.comment: Flipped classroom (which I liked, great for going at your own pace with notes). TAKE GOOD NOTES. Great lecture videos, and class time is used well to expand upon them and practice with concepts. Group section on exams is a nice chance to try and earn points back, but exams are cumulative and there's not much guidance on what to focus on studying.

Do not be scared by all of the negative reviews on here - BIOL152 with Archibald is not as awful as everyone on here makes it out to be. Make sure to actually go through the modules completely before lecture, pay attention/participate during lecture, and attend TA sessions, you will do just fine in this course.

She does not care about the grade you receive. She is going to give you almost nothing but trick questions and lectures are mandatory. Close to nothing is taught in class, so get ready to teach yourself the material yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is not a good professor by any means. The TA sessions, and the SI sessions are not helpful. Good luck if you ever have to take this class...

I think that Dr.Archibald is an expert in her field, but that does not mean she is good at teaching. reviews.comment: I made a RMP account just to rate this class. This is the bio major weed out class. The structure of this class is horrid; it's a flipped classroom for no reason, and it's designed for students to suffer to get an A. Yes, she offers extra credit, but the amount you get for the work required is ridiculous. Few points in the gradebook too. Good luck.

Dr. Jenny Archibald is a nice person, but horrible teacher. She does not  discuss everything on her modules in her once a week lecture, her modules take almost 4 hours to go through the information, she doesn't provide study guides for her extensive exams, and her questions purposefully trick you. I found myself very frustrated by her class.

Hybrid class so all of the learning is done before class. Lecture is used to repeat information said in the online homework. Pointless 75 minutes, the TA's are the only people that teach and explain concepts in this class. Tests are always trick questions and purposely worded to confuse people. Minuscule opportunities for extra credit in this class

Easily the worst professor I have ever had. The exams are so hard, and there is no clear cut study guide. She does have quizzes that do help boost your grade, get ready to learn a lot of content with no clear guide on what to study for exams, exams are 32 MC and 4 short answer. Each exam is cumulative besides the first exam. ARCHIBALD IS TERRIBLE!
No study guides so there is never any way to prepare fully for tests. Rarely goes over anything important in lectures that were on the quizzes or worksheets.

She never goes over the worksheets done before class, and you're almost never prepared for the exams because there is no study guide or previous exams provided. There's no way to fully prepare yourself for the exams because some questions are just so specific and there's too much information across the modules to study for.

Okay, so this is probably the worst teacher you'll ever have to deal with at KU, plain and simple. I would say this class is a test of how well you know English more than biology, her questions are a trap. She doesn't care about the students at all. Her only goal is to make her class seem harder than it really is.

You need to do all the modules to understand what happens in class because it is a reverse classroom. Yet, for her quizzes, she words everything so weirdly to "have you think about the concepts", yet they are just traps. Prof Castle is amazing. Hands down one of the best if not the best instructors on campus. She is very caring and takes time out of her day to answer any questions you might have. Extremely knowledgeable when it comes to the law.  Take her class you will not be disappointed.

INCREDIBLE PROFESSOR. I advise every business student to take Professor Castle. Very caring for her students, hell, she takes the time to learn the names of all her students - EVEN HER SUMMER CLASS WHICH WAS LESS THAN 30 DAYS! That tells you enough about her! Attendance isn't mandatory but you lose points if you do not show up.

Teaches the subject very well and will help students who need it. Clearly tells students what they will be tested on and prepares/gives them everything they need to succeed in lecture. All around great professor.

Amii is amazing, I love her class. Very good at lecturing and i never want to miss her class. Textbook is helpful to summarize everything, she posts lectures online but it definitely helps being in class. Tests are graded by the next class period. She is such a nice person I wish I had another class I could take with her.
Cares about teaching. Quality teacher. Textbook is recommended as it's good review.
Professor Castle is awesome! The material is a little dry, but she try her best to make it as exciting as possible.

Professor Castle is an awesome teacher. She is very thorough with her lectures and very caring to her students. Come to class and you will pass with an A. I learned a lot from her class and would definitely take another one of hers' if I can!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Castle is one of my favorite professors I've had at KU. Very knowledgeable of the material and fantastic at explaining it. Exams aren't too difficult and do a great job of reflecting the material in class. She generally cares for her students and is always willing to help. Only criticism is the textbook is unnecessary.
Awesome class and awesome professor who cares about your learning. Simple as that. Buy the textbook if you want an A, atleast a B otherwise.

I was floored by Professor Castle's charisma and ability to teach her students. Take BLAW 301 with her, you will absolutely not regret it. She gives you so much extra credit and help. Her tests are challenging, but not as much if you READ. Read the textbook and you will certainly reach in the high 80's and 90's on tests. Fantastic professor.

Professor Castle was my favorite. Although the lectures were long, it was filled with great information that made you very prepared for the tests. There were 4 tests and lots of extra credit. Read the textbook if you don't go to class. Fairly easy tests if you go to class. This class made me consider law school!

Unlike many professors, she actually cares about her students and wants nothing more for them to succeed. She is very enthusiastic during the lectures, which kept me attentive and focused the whole time. Highly recommend taking this class; It has been one of the most interesting and entertaining classes I have taken at KU yet.

Really nice professor, she does truly care about her students succeeding. Lectures are a bit long but it is necessary for you to understand all the materials. Definitely take this class with her if you have to take blaw, she offers a ton of extra credit and no homework!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Actually pay attention in class and carefully follow the review sheet she gives before each exam and you will do fine. Very nice teacher and truly cares about the students and her teaching, one of the most enthusiastic ive ever seen. Extra credit available and look out for attendance quizzes.
Really nice lady, you learn a lot, and she makes boring concepts interesting. 100% would recommend. A ton of extra credit opportunities too.

Definitely take a class with Prof Castle if you ever get the chance. She is a fabulous professor and even better person. She truly cares about her students and offers tons of opportunities to talk face to face and is a great person to talk to. Her teaching is very clear and you won't have a problem being successful in her class if you put in effort

Prof. Castle is the best professor the School of Business has seen. She is an inspiration to her students and would sacrifice an arm and a leg for any one of her students. Go to class, do your readings, and stop by her office if you have any questions (or even just to chat). She wants you to succeed but you have to put the work in.

I am a Junior and Prof. Castle has been my favorite teacher & I am not even a Law student! I wish she would teach my other business courses too. She is very prepared, clear, and concise. She does her homework and applies her content to the real world. She actually cares about her students- how well they do in her classroom as well as outside of it
Professor Castle is a great professor who loves what she does and sets up her students for success on the exams by keeping the class entertaining and explaining the topics in a relevant light.

She goes out of her way to find answers that she doesn't particularly know and actually remembers to go back and tell you the answer. She has a lot of real-world experience so she often use that in her lectures. She also teaches current events which makes it easy to understand and grasp ideas easier.  Best professor ever!

Probably my favorite professor at KU! None of my friends had as a professor before me so I didn't know what to expect, but she has made the class so enjoyable. You can tell that she is very passionate about what she is teaching and that makes the lectures fun and interesting.

Professor Castle is easily a favorite of mine. Her lectures relate current events into her terms which can be confusing if not explained properly(however she always does). She gives pop quizzes, but if you go to class and do the readings it's not hard at all. Her tests also don't give you trick questions, she's very straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Castle is by far my favorite teacher I have had at KU. Her class has inspired me to consider law school, and she has been so much help in figuring out my path to get there. Her class is interesting, and I've learned so much through taking it.

Amii is a great teacher who enjoys teaching this class. Show up to lectures, take notes, and listen to her examples and you will do great in the class. I bought the book but haven't read it and I have still gotten As on all the tests. She really makes this class interesting and worth showing up for. Not a cumulative final which is awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This professor is great! She uses real world experiences to give the class life and make it more interesting. She is new, so she doesn't seem like a professor and she really wants you to learn. I read the book 3 tests, and got A's on every single one. Without reading, I got a high B on the test. Pay attention to lecture and do the extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really sweet teacher, this is only her second semester teaching at a university in general. She expects you to read the textbook, but if you read her power points and go to class you will be fine. If you study and read the textbook before the tests, it's an easy A. There are also lots of extra credit opportunities.

This professor is great! She is passionate about the class and her students and is so interesting to listen to. This is by far my favorite class I have taken so far in college. I feel that she teaches on a touchy subject (government/law) in an appropriately neutral and informative way. There are pop quizzes, but if you try you will succeed!!

Let me just say that this professor has to be the most engaging professor I have had since attending KU. She uses real world examples to prove that what we are discussing does not only apply to the 18th century when these laws were created. She keeps it interesting. She is a wonderful professor. I wish there was no character limit on this.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really good teacher. You can get an A if you study and read the text. She has great slides and uses the book so you definitely need it. There is an occasional pop quiz but you get 5 points on the quiz just for being there. If you have any questions she always gets back to and is very engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is actually so sweet and wants you to succeed. He posts everything on canvas and is clear on how he will grade you and what will go in the gradebook. There are only exams and quizzes in the grade book so make sure to do well on those. i definitely recommend taking this class with him, you won't regret it, he' awesome!

Super easy course, it's basically online. Attendance is not mandatory and he posts all the lecture slides and recordings. All homework is submitted through canvas and you receive your feedback through there. Exams are online, non-proctored or lockdown browser, including a cumulative final. Highly recommend!
Class was entirely online, attendance was completely optional. Very easy grade.

An incredible professor. His lectures are certainly worth visiting, the time doesn't allow much for discussion, but he creates an environment that made me more engaged than when I was listening from home. The content difficulty ramps up halfway through but exams were never a "huh when did we learn this?" Exam format is similar to practice exams.

The best, in-depth lectures I had during COVID online classes. Never tested on anything he didn't lecture on. Offered extra credit on all exams. Truly cared about his students' well-being during COVID and talked about taking care of ourselves. Learned so much from him and truly enjoyed it.

Lots of people in my class had a couldn't understand his accent, but I didn't have a problem with it. His tests are based directly off of the PowerPoints so if you know those then you'll be good. The entire class grade was based on tests. Attendance isn't mandatory but he gave us 3% EC on our final course grade if we answered 2/3 clicker questions

Dr. Azuma is a great professor who really cares about how his students do. The material is very tough and the tests are extremely in depth, but everything on them can be found on his slides. He also posts past exams that were extremely helpful in studying. The class is completely test based, so study hard and don't be afraid to ask for help.

Dr. Azuma genuinely cares about his students. He makes sure that we understand what is going on in the class and explains his slides very clearly. He also takes the time to emphasize what is important for the exam on his slides which makes studying for exams easier. The exams are based on information covered in lecture only so studying is easy.

Exam grades only. His exams are difficult if you aren't fully prepared. By that I mean there are lots of "reverse" multiple-choice questions so if you don't know the little details scattered throughout his slides, you may find yourself in trouble. Study the slides from the lectures heavily because the exams are 100% based on the slides.

Dr. Azuma was an excellent professor to have. The class was all lectures, with most of the information coming straight from the textbook. Grade is all exam based. Exams are easy as long as you study the old exams. Dr. Azuma was very helpful in explaining concepts during class, and I loved his funny little anecdotes. Cool guy-ask him about youtube.
Her lectures move fast, but she truly does want all of her students to succeed. She does a great job preparing you for the exams.
I loved this class. This was the best class I've had at KU. She taught the material and made it engaging. I wanted to go to class. It wasn't easy, but I learned so much!

I really loved Dr. Bechtold's lectures she's so passionate about science that it actually makes you want to learn more. Even in a huge lecture hall, the vibe is great. Highly recommend her, just don't skip class.

She drops a fair number of low in-class grades and 1 test. Had weekly assignments outside of class that were easy to complete and followed the lecture. Exams are in person and follow very closely with the lecture, and a 3x5 notecard is allowed. I had her previously, and both classes were amazing.
Dr. Bechtold was really nice but her class was pretty disorganized. This made it more stressful than it probably should have been. Still not necessarily a bad class though.

The time goes by quickly in her classes because it's not all lecture- we applied and practiced ideas which helped a LOT for the exams. She's smart and that knowledge sometimes becomes an odd little story, which was ok. Some of the topics she teaches are tough for intro bio but I got it in the end! It felt SO good when I got 5' to 3' correct. IYKYK

I would take this class all over again if I had the time! She was a fantastic professor and lecturer. She clearly cares about her students and loves teaching! 10/10 would recommend! Hope to have her as a professor again in the future!
She's strange but in a good way. Extra credit for every test. She's pretty goated. Just put in the time for studying.
Dr. B saved my test grade with her lectures. I skipped out at first but if you go to lecture you will see the groupworks and iclicker are often on exams.

We have two more tests in the class so I hope I keep my A! If you aren't good at keeping a schedule then don't do anatomy or physiology online, it's work! Everything was pretty straightforward. Some of the test questions were weird but mostly pretty predictable. Dr. B is easy to reach and responds quickly, even with an online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The Connect work is mid but if you go to lecture you can do ok on exams. I don't think I would take Biology 246 and anatomy again at the same time!

I like her! Sometimes she gives us a few extra days for homework in Biol 246. She listens to us and makes the classroom not feel like a lecture hall. I have met with her during office hours and she takes the time to explain concepts that don't click. Super, as far as large classes go!

Not Biol 150, it's principles of human physiology. Usually has assignments due thursday but switches it around sometimes and does not update calendar so you have to know when everything's due without it telling you

Took Bio 246 with Rachel, she is an amazing teacher, makes the content easy to understand! Go to class, she uploads the slides for each chapter but theyre difficult to understand if you didn't go to the lecture.
Don't skip class and do all the assignments and you'll be ok
Dr. B was a great professor, the class is very lecture heavy, but the way she taught was very engaging, even though the content was boring.

I had Dr. B for Biol 100 and Biol 150. 150 was way tougher but I learned a lot. The classroom is huge but you don't notice that after a while. Ask questions and interact with the TAs, they are so helpful!

Bio 246, she is very entertaining, easy to engage in the class most of the time and very down to earth. Material in the book is not always tested, but lecture is VERY testable and rewatching lectures is going to be a great key to success.
Hard to keep up at first- but if you can just hang in there and get good study habits you will see your grade bounce up at the very end with some low grades taken off!

Biol 100 is super fun but it gets harder in Biol 246! Go to class and listen to what is talked about in lectures. Often there is way more reading assigned than can be tested over so the lectures help you know what to study. Attendance matters! Low grades get dropped at the end which is nice.
Amazing professor
Absolutely amazing profesor, very understanding and needs a huge pay raise.

At first, the mandatory iClicker attendance points really irked me, but she rounds up to 100% or close at semester. One exam score is dropped so I didn't have to take the final. Go to SI sessions and reviews before big tests. Other than that, she is very easy to follow and makes a lot of dad jokes. She also has a silly biol account on Instagram

Dr. B teaches her class like a high school class, will walk up and down the stairs and call out people if they seem to not be paying attention, scribbles all over the lecture slides excessively and makes it unclear what is the most important part of what she is saying.

Very in-depth lecturer! I recommend downloading the ppt slides and mimicking any marks or phrases she puts on her slides in class! The group works are almost always exactly what is on the test, sometimes it was exact questions. She will not round up even if you have a 89.999 so beware, but your lowest of every assignment is dropped, even exams!!

She seems very genuine and tries to help her students but her lectures are almost incomprehensible to me. She is big on attendance though. To achieve an A you need to take every exam and show up to class on group work days. She does iclicker attendance with graded questions every lecture though. She is a very fair grader.

Dr. Bechtold was a great biology professor. The class is exam-heavy and requires studying but is also very similar to high-school level biology classes I have taken in the past. Having taken AP Biology I found the class to be pretty easy but I still learned a fair amount and enjoyed lecture. There are many supplemental instruction sessions!

She is a cool person but she is super strict on grading. Her tests are a bit rough as a freshman but if you have a SOLID study technique, you will be okay. DEDICATE TIME to this class. This is NOT an easy A. Go to study sessions.

this was my first college bioclass and it was alright. i like Dr. B as a person but i didnt like her teaching style, she talked at you from the lecture slideshow but didnt apply anything so studying was full of content to understand. every week theres about 2 mcgraw hill assignments with about 30 concepts so have fun w that, but it was whatever.
She is the best professor I have ever had. She explains things using analogies and has great humor. I love her so much!!!!

For this being my first course in college, definitely difficult to study for. She is not the greatest during lectures but it got better towards the end. Learn your study method early. 5 exams. She drops a lot of stuff though. Groupworks are similar to exams, don't just cheat through it. Make sure you know the material not just memorize for exams.
She's amazing

Loved Dr. Bechtold she was amazing and was so funny. Lots of engagement throughout the class while working in groups which help so much to actually learn the material. Quizes weren't bad and or neither was the homework. Theres no exams! she was just overall awesome and actually cared about you. Don't pass her up.
Easiest class I have ever taken. No tests no projects just a weekly online quiz and worksheets every couple classes.

Just go to class and do the assignments and small quizzes, she didn't have big tests and I learned a lot. Very fun and enthusiastic lectures, not a hard class at all. Very understanding professor who understands things come up. Will call you out in class if you are talking or being disruptive.

Bad teacher with videos that don't help and lots of homework that doesn't help. Do not recommend. She locks your grade so you can view it throughout the semester because 30% of students fail the class, and she doesn't want everyone dropping it.

Dr Browne is one of the best math professors at KU. She gives fantastic lectures, deeply cares about her students and is always available for questions. She is also the course coordinator, which involves lots of planning prior to and throughout the semester. If you want to actually learn math and aren't afraid of hard work, make sure to take her!
Her videos are very unhelpful and there is a lot of homework assigned that leaves you no time to go back and practice old concepts. Do not take if possible.

If you like to be taught by the actual professor, skip this class. You can't submit any late work even for half credit and to get through the homework without cheating you have to spend 3+ hours in the math help room. If you enjoy your sanity, do anything you can to avoid this professor and teaching style.

Most of the bad ratings for Dr. Brown are for 115. I can't speak for the people who had her as the course coordinator for that but as a lecturer for calc two (126) she did a wonderful job. She spent plenty of time going over examples while still making sure that we understood the concepts behind the math. Overall she is a good lecturer for 126.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Browne was very helpful in office hours and her lectures would be boring at times. The class was not hard if you did all the homework and studied reasonable amounts.

Browne tries to engage her class and talk to people/ask us questions, which is awesome. Calc 3 is hard though, it feels abstract and there's less intuition you can use- also it's fast. You still have achieve assignments and weekly assignments. Dr. Browne does try to respond within 1 business day of emailing her though. She also knows resources.

Do not take MATH 115 at KU if you can avoid it. TA quality varies widely. My TA was nice but unhelpful, making learning harder. Dr. Browne is rarely accessible. Online lectures are hard to follow, there is no textbook, grades are unclear, and burnout is common. Practice exams help, but the course feels unnecessarily tedious and poorly structured.

The people rating her terribly are business calc students who don't care for calc, so they complain and say that it's Browne's fault. Everyone I know who has taken the 125/126/127 sequence loves her. Don't listen to the business students. Both the 115 course and the other sequence are well prepped for exams. She is an awesome professor.
Class is taught by TA's. My TA Samuel Armstrong was an absolute goat and made the class pretty easy. Overall

There's a lot of homework in this class so lowkey be ready. But if you have a good calc 2 foundation you'll be great in this class. she is also so kind and has a passion for teaching which you can really see through her lectures and when you meet with her one on one.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Calculus is a challenging subject, but Dr. Browne shouldn't be blamed for that. Her lecture pace is a bit fast, but it  leaves more time for working through examples in class. Also, she keeps things enjoyable with her weekly British word, a fun highlight.

Doctor Browne is a great lecturer. My only critique would be that she tends to move pretty fast, but overall she takes a lot of time to prepare the material ahead of lecture. Each lecture she works through at least 3-4 practice problems that are quite difficult, preparing us well for the exams.

I had her for both Math 126 and 127. She moved to make herself more available and she facilitated reviews for each midterm. Those classes have ample homework, but, you can do it in groups in lab.  Despite both 126 and 127 being difficult classes, if you go to office hours, she will help you succeed. She has been one of my favorite professors at KU!

Flipped classroom is terrible for learning calc. 5 exams are 70% of your grade. Can be very easy to get overwhelmed with everything in class. Give it time, be open minded, and do A LOT of practice problems. Grade it locked the entire semester.

easy and enjoyable class but oh my god her lecture videos were insufferable. i frequently had to turn them off due to the constant squeaking of her marker. also they lock the grades until it shows up on your transcript which is so so so incredibly frustrating.

You won't actually see Dr. Browne other than on test days and the lecture videos. The material is difficult so utilize the math help lab. That is the only reason I got a B in the class. Shoutout Marcel, Ben, and Mark. If you have any of these TA's, consider yourself lucky. DO NOT GET BEHIND. I can't stress this enough. Good luck.
Most of the hate is unwarranted and very exaggerated. Perfectly fine as a calc professor, the class is difficult but that's just the material. She posts the lecture slides before class.

If you schedule office hours with her she is very nice and understanding. The worst part about this course is the squeaky marker in the videos and how she locks your grade so you can't see it. The only way to see your grade is if you go into office hours. Overall, She's a nice person, but sucks you don't actually see her. Shoutout Marcel/Ben: GOATS

They need to start warning students in the enrollment phase if a class is going to be taught flipped. If a flipped method isn't for you, don't take Calc with her here. I'm not sure if all KU calc classes are taught by TAs or not, but if I had known what I would be getting into I would have taken the class at community college instead.
Class will only be taught be TAs. They will probably have heavy accents as well. Hw isnt hard but very time consuming.

Although this class was taught truly by GAs, Sarah Browne provided good videos for the lessons, although I do feel like they need to be improved in some ways. I can't rate her fully because she never taught in-person and only showed up for exams. This class is kind of diffucult if you fall behind or don't understand the concepts. Pretty good class

As someone who failed college algebra twice and got an A in this class, the most important thing you can do for your success is to take time to study the material. If you do not understand something, go to the help room or watch YouTube videos as the provided online lecture videos do not give you a chance to ask questions. YMMV with your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lectures are videos. They are actually helpful. The homework was also not too bad. In class experience depends on your TA. They might be good, or they might be like mine who seemed like he had no plan for class and was a little difficult to understand. You also can't see your grade until it is on your transcript and I don't get why.
Browne is a nice person but not good at teaching students. Just look online at Youtube videos and you can pass.
She was the worst calc 2 teacher. I felt like I never learned anything and my calc lab professor didn't help at all.

Dr. Browne is the perfect example of why you shouldn't always take reviews at face value. The class was probably 2-4 hours a week, but that's not at her discretion. She cares about her students and always made me laugh in lecture. She recognizes faces and is always happy to answer questions. Lectures move fast, there's a lot of content in calc II.

Acknowledges difficulty of class and therefore grading is very generous: 88% counts as an A, no plus/minus, drops lowest quiz and HW grades, offers 2% extra credit for lab attendance. She cares about her students and spends lots of time outside of class creating opportunities for help. GO TO PRACTICE EXAMS!!! Easy A if you put in the work.

The only time you will see or hear Dr. Browne is when you watch the prerecorded lecture videos before each class. If you have to listen to them, you will very quickly realize that you never want to hear the number 3 or the letter H ever again. Classes are taught individually by Graduate TA. Lots of online homework but not too bad.

In this course, you only are taught through lecture videos. Sarah Browne is not your professor you are taught by TAs and you barely interact with her till exams or the lecture vids. The worst part of this course is the minimal guidance and the fact they LOCK your grade for the whole semester so you have no idea what you have till after finals.

The class is flipped classroom, so Dr. Browne's lectures are all pre-recorded videos before class. Class is just the TA reviewing problems and Dr. Browne never shows. It's not that hard of a class but it depends on your efforts. Do the WebAssign Work 24 hours before the deadline and you can almost always get 101-108% percent on each HW assignment.

The videos she creates are extremely helpful. It's very time consuming, but if you dedicate that time to taking notes and going to help room, this class shouldn't be too horrible. A lot of the TAs are awful, though. You'll learn which ones to visit in help room.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Browne is a nice person and willing to help in office hours. It was more hard to understand her in class because, she can go all over the place. I just watched professor Leonard on Youtube and passed the class. The homework online does not really help only the LGA's helped. The LGA's were problems related to more test and quizzes. Work Hard!

She is a good professor, calc 2 is just hard. The two midterms and final all have about 10 points of extra credit, and are very similar to the practice tests. Do the practice tests multiple times and show up to class and you will be fine in this class. The grading scale is A=>88, B=>76, C=>64 which is generous.

I had never taken a calculus course so I was nervous because it was a flipped classroom style with prof.Browne's lecture videos and a GTA teaching the in person class. I recommend going to the math help room as needed/ just doing your homework there. As long as you stay on track and use the help resources available to you, it's really not too bad.
I can not stand listening to her lectures she smacks her lips every time she starts speaking.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: why the heck does she disable grades on canvas. also, the exams are graded insanely strict unlike calc 1. there are barley any partial points on exams.
You will have to teach yourself this class, she won't let you know your grades, and is all around stubborn and unhelpful
Sarah's notes are not the best. Be prepared to do your own studying and go to help room/ tutoring.

The TA's teach math 115 so choose Debjit if he's an option. Best TA out of everyone, gives the most help and feedback. Sarah Browne has practice tests before exams and a practice final. Its a tough class but go to the help room and you'll be fine.

midterm and final grading is extremely harsh with little explanation. do not bother taking notes in lecture she goes faster than your hand can physically move. youtube and helproom will save you, WOULD NOT RECOMMEND HER.

This class was hard because the math was difficult, but this professor was very organized and cared about the students. She would answer questions to make sure you understood what you needed to, and go over problems if you asked. She was a nice person which made it much easier to get through the lectures. The British word of the day were also fun.

I really liked Dr. Browne. I went to her office hours the day of a test and she helped me so much. She cares about your success as long as you do. Lectures are clear and British Word of the Day is fun!

Sarah records lectures online, and typical lecture format is taught by random TA's. This is about the class- not the professor. Get photomath+, it shows you steps of how to solve problems so you learn. Use the free tutoring at anschutz, watch youtube videos, STUDY practice exams as the tests are the same. Prepare to be BUSY if you want a good grade

sarah brown is a great professor, but the TAs are terrible. I didnt learn a single thing from my TA. the practice exams are the same as the actual exams, so definitely take advantage of those. if you are struggling, reach out to sarah directly or else you will struggle to pass the class. this class NEEDS more experienced TAs!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is not set up for the success of students. The flipped class could be helpful if taught right, however time in class is not maximized and is quite honestly a waste of students' time. You cannot see your grade until the end of the semester, so you have no idea where you stand going into the midterms or the final. Prepare to have a tutor.

She's quite friendly and accessible. The class is very difficult and test-heavy but she does hold practice exams and out-of-class review sessions. There is a lot of homework for this class and she lectures at lightning speed, but if you're willing to go the extra mile an A is gettable in this class.

Professor is nice and good at teaching. People's gripes are with how math is taught at KU, not with the professor. KU Calc is taught by inexperienced TAs. They are often REALLY bad at teaching or hard to understand because they're foreign. I'd recommend taking Calc at JCCC where the class is taught by real professors and math help system is better.

You'll rarely if ever meet the professor instead her Calculus 115 classes are taught by TA's. I've only had success so far through tutoring, working diligently outside of class and THANK GOD FOR MY CHEMISTRY TUTOR ON YOUTUBE. Watch out for tests, as your two midterms and final dictate your grade for the entire class. Assignments will not save u.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
There is no actual lecture from a professor, just videos and problems with a TA. TA's are unhelpful and hard to understand. You WON'T BE ABLE TO SEE YOUR GRADE in the class until it shows up on your transcript!!
Be prepared to teach yourself. You will spend hours at tutoring, watching extra videos, etc.
TAKE THIS ELSEWHERE IF YOU HAVE THE OPTION.

I would recommend taking this at a community college for credit instead. Weird power dynamic with Dr. Browne and the TAs, they are not suppose to teach or help one person at a time. Most of the time the class sits in silence. There are no official lectures just videos. You are basically teaching yourself. No wonder it is the most dropped class @KU.

Professor Browne was an alright professor. She wasn't the best one I've ever had but wasn't bad. I think my biggest complaint would be she never had canvas calculate your grades, which made it hard to know how you were doing in the class. She did give us British words of the day, which gave us something to look forward to during the lectures.

You have to watch the pre lecture videos and the videos suck and they are long then you got to class and the TA's don't teach. this department has a strange obsession with explaining why methods work more than ACTUALLY just applying them and showing examples. Dr. Browne is awesome! Practice exams, regular assignments, small labs, help room open weekdays, practice problems in class, and lectures available online. Tough course with difficult material, but if you attend lectures and labs and keep up on the work you can do well. Dr. Browne's lectures and review sessions are super helpful.

Dr.Browne is a good professor overall, however the instructors are awful. They do not have a masters degree in math and most of them hate their job either way. Dr. Browne is a great professor. I am naturally good at math, which I'm sure helps, but the way she taught and engaged students during a lecture was really nice. I would never recommend any KU student take a math course through this instructor. This has been by far the most disorganized way I had to learn a class. Honestly, I loved organic chemistry because of him. Took OCHEM 1 and 2 with him and although he isn't the nicest guy, he is fair with his exams. DO THE WORKSHEETS AND PRACTICE EXAMS until you understand them and you will for sure get an A. Shoutout to PLUS for being so helpful with this class, I owe a lot of it to them too.

Go to PLUS sessions, get tutoring, and be willing to make extra time out of class to understand the concepts. Dr. Benson gives a lot of resources and access to the 330 course for review -- spend time during the break to make sure you understand the reactions and basic terms. Dr. Benson was very understanding and covered the material extensively.

Dr. Benson is a passionate and well-organized lecturer. It is a flipped class, but it is by far the best-organized flipped class I have ever taken. His out-of-class lecture videos are anywhere from 5-20 minutes on average, so not long, and his in-class worksheets are very helpful for the exams. Also, take advantage of his practice exams!

I did poorly in this class and I STILL enjoyed it. Dr. Benson is a very fair person who really gives it his all. I really put in a lot of effort into this class and sadly fell behind due to taking ochem 1 with a different professor. I highly recommend putting lots of time into notetaking if you want succeed. reviews.comment: I dare you to find me a better structured orgo class than Benson's. He cares so much about orgo that his passion got me excited about the material. Some may say he is a little rude but I believe he is misunderstood, man is a sweetheart.

Dude is the goat. Gives out a bunch of accessible resources and makes sure to walk you through topics you don't understand. Dr. Benson is very intelligent but I struggled in his class because of the difficult content and the flipped classroom style of learning. If flipped learning doesn't work for you, don't take this class.

Most classes don't work in a flipped classroom style, but Dr. Benson made it work really well. Benson is an amazing professor for OChem! He truly cares about the success of his students, and is offers additional help for each learning style. Dr. Benson is a very competent professor. The class is SUPER exam heavy. Thankfully, he gives practice exams that are similar to the actual exams. Professor Benson is very organized and is very knowledgeable about the material. He explained the concepts in a way that made sense and held study sessions frequently. He assigns a good amount of homework, but there is a ton of material to cover for this class so it was helpful.
