The graded work and the after class problems aren't enough and the book does not have the answers to the practice problems in there unless you pay more
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He does not seem to care much about students at all. At review sessions he speeds through material so he can go home, he makes no effort to make any conversation with students, and does not like to answer questions. This is the first class I wont be getting an A in and I would highly recommend taking this course with another professor.

If you read before lectures then go to class and do the in-class practice, you will definitely be prepared for exams. The types of problems you do in class are the types of problems that make up 80% of what is on tests. If you do the bare minimum of reading and going to class, you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Benson was incredible he provided different styles for learning and really put effort into additional lectures for outside of class Take organic chem with him please, best organic chem teacher, the material itself is difficult but I really enjoyed his class and you have everything you need to do well

Benson is an ok professor, but most of the class is teaching yourself the mechanisms. Class time is just going over practice problems and asking questions so definitely read the book and watch the PCEs before class to do well. The final is really hard and he did not curve any tests over the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally the worse class I have taken ever in my life. I took 330 & 335. Usually a straight A student, put in hours and hours into this class, and still did not do well (struggled for a C-, got a B in 330). Hard info, he doesn't seem to care about students, could tell that he gave up in the middle of the semester. Online/hybrid due to covid
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Benny is kinda a homie, but also kinda not. He definitely made this semester extremely difficult because he caught so many people cheating last semester. I know it makes sense technically, but there are definitely still people working together which drives up the test average and screws everyone who's following directions. Great at teaching though
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His class was super informative and he is really funny sometimes. Not a bad class but do NOT get on his bad side. I had a class on the 3rd floor of Fraser that ended 10 min before his class so I would sprint down Jayhawk Blvd to get there but would always be a minute or 2 late and he would call me out in front of the entire class so just a heads up

You do all learning outside of class through PCEs, but if you pay attention to those he covers everything you need to know. Lecture time is spent practicing and reviewing concepts. is plus/minus sadly meaning 92.5 for an A. He really does make OChem make sense. he explains mechanisms and the logic they follow really well.

Dr. Benson was an ok professor. Youre mostly teaching yourself . Your grade is determined by your scores on tests so study. He is impossible to get in touch with and is very strict on his guidelines. The TA was also a bit pretentious and insensitive when discussing coursework. Just take the course and get it out of the way as agonizing as it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He will help you out in class and outside of class if you are stuck on problems from his lecture. Reading before class will help you understand conceptually but it is more important to do practice problems and understand the logic behind them in order to do well on exams. If you fall behind, it is difficult to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Benson is a good teacher and he is very firm on his expectations. He makes it pretty clear what will be covered on his exams through his lectures and worksheets. He teaches straight out of the textbook and he hardly throws any curveballs out to his students. As long as you practice the problems, you will be fine. He never responds to emails.
This class is really, really hard. Dr. Benson makes organic chemistry a little more accessible to people without a strong chemistry background. Would recommend.
Professor Benson is an awesome organic chemistry instructor. Reading and taking notes over the assigned book work is the key to doing well in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Read the textbook before class. He offers lots of practice. It's a lot of work but if you do the things he suggests then it isn't too bad.
These recent hateful comments do not reflect the learning environment that Prof. Benson creates for his students.

Dr. Benson was the absolute worst professor I have had, he is never accessible during "office hours," he lectures straight from the book, he is extremely unprofessional, he says he will give partial credit on tests and then ends up not giving it, the list goes on and on. If you can take a different prof for chem335, please save yourself and do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I had Benson for Chem 330 and he was great. It's like he was a completely different person for 335 though. He's barely accessible & when he is, he isn't helpful at all. He suspected that people were cheating so he purposefully made each test harder than the previous to weed out the cheaters, meaning the people who didn't cheat were left high & dry
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you can't dedicate 3+ hrs to this class every day/took a different professor for Ochem I, this class will be a struggle. Class is a brisk review of topics with not enough TA's to answer everyone's questions. I reached out to him after failing an exam and his response was short and he didn't seem concerned or to care. Not a great experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I expected to absolutely HATE o chem, but Dr. Benson made it enjoyable and relatively easy. The final is optional and replaces the lowest test grade so that helps out a lot! It's clear that Benson cares about his students. When doing practice problems in class, he'll walk around and check your work personally, doesn't just leave it to the TAs.

Benson's super chill but don't let that fool you; he'll make you work for your grade! I'd suggest reading the sections (they're short). I didn't do practice problems outside of class but we do a lot in class & they're similar to the test, so make sure you understand those. Tests are 86% of the grade; the final replaces your lowest test score.

Dr. B is super chill. Be prepared for class! Lectures are for reviewing material you've practiced at home & problem solving. If you're not prepared you'll be lost (not an option to cram!!). Don't be afraid to visit office hours and ask for help. Read and practice! Ask ?s from the beginning and again, practice! Read, practice, ask ?s, practice!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Benson makes organic chemistry fun and enjoyable, despite it being a very challenging course. The lectures are never boring and attendance is not mandatory but there are in class clicker questions. Homework is pretty minimal, just small 3-4 question pre lecture assignments. To pass, read/take notes over the reading. It really does help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Benson is very smart and expects his students to reach his level fairly quickly. He will not curve or adjust any test grades despite if the TA who graded it just scribbled out your work in pen. It is very test heavy but you do get to drop your lowest score and have it replaced with the grade from the final. Do lots of practice problems!

I was nervous about taking ochem because it's known to be a difficult class. However, if you read the book and take good notes, participate in class, and do practice problems, this class will be fine. You have to put in the work to get an A. He lectures well, and I am looking forward to having him again for ochem II.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: READ the textbook BEFORE each class; the sections aren't that long and it does an amazing job at explaining tough topics. Get heavily involved when doing in-class group problems. Lastly, PRACTICE problems are critical. If you neglect to practice, you WILL NOT do well. Benson will curve scores if exam averages are low enough but DON'T rely on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: To do well in Ochem in his class, read the textbook before the lecture. Group problem is really helpful for your practice. The test is quite challenging but does the practice exam help. For the final, study from his study guide and do the old exam.

This class is all about preparedness. If you can't learn from the book/outside of class or lack solid Gen Chem & OChem 1 foundations, you'll be fighting to catch up all semester. Doing the reading and practice problems is required to understand the lectures, which involve a lot of practice too. Tip: Immediately drop if you fail Exam 1. Don't be me.

Do the reading prior to the lectures, and be prepared to actively participate. The more problems you do the more simple the material seems. Also, memorization doesn't help, its the knowledge of how to use certain reagents to get a desired product when conditions change.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I learned more in his classes than I have in any other class. He is good about going in depth and giving examples and practice problems that are very relevant to test questions. He also gives the class the exam from the previous semester to help study - which is very very helpful!

Very nice and easy going, but doesn't like seeing people on their phones instead of working. See him around campus sometimes and he's always down to answer questions or just chat, super down to earth. If you do the assigned readings, pay attention to what is stressed in class, and then do practice problems and the practice exams you should do great

Unless you're really gifted, O. Chem is going to be a struggle. That being said, Dr. Benson does his best to help you through it. Be ready for lots of reading and practice problems, and, like most of the KU Chemistry department, a lot of exams.
Dr Benson was a great professor and I really enjoyed the format of the lectures with all the group problems and clicker questions. Made everything really easy to understand and apply.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: O-Chem is going to be a class you have to work for. Benson is the best teacher you'll get at KU for this class. He's clear and replies to emails quickly and will always meet with you outside the class. Listen to his advice- read the textbook and do TONS of practice problems. He is on your side at the end of the day.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Benson gets a lot of criticism, but I think he's the best bet for actually learning organic chem. Other professors have exams identical to practice exams, which is nice, but if you need to take the MCAT or just genuinely want to understand the material, Benson is your guy. Read. Also understand Dipoles.
This course was descent. Don't go to class, read the book, and you will get the grade you want.

He is smart, but so smart that he doesn't even fathom why others can't understand the concepts. For everyone who O Chem doesn't come naturally to(the majority of students), expect to put in an obscene amount of hours to reading and studying just to get a lower grade than you expected. Choose different teacher if you have the option.

Benson was a very clear teacher, but organic chemistry itself is pretty difficult. I found the exams to be hard as hell, with little remorse. I studied for each exam around 30-40 hours I'd say, and only a couple times did I pull off an A. READ THE BOOK OVER AND OVER IT WILL GET YOU THE A

Dr. Benson is a very smart man, but unfortunately that means he expects you to be, too. The tests are over a ton of material and always have curveballs, and they are very hard. Homework before every class, but the majority of the grade depends on the tests. His lectures are helpful but excruciatingly boring. He tends to be cranky and rude.

There's no getting around it: OChem is hard. There's a lot of work and studying, just because of the subject matter. Benson is very smart but isn't great one-on-one. Do not skip lectures. The tests can be a little tricky, so you'll have to put a lot of hours into studying for them.
I liked Professor Benson. O chem is a hard class but he is a very clear teacher. Reading and doing the pre-lectures are super helpful and then do practice problems. He is really willing to help.

Organic Chemistry is difficult and he puts some trick questions in the exams. Go to class no matter what and pay attention. I did every single online and textbook problem and managed a B, but a lot of people didn't. You have to put hours of work into this class. He can get really sassy and rude during lectures so sit away from the front.

I was pretty scared of this class before, but Benson made it manageable. The pre lecture questions are an easy 60 pts and help understanding the material. Read the assigned chapters and do practice problems; it makes all the difference. He also gives the previous year's exam with an answer key that is a life saver and is similar to his next test.

Dr. Benson does a great job conveying the information necessary to succeed in organic chemistry. DO NOT SKIP LECTURE. If you go to every lecture and put in the work to understand the concepts and not just memorize them you will do just fine. The tests can be difficult, but he has been known to curve them depending on the average scores received.

Dr. Benson is an excellent professor who is deeply passionate about Organic Chemistry. He cares about his students very much. He teaches how not to memorize the subject but to understand it. He doesn't demand you do things, but he is there if you need him. I wish I went to class more. Exams are beautifully designed and very fair. Curves when needed

He gets on the kids in the front of the class to participate in class. Then he laughed at a guy I knew in class for making a totally reasonable guess. I've heard, too, that he has made fun of kids in office hours. He's a decent teacher, I got an A,  but that behavior struck me.

Dr. Benson writes very fair exams and will not try to trick you. He is not afraid to curve and has done so several times. Lectures are problem solving sessions, so they won't be helpful unless you're caught up with the reading, which can be difficult when you are busy with other classes. If you can do the homework, you'll be set. Don't cram!

Dr. Benson is a nice guy and makes lecture as engaging as possible for such a large class. He is really friendly in office hours, and met with me outside of his hours just to go over my tests. In class activities are primarily what the tests will look like. Homework is really easy, should be an automatic 60pts. Old exams are VERY helpful.
He's a great teacher, you just HAVE to come to class! Otherwise it's not that hard.
Very similar to CHEM 330. Great professor. Taught everything you needed to know for tests I just didn't study enough.

It's not necessary whatsoever to attend this class. I read the book and did the homework and did fine on the tests. Work hard to get a good grade on the first two because the third one is super hard. Benson is not a very good teacher, so like I said it's useless going to class.
Dr. Benson has a temper and storms out of class sometimes. Loves his in-class exercises for tests. Good luck, because his class is close to impossible.

Benson is a good teacher. Definitely read and use the book. My advice would be to get your hands on as many old tests as possible, and PRACTICE them, because the questions are going to be very similar to what you see on exams. End of chapter problems are helpful, but not necessary because they are so time consuming. Easy if you put in the effort!

Dr. Benson is my favorite instructor at KU. Before taking his class, I had heard horror stories about OCHEM. I can see how the subject can be intimidating, but he did a great job of making it very clear. It is a tough class, but it helped me a lot on the MCAT - of the subjects on the MCAT, OCHEM took the least time to study for. Pre-meds, take him.

Dr. Benson was a great teacher.  He follows the textbook really well which makes studying much easier.  Do all the end of chapter problems that he recommends; they are very similar to the test questions/format!

Dr. Benson was amazing at teaching such a hard class. He walked through every mechanism and had students come up to the front to do examples. NOT helpful one-on-one. Very condescending. If you work hard and practice JUST as he tells you, you'll get an A no problem.

Another course where the book is much more helpful than the professor. Not going to class hasn't hurt me at all because I know how to teach myself. He posts lectures (not notes) online that kind of help to stay on track. Tests part MC part drawing. PRACTICE PROBLEMS!!!!!!! He was alright as far as professors go.

Dr. Benson is a great professor. His lectures are easy to follow and fairly helpful, but I got the most out of reading the book and doing the practice problems, which are really similar to what you will see on the exams. This class was a ton of work, but I definitely learned a lot and ended up with an A.

I only went to class a couple times last semester...I found the textbook to be much more helpful because you can read at your own pace. ALWAYS do the "suggested problems" because they are very similar to what the test questions will be like!!!!

Dr. Benson is a great professor. I went to every lecture and found them very helpful, in addition to doing many of the suggested problems at home. The class isn't hard if you put effort into it, but try your best to not get behind on problems or notes. Your grade is dependent on how much work you put into it.

Going to lecture is unnecessary. Just read the book and make sure to do ALL the recommended book problems and go over old tests. The tests get progressively harder so do well on the first two especially. DO NOT BLOW OFF THE FOURTH TEST IF YOU DID GOOD ON THE FIRST THREE. The final is almost all the fourth test. Not too bad of a class. I got an A.

Very smart guy, but not all smart guys are teachers. He is like a talking text book who talks way too fast, which is why I stopped going to class. I managed to pull out an A, but I have put more time into this class than any other in my college career. Be prepared to study. A lot.
This subject is just really hard, but he's good.

Benson is alright as a teacher. He does a good job with his lectures. He isn't someone that really wants to interact with you face to face though. The amount of effort you put into the class will ultimately dictate your grade. Read the book and do all of the recommended practice problems and the tests will be very manageable.

A very good teacher in lecture, but if you need help then don't even bother going to him. He's rude and unhelpful. I recommend going to PLUS, instead. Tests are much easier if you read the book and do the practice problems he posts online. I didn't think the material itself was very difficult, but it takes a lot of time and practice to master.

Your grade reflects how much time you have to devote to this class. If you do practice problems you can get an A easily. He isn't sympathetic to situations (personal or emergency) since he drops a test. Overall very straightforward and FAIR teacher. Just make sure life doesn't get in the way of Chem 626.

Dr. Benson is great. He teaches in a logical, clear fashion that shows a firm grasp of the material. And I found him to be a very friendly and approachable person outside of class. His tests are certainly reasonable, as long as you put in the work he asks of you. I'm glad I took his class--I feel that I learned quite a bit.

The textbook is your best resource in this class.  I learned a lot more from it than from Benson.  Be prepared to for an attitude if your ever approach Benson.  I didn't find him to be a likable person.

Benson was very rude to me when I inquired as to the grading of a test.  I also had problems with Rachel (head TA) responding to email.  This class is tough.  Do your best on the first 2 tests bc the 3rd is hard, and the 4th & the final are killer. This class spoiled my 4.0. Oh well.

Benson is a good to average teacher.  OCHEM is just a class that is going to require a lot of extra work on your part.  I didn't start reading the book until the end, which was dumb.  I think the best way to learn OCHEM is to read the book, and  MAYBE Benson's lectures will help clarify certain things.

Benson is extremely fair, predictable, and straight-forward. If you don't get the grade you wish, it's your own fault. O-Chem is difficult and you must dedicate time to study it, but Benson will guide you if you meet him halfway. Use his study tips; he knows what works! Also, don't bring electronics, of any sort, to class. He'll call you out.
Attendance was definitely not mandatory. Found the book extraordinarily well structured though. Tests are very fair. O.Chem isn't all that bad.

Benson makes this class great.  He really loves what he does and makes his exams very straight forward as long as you attend class. As for myself I went to class everyday yet never looked at a book and received an A in this course.
Organic Chemistry is my favorite class at KU thanks to Benson. Benson is an interesting and smart dude. Gives fun and interesting examples of chemistry.  Just read the book and you'll do fine.

Dr. Benson is incredibly interested in this subject and tries hard to extend that interest to his students (to the point that I would add !'s to my notes). Students may complain that it is a lot of memorization, but working consistently on the quizzes and paying attention in class allows you to learn how and why mechanisms work without memorization

I understand one of the comments about him seeming arrogant. However, the people complaining about the difficulty or his teaching are completely wrong. He is clear and thorough and you get to drop a test, that's like a curve.

Benson's a good instructor, but if you're not a chemistry major, then memorizing reagents and mechanisms is about as interesting, meaningful, and useful as memorizing strings of random numbers. The biology department really needs to come up with its own version of this class.

Amazing teacher! Read the book, go to class, and do the problems and you will be fine! He is nice and will help you outside of class, although I believe he is lear in lectures. His fourth test is the most difficult by default he doesn't make it that way on purpose, organic chemistry just contains a lot of material. Book is very helpful.
He teaches the material well, but comes off very arrogant.

He is a decent teacher, however I taught myself much of the material that I learned. In class he gets upset about the slightest interruptions,which is kind of ridiculous considering its a room of 500 20 somethings. He made the fourth test of the semester extremely difficult because he was upset about attendance. Needs to lighten up/enjoy his job

I am not allowed to say what i would like to say about professor benson in this text box. I have never liked chemistry but i enjoy biology. Taking ochem with Benson has given me two options: drop my dream of going to med school simply because his tests are ruthless OR transfer.

Organic chemistry is not easy but as long as you are willing to put in the work you will get a good grade in this class. Benson is a good teacher and provides discussions outside of class to allow you to ask questions and get extra help. Tests are hard but as long as you do all the homework problems and understand them you will do ok.
he decided because the class average was to high and the attendence was low he would create an extreamly dificult test and drop the average although this even hurts those coming to class!

Dr Benson was awesome. I had him for O chem 1 & 2 and I couldn't have asked for a better prof. He has discussions almost every day. And his exams are very reasonable. Organic is not cake but he tries to help out as much as possible as long as you take the initiative.

This class sucks, but I personally can't stand chemistry.  I went to maybe 3 lectures becuase it was so boring.  Somehow got a B but i almost screwed myself by dropping Test 2 instead of Test 4.  Make sure that the LAST TEST is the one you drop because it is ten times harder than the first 3. Final is a lot like the old final, not bad
Don't expect him to help you out on your final grade.

Excellent teacher who is effective at getting the message across. Draws diagrams by hand rather than powerpointing them. The material can be difficult if you get behind in reading. Read and work on practice problems consistently, and it will be simple.

OChem is a hard class but the way Dr.Benson teaches is GREAT. He really helps you understand the material. The End of Chapter and Extra Problems help out a lot for tests. There are times when he gives tons of reactions and mechanisms but it's not so bad. He's also extremely helpful. I thought OChem was difficult but it's doable with him.
Hey this guy is a great professor. He truly loves o-chem he's smart and he will do whatever he can to help you do well in the class. Overall a great class =].
I thought he did a great job getting the material across. It actually helped to go to class and listen to his lecture unlike some prof.

Dr. Benson appears to be friendly and interested in the material. His testing average is fairly high, towards an 80%, and can be easily studied for by examining problems in the back of the book.  However, he currently has the tendency to review a lot of chemical equations, which can get boring somewhat quickly.

I agree with the guy below me, this class wasn't as difficult as i expected. was it easy? hell no, but its certainly not impossible. i recommend pro-active studying and READING the book instead of relying on lecture notes. Read each chapter 2 to 4 a piece (it gets easier everytime, i promise) and work the practice problems he posts. u will succeed

I thought this class was really easy.  Everyone always talks about Organic Chemistry being really hard, but the class average for the first test was around 86-88%.  Second test average dropped to around 77%.  I don't really ever go to class, but if you can do all the problems he posts (which aren't too bad), then you should get an A in the class.

He wasn't really that bad of a teacher. Sometimes he had a lot of trouble explaining the topics but usually got his point across. The homework was CRAZY long and pointless and some fo the tests we're tricky but review your power points and read the book and you'll get an A in the class.

I thought his lectures where pointless. I struggled in hs with chem but not too much here. The test are hard but do well in lab and on hw and you will be fine. He curved our class like 10%, really. But the homework sucked, make friends.

I thought I knew a lot about Chem before I took this class..boy was I wrong.Be careful with the tests, the questions can be tricky.The homework takes forever.He clearly knows alot about the subject but does not express it very well.Thinks he is funny but really he is not.

Benson enjoys the subject but makes isn't very good at teaching it. Tests are nothing like the homework. Btw homework takes forever!! He thinks he's funny but it just ends up being awkward. Hopefully your good at Chem...I thought I was until I took his course.

He is really smart, and this semester (Spring 2008) is his first time teaching Chem 125...He's so smart he can't "dumb down" the subject so that it can be understood...And I never knew CHEM 125 (the easiest chem class...supposably) has homework that takes over 4 hours to complete...I just hope he curves the grades... Just hope your lab is easy!

Professor Benson is not a very good educator for Chemistry. His lectures are an overview of the book word for word. Be careful on tests and make sure to study subjects w/in the chpt. not talked about. If you don't understand by just reading the book (like myself) lecture is somewhat useful. I suggest finding a friend who does well in Chem for help.
This man is horrible. Lectures are almost useless, since the book is a much better teacher than Prof. Benson. The tests are hard and sometimes near impossible. Avoid this teacher at all costs.

Terrible class and teacher!  Tests were impossible and homework was ridiculously long.  I never had a clue what was going on in lecture.  He tried to be helpful, but wasn't very successful.  I wish I had taken regular organic instead of honors.

I LOVE Dr. Burger-Dunn. I am so glad I was able to take her class for CHEM 130 & CHEM 135. She is super organized, knowledgeable, and approachable. She really cares about her students and made chemistry as easy to understand as possible. It's still a really hard class but she does the best she can to make it easy. I couldn't recommend her enough.
Fantastic lecturer!

I have her for CHEM 130 and CHEM 135, she's an amazing professor. She's well organized with all her lectures, assignments, homework, quiz, tests, and study guides. She gives study guides for every chapter, the study guide are basically like the tests but harder which prepares me better for the upcoming tests.
The lectures are very well organized, we always have the class day before the test to review, and she explains everything very well!
one of my favorite professors. made a hard class a bit easier
Burger-Dunn is the best professor I've ever had! I took her class for CHEM130 and 135 and got B+ in both.
She's a great person and better professor. If you are taking Gen Chem at KU, take it with her. If you are thinking about taking Honors Gen Chem, don't. Take Chem 130/135 it with her.

Amazing x1000. I love her dearly, QUITE literally the best chem professor you could get at KU, always explained concepts clearly, gave physical demonstrations, and explained them. iClickers were easy; I actually wanted to come to class. Brought back my love for chemistry after suffering from AP Chem. Will never forget her, love so dearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Love this lady so much. She's so helpful and accommodating and genuinely cares about her students doing well in the class. There were so many point opportunities. Anyone who puts in at least some effort in the class can do well, Dr. Burger-Dunn makes it easy for everyone to understand. By far my favorite professor, I'm taking another class of hers!

She teaches gen. chem. with the assumption that it is her students' first time ever taking a chemistry class, which I really appreciated since it has been a few years since I last took chemistry. She also wants all her students to succeed and gives lots of opportunities to practice class content and make up points before and after tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Burger-Dunn was fantastic. The best way to describe her is mother-like. She just is approachable, caring and wants the best for her students. Pay attention when she lectures cuz it'll all make sense- she really dumbs things down & explains things well. No dropped exams but it's really not a big deal. No joke, this course made me love chemistry

She is an awesome person. I was nervous coming into chem but her lectures are amazing and easy to understand. She gives you so much practice work for the exams it's near impossible to fail if you do those
This women is amazing. I actually love her, she helps anyone pass her class with her best abilities. She's so understanding and kind. Her lectures are great and i just actually love her so much.

She made chemistry super easy to understand. I felt like I knew what I was doing and if I didn't her office hours were very welcoming. She doesn't go super fast and does experiments to make class fum.

Even if you're bad at chemistry, you will be fine. There are 3 exams plus 1 final. She gives you so many resources to prepare for the exams. And extra credit. If you get your work in, you're fine. She mentioned that you can average an 80 on exams and still have an A. Such a great professor and she is soooo nice.

Homework: weekly ALEKS hw, pretty ez, worksheets and quizzes are every other week. 

Exams: up to 100 points each (x4). A written portion (85 points) and an online portion (15 points, ez).

Extra credit: 5 points extra after exams

Lectures: steady normal pace, and is easy to follow, does demos in class.

Professor Burger-Dunn was my favorite professor. She gives plenty of time for homework, tests, and quizzes. Lecture notes and answer keys are posted online for review. She properly prepares you for tests with study guides and practice tests.

135// She 100% loves chemistry and has your best interest at heart. She's a great lady and strives to make sure you actually understand the content. She doesn't have geo-location on for IClicker wich I love and she gives enough material that if you fail the tests or quizzes, you can bring your grade up with the hw or extra credit.
Good at explaining, personable.

Absolutely loved Burger Dunn. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS!! They are so helpful, and she truly does care about her students a lot. There were 4 exams (and a final), but each is only worth 10% of your grade. My average was an 80% on the test, and I still got an A+. You only need to have 80% of clicker points in order to get full points in the category.

Amazing professor. She is always willing to help and accommodate students when needed. It is clear that she cares deeply for all her students and their success. The difficulty of the class itself really just depends on your comfort level with gen chem. I thought it was pretty easy. She is very clear with what needs to be done to pass.

She is probably the best professor I have taken so far. I have taken both Chem 130 and 135 through her, and have gotten an A in both. Her lectures are well paced and helpful, and match well to what is asked about on tests. Nothing is a surprise if you utilize class and her practice exams well! 
Homework is completion-great grade buffer.

Professor Burger-Dunn was great! I was nervous about taking chemistry, which is not my strongest subject. But in Prof. Burger-Dunn's class, I rarely struggled. She gives many great study guides and practice exams for all exams.
Burger Dunn is the best professor. She not only an amazing teacher but she also cares deeply about her students well being. As long as you pay attention and stay on top of y

Prof B-D was very helpful when I had a accident outside of class that required me to be gone for about a month. In class her lectures are very good and she is very welcoming and encourages her students to ask questions.

This class was very well structured. She is so nice and a great professor. All assignments, quizzes, and tests are very well written and valid for the course. She is very forgiving in the way her grade weighting is for assignments, quizzes, and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Burger-Dunn made learning chemistry super accessible. I believe if you: show up to class and participate (in iClickers), try hard on the test and just complete the assignments you will be okay. She used a 1000 point-based grading system that makes visualizing your progress super easy.

The way Prof. Burger-Dunn explained each concept during her lectures made you understand everything immediately. She posts a practice test you can look at before every exam and if you understand what's on that you will get an A on the exams. She gives out lots of extra credit opportunities and you can tell she cares about what she teaches.
Amazing professor. Go to class!! Exam criteria is clearly outlined, so if you use what is provided you will be fine. I really enjoyed chem 130 with burger-dunn.

Professor Burger-Dunn is amazing! Her lectures are so clear and engaging, and you can tell that she cares about her students' academics. While the tests are worth a large portion of the grade, she gives ample extra credit and other opportunities to make up points.

Genuinely an amazing teacher and teaching style. She has many options for office hours. There are opportunities for extra credit or other assignments to get your grade up. However if you just do the homework, worksheets, quizzes, and study just a bit then you'll get an A.
She is an incredible teacher. For starters, I strongly recommend Miss Burger-Dunn

Dr. Burger-Dunn is one of the best professors I've had at KU. She's very nice and responsive outside of class. Her tests make sense and the homework system actually prepares you for the exams. So much extra credit offered. Highly recommend taking her class for both 130 and 135
isnt a good teacher overall. goes way to fast

"Burger-Dunn on a million backs, Burger-Dunn for a million flashbulbs"

Generational professor, contender for Ballon d'Or. Super clear lectures. Tests are true evaluation of your knowledge, not trying to trick you or be intentionally confusing. ALEKS HW system is easy and very helpful. She is very easy to talk to and wants you to succeed.
She's a great teacher, but if you want a good grade, make sure to go to all of the lectures

She is awesome. Her lecture slides are great, they walk through every step to solving problems. She is very accommodating if you are sick and wants her students to succeed. There are no surprises on her exams, they are similar to study guides!

Amazing professor someone you can build a relationship with outside of academia. Runs a normal classroom. Quizzes and worksheets alternate with one another every other week. Extra credit opportunities are accessible outside of class. Night exams, which I prefer so I can do extra studying during the day as needed.

She is an amazing professor! She gives extremely clear lectures that are engaging and oftentimes include interactive demonstrations. A majority of the points for the class are from homework or quizzes, but even though there are a few tests, she offers plenty of extra credit throughout the year. As long as you study, you will do well on the tests!

I've taken both chemistry sections with Dr. Burger-Dunn and she's fantastic at explaining concepts. She also really cares about your success and even though it's a giant lecture bowl class she still tries to make it interactive and provides a lot of resources for help. The online homework software is also much better than other programs I've used.

Amazing! She explains everything very well and takes a LOT of care to make sure everyone understands and feels comfortable asking questions. Lots of opportunities to earn points, plus provides lots of study resources. You can tell she really cares about students' success. First time I have had really solid understanding of some of these concepts.

Amazing professor. Dr. Burger-Dunn is so caring towards every one of her students and she has made a huge difference in my passion for science and the chemistry department. The class is extremely easy, just focus on understanding the basics. She wants you to succeed, so use the resources, including office hours.

She provides the lecture PowerPoint slides on canvas. These slides an extremely detailed and are not overwhelming to read. I suggest listening in class and writing the notes on the slides outside of class. She goes though information slowly so it can be understood during lecture. She is amazing! I suggest going to the TA help sessions too.
Such a good professor who provides helpful study material and really tries to take it easy on students. Loved her class.

Professor Burger-Dunn is fantastic. Her lectures are clear and the homework seriously helps to prepare you for the exams. She makes chemistry easily digestible and will over-explain anything if you just ask. Her tests aren't necessarily easy, but she works to prepare you. As long as you do the assignments and listen, this class isn't difficult.
Her goal is to help students succeed. Great informational lectures. Many extra credit opportunties. I wish she taught all my classes
Take intro Chem with Burger-Dunn. She gives plenty of materials that prepare you extremely well for the exams. Plenty of extra credit, and the exams are fair and easy.

Great teacher explains the content in a way that is comprehensible. You can tell she enjoys teaching chemistry. Homework takes a bit of time but prepares you well for the test. The tests themselves are mildly challenging, if you study you'll get a decent grade.

Professor Burger-Dunn is amazing. She makes things VERY clear in her lectures, allots plenty of time to ask her questions or get one-on-one help with her. She adequately prepares me for each exam, with a helpful study guide and review sessions. I have done GREAT on all her exams because I always feel prepared! I enrolled in Chem 135 with her too!

Dr Burger-Dunn is an absolutely amazing professor who cares about her students as individuals as well as academics. Her lectures were so comprehensive that the textbook was not needed. The homework assignments were easy to do and her office hours were very accessible and very helpful. She is a wonderful and caring teacher.

I took her class last year. She is so good at explaining things clearly during lecture and her examples are excellent to follow. Tests can be tricky, but she provides all the resources and support needed to do well. Just study alot.

I loved Prof. BD!! One of my favorite professors to date. She is so welcoming and able to talk through class topics in her office hours if needed. The tests are hard but manageable if you study and pay attention in class. Another thing is you should go to class even though it is not required. Again, love her so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher, I would take any of her classes!

BEST PROF EVER. i could not say enough good things about prof B-D. she is very genuine and wants you to succeed. chemistry has always been really hard for me but i took her for CHEM130 and CHEM135 and easily got an A because she is just so good at teaching. ILY PROF BD

I loved Mrs. BD and her teaching style! It is a very fast paced course so if you need more time to learn, I would not recommend however her office hours are super helpful and she's a great person! Beware of the tests though they can be difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Burger-Dunn is an extremely good professor. Her lectures are very easy to understand and if she knows the class is struggling, she will go into more detail. There many study and help resources, and expectations are clearly stated. A lot of easy points to earn and there is extra credit available. Sometimes she can oversimplify topics.
Love Proff. B-D. She is always super helpful and answers my emails very quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: As long as you actively participate, you will pass this class. My average on exams was 60%, but, I still have the minimum needed for a B. Attendance isn't required, but you do need to bank enough clicker question points (participation only). Lectures are clear and easy to follow as long as you keep up; they are also recorded.

Dr.Dunn is an amazing person and an amazing teacher. Dr.Dunn went the extra mile to help me learn. Dr.Dunn is very easy to email and to work with. She is very good at accommodating people's needs.  The class wasn't easy, but Dr.Dunn made me want to learn more about chemistry. Go to office hours and you will receive the best teaching possible.

Dr. Burger-Dunn is the best and I will be taking her class for CHEM135 too. She is very helpful when you go to office hours and it is clear that she wants you to succeed. There are quizzes a couple times a month but they are very straight forward and she tells you exactly what you need to study. The tests are not unnecessarily hard either. 10/10.
The way the class is structured sets you up to do well. The lectures are great, and if you pay attention in class you wont have to read a word from the textbook all semester.

She is amazing! Her lectures are easy to understand and she records them so you can always go back and watch them again. The homework is actually very helpful and the quizzes/tests are pretty much what you learn in class. No surprises. You can tell she constructed the class for you to succeed. Loved her!

She doesn't assume you learned all this material in high school and actually takes the time to explain everything. Yes, there are quizzes every Friday, but if you do the homework and pay attention in lecture they are super easy and usually only 3-5 questions. The quizzes were probably the only reason I kept up with learning/studying in this class.

Her lectures were really helpful in understanding the material and she would provide you with answers to the questions online before the test with explanations. Every resource that she discusses in lectures is provided online and she is always open to accommodations to help out students.

She explains things very well and makes complex concepts seem simple. There is only one homework assignment a week, and you can still get a good grade in the class if the exams didn't go well. I took her again for my next chemistry course.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Overall, she was a great professor and explained things well. Her class is structured very well with a quiz and assignment every week which seemed annoying at first but helps keep you up to date. She is understanding and will give extra credit chances. You can tell she is passionate and wants you to succeed.

I was super nervous about taking chemistry in college, but Dr. Burger-Dunn made learning chemistry so much easier and less stressful. She is so kind and understanding and was always able to answer any questions via email or during lectures. I would definitely recommend taking chemistry with her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved this professor. She very clearly respected her students and our time. She explains things in an amazingly clear way but sometimes she can explain a little too much. The way she answers questions is excellent. It's clear that she genuinely cares about her students' success. Take her class above any other chem 130 prof.

Burger Dun is easy to understand during lectures and very easy to get along with if you need help. The only thing is that she gives you participation points so you have to show up to at least half the lectures to get the points. She is very understanding though and is very willing to work with you if you need anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Literally my favorite professor at KU right now. Her lectures are very clear and she's very good at explaining concepts without overcomplicating them. If you lose track in class, you can always go back through the PowerPoints because she uploads them to Canvas and they're easy to follow. Gives us so many resources to study and she is so kind.

Burger-dunn was an amazing chemistry teacher. Lectures have clicker questions for points, but you don't need to get them right to get the points. There are EASY quizzes every Friday and you can drop 3 of the 10 of them. 15 extra credit for the course survey too! Exams are easy too and only one online homework assignment per week. Overall, very easy

She's super nice and willing to stay after class to clear anything up for students. We never used the textbook for this class. The homework is easy, but the tests are kinda hard, even if you do well on quizzes and homework.
Super nice but explains things in the most difficult way

I am a person who does not like chemistry, but this class was my favorite class the semester I took it because of Dr. Burger-Dunn. She is someone who is easily identifiable as a lover of science and chemistry; you can tell she really cares about everything she does. She puts lots of effort into her lectures, and I rarely left being confused.

Love Dr. Erin! She is able to take Chemistry, which is typically seen as a difficult subject, and can make it easier to understand and does not speed through lessons. She cares for students understanding and clarifies any possible errors that accidentally makes its way into lessons (iClicker answers etc.).
Best teacher ever! Take Business French!

literally my favorite professor ever. I took buisness french with him and it was super useful and I learned a lot of real french culture info. he did quizzes over words we discussed in class and we had like one mini assignment each week plus a final
It's so refreshing to see a professor that loves being there and cares about the students learning above everything else. The class would be a good option for sophomore/junior level French students.

Professor Hayes is a great teacher. He's very good at motivating and students to do their best work. I enjoyed that he gave insights based on his own research and experience with engaging lectures - he's a great storyteller. I liked that he gave students the opportunity to teach each other: he has a good balance of hands-on and hands-off teaching.

Professor Hayes made class exciting and fun. I was always motivated to attend class. The content was understandable and in-class discussions allowed for context and a deeper understanding of the readings. Professor Hayes provided helpful feedback on writing assignments as well. To top it all off, Professor Hayes helped me declare a German minor.
Really nice professor, cares a lot about the students and connects with them well. There was a good amount of reading but it was never overwhelming, and he made lectures interesting as well.

Dr. Hayes is a great professor! I appreciated that weekly readings were brief but interesting and that he didn't require books. The class was discussion-based so attendance is mandatory. Grades consisted of reading assignments, two essays, a presentation and participation. Hayes graded quickly and gave individual feedback for each assignment.

After studying abroad with Dr. Hayes, I decided I had to take a class with him. Lectures are engaging and fun. Interesting and challenging readings. If you do the readings and make an effort, you'll get a good grade. I have to say, he's my favorite French instructor. He's awfully talented and a delight to work with.

I went to Paris on the study abroad summer trip with Prof Hayes and he is a wonderful teacher! I learned so much from him. He is hilarious and a genuinely nice guy, which makes it fun to travel with him. He knows his stuff and he expects a lot from his students.

Honestly I don't remember the exact class number. It was France Today. He was a very engaging and enthusiastic teacher. I got a lot out of this class and enjoyed it. He must've recovered from his gossip issue mentioned earlier because he never gossiped.
a very nice and talented professor. very patient. Recommended for all of his classes.
Very interested in subject matter, however unbelievably unhappy and the worst grader I've ever dealt with.
I took Renaissance lit. w/ prof. Hayes.  He truly is one of the best professors I have had.  Totally worth the effort, and I really improved my reading and writing skills.

very helpful, very enthusiastic. loves his work and his students. the class can be intimidating at first, but by the end, you will have improved both your reading and speaking skills. classes are fun and prof. hayes never gets tired of the material he teaches. he is an amazing teacher and goes out of his way to meet with students outside of class.

Prof Hayes is definately one of the best at KU! He genuinely loves to teach, is passionate about his tecahing, and really wants for his students to succeed! You have to work hard in class but it is rewarding! Definately take one of his classes!
Likeable teacher, funny, and mildly interesting, but feel like he's just parroting information. Seems like kind of a phoney, a paysan parvenu.  A huge gossip!

This class was really amazing--one of the best in my college career. (I am a junior.) We learned comprehensively about the 5th Republic and current events in France/the Francophone world. There is quite a bit of work involved to be successful (lots of quizzes and a large research paper), but it is well worth the effort. Bruce makes the class fun.
Probably the best teacher at KU. He stresses writing and doing a presentation, but he can be extremely helpful on both.  If you are a French major, you MUST take one of his classes.
This was a new class, so there were difficulties, but overall it was really interesting.  If you know Bruce, you like him. Great teacher, very excited to teach and a fun guy, to boot.
ah damn, beat me to it...oh well, here's another.
How is it that nobody's given him a chili pepper yet?
No Comments

Some young blood in the department! Don't get sucked down in the gossip Bruce! You gotta stay boyant for a few years before they give you tenure and drown you in departmental meetings that will deprive you of your youth!
No Comments
Very funny guy and very fair. Requires a fair amount of work, but it is rewarding.

Not a bad professor at all, just a bit... much at times. Exams are fully open note, but the project that lasts the whole semester is what weighs your grade. TA's were alright, no complaints but wished they helped out more. Attendance required which is annoying for guest speaker days. Make decent notes and print them out for exams to do well, easy A

Homework is based on completion rather than accuracy, exams are open note, there is a big group project, but  it's pretty simple.

Liz is chill, sarcastic and straightforward, but funny. Can be condescending at times in an uncomfortable way.

You should be fine as long as you don't misbehave.

Liz was a great professor. The online assignments are graded on completion rather than score and the exams are open note. There is a group project that spans the entire semester but it was light and as long as you communicate with your group you can complete it easily. She knows what she's talking about and I would take the course again.

Liz is such a cool and chill professor. I enjoyed her course so much it was an easy A class, and the best part is that she quite literally gives extra credit for free, she's great! If there was something that I disliked just a little bit it was the group work, though it makes sense since it's a marketing class and it depends a lot on group work.

She is a good professor but the main part of this class is a group project that goes throughout the semester. Expectations of projects are pretty unclear and unorganized. However, exams are open note, homework is easy, and overall this is a good class to take with this professor.

Easy A for an Engineering student. You get 100% on the HW if you just do it. Tests are directly from notes. If you can't get an A in this class, you shouldn't be in college. Very much busy work. Never watched a lecture. Finished 8 weeks before class ended. Take for an A. Nice professor. Simulations were fun.

She doesn't do a lot of lectures, so more hands on work which is nice, but that leaves you to reading your book for the quizzes. Quizzes are usually open book so if you take good notes, you should be good to search your book and notes. Make sure to participate in class because she takes note of that. Overall would recommend her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is very reasonable about deadlines and a nice guy, however, there are many assignments that don't have real purpose, most felt like busy work. Grades way harder than you would expect. Wants you to write as little as possible but then will count off major points for not being detailed enough. You have to get a 94 to get an A which is odd

Chris is very nice! Also cooperates if you need to miss class. There is no attendence but you evalute yourself for points at the end of the week and need to be honest. Lecture heavy and homework heavy. The finals are pretty difficult and some of the other projects are to. There is plenty of extra credit if your struggling. I would take him again

Professor Etheridge is great and genuinely cares for every single student. Show up to class, ask questions, and you will be fine. He is very understanding of circumstances and puts in the work to make sure you are caught up.

A lot of the other reviews on here are about Chris's classes rather than him as a professor. I feel like that is entirely unfair to him. Chris is absolutely wonderful and takes care to actually know every student he has. He helps when you need it and is overall a welcoming presence. Even though I wasn't a fan of the class, I was a fan of him.

The material in 345 was interesting and the lectures were engaging due to his fun, charismatic attitude. Whenever I needed an extension for an assignment, he gave me one with no hassle; he cares for his students and is supportive of their needs. Ethnographies and reflections were interesting but also tedious and required exhaustive information.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Etheridge is such a caring professor! Almost the entirety of the semester is spent working on a group project which could be annoying at times, but you get to choose your group at the start of the semester. This class only met once a week in-person (lab) and then the lecture portion was online but this may not stay the structure.

The lectures were seriously so boring and I think that this class could be fully online with no issues. There is also an INSANE amount of homework. I spent probably average of 5 hours a week doing homework for this class alone. A lot of the homework was just pointless busy work. Show that you're putting the work in and you'll do fine in this class.

Dr. Etheridge is at the helm of the least engaging, least informative and least applicable journalism course at KU. The class, due to his fault, is structured to take an obscene amount of non-class time, even if you choose to take the class in person. Lastly Dr. Etheridge gives incredibly lacking feedback and over-enforces assignment deadlines.

Professor Etheridge does genuinely care about his students and and their success. However, this was the most difficult 101 class I have ever taken. The tests didn't really match up with the content, and there was no curve despite the majority of the class not reaching a passing grade. Every lecture was from a guest speaker, not him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Chris is nice but he needs to figure his own class out. Even though he was a new prof teaching an online 300-person lecture during a pandemic, the tests always dropped peoples grades. When everyone bombed the 1st test he basically gave up and the TA held study sessions for the tests (which helped a lot) Learned more from TA than from Chris.

Dr. Etheridge didn't respond to students timely, didn't prepare students well enough for tests and broke down after our first exam, changing his policy making us not have to attend class. After this, the majority of my classmates didn't take the course that seriously. But, he's also new to the university and teaching during a worldwide pandemic.

This class was rough. Our TA saved the majority of the class wouldn't have passed. Everyone bombed the first test. Dr. Ethridge was never available by email, you spend over 3 hours a week watching his videos (even on double speed) and you need VERY detailed notes. He's super knowledgeable, but not super engaging. Good luck staying awake.
This class was one of the best classes I took during my first semester. Chris is the only professor for this course, and I have no problem keeping it that way.

She is so much nicer to her students in o-chem 2 lab compared to in o-chem 1 lab. And she kindly re-explains and re-teaches things to students that Dr. Malinakova did not teach well/clear enough during the lab lecture.

Dr. Carter is the O-Chem lab coordinator. She would visit our lab and lowkey be condescending about the work we were doing. Hate that. She thinks the TAs aren't harsh enough with grades. Shoutout Peace, my TA he is awesome if you get him. Rubric's aren't always clear but unforch you can't escape Dr. Carter. Itll be okay this is just being nitpicky.
I am only posting this to disagree with the previous review: she is not nice even if you are nice to her. Do not go to her office hours. She was so rude that I cried.

This class was a lot, but visiting Dr. Carter's office hours helped—she's kind if you're kind. The grading is tough and very nitpicky, so follow the rubric exactly and hope for the best. I think people exaggerate a bit; just do the work carefully and you'll be fine lol. The TA def can make or break this class. Also, the labs ARE cool- not the work.

RUN. Every interaction I've had with her was traumatizing. Did way too much work for a 2 credit class and then do horribly on assignments. Not clear on criteria at all as TAs have a completely different rubric, so have fun. She'll also lower your grade to generate a bell curve. Felt like she did everything in her power to ensue no one succeeded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely evil. Liked to come into our lab section and be horrifically cruel to the student. She also enjoyed regrading assignments that she felt like the TAs were to lenient on.

Very very unpleasant and rude to students. The class isn't that hard; but interacting with her is very difficult and unpleasant. She floats between lab groups to humiliate students and yell at them aggressively if anything is even slightly off. Something hard must be going on in her personal life for her to act this way..

Everything you see in these reviews are completely true. I find spending more time on this lab than even Chem 380. Gives you a general rubric but the rubric used for grading is completely different, requiring items that weren't in the rubric provided. I didn't wear a seatbelt whenever I drove to the lab, hoping I would perish on my way there.

Disrespectful is the only word that comes to mind when the name Mary Beth Carter is brought up. Not only is she incredibly unhelpful, she is additionally just a close-minded chemist that lacks the ability to sympathize with other humans.

Dr. Carter always seemed bothered by the students and made it difficult for us to feel like we could go to her if we needed help. She groaned when she saw my hand raised during lab lecture. The reports were graded strictly and the criteria felt unfair. For a 2-credit class, I found myself spending more time on this class than on any of my others.

Organic Chemistry is not an easy class, and she definitely makes this lab way more stressful than it needs to be. She is rude and disrespectful and doesn't even give a clear criteria of what she wants. Even with that, she takes off points like taking candy away from a kid. There is no other option, but be prepared to put a lot of work in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, one of the worst classes I have taken. The professor is rude and disrespectful, and her rubric doesn't give you a clear criteria of what she wants. TA's told me they get a more extensive rubric of things we need, but those things are not in the rubric the students have. She is hard to talk to, and always has something negative to say.

she doesn't realizes that most students don't have 30+ years of experience in an o chem lab. extremely pretentious towards students when they are confused on a lab procedure. Also she constantly counts off in assignments for writing too much or too little. Rubric is super unclear and often I would follow to a tea and still get points off.

Your grade fully depends on which TA you end up with. Dr. Carter is difficult to negotiate with and doesn't seem to enjoy working with students. Every student I have talked to does not enjoy interacting with her and everyone is on edge when she walks in the room. Really wouldn't take this again tbh.

took more time outside of class than many other of my classes for this lab just to do the weekly notebook assignments and stuff. kinda hard to stay on top of things. MAKE SURE YOU GO TO THE GTA OFFICE HOURS. the ta office hours were literally a godsend and the only reason I passed. bless those angels.
Harsh grading. Little to no feedback for reports. Unclear instructions. Always referred to the rubric but the rubric was NEVER shared.
I hate him so much. Goes on political rants in every class. He actually sucks so hard, he is the stereotypical professor that Fox News claims all professors are

The instructor made the class unbearable. He was openly condescending to anyone with a differing opinion, creating a hostile environment. Additionally, they didn't grade the majority of our work until two weeks before the semester ended, leaving us in the dark about our grades until the last minute: unprofessional behavior and poor management.

Such a tough grader and doesn't grade anything until really late in the semester. By the time you get your grades you will have to redo most of them while also getting other assignments from him. In the begiining of the class I loved it but then his grading changed him and he became a stickler for so much.

Worst teacher I've taken in my years at Kansas. Doesn't grade anything till the final week of class then gives absolutely zero feedback back on his grades. Tells you to figure it out yourself majority of the time. You can put your heart in soul into a paper then throws you a D-.

Chandler is a somewhat reasonable teacher and will let you change assignments as long as you have something to replace it with. He is a very difficult grader though. He doesn't use the normal grading scale, his A is from 80-100 which you would think is nice but he says that an A is worth outstanding and over the top work. Which he rarely gives.
Great Professor and I really enjoyed the class, although many conversations were very political, where you could see clearly his side, which made many students uncomfortable.

Dr. Classen genuinely cares about his students. The class is very discussion based and the readings are super doable. He really encourages asking questions. He hates giving tests and will only do so if he finds the class is using AI on assignments (assignments are easy though so there's no reason to cheat anyway). Super generous with deadlines too.

Chandler teaches in such a way that the lessons are mostly guided by the students and are hardly based on the readings. I decided to striclty read every single document he assigned us to read--you'd be wasting hours by doing this. You can get away without doing any of the readings in this class if you know how to bs and enjoy in-class discussions.

He is awesome! One of my favorite teachers at KU. Had him for Comms 244, and he made class always interesting and fun. He really takes the time to get to know his students, and is very kind and respectful even when talking about potentially controversial topics that the class covers.

Take this class! I loved having Chandler as my prof. This class will go down as one of my favorites at KU. He is so caring and makes his class seem like a safe, non-judgmental space. He is also very flexible about assignments. He is very left-leaning as a warning. He is very knowledgeable. Participate in discussions, it will make the class more fun

Chandler is very understanding and cares a lot about his students. The readings were very entertaining and he cares a lot about student's feedback. As long as you participate in discussions, the class is very easy and honestly enjoyable.

Chandler is a wonderful, inspiring man. He will make you think critically and teach you with passion. He will help you become a better writer with his impeccable vocabulary. He encourages student-led discussion and creates open environments to ask, diatribe, and debate about interesting topics with current relevance. Not a lot of public speaking!

Flipped classroom format with decent video quality, though supplemental resources were often necessary for clarity. Grading turnaround was delayed, with lab reports taking up to two months to return. The pacing was inconsistent, specifically the inclusion of two new lessons during the final week of the semester.

Turned our Strength of Materials class into a flipped classroom and could not be lazier. Does not teach what the other class learns but gives the exact same test. When going over the test fails to realize that the reason students are doing exceptionally mid is because he does not teach or for that matter do anything whatsoever.
Class is challenging with the amount of material. He makes it very easy to learn and is great at teaching the material.

Homework requirements are pretty strict and "Failure to adhere to these guidelines may result in loss of credit for the homework set, regardless of the correctness of the final answer." -Syllabus, You can't sit with the people you want and seating is assigned, if you try and reach out to ask questions he will answer his questions like a politician.
Took a lot of time to get grades back. Midterms were harder than expected. Some class periods were spent going over only one problem.

Super friendly and accessible guy, cares about his students and wants them to do well. Grading is fair, partial credit is available on all problem, homework, exams, etc. The grading scale is balanced and allows you room for error. Ask questions and go to office hours, he is super easy to talk to and great at explaining concepts/answering questions

By far one of the best professors Ive had at KU. Really cares about his students and makes an effort to get to know you. His lectures are extremely straightforward and easy to understand. His exams are somewhat difficult but hes really understanding when it comes to grading and gives plenty of opportunities for extra credit. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN!

Super great professor! The project was a little much for the given shortened/hybrid semester, but overall the class was enjoyable. It was just a ridiculous amount of work. I feel like I learned quite a bit. He was super funny and I really enjoyed having him as a prof!
He gives lots of feedback and may grade harsh at first, but you can redo every assignment and get a better grade. He also will look over all assignments and quizzes before turning them in.

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I have ever had, if you have the option do not take him. I looked at these comments before this semester and thought there is no way hes that hard, he is the meanest professor I have ever had. He doesnt give feedback, instead just degrading comments.

Ted Cotti is one of the rudest professors I've ever had. His "feedback" is just insulting comments about your work and does not help in any way. You can resolve all criticisms and talk to him in class; he still won't approve.

I liked him at the beginning of the year but as time went on I began to see what the other people are saying on here too... he is not a nice teacher and his "feedback" can be super discouraging and stright up mean. He grades superrrr tough but does give a lot of extra credit which is the only reason why I passed. I would pick a different teacher..

Ted Cotti...no, simply no. Ted teaches just fine, just be prepared to take some time out of your day to talk to him. He is a very harsh grader. I have always been a good writer, gotten a lot of compliments from my peers and professors, until Ted came in the picture. He at least gives extra credit🙏. He should not be your first choice when enrolling

It is a grammer class so he is a pretty tuff grader when it comes to writing assignments. But he always gives feedback and is super open to questions and helping you through it. You can resubmit any work for points back and gives extra credit pretty often.

Don't let the other reviews fool you. All you need to do to succeed is to ASK ?s. Every week you have a writing assignment but he will grade it for you before you turn it in to get a better grade. It's a hard class but I found him easy to approach. His grading is nitpicky but for a J Class, it's fair. If your not a good writer don't take the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Cotti is the worst professor I've had. The comments he left on my assignments were incredibly condescending and made me feel incompetent. All my professors have complimented my writing skills and I think it's my biggest strength; however, his instructions are unclear and don't correlate with the lectures, so it was impossible to get a good grade.

Going to his class made me want to scream and cry and throw up all at once. Ted made me feel so disrespected that I almost dropped out of journalism. I didn't ever feel that I could ask Cotti for help because of his behavior toward me. Expect to fend for yourself in J104 with Cotti.

Ted Cotti expects you to complete every assignment to his liking, even if the instructions do not explicitly state all of his requirements. He gives very little feedback on assignments and tends to be rude and condescending unless called out on it. Cotti does offer extra credit and is available after class if you can get past his hostility.

Incredibly discouraging, rude, and full of attitude. His version of feedback on papers/assignments consists of leaving snarky comments with little to no relevance to how you can improve. For someone who grades tough, helpful thorough critiques would be expected, however, that is not the case.
Professor Cotti was a great professor and really understands his students. He provides several opportunities to gain points through rewrites and extra credit. Would definitely recommend!

It's a writing and grammar class, so be prepared to write a lot and be frustrated with getting points off for grammar. This course was easy to me, and I found that the professor made himself available outside of class time to help you boost your grade. Rewrites and extra credit were available to me, and I thought the feedback was good

I found Cotti to be really mean. His comments on my papers weren't really all that helpful and just made him really off putting -- making me not really want to go to him for help. I found the class difficult, there is a lot of content that you need to remember throughout but there was more than enough extra credit given. Beware!

Cotti is a good professor. He gives really good feedback on your writing and spends time helping each individual in the class, as long as you ask for help. I would definitely take a class with him again. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: While Professor Cotti does not create the modules, he still teaches the content very well. There are two weekly quizzes and one weekly writing project. He is one of the most caring professors who truly wants his students to succeed and does so by providing a lot of feedback. He is always willing to help and offers multiple extra credit assignments.

I took J104 with Cotti so the course material wasn't stuff he made, but he would go out of his way to add in EC and to make the assignments more interesting. He also sat down with me and helped me edit my papers. Very helpful and understanding, and he has a lot of passion for journalism. His grading can be tough but he just wants the best out of ya
Cotti is a great teacher, a good listener, and helpful, learned a lot. would recommend.

The J104 curriculum is the same regardless of professor. 1 content quiz, 1 grammar quiz and 1 writing assignment a week. Cotti can be blunt. He won't sugar coat things, but I didn't have any issues with him. He is very generous with extra credit and will give you points back if you rewrite assignments. I had a 117% at one point. Don't stress.

Prof Cotti made me feel so disrespected in class and did not try to help me with editing my papers. He just assumes that we will all be able to know how he likes it to be written without much instruction. He will call you out in class for being late or looking like you didn't get enough sleep and he definitely has a bias against Greek Life.

To start, Carl is a great film guy. That's it. He hasn't graded 70% of my assignments going into finals week, enjoys making lectures not at all understandable, using post-grad vocabulary to freshman/sophomore students, and freaks out at his TA's throughout the year. reviews.comment: (FMS 200, not 100) as of the last day of finals week, professor swanson has graded maybe two of my assignments. the lack of feedback on assignments is incredibly frustrating. aside from that, the class is very heavy on in-class group work. he's clearly passionate about film but he is not a good instructor. don't take his courses if you can avoid it

Just took FMS200 and be prepared to not see your grade until the very last day. The last thing he actually graded was in August so good luck trying to know what your grade is at any times during the semester. Swanson is great at Lectures, but not the best professor.

Hands down the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. He was late to class. I never knew my grade until after the final. He is a harsh grader. Lectures are so boring. He is not funny. Honestly, it did not seem like he cared at all and he seemed to have an attitude most days. Transfer out if he's your teacher. He doesn't care about his students.

reviews.comment: I had him for FMS 200 and it was such a two sided coin. I will say his lectures are actually interesting, and he clearly loves what he teaches.
