Doesn't grade until the last week of classes. Easy class though. He's just kinda weird.

Swanson's reviews are too harsh. It can be hard to keep up with the amount of work, but he does not penalize for late work. As long as you show effort, you'll do fine. He can be disorganized at times, but other than being slightly annoying, it won't affect you much. His lectures were enjoyable, and he seems to care about both film and his students.

I would like to start by saying Professor Swanson seems like a very cool guy, but sadly he is not the best professor. Not a single one of my assignments or any of my classmates' assignments have been graded and the semester ends within the next two days. Lectures are jumbled and notes are not always the most clear, but he is a nice guy.

reviews.comment: Carl oh Carl. I wanted to enjoy this class. Let me start by saying Swanson is a very funny guy, he just tends to get off-topic with his lectures and its hard to follow. He also has only graded about 4 of my assignments and the semester ends in 7 days. It would be really nice to see what grade I actually have in this class so i can plan accordingly.

Mr. Swanson definitely knows a lot about films and is highly intelligent on such topics but he was noticably late to class everyday and graded all of our stuff late. Everyone would just get so bored during his lectures and most of them just felt like ramblings. It's an easy class even if you don't watch the weekly films and readings.

He is late every single class. Every time. He also just gives lectures that are the exact same as his "required videos" online, so attending is pointless besides him requiring it. If you're wanting to take a film class because it'll be fun to just watch movies, know that this class requires two movies each week. Even as a film minor, it's a lot.

Professor Swanson was always late to class. It was extremely unprofessional. The class setup and due dates were very unclear to students and it took nearly the entire semester for them to be understood by the students. Whenever coming to him with questions, you would never get a good answer because he did not write up the materials for the course.
He was a chill teacher and very nice.

Carl was 10 minutes late to class everyday. He used the same film materials in FMS530 that he did in FMS100. There were no due dates. He never graded anything. He lectured for 75 minutes and forgot the points he actually had to make. One of the classes we literally watched the X Files for an hour. He didn't care. This is a mandatory FMS course...
This guy can sugma

I think most of the problems with Swanson's classes are that his lectures are just long ramblings. I've had him for multiple classes. In each, he saved all the grading (and I mean all the grading) to the very end of the semester. I know the issue isn't with the content, his lectures are just very "sesquipedalian" as he would say (long-winded).

Bro sucks at grading and talks for way to long before and after every movie we watched. Could easily spend 4 hours in class, and then expected to write a pointless "synthesis paper", which aren't graded for months after being submitted. I took this class to get my GE3H requirement out of the way, but took up more time than any of my major classes.

Carl is awful. He just talks for an hour straight with no powerpoint and expects you to remember everything. He also tries to flex on you with his high vocabulary and he is very arrogant. I feel like he only really ever cared about himself. He also didn't grade any of my papers until the last week of the semester .

There's a quiz every week based on the chapter we read. We also had papers throughout the semester, but they were all graded on the last day grades were to be put in so we never got any feedback. Don't bother taking notes, just listen to him and grasp what he's saying. He's super funny but I just wish there was more structure.

reviews.comment: GEOL 562- A very well read and respected professor. Doug cares and wants to make sure everyone understands what he is talking about in a difficult subject. He also has the best dad jokes of all time and they are hilarious. Pay attention to the lecture and think about concepts and you'll do fine. A hard class, but was still very enjoyable.
Professor Walker isn't a bad guy and he really tries to explain the text, but his lecture notes are super confusing and extremely dry and boring.

Really great! He's done a lot in his field, and his knowledge runs deep and wide. This shows through in class (in a good way). Seems like he puts thought and effort into explaining stuff that would be otherwise confusing. Lax about quizzes/tests compared to the other prof co-teaching the course. He made this class worthwhile and valuable.

Awesome Guy. Gives you the grade you deserve if you work hard and show constant improvement. If you get a better grade than the test before each time, you will most likely end up w/ an A. Very smart, but a bit boring sometimes. Then again, were studying rocks.

I took ENGL 105 with Dr. Dennis, and she's an amazing teacher. I don't love writing, but she made the class enjoyable and manageable. There are only two essays, a mini podcast, and a take-home reflection. She grades fairly and is very understanding. You read a lot for class, but it's not tested, just class discussion, which is very chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Dennis is my favorite professor. She does not grade harshly, there are only a few essays and honestly quite a bit of reading but I did not mind it because she is such a good professor. She allows for extensions on all essays with no penalty as long as you communicate with her. I was always excited to go to her class because she is so funny.

Dr. Dennis is caring and willing to give extensions on assignments which I do appreciate. However, she doesn't even attach rubrics on your papers and she grades very strictly. I don't understand why it is so challenging to receive an A on a paper for an entry level English class. Also, don't buy the $60 book she requires, you won't even open it.

I had Dr. Dennis for ENGL 101 & 102 and is one of the best professors I've had at KU. Her assignments and feedback greatly improved my writing abilities. She is very lenient and helpful as long as you show effort.
Such an amazing professor. She is very understanding and cares about the well being of her students. She will give extensions and reopen assignments so you can turn stuff in. So awesome!
Dr. Dennis is super caring, and is willing to help you with anything you need. The papers are important, but she gives feedback, and there are workshops to help. Her class was awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dennis was one of my favorite professors this semester. She genuinely cares for her students and their well-being. She grants extensions usually, and will help in the writing process. Clear grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved my class with Professor Dennis, mainly because she is so caring, understanding, and genuinely cares for her students. She would often encourage us to make sure we are taking care of ourselves above all. She is also an extremely talented teacher. She explains concepts and ideas in a way that is long lasting and informative.

You will essentially read poems before class and then discuss them in class so doing the assigned readings is essential to a good grade. Your papers have to be of a good quality for her to give you a good grade. Honestly her grading is a little harder, but that can be attributed to it being her first year teaching the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Rahn is a very nice guy and very passionate about the weather, however if you are taking this class to simply knock out your science core credits, I must warn you the class is really hard to get through, and I recommend you have a vested interest in weather. Extremely generous grader, curves tests, pretty easy class overall.
He really liked talking about the weather in class, so it kept it interesting, and was pretty reasonable with the test curves.
Very passionate about Meteorology and a nice person. The class was detail oriented and if you got behind, it was hard to catch up.

Incredibly passionate about everything to do with Atmospheric Science. Incredibly intelligent and sometimes goes on tangents about stuff that is a little confusing. Grades Test with a Curve, but the Tests are pretty challenging, especially as someone who has no prior knowledge. Review for tests is incredibly helpful!
Dude is awesome.

I really liked Dr. Rahn and I could tell he was passionate about the topic, but sometimes he would start talking and I would have no idea what was going on because he's so smart and I didn't understand the concepts. He was really helpful with tests and provided lots of study material. Definitely access that, so helpful on tests!!
Avoid this course.

She edited the gradebook this semester so that tests were weighted more, so it is much more difficult than in past semesters. The GTA's and TAs were amazing and very helpful, but without sufficient in-person lecture time, it's hard to succeed in this class. And the 15 hours you spend on unhelpful smart book assignments do not make up for it.
You can read who the problem is and the made up info is hilarious.

I have never been so angry towards a class before. The amount of homework is insane and Hemingson never responds or posts anything on time or with notice. I have been doing hours of smart book assignments and have not even started studying for the final because of the homework load.  In person was ok, but 15 hours of homework a week. Do not take!!

This class was genuinely the worst class I have ever taken. Hemingson never posted anything on canvas on time, never responded to emails (yet she has time to respond to rate my professor comments), and the amount of homework was absurd (this week was 15 hours worth of smart books). I've put my blood sweat and tears in this class. Don't take it

Is not punctual, accessible, nor helpful in any meaningful way. She is usually too busy being passive aggressive or worrying about her ego to actually take time to do her job. I feel bad for everyone who is forced to take anatomy with this so-called 'professor'; I feel even worse for the poor GTAs who have to deal with her even more frequently. :(

Didn't have a syllabus like 3 weeks in & is passive aggressive. She had a lot of problems posting assignments and exams on time and got mad when people asked about it. She's also the Lab Director, not the Prof, she doesn't directly lecture. The GTAs are awesome, though.

Uses ChatGPT. Looks like spends more time responding to 1 star reviews on here than she does on her actual course, and it shows. She made a weird Canvas post about students stealing her sparkle? I love anatomy as a subject, but dear god, don't take the lab at KU if it's her! She almost stole MY sparkle.

This was my first career focused class at KU, and I was worried, but the TAs and Doc H made it very easy to learn. The homework helps a lot with the exams. We had four in lab exams, but the Core34 assignment basically cancels one out so you can make mistakes and not tank your grade. She wants you to try so then you can learn and thats cool.

reviews.comment: If you plan on taking BIOL 241, and don't follow a religion currently, I highly suggest you begin and start praying immediately. This course has been the most disorganized and confusing, semester of my life. The GTAs and UTAs are all AMAZING! However, Dr. Hemingson sets students up to fail. Good luck getting an A. I wish you best of luck...

One of the most disorganized lab courses I've taken. Exams often did not align well with the material emphasized in class, which made it difficult to prepare effectively. Homework was time-consuming and were posted only a few days before the deadline, limited time to complete them. Study materials limited, made it harder to succeed in the course.

Anatomy lab is challenging, and this course lacked consistent structure and a clear schedule. Exams did not always align with lab material, and cadaver access felt limited. A key study resource was introduced about 10 weeks into the semester, which reduced its usefulness.

reviews.comment: This was the most difficult class I have taken at KU. I am shocked that anyone is allowed to run a lab as unorganized as this was. Homework takes hours and it is impossible to do well on. There is no help available and she seems to not care. She simply does not respond to emails and doesn't show up even when you have scheduled office hours. Run.

Dr. Hemingson's research is in effective human anatomy education methods. This is so funny to me because she seems to want her students to struggle in her lab. Dr. Hemingson doesn't bother to show up to lab or actually talk with her students but she will gladly give Homework and SmartBook assignments that are anywhere between 200-500.

One of the nicest professors I have ever had. Hard to get a hold of. SO SO many assignments/ homeworks but they help your grade immensely. I didn't even have to take the final and I still got an A because exams aren't weighted that much. SO many points possible so you can do bad on exams and be fine.

so many points available, its impossible to get an A. just do the insane amount of assignments and ur fine. did horrible on my exams and still got a 95. the professor is really caring and nice. shes a little disorganized but most smart STEM professors are.

I've had Dr. Hemingson for two semesters now in two different classes. She is by far one of the most qualified and caring science professors that I've had. Yes, she is a tough grader, but that is because the little things matter in the medical world. At the same time, she tries to offer as much outside help as she can, and always responds promptly.

She is the most caring professor and she cares about everyone! Yeah sometimes she makes you do things to learn, that you might not want to do like answer a bunch of questions... but she is also there for you even when you dont know you need someone to be. KU is lucky to have her, we are lucky.

Hemingson is one of the most DISORGANIZED professors I have ever taken in my entire life. She has absolutely no clue what she is doing at any given moment, and she is extremely difficult to reach. I was able to receive an A, but it was more due to her efforts than because of her. However, I did take the class when she was a first-time teacher.
She is like the best kind of chaos love joy energy and smarts all in one professor. Queen energy.

In it now and it's the first hybrid time. I heard rumors it was like ‘go go go' but it actually started off chill and she's more causal than I thoght. Like she really eased us in to it all and I met with her already and she's legit. It's good, Doc. H. is good and just wants the best. And yeah… it's a lot… like…… duh.

she had no idea what she was doing because she changed the way she did things this time. for reference, I took this in spring '25. If u misspell the word, u get points off. if u aren't specific about a left or right arm you get points off. doesn't post the notes beforehand so you're expected to know where everything is after only looking at it once

As a student who has taken the course w/ two different structures, Doc H. puts in so much effort to make this subject more applicable and useful for students. I really appreciated her willingness to connect with students too. The past instructor wanted us to be intimidated but she really wants you to learn anatomy so you're ready for your career.
Come to lab and watch the TAs teach. Dont worry about taking crazy notes because you will get them posted. Its more helpful to see what they are pointing too.

You have to study. I wish there was a customized book or something but it's doable if you listen and pay attention. Oh, don't freak out about notes!!!!!! Practice spelling outside of lab, but pay attention IN LAB, don't freak out about taking notes. And talk to her, she's way understanding about stuff, but also don't lie. She don't like that.

She actually cares about her students and this is way better than what it used to be! I took it twice (Spring 24 and Spring 25) and the second time was WAY better! She wasn't the professor the first time but she is now thank god.
It's not that hard if you study a little everyday. I don't know why so many people are complaining but she definitely grades on spelling, but it's healthcare so……
Attendance isn't required but basically it is or you get behind. Learn to spell the words, she grades on spelling. My UTAs were really cool and I liked my GTA.
Easy to meet with and wants you to know stuff so you don't get embarrassed when you go on to upper level classes or nursing school.
The exams really matter and she wants you to build as you go so it feels like a lot until you get it. SPELLING COUNTS!!!!!!! Practice spelling from day 1. She wants you to spell things correctly.
She doesn't lecture ever but I wish she would teach every lab. She makes it make sense and is really fun. She knows what she is doing and she really cares about her students.

She is a boss. You have to study to do well in this class and it's a lot of structures to learn. It took me a minute to figure out how to study, but once I got it, it was way easier to get the class. Just study how she suggests and it will be way better for you.
She cool. Cares about spelling which is liiiiike I get it but bro
She is super willing to meet with students and is really chill. Good people. The class is hard but I took it at another school and it's hard everywhere so.

reviews.comment: Do not take.

Great professor but the TA's grade assignments extremely strictly. Assignments are weighted very heavily. You also need a 95 to get an A in the class. 2% EC for perfect attendance. The desktop specialist exam is a great opportunity to replace the final.

reviews.comment: Extremely useful class and she is absolutely amazing

You can take the Tableau Specialist Desktop Exam for free in place for the final, which is a great opportunity.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You'll learn SQL and Python packages. The material is super interesting, but sometimes it's hard to stay engaged because you're basically watching her explain the code on the board most of the time. The assignments are clearly defined, and the tests are mostly conceptual. The professor is super sweet and knowledgeable. Attendance is graded.
Very simple an easy class.
Prof Stoyanova is a great person and sets each individual in her class up for future success by providing outstanding feedback and good lectures with grading done on the completion of certificates.

Can't talk to save his life, and will degrade you if you do ANYTHING expect his LGA. Your mother could be on her death bed and he'll say "why couldn't you have handled this outside of class". He also jumps in front of you to try to catch you not doing there assignment. .Genuinely the most insufferable TA I've had, please switch if you can.

He doesn't know how to do his own problems and cannot interact with anyone on any type of level. Will argue with you over even 1 point on an exam or quiz. Get out. I repeat. GET OUT of his lab section. Every other GTA in this course will help you through the LGA's and quizzes but David won't. Is like sheldon cooper but without a personality.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This guy didn't even know how to do the problems, he would use his cheat sheet. If you ever asked him a question he would become the Riddler and never checked your work. One specific case was when I asked him a question and he told me to 'abuse the equations'. Friedman suits his name.
He's just a GTA (for now), but switch your lab section immediately if you see him in your schedule

Terrible TA, will not answer questions, and is very condescending. If you ask for help, all he does is tell you to check the slides for examples or "I would take that into consideration." He walks around class for the entire 50 minutes and sneaks to see if you're doing the LGA. God forbid you do something else in there or take a 2-minute break.

Overall, this class was one of the best classes I have taken my entire time at UMKC. Professor Patrick has good expectations and pushes you to dig deep and think more strategically for every piece of information given. Not only is amazing feedback provided, but real-life examples are also shown, which give another perspective, which is amazing!

Dave is an incredibly smart person and a great professor. While this course was a bit difficult & the workload was quite heavy, I left this course feeling more confident about my abilities in creating effective website strategies. Note: The course is designed to get students to think critically, rather than holding their hand along the way.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor was very knowledgeable about the topics in the class, with years of leading industry experience. He often used real-world examples and directly applied topics from our book to assignments. The tests were a bit long, but this class taught me a lot about marketing and critical thinking. This is the prof. I think I learned the most from.
This is not a class, it's a workshop. The skills you learn are worth the work. I can finally say I am a critical thinker after this class.

The course is heavy and backloaded, but I felt it was a rewarding course with Professor Patrick. If you're interested in Marketing, you'll get your moneys worth. With it being an online class, following each weeks deliverables and watching the lectures is a must. He was easy to communicate with and always gave useable feedback on assignment's.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: At first, I was very nervous with the course schedule as it was presentation heavy and we were going to be working in groups through the semester. As the course progressed, I was learned about myself and how to communicate in the business realm. Professor Patrick is a warm hearted, caring person who cares about the wellbeing of his students.

Professor Patrick's competitive grading fosters real-world marketing readiness. Emphasizing proposal writing and research analysis, he imparts essential skills for marketing/social media success. He responds kindly to emails, providing clear clarification, and genuinely cares about his students' success and learning.

Dave challenges his students to learn by doing. In this class, students are challenged to become experts and think beyond the "what" and instead consider the "why" through research and application of real-world skills. Dave challenged me to be a better student and a better learner. I cannot recommend this class enough.

If you like reading textbooks, taking quizzes and hand-holding, this instructor is not for you. The class is structured to offer students the creative freedom to learn wholistically from professionals and get superior feedback. He makes you think and act with strategy. This is less a University class and more a Master class.

Even in this online asynchronous course, the professor showed exceptional engagement and tailored feedback on assignments. Beyond academia, he facilitated networking with executives, offering valuable mentorship and post-graduation advice. His industry experience was passed to students through lessons learned course assignments, and video lectures.

This class is hands-on research, discovery and interpretation of your findings. David's class structure allows you to learn in a style you know works best for you. David provides robust assignment detail, professional insights and career experience to this class. Make a plan for organizing, do the work, spend time each day on it and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Patrick has a unique teaching style that you either love or learn to deal with. The course is lecture based with an emphasis on group projects. He won't give you a list of marketing tactics to study and regurgitate, rather he will give you real life examples and concepts that you will learn to apply throughout the semester.

Big emphasis on group projects. Had a really solid group to work with so that was all good. Other than that just follow the advice he gives in outlines and in class. Participate in class and do extra credits if needed and the class is quite good.

Professor Patrick makes it clear that he is knowledgeable and experienced in the world of business. He provides real-world experiences from his time in foreign nations, as well as bringing in new speakers. His method of providing a homework/project schedule can be confusing, and the projects can have abstract grading (which he can fall behind on).

When Professor Patrick outlined the entire semester, I was intimidated. I thought this class might break me. This course is challenging, but the experience will make you a better student and professional. You'll learn a lot more than marketing from him. I'm an IT major, and yet I found value in his class. Apply yourself and he will notice.

Professor Patrick is definitely a tough grader. However, he provides great feedback. He also provides many opportunities to redo assignments and gives easy opportunities for extra credit. I took him for an 8 wk course, and it was really tough due to time restraints. Also, I had him for JMC 866.

Professor Patrick was a teacher that left a lasting impact on me. I am writing this review two years after taking his course. His achievements and experience was something that i found very inspirational. He is an out of the box thinker and pushes his students to do the same. His insights and feedback were always genuine and meaningful.
He gave many assignments based off of assignments he was given in his marketing career. Good person.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Patrick is a very intelligent individual and has a lot of knowledge to offer his students. His coursework is not easy by any means but as long as you apply yourself, you will be fine. Your grade definitely reflects the work that your willing to put in!

I would recommend this course to ALL business students! I loved the guided challenge and insightful assignments it provided. There aren't busy assignments, rather few meaningful projects that develop your confidence in marketing! The professor was kind and extremely knowledgeable. I would take this class a million times again, one of my favorites!

In MKTG 435, Professor Patrick digs deep into what the world of marketing looks like in a business sense. Throughout this class and its assignments, he prepares students for careers in marketing by giving them insights about how to successfully develop a marketing strategy, fulfill numerous marketing roles, and develop a personal brand.

He strongly believes in you get what you put in. Depth of thought and strategic connections reaching beyond surface level thinking will be rewarded. The course is real-world based as opposed to lecture/content heavy. He gives insightful feedback. Your class participation (attendance) will enable you to gain the most valuable learning experience.

He strongly believes in what you put in you get back. He values depth of thought and strategic connections that prove you went beyond surface level initiatives. Your class participation will add value to your experience and learning, so attend class. The class is real-world based rather than content/lecture heavy. He provides insightful feedback.

Professor Patrick is one of the few professors who truly cares for his students. If you are someone who needs clear grading criteria, you will struggle with this course. He enjoys sharing his experiences and sometimes it is difficult to discern what will be on the final. Show up to class and you'll get lots of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed Mr. Patricks class. I felt it was the most marketing material and hands on learning I had done during my time so far. He is the first professor I have had that really seemed to have a surplus of valuable experience in his career - and is capable of purposefully relaying this knowledge to his students. His assignments are no joke, but he gives very clear instructions as to what he is looking for. If you listen to the tips he provides, you will excel in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

Professor Patrick's class helped challenge me to go above and beyond. The assignments given in this class were difficult and took some time. I would take his class again.

Dave is a great professor. This course provided me many opportunities to learn real world information and practice it. He also offers extra credit which can really help bump up a grade. I would definitely recommend his as a professor!

So much extra credit offered in this course that's pretty much given just for following directions or showing up. I really loved professor Patrick's class. It was one of the most useful scm classes I took. You have to participate and put the work in to get an A but it's doable. This was one of the best courses that I took in my college career, because it prepped me for utilizing my marketing skills outside of the classroom. If you are looking for a course to truly prepare you for a real-world Marketing career, look no further. Discussion wasn't helpful and I found that most students had no idea in which direction the class was ever headed.   Somewhat easy class, but kind of a waste.  I don't remember much from it.

This man is the most strict professor I've met @ KU, but very knowledgable.

This man has no right to be teaching!The lectures were extremely boring and nothing he talked about ended up on the test. His TAs didn't speak English and Earnhart didn't communicate with them, so they rarely knew what was going on. The only way I survived the class is because I taught myself.
Extremely Easy, No Final. Curves final grade to the 3rd highest person. Like everyone said, pay attention to the homework and you will do fine.

Discussions are worthless.  His notes are worthless.  The lectures are worthless.  The textbook is worthless, I never read a single chapter and got a perfect score on his midterm.  Just understand the homework and you are fine.  Don't waste your time in class.
If you do the homework, Econ 142, Econ 330 and Econ 610 are all incrediably easy! His tests are just like his homework. Strict man but very knowledgable.

one of the easiest classes i've ever taken.  not the most interesting, but very easy. if you listen, you don't really have to study at all if you can do basic algebra and understand graphs.  kinda weird guy that is not too helpful, but entertaining at times.
My girlfriend sat next to me in class.  Earnhart's class was so boring I would paint my girlfriend's toenails everyday in class for entertainment.
Fishing is a jerk at one end of the line waiting for a jerk at the other.  Speaking of jerks...

Not helpful at all.  He is unclear and when you ask him questions, he either ignores you or makes it your fault.  He also refuses to use e-mail and it is hard to get ahold of him during office hours or via the phone.
Lectures were never completely clear.  Made no attempts to help me when I asked him a question after class, he would not even look at my test to listen to my grading complaint.
Starts class late and ends late.  Notes are on Word and are horrible.  Discussions are worthless.  He refuses to use scantron.

Changed all homeworks into quizzes (no notes allowed) in the middle of the semester. Notes in class are presented on Word and are very unclear, hard to follow and boring! Discussion is where you learn something, but that something is not worth the class.
She's a good person and cool but I've lost hope
Smart people shouldn't take this class. She isn't smart

I loved Jill as a Prof. I had her for 410 and 416. She was super respectful and gave good personal feedback on scores. She is a tough grader but gives you feedback before turning in projects to help you get a better grade. Both classes were only out of 100 points which is tough but it is not impossible to get a good grade!

Jill is one of those professors who seem really helpful, but in reality are never available to help you. She was very harsh on grading, her lectures was just her reading off slides, and the class is based on points not percentages (if you lose points there is no way to gain more back). Honestly, I would avoid this professor at all costs.

Had Professor Jill for MGMT 410 and she was the worst professor I have had at KU. I do not recommend taking MGMT 410 with her as she is an impossible grader and extremely unclear about what she wants. Extremely difficult to get an A in this class even though it is a simple class about HR management, policies, and practices.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought Beth was an excellent professor. As long as you show up to class and engage with the material it should be an easy class. Tests aren't that difficult as long as you read the cases. There is also a lot of collaboration with classmates! Overall it was a great class and Beth truly does care about her students!

Only tests are case exams, and she gives you a chance to redo it for more points. Super easy class because the teacher is so involved and on top of things. Definitely would try to get her as your teacher for 410.

grading is vague and inconsistent.

course material has little-to-nothing to do with owning, starting or maintaining a business

lectures are based on vague, leading questions that she expects to be answered precisely without guidance.

the course, teaching and grading is obviously biased towards business majors, not those looking to self employ.

The class is worth 100 points and you miss 2 points for every class you miss so you have to show up to every class, her teaching style is not effective, and you go into the first exam not knowing what to do and you will automatically have to do corrections on it.

Her workload is not incredibly heavy, but you do have to pay for access to some readings. The tests are for the most part straightforward, and she gives second chances! I have respect for her, but her teaching style is just not for me. She is an understanding individual.

Dr. Hotze is one of (if not the best) professors at KU. She's open, welcome, understanding, and makes learning fun and engaging. Her class is set up for student success and she makes sure you KNOW how to study. Her class is lecture and exam heavy but she is not unfair with tests. She makes your life easier by highlighting must read textbook parts.

If I could profess my undying love to Dr. Hotze I would. Lectures were an amazing experience. She's incredibly knowledgeable and friendly. If you interact with her directly, she WILL remember your name. Study guides were useful and were very helpful for exams. The McGraw Hill assignments were tedious but useful if you take notes! #Hotze4Life

I know everyone says this, but Dr. Hotze is truly amazing. She made me feel so welcomed/excited for class. I have a strong interest in biology now due to her. You kind of have to lock in during the lectures-they go fast. She gives lots of credit to help balance (even EC). Def had to study for the exams but what she taught is what was on there-10/10

The best biology class I have taken at KU! Hotze genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Highly recommend this class for anyone remotely interested in micro. She lectures make the topic engaging and interesting!
She is a wonderful teacher and the lectures are made very well and easily understandable. She is super caring (don't get on her bad side) but she aims for everyone to succeed if they try.
I would literally die for Eileen Hotze I am not even a little bit joking. she is the best professor I have ever taken at KU, and if she taught every course for me I would have a 4.0 fs.

Dr.Hotze is amazing! She is considerate of her students and easy to talk to. Lecture videos are a bit disorganized, but in-class lectures help. The online homework is VERY time consuming, DON'T put it off! I took it in Spring where she does group work. Be careful, the big group project can sneak up on you because you don't get much time in class.

Quite literally the best professor I have ever had. Genuinely cares about her students success and will know you by name. She is engaging, kind, articulate, fun, all-around a wonderful professor. Her office was always full during office hours and there were always students staying later to chat. Makes difficult content easy and fun to navigate!

Dr. Hotze was such a great professor to have. She was clear about expectations throughout the semester, was always available for students, and made her class engaging while keeping the coursework manageable. Highly recommend :)

Hotze is one of the most incredible professors I've ever had, she cares about her students. She's funny, kind, and gives you many tools to succeed. It's a flipped classroom, but it actually works well for this class and she's always trying new approaches, incorporating student feedback, and answers your questions. Pinnacle of science education
I would probably pursue a PhD in microbiology if Hotze taught all the classes.

LOVE Hotze! She obviously loves lecturing about microbiology. She wants her students to be interested and engaged in the content. Participation is not required but encouraged because participation is not like answering tough practice questions, it's asking about your experiences, your opinions, and your recollection of terms from previous biology

Dr. Hotze is THE BEST. Micro with her was seriously one of my favorite classes ever, and her lectures were a lot of fun! There were so many resources for us to get help when we needed it, as well as her office hours which are perfect for just saying hi and asking any questions! I would not hesitate to take another class with her.

Dr. Hotze is my favorite professor I've taken, and I'm in my 4th year. She provides you with all of the tools to do well. Her lectures were very thorough and easy to understand. She gives you study guides for the exams and practice exams online. Attendance is based on iClicker, you have to have 1/2 the points to get 100%.

I have so much respect for Dr. Hotze. She is outgoing and kind and cares about the wellbeing of her students. Prepare yourself to move quickly through her lectures and notes. She speaks fast and flies through lectures even faster. Overall I loved her class, but be ready to do a lot of memorization.

Dr. Hotze made the class fun and informative. It was not a monotone of lectures and had interesting TED talks. The exams tested exactly what we learned in class. If you rewatch the lectures you should be more than fine when taking the exams.

Dr. Hotze is an amazing professor and I was blessed to be a student of hers in my first biology course at KU! She is charismatic and prioritizes the student. Her exams are not very difficult and one is dropped in the course (including the final).

Could not recommend  Dr. Hotze enough. Material can be difficult, but if you put in effort its a smooth sail. Dr. Hotze was accommodating, realistic, and knowledgeable with every question. All exams were offered with the choice of taking online or in person, and plenty of extra credit was offered for every exam.

I absolutely love professor Hotze and all the biology professors. She make sure everyone understands the material and loves giving extra credit assignments. Granted the smart books are long and irrelevant (IMO) I didn't do majority of them and still passed the class. I recommend going to SI sessions they are the best.
good

Dr. Hotze gives great lectures and really tries to make sure students understand the material. This class seems difficult, but the professors make it quite easy. There are SO many opportunities for points- as long as you come to class and study an average amount, you will get an A. This class is always at 8AM, but the profs make it tolerable.

this professor's lectures were amazing! she follows along with powerpoint slides and write on the slides extra/helpful information. although attendance isn't necessarily required, iclicker. questions are utilized every lecture. so if you aren't there or don't answer the iclicker questions, that will harm your grade.
tldr; go to class & take notes
The easiest 5/5 I've ever given on this website. Although the smartbook assignments are arduous time consuming, they contributed so much to my understanding of the content.

As a freshman, I enjoyed taking BIOL150 with Dr. Hotze. She was very engaging during her lectures, which helped a lot given that this was an 8 am class. Her exams were pretty straightforward, and she offered extra credit as well. As long as you study on your own & put in the effort, her class should be easy.

First class at KU, easiest class at KU. You have group work during class that is just like test questions and the tests are very easy. She makes sure students understand the material and is always willing to help. You should be able to get an A very easily.

Dr. Hotze is a great lecturer and presents new information in a clear, easy-to-understand way.  The tests in this class were very easy multiple-choice questions and test for surface-level knowledge.  As long as you go to class and pay attention, this class shouldn't be too difficult.

Dr. Hotze is a great prof. However, if you are not STEM I heavily suggest not taking this course.. take BIOL 100 instead! I hella struggled and it can be difficult to keep up at times. Also, go to class for your iClicker points! Good luck.

Dr. Hotze was an amazing professor, you can tell she really cares about her students. The exams are pretty content heavy but if you really put in the time, go to class, and start studying early you can do well. She offers extra credit for every exam and wants everyone to learn the material and do well.

Dr. Hotze gives you clear expectations of what you need to do to succeed in her class. This does not mean that the class isn't difficult. The lectures are hard to grasp, although she does a good job at explaining the material. She provides many resources for help. Going to office hours or TA sessions are extremely helpful, though not mandatory.
