reviews.comment: If you suck at memorization like me, you might have a tough time in this class. Mnemonic devices are your best friend. Dr. Hotze's awesome though, and does everything she can to make the class accessible. It's just a LOT of memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Hotze is a great professor. In a lecture hall of about 300 students you are still able to get questions answered and she stays after class most days to make sure. The lectures are engaging and she does a great job making sure the TAs are attentive when doing group work.
Education recieved was not worth a cent in the real world
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Before class prep is important for understanding lectures. Lectures include class participation which makes them more entertaining and productive for learning. It's obvious that she cares and I'd love to have her as a prof again. Something nice about this class was one exam was dropped, and there was a group presentation instead of a final.

Dr. Hotze is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. Her flipped lecture structure made learning content that was somewhat difficult a lot less challenging. She always explained things well and I think it was overall a great class.

Hotze is literally the best professor ever. Her class is hard but doable and she is ALWAYS willing to help her students. Her lectures are hilarious and she's just a truly caring human being. I so wish she could teach all the biology classes at KU. She is AMAZING!

Eileen Hotze is the best thing to happen to KU biology for a long time. She truly cares about her students' success and wants the best for them. If you have problems, attend TA and SI sessions for extra help. The most important thing to worry about in this class is the exams, everything else is graded solely on effort and participation.
It is clear Dr. Hotze cares about her students. A lot of material is covered in the class, but she does a good job making it doable. Go to office hours if you're struggling.

Loved Hotze! She always was very clear on what we would be tested over and gives TONS of extra credit. You can tell she genuinely cares about her students and their well-being and is not afraid to stop and explain unclear topics. She makes an effort to connect with her giant lectures which says a lot about her. Tests are a big chunk of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Hotze knows the subject very well, but I think she forgets that us students aren't as familiar with the subject as she is. She uses a lot of unfamiliar terminology and goes really fast in lecture. I would STRONGLY advise reading the textbook sections that she's going to cover in class beforehand, and using the textbook to study as well.
Her classes require a lot of studying but the information you need is there.

Hands down one of the best professors at KU. Not only is the lecture simplified from the textbooks wording, but she is also a very funny person who makes the lecture even more entertaining. She doesnt round grades, but thats because she builds in bonus points to every single exam. Talking to other biology professors, she definitely is respected
She is really willing to go over anything all you have to do is go up and ask.
great teacher, keep up in lecture and you are solid, tests are fair. Would definitely take a class with her again, made me love biology

Hotze was an amazing teacher, she explained the material very well and always was available for help. She answered any and all questions you had and the grading criteria was given out right at the beginning of the class and what was expected. The material was not super hard you just had to put in some study time outside of class.

Hotze was a very nice and responsive professor, but I found her lectures very hard to understand. Almost like having an iPad to take notes and pictures of the lectures with was an essential part to getting any kind of decent grade. Tests and quizzes were also confusingly worded which led to a lot of missed points in my opinion.
Great professor but the content is conceptually challenging. If you put in the effort you should be fine.

Dr. Hotze is probably my favorite STEM professor Ive ever had! Shes incredibly helpful and cares deeply about her students. She gives ALL the necessary tools to succeed, and was the only COVID class I feel like I actually retained material in. Shes engaging, funny, and easily accessible. 10/10!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Hotze was an amazing professor. She really cares that her students get the material down. Her lecture videos are great. I usually prepared for exams by reading the textbook, going over her lecture videos, and doing connect assignments. The questions on the exam were very easy and all stemmed from what she taught.

Dr. Hotze wants everyone to succeed! She makes every single effort to give online students the best resources possible. She makes the best efforts to make clear, concise powerpoints for students and note-taking purposes and assigns SUPER HELPFUL SmartBook Assignments that can easily be made into online flashcards in order to study for exams!!

Took during COVID. She clearly wanted everyone to succeed. There were several different methods of learning: video lectures, Zoom meetings, discussion boards, homework, etc. Both she and her TAs were accessible. There was extra credit on every test, and she also dropped the lowest test from the final course grade. Overall, she was fantastic.

This is one of my favorite classes I have taken at KU. Dr. Hotze's lectures were very interesting and there were no surprises on the exams. It was very obvious she cared about her students and their success. If you need help understanding the material, she or the TA's are more than happy to help. I wish I could take this class again!!

I had her for BIOL150 my freshman year, and I loved her so much that I took her for BIOL400. She provides clear information, and is very straightforward about what she expects in the class. Her lecture slides a full of very useful information, and she provides a decent outline of what is covered on the exams. I would 100% take another class of hers

AMAZING CLASS, AMAZING PROFESSOR. Dr. Hotze is great. I would 10/10 take her class again. Info is hard and you have to study to get an A, but it is attainable. She makes you understand the info and teaches in a way students understand. Phenomenal woman.

I had a great experience in this class. Dr. Hotze's teaching was very clear and understandable. I never felt overwhelmed like I have in other classes. Dr. Hotze was one of the best professors I've ever had. She was very helpful, very kind, and I can tell she genuinely cares about the topic and her students' success!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hotze's biology lectures were always enjoyable. Lectures were always very engaging and used iClickers as well as class participation to keep you focused. She would give out candy to students who showed proficiency in their participation. We had a group assignment to do every Friday in the lecture, which was a good break from the usual content.

very meticulous when it came to knowing the details of each topic. all the tests were applying the knowledge and then applying it to a situation, so you have to know the information that was in the unit and the information that was in the previous unit. if you don't go to class you won't pass because she goes over details that isn't posted online
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Such a classic gal. I loved coming to this class, the lectures were interesting and you can tell she cared about it too. Pay attention in lectures, go over notes and watch videos, and if you need to reading the book helps a lot. The tests are pretty easy, she doesn't ask about specifics, but just have a general knowledge about it each topic

1 group day every week-dont miss these. 5 Extra credit available on all tests, lowest scores in all categories are dropped. Just do all the homework and do okay on exams and youll be fine. She posts lecture slides online and pro tip, you can do clickers on your phone in your bed if you wanna skip. Final is the easiest of all her tests.

She was kind and worked to learn everyone's name in a 600+ person lecture. The information is at a very fast pace and you're expected to learn the material before lecture from the textbook. Homework almost every class. Exams are pretty accurate to what you learn in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hotze made lectures so interesting. She knows her stuff and is very nice. The way she broke down the class made the material easy to understand. She was very quick to reply to emails as well. Definitely recommend taking her class.

While the class wasnt as easy of an A as I was hoping, Dr. Hotzes great lectures and guidance toward resources was a big help. Everything she goes over in class is at least somewhat important, and showing up is crucial, along with attending things like PLUS sessions. Shes very approachable, helpful, and nice  I totally recommend her.

Her lectures were straight forward of what you need to know for the test. The book is not required but I would recommend using if you want to do better. She is easy to talk to and makes her students feel good.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: lots of extra credit and easy grader

There's a lot of cushion with your grade, and you're able to drop one test. Most students did really well in the class. She also posts study guides and old exams, all are helpful. This was one of the easiest biology classes I have taken. Dr. Hotze really cares for her students, and you can tell she loves what she does.

She is fun to listen to and lectures are recorded. You have to relisten to lectures to do well and read the book. One time 75% of the class got this problem worth 15% of the test wrong and she got mad at us for not understanding when she did not teach it. Test are difficult to understand. They are worth 70% of the class. Other 30% easy to get 100's
absolutely terrible. She's not teaching anything. She talks all about her family and stuff. and you basically study by yourself and take the exams.

I loved learning from Professor Hotze. She made the material very easy and accessible and recorded all of the lectures, so if you really don't want to get up for 8am class, you don't have to. This year she also dropped one of the three tests, so I personally found it very difficult to get anything other than A in this class as long as you try.

Dr. Hotze is a great professor. She has made so many concepts such as Cell Respiration clear. Be prepared to read before her lectures otherwise you will be lost during lecture time. She posts practice exams which are very helpful and useful for tests. Also, be prepared to work in Groups because groupwork tests your understandingof lecture content.

Dr. Hotze is AMAZING! She is so good at breaking down hard concepts and mechanisms and teaching them in an understandable way. I never got below an A on any of the tests. She really cares and wants you to do well, grading scale is 87%  A-. Super accessible outside of class. Great teacher, made a tough class easy.

She was an amazing professor. I was terrified to take Biology 150 and she made the class go great. She sets extremely clear expectations as to what you need to know for the tests. I would highly suggest taking her if you can.
She was a good professor. She came prepared and made clear the expectations for every class and therefore what would be on exams. Do the reef polling/iClickers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Shes the best. You wont regret having her as your professor!
She has really great exmaples and uses a lot of class time to demonstrate difficult material. Her tests are pretty hard, but she evens out the test points with homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor!! So funny and never makes anyone feel stupid. Always so helpful and caring.

Study from the study guides she posts, they're very similar to the tests. Her lectures are good but sometimes she goes off on tangents and even answered her phone once in class, I thought it was funny though. Understand how the processes work. The textbook isn't quite mandatory but very helpful. A lot of her quiz questions are from quizlet.

Hotze very friendly and makes class interesting. The textbook was not required but as someone who did not use it during the semester, I regretted not getting it. Lectures are full of material with powerpoints posted online but if you try and skip class and rely on her slides that will not work out. Go to class and take notes

Dr. Hotze is great! Interesting and engaging lectures + she is absolutely hilarious. She's always willing to explain stuff in more detail if anyone is confused. Tests are relatively easy if you glance at the study guide and pay attention in class. Cool lady who makes microbiology fun and relevant. Wish she could be my prof for all bio classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Really cool person, funny. Wants class interaction/questions. Can be scatterbrained/confusing but will reexplain if needed. Supplements with online lectures posted. Tests are not too hard, provides quizlet/study guide. Lecture slides are hefty, can be annoying to take notes. Understand objectives-can easily get a good grade. Can skip on occasion.
She is somewhat nice and respectful throughout the course, but is a horrible, mean, and unfair person when it comes to grading. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hotze was so funny and such a straightforward teacher. Everything that was on the tests was right from the power points and the work load is not too much at all.

Dr. Hotzee is amazing. Teaches what you need to know and tests over exactly what she teaches, no tricks. She cares about everyone doing well and is very accessible and welcoming. She doesn't really teach out of the book, so going to lecture for the slides ( and clicker points) is important for your grade. Super easy to do well if u put in the work.

Best professor I have had at KU! I loved Dr. Hotze! She cares about her students and actually lectures about what you need to know.  Her tests were reasonably difficult but she held review sessions and the lecture material corresponded to the tests. She is a really great person overall, so if you are taking this class make sure she is teaching!

One of my favorite classes so far at KU. Amazing teacher, very engaging with the class by making a large lecture feel like a small class size. There was no homework in the class, just tests, but she held reviews where she went over exactly what would be on the test.; her lectures provided all the material you needed to know for the test.

Hotze is a great teacher. She makes class as entertaining as possible while still getting the information to you. She makes clear learning objectives which is extremely nice for study purposes. Tests are clear, short, and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was incredibly enjoyable and we still learned! Dr. Hotze made what would be on the test very clear and was very fair when it came to grading. She was funny and made biology apply to life. Definitely take even if it's not a requirement!

Dr. Hotze  The BOMB DIGGITY. Every biology student should take her course to remember that there are actually good educators in the biology department. She's really funny and down-to-earth and tries to make large lectures feel a lot more tight knit. She'll always remember your name and jokingly tease you in class. FIVE STARS!

Dr. Hotze is an awesome professor. Her lectures make learning fun and you certainly come out knowing more than when you went in. She is available outside of class, gives extra reviews, and gives fair tests. In lieu of homework, you just have more tests, but they are short and the material is manageable. I really liked the style of her class.
Difficult content, knows his stuff, and is a nice guy!

Mike Falk was the worst professor I have ever had at the University of Kansas. Gives you little study material, does not ever show examples of working things out in class and if he does only shows for 5 seconds which means you cannot write it down. You are on your own, don't even get me started on the tax return project that he gives no direction.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Skims over every single chapter. Better off skipping class after quizzes and reading the book because his lectures will teach you nothing. He also gives a massive final project at the end of the semester with little to no guidance.

I had Mike for ACCT 330 and loved the content but not the structure, so I was nervous to take his tax class in the MAcc. Now he's one of my favorite professors—flexible, open to feedback, and incredibly knowledgeable. I've learned so much from him!

His class is structured in a way that makes it hard to not get at least a B. He gave out 20 extra credit points on the final. If you show up to class and at least engage a bit, he will round up your grade as long as you are within like 3% of the next highest grade. The practice exams are VERY similar to the exams so do those and you will be fine.
Terrible teacher. Just lets mccgraw hill teach for him, doesnt even lecture, and when he does he just recites yet again, mccgraw hill slides. Shouldnt be teaching.

Class was incredibly useless. All over the place and didn't learn much as it was a rushed course with 27 chapters. The lecturing was pointless. Literally droned on about nonsense the entire lecture. Made me not want to take tax as my track. Single handedly made me dislike tax after working in it and studying it for 5 years.

The worst professor I've ever had at KU, and it's not close. Each class is freestyled on the day, and we are not once taught anything at all. We had an open note quiz a month into the semester and the material on it was nowhere to be found in the book/slides. I would genuinely recommend considering another macc track than tax because of Mike alone

What everyone else is saying here is 100% correct. He is the worst Accounting professor I've had at KU. Clearly very knowledgeable about the material, but he is an awful lecturer. The one saving grace of this class for myself and others was that he probably gave about a 15-20% boost to everyone's grade with how much EC he gave out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Smart guy, terrible teacher. Only goes off of powerpoints to teach and can't do much else. Doesn't really matter if you go to class or not because you're looking at the same thing he is to teach yourself. Homework was helpful but long for not many points as most was based off exams. Rather take someone else. First accounting course I had to drop.

Tax is known to be usually the hardest accounting class you'll take in undergrad. The exams in this class averaged about 50% and there wasn't a curve, but he offered so much extra credit that if you study enough, you'll get an A. He does care about his students doing well, but doesn't really capture his audience when teaching.

Michael Falk brought blight to my crops and famine to my land. Just kidding. But he did ruin my perception of tax, heavy power point reader for his "lecture" and tests and quizzes were very very hard. Try to take ACCT 330 during the fall with the other professor. Its clear that he knows about tax but he does not know how to teach effectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I was extremely let down by this professor.. He teaches off of a powerpoint, that has no correlation to whats on the homework or the exam. Our class average for an exam was 45%... he has to make up for it by giving alot of extra credit. thankful he did that, but it shouldn't be that way. So disappointed.

He does not teach anything that will be on exams. Completely up to you to read the textbook and learn the material on your own( and then still do badly on the test). Had to give us so much extra credit to save the class grades. When going over exams he wouldn't even be able to tell us the correct answers without looking at a key.

This is the hardest class I have ever taken. The class consists of tests only, so if you don't test well there is no opportunity to improve your grade. His lectures are very hard to follow and gives no direction on how to study for an upcoming test. When addressed with issues about his class he doesn't seem to care only “try harder”mentality.

This class is test based there are no assignments. He wants his students to fail. His test average has not surpassed a 59% on any of the exams and his response to that? Sorry figure it out. He gives no ways to study only old exams from 2014- 2016 I understand that this course is required for most majors but they need to find a new micro professor.
I feel like he explains things well but goes too fast.

Everyone is complaining about the difficulty of the exams; they're truly nothing special. I have not gotten below an 87% on an exam for this class. If you show up to class and read the textbook, the exams are not hard. The people complaining just aren't doing enough, or they don't know how to study, which, for this level of content, is depressing.

Microbiology with Funke is the worst class I have taken so far at KU. The course is extremely disorganized and grades are composed entirely of exam scores. The class averages on exams has not surpassed 59%. The daily 1-point quizzes contribute nothing to make up for these poor exam scores.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I haven't finished this class yet but it sucks. I wish I could drop but I need it for my major. Exams got changed, no longer online. They are super hard. The class average was an F and he basically said it was supposed to be hard and to study more. Questions were all over the place, topics barely talked about. Seems like he wants everyone to fail.

This class was fun but way more work than I expected. The exams were really hard—I got high A's in ochem but couldn't get an A on these exams. Be ready to work for it and take your time on everything. My TA was great which helped. Study practice exams, data sheets, ask questions, and aim for full points elsewhere to make up for tough exams.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams are HARD, but if you take advantage of the multiple extra credit opportunities you can easily regain those points. Lab exercises are actually interesting and applicable to content learned in BIOL400. He's a nice guy overall who does care.
The lab exams are so confusing and the grading scale sets you up to "fail" if you do bad on one exam. Funke is never clear in his expectations for students and never provides feedback at all.

I was dreading this lab based on my chem lab experiences, but I was pleasantly surprised by the low workload/difficulty of this class. You stay with one lab partner, which was nice. That being said, you will not be taught the things he tests you on, just expected to know. Instructions/report guidelines were very unclear, but overall, not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Funke was super kind and funny. The lab helped me develop a lot of skills -- I was told that the lab would be a lot of busy work, but I felt like it was very manageable. 4 stars instead of 5 because the exams were super confusing and the class is graded by only 200 pts, which was hard when exams were so confusing.

Honestly, his exams were graded pretty hard. For an “easy” 200 level class, a large amount of people did not do great on the exams. They were online;however, apparently a large amount of the answers were wrong. Many people ended with a B when it was supposed to be an easy class. He is also extremely passive aggressive on both lab and lecture.

This professor is hilarious but that's about it. Asked him a few times outside of class to help me with things here and there and he rushed the conversation and stated he didn't have time to help. The TA's that taught my class made me question if they ever took this class themselves due to the lack of direction and instruction provided.

Lectures were hard to take quality notes because they were all over the place, but he is a funny guy. All exams were online and "open google" so made the class easy. TA's are not good at all. They do not answer questions and instead leave you more confused than you were before.

Dr. Funke is great. Good lectures and he's very funny. He makes things clear and helps you with quizzes and such. he wants you to succeed and it's clear that he cares about students. His lab TA's are rude, unhelpful, and condescending though it's not his fault.

It is very easy to do well in this class, he explains everything, and if you pay attention he will basically give you the answers. All questions asked are explained thoroughly, if you still are unsure he WILL go back over it. Overall, Dr. Funke is a great teacher who wants to see everyone succeed. His lab TA's might not have the same idea though.

I took this class in the summer, so it was easier to talk to Dr. Funke directly. He's hilarious and if you ask him questions and communicate, he'll tell you everything you need to know. Made the first lab report worth less points so it wouldn't kill your grade if you did poorly and he gave good feedback. Don't wait until last minute to do things!

Overall the course is ok. No real need to go in person since very exam and quiz is online, including the iClicker quiz answers which are in the lecture vids. Felt like there was a lack of resources since the slides didn't really contain much text but rather just snapshots from textbook. I ended up just reading the textbook on my own time to study.

This is more about the TA you end up getting. It is a difficult lab and your lab TA does not really give much instructions. You have to know "lab math" and Professor Funke gets frustrated when you do not know what that is. Also, and this should be something you do anyway, wash your hands after lab. Every lab involves some type of bacteria.

He is a nice guy but he is not the best at lecturing. Professor Funke goes off on tangents during lectures that have nothing to do with the lesson for that day. It is easier to do everything online and teach yourself since attendance is not mandatory. Tests and quizzes are online. You get unlimited attempts on quizzes.

Honestly whether or not you like this lab depends a lot on your TA. Dr. Funke himself is pretty nice and was better than my TA at answering questions. I feel like I learned a lot from the lab and the exams weren't too bad as long as you read the lab handouts. Dr. Funke's instruction videos are super helpful and you'll know exactly how to do stuff.

He's frustrating. He's smart and tries to have fun, but inconsistent and all over the place. There weren't good resources to learn because all his slides are directly from the textbook, and there's variation between the old exams we get to study and the new ones he writes. You just gotta get through the class and stay optimistic about it.

The labs are generally pretty easy, just follow the directions on the datasheet. Quite a few assignments, sometimes multiple at once. Little to no direction was given regarding assignments. Old lab exams are not helpful, expected to know lab math, even though was never discussed in class. Was told, "you should have learned this in middle school."

Personally, I did not enjoy this class at all. He reads from the textbook during lectures, so I found it difficult to take notes. No assignments, and no extra credit. Daily quizzes are done in class, so go to class or watch Zoom. Exams are online, open note, google, etc, but are fairly difficult because of the way he words the questions.

The reason I rated this class so poorly is because of my TA. They were not helpful and so rude. It is possible to get an A for sure but know that little points will be taken off for everything it seems. For lab exams, use practice exams and KNOW LAB MATH!!! For lab reports set up a meeting and talk with your TA to get feedback before the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class could be done online, don't trust the practice exams because the exams are much more difficult. The exams are open notes and all online. How I studied was making a Google doc and writing down important notes from lectures and then you have a free textbook he gives. Use these tools on the exams and you will do okay. Three points EC.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Funke is passionate about microbio and you can tell he cares. He goes out of his way to ensure lecture videos are available online and does Q&As before exams. He is a little disorganized and doesn't put that much in the grade book, but he does offer extra credit and there are no +/- grades. I found the class to be interesting and not that hard.
BIOL 402 is a fun class. Get ready to learn the basic fundamentals of microbiology and be prepared to apply them with minimal help from the TAs. Really fun projects and a lot of autonomy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class as a whole is very interesting and hands on which I liked very much. You need to be ready to juggle multiple assignments at once. The biggest issue I had with this class is the exams do not correlate with material learned AT ALL. You do not use math whatsoever in this class, but you are expected to know it, and they do not teach it.

Dr. Funke and Microlab are both very fun, and made the class very enjoyable, but the lab is not a walk in the park! I understand why many people are confused about the strict grading criteria, with very little points in the class, but I found that a lot of the time I lost most of my points because I didn't study much for the exams. Maybe just me
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Funkes is a nice person overall but the grading criteria was very strict and with the class being out of 200 points, it was hard to achieve an A if you did bad on a report or exam. Lab exams are 40 questions with unrelated material for some of the questions that Dr. Funke never talked about. Be prepared to spend alot of time on the lab reports.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took microbiology with him and could not be happier. I was so stressed going into this semester and it was a breeze, im not super studious/smart and I still had an easy time. His tests were all open note open book online making it almost impossible to not do well. No hw was ever given and his lectures were fun and easy to follow. 100% recommend.

Dr. Funke's name really fits because he is a funky guy. Man is all over the place and never knows what to do with his hands which is distracting. He knows what he is talking about and is very knowledgeable about microbiology but doesn't teach ANYTHING. This is basically a trial and error class with very few grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Funke is a great guy, his lectures are usually pretty clear and interactive, and I feel like I've learned a lot in his class! All of his exams were online this semester, and "open everything" so they were pretty easy! There's also a daily quiz, but it is done together as a class and he makes sure we understand all of the questions and answers.

His rubric for the class is super fair and built specifically so that no one project/test can ruin your grade. Test questions were not too hard if you studied the exact materials provided. We did do some silly projects due to pandemic constraints-- but they could be kind of fun and he really encouraged creativity. Would take again!

Literally the worst teacher in the biology lab department. He is all over the place and makes us do stupid projects not related to biology at all. Ex: he made us perform sales pitches in which we were attempting to sell him laboratory materials. Hard grader as well and his tests are not fair. Most unengaging and tedious class I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Funke runs the microbiology laboratories. He is very accessible and helpful to students. Would recommend taking one of his labs.

Todd is a mess, but he had valid reasons this semester. All over the place during lectures. You don't need to go to lecture as he uploads all of them, but it's still useful to go. Tests make up your entire grade and there's next to no extra credit available. You can only miss 21 points total in the class to get an A. So be prepared for tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is such a unique and interesting professor! He is very animated in his lectures, and makes it very clear what to focus on for exams. He is very passionate and knowledgeable about micro, and if you're interested in any micro info outside of class, he has tons of it! Great guy. Posts lectures online.

Dr. Funke is an excellent lab director-willing to help out when TAs won't. He sets clear schedules and makes expectations for the class very clear. I do wish there were more assignments or points available - TAs grade hard and it takes a lot of work for a 2 credit hour class. Very helpful guy, especially with his review and technique videos!

The worst part of this class was the exams. The TA's post previous exams to study for the exams for. All of the experiments you do in the class are for your final project so it helps to take pictures and know what you're looking for. They held open lab on days there weren't other classes in there, take advantage of that early! It will save you!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Going to office hours was really helpful in this class. We had 38 quizzes but they were all online and you could take them as many times until you scored 1/1. All of your study material came from the book, and you could email TA's about free response questions the week before the exam. Lectures were also recorded so attendance wasn't necessary.
Dr. Funke makes his expectations for class very clear, but he is ALL over the place. Use old tests that he posts on blackboard!

Todd is the most scatterbrained, incompetent lecturer there is. Sure, he might understand what he is saying, but a class average of 65% in a lecture of 300 of the smartest students on campus cant mean anything good for him. Definitely do NOT recommend taking this class if you dont have to and ESPECIALLY DO NOT TAKE THE LAB!

The work loads he assigns are actually insane and I can only assume that he figures this must be the only class you are taking that semester. He is the walking definition of "busy work". Highly recommend taking the lab and lecture together because they do overlap some. Definitely read the chapters for comprehension, not everything is in lectures
He uploads test files that have about 75% of the questions that are on each exam. Super easy. Online quizzes due before each class for easy extra points. I never went to lecture and got an A.

An excellent lab director that is actually involved in the labs! This class is a lot of work, but it was fun. Make sure that you understand the information behind the tests, not just how to perform them, so READ before coming to class. Don't be lazy, or it will come back to bite you. Dr. Funke is happy to help you outside of lab, very approachable

A large class lecturer that actually cares about his students. Go to class, pay attention, don't miss easy points, and take advantage of the few e.c. opportunities, and you'll be okay. Study underlying concepts behind quiz and old exam questions. He even gives you pointers on types of questions he asks. Go to SI sessions if you need extra help.

Greatest lab director I have ever had. Always there popping in and out of lab rooms to make sure everyone is doing the right thing and always there to give good advice to make the class go by faster. Will always be there for the students.

While I agree orginization isn't his strong suit, I  have not met another 'big lecture' professor who is as helpful and available as he is. He truly does care, you just have to be proactive/patient. It's best to talk to him in person though, for sure. Test questions, while broad require advanced thought. It isn't all 'right there answers'

The  tests are pretty tough but there are a lot of resources available to study and do well. Attendance isn't really mandatory but it does help. He's really fair and knows what he's talking about, he just talks really fast.

Dr. Funke talks fast, but the lectures are only 50 minutes and there's a lot of information to cover. Go to SI sessions, asks questions, read the book chapter before class, and listen during lecture, and you should be fine. Study the quiz questions, old exams, and lecture notes. If you took BIOL 150, you're very well prepared for this class.

Wow, where do I begin! I've studied all semester, went to every class, but still got a bad grade because of test scores. He was never available when needed and don't care if you pass or not. I suggest NOT taking this class with him.

Todd is a fantastic lab director. He's very helpful and available if your microbio TA's are not. Makes a schedule at the beginning of the semester regarding each reading assignment, and posts rubrics for lab reports as well as old exams and quiz keys. STUDY THE OLD EXAMS AND QUIZZES FOR THE UPCOMING EXAMS. You'll thank me later.

Covers material too quickly, quizzes get confusing, but he does answer them in class before you leave, so show up for those points. Study on your own time, as he reuses quiz questions. Mostly self-learning here.

Be prepared for extreme disorganization - mostly in lab, but also in lecture.  He says things won't be too 'specific' but yes, he will write test questions that are definitely down to the nitty gritty.  Class is not mandatory, but he's entertaining to listen to as sometimes he cracks nerd jokes. Doable, but don't miss easy points.

I learned nothing from his lectures, as he tries to rush through 40- 50 slides in about 40 minutes or less. Very frustrating. He recycles old quiz questions on the tests and the tests aren't too hard as long as you study for them.

Covers the material VERY quickly during class. Goes through 40-50 slides in an hour. I studied for over a week for a test and still did not receive an A. You will definitely have to work hard from the very beginning if you want an A overall in the class. Read the chapters before class to better understand the material.

Funke hates writing test questions, most exams are repeats of quiz questions and lab exams. Definitely read the text book it just reiterates what he says based off his PowerPoint slides. Exam questions that are not repeated questions tend to be difficult, but he does curve some tests and the class depending on the averages.
Talks too fast during lecture, but goes through each quiz before they are due and gives answers.

He was a good professor, but he would often rush through his lectures. Highly recommend asking him questions and getting extra help because he always wants what's best for the student. Overall, the class is pretty difficult but is heavily curved.
Couldn't see grade all semester. He replies to emails like he's chat gpt, and also takes 5-10 business to reply. Oh and I was never informed that I failed the isq.
Dr. Frier is a really nice guy, and he's pretty funny. The material is difficult, but he's pretty good at explaining it. LGAs are very helpful for the exams.

Most clear lecturer I've ever had. Took 125 as an engineer. Explains Calculus in methodical way. Attendance quizzes as questions related to topic. Decent grading scale that ensures hard work = good grades. Discussed topics outside of class, and is extremely intelligent. Changed my view of my Calc requirement for my major and made me want to learn.
I loved taking calc 2 with Professor Frier. You can tell he really likes his job, lectures are good. Attendance isn't mandatory but he does iclicker. 10/10 would take calc 2 again.

I love when there are professors that are really bright but are SUPER humble. I can tell that Frier is a smart guy and luckily he knows practically anything you ask him. He's super helpful and I hope I have him next semester.

Ryan was my TA and he was incredible. Every day I looked forward to lab because I knew Ryan would be able to summarize the lectures in the best way possible. He is also so nice and willing to answer even the dumbest of questions. I could not recommend him as a teacher enough.

Very very great professor
As long as you show initiative and try your hardest he will go out of his way to help you.
He is very accessible outside of class and his teaching is very clear and easy.
I would recommend taking a class with Mr.Frier
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really great of reminding students of what they have to do throughout the course! He seems to really care about his students.
Very good he truly helps and cares

I made this rating because he is an exceptional teacher. He's eager to help his students understand concepts (easy or hard). Most notably, he doesn't appear condescending when you ask questions about even basic algebra. I think he enjoys teaching, which is rare for subjects like math (I think?). Take his section if you can!
Disorganized, but she's nice!
She has no idea what she is doing. Fumbles over her words and can't even do the math that she teaches.

She offers some extra credit. 

Other than that, she is the most unorganized professor. She frequently makes mistakes in lectures and in videos. This makes it hard to learn, because she will finish a problem, and forget a step, then redo the whole thing.

When I took this course, there were 2 professors. Agusto is a bad professor, maybe 2/5, but Marriage is a 5/5. There are 480 total points in the course: 3 Exams(180Points) and the Final(120Points). The rest of the points came from lab work and HW, which was completion. Listen, participate during the lecture, and do past exams - you'll be good.

Dr. Agusto seems like a brand new professor, yet has been teaching since before 2020. Her lecture videos are at least 45 minutes each, and she publishes 3 or more of them the day they are due. Her explanations of the content are long-winded, slow, distracted, and unhelpful. She wastes time during class by talking instead of letting you work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have ever had. Her lecture videos are generally 45 minutes each with 2-3 due in a day. She mocks students during lecture and will not extend the in class work if she takes too long to lecture, which is every class. She blames all mistakes on being “hungry” or says she “time travels” when something doesn't go her way.

She is the worst professor I have ever had. She should not be employed as an educator; she really struggles explaining concepts and teaching material. She constantly degrades and humiliates students in front of the class when they ask a question. She sets expectations that are impossible to reach because she does not give the resources to do so.

I thought that her lecture videos were not helpful and was not easy to learn from. I would say the textbook is your best bet on the chapters that she teaches. Also, she came off a tad judgmental when coming to talk to her over test questions.

Online during the COVID-19 restrictions. Dr. Agusto is a nice professor and means well, though the only couple of times I contacted her outside of class, she was rude and disrespectful to me and some of her other students. She isn't the best at explaining the ideas in a lecture; she tends to read off the slide and doesn't explain the concept itself

Don't listen to people complaining about exams, if you only look at the practice exam before taking the exam you won't do great. But every problem on exams is either in the lecture slides, handouts or homework, if you look at them all before the exam you will do great! Just show up to class and complete the in-class and it will boost your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have had Dr. Fattah for Fluids, Environmental, and Hydrology. His class format has taught me great study habits that have carried over into other classes. He truly cares about his students and if you take the time to visit his office hours and ask questions in class, you will see that. Look at problems in handouts, hw and slides before exams.
He is a good teacher for the most part. The class was more difficult for me than he was.

Great professor who clearly cares about the subject and makes lectures engaging and worth attending. Exams are very challenging but only about a third of the final grade and reflect the material well. If you show up and put in the effort, you'll learn a lot. Claims that he “doesn't teach” usually come from people who skip lecture.

This guy doesn't teach, he gives theoretical lectures on textbook concepts and gives difficult homework. Rather than provide examples of course work problems, Fattah shirks that responsibility to unhelpful and dull videos that do not give you the full picture of the problems you will be facing.

took CE477. Funny and nice guy, decent lecturing and exams. Homeworks will be difficult to learn but they're 1-1 the same format on the exam which makes studying very doable. Apart from exams and hw in class works you upload are a huge part of your grade, which if you are there every class, will drastically improve your grade.
Took 477, and it was pretty chill. Straightforward lectures and videos posted to canvas were useful. Not that much homework, exams where very doable.
He doesn't teach. He just expects us to know. The class doesn't make sense and is a bunch of chemistry that is hard for no reason.

I thought this class outline was pretty disorganized, but at times interesting. It seemed like the class got more disorganized, but grading got to be harder, as the semester went on. Overall, a little bit of a confusing experience, but not bad.
Genuinely a great professor, makes an effort to get to know her students and has clear and reasonable expectations.
love her so much
SOOOO sweet. I loved her
She is so understanding of your time and is very knowledgable in journalism. Such an easy class that taught me a lot! Love this woman.

I absolutely loved having Fraley as a professor. She is among the most caring teachers I've ever had, and she is incredibly accommodating. If you have the chance to take a class with her, I highly suggest it. She makes the content incredibly understandable, which makes the class very easy while still learning everything.
Amber is genuinely one of the kindest professors at KU that I have had the pleasure of meeting. She is one of those professors who understands that you have a life outside of school.
Honestly the light of my week. She is so funny and she is truly there to help and wants to help. She gives away the answers all the time and is just a great professor.

She is AMAZING. If you go to class you can get all your homework done there with her help so you'll get a 100. It is an easy class to skip but there is participation points each day which is a good chunk of your grade. She is seriously one of my favorite professors and this is easily my favorite journalism class at KU. I learned so much from her.

Dan is really great guy. He gives good feedback but not much help with solution would expect u to find it urself and sometimes it's not for everyone coming into first year but I think that really helped me with my problem solving and coming into second yr

I went into this class with hope that Dan was going to be a great professor. Unfortunately, Dan picks favorites and if you are not one of them, you will graded harder than others. Dan would tell me my project looked amazing and then proceed to give a worse grade than everyone else. My confidence was very much lowered through this class.

Taking Dan first semester can be rough, you kinda get thrown into Arch pretty hard and it can seem rough, but his critiques were quite the reality check and I can't say that they didn't make my work better. Compared to some professors who provide little feedback, he made sure you knew what was wrong and didn't give out points for just doing it.

I would not recommend Dan at all. He's a nice guy but a terrible professor. He is rarely satisfied with the work done and nit picks. He would also often give advice for a project, I'd take it, and he'd then tell me he disliked the changes I made even if he suggested them. You'll feel extremely lost in this course.

It seemed that Dan had good intentions, but in reality they often fall short. It is incredibly hard for you to figure out what he wants on a project, it seems sometimes even he doesn't know, and the feedback he gives you will change on a daily basis. His grading sucks, as for some people he lets a ton of mistakes slide but for others none at all.

Dan is very opinionated and holds a lot of favoritism. He just gives assignments and expects you to complete them on your own, no questions asked. He talks more than he should and wastes most of the class going on tangents. Critiques will drain your soul, If you make a project he asks for, he will never like it. Expect to be disappointed.

I love Dan!! He is ultimately the best. Everyone hates when he says "make the cake" but he doesn't say it often. He truly cares about you and your project. He wants the best for you and your project. All good things to say about Dan
Cares, but very knitpicky

Dan is a really nice guy. Sometimes you have to put in some effort to get a productive and helpful critique, but he is overall very involved with all students and their work and very approachable. He puts a big emphasis on graphic representation which is valuable but sometimes it seems as if he focuses on that more than your actual work.

Dan is great and at the moment, his comments seemed harsh but I believe they were very helpful. Be prepared to do small critiques often. Focus a lot on your graphic design regarding your presentations. He's understanding and kind of situations if you message him with time! Work feels heavy, but not terrible. Overall, studio was fun and enjoyable

Professor Finnel was a tough, yet fair teacher and I saw a huge improvement from the beginning of the term to the end. He brought great feedback to each individual and explained architectural concepts in depth. He encouraged class participation and collaboration which molded the studio into a better community.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dan never gave you feedback and if you asked his response was "bake a cake". There were multiple times he would make condescending comments against his students. There were many days he would disappear and go watch his sons baseball games instead of being in class. He was never clear on due dates and what was due. Good luck!

I like Dan as a person, he's an extremely relatable guy. He has prior experience in the field. You will get honest feedback from him that is not too tough; however, He will not tell you what he wants in the unit writeups... so yeah. Dan contradicts himself some, and I wonder if his grading is accurate for everyone, but I learned a ton from him

Do not take Dan. He is a good person but a really bad teacher. He has experience in the Architecture field but can not teach. He will tell you to "bake a cake" when you ask a question, due to him not giving clear instructions in the first place, then when he grades it clearly was a cake made for his taste buds.

Dan is a really good person, however he does not know how to teach the concept. He talks about it once and then tells you to "bake a cake" but when you "bake your cake" he never likes it. He is a tough grader. He will rip you apart in class critiques. He talks a lot. He overall just doesn't teach well.
She has coffee hours Verrrrry helpful

Quite possibly the least prepared professor at KU. No other professor I have seen makes their TA's rate her five stars and still has an overall rating of 2. It is sad that she still has a spot at KU and needs to hide her own failures.

She cannot teach, if possible show up to lectures and grab the worksheets then just leave and go to TA sessions because they are much better at teaching this stuff then her, and even if she says a certain concept won't be on the test don't listen cause she will probably still put it on the test. DO NOT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So much material that she teaches just once, moves incredibly faster than other classes, quizzes weekly, workload is unreal

Be prepared to do titration reactions, organic chemistry, types of reactions, and naming everything, all on one exam. This class feels like theres a dart board of random things to learn, none of it relating to one another, and MANY “you'll just have to know that” scenarios, yet no clear explanation of what exactly you need to know.
quiz every friday or an exam. spend probably about like 10 hours a week at least studying. everyone teaches themselves
Do not take this class. Just wait for the summer or something.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Doesn't teach. Don't try to go to her office hours, you'll leave more confused.
Great professor, its just a hard class. If you actually want to learn and understand chemistry take it with sharpe-ellis
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She does not teach and excepts you to learn everything outside of class while calling the readings “optional”. The only thing that happens in class is the weekly quizzes and worksheets every single class over topics she won't teach you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gives long test in 50 minute class making it hard to finish on time. Also flip
Completely flipped classroom, prepare to do a LOT of learning by yourself
Mean and condescending but easy class to do well in. If you need anything she will respond like you are inconveniencing her whether it's over email or in person.

She provides so many opportunities for extra credit and wants her students to succeed. Take advantage of coffee hours and SI sessions. Make sure to watch pre-lecture videos so you are more confident in what we practice in class.

Sharpe Ellis was disrespectful and rushed through so many important topics. She got frustrated when the class average on tests was 65% but didn't spend time working through things. Over time, the course gets worse and worse. Exams come up very fast and she does NOT use class time wisely at ALL. She waits until the last minute to go over things and wastes so much time. her tests are horrible. the workload is horrendous. she is such a strict grader and you will be counted off for everything. take advantage of the SI sessions and TA sessions.

You get partial credit for even trying on the tests and quizzes. The material can be confusing but not as much as other college classes. Just apply yourself and you'll be fine. She's not a good professor at all to smart for her own good

She does not teach AT ALL!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! All you do in class is clicker and she doesn't work thru any problems

She does not know how to teach. She throws things at students that we have never learned before and expects us to know what she is talking about. Never looked both ways crossing the street to gray-little because I wanted to get hit by a car before going to her class

She just teaches irrelevant information in class, and basically says I can't teach you it, so i'm going to REQUIRE you to go to TA sessions, which are also pretty mediocre. Terrible lecturer, take Berger Dunn

I would tell you not to take this professor. She doesn't teach you. It's all outside of the classroom. Half of the time in lecture you will have no idea what's going on. Do not take this class unless you want to cry yourself to sleep every night and study for 10 hours for a quiz and the things you study not even being on the test.

She is terrible at teaching and getting points across, almost all exams/quizzes had typos in which she would have to address during testing times, class would be confused 90% of the time and not be able to answer her lecture questions.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! I'm telling you all she do in class is stalking about stuff that we gonna do next time and bad with time managements. IF YOU TAKE THIS CLASS GO TO TA SESSION, THEY'RE SUPER.

She was the worst teacher I have ever had. I have never received a B in any classes until hers. She does not teach at all, but instead, she makes you teach yourself. Then, when the test comes you hope and pray you taught yourself enough.

Sharpe-Ellis we know you're the one writing the 5 star reviews, take the L and move on little bro.

ugh

Online quizzes no exams, just a big group project you have to sell to a buyer and then an assignment for the final, great class Gail also very nice... attendance graded out of 4 points... 2 points for participation and 2 points for actually showing up so participation actually matters

There were only a few grades in this class which I didn't like. The pop quizzes were pretty hard along with the exams. You don't get any homework, so you're graded on quizzes, tests, and one group presentation. She's a good professor, just don't like how she set up the points. Study quizlets online with the questions from the pop quizzes!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is a sweet women and very easy to listen to in lectures. The projects are easy and she is a lite grader, and test are also on the easier side. The only thing that wasn't easy were the pop quizzes, those I didn't do so well on. Fun class and great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: It was uncomfortable to hear him constantly promote AI. He even generated images for slides. If your response to students struggling is to just "use Claude", your mindset discourages learning. Grading is lenient, and exams aren't difficult if you actually read the material. Course material is interesting, but I wish AI wasn't involved in everything
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have ever taken. His lectures are so random, messy, and he talks about random stuff. Crazy final project for it being an undergraduate class with basically no pre-reqs. Exams are about random material. Will give u a study guide with 50+ topics, yet will quiz you on five in-depth. Dont take if you dont have too.

I liked him as a professor, and this class was not as challenging as others made it seem. His lectures sometimes weren't very centered on the actual material, but the textbook was easy to read. There is a large reaserch paper at the end of the class that's a lot of work, but thankfully it is just the one. Overall good teacher mid class

For an undergraduate course, I was blown away by the fact that we had to conduct an experiment and write a research paper based on what I would think to be graduate-level criteria. Never offered class time to work on it or ask questions, he just expected you to go to office hours. You were also expected to work on this WHILE learning new chapters!

I really liked the lectures and thought they were interesting, but nothing talked about in the lectures were on the exams. I had wondered if the exams being challenging was personal, but my exam grades would always be around 70-75 which heavily affected my grade. The Inquisitives were also very time consuming and not helpful to my learning.

taken multiple of his courses. they are pretty difficult, so get ready to work. I studied hard, took notes, joined study groups and all of that effort was for a very low B. he also tends to have group research projects worth a big chunk of your grade which is frustrating and the instructors for which are very unclear.

Ignore the negative reviews; Omri is known for "weeding out" those who don't care to give their best. His lab was fascinating! He is such a caring man, truly a fatherly man who will provide you with honest yet caring advice. He is disability friendly; just communicate with him properly. Mention his TedTalk to start the sem. in good standing ;)

Lecture was interesting sometimes. If attendance wasn't required, I would never go. Just read the textbook and do the quizzes to study for the exams. Dr. Gillath seems very knowledge about the content, but his lectures didn't cover much of the exam topics.

The lectures were kind of interesting, but he didn't do a good job of making the class fun and interactive. The exams were HARD. I read other people's reviews before taking the class and just hoped it was a personal issue with the exams. No. I studied hard and got a 78 lol. 2/4 were easy and I scored above a 95. Tests 1 & 3 were hard tho.

None of the material given in the lectures or on the study guide are on the exams. The only thing that matter on the exams is the information on the InQuisitive assignments (which are annoying and so long). He is also really rude and will call someone out just for getting up to go to the bathroom. He gives no feedback at all. He isn't a good prof!

Dr Gillath was a very intelligent man, but I just did not learn from his teaching methods the way I have from other psych professors. His exams were DIFFICULT, even if you spent weeks preparing beforehand. Attendance is mandatory, and its a large part of your grade. The class overall was interesting, I just did not like how he taught it.

If I could redo this class, I would take it with any other professor. The grades are locked until after finals, so you will think you have an A+ until it is too late. There is iClicker in every class, LOTS of busy work, a paper, and 4 exams. He also shares personal details about his life that I could have gone my whole life without knowing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: People are exaggerating the difficulty so much in these reviews. I took this class in my first semester ever in college, and pretty much all you have to do is pay attention during the lectures, do the readings, and study a little before the test. If you do those things, you'll be fine. I honestly really liked this class and Dr. Gillath's lectures.

Lectures are long but interesting sometimes. Exams are hard, and a lot of the topics are not even covered in class. Definitely read the textbook. Huge final project that isn't something you would expect for a 300 class.

Absolutely awful, which sucks because I love social psych. Most things he covered were opinion based, his lectures were long and hard to read, and none of what you study for is on the exam. Went off topic sm, and literally no lecture went past 10 mins before he talks about having sex. Just overall a mess and very confusing, basically taught myself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fantastic Professor

The tests in PSYC 360 are absolutely unforgiving and Omri's lectures are some of the most boring I have ever had the displeasure of attending. He won't enter grades into the grade book until you've taken the final and does not give a shit about how boring his class is. If you're used to straightforward grading and engaging lectures, steer clear.

I would not recommend taking this class. The professor is honestly rude and does not show any empathy when someone needs help or is having an issue. He is not willing to work with students and leaves all grading and questions for the TA's. The lectures can sometimes be interesting but overall not engaging. The exams are pretty difficult.

Lectures are interesting. However, moves fast during lectures it is hard to keep up. The semester is almost over, and grades are not put into canvas correctly. I cannot see what I have in the class, and there is no guidance on how to calculate our grades. Do not expect sympathy for any assignments or exams. TAs are much more helpful than professor.

Entertaining professor however mostly just goes over whatever you were to read before class. I had a hard time wanting to go to the class because of that. The attendance is through iClicker which you do have to pay for. Exams are easy but I struggled with the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very difficult exams

Exams are insanely hard. The exams were multiple choice, taken in the class, and there were 2 people that got ZEROS. No one got above 90. He had to add 10 points to everyone so we didn't all fail. Grading takes forever and are put in weirdly in the book. Will call you out in front of 200 people for things. Canvas/syllabus is not up to date at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Knows a lot, and is very encouraging for class to be engaged in his lectures. Fair essay grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zero empathy, this professor was rude. The TA does the majority of the grading, but knows very little about the class content. Tests are pretty brutal, and difficult to prepare for. The way he does lectures is pretty entertaining but it's a lot of information and kind of all over the place. Not very helpful through email. Do all the extra credit!

Overall amazing professor. Super interesting lectures which he connects to real-life social issues happening in real time. Exams are very difficult but if you show up to class and do the readings you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He made his TA do all the work in regard to grading as well as interacting with students. However, the TA had seemingly zero knowledge of the course content and was extremely disorganized. Professor Gillath said exams would be open note one day, then the day of the test would say he never said we could use notes. He also doesn't answer emails.

Test questions came straight from quizlet. (multiple ones) Without quizlet, I would've failed. Final paper is like 10 pages long but if you have written APA style papers, you'll be fine. Lectures can get off topic, just read the book and you'll be good. Even if you don't read, the hw makes up for not reading.

This prof is very political. He talked about politics the entire class and used very biased sources. I was very excited for this class, but this sort of ruined my experience since I am not interested in politics and like to keep opinions and learning separate. Politics has no place in the classroom. If you are a liberal you will love this class.

A LOT of papers but they aren't too hard just tedious, the final project is a lot and isn't something I expected for a 300 level class. He's a fine professor just a lot of work. He offers a good amount of extra credit and is easy to get in contact with and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I have Dr. Gillath for two classes. Online school is tough but you can tell he cares a lot about trying to make his lectures engaging and easy to follow along. He is awesome about stopping for questions and answering them. He is also very understanding. I love both of his classes & wish I could have him for more.

Omri made his lectures pretty engaging most times, although he would speed through some sections. He didnt seem to be available outside of class much. You should know how to write in APA format before taking this class! I am but a measly freshman and didnt find out what that was until I took this class, dont make the same mistake I did!

Dr. Gillath is chill and gives nice study guides for exams. You have online pre-lecture quizzes every week for topic reinforcement. Only weakness of 360 is lots of papers and a 8-10 page final paper. He really wants you to nail down the topics. He's a research prof and this shapes his lecturing style and final paper layout. An A is attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very impatient, does not help much. Good teacher, not a good person.

I will say I did thoroughly enjoy lectures and course material. That being said, expect very little empathy from him. The day before the final there was a snowstorm. We were sent a mass email informing us that if we had any issues getting there he would not care. We were expected to Uber. HEAVY workload. The final paper is insane. Beware!!

The greatest professor I have ever had the pleasure of meeting. My life is organized into two sections. Before I met Dr. Gillath and after I met Dr. Gillath. I would highly recommend taking all the classes he offers!
He's a great guy and a great professor. Does a good job of making lectures interesting, and keeps up with current events. The study guide is a good indicator of what is on the test.

Professor Gillath is great! Lectures are interesting and we had some fun discussion as well. There is A LOT of information presented in lecture, but he posts PowerPoints online. The tests are tough but if you do well on the papers and participation, you can still do well. End of semester paper is challenging,  but going to office hours helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Gillath is very engaging, and his enthusiasm for social psychology came out in his lectures. I didn't interact with him much outside of going to lecture, but the few times I did he was very kind and helpful.  Lots and lots of papers, but they're very short and easy. Study guides before each test make clear what you need to know.

Prof. Gillath is really an inspirational speaker, he made me think on many things that otherwise taken for granted. You can see that he invest a lot of time preparing his classes and while not easy he want his students to succeed and help them as much as he can

Dr. Gillath is great at explaining things and he is quite helpful. This is a challenging course, and students are meant to figure things out on their own, so the guidance Dr. Gillath offers is limited for good reason. There is only so much he can do to help students create their own research study.

Prof Gillath was really engaging and loved discussing with students. The media materials he showed in class were really interesting and helped me understand. Not an easy class but you will LEARN A LOT at the end. The exams weren't that hard, as long as you really read the book. One of the best classes I've taken and he was an amazing teacher!!

You will be doing a lot of work in this class. You have to write weekly papers (They are only 2 pages though) and read long chapters and take quizzes every week. It's an interesting class though. I worked hard and barely managed an A, (even then he had to bump it up) Nice guy though.
funny
great
Boring and hard to understand.

Dr. Gillath's accent can be a little hard to understand, but you get used to it. He tries to scare you the first day that his class will be incredibly hard, but it wasn't terrible. Reading the material and paying attention is very necessary in this class. The projects/assignments he gives you prepare you well for higher level classes and grad schoo

His accent is sometimes hard to understand.  Overall he is very passionate about the material but sometimes tends to get off on tangents.  My TA for his class was useless and didn't care about her students.
His accent is a little hard to understand but he's a really cool guy and very helpful if you ask him for it.

This class is interesting and challenging. An A is not handed to you, but is achievable and you can get plenty of help. Most of what is covered on tests is out of the book. 1 to 2 pg. papers are due throughout the semester and a final paper is due at the end over an experiment that you create and test yourself. Great for hands on learners.
He is great teacher, very interesting classes. Very good sense of humor.I would highly reccomend this class with this teacher I learned so much

After having him for the second time, I've had a change of heart. I ended with an A, but had to work for it. Not out of difficulty, but a lack of clarity/demands. He lectures on random, then has the TA make the test (lazy?). Also, his focus is not as interesting to everyone as he thinks it is.

I ended up with a B in the class.  His lectures aren't very interesting, and to be honest I skipped probably 1/4 of them.  Obviously, attendance isn't mandatory - but you do have to go occasionally to keep up somewhat. My lab section prof was a fool and had no clue.  Quizzes are given each time in the lab section.  1 essay req, but wasn't too bad.

I loved his class. Yes, his tests are hard.  You basically will need to know everything from lecture and the entire chapters from the book.  But honestly, there hasnt been a class I learned more from.  I would recommend him.  You can get an A.
He's great. Best Professor ever. Both funny and interesting.

If I had it over I would choose a different professor. He is a very nice man, his lectures dont put you to sleep and he has a sense of humor. However, tests were all over the place and lectures could have been more to the point and clear. I studied the text - and lecture notes - and some of the questions still seemed to be pulled from nowhere.

He is certainly not an easy teacher, but not unfair or a harsh grader.  He goes a little too fast.  His accent isnt hard to understand. But he does have a good sense of humor and the class is rather interesting.
No Comments
No Comments

Prof. Gaston is very knowledgeable in journalism, but her Canvas page is very unorganized with no labeled due dates, so it can be difficult to keep track of assignments. Also, had many interactions where she did not admit fault or take out her bad mood on the students. She is very smart and accredited, but a difficult professor to have.
She frequently raises her voice at students as a form of discipline. I would recommend a different professor if you're taking 304.

I would honestly try and get a different professor if you can. Due dates are extremely unclear and there is no way she will ever let you turn in something late, like an assignment you've never heard of because the assignments don't show up on your canvas, unless you're house is literally on fire or something and even then she probably wouldn't.

I had her at 8am & would never take another one of her classes. Whenever I brought up concerns about canvas navigation she didn't listen. On multiple occasions she raised her voice at the class. College is a professional environment so we should be mindful of how we are speaking to one another. Her classroom environment doesn't not reflect that.

My experience with professor Gaston was not positive, she is incredibly disrespectful professor. She does not offer substantial feedback, and has trouble operating canvas which we use. Details on submission and due dates are also vague and not listed correctly on canvas.
Doesn't put due dates on canvas so make sure you get stuff done.

This has been my least favorite class and lowest grade I've ever gotten. This professor was always is a terrible mood, rude to students who ask question for reassurance, and a really hard grader. She didn't give good feed back on papers instead she just pointed out what you did wrong.

If you have any options for teachers for 304, I highly recommend not selecting Gaston. If you miss any deadline, whether you're experiencing WIFI problems, etc, you will not be allowed to receive credit. Her Canvas is messy. Due dates can sometimes be unclear.

She is a very tough grader, but she has good intentions. She makes students do a news quiz, and she is very very messy in canvas. Structure is awful, but she is helpful 1 on 1. She is an alright teacher, but possibly in the wrong class. She just wants you to succeed, and if you show her you want to succeed then you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: So rude. Yells any chance she gets. Does more yelling at people for where they sit and having there phones out than actual teaching. Is super strict on no technology whatsoever, making it hard to take notes.

I have mixed feelings. Professor Gaston is harsh and unforgiving in her grading at times. She's also very knowledgeable on the journalism industry. I was disappointed in my experience in her class, but I appreciated her honesty.

Her grading isn't clear in any way. She is extremely messy on Canvas and doesn't tell you when something is I the lecture canvas or the lab one. Most classmates made mistakes off of her "clarifications" that she would double back on and say she never said anything.

She expects students to have previous knowledge of the material learned. Tough grader but with good intentions. Makes students do a news quiz that takes up most of the lab time. Students were barely assigned anything in the 1st half of the semester and then decided to cram everything in the last 3 weeks. Structure of the class is messy and awful.

I would tell a student touring KU to not come to the J-school solely because of this professor. She is one of the most cruel, mean, and disrespectful professors I have ever had. She regularly yelled at our class, and berated students. She is not understanding if you make any mistake either. This teacher made me cry more than once. Stay far away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Gaston is one of those professors who seems very intimidating at first, but as you get to know her, she's a great professor, and someone great to turn to for career advice.
