Professor Gibbons is great. I had never written Java code in my life before, but he made me love writing code. I highly recommend him.

Professor Gibbons makes the course engaging and enjoyable to attend. Lectures are very casual and very interactive. Not afraid to take class time to explain stuff if people don't understand. Cares about students' success. As long as you do the work and study enough, an A or B should be attainable with him.
Excellent professor.  Attendance is not taken for lecture and he still speaks to a packed room almost every time.
Great class
Best professor I've ever had in college

Prof. Gibbons does a good job of making introductory programming (Java) easy to understand.  If you have any prior programming experience this class should be a breeze.  Most of your grade comes from labs, though there are a few written tests.  We never used the textbook at all, don't bother wasting the money on it.

The class was taught lazily and could be so much better. Steve is nice, but just too much. He doesn't believe in global warming/climate change due to humans as an issue, which is very concerning for his field. Memorize the material; you don't really have to understand it, but it's easier and more interesting if you do. The class grade is 90% exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not be fooled by first impressions. Steve is a world-class scientist and a genuine person. His lectures are content heavy and not the best organized. He lectures fairly quickly. Ask questions! His logical approach to the scientific method is second to none. If you value your education, I would not pass up the opportunity to learn from Steve.

I am a pretty solid test taker but this guy gives exams that are 80 questions of super detailed questions after not giving you a study guide. I get it for classes that are harder this was a geology elective. I grew a kid that loved paleontology and he has ruined the subject for me. Most boring lectures of all time. Not a bad guy though just L prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Does not post slides or review material, only hands them out in class. Lectures past the end of class every time, and then gives a quiz on top of that. Exams are long, covering a ton of material with no guidance on what to study. He basically just reads from the slides, and rarely gives any info about what to actually know. Exams have about 70 q's

Okay, let's cut to the chase: Steve acts like a "cool" guy and as someone who is your friend but he really isn't. He is way more concerned with crude jokes than doing his job, which consists of some of the most boring lectures I've ever had to sit through. His office hours aren't helpful either. Overall not good. Definitely avoid him if you can.

Beware, his notes make absolutely no sense and are pretty much useless for study purposes. He will claim his notes ARE the study guide and that you don't need one. Will lecture past the time class is supposed to be over and then will give you a quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great Professor

He is a really good professor who knows his stuff. I had him first semester and I liked his class so much I declared my geology major and he is my adviser. Don't miss class, getting caught up in notes is harder than you think. Don't be afraid to go to his office hours! He is very helpful if you come with questions!!

This was actually the first class that I walked into at KU. It was a little bit intimidating at first, however when your professor wears a fanny pack, skin tight jeans, a hawaiian shirt and boots everyday it becomes more lax. He jumps up on the chalk board to continue writing down notes and is failry funny. Main thing is go to class!

Expects quite a bit of memorizing as well as a bit of reading before class. Knew his stuff very well and made it clear what the concepts were. He did seem a tad touchy and had some biased comments at times, but did a good job overall.

This class is taught like everyone is going to pursue a career in geology. He thinks he's hilarious but his jokes are kind of offensive. A lot of them at the expense of girls. And if you are a girl you will be touched. He's very touchy feely.
No Comments

this guy is crazy!! he is one of those teachers who keeps u past the end of the class everyday, gives a 5 point quiz everyday that has been impossible lately, and makes u take notes after you take a test in the same day.  This guy is ridiculous and unless you plan on becoming a geology major stay away!!
His teaching is distracting. He's rather obnoxious and way too touchy feely. Don't take this class if you plan to participate, cause he'll rub your back while you do. And he obsessed with Al Gore.

All notes given in class are read directly off of a powerpoint slide. Little is done to help understand common trends. Instead equal emphases is placed on everything leaving you to sort things out. He is a funny guy and tries to make class fun, however, he expects you to memorize the book in order to get a good grade.

Hasiotis is a good Prof. This is not a good class to take if you plan on missing it, you will miss about 400 million years worth of notes...take the class and you will understand what I mean.  Only bad thing is one of his TA's is a wannabe, he takes every advantage when prof. leaves town.  he doesnt give good notes, says its all in the book. Idiot.

Super nice guy, learns most of the names of people in the class, his tests are just as they should be... they cover the material you SHOULD know, if you dont study you wont do well, if you do study you'll get a great grade. Way energetic and even jumps up on the chalk board. He is the best Geol teacher at the school so take his class!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Awesome professor. Makes Geology far more interesting and gives notes at a fair pace. very involved with the large class and learns almost everyone's names. Provides review sessions for every test so that the material is clear and is extremely knowledgable and recognized in his field. go to class, take notes, go to reviews, and you're money.
No Comments

Ah Steve. What an odd guy. NOT a bad professor. Jokes bad. But it's cool. And I do like that he learns everybody's names in a huge class. He has been gone for a while though. Good guy, very helpful. Good ol' Steve. I hate geology, but he is very helpful.  GO TO CLASS. GO TO REVIEW SESSIONS. If you don't go to class, you're screwed.
He is not a good professor, he has been out of town for a month, I do not recommend him, he is also unfair in his grading procedures of tests.
No Comments
No Comments

He is SO wonderful. If you come to class and take notes every day, the tests aren't too terrible, but you do have to study for them.  The in-class notes are what the whole course is about.  He tells you you have to read the book, but you really don't.  Don't bother buying it.
Very nice guy -- make sure you study for tests though!

great guy, made a large class seem a lot smaller by learning a lot of names, engaging students, walking around the room, and telling great stories.  really enthusiastic and loves what he does.  also says 'bless you' when any of the 300 students sneezes... which is the only thing that gets annoying.
Tries very hard to get you included in the material. He's a good guy and is always willing to help.
Does 20 clickers within 5 minutes just for it to not have points. Do not take this class if you don't need it.
Dr. Deboer is awesome. Loved him. His tests were slightly hard but if you just put the time in to study and listen in class it is an easy A.

I hate to say it but he needs to retire. He is very boring and lectures are unengaging. That being said, the class is easy. tests are straight memorization from the slides which are posted. Class is 80% exams, but you get a drop exam. Also posts highlight slides, and practice exams. he sets you up for sucess, just a boring guy.

He is a very knowledgeable and kind person. His soft voice sometimes puts me to sleep. There's a lot to memorize for each exam and they're heavily weighted. Come to class even if you don't think you learn anything. You retain more than you think. Focus on the highlight slides, especially the pictures. I recommend using active recall to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: literally worst class I have ever taken. SO hard for no reason...he posts like a million slides for each exam but the slides look like an alzheimers patient made them, hard to understand. very in depth exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is 80% exam-based, with 3 regular exams (one gets dropped at semester end) and a cumulative final. The lectures are incredibly boring, and the tests are relatively hard, but his iClickers worked anywhere, so attendance wasn't mandatory, and the tests are mostly memorization. If you study hard, it won't be too hard to get an A.

DeBoer is very well versed and knowledgeable in physiology. His lecture slides are very well formatted, however, get ready to read a lot of the textbook. The lecture material can be very dense at times and there is a lot of information to retain in the 75 minute period. Tests are fairly difficult at times.

He's knowledgable, passionate about phys, puts effort into the slides and seems like a nice person. However the lectures are very dense and I could never pay attention the full 75 minutes. This class is lots of content/requires lots of time working/studying/effort to stay engaged in class- but it's not the worst and some content was interesting.

The course was an extremely interesting topic and DeBoer is definitely well-educated. However, the structure of the class makes it difficult to be successful. Exams were worth 90% of grade and 10% was iClicker. There were only lectures; no homework, no quizzes. I was eager to learn the content going into the course but structure made it difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor's notes make no sense and have little information on them. He gives over 200 slides to go through for exams that are unhelpful. The exams are very hard, coming from someone that studies over a week for them. He is glosses over important topics without thoroughly explaining them. He is also super boring and not engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Run! His exams are worth 80% of the grade and the questions are NOT over the things you go over in class. He is accessible outside of class, just be prepared to work HARD to pass.

Lectures were pointless and monotone, he would teach things in class that would make absolutely no sense and then they wouldn't be on the exam. There were 5 exams worth 80% of your grade so nothing else really mattered. you were better off skipping class and just reading straight from the textbook because the lectures make you fall asleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Final grade for course is 80% exams, the homework assignments don't prepare you for exams. 80% of the class has a C or lower, and during lecture he moves way too fast to even begin to try and take notes. He often has different slides than we have access to. His exam questions are ambiguous and confusing. Don't take this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not only is his class graded exclusively by exams, but his exams feature content that was not taught in class. Before the first exam which I just got back from, he asked "did I teach you guys the nernst equation? because its on the exam." He doesn't have a grasp on what he teaches and how his class is run, and his lectures are so tedious and boring

I had DeBoer for both a seminar and comparative animal physiology. The seminar was extremely easy. However, comparative phys grade was based entirely on 4 exams with around 2 points of extra credit per exam. Inherently hard to do well in the class. Exams were fairly hard. Final was partially cumulative, but entirely reused previous exam questions.

Dr. DeBoer is an excellent professor. Physiology is a tough subject which requires a great deal of studying to master. If you attend class, focus on class materials & notes, you will succeed. He is a good orator & didactics were very interesting. DeBoer is also extremely accommodating to students (e.g., alt exam dates, office hrs, TA linkage).

With how difficult tests are and how much they are weighted this should be a 400+ level course. At some schools it transfers as a 500 level. Lectures are uninteresting. I didn't learn physiology, just memorized random facts for exams. Much of the material he tests on he entirely skips because, "You should have learned this in a previous class."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the easiest senior seminar to take. The guy is an absolute G. We are having a pizza party for the last class and he bought the pizza for us. His grading is so cake if you put in some effort into writing the summaries.

DeBoer is very sweet but his lectures WILL put you to sleep. 4 tests make up 80% of your grade & they are not easy nor does he curve it. Provides a LOT of material making it difficult to prepare for such short, random exams. You need to know pre-requisite courses very thoroughly in order to keep up. Does allow makeup exams.

This class was brutal. The content was not too advanced, but Dr. DeBoer was so condescending. A unit exam went poorly for the class and he told us to withdraw if we failed. Lectures are prolonged and monotone. Attendance is taken through iClicker but is not required. I wish he was more engaging and kinder.

This rating doesnt reflect him as a person, hes very nice and responds to emails quickly! The class is 80% exams and 20% McGraw Hill Connect. If youre good at exams, this is the class for you. If not, take this class online.

A good professor with an interesting curriculum. Grades are very test heavy with little room for mistakes. Homework is graded on completion, not accuracy, so use them as an opportunity to test your knowledge rather than looking up the answers. Beware, his cadence could put you to sleep but he's more than happy to be asked questions and is very kind

Professor DeBoer is very test heavy with 80% weighted on exams and 20% on homework. He spends all of class time lecturing and is very monotone with his presentations. He responds very quickly to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He cares a lot about his students and the class. To his own avail, the course material is quite boring (in my opinion). Hard to stay engaged with the course, though pre-recorded lectures made it easy to go back if you missed anything. He is not a bad professor by any means, and I recommend him.

I had a great experience with Dr. de Boer. Not only did I enjoy his lectures, in my experience, he was very accessible outside of class (contrary to some other reviews here) and I thought he really cared about me as a student. I would definitely take this class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. DeBoer is accomplished and respected in his field, but his lectures are slow and his tests do not always cover what you expect them to cover. He is incredibly test-heavy and no tests are dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I didn't really get to know Dr. DeBoer because he got sick in the last half of the semester and stopped posting lectures. But from what I did have, he was pretty standard. Pre-recorded lectures that went over slides, homework from the textbook, and a unit exam after 2-4 weeks of lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: tests are 70% of grade, final is not cumulative, tests pretty straight forward

This professor lectured nonstop every single day in the most boring way possible. The average grade on tests in this class was a 65% and he saw no problem with this. He doesn't drop tests, homework assignments, clicker points or anything. He doesn't curve the tests or care how students are doing in the class. Oh and don't bother emailing him.

Tests determine most of your grade, 70%. My class averged 72% on each test. Online homework assigned randomly. A lot of his tests come from the online book, if you want to get an A, you have to read the online book. CQs just for participation, every day in class, 10% of final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor deBoer is a very smart guy but overall this class was one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. It is nothing but notes that fill up an entire slide. He gives out exam samples laid out exactly like the exam but it is not similar to the test in general. I highly recommend you taking that class somewhere else.

His voice is very monotone and it is difficult to stay awake. He tends to ramble and I ended up having to teach myself all the information. The slides are packed with information and there are a lot of them. They are hard to read and grasp all the information. He goes too fast for the average note taker.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a good teacher but don't take him in the summer you will be learning two chapters a day.
His accent is very hard to understand. He tends to ramble on about stuff that won't be on any exam or quiz- annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: he was horrible and went way too fast.
Difficult to understand the lectures, goes through material WAY too quickly, very vague and tricky with question wording
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super boring lecture, could learn better from my dorm room

deBoer's lectures go very fast it is hard to keep up with notes. He will read directly off of the slides and when he posts them online he only posts half of the slides he goes through so you have to be there or read the book to know whats going on. He is a hard teacher to sit and listen to his lecture he isn't helpful at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: deBoer has a hard time in lecture. He reads off the (many) slides and nothing else. He will help you if you go in to talk to him, but there's just SO much information. He really likes to include pictures of cute animals on some slides though. I also had him for my senior seminar, and he's a pretty funny and approachable guy in a smaller setting.
got an A by 0.2%, class is very hard and was where i spent the majority of my time in my 15 credit semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: deBoer is extremely boring and montoned. All he does is read off his slides which are so jammed packed with information it's impossible to actually retain anything. Do not try to read the textbook either, it is even more dense then the slides. This class is just based off of test files from previous years because the professor uses old exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Just as his name sounds, DeBoer is very boring. Could hardly pay attention in class because he reads word for word off his slides. Only go for clicker questions, worth 10% of your grade. Tests are hard, 80% of your grade, with 3 exams and final. He is a good teacher and knows his stuff but he is boring. Study hard and ahead of time.

de Boer-ing.  The only reason to go to his lecture is to get clicker points.  This guy literally just reads off of the slides, which there are LITERALLY thousands of for each exam, and the information doesn't even help you in studying.  Best advice is to get your hands on some test files and hope for the best.

If you can avoid it, do not take one of his classes.  He literally reads all the slides word for word, talks in the most monotone voice and puts half the class to sleep.   The only reason for showing up is participation points.  Just study on your own time when the highlight slides come out.  Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was an alright class, however it isn't easy. After the first test I saw the number of students in lecture drop by a noticeable amount. This class covers a lot of material, but I will say that it does help as a basis if you take anatomy or physiology in the coming semesters. It's not too terribly hard to get a good grade.

In lectures, the professor speaks in a monotone voice and reads slides verbatim. Exams are impossible- anything in the 300+ slides, (or 6 chapters), could be tested. I could barely even finish reading the questions in the 50 minutes given. I tried to speak to him about it but he was short and condescending. This professor  not very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests can be difficult but PLEASE just show up to class and ask for help when needed. Exams are taken in two parts. Part one you take it by yourself and that accounts for 80% of your grade, part two you take the exact same test but with other people, and that accounts for 20% of your grade. He really wants you to learn and he is passionate

He tried to explain things but the lectures never matched up to what we read in the book. Try to get the test files for the class because if you don't you'll have no idea what's happening on the test.
Long, boring lectures.  Required to be there for participation points, but the lectures are basically useless.

Gerrit De Boer & Brad Williamson taught this class. They tried their best to go over the material in a semi-decent way, but it helped more to actually read the book. They expect you to devote your life to studying for what's supposed to be a basic biology class for NON-majors. I hate science and that will never change. This class sucked. Boring.
Be prepared for last minute assignments! And not short ones either, really, really long ones...

I was required to take the class but he is hard to understand (has accent) and gets off topic easy. Show up to class because the participation points add up (yes you participate in an 800 person lecture).
He is really boring to listen to

All he does is read from the slides word for word. Too much information on the slides to get anything from them. Lecture is utterly useless. Very boring and dry. By the end of the semester roughly 80% of people stopped going to lecture. What does that say?
One of the best professors I've had. Really makes physiology something that ANYONE can learn. The tests were really easy. I got 100% on both, but I did study for a couple hours each night.

Very nice professor, but presents so much information that the tests are really difficult to study for. Also can be a bit boring, as he just reads the slides word for word. Start studying for tests really early for your best shot at a good grade.

Legitimately stands there and reads his slides verbatim. Tends to overwhelm students with several hundred slides per test, and test questions can be very tricky to decipher. Highlights important sections to learn, but expects that students know everything that he has discussed. Nice guy, but a very boring and difficult teacher.

Not a bad teacher overall. A little dry and boring sometimes, but a nice guy that wants you to pass the class. Gives a little bit of extra credit and only teaches the first half of the course. Do well in his half so you can fail the crazy hard Craig Martin plant half and still be okay!

This professor does not explain the material, reads off the power point slides and clearly gets lost in the explanations. There are only three tests plus the final and no extra credit available. Over 400 slides for each exam, little explanation or relation to the text. Good luck if you have to take the class.

GREATteacher, but he's not easy! It seems like he's crammed an entire semester of material into half a semester, so studying for his exams is a nightmare!! He does offer extra credit quizzes for up to 5 points, and his exams have extra credit since they're so long. He's lenient on grading but his exams cover way too much material, so study early!
De Boer is a great professor.  To me he's a little too easy on his students but I'm not complaining.  He stresses on topics to assure students understand them fully and is just a flat out great guy.
He is a great professor who really knows what he is teaching but strives for you to understand it too! His senior seminar is easily one of the best classes I have taken at KU.

This class requires you to give a presentation, as with any seminar. As long as you understand your topic, rehearse, and don't read straight from the powerpoint class should be a breeze. He's very friendly and willing to help students find their topic and understand their paper. Took this class Fall 09 and got an A.

No text book is needed. He provides everything in his powerpoints. Exams consist of multiple choice, short answer, and diagrams. No curve in the class, but extra credit through quizzes and exams. Great teacher. Took this class in Spring 2009 and got an A.

for 408 great teacher. easy to understand, well prepared powerpoints (provided & text not really needed) tests have no surprises (though sometimes they include minute details from the powerpoints.. but he stresses those). occasionally funny and always engaging. ---- for 420 also a good teacher. provides really interesting articles for discussion
Took his seminar class - chemical communication - very interesting, very nice teacher
I took crazy craig's bio 100 class in fall and De Boer's bio 100 class in summer and went from a D to a B. Enough said.
Teaches a seminar on Chemical Communication.  Very very interesting.  Learned mucho
No Comments

This class not only taught me about unique and engaging applications of microbiology, but it made me better at understanding and reading scientific literature. Dr. Hancock encouraged exciting discussions about weekly topics. Highly recommend taking the honors version!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Dr. Hancock is a great professor who cares about his students. I was in his class for the weekly honors discussion portion of microbiology, so the class was set up differently in that it was mainly made up of group presentations. He was clear from day one about expectations, and the structure of the class is engaging and such a fun environment!

He breaks down everything during lecture but you need a good attention spam. All exam material is from slides but the textbook is helpful. Biweekly quizzes, 4 unit exams. Clicker for accuracy and no discussing during most clicker questions. All exams/quizzes contain multiple answer questions which may have 10 answer choices total.

One of, if not the coolest courses at KU if you're interested in medicine. This class uses what you learned in bacterial genetics, immunology, and fundamentals. With that, I'd recommend taking Immunology first to make the first two exams easier. Dr. Hancock is a fantastic professor who is passionate and knowledgeable in equal measure. Use Anki.

If you are really good at memorizing a lot of details and regurgitating them on exams, then this class will not be very difficult. All his exams and quizzes pull random details solely from all his slides. I never really used his study guides or read the textbook. You need to use his flashcards more than anything else. He also replies fast to emails
His exams are tough. Study a lot and work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hancock is a very good professor. This is a tough class, but he provides every resource that you need in order to succeed. He is very accessible outside of class to answer any questions about material. Almost all information that is needed for you to learn is provided in either the lecture readings or the posted lectures. It is clear he cares.

Professor Hancock wants all of his students to succeed. This is a tough class that will require you to make it a priority, but it is very interesting! There is a surplus of information in the class, but everything that you need to study he provides in his lectures and lecture readings. He is super accessible outside of class to answer any questions

Others claim that he does not teach well, but every thing that is on quizzes and exams is somewhere in both his lecture powerpoints and provided study guides. Very kind. Quizzes and exams had multiple answer formats which helped a lot because it allowed for partial credit. Will get the grade you want, but takes more studying than most classes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't know why other reviews say he tests over material he doesn't teach, he provides a study guide with exact concepts that are on quizzes and exams. Have to put in the work to pass with grade you want. Adds humor to lectures and funny ways to remember some stuff. Quizzes are very specific and exam 4 is extremely content heavy. Great professor

I am not a microbiology major, but thought this sounded like a class that I would enjoy. He does not explain material well, he puts material that was not discussed in lecture on exams and quizzes, and is extremely nit-picky and chooses small details to test over. I am a senior with a 4.0 prior to this class - DO NOT TAKE IF YOU CAN AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class sounded like it would be interesting and not too difficult. It has been the complete opposite. I am a microbiology major and really struggled with this class. I did not struggle with any of my other micro classes as much as I have with BIOL 506. He does not lecture or explain material well. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DO NOT HAVE TO!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was very excited for this class because of my microbiology class however he has made this class absolutely AWFUL. He tests and quizzes over topics that he does not go over in class and does not tell you to look at in the textbook. The lectures are EXTREMELY boring and he does not explain the information well at all. DO NOT RECOMMEND!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Get ready to be thrown a lot of information in a short amount of time. Test heavy and geared towards those going to medical school so if you are on a Pre-med track and already amazing at memorization, you'll succeed. If not well change your major like I did.

He throws every detail you would need to know about Bacterial Diseases into one three credit hour semester course. If you remembered everything he taught you in this class then you could go straight to work as a doctor diagnosing/treating infections, but you won't. Massive servings of information up to immediately before the test. good luck.

He is a very informed professor, and shares many stories that help the material come alive.  What isn't there to like about bacterial infectious diseases.  From Staph to C. diff and the myriad of microbes in between.  Be prepared to study a lot for this class

Took Biol. 506 Pathogenic Microbiology with him. I'm a pretty good student and a Microbiology major. This class had few points, tests were hard and nit-picky out of a million slides. He did not do well to prepare you or tell you what to expect for the tests either. One of my least favorite biology classes.
I really enjoyed taking this class with Dr. Hancock. He made the class very interesting and I benefited a lot from this class. Overall it was a great experience for me.
Unresponsive to emails, numerous grammatical errors in reading materials/lectures, a lot of which were nearly incomprehensible. I'm sure this prof is fine when he isn't directing an online class.

Dr. Hannoum is truly an inspirational scholar. He is a true expert in the field. When you take his class you will certainly learn a lot. his lectures are extremely rewarding.  If  you to  do the work, keep an open communication  and attend classes you would be able to achieve a good grade . Very happy I attended his class Anth. of violence.

Mandatory attendance. Lectures felt thin, extended by often already-told stories/rambles. So kinda boring and basic. I figure he's a smart guy and probably fine professor but it was more just an easy major-required class. Not much work -- 4 essays (low expectations), attendance, and 1 class presentation. Only got final grade, no specifics.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE A CLASS FROM HIM!! His grading scale is awful such as a 74% is a D in his eyes. A lot of reading every week but they are mostly articles he found on the internet that only cover a little bit of what we are coving for the week. Doesn't seem to care about his students and gives no helpful feedback. A final paper worth 30% of your grade.

Do not EVER take an online class from him. Worst class I have ever taken. He is completely incompetent: deadlines are different everywhere you look, grammatical errors are so bad that some test questions are unanswerable, the final paper has only the vaguest instructions, and he doesn't care how good your answers are, just how much you typed.
Easy class. Lecture heavy. Boring.

He consistently would make us do a reading, give us a pop quiz on it, and then spend the other 60+ minutes to restate everything that was in the reading we did. He would rarely add any useful information for us. When taking his test, my answer described exactly what he wanted but with different words and I got no points. He grades very harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr.Hannoum is very interesting professor, and has a unique and engaging teaching style.  If you attend class and listen, you gain an enormous amount of knowledge.  He also shares personal stories to make the course content come to life.

I have taken 2 courses with this professor, one was ANTH 372 and the other was ANTH 484. I took these courses just to fill requirements, but little to my knowledge these courses were life changing. This professor isn't like the other professors at KU, he actually cares about his students gaining an insight and becoming more aware of other cultures.

This class is literally the easiest thing IN THE WORLD. If you want to take an easy religion class, take this one. I was a little mad because he puts his opinion in the majority of the lectures which is not cool being as it should be a factual class but you'll get an A. He's a nice guy but he doesn't post grades the entire semester...

Loved his class. He gives really interesting lectures, and he's pretty funny. Class will be easy for you if you go to class and take notes every day. I didn't do most of the readings, but the lectures are very informative.

I LOVED ABSC 160 with Isaac, he is so nice!! The class is lecture-heavy, but Isaac makes the lectures fun, and you get out of class early often. The homework is signature assignments, which aren't too difficult, online activities in the textbook, and just tests. If you study a good amount and understand the concepts of the class, you will do fine.

Easy class, but is actually fun to be in. The exams are 50 questions but genuinely if you just listen to him in class, studying shouldn't consume your life for this class. Highly recommend if you need an ABSC class for your degree.

This class is my favorite class so far in college. Dr. Melanson knows what he is talking about and wants people to understand and do well on tests.  There are required activities in the online readings, but he goes over the reading in class. Overall, this class is great, and the professor is wonderful at his job.

He is so fun and makes lectures not boring. Very understanding of situations and is always willing to work with you. He wants you to succeed and you can tell he is very passionate. You do have to buy a textbook online, but if you read and listen to lectures you'll do just fine!

Worst professor I have had at KU. Doesn't give any study guide for midterms or final exam, laughs at you in class for not answering a question correctly, and is clearly only here for his research. The TA does more than him and he's been late to class multiple times.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class with Dr. Crossfield to get out of my comfort zone. This was supposed to be an easy 1 credit hour seminar. But the readings were very hard for me to understand and engage with. I spent more time on this class than many of my actual 3 credit hour classes. If science/astronomy is your thing, then you'll do great, just not for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very good. He made an incredible joke at the end of the year about the Middle East. Grading is very generous with regrades possible. Do the readings and ask questions for the homework and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good professor can be a bit scary at first with the amount of options but if you like learning and prepared to work an extra mile he is a good teacher.

He is very kind, approachable, and eager to answer questions. He is very professional, so make sure to show up to lectures and speak respectfully. Deadlines are very clear and the homework is somewhat more challenging compared to other STEM classes at this level, but you have ample time and you are encouraged to complete it with other students.

LOVE his lectures, they're entertaining, straightforward, and include plenty of visuals of content. Highly encourages questions, and makes time to meet students outside of office hours if needed. Also allows corrections on anything for 70% credit back of points missed. Work in groups for psets, it helps!! Put in the work and you're golden :)
She never listened to my accent and make me reapeat myself. Bad at answering my question and never respond by email.
I did really well in this course however I feel like it was because overall Calculus gives a lot of help and review for you to do well. His teaching style is good and he is a fun person.

Dr. Indika was such an amazing professor. This course ended up being one of my classes and professors. He does a really nice job about explaining things along with tips and tricks to succeed in this course. He is also very personable and easily approachable to ask questions. There is lots of extra credit opportunity that will raise your grade.
The best Professor Ive had in such a long time. Gives so much extra credit, truly cares about his students. Puts so much effort in making his students be successful.
Very knowledgeable and explains things very well. Sometimes he focuses too much on proofs and doesn't have many office hours, but otherwise he's a great professor.
Great teacher, hard class.
he is good but sometimes difficult to understand the way he teaches

This was online Calc 115, in the summer. Class is manageable as long as you stay on top of assignments. Graded by 2 tests worth 40% of your grade (proctored on zoom). Tests are very similar to practice. Written Hw and Online Hw makes up the other 60%, and I ended up with over 6% extra credit from the written and online hw. Better than in person!

I enjoyed having Indika as a professor! He was great at explaining the material and paced his lectures well. On occasion I found him hard to understand, but he always responded to any questions respectfully. MATH 126 can be a tough class, so it is important to attend the lectures and do the work to make sure you understand the course concepts.

Dr. Indika was such a delight to have. The only thing I didn't love was how fast he had to go through content, but that was not his fault. There was just a lot to teach in very little time. He was amazingly clear in his instruction incredibly kind, willing to talk with you after class. I highly recommend you take this class with him! Such a joy!

Dr. Indika's takes a notoriously hard class and makes it a pleasure to take. You can tell that they love teaching everything math-related, and you tell from their lectures. The class has the homework structure of MATH 125, and studying for difficult midterms is necessary if you don't want to miss 60% of your grade. Great class, strongly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Indika's lectures are clear and easy to understand. He makes a very difficult class very manageable. The class has a lot of work, but its no different than MATH 125 in that regard. His lectures were great and I would absolutely recommend.
I had no issues with this class. The lectures were easy to understand and the professor will go over most notes that you did on your own. I would recommend Professor Indika.
Honestly, this math class was extremely easy and I could've easily gotten an A if I had put in a bit more effort. Avantha is an understanding professor and did well at teaching the lessons.

PLEASE consider taking this class at a CC instead of KU. Avantha is barely involved in this class. All he does is post one thing per week on the CANVAS, nothing else.  TAs are the ones teaching 95% of the time and have no clue what they are doing. Prepare to teach yourself all the content. No retakes on exams. KU math department, DO BETTER.

There are absolutely no retakes on any exams, he also has thousands of students and therefore doesn't like too much work being graded, you're graded in 5 exams. He has graduate teachers, some who are accent heavy and aren't qualified to teach, This professor has no time wahstover to email people about their failing grades and doesn't care at ALL.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Math has always been really rard for me and I was dreading Calc 2 because it is infamous for being the hardest Calc class by far. It was hard, don't get me wrong, but Dr. Indika's enthusiasm for the subject and care for his students helped me stay engaged in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Indika really wants his students to succeed and is a no tricks or surprises kind of professor. The way he presents and teaches the material makes the class easier. The tests were technically difficult, but the many resources he gave made them seem easy. As long as you study and keep up with the lectures, this class should be an easy 'A'.

This guy is a solid choice if you're going to be taking calc 2. Very lenient and understanding with deadlines for homework, and he cares about your success if you put in the effort. Just be on your A game, calc 2 covers a lot of topics that aren't necessarily difficult, but have very little relation to one another. *cough* sequences/series *cough*

I loved Dr. Indika for Calc 2! He does have an accent, but is super easy to understand. The class is very test heavy with lots of homework, but as long as you do it and show up to class you'll be ok. Dr. Indika is a really great lecturer that answers questions well in class. Would definitely take one of his classes again!
Expected to do the work but lenient with grading.
Assignments are fairly simple 1- pagers about the class material. Something a lot of people were upset by that wasn't a huge deal to me is the 6pm due dates.

Not a good professor. Extremely hard grader and I've had an A an English up until this year. Assigns all homework at 6:00pm rather than 11:59. Doesn't take into consideration that some people have jobs outside of school. The deadlines are horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Ellis was fantastic. Yes, he is a tough grader, but he will give you twice what you put in. Show effort and he'll ensure you have what you need to succeed. I wrote some of my best papers in this class because I knew I couldn't get away with slacking. Anyone who tells you he's too harsh a grader simply did not put in the required effort.

I think I am a great writer, but I have not received an A on a single writing assignment in this class. I am taking critical writing and spend 5 hours at LEAST a week on his assignments. I have improved, redone multiple, and still have not received a fair grade. I Have never reviewed below a B in an English class. Not A fan.

A great introduction to college english. An incredibly easy grader, and cares about your wellbeing. Doesn't make you come to class during paper writing, which helps. Most of the class "work" is just talking, which is much easier than actually having to do work. Incredibly engaging, and loved getting to talk to him.

he is quite rude. more so passive-aggressive. he makes assignments due at 6pm which would be hard if someone is very busy with work, school, clubs, etc. my class has 11 people in it or less. he makes you talk in small groups to discuss projects/assignments. a tough grader who has points out of random numbers instead of 100.

Dr. Ellis was the first college professor I encountered and set the bar really high. His lectures were mixed with student participation which helped me develop ideas for the few essays we had. Homework is about average and there's no tests/exams. Dr. Ellis always had a positive attitude and helped me a lot during the writing process.
Not a bad dude, just very narrow-minded about certain things. If you skip this class, you will fail

He was alright. I could've achieved an A in this class if it weren't for every assignment due at 6 pm, rather than the standard 11:59 pm. Not every student has the time to make sure things are due at that time, which is my major complaint. Also somewhat of a tough grader, and standoff-ish when students approach with questions in person. Good luck!

Personally, this is my least favorite class I've taken. There isn't much room for your error with Dr. Ellis. If you miss class it WILL count against you, and he's never been one to be super forgiving. My class had no more than 15 people in it, but I didn't get to know anyone because he talked at us the entire time. I almost dropped this class.

Professor Ellis was, by far, my favorite professor this semester. He has high expectations for his students, but also goes out of his way to help you meet those. There are a lot of in class discussions, but they are very informal and stress free. It is very important to complete the homework assignments in order to participate.

This class is focused on in-class discussions, so get ready for those. Dr. Ellis tries his best to make the class enjoyable by using music and film material and readings, so the class is not too boring if you are into that.

Very careful teaching students to write a good academic paper. Although English is not my mother tongue, Professor Ellis was careful and gave me special attention, but he was still very strict with me. It's all very effective. All in all. Professor Ellis is a very knowledgeable professor.

This class is boring. I hated coming to class because I knew he would force me to talk in small groups sitting 6 feet apart from each other. Writing assignments are basic and he grades unnecessarily hard for a 100 level class. Nice guy, just a boring class.

Personally, I loved the class and its format. It's very heavily based on in-class discussion and participation, but he will never force you to talk. He is very old-school regarding the set up of his class. Nearly all assignments needed to be printed out and handed in during class and his Word and Blackboard skills could use some improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Excellent professor. Makes class interesting and engaging. Clear grading criteria and expectations.

He does not consider that you are writing a PAPER in your second language and wants your English as a native ! That's impossible. I had to take the class as it is a required from the ENGR department ..

Definitely one of my favorite professors I've ever had. Even when some of the readings weren't my cup of tea, he made the lectures interesting and made sure you got what you needed from the text. The added impact of movies, music, and discussions about each era really made an impact.

Dr. Ellis is one of my favorite professors I've had during my time at KU. His class is incredibly interesting and the assigned literature is great. There is also a large amount of flexibility in the course. You get to choose what topic you'd like to focus on for every paper. A great class and a really cool guy.

Everything about this class is great other than his grading - he grades this class like it's an upper-level course. It is extremely difficult to get an A, and this is coming from someone with a 3.6 GPA. If you're all about learning, take him. If you value your GPA, take one of the many other professors who teach this basic course.

Iain was so nice. Always available for help, and actually cared about his students. Did not mind going to class at all. Material was not difficult if you went to class, and really touched on contemporary social issues.

Ellis is a great instructor. I never felt that I was graded unfairly in his class, and he was always ready to provide advice and/or criticisms. He knows what he's talking about and even when he disagrees with student opinions, remains respectful. The course isn't that hard if you devote a decent amount of time to it, and do the readings.

I am an engineering major but Professor Ellis is easily my all time favorite professor. He's clear about what he wants, his class (engl 203) is amazingly interesting, he will help you as much as needed to reach his standards, and by the end of the semester there wasn't a single person in my class who wasn't interested in the class.

I love love looove this professor! This class is all about youth rebellion, and includes A LOT of reading, but most of the books you read are pretty good/interesting. I think he is a great teacher, prompts good discussions, and is always willing to help you.     He also has a british accent, so that's cool too haha

Iain is by far my favorite college professor thus far. Very knowledgable and all around great dude. He'll help you out on any assignment. He might come off a bit harsh or condescending at first, but if you make changes according to his evaluations of your assignments, you'll do great! If you take ENGL203, read the novels! They're great stories!

I am an international student and i thought the teacher will be graded on my writing lightly, but it isn't! I tried my best to work on my papers and quizzes. He gave me a comment was "Non-English"! When I talked with him on my paper, he laughed on my writing and even my English. Do not take this class,international students! he is a unfair teacher!

Dr. Ellis is an extremely nice person, and a very knowledgeable professor. He is also incredibly interested in what he is teaching, which really shows through his enthusiasm. The class is not an easy A; you really have to work hard on perfecting papers and quizzes for a good grade, but but the end of the class you should have it down pat.
Dr. Ellis has a very narrow minded view of things, and if your essay does not follow his idea you are wrong. The class is easy if you can figure out what the heck he wants.

Iain has been my favorite teacher thus far at KU. before the semester started, I was dreading this class the most because i don't like to read. but he is awesome and this is now my favorite class. i started out earning low C's on papers but now that i understand the grading i haven't gotten anything below a 90%. i'd recommend him to anyone

He really likes the subject he teaches and what's being covered. However, he dislikes considering any other opinions over his own (especially in discussions). He starts out grading easy, so we understand what he expects, but he grades much harder on the last essays. Very candid and tries to make class interesting, but it doesn't work.

Seriously, these ratings do not do Iain justice! He was badass and covered interesting material. Yes, he expects a lot out of you, but if you take his criticism to heart and take good notes, you will be fine. I started off with low Bs and Cs on things and ended up getting all As after taking his notes into consideration! Loved him and this class.

Dr. Iain was incredible! He was cool, covered good material and worked with you! At first I struggled a bit with what he was looking for but if you read his comments and really expand on your ideas in the paper citing specific examples, you are golden. I got a solid A in the class.

Dr. Iain is an amazing professor! The books we read were interesting, and his knowledge of the novels and historical content was incredible. Hard grader at first but once you get the hang of it, he's awesome. Attendance is mandatory, reading the materials is a must and TAKE NOTES!

Started off good in his class. Then all a sudden told me I wasn't at a 102 level and gave me a D on a paper. I went in talked to him an he basically laughed in my face. I think he's rude and not a fair grader.
I had to try really hard to get an A- in this class, I'm sure if I were anywhere else I would have gotten an A+ but he's a cool guy, sense of humor is funny. A lot of reading though.

I took his expressions of youth rebellion class, and I really enjoyed it! I could really feel the different tensions of time periods in the books we read, and our discussions over them made me understand them even better. He values everyone's opinion, and is very good at making you see different aspects of text. He is very tough on papers though!

If you try to aruge you your paper if you get a bad grade, there is no way in hell that you are getting a better grade. If you want to challenge yourself and write and read alot then take his class. The material constists of reading short stories and writing one page papers on them. If you do the work, get A's papers, then you can get an B easy.

Iain Ellis is the most unfair teacher I have ever had. He does not accept other's opinions. If you don't agree with him, then you are wrong. If confronted, he does everything in his power to make you feel worthless. He "teaches" in order to fail students. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS YOU WANT TO FEEL BAD ABOUT YOURSELF AND YOUR WRITING.
He is a pretty good teacher, basically if you read the assigned books you will do fine, he is a very hard grader on papers though

Nice guy, very engaging and he keeps class discussions moving and really helps you learn the material. He grades essays extremely hard, but the class is based on points alone so those who participate come out way ahead. Good course but don't wait till the end on your essays.

Really awesome hip teacher. Readings and class discussions are normally very interesting and entertaining to participate in. When it comes to writing papers hes very clear and makes sure you understand the material and schedules individual meetings with you. Great guy, take his class!
Great guy who does expect you to speak up in class, but it is a non-threatening situation.  Classes are interesting and seem short.  Papers are easy and there aren't too many.  Great and easy class!

He is a great teacher, I fully enjoyed his discussions--he brought a new and innovative approach to the class. He was not terribly hard, put in enough work and he'll love you. If he knows you worked hard and deserved the grade I think he's willing to give you a percent or two boost on your final grade to get you there. He really cares.

i took his class because i looked on this first and everyone said he was awesome and easy..i dunno what they are talking about. he didn't teach anything just gave us more and more assignments and graded papers hard but didn't teach so we didn't know how to get a better grade
Ellis is the man. Wants to hear real opinions and will call you out if your not daring enough. All points are drawn together to a main point that he wraps up at the end.

He is a great professor, makes classes enjoyable and is good at moderating discussions.  Has a good sense of humor which keeps his lectures interesting and engaging.  Also has good taste as far as the readings go. A little demanding on his requirements, but very fair.  All around top-notch and one of my favorite professors that I have had at KU.
He is a great teacher.  He's fairly easy, all you have to do is be clear and articulate.  He really enjoyed listening to what the students had to say.
pretty easy about 4 papers and then just class participation, extra credit for perfect attendence which isnt hard because he cancels classes right and left. and he doesnt grade too hard

I loved his class. He's really into hearing different perspectives and pulling them all together to illustrate a point. Anyway, the key to doing well in his class is speaking articulately and writing very clear papers with no grammatical errors. I can't imagine why anyone would hate him unless they hated public speaking. You do have to work though.
Great teacher, really receptive to student's thoughts and ideas. I highly suggest any class with Ellis, you're guaranteed a great class.

I got a C, I think, and I'd still take the class again.  The subjects you get to discuss are f'ing great but, make no mistake, he expects more than scribbles and grunts from you.  If you're like the kiddies who gave Ellis poor ratings, this isn't for you.  This class is more of an adult swim.

Iain did a fine job. He's lectures were good, although at times his way of managing class discussions was a little heavy handed. This aside, I think I'd recommend his classes. Interesting subject material and a fresh perspective.
No Comments

An interesting paper, but he is very picky when grading papers and won't ever give an A.  He is one of those teachers who will tell you that a C is good, which pisses me off quite a bit.  Avoid if possible.

whoever left the 1's across the board must have been a frat guy.  anyone with a brain respects this teacher because he knows what he's doing.  anyone  who doesn't like him should consider going to class and learning something because this teacher is amazing

He is definitely a step up from the traditional english teacher I am used to having.  I did not learn crap last year and I actually have to be on my toes this time.  He keeps me awake in class and I actually want to do my homework!

So, I've only had him a week, but he seems to have the potential to be the best English teacher I've ever had. He's really interesting and has a good sense of humor. Comes off a little intimidating, but there is no doubt in my mind that I will learn alot

handsdown the best college teacher i've ever had.  incredibly helpful, interesting, and treats everyone with utmost respect.  not only is it a really fun class with an amazing teacher, he also has gil scott-heron and the sex pistols in the curriculum.

I love, love, love Dr. Illardi! I would recommend him so much I took disorders with him this semester and now I am taking personality next semester. Exams are lowkey hard and make up most of your grade so you do have to study but he makes it easy to go to lecture and its always interesting. He also gives a lot of chances for extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ilardi is an absolutely brilliant professor and human. He genuinely cares about his students, and is easy to access outside of class. Attendance isn't required and his lectures are posted after but I highly recommend attending class because exams rely heavily on things said during class. Anything he says, no matter how brief, is fair game

Best prof I've had. Lectures are fun and engaging. All lectures are recorded and posted if you don't want to go to class. Grade is mostly based on exams, but if you go over your notes then you should be fine. Have two papers to write but he gives you more than enough time to complete them. Weekly discussions that are easy too.
Best teacher I have ever had. Highly recommend,

I LOVE Dr. Illardi!!! His classes are amazing. If you do not study for exams, you will not pass the class though. Exams make up pretty much your entire grade. He lets you drop one exam grade which is nice. He brings his super adorable puppy to class also. If you do not go to class you will NOT pass the class. He truly cares about his students.

My all time favorite professor at KU. You can tell he loves being a teacher. His lectures are very engaging and he's very funny and witty. Best lecturer I have come across during my 3.5 years at KU. I have taken every course he offers at KU and cannot recommend him enough.
Amazing

Lectures were always really entertaining which made studying for exams easy. Dr. Illardi is a wonderful person who cares for everyone around him deeply. Aside from the content in the course, he showed me examples of genuine kindness and empathy. Plus, sometimes he brings his dog (Teddy the Wonder Dog) to lectures.
Makes class so fun and interesting. Very good teacher and also in general seems like he cares about you

If you have an opportunity to take a class with Steve, do it. Funny, genuine, super nice guy that truly cares about students. He is not trying to make life harder, he truly wants you to pass and do well in his class. Gives lots of extra credit opportunities. He likes to keep class light and will tell stories when it feels its too lecture heavy.

Dr. Ilardi is the BEST professor I've had in my 3 years at KU. His lectures are interesting and engaging, he sincerely wants students to succeed and the expectations for the class are clear and easy to meet. I did take time with the class (it was an honors course) but nothing overwhelming or impossible - and It was enjoyable so I didn't mind at all

Dr. Ilardi is the kindest human I have ever met. He is beyond helpful and accommodating and most of all just wants to be your friend. I wish he could teach every one of my classes. Prepare well for exams and take in-depth notes in lectures! The more the better!

By far the best professor I have had at KU. His passion for the subject make class so engaging and fun to be in. He is a bit intimidating because of his reputation and name but very funny and really wants to get to know everyone in his class. You take 4 exams throughout the class and can drop one exam grade/not take the final.

Amazing professor. He will stay long during office hours just to speak to everyone there. Take notes during class - everything said aloud is fair game on the test. Tests are hard but if you put in the work it's an easy A. Lots of extra credit opportunities. One major paper with book you need to read. Best psychology professor I've had KU.

He is a great professor but I took psych 120 and there was too high of expectations to be considered a 100 level class. There is a really long paper that is required and is a large portion of your grade. My paper ended up being over 30 pages long and it was graded way harder than expected for 100 level.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He is great! He records his lectures and puts them on blackboards so if you miss a class you can go back and watch it. He is super helpful, and his lectures are entertaining. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and do well in the class. Hands down the best psych professor at KU.
Very easy class if you listen to the lectures. Dr. Illardi is a great speaker and actually can be very funny. Tests are super easy, only one major paper.

He was awesome, he is extremely engaging during lecture and records almost all of his lectures. The text book isn't required because he only tests you on material specifically discussed in class. He was always very inviting to office hours and gives a lot of extra credit opportunity. A pretty long paper is due at the end of semester but its easy
This class was extremely difficult, but Professor Indika is pretty nice. He can be hard to follow at times, but ask questions and he is happy to explain his logic.

PLEASE consider taking this class at a CC instead of KU. Avantha is barely involved in this class. All he does is post one thing per week on the CANVAS, nothing else.  TAs are the ones teaching 95% of the time and have no clue what they are doing. Prepare to teach yourself all the content. No retakes on exams. KU math department, DO BETTER.

His lectures are very clear on what to do and there are lots of opportunities outside of the lectures if you need more help. The quizzes and tests aren't too difficult as long as you know what you're doing.

She seemed like a good person, and was outwardly passionate and animated about the class. She writes little to no plan for lessons and goes by a 4 word slide. She also likes to ramble on things that did not help with the class. I felt as though I was listening to her talk and jump around rather than actually learn about how to give great speeches.

She is such a kind soul!! She really listens to you and your perspective, even if it differs from hers. Its a reading HEAVY class with quizzes like every class and a discussion. She just wants you to think critically. We did a couple of projects. Go to office hours if youre not sure about a project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: She is a good professor but her lectures are very boring. But she is a nice person and extremely knowledgable. She gives great feedback. Oh and don't even think about plagiarizing anything she doesn't tolerate at all. READ the material and you can get at least a "B".
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Quirky enthusiastic teacher Straightforward speeches/writings to read & then rhetorically analyze for in class discussion& participation points almost daily. 2 analysis PPs & 1 short presentation Can be a tough grader at first, but gives great feedback. I learned so much considering I'd never taken a rhet class b4. Taking her next semester for 232!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's fine if you do all the reading, but she expects you to get creative with the most boring of presentation prompts. I had a hard time taking her seriously because she spoke to us like a kindergarten class, not college students. Not recommended for non-COMS majors looking for a gen-ed filler.

This class is a lot of work. Beth is very smart but the format of the class (a lot of discussion) can cause the class to drag a bit. Plan on working hard to get an A. I got a B and put in a lot of effort. Grading is strict. Attendance is required, plus if you miss class you miss  daily quizzes which affects your grade. Study guides give exact quest

Really freakin' intelligent. Be prepared to actually learn in this class. If you are open to it, it can be pretty engaging. She gives many opportunities to get in-class credit (she calls them PEOs). I was stupid and skipped too much. Make sure you read the blackboard/book assignments to get full credit!
No Comments
nice
Knows her material, smart, kind
No Comments
She will give tons of feedback, but is a bit dry at times.
No Comments

Amazing 
I had my doubts going into the class from the other reviews but let me tell you that she is so much better than the reviews. She does an amazing job of explaining things in simple terms and the discussions are usually very very interesting during the lectures. writings are fun & send her drafts to review before the deadline.

I took this class for the core requirement and was so surprised with how much I learned and how interested I became in the topic. Dr. Symons does a great job explaining. She comes off as tough, but she's always ready to help and showed a lot of patience.

While Dr. Symons was knowledge about the topics discussed in class, she could be confusing at times by contradicting herself. You will have pop quizzes but, at least in my case, she lets you use notes. She will also not give much feedback on your tests, quizzes, and essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't get why people say that this is a boring or lecture heavy class. There was more discussion in Phil 161 than in any other classes I took. And she takes all the questions there are, she does not rush to go back to lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Irina rocks!

I would heavily recommend going on her study abroad course it was amazing. Outside of that her classes are fun as long as you do the work and participate. Do be prepared to read and participate and Irina will then appreciate your work.
Awesome class, awesome professor. I'll take all the classes I can with Prof Symons!

Very boring lectures that make no sense, ended up teaching the same thing the same way multiple times. Gets confused/tripped up when asked questions, almost like she doesn't really know what she's teaching. Ended up having to learn from other places on the internet in order to have a shot at the exams.

Dr. Jiang loves math, and its evident just listening to him lecture. He also cares more about what the student learn as opposed to the grade. Dr. Jiang's lectures were not useful about 90% of the time. Most classes he rambled about proofs that didn't make sense. The homework was ok - only 1 assignment per week. He was very unorganized. We created a drinking game in our class groupme whenever Jiang said "Did I make a mistake?", "Who made these slides (He used MATH 126 slides)?", or "I don't want to do that calculation." If you have a great TA or are a natural genius, you'll be fine; otherwise, good luck.

Jiang is an interesting man. Very entertaining. Blows through difficult concepts and spends days going over proofs that should be saved for a 500/600 level course. I recommend this class to anyone interested in personality, even just a little bit! This was my first class with Dr. Ilardi, and he is a very engaging professor throughout his lectures. Really great professor and I really did learn a lot! I just wish he didn't spend as much class time talking about AI because it does not relate to course content. Other than that he's incredibly smart and knows what he's talking about.

Dr. Ilardi is the best teacher I have ever had. He is an amazing storyteller and manages to keep you engaged throughout the class. Although attendance is optional, it is a privilege to hear him speak and learn from him, as well as the fact that all the exams include information from lectures that is not in the notes. He made me motivated to learn!

Honestly, stopped going to class after the first month and just watched lecture recordings on 2x. Content is super interesting, but a lot of lecture feels like a long ramble. Exams were easy and the projects were also simple to complete. Would definitely take classes with Dr. Ilardi again.

Amazing class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but class is exam heavy and includes lots of what he said in the lectures. Lectures are very entertaining and I never got bored. Best professor I have had at KU yet. Highly recommend.

Steve is great. He's a bit of an old man sometimes, but is very respectable. Paying attention to lectures is not only interesting, but needed for the class- but the content wasn't redundant for me and I learned so much. I feel like this is the most applicable/generalizable class i've taken so far for my BNeuro major. You get to drop one exam grade.

Good and funny professor, exams can be difficult with the word banks but multiple choice and true/false portions are easy. Drops lowest exam score with 3 exams being kept. He's very engaging and incorporates stories into lectures. Weekly discussions, writing assignments, and the interview are easy for 40% of your grade. Overall, fun class.
He lectures the whole class but keeps you very locked in. He cares about what he's talking about and posts all lectures online after the course. Very helpful and overall a great guy.

Dr Ilardi is my favorite prof I've ever had at ku. he applies the course material through interesting and funny stories, and I literally enjoyed every minute of his lectures. attendance isn't mandatory but its important. no textbooks but he does a great job of posting videos, outlines, study guides, etc. he grades fairly and tests are reasonable

Dr. Ilardi is easily my favorite professor at KU! His lectures are super engaging and you can tell he is so passionate and intelligent. He also has amazing stories and really cares about students. Professor Ilardi is the perfect professor and I don't say that easily. His lectures are engaging, entertaining, and educational. He is fair minded and clearly passionate about this subject. Professor Ilardi's class is engaging, though the exams can be challenging. Using unstuck ai and taking good notes really helps. He's passionate and cares about students, making this a worthwhile course.

Steve is a wonderful human being. Personally, I feel as if he is the BEST professor at KU. 
4 exams (lowest dropped) 20% of your grade, 14 discussion posts - 15% of your grade, and some other activities not worth that much. You must study for exams, as they are not easy. Literally, just go to class, listen, and you will be fine! Good Luck!

Dr. Ilardi is so awesome!! He is genuinely so nice and cares about his students. The lectures are actually entertaining and he plays music before them. I kinda suck at taking written exams so I thought they were hard but if you take good notes from the lectures and actually study you should be fine. There are also extra credit opportunities.

Doesn't take attendance but anything in lectures is fair game for exam. That said, his lectures are amazing, super informative and he's funny and great at keeping you engaged. Loves to answer student questions, during and well after class is over. Available outside of class. Gives you lots of opportunities to get a good grade if exams went poorly

While attendance isn't required, it's the one class I actually want to show up to. He really keeps the class engaged. I have and would recommend this class to anyone!! The content is so interesting and he cares about all of his students.

steve is truly one of the best professors at KU! if you have the chance to take any of his classes, you absolutely should! dr ilardi is such a brilliant professor but is also actually good at teaching. just by sitting in class you'll learn most of the material without realising it. he is super caring and very fair about exams and credit.
Wonderful, amazing, lovely human being. Please take any class with him. #swag

Dr Ilardi is THE best professor. Lectures are interesting and funny. Exams are easy (MC / TF) with study guides and review sessions. He drops lowest/4 exams. 25% of your grade comes from a paper. Weekly ~150word discussion boards. LOTS OF EXTRA CREDIT OPPORTUNITIES. Attendance is not mandatory (lecture recordings posted on canvas) but GO. Easy A.

This class showed me the bigger picture of life. Dr. Ilardi teaches not only class content, but helps students learn how to step outside of black and white thinking. You will you learn a lot more about psyc and more about yourself as an individual and gain more confidence because of it. He is an inspiration and the most caring professor ever.

He was the most engaging professor I had while at KU. His class is one of the only classes I actually retained what I learned and enjoyed going to. Best professor at KU. You can tell he cares about his students very deeply which is so rare to find. Professor Ilardi is the best instructor I have ever had the pleasure of learning from. He truly cares about the things he teaches about and hilariously expresses the topics to the class. Ilardi is definitely one of the best professors at KU because of his hilariously engaging lectures. I would recommend him to anyone wanting to take this course.

By far my favorite and most inspirational professor so far in my college experience. he is so accessible and makes you want to reach out. Very smart and well respected. If me or anyone I cared about had a mental health issue and needed help, I would follow his advice word for word

Dr. Ilardi is by far the best professor I've had in college. His lectures are interesting and easy to follow. If you miss class he posts all of his lectures online. Easily my favorite professor I've had in college so far. He's an unbelievably engaging speaker and he manages to tie all of his tangents back into the lecture material. He clearly cares about his students too. Honestly? Make an excuse to take one of his classes - you won't regret it, I promise!

Dr. Ilardi is truly the best professor I've had in college. He is so genuine, hilarious, incredibly smart & fascinating. I almost changed my major after taking personality psyc with him. I never missed a lecture b/c I genuinely wanted to go. Take really good notes and you will get an A with flying colors, never got below a 95 on a test. AMAZING!!!!

If you have any chance whatsoever to take one of his classes before you graduate, do yourself the favor and take it.

Dr. Ilardi is probably the best teacher Ive had at any level. First, his lectures are amazing, they actually make you WANT to be there. Somehow he makes a huge lecture hall feel more intimate. Hell even put students on mic and theyll share crazy personal stories in front of hundreds of classmates. Ilardi also cares about students and it shows.

Ilardi gets a lot of good reviews, but I found him condescending. He refers to outdated information, rambles about things that don't pertain to the class, and is self-absorbed. I love this profesor and the class! I truly enjoyed going everyday, and he videotapes the lectures and puts them online so they are accessible from anywhere. Great Professor! Classes are super interesting, and he always held my attention.
