Only problem is that he bell curves essays. Not a lot of points offered in the class but if you pay attention then that doesn't matter
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very good listener and understanding. Grade is affected after so many absences
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Stephen is super unclear about everything and if you ask him a question, he doesn't entirely answer it. You can follow the grading rubric to a tee and get a B every time. He speaks in ambiguities all the time so you never have any idea what he's saying.

Johnson was a nice person in general, but as a professor I wouldn't recommend. I worked extremely hard on all my assignments/essays, showed up to every class, did the readings (which were 100 pages between mon and wed), and participated in discussion, yet I would only receive a mediocre grade. He is EXTREMELY unclear about assignment requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is very engaging and his assignments are original, but he is not entirely clear on the complete requirements and expectations. You could follow and excellently execute all objectives on his grading rubric, yet still receive a mediocre grade. He will make you write a lot, but if you put extra effort in, you can get an A. Participation is a must.
get out of his class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Johnson's class is painfully boring. He selects favorites and seems almost creepily interested in what they have to say. I would suggest taking a 50 minute version of this class rather than an hour and fifteen minutes because it was simply too long to stay engaged.

I actually really enjoyed Johnson as a person. When it came to teaching subject matter though, he seemed bored and not engaged. I know he has been teaching poetry for a while, but the class would have been more interesting if he made it so. The reading and quizzes were tedious and unnecessary in my opinion, but I got an A on all the essays
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a laid back person. He is nice and is willing to help you improve on papers. There's quite a bit of papers I had to write but they weren't that bad. Make sure you attend class so you know what's going on!

He is pretty laid back and class discussions are good but there is a lot of homework, although it isn't difficult. As long as you really read the assignments they are not hard. One thing that really bothered me is that he requires you go to office hours or do extra outside work to get an A for participation, doing all the homework isn't enough.

Extremely unclear about all assignments. I usually love english and writing but I hated everything about this class. If you are dying in the hospital it doesn't even matter because if you skip class you will fail whatever assignment you are working on at the time.

Professor Johnson is a nice, interesting, and very laid back guy. His homework assignments aren't too tedious, and he's good at answering your questions about the writing assignments. He's a very tough grader, however. I consider myself to be an excellent writer, and I would work my butt off only to get B's on some of the papers.

Probably the worst professor and experience that I have had. Extremely hard to get an A, expects you to be a poetry major and excercises his power of authority. Take another professor, this was the most frustrating class, and it's POETRY...

Mr. Johnson is a great English 102 professor. His class is very interesting and he is very connected to his students during class. I typically do not like English classes, but his class kept me interested. The only downside to him is that he does not like to give A's on anything. Other than that, I would recommend him to anyone willing to work hard

The last couple of months he just kind of gave up making a lesson plan and we had to read T.S. Eliot's Wasteland, which nobody in the class was fond of. As somebody who likes poetry, I was not impressed.
I didn't wear a seat belt whilst driving to this class because I'd hoped that I would die in a crash before I actually got to class.
Great professor! Open to ideas and not set in his own opinion of things. Keeps class interesting and isn't a hard ass.

Stephen is an awesome guy. Took 102 with him last semester and truly enjoyed his class. I have him again this semester because he was so good. His classes are fun to go to and lectures are very interesting. He is a very bright person.

Class is not terribly hard, as long as you exceed the requirements given for assignments. He loves if you go see him in office hours. Even if you don't really need to, make something up. Grading is weird. He will give requirements for assignments, but doing the min. will only get you a C.

One of the best professor's I've had. If you participate in group discussion, go to his office hours, and complete all assignments this class is an easy A. He doesn't look for perfect papers, just improvement's in the student's own personal writing. Great guy.

Stephen Johnson is great. His class was fascinating and the readings he chose were engaging and educational. There is a fair amount of reading and writing, but nothing too much. He is a poet warrior in the truest sense!
DON'T TAKE THis CLASS. His grading was unclear and going into the office hours didn't help any.. His directions are unclear on paper/assignments and he's not very pleasant. DROP it.

This isn't the Intro to Poetry class it should be. Johnson makes it a personal agenda to choose favorites and makes it mandatory to attend out of class office hours to get an A. On papers, he will only write "Great Analysis!" and give you a big fat C. His directions are always unclear, and he barks back at students who want clarification.
great class

I have enjoyed his class. He values participation, he looks for those that try, and he LOVES when people come to his office hours.  He is extremely helpful. I took Poetry with him, we had two papers and two projects.  I received A's on everything, so it is possible but I also put the necessary time into the class to excel.

Don't take his class if you value your GPA. He grades unfairly and isn't very helpful in telling you what you need to do to improve your writing. Would not recommend him to anyone, even people who excell at english.

He is a horrible professor. He always picks favorites (females whom he helps) and then he pays no attention to the rest of the class. He will exclude you from class participation is you are a mere minute late. He is power-hungry and loves his control over the class. I love English, but he has made me resent his topic. CHOOSE ANOTHER PROFESSOR NOW!!

He expects you to work hard but if you are willing you will learn a lot and become a better writer. Class is fun but you have to participate! He really is helpful if you go in during his office hours but COME WITH QUESTIONS. He wants your work to be yours and does'nt want to fully influence your ideas

I am rating him a year after taking his Poetry Class. Take my advice: HE SUCKS. He grades unfairly. If you talk to him about your papers, he pretends you're on the right track then gives a D+ on it. Clearly chooses favorites in class (and they are always girls) and seems happy to see unhappy students after they receive D's on papers.

He is a very good teacher. There is a lot of writing, but it is English.  It is not an easy good, but if you are willing to work a good grade is very possible.  He is also very entertaining during class time. It is a lot of group discussions which relates completely with the writings. Also, I find he is very helpful during his office hours!

Impossible to get help from or even get ahold of. Posts nothing on blackboard, never responds to emails asking for help. If you ask questions he makes you feel dumb. He is laid back and cusses a lot, but when it comes to grading it is ridiculous. you get only 4 absesences excused or not and then you lose participation points. DROP NOW .

Never take a class with this man! He takes obvious "favorites" and grades completely unfairly. I went into his office hours many times, and his "help" did NOTHING for me. This class has caused me more stress than any class I've taken at this university. I am a straight-A student who has NEVER gotten Ds until this class. SWITCH OUT WHILE YOU CAN!!
I feel as he graded WAY too difficult, like previous responses said were all not English majors. I don't think he believes in giving A's!

His poetry class was really amazing. He selects really cool poems to study and believes in the idea that there is no one textbook meaning to a poem. He really cares about what you think about each poem. He also has a really cool poem writing assignment where you hit up the Science Museum. He's pretty mellow and gives good feedback on papers.

At first he was very intimidating, but after awhile you realize how interesting of a person he is. His class is almost like a philosophy class and the papers you write are pretty much just him asking your opinion and he makes you think really deep. I really have enjoyed his class and he is very chill and easygoing. He kind of gets annoying but rare
his grading is absolutely ridiculous.  work that generally deserves an A or B is always given a C or D.  hard work and effort does not pay off.  avoid this guy at all costs.
he is the worst grader everrr!!!! c's and d's are his favorite. very nice guy and pretty cute but sucks at teaching and grades incredibly hard.

Difficult to get an "A" in this class, but I enjoyed his class. I felt as though he pushed me to become a better writer and to think for myself for a change. I did however, feel as though he was very unorganized which was somewhat irritating at times.
is very unorganized and expects a lot. however, his classes are normally fun and entertaining as well as thought provoking.

Nice person, however the assignments were progressively incoherent.  I feel like he was blatantly biased towards the attractive females in our class, naturally, but at some point it becomes a little too obvious. Also, we studied the "Wasteland" by T.S Elliot.  Stray away from the wasteland, it will be the end of you.
he is hard to understand and so is his grading policy. i would not want to take his english class again.
Anyone else but this guy...Worst class of my college experience.  I never want to hear "...so how does this poem work" ever again!
Avoid this guy like the plague.  It is impossible to write a good paper in this class.  Unless you are a hippy tree hugger, don't take this class

This guy is a great lecturer...he relates the subject material (poetry) in a manner that does not necessitate rote memorization and pointless readings/assignments.  He allows the students to present their personal opinions, and does not force you to be able to "know" the meaning of the poem in either his view or the poet's. Great teacher!

Under no circumstance should you ever take a class from this teacher! He is self-opinionated, rude, careless, answers every question with another question (proabably because he doesn't know the answer), and downright bitter. Morever, expect to get D's on your paper's without any explanation.
The lectures were very interesting and really made you want to learn. You will have a lot of homework, but you will come out a much better writer.

I'm an English major, and this guy gave me a D on a paper--I've NEVER gotten a D before. It was better than most of the others, but he made an example of me. He was pompus and self-important...but he picked out really good poetry.
This guy is a jerk and think good work deserves a C. He doesn't understand that everybody is not a english major.
No Comments
Grade is basically just attendance. She's nice, but the lectures are pointless.
She is okay, but the class is a waste of time.

What can I say about this teacher that hasn't been said about Sean Combs, except those victims at least got baby oil when they got screwed. Get ready to click hyper links within hyper links within hyper links to get any iota of information about your inevitable group work that will take hours upon hours to even comprehend.

Very kind person, but not a strong instructor. The class lacked structure and mostly consisted of guest speakers. Lectures felt like filler with no real direction or purpose. Easy A, but I didn't feel like I learned anything. This class made me change my major.

Worst Professor I've ever had. An extremely unnecessary amount of extra work and takes months to grade. So disrespectful and belittling. Made me resubmit an entire project just to put numbers before each question. Still resubmitted before due date yet she still docked my points for a personal preference so she could grade it easier.

For someone who demands respect, she fails to reciprocate. Very rude and condescending in in-person and email communications. Acts like she's inconvenienced by having to reply to an email or even grade assignments. Unless you like being belittled and treated like trash, don't take a class with her. Unfortunately, 230 is required for mktg majors

DO NOT!!! Take this class when I tell you I have not had this much classwork in all my other classes combined my whole life! there are at least 12 assignments PER WEEK, yes per week and I am trying to graduate this semester I think it is an easy A class but should legit be like 6 credit class for the amount of work DONT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS BY ANY MEANS. The worst class I have taken by far worse than BSAN 202 with Mark Haug, and that is saying alot. This class is three credits, but for the amount of work it is, it should be 7 credits. I spent more time doing assignments for this class than all of my other classes combined.

Professor Crane was nice and respectful to her students. She did assign more homework than all my classes combined per week. However, the assignments were not very difficult, instead they were very time consuming.

Alot of lazy students r on here lying so here's the truth:there is a lot of work but, it is all very relevant and good practice and it is not as time consuming / hard as some are making it seem. Professor Crane is respectful and willing to work with you as long as u communicate. Lectures r boring and repetitive. Not enough time to do in class work

DO NOT take this class with Kelly! Her class is the most ridiculous and time consuming course I have ever done. It seriously does not register with her students are enrolled in other classes and cannot spend all their time doing her busy work. The syllabus states to prepare 10-15 hours/ week on homework but it is realistically more like 20-30 hrs

Way, WAY too many assignments.  It's a flipped class, but for her, that means having assignments and quizzes before class then in-class assignments during/after class.  It's mostly group work which can help or hurt.  She's a nice enough person, but if this isn't the class you work on most, I'd hate to see what else you're taking.

Worst class I have had at KU. Most of the assignments are group work, and she assigns homework (busy work) every week, which is more than most of my classes hw combined.  She also scheduled class after the KU baskettball championship win when most professors cancelled class, if that doesn't show how much she cares for her students.

Kelly Crane waits until the very last week of class to start grading assignments from the beginning of the semester. This makes it extremely hard to know how you're doing in the class. On the first day of class, she was rude and passive aggressive. She assigns multiple long assignments a week and they will only be worth 10 points. worst professor.

Professor Crane uses what she describes as a "Flipped Classroom," where the student does ALL of the homework before coming to class that week. Commonly gives two weeks worth of assignments during the same week she assigns tests. Does not allow you to make up assignments you missed in class for ANY reason. Do not take this course with Crane, its bad

When you speak with her 1 on 1 she's a fairly nice person. However, she is probably one of the worst professors I've ever had. It's like she's trying to give you enough work for 5 classes put together. She is not very clear with directions when in class so you'll have to figure it out on your own. Also, EVERY little assignment is GROUP WORK.

Kelly Crane is the worst marketing teacher at KU. She ruined digital marketing/social media for me, as it is my major. All she does in class is go over announcements/never allows time for our group to work when there are dozens of group projects per week. Her petty, rude comments about her students work are extremely hurtful. Do not take her class.

The absolute worst Professor Ive ever had. Completely self centered and doesnt care about her students. Way too much homework with no teaching. I dont know how shes employed by the school when shes this terrible. Upset I paid tuition for this class. Save yourself and take any other marketing elective.

Professor Crane is extremely nice, but the workload is insanely heavy. Expect to spend several hours a week on work with strict deadlines. Unfortunately, she is not very well organized so sometimes the assignments are graded incorrectly or the homework modules don't work properly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This is the laziest excuse of a class that I have ever taken in my entire four years of college. There is no actual teaching, there is only homework, homework, and more homework. For instance, this weekend, in particular, I have 20 assignments due today. Crane doesn't care if you have other homework as long as her class is first. Worst professor

Sports & Entertainment Marketing Class is not hard. Do the work and you'll be fine. Her syllabus is SO LONG to read and a little confusing, so make sure that you're keeping track of your deadlines. A lot of guest speakers. No actual teaching/lecturing on her end. Can get by without actually reading. Nice person, just not a fan of class layout.

This was an 8-week course so the material was very heavy each week. With that being said, there is A LOT of work to do outside of class (readings, quizzes, leachers, etc.) Kelly does not teach new information additional to the outside work so it becomes repetitive and can be boring. As long as you do the work, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had in my college career. Marketing is a topic which I was very interested in, and she ruined that for me. She does not teach you anything, and only gives loads of busy work. It takes her 3 weeks to grade presentations, and does not give feedback or explanation of the grade you are given. Find a different professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She taught some material on the second day of class, but that was it. This course is solely guest speakers, pointless work, and a couple of test. She assigns a lot of reading. Attendance and engagement is for a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This was the first time she taught the class but she brought great insight since she worked in sports marketing. Homework is a joke. She doesn't teach much, it's what you put in. She just brought in guest lecturers for the days we met in class: great for networking and seeing the potential job opportunities in the field. 80/20 Sports vs. Music.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Reads off power points for her lectures, has us watch videos, but doesn't actually teach anything. Requires mass amounts of work and doesn't grade any of it. Class is painful to sit through.

Before first session, students are expected to watch 10 minute video(s) and take Blackboard quizzes. Too much coursework before even coming to class. Textbook is old and outdated, making it a confusing read. The first  video includes a modem dial up noise and an image of a baby at a computer as highlights. Don't pay for this. I already regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Love her. Don't take advantage of the grading system.

I cannot say enough good things about this professor! She is well respected in her field, very professional while also approachable, and genuinely has your best interest at heart. All of the Astro professors at KU are phenomenal, but I would place her at the top for several reasons! Take every class she offers, it is well worth the effort!

Dr. Kirkpatrick is great and funny professor who is very knowledgeable about astronomy. I learned so much about the universe throughout the course. I highly recommend taking one of her classes, if you get the chance.

Dr. Kirkpatrick cares about each student in her class and wants them to succeed. She was very flexible with working through issues and prioritized ways for the class to learn as much as possible. If you put effort in your work you will do well in any class she teaches. One of best teachers I've had at KU.

While I understood the content and did well on the homework, I found the tests really confusing. Like they were worded weird. She's nice and great at explaining concepts one-on-one, but goes really fast in lecture and often is overtime.

Her half of the physiology was amazing. Her slides are clear, and give great analogies to help understand. Class is 80% exams, with one drop. Sometimes hard to pay attention since the class is later in the day and 1.5 hours long, but overall she does a good job. If u pay attention in class and study in advance the class is pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed and preferred Dr. Holder's half of the genetics lectures and tests. Going to her office hours was extremely helpful, and she explained concepts very well to ensure that they were completely understood. I never felt intimidated by her and would definitely take a class with her again.

Lectures weren't too bad, and a lot of the content is a repeat of previous bio classes but more in depth. However, tests were difficult, and sometimes confusing. I her teaching style wasn't bad, but I preferred Dr. Choi's(2nd quarter teacher). The textbook is a waste of time—don't buy it. Office hours were helpful and I'd recommend going to them.

You can tell she's passionate in what she teaches, but she's not a great lecturer. The exams are very difficult, and the lectures are overwhelming and long. She said she would give us breaks since its a long class and never did. The homework is inconsistently graded, however you can get it checked before the due date which is nice.

I would not take any class with Dr. Holder again. She goes over lecture content extremely fast, her slides are confusing and don't have all the info you need for the exams. Her exams were worded weird. The way she explains info is also more complicated than it needs to be. Would not recommend at all.

She's an okay lecturer. Nothing special. Her tests are very tricky and they are never straightforward. You might learn the basics of DNA replication, and then the question on the test will be worded to trick you, there will be an impossible scenario with several different factors, or there will be an unnecessarily confusing diagram.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Holder is a great lecturer and helps prepare everyone for exams. Utilize discussions & GTAs..you should get 100s on every homework assignment. Exams are 80% you and 20% group (most everyone gets 100% on the group portions). Really enjoyed the class set-up and would highly recommend these professors over others for genetics at KU.

Taught the first half of BIOL350. Very kind and clearly wants to help her students succeed. Genetics is a tough class by nature, but her lectures were solid. You can get by without the textbook, but you will do better if you do the reading before class and treat lectures like review. Discussion section quality really depends on your TA.

Professor Holder taught the first half of BIOL350. She was a very good lecturer that knew how to pace the class well to fit in as much information as possible without it being too much. Her slides were easy to follow. The class overall can be tough at times but there is plenty of opportunities to earn an A through the tests.

Dr. Holder was a great professor. The textbook is not necessary, I didn't use it once. Attendance isn't technically mandatory, however, she does use iClicker so those points can affect your grade. Test heavy but 20% of each exam is from group exams that are exactly the same as the individual. Homework is straightforward. Highly recommend.

Holder is very passionate about what she teaches so her lectures are very informative. The material is difficult but manageable. However, the exams are very tough and no matter how much prepared I felt the exams were extremely difficult. Questions are worded to trick you and use ambiguous language. Exams are also worth about 80% of the grade.
Easiest class I've taken at KU. No exams, No final, no essays. You are graded on participation and online quizzes. Show up and you'll get an easy A

BIOL350 is a class you're going to have to study for. Attending the lectures, discussion sections, and doing the homework are key to doing well in this class. The lecture notes and homework do a great job of preparing for the exams.

Due to COVID-19, this class was completely online (asynchronous). This class was in conjunction with Dr. Marriage, another nice biology professor. They really want you to have fun learning biology and not feel pressured, so there were ZERO exams. We were graded on lecture quizzes, group discussion boards, and weekly "exploratory" assignments.

Show up and go the pre class assignments, go to the extra credit opportunities. If you do everything you should be fine if you don't get A's on every test. Your group won't affect you if you study and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor was very good at keeping students engaged and explaining the material. There is a decent amount of reading but not required to get a B. I would recommended taking a class with her. Very approachable and will respond to emails promptly if you ever have a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Holder is very nice and she actually did a great job explaining the mechanisms in Genetics. She is accessible outside of class and wants you to do well. She taught this class Dr. Orive (who is awful). The class is just tough because there is a lot of material but just go to class, take good notes and study a lot. Don't be afraid to ask for help

Dr. Holder is a little quirky but really good at explaining the concepts. Genetics is really hard in general, but Dr. Holder does a good job slowing things down and thoroughly explaining. She is way better than Dr. Orive. Dr. Holder tests your ability to put your knowledge to work in real problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: i liked her lecturers because she actually wrote notes along with the information on the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great lecture, very interactive

Dr. Holder is an amazing professor she has good power points and will post them online. During lectures, she will write notes and important things that you should write down and she won't just read off of the slides. She cares and will use props and other things to make sure that you understand the material. One of the best teachers I have had.
She sometimes just assumes that you know and you get everything. She goes very fast not enough time for note taking. The notes you take in class typically arent on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This teacher was so boring it was hell to pay attention! She was never available outside of class and did not teach material that was interesting. The tests always leave you guessing what will be asked because there is NEVER any kind of study guide!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Holder is a good teacher. Genetics is just a hard class in general. I would highly recommend reading the textbook before lecture. She goes very fast through slides and there is a lot of them. Her tests are difficult. Very specific questions on difficult subjects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Holder is an amazing professor. The class is large but when she's one on one in office hours she is incredibly helpful and understanding. She will work with you for whatever you need. Her lectures are interesting and she doesn't make it quite dull. Take time to understand homework and read before class, overall great experience

Dr. Holder was always willing to help outside of class. She has a genuine interest in Genetics. She cares about the students and wants them to do well. She taught alongside Dr. Robert Ward and was the easier of the two. I got low B's on Ward's tests and high A's on Holder's tests. Her tests are straight-forward.

This lecture was beyond useless. I read the book and did great on the tests. She tends to go off on tangents about some weird part of biology that no one cares about, usually to do with fish. She has a serious obsession with fish.

She is one of the most amazing teachers I have had for a Biology course. She is easy to understand and while her lectures weren't made to be fun, they were filled with information. If you can get her for your professor you will learn to love biology!
Loved her! They key to get a good grade is to listen to the lecture and take notes on every detail and you will do great! Everything she says in lecture is on the tests. Recommended!!

I think she is one of the best biology teachers I've ever had! She is so in to watch she is teaching and it actually made the class interesting. Also she drops your lowest test grade which was nice. The only thing that sucked was half way through other teachers started teaching, and they were not as good as her.
Probably the BEST Biology teacher I have ever had. She is extremely easy to understand and is very helpful. If you can get her as your teacher I highly recommend it!

Holder is passionate about Genetics and seems knowledgeable. However, classes were boring due to style of teaching. Exams weren't easy either. A lot of material to study in each exam & she threw trick questions in the short answer portions. Mostly, everyone averaged a B in the class. It's hard to get an A but easy to get a B.

She's a good teacher, who is very passionate in what she's teaching. The tests can be relatively difficult, especially if you do not have a test file.Rest assured, though, you can drop one test and I did perfectly fine without them, so if you work hard you should be fine!

Good teacher.knows the material can tell she's passionate about it. Give her a chance she does want to help u learn and succeed.gotta work hard to get a good grade but def not impossible she does want to help you if you ask! Ppl hating on her prob didn't study hard and are blaming her for their bad grades.Don't be afraid of this class it's awesome!
Awesome. Tough class.

Dr. Holder's lectures weren't the most entertaining lectures ever, but she had a lot of great information. She tended to talk fast and it was difficult to follow. Her tests were fairly easy if you attended and took notes. She team taught this class with Robert Timm.

The tests are so difficult studying the material does not usually help, they are tricky.  i didnt buy the textbook and the majority of the test is from the powerpoint slides, she talks a lot about pointless stuff, but she is better than the first semester teacher.

When Holder teaches she is just talking without any class interaction. Also she didn't curve our tests at all, and the teacher from the first half of the semester did. If you want a better grade take it in the spring.

She needs to take a break from teaching and eat something. Probably the worst professor I've ever had at KU. Going to class isn't important to get a decent grade in the class. I refused to go due to the fact that she is probably the most annoying lady in the world to listen to. Do yourself a favor and take the course in the spring.
Hardest class I've ever taken. I'm a biology major, had a tutor and still got a C. Take it in the spring with the other teachers.

She definitely knows her stuff and I think she truly tries her hardest to get the point across, i just couldn't connect or stay interested with her teaching method. However, she does teach a very difficult section of genetics. This class was had 2 prof. and your best bet for her portion of the semester is to become best friends with your textbook.
Great teacher.... those who didn't give her a good rate are mistaking bc the course material is challenging not this teacher... she knows her material and she is awesome...
refused to use microphone, hard to hear, lecturing ok but tests are impossible. Make sure you have the book committed to memory, verbatim, or there's no chance.

The worst teacher in the world is teaching one of the hardest classes people can attend. She made an exam cover SIX CHAPTERS. If anyone has studied genetics they know that this is insane. DON'T TAKE GENETICS EVER

Lets just say that the class average for the semester is a D and she isnt curving it at all...the lectures are SO boring and it seems like none of the material she covers is on the test, if i had to take this class again i would take it from anyone but her
Worst teacher I have ever had.  Will not look at the students at all, but instead talks to all of the walls. I went to every class, and still was lost.  DO NOT TAKE IT WITH KRIS HOLDER!

A little weird, but the class was alright.  I asked her a question on the test and she gave me the most vague response ever.  I probably stared at her for a minute.  I didn't go to lecture too often, but it did clarify material that was in the book when I did. Study the book and slides at least a week in advance for the tests and you'll get an A-B.

I had Dr. Lansdon last semester and it ended on a fantastic note. Don't be afraid to talk to him. If you can't get As on the exams, do ALL extra credit and homework. Those points are what helped me barely get my A. Also, glycolysis is the hardest unit. Study ASAP for it.

I really enjoyed this class, and the lectures were so engaging. Definitely stop by office hours and use the study guides/resources provided to help prepare for exams! Lansdon really made my biochem experience much more enjoyable than I expected.

He is one of the best professors I have ever had at this university! He helped salvage my grade and was so thoughtful. The class is so difficult, but if you show up and try he will help with the rest!
He teaches Biochem in a way that just makes sense. Simplifies the material so that anyone can succeed. Easiest biology class I've taken so far.

Incredible professor--really cares about student success, goes out of his way to make lectures interesting (one time brought Lego Duplo blocks to illustrate enzyme saturation!) and does an excellent job of explaining difficult concepts. Tests were difficult, but he provides study guides and practice questions w/ answer keys that reflect the exam.

One of my favorite professors EVER! BIOL600 is structured so well and organized. Exams are content heavy, but Dr. Lansdon prepares study guides and practice questions that are actually helpful. I would highly recommend taking any classes with him!

Dr. Lansdon is the best professor I have ever had. His lectures are so good, he explains everything so well. Some exams are difficult but he gives study guides, has study sessions led by himself, gives homework and extra credit every week to keep your grade up.
Dr. Lansdon is one of the best!

I have never written a rate my professor review, but Professor Lansdon is one I always looked forward to writing. Professor Lansdon is respected and delivers incredible course lectures. I've never learned more from office hours. Very personable. Fortunately, I have had the honor of building a strong relationship with Professor Lansdon.
He is a great teacher. I learned so much in the class and he has a guest speaker come towards the end of the semester and it is fun to see how much you have learned. Great guy.

Best professor I have ever had! Makes a complex topic so manageable, genuinely cares about students. Great lectures, kind, understanding, clear expectations. Study guide and the practice questions are all you need to succeed on exams. He outlines and provides all resources you need to do well, you just have to put the time into doing those things.

Prof Lansdon was amazing (super caring). Biochem is tough but he made expectations very clear and exams were representative of material covered in lecture. He gives 1 exam drop, 1 hw drop, and ~5 attendance drops, along with up to 2% EC. extra credit was super easy to get and I felt like he gave a reasonable amount of HW. Highly recommend!

Dr. Lansdon was one of the best professors I have had at KU. In class, he is quiet when not lecturing, during group work. However, during office hours, he is helpful and considerate. He will go out of his way to help you in any way he can. I would take classes with him over and over again.
AWESOMESAUCE and hot
Dr. Lansdon presents thorough, organized, understandable video lectures. I highly recommend this professor and course.
amazing class!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's very clear Dr. Lansdon enjoys teaching and is passionate about what he is teaching. I was dreading this class when I signed up, but it genuinely became the one I look forward to the most. It's going to be difficult, but you'll always have the resources you need to succeed.
He was super chill and gave a lot of extra credit opportunities, he also let you drop an exam. He is the best ever
Reads off slides says, um before and after every sentence, iclickers require attendance and lectures are a snooze fest.

Dr. Lansdon was probably one of my favorite professors that I have had at KU. The class is hard, but he provides you with a lot of materials to do well, as well as lots of extra credit. One downside is that the grade of the course is 80% exams, but if you study the learning objectives and utilize your resources you will do well.

Dr Lansdon is great and better than other biochem profs. Clicker points awarded as participation and you can miss ~5 lectures to get full points. Lectures are recorded and on canvas. Exams are 80% of ur grade but he is clear (& posts study guides) on what material is on the exam. Weekly hw assignments with 2 attempts, best score taken. Easy A imo.

Dr. Lansdon was an amazing biochemistry teacher. The course was very content heavy but he made sure to explain everything and always answered questions. Make sure to take the time to study using quizlet or some type of flashcards. Make sure to do well on the first few exams as the final is cumulative. He also gave 1 extra credit point every week!

Dr. Lansdon is a great professor overall. He teaches a very dense subject but makes sure his students know what they're doing as he truly wants his students to succeed. Highly recommend going to every lecture, office hours, and TA sessions as so much material is covered in the class. DO WELL on early exams, as the final covers 32 chapters.

Dr. Lansdon is one of the sweetest teachers I've ever had. He cares about your success and with his help, you can easily pass the class with an A. Utilized his office hours and rewatch his lectures then you would pass with ease. I would retake his class any day! He's the best biochem teacher ever!

Not bad, not great either. A very chill professor but for a public speaking class, I wish there was less of a lecture component. Speeches are obviously required, but nothing in the class is weighted differently than anything else, just point totals.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Lola's COMS 130 class. The grading and expectations were fair and clear from the beginning of the semester. I did feel for her on multiple occasions as the amount of blatantly chatGPT generated speeches with no prior rehearsal were hard to sit through, but she was always respectful during students' speeches and made everyone feel valued.

She was a really good professor, and she did a great job making this class somewhat interesting. I think some of the lectures could have been a little better, but overall she did a great job with this class. She grades fairly and gives you good feedback on your speeches. She is very helpful during her office hours.

Ms. Lola taught COMS 130 which is public speaking, she was kind of a tough grader but if you follow her rules for speeches and assignments it gets better. Attendance was mandatory and she is passionate about the COMS. She makes class fun with group work, and she understands her students especially when you miss class because you are a bit sick.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: In my experience, the online section had very detailed grading with a strong emphasis on formatting and specific instructions. I lost points for small details even when my answers were correct, so it required close attention to guidelines throughout the course

BUS 205 is a class taught by TAs. In the first 2 weeks, you are assigned a heavy load of homework, and then it slows down soon after. Grading is very strict, so double-check everything. Most concepts taught in this class felt self-explanatory. If you are able to not take this class, do not take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Graded very harshly, class is taught by GTA's, assignments feel usless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you can DON'T take this class. You will learn absolutely nothing. You will be graded harshly on assignments that a third grader could write. It is so pointless and is completely irrelevant to business writing. A stupid class KU forces students to take so they can pay the bills. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!
I'd rather watch paint dry then be stuck in this class any longer.

If you want to remove any humanity from your writing and produce AI-generated slop, write the way this class teaches you.

The class has helpful ways to provide valuable information in a concise manner, but it also removes any personality you may convey in your writing.

It is required; you just have to get through.
It is early on in the semester, but I doubt my opinion will change: this is one of the worst classes at KU I've taken. There is no meaningful instruction or learning to date.
PLEASE DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. I'm now graduating, in my 4 years here I never made a review. I hope she gets fired, good luck to those that are too late to leave it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
I had read all of the reviews of Barrett, before taking this class.  So, I was prepared!
But that was no defense to the brutal defense of Academic Fraud, by KU.
It is strange how this fraud is allowed to go on.  I am now out of here, so I really don't care.

WARNING: if KU hasn't fixed it by now, you are SOOL!
Glad this headache is finally over. It is the worst class I've had at KU. Everything was done by TAs, and my TA was too busy to provide any meaningful help of instructions.

you never actually meet Laura, but my GTA Matthew was great. with that being said, the writing coach appointments are often cut short because "there isn't anything else that needs to be fixed", but then I lose points on things that were never pointed out to me in these mandatory appointments. attendance is not mandatory. put in decent effort, ur ok
I learned nothing. Busy work and a waste of valuable time.
Dr. Barrett couldn't care about Business Writing. She never once attended a class.

No one gave this class (Business writing 305) nor this instructor (Dr. Laura Barrett) a positive review on our in class written evaluations. The Administration must simply ignore student input. Bus 305 has been a real problem for years.

My advice, take Business Writing at another school and transfer the credit to KU. You might actually learn.

She never actually taught and relys on TAs for the lectures. In the lectures we barely did anything and it was pointless to go. Also such a tough grader so make sure you really pay attention to details or you wont pass with a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Due to the structure of the class, Laura's involvement directly with students is limited. The GTA assigned to your in-person section will be your main point of contact for this course. My GTA specifically was a very strict grader and is inconsistent with grading scales. Lots of valuable material, but the way this class is run is disappointing.

Not once have I ever seen Laura Barrett. The class is entirely taught by TAs who grade way to harshly.  If this class is required to graduate it should be a 6 week class max. Out of the past 2 years I can confidently say this is been the worst class/professor I've had. I seriously don't understand how she has a job still. Good luck soldiers.
May genuinely be the worst class I have ever taken. If you're taking this class in the future my prayers are with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This course teaches you to write concisely. I agree with this approach; however, If you don't write like the professor - you're wrong. Each assignment contains >6 PDF files (5+ pages) FULL of instructions just to teach something that is relatively simple to understand. The assignments aren't difficult, but navigating the web of instructions is.

Only 4 weeks into this class and can confidently say this is the most pointless class I've ever taken. 0 teaching going on. TA's grade like their life depends on it. All busy work and I pray to God that they get rid of this requirement. Also does +/- grading scale, so good luck getting an A.

I am a senior. This is the worst class I've had at KU. No real teaching or learning going on. Professor Barrett never showed up; not for a single class!

This class is all "taught" by teaching assistants. 
If you want an "A" in this class, I'd recommend doing what my roommate did. Date your TA.

It really depends on your GTA. Mine was strict and marked off points for everything, even after seeking help from the TAs. The grading criteria is not specified well enough because every GTA can make their interpretation of it, making grades inconsistent. I dreaded this course, and the professor is so out of touch with the students.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Going into this class I was horrified by the reviews and what I heard. After taking it, I realized that it isn't that bad. Having stuff do on Friday and Sunday nights was honestly the worst part. If you go to the writing coach appointments, ask your TA questions to clarify things, and write specifically how they say to you will do fine.

With Thanksgiving in mind, I have paused and reflected on my blessings. I am an excellent student with a 4.0 gpa. And I am grateful to all of those who have contributed to my success. 
But, Business writing 305, allegedly taught by Dr. Barrett, is absolutely not something I am thankful for. This "class" is a total scam! 
No real teaching going on.
My TA is of no help. My TA is not qualified to teach writing. Dr. Barrett is too busy to help individual students.

This class ruined my business school experience. I have had some terrific classes and instructors at KU. This class was the absolute worst, with very little constructive instruction. I really wish the business school would take students' feedback into account. What could be a very helpful class ended up being completely worthless.
I'm having a difficult time in this class. I'm a good student and am trying hard. There is no teaching going on. Just assignments graded by TAs.
I've had many excellent classes in the B School. This one (Business Writing 305) is the worst one I've had!
I am finding the class difficult. no real lectures on topics. no real teaching going on.

I have a very strong background in English and persuasive writing. This class is taught by graduate teaching assistants who do not have any background in writing. This class is a waste of time and the gta's give bad advice and their "constructive" comments are often grammatically incorrect.

I am trying to be nice, so I 'm not giving my uncensored opinion. I'm learning absolutely nothing in this class. That would be okay, but I'm having to spend too much worthless busy time on assignments that have no direction, no examples and no advice.

Drop this class, if you can. Maybe next year KU will restructure the class.  Every KU student complains about this class.  It is poorly designed. Graduated Teaching Assistance teach the class and grade all of your work.

This is a joke of a class. It is a mandatory class, so you can't avoid it. And the worst is that it is only taught by one instructor. GTAs do all the grading. My advice, flirt with your GTA.

Laura Barrett does not teach the class herself. I never even once met her.

All these reviews are true. Learned good skills from this class but it just sucks and was the worst part of my week, like I dreaded the assignments Writing coach appointments and peer reviews are a lifesaver.
Worthless!
No actual instruction by Professor Barrett. GTAs do all the grading, and they are not qualified to grade (they have received no uniform grading policy)!

Dr. Barrett has created a class framework in which you the student never see her or interact with her (unless you complain).  All teaching and grading is performed by TAs.  Grading is completely subjective, so hope that you get a caring/easy TA.  Good writing style is not taught; instead, the main emphasis seems to be on conciseness.
Avoid at all costs!

#MeToo, John Q. Student
I was never able to meet with Dr. Barrett in person. In fact she never taught a single class. My GTA was terrible.
Find a different option.

Professor Barrett is a bad instructor. Grading criteria is unpublished and is 100% subjective. The reality is that none of Bus 305 grading is done by Barrett, but rather is done by a vast array of GTAs, who's grading is absolutely arbitrary.

John Q. Student

cc: Dean Fields, KU School of Business (with 5 pages of comments)
It's not worth the time to write a review. Nothing will change and it's a required class and Barrett is the only instructor.
Its a joke of a class. Teacher doesn't review anything. Make sure you get a good teaching assistant and you will be home free. The work is not that too time intensive.

Be prepared to waste your. This is the worst class I've had at KU. Laura Barrett is the only instructor for this class at KU. From my experience, no interaction with Barrett b/c all students funneled to GTAs.

Suck it up and kiss up to the GTAs.
Terrible.  TA Grace beed

This is a required class to graduate and everyone that I have talked to before talking this class warned me about it. She gives out busy work that does not make you any better at writing. She grades your rough drafts of papers like it is the real thing. She takes forever to grade the final papers. I turned in a paper a month ago and still nothing.

I took AP lit/ELA throughout high school & had never scored less than a B on any paper Ive submitted in college(I'm a junior); I havent even sniffed an A on a paper thus far this semester. The rubrics are many & have so many weirdly specific reqs that it's impossible to hit every criterion because there are so many it makes them mutually exclusive

They would grade papers so hard in this class, they hardly hand out A's to people in this class and getting an A on a paper is hard and I have been a decent writer all through out school. There are so many papers, I had a good TA but if i didn't the class would be way worse. One of the worst classes in the business school. Would not take again.

This may have just been my section, but getting an A on any of the writing assignments was impossible. I received a 5 on the AP Lit Exam last year and I was still getting 75-85% on EVERY paper. The instructions have so much detail that it is hard to write an actual paper with sustenance. It's like telling a prisoner to run a marathon in their cell

The class is taught my GTA's entirely, I have only seen Dr. Barrett once. Class is easy, just read the rubrics for the writing assignments and you will get a good grade. This class did require more effort than others, and the big focus is tailoring it specifically to requirements. It did deter from the "learning" experience of business writing..

Class was easy the only tormenting part was having to read other students papers for peer reviews, probably the people below leaving bad reviews. I think it is good this class is required because it helped my writing sound professional and concise. Class was taught by GTA Rajvee who was super helpful.

It is as if Laura is this almighty being that students do not have the privilege of being in her presence. She is so detached from this class and everything is done by the TA.  My writing skills did not improve from this class and the writing coaches did not help much.  This class should not be required for business students.

Worst class in the business school by far. So much busy work and nothing we learn in this class is applied in the real world. Can not wait to rail this class and the professor on the course evaluations.
A class completely out of touch with real world business practices, which is not a surprise considering the professor has not business experience or any experience outside the academic world.

This class is easily one of the hardest in the business school. Even after following directions and recommendations given by the writing advisors (who we are required to meet with), I still came out of several assignments with a poor grade and comments on things that were not discussed during my writing appointments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is dependent on the Journalism (not business) graduate student you receive. Cannot miss then two classes, and if you do, you will not receive those points back. Overall, the course requires a median/high amount of effort. MAKE SURE your grandma does not die while you take this course because Laura Barret will seriously not care
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She grades completely asynchronous with the actual business world. So much nit picking, good luck following the rubric with the absurd graders and no communication.

Arguably the worst class I've taken at KU, Professor Barrett's class is an exercise in obedience. Arbitrary grading scales and excessive nitpicking overshadows learning value. BUS 305 could not be more out of touch regrading communication practices in the real business world. This is of little surprise as she has only ever worked within Academia.

Class is taught by a GTA, mine was super nice. Wrote like 1-2 papers a week, 2 of them were research papers. I like the way they have us cite sources, makes everything easier. Tough grading, make sure your writing is clear and concise. Sometimes directions and rubrics are hard to follow.

This might be the most useless class I've ever taken and that's really saying something. Seriously, 50% of what's taught is common sense and another 30% is already taught in other GenEd writing classes. The last 20% is just useless 'fluff' that I seriously doubt I will ever need.

BUS 305 was one of the dumbest classes Ive ever taken. After spending a significant amount of time in internships, it does so little to actually prepare you for work, and instead creates arbitrary grading scales that are almost impossible to perform on. Im a straight A student and this is the worst class Ive taken

Class work is not that difficult, written papers and quizzes. Problem is untimely feedback on writing, extremely vague/unclear directions on assignments and some information and documents are not available till the day before a major assignment is due.

I enjoyed her class. She grades kinda tough and you need to forget anything you know about writing papers and just write very concise documents with no fluff. It took me a while to figure out. She is very approachable and gives a ton of feedback on papers so you know exactly what you did wrong. No extra credit and A- scale but overall pretty good
Class was taught by GTA. Laura did however grade our paper alongside the GTA. The course was challenging but if you pay attention, actually try and follow the rubric you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: GTA taught this class, but all instructors grade tough. Hated this class, only showed up for attendance points (only one day a week, at least). Though I put in the effort, my writing skills barely improved, partially due it taking up 5 weeks for feedback/grades. Seemed like the instructors for this class don't care about helping students improve.

Dr. Barrett did not teach the class, a TA did, but she graded our papers. There was little to no feedback that explained to you why you got the grade you did. I got a paper back that said "Great work" and I got a B on the paper. Super easy class, but you don't learn much.
She's very nice and easy. Take this class!
She was overall a good professor. She provided the materials necessary to do well. You just have to put effort into the class and you'll do well.

Very willing to help students out. Overall, the class was easy. Just make sure you complete assignments on time and occasionally go in for her office hours. I feel like my writing improved as I progressed through this class.
Dr. Barrett is excellent! She is so organized and very clear with the assignments. She always responds quickly to emails and is very willing to help. I would take this class again!

Laura is an average instructor. She is not very engaging and actually reads the notes when lecturing. The most I learned was from doing the assignments. There is a lot of assigned work in this class, but no matter which section you take, the same is required.
Extremely helpful and fun teacher. Has a good sense of humor that makes it more fun.

She is very passionate about what she talks about and does a great job applying the concepts to real world examples which is very important in SOC. I emailed her multiple times and she was very understanding about absences.

I loved her class and absolutely loved her as a teacher. She is accommodating to students needs and is great at making the concepts understandable in lectures. As long as you go to the lectures and ask questions when you have them this class is easy to understand. You also get a notecard on all 3 exams including the final.

3 books you have to "read", but you can get by without, and just using her summary videos that she posts. Go to lecture because she explains a lot of stuff that is not present on the slides. Class was incredibly easy and requires not much studying for the exams. Other than that there is one essay worth a decent chunk of the grade but nothing bad.

Dr. Wright always came in with a positive attitude every class. Attendance IS mandatory she goes over a lot of terms and definitions used on the exam. You are graded out of 100 points at the end for lecture attendance and 130 points for discussion. Lots of reading (3 books). Gender/sex was taught more than I expected so just be prepared for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of group work in the class, most of time spent in class is group presentations instead of her lecturing. She won't grade a lot of assignments until the last day of the semester so you won't really know how you're doing, only things she grades on time are things to do with the final project/group presentation. However, it was still a good class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very nice person but specific teaching style. Split into random groups for the final project within the fist few weeks. She lectures once a week, the other day a group will lecture about the weekly readings. Never grades on time, class always runs over.

Dr. Wright is pretty nice and often drills the terms you need to know for exam by recaping every class. She uses Iclicker, so it is important to show up to class. The exams are not bad if you study and read the books. Although the class is pretty political and left leaning. She also provides 30 points of extra credit!
She was amazing! I would love to take her class again, as it was my favorite class and teacher at KU ever.

Prof Wright was amazing. The lectures were so interesting and it was definitely a great class to take as a first-semester freshman. Read the books to do well on the tests! I'm not a reader by any means but it was interesting. Beware that the topics covered are very left-leaning, but it was overall. great class.

If I would've known that I was going to be in for a very strong opinionated course this semester about gender, I would've went elsewhere. A lot of her own personal opinion is giving throughout her lecture, she gives “study material” but it does not match or correlate at all with the tests she gives throughout the course. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's a good teacher and offers a lot of extra credit. Keep in mind tho that because of this she won't round your grade up even if you reach out and ask which is valid though considering all the extra credit opportunities. Definitely go to the lectures, but if you don't it's not the end of the world because she posts them online.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Prof Wright! Even though it was a 600 person lecture, she still made it feel like she cared so much about each and every student. You do need to attend the lectures because there's not a ton of info on the slides. Exams were pretty easy too and you get a notecard for each one. I actually really enjoyed the lectures and they're interesting!

Engaging lectures, though attendance is important as notes aren't fully online. The reading load is manageable, and tools like Unstuck study can really help with exam prep. Overall, a rewarding class with a fair grading system.

Three books read during the semester. If you don't want to buy/read them, you can probably get by with reading online summaries and looking at her review lectures. GO TO CLASS. Her PowerPoints aren't detailed, so if you want to pass the exams go to lectures. Writing assignment was quick and easy. Easy to reach and clearly cares about students.
For having so many students, Dr. Wright is always really easy to reach out to and really cares about her students. I could not recommend this class and instructor enough.

Dr. Wright is amazing. I took her intro sociology class a while back, and she is truly an amazing professor. Nothing bad to say at all. I was at an iffy point in my life, so I didn't score as well as I could've, but her class is well-laid out and an A is feasible. She seems to truly care about her students, and is an all-around lovely person.
she was super passionate about the class and brought in guest speakers often. tests were kind of confusing, but there is lots of extra credit.

Dr. Wright was amazing! If you take notes in lectures and do the readings, you'll do well on tests. She is also very caring and understanding. There are a few essays, but they are not too bad. There is also a weekly discussion held by a TA. Overall, one of the easiest classes with one of the best professors. There's also easy iClickers in class.

She is a great professor. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you go it makes it a lot easier to have the info for the exams. She chooses random days to do iClicker for points so that's another reason to go. The tests rely on lecture and the books. There are quizzes over the readings each week but you have 3 tries to take them. Do the extra credit!
I took away a lot on the social workings of society. It was also a good starting point to understand the intersection between medicine and social life. I recommend to any premed student.

She was a very nice professor and she did a good job explaining the concepts in lecture. She doesn't always put all the definitions or explanations in the slides, so paying attention in lecture can be essential. There is a good amount of reading, but keeping up with it in some way as you go makes the midterm studying easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class overall is pretty easy. The exam material revolves around the lecture slides and the assigned reading, and she summarizes everything the last few lectures before the exam. All the lectures and slides are posted online, so you can check ahead of time if there will be a iClicker question, as these count towards your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't technically mandatory but she does use iClicker. Don't bother buying the books- I didn't read any of them. 3 easy assignments a week. Easy prep for exams with quizlets. You get a notecard for multiple choice exams and one 3-4 page paper. Discussion sessions are pointless but mandatory. Overall an easy course and easy prof.

She is very opinionated and very liberal. She posts the lecture notes on Canvas but taking notes in lecture is still very helpful. Very centered around the books she assigns to read, I personally didn't read them. Study guides for all her exams are on Quizlet, which was very helpful. She does IClicker randomly, but attendance isn't mandatory.

While attendance is not mandatory, unless you have a friend in the class who will share their notes with you you need to attend class, because she does most of her lecturing without detailed powerpoints, so there is not an easy way to get the notes if you are absent. There is a lot of outside reading, but overall the topics are quite interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure to take good notes in class. Lots of reading too. Super liberal as well. She's nice but would not take again
I hate Lisa Marie Wright. Refused to round up my grade 0.03% from an A- to an A. Entry level easy class, and takes it seriously for no reason. 0/10 Strongly despise
Cool class to take, make sure to read the readings. Lectures can be boring at times.
certified yapper.

Professor Wright is wonderful at giving engaging lectures. The content is interesting and the class is easy with all the extra credit opportunities provided. She is very objective when talking about topics that may be sensitive to some leaving personal bias out.

this professor is very kind and understanding. in lecture, there is a lot of material covered so although attendance isn't mandatory, but it's definitely beneficial. there are required texts but honestly i did not buy/read a single one and passed the class with flying colors. iclicker was occasionally used. do the extra credit!
She is a very clear upfront and forgiving professor.

Class needs to be taught in lecture hall! Otherwise, get Lill! Or your at a disadvantage...

Not bad for an accounting class, but make sure you can get Lill as an actual teacher and not a GTA. Also don't waste your time studying the practice exams posted before the tests. Go over the old homework assignments instead because he will pull a handful of his problems from them.

As a coordinator, he fails. He sets it up as he would do it, but does a horrible job picking his GTAs and UTAs. He may have enthralling examples that he teaches, but his TAs either get confused by them, or just don't get the correct message across. I didn't think the class was interesting and should be taught in a lecture hall together.

Worst class experience thus far.Lill's example test he posted were nothing like the test we would have a week later.This wasted my time on the first test-I studied all the wrong things(examples were miss leading).Lill needs to get a grip on how he writes the tests too. Why write questions about detailed text when we had 300 plus pages to read/test.

Lill did a great job at explaining the material. If you can get him instead of a gta, i would highly suggest it as he makes the tests and the gtas dont always cover everything that is on them. Turn in hw and do well on quizzes.

This guy is a complete ass. He is so full of himeslf and doesnt care at all about his students. His project sheets are very vague and you have to bother him outside of class time just to get all of the requirements. Overall the class is not bad, just get your work done when assigned.

Jeremy did a good job organizing the class and providing good tests until the final which was a disaster. He was forced to put a huge curve on it to raise the average to respectable. Overall the class was average. Be careful with points because there is a plus minus scale. Losing a few points will easily drop you to a minus.

Lill was the prof in charge of ACCT 201.  Although he taught a couple of sections, I had a UTA for mine, which wasn't the greatest experience.  I felt like I was missing out by not having the prof.  Lill's exams were challenging,  but fair.    He posted helpful sample exams and lecture slides on BB. I had to put forth a lot of effort to earn an A.
I love him! If he asked me out I would say Yes!!!

Professor Lill is a remarkable man. He takes issues that seem trivial and reveals their importance through Houdini-esque techniques. Many students would call him one of their most memorable instructors. God Bless America, and God Bless Lill.

Prof. Lill was the greatest teacher I have ever had... he really taught me how to decide important things, and also to solve important problems.  Plus, now I can prevent future ones from happening.  Amazing.  Not only that, but Prof. Lill's Latin Flair is enthralling.

He's entertaining and funny but not the best teacher.  You can tell he goes off on tangents on what he's interested in instead of material thats more important to the course and students learning.  On the first midterm the class average was a failing grade, he did curve it but only 11 people had A's after the curve in a class with over 100 people.

There are only 3 assignments: 2 exams, and a 5-7 page research paper. The last exam is 40% of your grade, so if you do poorly, you're destined to fail the class. Given no outline and no study guide for 1st exam. Grade average sucks because he sucks. There's extra credit, but very few points. Yaps all class with very few helpful notes in lectures.
Very chill
Lectures are clean and clear.

I personally like this professor. As far as tests and grades in this class are concern you have to read the book and actually study the materials rather than just skeem through them in order to get a good grade in this class due to the pace of the class and the amount of the material covered in this class. He is a funny and nice teacher as well.
hard

Not a typical 101 class. I agree with the previous statement and this is not a good class to take. He goes through material so fast you don't even have time to take it in or even write down half a sentence. Sometimes he acts like he cares but that lasts about 5 seconds and he is off onto another subject. Again avoid class at all costs!!

Don't take him. He does not care about students at all. He aims to fail students. Clear lectures available on blackboard.  Tests were reasonable.  Good teacher.

The international journalism class brought out a different side of this professor. She constantly wanted us to be involved, and I loved learning in this class. She was knowledgeable about the class topics and graded well. Sometimes we were assigned things not covered in class, but it was overshadowed by her passion for the subjects. She was great!
Unorganized and challenging to understand.
She is the best! If you participate and answer questions in class, you will learn to love her!

Do not take a class with the professor. She does not structure her class in a way that is understandable, nothing is posted on Canvas, she is unwilling to work with students who have questions, she is also often combative and not understanding when students have issues. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR.

By far worst lab instructor I've ever had. Extremely unorganized, under prepared, and unclear. Constantly argued with students who had concerns. Larry's teaching style is very confusing and unhelpful. He likes to turn a relatively easy subject into something way more challenging then it needs to be. Constantly uses Excel examples in class that are no where near to be found in his exams. He is clearly out of touch and should consider hanging it up in the near future.

My favorite professor I have had at KU. He is absolutely hilarious and keeps the class engaged with his energy and enthusiasm for the material. If you are slacking off or not paying attention, he may call you out. If you make sure to do the work and stay prepared in class, this will be the best professor you've ever had.

My favorite teacher ever at KU. Some people might say the exact opposite funnily enough. If you want an engaging teacher who has a good sense of humor then Larry is your guy. I genuinely have learned more from him in two classes than most of my other classes combined. 10/10 recommend.
Best class I've taken as a finance major. Practical knowledge and the material was very easy to understand if you pay attention and do the work.
Lectures are mandatory to pass the class. Tests are heavy but if you pay attention you should be fine.

Larry Morriss is a professor that will improve students' data analysis and make finance click to me. His class relies more on critical thinking than rote memorization, making students struggle. His class model and content teach students life and financial skills that will prepare them for the Finance world.

Attend every class and take time to study before quizzes and exams. I failed this class before passing and was humbled. You must attend class, be attentive, and participate in discussion. Professor Morriss can come across as strict, but is very fair. Give it average effort and you'll pass with a B. Put in extra effort and you will get an A.
He is a tough professor but you will actually learn. If you go to class you will be okay.

Professor Morris is a great guy. He starts off almost too strong at first and puts some students off. The big focus of the class is making you understand the "why" and then solve based on that. If you don't go to class you will fail. I recommend going to all of his office hours that you can to ask questions and it will really help you out.

One of the best professors at KU. He uses the Socratic method during lectures which keeps the lecture lively and fun. If you don't go to class consistently you will fail. His lecture material will be the exams and quizzes - take good notes. Study the practice questions and exam outlines. Go to class, do the work and get an A. Otherwise you struggle
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a discouraging and humbling course if you arent already a good accountant. Quizzes are harshly graded due to the lack of partial credit. Same for exams. Learn the process, dont just memorize the end result or answer! Do what he says, make sure your attendance is near-perfect, and be prepared to fight hard for a passing grade.

reviews.comment: heres how the class goes confusing lecture where you jump from topic to topic somewhat randomly. hard homework on that topic you get barely any assistance or guidance on from the lectures then you take the those graded about 5 days from the exam. take an insane exam and hate your life. hes also a jerk who thinks he can never be wrong about anything

I have had Professor Morriss for 3 undergraduate classes (ACCT 321, FIN 415, FIN 428) and 1 graduate class, FIN 728. He is a great teacher, I learned more than all other classes at KU. His lectures are fast paced and often very humorous. His courses are not easy but students who want to learn will learn. Do the work go to class you will do well.

Have taken 3 courses w/Morriss. If he hurts your feelings, you're soft, and you weren't paying attention in class. Homework/exams was extremely simple/straight-forward. YOU WILL ACTUALLY LEARN IN HIS CLASS. By far the best prof I had during my time at KU.

The grading scale is really student-friendly, and there is a lot of extra credit to be had. That being said, Professor Morriss will publicly embarrass you at times if you don't know the answer to a particular question. He also has a tough time admitting when he's wrong. He's quite the character though, and his lectures are generally pretty good.

Almost impossible to pass this course, especially if you already struggle with accounting

At the beginning of the semester, I realized I was struggling in this course, so I thought I would be able to contact the teacher for support. He is very smart! Very good at accounting, but not so good at teaching accounting! I would choose different man please next time for class to teach.

Easily one of the most useful courses I have taken in the Business School. Yes it is challenging and you will have to put in the work for the grade you want but it is very achievable.
