Megan speaks intirely too fast. shes down to about 5 people in class because everyone dropped. She only speaks in spanish and rarely helps you in english. Stay away!! Far away!
Megan is great! Make sure to do ALL the homework and participate and you will be fine
I didn't think Megan was a bad teacher, I enjoyed this class.
Terrible teacher. She speaks too fast and doesn't know how to explain anything.
Talks a million miles an hour in Spanish and no one really understands her

Megan is an amazing teacher! Not only does she make the material understandable and easy to learn, she makes the time spent in her class fun and entertaining.  She's funny, young, down-to-Earth, fashionable, and REALLY cares about the subject.  She was the best part of our day, and we're sad the class is over. Hope she likes the scene music!
lovely guy, I've had him for three courses and every lecture he is confident and curious for student's learning. He is a super tough grader though be specific on exams.

Took Diff EQ with him. Compared to other professors he is by far harder. Not allowing any equation sheets and requires you to derive every equation yourself. Also will count off on exams for using shortcuts even when your answer is correct.

This class was pretty difficult for me as he does grade very harshly. However, now that I am not taking that class anymore I understand why and I can respect it. He focuses a lot on theory and its not that hard to grasp but if you don't try its gonna be hard. Honestly, show up and actually pay attention and you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Kind of a brutally tough grader but he's otherwise great guy. Super kind and helpful, and he cracks a lot of jokes during lecture which make them engaging. He's very clear about expectations and when quizzes will be, even telling you what will be on them ahead of time. Overall I would be overjoyed to take another class with him.

I took his calc 2 class which is just hard in general, but he made it pretty ok. He does a good job of explaining the difference between methods of solving and he uses some fun analogies when explaining the things we learn.
I think he was an okay professor but he really sped things and when it came to explaining stuff he would just say look back on the notes for further explanations.
Prof is good. Shout-out to Debjit Basu for motivating me and helping me when I was struggling
He is amazing at taking any class like Calc 3, Differential Equations, or Linear Algebra. Any Class Nick teaches is 10/10

I took differential equations with him and he was a great professor. The content is pretty hard but he was good at making it easier to understand. Occasionally he was passive aggressive, but the way he organized and taught his lessons was very successful. He was gone one day and nothing made sense that day without him. But the homework sucked.

I took Calc III with him and he was a great professor. The content is pretty hard but he was good at making it easier to understand. He is good about asking if people have questions, and he was consistent when going over problems which was helpful for learning. He was gone one day and nothing made sense that day without him.

Awful professor, i took him for linear algebra and so much of your grade depends on conceptual 5 minute quizzes in the beginning of class rather than actual computation things. very rude and snappy when you ask a question and has no remorse for his students. the only way he will like you is if you kiss up to him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, he explained concepts well and at a pace where everything was mostly understandable. The in-class quizzes he gives are really dumb and are worth an obscene amount of your grade.He grades tests pretty easily. When you ask him questions he sometimes gets upset because he feels as though you should know the answer already. Overall good
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great prof, learned a lot. The class was harder than it needed to be. The quizzes should be open note just because of how hard/important they are. His grading is annoying too. You don't really know what he wants for an answer until you get the homework back and sometimes you get it back too late so you miss the same points. Overall A- prof tho.
I have never liked math.  I will never like math and I'm okay with that.  But this professor made equations interesting.

Nick is probably the best math teacher I have ever had. He explains clearly and reviews frequently. In class we learn in groups which is a very effective learning style for math. There is A LOT of WebWork homework each week. (About 20-40 problems) One thing about this class is that a few of the prof's comments will catch you off guard.

Nick is obviously loves calculus/algebra and is really Helpful if you go to his office hours, offers take home extra credit problems and one on every exam. You can get an A in his class but you have to work for it.

Packauskas was a great 116 teacher. It was is first time teaching the course and he did a great job. I took a few years between 115 and 116 so I had to work my ass off, but he was very helpful and answered questions without that pretentious/judgmental tone that seems to be common in math professors. Overall, great job!
Seems to enjoy teaching.  Gives historical stories about math to make the dry subject somewhat more interesting.  A very kind grader but you need to be willing to do the work and learn in his class.
Pretty difficult but was one of his first times teaching the class. Be prepared to study, you really have to earn your grade.

Worst professor I have ever had. She was extremely mean and derogatory. She called us ignorant and ended class early since no one was answering her questions because we are afraid of her. Today was our last class and we still don't have grades. She threatens to fail people. She implements policies and does not tell anyone
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class gave me the most stress and anxiety I have had so far. I already have a hard time speaking up in class, but being forced to and then being talked down to when you do is incredibly unhelpful. It's a shame because she is really knowledgable, but I was just put off by her not understanding that we are not experts, we are still learning.
Professor Nualart was really helpful. It was definitely a challenging class but the lectures were good at clarifying and I never felt totally confused.
His accent was sometime difficult to understand when lecturing, however he was extremely helpful if you had any questions in lecture

Could skip class and read the book, but his lectures are quality though dry at times. Weekly homework from the textbook, but never overwhelming. Tests can be tough, but he always tells you what type of problem each question will be, which really helps studying. Allowed a cheat-sheet for a couple of tests including the final.
Clear expectations and helpful lecture

He teaches as if he's talking to students who have taken multiple statistics courses before. There are no prerequisites to this course, so most of the students are way behind his level of teaching. He doesn't answer questions very well - just repeats what has already been said. I chose this professor based on this website and I regret my choice!

Professor Nualart got stuck taking over this class after our original professor bailed mid semester. The subject matter is extremely tough. My biggest complaint was that he does not write everything down so it can be difficult to take good notes. I did most of my studying out of the text for this class. His tests were straightfoward though.

Nualart is an amazing teacher who is always eager to help students. He knows his stuff, but always works through examples with the students in class. Therefore, he doesn't just ramble on, but actually works through each and every example so that students know what is going on. I highly recommend him, especially for honors calc II.

The prequiset for this course is 123 Math, but the truth students need to have strong back ground in math like measure theory. The professor expects all students are PhD students in Math department while the class is required for students from different department like Econ,so most Econ students struggle in his class.I do not recommonded the Profe
He has an accent, but his teaching ability is amazing.
Great teacher, made linear algebra seem like grade-school stuff.  Excellent at getting his point across, and is a real nice and helpful guy, too.
bad

I really enjoyed Prof. Nualart. He's a very good lecturer. He has a Catalan accent, which I think is a beautiful thing. He also made linear algebra phenomenally cool in the eyes of a math geek like myself. He proved things and demonstrated cool facts.
Why are we printing screenshots of Excel files? That doesn't even begin to make sense in 2026

She was fantastic! One of my least favorite classes, but she did a great job checking in and making sure everyone understood the lectures. She was always really nice in her office hours if anyone had a question as well.

She has a very dry sense of humor, which helped pass the time in a class that is not the most exciting in theory. The homework and tests were very intuitive and always looked like what was done in class.

Genuinely cares about the students and their needs in the classroom. Clear and thought out lectures and helpful practice problems. I have taken two of her classes and think her teaching style is very conductive to learning.

Fantastic professor, had her for 325 and 511. 2nd favorite in the department behind Dr. Gerhke. Really good notes. Makes a thorough review sheet with the topics covered on exam before each exam. She can be a tough grader, but is fair. She clearly loves what she does and cares for all students. I've learned a lot from Dr. N.
grading scale for class is difficult, have to do really well on all exams.

Love Prof. Nordheden! I couldn't recommend her enough! She goes at a great pace in her lectures, and is great at articulating everything so you understand it. For the most part, she handwrites notes in class. She's a very fair grader and great at demonstrating how each concept builds into the next. I wish she taught every C&PE class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was poorly prepared for us. Majority of her notes were from the internet and not her notes, that being said, the notes were just garbage. Like she went down the hall trash bin and picked up the notes. But her assignment were hard because she doesnt know what she wants. She just bad lecturing,and we spent 80 bucks on a book we never used

Dr. Nordheden is an angel sent as a savior for the KU students of CPE. I have taken two classes with her as my professor and cannot recommend it enough. She has helped me with as her student and regarding my overall success as a student at KU.

Nordheden was clear with expectations, the homework was fairly reasonable, and when I had health issues in the middle of the semester, she did what she could to make sure I caught up and passed the course. She knows we have other classes, and coordinates with other professors to not schedule tests same day. She's also just a good person.

Nordheden is a nice person and a good teacher who got stuck teaching the most boring material. Chemical engineering has a bad retention rate, and if KU jazzed up the subject in this class, they might be able to keep a few more people. The class is super easy, got high A's on every test with minimal studying. Class is like a chemistry-math hybrid.

Material is not particularly exciting, but she is extremely clear about her expectations. Attendance is 10% of your grade, but in class you go through practice problems that are helpful for homework assignments and exams. Practicing  problems in the textbook is extremely helpful as well. Getting an A will require some work, not bad though!

I thought this class was fairly easy. The hardest part for me was the homework, which was hard to understand just from the examples in class and in the textbook. She was always willing to help and you could tell she wanted students to do well. My friend and I went through all of the hw and in class problems to prepare for the tests and did well.

Dr. Norheden was very confusing and her lecture tended to not make a lot of sense. The TA's were helpful if you went to their office hours but other than that I pretty much taught myself the material. This class also isn't mandatory to take and is frustrating in that the homework is usually WAY harder than the tests.

Dr. Nordheden takes attendance and counts it toward your final grade, so you must go to class. Her lectures aren't very clear, but if you follow along in the text book, tests and homework are very manageable. I studied for about 2 hours before every exam and got 100 on all of them. Not the best teacher but a very easy course.

Class lectures and homework assignments are nothing related with what's on the test. You are expected to write equations on every single assignment and test, instructions on homework assignments were not clear, if you want to get an A in the class, you have to use TA's office hours, professor will not answer your question!!

Her homework assignments and tests are fairly difficult if you aren't familiar with physics (at least that helped me) but if you complete and fully understand each homework assignment, this test is a breeze.  not the most fun class to sit through, though

Nordheden is a really good teacher.  She is funny and her notes are very well organized and help you through the homework.  You get to use all of your materials on the tests; however, she gives you 50 mins for an exam that should have twice as much time to complete so your grade suffers for it.

Great teacher, seemed to be the most down-to-earth engineering teacher in terms of expectations for students to do work that I've ever had.  Homework is assigned once a week and consists of 4-5 problems, and exams are pulled straight from that.  Semester project is simple, as well.
No Comments

She is awesome..tests will come from the H.W or similar concepts..half of the exam will be a free bee ..while one prob or two will be challenging..but ..u will be able to figure them out...she is really cool for a engineering teacher...

It was alright overall. She doesn't really give feedback on your work individually or as a class which can be really inconvenient if your schedule is too tight to meet with her 1:1. Tests were too open-ended and often word choice makes it confusing. Personality was pretty fun and engaging and lectures were clear. She glazes ChatGPT too much though.

She is very lecture-heavy, but they are easy to follow along and understand. Attendance is a large part of your grade, but if you show up every day you will easily pass. She has funny anecdotes and is very kind. She occasionally gets off track, but the course information is still clear. Beware of several group/solo projects and essay-based exams.

I literally love this class so much. Its a combination of lax and engaging. If you give any care at all toward the class, it will pay dividends. It is possible to backseat this class and still do well, but it would be a disservice to yourself not to engage. Shes great! 10/10 would reccomend.

I truly loved this course and Niki as a Prof. She is a generous grader on tests and truly wants you to succeed. She is funny and made class interesting which is hard to find in a prof. From what i've heard she is the better prof for MGMT 405 and I would extremely recommend taking this course with her!!

Don't take this class if you're of European heritage that isn't Dutch. She spews her political bias in every class. Tests are extremely subjective and she will insult you if you don't know something SHE considers "common sense."
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: first of aallll- so hard to understand, and also just very rude to students.
Won't pass if you don't attend lectures but otherwise very caring prof. Accessible outside of class. Lectures can get boring and she does go off topic sometimes but overall good course, good prof

Do not be afraid of her. She is very easy going as long as you do not go on your phone! She is an understanding professor who actually cares about her students. Never be afraid to speak up in her class because that is what she encourages.

Niki is very opinionated & dingy. She has no real world experience outside academia and pushes her european political views on the class. She makes sure the class lasts full session by adding in fillers like 2 hour group presentations each class & excessively long/boring videos. Guest speakers were the best part. Avoid this teacher if possible.
Very genuine and caring and wants you to succeed in class. Clear grading criteria, but lots of reading. Also gave easy extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Wood is hands down one of the best history professors I have ever had. He is incredibly knowledgeable about what he teaches and I always leave class with new perspectives. I have taken 3 classes with him so far; his passion for history and care for his students make all the difference. This class has a decent amount of reading.

He is so nice and a really great professor. Participation in the small groups matter, but super easy as long as you prepare and at least read some bits and pieces of the readings. Attendance matters, but will be lenient if you email him about why you miss class if it isn't often. He is super caring and genuinely wants us to succeed.

This is the only History course I took at KU and I am so happy it was with Dr. Wood. His set-up was to lecture during one class and then have small group discussions in the next class that week. Make sure to do the readings, as he picks them specifically for each class. Amazing professor, who is passionate and knowledgeable about his subjects.
One of my favorite professors Ive had at KU. He genuinely cares about his students, and about his profession. Take one of his classes if possible.

Participation is what can make or break your grade. Speak up in class, and make sure to do readings a head of time. Papers can be tricky at first, especially if you're not a history major. Prof Wood and TA were helpful in providing feedback. Go to office hours to get help with the papers, and you're almost guaranteed an A or a B.
Amazing lectures - lets his students make up test and study guide - definitely taking another one of his classes!

First, I think every hist student (and many others) should take a class with Prof. Wood before they graduate.  He may not be the best professor out there, but he is very good and will challenge how you see the history of the world.  Tests and papers are challenging but he does tell you exactly what he expects (he actually has a session and says it)

He is a great teacher. His use of primary sources during lectures makes the class interesting. He also keeps students engaged by having them critique art. His class is not easy, requires a lot of reading, and can seem esoteric at times, but, he is a great teacher that is worth getting to know.

This class did not interest me at all. It was very boring and sometimes unclear but overall it was a good experience. BUY the texts you will use them everyday! If you ever get confused or need help with an essay go to his office hours and ask for help! Don't start the essay's the night before they are very long and time consuming!

Very energetic and interesting teacher. This was, for sure, my most interesting class of the semester. However, there is lots and LOTS of reading, and he expects you to be on top of it. Also, he's a harder grader on the papers and essay styled exams than most English professors. You will learn a lot, but you'll have to work hard.

He is a kind professor who will answer your questions and respond to emails. He is reliable, and if you go to his office hours for help you will do better. It is a lecture class, but he passes around an attendance sheet, which seems childish and is annoying. I would give him a solid 4.

His class was very challenging in the fact that you have to be very involved and keep up with the reading, but he is a very good professor. He genuinely cares about his students and he is very engaging during class to keep everyone interested.

Too much reading of the same type of information. He needs to realize that his is not the only class that students attend. He also says he gives you 4 "free" absences before dropping your grade, but this seems to be a false statement. Interesting class but it gets hard to motivate yourself to attend around mid-semester.

He actually teaches the ins and outs of communism and doesn't focus on all the bad parts of it, which was very educational. He even incorporated aspects of the culture that are interesting to college students, like rock music and film. The only major assignments are a few papers and a project, but there are no tests!
His Communism class was very interesting and his lectures are superb. You learn a lot from his lectures, essays, discussions, etc. One of the best teachers I have ever had, including K-12.
Easy class but you learn a lot.  He's an amazing lecturer, and can make any subject interesting.  (He is also absolutely adorable, which doesn't hurt.)
He is a great professor and a genuinely nice guy. He keeps his lectures interesting. Does not assign busy work, but the class is not an easy A. Work hard and you'll learn a lot!
Fantastic teacher.  I learned so much in his class.  But yes, he will actually require you to learn and study.  Prof. Wood is a great guy!

I learned a great deal of information regarding Eastern European history that I never thought would interest me.  Professor Wood made the class interesting and sought active participation from his students.  If you're at all interesting in history in Europe this is the go to man.
He was a great teacher and is passionate about  history
He was a one of the best teachers I have ever had. He made modern european history somewhat interesting. Was very energetic.
Without a doubt best class of that semester, maybe even this year. He is fun, helpful and enuinly interested in helping kids learn. Take him, you will be glad you did!
Prof. Wood was one of the best professors I've had at KU. Very fair-minded, engaging and especially knowledgable about Eastern European history.

Tests are very hard, but after the first one, you know what to study for and papers are graded easy so that helps your grade.  GO TO CLASS-HE TAKES ATTENDENCE AND GIVES YOU POINTS FOR IT AT THE END OF THE SEMESTER!
Dr. Wood is one of the best professor I have had, He is well prepared, his lectures are engaging, and he takes time to meet with you outside of class

Elijah was a great GTA. This course was my first experience with neuroscience which caused me to be confused at times but he is so helpful in his office hours. I also found his way of explaining the material to be more clear compared to the professors lectures

Elijah is so so caring and thoughtful. I had a serious family situation come up and he was so helpful in my success. He checked in on me and also sent me some resources. I honestly do not know many professors who care about their students success and well being more than him. He also is super informative and helpful during office hours.

Elijah was one of the GTA's for this class. He gave specific feedback on assignments and seemed to take the time to grade fairly. This course can be frustrating with the group projects and others not putting in the work but with the clear grading rubrics they used and the feedback from the GTAs the class was not as bad as others say it is.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Elijah was a GTA for this course, but he was a saint in this nightmare class. There were many moments in this class that were hard and the professor made this course so tough and confusing. Elijah would help and advocate where he could. This class was extremely tough with the work load, but I want to shout out Elijah for helping me feel successful.
The most knowledgeable and helpful calc 3 TA KU has to offer. My professor himself said that Nikos runs the department. All around a great person who wants to help you succeed.
Best TA ever! He genuinely cares about all of his students and wants everyone to succeed. He's knowledgeable in math and explains the problems well!
Best Calc 3 TA you can have at KU. Treated all students genuinely and wants you to succeed. He's so fun and really knows what he's doing. Overall great person and helpful instructor.

Nikos is such a great guy. Super nice and caring. He also has good knowledge on the topics and always was able to help whenever I was confused. Attendence isn't mandatory but is really helpful as the problems he goes over really applies and helps in the class.
Awesome teacher
Would Take Again
He was a great professor. If you get the chance take a course with him!
Absolutely chill and goated professor. Had Professor Olinger for an 8am session and it was very enjoyable and engaging to be in! I definitely would take this class with him.

He gives a lot of time in class to work on projects, which is really helpful. He provides great feedback on assignments and genuinely helps students improve. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him.

He is an amazing professor. When I had him, it was his first semester and he still did a great job. As a management major, many classes feel like lectures with little value, but he made lessons meaningful by connecting them to real-world ideas and making assignments practical and relevant.

Super cool dude. Very understanding and relaxed. His class was pretty interactive and the course was interesting. He gives you a lot of time to work on the project in class. Definitely would take a class with him again.

While taking this class with Robert, he was very clear on his standards for grading and followed the rubric thoroughly. I recommend taking this class with him. He gave us lots of free time to work on our group project together in class, which was extremely helpful as we didn't have to work much outside of class on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He adjusted the project based on the progress being made by the teams but the second part of the project would have been good to do. The reading wasn't as helpful as the lectures and in-class activities.
I appreciate that he switched from a boring textbook to a good novel. The project could be more meaningful if we were working with a live company.
The course was very informative. We read the book Difficult Conversations which was very helpful. I had some personal matters come up during the course and he was very understanding and supportive.
Peter gives great lectures and is easy to reach and super helpful outside of class.
Just show up and do your best. Good guy.
Awesome course. Great professor with polished lectures and clear quizzes and assignments.

Assignments teach research skill and you get to learn about building and architects that matter to you. The exams are not hard. It is rather easy to get a good grade. Prof delivers great lectures that are polished and informative. This is a real college course that everyone should take.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Olshavsky is smart and helpful. Course is very clearly set up. Content is interesting. Studying for exams just takes some time but is not hard. The two assignments are research based and you learn research and writing skills while looking into things that interest you. Honestly, this is a great class.

Course set up is clear. Assignments are given at start of the term to allow everyone to set their own schedule. Yes, you have to learn how to use the library system and do real research. Weak students will complain. But it is very useful to find knowledge. Lectures are great. The arch content is very interesting. Peter is always helpful.

Peter is very knowledgeable but the class is set up very poorly. The entirety of your grade comes from 3 tests and two assignments. Finding textbooks were very difficult to say the least. Lots of of content covered in mandatory lectures and assigned readings and studying is completely depended on you there are no study guides or outside resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Whole class was based on three exams and two papers. The papers were graded kindly. And attendance was taken everyday.

Peter is nice but structures the class horribly. 2 Essays, must use physical books from KU library that you can check out as sources & you must scan each page you site and highlight the passage you are siting to submit. Exams are 1/2 lecture and 1/2 of the 100 pages/week reading you have to do. It is too much info to memorize in such a short time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures make mandatory attendance worth it. Grading on writing assignments is more focused on content rather than nitpicking structure and phrasing. My only downside is no homework grade to buffer a bad test or quiz.

Peter is a really knowledgeable person and have engaging lectures if you like history or architecture. Class projects were straightforward and if done correctly, getting full marks is easy. His quizzes are really hard though, very specific and expand over hundreds of years, covering many contents. Nevertheless, enjoyed him and the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This rating is more for how Peter set up this class... not my opinion of him. Peter is an amazing person, and I'd take any other class he teaches, but he structured this History class horribly. The quizzes were tested over thousands of years' worth of stuff that he vaguely expected you to know. I felt I didn't learn much about architecture history.

Dr. Ostermann is a very nice person, but very bad at teaching. Didn't understand any of the lectures and mostly just attended so that I wasn't wasting my money. So far have relied incredibly heavily on learning everything from the textbook myself, as nothing Dr. Ostermann has covered was intuitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ostermann goes through random notes without explaining what is going on and his handwriting is impossible to read. No practice problems in class and he runs through some examples way too quickly. This class would be vastly improved by handwritten notes. He is a good guy and fun lecturer, but the classes are almost useless.

Dr. Ostermann mumbled through most of his lectures this year. I usually played games on my computer or did other homework during class. Tests (2 midterms and a final) are open note, open computer. This class is not a struggle, but a nuisance to attend. It's the easiest engineering class I have taken thus far.

I have no idea what this semester was. Lectures were random pieces of paper-we never knew what topic we were learning. Grades are simply unknown the entire semester. Exams are open everything, but that makes it worse honestly. Every assignment is a random assortment of topics we never learned. So stressful for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He needs to retire

Dr. O has a very laid back and unorganized style about him. While this might make for a fun person to get a beer with, it creates a terrible class environment. No one paid attention during lecture, and we didn't learn. All that said, the class wasn't too hard to pass - definitely ask for regrades on your exam because he's a very generous grader.

Dr. O seems like a nice person, but clearly hasn't been a student in years. No understanding of what is necessary to learn the material at all. No one knew what was going on in class, including TAs. Assigned HW randomly with little to no time prior. Final grade test heavy with no EC opportunities. Lectures and notes were incoherent and unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boring lecture that no one pays attention to. Very easy exams.
I LOVE YOU DR.O !!  BEST PROFESSOR AT KU.

I have had Dr. Ostermann for several classes now, and he really is a great teacher. He is very smart and interesting to listen to. Assignments and exams are fair. If you pay attention in class and try the homework, the exams will be extremely easy. His voice can be soft, so if the class doesn't have a microphone, sitting up front can be useful.

He teaches differently than most. If you can follow his lectures, they are the most insightful in to the profession than any other professor. BUT they won't help you on the tests. Practice Exams and the TA will do that. If you get an A, don't question it. Just move on to next class. I hope he never leaves KU. Favorite professor in Petroleum.
THE BEST PROFESSOR IN THE PETROLEUM ENGINEERING DEPARTMENT AT KU. IF HE LEAVES. I LEAVE TOO.

Prof. Ostermann is a very smart man, but not a good teacher. It is extremely easy to get an A in his classes, but you really won't learn the material because it's hard to understand him. He speaks very softly, and he doesn't really have a lecture, he just seems to talk to himself and make sound effects. Practice tests will get you through his class
Dr. O is one of the nicest teachers and easiest to talk to at KU. Does not do a very good job teaching however. Don't worry though because the classes he teachers are a joke.
get away
WORST CLASS EVER!
Easy class, but I really didnt learn very much at all...
u can get an A easily but u won't understand how u got an A

Dr. Oh is very knowledgeable, but lectures can be pretty rough. First things first, it can be hard to understand what she is saying. I don't hold that against her, but it's a fact. As far as explaining concepts, she tends to just read straight off the slides and doesn't elaborate on them, resulting in her teaching feeling incomplete.

Wish I could give her higher, but honestly this was a hard class to trudge through and Oh did not make it easier. Difficult lectures, often does problems wrong. People don't understand her when she speaks. If you take Oh, prepare to self guide yourself through Calc II

A teacher whose goal is clearly to help students succeed. She will give you plenty of opportunities for extra credit and many many resources to prepare for exams. Her notes can that she posts on canvas can be difficult to understand at times, but you can always refer to previous examples to try to figure the process out.

Weekly quizzes, but if you understand the homework they should be more of the same. Exam questions are taken directly from the homework. She let me make up a quiz that I had missed because my alarm didn't go off. Great lectures.
Solid lectures, she goes over everything you need for each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Oh was a great professor to teach Differential Equations. The content of the class is hard, so I won't hold that against her, but she explained concepts clearly and had office hours multiple times a week. Very good professor, made the class completely doable despite the challenging content.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Oh really does care about everyone in her class, however, if you dont take this class seriously you will not pass. Lecture attendance is essential and the homework will be difficult due to the material. She does her best to teach the content but in the end its still a very hard class.

Lectures are fast-paced and disorganized. If you look away for a second, you miss crucial info. There are weekly quizzes, hard homework, toughly-graded exams. She thinks 290 is a pre-rec, so you'll have to teach yourself matrices. If you have to take 220 w/ Oh, sit in front, email her, and attend office hours. 220 consumed my life when I took it.

Really hard homework but the tests are more than reasonable. Very good professor and her lecture notes are really well put together in case you missed class! Definitely one of the best professors to take 220 with
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: dr. oh does her best to teach a weird subject, but it doesn't always work out in our favor. her in-class notes and examples are hard to follow, and the homework is sometimes so hard to the point that it's unfair. she always posts practice problems before exams that are similar to the actual problems. not a good class but not a bad one either.

My problem was she wrote all the lectures as she was teaching incredibly fast, disorganized, and in terrible handwriting. Looking back at notes made no sense: no headings, tons of side notes anywhere theres room on the paper, lots of skipped words and example questions aren't written out so you don't know what question she's solving.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Oh was very thorough teaching MATH 220. Glad to answer any questions.

I took diff eq with Oh. Compared to other KU math profs, her class is pretty bearable. The hw was often much more difficult than the tests and in-class examples. The tests were very difficult and required thorough studying to get a good grade. Lectures were often faster paced w/ mostly example problems which was helpful but confusing most times.

Oh is a great professor who I'd highly recommend for 220. The lecture notes are put together very well, and she makes sure to provide additional examples on more difficult concepts. The homework is more difficult than the exams, so if you understand the homework you'll do great on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Oh was a solid professor. She tells you what you need to know and her tests are very reasonable. Her teaching style is almost only doing examples. Very little conceptual thinking goes on and proofs are never explained. You can still do well in the class, but it makes it a little dry. Overall, not bad, but I didn't find lectures to be interesting.

Dr. Oh was an AMAZING prof! Instead of powerpoints, she writes EVERYTHING during class with the projector--you get to see every step of each problem this way! Quizzes every day, but if you do the hw problems before class they are easy! Exams are based off in-class examples and quiz problems, so as long as you study those you are good to go!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Accent, talking fast, and poor handwriting made lectures very hard to follow. But there are quizzes everyday, so you review her notes before class, then she does an example almost identical to the quiz right before you take it. Very fair tests, much easier than the hw which is long and difficult. Have heard of bad Diff Eq teachers so I'd recmd her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Meh. She's not awful, but definitely not amazing either. I don't recommend her unless you are already somewhat comfortable with the material prior to taking the class. She skips tons of details and doesn't explain how her proofs she writes even prove anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Oh is very clear on what's expected in her class. The textbook was difficult to comprehend, therefore I relied heavily on class lectures. She doesn't have any surprises on her test; tests are a reflection of what's on her quizzes. As long as you study the lecture notes and work on the homework daily for about an hour you should do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Oh is an overall decent instructor. The lectures are critical, her homework reflects  quizzes and tests, and the content is manageable. The truly difficult thing about her class is how incredibly tough she grades. Also, when she takes off points, she is not specific as to why they were taken off, so you may no idea what you did wrong.

Most fair prof I've had and best Math prof. I got a C because I'm bad at math. Very clear on what she wanted from you and exams were VERY fair. Does grade the problems a bit harsh sometimes (mess up an integral in the beginning of a prob. and she'll take off a lot for consequential numerical inaccuracies) but 10/10 recommend. Had for MATH 220& 290

The worst professor I've had at KU. She's used to teaching graduate classes, obviously, and expects us to have learned the material before the semester even started. She does curve a lot (around 20% on one test) and gives a lot of extra credit and is always willing to work with you on ways to improve.

Most useless professor ever. She was very confusing to listen to, and would be even if she didn't have an extremely thick accent. And her TAs, looming over you in the aisles, are just as helpful. Tried to go to one of the help sessions and no TAs were there, and the professor sure as heck wasn't. Take this with ANYONE else.

The class was a requirement so I had to take it, but I did not enjoy it at all. I didn't do well on the tests, but still ended up getting an A because of extra credit and a perfect hw grade. All of the hw is online and you can retry questions as much as possible. DON'T BUY THE BOOK. She had a very soothing voice so it was hard for me to stay awake.

You can't understand her but she is very clear on what she expects. Attendance is extra credit but, quite frankly, you probably need it. If you're in this class I'm assuming you aren't great at math and her tests are fairly tricky. Do your homework it's a chunk of your grade. You only need the online textbook for class. DON'T buy the physical book.

It was difficult to understand her a lot of the time because of her thick Chinese accent. I failed every single test (Even though I got 100% on ALL the online hw). But each and every class you would receive one point for attendance, so I ended up with a B for the semester!
One of the best math professors at KU. She knows her subject and how to teach it well. Go to class take good notes and you will do well. She is very fair. Highly recommended.

She is the very nice. The notes are clear and she knows how to teach this subject very well. There were days that she acted like she didn't want to teach, but most of the time she does just fine. The homework is easy if you attend class. The tests and quizzes can be a pain, the reviews are helpful. This is now one of my favorite math classes now.
Ms. Oh is awesome. She is very thorough with the material. Her tests are very straight forward and are very similar to the study guide. Take her class b/c she is fair and she really knows her stuff.

Oh is by far the best math professor I've had at KU thusfar. Any one who says otherwise probably didn't come to class and ended up failing the tests because of it. Come to class, take notes, and do the homework. Her teaching was so clear that I never had to reference the book's text. Never got less than a 97 on any of her tests.
One of the best math professors I've had.

She's got an accent, but that doesn't mean she can't communicate. Her handwriting is perfect, it's sick. Her organization is insane. The homework is always harder than the test, so you know what she expects of you. She's flexible (I had to get my wisdom teeth taken out and she let me make up the test no problem), funny, and a great math teacher.

As others have said, Dr. Oh is extremely fair in her grading and what she expects from you. She is always available to help and will entertain any questions people might have in class. Count me in in the "She's the best math prof. I've ever had" club.

Oh is one of the best math professors at KU. Not only is she amazing at math, she also does a great job of conveying the material to her students. No matter what class you take with Oh it is guarantee that she is going to do a good job teaching you the material. The work load she assigns is fair. Lastly, she is the most fair professor I have had.

The best math class BY FAR I have taken at KU.  Her accent doesn't really get in the way, I actually enjoyed hearing her say words funny, because I knew what she was trying to say.  Her test reviews are SO HELPFUL and she loves what she does.

Her lectures are hard to follow and she's a pretty tough grader.  She's easily available to meet outside of class, but often seems to give you a blank stare when you talk to her, not really giving you much insight.  She's really nice, but not a very effective teacher.

she is very nice, but can be very confusing sometimes. some of the homework is irrelevent to the material, but study the example problems on the practice midterm/final and you should do fine. show improvement and she will pass you.

Tries very hard, but has a thick accent, and is difficult to understand.  (It took me the first two weeks to figure out that "kwefshien" was co-efficient.  Her notes are very disorganized, and sometimes the homework does not match up with what has been taught.

Frankly, Dilshan is not good for teaching 531. His lectures make absolutely no sense and don't relate well to the homework. Something needs to change with his teaching style, because the content is mildly important, and the majority of students can't pick it up.

ARCH 209 - His studio was alright (I was in his first Studio here at KU.) Did some pretty good projects while I was there, easy to talk with and workshop improvements. You really have to go out of ur way to get his attention, but once you have it, his suggestions (in person) are quite good.

Not the best at using technology, better go find him irl.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Difficult to follow during lectures. Assignments are not helpful. He blames us students for failing but really he's just failing as a teacher. He does not know how to use Canvas so quizzes, assignments, and grades are messed up. He creates unnecessary group projects that are more difficult than need be. Overall not a good experience.

Great professor! His classes are extremely interesting and easy. All you have to do is write 5 papers during the course of the semester. 4 of them are 4-5 pages and one of them is 10+. Be ready to participate in discussion. He makes sure that everyone speaks during class time. He will give you extensions on papers if you ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Pierotti was definitely one of my favorite professors I've had at KU. His class was super easy, yet extremely interesting. There were no exams, only 5 4-5 page papers throughout the semester.
Dr. pierotti is hilarious and gives fun lectures. I am only a month into the semester and I already like him!

Goes on tangents, screams pretty loudly when teaching, and is pretty in your face about everything. I thought I was taking a course about the Conservation of Marine Mammals but it turned out to be a course about Native peoples of North America. His personality might not click with every student, so be wary of signing up for one of his classes.

I took a class with Dr. Ray Pierotti back in 2007 or 2008.  I think it was called Native and Western Views of Nature.  We spent a lot of time talking about Traditional Ecological Knowledge and the differences between Western (white) views and Native American views.  Great class, lots of open discussion.

Ray's Environmental Justice class has the potential to be a great class. However, there didn't appear to be a single student who enjoyed the class. It was nearly mandatory to regurgitate his opinions. Outside opinions did not seem welcome but instead seem judged. His teaching was not clear. Do not take this topics course if you don't have to.
He's a rambler and talks way too loud. I had him for a seminar and you can tell he's passionate and does really want you to learn. Doesn't dumb it down and assumes prior biology knowledge.

Although he is very opinionated at times, he means well and is very passionate about biology. He grades rather easily and keeps you entertained during lectures, but he may go off on tangents about the government, philosophy, religion, etc., or talk endlessly about his ventures with old colleagues.
Dr. Pierotti's class philosophy is great. I only have him in a topics class but I would take him over Gleason in evolution any day
No Comments
Rambles on for hours about anything but topic.  Key to passing the class: if you regurgitate his opinions you'll get an A.
His tests challenge you but are not impossible.  Likes to tell stories and gets off topic a lot.
This was the worst class I ever took! The material was not well explained, and the tests were ridiculous.

SPLH 161 was a really easy class, I seriously don't know how it would be possible to fail. Theres no exams, only 1 final project which was a breeze. Dr. Rong is super smart but sometimes her lectures were just a little dry. I wish there would have been a little more in class engagement.

I don't like the flipped classroom format; most of the time, going to class feels unnecessary. Do your online work and make sure you get the in-class assignments done on time, and your grade will be fine. The final is an easy group project.

Hybrid class. Very sweet professor, just didn't learn much. In class assignments every week due at the end of class were stressful, but if you reach out you may be able to get an extension. No final, just a group project that was super easy. Replies to emails fast and is pretty helpful one on one.

Lectures rarely make sense, she's redundant but explains things differently/confusing. Tests are HARD (short answers, matching no word banks). If you have an iPad, use it bc she relies on pictures A LOT. Tests are lecture heavy, but lectures make no sense. Her feedback to questions is SUPER confusing, & she doesn't seem to care for students at all.
the lectures are super fast. she teaches like it is a review and not something we are just  learning. got a good grade because the final project was easy

The class felt pretty disjointed. Professor was nice but I never felt topics and assignments were clearly explained, making the class overall more difficult than needed. I also felt very rushed to complete the in-class assignments. Not the best experience, overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly one of the worst professors I have ever had. For someone who is so educated and respected, she lacks common sense. First off, nothing that we learn is on exams so basically sets us up for failure. Also, she gives quizzes AFTER exams over what was tested, which is the dumbest thing. Her lectures make no sense, and overall very bad course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (Hybrid course) Do NOT take a course with this teacher. Really easy because its just quizzes on canvas and discussions in class but you will learn nothing! In class, you do a reading and sharing activity every time. There is so many interesting things about this major the professor ruined it for me. Lots of extra credit given though.

Class is not mandatory as everything is posted online. The lectures included her reading off the slides, so were not very helpful. If you complete all the online assignments you will get an A, and so much extra credit is offered so there is no reason to not get an A. There is no tests, only online quizzes every week which are very easy.
This professor reads verbatim off of the slides. Not very helpful in OH, will tell you to read the supplementary articles that she posts. The articles make the material more confusing.

Contextualizing history of sociological theory to meet the environmental moment is vital & engaging task for all who take this class due to the adherence to sourcing standards. Nobody who takes this class seriously should be afraid to seek publishing their findings about industrial applications of global improvements in environmental sensitivity.

I wanted to like Dr. Stock as he is very well-versed in what he knows. But, his rubrics are genuinely the most confusing things, his tech skills are incredibly lacking, and overall his class is unfortunately boring. I went to almost every class and am leaving feeling like I learned next to nothing....

Paul stock is an incredibly boring teacher and doesn't teach anything. He is smart and knowledgeable but talks about irrelevant stuff. His lectures are boring and leave me falling asleep and I can't ever remember what I learned. He goes on 30 minute rants. The class itself could be much more but he only talks about New Zealand. Don't take!

Paul is a good man and I respect him as a person a lot. He is very kindhearted and will be happy to work with you on any issue that you have. However, it is hard to actually learn from his teaching. I'm not actually sure what exactly I learned from being in this class. Also a very reading heavy class, great guy tho.
Best class I have ever taken. Great professor I honestly would reccomend any of his courses!
He's rude tbh.

Not a bad professor, but so boring. Did not learn a single thing in the class because he expected us to learn everything from the readings and I can't learn like that. Had very little to do with Sociology, mainly just environmental issues.
He is amazing

I took Environmental Sociology with Prof Stock and also had him in EVRN 140 & 142. He is a very knowledgeable professor, but his only downfall is that he can be a bit slow at times. Other than that he is quick to advice, feedback on any papers. I even got extensions on two assignments. Very laid back. Must do outside classwork
He is always available and caring. He offers extra credits for two or three things, which can help
This guy knows his stuff! Caring, to-the-point, and smart! Go for it
I recommend him. He is teaching you what you will need to know in the real world when teaching multilingual students. He knows what's important and what's not. He is a nice and understanding guy.

He was the best source of feedback I had at KU. From him, I learned a great deal about becoming the kind of teacher I aspired to be. I truly owe much of my confidence and positive feelings about myself to his guidance. He is a respected young man.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: I got a B-, but I can say that he is a great guy. If he hadn't helped me, I would have failed the course. You can see that he is willing to do things to help people. He cares about students, really. I found the personal connection at the beginning of each session really nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lots of readings & discussions. Readings average 20+ pages. Cold called and asked us to take turn reading to get us engaged. Projects aren't too bad, not always a lot of specific directions. Didn't have to attend class during field work weeks. Smart, nice and willing to take feedback to improve his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Peyman's comments for my assignments were very helpful, and it was in a way that you could see yourself learning something. This course was asynchronous online, but I wish I could have an in-person class with him. He was a nice guy, and you could see that he really invested a considerable amount of time in reading your response.

Peyman is amazing, but you should be ready for MANY papers he gives you weekly. Some weeks, they are A LOT!!! He has a balance in discussions and lectures, to me!! And the field experience thing was AMAZING. It was a real one!

He is very caring. If you like both discussions and lectures, you should go with him. He professionally connects theories with real-world practices, and this is amazing. He had many related short clips during his lecture, which made the class more exciting. I would shout for his knowledge and great character.

Class discussions are really important for him. I suggest you read before going to class; otherwise, you will be alone and silent! He is extremely adaptable and knowledgeable. He has an international perspective, something we miss here in the US!

He is gone now and this is a tribute.  In the mid 60's he was in his prime.  When I think of my years at KU, he is the one who stands out as the most inflluential. He was the very best. May he rest in peace.

Among the best professors I had at KU, 1980-87 (4x). A passage studied was "The quality of mercy" (from The Merchant of Venice) "The quality of mercy is not strained./It droppeth as the gentle rain from heaven /.../ It is twice blest:/ It blesseth him that gives and him that takes." Read his "Iris Exiled: A Synoptic History of Wonder."

When I took his class some years back, his goal was to show us how stupid we were (yes, he said that).  Well, I guess by testing us on stuff we never covered, including expecting us to translate things from Latin (naturally we ALL speak Latin these days), I sure felt dumber than when I started.  But I still got a B.  Go figure.
No Comments
No Comments

Wow, this professor speaks English a little too well.  He is very concerned with literature and literacy.  I thought I knew a lot about English before I took Dr. Quinn's course.  He addresses a lot--he even knows his Olde Englishe historie.  Intersting, if you enjoy word history.
He is senile. Do not take from this man. It will be detrimental to your health. Please. Please. Please. I'm begging you - do not take his class.

If you hate the following: syllabi, structure, improving your knowledge, knowing when essays are due, feeling like your not wasting your money...THAN THIS IS THE CLASS FOR YOU! I couldn't answer the easiness question because he doesn't grade or assign anything! But it's not easy, don't be deceived!

He is so old that I am surprised that he remembers he has class each day.  We asked him what book we were supposed to read next for shakespeare, and he told us to read a book from his childrne's lit class. He might have expected a lot in the past, but I think he's too old to know the difference now.

DO NOT TAKE Shakespeare or any class from this man. He is the worst teacher I have ever had and probably will ever have, if I am lucky. I can't believe how horrible he is....He should not be teaching anymore.
Worst professor I have ever had. We were tested on a book we didn't read and he said "Do the best you can!" One of the reasons I left KU!

if you take chivalric lit. with quinn you'll read some cool stuff but he always wants to talk philosophy. he'll remind you often that he's the senior professor in the eng. dept.-great, he's been around so long he's lost touch...
No Comments
HORRIBLE; what a mean, sad little old man that has completely lost touch with KU
Horrible. Doesn't communicate well with class, demands a lot
No Comments

Ok most of the time nothing special or horrible, but when test time comes around, Hong is your best friend. you can take anything you want to the tests. including the practice test and the answer guide to the practice test, the book, everything. and shes willing to curve if she thinks the class needs it

Prof. Hong taught the course very well. As everyone else stts, the exams are open book/note and her reviews are very similar to the exams. She will take time out of her already very open schedule to help you learn in this course. Make sure you turn in your hw..that's the only reason I got a B+ instead of an A! ha

Dr. Hong is a very, very sweet lady. Her tests are straight forward, easy, and open note and open book. She actually wants you to learn the material, and get a good grade. She's rooting for your success. She's also very open about office hours, and is not afraid to help her students out when they're stuck. Her English can be broken at times though.

Dr Hong has minor issues with English (v/w, calls "x" "es") but nothing that gets in the way of... anything. Her tests are open homework, and you can put your notes, formulas etc. in with your homework. She curves test results when it will help (and when non-Gaussian dist.). Very generous with her time, answers questions, etc. Off hrs 4 dys/wk.

Overall, a very good professor. She was kind of hard to understand at times, but it really wasn't bad. She is a super kind grader and tests were VERY similar to the practice exams she posts. Plus she let us fill out a cheat sheet for each test. Go to class, do your homework, do the practice tests and make a good cheat sheet, and you'll be fine.

she is really working hard to let us pass with good grade. her main reason is teaching us not to make it hard to pass the course. sometimes we don't know what is she trying to say but overall she makes it easy A course.
You cannot understand what she says very well. It makes it hard to understand math at all. I had to get a tutor because you can't understand. Youtube is your best friend in this class for sure.
loved james quinn! very nice, wants to be as helpful as he can. he genuinely wants his students to do well, not one of those teachers who seems like they want you to fail.
I absolutely adore this man.  Extremely reasonable.  You'll get the grade if he KNOWS you're trying-- so do the work and you will be rewarded.  He loves his subject and knows his stuff.
He was my discussion teacher for western civ and i hated that class, he did TRY to teach, but the result was terrible. I think I could have done a better job than he did.
great guy really helpful really nice.  he puts a lot of effort into his class.

Assigns an insane amount of busy work. She is so unorganized. I'm not kidding, she literally just assigned more busy work due at 11:59 pm Thursday with an exam in her class on the same day. So not only do we have to do the assignment, discussion, and contribution, but we have to study for the exam! Literally a 0/10. Can't wait to be done.

Dr. Schmalzried has a great personality. It's clear that she is passionate about her job. But she doesn't do her job very well at all. Grading was poor and super late, and she always forgot to post assignments on time, which left you with little to no time to work on them. It's all busy work and pointless for the class.  Steer clear

Very very kind professor and you can tell she cares about what she is teaching. She cancels class sometimes if she feels it is not necessary, which is nice. All exams were online and not too many assignments, she is very easy to contact both in and out of class.

This class is interesting at times, BUT extremely unorganized!!! She reads off the lecture slides, and half the material is not on the exams. She takes the whole class period on one topic. She releases assignments right before they are due, so we barely have time to complete them. If there is a different professor for this class, I would do that!

Dr.S seems to be a really kind and caring person overall. HOWEVER, her class is super unorganized. Throughout the semester, there have been multiple times when she has forgotten to post assignments, sometimes not posting them until Thursday (most are due Sunday). The lectures are also very boring and not helpful. Plz don't take this class.
She is a very caring and understanding professor. This workload isn't super heavy and the class is interesting! I would definitely take another class with her.

I took PSYC 200 with her. Very nice but extremely unreliable. The class was not super difficult, all exams were online but there were like 5 assignments due every Monday. She's not very helpful, if you need to contact her outside of class for anything, good luck. She does not respond to emails, even if she tells you to contact her via email.

Do NOT take this class. Ever. I mean it. I feel like I wasted good tuition money on this seemingly useless course. RaLynn does not grade anything until the end and unreliable with the class schedule/informing us of WHAT we need to be doing. It was incredibly lazy. KU, please find someone else to teach this. If you do take this class, DO ALL WORK!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: When I tell you my entire class was confused on grading criteria, the "optional" assignments, and the fact that half the time RaLynn couldn't get her act together, I MEAN IT! You could learn the content from the entire 15-week course from my peers rather than her. Attendance is iffy, as she likes to change her story on grading, too. 0/10.

Dr. Schmalzried is really caring about her students and the class, but in PSYC 484 be aware of what you're getting into. Some assignments are "optional" but to get even a B, you have to do 95% of them. With a lack of guidance and due dates, you're diving into the deep end with this one and you better be prepared for lots of busy work.

Professor RaLynn is a caring and smart person but the class felt too unstructured to really get anything out of it. I was very confused on what was happening due to a lack of due dates for assignments and the unconventional structure of the class overall. My peers were also on the same page of confusion making it harder to ask each other for help.

I am a straight A, honor roll student paying for school on my own. Dr. S. does not respond in a timely manner (sometimes weeks, sometimes never). Be EXTREMELY careful on what is listed as "optional" on Canvas (nothing is optional). She doesn't grade until well after the class is over so you truly have no, and I mean NO, idea how you're doing.

I took her for psyc 200 research methods. Prof RaLynn really cares about her students. Her lectures were engaging and she is passionate about her work. You have 2 quizzes every other week, 2 exams and a final. Great prof

I took Schmalzried for research methods in psychology and she was great. Lectures go over the reading, you can get away with not reading the book before class and you'll be fine. 2 quizes per week over readings, 2 Exams, 6 HW assignments and a final. All exams are taken at home. She is very engaged in her classes. I'd 100% take her again

I didn't get much out of this class. It wasn't hard, but our only learning resources were really short videos that barely covered what we were quizzed on (the rest was from the textbook). She also never responded to emails, which was really frustrating because that was the only way to get in touch with her. Easy class, just annoying.
This was an 8-week class for me, so a lot of assignments. Fairly easy course, but multiple assignments and discussion boards each week.

Her class is very easy to get an A in. She doesn't grade quickly and doesn't respond to emails. I feel like this class was kind of boring and she takes off some points with no explanation it feels like. I think her class was okay but I didn't get anything out of it.

Schmalzried is a very genuine and intelligent professor, but for me my biggest complaint is that I feel like lectures are dragged on for the whole 75 minute class period. I think I timed it out to be an average of 15 minutes spent per slide, and each slide only had 3 bullet points! Homework is easy, and exams are open note.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best teacher I've ever had in college this guy is goated
Great instructor who makes intro microeconomics relevant. Lectures are well-organized.
His lectures weren't only informative but also enjoyable. Can't hype this guy up enough. He definitely knows what he's talking about, wants you to do good, and will help you achieve that.

David is a great instructor. He gives easy to understand feedback on all exams and papers. He creates a positive classroom environment that made it fun to learn in by always striking conversation before/after class and always being in a good mood.
Dr. Marriage was pretty disorganized and the lectures were right off the slides. The groupworks end up on the exams tho so it was aight.
Don't be afraid to ask question
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of my favs, she's hilarious and makes biology very fun to learn. Heavy content so show up to class and do ur clickers. She gives out plenty of extra credit points on exams. Every new topic there's group work, and it's ez you can check with the TA/SI.

When I took this course, there were two professors. Agusto is a bad professor, maybe 2/5, but Marriage is a 5/5. There are 480 total points in the course: 3 Exams(180Points) and the Final(120Points). The rest of the points came from lab work and HW, which was completion. Listen, participate during the lecture, and do past exams - you'll be good.

This was my first science class at KU, and I was worried, but Dr. Marriage made it very easy to learn. Her lectures are clear, and the homework helps a lot with the exams. We had five exams, could drop one, and got 5 points EC on each. The exams were very straightforward and all MCQs. To study for the exams, look over lectures and do SmartBook HW.

Dr. Marriage is not only an awesome professor but she's a great person. She's super accommodating with mental health and disabilities, and she emphasizes the importance of taking care of yourself. She's also really great at explaining things and she's super interactive. I would love to take another one of her courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She clearly loved what she teaches
Dr. Marraige is SO caring and SO funny. She gives you everything that you need to succeed so if you stay on top of work, you will do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a really chill and fun teacher to have! Great at explaining concepts

I LOVED Dr. T - hands down one of my favorite professors. She is very nice, flexible, and willing to meet u where u are. She is passionate and wants her students to not only do well in her class but in the classes they will take going further into bio. Clear grading/ expectations on exams - genuinely, if u put effort in, u will THRIVE with her!

Dr. Marriage is by far my favorite professor. She is very caring and clearly has a passion for what she does. She checks in on how the class feels during lectures to make sure everyone understands. She keeps lectures engaging. If you keep yourself to a schedule, study, and do your homework you will do well in the class.

The tests in this class were weighted at 65% of your course grade and were mostly multiple choice, worth three points a piece. This adds up quickly. If you read the book before attending lecture, take good notes, and do all the online assignments, you should be fine. Be careful of the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: When I took this class, the first three exams had test corrections that gave you up to 20% more points on each of them.
This class is pretty easy as long as you keep yourself disciplined. She will give you extra credit points on the tests which is helpful.
hi

Dr. Marriage is an AMAZING professor! Her lectures actually make sense and you leave feeling like you know the material. This class is very content heavy, but attending class is the best way to manage it!  It is easy to tell that Dr. Marriage cares a lot about her students! I would take any class from her!

dr. marriage is so sweet and funny, her lectures will keep you entertained.
for biol 150, mcgraw hill connect & iclicker were both required and they were both fine. GO TO CLASS AND TAKE GOOD NOTES!!! AND STUDY THOSE NOTES!
quizlet saved my life

I took bio 150 over the summer. This lecture is typically offered in person during the school year although there is an online section. There is a ton of reading and assignments and it is very fast paced, but the work is fairly easy and can be completed for the most part within a few hours. Online tests are open note. Overall would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Easiest A I've gotten at KU. Ended with 99%. Just do the HW, it's free points, directly from notes or online. Online format didn't waste my time in lectures. Group assignments were easy, but my group was very slow. No tests, and can finish as quickly as possible. I finished 4/8 weeks in one day of grinding. Take it for the A in a science credit.

BIO 100 is a non-major biology class. There are no exams or tests because she realizes that there is no point to go super hard on students who are all non-majors. If you show up and do all the assignments it is an easy A. Also the lectures were really fun and actually interesting to learn about.

Online version is asynchronous and really easy to complete. Professor Marriage is easy to communicate with and she posts a lot of announcements so you are never in the dark. A couple easy extra credit opportunities but you won't really need them if you complete the work. Discussion Board posts, lectures, quizzes and Exploratory Assignments.
loved how she taught online
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Due to COVID-19, this class was completely online (asynchronous). This class was in conjunction with Dr. Holder, another nice biology professor. They really want you to have fun learning biology and not feel pressured, so there were ZERO exams. We were graded on lecture quizzes, group discussion boards, and weekly "exploratory" assignments.

Good prof. Dr. Marriage was always available outside of class to answer any questions I had. The class itself was pretty straightforward with lectures, outside pre and post-class assignments, and tests. There is a group portion to the tests that will help bring your overall test grade up. Overall if you show up and study you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Since it is a big lecture class, you get separated into groups with about four people per group for the entire semester. You are graded off clicker questions, the bluebook questions, bio quizzes online outside of class and the tests. The tests are easy and they drop your lowest test grade. Just show up to class and you will be good for an A.

Go to class/ do clicker questions and do all the pre-class assignments. pay attention in lectures because that will be what's on the test. You don't have to read the book often and you don't need to do a lot of studying either. as long as you do your work you should be fine regardless of your group.

I had two teachers for this lecture and they both taught very well. Sometimes the lecture can become boring but for the most part the information is easy to understand. There are 2 quizzes every week that require reading in the textbook and the tests are taken directly from quizzes and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: she is so kind!!! i created a sincere relationship with her and her lectures were very interesting as well. def reccomend going to her with any questions and not just using her to pass.

This class was very difficult. Expectations were very high for a 101 course, and the homework load was overwhelming. Tom was hard to reach and meet with. When feedback was given it was vague, hard to understand and sometimes harsh. However, he did offer chances to improve grades, which was helpful in the end.

I loved having Tom as a professor, it felt like he really cared about his students and gave us good advice on how to succeed in class. BDS103 is a difficult course, there's a ton of homework and you absolutely have to come to class. However, I thought Tom explained/critiqued my work well and really helped me improve my drawing ability.

Tom is a great guy, cares about his students. Approachable if you ever need anything. If you get bored in his class just talk to him after and give him suggestions about how to make class more engaging. He's ready to listen.

great professor, i improved so much in his drawing class! hes a super caring dude and gives great critiques without being rude, and always phrases them in a kind but constructive way. we always would chit chat and is super approachable :

Here's the thing about Tom. He will talk for the entire 3 hour studio.. every day. Just when you think you'll get time to work or discuss a project he'll find something else to talk about. Likes to be constant center of attention. Arbitrary grading, weird manditory reading assignments. He works on personal projects during class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I loved Tom!! I always looked forward to class because he really cares about what he teaches and how his students are doing whether in class or out. Drawing for design isn't an easy class, but Tom makes it enjoyable and gives helpful feedback. Super fun an easy to approach.

Omg let me tell you something about tom. He only cares about the ID students and couldn't care less about any one else. His time during class is spent helping the students he deems worthy and ignoring the rest of the class. If he doesn't like you then don't expect any help or feedback on even the smallest of things. Also he dosen't answer emails.

reviews.comment: BDS Studios are where you have to depend on each other, mostly because Tom is not a resource you can rely on. He never reads an email and picks favorites, mostly ID students. reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tom is a teacher you take if your really want to learn. If you don't get along with Tom, you are the problem not Tom. He grades tough because he wants to see his students do as good as possible not just slide by. A lot of the reviews here are overly dramatic, so take them with a grain of salt. I've taken three classes with Tom so far. Good Teacher.

reviews.comment: The class was well organized and I appreciated his feedback. Its obvious he is passionate about his work and pushes his students to a professional artistic standard. However, I found his feedback vague with a harsh demeanor. He wasnt good about checking emails and missed class which wouldnt be acceptable for students. I would not recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I had Tom for a drawing class and a design class (glorified woodshop class).  Both classes were well organized until it came to evaluating your work.
