Always available for help... Difficult prof though.
No Comments
Max doesn't look carefully at your work... make sure to impress him on the first assignment and he'll back off some for the rest of the semester.
No Comments
No Comments

I would not suggest taking this class unless you are really, really interested in going into the community side of behavioral sciences. The class is all based on a group project, and the time during class is spent talking about the things Dr. Francisco has done throughout his career and working on a group project that is super repetitive.

While he seems very experienced in his career field, the structure of this class is confusing and unorganized. Group projects were tedious and repetitive, and he would never answer questions effectively. Deadlines were confusing, for assignments would be due at 1:30pm, 5:00pm, on random weekdays. Respectfully, never again.

This class is a rough one. It all surrounds a group community service project you work on the entire year. His grading criteria is confusing. He seems very nice and definitely has passion for what he does but I do not see a point in coming to lecture. He does not really lecture on what we are working on.

He's an interesting guy that's lived an interesting life. He's very qualified to teach. I found the content boring- it wasn't taught in an interesting way, but it's not a bad class. He talks about his experiences and we work on a group project every class. Beware of heavy reading he assigns at the start of the course. Community service is required.
A king among peasants.

A group project was the main focus of the semester. We were to come up with a hypothetical community project but it isn't very motivating if you don't actually do the project. All you do during class is work on the group project. He doesn't lecture, just talks about his experiences. Also, he failed to give clear deadlines, so there was no structure
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The course title is Building Healthy Communities. Im a premed student so the class seemed relevant. I have yet to learn anything about communities. The class is just a huge group project that is completely made up (he doesnt teach anything). The TA tells my group that our project looks great then we get counted off by Fransisco. No communication!
This was an easy class, but there were no clear deadlines! My group mates and I were very confused on what need to be done by when. There was also no clear grading criteria. 7/10 don't recommend
No good, hes very difficult to learn from.
Essentially reads off of the slides, and doesn't teach whatsoever. The the ta has to teach lecture all over again in the lab section to compensate, and thankfully save the class.
Reads off the slideshow, doesn't know what he's talking about.
He reads directly off the slides and sounds like he knows nothing about aerospace
Not sure how he has a job teaching
a  v o i d

Lots of online course homework that is not used as material for tests. What is used/given for test prep is unhelpful and irrelevant when the test does come around. Material on the tests that was not taught or given once. Reads of slides and is not helpful when trying to learn.

He read straight off the slides and often didn't finish them. TA's for the class were amazing and taught me everything, but I learned nothing from VJ. Slides were often wrong and had to be corrected by TA's, and he would put questions on the test that were never discussed. Shout out the TA's Jackson, Garret, and Will for making the lab fantastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The first midterm had a grade of 70 (WITH EXTRA CREDIT!) I went to every single lecture and would learn more from the TA's Office Hours (Shoutout Garrett, Will, and Jackson) than I ever did the 50 minute lectures. It was clear he only read off of the slides and threw questions into the exams and homework that we never once touched upon during class
I have no idea what I learned in this class.

He always seems uninterested in the course. Even though it's entry-level, you can't expect to learn much unless you teach yourself. He reads slides in a monotone voice, often doesn't finish them, and yet he still expects you to know the material he skips or spends very little time explaining for the exam.

VJ did a poor job communicating and teaching the material. Lectures were largely unhelpful, and we were often assigned homework on topics never covered in class. The TAs were excellent and essentially taught the course during review sessions. Without them, success would have been very difficult.

Honestly, the TAs taught more in this class than VJ did. VJ would always be super quiet during lectures, I could barely hear him and I was near the front. He gives HW about every week about topics he never finished lecturing about and gives very specific/unclear test problems. The TAs had to make multiple announcements in the final to clarify them.

Dr. VJ somehow manages to make the very interesting topic of aerospace extremely boring, unengaging, and completely uninspiring for students. The TA's essentially teach the whole class since the lectures leave out homework related material, needed equations, and anything usable for exams. Overall, the TA's are fantastic, but the professor is awful.

VJ is probably a nice guy, but he shows no effort towards his class. The TAs are great and, unfortunately, had to deal with VJ's mistakes. The only good lectures I had from this class were when the department chair of Aero (Dr. Hale) taught ethics (when VJ was gone for a month). Overall, VJ shows a very surface-level understanding of his own class.

Dr. VJ doesn't seem to be invested in teaching AE 245. He always shows up and reads off the slides; I learned far more from the TAs than I ever learned in lecture. Labs for this course are great when you have the right group, and overall, the only downside to this course is Dr. VJ.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't expect to learn anything in this class. IF he teaches, its the same thing over and over again with no progress then randomly backtracks to stuff he SHOULD'VE been teaching AGES ago. Avoid his classes if you can, if you can't I wish you luck on learning anything at all.

This professor does not know the course materials at all. He constantly messes up on in-class examples. I was expected to know many different codes for the test that I was not taught in class. The homework makes no sense. Overall, the class is not easy if you take no liberty in teaching yourself. He does not teach you enough to pass the class.

Absolutely horrible. He thinks he is the smartest person to walk this earth. Teaches you nothing related to aerospace. Consistently messes up on in class examples then expects you to be able to do them on your own. Assigns an insane amount of busy work. Stay away from him.

Dr. VJ's lectures seem very unprepared and he never goes all slides; the class was more cosmetic than actual information. Both the students and the TA's had to suffer because he would change deadlines and even details of various projects at the last moment. Seems to care about students but not specifically with helping them learn.

Dr. Urie is one of my favorite professors I've had at KU. She made hnrs western civ so interesting and engaging. Each week there are assigned readings, some of which are longer than others, and a prerecorded lecture to watch. There is also a discussion section in which you are graded on participation. I would recommend Dr. Urie's class to everyone!
Has absolutely no business teaching. Worlds worst teacher. I've met bricks with higher intelligence.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Urie was absolutely incredible for honors western civ! Half of the classes were lectures and half were discussions over the readings. Her lectures were always so interesting and engaging. She was also extremely good at leading meaningful discussions. Loved this class! Make sure you talk during discussion because you are graded on it :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Regardless of what amount of effort you put into the class, if you ask her for info on why your grade is low, she will always say you seem to not put in enough effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very harsh grader. Have to take notes on readings for in-class discussions and she will grade them very harshly. She's nice enough if you talk to her in person and form a connection, but she will likely grade you harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Urie was simply amazing. Her class was well organized, set up to allow students to be successful if they did the assigned work, and extremely enjoyable. Her grading was very fair and she gave clear feedback - both positive and where improvement was needed. She's a must take for humanity students at the University of Kansas.

I'm a non traditional student who needed to take 4 classes 40 years after starting and Ms Urie's class was the first one I took - I was nervous. She did such a good job targeting lessons to prepare the class for texts and assignments. The class was not easy, but if you followed her direction carefully, you can score well.
He is very intelligent and great at leading class discussions. Speaking of which, the class requires a large amount of discussion and willingness to speak up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great professor for my honors Western Civ class. It was I didn't expect to like to like too much and wasn't my fav of the semester, but I felt she made a core credit class interesting and appropriately challenging. It is possible, though quite difficult, to do well in the class without doing much reading, because she grades on discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Urie is the best teacher/professor I have ever had. The way she lectures is both unique and engaging. I was always excited to go to her class, and I was honestly sad when it was over. While she expects your best work from you, it is all easily attainable. I highly recommend her as a professor and look forward to taking class from her again!

Fantastic teacher. This was an honors class, so she had very high expectations. She will show her frustration with you if she knows you aren't trying or didn't do the readings. As long as you read and at least try in discussion, this class is pretty simple. If you don't, she will be very hard on you. She is a very caring professor
Professor Urie was very available to help students. She responded to questions helpfully and presented difficult material in an interesting and engaging way. Really made class enjoyable.

I really enjoyed her! I was always really interested in the material and what she had to say. There was a lot of reading that you will discuss so be prepare to pick out important quotes. Participation is really important so be ready to talk. She's generous with grading the papers and the tests. Highly recommend!

Prof. Urie is an absolutely amazing teacher at KU. She will challenge you to consider ideas and how they led to actions. She has an interesting take on history but won't push an agenda on you. She rather shows the full spectrum of the ideas she has you look at. Phenomenal discussions, must talk at least 2-3 times to get full credit. Good class

Dr. Urie is an incredible professor who is willing to help you, but the respect you give to her class is the respect you can expect to receive back. Work hard and you'll learn something that goes well beyond just history. She's fun and very personable so don't be afraid of her!

I took HWC/EURS 435 last year. One of the best classes I've ever taken. Dr. Urie is smart, funny, fair and approachable. She makes you read a lot, and participation is absolutely mandatory. But if you do the work and comment a few times per class, you can get an A no problem. This class changed the way I look at the world. Highly recommended.

Dr. Urie is an amazing professor. She is funny, entertaining, informative, and leads good discussions. The materials she assigns to read are not easy, but the lectures are super helpful and her discussions are well guided. Easily one of the most enjoyable classes I have taken at KU. Not the easiest grader, but hard work can get you an A.

I'm not interested in history at all (I took the class more for the philosophical aspect) but her lectures were extremely interesting. Essay/short answer questions on the tests, but you got the questions beforehand. Loved the class
She was ok at first but she became a really tough grader and is condescending when you ask for an explanation of why your grade ended up the way it did.

Dr. Urie is by far my favorite professor I have had a KU. Her lectures are informative and extremely interesting. There is one midterm and one research paper and you must participate in discussion. Honestly, this is the best class I have ever taken at KU. Also, she does not promote stereotypes, but she presents multiple viewpoints on this subject.

I learned more in this class than all my other history classes combined. Dale is the best teacher I've ever had. She made every class very interesting. The work was not hard, just read and then make an outline of the reading. Only one paper and one test; participation makes up a big portion of the grade.

Prof. Urie's class was the best I've taken in four years at KU. It was once per week for 2.5 hours and every single discussion stayed lively and interesting. Not particularly difficult either: only one paper of 10 pages and an in-class midterm.

Fair and consistent grading, but it is not an easy A. Course material is complex, but she allows all opinions, if you can defend yours. For the record, she does not hate Islam, but dislikes the way it is being used by individuals and organizations.

Grade is evenly split between discussion, 4 short response papers, midterm, and the final. She allows and encourages you to get pretty tangential on the response papers. The midterm/final is just regurgitating short answer/essay prompts that she gives you a week in advanced. She is good at lecturing, but terrible at leading an engaging discussion.

I had heard horror stories about Western Civ, but Prof. Urie was a really good teacher. You were required to write 4, two-page response papers, take two tests, and partake in discussion, and that was all to her class. Her lectures were often very interesting. The only thing that drug was the discussion but that is dependent on who's in your class.

Professor Urie is one of the best teachers I have ever had! She might be a difficult teacher and require a lot of reading, but I have learned more in her class than any other class this semester. If you take a class from her you will not regret it. She is also really helpful, funny, and nice. Highly recommended.

Dr. Urie is in no way qualified to teach about Islam. Her class is entirely focused on "Clash of Civilizations"and western superiority. She is not objective or knowledgeable about Arab cultures, Islam, or M.E. history. Her class depicts Muslims as problems in Europe perpetuating stereotypes and hatred. This class only encourages ignorance.

Brilliant lecturer! Prof. Urie brings ancient texts to life with irreverent humor and verve. She's great to chat with as well. Also, people say her tests are hard, but a more accurate description would be tedious. She tells you what you need to know. The rest is drilling it. Can't recommend her highly enough.

Great teacher, but class is hard. What is expected on tests is clearly defined and you know what to study, but it still takes a lot of time. The discussion was painful because there were a lot of people and she grades on quantity AND quality of participation. It was hard to get enough words in. Otherwise, as good of experience as one can expect.

One of the best teachers I've ever had at KU! She is an extremely intelligent woman but you have to be prepared to work your ass off. To get an A, I didn't miss a single day and said at least 3 comments each discussion class, discussion is worth 30%. But it was worth the work because I feel like I've learned more in her class than any other at KU.
Fantastic experience!

Must participate in discussion, but Prof. Urie makes it easy because she is nonjudgmental on comments. Her lectures are interesting, and she makes concept clear to students. Her midterm and final are difficult, but not impossible. She is willing to help you study if you go see her.
This woman is amazing. I was scared to take W. Civ, but she made me love this class. So much fun! lectures are interesting and discussions are fun. I would suggest to take it from her!

Wonderfully nice, and very willing to help you if needed. However, class is very difficult if this isn't your favorite subject, and discussion is crucial (and pretty painful if you don't like to discuss) very very hard, but not miserable because she makes it very interesting. if your looking for an easier class however you want to pick someone else

My favorite class at KU so far.  Its a lot of work... but the content is interesting and useful.  The class is discussion/attendance based but you get points just for talking.  She is interesting and intriquing.  I am taking another class with her because i really enjoyed this one!  Definitely take a class with her if you can!

brilliant woman! it was a pleasure to be in her class; her lectures actually make history interesting and relevant. as the previous poster said, attendance and contribution to discussions is a major part of your grade, but such is the case in all western civ classes. not a coasting class but one that you will value beyond credits. A++ professor

Took the class at JCCC, but same format as KU.  You know from the first day what is expected of you.  You HAVE to go to class and read the book pages because so much of your grade is based on having insightful discussion topics.  Tests are cake because you already know the questions.  Dr. Urie is kinda hot too.

I didn't like the class at all but she made it bearable.  A must to take good notes and participate in discussions.  She gave us a list of questions for the test and then she picked so many off the sheet.  A hard grader but if you work hard and talk during discussion its not too bad.
love her.

She changed my life, and I'm not exagerating.  The best professor I had at KU.  A very intelligent woman who says what she thinks but has the knowledge to back it up.  Discussion does matter, but she lets you say be pretty free with what you say, and the smaller classes of her's are fantastic.  Take a class from her, and you too will love her!
Go to class, take notes, read, you'll do great, she's really helpful.

When you go book shopping, you might think this class is impossible, but she makes it really interesting. She gives study guides for the final and midterm that have all the short questions on it and the major essay. Discussion pulls your grade down unless you talk a lot. It is the same percentage of your grade as the midterm and 4 papers.
I had her at JCCC and she was awesome

Not the greatest class.  She is good at explaining things, but the discussion part was difficult because the class was so large.  It is hard to make an A in the class because of it.  Very relevant though.

I had her (yes HER) T/R lecture and discussion WCiv 1 class and it wasn't that bad. The biggest pain in the ass is the fact that discussion is 30% of the grade. A lot of us complained about this in the teacher evaluation so maybe she'll change it. Otherwise a VERY smart woman with great insight. Not an easy A but not impossible either.

I NEVER write rate my professor reviews, but Professor Vanderhurst has easily been the best professor I've ever had. Be ready to receive real feedback that's extremely helpful, even if a little humbling in the moment lol. She's more accommodating than most profs and will spend time with you outside and inside class to make sure you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I've taken several classes with Dr. Vanderhurst, and it's true that she can be a tough grader and tends to assign larger projects. But you can tell that she truly wants you to succeed and has a passion for her work. If you communicate with her she is more than happy to help you get the resources you need to be successful in her class.

Dr. V is very kind and caring. If you need an extension or have a problem, she is incredibly understanding. I took her class, Sex and Power, for my honors seminar. The class is very interesting and a lot of fun. There was a decent amount of reading each week and two informal papers throughout the class. I would highly recommend her and this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Incredibly surprised by negative reviews here. Took 1 credit ("Sex & Power") seminar, so not much hard work expected, mostly just discussion over readings. Vanderhurst is intelligent and quite kind in discussion, felt conversations flowed smooth and were productive. Would enjoy taking a WGSS class with her in the future.

Took during pandemic. Dr. V was knowledgeable & hilarious while discussing the course concepts. We had informal short papers (1-2 pages) due every Sunday, with a longer, formal paper due 3x during the semester that was built off of the shorter papers. Participation was required, but we had several forms of participation we could choose from.
Stacey is amazing. She's my nicest teacher at KU! She really cares about her students and keeps the work load small for a one credit hour class. Wish I could take this every semester!

WGSS 301 (being renamed to 501 I think?) was so unnecessarily hard because of the way she teaches. She presents the material in a confusing way and makes her quizzes/tests nearly impossible. She gave a midterm in which 50% of the class did not have time to finish and she had to curve it like 10% to even it out. Good luck

Vanderhurst knows what she is doing and what she is talking about. She is credible and intelligent. Sometimes this gets in the way when material gets dense, as she can struggle to break it down. She takes feedback really well, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible. Is too wrapped up in her own anthropology experience to be good at teaching a WGSS class. Gave a vocab quiz on terms that arent in the textbook and never gave concrete definitions on. Is incredibly patronizing and full of herself. Easily the worst WGSS prof KU has.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ohhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh. No thanks. Wouldn't recommend her. Please don't take this class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Worst teacher ever in KU.

The Professor is so awefull. Gives very little details in the emails and she is so unprofessional. She should be living in a trash bin. She will blame you for every single thing. She knows nothing about anything.

Dr. Vanderhurst is a great professor and honestly cares about her students, her research, and our learning. Even though attendance is optional you should come to class. The weekly logbook assignments can be tough but they prepare you so well for the final project. Show up and pay attention (especially in the first half) and you'll do great
Took a 100 level course for my last semester of college. Hardest online class I've ever taken. Definitely would not recommend. The amount of homework you have every week is insane.

40% of the grade is participation & students expressed concern abt this & lack of grading feedback, yet there was little effort made to improve the course. 2 students were allowed to regularly control the discussion. Every class it was "so what did you think of the reading" for 75 mins instead of small groups, response questions, and/or activities.

Honestly a boring class. Dr. Vanderhurst was a great professor, but the material was unnecessary. I'd definitely take a class with her again because when she spoke about her own research it was FASCINATING. I just feel terrible that she got stuck having to teach a new and dumb class.
She is very engaging and understanding!

She stopped speaking in English after the first week. The homework is what youre going to learn the next day and was often really difficult. Class consists of doing assignments almost exactly the same as the homework the night before and not much actual teaching. takes attendance everyday and rarely excuses absences. Hard to learn spanish from her
I took SPAN 328 and she is a great professor. Very kind, funny, and supportive. Willing to answer questions. A lot of easy homework to ensure class discussion and participation.

She didn't teach my class, but the Spanish department needs MAJOR work. So much online hw, and NONE of it was discussed in class. Why do so much, then come to class which is 25% of your grade just to do silly, meaningless activities instead? Also, there are absolutely NO late penalties/allowances with anything. I retained barely any information.

Etty is very kind and understanding. There is a lot of homework for this class, but none of it is overly difficult. The tests are done in groups. As long as you complete your homework, show up to class, and put in some effort, you should be just fine. She made this class lots of fun!

This class is simply not meant for online. Homework piles up to the point where it gets overwhelming. I was not expecting how easy it is to fall behind. If you miss one day of class/homework, you already have a C for that week. The bulk of your grade is participation and completion points on homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is very sweet. She is from Puerto Rico, so her accent can make it hard to understand when she is speaking quick spanish. Do all of your homework and participate in class and you should be good to go. Do not skip class otherwise your grade will definitely reflect. Even one day can make you grade go down.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: etty speaks in spanish the entire time, which was fine for me because I took 3 years in highschool- but most of the class had not ever taken a spanish class before. if you have an issue, talk to her because she is all for helping her students succeed. she is sooooo sweet. I will miss her!

Seth is an amazing professor who clearly loves the topic he teaches. I highly recommend taking any of his courses. I love the personal stories he adds to his lectures that go along with the topic we are talking about. The course had really interesting topics and gave a chance to deep dive into conversations that are hard to talk about.
The literal best teacher ever. Taking his other class because he was awesome
Amazing professor who truly cares about his students and his career!!! He is incredible

Professor Wescott was unlike any professor i've ever had. His passion for his work and field is inspiring and is really shown through his incredible lectures, guest speakers, and video testimony. He is very knowledgeable about the content and had very engaging classes. If you are interested in Criminal Psychology, I highly reccomend!

DO NOT BE INTIMIDATED BY THE REVIEWS. She's an amazing professor who has a real passion for what she teaches, and you can hear it in her lectures. Her passion towards physiology makes the lectures so easy to follow. Sure, the content is a really detailed but there's no getting around it. Tests are really easy if you pay attention in class.

Exercise physiology was extremely difficult to pass. The only credit you get in the class is tests and quizzes. Nothing else to help pad your grade. Tests are curved though. She lectures as if her students are already professionals in the field. Doesn't simplify anything at all.

she doesn't deserve the amount of hate that she gets. she is passionate and knows what she is talking about. she wasn't the most empathetic compared to my other professors, but her knowledge made up for it. if you put in the work, you can get an A. she also curves a LOT which is nice when the class is very exam heavy. attendance isoptional
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her and her husband are a JOKE!! Extremely unprofessional telling students they won't be successful in future careers for asking a simple question. Asks for students advice but then gets mad at the class for listing too many cons and didn't change anything we asked for. I've never wished for someone to lose their job, but I do wish both of them do.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have loved taking classes with Dr. Weir, not sure why she gets bad reviews. Her lectures aren't recorded, but as long as you go to class, or get notes from someone in class if you miss, you'll be fine. Plus she gives a study guide which helps a lot. And she's super helpful if you go to her office hours. Can't say enough good things about her!
As someone who is Pre-PT, I really enjoyed the content of this class. Everything was super relatable to my daily life and in the clinic as a rehab aide. I would highly recommend.

I don't get why she gets such bad reviews. If you go to class and study you can achieve a good grade. No, she doesn't record her lectures but the textbook is extremely helpful if you did have to miss a class. Her exams are pretty straightforward and she ends up curving them quite a bit.

Terrible. Most slides are just pictures that she talks about and without lecture recordings I can't go back to see what I didn't write down or to review difficult material. If you can avoid taking a class with her, i recommend it. Go to class even if you're sick because you'll have no clue what was taught from just slides given.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrible. Attendance is mandatory. Doesn't record lecture and PowerPoints are mostly wordless pictures. No assignments, only quizzes and exams. Cumulative final. You would be better off taking over the summer or at Edward's campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely hated this class. Attendance is mandatory as she doesn't record lectures and her PowerPoints are all pictures. You would be better off taking over the
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The entire class is test-based. The only other grades were online quizzes that are basically worth nothing once you take tests. Your entire grade is made up of tests, it's awful.

Bad teacher who doesn't care about teaching and most likely just wants to research. Everything is online including the midterms and finals so very easy A. Does have a iClicker for attendance which counts towards your grade. Most just use as a study hall.
he doesn't give a lot of homework and all quizzes and test are taken at home and he is super sweet

This class is super easy, just has a lot of work. But you can find most of it online. He says it is a flipped classroom but it really isn't. You don't have to show up at all. I used it as a study hall.
If you fail this class or dislike it, you have either no work ethic or no brain cells. Potentially both. Great professor.

not sure what all the bad reviews are for. People act like they truly care about their education and not just want the stupid credit. Great professor, flipped class, easy (needs some effort) assignments twice a week with quizzes on top. I put 2 hours of work every week towards the class and finished with a C after skipping damn near 10 assignments

Flipped Classrooms are the worst. I stopped showing up to lecture after week 2. Class is made up of 2 weekly 5-question quizzes, 2 weekly assignments & 2 Exams, all of which are conducted via blackboard. Many of the assignments come straight from online resources. I seriously question how much effort Prof. Van Der Veen puts into teaching, if any.

He does this thing called a "flipped classroom", which in my opinion is the most ridiculous thing because what am I paying so much money for? He is also very hard to understand because of his thick accent and is not good at explaining things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: knows what he is talking about for his profession but really shouldnt be teaching. never awnsers emails and makes you feel dumb. should really give study guides for the tests or at least have a better review session. either find a different professor, drop the class, or do credit no credit because hes not helping you

Soooo ya just dont take him for geography. No one in my class felt like they learned much. He makes you feel dumb for answering questions and asking questions. Smart guy for his field but such an awful teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This professor literally knows NOTHING. You can ask him a question and he will stutter and a TA will have to answer. He tells you the wrong things to study for on tests. The things he says to worry about are not on the tests, and the things he says to not worry about are ALWAYS on the tests. He needs to leave this department.
You can tell he doesn't care about the students. He just needs to teach in order to be qualified for research. Very vague, dry, and awkward. Smart guy but not a good teacher at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Boring lectures. Seems like he is very smart but just is not meant to teach. Taught by 3 teachers and they ran the class. His sections were hard to sit through. DO the EXTRA CREDIT
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HIM!!!! He is vague, yet demanding. His instructions are never clear but he wants very specific answers. I am almost always an A/B student and I failed his class. You would think after several years with people struggling he might catch on that he might be a problem; but he always teaches class with the air we're morons.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Course had 3 professors and was very disorganized. His lectures were the worst. Not engaging at all, and I couldn't understand any of the material. Lots of awkward pauses when he asked questions or just randomly stopped. Would not recommend professor or course.

In the assignments the instructions were vague, but the things he was looking for were specific, he doesnt let you redo assignments, and we had to beg him for extra credit because our class of 12 had a low grade average. Overall Not a hard class but if you take it with Vanderveen and he doesnt like you, good luck

Every Geog 104 professor's section is difficult, Van Der Veen's is no different. I thought I could get away without reading the book, but those trying for an A or B, I realized, must read. The tests are difficult and the material comes directly from both his PowerPoint slides and the book. Do no get discouraged, though.. the class is curved.
Extremely hard class. The tests are impossible whether you go to class or not. Whatever you do DON'T take Geography 104 with him.

Whatever you do, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! He is literally the worst teacher I have had so far. His lectures are no help and his tests are ridiculously hard. I'm an A/B student and I found myself struggling to get C's on his tests. I had an A in the Lab section and a low C in his lecture, which is ridiculous. Just don't take this class with him!
Whatever you do, DO NOT take a class from this guy! He is the worst teacher I have ever had, grades extremely hard, gives no direction!

Do not take any class from this man. He is boring, monotone, and his go to phrases include "and what not" or "uhhhhhhhh" followed by silence. He is also quite full of himself. He did an entire hour and a half lecture about how him and his buddies disproved an article about the Himilayan glaciers melting in the next 20 years. Grades really hard.

He does nothing to make his lectures interesting. He is not helpful if you ask questions in class and he does not provide study guides or any test help. His test are random and you have to read all the material multiple times to be fully prepared. Do not take!

take this class with another prof who does online tests.  You'll get a better grade and wont need to attend class.  I am the kind of person who tends to be interested in classes like this but found myself falling asleep almost daily.

He doesn't take role which is nice and the slides gone over in class are online.  Cornelis is probably a nice guy but is not an interesting teacher AT ALL! He likes to say etc, ummmm eerr, and what not alot making it hard to understand the material. Pretty much if you ask him a question he will just make something up as well..so that's always cool.

She only reads the slides and does not teach. The practice problems she has us do are straight off the ALEKS, which she assigns. I had to teach myself all of the content. She does not follow her own syllabus and randomly has quizzes right after exams. She is a nice professor, but I would not recommend taking her class.

She is very nice, and she cares about what she does and her students. I actually took Math107 intro to stats, which is an easy class. I had a prolonged absence and she made sure I had all the make up material and helped me be successful.

She is very sweet but hard to understand. She just reads off slides. If you express to her that you want to do well in this class, she will make sure you do. I did poorly both exams but ended with an A still.

A very sweet professor. Difficult to understand. Just reads over powerpoints for lectures without explaining how to do problems which is very frustrating. I'm very good at math, but this class was beyond difficult. Tests were nothing like the homework or study guides. Do not take.

She is very kind but she reads through the lecture slides so fast that you aren't able to keep up or understand the material before she's onto the next slide. You end up having to teach yourself all the material. The study guides for the exams are no help either, as they are from a website that doesn't correlate to the exams.

I took MATH 365 over one summer. She is very strict on deadlines so you need to really stay on top of everything. Only the midterm and final were in person. All if the homework was on MyStatLab. Extra credit towards the final grade was rewarded if you turn a certain amount of assignments in on time.

I have never struggled so much in a math class. This was the worst class I have taken. She is super nice and wants to help but in class, she goes so fast I cannot keep up and even process to ask a question. Go to office hours and put all your effort into this class to do decent. She gives extra credit which helps. I recommend psych stats instead.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very kind person but the class was just really difficult. I have always gotten A's in my math classes but this was just a difficult math course in general, but it was hard to learn off of just reading slides. I'm a nursing major and if you are too, I would recommend getting a tutor or taking psych stats.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wang is a compassionate instructor and I enjoyed learning from her. I wouldn't agree with any of the other poor reviews, she is always wanting to help and loves when students ask questions in class. The material can be hard, but if you put in the work you'll do great. Go to class and do the homework and you'll receive extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is not hard as long as you're willing to do the work required to succeed. To fail, don't do the hw and show up to only exams. If you do the opposite of that, u will be fine. She is also pleasant and understanding of the fact that life happens. Take all these poor ratings with a grain of salt. If you put in effort, you will be rewarded.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I disagree with a lot of the bad reviews this professor has. She explained in-depth many examples in class. She didn't read off the slides and provided extra instruction on how she used a calculator to solve a lot of the problems. I personally learn math better by teaching myself but, had I needed it, I think she would have been a good teacher.

I am extremely good at math, this class is impossible. I had to teach myself everything. She reads off the slides and expects us to know what to do. HEAVY on homework load, hw and quizzes are all online graded by a computer. Nursing majors please take psych stats instead of this. She's hard to understand too. Attendance is not mandatory though!

Statistics will always be hard, no matter what teacher you have. However her lectures are really good, she has a very good understanding of stats and provides really helpful examples and goes through practice problems in class. The mystatslab or whatever for the online homework is kind of a pain though

yall... the class is not *that hard* i promise... though I did take this in person (tests too). The tests are decently fair and in-person. I showed up to maybe two lectures because the content isn't hard at all.(and I'm saying this not just as an engineering kid with a STEM ego with spite towards this required course)

No teaching from her end (fully online course), everything is on a website called Mystatlab. The website is the worst and marks you off for the tiniest errors. Exams are timed and difficult, quizzes have no time limit but a common trend I found was that I spent 3+ hours on them only to get 75%. Unresponsive over email and unhelpful. Take in person!

If you want a rigorous foundation, choose Dr. Wang's class! Like the others have said, this is not the most exciting class, BUT if you want to have a solid introduction to statisitcs, I highly recommend that you take this class. Weekly homework, one midterm and one final. Practice tests are really similar to the actual ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hardest class I have ever taken and its like she wants to make it hard. Homework is not graded personally rather by a website that counts off for minor things. With covid 19 she pre records a lecture then plays it on zoom. She does not get back to you in a timely manner at all, and when asked for further help about final I was told to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was difficult, and prof Wang didnt help that whatsoever. She held zoom sessions that were recordings and didnt even grade our homework personally. Our homework and tests were graded on mystatslab, which is very fickle and sometimes counts you off even when youve gotten the answer right. When confronted about this, she did nothing.
Really unorganized but respectable. Personally wouldnt take again.

I'd rather die than take this class again. All of her lectures were on slides that she just read off of and eventually during the zoom classes she would just play a recording of her teaching the class earlier. All homework and quizzes were on a website that she doesn't even grade, a robot does. I was teaching myself this whole semester.

Before quarantine, her lectures were boring and unhelpful as she simply read off of the slides. During quarantine, she stopped helping us completely and expected us to do the work ourselves. The quizzes and tests are way harder than the homework and lectures, and have different content than the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's a nice person, but as a teacher she isn't very helpful. She reads off of her powerpoint slides and goes over one example in class and expects you to be able to solve the problem. With all of the COVID stuff going on, she's not doing any zoom classes so rn all the material we have is the textbook and her pretty unhelpful slides :(
THE WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD. so inconsiderate. we never did one in class example and then were expected to know how to solve the problems.
gives extra credit for attendance on random days (20 points total). tests are exactly like study guides

Nice woman, but teaching habits should be reviewed. Will just read off of slides every class the whole time. You will still end up teaching yourself. A lot of random extra credit for showing up to class (attendance). Midterm/Final are similar to study guides. TA is your best friend; quizzes are HARSH; time consuming for a good grade (perseverance)
Shes terrible

The only way I passed this class with a decent grade was because attendance provided strong extra credit. The quizzes in this class were next to impossible, but in class tests weren't too bad. Her heavy accent makes her very hard to understand. She also rarely went through examples. I had to learn most of this class material on my own.

I love math, and this class was excessively difficult.... not because of the coursework but because of her inability to explain how and why we take the steps we do for the problems. She's hard to hear, pay attention to, and has no true way of predicting your grade.
I find myself not paying attention in lecture and only learning by doing the homework, hard to understand her.

Attendance is randomly checked. She does mumble and have an accent, but this is intro stat and one of the easiest math classes there are, so learning it yourself isn't hard. Do the homework and practice tests and you'll get the grade you deserve. She only gives 2 tests, (midterm and final) but are very similar to the HW and practice tests.

Based on what I actually do in class, I should have taken an online course instead. I show up, pull out my laptop, and teach myself through the online assignment while she stands up there quietly murmurs through the slideshows. I wouldn't show up if it weren't for the random extra credit participation and it being a quiet place to do Stat homework.

Just take the online class. You'll save yourself a lot of misunderstanding. She's unclear & reads off slides. You can kind of save yourself the before the midterm because that's just basic statistics, but after that it's every man for himself. You have to teach yourself a lot and there's a lot of homework for a basic statistics class. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: pay attention in class; it's a hot mess go to class for extra credit points. i was able to find all my homework on chegg.

She has better English compared to others. I would have taken the online class if I knew how bad this class was. Lecture is basically her reading the slides as you sit. It's the worst type of hostage situation. I would work on the homework in class and make my own notes during lecture, instead of listening.

Somewhat hard to understand but is VERY helpful. Study guides are incredibly similar to tests. Attendance will give you extra credit points (saved me on the final), and she goes over how to do homework problems in class. Always happy, and the powerpoints she has provide in depth examples.

As with any Math class all of the things listed above matter. I would have been happy with that if I had understood a work she said. I ended up taking the class twice and withdrew twice before the midterm. She is awful and should not be teaching class until her English is better, that doesn't mean that she needs to speak she needs to comprehend it.

She was the worst teacher i have ever had! Stay way from her at all cost! was no help at all and cant speak well English  AT ALL! Had to have a translator in class with us! IF you want a hard class this is your class! I understand math well when it is explained. All she did was show power points and say okay understand and move on to the next slide

Lectures are long and boring but you don't need to go. You don't need them to do the labs or final project. Labs are dated and confusing. But Dr. Li is very nice and knowledgeable and a reasonable grader.

Dr. Li is very passionate about GIS systems and mapping, and it most certainly shows in his lectures. However, the only grades for this course (minus the lab) come from a midterm and final. He lectures the entire time and goes through slides very quickly. This course was very unenjoyable and I wouldn't take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best GIS professor at KU by far! Really passionate about his research and really wants you to do well. That being said, he will challenge you. Be prepared to work hard and don't be afraid to ask questions. He will help you but you have to reach out.

I really like his class a lot. I took two of his classes -programming and 658 and he is my favorite professor!! His grading is super fare. His materials are well organized. You can ask for help :) He replies your emails!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Doesn't explain material completely.  Supposed to be an intro course, but doesn't grade on fundamentals of programming rather then your understanding of math.  Provides you the formulas to do calculations but then says there wrong or doesn't explain how to implement then correctly in the python code.  Expects everyone to have knowledge of these things.  Trigonometry and calculus should be prerequisites thise who aren't strong in math are getting shafted.  Over half the class is failing

Extremely hard to understand, does explain material fully, expects you to know materials not covered in book or in class, provides you with incomplete information ad expects to to find out its not complete or wrong on your own.  supposed to be an introductory class, but material and knowledge expected you already to know should dictate prereqs

I LOVED the lab portion of this class. Li is very smart and really awesome to talk to outside of class but the class itself was too long. Each day he would talk all class period long around the hour mark I just couldn't pay attention anymore. With that said, he is extremely helpful but good luck with the midterm and final, they KILLED my grade.
Overall a great teacher.  Can be a little hard to understand at times, but still does a great job.
Great teacher.  Knows his stuff and is very helpful.  Doesn't baby students who can't keep up. Challenges students who can.
Good and helpful professor. But the TA is a tough grader, and I receive B for homeworks most of the time

He gives 20 homework problems per week sometimes they take too long but as long as you do not wait till the last minute you should be fine. Only one midterm was nice. He walked through steps off printed out problems instead of writing them out which got to be hard to follow at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
He doesn't always understand your question the first time you ask it, but he's very willing to help. The posted lecture notes are a lot less helpful than when you go to class, but still useful if you miss a lecture. 
Midterms/final were much easier than the homework and very similar to review questions AND he gives extra credit on them.

His lectures were mostly reading off slides which was not very helpful. Whenever he did work through problems on the board, he was super clear and easy to understand. He responds to emails pretty quickly and gives good feedback to questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is hard. But Xu does try and make it as easy as possible. Our first exam was so low he let us make corrections to help us improve our grades. Final was open notes.

Professor Xu cares a lot about his students. He gave us the option for +/- at the beginning of the course. Some of his more theory-heavy lectures were really dull, but we were never tested on it. The exams were a lot easier than the hw. His English is really good and his lectures engaging. You only really need to go to class to turn in hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Crazy amount of homework, but otherwise a pretty easy class. Hongguo is a gem of a professor, you will not regret taking it with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Doesn't use BB, which is annoying for grade checking. Not super test heavy (only 60% of grade), teaches very close to the book, so you don't really have to go besides for HW turn-in or for tests. Nice guy, answers questions, knows his stuff. Chegg recommended for homework. If you understand HW, tests are a piece of cake, HW problems harder.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had very similar experience with calc 2 as calc 1 - a prof accustomed to teaching graduate-level courses, who mostly reads off the slides and doesn't add much on his own. Dr. Xu was perfectly competent and willing to answer questions, but didn't really capture our attention or respect. You could probably skip lecture if you studied the book.
Professor Xus Math 590 has been one of the best courses I have taken. He is a very proficient professor and very helpful with homeworks. Do not hesitate to take any course he offers.

Gives excellent class notes on his site. Homework is clear, but it is strictly due every week with no late assignments accepted. All tests are take home and fair. Most people skipped every class, but I thought his lectures were helpful and engaging.

Professor Xu is a great professor. He was very straightforward; he taught us some numerical methods, and then he gave us homework over them. All of the tests were take-home, which seemed appropriate for the class. Challenging if you fall behind, but very easy if you stay caught up. Also, his English is fantastic. No textbook; lecture notes online.
Very good lecturer. The material is very difficult but he does a good job of explaining it and he pretty entertaining at times. I really enjoyed this proffessor and I would take  him again.

He goes through lectures very quickly and he has a thick accent, so i couldn't understand anything.  I gave up going to lecture because it was a waste. Test's are fair, and there is usually a 10% curve on each test. I got an A in the class and i only attended lecture about 4 times. The calculus help room was my saving grace.
I actually have no idea how Xu is as a professor -- I went to 2 lectures all semester and got an A. The exams were challenging but fun.
Lectures are okay, could be skipped if you use the book. No quizzes, speaks absolutely awful english.

Xu knows his stuff.  He is very thorough in his explanations, and offers insights into other areas of math.  He runs a help room for the course.  Read the material before class.  He covers a lot of ground in every lecture and you won't have time to write everything down.  I took pictures of his notes on the projector and reviewed them after class.
Simply the best math professor here at KU. Incredibly intelligent, clear, approachable, and helpful. He clearly cares a lot about his students and will do everything he can to help you succeed.

Very good teacher. Has somewhat of an accent so the first few days are hard to understand but after that you understand him. Tests are very straightforward,no tricks. Very flexible if you have a legitimate problem. Follows the book closely but uses his own examples and add bits of useful info. Was coordinator for 122 this semester.

His lectures always went over by a minimum of 5 minutes and most of the time it was 10 minutes after. Midterm exam: he told us to know the concepts and not the formulas. What happened? The entire exam was plug-and-chug using the formulas. Half the class flunked and this was the only exam other than the final. Terrible professor!
GREAT TEACHER!  He was a little difficult to understand at first, but he was always available to help.  He also posted really good review problems before each test.
GREAT TEACHER!  A little difficult to understand at first, but he was always able to help.  He also posted really good review sets for the tests.
Great professor! He's very organized and extremely helpful. He really cares about his students and his teaching, and he really enjoys it. He also lectures at just the right pace.

One of my favorite professors of all time. He is hard to understand at first, but you'll get used to it. The tests are straight forward, & the assignments revolve around lecture. If you are confused, GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS --he is one the most helpful professor I've ever had. If you put in the effort you can get an A easily. I highly recommend him.

His lectures are sometimes hard to follow, but he is very friendly and helpful, and will take a lot of questions.  He puts very good study guides on his website, and there are no surprises on his tests.  Homework due every class, but the assignements are usually about four problems.
Great teacher, helpful office hours, gives you pre-exam study guides, exams are straightforward (no tricks) If you can take a class from this guy, do so.
Hes the best Math teacher ever, very clear, and very goal driven and hes willing to help u out anytime. Just ask
I learn a lot more from reading the book than I do attempting to listen to this guy.
Very organized and goal-driven.  If you like outlines, you will love this man.
I enjoyed the class very well. Prof. Xu is an all-around good guy.

He was one of the nicest professors I've had. His class was not hard, and he didn't want you to fail. I submitted the final wrong and he gave me a chance after the due date to redo it and didn't give me late points.  Attendance is only mandatory because he would post a question every day that you could only access in class, but they weren't hard.
He is the best

Very chill guy. Gives good time to get projects in and allows plenty of extensions. His classes felt like a little bit of a waste of time and you only had to go because the reading participation questions make up a lot of your grade, but at the end of the day there's nothing much to complain about.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very caring and passionate professor.
He's the man.
Wen is a great professor. Very supportive and able to explain difficult topics in a clear and easy to understand way.

Wen is an absolutely amazing professor. ENGL 102 was my favorite class this semester as a human bio major. He will always try to have a conversation with you before class. Great professor who genuinely cares about you. Readings before each class, three papers, and one oral presentation. Highly, highly recommend this class. You won't regret it.
He was such a great professor! Will miss you lots Professor Xin!

best ever. No book, no attendence. Dr. Xin is a very cool teacher, easy to talk with and he loves to talk with you even not for the course. he does has some accent but that's alright, you just work on your papers and hard to not get A. Heard he's graduating next semester, so take the last chance guys!

Best class I have taken. Wen is amazing. He has shoe game the man wears yeezy's. Would recommend to everyone. Very laid back professor. If you show up, do all of your work, and at least act like you care there is no way you wont get an A or B

Unfortunately, I took 2 of Ron's classes, barely passed the first and had to drop out of second. I'm seriously considering going to KU about him, it doesn't matter how hard you try if he doesn't like you, you will fail. Yells at his students, never seen a professor hate his job so much that he takes it out on his students. Avoid him at all costs!

Class is so easy. The homework can be a bit hard if you aren't a film major but for the most part assignments are pretty simple. Lectures can be boring at times. Sometimes a strict grader. Very average professor.

Ron seems like a nice guy, but he comes off as a rather sporadic grader. Accused me of using AI on a paper and gave me a zero. Nearly two weeks later, suddenly regraded the assignment to a 7/10 without any explanation or notice. Later gave me an 8/15 on a paper for “not using scholarly sources.” My sources were from the KU library database.

3 hours can be long at times, but its a pretty chill class. as someone with attention issues, i lock in for the lecture, or do something simple while listening. he covers some stuff to do with the film of that night and then you watch the flim. I've gotten by working on other things during the film to stay focused. Good class, would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ive had him for 3 classes and honestly he's really not that bad. He can be a hard ass in lectures and those same lectures can be pretty boring but the guy is obviously very passionate about the subjects he teaches and the work load is reasonable. If you take the film major you will have him for a class so just show up and you'll be fine.

I have taken 4 of Professor Wilson's classes now, and though his classes can be later in the day and sometimes the movies you watch can be boring, I found Professor Wilson's class content to be insightful. I can overlook the aspects of his classes that I don't enjoy and look at the bigger picture; he is one of the best FMS professors at KU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ron is a thief of joy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Ron is the kind of professor to have an assignment due on the Friday before spring break, and another one due on the first Sunday after spring break.

This class is a 3-hour-long lecture, at 6 PM after a day of classes. Make sure not to fall asleep while watching very boring black-and-white movies about the atomic bomb, or he will yell at you and call you out in front of everyone. Also, prepare for quizzes on movies that are not yet covered in the class, long essay papers and discussion boards.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I have had Mr. Wilson a few times at KU and have always enjoyed his lectures. There are textbooks he assigns but I don't find them particularly necessary to read at times, usually the lecture will cover any material for papers. However, PDF readings are posted and should be read as they will be asked to be covered on papers. Overall a great class!

Ron was totally unprofessional. Ron never answered his emails, I remember sending countless emails on canvas and KU email and not once receiving a response. It seems I never got direct feedback from the professor, which makes it feel like he doesn't even read our work, just makes the TA grade everything. Ron yelled at 2 stdnts in front of 200 ppl.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Knows what he is talking about and cares about his students. Tries to learn all names

Lectures were pretty boring and long. Selection of movies was okay, he chose some odd ones. The reason I am rating him low is because he relies heavily on participation and I was in a class with 200 people which makes it hard. He also yelled at students in front of the whole class, which I felt was very unprofessional.

Overall pretty entertaining class, lectures could be a bit boring at times, but the films we watched kept the class pretty interesting. As long as you go to class and have a general understanding you should get an A. Assignments were mostly discussion board posts and short papers, with the final being a 7 page paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are way too long, and they're paced far too slowly. Mr. Wilson is clearly knowledgeable about film history, but his lectures are so hard to get through. With COVID-19 this year he's doing cohort classes that alternate between in-person and online week-by-week. For all intents and purposes, this has been a technical difficulty trainwreck.

This man managed to give three hours of the most boring lectures I've ever heard every class without fail. The biggest challenge was just retaining the willpower to not skip class. If you can avoid taking his classes, do.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really loved this class and Professor Wilson's teaching ethic.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Long and mind numbing lectures. You'll desperately want to skip his class every time, but you'll struggle with points if you do. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Wilson is a great lecturer. His presentations are informative as well as entertaining! I would definitely recommend taking one of his FMS 380 classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great Class! The teach was brilliant!

I took this class because it was a Trash Cinema class and I was hoping to have fun while learning about something I am interested in. Instead it was incredibly boring and horrible. It is so impressive that he could make a class about bad movies the most boring class I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Wilson's lectures can get a bit monotonous, but this is the best of the three classes I've taken from him. With 3 short papers, a research essay, and an essay-style final, you have to work for your grade, but he grades very fairly. He's big on discussion so go in ready to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Prof Wilson is a bit of a monotone lecturer, but his lectures are interesting and informative. During my class, there were two discussion boards, two essays, and two tests (midterm and final.) As these and attendance points were the only grades included, be prepared to work hard on these!! Wilson is a pretty hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Wilson is a very dry lecturer and makes his tests quite challenging. But if you get past this, he's a fine professor. Grades very fairly and appreciates when students participate and show effort.

Very informative lectures.  Discussion of films and readings are a large part of the course - if you speak up several times during the semester he notices.  He gets to know repeat discussers by name - which will help your participation grade!

Professor Wilson is a fine professor. Although, there were definitely times when I didn't completely understand his lectures. It's fairly easy to get an A, but expect to work for it (this is college after all).
Wonderful instructor.  Challenging but informative!
Literally blew me off when I politely and directly asked about if my topic fit, then when papers were graded they said mine didn't fit the requirements and gave it a zero.
Dr. Wilson is a great professor. He is really helpful and his class was a lot of fun!
Excellent class. Excellent instructor.  Really knows his stuff - and communicates it well. In my opinion he is the best instructor in the department, by far!
This was one of the best film classes I have taken in the department!  Professor Wilson is fantastic! Great teacher!
Mr. Wilson was very helpful and easy to talk to. Great guy. As long as you attend his class and speak at least once in discussion, you'll be fine!

Great instructor Knows his stuff and is extremely competent in his lectures and use of power point.  Discussions are instructive and thought provoking! My favorite teacher at the University of Kansas!!!

His lectures aren't always exciting, but he is very passionate about the material and knows his stuff. Class is fairly easy; show up, take quiz, and submit 3 papers throughout the semester. He is big on discussion, and encourages students to participate.
Great professor!! He is interested in his subject and in the students!
Straightforward, interesting subject.  Very knowledgable lecturer, kind of boring though.  Go to all the classes and do the work, or you'll do poorly.
Great prof, I have taken many classes with him and his lectures are informative, interesting, and structured. He won't let you get off easy, but he's one of my favorites in the film school anyway.

This class was so interesting. He is a great instructor and is very passionate about the subject. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS if you're just looking for an easy A. The midterms and final are ALL ESSAY and require insightful application of learned materials. and attendance is worth a quarter of your entire grade.
Great professor!  He makes the subject interesting and relevant.  Encourages class discusion after screenings and is prolific with his use of Blackboard.  Highly recommend taking one of his classes!

weird to say, but probably my favorite teacher in my college career. he knows his topics very well, especially gangster and violent films from all time periods. seems to enjoy what he teaches and makes things fun to pay attention to. quizzes are daily but i actually enjoyed going to his classes. tests and papers were graded very easily. fun teacher

Completely useless. 1/4th of our grade was based on attendance quizzes. It's all very easy and makes me wonder why I'm paying so much for a class that is taught at a junior high level. Seriously. Give me a break.

This guys is a walking talking IMDB.  I don't know anyone who actually dislikes this guy.  His tests are extremely easy.  The only hard part is an 8 page paper you have to write but the grading on that is still fairly easy.  I had him for pop culture of the 50's which was a bit of a let down.  His specialty I hear is violence and gangster films.

I read the ratings on Chuck Berg for this class but he had a medical problem and got stuck with Wilson for the American Gangster. His midterm was a **** and I kind of lucked into an A as a massive ice storm hit during the final and it got turned into a take home paper. Silent films sucked but as the timeframe progressed, it picked up. Id pass tho

Easy. Never cracked the textbook and still got a decent grade. Attendance is "mandatory" because of quizzes, but you can come in late. Also, the test and quiz material is basically all from his lectures, so if you listen you're fine. There is one big paper, but grading is pretty lenient. I got an A on it and didn't start until the night before.

Prof. Wilson is a really good prof. Though his lectures do tend to get monotonous at times, I still learned a lot from them. I totally disagree with those who say that his tests are hard because I found them to be a cakewalk and I was able to get an A in the class without having to study too much. All in all, I learned quite a lot from his class.

Boring, useless class. Attendance is a must because of daily quizzes at the end of class. Tests are hard and require endless memorization. Films are boring. His voice is monotonous. Very easy to fall asleep. Looong paper required. Take the extra credit if he gives it (it's worth a lot). Reading isn't mandatory, but it helps. I give him a C.

Most of the class is a breeze with a sprinkling of you've-got-to-be-kidding-me. A piddly paper proposal is 15% of your grade, but the SEVEN page horrid paper is 30%. He's pretty bland and obsessed with his specialty (gangster films, what a critical component of society...)

Prof Wilson isn't really all that exciting but our class is about American Gangster Film so we watch a screening each class period. The tests aren't extremely hard. If you attend class and review the material before the test you should be able to pass with an A. Their is a 7-9 page paper thats not all that fun
He is a good teacher. I had him for the American Gangster Film. Became my FAv class. he can get boring and his voice is monotone, but intresting lectures
not interesting, not helpful, BAD ta's

Prof. Wilson is a very comprehensive teacher. If you want to learn more about Pop Culture... take his class. Very detailed and the tests are easy if you pay even the smallest amount of attention and appreciate the class for what it is... A piece of Amercian Popular Culture.
Proffessor Wilson was one of the best teachers i've had at KU he is very knowledgeble and his class very entertaining

The only reason he put the test on Wednesday night is because it's a Wednesday night class! Duh!! I thought he was a great teacher with a lot of love for the film industry.  The tests were easy enough if you went to the lectures and took notes and actually went over them a couple of times.  Nothing too hard.
Teacher was very boring, and mundane.  Showed no excitement or enthusiasm when delivering the lecture.
Kind of a boring class but if you go its one of the easiet A's you can get.

Probably the worst teacher i have ever encountered in my entire life, stands up there and reads off a piece of paper little facts about songs that your expected to know for the tests, dont care about students at all.  he put the midterm on wednesday night of fall break so those of us who were going out of town had to wait until thursday.
No Comments

I agree with the others, horrible teacher that helps his students very little.  Doesn't care about concepts and ideas, wants you to meamorize impossibly long lists off names, dates, and movies.  I learned very little.
horrible.  he yelled at students who were too bored.  He hates teaching and is taking it out on all his students.  What a terrible way to waste an interesting class on a bad teacher.
No Comments
No Comments

The most horrible professor I have ever had. I have never met a teacher who is so mean-hearted, disrespectful, and unwilling to help students in any way. The fact that he still has a job offends me. I pity whomever might be forced to enroll in a course with this professor.

Really dreaded his lectures, very long and detailed, never quite knew what to study for on exam even with study guide. Had to know over 50 people, 30 films, 30 terms for each midterm/final. Very informed in subject, a walking IMDB, but an overwhelming amount of info he expected to you to know.

Bring a book. I am surprised that he is so accomplished in film and theatre, because he lectures as if it bores him as much as it does me. I looked forward to this class, but the discussions are the only good part thanks to Joy Richmond.She is the only reason I haven't dropped this.
Some what of a boring dillhole.  But I am a film dork so I found the class interesting.  Losts of short assignments and a few large ones.  Lots of reading.  Attendance is a must.
I love her so much because she is my friend now.

cutie professor with a very thick accent and talks very fast. you get used to it. only thing i complain about is that the questions on the exams will use very weird wording that we have never used in class?? also, there are zero lecture slides or any resources available on canvas. ATTEND CLASS.
One homework a week. She works out problems in class that you will see on your homework and as long as you go to and pay attention in lecture then you should be fine.

Professor Tu has been an absolute gem. She made differential equations much easier to understand. She genuinely cares that you understand the content and are prepared, stop frequently to ask "is everything clear?". Don't be afraid to ask her questions after class, because she will gladly answer them,.

I found Dr. Tu unintentionally hilarious. Her lectures were very easy to follow, but you better show up to class because she prefers an old-school chalkboard and does not record lectures. The exams follow the homework exactly. Overall, an easy A if you can understand the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I was scared to take Diff Eq, but she made it so good! The notes/homework are exactly like the exams and final. She gives generous partial credit on exams. She is very caring and makes sure everyone understands concepts. On the final, you get to have a cheat sheet. There is extra credit on each exam. Professor Tu made this class by far my favorite!
She's an absolute gem. I don't know anything about her life outside of class but I think she deserves the entire world. great human. great teacher.
This by far was the best teacher for DEQ, she only do problems what you are expected on the test or exams. The HW she assigns are exactly or almost like the rest. Do the HW and end up with A

Prof. Tu truly explains Diff Eqs and makes them super easy. She is very willing to meet outside of class time to help you understand the material. As well, she is very clear what will be on the exam giving good practice problems that are very similar to what you will see on the exam. Overall, would recommend her as a professor without hesitation.

Everyone is saying that the notes are essential, but I did not pay attention in class and got an A. I got a 74 on first test. 93 on second test after I studied a lot more, and a 93 on the final. Just do all the assignments since they're 25% and do them all again before the exams and you're golden

She made Diff Eq simple and easy. Her notes are freaking amazing, so don't miss a single class and write down everything she writes on the board. Just do the homework with the help of the notes and you're set. The exams are exactly like the home work. This class is awesome.

She is by far the best teacher I have ever had here at KU. Homework is very short & simple. Tests are just like the homework. Diff EQ may seem like a hard subject, but Xuemin Tu makes it extremely easy.

She's a very good teacher, and she's very easy going. A bit difficult to understand at times, her English is pretty rough. Her tests are pretty stinking easy, and she copies the test problems straight from the homework. Her grading is lenient, and it is very helpful. I would highly recommend her to anyone.
