Very clear about expectations for the class and always willing to help or clarify further. Homework taken once a week with two midterms and a final. Differential equations is tough, but she makes it much easier.

Look, I liked Lu when I took his class last year, but I hated his teaching style. Yes, a language course has to be quick and to the point, but it was largely reading the chapter for the next day, coming in, and writing it on the board. He was a bit mean when giving criticism, and gave a lots Canvas work. Got nicknamed as, "Lu's Latin Deathmarch."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Lu was a great professor for the short time I had him!  I took latin with him as well as a course on Caesar. He is strict and expects a lot from you, but I saw the most improvement in myself as a student during my time with him. Students who are ready to work hard and care about learning and not just getting an A will appreciate him.

Ximing's class was difficult but it was in no way impossible, he truly wanted his students to succeed and if you put in the effort he would be more than willing to help you. His class drastically improved my latin more than any other and I am sad that I only got one semester with him. If you struggled with him I would look in the mirror for why.

Dr. Lu killed any dream of mine to continue with Latin. He was an unfair professor, who made a difficult class even more difficult than it needed to be. He would make comments that were along the lines of "we went over this in class. if you got it wrong, you should look at yourself and how well you pay attention to this class." Do not ever take it.

Professor Lu was extremely hard to interpret and would often cold call students which in my opinion is a little bit silly for a 100-level class with less than 20 students. I don't recommend taking Latin to begin with, but if you do I do not recommend Professor Lu, as he's new to the school and not very helpful or personable.

Dr. Li organizes the class as guided lecture notes (recommended to read beforehand; I hardly ever did), in-class problems, discussion sessions, quizzes, and exams. If you go to office hours, you will be helped. She really went above and beyond, as long as you make the time to go. To succeed at the highest level, lead the discussion sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very caring professor, probably the best professor I have had at KU. She genuinely wants her students to succeed and all of the assignments, quizzes, and exams are very reasonable and it is clear she is not trying to intentionally trick us. The workload is very manageable and I found it to be surprisingly easy considering it is a difficult subject.

Lectures are fairly straightforward, but could be messy at times. Labs are not beneficial for learning, you just have to get through them. Homework can be found in the back of textbook. As long as you pay attention during lecture and study for exams, you should do well. This class is difficult but Dr. Li gives you all the resources you need to pass

the entire semester I spent teaching myself when I actually learned the topics I really enjoyed it. The structure of the class was awful lacked example problems and almost passion for the subject. I wish I could retake w a different professor and structure because I do really enjoy it but this was hard and didnt prep me for the next courses waste

She really is trying her best, and I can see that... But good lord she expects so much from the students. She mentioned in class that homeworks should be taking about 15 hours (for a 3 credit hour course). And then the exams are only 2 hours but have questions of similar length to the homework. Just makes no sense at all. Try a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Li went from open book/note to closed and does not provide formulas. She expects you to memorize a dozen formulas for each test and if you mess up a coefficient or anything will give you no points. She offers no partial credit, her lectures are poor and she has terrible averages on exams and blames students, even though her teaching is sad.

Dr. Li is wonderful! She is very knowledgeable on the subject and willing to explain in further detail if needed. She is great during office hours and will work with you calmly and respectfully until she runs out of time or you get it, what ever comes first. Her test can be tough but doable if you go to class, the discussions and do the HW.

His lectures aren't the best, but he makes up for it in other ways. If you reach out to him over email with questions, he responds crazy fast and his directions are a lot clearer. He does his best to help students succeed in the class even when he doesn't really know what he's talking about. You can tell that he's getting better at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Final grade was consisted of three homework assignments, one midterm that we took before fall break and didnt get back until after drop date like the second to last weekend of the semester and a "participation grade". Entire class failed the first test probably since we didn't get a formula sheet, the final we were allowed a one page note sheet

Took a midterm before fall break and didn't get a grade back for 2 months. Grades have been out of whack for the whole semester. Lectures consist of reading equations/examples off of cropped textbook scans. Class wasn't engaging and it was very hard to comprehend the content being taught. Good person but needs to get better at running a class.

Yun is a thorough professor who challenges her students; however, she is one of the most caring professors I have ever had. She constantly ensures her students understand the material and is always happy to help in and out of class if you have a question. Take Yun for Korean if you want to LEARN. She is very generous and an amazing professor.

She does NOT care about you. She does not care about mental health, or familial issues, to her this class is the ONLY thing you should be prioritizing. If you tell her any issues she will just tell you to try harder, even if it's literally impossible to try any harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: While Professor Yun is a super sweet lady who really cares about her students, she is strict. She takes off points for word choice, which is a bit annoying. Sometimes things were also not explained clearly, as the class is mostly discussion-based rather than taught through lecture. Overall, if you want to be pushed in a 300-level class, take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Very fun and enthusiastic teacher. She provides clear instructions and expectations are easily achieved.

Professor Yun is very very sweet. I love how her class is organized, but it is more like a graduate level course. Some of the readings are quite easy, others are incredibly difficult, but overall it's a very comprehensive overview of Korean culture and history. Readings are mandatory to do well! I will be taking more courses with her!
Excellent teacher!  Very clear about her expectations for the class.
Brutally difficult, hijacked "East Asian Pop Culture" and made it about anthropology and economics. Run for your life!

This professor was one of the worst professors I have had. He is very lecture-heavy and only reads the powerpoints which does not help during the exams. The quizzes are very subjective and are hard to read if you miss one day. You will be far behind if you do not pay attention to the whole class, and it shows.

I know he can seem like a tough nut, but Dr. Yi is incredibly caring towards his students who ACTUALLY care. I'd be mad too if I had to teach a freshman class where nobody pays attention. So intelligent, over-qualified, and incredibly wise. He gives great feedback and is a wonderful professor. I would recommend getting involved in his research!

The class overall was okay. Lecture is boring and not required, but helpful when taking the quizzes. There are options for extra credit on every assignment if you turn it in early. I did well on the first exam but bombed the second, but was able to pass with an A barely because I got a 100%  on my final paper. Beware: final paper is A LOT.

He talks quite a bit but he explains things really in depth to make sure students understand the concepts. Had to communicate with him over a missed assignment and he was very nice and understanding. Attending class is optional. I enjoyed Prof Yi.
This class was a joke. Very boring and the professor put in very little effort to teach as he just read off the lectures and nothing more. Dr. Yi was very rude at time when talking to him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Yi was not a good lecturer or a good person. When talking to him one on one he was rude and did not help with anything. The tests are doable and there are extra credit for every quiz if you summit it on time. There is a big final paper, but if you talk to the TA that are assigned to you it should be easy. Overall a bad class.

He definitely talks a lot, but if you need examples or connections to real life to get information into your brain this is the teacher for you. There aren't a lot of assignments but if you put in the effort, take the GTA critiques, and have communication with your assigned GTA you should be fine on the paper assignments.

This professor is rated a lot lower than I think he deserves. If you show up to class, everything is easy. We had a few "quizzes" but it was literally information told to us straight from lectures. The quizzes are virtual and you get two extra credit points just for turning it in on time. Lectures are boring but you do not have much work. One paper

This class is a joke. It is exceptionally more difficult than a 200-level class should be. The exams are as difficult as a 400-level class which is NOT okay. Dr. Yi is also a horrible lecturer, and gets distracted easily as well. I would recommend taking this class with anyone else if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Yi is alright. He's a nice guy, but not the best professor. Extremely dry lectures, and he kind of just rambles on and on the entire time. The class grading system is technically a 600-point system instead, based on bi-weekly quizzes, two 150-point exams, and a GIANT research paper project. Acheiving an A is possible, but prepare to work!

This professor is horribly unhelpful and the class is structured poorly. Your grade comes down to two big exams that are way harder than the lecture material, and one big research essay with super difficult grading criteria. I would never take a class with this professor again, he is an extremely dry lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor was incredibly boring and repetitive. His lectures lacked substance and he often got distracted. Hes a tough grader and there isnt a lot of assignments in this class so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a 600 point class where only 72 of those points come from very easy (if you go to lecture) assignments. There are 2 exams (150 pt each) that were questionably harder than I was expecting considering I went to all lectures and took notes. Because an A is only 93.5 and above, the paper is likely what will determine your grade. Irritating.

Dr. Yi's class is way more difficult than I ever expected a 200 level course to be. Your grade is based on how many points you get, and a 94% is required to get an A. Anything below a 94% is a B, and the only things that you are graded on are a few homework assignments, 2 really difficult exams, and a massive research paper. Look for different prof
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I learned very little from the lectures; you'll just learn from the internet and homework. The first test was online, and the second one was similar to the practice tests. Write as much as you can on the cheat sheet and pray. I went to office hours once, and she helped but also told me I was okay and knew what I was doing (I did not).

Doesn't take attendance which makes it very easy to get behind because I can hardly learn from her lectures anyways. Everything is on the slide already so she does not show many steps on how to solve problems and jumps from slide to slide. The test are basically your entire grade and the first is online unproctored but then the final is in person

shes nice to the people that actually show up. the first exam was online and you had unlimited time (easiest A ever) and the final you get a full piece of paper as a cheat sheet. an A is not that hard to get. however, everything comes from Pearson. the slides, the hw, the tests... basically an online class and we dont get any of her expertise.

Practice test are exactly like the real one, you get a cheat sheet. She says only equations but you could probably sneak on some work for problems. We had one midterm over the first half and the final over just the second half. Hard to understand and have to teach yourself but I skipped & did the homework with the help of Chat

Lectures are the worst, so get ready to teach yourself. Exams are weighted WAY too much. She's hard to pay attention to and never answers any questions or provides examples. The sample exam and cheat sheet allowed will be your best friend...good luck if you end up with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very hard to understand her and exams are worth way too much
Would rather have a 5 year old try and teach this class.

Her lectures are hard to understand and very dull. I attended very few lectures and have a good grade, but the exams are worth more than 60% of your grade, so despite all the good work, the final is a make or break moment.

The lectures were kind of difficult to follow and the exams were hard; however, if you put effort in and try, Prof Kang will help you. I did not do well on the exams, but I put effort in and I expressed my struggles and Prof Kang was kind enough to round my grade from a D+ to a C-. She will help you succeed if you ask for help and try.

She doesn't teach she just reads off of slides that are wrong half of the time and we have to correct her. Her accent is super heavy which is backed up by her rambling saying the same thing over and over without getting to ger topic points leaving you wondering .  she is mean to kids if they ask a question and makes fun of them for not knowing.

After reading reviews for Kang's 526 class, I went in expecting a lot worse. While I didn't go to Kang's office hours or ask for help 1-on-1 like some of these reviews mention, in lecture Kang was generally very helpful and explained the steps required to get an answer well. She seemed very sweet, and I don't agree with her overall rating on here.

Lectures are slow and boring. She takes so long to get through material. Xiuli does not know what she is talking about when questioned about the deeper meaning behind a concept.I went in for help and she told me I did things wrong, but not what I did wrong. She then proceeded to blame me for not understanding because she reviewed it in lecture!

She reads off the lecture slides and does not further explain the problems. She expects you to know the material already and if you do not understand she becomes condescending and does not help. States that "you should have learned this in middle school." Wants students to use calculators yet does not teach how to properly use them for problems.

She doesn't teach. She reads off the slides she prepared and doesn't further explain how she got the answer. If you ask a question she makes you feel dumb and thinks you should already know it, which feels very condescending. She's not accommodating, and personally I love math, but this class had me in absolute shambles from her teaching.

Teaching skills are HORRID
The language barrier makes the class harder 
Teaches off of the slides and speeds through them; she expects you to already know where the numbers go in the equations.
Doesn't take the time to help you with problems.
Doesn't put in grades 
You will be teaching yourself have fun if this class is required for your major.

I ended up dropping this class but not because of her. She does have an accent but she's completely understandable during lectures. She does just read off the slides though, so you can 100% teach yourself the class. Tests completely parallel the study guides she provides + you can use a cheat sheet. Memorization will be your friend. Not so bad tbh.

The professor gets mad and makes students look and feel dumb when they ask a question during a lecture. She gets mad if you show up to her office hours to ask for help and tries getting you out as soon as possible with no help even if you still don't understand. She makes you teach yourself and doesn't give a heads-up when assignments are due.

Honestly I am so scared for my grade in this course this woman makes no sense!!! Like actually she has no idea how to teach a course it is concerning. the worst part about it is when students ask questions about past concepts, she gets annoyed and accuses them of not paying attention lectures are SO unrelated to the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Shes literally the worst professor Ive ever had. She doesnt teach the class at all and just reads the graphs that are on the slides. The stuff she teaches has nothing to do with the homework. I am a straight A student and I just received at 61% on my midterm. I dont understand her grading at all, much less her teaching. 10/10 do not recommend

I had to take this class for my major and she was horrible. I was only able to get an A because I taught myself using the "explain this problem" on the homework. Her lectures were hard to follow, she jumped around only reading off the slides without explaining the problem. She had just as many problems understanding us as we had understanding her

Professor Xiuli's class would have been easier if there had been more communication between student and teacher. We had our lectures 3 times a week, but outside of that, no emails were sent and there were no office hours. We were expected to know due dates of HW, quizzes, and tests with no reminders over email or in class. Not a lot to grade by.

THE WORST PROFESSOR EVER. do NOT take professor Kang if you don't have to. She was 30 mins late to both of the tests. She is indirect when asked questions and reads word for word off of slides copied out of the textbook. you will get no help from her so be prepared to teach yourself. I would have gotten an A if I had a better professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would not take another class with professor Kang again. She strictly teaches off of the slides and was hard to understand. She only did examples out of the book and wouldn't offer more than that when students asked for more. She also was late to the two tests we had. I only got an A because I was able to teach myself outside of class.

I would never take a class with this professor again. She has a very heavy accent which makes it hard to understand. Most of the lectures are just her jumping around random slides in the power point. Most of the information you have to teach yourself or see the TA to understand. She says attendance is random but it wasn't at the end.

She's a sweet person, but she is not a strong teacher. I felt like most of what I got out of the class was from reading the textbook. She is very jumpy in lecture, so be careful of that. Attendance was mandatory, but she only took attendance in maybe one out of every four classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is very direct in her teaching. I think that she is an amazing and intelligent professor. English is not her first language. I believe that the reason most people don't like the course is because there is a bit of a language barrier, but if you follow along in class and take notes, it's really not bad.
Dr. Kang can be difficult to understand which can make it a little challenging to understand what is going in class. However, the content is not too difficult.

There aren't any pop quizzes but attendance was supposed to be at random and she decided to do it every class, and attendance was worth 8% of your overall grade. I was retaking this course, and the previous professor reminded us of deadlines while Kang did not so keep a schedule of your assignments. Make sure to create a cheat sheet for exams!

While the class provided useful information, Dr. Kang was a lackluster professor. Attendance is mandatory, but even if you attend every class, her teaching style makes it difficult to actually learn the materials. I had to teach a good portion of the class to myself using the textbook. Its not the worst in the world, but avoid if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Kang was not as bad as I had expected based on other reviews here. Her accent was not difficult at all, and she was very sweet and truly wanted to help her students. That said, her lectures were very fast-paced and jumpy, and her class relied mostly on straight memorization of formulas rather than learning concepts. Attendance is also mandatory

Ms. Kang is hands down the worst professor I have ever had. She is difficult to understand to the point that I don't even try; I wouldn't come to class if it weren't for the fact she takes attendance. Be prepared to teach yourself the material. She is not a people person and is abrasive when asked for help. Avoid her class if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I don't mind her accent as much as some do- I don't expect her to pronounce things perfectly. Her lectures are hard to stay engaged in as much as she tries. Big pet peeve is her not putting the powerpoint in presentation mode so its just the preview on the computer screen.

I would not take this class unless it is for a requirement. Kang is very hard to understand and I'm a great math student but it was very hard to even understand what she was saying. The homework is mostly online and her practice tests are really similar to the real ones, that's how you'll pass this class. She also reads directly from the slides.

Hardest class ever. She doesn't speak good english, so you can't understand majority of what she says. Will call you out in class if you don't understand or even if you don't have a calculator. Goes of the same slides 10x in class it gets even more confusing. You will spend hours on homework, because you need to teach yourself. Not worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kang is not a good math teacher. She taught statistics by reading powerpoint slides. Not an effective way to teach math. She was very difficult to understand. I had to teach myself mostly through the textbook. Only good thing is her sample exams were very similar to the real exams- this is how I passed the class.

She is a really nice woman and wants everyone in the class to enjoy the topic and be engaged. She reads directly off the slides and doesn't do much ad-libbing when it comes to explaining the multiple examples she goes through them. The online component for homework and quizzes was what helped me learn the material best. It is hard to stay engaged.

Horrible teacher, goes back and forth through slides, and never explains anything. Assumes you know where all numbers go, and seems like she just figures it out as she goes. Would never recommend her at all. Very hard to understand. Nice lady, bad teacher.

Powerpoint professor, also difficult to understand. Standard Deviation as an example is pronounced "stenuation." Uses the entire lecture time with few moments for questions. Waste of a trip since you have to spend hours teaching yourself then doing homework. Also irritable if asked something she has covered.

Dr. Kang is the worse professor I've ever had. Her lectures are long and boring, she reads directly from the power point, she doesn't answer questions. HORRIBLE!! I spend so much more time than I need to on Stats homework because I have to dedicate time beforehand to actually learn the material. Avoid at all costs!!

Miserable. Does not have command of her English. Flat out won't answer questions during lecture. She literally made the book into a power point and used that as lecture notes. Frequently late to class. She never once demonstrated that she knew what she was attempting to teach.   If you can avoid taking  her course, you'd be a not to.

During office hours she was no help, went in because all she uses is examples from book and would not offer any additional help (couldn't answer questions wo solution book). At one point a group  was caught cheating on hw and all they received was a 0 for that assignment (#6 of sem). I never review profs but she was that bad. Teach yourself stats.
I would highly recommend not taking her class.

Kang is one of the worst math professors I've had at KU, and is extremely difficult to understand. Lectures are worthless and unintelligible, yet she gets angry when students don't pay attention and sometimes even calls them out individually. Takes attendance. Avoid if possible.

She is the worst math instructor I have ever had in the math department at KU. She basically copies all contents from the book and put them on her slides. Not very effective teaching, and the worst part is that she takes attendants for her class! Her examples are all from the book so not very helpful to come to the class.

Avoid taking a class with Kang if at all possible. Her lectures are nearly worthless, she is very difficult to understand, she gets angry over ridiculous things, and she is very unorganized. Fortunately, her tests are fairly easy, which is good considering you'll be teaching yourself this class.

You can tell he is VERY passionate about his teaching. He explores "outside-the-box" methods when it comes to teaching Mandarin and he would even crack up a joke or two throughout class. He pushes his students and challenges them every now and then because he genuinely cares and enjoys teaching
Easy and helpful
Very passionate and educated! Loved the way he instructed.

I also had Pan Laoshi for CHIN108 and 204 before this. He's an amazing help with pronunciation and grammar structure; he gives each student his full attention when speaking. Participation in class matters a lot, and he is hard on his students to ensure they make strong progress. Don't be afraid to struggle, he truly cares about his students.

Loved this class! The articles we read were really insightful and relevant to today's society. Pan laoshi was always very encouraging and helpful to students during our class discussions. The vocab lessons did drag on sometimes, but overall I felt like this class improved my Chinese skills. Would definitely recommend taking a class with Pan laoshi!

Pan Laoshi was the best professor I've ever had. He was very caring and very specific. He cared about his students and really wanted them to understand the concepts. He could be lecturing but if you have a question, he won't continue until you understand everything. He is very understanding and treats you with all the respect you could ever ask for
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Hes a great professor! He is amazing at explaining why things happen in the Chinese language and when to use the grammar points. He corrects you on your tones whenever needed which is really helpful in the long run. The course overall has a lot of homework, and every day there is either a quiz, test or homework due. Its a lot of work but its fun
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is knowledgeable in his field of study. He also is experienced teaching Chinese to English speakers. He will research answers to questions he cant answer during the lesson and follows up during the following period. He is patient and goes at the learners pace. He spreads his questions out to everyone so that we can all practice the language.

Pan laoshi was great! He was great at explaining everything and answering all of our questions. I also enjoyed this class because it is a class for those who took Chinese in high school, so it is the same material as Chinese 104, but the class moves at a faster pace. It was great to take this class instead of waiting to take CHIN 108 in the spring.

Only uploads notes similar to those in class to Canvas. Handwriting is hard to read. Tests are very difficult but you get a notecard. Doesn't post answer keys for homeworks or midterm review. He did curve the final class grade a little, though

His teaching makes sense and I like him overall. I wish the exams had more problems cuz missing a single problem takes like 30% of the exam grade. For some reason the exams were weighted the same as the homework so my grade was fine.

Dr. Wang has taught this course nicely by having good lectures and assigning homework assignments that help students during midterm and final exams. Also, he has helped students' grades by providing extra credit points and dropping the lowest homework scores. Differential Geometry's topics are slightly confusing, but they are not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Wang has good lectures, and the notes are well done with pictures and examples, and all of them are posted online. The homework is challenging but reasonable, it took about 1-2 hours a week. He's always reachable by email (sometimes even past midnight) and is willing to help. He's also just a very funny and upbeat guy in general.

Dr. Wang's lectures were very to the point. So were his tests and quizzes. The homework was challenging, but fair (and not too time consuming). His exams are almost exactly what he does in class. Very possible to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Diff Eq can be a bit difficult. But he does a great job boiling down the strategies and techniques as clearly as possible. There are weekly quizzes, but the quizzes are simple for those who have done the HW. He does HW problems during lecture. He allows notecards during exams. He lectures clearly and concisely. Great lecturer in my opinion.

At the beginning of the semester his teaching was fine, but as the semester went on his teach depreciated. His exams are awful and way too long to finish in the allotted time. He is absolutely UNREACHABLE outside of class. I emailed him 4 times during the semester and was in the ER and had to miss class and he never responded.

the midterm/final were both incredibly difficult. both tests were too long for the allotted time, and both contained a lot of material that was never discussed in the lectures. the homework is not for participation and he will dock points off. overall i felt like it was unfair to include stuff on the midterm/final that was never in the lectures.

Great and engaging lecturer. He explains things really well, and I found his class and lectures to be very enjoyable. He curves the exams well and is very understanding towards his students. Highly recommend having him as a professor.

Professor Yao teaches through his class lectures. There is no homework in the class aside from the lab. He responds very well to questions in class and he clearly demonstrates that he wants to help everyone succeed. He takes attendance 4 times throughout the semester, each worth 2.5% of your grade. Exams are open note and he grades on a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Love this professor! So sweet and sometimes puts hilarious/adorable things (like dogs) in his lectures... sometimes has short youtube videos we watch and his examples are easy to follow. EECS 268 on steroids (although attendance is taken randomly)

Still somehow reading slides but his slides are very detailed and worth read of. Posts all class video online and do not require attendance. Very nice on hw grading. A well organized data science class.

Professor Chen is one of the most amazing people I have ever met. I took her First Year Honors Seminar: Mindfulness in the Modern World, and I would take it 10 more times if I could. I learned a lot about myself, my classmates, and the world in general, and I believe this class made me a better person. Thank you, Professor Chen!!

Dr. Chen certainly gives you tough assignments, but I promise you will learn from them. She is always there to help you if you have questions, and she cares immensely about your success. She will reward you if she sees you putting in the effort. She can come off as a little cold at first, but Dr.Chen is very kind and a wonderful professor.

You will no doubt learn a lot from this course, but sometimes Prof. Chen can be a bit rude or degrading while you are trying to learn. There are no "free" absences, your grade will be lowered if you miss any class without an excuse from the university. I learned a lot from this course and I respect Prof. Chen immensely, but she can be a lot.

I was in Dr. Chen's JMC 104 class, and she was a fantastic professor. At first, the content was difficult, but then you get the hang of it. Dr. Chen cares deeply about her students, and it shows that she is always there if you need her.

This class was very easy but definitely taught me a lot. Dr. Chen has so many wonderful insights into many facets of the world and is a great honors mentor. She is also very laid back and understanding. Though attendance is mandatory for this class as there aren't really any out-of-class assignments except for the final, she is very understanding.

Overall, Dr. Chen is a good professor. She is very big on participation on Zoom and will call you out if you aren't smiling at her or don't react to a joke she makes. Sometimes she seems to treat students like children in lectures but is very helpful over email and when you meet with her outside of class. If you put in work, you will do well.

Dr. Chen is, without a doubt, the best professor I have had the pleasure of taking a class with. She cares... a lot. Need I say more?  The class is mostly group work, so your grade depends on them, but Chen is willing to look at your work days before you hand it in. If you don't take advantage of that, it's your fault.  Just take her class.

Dr. Chen loves her students. She makes you feel welcomed and important as a student. Very clear, will always help you, and gives GREAT feedback on drafts. She is a tough grader, so you will need to work hard. If you don't have a problem with that, Dr. Chen is a phenomenal teacher.
Incredible professor. Loves her students. Super current and up to date with journalism trends and research. Tough grader, but she gives great feedback.

Dr. Chen just transferred to KU. It was her first class teaching and she really put a lot of effort into it. I definitely think she cares a lot about her students. Only problem was 2 tests is 65 percent of grade and 7 projects is 25 percent of grade.
Very GOOOD~~~~!!!

Li laoshi is an amazing professor and I highly suggest choosing her. She is very funny, makes sure everyone participates, is willing to answer any questions you have, and wants to make sure everyone is prepared for exams. She's a great professor especially for first year students easing into college.

Li laoshi is a great professor and excellent for fourth year. She is caring, works well with the students and explains everything clearly. As long as you keep up with the readings and participate you'll do great!

Gets through the lectures pretty fast & efficiently. Makes sure everyone understands the content before moving on. Responds promptly to emails & is understanding about potential conflicts. Has really funny & cute mannerisms that keeps the class alive throughout the period. Love her energy & kindness!

Li Laoshi is sweet and cute. She is polite, but firm in her belief in teaching students Chinese. This class require quite a bit of time in homework and memorizing passages, but it will definitely improve your Chinese, especially with Li Laoshi as your teacher. She also usually bakes goodies for certain holidays!

Li Laoshi(teacher) is kind, cute, and helpful. She respects her students and wants them to learn Chinese. In this class,  you are expected to speak often and there is quite a bit of homework, but overall isn't too hard.

Absolutely loved Yan Li! It was my first time taking Mandarin & I was a little apprehensive going in to it. The class turned out to be my favorite of the semester - Yan Li is very helpful, clear, and so sweet!  Be prepared to study though - it takes effort. If you put In the work & show up to class you will do fine!

Li is a great professor but there are a lot of assignments due in the class. She's amazing though - will answer any questions, grades are up to date, lecture notes go online almost as soon as class is out, etc. She's a bit of a stickler with pronunciation but it pays off in the end. Word of advice: go to class. Each absence is a .5% deduction.
His lectures are pretty interesting and engaging. The class has very straightforward just weekly homework that wasn't too bad.

This was easily the best economics class I've taken at KU. It was much more difficult than undergraduate classes, but it was a necessary step-up for those wanting to dive further into economics. The problem sets were extremely well-crafted, and solutions were discussed collaboratively in class. Attendence was non-negotiable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures, while optional, are very informative and I highly recommend attending because the professor is very helpful and informative. He clearly knows what he's doing and he explains the material very well. The homework and tests are straightforward with the content and deadlines, and the tests are online and you get the entire week to do them

Great prof. Explains everything very clearly and intuitively, and made a hard subject easy to understand! Exams are kind of rough, though, and he's a bit of a harsh grader. But if you study and do the exercises you'll be fine.
His lectures are engaging and you can really tell he's passionate about what he's teaching! He made a basic microeconomics class into something fun and made me genuinely excited to go to class.

He teaches from a PhD-level book called MWG and puts a lot of effort into his lectures which are recorded and available for self-pace learning. Homeworks are to be typed in LaTEX and are solved in class before, but his midterms aren't. His midterm review class is essential. He's tough but fair.

The homework is basically all excel but Jeff goes through examples in class that are very similar to the homework. He does go through the examples fast. If you are a supply chain management major, take it with Jeff he will teach you everything you need to know. He makes class interesting by connecting the class work to real-life examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly his teaching style is lecture heavy to say the least. He does random quizzes that count towards attendance but attendance is not mandatory. he assigns 2 homework assignments each week that takes a few hours to do ( if you're not supply chain major). TA's grade the homework so I recommend going to them to check it before you submit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Jeff is knowledgeable about the subject and is a good guy. If I had to change 2 things about the class it would be 
1.Get rid of the +/- grading system.
2. Make homeworks a little easier. Many of them took me 1-2 hours to complete and you get two of them a week.
I could go on and on. Just don't take his class. His last Rate My Professor profile had like 20 1 stars until it got taken down.

If you show up regularly and pay attention you will be fine! There were 5 "pop" quizzes on Canvas (the dates are listed on the syllabus, so not a surprise) that you have to be in attendance for. The Excel part of exams is exactly like the practice problems. if you put in a decent amount of effort you will have a fine grade.

I wasted so many hours studying for this class and never got the grade I hoped for. Time consuming and difficult. Would not recommend taking SCM 310 with this professor if supply chain is not your major. Worst college course I've taken at KU by far!
Very well-connected in the industry and gives great advice. Most of the class is him interviewing industry professionals that he taught or worked with, and then you answer an easy quiz about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR! The other professor for this course did not assign homework and allowed the final to be online. This teacher was terrible at explaining things and made us complete long excels for minimal points that he barely even knew how to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My class period has 3 times as many Fs as there are As, yet there was no curve or opportunity to get points back. Never take this class unless you want to be convinced to drop out of college.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
The most frustrating intro class. Do not get the textbook. Exercise assignments were worth 5 points each, but could be so incredibly difficult and took a lot of time. If you have the time to go to the TA hours, DO IT!!! This is the only intro class I genuinely have learned nothing. 

Study guides are very similar to exam.
Teaching 500 level course in an into level class.

He is very clearly enthusiastic about the topic and having his students understand it. Lectures can be monotonous and there are not a lot of assignments (only essays and exams) so one bad grade can tank you. Amazing professor if you can teach yourself outside of class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very clearly enthusiastic about the topic and having his students understand it. Lectures can be monotone and there is not a lot of assignments, so one bad one can tank your grade. Amazing professor if you can also teach yourself outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zogry is super nice, and unless you're not paying any attention to the lectures and not looking at the review sheets before exams there's no reason you should do poorly. Only exams are graded. His grading is slow, and the lectures can feel like a drag, but you can tell that he has a passion for his subject and the class is far from hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Takes literal years to grade (8 week course, did not receive grades back for 6 weeks). Class is unorganized.  Posts 3 hours of monotonous lectures slides a week.  Only graded on tests and essays. Do not recommend taking this class to fulfill core requirements or if you think it might be interesting. Just take something else.

Pretty nice and chill dude, but the lectures are extremely dull. You learn dates, events, etc., and have to write it all down during class because he does not post the slides to Canvas. Very lecture heavy, not a lot of projects or class participation. No homework outside of readings besides the two writing assignments.
The only reason this class was taken was for credit. He a horrible teacher. DON'T TAKE THIS DUDE UNLESS YOU ABSOLUTELY NEED TO.
DONT take this dude unless it's totally needed. I would rank him as a NEGATIVE if possible.
Take this class if you want to hate your life. He has NO powerpoint skills, yet expects a 15 page thesis from his students, after the 5 pg paper, two tests and extensive readings of course.
His powerpoint slides were novels.  Way too hard for an introductory course.

This is your typical McClass. Not boring, not exciting. All lecture. Contrary to other comments, he is a very nice guy, VERY willing to meet with students and accommodate. Tests are challenging but not unreasonable. Yes, he's a stickler for attendance. I had wished for less history and more religion but what can ya do?.
this class is a joke

He walks around the room and never makes eye contact with any of the class and then ignores someone when they have a question.  He says 'whatever' a lot which is strange because he is old and it makes him seem like he doesn't care what he is talking about.  Even though he does because you can tell he has a passion for the subject he is just boring.

Overall impression: he knows his stuff but doesn't think highly of students' abilities-I felt like he was bestowing us with info. Reading assignments were great but lengthy and dense. Visiting outside of class was difficult and unhelpful.  He got into childish arguments with students in class. Assignments and tests were in convoluted formats.
Attendence is everything, even in lectures... if you study and take good notes his test are fairly easy.
not that bad of a class, yes he's strict on attendence but anyone who knows anything about religion should just take the class cause that makes it very easy for you, the concepts aren't hard at all.
this class is sooooooo boring and the text is even worse. very strict with attendance even when it comes to funerals.
No Comments

Lots of reading and information, lots of work.  Takes attendance and is very strict.  Tests are not as hard as I thought they would be, but prove you know the material.  Very helpful if you come to him out of class.  After the class you know the material.  Not a breeze class, but great if you're willing to work a bit and want to learn the stuff.

the man can't stand still to save his life....he is constantly blocking the notes w/ his body, yet expects you to write everything down...does not post the notes on blackboard b/c it's "plagiarism"....

Zhang is unpersonable and dismissive, often coming off as fake or snobby. Lectures lack substantive value and are quite boring, while feedback remains sparse despite the 40-120+ pages of weekly reading. His communication is poor and he carries a superiority complex. Save yourself the headache and steer clear of this course.

Attendance is important and mandatory on quiz days, which are open-note.  If you pay attention in the lecture, it's not a very hard class.  The only exam was the final, which he prepared us well for.  All the other assignments are papers for simulations, which are very important to attend.  Overall, Dr. Zhang was great.

I liked this one lecture day when Dr. Zhang talked about this book he had read about the telegraph and compared it to what we were learning about in class. It was a change of pace and extremely interesting as a student since I could tell he was interested as well. I heard other students share the same sentiments after class.

I really liked the group assignments for this class. They helped me understand how political and economic decisions play out in the real world. I learned a lot from working with my team and researching different countries and industries. Highly recommend!

Dr. Zhang is very understanding and encourages participation during lectures. As long as you stay on track with textbook readings (~50 pages a week), the content is easy to understand and the lectures are interesting.

Professor Zhang is really impressive and knowledgeable! The class is very reading intensive but he is accessible and explains it well. There's room for a lot of extra credit and the course load is manageable. He is also such an understanding overall good guy. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang knows what he's talking about. He situates topics in both their historical & scholarly contexts to give his students a broader understanding compared to what is typical in most political science classes. Rich content does come at the expense of reading time, but don't get caught up in that. It's about perspectives not minute detail
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Dr. Zhang's class! He cares about students and responds to emails. The simulations were also fun!
I really like Professor Zhang. He teaches pretty rigorous, fast-paced classes. Really passionate about the source material and teaching in general. Get ready to read!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is not very well spoken and tends to ramble or mumble, so it is very important to read the textbook thoroughly to understand the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: After taking this class, Dr. Zhang is probably my favorite professor in the Political Science Department. I thoroughly enjoyed being taught by him.

Professor Zhang does a decent job of explaining concepts in the textbook; he sometimes goes off-topic or mumbles, so it is good to invest in a book as well. The simulations/assignments are straightforward. The quizzes were a little challenging though. Zhang is very understanding of different situations and is a good professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang is an amazing professor. He really cares about what he teaches out and is always trying to make the class easier and more interesting for students.

Dr. Zhang is very knowledgeable and his lectures have tons of interesting content, but he also makes the class easy and accessible for everyone. He puts more weight on a trade war simulation, which is very easy. He also gives study guides for the two exams. Amazing mentor too and willing to talk about opportunities outside the class!

Dr. Zhang is an awesome professor. He cares about his lectures, is always accessible and clearly cares about being a good professor and mentor. The class includes: one quiz most weeks, midterm, final and few page paper. If you're interested in East Asia, International Relations or Foreign Policy, this class is a must take.
Really nice professor! The class was well organized and the lectures were engaging. Theres a decent amount of reading but I enjoyed the material and really liked the simulation
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This was an easy class with lots of extra credit opportunities. Theres only one exam and most of the assignments are from the simulations in section.

Great lecturer, very engaging and conveys information well. The class itself was interesting as there was no textbook, but rather only primary sources which was much better IMO. Final assignment is extremely difficult but rewarding. Inspired me to take International Studies after taking POLS170 with him, both classes felt very satisfying.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang is a fantastic teacher. I enjoyed his lectures. The readings are a lot but you can make do on the reading quizzes if you just skim well. The simulations are a lot of fun and really get you interested on the topics.
The lectures in this class were very dense and boring. I enjoyed the discussion way more. The content and homework load was fine. It was overall an average experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang's International Relations of Asia class was overall a great experience. We started the class by walking through the early history of Asian politics and then delved into economics in the latter half. The U.S.-China trade war simulation was really fun and informative too. He's very professional and fair, and he REALLY knows his stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Zhang know his stuff. His lectures are long but full of good information. The readings assigned outside of class are helpful and relevant. I greatly enjoyed how the first unit dove into the background of E. Asia. He was always very accessible outside of class and helped me a lot for the midterm. Overall a fairly challenging but great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Political Economy of East-Asia was my favorite class at KU so far. If you like the subject matter, you will love him for giving you in-depth, challenging, but rewarding instruction. He teaches you as if you were a graduate student, which could be a good or bad thing depending on what you want. Extra credit is given, and reading is long but good
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Never take his course.... I just say never!!!

The most inaccessible and unhelpful "professor" I've ever had. Wasted a lot of time to explain that I had an internship during finals week, only for him to refuse to work with me in any way. He told me to retake the class next semester, and only did anything when the Dean got involved.

Do I regret taking this class? I actually don't. I think the videos were very good and I learned a lot. Was this class structured good? Not at all. There was a whole confusion about if it was a flipped classroom or not, and the exams were tricky to the point that it seemed they wanted you to do bad. The homework was very manageable though.

If you want 50% of your grade to rely on 2 tests that have extremely predatory grading techniques, then this is the professor for you! No matter how deeply you understand the content, horribly formatted exams will destroy your grade. The lab assignments are essentially Pass-Fail, with no room for partial credit. Lectures are barely followable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I will be winning any "I had the worst professor" arguments.

Most of the time spent in this class was just long periods of silence after Zhong asked the class a question that had nothing to do with the videos. The material in the class isn't even that hard; he is just completely inept at teaching. Take the class in the fall unless you enjoy watching a professor fumble around in MS word talking about nothing.

Avoid at all costs. First day of class says it's a flipped classroom, then complains when no one shows up. Labs aren't difficult if you “use your resources” but exams are brutal. No clear study guide other than a list of random questions from the lectures that never show up on the exam, and consistently messes up homework questions
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bless the lord he isnt teaching this class anymore

Far and away the worst professor I have had. He doesn't want to teach. It is insane to me that we had to pay tuition and got him as our teacher. He showed up late to the exam, and the TA said they would give us the last problem for free and then he comes in and says that's not true.

This class has by far been my least favorite at KU. In other classes a majority of the time the professor is not to blame but EVERY single thing in this class is to blame on the professor. Labs that are pass fail, Exams that have absolutely nothing to do with a study guide provided. You are only a number to him. Curves are the only saving grace. GL
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The number one worst professor I've had at KU. Does not care at all about the class, does not want to be a professor. Labs require hundreds of lines of code and are graded pass fail by a program. Lectures are boring, monotone, reading from slides YouTube videos. Constant typos and wording errors on exam questions, and 0 helpful study info. Hated it

His teaching isn't horrible, but yeah, he just doesn't care about the class one bit. TA grades everything in a very strange way. Labs are extremely challenging with very poor instructions. You do learn a lot of good information and he curves the tests. He also changed the final from 40 or 35 % to 30.

I hate this class so much, I hate it, I hate it, I hate it. The labs were a complete mess, they're so hard for no apparent reason and the system works as you either get a 0 or a 100, by far the worst lab I have ever experienced. Avoid at all costs no matter what!

I hated it. Assignment/exam questions are subjective, during the exams he had constant line of students needing to ask questions. Labs are graded using automation with all/nothing grade. Hes gained a bad rep but gets to stay becuase he does great research for KU. He simply does not care about the class or put effort to improve.
The professor is not bad, not the best at teaching but it's alright. My biggest issue was the labs. By far the hardest labs I've ever done and I don't have any classes left with labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He has improved so much this semester. He gives study guide questions for each lecture that are very representative of the exams. The labs aren't too bad. As long as you pay attention in class and learn the study guide questions you'll be good.

Zhong is not a bad lecturer, sometimes he can go a bit fast and you may need to follow-up for clarification. Labs are doable, but the 16-way polyphase lab was unreasonable, although he did offer an optional bonus lab.

Tests are hard, w/ questions like prove complexities and writing our own proofs. An implied curve was also not delivered.

I've had Prof. Zhong twice. While he's still not a great teacher, he has improved in some respects. His teaching is still rather dry, and he still throws curveball questions on exams. On the other hand, his labs have become a lot more reasonable and he made the final exam take-home due to its difficulty. Doesn't deserve a 1.4, but not great either.

So awful at teaching an important subject. The material you should be taught in this class is crucial for tech interviews but you won't learn a thing from him. His only good quality is that he is chill in comparison to Saiedian, he let me resubmit an assignment that didn't compile. He doesn't care at all about teaching and makes super hard tests.

This professor goes as far as to acknowledge that students don't like him, but does absolutely nothing to improve. Absolutely no review material for a comprehensive final worth 25% of the grade. Added proofs to the scope of the midterm exam at the last minute with little in the way of preparation material. Do yourself a favor and run far away.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He is aware of these reviews yet does nothing to improve his teaching style. For midterms and exams he offers no review session or previous exams unlike other courses. It almost feels like he finds the class a chore to teach because rather than explain something he says "Just read the book the implementation is there"
Can't wait for this to be over
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Unhelpful lectures, unhelpful out of class, ineligible notes, one office hour, test questions could be one of a million different things, course weighting is the only positive thing, awful.

If you are an active student and willing to argue back and forth on proofs and do the extra homework to learn the real trick in the broad ocean of computer science, Cuncong is the best prof. If you are not, Cuncong is the worst. One of the old-school tough meritocrat teachers our public school systems have not seen in a while.
Professor Zhong needs to be fired...they should have Gibbons teach the upper level courses as he actually knows how to teach.
Mary had a little lamb and that lamb gave me a proof on an exam (this class has traumatized me)

You MUST know C++ prior to taking this class otherwise it will be insufferable.

The class is now called EECS 330, not EECS 560 but it is still being taught like a 500 level course. His notes he takes during class are unintelligible.

When we asked for study guides for midterm, he said 'Go to the library & check out a book.'

This class is a joke.

There have been many villains throughout history. The Joker, Darth Vader, and Frieza to name a few. Well Cuncong Zhong is the villain of the EECS department. This man has single handedly ended the potential careers of his students. he was put on this earth for one reason and that is to absolutely destroy the happiness and dreams of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
EECS 330
*Extremely horrible lectures
*Expected to code in C++ since day 1 after only being taught python
*Threw topics on test that we LITERALLY never talked about
*When pressed for study aids/practice problems just posted 600 slides from other courses a few days before test
*The entire class is on the same page with how frustrating this class is
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My experience here parallels a Shakespearean tragedy. I entered Spring an energetic and gleeful young student. Little did I know, 2 months into the semester, I would be a hollow shell of a person. What Zhong has done to me is vile, twisted, and humiliating for the Department of EECS. I now fear the dark as it reminds me of the evil within his soul
Be prepared to study algorithm analysis on your own time. He doesn't cover this important topic, but his exams sure expect you to know how to prove complexities.

He will tell you at the beginning of the semester that there will be no proofs on the exams, and then three days before the first exam announce that it will be "very proof heavy" with 400 "supplemental" lecture slides to prepare. It's like watching a YouTube video of someone messing with Vim for an hour everyday.

Data structures. I had C++ background but 2nd half of course was still hard because I hadn't taken discrete structures. The lectures and slides were great but sometimes too fast. This will be a rough semester

Wow. I don't even know where to start. Consistently lies to the class about expectations and material. Condescending when trying to reach him outside of class. Does not provide feedback to anything. If Dr. Zhong says that there will be a curve and no proofs for exams, then don't be too excited. He doesn't give a curve because he thinks that everyone will ace the exam. I can't think of a good part of this class. As other mentioned he lied about proof being on exams. Be ready to memorize everything he puts on his bad notes as route recall is expected. Labs are awful, not hard just poorly designed. Awful lecturer, not engaging at all. STAY AWAY at all costs. Was not helpful when asked questions about labs.

Zhong is a poor lecturer, the exam preparation is misleading, labs are not well designed and he's hard to contact. He lies and says no proofs on exams then surprise!

Worst prof ive ever had.

This Prof. is not horrible because his finals are hard or because he makes you write proofs, as other as suggested. I would love to have a hard professor who makes you write proofs! This professor is horrible because he is a lazy and bad teacher who doesn't care about his students. Waste of time and money.
Labs are easy. Exams are tough and proof heavy. He tries his best as a lecturer. Pretty average class.

Do not take his course basically. His final are ridiculously hard, and are all proofs. I have nearly 100% before the final, and I only get 51% on Final. I feel he reads the textbook during the lecture. He does not care his students. If you wanna learn how to prove instead of CS things, take his course then. Again, do not take his course if u have

If you have other choices, do not take his course. His labs are easy 100% if you pay attention and work hard enough. But his exams are hard, most of them are all proof related. reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Says he will stop grading any answer you give the first time you say something wrong or unsupported, but likewise doesn't want to think student answers all the way through, so don't use your own examples or get creative. Memorize what he says and regurgitate it; while it's hard to fail the class mathematically, it's still annoying.

My data structures course with Prof. Zhong was of extremely low quality. His class is beneath the dignity of KU School of Engineering. The quality of instruction was beyond horrible. He made no effort during class or office hours. I love CS and was motivated to learn from the textbook: Prof Zhong did nothing for me. His class was disgusting.

Zhong will try to trick you every chance he gets, if he tells you you don't need to know a formal proof. You need to know it. If he tells you something wont be on an exam. It will be on the exam. His class is poorly taught in the first place and to top it off he straight up lies to try and screw you out of your grade. Avoid at all costs.

This is by far, one of the worst professors in the EECS department. The labs in this class are 0 or 100 only, no inbetween. Takes days to respond to emails (sometimes never) and will only give you a couple word response and call that good.

One of, if not the worst professor I have had in college. The only things that we were graded on were 6 quizzes, attendance and a final. The grading criteria was incredibly harsh and inconsistent. The only way to get good grades on the quizzes was to memorize exactly what he wrote out in class. It only tests memorization.

Professor is absolute GARBAGE. Terrible notes, lazy professor, awful lectures. Zhong does not care about his students and does not respond to emails or questions effectively. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS. Worst Professor at KU.

Worst class I have ever had at KU. Teaching is bad. Notes are scribbled around without any attempt of organization. Just don't take it if you have a chance. You'll definitely learn more elsewhere with the same amount of effort.
Worst professor I have had in my 4 years at KU. Notes are terrible, It seems pointless studying for the exam since everyone will fail anyways. Median on the first exam was 28/100

Jeff is decent and goes through Excel examples that mirror the homework. The problem is the TA grading. Jeff gives great feedback and had plenty of experience in SCM. If you have a question he has an answer and I absolutely reccomend taking his class.
Great teacher and if you go to class you will do well

All in all the class if you pay attention in class and go to office hours the homeworks are really not that bad. The reviews for the exam line up well to the exams and are great study tools. All things considered if you pay attention in class and put in the work you can easily get an A.
He is a really wholesome guy, and Caden is the best TA!
Class is mostly excel but he works through identical problems to the homework in class

Jeff makes supply chain very confusing. He just rambles about the supply chain process in probably the most boring way possible, and the other 80% Excel sheets. Guys a complete dork. I had multiple people tell me he wouldn't round up their grade and many of them had around a  89.4. Take the other guy for SCM. Don't waste your time. He makes supply chain as hard to learn as rocket science
First of all, his voice was the most infuriating thing to listen to, second of all, he is by far the worst professor I have had at the business school. AVOID THIS MAN AT ALL COSTS

This professor is the hardest i have had at KU thus far. If you do one thing for yourself, do not take this class with Professor Zoroya. Terrible professor. His exams, excels and quizzes are almost impossible to understand. He just sits in a chair and reads off slides for 75 minutes. The homework assignments will take a while to do, and TA'S are all inconsistent. Exams are basically your whole grade

reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: "I have earned a lot of money not knowing how to do any of this," -said Jeff. He proceeded to spend 10 minutes doing an easy Excel problem. If this isn't enough to prove how bad of a professor he is then I don't know what will. Spare yourself and don't take it with Jeff!

His voice drones on and on without clarity on what he is teaching. He fails to explain concepts and leaves students with homework after every single class, often on material he ran out of time to teach. He uses the most inefficient methods to approach simple problems and attendance is basically mandatory because of heavily weighted pop quizzes.

By far the least engaging class I have ever taken at any institution. If you enjoy staring at a PowerPoint presentation for 75 minutes, then this class is for you. Awful professor who gives long/difficult excel assignments without understanding that this is a required course for all business students and this is their first time taking this course. If you have common sense you can easily excel in this class w/o studying til you get to graphs.

Absolutely incredible professor, definitely my favorite throughout my college career. So flexible and understanding with students' schedules. You can tell he cares about his students a lot and wants them to succeed. Definitely recommend taking a class of his. He will be your favorite.
Easy on missing deadlines. Helpful for students sictuations. Very kind.
The professor is nice and knows the content. My only biggest concern was the McGraw Hill textbook. Was a waste of my time. But I had no problems with the professor
I'm disappointed with the other reviews. Carlos is a very good professor and knew what he was teachn

Literally not even a teacher. Everything is done through McGraw Hill. No reason to go to class because all he does is read the slides.

Class lectures are awful, the slides are taken straight from mcgraw hill and all homework is through them too, the homework "practice problems" are way too difficult and we have never once in class gone over a problem as complicated as the ones on there, over all its difficult to understand him in lectures and you learn everything yourself

Was incredibly empathetic to issues outside of class that inhibited ability to get papers in on time. For every project he gave a lots of constructive and helpful feedback. Only can do well if you know everything about the class beforehand. Genuinely cannot teach and has insane amounts of the work, and has irrational expectations from students. If you have the option do not take him.

The HW and quizzes were easy, but he was really unclear about the tests, especially the final. For some reason he was really anal about dumb things like HW format and leaving class early. Accent is not bad.

NOOO sense of humor. None.

Dr.Talata is a very good lecturer. His English is not great, but it is good enough if you are interested in learning the material. He develops the concepts very well by posing very good questions. His English is bad, so it is hard to understand the lecture. His lecture is not clear, but he is a nice guy. He is always willing to help you, even thought it is not very helpful.
No Comments

He teaches nothing at all, and his English is sketchy.  Very disappointed with the results.  Leave this class immediately if he is your professor.  I promise it will be your best decision.

Not an effective communicator or teacher by any means. If you struggle in math and need step by step instruction, do not take his class. If you can teach yourself and don't need the help of the professor, his class is for you!

He is a good person but not a good one at teaching. Needed to self study every subject.

Great professor. He does a good job explaining concepts and giving practice problems during lectures. The practice exams were extremely helpful for exam prep. Hard class but awesome professor. Study the lecture notes and practice exams and you'll do just fine. Lectures are recorded but you have to show up for the clicker points.

My favorite prof I've had so far. Super approachable guy, gives great lectures with all the info you need to do well, and provides tons of study materials for the exams. If you have the chance to take Teator for CHEM 330 you should do it!

Really helpful and nice guy. But I did not learn much in class or with any materials he personally provided. Enjoyed the class a lot

Great guy, would take again and was thorough with all material. Anyone who struggles in the class must just pay 0 attention to not do good in his class. Great professor clearly cares for what he does. Exams are bit harder than Benson but he makes sure you are prepared and as long as you study you will do great. Teator was the best and my favorite professor I have had at KU. He is so unbelievably nice and knowledgeable about the subject he is teaching. need more study materials for sure. it's not the student's problem to do not have extra 874352934654 hours per week to go to his office hours bro..
just a huge NO

reviews.comment: He knows the material, but he's not a good teacher. He always chooses the harder way to explain topics, making learning unnecessarily difficult. His exams are much harder than Benson's, and he provides no proper study materials. Honestly, any random classmate could teach better.

There was very limited options for OChem professors at KU, he was definitely a good addition. I know many people take Professor Teator because they couldn't get into Bensons class. Thank you for my letter of recommendation for graduate school!!!!

I have taken ASL III and IV from this professor. ASL I and II that I took from other professors was  E A S Y. I really had to work in ASL III and IV. Learned a lot of new material and improved my signing skills. He returns graded tests quickly. Gives good feedback .
I. just found out that I got into graduate school. Thank you Dr Malcom for your letter of recommendation. I learned alot from you and appreciate what you did for me!!
He is one of the BEST professors I have ever worked with. He has NO favorites and expects everypone to take this new language seriously.

He provides quick feedback on everything. In my other ASL courses, I barely received any direct feedback. In this course, I receive feedback each week. I knew exactly what I had done wrong. If you are serious about learning how to sign correctly then this is the class for you.

He helped me get into Graduate School. I learned so much in his course. I really had to study hard to learn the material. He always answered my messages immediately and gaveme the extra explanations I needed to learn the material.

What a great professor. He is super quick with his feedback and grading of assignments. It allows you to fix mistakes before submitting your next assignment. He is also willing to work with you by offering early reviews of your signing project for the course.

Be ready to work in this class. You'll get what you put into it. Students who complain are doing so cuz they are trying to get by without fully doing his work. He is a deaf professor and knows his stuff.

He is extremely frustrating.

I took this class online to match my schedule at KU and my job. You need to study the videos each week to know how to gloss everything. I'm glad I took this course from a deaf professor. I learned alot about deaf culture.
You have all semester to work on your ASL project. I loved the ASL III class. I'll miss having him as my teacher. in ASL IV.
He gives fast feedback each week. If you follow what he tells you then you'll see an improvement in your signing. I have had him as a professor before and each time I had a positive experience.

I worked hard for my grade in this class. The class was well organized and everything was online. It let me work around my schedule at my job. I liked the diversity of signs that I learned during this course. Professor was always responding quickly to my questions.
Excellent course. We had to learn to gloss a storybook. He gave us early feedback and all semester to work on the storybook. Everything in this class is done online.
