Dr Malcom thank you so much for all your help on my storybook project. Your early review really helped me see what I was doing wrong. I appreciate your help. Your the best!

I have never received such quick feedback on my tests from any other professor. If I had a question, he always answered within 24 hours. This course allowed me to better communicate with deaf friends I have. He takes this course seriously and also offered early reviews for feedback on the main course assignment for the semester.

I was going through a rough time and he constantly checked on me. He explained things to me that I was not understanding and was available consistently. Always received responses through e-mail quickly. Can't wait to take his ASL 4 class.
He wrote a letter of reference for me to get into graduate school.

So unwilling to work with students in any scenario. Students struggle, they go through things as people and this man simply doesn't care, he ignored my emails asking for help and to meet up, and gave me no slack. Will knock off 40 points for not doing something as simple as raising your eyebrows. Good luck.
I learned so MUCH in such a short period of time. This professor kept me on my toes. He gives great feedback for you to follow to improve your signing.
Loved the class, loved the professor and can't wait to take ASL II
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He allows you to work all semester on your project. He will also give you early feedback on your signing skills. This helped me alot. He does not accept any late work so have everything turned in on time. Great guy!

Dr. Malcolm was ok for ASL 3 but not ASL 4. I really want to learn ASL, but the environment is not conductive of learning, just copying. You sign sentences and words in video submissions as shown in the prior videos. Final was tough: sign the song glossed in ASL within the two min of the song. Not taught how to do that. Didn't learn in his class.

The reason I got into graduate school is because of Dr Malcolm. I worked hard in his class. He shows no favoritism with his students. If you expect to turn in late assignments this is not the class for you. He is strict and will not accept them. He gives you all semester to prepare for the final project.
I have NEVER liked learning foreign languages. I enjoyed this class and the professor.
Be ready to work. His goal is to make you as fluent as possible. Listen to his feedback and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: You have all semester to work on your main project for the class. Lessons are well organized each week online. Doing the weekly lessons made doing the final test easy. Everything is taken from the weekly lessons.

I have taken several of Dr Malcoms ASL classes. You have to do your assignments each week to learn how to gloss correctly. Dont try to submit work late cuz he wont accept it. He has inspired me to become an ASL Interpreter.

You will have homework every week. It helps to prepare you for your final exam and class project. If you do your weekly assignments you will do well. Be open to his feedback and you'll improve. Submit your project for his early review option and he will help you.

He provides weekly videos to show you how to correctly gloss your work. Major assignments are not due until the end of the semester. Questions for the final exam are all taken from his weekly videos. He will not accept late work. If you expect to cram everything at the end of the course you wont do well.

I am so sorry to see this class end. I wish he taught more ASL classes at KU. He helped me all semeser with my ASL issues. He is the quickest grader I have ever had at KU. I knew exact what work needed to be completed by the end of the semester. Everything is so well organized. I will you next semeser!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I learned so much in this course. I just received my grade and I'm pleased with my progress. During the course he offers early reviews where he helps you with the song project. He gives you the entire semester to work on it. Take him up on the early review.  He will show you how to do better. He did the same thing for me in ASL III.
You will learn a lot in this course. He wrote a letter of reference for me that helped me get into Graduate School!

This class was online. He gave the entire semester to work on our ASL project. It was not due until the end of the course. He also reviewed my project "early" before I submitted it to give me feedback on how to improve. Not many professors offer you that kind of assistance.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The professor is deaf and provides everything in an asychronrous environment. It worked perfectly for me to do around my job on campus. He really knows his stuff.
I worked hard in this class and it paid off. He explains things clearly. Don't be late with any of your assignments. He gives you all week to complete them before they are due. He really helped me.
You will get "out" of this course what you put "into" the course. He is very helpful and kind but will not tolerate late work or disrespectful individuals. My ASL skills have improved because of him.

I have never had a professor who was so disrespectful to students. It's an online class, but he has a no tolerance policy for late work. Even after emailing him all week that my laptop was broken, he still wouldn't let me turn it in late and gave me all zeros.

I absolutely love Professor Malcolm. I have taken him for both ASL I and ASL III. He is extremely knowledgeable about the deaf community and ASL, since he is apart of it. All assignments are very straight forward and we have discussion posts once a week. He cares a lot about his students. He is an awesome person!!

Literally such a nice guy. When doing papers that might have confusing criteria he had all of us book meetings to check in to make sure we were doing okay. He gave really good feedback and his grading criteria was clear. Would take again!

Aaron Long is one of my favorite professors I have ever had at KU. He is really funny and extremely personable so feeling intimidated to talk to him was never ever an issue. I'd always be laughing in lecture. His writing assignments are difficult but he makes it easier by being there to answer questions and he is always happy to help. 10/10 rec.

He grades his papers extremely difficult for a basic-level English class. He takes multiple days to respond to emails. He does not care about his students. He told me he would respond as he is able. That is not the tone of a professor who wants you to be successful. I would not recommend his class. I would try for a different professor.

Professor Long really cares about his students learning. He always is ready to give good feedback and is always interested in each student's ideas. While some of the papers were tough, the class is definitely set up for student success.

Dr. Long is the best English professor I have ever had and the best professor I have had at KU so far. He truly cares about every student and puts time towards making sure everyone succeeds in the class but also in the future. He gives great feedback on the writing assignments, which can often be a little tricky but he always is there to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is very fast paced and you'll have to be ready to write papers weekly. That being said, Aaron is very knowledgeable and overall friendly which makes his class a lot of fun. He'll make you work for it, but he will also make you a much better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Aaron was one of the most passionate, helpful, and encouraging teachers I have ever had. Meet with him outside of class because his knowledge is expansive, and he is extremely easy to talk to. I highly highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you don't love literature and are unwilling to follow provided instructions, I might not recommend this professor. But, you would /really/ be missing out on a fantastic class. Mr. Long cares about the subject and his students - you will learn SO much. Do follow the rubric! Not enough to just write well - he grades exactly how he says he will.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor, made British literature exciting and interesting, and I'm generally not one to get excited about English classes. Couldn't recommend him enough. Enlightening, engaging, and humorous!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you are willing to keep up with the readings and want to learn, then I cannot recommend Aaron's class enough.  The papers are challenging, but doable. I recommend outlining to make sure all criteria are met before writing the actual paper itself. The topics make it difficult to write a great paper the night before it is due.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Aarons tough but he also helps you out if you go talk to him. Also go to his review sessions, they make papers easier.  His papers are tough but his assignment sheets are detailed and we talked him into giving us a later due date. Good guy.  He makes you think.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The feedback on your papers is minimal. The expectations in the class is outrageous. The essay topics could encompass 1,000 ideas but he wants you to pick 1.  Find another professor, trust me. I'm helping you :)

This is one of the best professors I have had at KU. He does grade essays tough, but he is more throughout than almost all other professors. He incredibly easy to talk to during office hours and is interesting in your growth as a student.  Hopefully I can take another class from him soon.

I have taken two courses with ALong. He sets very clear expectations for the class in the syllabus. He reports grades quickly with clear feedback. The classroom is discussion based ; he doesn't have the final say. Be ready to read the material, participate, and write papers. He is quirky, passionate, sensitive, and relates topics to current events.

Aaron really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He is always available to discuss papers during office hours, and provides clear and helpful feedback. In this course there is a lot of reading, but Aaron clearly has a passion for the seamonsters and submarines topic of this course and works hard to make class discussions interesting

You'd better be ready to read. Be sure to follow the course schedule and instructor since you sure have to find something more than just reading it outloud. Also, if you think you are lost, don't hesitate to talk to instructor. He has great ability to guide lost student to right direction. Also, when you write, you'd better spend some time on it.

Definitely by far one of the best professors I've ever had. Very professional, easygoing, and understating. Cares about his students and wants them to succeed, but will also give constructive criticism when necessary.

No tests except 4 papers which are super easy if you follow along. He gets pissed if he finds out you don't read the homework but theres not usually a way he can find out and if he does he doesn't act on it. He's super easy to talk to which makes him more helpful than other professors. I would take his class again.
Aaron is awesome! He is always there for each student and cares about everyone. It is very obvious that he wants you to do well and will help you to succeed.
Great guy. He's really helpful, and wants to meet each student individually. Sometimes papers can be difficult, but he's a phenomenal teacher.
Aaron really cares about each student, he definitely tries to make you learn everything he can teach you. Won't regret if you take the course with him.

Mr. Long is an excellent teacher! He makes the classroom fun and engaging, which is important to students because then we're more likely to participate. You know how they say the more you put in the more you get back, that statement is true for this professor. I would definitely take another one of his courses.

Mr. Long is an excellent teacher! He made lecture fun and engaging, which is important because it makes students more prone to participate in class. You know how they say the more work you put in the more you get back, that was true for his class.  I would definitely take another one of his courses.

Easily one of the best professors I've worked with. His treatment of the subject material makes you want to come to class. Class time is always engaging and thought-provoking. Subject matter for this class was decided by the professor. He put together a unique and very interesting schedule of study - one that applies to real-world developments.

Long was one of the best instructors I have had as an undergrad. He really cares about his students, their education, and their futures. He will not hesitate to work with you outside of class to accomplish your work if your schedule is crammed with other things. You must participate in class. He makes it very engaging and easy to do this.
Aaron has proved to be more helpful than any professor or other TA that I've had. He is professional, personable, helpful, and makes class enjoyable. Easily one of my favorite classesteachers.

Great teacher. Never been the biggest fan of English but always loved reading. ALong is so passionate about what he teaches that you become engaged without even trying to. Our final assignment was a paper analyzing a song of our choice, it was awesome and forced you to think critically. Tough grader, but very clear expectations.
Ron's one of my favorite professors at the Univarsity of Michigan. He is the reason why I added an Economics degree to my plans. Long Live The Ron.

This professor is ableist. He does not like to accommodate students with disabilities. Expect significant pushback, even if you have a visible disability and approved accommodations. He made me take an exam for half my grade from a hospital room with an IV in my arm. He had no understanding during Covid. He was never accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher. Very funny in class. I would definitely recommend him.

Although he left the University I figured I'd rate him for anyone at his new school. He is by far the best teacher I've ever had. Very thorough, clear, knowledgeable,helpful, etc. Use the practice problems he hands as, they are very helpful

He's awesome! He gives you practice problems, which are almost the same to the questions asked on tests. If you need help, go to his office hours. He's always willing to help and explain what you don't understand. If you try & study enough you'll get an A. Just make sure you understand the concepts.

Great Professor, he does a great job of conveying the material and making sure you know what will be on the test. Very laid back but also very knowledgeable. He gives out practice tests WITH ANSWERS and if you practice these you will ace the tests. I took another one of his Undergrad classes and both times I enjoyed them and got an A.
Excellent professor! He is extremely helpful and very clear. Great charisma as well. He makes his class really interesting
Without a doubt, best professor I have had so far at KU. I recommend his class to anyone.
The teaching staff for Econ at KU is overall very good, but Caldwell is by far one of the best educators at the entire University
Best Econ professor at KU! Explains material so that it's easy to understand. Very helpful outside of class and enjoys talking to students. Test are all essay but fairly easy...no homework

Very good professor. Cares about his students and really teaches in a way which is very easy to understand. He outlines everything that is due in the class and gives MANY helpful handouts before tests. He is also very quick on grading so you don't wait a month to see your grade in his class. Overall I had a great experience.
Amazing!

He's a great teacher/person! The material is a little boring but he does his best at keeping your interest. The tests are basically over what he does in class, so even though it's not mandatory, come to class. He explains both concepts and practical uses constantly and really helps students understand the material. I would definitely recommend him!
Recommend! He really thinks of the students. Approachable, patient and caring. Loved his class! Go to class, take notes and you'll get a good grade. Text book is not necessary.

The class was well structured, well taught, fairly grade (as in I don't think a single person could have had any surprises).  And more importantly, he is quite entertaining.  I enjoyed going to class.
I would recommend anyone to take this class. He explains everything clearly and is willing to help his students. This was the best Econ class I've taken at KU so far!
BEST ECON PROFESSOR AT KU BY FAR. KNOWS WHAT HE'S TALKING ABOUT, LIKES WHAT HE TEACHES, LIKES TEACHING. WHETHER YOU TRY TO, OR NOT, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE NOT TO ACTUALLY LEARN SOMETHING FROM HIS CLASSES.
one of my favorite teachers ever. very intelligent and a really good teacher all around.

my favorite teacher on campus. Labor is really interesting, hes very straightforward, funny and sometimes brings treats!! very in tune to students status in the class and will take time to help individuals. thanks ron, and thanks for including me on the final exam lol
Great teacher.  Rons the man.  He explains evrything with clearity and is very helpful as well.  He has many office hours and is always willing to help a student.
Awesome teacher. Very nice and very fair.
He is a really good professor, I would only highly recommend his classes, he will work with you extensively inside and outside of class and is generally super helpful.
A very good professor.  One of the best I have ever had.  Show up to class and coplete the assigined homework and the class will go smoothly.  A few missed classes are no big deal.

Prof. Scurto's lectures were extremely unengaging and he simply read the slides word-for-word. This class has the potential to be applicable and engaging, alas that does not happen here. Exams were extremely difficult. He finally came to his senses and made the last two tests online and open note. I am glad he is not teaching this class next year.

Lectures are not engaging, Prof. Scurto just reads off slides that are very close to the textbook. Tests cover large sections of content and questions get very specific. Tests are mostly memorization MC and fill in the blank with an essay section without clear instructions of what is needed. Do the extra credit assignments as offered.

Prof. Scurto was the worst type of engineering professor. He acted like he didn't want to be there and it was him vs us. Lectures consisted solely on flipping through Powerpoints. He would answer any questions you had on homework with conceptual answers hoping you'd guide yourself to the next step and told the TAs to do the same.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Scurto makes this class impossible. Homeworks take a full week in order to finish and you will only get half credit anyways. Few examples are given to understand how to solve any problems and you are expected memorize everything in every chapter. Exams were alright but they had no exam reviews besides going over every lecture slide. Prepare to fail

Scurto talks at you about his days at DuPont and the only examples he gives you in class are those that apply to being a professional engineering nothing to aid you in homework or his tests. If the amount of time on his homework doesn't drain the soul out of you then the 50 you get on each exam will.
Dr. Scurto will make a man or woman out of you if you pass both semesters...

You can't be considered a Chem-E unless you had Dr. Scurto. He is one of the best professors I have ever. had. Dr. Scurto has so much knowledge and experience in Thermodynamics it's not even funny. If you are serious about learning, you can gain so much knowledge. Expect to work your ass off.. I spent all-nighters for almost every HW. Respect

This is pretty much a self-taught course. Only reason I attended lecture was in case there was a pop quiz. I ended missing all but one of the pop quizzes and still got a B. The material is not hard but let's be honest, the expectations are unrealistic. Good luck kiddies.

Not only is Dr. Scurto an incredibly gifted lecturer, he is also terrifically helpful during office hours. I must place a caveat on the latter comment: you must learn how to get help out of him. He is a believer in the "figure it out on your own approach" so learn how to ask good questions and go to office hours frequently so he knows YOU better.

The class is manageable, but it's definitely not one to blow off. Scurto is usually helpful during class, but his 'ask you more questions than you ask him' approach to office hours often doesn't get anything accomplished. There's a monster curve at the end of the class, so calculating grades will only get you a very general idea of where you are.

This is a hard class, but not as hard as it is hyped up to be. The key is memorize every one of those slides he posts for the qualitative section of the tests and know how to do EVERY in class problem and suggested problem. Do not waste your time on the text book. I did that for the first test and got a 66 memorized slides for the next, 96.
Lube up, this class is coming in hard. Homework takes legitimate days, pop quizes will demolish you, tests are graded ridiculously harshly. If you really wanna be a ChemE, just survive and advance.

Professor Scurto is hands down the worst instructor ive had at any university. He blatantly disregards students emails, spends the majority of his time telling you how you can learn better, rather than actually teaching, and expects unnecessary amounts of time. The courses he teaches would be exponentially easier if a caring professor taught it.

If you have passed CPE 221 with Scurto, then you should already know that this class will devour your semester. Take the difficulty of CPE 221 and then double it. Homeworks will require much of your time, about 30+ hours per assignment. You are to learn and memorize everything in order to do well on his exams.

This class will control your semester. You are basically expected to know everything about everything covered in the book and notes, even if it's not covered in class. There were topics on the final that we never went over. He doesn't curve tests like other teachers so you have no idea what grade you're getting until it's posted by the registrar.

Scurto is a beast. He is very hard. I was a 4.0 student my whole life. Until you enter real ChemE and 212 with him is incredibly hard. Do not expect any grade, just study your hardest and see what happens. Not impossible, but converts you into a real chemical engineer. Good luck sophomores!!!

This is a hard class. I think it would be a hard class regardless of who is teaching; Scurto doesn't really make it easier but he doesn't really make it harder either. Know the equations he says to know; he'll give pop quizzes on them. Make sure you look at the book examples, as sometimes he puts them on the test.

Scurto will ruin your semester, but if you have a little drive you should pass with no problem. Don't cheat in the slightest though. Gives large curves at the end so just keep working, the tests will be very similar to the HW and the final will be the easiest test. Very effective teacher, you will probably know a lot of thermo at the end

Class is useless and office hours are even more useless. Test averages are below 50%. Save yourself time and switch majors now; civil, mechanical or petroleum. He has never had a real job so what does he really know?

The material that this course covers is very difficult, and I think that it would be a very stressful class regardless of who was teaching it. However Scurto made it more difficult than was necessary. He was very unhelpful in office hours and his lectures were basically useless. He expects you to put his class above everything.

Process thermo will be one of the most difficult, stressful, and frustrating courses you will ever take. Dr. Scurto is very effective communicator and sets clearly-defined expectations. The griping about this course should be attributed to the nature of the material and the textbook, not the professional qualifications of the instructor.

He's a good teacher because he knows his stuff, is perfectly capable of explaining everything, and cares about the students. Unfortunately, his philosophy of teaching the class is to make it absurdly difficult, which in itself is destructive to the students' learning experience. He somehow takes a serious job too seriously.

You don't have to ask Scurto for help. He comes to you and asks if you want help. He is so informative and is very adequate and precise in his teaching style. He immerses you in the world of fugacity, balances, and  activity coefficients. It is undoubtedly an experience to savor. Why go to the movies when you could go to Process Thermo!

After 2 years of grade inflation everybody is appalled to have an instructor with standards. The class certainly does feel hopeless and many may not do well. But the problem is reading the very difficult book in the time required, not the guy teaching it.

Professor openly regards himself as the self-designated gatekeeper to the profession. Does not do examples in class, will not post homework solutions online, bans solutions manuals. Designs exam questions that can't be answered and admits to it with pride. Does not suggest study material before exam - student expected to memorize all equations.

Homework is incredibly difficult, but make sure you put a lot of time into it. It can determine if you pass given your riding the line.  Tests were graded unfairly and inconsistently.  Other than that, his goal is to turn you from a student into a professional chemical engineer, and he does just that.

Takes a hard topic and makes it even more difficult.  The notes he presents in class are useless and typically just formulas and figures from the book that he decides not to explain.  Expects students to memorize pointless equations for essay questions on exams.  Does not provide useful feedback or post solutions on blackboard.

WOW.  Process thermo is a hard class in itself, but Scurto takes it to a whole other level.  You will need to put in at least 20 hours a week (no joke), or you will get burned by his tests. If you are not meant to be a Chemical Engineer Scurto will be the one to make you drop out of C&PE.  Good Luck.

HAHAHAHAhaaha good luck. You're going to need it. If he tells you to memorize or learn something...do it because it WILL be on one of the few quizzes he gives. Plan on spending 10 hours or more per homework assignment and 20 plus hours studying for each test.
No Comments
Best Teacher Ive ever had

Definitely a great lecturer. He presents the information in a concise way that's easy to understand and is also very funny throughout. He shares a lot of funny stories throughout lectures which make class a lot more enjoyable. He's a really fun guy to learn from.

Great lecturer, but only take this class if you have a prior interest in the study of Christianity. A good grade was dependent on if you personally felt the need to engage in the material. Lots of reading and his lectures are long, but Dr. Ketchell is a great speaker and will always present the material in a funny and thought provoking way.
Very hard class to be 100 level. Have to do hours of studying for the exam. Study guide is put up only a week before test. It takes 2 weeks for the TA to grade exams. Try avoiding this class.

I did not take this class by any means thinking I would get an A but my god for a 100 level class to be as difficult as this was. Ketchell wants you to actually learn in this class and I absolutely did. But when it came to test its like he wants you to fail. I don't recommend this class to anyone unless you're looking to kill your GPA.

Ketchell is a great teacher.  Somehow we managed to learn a lot while simultaneously having a great time.  Classes are dynamic and interactive. You have to do the work to get an A but I always looked forward to this class so that was no problem!

This class is a lot tougher than I thought it would be. There is a ton of information to memorize and he assigns about 10-20 pages of reading per class period. The only grades are 4 tests, each of which require writing an essay over a given topic. The TA is helpful and he is too, but the class is still pretty difficult. I thought about dropping.

Not a difficult class at all.  Yes you must read, but it is easy reading and no more than 10-20 pages per class.  Lectures are straight forward and the questions on the test are straight from lectures and texts.
This was an undergraduate seminar class on American Popular Culture and Religion. Take this class. No tests!
Great teacher, had him in the Christianity class, highly recommend him and he has a good sense of humor
D-Ketch is an amazing teacher and super sexy. He gets the job done quickly and teaches us everything we need to learn. TAKE HIS CLASSES! ROCK CHALK!
Easily the best professor I've had in years. I am in REL 339 right now, and it's amazing. Take his classes! He is extremely wise, ask him questions too.

rel104 required way too much studying for an intoductory class- tons of information... made the class very overwhelming. tests were extremely precise you really have to know the material to get a good grade on them... i'm talking HOURS of studying
By in large, loved every minute of it!
Very bad Teacher

I took Rel in America (i can't remember the section #). It was Amazing. The class was great and he had a lot to share. The use of the text book is tremendous. He brings in videos and uses a lot of various media forms. Great topic to study.
No Comments

Dr. Joy is a great prof he cares a lot about the subject but really makes you learn it. He is literally always available to help outside of office hours and he is super fun to get to know. There is a Quiz at least 1 time a week and it is extra credit so attendance is highly encouraged (you will not pass if you skip). He is super test heavy so study

He's very clear and informative, and makes a lot of great geeky jokes. He taught me a lot about Numerical Analysis, coding, and even Differential Equations (which was a poorly taught prereq for the class). Plus, he printed out the textbook instead of making us buy it.

Joy's a really great teacher. He asked a lot from his students, but taught Numerical Analysis very clearly, and even taught the Laplace stuff in a way that made it "click". This course also gave me a lot of great Matlab experience. He printed off sections of the book instead of making us buy it, which was another bonus.

He's a really nice guy, but I found the class to be pretty difficult.  He definitely knew what he was talking about, but most of us were lost when it came to the tests.  He gives out a lot of extra credit and is willing to explain things after class or in the help room.

He was my TA for MATH 101.  It was his first semester of teaching a class, and he wasn't the best by any means.  He did know his stuff and was always willing to help.  Gave out lots of extra credit.  If you're willing to work, he's a good TA.  I think most of us passed his class.

I was consistently challenged in this course. He encouraged me to do better each week and gave me written feedback to follow. He wrote me a letter of recommendation for Graduate School and I just found out I was accepted. Thanks you Dr Malcolm!!!

I have never had a professor grade my assignments and give me written feedback weekly. He also sent me weekly emails riding my butt to follow up with me to do better in class. I ended up passing the course and I'm thankful for his caring about me.

I only took this course to fulfill my foreign language credit. I never thought learning sign language would be so challenging. The professor pushed me to excel and learn this new language. I felt challenged every week and im now thankful I took this class and learned about a new culture.

I learned many signs during my time in ASL. The professor is strict but will push you to do your best. Turn all your assignments in on time each week. Watch all his videos throughout the week. I took his online course so he allows us to work with the videos all week.

Everything was well organized. He broke our major class project down into individual parts. He even gave us an early review with his feedback on our signing skills before he graded us. He wrote a wonderful letter of recommendation for me to go to graduate school.
Loved the course and the professor. Everything was clearly explained and laid out from day one. He always responded to my e-mails in a timely manner.

He lets you take all week to do assignments. He gives written feedback on all assignments each week. All lessons are videotaped so you can watch them over and over. I have learned a TON of new signs in this course. He does not accept any late work so submit everything on time.
ASL was different from perosivius teachings, grades were never consistent. Feed back was useless, no opportunities to actually learn.

Super fast to give feedback on assignments so you can correct your mistakes. You have a full week to do your assignments. I was glad that this course was offered online so I was able to take it since Im not on campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The entire course is asynchronous. The professor is deaf so you are learning from someone who actually uses the language daily. He gives you all week to complete the assignments. Everything is well organized and as long as you submit your assignment by 10pm each Friday, you will be ok. Just dont submit late. He doesnt play favorites with students.

Everything is so well organized for this course. If you follow his syllabus you'll have no problems. The dues dates for everything are exactly the same each week so you never have to worry about sending in anything late. He even offers early feedback on the major project for the course. Follow his advise on how to improve your skills.

As ssoon as I came into this course I quickly realized that other students were ahead of me. I found ASL I and ASL II to be courses where I got an easy "A." My other courses in ASL did not prepare me for ASL III. This professor helped me to get caught up and to realize that learning is not always about getting an "A." He is well respected.

Definately look foward to going to it every week, and its a shame he only teaches this one class!  If you have an opportunity to take ASL I, you should definately do it!!!!  We love Dr. Malcolm!

I was a bit annoyed with her teaching style. She rushes through topics and gives no practice on them at all. Additionally, she doesn't round grades, so have fun being stuck with a B if you get an 89.5. I think she grades too harshly in proportion to her lackluster instruction.

Probably the worse professor I have ever had at KU. I'm a senior double majoring and I have never had a teacher who can't communicate or teach to the level of this teacher. I learned nothing from this class and had to threaten to go to the dean to get errors fixed. Don't take this class!

She lectures heavy by reading off the slides and throws random top hat quizzes everyday that most of the students miss. She will quiz you then after you get it wrong she'll explain (partially). Then, onto the next question. Would not recommend if you actually want to learn.

Professor Maeng seems like she is a nice person, but as a professor I just do not find her engaging at all. Her lectures just consist of reading slowly off a powerpoint for over an hour and then you have to do tophat questions over it. The class is not very difficult, but it is hard to want to focus when you are just being read information.

Maeng is by far the worst professor I have ever had. Want to get in contact with her? Better hunt her down because she will not email you back. She reads word for word of the slides & doesn't actually teach. She uses tophat to test throughout the lecture how well you understand but then doesn't explain the questions and moves on even when wrong.

I found this class to be very useful for my major. Material in it of itself can be challenging if you don't pay attention in class, so pay attention and participate! She made herself available whenever I needed help. Go to her office hours, she'll pretty much walk you through whatever you may not understand. Put in the work and you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This professor is amazing and is incredibly easy to work with. She is so easy to talk to and she's always willing to help out anyone that asks. There were some "required" online articles we had to buy, but if you split the cost with someone that'd be fine because we didn't really use them. Follow her rubric and you'll get an A+ without doingtoomuch

I liked her overall. Her accent is very strong and I can see why some students may have trouble with the course. I only opened the textbook 2 times during the semester, and since it is $300, I would save my money. Go visit her in her office for a look-over on group projects and she is extremely helpful. Very nice person, just hard to understand.
Dr. Ahn is one of the best professors that I've ever had. She's hilarious, dedicated to her students, and very clear in her teaching and expectations. I learned a lot without being stressed out.

Dr. Ahn teaches in a clear manner. She will ask for your participation in the class, but you will want to do so, because she remembers her students. She is very kind and wants her students to do very well. Skipping class will diminish your learning experience. Best class I've had, always looked forward to class. Didn't like chemistry, now I love it

Dr. Ahn is amazing. I thought I hated chemistry going into this class, but I came out surprisingly interested in chemistry. Dr. Ahn is the most helpful professor and I loved attending her office hours. Go to them! She wants to know you. by far my favorite professor so far at KU. She was the best.
I dreaded O-chem my entire life but Dr. Ahn makes it easy and understandable. Go to her office hours and ask questions and you'll be golden.

Dr. Ahn is the best teacher I had in my undergraduate career at KU. Very knowledgeable in Organic Chemistry and sincerely wants students to do well. Go to class, take quizzes, read book, attend review sessions and you will get an A. She offers random extra credit for attendance as well, so make sure you do attend class. Very very helpful professor.

Dr. Ahn is an amazing teacher! She's incredibly knowledgable about organic chemistry and she also makes herself very available to students outside of class to answer all their questions. Definitely the best teacher I have had in my undergrad at KU
she is extremely nice and cares about her students.
I loved her. She is really nice and definitely recognizes your hard work. She might seem very serious but she is helpful and hardworking.
She is super nice and very fair in her grading of lab reports. I definitely recommend taking it with her. Just ask whenever you need help.

Prof. Ahosseini is a really nice Prof. She really wants her students to succeed and will help you understand anything. You just have to go to her office hours. Don't just expect to get everything in class. This class was hard because it was the first thermo class i took. But it was a good experience.

Dr. Ahosseini is nice and surely educated, but her attempts to relate course material to examples students can understand stretch as far as the book does. There is little help to be found outside of the solutions manual, so I would invest in that to get through the course. This course coupled with her teaching made me seriously reconsider my major.

Professor was great but it's hard to explain just how much of a waste of time this class was. Attendance is required just to talk to someone who doesn't want to be there about their pet cat. Biol499 just needs to be removed from the school entirely

100% the best professor that I had in my 3 years at KU.  Only complaint about him is that he does not teach more undergraduate classes. Hilarious and you can tell that his main priority is that the students are learning to their best ability. Lenient with deadlines as long as you approach him about it and gives benefit of the doubt when grading.

We had TONS of work in this class this year, but it got easier as the semester went on and it helped a lot with keeping a good grade. Ackley is a great guy and really cares about his students. We did have to wait a really long time to get any feedback on the assignments, but other than that it was a decent class. Definitely not easy but worth it.

One of my hardest courses, mainly due to the amount of homework. Expect to really engage in scientific literature--if this is new to you, it will be tough, but its a necessary skill that he teaches well. You should get good at this by the end of the course, so I recommend it if you plan on entering research. Really cares about his students.

This class is tough but for good reasons. This is a capstone course, and heavily integrates previous classes. Memorization is not enough to pass, familiarization and understanding is. No textbook, only lecture slides and papers for review. Open ended exams, be prepared to think. Dr. Ackley always provides feedback and is accessible outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I really like Ackley, but he is not a good teacher. He really wants to help students get a good grade, but his lectures are disorganized and confusing. He could prepare the powerpoints much better so they make more sense. He also basically reads his slides and breezes right through the material. Hard class for those unfamiliar with the subject.

Dr. Ackley is pretty helpful. Whenever you have a question, you can set up an appointment and he will make time for you. You don't need to get  the book but if you don't understand something you can ask him. He makes the classes very interesting. The tests aren't that hard, you just have to study for them. LIke in any other Biology class.

If you like paying thousands of dollars for a class to have someone read to you, this is the class for you. In-class quizzes force you to come and listen to him read verbatim from is disorganized lecture slides. Class is just another part of the broken system we call "Higher Education".

Tries to keep things entertaining while keeping the lecture material straight. He doesn't really use the book, all of his questions come directly from lecture. Attendance isn't really mandatory, but he gives quizzes almost every day. Easy enough tests if you study, though some questions are unfair. Good to go to office hours, is a cool guy.

He is a wonderful professor for first year Architecture students. You will do lots of sketches, and I mean a lot but he really enforces "practices means perfect". The work load is on the heavier side but it is nothing too difficult. His instructions can be a little vague at first but it is nothing a one on one conversation can't solve.

I loved having Todd for studio. He was a great introduction to the degree. You will hear lots of things about him, but save any judgement until you take the class. He is absolutely hilarious, and he is almost always joking, it just takes some time to realize he isnt being serious. You will absolutely warm up to him! I would take him again anytime!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Todd cares about participation and attendance more than anything! He's not one of those professors who tries to intimidate you and maintains a casual studio setting. Be ready to pin up for the whole class and frequently. Not an overly harsh grader but you do have to work for it. Take risks in your projects, show up, and be eager to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Todd will give very unclear feedback and will contradict himself several times while critiquing a project. You essentially have to do what he wants in order to maintain a good grade, for he is not very open to new ideas. He will always point out everything wrong with what you did instead on helping you improve. Try to avoid taking him for your sake

It may be easy to slide by with a passing grade in his class, but it's not an easy A, you have to do the work. He gives constructive feedback and will create one or two projects that other studios don't do, which is unique as the curriculum is fairly uniform across first year, and this gives a bit of an advantage to whoever takes his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Todd was a fine teacher for my first semester of architecture. He is fairly vague, however, and his feedback makes it hard for you to improve your work. He's not a harsh critic, but his grading was tough like most other studio professors (but fair). If you want a good grade, you'll have to work for it. He's not as notorious as he's made out to be.
Becky really knows her stuff and she is a great professor. The class isn't too demanding and she makes it interactive and exciting.

Becky is awesome. She was extremely helpful throughout the semester and always made time to meet with students (I was in her office about 8 different times during the semester). Tests can be a little tricky but papers, homework, and attendance will save your grade. There are days when she looks really hot so it makes attending regularly worth it.
Becky really cares about her students and is there to help you 247.

Becky is awesome. She's super helpful. You don't need a text book which is extremely nice. Basically the class consists of 4 3-4 page papers, readings that you must submit responses to online, and 3 tests including the final. She gives an incredible amount of extra credit too. If you try, do the work, and the extra credit it is an easy A.

I feel I really lucked out in getting Ashley as a teacher for this Western Civ 2.  Her lectures are so interesting, that as long as you show up to class you can easily learn about each book.  I never did the reading but attended every class, and ended up getting an A.
Best professor at the university.

Ashley had some of the most organized and thought-provoking lectures I've ever seen.  She was very engaging and brought up important quotes in the lectures so you weren't left trying to figure everything out on your own.  She was helpful and fantastic.  If you have the chance to take her class, do it.

Ashley is fantastic. She makes this class really interesting and fun. Her lectures are so helpful that you really don't even have to read the books if you don't have time. She comes off as a hard ass the first day, but I think she just wants to establish her authority and make sure you know that coming to class is crucial. I highly recommend her!
Ashley is an awesome professor! I did not read a single western civ book but thanks to her lectures I did well in the class!

Honestly, she was pretty off putting at first. I had a family issue that put me way behind in my paper writing and she was beyond understanding. A very kind and caring person, who is also passionate with a dry sense of humor.

Ashley is easily one of my favorite teachers I've had at KU. She is passionate about all topics covered and makes the material written incredibly relevant to today's society. Creative paper topics, honest discussions and links to modern issues make the class so interesting. You won't have this much fun in Western Civ with anyone else!

Second best teacher I've had at KU. Amazing, easy to talk to, respectful(mostly). pretty free etc. Sometimes I felt though that she was too critical of religion and conservatives. Even if I agreed w/ her. Kind of a crazy feminist though. Don't let my last 2 comments scare you though, she is great!
Tries to be hardcore, but is one of the nicest teachers at KU. She is very devoted to teaching and is very good at it.
She is VERY strict in her grading & is not helpful or kind when you have questions. You either pass or fail w/ her...a lot of the class received C's & D's.

Ashley is one of the best teachers I have had at KU. She is absolutely amazing and makes Western Civilization FUN! (I know shocker!) If you are taking West Civ you should definitely try and get her! As long as you speak up in a class and honestly try you should do fine.
If you need to take western civ take it from her. No joke, one of the best GTA in the department or KU for that matter.
Ashley is simply one of the best GTA's ever. She's passionate about the material, funny to listen to, and great to talk with. Really, she's just the whole package.
She is cool. She cares about your abiity to do well in class. Her discussion will always be semi-interesting, and you will laugh. Hard paper grader though

Abbey is a nice professor who is knowledgeable about what she is teaching. She is very helpful with learning online programs. She also allows a lot of creative freedom. I enjoyed her class, but she takes forever to give you feedback. I Would often spend most of the four hour class waiting to get her feedback before I could continue with my work.

Like someone else mentioned, this review is more about ARCH 215 than Abbey, she is very nice. The class feels like a waste of time, everything taught could've easily been done online. The projects are super rigid, and with constant homework, it gets to a point where you're just turning things in to meet deadlines, not to actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is more for the class than Abbey as a professor. Abbey is very nice and I have heard she's a good studio professor, but this communications class sucks and is a waste of time and money. She has this class structured to do about everything else but learning how to present. It's a bunch of busy work that doesn't relate well to communications.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: While I really like abbey as a person. And appreciate how personable she is. As a first year architecture teacher she graded too harshly in my opinion as well as many other peoples opinions. And while was very understanding in some ways, It did not show in the grade. Again, very nice person but harsh grader and LOTS of outside work.

Abbey's really chill! I'd take her again, her feedback is good and she's personable and friendly. The class was remote with some in-person speeches but noticeable improvement in design, presentation, and public speech. Solid class with posting working and discussing methods and design.

Abby was one of my favorite teachers. Super flexible and helpful if anything comes up. Made sure I understood every project. It's definitely not an easy A kind of class but if you show up and do the work she will get you through. Lots of writing projects but decent amount of opportunities throughout the semester for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took Engl 102 with Abby. This is the first time in my life I actually enjoyed an English class. She is a very caring professor, and if you visit her office hours before a project is due, she gives you detailed feedback about what to change and whatnot. It is an easy A class if you are willing to put in the work. You do makeup for missed classes.
super sweet and understanding. works to make her class a stress free experience
I loved Abby she was understanding, a clear and easy grader, very thorough, and overall an excellent teacher. I would take another class with her.
Professor Breyer is young and cool. She is really relatable to students and wants them to succeed. She's also really understanding and communicative.
Professor Abby was a chill teacher. Enjoyed the class.

NEVER take this man's class. I have taken two of his classes and in both of them he was incredibly disorganized, unhelpful, and rude. He would leave out instructions and then fail us because we didn't read his mind. The worst professor I have ever encountered at KU. I will never take another class from him or in this department because of it.

For WGSS 344: Black Feminism, Abe and Arlowe were fantastic instructors. The space they created was unlike anything else I have had at KU and I only wish I could have engaged with it further. As long as you're down with the ideas and figures behind the namesake of this course, it's absolutely worth taking.

Weil is a great professor and his lectures are very enjoyable. There are essays, but I thought they were very fun to write and he's open to extending due dates. There are weekly quizzes about topics discussed in readings and in class but are really there to help your grade. The GTAs were also great and very knowledgeable which made class more fun.

The class was very disorganized and grading criteria were not always clear. Readings were often in the wrong order or TAs prepped the wrong readings. Dr. Weil opens the floor to students frequently allowing a handful of students to speak more than the professor or guest lecturer making the class feel like a never-ending discussion section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Weil is incredible! He really cares about students and even though the content in his classes are hard, he is extremely knowledgable and more than willing to work inside and outside of the classroom to help students understand content. I can't say enough good things about him, if you get the chance take his classes!
Easy class but she chooses favorites. She is also very condescending and passive aggressive.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have never wrote a review for a professor but this is the exception. Her class isn't hard with very limited assignments, they are very boring but she usually lets you out early. She grades so weirdly and never is consistent, she is passive aggressive and does not offer extra credit. Please try to avoid her at any costs.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER. She dances around the question if you ask a question. She is a rule follower so she then is also a hard grader. She comes off nice but is not really willing to help you. Good luck with this class if you have her
"I do not negotiate grades." She is not lenient about anything and very inflexible. Won't let you make anything up and offers no extra credit, so if you miss one thing it really hurts your grade.

She's the kind of prof that starts you out at a C and if you don't please her enough, you can kiss an A goodbye. She picks favorites in the first few weeks. I used to like public speaking, not anymore.
No Comments

Abbie is an excellent teacher.  Alot of her lectures aren't in the tests, but they are important to pay attention to if you want good grades on your speeches.  Don't start every speech with a question - it gets REALLY old ;)
No Comments
She is very fun and helpful and I like coming to this class.
If you are a girl, you get an A. She hates guys, and is the biggest feminist in the world.
Fun class.

I cannot begin to describe how passionate she is about her students succeeding. This past semester, I was in the process of getting diagnosed with an unknown illness that was making it really hard for me to show up to class. Not only was she the only professor to take me seriously, but she made sure I would succeed. I can't thank her enough.

She's the absolute best! Whenever I needed help she was there ready to assist me. Even though this class was difficult, she made it more manageable. She really cares for her students and wants them to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She was my lab teacher for my JOUR 150 class and she was a blessing to have as a professor. She would always respond to my emails and grade quickly. Gave great feedback on presentations and assignments. Great class to take if you are looking to complete you Oral Communication Goal!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She made me fall in love with business writing. Literally the best professor I've ever had in B school.

Professor Abwao is a fantastic professor. You can tell that she truly cares about her students and wants them to be successful. Having hailed from the journalism school, her lectures were always well-prepared and she remembers every little details about us. That being said, she is a tough grader, but she always gives good feedback.

I honestly hated how hard she made the class. But when I went to her office hours, she tried really really hard to make sure I get the best grade possible. Super kind and nice. Learned a lot more than I ever wanted. Great person. I just don't want to work so much for an A ever again
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: It is a lot of work with a discussion board and a 400-700 paper due every Sunday. She gives good feedback but does grade pretty tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: As is the case with online classes there is quite a bit of homework since there is no actual classroom time. It is manageable, though. She gives excellent feedback. You can take the quizzes more than once with only the best grade counting, so there is really no reason not to get 100% on them. Discussion board points are easy to get max value.
Great professor. Inspiring, aware of needs of students, and very fair. Also really knows her stuff. Strong recommendation

Dr. Dvorak is a kind and caring woman. However this class is somewhat of a joke in terms of actually learning valuable information. What is learned in class can easily be learned by reading the textbook. Attendance matters and you do a lot of group projects. The class sometimes felt like an 8th grade music class.

This is probably the slowest most mundane class I've ever taken. I can't think of a time I actually enjoyed the content and activities. There's this ridiculous idea that it's not a research class, but ALL YOU DO is related to your research project. The class feels very basic with spats of unnecessary projects and group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class moves at a glacial pace. She discusses the chapter quizzes that you take on Blackboard every class period, which is extremely boring. There is group work every day to "provide another method of learning." Its just time consuming and pointless. Overall, Dr. Dvorak is a nice person, the class however is a waste of time.

He usually cuts the lectures short. You can understand what he is saying, just ask questions if you don't understand. You don't need to use the textbook at all if you don't want to. The homework is all online. You get to use cheat sheets for the tests.

Dont get me wrong i am not biased by my grade in the class. His expectations are far greater than that of a lower level elementary algebra class. His curriculum went to chapter 10 where as other sections went to Chapter 4. The class is fast paced and the he assigns about 6 hours of homework a night. I will retake with other instructor

Abhik isn't too awful at teaching the material, but he assigns a ridiculous amount of homework (sometimes 10 hours a week for a 2 credit class) and the tests are very hard.  Everyone I had talked to said this was supposed to be an easy class, but apparently not with this Prof.

Very tough grader. Exams are a lot different than the homework problems. I heard from multiple people that took the class before that this was an easy A if you did the homework and paid attention. Wrong. Avoid if you value your gpa.
Run away. This guy was the most rigorous grader I have ever experienced.  I failed more quizzes in his class than I passed, unhelpful and condescending.

This professor is the WORST I have experienced in my college career. His grading criteria for tests is absolutely ridiculous and even if you got the answer right, if you don't find the answer the exact way he wants you miss the problem. Not helpful at all and treats students like dogs. NEVER take a class with this prof. AWFUL. Cannot stress enough

Not a lot of professors actually care about you especially in EECS but he does and he wants to see you succeed. This professor after every exam would always ask for feedback whether it was good or bad feedback. I never really went to his class but his assignments are very helpful and as long as you go over notes its easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Agah's class feels well structured and easy to digest. No comprehensive final so tests feel a lot less overbearing. Only critique is that multiple choice is only beneficial if you don't know what you're doing. All or nothing means a few questions wrong will land you a B or lower even if you knew most of the material.

Dr Agah is pretty funny, and although attendance at lectures isn't required, I recommend going just because he's so fun and you can learn a fair amount. The tests are only multiple choice, however, and I would say they aren't a good measure of understanding at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are very engaging, and he seems very down to earth. Labs aren't too challenging, but I also had a really good TA. Lets you make a cheat sheet for exams
Hes a good guy

Professor Agah is very caring about the class and his students. He ensured all lab TAs graded the same. Lectures were boring IMO but I could study and fill out my cheat sheet and do well enough on tests. Labs were pretty easy.

Dr. Agah is one of the best of KU EECS, funny and kind! 

He once came up to me on campus and asked if I was okay since I wasn't in class :( so sweet.

He makes you care about what you are learning and ties the topics back to real-world applications. 

One small problem I had were that the slides were a bit wordy and hard to read.

Just a genuinely great guy. Cares more about your understanding than anything. Labs and homework's arent too bad, and TA's are always a great help. Midterms were both all multiple choice and not too difficult. Should be easy to get at minimum a B if you check your work. Otherwise, Agah is a great man, and will make sure you truly understand.
Very cool guy, big fan of his class. Lectures were pretty slow pace but not terrible. No final was nice too.

Had Dr Agah for EECS 210. Great personality and cracks jokes. Hard to understand what stuff from lecture is actually relevant but homework and labs help focus in on what you need. Hes genuinely passionate about this topic so he gives many fun facts in lecture. Midterm was all multiple choice and fairly easy, cheat sheet allowed. Would take again.
**took EECS 210; the homeworks/labs/tests are easy, he also lets you have a double-sided cheat sheet on exams. Some of the lab GTAs grade harshly, but that is not Prof. Agah's fault.
Great guy
Dr. Agah was/is one of my favorites, he is absolutely wonderful.

Also had Dr. Agah for EECS 690, EECS 649 & EECS 700.  I would highly recommend his courses.  The classes he teaches are primarily project based with about only 25-45% of the grade based on tests.  If you pay attention to the lectures, the tests are easy but sometimes the lectures (so many slides!) can get a little boring.  My favorite professor.

One of the better personalities of any EECS prof. I agree that when he plays the "client" during the final, he can be harsh.  Lectures endlessly. Exams pull random facts from the lecture notes, so make sure to read over everything before the test.

He is very laid back during the course of the class. He jokes around about a lot of things. But when it comes to final project presentation time, watch out! There are no jokes about it. (The sudden shift in personality isn't fair in my book, so I give fair warning.)
Arvin Rocks!
Class was really fun and I learned a lot.
Great teacher, My favorite so far.
It was a good class overall! Would take him again if I can. He is very tech savvy and smart.
would not take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He grades the essay fairly. All other assignments and tasks are multiple choice or true/false. I actually enjoyed the lectures and found them helpful. he uses this platform called perusal which was confusing at first but it's a good way to interact with other students. He is chill yet very professional, I hope to take other classes with him.

Maz was very nice and helpful. He replies to emails fairly quickly. It took me a while to get used to perusal but after two weeks I found it easy to use and interesting. For an online course I think Professor Afifi made it fun. The content can be both difficult and easy at times so prepare to read a lot. the assignments are not that time consuming.

The content can be difficult to understand for those who are not business majors, like myself. Nonetheless, the assignments were simple and his grading was alright although I found it a bit picky at times. I was very put off when he informed me he detected AI in my essay when I most definitely didn't.

This is definitely the easiest online class you can take at KU. Most if not all of the content covered is common/general knowledge. The only thing you have to do is one or two weekly assignments that are just commenting a sentence or two on parts of a textbook that takes 10 minutes at most. The final (1000 word essay) is worth a lot so watch out.
Things you gotta know is very clear. If you are able to do all the homework by yourself, you can pass this class with A easily.

She is really caring, but isn't the best at explaining during class. If you visit her office or come to the review sessions, she explains stuff much clearer. Quizzes are worth 40% of the grade, but she does let you do corrections. The online homework can take a while, & many of the problems she doesn't go over in class. She did offer extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Terrible at explaining the material. Homework has nothing to do with what we went over in classes but played a big part in final grade. Blames all shortcomings on students. Class average for an exam was 60% and refused to admit that it was due to her teaching

Miedlar is GREAT at teaching. I will say she is semi-intimidating, but she makes sure you understand the material. Her lectures are always available online and she provides great examples. Her tests/quizzes aren't incredibly difficult, especially if you do all the homework.

She is a great teacher. This class is a flipped class, so most of the learning is done online and practice is done during class. She gives good feedback and has a wide array of ways to learn about the subject, like music, videos, movies, short stories, etc. She really cares about her students and really helps student who are struggling with a topic
Professor Sommerville is an amazing professor. I recommend her to any student wanting to learn and actually learn the concept. She made class fun yet knowledgeable.

Super nice and understanding!! She reads the lesson plans as she is giving the directions. Granted, it was a conversation class, so it was all about participation. As long as you talk a couple of times in class, you'll be fine! Interesting topics and a couple of presentations but small class sizes.

She literally never knows whats going on. Like ever. Thats the best way to describe her. She is a easy grader, but she just doesn't ever know whats going on and seems clueless about the things shes teaching. Attendance is worth 25 percent of your grade.
She was the best professor I have had. Amazing.
Professor Adriana Sommerville is an amazing professor. I recommend her to any student wanting to learn and actually learn the concept. She made class fun yet knowledgeable. I loved her!
Sommerville helped me succeed. Most understanding professor I have ever had. Muchas gracias profesora!
Best professor I had. Super caring. Really loves her students. Thank you so much!

Professor Sommerville was very kind to me this semester while I was dealing with health issues and the loss of a loved one. She is a difficult professor sometimes and certain deadlines and instructions were confusing at points but you can tell by her teaching that she loves what she does.

Prof. Sommerville was difficult but nice. You can tell that she cares about the class and her students. She can be difficult to deal with regarding anything to do with technology or deadlines but she is good at presenting the material and she is happy to answer any questions related to the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Sommerville's class is VERY easy to get a good grade in if you talk 2 times each class & just complete the assignments. She gives full points on basically everything. Despite this, she is VERY difficult to communicate with and I hate to leave bad reviews, but she is one of the most demeaning adults (not just professors) I have met.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is very strict and has high expectations for her students. Participation is around 30% of your ENTIRE grade (SHOW UP TO CLASS!). Also, show up prepared: you only get points if you actively engage. It is a college level course and not all individuals may be prepared for this. Challenging, but very much worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: literally the worst teacher ive ever had. demeaning towards students, rude, and scares me to death. do not take Spanish with her unless you want to feel like the stupidest person in the world
Professor Adriana Sommerville is an amazing professor. I recommend her to any student wanting to learn and actually learn the concept. She made class fun yet knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Frequently talks down to students and tends to not engage with us completely. Late to her own class on a regular basis. Rarely prepared to teach, class sessions are highly disorganized. Unexpectedly heavy workload for a conversation class. Relies heavily on technology that she doesn't know how to use.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She seems nice at first, but she is very difficult to work with. She blames her students for a lot of things that are her own fault and ends up hurting our grades. It's not too difficult to get a good grade, but it is easy to do very poorly as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Conversation class, make sure to participate in order to receive points. She is demeaning at first but gets better throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Sommerville is fair and kind. She really cares about the class and student learning. Participation is VERY important and you can only miss 2 class periods. She is willing to work with students however if serious issues arise. The class is enjoyable and the main expectation is that you talk in class!
Very sweet. Cares about students, really enjoyed her class and how understanding and caring she was.

Adriana is my favorite Spanish professor I've ever had! She is so caring and I enjoyed going to her class everyday - it was so fun. You can tell she really cares about her students' success. I would absolutely take a class with her again! Also, don't be afraid to talk in the class - you have to to get participation points.

This class was miserably difficult because there was nothing you could do to guarantee an A. The most correct answers, the hardest work, it didnt matter, nothing could guarantee you an A. It was all based off of his arbitrary whims. There are no rubrics. There are no assignments where the grading is objective. It's all just his opinion
Graded super hard, was pretty rude.

Be ready to listen and take close notes. Professor Lewis goes through a lot of information quickly (don't miss lectures), but you can keep up as long as you're paying attention. Limited assignments, but the content is always interesting. If you come ready to work, you will do just fine and really enjoy the class.

The WWII course is intellectually demanding & profoundly tough. I'm grateful for the incredible lectures & the remarkable perspective his book provided. I did worse than expected but I'm not disappointed that I took the class. I learned a lot—I had to face my fear of tackling a few topics. Overall excellent & organized. You have to stay focused.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This guy gives no feedback. He gave me a 70% on my first test and had no feedback on it. Even when I asked what dropped my grade so badly he brushed me off
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is disorganized. We ended up having to cut multiple class periods worth of contents because he would get so off topic and waste so much time. He also does not have any set rubric for tests, and this makes them difficult to properly prepare for. He is not receptive to helping you understand any expectations he may have in grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Over the course of the semester I was forced to spend an average of 20 hours a week on this 3 credit hour course. This was ridiculous and tiring. I love history but I never wanna hear about World War Two ever again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are three exams that consist of the majority of your grade, they are difficult and require more effort than most classes at this level. However, the syllabus provides you with all the possible questions and lectures are structured in a way to provide all of the elements to address each possible question. The class is hard but rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very disconnected and often off topic. Over the course of the semester I think we ended up cutting out 5 or 6 full days worth of class content because we were so far behind. It also just made lectures confusing and notes hard to take. He's knowledgeable but not particularly good at conveying the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is not a 300 level. The amount of reading and studying required is more than most 500 levels classes I've taken. He is looking for a reason to give you a C when grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Lewis is the kind of teacher who is always sure they're right. He would discuss politics before every class. This class has only three tests, worth a combined 80% of your grade. He said if you come to class you will definitely get an A or a B. The class average, even excluding anyone who skipped, was a C. He teaches fine, but grades unreliably.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are fast paced and very in depth. You'll need to come prepared to take notes and it will be difficult to pass if you skip lectures. The discussion days with the TA are very useful when preparing for Bluebook tests. All said if you enjoy history and are passionate about it you will respect him and appreciate the class.

Professor Lewis is very knowledgeable about military history; I learned a lot from him. If your focus is on the culture of history, you might struggle. Reading is essential to be successful. You will also need to study hard. Lectures are interesting but unorganized. Also, he doesn't post grades on Canvas. This class is tough; be prepared to work.

The class was extremely difficult because there is no clear grading criteria for Midterms and Finals. However, if you reach out to Dr. Lewis and you are humble he will help you all that he can. He is extremely knowledgeable of the course material so he rarely uses slides, he wrote the textbook. I highly recommend that you join a study group ASAP.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lewis is one of the smartest professors at KU but his lectures are very hard to follow as he just talks at you with no clear organization which makes note taking impossible. Very tough grader as he never gives feedback on assignments or posts them in BB. Overall unless you are super into military aspects along with history do not take this class.

Amazing history proffessor. However, if you are not a history student, his undergraduate courses are difficult. Very content heavy, as history tends to be. Be prepared to read and study. There is a lot to learn from him.

Lecture style is different than what most students are used to. He just speaks to the class about a topic, no slides or anything else to assist. Also- he does not put any grades into blackboard/canvas, only the final to KU. I put an extensive amount of effort into the class and still only received an A-. Wish I would have picked a different class.

You should most likely not take this professors class. He does not use blackboard at all making it extremely difficult to know when exams are. All his exams are only open for 24 hours then close. The final exam is 15 typed pages and the prompt is reveled for one day and closes the next. Gathering your thoughts to write a decent paper is very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's an awesome guy and leader. He is one of the Great professors at the university. The only reason you would have an issue with this professor is that you grew up hating people who look like him.
