He is truly the most intelligent professor I've had at any college/university - the past three years.

If you are a culture major or anyone that is not within the military, don't take his class. I took the Korean War course and was not happy about all the comments. He works through his GTA so its hard to even talk with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is a solid professor, no joke. Anyone say different, they didn't do the work.

I'm baffled by all the positive comment to be frank. Adrian is a knowledgeable man on military history. However that does not make him a good teacher. His lectures are disorganized and hard to follow because he does not organize his lectures in any way. If you want to get an understanding of any history subject avoid his classes like the plague.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I love him as a person. Very fast pace lectures. YOU HAVE TO TAKE NOTES. You have to listen to like every word he says. He is very easy to listen to though as cares alot. Test are 80% of your grade. All essays. One paper not too bad if you have the TA read it before so you can get an A. Not too much studying. Only the night or 2 nights before.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Get ready for a good time

Positives: Dr. Lewis is clearly an expert and an engaging lecturer. It's obvious he enjoys teaching. Lets you see every possible test question. He's very willing to help you during office hours. He also shares some life tips during class that are helpful. Negatives: Jumps around a bit during lectures. Uses coarse language.

Professor Lewis is an amazing professor who teaches multiple arguments, and the method in which that person reached an argument. If you are a history major, or with to understand how historians are suppose to approach a topic, take his class.

Prof. Lewis is someone you have to get used to but you can def tell how great he is by the number of people in each of his classes that haven taken 2 or 3 of his courses. He is a fair grader but if you want to receive a good grade you HAVE to show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Difficult class if you're not used to military lingo, but attend class and take good notes and you'll be fine! Tests can be hard, but he goes over everything in class. He doesn't use PPT so you have to pay attention. Great guy, recommend talking to him outside of class. Assigns A LOT of reading but you don't actually have to do it.

The lectures were amazing, but I had difficulty understanding the language of his lectures at the beginning since he uses military lingo. Take great notes and pay attention. You'll do fine on the test if you do. Very engaging lectures and I really enjoyed this class. Very insightful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The first month of taking Dr. Lewis' class, I was really lost because of the frequent military lingo that is used. Although, after bombing the first test, I started to pay more attention and attend regularly. Attendance is really important, as he doesn't use slides or anything. I ended up liking the class and coming away with a lot of knowledge.
Tough but meaningful.

Prof Lewis definitely has a different style of teaching, which for me took a bit to acclimate to. However, he gives great lectures and is very knowledgeable. My best advice is to attend class always (he notices, even if he doesn't take attendance) and go into office hours to ask for help. He respects hard work and determination.

He is excellent at teaching soldiers, but he's not too good at teaching the rest. He spends a large portion of the class talking about how the military operates, which you won't really understand unless you're ROTC. He doesn't really talk about the politics behind the war or the people effected. He will not post grades until the semester is over.

He's a brilliant professor. He is authoritative in the field, and if you care at all about your education, you will take advantage of the immeasurable resource professor Lewis is. He really makes you think about what is important as far as national security is concerned. he is very willing to write LORs if you earn his respect.

Dr. Lewis is highly decorated and very intelligent in his field. He cares about his students and want them all to succeed. I missed a test due to being sick and he came in on a Saturday just so I could retake it and pass.  If you want to learn about the United States and the things they do, I totally recommended Dr. Lewis. There is no one better.

My favorite professor at KU. Expects a lot out of his students but really cares. I missed a test due to being sick and he came in on a Saturday just so I could retake it. Highly decorated professor who has a lot of experience in this field. If you want to know more about how we work militarily around the world, I highly recommend Professor Lewis.

Good guy, speaks well, honest. Treats students very well. Hard class if you are busy with life. I read only one book out of all the others and got a B-. My writing skills are very good, in my opinion and I read about the war from time to time online, habitually.  Good class if you like the subject, stay away if you just don't feel it.. for real.
The best class.

Dr. Lewis' lectures were, at times, difficult to follow. It depends on the TA you have for discussion. His tests are the most difficult I've ever had. Two 3 page essays, and 2 page ID questions in 40 minutes. There's a lot of reading, but you can get by without most of it. A lot of what's on the tests aren't in the books, so make sure to show up.

Dr. Lewis was by far one of the best professors I have had. I learned more in his class than in any one of my other classes. HIST 390 was one of the hardest classes I have ever taken but it was worth it! Amazing professor. I liked him so much I asked him to be a mentor for me in the future.  You absolutely need to attend lecture and read to pass.

Professor Lewis will MAKE YOU THINK in this course.  You may be able to sit at the back and coast along, but you will get a lot out of being prepared from the readings and participating.  He is a great lecturer and really knows his stuff.  I look forward to another class from him.

I have taken 3 courses with him and he is by far one of the best professors I have had at KU. He is very intelligent and passionate about his subject and is always willing to help if you have questions.  He also seems to care about his students and wants them to be successful in life.

Dr. Lewis is a pretty good professor after you get used to his teaching style. He can be intimidating at times and the class can be difficult, but if you attend lecture and do some reading/studying you should be fine. The great thing about Dr. Lewis is that he truly CARES about his students' success.
Excellant professor. Classes are demanding but alot can be learned,

He would be excellent at teaching soldiers, but he's not too good at teaching students. Everyday he talks about why the US military is good and purposely leaves out details of events to portray things a certain way. He doesn't really talk about the politics behind the war or the people effected. All I hear about is effiecent war strategies.
Adrian Lewis is brilliant. He really knows his stuff.  The syllabus has all of the exam and final questions on it.  As long as you show up and take notes you will do well in this class.
Really knows his stuff. One of the top human beings in the country in regard to American War history. Passionate and clear. Gave the best lecture I have ever attended.

I loved this class. I took it during the summer so it was cut short and we didnt get to go over a lot of things i wish we could have. But this man is a great teacher and keeps the interest level very high. Pretty heavy reading load, but they were good books. So i would definitely take another class taught by him.
I loved this class. He is a truly brilliant man. The lectures are worth every penny of tuition. He will make you think and make you laugh. Plus he never takes attendance.

he is a brilliant man. Going to class is a really a treat. Just read his book and/or show up for class and you will do fine. At first his book/s might seem daunting but it is really easy to read and full of info. plz take a class from him. he loves students, and does not fear questions or arguments. i hope he never leaves our university. rock chalk
Passionate about his field (history) and transmits this passion to students. He's one that you'll remember.

Great class, in depth learning about world war two. If you go to class, and review sessions you should do extremely well.  Exams are completely essay, and the questions are given to you prior to the examination.
Sorry last comment was for history 340.
Sorry that last comment was for History 340.

If you go to class and try to take notes, you will be absolutely fine in this class. He sometimes goes off topic but he really knows what he's talking about. The tests are all essay but he gives you study guides that cover all of the possible essay questions. Try to get a good TA...that will really help. Go to the review sessions before the test.

Lectures are clear and concise, covering everything one needs to pass the exam(s). His syllabus is a mammoth blueprint of everything you'll need to succeed in the course. Great professor who knows the discourse within his field.

This class is not what you expect. Lewis brings up many theories and arguments that never are fully discussed.  He mentions events and other arguments, but never explains things. Instead, he jumps around alot. Taking notes in his class is confusing. He can't stick to one topic.  Also, there are 5 books required and a seperate research paper. 8-10 p

It is really hard to understand his lectures.  He talks about a lot of stuff that isn't part of the stuff I thought was in the class.  It is a lot of military theory stuff and not much on the Second World War, which is what the class is supposed to be about.  Be ready to be confused.  The TAs are helpful and I have a good section leader.

genuinely the most wonderful woman. cares about what she's teaching an cares about lot about her students. to wgss majors/minors: take this class its so easy just repeating the same stuff. but yeah, love her, she's my queen
I don't have anything to say.

She really cares about her students and the content she teaches. She wants to see her students succeed and engage with the material. Always has a positive attitude and is a very fair grader. I loved having her as a professor, she is very personable and caring!!!

Take any of her classes if you have a chance! She genuinely CARES about the topics she teaches as well as her students! Combine that with fair grading/coursework and your have yourself a class that cannot be passed up. Adrianne is simply the best!!!! Learned so much in her classes and left feeling so blessed to have her as a professor!

One of those rare Professors who truly cares about both her students and the subject matter. She is simply an amazing educator. The reviews don't lie, she is awesome. I learned more from her than any other professor at KU.

Amazing person and an amazing Professor. Adrianne is the best professor you will have at KU. She is kind, helpful, and grades fairly. In addition, Adrianne truly loves what she does and her positive energy is infectious. Take a class from her if you can.

Kunkel is very nice and helpful, definitely recommend meeting with her for any reason. She'll do anything for a good student. That said, this was an incredibly easy class, and I didn't get much out of it. If you're a WGSS student, you won't learn very much that's new. It's cross-listed as a COMS class... a good WGSS intro class for those majors.
By far my favorite professor here at KU
Wonderful!
Very sweet and easy to understand.
Great Teacher! Understanding, interesting, easy to understand for the most part.
full of herself and not very bright.  easier on women than men, seems to like women better than men.

Nicest teacher in the world and very intelligent. Class is mandatory but she's understanding if you miss class...just let her know. Plus class was mostly discussion anyways, so it wasn't a difficult class to sit through.

One of the best teachers I have ever had!  Her tests are super easy, but gives you a study guide that she already has filled out for everyone.  Very passionate about gender communication and makes for an interesting class. shows a ton of films and grades super easy.  goes out of her way to work with you.  I am taking all the classes i can from her!
She's kind of like a dumb cheerleader type of person.  No common sense at all!
She is a very sweet teacher. You can't say anything wrong. Gives you lots of points for participation ~ you just need to be there. I am taking another course from her.
No Comments
No Comments
Not at all helpful outside of the classroom.  Doesn't have time for you and sends you her grad student helper.

Adam is one of the best English professors/teachers I've ever had. He makes the most boring or mundane subject matter into something fun and engaging. Adam also gives very precise and helpful feedback on your stories without beating around the bush. I would highly recommend him for Fiction Writing I.

You will get out of Adam's fiction classes what you put into it. His lectures can be all over the place, but if you ask questions, engage with the material, and pay attention, he'll reward you with lectures that are among the best you'll receive in college. I took Fiction I and II and have 20+ pages of notes on the art of storytelling.
Super funny and caring! You only get three grades for the whole semester so your short stories better be good.
He's awesome, the keys in E351 are to participate, critique, write, and don't be afraid to share your ideas, it only makes you a better student. Very encouraging; great professor.

Surprised to see negative reviews. Adam has opened my world to so many amazing writers that are not typically discussed. He allows complete creativity and trusts you, the writer, with where you want to take the story. Duh you have to follow the assignment foundations. He's very very loose with the ones he does implement. He is a breath of fresh air
He's very funny, and his experience as a writer shows. His class has been, by far, my favorite and most helpful in my college experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Desnoyers is the worst college english/writing instructor I've had. He is not a professor, and has no actual qualifications to be teaching this class that I'm aware of. The stories he assigns as readings are horrible, and it's clear he pretty much just wants you to copy them. He gives horrible feedback, is rude, doesn't offer help outside of class.

Adam is the best teacher I have ever had. His advice has shaped my writing, and his viewpoints, insights, and hilarious stories about the exquisite ordinariness of life, family, and relationships are those that could only come from a writer's mind.

Adam is an awesome teacher. You have to participate in his class if you want to pass. That means turning in your stories and reading and meaningfully critiquing other students' stories. He'll also spend time telling hilarious stories. While his prompts may sometimes feel constricting if you ask him he will give you a different prompt to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Adam tells a lot of stories, which is entertaining, but not helpfully whatsoever if you are trying to become a better writer. Critiques are not graded, so there is no incentive for anyone to give you any feedback on your work. He cares about literature, but talks incessantly. The entire class is a waste of time if you are a serious writer.

He gives great and very clear writing advice. His love for literature and for what his students write really shows, he genuinely wants to help his students be better writers. I will be taking another one of his classes. If you don't like teachers that talk about their personal lives, though, probably not a good choice for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Adam is great. There are only three papers the whole semester and little to no reading. He gives great feedback and has fun lectures. Lectures are filled with hilarious stories that he then ties into fiction writing. I learned the most I have ever learned in any English class. I am prepared to take Adam's class again.
This was a great class. If you show up and do the work (which is not arduous) you'll get the A! Desnoyer is super down to Earth and a fair grader.

You sit in a circle and have to get over the fact your paper will be read to everyone, but it isn't that bad after a while. and he is really attractive so that is a plus. he is awesome. if you put forth an effort and implement things you have talked about in class you're good.

The class that place in a circle with students giving a critique on your story. Most students are very opinionated and take it really seriously.. which is very annoying, when you don't want to be a fiction writer just trying to take a class for credit. He also collects written critiques to other students, and judges if your giving good feedback..

Desnoyers is the most chill teacher I've ever had at KU. His ENGL 351 class was always filled with hilarious stories about anything at all, and there was never a dull moment, even during critiques. Class attendance is not needed, but showing up means constant laughter and giggles. Toward the end, his hilarious personality grows on you a lot.

Awesome teacher. His personality and humor class made the class interesting. My writing definitely improved a lot. Expectations were clearly defined and easy to follow. Got a better grade in the class than I expected, so it was a pretty easy class.

Adam is obviously a great writer and the classes are hilarious. However, he allows little creativity with what he expects from students. He wants students to follow certain formulas in their stories, yielding pretty similar stories. Overall good though.

Adam is truly the best and most caring teacher I've had at KU. He brings life to the classroom and his dry sense of humor makes going to class enjoyable. He's a great guy and truly cares about his students. If you don't take his classes, you're missing out. I love writing because of this class!

Took him again after loving Engl 351 and the only that thing really changes between those classes is that the prompts get a little more complicated/interesting. Really enjoyed the class and would recommend it to anyone who loves writing. Go into it with an open mind!

Adam's class has been my favorite class at KU so far. He's hilarious in a dark, dry way and his suggestions are very specific and helpful. Attendance is optional but most people come every day anyway because no one wants to skip. Definitely take this class from him.

This is one of the best writing prof. you can get at KU. While he may seem laid back listen close. What he says will change the way you write. He is truly brilliant and KU is lucky to have him.Take anything you can from him, it will be one of your favorite classes. Not too hard and he doesn't pour on the  reading. Great guy, my favorite prof. At KU
Amazing.

I had Adam for Fiction writing and the first week I was a little put off by his sense of humor and personality but I got used to it and eventually it became my favorite class of the semester and he became my favorite teacher. I highly recommend taking this class, you will learn what you need to and also its a great class to get creative in.

This class has been one of my favorites this semester. Adam's really funny and laid back, and as a student going into the Creative Writer major, I really appreciate the tips and tricks he suggests in class. His commentary is always helpful and hilarious.

I actually enjoyed going to this class. Sometimes it was pointless but Adam always makes funny comments that keep you interested. You just have to use the tips he gives you in class and you will get an easy A. My writing might not have improve from this class but it was helpful to my GPA and I enjoyed going.
Awesome class. It may not be a challenge to all, but it was interesting and I literally looked forward to attending each class. Our class as a whole was bummed when the class was canceled one day.

Don't get me wrong, it was an enjoyable and memorable class, and he's a great, fun guy- but so are the other CW classes and profs.  If you don't like writing modern, gritty fiction with relationships, life lessons, and no supernatural elements... try for a different section.  He tells you what he likes up front, and he grades based on his whims.

As far as I can tell, adam is INCREDIBLY full of himself. He is an uncomfortable lecturer, often coming in and breathing heavily, as a gorilla would behave in his cave. He literally has put incredible structure on fiction writing, as though writing a ficticous book is as building a meticulously engineered technology. I cannot breathe life into art.

Yes, this class is fun, Adam is hilarious and a great guy. He is perhaps moderately helpful. Workshops, you rely on feedback from students who don't care and never show up how helpful is that? He is also unavailable outside of class.  Yes, he's fun, but you won't learn a great deal. I think he has a lot to offer, it's getting it that's the problem.

This class was fun.  Adam is a great lecturer.  He gets straight to the point when he's makin a statement and how he wants his papers.  One key is to not be late to class, and stay more on the humorous and spontaneous side when u are doing his papers.  Overall, I enjoyed his class.  I highly recommend him if u want a good first year.
cool guy, very chill

Class is a joke.  Forget the classical literature that branches out from modern paperback bs that fills airports.  He wants sappy, uninteresting, typical, predictable stories.  Fiction is more than relationships, and if you appreciate that, don't take his class.  Good for people that have never written before but not people that are seriously write

Adam's classes are the best I have ever taken at KU. Great fiction writing advice, awesome class set up, great recommended writers and stories. Adam knows what he's talking about and if you pay attention, you'll be a better writer for it.
Coolest teacher ive ever had. Honestly, great guy, down to earth. Gets it. Hes a nice guy, take the class
Best class I ever took.
Probably the best professor I've ever had. Caring, dedicated, hilarious, well-prepared, and REAL.

I've been at KU for three years, and I've only had one other class that I genuinely couldn't wait to come to every week.  Adam is hilarious, hip, and inspiring.  He helped me with my writing a lot, and introduced me to a lot of good writers.  Take this class, that's all I can say.
Best teacher ever.
Best teacher i've ever had.
Great instructor, inspiring ideas, cares about his students, and obviously loves his job.  And he's ripped - don't let the ponchos fool ya.

He's cool as hell and very funny. I took his class almost 3 years ago and I'd still say he's one of the best profs I've ever had. He knows what he's doing and genuinely gives a sh*t about your writing. Class is pretty much always entertaining and engaging. Take it if you're serious about writing.
totally hot , and a brilliant teacher.  don't mess with him, though or be a moron or a vindictive nerd.  peace.

Instead of giving constructive critisism to your work, he will tell you and the class how YOUR story should have gone, and what he thinks COULD have been cool about it.  If you don't write his style of stories then your grade will suffer.

I took AAAS 106 for one of my KU Core clases, and I strongly recommend to everybody to NEVER take any of his classes. I am in my 4th semester at KU and have a 4.0. His class ruined this for me. He grades tough and includes very few guidelines in his assignments so that he can doc points on everything in your assignments.

Professor Adams is hard to get ahold of outside of class and grades very harshly. According to him, grades do not matter yet he grades students down on super small details. I have taken courses in the 600s such as a Constitutional law where it was literally a prelaw class, got an A, but in this class I have a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Far too much asked for what is a 100 level course. Seems very unforgiving and hard to work with, avoid taking this class unless you absolutely have to.

I think this course could use a lot of work. The instructor expected such specific answers for a 100 level class. The professor was unwilling and honestly hard to work with when I voiced concerns. I had points marked off for absurd details. Ive done better in my higher level (300-500 level) critical thinking classes than I did for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Is not willing to listen to students concerns, very stubborn and unforgiving.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Adams was very disorganized and often made the course material into a long personal narrative that took up class time where his students could have received participation points. Most classes had reading assignments that were relatively easy and required low effort, but papers and projects were very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: great teacher, talks about his dog, brought Darcy to an office hour

Decent lectures with "learning objectives" so you know exactly what you're supposed to learn. Does his best to connect with students by talking about his personal life and cracking jokes. Really nice guy. Makes a difficult subject bearable through straightforward notes, but homeworks and tests sometimes weren't really relevant to the notes.

This was a difficult class. Be prepared to code. Unless you have fully mastered coding in MATLAB, the best (maybe only?) way to be successful in this class is to go to his office hours. The exams and homework are also pretty difficult, but they are more manageable than the coding assignments.
Dr. Husic has been one of my favorite teachers thus far at KU. He really cares about his students and provides us with relevant material in class and on homeworks. He made a difficult class enjoyable

Husic was a decent prof. His lectures and lecture notes were thorough and understandable. Midterms were fair for the most part. The final was much harder than the midterm exams. The homework was very doable, although not always relevant to what would show up on exams. Would not recommend if you don't like cold calling, he's a big fan of that.
Great prof

She's kind but had an issue with her teaching. Her syllabus was inconsistent with her grading and she was late in giving out rubrics. She didn't write our final essay prompt in time and expected us to be able to write a 7-8 page paper in one week. It's hard to reach her outside of class. I honestly learned more from the reading than her.

Had her for WGSS 359. Amazing, kind professor and readings were diverse. Grading was fair, extra credit was offered for missed attendance. Extremely sympathetic and helpful when I had trouble with my group project. She seems like such a smart person and she was supportive of everyone.

I took her class over the winter and it was very easy and interesting! She shares a lot of new perspectives and made the readings enjoyable. She graded very easy and the essays were reflection essays. The hardest thing about this class were the reading quizzes which were not that bad at all. She's super sweet and very knowledgeable.

She takes attendance in class. I never learned much from her lectures and powerpoints. Extremely long readings are assigned every week. I've never read any of them, and have the potential to pull an A in the class. You have 2 tests and the rest of the points come from discussion. Overall an easy class, just wasn't my cup of tea.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Akiko is so caring and invested in our success. There is a lot of reading and it's often repetitive. She didn't use PPT the first half of the semester, and then she did. There is a midterm and final paper which were graded pretty easily. I really appreciated that she was open to feedback re: the overall course and her teaching style.

If you miss three or more classes, including discussion classes, you receive a zero for participation points regardless if they are excused or unexcused. Participation was 25% of your grade. Lectures and powerpoints posted on blackboard. I easily just skimmed the reading material (no textbook!) and still passed with an A by really listening in clas
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The readings she assigns are a lot but you can definitely get by just skimming them. Other than that the class is really good and really easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: To get an A in this class is pretty easy as long as you read, participate in discussion & ask questions if you have them! She posts lecture notes online, so I  just listened during lecture. I would study two days before the exams & received  As. Midterm, final, participation & a group project constitutes the grade. She also takes attendance!

She is so adorable.  However, your grade in this class really depends on your GTA for discussion. Takeyama does not grade anything. The only difference between the 108 and 308 is that 308 has a couple of extra 4-5 page essays. It's a good choice if you need 300+ hours. I would recommend this class, just be prepared if you hate group projects.

Prof. Takeyama was nice, albeit a bit hard to understand. Group research project is required, but being a 108 class the expectations are set in line with skill level. Takeyama does a great job of tying weekly reading to chapters in book while providing great insight during lecture.
Dr. Takeyama is a good professor. She made the lectures interesting and always explained the concepts.

Prof. Takeyama is great.  While her accent can be a little heavy at times her lectures are easy to follow and interesting.  Taking notes on the powerpoint slides, doing the readings, and showing up to class basically guarantees an A.
A really nice and engaging teacher. Can be hard to understand sometimes but is very inteligent. Just take good notes!

I thought that this class was very interesting. Dr. Takeyama knew how to keep her student's attention and did a really good job at teaching the material! She does fun little exercises that get everyone involved in what's going on. Definitely recommend this class!
Summer course is demanding but manageable, she if flexible if work seems overwhelming..take your own notes she jumps around and tests are easy if you read.

I love how she taught her own material, I always learned something new from her lecture days. Everyone should be required to take a class like this! however, sometimes I felt like the students were controlling the class. The work load is deceptively easy.

Akiko Takeyama is amazing!  I didn't like the class at first, but once you start learning the subject matter the discussions get intense.  Akiko knows her stuff!  Talk to her outside of class.  She really cute and really smart.  Her own research is really interesting and she teaches it to the class.  Simply amazing.

Very Nice person but unfair grading. Subjective grading based upon if he likes your art or not and you pretty much don't know what grade you are going to get until his decision at the end. Enjoyable class though and if you don't need scholarships and want to leave your GPA up to an art teachers opinion, then go for it.

Norman is an accomplished and well respected artist but I have always felt like an equal in his class. He is a joy to talk to and has further developed my perspective of art making. I'm in his landscape painting class and sometimes it is difficult getting to the locations but it's all a part of the experience. Someone is always willing to drive too
Boring! You only draw the same objects over and over again. I wouldn't recommend it for a drawing 101 class, the other teachers have a lot more change in subjects/focuses over the class.

Not a very nice person, especially if you get on his bad side, and that's a lot of people. He was eventually fired from KU for being such a poor mentor and driving his students to tears - which he just says is the nature of the journalism world. However, I refuse to believe most people are as heartless as this man. I hope he doesn't teach again.

I had Brett because I had to do newsroom shifts during my Journalism 415 class. In the newsroom they often use the metaphor "when you buy an iPhone you figure out how to use by yourself, you can do it with the cameras." Well, when I buy an iPhone it doesn't come with someone who is PAID to teach me how to use it. Avoid this teacher at all costs.

Brett Akagi is the absolute worst. He knows his stuff, yes, but he does not know how to work with people. He thinks his way is the only way and if you don't do it his way you're going to get yelled at. He's made me and plenty of other people cry. Please do not take a class with him. Save yourself the stress.

A jerk. EXTREMELY mean to students. Used to work in the TV industry, but if you Google him, he was chased out of channel 41 in Kansas City because people did not like him. He forces you to make his class your life and soul. Doesn't care if you get stressed. False representation of the TV industry. MANY have dropped him. DONT TAKE HIM! Barely passed
Hardest, most difficult person to work with. Period.

Glenn's arrogance is insufferable. He incessantly promotes his own research as the definitive source of knowledge, using convoluted terminology to baffle students and inflate his own ego. His monologues are more concerned with self-admiration than knowledge. It's evident when someone possesses genuine intelligence versus when it is mere pretense

This man is antisemitic! If you are Jewish, be careful and probably avoid mentioning it. Uncertain how he feels about other minorities, but he isn't always disability friendly either. Read the other reviews for a better understanding of the class structure, but keep this in mind if you enroll in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not give any feedback for anything so no chance for improvement. Ridiculous grades and 60% of the grade is based on the test. That's not to say there isn't a good amount of other homework, it's just hardly worth anything in the end. Worst teacher I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is honestly super arrogant, grades extremely hard. overall terrible class, his lectures make zero sense. He uses words that make the lectures even more confusing. Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Adams is the most arrogant professor I have ever had. He uses his own research as material in the class and uses words that I have never even heard of in order to explain other complex words I have never heard of. The only thing about this class that isn't made to make you fail is his grading scale. DO NOT TAKE (unless you want to cry)!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unfair grader, as you have to have the exact words from his brain on your test. The tests and grading are the hardest I have ever experienced. All sources come from his own research, very few outside sources. I almost did not graduate with honors my senior year because of this class. Only class i've ever gotten a D in. Don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst thing I've ever taken and would never put anyone through this class. Tests are extremely difficult and makes it worth 80% of your grade, but only accounts for your best one. HORRIBLE!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you aren't willing to take responsibility for your own learning, then you probably will hate this class. DO NOT BE FOOLED. This is a great grad prep class. If you listen closely, come prepared, and participate in the discussion you really will learn to think in new ways. His style is very hands-off and growth oriented. Deal with it and learn!

Glenn is so very smart. Extremely passionate. But kind of passive? He uses very complex academic speak and has us reading his own research papers that are full of heavy layers of complex jargon. As a psych major this man and his class made me fear I had no chance of being a psychologist. My other Psych professors confirmed I am doing fine it's him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is the worst class I have ever taken. His lectures are long winded, repetitive, and boring. The MAJOR research project was poorly created, a huge time waster, and at that point everyone else has given up trying for a decent grade. He is disengaged with his students. His exams questions are confusing and he grades the exam essays harshly.

The only good thing about this class is that you are forced to do most of the research portion with students that hate the class just as much as you. Be warned: members of your group drop the class last minute because they are just over it. I dont blame them. But that only makes all the work you have to do increase drastically right before Finals.

It is not uncommon that Dr. Adams will surprise you with an extra assignment, mandatory lecture that isnt during class time, and a research paper, due during finals week, that wasnt ever listed in the syllabus, and that he told us about with over Thanksgiving Break. This class is a major time suck and I wouldnt wish it on my worst enemy.
Dr. Adams uses complex terminology and explanations; indeed, he words his exams in the same manner. This is certainly a challenging course.

Hardest professor I've ever had. If I could of switched I would have. He is way to smart for his own good. I actually had To go to another professor to understand what he meant. He was so hard. I would not recommend his classes.

Prof Adams is clearly very dedicated to his subject matter. But just because you have a PhD does not mean you should teach. His job is to make the concepts understandable to the students, not to shove them out there in an overly complex manner and hope they get it. Tests are full of double speak and hard to understand.

Questions on tests are very complicated. He is not very helpful when you ask him questions he just keeps talking without answering the question. Boring lecture. Makes simple concepts harder to understand than they really should be.
Good class he averages the final and midterm in a way that REALLY  helps out your grade. But lectures can be a little boring, but overall good class and applicable to everyday life.

course very applicable to living in the world. More students should learn to recognize brilliance & how lucky they are to sit in a classroom and gobble up brain food prepared by highly knowledgeable scholars. Lectures very engaging and thought provoking.  ask questions if you don't understand something. if you're brain is lazy take a grad student.
The one thing I didn't like about the class is that the test consisted of in class stuff and out of class/on your own material.  Other than that, it was a pretty good course.

I thought the class was sometimes interesting, sometimes really boring. he might be hard to understand, but if you work hard, an A is very possible! Not a bad class, but I expected more. Need to read book for discussion quizzes
The class was very interesting and engaging.  Do not take if you're not interested in a global perspective/are not willing to work hard.  Can get an A with attendance and participation.

Dr.Adams is talented and engaging. If you want to expand your way of thinking, become a better person,and get credit take this class; slackers don't bother. Psych mjr: don't miss it. Come to class & ask questions if you don't get something. 1st day he says there are easier sections & encourages switching if not interested in global perspective.

Dr. Adams is awesome. He will challenge your way of thinking and open a whole new way of seeing the world. Many students expect to be fed the same things they know, but grow up... a university class should challenge your way of thinking, otherwise why get a higher education.    Basically, hard but TOTALLY worth it.

What some of the people here are saying is true, Adams is a tough teacher, and he expects a lot.  I got a crappy TA, which didn't help.  BUT I worked really hard and got an A. I learned more in this class than half of my other KU classes combined.  So, if you want to work hard and learn A TON then take his class. If not then don't take his class.

This class isn't as hard as people say it is... they just expect it to be easy. He was a really funny guy and has a dry sense of humor. His tests weren't that bad at all! I don't know what these people are talking about. In all fairness to him, he tells EVERBODY when they sign up for his class that it isn't going to be a blow off class. Enroll!

I took PY 333 & 360 and found both very informative and looked forward to the lectures. Honestly one of the most helpful classes you can take if you are a psych major. You have to read the material to do well on the tests, but grading was fair. Sometimes he did not seem open to differing opinions & I hated how the group project was large % of grade

Worst teacher at KU. I went to class only to get participation points.  His lectures were worthless because he jsut talked about random things that had nothing to do with the test.  I would switch if possible.  I HATE THIS TEACHER.
Ambiguously worded tests. Annoying gestures while speaking in context that is not understandable. Not sympathetic to students efforts and needs for help.

I thought he was an awful professor.  His exams were extremely difficult and did a horrible job of explaining things. I felt it was a waste of time and money while I could have put as much effort and studying into a class where it actually payed off. I do not recommend him as a professor.
Horrible. Just one word to describe.. "horrible"

i totally and completely dreaded the class and i could not wait until the end of the semester...he was impossible to understand and his lectures had nothing to do with the exams he gave. the exams were tedious and you need alot of time to prepare for them. he was not much help out of class. I suggest switching teachers.
very hard...he talks in a way you can't even understand. He makes everything way more complex than it needs to be. If you can avoid taking this from him.

Ambiguous.  Definately. The exams were very difficult. And you needed to come to class every day because he was changing everything at the last minute. My TA was hard to understand, and I didn't get much out of the discussion either.  Too bad, because I had a lot of interest going in, but frusteration coming out.
He sucks
He gave interesting lectures, and I could tell he was extrememly smart. But the class was very disorganized, the tests were hard, and his explanations of concepts was overly complex.
BORING! worst teacher ive ever had!
His notes in class are not that great. I had a good TA and the quizzes in discussion helped my grade a lot!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

His views were very black and white. If a student did not see it his way, they were wrong. He also did not attempt to use the language of the students. He took a simple concept and made it impossible to understand.
Glenn is a good guy.  I had him as an independent study prof. as well.  Give the guy a chance!
No Comments
Good teacher, not bad exams
One of the hardest classes in the B-school similar to Beedles FIN415

He is a really nice guy and very helpful. A handful of cases, midterm and final. Attendance is not mandatory but you should better attend as participation is graded. Mock exams are very helpful and his exams are moderate.

This class wasn't too bad.A few cases which he graded pretty easily, midterm and final, both of which were curved.  15% of the grade is for participation-make sure to attend. He doesn't put your part. points up until the end of the semester, and even if you didn't talk much in class, if he recognizes your face from being present you'll get most pts

I really enjoyed the reading material and she does give some points for participating/engaging with the texts. The main issue i had was the fact almost ALL the grade relies on the exams and midterms and shes a lot tougher on them. It was hard to gauge if my grade wasn't going to take a hit or not, so I was pretty stressed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took WGSS 176, and she very much so cared about her students. However, she was a pretty hard grader especially for a first year seminar. Also, there were only four grades in the whole class which was pretty stressful at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The readings chosen are interesting, relevant, and consistently unique. You will get a lot out of this class if you do the reading and participate. She is a teacher who truly cares and gives meaningful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Graded by participation, weekly (short, informal) writing assignments, two essays over class content, and a final research proposal project (which is split into cumulative parts). Only essays + project are graded critically, but with a little effort shouldn't be too much of a challenge to get a good grade. Good/interesting presentation of content
Makes it almost impossible to get an A with 45% of the class being 2 writing assignments she grades way too strictly for a 100 level course. Don't take her there are so many better options.

I enjoyed Professor Wilson as a teacher. Class was always interesting and engaging. However, she was a pretty hard grader especially for an introductory course. You need to do all of the reading assigned, which is a lot, because that's what the exams and essays cover. Make sure you participate at least 4-5 times a class otherwise you will get a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Wilson was a fine teacher. She was, however an extremely tough grader. Participation is a huge thing in this class, even if you raise your hand to participate, you will only average about an A- or B+ for your participation grade. You need to almost be the annoying kid that answers everything in order to meet her expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Wilson is very intelligent and gives great feedback. Attendance is mandatory and you have to do the readings. If you pay attention and get stuff done you'll have no issue in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Aimee was extremely hard on grading and gave the whole class a test right before Thanksgiving and soon as we came back from break with no study guide. SHE NEVER GIVES STUDIES GUIDES OR REVIEWS!!

Took this class to fulfill a Literature requirement and I'm glad I did. She was truly passionate about what she taught and the way she spoke was captivating. Lectures were mandatory but honestly it was the only class I've ever wanted to go to. Relatively easy grader. Readings assigned every class but if you skim briefly before class you're fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: eh

terrible teacher. i went to her for help, i went to writing center for help, still failed the papers. i went to her for help on the second paper and she offered suggestions. after i changed my paper to fit her ideas, she gave me a D!!!!

She is my favorite teacher so far. I got a C in the class, but I didn't go to her for help very often like I could have. She makes everything extremely interesting, though I never would have found it that way without her teaching. She always had a lot of energy, and she was a great teacher.
Grades too hard and is way too into the reading

One of the best teachers at KU! She truly cares about her students and goes out of her way to make sure everyone understands the material. She gives a lot of helpful and detailed feedback that really helps you improve. Her classes are engaging and well-organized. As long as you show up and take part in class discussions, you'll do well.
Even though I dropped the class, she was a great teacher. Very patient and reasonable
Excellent teacher

Aidana was an incredible teacher who met everyone where they were coming into the class, and helped anyone struggling catch up. If you get a grade below a B she has you do corrections and work more to understand the subject. Very forgiving grader, made the language more accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really relaxed professor with some good lessons on personal finance. Would totally recommend if you're looking for advice and learning opportunities in the field of finance.
Very laid back does exams and everything outside of class.  Attendance is online so you can skip sometimes and join attendance from anywhere.  Has really easy assignments and exams.

really laidback. show up for the lectures to get points on the daily quizzes (which are often just "did you complete the activty today") so nothing to really worry about. Just make sure you keep track of deadlines for the assignments, and those aren't too hard either. dude's pretty chill and willing to help you out. really good math credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Jason is very knowledgeable and is a great lecturer! You will learn a lot of useful information to use daily. An online textbook is required but it is free.
Jason is a great professor and very professional. While yes, this class was very easy it was also very useful if you do choose to pay attention.

Anderson was very professional and made very clear expectations at the beginning of the year with as long as you do the work you will succeed. A lot of his work is done online, but notes are done in lectures. Most quizzes are easy as long as you pay attention. As long as you take the time to care you will succeed

FIN 101: The Professor was great and always answered his emails even though he had over 200 people in this class alone. You really don't have to go to class as all of the work was online even the lectures and slideshows. I would definitely recommend this class and professor to anyone especially if you use this as a math credit.

Don't think I've learned anything after taking his class. He was kinda lazy and would shallowly discuss the topic and assign students to do his job for him. Classes were frequently canceled for whatever reason. Nice guy and an easy A nevertheless.

Jason is pretty awesome! He wrote his textbook during the semester using AI and made it cheap. The class is ridiculously easy and there are lots of opportunities for extra credit just in case. The material is super useful and the class is great. Recommend taking this class if you need a math credit, it only uses basic math and a finance calculator!

I loved this course and the teacher. They were both very interesting. The class isn't difficult if you do the work and she's very witty, which makes the class more entertaining. I'd take more courses with her if I could!

Aislinn is a very interesting person. She's funny and straight to the point. Notes are very easy, tests are easy if you pay attention during class and do the assigned readings. Essay is easy as long as you put effort. Grade is based off attendance, inclass writings, and exams.
Super nice and helpful. A fun and entertaining class!

TA for Sociology 104 Discussion section with Kelly Massoni. Super easy class as long as you read the texts assigned before the discussion section. A lot of videos in class and very interesting subject matter. Grade is based on attendance, attentiveness, 12 tests (lowest 2 dropped) and 2 papers.
The class is hard for a good reason but Alex makes it a breeze, his crit is extremely easy to understand. I have come to him for help with other classes to get crit!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I've had alex for three semesters so far. as the other reviews say he is pretty quiet and a tough grader but from my experience this is very beneficial for our growth as designers. He is always responsive over email even outside of his office hours. in this class you get what you give out of it, its important to give your all in this program.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Alex is a wonderful teacher and designer who's really passionate about both in equal measure. Gives great design feedback while also keeping things open-ended enough for you to grow and think critically about your own work. He pushes you in the right direction and is very kind about telling you what you need to hear. Highly Recommended!

Alex is an amazing designer and an even better professor. He clearly states what is required in his projects and pushes you to explore every outcome. He gives great critique and if you have more questions he is happy to answer them. He responds quickly to emails and is frequently available in his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Alex is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He gives excellent feedback. With his advice your work will improve a lot. He cares a lot and wants each student to be the best they can, no matter what level of skill they're at. He has an impressive portfolio and every designer has something to learn from him.
Love him, he seems cold and curt when you first meet him but honestly, one of the best professors I've had, plus his critique is really good
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I've every had. His critiques were so helpful in helping us grow as designers and our whole class probably feels the same way. His feedback was great and he was always understanding of outside struggles if you communicated. He can be a tough grader but only because he really does care about his students and their success.

I've had Alex 3 semesters. Pretty quiet, doesnt care to chat. Many students dislike him bc of the workload and being a tough grader, but I've personally grown a lot and pushed myself so much farther because of this. KU design is very intensive and I don't think Alex should be blamed for having standards that a designer would face in the real world.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Alex is great, but you will not get any emotion out of him. Very tough grader. If something traumatic happens still no emotion acts like he doesn't care. If you do not have multiple ideas or don't show process you will not pass. most feedback consists of "Keep pushing", "you are so close" or no feedback at all. Good feedback is hard to come by
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just an absolute horrid class. Haven't met a singular student in this her class that actually enjoys it. I am in a multitude of higher level classes and yet this CORE class is what I have spent the most time on. I enrolled in this course to fulfill a A&H credit for an easy A, though it is the furthest thing from that. Don't take this class.

It's a core class, but the workload is pretty heavy. There are many assignments, and the final project (artwork + a 700-word essay) has a lot of detailed requirements. It can be stressful, so keep that in mind before taking it. I hate her
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: SUCH A TOUGH GRADER
I hate it here. I hope she reads this and notices how POINTLESS the assignments are

So annoying. She is so strict for a core class. The assignments feel pointless. I took this class to get an easy A, and it's literally the one I'm stressing about the most. In the writings, if you state your opinion and she doesn't agree with it, she gives you like a 30/50. There are other classes that fulfill this core, so don't take this one. BYE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Such a tough grader. There are only 2 TA's and both  are extremely annoying.

Overall good professor who really cares about her students.  Germ 145 was really easy and fun you just have to show up to lecture and do the readings.  Only complaint is that you have to watch what you say/write in the free write because she will mark you down if your opinion doesn't agree with her political views.

She is a sweet person and allows late work and allows you do redo assignments to get full credit. But in assignments like free writes she asks for your opinion on different topics but when you don't say what she wants you too say she will mark you down.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Two lectures and a discussion on friday, all mandatory attendance. You have readings every class you have to read, really useless class and hard grader. Also multiple group projects you have to do through out semester. don't recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Meyertholen! You can tell she really cares about her students even when your German isn't perfect. Her lectures are interesting and she keeps everyone engaged the whole hour. The grammar assignments were tedious and a little repetitive but the overall helped when it came time to speak in class.

Very easy class. Show up to every class for participation points but most students work on other homework/go on their devices during class discussions anyway. If you need an easy A credit class to take with your important classes then this is for you. Boring but worth it. No tests or quizzes. Just online assignments, group projects and attendance.

I took her lecture as a CORE requirement and it quickly became my favorite class. She puts so much effort into her lectures and she is so passionate about what she teaches. She is always willing to work with students to improve grades and she cares! AMAZING
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She has a reputation of being very tough, but I saw the opposite; she rewards obvious effort with an A, even if the technical execution is lacking. Very fun and kind otherwise!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's super fun to have for class and very understanding about anything. She does assign a lot of reading and some of it can be a bit boring, but it's not incredibly crucial to the class.

I loved Professor Meyertholen's class over German fairytales! Almost every class session was entirely discussion-based, and it was truly a safe environment for everyone to share their interpretations. The main projects are not too difficult, and aside from one paper, they're mainly group and presentation based. I highly recommend this prof!!

I struggled with this class because of personal issues during the semester, but she was an amazing teacher who propelled my skill in German to higher levels. She was there to help when I needed it and her lectures and study materials were designed to help me develop my skill.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

He is average I suppose.  He posts 3 study guide tests that were from previous years before each test.  Most of the questions from the exam involve the material that are on those.  His quizzes suck, and are very hard.  Gives a lot of assignments that take about an hour or two to complete.  No textbook required.
Terrible teacher.  Avoid at all costs.
Anne Patt is an okay professor. For a first year professor, she gets decent work out of her students, but can often be extremely blunt and rude.
honest but super impatient for a teacher

Although she does give good criticism over your work, she can be very rude and think it is funny. Sure she may mean well but when she is just telling a student there work is terrible in front of the class then laughing about it as well as making snarky comments about peoples work it seems a bit unprofessional/bully like to me. LOL

Anne is such a lovely professor and person. She is extremely passionate and our introduction to it. You will need  to put in the work but it is so rewarding. As long as you are engaged, and active, you'll have a great time. She can seem a bit harsh, but she will actually give you criticism, plus she's hilarious. I can't recommend her enough.

Anne is one of the treasures of KU architecture. She's never afraid to say it how it is, even if it comes off a little harsh at first, but you come to realize that it's because she really truly cares about good design and wants you to succeed. This was incredibly useful and necessary in first year. Honestly inspiring and just a wonderful person.

Anne Patt was the best teacher ever. She was brutally honest but in ways that were funny and helpful. She made me love architecture even more. Bond with your classmates and create a community and you will have so much fun.

When I first met her, I was really intimidated by her and overall the college experience... But she was a great introduction for architecture and made sure to create the studio collaboration culture. She'll make you come out of your comfort zone, but thanks to her studio culture I made my closest college friends, fond memories and cool projects.

Anne is an amazing 1st year professor that will help you get introduced into the school of architecture. She gives you amazing feedback and only expects effort in return. Expect long hours as this is a studio class, but if you use time wisely and show up to class you can get work done.

Anne makes you work for your grade, but she's really good at giving good feedback and really helped me improve my work! She's an awesome 1st year professor who has a great sense of humor and highly critical.

In arch 108 with Anne Patt you'll definitely be busy and participation matters, so don't show up to class with nothing done. However, she makes the class fun with her witty sense of humor and good feed back.

I love Anne Patt! She cares about you excelling and finding a passion while working with you and bouncing ideas between you both. The class is a studio class so be prepared for long hours and late nights. The textbook is useful but she also gives in-class examples and shows you past work to inspire you. Would definitely take her again!

Professor Patterson is amazing. She is relatively lax about tardiness. She gives excellent feedback, and will definitely tell you that your work is terrible, but that you can improve by doing x, y, z. There are no rubrics in the course, so work to improve and grow, not to complete a checklist. Patterson is hilarious, relatable, and friendly.

Unprofessional and spiteful. I found her to be somewhat disrespectful at times as well; she sent me multiple rude emails and ignored mature apologies. Helpful in the classroom and a good professor, just not great when shes in a bad mood. I think she needs to learn to not lash out when she is dissatisfied with something minor. Hard to please.

reviews.comment: Anne Patt makes you work for it, soon you will realize she is there to instruct you and manage the worksheet but you are the architect. ASK FOR HELP, show effort, prepare for presentations. She rocks, would deff take her again.

The best first-year architecture professor. I ended up taking her for both semesters. I cannot imagine what I would've done without her. I learned so much and I feel well prepared to take on my sophomore year. She is knowledgable in what she teaches, she gets to know and cares for every student, she is funny and pushes you in the right direction.

Anne Patt is truly one of the best. While she can be blunt and will tell you if your work is bad, she certainly helps you grow as a student. She can be both incredibly funny and terribly fierce. She gave me a hard time at some points in the class, but I really think that in the end, it helped me grow. I highly recommend her for first-year students.
Honestly, Its a lot of work but it is worth it.

reviews.comment: Anne Patterson is the perfect professor to have for your first semester of architecture. She is a tough grader, but her feedback and criticism is phenomenal and will only help you grow in your career. Truly the best.

Annepatt really makes you work, there are four units with multiple parts to each project. They all come full circle. At the beginning you'll think you don't know what the heck is going on, that's because you don't. She definitely knows what she's doing, you'll learn A LOT from this woman, some hate her, some love her. I loved her and will miss her.

Annepatt is a badass woman, who gives blunt feedback and makes you work hard. You get out what you put in. She's definitely someone to take at least once (or twice) in your architecture career at KU. She's hilarious, fun with a fierce attitude. She knows what she's doing and will definitely tell you if your work is crap. She's a force of nature.

She's a tough grader and sometimes says some offensive things (I think she does this without realizing). Just be prepared for a lot of critique. I actually changed majors because of this class.

She is definitely tough, but a great professor. The work load is crazy. To say "you have to work for your grade" is an understatement. You can expect to spend 15-20+ hrs outside of the 4 hour class 3 days a week. She always has ideas about how something can be better which is a good thing, but gets really frustrating when you want to be finished.
Don't recommend if you consider yourself the average student. She says thing that may come off offensive. I believe she means well but at the same time its rude.
The best first year teacher they're is.

Annepatt is a decent professor. As the semester goes you will feel more comfortable with her abrasive style of critique. She seems to go after students more if she sees potential, but also plays the favorites game. Overall, she seems like a better option for first year than the other professors.
She was amazing!

You will learn tons while having a blast. She is hilarious, slightly crazy (in a very good way), and more than willing to help out. Studio teacher that i recommend greatly.  She is fun while still teaching you the foundations of architecture.  Made my first semester, which i heard was very boring, a blast. great teacher, putting in hard work only gets you halfway to the good grade. the other half is done by helping yourself.
very good studio professor, but a tough grader. in the end you learn a ton, but you need to be prepared to put in the work.

Always helpful, fun,and enthusiastic. I never saw her in a bad mood all semester.  Extremely helpful, especially if you seek her out with specific questions. If you are willing to put in the time, you can learn alot. Overall one of the best studio teachers I've ever had

she's a great prof with ample knowledge. she grades hard and you have to put in your hard time workin to get a good grade, but she's pretty helpful if you're willig to seek her out of class. in class it's sometimes hard to get her attention w/ 30+ people in class.
very funny. Definately plays favorites. Very opinionated. Grades pretty difficult

The hardest part of this class is listening to her ramble for 50 minutes. She does not seem to know much about anything, though she boasts constantly about going to CERN. The writing assignments are ridiculous and unnecessary. Her grammar is terrible as well.

I do not know what the person who rated her before me is thinking...she is so easy. And this is coming from a person who sucks at physics. Her test questions come FROM THE BACK OF THE BOOK. So if you read the book and go to class (She gives points on attendance) You will do VERY WELL
Hardest Class I have ever taken! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

She does a nice job explaining things. If you have brains in your head, you should be able to grasp her class and get an A or B.
She sometimes doesn't know what she's talking about.

Difficult subject but fantastic professor (my favorite at KU now). He is very fair with partial credit and adjusting deadlines. I probably spent 5+ hours on the projects outside of class each week but I truly learned a lot in this class. Definitely take if you have the option to!

Genuinely one of the top professors in the EECS department. He makes sure that students are able to take the class in a way that best suits them, and when it comes down to grading he is very fair. reviews.comment: This professor is truly an anomaly. A friendly, patient, and a professor that truly cares for his craft and students. He makes a difficult class easy to understand. He is epic. Actually a good professor who shows passion for what he teaches. He indirectly encourages students to learn instead of trying to regurgitate information, Tests are very fair and he makes sure you are properly prepared. Literally nothing bad to say.

Great professor. One of the best professors ive had at KU. He cares about his students and make sure they learn the materials well. 665 is a tough course with a lot of project and lab. But you will learn a lot.

Drew Davidson is a phenomenal professor. He truly cares about how all of his students are doing and caters to every level of ability. Hands down probably the best professor in the department. He's very organized and tells you exactly what you need to learn and when you need to learn it by. Class was challenging but rewarding. Dr. Davidson puts more effort into course quality and resources for students than any other professor I've had at KU. You'll learn so much in his class if you are willing to put in the work.
Lectures are semi mandatory. Have to do an assignment and turn it in if you dont attend. Good class though. Projects feel well balanced

Dr. Davidson is an absolutely fantastic professor. He is incredibly knowledgeable, caring, and goes way above and beyond for his students. JMC 330: Although Al was a tough grader, he prepares you with what the sports industry will be like. Assignment directions are very clear with everything being in the syllabus. I recommend EVRN 336 with Dr. Brox. While I'm not an environmental studies major, this course helped shape my thought process and career goals. Ali Brox is an amazing professor. She is very passionate about the environment and ethics. You will have to do a lot of readings, but not many of them are particularly dense. Just get ready to talk a lot. The papers are pretty easy as well, as long as you synthesize.

Fun, good-humored professor. Enjoyed the relationships between professors and GTAs in this class and overall discussion was fun. Class was interesting but grading got gradually harder, which was unexpected.

Ali was a great teacher to have for a topical english class about New Orleans literature. She was a great discussion leader and had very relevant readings and assignments for the class topic. She is very fair in her grading and always willing to help if you are struggling.

Took this class during the summer and had a great time. There were a few readings I didn't like, but that's the point of this class, to introduce you to a variety of literature you may not normally pick up. Lots of reading, of course, but the hm was easy enough. Also of note, guys (and certain girls), she's hot.
Great and makes class fun
Awesome, fun teacher. Super nice and super foine. Seriously, she's pretty hot.

Ali is an awesome teacher. Her expecations are clear and she will always make herself available to help you whenever you need. Nice, and fun. Come to class with something to say about the readings and she'll love you forever

Awesome teacher! Very cool and helpful. The readings are sort of interesting and short (250 pages max for the novels), with short stories here and there. 3 papers, she grades fair. Overall, a good class to take.

She was a fantastic teacher. Her grading is very fair. You write three papers over the course of the semester, all of which are fairly short, and the third is the final. There is some required reading, but homework is fairly minimal. I enjoyed this class very much.

infuriating class because the course material isn't too bad but the way he teaches it makes it harder. he picks favorites and is very obvious about it. the course organization was abysmal and he changed the percentages and final project in the last month which stressed the whole class out. he's definitely traumabonding us all together.
Very unorganized with assignments and lectures, and also unclear with grading criteria. Just hope that he likes you.

Dr. B cares a lot about students and the department. Three ways I'd describe him: high energy, disorganized (esp w grading), willing to help. If you are struggling, go to office hours. He will stop at nothing to help you out and does not demean students for not knowing material. Makes internet references to be hip with the kids.

I took his CPE112 class last semester and went on here to read the reviews and let's just say I'm not surprised. He picks favorites and can RUIN the class for you. I did good in this class yeah but I hated my major so much because of this class so I switched.
Professor Bertuccio genuinely strives to establish a personal connection with every student in his class, regardless of its size. He is kind and understanding. I thought he was great overall.

The reviews for Dr.B are very split & I understand where that may come from. Although the class layout may not always be the most organized and grading can take a while, Dr.B truly cares about his students and if you put actual effort into his classes you will do well. I think 211 is a great marker for evaluation on if ChemE is a good fit for you.

Cares about his students and strongly encourages us to reach out for help if needed- it's clear he is deeply passionate about both his job and the well-being of his students. The TAs grade the assignments, and "if you don't know the material you're screwed" is applicable for literally every class. Participate in class and you'll succeed.

Extreme workload, weekly quizzes with the hardest component being time. If you don't know immediately how to solve the problem you are screwed. Graded the REAs very hard, each one was 50 pages long. Didn't grade 40% of the course and my final grade was suspect.
All the other reviews should speak for this class.

Material and Energy Balances is the first ChemE course where you finally learn the fundamentals; unfortunately, because of how this class was taught, I may not do well in the following classes because I lack the basics. This was a "flipped classroom," but the video lectures never really helped with the in-class assignments which were difficult.
He does not grade in a timely or fair manner.

If he decides he does not like you, he will make your life harder. Seriously, I bet you he does not remember most of his undergraduate-level mathematics, so try not to mention any concept related to calc 2+, linear algebra, and statistics more than once or twice to him. I don't think he is qualified to be a professor.

I really enjoyed Dr. B's Material and Energy Balances. It is flipped, with the homework assignments essentially being guided lecture notes. Your grade is made up of quizzes, in-class work, and reverse engineering assignments. Dr. B is very social and cares about each student individually; he also provides a lot of extra credit opportunities.

Dr. B was a great professor in CPE111, but in CPE112, he was by himself and it felt unorganized and unprepared. We spent 3 classes working on spectrophotometry which we had already learned in a previous chemistry course. While the lectures were slow, the labs were fun and engaging (except the conductivity lab where we literally watched ice melt).

Dr. Bertuccio is amazing! This is an intro to ChemE and he made me excited to continue. He is "naturally caffeinated," so he brings a lot of energy to the class! He genuinely cares about your success at KU and in engineering. He also has a YouTube channel and Instagram to help answer questions commonly asked by undergrads (go check it out!)
Don't recommend taking her class. Felt like we taught everything to ourselves. HW grading was also tough.
Put way too many assignments, and often did not transmit clear guidance and firm knowledge regarding the subject matter

Really sensitive to the response of the class and you can tell that she actually cares about the content being taught to students. Advocates for ChatGPT usage on homeworks as long as you're honest about it. Only exam is a short-answer midterm. Final is an essay. Lectures consist of interesting ethical case studies and table discussions. Cool class.
Good professor. Coursework was reasonable and has good understanding of the topics covered

By far the worst professor Ive had at KU so far. If you can avoid taking her class by all means do so. The escalation from in class examples, to homework, to tests is extremely unreasonable and she gives no review content whatsoever and will teach new content up until the day before the test. Also does not respond to emails outside of school hours

reviews.comment: Homework was easy, and exams weren't too difficult.
