She wasted an insane amount of time having us do practice problems--they weren't bad, but too much time was given for them. Easy lab.

keep in mind this was her 2 year teaching. She appears to have a good grasp on the material, but there were several times where students had to correct her or she would come back the next day saying the info was wrong. She also changed both the layout and the grading of the homework for every assignment making it hard to know what she wanted.
She wasn't a bad teacher, however I just wished she posted the lecture slides before class if she's going to go through them fast and add new material.

Amy is a new professor so although her lectures were dry you could tell she really cared about the class. The tests were mostly based on the homework which was easy if you own the textbook. You get a cheat sheet on all tests but the tests were hard so make sure to still study. The lab is a very easy A.

Harsh grader, no rubric, vague feedback and unclear instructions for big projects that determine the majority of your grade. Incredibly smart professor with thorough knowledge of her field, does a good job keeping students engaged during long lectures and offers wonderful field sessions.

No rubrics/clear guidelines for design projects + portfolio- both are a majority of your grade. Gives very little feedback. My group failed the second project despite each of us working 20+ hours on it. Projects are stressful + confusing. Lectures and field sessions are very interesting, tho. Surprised I still like permaculture after this class.

This class is incredibly demanding and does not have clear guidelines for assignments and projects. Be prepared to be graded harshly and to only get loose instruction. There are no rubrics and the grading is entriely subjective. The content was very interesting though.

Amber's Permaculture was my favorite class at KU. The classes are long, but worth it - fascinating and engaging. Participation and final project are the majority of your grade, and she expects good work - write down the reasoning behind every decision to show you've put in thought. Very receptive to questions and has a lot of knowledge to share.

I absolutely LOVED Amber's Permaculture class. The lectures are long, but Amber has good humor about it and makes it interesting for all of us. The field sessions are so much fun, but unfortunately got moved online this semester. You can't slack off and the group project is big, but the life skills learned from this class are phenomenal.

Can't stand her as a teacher, she has no right to be giving lectures to anyone. By far the most opinionated and passive aggressive instructor I've had the displeasure of meeting. Whoever pushed her through her classes has done the education system a great injustice. Assignments are too vague, and grades were returned too late to change. 0/10

Amy presents herself in a mostly professional manner, and seems to strive to relate to students at Haskell University, but doesn't do much connecting with them. Amy's not afraid to incorporate her opinions into her classroom, often lining her lesson plans with views that shouldn't be expected to be elaborated on or discussed. Take this as you will.

reviews.comment: The topics of discussion and essays were way too advanced for this course. Papers are rarely handed back to look over. She was very leniant with the topics which was nice but in the end it was a very difficult course, perhaps too hard compared to what the description said.

I think the class ID is right. It was intro poetry. Class is not structured but that was a plus for me. The writing assignments are extremely difficult. And long. Literally 5 assignments total for the year, if you suck at writing AVOID THIS CLASS. Only assignments are long papers (just finished a seven page minimum paper), and responses to poems.

Waited till end of the semester to give papers back, never told us why we got our grades, never available to help when a student had questions, and very unorganized. i would not recommend this professor

Literally one of the most incompetent and idiotic people i have ever met in my entire life. Period. she is easily intimidated by anyone with an opinion and provides no useful knowledge or feedback. Gave me a D- on my first essay because she said I used "too many big words" that she didn't understand. Amy Hume has no business teaching
Very friendly and helpful during office hours.  Her essay assignments were far too obscure for an general education english course.

Like everyone says, she is vague, but helpful if you visit her during office hours.  Papers were very difficult. She says and shows that she is a  feminist, so make sure you are able to work with someone that has a different perspective than you.
Although she's late for class all the time, and not well-prepared for class, I love her analysis of essays, very interesting~~~
No Comments
If you spend the time to improve your writing, she can be very helpful.  Papers are difficult and lengthy.  Overall, I enjoyed the class.
She was very vague in her assignments. If you asked her to critique your paper, you would answer with vague criticism. Didn't learn anything.
Ridiculous. Hard to understand. Very unclear assignments.
Have to attend class or she'll "fail" you.  The class is pretty fun I guess, because she talks the entire discussion.  Papers are a little bit confusing and it takes the entire class to explain them.

she is ridicuously hard...i missed class only twice (we were allowed to miss up to 5x), did all the homework and reading, participated in class discussions, and wrote all the papers.  I got a C in the class...

I loved this class and Amanda was great. It is a difficult course for most people, but if you go to help room and do the WileyPlus as well as you can, it's definitely passable. Amanda lectures using guided notes from her iPad, so make sure to write down the side notes she mentions and not just the blanks.

Amanda is a very alright professor. For a freshman-level class, she doesn't allow computers and instead forces people to buy the lecture booklets. Her handwriting is pretty horrendous, and she tends to abbreviate everything. Very nice person, needs to figure out keeping the class somewhat enjoyable. Labs with TA's are great, study material is meh.

Amanda is a good professor who explains the content in the lecture well enough to understand without much trouble. However, I will say that she does go quite fast in lectures, and sometimes she doesn't end up explaining certain topics. Hence, I'd end up leaving the lecture more confused than before. Show up to every lecture and lab!

ACCT 200 is very much a freshman class. Professor Winn does a good job catering to that demographic; everything is relatively dumbed down and we spend lots of time on the basics. The class moves slow and can be boring, but you have to take it, and it's a free A. Professor Winn is knowledgeable and easy to talk to.
taught well and pretty clearly, she just went very fast in lectures because we had a lot to get done and go over. Sometimes was hard to read her hand writing while she was going through lecture.

Loved her teaching style, and she tells you what is on the test throughout her lectures. If you show up to every lecture and lab, you are golden. The review for the exams is not a great way to study. Stick to notes and in-class practice problems to study.

She is so easy to understand and as long as you show up to lecture and actually pay attention, you can easily get an A. You just have to actually put in effort studying and understanding. The daily lecture quizzes are easy if you just look over your notes before class.

Amanda is a great professor who cares about her students whether she knows you super well or very little. Lots will agree that her lectures get pretty slow sometimes, but if you don't pay attention you'll get lost easily. Show up to lecture and lab and pay attention in both to get an A.
She isn't that bad but man shes so slow at teaching

This class has so much content, but I felt like the professor did a great job at teaching the material. To be transparent, she taught my class of BLPs. She's very sweet and understanding and will spend time after class to answer any questions. There are a lot of assignments and in-class work.

Very fast paced lectures, rely on labs to review and apply material. Amazing teacher and very personable though. 3 midterms+final. Tests are very difficult and you have to put in effort to study. Use Help room as much as possible. All homework online. Lots of extra credit opportunities during labs. Everything in lecture is on a guided note packet.
Amanda Winn was a pretty good professor. If you have to miss a lecture it is not the end of the world, they do a good job reviewing the material in the labs.
It is so important to know and understand the context. She is a great professor, but the class moves by so fast so it is important to make sure you understand everything being taught.

Amanda Winn is such a caring teacher! She takes the time to get to know her students, and she makes accounting an enjoyable class. She is always open to questions and is super fun to be around! Would definitley take her class again.

Professor Winn is truly great. She tries her hardest to make sure we (a class of 400) retain all of the information. The class and material itself is what's difficult, as the course booklet (notes) of 200 something pages will be utilized to the fullest. Do all the extra credit offered. Go to lectures and labs. Have to pay attention in classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. The class will get hard if you don't stay up on content but Amanda will walk you through every concept. TA's are very helpful. There is a usually easy quiz every class to make sure people are coming to lecture. Amanda couldn't have done better as a professor although you get out what you put in to the class.

probably the most annoying class ive ever taken. the class seems like it should be easy but is so difficult for no reason. one thing she did that I didn't like was that she abbreviated EVERYTHING. lectures require a lot of focus and attendance is absolutely mandatory to both lectures and labs. a lot of the webassign answers can be found on Chegg...

The class itself is somewhat easy as long as you attended classes and labs to understand the material. She gives you up to 3 percent of extra credit which I strongly suggest you use! She does go really really slow teaching lectures in class and you have a quiz everyday.
She cares and makes sure you understand the material and helped with exam review

Prof Winn was awesome! although i didnt do great in the class (my fault) i really enjoyed her lectures and she made them easy to understand. she is always happy to answer questions during her lectures, and the TA team was awesome!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amanda was a great lecturer. the tests were difficult because the multiple choice questions can be tricky but she offers extra credit. I never read the book and still ended with an A but I'm pretty sure you need to buy the book in ordert to do your homework

Professor Winn is very passionate about accounting and it shows in her lectures. She is very caring and doesn't make you feel ashamed for asking questions. She will make sure you understand the material if you take some initiative seeing her after class or during office hours. Accounting topics can be hard, but she is good at making them easier.

While this class can be extremely lecture-heavy, her lectures flow well and she is always open to questions. I would recommend that you do your best to always make it to lectures, or the homework won't make sense. Amanda Winn is a solid choice as a professor.

reviews.comment: Not good

Amanda is nice but her teaching style isn't for everyone. Definitely make sure you have a good TA because that is who you go to for all your trouble in the accounting world. Accounting wasn't the best class but she did the best she could with what she was given

If she makes a mistake for an assignment deadline, your grade pays the price. Do not take her class.
It was a very chill class. I could get up and get food be gone for like 30 min and it was fine.

If there are try hards in your class with him, good luck, or become a try hard yourself.

He glazes the try hard a lot, leaving you with less of a chance to get a good grade based of him grading by the standards of the class.

GL

reviews.comment: AMAZING GUY!! He is so sweet but gives constructive critistism and only wants you to get better. I thoroughly enjoyed having him for first sem because he really cares and gives great advice. Architecture as a degree is hard but with alejandro he really helps simplify it.

We loved Alejandro for our first year studio. He was so understanding with deadlines and really wanted you to succeed. Be prepared to present through every stage of your project because he wants everyone to show their progress. Honestly no complaints.

Alejandro is an amazing professor who cares about his students. He expects a lot from you, and you will spend much time working on projects on your own time. But he is funny, very nice + helpful, and wants to see you succeed. I would not say he's a hard grader either, but there are about 4 projects you get grades on. Would definitely take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Alejandro is a proficient instructor and architect. My experience with him was fruitful and challenging. Sometimes he can overload us with many instructions at the time, but he will always be open to go back and explain or clarify. Overall he is respectful, professional, and motives students to explore and further develop ideas.

Professor Aptilon is one of the nicest guys I've met. He's very caring towards his students and wants you to succeed. That being said, he is a little hard to understand. He tends to go off on tangents that are confusing. He is not the best at explaining things but if you listen to his feedback and trust yourself you should do well in the class.

Great person and decent teacher. Not the best at explaining things but if you ask he will explain it til you understand. Doesnt always understand your question but is very willing to work with you and give you feedback. Hard to read if he likes your stuff or not but the less he says at desk visits the better you are doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Alejandro is a super nice dude and clearly very talented and respected in his field, but unfortunately he's not such a great professor. He has a tendency to not be respectful of our time, doesn't give very clear instructions, and sometimes his feedback isn't very helpful. He's also very difficult to get in contact with so I wouldn't recommend him.

The biggest thing to say here is that Alejandro tends to be a little hard to follow, sometimes this is because of odd tangents in his lectures other times it is in his feedback on your work. However, if you can adjust to and follow his thought process, there is some great feedback given and a lot of opportunity to show creative ideas.

Alejandro was an absolute awful teacher. He was never around to help outside of class for office hours and was very hard to get ahold of via email or the other ways he told you to contact him. He did not give good feedback, rather in my experience he just told me my work was "bad" or "not very good" without providing suggestions for improvement.

Great instructor, he really helped fuel my passion for design. At times his instruction was confusing, however after finishing 108 and 109 with him it's clear that his ambiguity when giving instruction is intentional and ultimately helpful. He assigns more projects than the other first-year instructors and really pushes you to do your best work.

Alejandro is a great Professor but harsh grader. He doesn't only focus on grading the end result but looks at you process throughout and grades upon that as well. His feedback may be sometimes confusing. Studio time never expect to do actual studio work but have a four lecture. Studio Work is done outside of Studio Time in this class. Also Arch 108

Alejandro is a very caring & hard-working professor. He really wants his students to succeed! At first, he is difficult to follow but once you warm up to him he gets much better. His feedback is not always the clearest & he does not put grades online which is frustrating. Overall, very nice but not my fav teacher. Some people loved him in my class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Alejandro was my studio professor for Arch 109 and I would definitely recommend him as your instructor. Alejandro has experience outside of the classroom both with practices in Mexico City and in Kansas City; he is well respected in the field. Alejandro allows a great deal of creativity and flexibility in the classroom and promotes teamwork.

His classes are done in a way that helps you think about HOW to develop your projects, not just a critique of your ideas. He does expect a lot, but will always help you get there, and give creative feedback. He is very hands on with projects and his class will take a lot of work and effort. Its not an easy A, but will be extremely rewarding.

Very unclear grading. Throughout the year he gave vague feedback on projects, used the term "ultimately" anytime you asked a question- which you then didn't truly understand his answer. VERY NICE GUY. Clearly loves what he does, but is a poor teacher and needs to stick to his prof practice not teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Ashourvan is a very smart man who cares a great deal about your success, however it is obvious there are some unknown aspects of his personal life that leach into the classroom. Some days he is very kind and will joke around with you while on others his head is somewhere else and he is short and can be borderline hurtful with his feedback.

Seems like a decent person, but as a professor, not great. He randomly assigns work a few days before its due date with little to no rubric. No specifics on what he wants for said work, but if we do not meet his expectations, he will criticize us in front of everyone and accuse of "AI-use." A lot of his feedback on coding is "use AI."

Assignments felt rushed and given without clear expectations, and then we were all criticized in front of the class when no one met those unspoken expectations. When we were experiencing issues with code, we were told to "have ChatGPT do it for you" which didn't feel like learning. A lot of course materials were unorganized and created using AI.

Decent PERSON, awful PROFESSOR. You don't have time to really learn the material, you cannot absorb the information in lectures, and exams are literally just studying specific questions and answers found on Quizlet. He said in class that he didn't know the campus's AI policy, but was personally okay with it. Negatively set the tone for this class.

DON'T TAKE THIS COURSE. Each class covers an entire chapter of content, and it's just totally incomprehensible. He speeds through the content, and the slideshows for ONE class are 50-60 slides long. All full sentences, SO hard to take notes. The tests are impossibly difficult, even if you take his practice quiz. No learning, just memorize or fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Ashourvan went through 1 chapter each class. I don't know if it was the textbook that was used or his teaching style, but it was too much content delivered at one time. There was also no checking to see if we were understanding the material, like assignments or hands-on learning. He is insightful, but does not have an accessible teaching style.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ashourvan seems very passionate about his topics, and is good at responding to students and answering questions. Arian was a great introduction into Neuroscience for me, and taught with a really good balance of letting me explore what I wanted but also moving through the course material.  The lectures were really interactive and fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Covers the material very thoroughly, and his lectures are interesting and well-prepared. Cares a lot about his students and seems very passionate about the material. I would definitely recommend taking a class with Professor Ashourvan if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I would take this class with any other professor over this one. I had to drop this class due to his teaching style, and he created a very unfavorable learning environment. reviews.comment: I would stay away from this one. I had to drop it because of the teaching style. He doesn't answer questions and just reads straight off the slides. I would make sure you never took this class with him. He moves through content very quickly with little explanation on the topics.  The tests are beyond hard.

reviews.comment: He's a caring and approachable professor. His lectures are clear, and the workload is manageable. The class is stats-heavy, but he and the TAs are willing to help. Overall, I enjoy taking the class.

He's such a fantastic professor. Just don't miss the homework deadline or turn in anything late, make sure you pay attention to the mock exams and use the notecard, sheet to the final. He just only want his student to succeed and does everything he can to help you do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He's my favorite professor at the business school. His accent may take a little getting used to, but he records every lecture, which really helps if you need to review. Make sure you use the mock exams—they're a great preview of what to expect on the actual exams.
I learned a lot in BSAN 202, Weimar is a good professor and his TA team really supportive.

He is my fav prof at BSchool. His accent might be a little heavy to listen to, but if you did not understand, he got the record video for all the lectures. Take advantages of the mock exams, they would be super helpful for the actual ones.

I took AP Stats in high school so the class was pretty easy for me. If you actually want to learn statistics, he is not a great professor, but if you just want a free A, then this professor is for you. He often overcomplicates things and makes it more confusing. The study guides for each test is identical to the actual test itself. free A- but nice

Honestly, he's an amazing professor, just for the love of God don't miss the homeworks' and don't make them late, I screwed myself out of an A for that, but pay attention to mock exams and take advantage of the notecard (you can bring on exam day) and sheet (you can bring on final). He's a great professor who really wants you to succeed!

Attendance is not mandatory, but there are weekly quizzes that require a code to take. Weimar is super smart and caring, but not the best lecturer. The supplemental materials are really useful (especially the mock exams). There are also plenty of opportunities for extra credit.

He's the nicest guy ever, just very hard to understand and the lectures are a bit confusing. Will always work through with you in office hours. Definitely go to the lab as that is where you learn most of the content

Weimar is cool, he's easy to reach, it's just difficult to understand him sometimes and I don't like his teaching style. The mock exams are nearly the exact same as the tests so make sure to look at those. There's quizzes every week so attendance is basically mandatory. I only made it through because of my high school stats knowledge. Good luck.
I like this class. Weimar is super accessible outside the class room, and he really cares about helping you to get an A.

I have never received below a 95% in a math class besides this one. I could not understand him the whole semester and resorted to teaching myself because when I went to his lectures, I would leave very confused and have to reteach myself everything.

Weimar is very nice but he is not the best teacher. He often overexplains or complicates things or goes over stuff that just wont be on the tests. Regardless, the class is easy. Tests are nearly identical to the mock exams. Curve and extra credit on all tests.

I love him. It took me a little bit to understand him with his thick accent, but you catch on quick. He makes things very clear and he has a lot of grace for students. It is hard to run a huge lecture class, but I think he does it very well!

Professor has a very thick accent, making lectures hard to understand; rely on TAs for clarification. Tests are moderately difficult. Discussion required, lecture optional. Overexplains, wastes time; occasional announced quizzes
He is really amazing. His accent is thick so it is sometimes hard to listen. But he has recording videos so yall can review at home.
Solid class. The mock exam was super helpful.
I can't understand him during class and he makes me more confused. He doesn't explain things at all either and it makes no sense.
Great guy! He's super flexible and always willing to help out whenever needed..

Professor Weimar was the best professor I have had at KU.  Always go visit him during his office hours as he was always extremely helpful in clarifying coursework.  The practice exams are exactly like the real exams so study those!

This professor genuinely cares about his students. He's incredibly flexible and willing to provide accommodations if necessary. I got A just by doing all the homework and attending the labs. Mock exams were also helpful.

reviews.comment: He is such a caring and funny guy! I attended all the lectures and while he's hard to understand at times he knows his stuff. I didn't put that much effort and got an easy A

Overall, this is a solid class with a good instructor. The lab sessions and office hours are very helpful. Attend class regularly, and you'll do well!

I don't understand all the negative reviews. Weimar is such a nice guy. He's a bit hard to understand but he is accessible outside of class and is more than willing to help answer questions. lots of in class quizzes, lots of people skip cause he doesnt take attendance, the only thing that helped me learn was the labs ran by the TAs-- didnt like how weimar teaches, final exam is easy if you just study

65% of your grade will be determined by 65 multiple-choice questions, which is utterly ridiculous and a slap in the face to your tuition dollars. Worst lectures I've ever been in, I'd truly rather watch grass grow. Everything I learned was self-taught. You ca survive the class but it's a joke.

reviews.comment: Take these ratings with a grain of salt. Lectures are recorded, so attendance isn't mandatory. Be sure to memorize the *steps* of a problem, especially if it's on a mock exam. If he provides a problem in class, practice with it for an exam. Kind of inconsistent in how hard he makes the class, so as long as you can be aware and adjust you'll do fine

Be sure to do the extra credit, and show up to class and labs. He is very nice, but most importantly pay attention in class, and make sure you understand it then you'll succeed.

Very easy to get an A in this class, especially studying with Weimar. He is one of the best professors at the university. He recorded all lectures so the class was not required attendance. The quizzes were super easy and the exams had all what he taught in class.

reviews.comment: An A is definitely achievable under this professor. Very soft-spoken but knowledgeable. Practice tests align so closely with the actual tests and in-class problems align with homework so concepts make sense. Overall just a good guy and makes stats understandable at every level. You definitely want this guy as your stats teacher, undoubtedly.

Weimar is one of the best professors at the University. He turned a class that countless students have failed in the past to a class that is extremely doable with effort and attendance. Weimar is awesome. Before this class, I was a finance major and switched to business analytics because of this class. Weimar is an absolute dawg.

Great professor, very smart and knowledgeable about the topic and offers tons of help outside of class. Get used to his thick accent fast because he is difficult to understand ontop of the big auditorium and microphone. Other than that he is hands down the best BSAN professor to sign up for.

I believe this is Dr. Weimar's first year at KU. He teaches Stats systematically, provides a free textbook, but it's math-heavy in a notation sense. Exams align with teaching material. reviews.comment: i dont recommend to be honest

Professor Chhikara was very caring about our class on how we were doing in the class and was helpful with any questions in the classroom or during office hours. Dr. Linden is very clearly knowledgable on what he teaches. He is very caring and you are guaranteed an A in his class as long as you participate and do the work.
