Highly passionate about his work and enthusiastic about others', he's definitely the best professor in the German department.

Ari is a fantastic professor. You can tell hes just an all-around easygoing and kind individual. Nevertheless, hes very intelligent and will push you to truly learn the German language through creative writing and audible comprehension. *Get ready to advance your proficiency*

Prof. Linden is pretty great. I had him for a literature class and a language class. He's very approachable and cares about his students. His lectures are always well-done and fun to listen to.  Make sure to do the reading. This is one of the ways to do poorly in his classes.

Professor Linden is awesome. He cares about his students and whether or not they learn and understand. He's also pretty funny and personable. If you reach out to him for help, he will guide you to an A.

He was actually a really good teacher for the most part and uses relevant examples aswell as does engaging activities within the lectures to keep it interesting. The coursework is kind of hard but he does a good job of trying to explain it
Not a good teacher in lecture. Totally random and off topic a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's not a bad professor, but his lectures get incredibly boring because of the way he talks. He often talks in circles and even spent an entire class explaining what a budget is. Otherwise, the class is light work.

Very nice and enthusiastic about teaching and also understanding about absences. My only gripe is that he intentionally puts text on his slides that are quite different from what's in the books, which gets confusing at times.

Josh was a fantastic professor. The only reason I received a B was for personal reasons, and it is not reflective on Josh as a lecturer. The class in itself is somewhat simple, but participation and keeping up with homework are vital. Exams can be tough if you don't put in the effort, but TAs help, and the practice assignments help a lot as well.
Josh is a great lecturer and he picks wonderful TAs as well. The class is pretty easy as long as you go to lectures and there's plenty of opportunity for extra credit.

I love Josh! I understand that he can sometimes be hard to follow along with because his slides differ so much from the course packet; however, he is truly there to help. If you are not an accounting major, you will have to put some time in, but if you stay engaged with the content, this class should be a breeze!
Really amazing in lectures, and picks amazing TA's to help with lab and everything else throughout the semester. Got an easy A, just go to lectures and lab, and ask questions if you need it!
Great professor!! The class was very clear and the TA's were also great. It's a good mix of homework and tests so it doesn't feel like too much but you also actually learn the content.

Accounting 201 was a great class, extremely doable if you even pay the slightest attention. Slack off and yeah it becomes a challenging class with hard grades to come back from. The exam replacement policy is huge for some. 2 group projects with lots of extra credit between.

2nd class taken with Josh. Great professor, clear grading criteria and is lax about things that he's also assigning for the first time. He was overseas for a portion of the summer so class had two due dates. Tests aren't difficult as long as you watch lectures and take time to learn material. I'd personally take the class over the summer if avail.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Josh is one of the best professors I have had at KU. You can tell he wants his students to understand and succeed. Attendance is not mandatory, but you have homework to turn in once a week in class so your grade will suffer if you frequently skip. Lecture and lab were genuinely beneficial to my understanding in the class and I enjoyed the course.

Josh is good at covering material during lectures, and everything he makes clear that what he teaches will be on exams, unless he states otherwise. The problems we do during class are good practice for tests.

very strict about timelines. Shark Tank got cancelled for us, and he threw a fit. Lectured for 10 mins about the scheuelde of class. Very Stubborn about everything. Takes every last second of the lecture.

ACCT 313 is a fairly new course created to be taken after ACCT 200 and before 201. I took it after both.

Very helpful if you're ACCT/FIN double major bc it touches on financial analysis and accounting

Course packet is given, but its mainly conceptual with some important equations to remember for exams. Exams are 1/3 MC, 1/3 SAQ, 1/3 Problems

I took Josh's ACCT 201 Spring 2024 and I enjoyed the content and the way he presents the topic. Reviewing notes is very helpful, especially since he goes pretty fast paced and it's very different than ACCT 200. 

Josh's office hours were very helpful and it's good to stand out in a class of 400+. Many easy opportunities for extra credit too!

josh and his ta teams were amazing! its a hard class but if you pay attention and do all of your assignment you can pass with an A, study all the course book practice problem and the ones posted on canvas and study quizlet for the concepts parts and you'll do great!

Josh and his team of TAs and graders are great. Be ready to study and make sure to attend all lectures or else you may fall behind like math this class builds on past lessons so be ready. Make sure to start studying early. This class is point-based so it helps to do extra credit as well overall, good guy who cares about what and who he teaches.

Josh and his team of TA's and graders are great. The material can be difficult, but if you come to class, do your homework, and spend a few hours studying before exams you should be able to get an A, if not at least a B. TAs are super helpful and you can tell the whole team really cares. Lot of easy extra credit as well. Clear expectations

Content-heavy course built on ACCT 200. To be transparent, he taught my class of BLPs. Frequent in-class assignments, but manageable. Very communicative and cares about students. As per almost all ACCT courses here, you'll have to buy external materials.
wasn't great at preparing students for test material

Josh was a great teacher! Although his lectures were sometimes boring, he explained concepts and practice problems in class so that there were no surprises on the exams. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to do well.
Doesn't utilize class time and learning depends on the TA at lab.
had to drop also makes you buy a 100$ textbook

He does pop quizzes every week, and it is good to know the material and make sure you understand it. He is a great professor and it is good to get to know your TA because in the end they are the ones who decide on your grades. They are the make or breaks. Also be sure to show up to class and do the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The lectures can get pretty boring but he is still a great teacher, cares about his students a ton and will help you if you need help. The lab is very important to go to and the TAs are great and help you learn everything better. Easy extra credit points are available.
Easy class, Josh has it down to a science. I found him to get a little boring at times but he always taught to the exams and covered what needed to be covered. Good enough.

This class was very different from ACCT200 and in my opinion, is a little harder. Josh's lectures are very boring and it's hard to pay attention, so definitely go to labs. Keep looking over your course packet to understand everything taught. Overall he is a nice professor but the material being taught is sometimes hard to comprehend during lecture.

Arpin and the accounting team do a really great job of creating a team to help you through the course. 201 is different from 200, as in 200 labs were a time to practice material, whereas in 201, you learn a decent amount of the actual content in lab. Arpin does a great job of preparing you with all of the different types of questions you might see.

Josh isn't a bad guy. But his lectures are so dull and boring, it's impossible to pay attention. This class was super tough and homework is really difficult. I basically learned everything myself studying the course packet and going to lab. Lab is essential to understand the content poorly covered in lecture. The TAs are great on a bright note.

The course itself isn't that difficult, but this man's lectures are so mundane and boring that it is nearly impossible to engage and understand. I am usually attentive and engaged in lectures, but he makes it so incredibly hard. I always end up just going back to my dorm and reviewing my notes on my own until I understand them.

Josh is great. He does ramble, and his lectures can seem longer than they are. You do need to go to class. If you do, the material is super easy to learn. There are so many extra credit opportunities and everything is graded pretty easy, so you should have no problems doing well in the class.

Josh Arpin is awesome! I struggled in this class just because of the material, but there is lots of extra credit opportunities that helped a ton. he is always willing to work with you and is easy to reach outside of class. attendance for lectures isn't mandatory, but I definitely recommend going. lab attendance is mandatory, but is also helpful.

The class had many opportunities for extra credit and had group projects to help your grade. The lectures and labs are really helpful to know the material and for test they give multiple things to practice ad study. I enjoyed the class way better than ACCT 200. Going to class is important and they do bump up your final grade if it was close.

You get what you put in to this course. Josh is clear on what is expected in the course and how you will be graded. Yes, you have to go to class and pay attention but it is only 50 min. Labs are also very helpful to your grade, and plenty of extra credit to help. The course packet is a must and the test are same as review problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Josh! His lectures were as entertaining as an accounting lecture could be. Needed to contact him once outside of class and he responded within minutes.
The tests are nothing like practice problems. Cares more about his Cadillac than students.

This class's content isn't too hard to learn, it just feels like there isn't much teaching in lecture time since it is only a 50-minute class. By the time the class gets started, it feels like we've only learned 5 minutes of content. You learn content in your lab, but if your TA sucks, you're out of luck. Overall not terrible, but could be improved
Great Prof, tests are not hard but cover lots of stuffs so make sure you review examples from the course packet. Lots of quick extra credits.

Arpin was an amazing professor and super understanding. He rewards hard work- I didnt have to take the final! TAs hosted study review sessions day before tests that were super helpful. He gave many extra credit opportunities it is not hard to end this class with an A and I am not an accounting major. Really nice guy and made accounting enjoyable!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Josh was one of my favorite lecturers at KU! Lectures were enjoyable which made the class easier. He always sent out emails (which included extra credit) and was kind enough to offer tons of extra credit and extensions. 10/10 recommend!

This guy straight up sucks. He tells you to study one thing because it will "for sure" be on the test and then doesn't even put it on the test. After every exam the following class he would wine about how the class did so bad and he didn't know why. If you want to pass with a grade higher than a high C low B take it with another teacher.

Arpin gives a lot of assignments and expects you to work hard in his classes, but he also puts in the work on his side as well. He fine-tunes his classes so that the information you're learning will be applicable to your real-world jobs. He's also very flexible and understanding with students. I've taken him for a couple classes and he is great.

Josh Arpin is AMAZING. As a Marketing major, he made Accounting easy to understand and manageable, and an overall awesome experience. Offers a ton of extra credit opportunities and office hours. He is super personable and cares about you if you care about the course. The whole TA team is awesome as well. 10/10, loved it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Josh is a really good professor who made accounting really easy to understand. He tries to make lectures interesting using videos and examples. There are four group projects that can be hard if you have a bad group. TAs are good too.

Josh is a good teacher and uses good examples that are easy to understand. 4 group projects that turned into individual projects, these were moderately difficult. Tests were hard, so study. The final was ridiculously hard (online due to Covid), most likely to catch cheaters. TAs were nice and helpful.

Josh is amazing and I couldnt imagine taking ACCT 201 with anyone else. He gives you a lot of resources to succeed, keeps you engaged in lectures, and is very personable even with a 400+ lecture class. I highly recommend taking him if you get the chance!

I loved Josh, he is a really cool dude and his lectures are easy to follow. He uses tophat throughout the lectures which I think is a good thing because it kept me paying attention to the lecture. He cares about his students and he does give a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Definitely recommend him.
If you have Josh get ready to have a homework assignment every class period, and extra work on top of that. He loves to cover the basics in class and test you over extremely in-depth concepts.

Overall an easy class and interesting enough. The tests are long but not difficult if you know most of the material. A few projects including one group project, but he lets you choose your group if you want. Lots of extra credit. Easy A.

You can tell Josh really respects students and wants to help everyone. He's very open and responsive to student feedback, and does his best to make an accounting class as entertaining as possible. There are four major projects, with the last one being a group assignment. Opportunities for extra credit abound.

Josh is a good guy who cares about his students. He makes accounting relevant and adds value to his class with the unique industry experience he has. We did a long project instead of a final but he gave a lot of feedback along the way and always responds to emails. Quizzes were easy if you did the homework. Hopefully he changes group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Gives tons of free points, test questions, and extra credit. Seriously. And the content itself is already quite simple. If you get a C or below in his class you should probably consider dropping out of college.

Josh is a great professor and cares about his students. The lectures were a little boring because the material is mostly theory; however, josh tried to make them a little interesting. The tests are difficult since its mostly theory. The apollo shoes project is hard since there is little guidance but you can ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Josh is a really great guy. He has a good sense of humor and does everything he can to help you do well. Made the class fun. The TA's were great and also very helpful. Gives lots of extra credit and allows you to miss 30 of 300 HW points with no grade penalty. Curves the tests if needed. Group projects are easy points if you put in a little effort.
Josh Arpin is the bomb professor. He teaches well, makes it fun, and if you give effort you will pass this class; guaranteed.

Professor Arpin does a good job of teaching accounting in a way that makes it a more fun and interesting than the subject sounds. If you go to class and simply fill in your course packet you should be fine.
He's a good guy who is very helpful and wants you to succeed. If you pay attention in class and study a little bit before each test, you will be absolutely fine.

ACCT 205 isn't super interesting, but it's not a super challenging class either. His tests are extremely similar to the practical applications you do in class. The quizzes are also very similar to the homeworks. He also gives a lot of extra credit if you just show up to class so don't skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Tests are moderately difficult, I skipped several classes and I'm really struggling now. A lot of material is covered in class. He does seem to care, as he has always been willing to meet with me and help me outside of class. There are several projects throughout the semester, all of which are easy. If you show up and pay attention, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Huge class but if you don't go you won't pass. Pop quizzes and in class points. Tests are difficult. HW can be lengthy don't wait til last minute. Josh is kinda pompous and comes across arrogant.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Arpin's lectures are not terribly interesting but he does a good job of teaching the subject. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he often gives assignments or quizzes in class for points. His tests are a lot like the homework and are very fair. Go to class, pay attention, do the homework, and you'll easily get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This professor prides herself on this aura of professionalism but the way she organizes her class is so amateurish. What she asks for on the projects and the deadlines she gives for them are absurd and unfair. We are simultaneously doing two group projects and having homework. Her "care" for her students is so fake once you get to know her.

Large amount of handwritten notes coming from textbook and tells you what to study before each test. Prompt grader w/ good partial credit. Tests are more concept-based. Group project is kinda bleh. Answers questions pretty well.

725 is focused on the mathy definition of optimization and doesn't really showcase 3rd party optimization tools.
The professor never replies to emails, when I had questions. The professor is not friendly or helpful.

Dr. Arnold is very professional and a fair grader. 421 is a fun class but LOTS of work-- which is fair since you need lots of independent, hands on experience to learn CAD modeling. We did 3 group projects, each with a presentation, and could only pick our group for the final project. They were intense, but I learned the most from those projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I actually took advanced ballet with Professor Brittingham.  It is the best ballet class I have ever had.  She respects each individual and why they are taking the course, focusing on artistry and healthful technique practices.  An inspiring teacher that supports your growth and makes ballet fun!
I absolutely loved this class my only qualm was that I wish we had learned more basic dance techniques. Overall she is a very kind teacher and everyone should take musical theatre dance!

Professor brittingham is an amazing dance instructor and not strict or mean like many ballet stereotypes. She is so funny and insanely kind and supportive of all of the dancers and truly wants to help you get better. Take her classes if you can!

I wish I was not graduating or else I would take another class from him. He is such a good teacher who really cares about the lesson he is teaching. I wrote a handful of papers for his class. No midterms or finals. He gives a lot of feedback on course work and was always willing to work with students on deadlines. My favorite teacher at Ku.

Asaf is the best! On written assignments, he always leaves lengthy feedback that is relevant and helpful. He responds to emails quickly and is a fast grader. He gets to know all of his students and does his best to make class fun. He is extremely knowledgeable and a great resource to have. He is one of the nicest and smartest professors I've had.

Would recommend this professor to anyone. Very understanding and always responds to emails. Lectures are fun and always have interesting questions at the end. He doesn't do many assignments besides one weekly assignment but definitely study hard for the midterm and final exams. He also does extra credit sometimes and will work with you on due dates
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Muddiman is a great professor! She makes everything very clear and always checks up on students and their groups in class. She assigns the final project early so you have enough time with your group and provides feedback the entire time! I highly encourage you take a class with her if you are able!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: So helpful and kind. She is very interesting and engaging with students, which made an online class more interesting. She is a clear and concise grader with great feedback. Highly recommend!

Professor Muddiman was a fantastic teacher! She is a rather tough grader but provides insight that is invaluable and has taught what might be my favorite course at the University of Kansas. 607 is a participation heavy class which focuses on utilizing theories that Muddiman teaches and outlines extremely well. Excellent course!
Group project is a lot of work and tough to find meeting outside of class. Her tests are tough and reading material helps a lot. She is very nice and helpful but also stern with what she expects.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She has a skill for being clear and precise about what she expects, and it is reasonable. I would take another class from her.
Muddiman is a good professor. She sometimes seems flustered or nervous and talks quickly, but that is just how she is all the time. Very responsive and flexible. Would take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class is fairly easy. If you're looking for an easy A, this is it. She barely showed up to class but attendance was mandatory. We only had one midterm instead of two because of the pace of the class (probably cause she didn't come to class most of the time) we had 3 group projects and a take home final.

I could forgive her attendance policy if she herself followed it. It is very disrespectful to people who paid $950 to be there to not show up to an early morning class, but send a TA to take attendance. She could at least send an email out. I never paid attention to the lectures and instead just read the terrific book written by Greg Mankiw.

She is a very nice lady, and I enjoyed taking her class. A lot of interaction in class and she teaches you how to think critically. The only downside is that half of the class was taught by a TA instead of her (the TA was great though thankfully).

Disorganized, often absent from class, pretends to be nice but she is actually the worst professor I have ever had. Her knowledge of the material is very superficial. I would not recommend her class to any student.

Professor is extremely disorganized and is unclear about the structure of the class. Attendance is mandatory but there are no attendance/participation points.Our TA was kind but she was incredibly quiet and was hard to understand. Homework assignments are randomly assigned and the exams can be challenging, use the end of the chapter reviews.

Class was extremely easy, but she was by far the worst teacher I've ever had. She just used the questions at the end of each chapter for her tests, lectures are pointless except mandatory attendance. Just read the chapters and review the questions and be fine. She was extremely disorganized, walked out of lectures and student presentations often
She is really bad. It is not hard, but she treats us like elementary students rather than college level. Not a problem if you want to be treated like a child.

She can be kind of absent, but she is very nice and helpful.  USE the sample exams.  The test questions are sometimes exactly the same; numbers and all.  Reading the book is important for reinforcing everything.
Great teacher and is willing to go out of her way to help.
She is a great teacher.  If you don't understand the material, she does not mind going over it again to make sure the students understand.
She is a very nice person, but lectures were not well organized. I never felt confident about anything taught in the class.
Great Teacher. Really helpful and works with you. She records the class so if you miss you can still watch the lecture.
Great professor. Really cares about her students.

I took her class online and she gave great feed back for essays, the syllabus was clear and direct, and the material, while sometimes kind of a lot, was always easy to get through, interesting, and varied in style. You do have to do your homework, but if you do, then you shouldn't have too much trouble. Loved her!

This class was online and lasted only a month. There were daily reading responses due, but they were really just 4 question MC quizzes or a film sheet that you could easily fill out while watching the assigned film. Yes, it was a very easy course, but I really did learn a lot. Ashley was always quick to respond.

Ashley is, in a word, incredible. Her course is one of the most interesting AND flexible classes to take online. My class was only a month long and from day one I knew what to expect. Very clear syllabus with due dates, and you can work ahead. Lots of reading, but all very digestible. Ashley keeps herself accessible and really tries to help you!
I LOVED Ashley. This is my second class with her and she is amazing. I have never met a more dedicated GTA at the university.

Ashley rocks! She's a wonderful teacher, and has so much insight on a broad range of theories and topics within the Women Gender Sexual Studies realm. She works to make herself available any time her students should need her, and she is a lifesaver when it comes to flexibility. She genuinely wants all her students to succeed.

Ashley is one of the greatest TAs I have ever had at KU. She was incredibly accessible and willing to walk students down harder concepts when needed. I loved her so much that I'm taking another class in the fall specifically because she was that amazing. 10/10 would recommend!
Ashley is a great TA!

This class was way harder than it needed to be. Lecture slides make no sense unless you take notes during class. The exams are very difffcult with the average being in the 60-70 range. Do all extra credit and take pictures of all the specimens during lab to study for the practicals.

Brian claims to make the exams as fair as possible by dividing up the material evenly. It sounds good in theory, however, is it really fair to have equal amounts of the exam dedicated to material you learned the day before & 3 weeks prior?
-Lectures aren't recorded
-Do ALL extra credit
-Use pictures to study for practicals
-Show up and take notes

Gives so much information during lecture that you don't know what content to prioritize. Average for exams are high D's to low C's. Exam questions are hyper specific in the sense that it'll ask you a question that he only went over for like 1 minute in a lecture a few weeks ago. Lecs aren't recorded. And his slides are pictures mainly.

You'll see my review on Glor's portion. I preferred Atkinson's portion, but this class is fascinatingly hard. Anticipate most of the exams being on material you learned the day prior, with questions about minor fun facts that you would have never studied. The organization of it is especially hard for students who work, making the class inaccessible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Could have been a very straight forward course. Refuses to make information easily accessible. Everything is cryptic, lots of tricks. Have taken O-Chems and many difficult classes in college and never have gotten a B in college, definitely will in this class. Terrible professor.
Dr Atkinson was a very kind and caring professor who cares about the material and is very passionate about teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Brian is such a fun professor, and he puts so much effort into his class and his students. He co-taught with another professor, and they were both great. He is a great person and I high recommend him. The first time I walked into class, I thought he was a student but then once he started lecturing it was clear how extensive his knowledge is.

deducted points from someone in 2014 for going to their grandmother's funeral instead of going to class. Even though they told him they would be gone a week in advance, and they got a letter from the cremation society upon return. No makeups on assignments allowed, and zero on their attendances for those days.

There were no lesson videos or any lectures, only pages of notes to read and decipher. He hosted weekly zooms which could be helpful. The tests only had 4 questions with no partial credit, making it extremely difficult to get good grades on them. Had to rely heavily on youtube and other sources to teach myself. (taken online at another university)

His lectures were fine but nothing special, His accent is really a non-issue, there was no graded hw and the weekly quizes were drawn from the nongraded homework questions. He does use wolfram to solve for lots of things which isn't very helpful. Exams weren't bad and there was EC worth 10% of grade, but there was very little grade transparency.

Dr. Stefanov is a good instructor, sorry that the business majors in 126 couldn't handle him! Bet they didn't even visit office hours. He is tough and, yes, you will want to do some reading outside of the class. However, his lectures are quite good and he is far less dry than some of the other instructors in the department. A good dude.

He's a really good professor! Go to the class, review notes and complete the weekly homework and you would start loving differential equations. He provides lots of examples in class which makes the class easier. Also offers a 10 percent extra credit as a grade booster! Take him!

Dr. Stefanov seems like a nice guy, but it's unfortunate that his lectures are very hard to pick up anything from. He moves too fast when explaining new concepts and also does not explain them well. If you have the opportunity, do not take a class from him.

This guy has made me hate math in a way no teacher has ever done before. Let me attempt to give you an idea of what this guy does. He once typed a problem in to Wolfram Alpha, pointed at the answer on the screen and said "there you go", then moved on. He goes incredibly fast, writes stuff down without explaining, then says "that's how it works".
awful teaches nothing moves really fast russian
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The previous comments are a good indicator of what's coming. Stefanov definitely understands math, but he does not explain things clearly and won't clarify even if asked to. If you aren't focused, you're going to miss a lot - he does write very fast and doesn't even get the problems right sometimes. I switched to another prof - great decision.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's faster than Jesus at writing and has horrible handwriting. If you look away from the presentation for more than a second you will never catch up. He's very rude, doesn't answer questions, and is very hard to understand. The lectures are horrible.
Terrible, absolutely terrible professor.  He uses WolfRam Alpha for everything.  My engineering adviser even knew him by name and told me to avoid him at all costs!

The worst math teacher I have ever had. Uses Wolfram Alpha pretty much everyday and flies through everything so you don't even have a chance to write things down. The class average for the first test was a 40/100... I would rather take the 8 am version of this class just so I wouldn't have to be in his class.

Undergraduates don't appreciate the effort professors give to help them. It's the student's job to learn the material, the professor's job is to facilitate. Stefanov does a wonderful job of that in 766. I only wish that we could solve more text problems in class instead of qual problems; it reinforces what we learn in the text/homework.

Literally uses wolfram alpha for EVERYTHING. Not exaggerating. Every single example. It makes it very hard to follow what he's doing in the class. He does offer extra credit at the send of the semester and curves if necessary. Still, he sucks. Hardcore.

I disliked this teacher with a passion. I hated going to class but he kind of makes it mandatory because he gives out daily quizzes. I never learned anything in class, he is hard to comprehend and understand. I had to teach myself at home and had to have a tutor and still only came out with a C... My advice: AVOID him at all costs!!
Thick accent and no real benefit to attending class although he will notice when you don't. Avoid this teacher if you have any other options as he is just a headache waiting to happen.

Sometimes his handwriting is a little sloppy and/or hard to follow, but his proofs are good, different from the book, and plus he really tries to teach the process of arriving at a proof from scratch, i.e. how to think like an analyst, over merely providing you with the prettiest proofs he can find. Lots of good commentary about math in general too

This teacher is awful. He is extremely unclear, both in his teaching and in his expectations for the class. One day he well tell you that you can use a computer on the test, the next day you're told you aren't allowed to use a calculator.

He knows his stuff, but can be hard to understand, especially if you've never taken calc before. he curves the class and lets you come in for extra credit at the end of the semester if you are close, but the tests are really hard. only take this class if you've taken calc before or want a challenge

I took honors Calc 1 in the fall...this guy really knew the material, and rarely messed up giving examples in class.  But he just doesn't empathize with the students and seems kind of condescending when you ask a question--like "Seriously?  Ziss is easy stuff, guys."  He didn't know what we struggled with, and I don't think he really cared.

Quite possibly the worst teacher I have ever had.  He does not teach at all what is on the assignments, he is almost incomprehensible most of the time, as well, when he is asked a question he becomes somewhat hostile, and acts almost apalled at the thought of a question.  Terrible teacher, Class Avg on test: D Class Avg Overall: C

Not the easiest class. However, he does a really good job of preparing you for his tests.  Great reviews.  Attendance is not mandatory, but definitely recommended.  I found that when I went to class, I understood the homework completely, and did really well on the class.

Avoid this guy at all cost. He is terrible. Very disorganized, and kinda mumbles too. He makes a lot of mistakes when explaining and doesnt care if you learn or not. He smokes a lot too which is gross if you are going to ask him for help in his office.
He doesnt curve but gives pretty helpful reviews before tests.
No Comments

At first the course seemed very difficult and I didn't like him, but as the course progressed I realized he was teaching the material well and always made sure we understood it.  Tests can be a little tough, though.  I'm probably going to come out with a C in that class but I know I could have done better had I put more effort into it.

She is extremely monotone which makes it really hard to pay attention to her lectures and she assigns about 150 pages to read every week which is ridiculous for a gen ed. I highly recommend not buying any of the books and just reading summaries on sparknotes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: very nice. great class. you can tell she cares about what she teaches.

This class can easily be done if you read sparknotes and all those other online sites. Many people complain about it, but it wasn't too difficult if you go to discussion and read online analyzed information. Antha can be quite boring, though, and she reads straight off her powerpoints. Most of the information is irrelevant.

Terrible teacher for a terrible class. Makes your midterm the day after fall break in a failed attempt to make her class seem important. Assigns 3 essays which is INSANE for a gen ed course that NONE of the students care about. Assigns between 100-150 pages a week to read to a class that once again, NO ONE cares about. Must buy at least 15 books.

She honestly is the most boring teacher ever. You have to attend class because she does not provide anything online and her slides do have information, but she is not engaging in any way and is extremely monotone. There is too much expected for this Gen Ed class and it was honestly painful to attend lecture.

She is always interested in what she teaches, and it shows in her lectures. But, she tends to be very monotonous and boring at times, as she rarely uses visual aids. She knows what she's doing and grades very fairly, but she can be tough. Reading-intensive. Overall, she's a great professor and you can learn a lot from her class

Antha teachers your lecture class and just provides the outline for your readings and then during your discussion you go over everything in detail.  She was a great teacher, a fair grader, and reminded me of my Grandma.  Take her class!

Mandatory class for mostly all majors.  Not as bad as what everyone else makes Western Civ out to be.  Could be Cotten-Sprekelmyer or the TA I had.  Overall as long as you read (or read Spark Notes) and prepare for discussion, the class is an easy B.  Could be an A if it wasn't for one low grade on a paper.
Very nice person. Not too harsh when it came to grading, but lectures could have been more interesting. Approachable person and overall a pretty good class.
Absolutely awful professor, clearly an intelligent human being but has great difficulty translating that into teaching material to her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her experience allows her to understand the do's and don'ts of being a professor.  She shows tact, gives respect, and guides the class with skill.

I took Psychology of Sleep and Dreaming. It was a difficult class, but Dr. A was there to help every step of the way. She is encouraging, understanding, and incredibly intelligent. I had some personal issues this semester and did not receive the grade I had hoped for. However, should this class be offered with Dr. A, I would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Atchley went off on tangents regularly & was not very helpful any of the times I spoke with her. She made participation an integral part of a research methods course, which felt unnecessary with the amount of time we spent covering material that had nothing to do with our class.

Professor Atchley is very intelligent and truly cares about her students. She is a great lecturer and explains concepts through examples of research either her or her husband has done. She gives a lot of homework! But she basically grades on completion (unless you royally screw up the assignment). Tests were reasonably difficult. Overall very good!

She's way too smart for her own good, and especially for yours. She goes off on many tangents in the short time you have in class. She is a good teacher and knows a lot about the field, but isn't good at intro level course teaching. Switch teachers if you can. Her grading is also stupid, if you miss 2 points you could be at an 86% for that section.

One of my favorite classes at KU so far. Dr. Atchley is a great teacher, especially for only meeting once a week. That being said, this class is quite a bit of work. We always did very helpful and engaging class activities. The exams are easy if you read the book, study vocab, and participate in class. Reading the book is 100% necessary.

I know intro level psych classes aren't supposed to be anything special, but I wasn't especially fond of this one... Dr. Atchley isn't a bad teacher but I don't think she should teach lecture classes. She tried valiantly to do a lot of class participation but it was awkward and not very helpful in the end. She takes attendance and hw is CRUCIAL.

She was probably the worst teacher I have ever had. She assigned homework due on a Saturday at midnight. She is full of herself, and treats her students like they're children, especially when giving instructions. I would fully recommend finding another professor if you are required to take this class.

Nice teacher! I took her general psychology class. She pushed everyone to study by themselves. I learned something which may benefit me lifetime. BUT, this class absolutely not an easy A. She took attendance EVERY time. Her exams are difficult but have some curves. Need to study 3-5 hours beyond the classroom weekly. Recommended!!!
She is very difficult and is definitely going to push you.

Awful teacher! Annoying, full of herself, ignorant to technological advances (including how to enter grades into a grade book, doesn't answer phone/emails, etc.) requires about 5 hrs on average of outside online homework each week. Writes unfair tests

Really cool class if you like learning about the brain and how different types of brain damage affect behavior. If not, then you won't like this class. Lectures are entertaining. Tests really hard, STUDY A LOT. GO TO CLASS.A ton of material is covered and needs to be memorized. The typical filled out study guide won't do; flashcards etc. are a must

Took Brain and Behavior from her and HATED THIS CLASS! The lectures were boring and waaaay too much specific information she expected you to memorize. I studied an enormous amount for her exams and still got a C. Pretty much impossible tests because they ask you so many specifics you can't remember them all. Also very arrogant.

i could not stand this woman.  she's not a bad teacher, but certainly not the most interesting, and in definite need of a good dose of humility.  she makes it seem like she is such a big shot brain researcher, and obviously i am not impressed.

She has a good sense of humor, which makes her class tolerable which is saying a lot.  The class by its subject matter is pretty dry, but it is somewhat interesting.  Easy to get credit for journals, but activity days are annoying.  Tests are hard, but if you do the study guide the tests are easy.

I will not take one of her classes ever again. Extremely arrogant (seems to be in the family), and incapable of admitting to mistakes. I learned nothing in the class. Tests are open book, open notes, but the tests do not always refer to your notes. Very poor writing abilities and grades entirely too hard on your writings.
I will never be caught in another one of her classes.  Activity days SUCK and she will accept NO excuses.  You better make sure Grams and Gramps are healthy before enrolling in her section.
I found her funny in class, she's pretty intense, and keeps the material interesting.
Loved her lecture, so interesting.  Test is not easy, but as long as you pay attention in class and study, you will be fine.
No Comments
No Comments
Not impossible but definatly not a blow off
Awesome lectures, tests were extremely hard though, go to class is the general consenus
This was a very interesting class that was informative.  The students took it very seriously as did Ruthann.  I strongly recommend this class and prof.

Journals are annoying and I dread activity days. Her lectures are a little boring. The tests are purely from her lecture notes, a lot of memorizing is required. But overall she's very enthusiastic about the subject.
Her lectures are interesting.  Some of her inclass assigments are annoying and there's a lot of memorization, but overall I liked the class.
No Comments

I've taken three classes from Professor Atkins. He is an excellent teacher and has helped me understand how studying English literature applies to life beyond the classroom. He is not an easy grader, but expectations are fair and grades must be earned. He is the best teacher I have ever had and has greatly impacted both my education and life.

I didn't like him at first, but over the semester the class grew to be one of my favorites. My writing improved in his class, so if that's your goal it will definitely happen. He's retiring at the end of this year so this review is basically worthless. He's got quite a few books published, so you can be sure he knows what he's talking about.

G. D. Atkins is simply one of kind. He's a teacher that you will rarely come across on any campus or around the country. He holds a high standard for every one of his students and holds a personal interest in every student. He will quickly become an inspirational figure. The class is difficult, though, and not for the novice English students.

G. Douglas Atkins is a wonderful professor, and a great guy. Take his class, sure, but also go to his office hours. Get to know the man behind the beard. It's worth it. Beneath the slow speech lies a subtlety of wit and insight unlike most other professors/people in general. Take English for your grades. Take Atkins for your mind.

Prof. Atkins was one of the best professors I had. Like others have said, he genuinely cares about his subject and his students. He expects you to forth a great deal of thought in your work, so do not slack off. Classmates and I joke about him being a mix between God and Stanta. Just take his class and see for yourself.

At first I didn't like Atkins, but by the third week into the semester, I really enjoyed going to his class. He gave us the option of choosing what we wanted to write about, and genuinely cared if we improved as writers. He had very insightful things to say about everything we read, and he encouraged discussion. G. Doug rocks. Take this calss!

He is a very difficult professor, but definitely worth your time. A large amount of effort is required for this class, but you will improve skills unlike some English classes that seem to reiterate everything you've already learned. He is sometimes hard to understand and very quirky (in a funny way). Genuinely interested in his students' writing!

Professor Atkins made this course an incredible experience. He doesn't just teach great works of literature; he genuinely cares about cultivating his students' intellects. While this class is not for those looking for a breezy 'A', it's an invaluable course for those willing to put in the time, effort, and thought necessary to succeed.

He is a truly terrible and manipulative teacher.  His positive reviews are from people who have played his game.  He only accepts his way of doing things and is completely uncaring about his students efforts.  He never gives back grades and is unwilling to give a clear outline of what he wants.
Great professor, very intellectual and willing to work to make students actually use their brains.

This was the best english class i've ever had.  The only problem I had with the course was that he didn't like it when you disagreed with him and anything that contradicted his opinions was wrong. He grades essays very throughly but the classroom discussions totally make the class. I never wanted to miss a class, i liked it so much.

I may not know much as a Freshman, but it seems like Prof. Atkins is the model college professor. Always prepared for class. While at times he was very vague on what he wanted for assignments, I believe it encouraged students to aspire to do great quality work. I can't recommend this professor enough. By far the best English teacher I've had.
Best English teacher I ever had.  He knew just the right amount to push students to help them produce the best possible paper!

I didn't realize that there still WERE professors who actually care enough about students to bring out their best work from them. I learned so much from this essay class. This man KNOWS what he is talking about. You must take this class!
A generally disappointing professor. He's a very nice man up front, but would regularly talk about other students' performances to other students, which is incredibly inappropriate.

He is interesting and witty but a TERRIBLE professor. He was never clear about the guidelines for assignments, and he was vague on his grading criteria. When asked specific questions about assignments or grades, he was evasive. I planned on using him as my thesis advisor, but changed my topic after having him for this class! I do not recommend him.

Dr. Atkins is, in short, the best professor I have ever had the pleasure of learning from. He is extremely demanding when it comes to quality of writing, but he helps you much more than most other professors. You find yourself wanting to live up to his expectations, and thus the quality of your work increases, too.
The man's amazing and a genius.  Great professor, I learned a lot from him and enjoyed his class.  He one time gave me a ride to my next class when it was icy and very cold outside.  A class act.
Need to write how he wants you to.

Very witty, very friendly man.  He never failed to encourage students, and made class more fun than I believed possible.  He was flexible according to students' interests and needs.  Every student was responsible for presenting part of the material, and for "workshopping" each others' essays.  I was never bored or confused.
No Comments

Love this man. Love his fountain pens too! If you hope to write, and write well, take a class from Douglas Atkins. You won't regret it. You'll work hard, and you'll love every minute of it. Just do it now!
No Comments

As others have mentioned, Dr. Atkins pushes you, and asks alot of you as a student, but his classes, and the understanding you gain from them are well worth the effort. Whats great about Atkins is he's willing to spend time with you out of class to help you understand if your struggling. Few teachers I found were ever as willing as Atkins, and even less shared his personally desire for students to actually learn.
Cares more about student progress and development than point totals.  A class act who cares about his students.
Pushes you hard, then congratulates you for excelling. Don't take his classes unless you're willing to work, think, and get things done neatly and on time.

He's a little quirky, and I suspect he pushes students a bit harder than they most are used to being pushed.  He's got his own ideas about things, and I disagree with plenty of them.  But I learned so much, and I enjoyed every moment of his class!  Highly recommended!
An amazing professor.  I wasn't interested in the subject before I took this class, and now he's directing my Honor's Thesis in it.
Best class I've had so far.
Atkins is a good teacher, though not always the most professional.
I love this man, and he loves his students.  Cares about their interest and investment.  He pushed me to excel and then blamed any sucess I had all on me. :)
hard!  but worth it
Extremely nice but very out of date.
Eccentric, but a very good professor
No Comments
Had him fall 02. He was a wonderful prof, and I'm taking him again because of that :-)
The hardest and the best.
There's TAs for this class so u won't see this prof until finals ngl. Class should be super easy j do notes and reviews. I got A and rarely went to class.

I'm better at math in comparison to other subjects, so this class was fairly easy for me. However, my peers who struggled in math were not fond of this professor. The days he was gone and our TA had to teach everyone was instantly in a good mood. I personally found many students agreed with me that he was difficult to understand sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes the head of the Kansas University math department hes very smart good pace and very nice
Will accept excuses for attendance and wants you to do well in the class. Very likable professor and I had a good time in this class. Weekly quizzes sucked.

Professor Indika is super nice and understanding. Super lenient on excusing attendance if you have a valid reason. Explains things well and will stop if you are confused. Easy to reach during the week. Has an accent but easy to understand.

Class work can be hard but if youre falling behind he will reach out and help you. Very nice and understanding, had a hard time with an exam and he helped me get the materials I needed to do better. Quiz every week but its nothing too bad.

I enjoyed the content of this class but students are required to develop an understanding of concepts by themselves. The lectures were 15-40 minutes long for 2 weeks worth of content and they were very surface level. The grade is made up of bi-weekly quizzes, 2 discussion posts, and a final. Not the class to take if you don't enjoy dense reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Avdan is a fine lecturer and I would have no issue w her class if it weren't for the insane structure. You get assigned 12-15 hours of reading every two weeks and then take 10 question quiz that is 5% of your final grade. You could do all the work and still screw it up by misunderstanding the phrasing of a question. AVOID.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is awesome, her powerpoints and lectures are informative and engaging. Also you only have a quiz every OTHER week. Theres like 3 discussion board posts and then the quizzes and a final. I learned so much and it wasnt that hard! Great prof to take for online

This class was very enjoyable. It requires a lot of reading but you are given two weeks to complete each Module. This class does not have a lot of homework. One assignment is due every two weeks (usually a 10 question multiple choice quiz). There is a 3 point extra credit assignment at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Clearly very knowledgeable about terrorism and immigration. Really good lectures.

Understood the material well, but missed one online quiz and it tanked my grade even though I got a B on the Midterm and Final. Discussion posts are engaging, but be sure to cite your sources and stay on topic because she grades pretty harshly if you try and relate it to something more current. Be careful about due dates and don't miss a quiz.

Professor Avdan is an underrated gem. She is extremely intelligent, knows a ton about her topic specialty (this isn't some random PhD, who just happened to pass a dissertation), and is going to go far in her field. Not only is she informative and engaging in her lectures, she is similarly available and caring outside of class time. A real teacher!

God bless Avary Kolasinki! Choosing Avary's section was THE best decision. She simplifies everything down so well that is almost impossible to not understand (and I suck at math). I've taken other classes led my GTAs before, all of which sucked and did not truly care how they're students did, but not Avary! Absolute goat.

I went into Calculus thinking it was going to be my hardest class but Avary made it so fun and so easy to understand.  I really couldn't have survived without her as a GTA. You could tell she really cared about our learning unlike a lot of other GTA's I have had. Really the best GTA I have had so far in college.

Avary was a really good TA for Calculus II. Our professor made a lot of the material extremely confusing, but she clarified everything really well. She also prepared us well for exams with lots of example problems.

Avary is probably the best GTA you will have for a math lab. She's really funny and explains the material well (better than the professor for this class). She gives very easy extra credit questions on the quizzes and is lenient on deadlines. 5+/5
Hilarious TA, the discussion is basically show up and you will get all of the points. Will share stories and class will not run the usual 50min
Pretty Chill TA. He thinks he's Alex Trebek and the class just went along with it. Unrelated: Also is beard is pretty rad.
Incredible TA, even more incredible beard. 10/10
Honestly a chill class, consists of lots of guest speakers and the coursework is very easy.
Very passionate about his teaching, about his students, and his job overall. Very solid professor for any student looking to learn more about sports.

Dr. Bogina is a great teacher but everything is strictly lecture for intro. So many guest speakers that are helpful most of the time but other times they suck. Bogina is great if you go to his office hours and he's really personable and helpful. Class is super boring but you will def learn more about sports. DO NOT TAKE IF NOT SPORT MANAGEMENT!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bogina was great for an intro class and offers great resources for working in sports and connecting you with professionals.

Hands down the best professor that I have ever had at KU. Dr. Bogina goes above and beyond to help his students succeed and cares about each one. Building a relationship with Dr. Bogina helped me accomplish many goals. His teaching practices are as straightforward as can be as long as you show up to class and take notes, you'll be able to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Bogina is the best professor I've had at KU. I've had him in 3 classes, each of which I loved. He does an excellent job presenting information and assigning projects that are interesting and insightful. He takes the time to know and understand his students. Office hours always open. If you seek to elevate learning I highly recommend Dr.Bogina.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Extreamly disapoitning. I received a B in his class becasue I left class 10 minutes early for a job interview (that he incouraged me to get). When I told him I was leaving for my interview, he was very rude and proceeded to bring up the missed class the rest of the semester. He is a certified narcissist and loves hearing the toot of his horn.
Dr Bogina was really amazing for a intro class and provided us with interesting speakers while also keeping a good balance of interesting lectures.

Very chill class, honestly did not need to take notes. I honestly only learned things in the very first week, he gets lots of guest speakers, yet does not teach any new or extremely valuable information (to be fair it is an intro class).

Dr. Bogina is the real deal. He is easily one of my favorite professors I've ever had. He is wise but young and loves to share advice and life lessons with his students. He knew my name even though I didn't participate all that much in class. He truly wants to see you succeed and will go out of his way to help you out.

I took Career Development at USF Tampa as a sophomore and recommend this to every psych major! Try to take this course as early on into college as possible He provides you with resources about everything psychology from finding a career that suits you to how to build a resume, find internships,research experience etc Also an easy A if you do the hw

This Career Development in Psychology class (at USF though not Kansas) was extremely beneficial in the development of my career plan. I would recommend this class to anyone pursuing a psychology related career, even if you think you have all your plans made. Classwork was pretty easy and the professor was helpful whenever I had Qs or concerns.
Awful at communicating. Class is mandatory and an utter waste of time. Did all the assignments and somehow STILL got a U. No idea who he thinks he is.

He literally uses his students as a guinea pig experiment for some tests. He is arrogant and will go on and on about his research. Also, he's more quick to believe you are trying to cheat your way through class than actually need help for it and try to improve your grade. If I didn't have to take this course, I wouldn't have.

Was not clear on his expectations; provided only very vague grading rubrics, which he then changed without notice. Did not cover important information that's was on the exams. Would not answer our questions. Most difficult class I have taken thus far.

Took PSYC 102 and completed all of the assignments on time, meeting all the assignment requirements, and somehow got a "U" (unsatisfactory). I spent more time on this 1 credit hour class than my 300 level courses (which I got A's and B's in). This course is a complete waste of time, but required for a psyc major. Cannot stand this man.

Giving him a review now because I found out he used our class last spring as a study w/o informing us. Made us do fill in the blank based on pure memorization while other classes were given multiple choice or multiple choice plus short answers. The test format stressed me out all semester, and I was lucky to make an A (curved test). Unprofessional.
Overall I enjoyed this class. Make sure you keep up with the online assignments  and homework. He makes it clear what is expected of you. Put in the effort and you will do well.

Useful class; I learned a lot. But Dr. Atchley tends to digress in lectures when he should focus on course material. The course is NOT easy. Not my favorite professor at KU by far. The midterm and the final were fill in the blank; therefore, you need to really know the course material to get an A, but it is achievable if you study hard.
Required class for the major. Paul does everything he can to make it interesting. He does lots of activities in class so good idea to go!

Incredible professor, truly cares about what he's doing and whether or not you're learning the material.  The work was a little tedious, but I really feel like I *learned* something, which is hard to say of other classes.

Came into the class not thinking that I would like research methods at all. First day i thought he was going to be horrible, he ended up being super helpful. If you just do the stuff online (which isnt hard) you get a good grade! he has an awesome grading system that doesnt rely on two tests a semester like many other teachers! I would suggest him

Small lecture, ~100 people. Thought I was going to hate it. Atchley/this class changed my mind about staying in psychology. I really loved the class and everything was very direct and straightforward. He doesn't "compete" with you to get a good grade. Very interesting and funny. Remember to do your online HW! I hope to take another class w/ him.

Honesty, I thought that this class was going to be awful and that he was going to be a jerk.  I was very surprised to discover that both he and the class weren't all that bad!  We had some interesting discussions in class and it somehow became one of my favorite classes of the semester. Not too hard, lots of online assignments.

This class kind of sucked. The information was somewhat interesting and useful at first but soon became mundane. You need to keep up with the online homework and quizzes or else you can easily screw yourself out of a good grade. Overall an "eh" class.

Worst teacher in my college career. Material's super easy - being around him isn't. So pretentious and egomaniacal. Says every day how his class is the most important & difficult you will ever take (it's not). Relates every lesson back to his research on cell phones & driving (we get it, they're distracting). A truly painful, worthless experience.

He is a really nice guy, very entertaining. My class always had great discussions in his lectures and I actually enjoyed going to class even though I expected to hate a class about conducting research.

Unnecessary and tedious. I never read the e-pages, I just took the quizzes over a few times till the answers were right. About 6 Quizzes & 10 journals. Basically the course is online, he talks about all of the resources KU has to offer, and wants you to make goal plans and discuss your interest in PSYC. Easy A---just long and boring as Heck.

Professor Atchly is a very unique man. He has a gift for teaching his students how to apply knowledge in a way that they get the maximum benefit from the knowledge. He teaches in a conceptual world that requires the student to invest in the learning process in order to grasp the information. You MUST rise to that level. He also loves his students.

Professor Atchley is a wonderful teacher, that you have to invest yourself in to get the most from him.  He is very gifted and knowledgable, and loves his students.  Its a knowledge however that you have to work to understand because its more conceptual than informative.  He teaches you how to apply information to get the maximum results from it.

You have to go & the tests are in his own words "the hardest of your undergrad" BUT I actually learned the material,that is why they are hard;they test what you know not just what you "scanned" an hour prior.I took this course 2yrs ago & still regularly use what I learned.He is extremely helpful & full of useful info!Engaging lecturer & great prof!

I took this class online. It was a lot of work, but it was an easy A if assignments are completed. Test questions come directly from the book. I recommend this class because not only did I get an A, but I learned so much about research methods.

As a precursor, I took this class online. Expectations and grading are clear and unambiguous. VERY good at responding to emails. All homework and papers are graded on completion, and quizzes and TESTS can be retaken. The course material was not hard, either. The only limit to getting the grade you want is your motivation. Not a difficult A for me.
You cant skip class if you want a good grade.  ten homework assignments, three reports, and two tests.
Approachable and readily answers questions

He IS arrogant. The homework is busy work which I think we all grew out of before we came to college. The only reason coming to class is helpful is because he doesn't have a class schedule and you have to find out when assignments are due. The substance of the discussion is underwhelming and his expectations are not at all clear. Good luck.

I really liked Professor Atchley.  He's a funny guy.  Sometimes lectures were a bit dull and the homework assignments were tedious at times, but you do learn a lot. The final was a lot easier than the midterm.  An A is pretty easy to attain, just don't blow off the assignments, reports or quizzes!!!

He understands quite clearly that college classes ought to require some work. He rewards the effort for the work. 10 assignments, 3 reports total assigned. 3 reports and 8 assignments (1 of these 11 can be turned in late) have to be done, graded on completion, to get the A. How is this hard to understand or do?

The guy is brilliant.  I always felt like when he lectured, he was amused at how much he had to dumb things down so that we can follow his point.  He is a true believer, though, and will try his level best to get you through the class.

loved loved loved loved professor atchley. best class i have taken so far hands down. lectures are interesting. homework assignments are completion. midterm and final are not that hard. can be easily prepared for. did a unit on what you can do with a psyc degree. most ive learned in any class ever

The tests are fairly brutal.  With that said, one only needs to get an 80% on them (including the easy blackboard quizes) to get an A.  Professor Atchley is funny, his teaching style is clear, and I'd gladly take another class from him.  Just turn your cell phone off, unlike the girl below who apparently wasn't smart enough to do figure that out.

This class was somewhat difficult; but he takes that into account when figuring your grade. All tests are curved, homework is pass/ fail. Easy B without much studying. He is funny and brought his dog to class! His sense of humor might be taken by some as arrogance.Go to class, do the homework and you will be fine!
This guy is so rude and arrogant. If you email him he never gets back to you, and when you come to his office he treats you like an idiot. Hates cell phones!

Professor Atchley is awesome. You will need to put forth effort to do well in this class, but that is to be expected if you're going to college.  Atchley is funny, entertaining, skilled at listening, explaining, and coming up with great examples to apply your learning.  Go to class, take notes, do the homework, study for tests.  You'll be fine.

His class is set up to be difficult, but he knows that and grades for it.  Tests are ambiguous but they are for everyone so he curves it, and he lowers the grade needed for a A. reviews.comment: Dr. Lamb is an excellent teacher who has lectures that are entertaining and easy to follow.  The tests require a lot of studying but are straightforward and not meant to trick you.

PS Never give up.
taking Biochem I with her was the best thing I did as an undergrad.  not an easy class, but you will learn the foundations very well.

Barney Warf is one of the greatest professors I've ever had. I loved him so much in class that I even started going to geography events outside of class to meet with him. He's humorous, loves what he teaches, and lectures it effectively. The grade I received was what I deserved because of my low attendance. It's very test heavy.

Professor Warf was great. I was a little nervous at the start of the year, as the first few classes caught me off guard and made him seem a lot tougher than he was. Very nice guy who is very fun to banter with, he'll say some of the funniest out of pocket stuff during lectures. Go to class and take good notes and you'll be fine.

Professor Warf is clearly one of the most knowledgable and respected professors at the university. Very few assignments: tests, quizzes, and attendance make up 88% of your grade. Engaging and entertaining lectures. Take if you can.

Barney is a guy who knows what he is talking about. His colorful octopus button up shirts and his old man rumbles give emotion to a course which covers a lot of topics. There were few assignments, and you can find the quizzes questions and answers on Quizlet. Overall, a really cool professor.

awesome
