This class is boring, but Warf is very knowledgeable and knows what he's talking about. The tests are HARD. No multiple choice, only short answers and fill in the blanks. Long study guides, have to memorize over 100 questions with long answers. Thought it would be an easy class, definitely not.

This class could be boring, but Dr. Warf makes it entertaining. He's very passionate about what he believes in and he's not afraid to share his thoughts. Tests are a combination of textbook and lecture questions he posts online. Tests are all fill-in and short answer that need tons of memorization. His class is a real eye-opener. Good 4.2 choice.

I can honestly say that I learned a lot more from this class than I had anticipated going into it. However, if you are looking for an easy 100 level course to meet requirements this isn't it. I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone who is planning to be, or is already in, a major with classes that require a lot of studying. It's a lot of material
Great teacher! Very very intelligent! Would recommend to anyone!

Grades are based on 2 midterms and 1 final. The lectures are boring and you take an insane amount of notes. He does give study guide which if you know it (all 120 questions) you can get an AB on the exams. Its A LOT of memorization but if your good at that you would do okay. I don't recommend though especially as a 100 level class.

Warf is THE best professor I've ever had. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you want a good grade, you need to go to class. Powerpoints during lecture tell you exactly what to write down; he gives study guides before tests and ample extra credit. Oh yeah, he's also hilarious and very entertaining.
i like his class best.his speech is very clear.

Great teacher, knows his subject very well. His lectures are very engaging, it's worth coming to class just to learn. Textbook is used a bit, but the tests mainly draw from lectures. Just go to class every day and take good notes and you will be fine. His liberal bias shows in his lectures a bit, but very educational nonetheless.

Devoted to his field, very passionate. This guy has a very dry and hidden sense of humor sometimes that gets missed by most of the class. It is hard to pay attention sometimes, but show up to class and he'll go over almost everything you need. He's a really nice guy even though the first couple of days make him seem like a nazi. He's not.

Professor Warf is a great professor and easy class as long as you attend and take good notes. He is a funny man and keeps class interesting! He is very helpful when you need to go in for office hours. I would recommend him any day!

Dr. Warf is by far the smartest man I have ever met. He encases you in knowledge and intrigue, releasing his intellectual grasp exactly 13 seconds after the class has ended. And if you my dilligent reader have an IQ above 120, and care about anything besides your IPOD and where your going to kill brain cells this weekend, you will learn everything.

Course only had 3 tests, no other grades whatsoever.  The tests are difficult if you do not attend every lecture, reading the book is a must.  Tests are 70% Lecture 30% readings.  This guy is very animated, captivates audience.

I hated this class personally.  He is so biased and inaccurate at times that it takes a lot of fun out of the class.  He thinks he's funny, when he's not.  Oh, and he likes to show off for sorority girls.  On the other hand if you do the extra credit, it's an easy A.  Otherwise you'll fail.
No Comments

I loved Betsy so much when I took her last semester. I had her for BDS101 and was very helpful when needing feedback. Sometimes she wasn't sure what was going on which was a little frustrating however she made up for it by offering lenience on all of the projects. As long as you come to class and get your work done you will love the class.

Betsy is an amazing professor and really cares about her students. Her feedback is the best at KU. If you are sad about your work and need help, she is able to inspire you with truthful feedback that actually helps and gets you excited about fixing the problem. She works with you if you are struggling, but not to the point you're able to slack.
I learned more in this class than in any other. Her expectations are extremely high, but are based off of expectations in industry. I've never worked harder in a studio, but I got a lot out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Will is a nice guy. But the semester I took this class there was two teachers. Wills class was graded by 2 exams which are very difficult. The other teacher had many different grades with all quizzes and exams being open note. When you look at the grading criteria of other teachers I don't see why anyone would take this class with Will.

Wills talks very fast and at times is hard to follow. He does do a decent amount of practice problems in class. He is helpful outside of class if you meet with him. The only real downside to taking the class with him is that you are basically graded on two exams and the final. Other teachers for this course have an easier grading scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Talks the entire class. You don't have to show up but will be lost if you don't. Go to the exam reviews, he will go over everything for the final. honestly one of my favorite professors at KU. Really willing to have meetings one on one to help you understand what you are missing
Very hard to understand and very quiet

This was the most absurb class I have taken so far. No clear grading criteria, Very slow grader. It has been 3 months since I submitted my first paper and still have not got my scores back. Very bad at giving lecture. I would suggest take this class with any other professor and if you already in there just drop it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Her teaching style works really well for me, though she is not always clear. The other reviews actually kind of surprised me -- my grade in her class is one of the higher ones I've gotten since middle school. Low pressure course which involves a lot of interesting discussion.

Avoid this class at all costs. Ayah does not provide a clear rubric for any of her papers or the final exam. She expects a lot but does not explain what she expects. She takes a long time to grade and often has few comments. On one of my papers, she copied and pasted comments from someone else's paper and even forgot to remove their name.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ayah is by far the best professor I have had while attending KU. She is compassionate, understanding, and willing to meet you in the middle. She genuinely cares about her students and the curriculum. She is an amazing woman and professor, of whom I recommend strongly.
One of the hardest class I have ever taken. If you can, transfer out. You can try your best and pour hours into papers but still, receive a C on your work. She changes due dates every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She is an amazing teacher and she loves her class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: TRANSFER OUT. She is much harder than any other ENGL102 teacher. Her rubrics are super vague and yet she expects a specific end result. It's truly a nightmare. Not a single person in my class felt they learned anything and were put through many hoops for no end result.

This class was tough and confusing. Ayah is not clear with what she is asking for in assignments and she grades very tough, so it is hard to do well in this class. Students never know what to incorporate in their essays because she never explains  it. Avoid this teacher if you can.

This was probably the easiest English class I've ever taken, yet my lowest English grade. I've never done this bad in an English class. Her grading is pretty harsh and she expects a lot for a one hundred level class. She's also new to teaching in the US and doesn't seem to know how the American classroom works. She would often ask us how things go.

reviews.comment: Hardest essays of any 102 class

reviews.comment: I love English, it has always been my favorite class. This class is hell. That means a lot coming from me.

Terrible professor. The pop quizzes were so specific that no matter how much you read or understand the text, good luck passing the quiz. I asked for help on multiple occasions and she simply did not give me any. I lost all passion for the course material because of how unlikeable her lectures and sporadic quizzes were. I don't recommend her class.

reviews.comment: No passes on missing a pop quiz, even if you have a suspected/confirmed COVID case. Youll still get a zero.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Hardison will make you work for your grade, but she's also fair. She knows different students' limits and grades accordingly. It helps to go to her office hours. She's incredibly helpful and insightful. She's also really good at being there for her students. I was going through health problems, but she was very understanding and accommodating.

I took Freshman Honors English with Professor Hardison. I didn't particularly care for the class and would have appreciated more variety in the books we read, but she was not a bad teacher. She was also a fair paper grader, which is always hit-or-miss with teachers.

A lot of readings, but such an interesting class! It is discussion-based, but Professor Mizumura provides many materials to reference and guides the discussions well. She has well-defined expectations and really wants her students to succeed. Overall, I loved her and her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This teacher assigns a lot of work, but at the end of the semester you definitely will have learned the material.  She's passionate about her classes and really cares about her students. If you're struggling, just ask her for help and she will do everything in her power to help you. I love Mizumura.

She was my lab instructor for JPN 208. She's a wonderful teacher and will always take the time to help you. She speaks very, very fast Japanese so you have to listen carefully and adapt to that. Practice the dialogues well before class and prepare for the oral exams, because they can get difficult!

She is nice and cares a lot about the subject matter. Attendance is mandatory as many of the points come from in-class assignments (videos, etc.) Tests aren't very hard and the final is a group presentation and individual paper. If you go to class it isn't difficult to get an A

The class and teacher that helped me decide my major. A very frustrating class at times, and, not to sound cliche, the one that opened my eyes to the world. I felt very supported in all discussions and LOVED the anthropology textbook. The only negative is the difficulty of the assignments, however, she will give you the grade you deserve

Professor Saraswati is the best I've had so far.  She's so passionate about her subject and incredibly open-minded. Her class is mostly discussion, so reading is a must, but it is almost always enlightening.  There were no tests, just fun projects. I would definitely reccommend her to anyone interested in womens studies!

It is a must that you attend class. She takes attendance everyday and you have to participate, its 20 percent of your grade. Then there are a few projects. EASY! She is fun at first but then becoming annoying. But this is the 2nd class I'm taking with her because its an easy A. I have never got below at 98 percent on anything! Finished with a 103%!

Professor Ayu is awesome, fun, and the discussions where the best part about the course.  She always knew how to keep the class interesting and she knows her material.  She does ask a little too much for the projects but if you meet with her then you will get a good grade.  Overall, do your reading & be involved in the course & you will get an A.

Saraswati's a fine addition to the WS program.  She clearly knows a ton about gender issues and articulates complex ideas with ease and clarity.  Keeps her material very current and interesting - we listened to music, watched youtube and other videos.  Discussions are fantastic and lectures are well laid out.  Final project is hard but creative.

The exams are very straightforward if you study the material & watch the review sessions. Attendance points WILL pile up & matter. The way she teaches helps with actually learning & understanding how the material applies irl instead of just more things to temporarily memorize. Very approachable & understanding

I love her halftime shows though where she blabbers on about random science that has nothing to do with the class for 20 out of 50 minutes and then complains that people don't come to class. Joke of a professor.

Took her Cell Bio lab online. The grading criteria/expectations were not very clear for lab reports until after you got your grade back--at that point, it's a bit too late. Regardless, the class was pretty easy, but miss more than one class and you automatically fail the course. She is very kind and willing to meet to discuss anything.

reviews.comment: WORST PROF EVER. I had Azuma in the fall, and had such a terrible experience with her. Everything that others have said applies to my experience as well. She was so difficult to please and grading criteria was so unclear. I had no idea what was expected of me - I usually get A's in every class, and this one I worked so hard just to get the B
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Azuma's exams are the most difficult exams Ive ever taken. If you think you've adequately answered her short answer questions you have not. If you think youve fully explained EVERY ASPECT of the answer you HAVE NOT. Azuma will always find something you did not do right, and you will miss a ton of points because of it. Grading criteria VERY UNCLEAR.

Mizuki seems like a nice person but after taking her class in the fall it's pretty clear to me that she really doesn't care about your GPA at all. If you take her class, make sure to go to office hours and present a VERY STRONG argument to get points back on exams, or you won't get an A. Or take a different professor - best choice if it's an option

The grade is composed only of exams, and 50% of those are short answer where she's looking for specific keywords. Then, it turns into a debate to get points back that you should have gotten in the first place. If you can take this class with ANY OTHER PROF even at Edwards, spend that extra campus fee. I promise it's worth it to avoid the WORST PROF
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The grade's entirely test-based, and 50% of that is short answers that she grades on the presence of "keywords," so most of us failed that section each test. She does let you try to earn points back if you talk to her during office hours though. Study the practice tests and attend the review session/look at the review slides before taking the test
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Online during COVID-19 restrictions. Dr. Azuma is a very kind and caring professor. Her lectures are helpful and, for the most part, everything you need to know is in her lectures. The entire grade was made up of tests; 50% of each test grade were essay questions with unclear grading criteria. Meet with her and she will give you points back!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is very nice but her essay questions answers are super specific and she counts off a lot even if you explain the concept. It's essentially required that you talk to her after the exam to get points back on the short answer in order to get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Exams scores are your only grades. Know the slides front to back and you'll do fine. Dr. Azuma is very friendly; she'll allow you to get a few points back on exams if you go to her office hours. I strongly recommend doing this after EVERY exam. I only did test corrections for one exam and I payed for it by getting an A- instead of an A.
Dr. Azuma is so cute and lovely!!! She is very intelligent but respectful. I definitely recommend her.

Nice lady. Hard exams. You will not only need to go to lecture and memorize her slides but you will need to memorize them exactly as written because she asks fill-in-the-blank questions where she wants you to state exactly what she's listed in her slides. They're collectively worth 15% of each exam. TOUGH GRADER, for sure.

Dr. Azuma is nice. Her exams are not. Essentially, all the multiple choice options are the same, with either the order or the word changed. This approach sharply penalizes students for understanding the material, and the only way to do well is to rote memorize the slides provided, bearing no mind to what is being memorized. You'll see what I mean.

Dr. Azuma is very nice and helpful. Her classes are pretty easy to understand. She basically summarizes the book so you don't have to struggle trying to remember unimportant things. As long as you read at least 2 or 3 times her slides, you can get an A.
He was hard as he'll but really wants to help and see students succeed

she is very nice. 5 tests you get to drop one. her english is not very good, spelling isn't either. if you listen in class she is very good at explaining the concepts and how things work. Much more interesting than kelly.Funny Cute. We get to take breaks and tells us interesting things happening in science and new technology and stuff. Pretty cool
Mizuki is the nicest professor I have ever met!  She is so willing to help you out, and really cares about your education and wants you to do well in the class!

He made us write so many notes for the entire period, just so we could throw them away at the end of the day. he wasted my time. He was also very confusing with his grading system and didn't offer many opportunities for points.
Brian teaches what you want to know and is relevant to theory AND real situations. He is human and genuine in his interactions.
okay
If you have class with him?.switch instructors!!  He is rude and confusing.  Study guides don?t help and he awkwardly words his tests.  He is all over the place.
Thinks way toooo much of himself.  Really disorganized and confusing.

Overall a good class to take. Brian was a little hard to understand in the beginning but only because he has so many thoughts and has much knowledge of this subject. We didn't use a book for experiamental purposes but I think having one on the side might have made things a little more clear. All in all it was a good class with a good subject matter

Great teacher.  Took this course in the summer so it was very face paced and reading intensive, but Brian was always willing to help clarify any questions over reading.  He scheduled several study groups for exams and discussed all reading in class.  Attendance is a priority if you are going to pass this class.

He is great!  I was in the night class too and have taken lots of night class and sometimes they can be really long.  He did a good job of breaking it up with activities and video clips.  As long as you went to lecture and did the study guides the tests were easy.  He gave lots of good examples and funny stories to help understand the text.
Took as a night class - he kept everyone involved and engaged, great sense of humor and great lectures.  Reviews for the exams are very helpful.  Great teacher!!
Every day I prayed to god that I would crash my car so I would not have to hear this man talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Professor Sherwood for graduate courses for the MBA and MS BSAN, do your work, ask questions, attend office hours, and you will learn skills that will serve you the rest of your career and life. Highly recommend Ben.

He is very condescending and rude when teaching and chatting. He also called multiple students by the wrong name. Make sure to put everything in your reports. Noticed something in the data? include it. Not sure if you need a boxplot? You do. Did you do your assignment with your cat on your lap? include it. Otherwise he will dock you a letter grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Vomit= his teaching skills
Ben Sherwood is a true gem at KU.

My least favorite class EVER. I was so upset after this because I tried so hard and the transitioning to online did not help. This was my first programming class and he acted like we were supposed to know everything already so I was behind there. He is super smart and goes super fast in class. This class made me feel like I didn't deserve my major.

reviews.comment: Hes pretty condescending. The class is pretty hard and he seems to enjoy that aspect of it. Its not worth taking for an elective because all the other classes are way easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ben is one of the few professors who REALLY knows what he teaches and REALLY knows how to teach. I enjoyed his lectures a lot. The homeworks were a bit hard, but you can always go to his office hours and ask questions. The tests were not that hard at all.
Professor Sherwood is intelligent and helpful. He seems to want his students to really understand the material. Pay attention and put in the effort and you should get a good grade.
Prof. Sherwood loves to make fun of students and not in a funny way. Homework is extremely difficult and the lecture helps only marginally. Would avoid this class if possible.

Mr. Sherwood was not only the funniest professor I have ever had, but very intelligent. If you took 202 with Mark Haug then you should be fine in 415. 415 is pretty much into to stats. Sherwood walks you through/ gives you all the code you need to complete assignments. It can be confusing from time to time, but go to office hours when possible.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He basically just reads from the slides during class. Be prepared to go to office hours because the homework is difficult and takes hours to complete. He also expects you to have an understanding of RStudio.

reviews.comment: grades very difficult and specific. rude. doesn't offer extra credit

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This is an interesting class so far and I appreciate Dr. Roselyn's policies on late work, but do *not* take this class unless you are absolutely sure you can handle the work load. It is a *lot,* and Dr. Roselyn has a lot of specifications for the work you'll be turning in. They are kind and communicative, will admit errors-- just be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Roselyn was incredibly caring and understanding. You have to be proactive and organized in the class, but they were more than willing to work with you and seem to genuinely care about their students. I would recommend!

As a person I really enjoyed Dr Roselyn, I just found their course difficult. They were very kind and understanding and easy to access outside of class, but the readings were a lot and the quizzes you take over them are difficult. I like them as a person a lot, though. This course is an easy way to cover some core requirements.

Very difficult course.  HEAVY readings. Assigns inappropriate and confusing articles and readings from a textbook that are not accurate of what is going on in the real world. Would NOT recommend this course or professor to anyone. I don't know how I even passed, she is A TOUGH grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took their class asynchronous online. Each week you read some pieces, take a 10 question multiple choice quiz (I think you get two tries), and write on a discussion board. Also a research paper 5-7 pgs. Good fascinating material. Only real feedback or interaction w/ prof was comments like "Excellent" or "good job" and one office meeting. Seems nice

Beth is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. I took this class to fill a core credit but ending up learning SO much and it led me to take more gender studies classes. The class was heavy on group discussion boards, but the readings were actually very interesting(BTW I am not a reader) and easy to engage yourself in
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Amazing professor that you WANT to have. this professor is highly respected and is highly knowledgeable in his field of work. He's a great person to have in your corner if you need recommendation letters and a great teacher overall.

This class provides an excellent opportunity to explore global cultures through the medium of film. ANTH 301 was engaging, thought-provoking, and fun. Weekly quizzes and short writing keep you on track in the on-line format with insightful lectures, readings, and powerful ethnographic cinema.

Professor Dean's ANTH301 class is an immersive journey through film. The visual medium and thought-provoking assignments expand my cultural understanding. unstuck study has been a helpful study tool alongside the lectures and films.
ANTH 501 is a must-take for anyone interested in the anthropology of revolutions, and Prof. Dean's dedication and knowledge made it a standout course.

In our class, we dove deep into the history and cultural aspects of genocide and ethnocide, looking at examples from around the globe through an anthropological lens. You've got to show up for discussions and submit a final term paper with a bibliography. I recommend this class, especially with all the mass violence happening these days.

Learned so much in Anth 160 about all these different cultures from around the world, and it's crazy how they all have their own unique stuff going on. It really makes you appreciate the beauty of diversity and how it matters right here in the USA.

Using movies as a study medium, ANTH 301 provides a visual and immersive learning environment beyond conventional text-based instruction. Written tasks to evaluate the movies we watched weekly tests, quick reads, and recorded PowerPoint lectures. I was introduced to various cultural viewpoints, thought-provoking ideas, and ways of seeing the world.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof.  Dean organized the course by film genres and themes, including documentaries, impressionistic, and observational films. His passion for anthropology was evident in his teaching, and I appreciated his feedback and the opportunity to interact with him during office hours via Zoom. I am excited to take more courses with him in person!

The class provides a great opportunity to examine diverse cultures and perspectives using the medium of film, which I find both enjoyable and intellectually stimulating. The course involves completing brief written assignments and a weekly quiz (8 in total) based on PW lectures, short readings, and fascinating Ethnographic films.

I am having a blast in Prof. Dean's Anthropology Through Film class. It's like watching Netflix but with a twist. I get to see how different people live and think worldwide and how movies can tell their stories and struggles. It is cool to compare and contrast films from various places and styles.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a nontraditional student, this is my 4th online course, which I greatly enjoy. It is by far the best one I've taken at KU. Thanks to ANTH 301, I have entered the serious study of the production of ethnographic films to document and represent human cultures and behaviors. Needless to say, it's given me a new way of seeing the media-filled world.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took an online class with Prof. Dean, and was pretty disappointed. I barely got any feedback on the weekly papers we had to write, and when I did, it was one or two words. I felt like I was going in blind every week. Also, the online formatting for the class was pretty poor. I'm sure he's a great prof in person, but don't do an online class w him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am really enjoying the online Anthropology of Film class. It covers new issues and ways of thinking. I like the way the course is designed. This is my first film and anthropology class, and I love the topics we are covering. It makes me "view" the world in a new way. I'm now thinking of adding anthropology as a minor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The history and cultural dynamics of genocide and ethnocide are clearly presented in the course. We analyzed cases from all across the world from an anthropological perspective. One must participate in class sessions and turn in a final term paper and bibliography. The class is highly recommended especially in today's world of mass violence.
Peoples and the Rainforest was a great introduction to the study of Amazonia. Worthwhile course taught by expert on the topic.

Anthropology of Ethnocide and Genocide was a great course that challenged many of my preconceptions about humanity. Having finished a final paper I am really proud of, I have direction for my Honors thesis.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took Anth of Geno/Ethnocide. Graded on participation and a final paper (+ paper presentation + annotated biblio, free points). Class routine was informal discussion over a reading, sometimes submitting a note card with thoughts. No hard deadlines. No grade except final grade. Probably easy class if you don't skip *too* much. Interesting content

Even though this course covered a depressing topic, I am glad I took it. I had no idea that people could be so vicious to one another. We addressed the likelihood of atonement while covering situations from around the globe. I heartily advise enrolling in this course with Dr. BART.
A great introduction to the people living in the Amazon. Wonderful lectures, films, and readings were engaging. The final project is a research paper on a class topic. Highly recommended.

Excellent course on a very gloomy subject. Professor Dean gives informative lectures and constantly promotes student involvement. Both attendance and the final paper are significant factors in the grade.
Great class. We learned the basics of anthropology and why is useful in the globalizing world. I have added it as a minor.
I took ANTH online in the winter and enjoyed the material and structure of the class. With consistent work, I did well in a course that challenged my way of thinking about the importance of culture.

I cannot even judge Dr. Dean as a lecturer since he never even lectured for the class.  I took this as a winter class, and he just sets up the class where you do discussion boards, weekly papers, and chapter questions over a textbook he wrote.  The syllabus has no grading criteria and his feedback is vague.  He is very lenient so that is a plus.

Passionate about the subject, Prof. Dean was always prepared, knowing the material & how to communicate it in a sensible way. Thank you very much for the course. I enjoyed every minute of Bart Dean's class lectures & his marvelous sense of humor, which made the study of violence more tolerable.

Classes with Bart Dean have been so worthwhile! Bart has an amazing way of breaking complex things down so that they are understandable, and always keeping it light and fun--even in a course dedicated to the study of violence.
I love this course. We have earned to evaluate, analyze, and in some cases, change our thoughts, beliefs, and emotions about challenging situations in the Amazon.
Well worth taking. I knew little about Anthropology and I have now changed my academic path thanks to this eye-opening class.
Prof. Dean has challenged the way I have imagined the Amazon. His lectures are awesome and he always encourages class participation. Well worth attending class.

I took ANTH 160 over winter break, so it was super condensed. Lots of reading, practically read the textbook cover to cover, but it was really interesting material. Professor Dean didn't really communicate with us, didn't respond to emails, and took a long time to grade things. But it wasn't really a hard class, just do the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Dean never responded to any of my emails throughout this short course. He would randomly grade assignments weeks after I submitted them but ignore any class questions I had so I had to resort to posting discussion boards about my problems. It wasnt too hard to get an A, but the lack of direction and response was completely unprofessional

We didn't get a comprehensive syllabus until 3/4 of the way through the semester. Instructions on assignments were never clear, we wasted money on textbooks written by Dean which we never used. The TAs were the only saving grace. Absolutely easy A+ class, but F- for mental health and wellbeing.
Do NOT take this class during the pandemic. He is not a good professor electronically. just don't do it

I hated this class. Extremely disorganized. Expects us to buy 3 books and pay to peer grade eachothers hw. They don't specify that we need the online textbook to turn in hw online, so many ppl are stuck having to buy it twice since they already bought the hard copy. He talks over everyone and shows little respect.

He talks over everyone who talks to him, has been very unclear of the expectations with the class and grades. He doesn't have a schedule for the semester and chooses to email out the week's instructions on a week-by-week basis. He also cannot use zoom well and struggles to get lectures going, taking usually almost 10 min to share his screen.

His lecture slides have huge paragraphs on them but he changes each slide in a minute. The lecture topics are interesting but the way he teaches it is just downright frustrating. He needs to slow down and actually explain, you also have no idea what will be on any of the tests.

Interrupts and talks over everyone he calls on, plus he required 5 TEXTBOOKS, two of which he wrote himself. I think it's completely unreasonable to require over $300 in purchases for one class. They weren't listed online after enrollment until a week into the class- no time to prepare financially, I couldn't buy two of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was a lot of fun. It was in a huge lecture hall so you could goof off or watch videos during, but the discussions were more personal. The instructors care a lot about the subject matter and will pretty much talk to you about anything. Keep an open mind as you learn about cultures around the world. Also, a pretty easy A.

He was a great professor and very nice. All you need to do is show up and you will pass. all of his exams were very easy. The lecture was interesting and fun! The discussion is where all the points are.

Really engaging lectures, I skipped quite a bit but I enjoyed the class. I put in very minimal effort and came out with an A so don't sweat this class. Learned a lot and had a lot of fun listening in lecture.

I had Bart for my Honors seminar on Human Rights, and he always had interesting things to talk about. Great guy, very engaging, super informal and casual. He's not so heavy on lecturing; he likes to hear from students and have an open discussion.
Great teacher, hilarious and makes the course work fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: One of the best classes I've ever taken! Professor Dean is an amazing teacher, and as long as you go to class and take notes on the lectures, the tests are easy to pass! The readings are helpful, but if you go to lectures they aren't really necessary.

Bart is an awesome professor, and it isn't hard to pass his class. Just show up, put in a little effort, and talk in class. He doesn't use BB to update grades and just grades you based on how you did overall in the class. I don't even think he reads the assignments you turn in, he just keeps track of IF you turned it in.
Worthwhile course. I bought the texts and went to class. My grade reflects my engagement with ANTH 160. I really enjoyed the semster.
I skipped this class all the time, didn't buy a text book, never did the reading and I got a high B.

Love him! Go to lectures & discussion, take amazing notes & you won't have to read. Ask questions in discussion! You will never type faster in your entire life than in one of his lectures, but it's worth it! Find people w/ diff TA's so you can share study guides. Tests were the only sort of difficult thing about the class.Q's were too easy or hard!

This guy is an amazing lecturer! He is hilarious and his TA's make class fun as well! All around this was a fantastic class. You need to make sure you read everything he gives you, although it is a lot 90 % of it is on the tests. You need to go to every lecture because this is where homework is given and MAJOR test questions come from it!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Online lile Learning over. We befriended each other just because we have the same sounding names  and I have been a fan of his  page & the books he has written.I have asked him a number of questions about South Americans & the historical culture,fascinating .Bartholomew lives what he teaches and inspires non majors for life.
Favorite professor so far, he makes classes super exciting.  I would definitely suggest one of his classes.  He talks a lot during lectures and sometimes it's hard to keep up.
Exceptional class dicussion, inclusive environment and great lectures

Awesome & knowledgeable. Class discussion/readings are  interesting, but there's no organization to the course. Lectures are all over the place and I'm often confused about what I should be learning. Little homework. Participate in class and do the readings! (He seems like he's chill about it but he'll deduct points!)
Solid course. I learned a lot about a new field I did know even existed. Thinking about a minor in Anthropology now. Thanks Prof. Dean!!

This guy is clearly very knowledgeable in the field of Anthropology.  But, he has so much to say every lecture that it was personally very hard to follow along and ended up confusing me more.  Reading the textbooks is vital, the majority of the questions on the tests were taken directly from the reading (a few random from lectures.)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Bart Dean is a real interesting guy. Sometimes he says the funniest/weirdest stuff, but it definitely makes the time fly by faster in class. Class wasn't incredibly hard. Test answers are basically provided via the lectures, but Dean does have a bad habit of talking too fast and moving through the slides very quickly. Overall great class though!
Great Class

Professor's Dean's lectures were very interesting. He is a really funny guy. If you read the materials you are supposed to read and show up to your discussion you will do good on the tests which are your only grades in the class. The Discussion portion of the class is where the other half of your points come from. Overall, very laid back.

One the best professors. His lectures are fun and interesting. He really knows what he's taking about. You don't need to go to lectures but I strongly recommend. Tests are not hard. Definitely take anthro 160 with him (i'm retaking the class and I enjoyed this one A LOT).
Dr.Dean is very engaging, interesting, and knowledgeable.  His classes are interactive (he wants student input and opinions).  He is by far one of the best professors I have had at KU.

Bart Dean is a very animated man! His lectures are always interesting, but you don't have to attend them consistently or take detailed notes to do well in the class. Great reading selections and GTAs for discussions. Highly recommend!

My roomate told me to take this class when Bart Dean teaches it. She was not wrong. What agreat course. I am thinking about joining the Peeace Corps (Africa) thanks to Bart Dean's class. It was a real life changer!

cracks me up everytime im in class! he can be all over the place, but he will really teach you things. actually go to lecture, because you can get super behind. make sure you take really good notes cause he goes fast, and read the books cause their cool! def check it out. so worth it!

Take this class if you want to learn the basics of anthropology. Take lots of notes cause he talks super fast, but fun in lecture hall. Learned about cultural relativist And human rights topics from amazon, Africa, Rastas and the united states of America. Testing was judicious. Happy I was Last year in this fascinating introductory course
This is a must take class: Prof. Dean gives us tones of sassafras, indigo insight and sacrosanct wisdom.
Awesome class. Fast paced and chocfull of basic anthropology. Highly recommend this class, well worth it. :-)
This guy rocks! This is one of my favorite classes I have taken so far at KU! Take it!!

This class was not a bore, I can say that, but since he was so crazy and scatterbrained sometimes, it made it hard for me to want to get up and go to class. If you read the assigned chapters, you are golden. Overall, I didn't enjoy the class, but whatever.
Adored this teacher. I wonder how he would like his eggs in the morning????
Amazing class. Never a bore. Im gonna switch to Anthropology now thanks to this summer class. Fun and relevant.
Bart is by far one of the best professors at KU. He is extremely entertaining. I would highly recommend him to anyone!
Great teacher, I loved ANTHRO before, but he made it even better. Show up to class, and you'll do well.

He makes lectures really ejoyable, and as long as you attend class, do the readings, and briefly review notes, tests will be fine. He really knows what he's talking about and his stories are hilarious!
A hilarious and eye-opening class. Bart Dean tells the real deal about anthroplogy and the world around us.
Bart was awesome. He talked without the microphone and it made class exciting. The only negative is that he sometimes is bad about interrupting students when they speak.

The model of a great teacher. Serious, yet hilarious lectures. Enjoyed Prof.s critique of the****ty nature of capitalism and the inherent humanity of indigenous societies. Remember dean hates emails, so talk to him, he was SUPER cool when I met him to discuss my thesis project in philosophy. Thumbs up^^^^^^!
AWESOME CLASS

Lectures were fine, but be wary if you have him as your discussion leader. He takes forever to give back tests and doesn't use Blackboard. I will never know my grades on participation, my final paper or final exam. You learn a lot, sure, but don't take his honors discussion without expecting some headaches.
Show up to class, pay attention and study a little for the tests and the class is really easy!
He is a really fun professor, he talks really fast though, but he makes the lectures a lot of fun and interesting.
Great!
What a wonderful class by a gifted teacher. Learning about the Urarina has enriched my life. Thanks to the lively lectures I have kept up with all of the reading, and the exam was fAir.
Excellent teacher. Cares about his students. He has real world experience in his field and has lots of great stories. The lectures are fun and educational.

really excellent prof. i wasnt interested in anthro but he chose varied and interesting readings. lectures were easy to follow, he has a great personality, and was very helpful when i needed to make up a test. NEVER bother emailing him, he probably wont read it and definitely wont respond.
SUPER COOL CLASS. not hard, but kept my attention going. knew nothing about anthropology, now i do.
Anthropology of Amazonia was fantastic, it has shaped my future career trajectory. Dean knows his stuff. Highly recommended.

Took Peoples of Amazonia (or something like that).  Very interesting. He's a different sort of teacher.  Very laid back, easy to talk to, understanding, etc.  But!  If you act like his class doesn't matter and it's obvious that you're not keeping up, he'll act like it's not a big deal and then you'll pay for it in the end.  Luckily, I did the work
Excellent class,I am now an anthro major thanks to Bart.
Sweet class

Excellent introduction to the world of Amazonian anthropology. Professor Dean is a gifted teacher, and has made me rethink my course of studys. Why am I still studying environmental studies and not anthropology??
Gresat nonwestern requirement course. Prof. is funny and keeps class moving. I recommend this anthroplgy class to all my girl friends.
Da bomb! Bart Dean is the man. Great class for non-western civ. requirement. Eccentric and provocative.
Blazing hot, I recommend this course to all. tests a Little hard, but now I know about anthroplogy
Best anthropology course I have taken at KU, Dean is an amazing teacher
Loooooooove him! He is truly the Indiana Jones of the Anthropology Dept! I love learning from him, made me want to go to class.

randomly a really hard class because its SO BORING. bart is a cool guy but my interest level was just not there.  lectures are very random and he kinda jumps all over the place. tests are somewhat difficult as well but the TA's were pretty cool
Prof. Dean is very entertaining. His class is simple yet informative. (And he's really cute!)

Professor Dean is a great teacher. His lectures are filled with humor and attention grabbing first hand accounts of indigenous peoples. His tests are based on the "big picture," which tends to make them easy. Even if you have no interest in Anthropology, this is a great way to meet the Non-Western Gen Ed requirement.
Dean is a baller! I only went to lecture on test days and ended up with a B in the class with little preparation.  Easy class, make sure to go to the discussions and you will be fine.

Bart was a very interesting guy. Kept the class awake and would point it out if you did get side tracked. Reading was very helpful and so was attending discussion which is now mandatory. Lecture, of course, wasn't. He talks a lot, but taking some notes did help in the end.

Very lively class, not boring at all. He's a great teacher with a passion for his research. If you are at all curious about anthropology, or even if you're not and just need Jr/Sr credits, take this class. Weekly readings were required, and not difficult at all, but were pertinent to the lecture. Plus, he's a really personable guy.

Bart was extremely laid-back, personable, wanted his students to do well, and was very understanding that we have a life outside of his class. He let us lead the way on what we were interested in learning for the most part. He talks A LOT but he knows it and jokes about it; he's very humble. In addition, he's not at all bad to look at! :)
Cool class!
Discussions required, but lecture isn't.  It is hard to stay motivated in this class, but it is an easy A if you apply yourself a little.

Extremely easy class! Knew a dude that didn't show up till the first test and still got a C+. Let you have "safty net" cheat sheets for the test: front, back, full page. He manages to make lectures incredibly lively yet very vague and the reading is extremely dry, but still and easy class. The T.A.s were AWESOME! Do it, DO IT!
bART Dean is awesome, he shakes up the blah blah blah of Ku. I think its a great class

This guy is pretty crazy and entertaining, so I guess he wasn't too bad.  His lectures were sometimes pointless and jumped around a lot, a lot.  It's beneficial to go to class though b/c some of the stuff of the test is word for word what he said in lecture.  If you do all the readings the tests are really easy. You hardly have to study to getta A.
This class is very poor, and it is very unorganized, if you are contemplating taking this as a gen ed. do not, it is a GPA killer.

He's hot and loves what he's talking about, but seriously one of the most boring and vague classes I have ever taken.  The tests come out of nowhere and have 9 page study guides.  Also plan on spending hours reading if you want to do well.

This class sucks.  Extremely vague and i feel I haven't really learned anything.  He is a smart guy, but it's hard to understand what he is trying to teach.  Tests are ambiguous as well.  And i am a fairly good student.  Maybe if you like to read really long and dry texts then you will enjoy this class.  I however; am no one of those people.

The class is really easy as long as you read the book and the articles.  They also throw in test questions from his lectures about his views.  Do the extra credit too, so you do not have to study as hard for the final.
Varieties of Human Experience  rocks. Great lectures, funny Professor, and serious topicd.

The best thing to do in this cool class is takes notes in Dean's lecture, even examples he gives that aren't part of the course readings, the pace is fast & furious, you are required to go to discussion, the TA's are helpful covering the obscure material. Exams are multiple choice, but easy if you know the general point of the class.
I learned a lot from a great teacher of anthropology. He is a great person, someone you want to hang around and learn from. He makes going to class fun and never took himself too seriously.

Snap, not enough lecture time with this Prof. Maybe that's why we are in red Kansas. If you like anthropology, an easy grade, and are willing to shed your egocentrism--a must take. too bad i graduate with the wrong major, try and take this before you major in something worthless. I now know about anthropology, better late than never!

Bart is the man. No matter what anyone says about his class, trust me, it's way interesting and super easy because of it. He's a really chill guy too! Even if you don't like Anthropology, you'll love this guy/the class. His TA's were really good too. I had Rachel *i can't remember her last name* but she was AWESOME. YAY BART! Easy A.
I really like my professor. He is the best yet, and a sweetheart as well (sexy too). Way to go KU.
da bomb!

If you are interested in a NW civ. req., this class is great. Attendance in lectures aren't required but key if you want to get a good grade. I didn't like my TA, but the class was fun & not BORING. Mygirl friends & roomate know about anthro. & blew off the clas & still did fine. But I got my $ worth from showing up at lecture + he is a stud.

Class lectures interesting, discussion section was OK. Class was not difficult and I liked the interactive 'speakout' part of the course. Topics covered in lecture were diverese and my roomates and me debated all the time about our views on what we covered in class.
this class is the bomb, not too difficult and covers topics rarely discussed at KU, i respect the instructor's perspective, even when i disagreed with him
lectures interesting, grading fair aNd i learned alot about a field I never knew about. I like know to take more anthroplogy classses
No Comments
superb, easy and insightful, made me think, highly recommend Dean's clas
He emphasizes opinions rather than reality. Tests and expectations for the class are rather blurry. Overall he seems like a good guy but his teaching abilities need work to be successful
No Comments
He's a great guy!  As a teacher, however, not so much
This class rocks

I am in his class right now and I love how he keeps it interesting and fun.  If you need jr/sr hours take the 360 option instead of the 160-(the only difference is that the 360 students write an 8-10 pg paper).  Excellent choice for the non-western credit!

I'd say don't take this class, there are much cooler non western civ classes. He interrupts students when they try to "speak out," he spends more time finding cool pictures for his slides than creating a cohesive lecture, the TA's don't even grade the hw, so really you have no idea what is going on.
Best teacher I have had at KU, he keeps class fun and interesting, and lets you learn without just reading... great class, great teacher.
professor dean is the best professor I had while at ku, he is as passionate as they come. Sorry I graduated before taking more of his classes.
No Comments
So interesting...so hot...so smart. opens your eyes to new things and gives you the chance to be heard
super dude...he knows his stuff and he ain{t afraid to tell it like it is!

Super hot, great personality, never skipped a class. He's so interesting to watch and I love the fact that you can come down at the beginning of each class and speak your mind about any topic. Everyone should take his class to be a more well rounded person and understand that there is more to the world than the US. Great TAs. I loved Nancy. She's really good and very helpful.
No Comments

I had him for ANTH 106 and another upper level class. I love Bart Dean and will take any class I can offered by him. He is very easy and very personable. He is a little cocky and pretty messy and unorganized but thats just him. Many of his classes are discussion based so don't take it if you don't like talking about articles and books.

I took 360 instead of 160 (the difference being a 5 pg paper and 1 pg essay on each test), never went to lecture after two weeks, did the paper the night before and got a B. Easy enough class depending on the TA you get (DON'T get Robinson) and it's a nice, cushy way to get some Junior/Senior hours while fulfilling that Non-Western requirement.
No Comments

Unlike the comment posted below about Prof. Dean, I found his course wonderful. 5 stars for WOW! What an eye-opener...andwe need this in our bigoted state. The neo-Con. student clearly missed the point of discussing "drugs", not to mention that prof. Dean does not teach Anth 161! If you want to think out side of the box, take Dean's class.

Bart Dean appeared to be helpful, but missed every single appointment I made to meet with him.  He also lost my papers and blamed that on me.  He is very cocky and has no need to be.  He relies on jokes about drugs and alcohol to keep the class interesting--it didn't work.
Bart is sooo hot! Take his class if you can!
easy
Dean is the****- he is so passionate about anthropolgy and has made me consider taking more classes.  His lectures are awesome and his tests are a breeze.  The TAs are awesome too!

Give that man 2 peppers he's smokin hot and funny too (for a professor). His lectures are great...simple and to the point. Bottom line, if you want to take an easy class where you can just come and listen and get an A, then Dean's your man!
Best class I have taken at KU. Amazing lectures, never boring and he is very passionate about anthropology. He is a sight for sore eyes...wow!
superb class--great prof
Rather easy class, but a worthwhile learning experience of areas not often touched on outside of anthropology.
Bart displays an uncanny ability to always appear in extremely tasteful pants. I'm not sure if he is rich, but the quality of his styling products is undeniable.
Very interesting lectures, very loud mouth, very passionate about the URANINA
pretty easy class

Charismatic. He pointed out that he looks like Prof Utonium from the Powerpuff Girls and he admits he's a loud mouth.  He's funny & good.  He seems to like photography & music.  plays music before every lecture.
really, really hot...like Harrison Ford in the Indiana Jones movies hot

Amazing lectures!  Does not even use a microphone in Budig 120.  Speaks clearly and enthusiastically about subject!  Gets your attention with his engaging lectures.  Must do soem reading for this class, but worthwhile.
Very easy if you go. This was the honors section, so more essay on the tests. Expect at least a B.
Cake class if you show up.

In response to previous post, he will back up on his overheads if you ask. Notes aren't as important as reading. Interesting guy. Entirely possible to make an A just by attending lecture and discussions regularly without putting forth any extra effort.
Easiest class I ever took @ KU... and it's very interesting.
No Comments
What a bad professor.  He went really fast in his presentations during lecture.  We could never get the notes off PowerPoint.
Really hot!
No Comments

RUNNNNNNNNNNNNN AS FAR AWAY AS POSSIBLE. THE FINAL IS OPEN NOTE WITH PHONE, CHAT, TEXTBOOK, ALL THE ABOVE, AND PEOPLE STILL AVERAGE A D ON THIS DANG EXAM. I go to this class with no seatbelt on and with my eyes closed on the road, hoping I won't have to go to class. Anyway, stay safe y'all, you got this ig, cause I didn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hard. You will struggle to understand the concepts, and exams are worth 91% of your overall grade. However, his lectures are very thorough. They can be hard to keep up with and he does not post them in their entirety so be prepared to take photos. The lectures cover all the content you need to know for his exams so pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do whatever you can to avoid Bergman. Take classes with another professor if you can. He does not post anything on canvas. If you miss class, you have to get notes from someone else. He acts like questions are beneath him, and will never fully answer your questions. He doesn't understand that students don't understand things immediately.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 91% of the class is exams. no info on canvas. very outdated teaching style. failed the class crazy style.
Made me cry cause yelled at me

Very complete and thorough in presented content. Includes applied examples of physical industry application. Dry humor, and lectures can be boring. All handouts and lecture notes are on paper, so if you miss class grab an extra copy from someone. Expect propagated error affecting grading. Textbook is your friend, do the example problems.

Prof. Bergman is very knowledgeable about the subject. As an expert, I am sure he is unparalleled and highly respected. As a professor, he is brutal. 91% of the grade is based on exams and the 30% final. All of his lectures are done by hand, and not posted online. He tends to answer questions as if they are beneath him. I hear he curves though.

As a lecturer, Bergman is pretty alright. Clearly knows what he's talking about, but kind of dry. As a professor, he's awful. Never posted grades or lectures or anything to Canvas. The final (which is also like 30% of the grade) is tomorrow and I have no idea what my grade is. Would sometimes mock students when they asked questions, unpredictably.

Moves too fast through lectures that they are impossible to follow. All of your grade is based on the tests. He is so condescending and rude it is impossible to ask him a question without him making you feel bad about yourself.

Most important things are that you need to show up to class, pay attention, and take good notes. Lectures are great and you can do well without reading the textbook if you take good enough notes. Posted homework solutions and exam solutions are great for understanding how to solve different types of problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Its a hard class and he's gonna make you work for the grade you want but he's fair and open about what's going on. Everyone posting bad reviews for him is just salty that they were too lazy to get a good grade. Definitely a hard class but I learned a lot and it was one of my favorite ME classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bergman is stuck in the olden times of being a professor. He handwrites all his notes before lecture and goes through them very quickly in class. You either only have time to listen to him or take notes. Doesn't post anything on blackboard. If you miss even one class you are screwed. He is NOT helpful in office hours; he will barely answer Qs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures are pretty good if you know how to take notes in his class. He has nothing online, so dont skip, but his lectures are well put together. if you take pictures of his content during his lecture, while taking notes over important comments he makes, copy your pictures later, you will find yourself actually learning.

In retrospect, ME 510 was probably one of my favorite classes. However, this class sucked when I was taking it because the material is NOT easy. Due to the fact he has always (in every class he teaches) grades on a heavy curve, I ended up crying when I saw my final grade was an A. READ AND DO THE HOMEWORK. Take him for 510 so that 612 is familiar

One of the hardest classes I've taken, but worth it. I Learned a lot. Dr. Bergman could narrate audio books, and he provides excellent notes. You'll spend a lot of time on homework and reading the book. Tests are fair, but tough. The naysayers likely did not put in the work required. I took his class in a 20 hour semester and got an A.
Great lectures, but generally a very difficult class.

Literally lectures straight out of the book.Don't even need to go to lecture.Which is great. His textbook is excellent. Tests are a bit difficult depending on how quickly you can learn how to do them from the book.So if you are complaining about him not wanting to talk during office hours.The answer is in the book.Guaranteed. And it's easy to find.

Good lecturer but horrible people skills. VERY condescending and is no help in office hours. I was told to look in the book every time and if it was a question from the book than I just needed to "figure it out". Guy does grow a nice beard though.
The person who gave him such a high rating is a lair. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR!

He uses a tone of voice that makes you feel like he thinks you are three years old. He is useless in office hours. I went in for help and he just told me to look in the book every time. He wrote the book he thinks it is perfect. Be ready for hell.
Indifferent towards students. The most condescending person I have ever met. Don't expect him to talk to you during office hours let alone help.

Author of the textbook. Explains theory and work thoroughly. Homework problems are often difficult, but test problems were very fair. Read the book, make sure the material makes sense to you, work a few problems and you'll do well. Very good lecturer.
Good professor, lots of in-class group work, projects are fun, but she is a very tough and SLOW grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She was just flat out mean sometimes, she was sort of helpful sometimes but she was just really mean.

A wonderful and caring professor who is passionate about literature and her students, however, she often tends to go on long tangents on topics relevant to the class which is interesting but can take away from work time.

Fiction Writing 1 with her was wonderful, and I feel like I got a good introduction into something I'm really interested in. She gave good reading assignments that weren't too difficult and interacting with such a small class was fun. She has a good sense of humor and her background in historical fiction was cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is very helpful on feedback. She wants you to do well in the class and is very caring.
The amount of busy work is out of this world. In-class assignments can be explained in 20 minutes but are described in an hour plus sometimes making me more confused at the end. Change right away!

means well but the way she presents it to her students is not engaging and slow. she is also hard to get an answer out of if you have a question. very much a "mental" game class as it most of the work could be done in 15 mins but extended to fit a class period. most projects were fine but just time-consuming. means well wouldn't recommend though
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is clear she knows what she knows what she's talking about but the way she presents it to her students is not engaging. The class is easy and she has pushed the due dates of several assignments. Easy A if you attend, but you're going to have mental willpower.
Extremely rude and disrespectful, tough grader failed me for no reason.
Terrible professor, do not stay in her class. :/
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take her if you want to learn anything in english your freshman year. She speaks extremely quietly, rude, grades harshly and constantly messes up assignments and tests. Talk to your advisor if you get her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is a terrible teacher who speaks quietly and expects you to know everything. Please ask your advisor for a new teacher.
I had her online. She was overall a really nice person and the homework was fine but her class was slow it make me sleepy. she is lenient with due dates and willing to work with you on your grade.

Divya was an amazing professor! Extremely knowledgeable about creative writing and writing in general. However, you write A LOT. My class had 17 people (including me); 3 different papers, so 48 one-page critiques, plus the 3 i had to write for others to critique. We had workshops, which is very helpful, though!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: You have to write a LOT for this class. However, Bhalla is extremely passionate about creative writing, and I genuinely felt I became a better writer because of this course. She has very specific feedback which was amazingly helpful. Also, she's very funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ms. Bhalla is one of the most caring profs I've ever had. She genuinely wants to see everyone grow as a writer & implements the means to do so in class. We did workshops where we discussed each other's writing & it was always helpful. She is clearly passionate about creative writing herself. I loved her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Although the class wasn't the most enjoyable, she enjoyed teaching it and that showed a lot. She makes an effort to be available and try and help/answer questions. I enjoyed her as a professor. Attendance and participation are a must.
I thought Miss Bhalla was unclear when I asked for help on papers, and most of the time I would leave our conversations more confused.
Its been a few months but I and many others still miss you dearly. I always will and I hope wherever you are you're having a blast and dancing to Taylor Swift.
She was a wonderful instructor, and was great at keeping people engaged. She had good humor too. I will miss her

Bliss was the best professor I had ever had. I can't believe some students have to go through psych at KU without being able to take one of their classes. Rest in peace to the most caring and understanding person ever.

I'm writing this after Dr. Bliss has sadly passed. She was a wonderful professor who pushed her students to be kind and stand up for what's right. She is the reason I'm going to grad school as a 1st gen student. She will be missed

One of the best professors I've had at KU. Brilliant, very accommodating, and fun to listen to. All exams were online and open book and she gives lots of opportunities for extra credit. Attendance is technically mandatory but her policy is very relaxed and communication goes a long way. Definitely recommend taking a class w/ her before graduating

My favorite prof in the Psych Dept. She's incredibly caring and wants all students to succeed. She is the sole reason why I am pursuing higher education after my bachelor's. She is truly an inspiration. She teaches us not only about the material of the class but also about the real world. I'm taking one of her classes again before I graduate fs!

Bliss is literally one of the best professors I've had at KU. Her attitude and relationship with students is what makes her special and one of the best professors. She is very knowledgable and gives students so many opportunities to have a good grade. I genuinely went to class just to see her. If you can take one of her classes DO IT!

Bliss was and is a great professor and lecturer, just because she doesn't necessarily fit the image of a college professor does NOT mean that she is not knowledgeable in her field. What I enjoy most about her specifically is that the emphasis is put on actually learning and understanding the material rather than just getting a good grade
Always has a positive attitude and is amazing at keeping the students engaged. Probably the best professor I've had at KU.

My absolute favorite professor of all time!! They are totally amazing and don't just care about the course content, but also how their students are doing in their real lives. I also took their Addictive Behaviors class. They taught us things about drugs that weren't just in the textbook but also things that we would need to know in the real world.

Dr Bliss is incredible. One of the most understanding faculty members at KU. Their lectures are interesting and they do an AMAZING job at making the material digestible and fun for us. Highly recommend!!!

Dr. Bliss is an amazing professor. Her lecture style is engaging. The final for the class was a group paper, but they managed to make it not stressful. I normally hate group projects but this one was okay.

Dr. Bliss is AMAZING. So incredibly caring and smart, and she is officially my new favorite member of the PSYC department. This class used McGraw Hill for assignments and exams, so be prepared to pay for the access code. Otherwise, I truly enjoyed her class, lecture style, and personality. I would recommend that anyone take Dr. Bliss's courses.

HIST 352 with Dr. Blansett is a pretty classic-style humanities course; sit and listen to lecture, do readings between classes, write an essay for the final, etc. His teaching style is a bit dry, but the course material is captivating. If you engage with this course, you will gain a new perspective on the people, country, and land around you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed his class and was blown away by how caring Professor Blansett was. Many things came up in my personal life, and he was beyond kind and respectful, both over email and in class. He is a great guy who deeply cares about Indigenous history. Each lecture was detailed and told a story, I would for sure take a class from him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved him as a person, not so much as  a professor. Very lecture heavy, and he tends to draw on a bit. There were 4 books required not including the ones you have to read for your research paper/book reports. He does not respond to emails. Incredibly vague about instructions and changes due dates last minute with no notice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A lot of the class was based off of the readings with supplemental lectures in class. There are 2 big writing assignments that are each worth 50 points but you have weeks to do them and they are take home. There are only 2 exams, the midterm and the final. As long as you study the study guide he provides, you shouldn't have any issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, he really knows how to capture students attention. Amazing lectures and he is always open to feedback.

Dr. Blansett is very passionate about his subject. His lectures can draw on a bit but most are pretty interesting. He reduced the class load because of Covid, which was more than welcomed. He offers extra credit and is more than happy to talk outside of class. We did use every book required for the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Stay away at all costs. Besson has no dropped exams, no extra credit, never answers email, doesn't hold office hours, puts in the minimum time, and only 10% of students get A's. The other professor teaching this class in the fall gives mostly A's and lets you take exams until you get the grade you want.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was based heavily on multiple choice no partial credit exams that had class averages around 40-60%. He had poor teaching methods that consisted of lecture covering one individual question. This one question was the only practice given for the entire concept. The assignments were creating one question and solving it. Nobody learns. Will fail!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Accept that PHSX 114 at KU sucks sorry. Besson is funny and if you have good attendance, you are guaranteed not to fail. His tests can be tricky, but if you've done the caps and look over the slides, none of the problems will surprise you. The cheat sheet is very valuable. He gives you multiple opportunities to regain credit if you do bomb an exam

Grades heavily rely on exams and make up 65% of the final score. He knows his class is incredibly difficult and has had issues with the administration multiple times, but refuses to change his teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your homework is creating your own problems which has a bad time at explaining in class and assumes you already know how to do half the topics.

Besson's class is tough—exams are hard with no partial credit, but you get a front and back cheat sheet and an extra credit question from past material. His lectures are generally engaging, often with weird stories. He's super helpful in office hours and always willing to answer questions. A nice person who truly wants students to succeed.

If you work hard in Dr. Besson's class you will be successful. He offers extra credit on all homework and exams, plus the final can replace 2 (of 7) exams throughout the semester. Before class he also offers a discussion time where he goes over the homework for that day. You get a cheat sheet on exams, so if you use it, the exams are easy.

Theres very little room for error in his class. If you bomb 2 exams out of 7 its very difficult to climb out of that hole. Extra credit will actually lower your grade about 2% per CAP which doesn't make sense. In his lectures he will sometimes talk about his old rock band instead of actual physics and it feels like a waste of time to be in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All he does is tell stories in class. I am always really bored in his lecture. His past lecture videos help with the homework assignments but attendance is mandatory. Yawnn
He is not a good professor at all. Back when I took this course, he wouldn't even check the homework and would give credit for blank sheets of paper turned in.

The ppl claiming he does not care for students have never talked to him outside of class. This class is very difficult, but he gives so many chances to bring your grade up (EC for every HW, EC on exams). But I agree that exams are very difficult and hard to study for them bc assignments and lecture are very diff from the exams+no partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The literal definition of not caring for your students. I did every problem, watch every lecture and attended very class, and there were problems in the exam that were never discussed. I hate how for a phsx exam he chooses MC, and questions are based on previous one, so if you missed a "-" you have 50% less in your exam grade.
This class is very challenging if you're not strong in math. The professor doesn't provide much guidance, so relying on a tutor and study tools like Unstuck ai are essential to succeed.

Dr. Besson is the worst professor I have ever had. He wants his students to perform poorly. The class average for each exam was never above 75%. There are 10 exams with only 10 questions each. The exams covered problems that were never discussed in class. We were not allowed to take the final if we had missed 3+ classes. He is not helpful or kind.

Watch the DSO videos posted to Canvas and ignore the main lectures. He's good at working through homework problems and explaining things there but things kinda fall apart and get chaotic when he's teaching in front of a bigger audience. You do need to show up and iClickers are timed. He'll talk about unrelated things during them, it's distracting.

If I could rate this class a 0 I would. By the third exam, the class avg was a D+. Despite watching all of his videos and doing the 10 practice questions, I still am doing terribly on the exams. He does not teach WHY or how to solve problems. He goes through examples in class and expects you to follow without knowing where he is getting each value.
Just don't bother
Very bad if you're at all rusty with math. He doesn't explain things well in detail. Had to fully rely on a tutor to get through

Do not take this professor! He pretends to be one person in class and outside of class when you ask for help or have questions he attacks you. DO NOT TAKE! He also manipulates students into defending him when he fears that administration has concerns.

Besson is the best professor I have ever had at KU. He gives homework every class but he has discussions that go through it step-by-step. You are graded on participation. Exams are online, open book and open note. He knows students names and will go through questions in class until every person understands. You have to be willing to ask questions.
definitely do not take this course - besson requires that you actually understand the material in order to get a good grade. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Don't choose Besson if you struggle with math and would rather prioritize other classes. There are exams every other week and even if you studied, they don't solve like the homework with harsh grading.
