Loved professor Biernat! I took Psyc Stats from her and she was great! Just do the quizzes and homework, go to lecture and you probably won't need to read the textbook. The one thing the textbook is useful for is the quizzes, some of the questions aren't specifically covered in lecture. I would definitely take from her again!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Though her lectures can be dry at times, it is more the fault of the subject than of her. Her lectures make sense of the confusing subject. I tried to read the book on my own and was instantly lost. If it weren't for her teaching and explanations, I would have never passed on my own.

Dr. Biernat is super nice, and genuinely tries to makes lectures interesting. She responds to emails quickly, and is lenient in emergency situations. If you go to class and put in a decent amount of effort, you'll do well. My only one little complaint is that she takes forever to post grades. Aside from that, she makes the class easy.
Professor Biernat makes research methods an easy course. Pay attention in class, and you will pass.
Very easy class if you put in a little effort.

Ithought this class was going to be hard and i don't know if it was just becasue of dr. Biernat but it was really easy. There are assignments where you have to be in class AND turn in the assingment to get credit but it's not every week. Her class gets a little boring but i didn't mind because she tests easy. all lectures are from ppt and online.

If you need to take research methods, take it with Biernat! The lectures aren't super fun, but she tries to make it interesting (it's research methods, nobody should expect it to be fun). Going to class isn't required, but she explains everything so well that you really should go so you don't get confused. Her exams are a little tough.

Dr. Biernat is a great professor. If you are going to take research methods, take it with her. She is so nice, and very intelligent too! She is willing to help her students, the quizzes are all online, the exams can be tricky but her lectures should make things clear. She WANTS you to ask questions so if you don't understand just ask her!
Wow, muy fantastico!
Very nice and helpful :) Class is pretty boring, although you have to realize that there is no easy way to make research methods too interesting.

Dr. Biernat is a wonderful teacher! The material is kind of boring but she teaches in a way that makes it interesting. The class consists of 3 tests, 14 quizzes and about 10 assignments. Assignments are easy you get points just for doing them. the quizzes are out of 10 and if you read the material its pretty easy to get an 8 or 9. Great Class!!!

Her first time teaching methods, but she did a fairly good job. If you attend class I found you don't need to read the book. Has a lot of easy points with online quizzes and in class assignments that are only completion points. Class gets a bit boring though when she uses 10 examples for every new concept.
Nicest teacher. Attendance isn't mandatory. Pretty easy class and interesting.

She is really a good prof.  Just read your book, seriously. and study your notes. the quizzes help you get through the book easier. but the more you read your textbook, the better you do. i should have read more lol...but over she was an awesome prof and really cared about her students success!

Assuming that you come to class, read the book, do the online quizzes, and show up for discussion sessions, you'll be fine. There's little excuse to get a poor grade in this class - Professor Biernat wants you to succeed and gives you the tools to do so.
This is a very good class!  Everything is clear, easy, and understandable.  She's very fair.  Just be sure to go to class, read the book, and do the chapter questions.
Interesting class. Gets a bit boring, but she does a good job of trying to make it fun. Very good teacher. Highly recommend anything she teaches!
She made social psych more intresting.
Very fun, nice, clear, and the class is easy if you do the work.
great teacher! as long as you go over your notes you will do well on all the test and she is great at explaining concepts and making sure you understand them

Easy class. You just have to go and read the book. Biernat knows what she is talking about and actually makes a point to make sure her students are learning. If you fail her class....your just plain dumb!
Easy class if you read your book... shes not to helpful and lectures are a little unorganized but go because questions come from studies mentioned in class.  Interesting class.. "ok" teacher.
Interesting lectures, is a good teacher.
No Comments
Really interesting class... Great Book.. Biernat is a huge ****.  Tried to fail me for not going to class.. pulled an A.
No Comments

Really good teacher and picked an excellent textbook. Easy to follow in lecture and relates material well to YOUR experiences. Tests are straight from the book, just know all vocab and a few main studies in class/lecture. TAs were ok but were very nice. Requires some dedication but a very rewarding class! You will learn a lot.
Professor Biernat is willing to help you with anything; she will allow you to make up anything and everything;interesting material;easy online quizzes;paper is hard, but not grades to harshly
Social Psyc with Dr. Biernat is a fantastic class with excellent TA's and discussion sections!  Biernat is a GREAT lecturer.  Very interesting.  Take this class!
Very nice... very hot...

This was the hardest class/worst grade I've ever experienced at KU (I've taken OCHEM and physics.) Material is not cohesive and makes zero sense. It's impossible to take good notes because she just puts photos on the screen, making exams impossible. There's a ton of math/graphing on exams and no calculator. Textbook is required and very exam heavy!
She's nice, but I would say her class was tough and she's not always clear about her exams. She grades very strict.

Dr Billings is very smart, but her teaching style is awful. The exams are often over random topics that were on one slide that had no words on it. You are expected to do all of the math by hand, including complex fractions and decimals and are almost impossible (she doesn't even work them out in class, you have to teach yourself).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The course was very exam heavy and the exams were graded hard. It was impossible to study because the study guides were nothing like the book and vice versa. I always ended up studying a week before the exam just to do better but it never helped. The lectures were all research studies:/ and they were never on the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Billings is a very smart woman but her lectures consist of close to nothing. There are literally no words on her lecture slides, which forces you to rely heavily on the textbook. There is barely any homework in this class which sounds great, but it's not. Your entire grade is based off of extremely wordy exams. Skip this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Dr. Billings is very intelligent and well-respected, but that doesn't transfer to her teaching. 

As opposed to her co-prof. Dr. Foster, she is more reliant on the textbook, with her lectures being scattered and incomplete. She is more pretentious and less accessible as well. I felt less prepared and more anxious for exams over material she taught.

Her lectures have almost no words in them. I had to rely on the textbook to teach myself the material as the lectures were useless. The course doesn't have any homework or extra credit so your entire grade is quizzes and exams. Her exams were difficult and contained content that was mentioned one time. Calculators weren't allowed during exams.

Her lectures slide consist of pictures and graphs from the textbook.  She also includes graphs from studies on her slides that are impossible to interpret if you don't attend lecture. Her lectures are uninteresting and she speaks way too quietly. I just read the book and attended half the lectures. Good thing though is test are super short.
It is a tough class, but she's brilliant and really knows her stuff. Don't come in thinking it's an easy A, but if you work at it, you gonna learn the subject just fine.

She was terrible.  Tests didn't make sense.  Told us she wasn't going to test us over a subject and she would. She would lecture about stuff she didn't know anything about and she would claim that they are still studying the subject, THEN WHY LECTURE OVER IT!! Take the other professor if possible.
She was a terrible professor. Extremely unhelpful and she usually didn?t know what she was talking about.

(COMS 246) 

Amazing professor. Super caring and understanding. Learned a lot and enjoyed the assignments

She's one of the best professor's I have ever had at KU. I am considering graduate school because of her classes. It's not common that you meet someone who is both brilliant, reasonable, and empathic. The content is challenging, but she really want students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang is one of the best at KU. She is approachable and funny, and brilliant. I could take every class with her as the instructor. Make sure you read and participate - she is always encouraging and acknowledges student effort.
Yan Bing is the best professor I've had at KU. Do the reading, and you'll get an A. Go and talk to her and she will love you.

Took East Asian Communications. She is a great teacher. The course started off incredibly hard, but very quickly got both interesting and engaging. Staggering amount of technical research to read, though she walked us through the important parts. A+ teacher.
Took multiple classes with her. One of my favorite professors in college.  She is genuinely caring.  She grades fairly.  Her English is very easy to understand though with an accent.
Most amazing professor and person ever!!

DON'T DO IT!!!  the worst grade I've received in college (C-) just because I did not know how conduct research properly.  I worked harder in her class and lost more sleep than I ever have and was poorly rewarded because I took the class too early in my career.  B-WORD EXTREME

Great teacher, very helpful and respectful.  I enjoyed this class and her style of teaching.  she lectures a lot but gave take home tests in this particular class so made it easier on the students.  would highly recommend!!

Seminar in East Asian Communications. Yan Bing is a great rofessorwho is really willing to help you if you want to help yourself. Don't take her if you expect to get an easy A. She is firm but fair, especially regarding attendance. She is very intelligent so be prepared. You will read A LOT, both in the text book and in journal articles. Put in an

Yan Bing was my favorite teacher that I've had in my entire lifetime. She does everything within her power to help you. She is also extremely knowledgeable concerning the subject of Mass Communications. She is a very sweet lady with a great sense of humor! The class mainly focuses on analyzing journal articles. Take one of Yan Bing's classes now!!!

Very fun online course! Loved the readings, but there were quite a few of them, and also some writing. Easy to fall behind if you don't set aside time to work on the class, but you could complete an average week's work in 3-4 hours. Towards the end of the class, the work got heavier with projects, so 5-6 hours. Had lots of fun and learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bogi was a great professor for Mystical Traditions of Judaism. They are very knowledgeable and passionate about the topic and do their best to express this to their students. My only issue is that the class is extremely reading-heavy and involves texts that, at times, are borderline unreadable. However, I would recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class for a Jewish Studies credit and I'm so glad I did! Bogi is awesome. They're caring and understanding, especially when it comes to needing help with anything. Textbook was required to complete various assignments. Very lecture heavy, but discussion and participation were heavily promoted. Hope I get to take another class of theirs!

While I never met Dr. Perelmutter in person, they are a very caring professor. They respond quickly to emails if you have questions. Short semester course. The assignments are online textbook readings, discussion posts, and weekly quizzes (3 attempts for each quiz). Honors students write a final paper, but it's not strict; more for your learning.

Great guy, but can come off as lazy sometimes. Tests can have trick questions, which can be irritating. Otherwise his lectures are phenomenal, and the labs are genuinely
A great way to learn the topic. Take him if you have the option to
Class and professor are interesting. Lots of collaborative assignments labs and a semester project. Exams are no surprises with a few trick questions. Great professor!

Took for EECS569. Great guy, clearly cares about his work, but can be a bit lazy and unclear about assignments. Exams can have some "gotcha" questions that feel a bit unfair, but gives you a double-sided cheat sheet. Biggest issue is the lack of clarity with assignments/labs, but otherwise an enjoyable class, as he clearly loves the topic.

The mini-projects, the homework assignments, the quizzes, and the course project are very easy and simple. But the exams are slightly difficult and tricky. Take this course if you want to learn SQL and database topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: EECS 447: Definitely gotta study a little-- but fairly easy A imo. Bo is a cool guy, delivers good lectures. Probably the best prof I've had since John Gibbons, at least in terms of not making the class too hard, but also making you learn. The "mini-projects" and hw assignments are stupid easy; the tests have a few tricky questions, but nothing bad

Dr. Luo is good, but his grading policy is not efficient. The assignments and the mini-projects are simple and helpful, but his exams are extremely tricky and hard. The good part is that he gives a curve that slightly improves the students' grades. His lectures are confusing, but they are not terrible.

Delivers excellent lectures. Homework and projects are both reasonable and relevant to the class. His exams are well-written and have no surprises, which is great because they're worth 68% of your grade. Clearly passionate about cybersecurity and passionate about teaching. KU needs more professors like Prof. Luo.

Favorite professor I've had while getting my CS degree hands-down. I've taken 3 courses with him (569,647,767) & almost wish I was going to grad school to continue learning from him! He is such a strong lecturer, & you will get the best understanding of the course topic that you possibly could in the time given. Could not recommend Dr. Luo enough!

No homework.
Up-to-date material - updates slides regularly.
Gives examples from the industry to connect the learned material to the real world.
Interesting group projects. Lots of freedom.
Exams are somewhat difficult and very comprehensive. But does a good job of preparing you

Good option for a senior elective. Emphasizes common student mistakes and explains the material well to make sure we understand. Curves exam averages up to 80. Very little work you have to do for this course beyond the exams which are primarily true/false questions.
He is a great professor, and he made the class a lot easier. Cheat sheets are allowed during exams but it takes time to prepare it.
Luo makes everything very clear and makes himself available to answer questions and help.

Literally just don't fall asleep in class and you are so smooth sailing. Super smart in the way she directs her lectures and you only do like 5 assignments total (and she dropped one of them for our class). Readings every class but the guides aren't graded OR even collected… If she's your professor she's gonna be your best friend.
I don't normally leave RMP reviews but I had Dr. Bourgeois for FREN 435 and wanted to add another new 5 star review to show that she's still incredible

Christine is an absolute angel of a professor. She gives wonderful feedback that prompts further discussions that are meaningful in the modern day as well as the Middle Ages! Her assignments were never meant to be busy work, but were always tied into the other main pieces. Would absolutely take again!

Woooooow. Christine has got to be one of my favorite professors. She gives handouts to take notes on each class. The handouts combined with the powerpoints are really useful for studying for the tests. Really all I needed. Also, I find it important to note that she wore high heels almost every single class. She always looked so put together.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Great professor. Dr. Bourgeois knows her stuff, and she makes the information accessible. She's also very funny, and she's always willing to help with the material. Don't hesitate to see her in office hours or make an appointment if you need help, but it's not a difficult class.
Awesome teacher! It's not an easy A, but what she expects is fair and well-defined. She knows her stuff and she's hilarious. I would recommend taking a class with her!

An amazing teacher. very passionate about what she teaches and you can tell she knows so much. She's kind and understanding so whenever we got lost she'd explain. I have taken several classes with her and she's amazing! highly recommend
Awesome Teacher, totally recommend.

I'm not prejudiced. It's true that she grades toughly. it's also true that she values industrious students. She is not indifferent. Instead, she has strong sense of right and wrong.Getting an A from her makes me believe I can succeed in my studies if I work hard enough.

She's knowledgeable and competent about her subject. The problem is that you have to be a major loudmouth to get better than a C on the attendance, which counts as a major part of your grade - there were some classes where students were yelling so much that hand-raising was useless. I had perfect attendance, took diligent notes, and still got a B.

I didn't think that she was a horrible teacher. Clearly explains what she wants in a paper and I thought her grading was fair. If you e-mail her your papers and set up conferences to discuss them, you should be fine.
If you attend class, you will be fine. You also have to read the books, but they are decent. Plan on reading like 10 hours per week, though! You must attend!

Many people on here are being unfairly harsh. If you are looking for a blow-off class you can pass without effort, she is not the professor for you. She is a tough grader, but very fair. And she expects quite a bit from her students. But people who say she wouldn't help them either didn't really ask, or expected her to just do the work for them.

Make sure you go to class and PARTICIPATE so you can boost your C to a B.  She loves giving out Cs, and I went in to her office for help and still got a C on each paper.  She's nice enough, but I didn't know what she wanted from my papers, and was pretty useless in giving me helpful advice.  Take a different English class.
No Comments

She is absolutely impossible. The worst teacher I have ever had and the hardest grader. Teaches and grades as though this is a grad course, not a 300 level. The whole class was lost and she still did not go over material again. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER!!!!!!!!!
Worst teacher I've ever had. I would transfer schools before I took another class with her. Awful! Run for your life!

She is a good teacher, It is lots of reading but not too bad. We only had a few 3 pages papers. Pay attention and go to class and you will do fine. She is a pretty difficult grade but is willing to help.
No Comments
No Comments

Class:Lancelot and Guinivere. She was clearly interested in the subject of the class and allowed a lot of discussion in class about books we were reading. We had to write maybe 2-3 papers and I found her grading fair. If you know how to write well, the class should be easy to kinda challenging. She was flexible and took constructive criticism well.

She is an impossible grader.  I scheduled many conferencs with her and even visted the writer's roost and still got a C on every paper.  Her conferences are not helpful unless you e-mail the paper to her the night before the conference!  Take this at a community college or find a different teacher!
She grades very hard.  Find a different English class and don't take her.
It is hard to get more than a C on a paper and sometimes she is not clear about what she wants. In-class participation points really help!

Dr. Bolden is one of the best professors at KU hands down. I've been lucky enough to have him for 2 classes now and in each class I was able to leave not only knowing more about my subject but also having a better appreciation for it. His lectures are always easy to follow and engaging, even though they were recorded. 10/10

I had Professor Bolden when I was a freshman taking AAAS 104 and I have him again for AAAS 325 so I can confidently say he really is one of the best professors at KU. His lectures are always thought provoking and informative. He gives good feedback on writing assignments and you can tell he cares about the content that he is giving to us students.

Great professor and funny. There are a few quizzes, but they are very easy, 2 major papers(1200-1400 words) and multiple 500-word journals are due before the start of class, but those are also very easy. Overall, the class is excellent.

Great professor, funny and understanding.  Course material provided! Participate in the lecture, do the reading, and write short journals for homework. A couple of papers but if you pay attention they're easy.

This was easily one of my favorite classes of my first semester. The lectures were always good and easy to follow. There was a reading and journal due almost every class but nothing too hard. Gives good feedback on essays also. 10/10.
Barely any points for the class, Dr. Bolden is a very nice guy

He's organized, passionate, and full of incredible insight. I don't like paying exorbitant amounts of money for electives I could easily take at a CC but professors like Dr. Bolden force me to reconsider. I learned more than I ever expected in Dr. Bolden's class and I wouldn't hesitate to take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Bolden is without a doubt one of the most extraordinary professors I have have ever come across as a student: his devotion to the subject matter, and the dedication he has in his students, is unlike anything I have not seen. He is a fantastic professor, and is dedicated to make you not only a better writer, but a better thinker.

Dr Bolden was one of the most encouraging professors I ever had at KU.  He was always so helpful and understanding.  He did everything he could to provide us with every resource he thought could be at all useful.  Talk to him, take his classes, and talk to him some more.  He will inspire you to write the best paper possible.

Really insightful class when you actively engage in class discussions. You can do really well without a lot of effort but you get a whole lot more out of it when you actually participate. Great class and Dr. Bolden is really cool!

He is a great teacher and really willing to help his students.  He really knows what he is talking about and he encourages his students to interact, actually, it's basically required. His journals are pretty easy but he grades essays like an english teacher so watch out for grammar and sentence errors. I loved this class and it was very interesting
Best teacher I've had at KU. He really cares about his students.

He is a great teacher. You just need to show up to class and have your journals done. He grades his papers pretty hard so just watch out for that. He is very funny and he will work with you if you need it.
A very thought-provoking teacher.

Every lecture is nonstop hand-cramping notes for an hour and 15 minutes straight. The only things in this class for a grade are quizzes every other class and 4 total exams. Super strict on attendance and will fail you if you miss 3 or more classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Brian is one of the few teachers in the business school that doesnt really care for his students. Lectures are extensive and super boring. There are about 6 things in this class that get graded 4 tests being of the 6. Tests are very hard to prepare for and will tank your grade. DO NOT TAKE BLAW with Brian.

Suggestion: MGMT 718 in place of BLAW 703. 

The class grade includes quizzes, exams, and 1 assignment. You need to get a 75% on the final to keep your letter grade. Markley does not answer questions about the assignment or exam content unless you ask him in class (responds with vague answers; not helpful).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have ever wondered what it's like to hate yourself, well sign up for a class with Brian Markley. He is inconsiderate of students. He does not take criticism lightly. He grades so poorly. Did I mention the only grades in his class are from quizzes and exams. All of the other professors run the class well, without giving students poor grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard work goes unnoticed; and grades do not represent the amount of work and effort that is put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When compared to other professors BLaw courses, it seemed he made his course more difficult. Often had in class quizzes that were not always simple, missing two questions was a 60%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Brian was a good professor and clearly cared about his students, just was not very engaging at times. This class is not hard and has little to no homework, but requires studying and memorization. If you attend class and study before exams, you will get an A no problem.

He offers a lot of extra credit and if you pay attention in class you will be fine. The lectures are interesting and he really knows what he is talking about and you can tell he really enjoys the subject. I feel like I learned a lot in the class and would definitely recommend this professor! I bought the textbook but ended up not needing it at all.

I don't understand the hatred towards Brian. I'm not the most intelligent guy, but his class was so much fun and interesting. He is such a laid-back teacher and he's excellent at teaching. He gives out lots of extra credit, and his tests aren't as hard as people say. All you need to do is pay attention in this class and you'll be fine!

This is an easy class if you show up to lecture knowing what was discussed last time. There are occasional quizzes but as long as you study your notes throughout the semester you will be fine, and it will help you with the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to maintain a good gpa, avoid this professor at all cost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible professor that does not care about his students, do not take this class if you care about your grades and mental health. For finals week he gave us nothing just like every exam weve taken and only had 1 homework assignment all semester which he graded extremely hard. Save yourself and sign up with one of the other 2 professors who care
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. You're going to need to put in a little outside time reviewing the concepts because the content is difficult and extensive, but Prof. Markley is incredibly knowledgeable and well-spoken. While he does grade on the harder side, he makes this clear and allows for notecards on the exam that are as beneficial as you make them.

This professor sets his expectations very clearly and his class may be hard for people who struggle with reading comprehension. Otherwise the professor is very good at explaining the important concepts of the class. Attendance is not mandatory, but the professor may randomly call on you or there may be a quiz that you miss. Overall loved this class

Professor Markley is nice and seems like a good person, but he is a tough grader. I think him being a lawyer creates an expectation on his students to think like lawyers and catch onto/memorize everything super quickly. Take BLAW301 with the professor (I forgot his name) who allows you to do corrections on your exams!

Prof sets clear expectations and sticks to them. I would disagree that tests are hard. Many tests/quizzes reuse questions/ideas posited in the lectures, so diligent note taking means quite approachable testing. 
I also think lectures are clear. They start by introducing a new concept, then applying them for student discussion.
Prof is approachable.

Lectures are long and use complex legal vocabulary that can be difficult for non-law students to understand. Tests are very hard and frustrating, with tricky questions that don't reflect students' knowledge. Attendance is optional,  But missing may mean a 0 on pop quiz. While a good person and lawyer, the teaching style needs improvement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Needs to work on explanatrion

She does care about students, her concern focuses on whether they performed well and felt confident. If students answer positively, she is pleased. However, if they struggle, she simply tells them to spend more time studying rather than offering help, as she expects there to be no issues.

Terrible. Horrible. Never learned a thing in her class. Learned everything from the book. We were instructed to do group projects instead of a final, but we weren't given any instructions until the night before it was due. I think she would rather lecture on a class about her life than have any of the classes she actually "teaches."

Liked the first third but it devolved quickly afterwards. Lectures often sparse and disorganized w/lots of personal tangents. Tests are way too long & both of mine came back with grading errors. Often completely misses the point of a question being asked. Contradictory update emails. Cares about students at least. Still a very frustrating class

This was my second semester with her. You just gotta learn how she rolls. Homework and tests can be a lot. Our second test was take-home, which was nice. The final was a group project, which was way better than an actual exam. Coming to class is rarely useful, as she rambles and doesn't provide good examples. She did bump my grade up at the end!

During the 50 min lecture she spend 30 mins talking about her life every single class through semester. She does not teach the concepts precisely nor go through lot of examples. She also gives hard exams out of lecture and rants on students for not studying for the exams. She gives grades very generously tho.

She is very understanding and genuinely seems to care a lot about her students. Her lectures were ok, but not very specific so I got a lot more out of the textbook. I didn't find grading to be tough in this class, and she also offers a lot of extra credit throughout the semester.

Her tests are insane - made way too long for a 1 hour class period. The only reason I got an A was because we convinced her to make the second test take-home and the final be a group project. She is caring, but also expects a ton. Going to class is such a waste of time because she just rambles about herself, never doing helpful example problems.

Dr. Pasik-Duncan expects a lot from her students. Everyone that I knew felt overwhelmed. Regularly spent 8-12 hours on take-home tests, several hours on homework as well. Also, not a great lecturer for me - read the book if you want to learn. She does care a lot about her students, and will communicate that.

IDK what the last two reviews are thinking, but this class was awful. Completely online with pointless lectures that have very few in class examples worked out. Basically just her talking over handwritten notes on Zoom. I learned 99% of this class outside of lectures from the book. Pretty easy class though if you're ok teaching yourself stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pasik-Duncan is a highly respected mathematician and has tons of connections in the world of academia. She's not great with technology, so her teaching online is somewhat dull. Her teaching isn't her strong point, though-- it's the opportunities she'll give you to get involved in academia and research. If you're serious wrt mathematics, take her.

Very passionate about teaching and it's clear she wants her students to succeed. Lectures can be a little unproductive at times but it's nothing reading the textbook can't fix. I normally hate math, but I loved this class.

Dr. Pasik-Duncan cares a lot about her students, and is truly passionate about teaching. That said, her lectures are often unorganized and at times, scatter-brained. If you want to actually learn the material, you'll probably have to just teach yourself. There are many opportunities for extra credit, though, so you might not even have to.

Bozenna is a unique professor. She truly understands the material, but is sometimes scatter brained and unorganized. The material and tests are definitely honors level, but she gives many extra credit opportunities. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. This class would've been hard without taking calc 1 before.

Usually gets rid of the final. She rambles a lot during class and doesn't really teach anything. If you want to learn the material just read the book. HW was graded pretty tough but it wasn't really worth much and it got better when our grader switched. She drops two anyway. Look at her website for more info, she has past classes' info posted there

Dr. Pasik-Duncan is really hard to understand in a classroom setting. This is not because of her thick accent, but because she simply isn't always organized.  Extra credit makes the class a joke. Whatever you do, email her as a last resort because she thinks student's emails crash her computer.  Good luck, and remember the five C's.

She can be confusing at times and goes off topic a lot. But she means well and tries to make us not just understand math but to enjoy it. If you do the HW and read the book, at the minimum you should do fine. But she does announce extra credit in class so you may miss some by not showing up. Easy A is you study plus optional final.

Spends over half of the class talking about her own life and then quickly goes over a few useless examples before telling students to reference the book. Changes the format and gives weird questions on exams just for fun. Grades everything very easily and gives easy extra credit, final is optional if you have an A. She's a nice lady.

Very passionate and nice almost too passionate. She always spends the first 15 minutes of class talking about how important stats is. It gets a little annoying. If you try, you'll get an A no problem.

Very enthusiastic, goes off on tangents. If you ask a question be prepared for a long roundabout answer that may or may not be helpful. Pretty thick accent but not so difficult to understand. Material is somewhat confusing but large opportunities for extra credit.

She actually cares about students and what they learn. If you do the homework and practice tests it's pretty easy to get an A. But the three tests are all very different which makes it a little more difficult. There's a lot of opportunity for extra credit but you have to check her website because she doesn't anyways announce it in class

Pasik-Duncan genuinely cares about your grade. She does have a thick accent, but you will get used to it. She explains the concepts very well. To get a good grade, you need to take good lecture notes. She bases her exams off the examples from the lecture. Do your homework!!! Her tests are fair and straight forward. She offers alot of extra credit.

This was a large class lecture in an auditorium. If you have trouble hearing you may need to sit near the front. She really cares about her students success and holds office hours. If you need help, I suggest that you get it. Tests are straight cut. If you pay attention in class and really study, you should be fine!

She is nearly impossible to understand in her lectures. She rarely stays on topic and she is far from organized. The only reason I passed with an A is because I took Calculus in highschool. Lab section TAs are more helpful than she was.

Pasik-Duncan is very passionate about what she does, and always gives 110%. Her accent and syntax is easily understandable after a little listening, and her class is very doable if you attend lecture and do your homework--she won't throw any curveballs to screw you over. Basically, she's a good professor, and always willing to help her students.

Dr. Pasik-Duncan is very passionate about math and she truly cares about every student (even in a class of 400). With no previous calculus experience this class was very easy and her lectures were always clear. She does have an accent, but you will get used to it after the first lecture. I hope to have her again in the future!
I love her passion and enthusiasm, she cares a lot for individual the individual student. She does have a fairly strong accent but as long as you pay attention and focus it is easy to understand.

Although her accent can be overwhelming at first, it gets much easier to understand with time. She is an extremely effective teacher and writes all of her notes by hand, which makes them much easier to understand. She cares deeply for every student, which is apparent everyday. I would highly recommend her!

She is very hard to understand. Her accent is horrible. The TA could make the difference. This class was super easy for me since I had Calc in high school but if you haven't had calc before you WILL BE LOST

I have had Professor Pasik-Duncan for more than one class. Her regular teaching is probability and statistics. I took this class with her and while it was easy I did most of my learning from the textbook. She gives a little preparation for proofs but all around I didn't feel I was prepared for the next level. Not recommended for 290.
Professor Pasik-Duncan is a good teacher. She cares about her students success and tries to make the subject more interesting. I would highly recommend her for any probability/statistics class.

Bozenna must have gotten stuck in as Math 290 teacher at the last minute because her knowledge on the subject was negligible. Hardly anything she said made sense and she often contradicted herself. Class was extremely easy to get an A but was very frustrating for someone pursuing higher level math to come out with little knowledge on the subject.

Took Hnrs Calc 2 with her, she was great. She really cares about the success of her students and raves more about them than she does about her research. Does a great job in the classroom lecturing. Tests were actually easier than expected, kind of a let down considering all the hype and build up that she injected into the class.

Prof. Pasik-Duncan cares deeply whether or not her students succeed in her class and their other classes. She encourages you to do your best and expects you to perform well because she is performing at her best for you. Take any of her courses and you will absolutely love her and her stories! You will master the material with her help!

Wow, great professor.  She creates a different teaching approach for each of her classes.  She never goes to bed until after 2:00 because she is working on the next day's lecture, she asks the students if they would like something different in class.  She also lets you choose 5 of 8 questions to answer on tests.  My favorite professor ever.

Her probability theory class was interesting. I thoroughly enjoyed her class. Her accent is awesome, too! She says things in a way that make them memorable, which really helped me retain what I learned.
She does everything she can to make sure her students learn...although sometimes it'll guilt trip you. Just listen carefully during class...Can be hard to make it all out sometimes. Good teacher.
I thought she was a very effective and clear instructor, especially for a difficult subject like math.  She was also a very easy grader and gave everyone A's and B's.
I'm surprised by the negative comment - I thought she was an extremely effective instructor for this somewhat difficult subject.  I don't think I would have learned calc better from ANYONE else!
What the hell?  She knows her stuff and she grades fairly, but her lectures border on unintelligible sometimes.

The class itself is good, the grading setup is horrendous. You get one midterm and that's it; if you do bad on it, your only hope is the final. Someone had the bright idea to set up the class like this and put an A at 93.5%. Get ready to wait till eternity for grades to be updated.

Rafe is one of the best professors I have ever had. He's a super smart guy and very respected and lived up to it. Super easy to talk to, super accessible, and a really good lecturer. Take good notes, come to class, and you'll end up with an A

I've had Rafe for a few different classes, but most recently herpetology. Exams and quizzes were not difficult (online, open note), but get the textbook -- many questions are based on figures or text from it. Rafe is passionate about his research and ensuring you succeed, and herpetology was a really interesting class.
Knowledgeable and caring for students. Tough content and a subject matter expert. Little dry but what did you expect. Reptiles rule.

He is an okay professor, he talks a lot during class and lectures are long. There are not many tests but a lot of quizzes. You have to really pay attention, he likes you to know details that I found often pointless.

He's definitely one of the best professors I have ever met so far. The exam is based on the question sheet he gave you, so as far as learning all of them, you should be good.
Easy and interesting course. Just breeze over the readings each week, which are provided for free on Canvas. The exams were easy to study for with his provided study guide.

This course is great. It's a very easy arts & humanities fulfillment but, Professor Bruce is also an elite lecturer. His presentations each day are great with lots of photos and minimal words. He clearly is very passionate about the subject and it makes the class a lot more interesting. This is the course to take for your arts & humanities req.

If you are debating taking a class with him, DO IT. He's so funny and very pop-culture knowledgeable so his lectures are very engaging. You can get by not doing a single page of reading and he gives a complete study guide for all tests.

Amazing guy! TA was also incredible. Attendance is taken through very easy pop quizzes over the readings, but he drops the lowest three so it's nothing to worry about. There are two course practicas due by the end of the semester, but they are interesting and pretty low maintenance. His lectures are amazing and it's clear he is passionate.

Genuinely the best professor I've had, I scheduled my courses next semester to fit in with his class that's how awesome of a teacher he is! His lectures are never boring and his personal experiences in archaeology really makes his class stand out. 100/10

Bruce is the GOAT. His lectures are super fun and he gives plenty of supplemental info that either helps you understand the lecture or it's just entertaining. Really easy to study for his exams since the study guides contain the actual exam questions. You learn so much in his classes without the stress that usually comes along with learning.

Beloved. Lectures are 80-150 slides long but interesting and there's always something funny. He knows stuff so well and most pictures are from his own adventures. The nicest guy. Test example = study guide with 40 questions. 30 will be on the test. you pick 20 and answer 3-5 points about each. Super simple. His classes fill FAST. 100% recommend.

This dude is so awesome!!! He gives unlimited attempts on quizzes and provides great resources. He grades very fairly and is open if you feel like you didn't get the grade you deserve. 10/10. LOVE THIS GUY!!!!!!!!
This is the most amazing professor at this school. He is truly so caring and all he wants is his students to enjoy his class and succeed. Definitely take his classes, they are so easy and so fun.

A solid professor who makes every class and assignment genuinely valuable for you as an accountant. He's very knowledgeable about the material he teaches, adds a touch of humor to lectures, and has a way of keeping class periods engaging. He responds promptly to emails and seems to grade fairly.
he's cool and pretty neat

AWFUL!!! He uses pre2000s technology and when asked why, his excuse is we need to know coding. There was no analysis of financial statements or transactions in an accounting class with him. Cal is a good professor and definitely cares about students, he does grade based off of personal preference, though. Cal is great and will get you career opportunities if you continue to take classes with him or work in student media
Great professor who really cares about his students

Was always open to help with anything you needed to understand or learn outside of class. Participation in activities outside of class matter towards your grade and your learning growth. Cal is fantastic. He actually does everything in his power for everyone to have A's. It does take some time to learn how to use Adobe Premier well, but you can use it for free in the building and he is always there to help. There are small weekly assignments, but they are super easy, and a good way to get a lot of easy points. Good through email.

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Genuinely cares about your success. Some assignments might be hard for beginners, but he is sure to help you if you need it. Its not as big as a load as it first seems.

Go to class, do the volunteer hours, and projects and you will get a good grade. He grades you based on your ability he knows you have and not a flat scale which is nice. Fun class and one of the most valuable connections to get work that I have made at KU! Taking the class a second time for credit because I loved it so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Cal is a great person. He wants his summer class to be fun and it can be fun and difficult at times. Make sure you have story ideas every week and do your stories because that is the majority of the class grade.

Class structure: Must work 2 "shifts" per week (usually 1 hour working on a show). One final quiz. Four video projects growing in difficulty.  Take 210. You'll meet awesome people!!

He is a very intelligent but is not a good presenter.  His lectures frequently went off track. He uses his own textbook which is very diffucult to understand. Homework doesn't help for exams and he is not accessible.

Professor Laird is a good person but his teaching is awful. He speaks exactly how his text book is written: too academic for students to understand. reviews.comment: This class was difficult but Dr. Laird is nice. Just a bit difficult to understand sometimes.

Great professor if you like reading the textbook - all of his lectures linked up perfectly with the assigned reading and he always explained topics in good detail, especially during office hours. Some complained about lecture being hard to understand, but reading the textbook makes the class way more enjoyable and easier to comprehend.

I don't know why people are complaining about Chem 190 so much. The only thing you need to do is READ THE TEXTBOOK (crazy concept ikr?). It is that simple. Keep up on your reading and you'll be fine in the course. I ended up with a 96%. The hard parts to understand are the quantum theory stuff but the main thing you need to get is quantization.

I would not recommend this course for first-year students. The problem sets, textbook readings, and tests did not align very well. The problem sets were so hard that sometimes the TAs did not even know how to solve problems. The tests are curved, but still most people got Cs as their raw score. Tests are a large part of your grade. He cannot teach.

Laird is clearly an intelligent man. However, he does not--for the life of him--know how to teach or transmit all the information in his brain. He assumes you will pick up subjects like quantum mechanics easily (you won't with his teaching) and gives you homework that will take you more than 5 hours at minimum. He's a nice guy, but not a good prof.

Dr. Laird is a skilled teacher and if you're smart you'll have no issue with CHEM190. Professor Laird is very passionate about the content but you will have to do a lot of outside work to make sure you understand the material. I found it extremely difficult to both motivate myself to go to class and then pay attention once I got there. Two positives though: cool demos (like 4 total I think) that effectively demonstrated what he was talking about and an automatic curve on tests - square root * 10.

Chem150 is a HARD class for freshmen. I took this class as a junior, and I realized that I would have failed this class as a freshman. You're going to have a to dedicate a lot of time to this class. It's definitely one of the weed out classes, so if you feel like you suck at this, you're going to be a crappy engineer - don't. This class just sucks.
This class is HARD. It will take up a lot of your time during a semester if you want a good grade, so don't take this class with any other hard classes you may have in one semester. Good luck!

Very hard class. Obviously in place to see if you are really serious about engineering. Tests are insane even if you feel like you understand everything. Sometimes what he is trying to say doesn't come across as clear as he probably thinks it does. He is extremely smart though, never arrogant though, which is a huge plus.
Dr. Laird is a very nice guy but sometimes he is hard to understand. This class is obviously a weed out class for Engineers. READ THE CHAPTER AND GO TO ALL THE OFFICE HOURS AND CLASSES! Good cluck

Dr. Laird's lectures are pretty engaging, considering the technical level of the material.  He is very smart, but not arrogant at all.  He seems very aware of how difficult his tests are, and he curves accordingly.  I feel like I learned more than my C would indicate.

Seemed to be a really nice guy, but did not want to be teaching this class.  Was called back from California for one semester and was forced to teach it.  Curve was huge at the end of the semester (square root grade *10+ 5 pts), but still was difficult to get a really good grade. Felt like I didnt really learn anything in the class.
Exceptional professor for a course on classical molecular simulation, he really knows his stuff!  Very helpful in office hours.

too hard, derives formulas all day, tests over material not emphasized in course, expects infinite knowledge of calculus

Burcu is one of the nicest professors that I have ever had. BSAN 302 can be a tough class for some, but she does her best to really help everybody out. I recommend just going to class, paying attention, and participating in discussion.

Best. teacher. ever. He takes his pedagogical responsibilities seriously, and it shows. My personal fave.

pushes students to really think about the topic. he's teaching what he knows, so he does a good job.

cool teacher. very enthusiastic

HIGHLY recommend this lab. probably my favorite college class i've ever taken. All policies were clear, there's great communication with TAs, absence makeups, and very fun and laidback labs in my opinion.

reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

She goes very fast
If you take this class and don't get an A, you've got issues. Seriously, this class is VERY easy. You will have a TA most likely, but the TA is normally a nice, intelligent person.

This class is super easy. 10 point quiz each week and she puts study guides online that are almost the same as the quiz, same for the two 50pt exams you will take. A TA will teach the class but the TA's are very helpful and know what they are talking about. Class is once a week and very laid back. I would definitely recommend taking if needed!
Class is relatively easy, if you pay attention and read ahead for the quizzes. The TA's help out alot, too, if you get a good one!
Do me a favor and get an A in this class. its very easy. any my TA was adorable!

great experience. every single lab is interesting and engaging. if you have taken a bio lecture previously or currently, then it is SO easy. you really shouldnt get anything lower than an A in this class

I love Julie. She is amazing and so helpful to the students she deals with daily.  And she deals with so many of them, over a thousand as the director of labs. Very good at teaching the basic 101 course

Her TAs grade the assignments and they grade very easily. She is very knowledgeable on the subjects at hand and super kind. 

This class was combined with Introduction to Civil Engineering when I took it and the curriculum was based 80% on CE and only 20% on ARCE the whole year. ARCEs won't get much out of it.

Dr. Bennett is a real expert in her field and you can tell that she is very passionate about the work she does. This class was an intro to engineering so there was not much material in lectures. reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Bennett is super sweet and an expert in her field! You can see how enthusiastic she is about the class and subject. She truly wants all her students to succeed and is very fair. Definitely one of the nicest professors from my first semester here at KU. She grades on attendance and assignments so just keep up with those and you'll be great!

If public speaking is not your strength, the class can be challenging, but it is designed to help you improve. Practice your speeches, put in effort, and earn an A!!

I would recommend taking the course with Cui Wenrong to save a lot of stress. This guy is a rough grader and you'll really have to work for the A. However, he's very accessible outside of class and overall a nice guy.
CB was a great professor, the only reason I did "so many papers" was because just COMS classes have lots of speeches. He was always super understanding and a great guy to have as a teacher!

always gives helpful advice and constructive criticism, setting you up for success. super accessible and gives all the information to pass the class with an easy A. can tell he really cares and always takes a lot of time to edit outlines and gives very helpful feedback!

one of my favorite instructors of all time. literally the nicest person ever and was ALWAYS there to help and answer questions. always replied super fast to emails also! recommend him again and again, super amazing person overall!

Berger was one of the most down-to-earth professors. He isn't a hard grader and will give you solid feedback on improving your speeches. He takes attendance so you need to show up to lectures. Overall, a fantastic professor, and would take him again.

Overall, be prepared for worksheets and some reading to go along with the quizzes. Not very good feedback even if you receive a bad grade on something.

The only good thing about this class is that he gives out every deadline for all assignments for the entire semester within the first week. Everything else is not so nice, he graded me more harshly on a review essay on a speech than my English professor did on any of our papers. He gives like a three word feed back even if you score bad.

He's really nice, but sometimes the class can get a bit boring. He talks a lot during lectures, which makes it hard to stay focused. The assignments aren't too hard, and it's easy to participate. If you need the credit it will be an easy A. If you try somewhat and show up you'll get an A.

He has a tendency to ramble a lot and it can be difficult to follow. He's very nice and easy to get along with, but will get passive-aggressive when the class doesn't do the readings. There's a bit of favoritism towards the Italian students. It's clear he cares a lot about his students and their success.

Very easy grader. This was a Freshman seminar so not much homework. Attendance wasn't mandatory due to COVID, but you do get a participation grade so do the readings and talk during class. He is flexible and caring towards students.

Patrizio is great! He's caring, funny, and sweet. He strives to make sure each student in class succeeds, always gives great feedback on projects and essays, and wants to establish a personal relationship with each student. How much he likes his job shines through with every lecture.
He's amazing
Mr. Burrows is a great teacher, you get what you put in with his class, if you work hard, a good grade will be achieved. He is helpful and I'm glad I had him as an Eng 102 teacher.

This was my first and last ENGL class at KU and I loved it. Cedric Burrows is a fair teacher and grades well. He gives random attendance quizzes and the projects (website and manual) are enjoyable. Attend class and an A will be achieved!
He's really not that focused on African American History. He grades the first paper harshly, but he gets easier as the semester goes on.

Burrows is an excellent professor. He grades fairly (sometimes a bit more harshly than some would agree with-- constructive criticism isn't always a bad thing)and his teachings actually help with your reading and writing skills. However he doesn't look at his emails often so you have to email him way ahead of time for him to get the message.

Great teacher, keeps you interested with various forms of media, using movies, documentaries, and various articles/books to his disposal.  Attending class is much needed and be sure to participate. He is easy to work with when it comes to help with papers and will give many good pointers on how to improve your paper.  Great ENG 102 teacher!

Mr. Burrows was a great teacher. His topics showed a consistent theme of African American history, and I found myself getting tired of it. However, he made the topics interesting and I learned a lot from his course. He made class engaging, fun, and very open for discussion. Bottom Line I had a great time in his class and I highly recommend it.

He's a pretty good teacher overall. However, he likes to focus only on African American history. I agree that it's an interesting topic, but after awhile, it will get extremely old to talk about only one topic. It's an English class, and he should focus on a variety of subjects
I agree that he is too geared towards African-American studies. Doesn't really allow you to choose a topic.
He is a horrible teacher.  It drove me crazy that an English teacher didn't speak English well.  Going to class was torturous.
avoid this teacher! I use to like english before taking his course

A very biased teacher. If you aren't black or a democrat you will not be able to get a good grade in the class, He only checks his e-mail once a week during his office hours, so good luck trying to schedule an appointment with him to talk about a paper. He is  a very unfair grader and only wants to talk about African Americans. Avoid having him.

He is one of the worst teachers I've ever had. His entire class is geared toward racism and how Africa Americans have been screwed by white people, I agree, African Americans have been shafted but any subject gets super old after an entire semester.
The class was alright. It seemed to be oriented in a high school manner though. portfolio checks? I don't need some to hold my hand to make sure I keep track of my work.
Not bad... But IMPOSSIBLE to get a good grade!

I really enjoy this class. He is an extremely fair grader. You can't get a crap paper past him, but when you really try and write a good paper, you earn a good grade. He also has very interesting topics for discussion and writing. Great class!

He's a good teacher, and knows what he's talking about. he's pretty easy, just do your work and write your papers. you'll get a better grade each paper you write. he'll help you if you just ask. he's a fairly easy grader.
No Comments
He is super interesting but be ready to learn. His exams are pretty straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Buechner is one of the best professors I've had at KU! Lectures are super entertaining & he provides you with lots of material to be successful (office hours, review sessions, vocab lists, study guides, etc.). Exams can be challenging, but if you put in the work, you'll be fine and find that you come away from the class actually knowing tons!!!

I am now a pre-med junior and this was my first biology class I took and he was ALL over the place in lectures, spoke at a million miles an hour, and he had only taught super upperlevel biol classes before him teaching his first intro to bio class. Made the test way too hard for freshman and a stick in the mud. Least favorite professor out of 15.

He lost his train of thought a lot so lectures were super difficult to follow. Tests were difficult, bizarre, and unpredictable (and biweekly!). I found that I had to read the chapters and watch a lot of videos because the lectures were not helpful.

Professor Buencher is an interesting guy to say the least. He really loves cell bio and it's easy to tell. There are test bi-weekly and if you don't keep up with the reading (a lot) then you will do poorly. His lectures are not good for he can't seem to focus on one thing without being distracted by something in his head. Nice guy, funny, difficult

We had tests every other week in this class and you definitely had to study to do good on them. I took really good notes in class and did fine. Buechner is a funny guy but not the best at lecturing. You can tell he tries to make class interesting though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Brilliant, kind, caring, and loves helping students. He has trouble getting to the point in lecture, so you often have to just teach yourself from the book. Besides lab, tests are the only grade in the class. Tests happened every other week, and were very detailed. you MUST read the book to pass. His final was almost identical to the practice one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: His class was really hard and required a lot of effort. I felt like I was taking a pop quiz because every test I took was not at all what I spent time studying. I would recommend taking a lot of time to really understand what you are learning because you never know what he might throw on test day.

He's extremely knowledgeable; almost too knowledgeable to be teaching an intro bio course. His lectures were intense and he got off topic a lot, making it difficult to take detailed notes. Tests are 35% of your grade and are lecture based, so pay attention in class! Attendance isn't technically mandatory but you won't pass if you don't attend class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's extremely charismatic & knows what he's talking about. However, his lectures are confusing & he switches topics frequently, which is confusing. He does lots of in-class demonstrations, which is rarely useful & takes up half the class period. Attendance isn't technically mandatory, but 20% of your grade depends on in-lecture activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Poor lecturer. Hes a cool dude, very charismatic and funny, but he spends more time making jokes and going on personal tangents than he does teaching. He stops in the middle of concepts to go on to other concepts and rarely returns to the original point. Youll do better if you read the book, but the tests are over very random bits of info.

The class wasn't hard, but you need to be willing to put in the time to study the book. His lectures are hard to make sense of sometimes, so it's important to attend and pay attention. However, he also puts his lectures online as videos so that helps if you don't want to go. The grade is really only based on the tests, so study!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He doesnt finish sentences or concepts in lecture. The tests are unpredictable and feel impossible to study for. Ive spent so much of my time focusing on just this class and studying in nearly all of my free time and almost none of the material in notes/lec are on exams. He moved our test a week early and told us about it with 3 days in advance.

He's an extremely smart professor. He knows so much that it is his biggest weakness as a bio150 professor. His tests were tough often looking for answers that was only said once. If you work hard & rewatch his lectures you will do good. He has a test once a week which is both good & bad. Great professor. If you put in the work I would recommend him

He's an incredibly smart professor--so smart that he really shouldn't be teaching a 100 level class. He expected the students to keep up with the very fast-paced but info-heavy lectures, which most people struggled to. You do learn a lot of biology, and his powerpoint animations are helpful when trying to understand complex topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He knows what he is talking about and is precise when lecturing, but often goes on tangents. There were weekly tests that were nearly unpredictable in terms of content. You could pay close attention and study hard just to receive a 60% on a test, or not pay attention or study and get a 90% on the test just based on the week. Very difficult class.

This class was a real challenge. Lectures were long and sucked at 8 am. You don't have to attend class but if you don't it will hurt you. We also had a test every week which were hard because there was always information on the test you had not heard of before. Professor is nice but I didn't do as good as I wanted to which such hard tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Felt bad for him; he was definitely teaching a class way below his skill level, and it showed. Awkward and manic at times. Tests focused on the most minute, random details, and curves were applied frequently because people were floundering. Can get an A even if you skip lectures; just get your clicker points & use his online summaries to study.

This class had such a weird structure. Tests every week, and the questions were not very predictable. You can study hard and pay attention to lectures and still miss points on random things. His lecture was very unorganized and all over the place. He went on so many tangents. He does offer a lot of resources on blackboard that helped a little
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Buechner clearly knows his material but as difficulty expressing his knowledge for a 100 level course. There are challenging tests every week with unpredictable questions sometimes. Be sure to read and attend office hours or tutor sessions, and you should be fine though.
Loved the professor but would rather him teach a smaller class. being in a class with over 600 people made it hard to be personable with him

Tests every week, but he said next time he teaches they will be every other. As long as you study, you will do fine. He is a little spastic with lecturing, but connecting what you're able to get from lecture with the book really allows you to understand pretty well most of the time. He's a great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class has a test every Thursday morning, but you are able to drop the 2 lowest scores. The lectures go fast and this professor does not give good explanations, be ready to rewatch lectures if you want to do okay on the tests. Tests are very difficult and is all taken from small things he says throughout the lecture, nothing from the book.

He is very smart even though he is all over the place. His smartness sometimes makes the lectures confusing for us who haven't take bio in years. He records his lectures so you can always go back to them. He does make the lectures engaging with humor which is nice. But he does do weekly tests which are hard, you have to understand the topic to pass

Very confusing lectures as he is all over the place and it is hard to follow. Other than that he knows what he is talking about and helps you understand what you are struggling with. His class is very test heavy though and it is like studying for finals every single week. Be prepared to study all the time for his class. The tests are very HARD.

One of the most confusing professors I've ever had. Tests almost every week, and the material on the test had nothing to do with what was covered in lectures. Lectures were disorganized, scatterbrained, confusing, and full of random tangents and useless information. If you're a bio major you'll probably have to have him, so good luck.

Buechner does a good job immersing students in learning. He presents the material quickly, so take notes and make use of his recorded lectures. The textbook will be helpful, but not mandatory. Tough quizzes and tests, but he curves the class. Try to attend lectures over watching recordings. Knows his stuff, and clearly loves his topic.

Dr. Buechner is by far one of the best professors I have had thus far in my college career. He is a tough grader and seems very scatterbrained at times, but he is an engaging lecturer and thoroughly wants you to succeed. Attend lecture and review sessions, study old exams, and go over his lecture summaries. Work hard and it'll pay off!

Here's a few words that describe Dr. Buechner and his class: Hilarious, scatterbrained, charismatic, intelligent, difficult, but fair.    He offers tons and tons of different resources on blackboard, I highly recommend going over the old tests(all of them), until you get every single answer right without checking, and also watching his lectures.

Hilarious and an active, engaging lecturer. Very interesting class but also very challenging. Grade consists of participation via clicker points, best 9 out of 10 tests (only 15 minutes each), and the final. Tests are VERY challenging, mostly short answer, applied questions and problems rather than memory work. Information dense lectures.
One of the best classes I have ever taken. Absolutely amazing professor. Tough, but worth it.

Pro tips: ALWAYS bring your clicker, go to review sessions, study the heck out of the lecture summariesre-watch the video lectures, and go to class every day. His class is incredibly hard, and there's almost no memorization aspect. If you can truly grasp the concepts he teaches, you might pass. Oh, and he has random interjections all the time.

This class is deceivingly difficult; it will require a lot of studying.  Despite this, Dr. Buechner is a great professor.  He is extremely helpful and wants everyone to succeed.  Writes lecture summaries after each class and posts them on Blackboard which I found very helpful for studying.

Buechner is an amazing professor and a great guy. He's incredibly helpful and understanding. Makes lecture interesting and fun, and does a fabulous job of explaining the material. There is a test almost every week, and the final is hard, but definitely doable. Just study the material weekly, go to class, pay attention. You gotta love this guy!
Great teacher! Really passionate about what he does and is willing to go out of his way to get to know you and help you understand the material.
Likes to trick people.  Tests often cover material outside of class discussions.  Avoid this guy.

He was a really fun teacher! It was definitely a lot of work to try to get good grades on the exams but an A is possible. Take notes and also read over the lecture summaries. He is also very helpful outside of class.

Great and interesting teacher. Most hilarious teacher I've had. Tests are hard and maticulous. If you want an A write down every word the man says in lecture and study it like the back of your hand and you will get an A.
Good teacher, but class is impossible. Extremely hard, really hard.
Easily my favorite teacher at KU. His lectures are fun and interesting, and you can tell he's passionate about the subject. He wants to see his students succeed and is very helpful outside of class.
He gets on random tangents frequently. Teaches his opinions like they are facts. If you can avoid him, do.
fun...
Good person and teacher, just a hard class...

He is definitely my favorite teacher yet.  He has a crazy sense of humor, and actively tries to make the lectures interesting (which they are). His tests require an understanding of material over mindless regurgitation, which some may find more difficult. I would strongly strongly recommend him.

Dr. Beuchner is without a doubt the best teacher/professor I have ever had.  While his class is quite hard, I learned a lot from him.  Lectures are very thorough, and make sure to have somebody take notes for you if you miss the class.  Lecture summaries will not get you an A.  He wants everybody to succeed and is very helpful!

This was the toughest class I have taken so far in my life. Dr. Buechner is an extremely good teacher and integrates the information at a level the class can understand and tests mainly on application of ALL the information. I got an A in the class, but it was hard earned. Lectures are fun and very informative. The book is not needed.

hard tests, do not take at the same time as organic chem if you are not a natural genuis, and have to work hard to get good grades. he is a funny teacher and kept the class entertained. and you actually learn something

This is the best class I've taken at KU for 3 reasons: 1Dr. Buechner is passionate about Microbiology and sincerely wants the class to learn.  2)Microbiology is an interesting and highly applicable subject.  3)Dr. Buechner expects a lot out of you and structures the class so that you can actually learn rather than cram twice and then forget it.
Probably one of the best courses I took at KU.  It was interesting and entertaining.

Informative lectures, but his frequent mumbling and tangents are VERY distracting. I often feel awkward in class watching him jump about and occasionally he’ll say something like “give it to me boy” that really makes thing feel weird. I’m not satisfied at all with KU teachers, and this course is no different. His daily lecture summaries are the onl

His lectures overall are informative. He's very helpful outside class with questions, but his test are really hard.  He doesn’t do a great job of letting you know what is going to be on the test. Having a test every week sucks, the TA’s are so strict on grading. Needs to reorganize how he gives his tests.  He better curve, the test average is 71%.

Buechner might be the best professors I've had at KU, and I've had some fantastic instructors. His lectures are a little disjointed, and his tests are more than challenging, but his enthusiasm, good humor and willingness to help really leave no excuses for not receiving a satisfactory grade. Fantastic teacher, fantastic person.
Awesome, hilarious

A very challenging class but you will definitely learn a lot from this teacher. He seemed to be very weird and nervous at first, but that is just his personality. His tests are almost all application, so if you just know the facts you may even end up with a C or worse. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Great teacher, although a little eccentric.  His tests are definately a little bit on the challenging side, but if you studied a few hours before the quiz, you should've been good.  His lecture summary onlines were key to studying.  Just compare them w/ your own notes to fill in missing information and you'll be golden.  Also, always ask questions!
No Comments
Difficult class but XTREMELY interesting! Keep up with reading & ask many questions to clarify lectures.
No Comments

Oh my god! Maintaining an A in his class is extremely tough...sometimes I feel like biting him, seriously...He is an extremely nice guy and I like him a lot but his tests are driving me nuts..one day u are in heaven and another day you are in hell....If takin this class along with O chem...Good luck, no time for chem...Man!!!!

The class was tough...i wouldn't recommend being enrolled in more than 12 hours while taking this class! Buechner and his TA's were very helpful and going to the review sessions helps. Yet his lectures were very unclear...he jumps around quite a bit, so ask questions to clarify what he says because those weekly tests are tough!!

Great teacher, you'll learn a lot in his class. His tests are pretty hard, but if you go to his review session the night before it will help a lot. Trust me on this one though: DO NOT BUY THE BOOK. I paid over $100 for it and used it once for a take-home test. His lectures are sufficient for studying. Use a friends book if you really need to.
ok but tests are hard
He's a good teacher, but he's not easy, the class is managable though.  I haven't taken his final yet, and I hear horror stories about the comprehensive final.
His test have nothing to do with what he talks about in class, and he acts as if its the only class you're taking
No Comments

He's a great teacher. The tests are hard. You have them every week, so slacking is not an option. If you have questions he's more than willing to help. He keeps me awake during class with his random comments and funny demonstrations. He tries to keep the class interested.
No Comments

It amazed me that someone so loud and obnoxious could still put half the class to sleep.  Bring earplugs and your textbook and you will do fine.  Don't forget to brush up on fantasy molecules and martian bacterial taxonomy.

i suggest pre-studying for this class. buechner is passionate about the subject but his lecture style isn't very coherent. has hard quizzes which are graded hard and a hard final which is leniently graded. a cramped lecture hall right after lunch is a bad time for a class also
