Wacky guy, keeps lectures interesting.  Tests are tough, and you only have 20 minutes to take them.  Study like it's your religion.

Holds review sessions before every test.  He is pretty off-the-wall, but that has kept students interested in what's going on.  You have to really understand the concepts to do well on his tests, but it's possible to do quite well in his class.

He is the most ADHD teacher I have ever had.  He is all over the map all of the time.  His tests are very strange and nearly impossible to prepare for.  You dont have much of a choice for microbiology though.  Good luck.
So cheerful!  A little on the strange side, but who witha Ph.D. in biology isn't?  Very accessible and approachable.
Extremely entertaining.  He tends to get a little off track, but he always regains his focus.
good teacher, good man

I loved this class!  Dr. Buechner is very entertaining, although at times unorganized.  The quizzes were tricky, but after a couple you start to learn his style.  His audience participation activities are the best!

The class was harder than I thought it would be for a public speaking class and Evan can be really strict. Yet, he was also super helpful, made class fun, was clear on assignments. Evan is easily one of the better teachers I've had so far and I'm a much better speaker because of this class.
The class is a little annoying b/c it's public speaking, but Evan is very good and funny!
Prettay Prettay Prettay good. He helps out alot and is a pretty cool guy class is relatively easy but is the first public speaking class its scary at first but you get used to it

I was really dreading taking this class but Evan actually made it both fun and interesting. He is by far one of the best professors at KU. I would suggest you take the class from him if you get the chance.

If you're not that great at public speaking, this is the class for you. Evan Center is an awesome teacher, who uses South Park and The Office to teach students on how to give good speeches. You will write about 5 speeches during this class.

Not bad, but nothing great about her either. She has an accent but it's not difficult to understand. She was nice, but didn't always explain things in the best way. I learned more on MATH XL than I did in class. The class is a piece of cake though if you do the HW. I didn't go to like half of the classes and passed with a B.
Nobody works harder!
Hard to understand but she tries her best to answer questions.

This lady is from Argentina and it is very hard at times to understand what she is saying.  I think that since it is her first year teaching here, that it is hard for her to adjust but I know she tries her hardest.  The class is very easy though.
Professor Celikbas is a good teacher. He provides excellent notes and gives his own homework problems. If you take good notes and do the homework problems you can do well in this class.

His lectures on the material were very brief and simple to understand. The majority of the class period was spent doing example problems. I felt that I got a pretty good grasp on the subject with his teaching style. His testing is very fair and consisted of no trick problems. I would recommend him.

I have done fairly well in past math classes, but this professor made learning near impossible. He skips steps when doing examples in class. When writing theorems he just copies them symbol-for-symbol from the book. Homework problems were easy, but they did not prepare me for the tests. Tests were nothing like we did in class, absolutely terrible!

Very motivating teacher. He will help you out but you have to seek him out. He makes it very clear what needs to be known on tests and really cares about teaching. Small accent but I got used to it in 2 classes and I'm white.
Very challenging coursework, but Rogan takes most of it for completion. If you take advantage of it, you won't do well, but if you take the practice seriously, you will get an A.

It's a graduate level Quantum Mechanics class so be prepared for the material to be hard. He doesn't keep attendance and has video lectures if you miss class but I would highly recommend attending the class. Problem sets are long and tedious but he holds homework solving sessions to work on them together. Class is engaging and fair. Do the work.
Excellent professor, makes even very difficult material fun and engaging. Very forgiving with homework grading/deadlines but there is quite a bit of it to get through.
I really struggled in this class, but Professor Rogan was always helpful and understanding any time I needed help with an assignment or an extension for a deadline.

I actually took PHSX 214, honors physics 2. No complaints about Prof Rogan. Lectures are very engaging, and he actively encourages you to ask questions and participate. It's obvious that he wants students to succeed and pass his class, unlike some other profs I've had. I really like the way he has grades set up. Dude knows his stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, really loves the subject and cares about his students. His analogy game is on point, and he is great at explaining difficult concepts in understandable ways. If there is any issue, it is that he generally assumes you are fairly familiar with a level of calculus beyond that which the university requires you to take before PHSX 212.

Physics 2 is has incredibly difficult topics, but Dr. Rogan made it easy to be successful in the class. You can have worksheets for all the exams, and you can write whatever you want on them, so its pretty easy to get an A. His grading system is pretty lenient as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer teaching a conceptually difficult class. The textbook and the supplementary materials for PHSX 212 were made by the director of the KU Physics program, Fischer, and they are garbage, but luckily Rogan is very talented at teaching and lecturing and can help make up for this.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Physics 2 is hard regardless of your professor, so you have to consider that. I think Prof Rogan did a great job. His grading system is bizarre, but in the end it benefits YOU. He's very easy to speak to and/or get ahold of, and very much cares about his students. He keeps lectures very involved and will not bore you to sleep. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Rogan is an excellent professor. He is patient and extremely willing to help his student when they need it. The class material is not easy. The concepts are very strange to wrap your head around if you don't simply intuitively understand them, that's what makes the class hard. However, master the concepts and you'll master the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: i meanahhh i meann ahh you see you seee ahh LAPLACCCCCEEE TRANSFORM!!!!
Can not speak coherent sentences, minimal effort given, tough grader super unstructured class. 2nd worst prof in aerospace.
not good not good at all

This class was caused severe anxiety in almost everyone I talked to. The level of carelessness shown by Dr. Chao before, during, and after this class shows that it is a second-rate course. Every single graduate student I would speak to about this course says it would be a million times better if it were taught by Dr. Keshmiri.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Wow thanks so much for going back and lowering my grade after the grade deadline. How is this guy still a professor at this school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Read the literature.
A complete joke

Terrible lectures. (1hr 40 minutes) Mostly gibberish and rambling. A huge waste of time besides the in class assignments which only take the last ten minutes of class. He asks unclear questions and picks randomly for students to answer.

Dr. Chao is an amazing professor for how busy he is. The main objective of the course is to build a UAS with a group. Chao was a great professor and very helpful but when it came to lectures over 50% of the material is irrelevant information and for actually learning about the UAS and the parts to it most of that was taught by the GTA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Chao is an aerospace professor who clearly knows a lot about his subject matter. However, he is unable to convey this knowledge to the students. In most lectures, he spends 90% of the class blabbering nonsense and useless information. In the final 10 minutes, he tries to cram the useful information. Required class for ae majors but be prepared
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Chao is a great professor who tries to give his students in their first semester hands on experience in the field of aerospace engineering. Many people aren't prepared for this and don't put in the work on the project that they should but still expect to be given an A. He cares a lot if you ask questions and aren't afraid to say I don't know
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Chao spends most lectures babbling on about his research and our group projects rather than actually teaching. I learned way more through the lab, which was rarely overseen by him. The only reason I don't give him a 1 is that he is very accessible outside of class and emails back pretty quickly if you have questions
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Willing to work with his students on their level (as long as the student communicates what they need). Dr. Johnson cares about his students as individuals and his passion for what he teaches is clearly conveyed in his lectures. Be ready to dive in!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: He acts like he knows it all.  He is well versed and well published. He does not stick to the schedule but can be flexible about turning assignments in.  He makes it difficult sometimes by saying that you don't need to study and that everything you need to know you learned in class, and he forgets transfers are harder and less natural for students.

Fortunately, we were blessed with his stagering three years of public teaching experience.  Nothing like an aggorgant, pompous, blowheart to start your day!  If there was ever a poster child for needing to reform the tenure system, congrats Chris Johnson, you're the man!!!  Lucky for you, you didn't let us evaluate your class!

This teacher does not care about his students. All he cares about is his research and his ego. I would have loved to tell the department how I felt about this teacher, but we were not allowed to do course evals, so I couldn't! Don't trust this guy!
I had him for several classes and loved them.  Interesting and fun.
What an ****... dont waste your time...
By far the worst teacher I ever had the misfortune of studying from at KU.  He would much rather spend time working on his own research than help students out.  BEWARE!
He not only knows his information well but he is also interested in helping each student succeed in his class and others.  He always gave helpful tips on how to study and how to get organized.
No Comments

She was very unprofessional, and often yelled at students. She once kicked all of us out of the classroom because she heard people talking and went as far as to curse at us. She had a no phones or laptop rule, and made sure the TA's patrolled the classroom the whole time. Would not recommend taking her class.
So unprofessional it was bad. Said I love you to the class.
Just awful intructor. So old school, tough grader for what the class is, does not want to see her students succeed. Is fake when talking to people, would not recommend.
This class was extremely easy but she would often yell at people during lectures or have her TAs patrol the lecture hall looking for people on phones. Seems unnecessary for a college course.

Cicily is a decent teacher, although I feel like any teacher could teach this class because it is pretty easy. There is a decent amount of assignments, but most only take a little bit of time. Attendance is mandatory and she is very strict on computers and phones. She was nice and funny but sometimes yelled at students if people were talking.

In a professionalism class, she is very unprofessional. She has the TA's guard the room looking for phones, laptops, or disinterest and punish the student. She kicked us all out of the lecture room one day due to talking in the back of the room.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cicily Corder is a nightmare professor who despite teaching intro to professionalism, is perhaps the most unprofessional person I've ever met. TA's stand around like guards and report to her if a student, talks, looks at their phone, or even looks slightly uninterested. Be prepared to be chased and yelled at if you leave her class early.
She really cares about her students.

She was a really great professor and fostered an environment that made students feel comfortable to participate and be engaged. She was always great with communicating her expectations and efficient in responding to questions. I now have a great relationship with Cicily after taking her course and still refer to her for advice and career planning.

Cicily was such an amazing professor!. Her class was extremely beneficial for professionalism in college and the workplace. Additionally, her class opens a lot of opportunities for getting involved within the business school. I highly recommend taking any of her classes!

This professor is completely unhinged and not professional. She's teaching a course on professionalism and she is the least professional teacher I have ever had. I cannot believe its required for all business majors to take her class.
I absolutely love Cicily. You have to take her course; she genuinely loves her students and it shows in her teaching.
Good professor with difficult tests and lots of theoretical questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Berrie was a great chemistry professor to have as a first-year student. She took her time to explain anything that students were confused about. You could tell she was passionate about what she was teaching and loved helping her students out. Would love if I could have her as a teacher again.

Dr. Berrie is a great professor and an amazing lecturer!  She does a fantastic job of explaining even complicated topics.  She genuinely wants each student to understand the material and not simply memorize it.  The tests reflect this and have questions that require applying the knowledge in a new way.

I LOVED Dr. Berrie, but this was also the most difficult class I've ever taken. She is very caring and passionate about what she teaches. Expect quizzes almost every week and don't take them lightly. They add up and impact your grade immensely. Go to her office hours! Don't expect an A, but there is a VERY steep curve at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best instructors EVER! Although this was a difficult class, I'm very glad I took it because Dr. Berrie challenged me. As a student who typically breezed through classes in high school, I not only learned more than ever about chemistry, but I also learned how to study. Be ready for quizzes every Friday! Very interactive and fun lectures.

For CHEM190 and CHEM195, I often found myself looking elsewhere to fully understand the lecture materials. Many times she would include questions on the exams and weekly quizzes that she would not expect us to know how to do, and would only explain how to do it after the quiz was completed. However, there is a steep curve at the end of the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! She really wants you to understand the material! Best professor I have had!

Tough class, but not unreasonable. Discussion sessions saved my life both semesters; GO TO THEM. Dr Berrie's lecture style takes a little getting used to initially but generally she is clear and also very helpful outside of class! Honestly the hardest part was writing the lab reports for CHEM191. Would recommend but be ready to work for your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Berrie is a brilliant person who cares A LOT about chemistry. Her class was incredibly difficult. She will test students on material that she didn't cover in class "as a challenge", which makes them hard to study for. If you're not already an expert at chemistry, take 170 or 130; you'll learn more of the essential information to advance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is insanely hard. She often has quiz and test questions over material that has barely or not at all been covered in class. The lab reports for 191 also require a ridiculous amount of work and are graded extremely harshly (class avg 50%). She is very nice, and she is good at explaining things though, and the class has a pretty hefty curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Chem 190 and 195 are not your average chemistry class. They are honors class so the pace and material covered is much more difficult than reg chem. Be sure to ask a lot of questions whenever you seem confused because all the material grows on top of each other. I highly recommend that you've taken at least Calc 1, Physics 1 and AP chemistry before
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I LOVE CINDY BERRIE!!!! In her class students learn so much about chemistry way above what is taught in CHEM 130. If you are a science major and want to take a more intensive chemistry course, this is it, chief. Side note: the lab reports in the concurrent lab course, CHEM 191, require a decent amount of work, so keep that in mind.

Dr. Berrie is an excellent lecturer. If you read the chapter before the lecture you will be in a good place for passing the class with a high grade. She doesn't narrow down what the tests will be over so doing the homework and in class problems are your best bet for passing exams. Clicker questions in class are counted as participation so show up.

Very hard teacher, she starts off with concepts normally taught in junior level physical chemistry. She is always wanting to help, so go to her office hours! This really helped me get an A in the course.  Unless you have a chem related major, do not take her class. You will be causing yourself unnecessary stress. She is an insanely hard teacher.

Awesome professor, by far one of my favorites at KU.  At the beginning of the semester she admits that shes a tough teacher and will definitely challenge you, but she helps you out not only by being a rather lieniant grader, but also by giving you awesome notes, answering questions whenever you need them, and waking you up with some sweet demos.
Looks beyond the normal way of teaching. It is very obvious she has a love for sharing the world of art.

She was teh most influencial teacher i had while at KU. Among the best faculty in the art department. Cima will make you work hard, but the reward is so great when you actually push and challenge yourself instead of just doing the work to get a grade. She's also a wonderful and nurturing person. I will stay in touch with her after i graduate.

pretty ambiguous when it comes to how you're doing in the class. she talked a lot about my unique compositions and insights, and then gave me a scathing portfolio review about the generality of my work. have fun with this one!!

She's alright as far as drawing classes go, but she is never clear as to how you're doing in the class. She told me I was doing great all semester, then wrote me a harsh final critique and said she was being "generous" by giving me a B-. She's a nice person, but I wouldn't recommend her.
Very clear, knows a WHOLE LOT about drawing.  You will draw everything that she owns in her house, which is not a bad thing
Fun lady. Basically you can do whatever you want and not much homework but a sketchbook!
No Comments
You'll draw ladders, cubes, naked people, things projection on cubes, your self, and random stuff from her house.  And... That's about it.

Beth is a great teacher. She truly cares about her students and will go the extra mile to make sure they succeed. If you put in the work and effort in her class, then you will do very well. If you do not put in the effort, this will be a difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: AMAZING! great teacher, and super nice. In lab you do activities that you did in elementary school, but you learn how to use it from a teacher's perspective. Great person overall. Love this class!
Lab is kind of a waste of time for middle math majors.
WONDERFUL!
extremely easy labs. you do activities that you did in second grade. its kind of a waste of time, but she's very nice
gotta love math lab! easy easy class and lots of fun. the games we played rocked.
Methods class was very easy.  She's very flexible with schedules and likes to get to know the students.  Extremely friendly.

More likely to have her for Math Lab these days, but you'll love her no matter what the subject.  She's fun and really cares about education, teaching, and her students.  Incredibly dedicated!  Love her to bits :)
HE WAS AWSOME

Honestly, I didnt think he was all that great. He is nice and respectful to students, but an arbitrary grader with little feedback. He knows the subject well, it is really difficult for students who arent pols majors to get through the course.
Great Teahcer,love going to class and often feel guilty if i don't. Students should feel lucky to be able to take on of his courses!!:)

Cigler has a great conversational teaching style.  He's nice enough, and fairly clear.  The logistics of the class are the only problem.  He provides exams questions beforehand, but is a somewhat arbitrary grader.  I'd suggest carefully catering your writing.  Beware, he's been around a long time, and isn't terribly interested in students' ideas.
No Comments

I'm not that interested in poli sci, but he is usually interesting to listen to.  He definitely likes to hear students' opinions and talk to them outside of class.  Has some very interesting views on politics - he doesn't really talk liberal or conservative, it's more "how things work" behind the scenes.  Not "how a bill becomes law." Good teacher.

Cigler is the nicest professor in the department. He always has time for students and loves to cultivate realtionships with them outside of class. He has helped me numerous times and I trust his opinion greatly.
Great teacher, learned a lot, always looked forward to his lectures and class discussions
No Comments
best by far

Cigler rules, he makes class interesting and worth going to. It's the first class in college I feel guilty about skipping when I do just becuase I think he deserves showing up for. Great teacher, great lecturer. Wants to honestly hear your opinions and what you think. Take his classes
Cigler is the BEST!  He's generally not hard and a captivating lecturer.
No Comments
I love my woke studies professor. Everything could be resubmitted for better grades, which I needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures and review videos are fairly confusing in that steps are explained that end up not being helpful or even needed later on. The best way to do well in this class seems to be by reviewing the posted homework solutions and then asking questions about what you're confused on. He cares, but sometimes struggles explaining some concepts.

Often skips a lot of steps when performing derivations. Taking Calc 3 the semester before really helped, as he never really walked students through any of the calc 3. There are too many exams in my opinion, there seemed to be one about every other week. The geometric average grading system could either hurt you or help you, no in between.

This is definitely not an easy class, since flipped classrooms at KU (especially for engineering classes) almost never go well. Pay attention to the syllabus, as it lists what kinds of questions will be asked on exams. If you go to his office hours, he's actually a pretty nice guy, it's just his teaching method is not very effective.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor single-handedly made me hate physics. The subject is very detached from the real world and is being explained purely in terms of mathematical formulas, without the use of any day-to-day events as examples to help us understand how are those physical properties affecting some common occurrences. The grading scheme is not helpful too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Fischer knows physics and isn't that bad at actually teaching. The biggest problem is how he's set up the class. Lectures are on average 15 minutes and move very fast. He doesn't take the time he needs to show example problems and explain the concepts. Some of the tests are very difficult and some aren't too bad. Be prepared to work for objective 2

I should have listened to the other reviews. Dr. Fischer may understand physics, but he is not effective at teaching it. The exam questions are much harder than the example problems in class. He only teaches for 20 minutes before assigning people to solve practice problems. My only saving grace was a massive curve he gave at the end.
Worst Physics profesor ever.. never again. Grades 1 question as 1 point so say goodbye to partial credit.

Fischer is by far the worst professor Ive ever had. He is absolutely terrible at teaching and uses a workbook that has tons of errors. He makes the grading fairly easy to do alright, but the trade off is he clearly doesnt care if you actually learn the information. Went to him for help once and he was completely arrogant. Avoid at all costs.

He recently changed the class structure to only focusing on a workbook. He doesn't provide how to solve the problems, but only the answers. Most of the answers are wrong. He grades very harshly. Don't even bother taking his class. The way the class is structured is based on the workbook so it's not worth it to even show up to class.

I think the reviews are accurate. If you put in the time and really really try, as in prioritize this class over all others, you will do well. The way the class is structured makes it hard to stay motivated. He's smart and creative, I can tell. In the end he remedied it by giving us free points and increasing questions so in the end it was fair imo

Here's coming from someone with good study habits that has never struggled on a science class before. Fischer is a terrible teacher. His few lectures are riddled with jumps in conclusion and the tests are unfairly different than course material. He has the "hybrid" style teaching which means you're on your own to teach physics to yourself. Get out.

One of the better profs I've had here at ku. He's really good at explaining things so ask a lot of questions! It's a physics 2 course so it isn't easy but if you work hard, do the homework, and go to office hours if you're confused you will get an A.
The best physics professor ever!

This is more of a mathematical course than a physics course which helps the student because no one will use the physics concepts 5 years from taking the course but helps develop a better mathematical understanding which is more useful. Hes a good guy and makes time for his students who need help . Use the class time appropriately
The format of this course is ridiculous! The grading scale makes it almost impossible to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've taken an electricity and magnetism class before, and this has been the worst class I have ever taken. It is a "flipped classroom" class, so there is no real lecture on the extremely difficult content. There are some serious problems with this: - Textbook is NOT helpful - Math used in class not covered in prerequisite class. DO NOT TAKE CLASS

Easily the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. It's a flipped class, meaning that he doesn't lecture. Also the grading is horrific. Even if you consider yourself good at physics, do NOT under any circumstances take this class, even if it messes up your schedule. Talk to an adviser about when else this class is offered by a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He doesn't lecture. We have to read his book and watch his videos, solve hw every other day, and solve problems in class. Not only is the material itself hard, but he makes it harder because: -He doesn't lecture at all -His book and videos could be a lot clearer (and I'm being generous) -Grading system: fail one of his "objectives", fail class

Flipped class, so he doesn't lecture at all... which wouldn't be an issue if the materials he gave us to study from actually made sense. Makes extremely simple concepts practically impossible to understand. Get a tutor.

I'm fairly good at physics but this guy made it (PHSX 212) terrible. It's a "flipped class". No lectures during class, only online videos, his own textbook, and none of them are good. He expects you to know stuff you haven't learned (and aren't in the textbook), and everything is explained using convoluted equations. Wait for a different professor

The class is one of the most difficult mathematical classes I have had to take so far, and this is due in part due the difficult nature of the material but moreover to the fact that some genius had the great idea to teach this class in a flipped classroom style, meaning that your learning of the material is left up to the convoluted textbook.

Try your best not to take him. I got an A, but learned almost nothing about electricity and magnetism. He doesn't lecture, AT ALL. If you want to learn anything, you rely solely on the book he wrote, which is terribly written. The exams consist of students scrambling around the room from group to group looking for answers. It's a bad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: PHSX 202 was an online class so I didn't interact with Dr. Fischer much. He responded to emails and graded tests in timely manner. Tests were 10-15 Multiple Choice questions and were pulled from the homework/quizzes from that lesson. The amount of homework was pretty high, but none of the problems were unfairly difficult.

He doesn't teach. Lecture is basically doing in class quizzes. Reading the book is supposed to be enough learning, plus self-instructed practice. His exams are incredibly difficult; even though the large groups are allowed to collaborate on a large portion of the exam, the class average is around a 60%. It might be better with actual lectures.
Too bad he is the only teacher for this course

He teaches in a way that he isn't expecting people to get everything, he just wants them to be familiar. I struggled with the material a lot and didn't feel like I got it even after the class. I highly recommend going to office hours. He'll do problems with you and show you trends. ASK A TON OF QUESTIONS. And the class will be curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Fischer is a good person and cares about his students, but doesn't get what his students don't get. He's rationalized physics in his mind differently than anyone else as reflected by the textbook that he wrote for the class. Although I did well, it was extremely frustrating to get an A. Homework and tests are very difficult. Good luck.

Fischer is a great guy who is really passionate about physics, but he's a terrible teacher. He is helpful in office hours, though. His tests are VERY difficult, but you can get some credit back from redoing it online. He says he won't curve but he ends up having to do it anyway. This was probably the hardest class I have taken (chemistry major).

He's a good teacher. Homework and readings are assigned out of class, and all you do in class is practice problems and ask for help. So it's really easy to skip class. Tests are alright, at least they're multiple choice.

Literally the worst professor I've ever had. I'm one of the top students in the class, and even with hours of studying I do poorly on the tests. The class is taught flipped, which translates to you must teach yourself all the material.  I learned more from skyping with my dad who's an engineer than I ever learned from Fischer.

This so far has been the hardest class I have taken. The book is necessary because it has little tips and tricks that he expects you to know, oh yeah, he is also the one that wrote the book (which is terribly written). The tests are very hard. The homework is long and you get it three times a week. I would never take a class from him again.

He wrote a textbook for this class. It is simply awesome. If you read the textbook, you can solve the homework problems.  His tests are very easy and the class has an online component for the exams. So, you will already get 50% marks without any hard work.

Terrible! Will never take a never class from him again. This was the hardest class I have taken so far and it was hard because he made it hard. He did not lecture and expected us to read everything from the book (his book). The book was poorly written and I feel sorry for anyone that has to take this class.

He uses His own summary instead of the textbook which makes things more complicated and harder to understand. the grading recipe does not make sense and his tests are above the normal level of what he teaches in class. DO NOT ENROLL IN THIS CLASS!! unless you are trying to fail it or barely get a C. Cheating is the only way to pass this class!!

Was a nice teacher.  He gave summaries of all chapters and provided his slides online.  Class did not have enough time to go over all concepts but he was very willing to explain any questions you had.  Provided Formula sheet for all tests. Just practice problems with formula sheet and he gives a very generous curve. Solid class.

I went to class every day and I still wonder why. The readings and hw assignments are overly confusing. Memorize how to do the problems he does in lecture if you want to have any hope in passing. He also never gave a review. He says no curve but there will be a curve. Then entire class was overly complicated content wise. DO NOT TAKE.

First of all, he doesn't use the textbook. Instead, he uses his own written summary which is so confusing. The class is so hard and the only way to pass is to cheat. I've taken the class spring 2014 and I had to drop it because it's extremely hard and impossible to pass because of the weird class format. Don't enroll in this class!!!
Horrible class format. You come in to class, do 4 problems in 75 minutes and get no answers. None of the TA's know the answer to questions and he rarely helps everyone. It's a terrible class format.

Worst professor. He never teaches in class and expects students to study the material and show up to class. The TA's cannot solve the problems. The class is very difficult. I would not recommend any one to take a class with fischer. Horrible professor.

Horrible teacher. His class is excruciatingly hard; homework and tests are all extremely difficult. When asked to solve some of his own homework during the discussion section he couldn't even do it. TA's tried to help but after the midterm they couldn't even do most of the material. Exams: multiple choice no partial credit. Miss one: automatic 80%.

People are a little harder on him as a person than they need to be, but the homework and tests are very hard. It's almost impossible to prepare for his tests. Unless you're already good at physics, I would suggest a tutor

Spends such little time focusing on the fundamentals and excessive time providing overly complicated solutions, i.e. solving for easy problems using a Taylor Series. It's difficult to hone your focus and one can't help but wonder if he is there to teach or show off. The class was enthusiastic about the material but felt trampled on by the end.

One of my least favorite teachers. Homework-wise, you know there is a problem when you ask TA's questions and they can't solve it without having to look up the solutions. Test-wise, it's a 6 question test, multiple choice. It favors cheaters and crammers as screwing up one part of the calculations gets you the same credit as a wrong guess.

Fischer knows what he is doing, but he flys through the solution in the way he understands it. The lectures consist of student writing down equation for problems, but having no idea what they mean or how to know to use which parts. The homework's are brutal. Expect to get half way through semester and have not learned much. Each test is 6 questions

Fischer is a good lecturer, but when he assigns homework its something foreign that he did not teach how to solve. I understand that you need to know concepts and use them to solve problems, but when the entire class is cheating to pass you know you have a problem. I have yet to have someone tell me that they are not using chegg or friends for hw.

I went into this class with an open-mind and very excited to learn physics, but I struggled the entire semester. He is a very funny, genuine, and helpful teacher, but the class is very hard. The class is also very fast paced. Be ready to go 200 mph in and out of class!
This was his first time teaching the honors into, and he made way, way too difficult.  I averaged 50% for three straight tests but managed to get an A because he had to curve it so much.
He is generally a pretty good teacher but some of his methods for solving problems are overly tedious and unnecessary.

Keeps you very interested in the material but has a hard time keeping students up with the pace by the end of the semester. Tests always have at least 1 question students can barely answer. Helpful when you go see him, and was very generous with his class curve. Challenging but overall enjoyable.

I though prof fischer was very fair with his grading scale and it's easy to get a A in the class. Make sure you do the homework and understand how to solve the problems. Also, go to lecture! His test questions are problems similar to the ones he did in class and on the homework. Read the sections he assigns and the recommended problems.

He is a good, reasonable teacher. He gave us extra credit because some people did bad on one test but overall the tests were reasonable. Homework is easy, although he gives some hard questions. Tests are more challenging but he is reasonable and they are all multiple choice. A good teacher in my opinion.

The homework is ridiculous, and the tests can be horrible. If you study enough it's doable. I struggled the entire year and still managed to get an A thanks to how the class is curved (82% is an A), and I didn't even have to take the last test or the final.

Homework is pretty tough and is assigned 3 times a week. There are four tests with 6 questions each and can be difficult as well. However, the cutoff for an A in the class is 82% a so that levels things out a bit. Just study hard for tests and do the homework and you will do fine.

Tried an "experiment", in which he didn't actually teach us anything - absolutely no lecture - but during each and every class had quizzes to test us over the assigned readings. Tests were hard. Poorly structured. His experiment failed.

The class would be easy if it were not based on 30 questions the entire semester. You have 4 tests of 10 questions each, he drops the lowest score. The final is a whopping 20 questions and is almost half your grade. He barely teaches and the book and others is your best friend. Solutions manuals and cliffs notes also are helpful.
Worst teacher. Can't learn anything from his ridiculous homework assignments and worthless lecture. Just hope he uses the majority of the questions from the book on the test.

I lasted an entire two weeks... he tried a new style of teaching: you teach yourself and come do clicker questions the entire class time about things you couldn't understand in the book. Very few examples for a physics/math class and when he does he hardly explains it. Many emails/complaints from other students! Gives out candy though and is funny.

He decided to go with a new course layout this semester. I'm very good at these kinds of classes...and I can't figure out a single thing about this class. I got a 60% on the first test and a 40% on the second. There is NO lecture whatsoever, he magically expects us to know the material from the book and from 2-3 crappy examples done in class. Avoid

Pretty funny guy during lectures. Takes most test questions from problems in the book. He goes WAY too fast in examples in class and focuses more on humor than the important concepts. He's helpful in office hours. 4 tests= ur grade. Each test is 10 questions. Cheaters=easy A. Non-cheaters=frustrating class. This class was run horribly in my opinion
Funny guy, really smart, makes class enjoyable
very nice, funny and helpful prof...seems to care about students. He makes physics fun by adding in his own jokes.

Great prof! Attendance isn't mandatory and no points for going but he's a good teacher and physics is tough if you've not had it before. Homework is fairly easy but tests are tough. He's very passionate and cares about the students. Loves when people ask questions. Highly recommended.

Great teacher, makes class fun and interesting while still teaching the material.  Be careful though, tests either very easy or very hard!  He teaches the theory, and you have to practice using the equations to really get it.

Robin Davis killed physics for me.  Chris Fischer brought it back to life. He makes lectures fun and interesting through examples and changes his speech pattern so he's not droning. Ask him about his experience w/ String Theory and get ready for a wild ride. He enjoys what he does and makes a tough subject better. Still hard, but fair and sorta fun

Professor Fischer is a great Physics teacher.  His lectures are very clear and easy to follow, and he tries to bring a little bit of humor and lightness into what can be a dry subject.  He puts notes and study materials on a website, and is very accessable to his students.
He's so funny and jokes a ton. Class is always fun! Participate!!
Cote is a good teacher and a cool guy. He's really nice and you actually get to know him. His class is pretty easy though but you still have to do all the work.
Cote was a great professor to have.  He made the class very comfortable and was helpful and available.  I'm glad to have had him as a teacher.

Awesome teacher, he has a sense of humor but in a sarcastic way. A lot of the class is reading essays out of the book then having discussions in class. Don't skip classes because sometimes he will give credit for showing up.

Cote is a very down-to-earth professor. He is sarcastic, but in a funny way, and is very genuine and real with his students. I personally hate english, but he made this class fairly enjoyable. He is very helpful, especially when you ask him a question.

Cote is brilliant. He is able to take a seemingly boring class and make it fun and exciting. There are only four papers over the course of the entire class. He is always very fair when it comes to the grading. Furthermore, he actually teaches you how to write! Most English teachers don't do that. Consider yourself lucky if you have Cote.
I have enjoyed Cote so much as a teacher. He is very helpful and would recommend him to anyone. Sadly, this is his last semester.

Cote is a great instructor. He values discussions over written word in a class full of non-English majors. He makes an effort to give us interesting paper topics and discuss our ideas. He does grade oddly sometimes, but this doesn't stop him from rocking.

Really funny, good class, engaging discussions... can't read his handwriting, though.  It's something that gets joked about, but I seriously wish I could get better feedback on my essays and response papers... I mean, I'm sure I get good feedback, I just can't read it.  At all.

Love the awkward moments. Fun guy to mess around with. Pretty open to help, wouldn't rely on feedback he writes on papers (you cant read his handwriting). His music choice is questionable. Good teacher, you wont be sorry for choosing him.
funny
He is super hot and really really funny.
He is very helpful, and wants the students to do well. He is very available, so go to office hours, they help!!
No Comments

He can be funny and brilliant, but I sincerely worry about his emotional capacity.  He's often so overwhelmed by the love and wonder that fills our classroom, that lengthy sessions of crying ensue.  Thankfully he brings his own box of tissues to class daily.  The sniffling surrounding all this is supremely annoying, but I still feel for the guy.
He's super funny. He makes the class fun. He's awesome.

I took the Spanish Inq. class that Luis taught alongside Prof. Manning. Luis is a fun lecturer, and it seems that he is willing to answer all questions at length, but his lectures always seemed to end on time. Attendance was mandatory, and the readings were extensive. However, put your head down and pace out the assignments and you'll be fine.
very understanding and patient. super good at communicating with his students
This class was amazing. The wealth of knowledge I gained and the extensive assistance for the final paper was truly appreciated. He is invested in the success of all his students!

He was very fun to listen to in lectures. He is very interested in what he teaches and makes it easy to learn. The TA was amazing and the final was optional. Participation is huge component and is worth more than your homework grade.
My European History class was my favorite this semester. Dr. Corteguera is not only interesting but genuinely excited about his subject matter. He also helps ALOT with the final paper for the class.

His lectures are interesting and organized.  He uses a lot of art and some film segments.  His tests are all short essay, also a few short papers.  You have to read 3 short books.  I liked the class. Dr. Corteguera likes to teach and he makes the class useful for people who have not had a lot of past history classes.  Nice and sometimes funny.

Corteguera is an engaging and interesting teacher.  He is very friendly and helpful.  Probably the best run class I have ever been in.  The amount of outside work was perfect for the difficulty of the class.
He is able to make a boring subject more entertaining.
Dr. Corteguera is the best teacher I ever had at KU.  He is very hard, but very good.
Good...I like

Expects quite a bit.  Work load of roughly 40 books plus two 15 page papers for the semester.  He was very helpful and available for advise/guidance.  Funny and engaging in class.  His personal interest in the history of religion dominated the class and the assigned readings.  Fair grader.
CORTEGUERA IS THE ****IN MAN!!!
Dr. Summers is great!! She makes the material very understandable and she is very nice and easy to talk to outside of class.
So relatable and easy to talk to, she is very real and makes the material simple and easy to understand, definitely recommend!
super nice and caring, made sure to explain eerything thoroughly and was not strict about homework or assignments and let us retake quizzes to learn from them
Dr. Summers is amazing. She takes time to talk about grad school and gets to know each student personally. Best SPLH professor in the department.

Dr. Summers is a great and caring professor. She made sure to know everybody's name. For this course she used a grading contract where we chose our grade at the start and as long as we met those requirements, we were good! For group projects we were assigned a case study for the entire semester, and I loved it! She chose our groups well.
Fantastic!

Colin is the best professor I've had. He actually cares about his students and it's insane how knowledgable he is. Knowing he went to Harvard, you can really tell how much work he puts into his slides to make it engaging. He explain things in a beautiful way that is super clear to understand. He also is lenient when grading.Exams offer corrections

Best professor I've had, hands down. The effort McRoberts puts into his curriculum to make it USEFUL to students is evident. He is a world-class lecturer who seems genuinely interested in the material and enthused to be teaching it. The grade is only exams and quizzes, but they are a breeze if you show up, listen, and take notes. The goat. Period.

Professor McRoberts is definitely one of my favorite professors ever. Attendance isn't mandatory and you can get a good grade without showing up, but please do, his lectures are super interesting and I genuinely felt bad that most of the class wasn't showing up.

His lectures/discussions are compelling and he relates everything to real-life situations you will likely face in the business world, and he wants you to know that. The busy work for BUS 150 sucks but you'll get that with every prof.

McRoberts is by far the most intelligent professor I have had in the B school thus far. He knows the topic of law like the back of his hand, and you can tell he enjoys sharing and teaching it with his students. I would definitely recommend going to lectures, as the class is actually very knowledgeable and makes the tests a lot easier.

Awesome teacher! Super accessible outside of class and explains everything in such great ways, with different analogies or stories. The class itself is set up in modules, so each module is a different concept. Just be prepared to read and you'll be fine. The class is set up the same for any of the teachers, but take him if you want to learn!

Honestly, not much to say other than McRoberts is a great professor. He understands all of the material he teaches in detail, and provides opportunities for students to make-up poor test scores. So far, he's been my favorite professor at KU.

Professor McRoberts' lectures are great. He encourages class participation and shares real life stories to relate to each concept. He is always willing to clarify and answer any questions. Large chunk of your grade will be the exams which can be a little tough, but if you study and do the corrections that he offers you'll be fine. Highly recommend!

He gave nice lectures and had fun stories. Lectures are not mandatory which is really nice. But my only complaint is that in the grade book there is only 10-15 assignment?quizzes and tests. So if you do bad on one test it messes your whole grade even tho you can do corrections it is not the best. Other than that he is a decent professor.

Professor McRoberts is by far one of the best teachers at KU. His class had optional attendance, but fs go because of how insightful his lectures are (plus he covers most of the material so you won't have to do much or any reading for homework). He taught us about essential life knowledge that I'd never been taught and am so grateful for that.

The best professor I've ever had. Incredibly relevant lecturer. Has practiced law for years, went to Harvard, and yet he makes the content so understandable. Inspirational and enthusiastic. Lectures can be tough with the amount of material but he keeps you entertained. Allows test corrections and is flexible with deadlines. Study for "Case Day".
Responds to emails fast, fun lectures, and great stories

Dude is the best teacher on campus. Very intelligent, amazing stories, very experienced. He is an actual inspiring teacher that makes you want to succeed not only in the class but in life as well. He is a Harvard Lawyer with a lot of different experience and he uses stories from his life to teach the class. It was a very engaging class .
Explained law using examples from his life, really made sure we understood. His exams are difficult but you can earn 50% of your points back. Super fun dude.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A professor who absolutely knows what he's talking about. The lectures are pretty heavy but he always keeps your attention. As long as you keep good notes, you would have to deliberately sabotage yourself to fail.

This was my favorite class I have ever taken. I loved the class from day one, he teaches so well, it feels like a story time instead of a boring lecture. Put the work in the night before exams and make yourself familiar with the content. Go in to his office hours to get help with corrections. Everybody should take BLAW with this professor 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really loved his lectures! Very informative! This course is difficult and if you don't attend lectures it will be hard to understand the content.  He posts all his power points and notes which makes taking the open note tests accessible to everyone! Genuinely cares about your success! Would recommend to any prelaw student!

So far, seems to be a great professor. He knows what he's talking about since he has the experience. This is the one class I actually look forward to attending. The lectures are great and real cases are presented. Wish more classes were like this. I highly recommend it.

McRoberts is a nice guy, he seems to care about his students. BUS150 is time consuming, but easy to do well if you put in the work. Don't expect your work be graded fast, or at all until the end of the semester. McRoberts would be a great professor if he knew how to manage his time better. The in class quizzes will be the hardest part of the class

Professor McRoberts is an excellent professor. His lectures are very informative and enjoyable. He's very understanding and compassionate to students. The class is an easy A if you do the reading and pay attention in class. I learned a lot in this class and I would highly recommend this professor.
I sometimes have a hard time sitting through lectures but I really enjoyed the class and the professor.

Professor McRoberts was very lenient and understanding if a student was falling behind because of another class' work. As long as you watch the lectures and take notes, you will succeed. The in-person discussions were also interesting because we discussed real cases. McRoberts is very smart, but he is still able to teach law in a simple way.

Very interesting, well educated, and nice man. He is a retired lawyer who is extremely good at explaining law in a simple way. Online lectures could get long (put on 1.5 speed), take notes because you can use them on tests. In-person class was either boring or really interesting, no in between. Not difficult, little effort will earn an A.

Grading is very test heavy, but he was a great lecturer and definitely knows what he's talking about. Really tries to make his grading as fair to everyone as possible and will take questions off exams if they were deemed too vague. Really wants to help you understand all of the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McRoberts is hands down the best professor Ive had during my time at KU. Highly recommend you take BLAW 301 with him, he is incredibly accessible and WANTS to help his students succeed.

McRoberts gets a bad rap sometimes, but I enjoyed his class. He's very to the point and he also uses a lot of real-world examples that come from his own experience. He's also the only Harvard Law grad that I know that doesn't rub it in everyone's face
He knows what he is talking about.

The book isn't necessary when it comes to learning the content. The slides are pretty informational, but you will need the textbook for a couple of extra credit opportunities (but you won't need extra credit). It is a critical thinking course so some students find the exams difficult, but if you just study the vocabulary and think. You'll be fine.

He is probably best sticking to being a lawyer. If you can, take class with other professor. His class is completely different and 100 times harder than the other professor, and he knows it. Tests are completely based on application and very hard. He's a nice guy, just makes the class way harder than it should be for an intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor McRoberts means well but is way over qualified. His tests are impossible and his lectures are uneccesarily infomational. He was a previous lawyer so many things he says do not make sense to college students. I would not take this class unless you want to take some of the hardest tests you can take.

I really enjoyed having Professor Morrissey. She's intelligent, kind, and the things we talked about in class were very engaging. I feel like I learned more about the English language in this class than in probably anywhere else, ever. Her essay grading is a little harsh, but her feedback is good, and I did feel like I learned a ton.

While there was a TON of reading in this class, I enjoyed it in the end and really enjoyed Professor Morrissey. She is understanding, kind, and challenges you to grow. I wish I had the opportunity to take another class from her. If you can, take her classes; you won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: She was an amazing teacher. Very caring.

She is very tough. No phones and no talking or she will call you out in front of the class. Multiple page (like 4-22 page) readings assigned for every single class. Attendance is a part of your grade for this course. Cannot miss very many classes or grade goes down. It is weirdly focused HEAVILY into anglophilia, I suggest another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Her class structure often built on group discussions with your peers as to where you input your own opinion about a given prompt and sharing at the end of class. She can be a little tough on paper grading and comments, but acclimating to her comments you should be fine. Just act like you care about her personal life and she'll probably like you.

She knows her stuff , but I find her mannerisms rather annoying. She is controlling.  During group discussions, she would give us a 10 min time limit, and remind us every 2 minutes how much time we had left. Super annoying, but is passionate. If English is not your forte, don't take her class. She doesn't realize not everyone loves English.

Everything the rater said below is true. We must have been in the same class this semester. WAY too many quizzes, assignments, 6 exams and a final exam going over everything in the 24 chapters. Way too many terms and concepts to learn in one class. This class really needs to be divided into two classes. Instructor needs to restructure this class.

WARNING!!! 8 Hw assignments, Final Project, Final Exam, 6 Exams, 20 quizzes. Prof. really cares, but the amount of work for this course is truly ridiculous. I've taken 650+ lvl Classes classes and nothing compares to this class. Prof FAILS to realize there is life outside of MWF 8-8:50 am and all the prep time to pass her material. GOOD LUCK!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr.Dozier MWF at 8am. I am not a morning person, but I genuinely looked forward to going to her class. The TA for the class was Butler Braren, and he was also amazing. We were given a study guide/outline for every exam, so there were no surprises. Office hours were right after class which was really nice, especially for exam prep.

Professor Dozier is one of the best professors I have had at KU. She is so passionate and knowledgable about applied behavioral science, her lectures are engaging and interesting. As long as you go to class and really engage with the content you can get an A. 10/10 would recommend Dozier.

Brilliant professor! She is very sweet and cares about her students and clients. She will not baby you or sugarcoat things. So, be ready to work hard and take constructive feedback. I absolutely love being in her research lab and would recommend her to any future behavior analyst. She will get you ready and make you knowledgeable about the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Claudia is a wonderful instructor. She makes it very clear what is expected. She wants all the students to do well and bends over backward to give the opportunity for an A to all students.  You must attend class and study your notes for quizzes and tests.  If you put in the time and effort you'll do well in her class.b

Claudia is an AMAZING teacher. One of my favorite teachers at KU. Even though her class is at 8:30, she makes class interesting and enjoyable to go to. It's very hard to poorly in her class, as she's crystal clear about everything and grades fairly easy.

Claudia is an amazing professor. She is SO nice and very helpful. She's very smart and a really great person to know in this department. Expectations for the class are crystal clear. If you do poorly in this class, you clearly did not put any effort into it.

Claudia is ridiculously knowledgeable about applied behavior analysis. Not only is she is well-educated and widely published, but she is able to explain all relevant material in an understandable way. She makes her expectations very clear and is extremely fair with her provision of consequences for exceeding or failing to meet those expectations.

Pretty easy class. Make sure you take the comprehensive final rather than the test 6 version, very very easy. Dozier comes off arrogant. Difficult to interact with her one on one. Explained materials well, just don't expect her to do anything to help you. Avoid her if you possibly can. Very specific grader as well. Meaning that you must have tiny detals in your essays or you get ripped apart

She is very rude and very self-centered. She says she is willing to help, but when she does, she is demeaning and egotistical. Never try and correct her, because according to her, she is always correct. She's very pretty, but not a very nice person.
Dr. Shelly Cline is an amazing professor. Her lectures are well-planned and entertaining. Your grade is composed of four papers, and she offers extra credit

Never read a book, did some spark notes and listened in class.  Gives a review sheet for both tests and they were filled out by the group on email, so I just studied that... got an A like it was nothing!

I was really nervous about this class, I hadn't taken 204 yet. But Now that it is done, I feel it was one of the most transformational classes I have taken in my four years here. And I think Shelley had a lot to do with it. She is so engaging and fair. You will never be bored and you can get an A easily if you show up and somewhat engage in the material.
Best teacher I have had at KU!

Great teacher. Didn't really have an interest in class since it was required, but I loved it. Class isn't that hard, and a lot of the books are on SparkNotes, even though its recommended not to be used. She gives study guides for the midterm and final that helped a lot.

I loved loved loved this class, and I think it is mostly because of Shelly's teaching. I had to work hard for my grade (read ALMOST everything, prepared for discussion, studied HARD for tests, and got help outside of class), but I learned a lot and had some very interesting discussions in class. Favorite class at KU so far!!

If you have to take Western Civ she is the woman to take it from! Loved the way she cares for her students and sparks discussion with ease! I really did enjoy her class, despite the topics we had to cover.

She was a great teacher. I have never really enjoyed classes like western civ, but she really made it interesting and sparked conversation. She was really helpful. If you have a hard time joining in on discussions, just talk to her...she's really helpful.

Absolutely the BEST Western Civ II teacher.  I actually enjoyed discussions as opposed to ones in Western Civ I with Shump.  She tries hard to make a topic interesting and sparks conversations well.  I STRONGLY recommend trying to get her for Western Civ II if at all possible.
Shelly is awesome!!  Best Western Civ teacher EVER!!!

She is genuinely one of the worst professors I have ever come across. All she does during class, is just read off the chapter slides and barely explain anything. She does not curve the exams, even if the class average is 63%. Pick someone else over her, you'll do yourself a favor.

I genuinely think that if you brought in a high school student from LHS and told them to read the slides, it would be comparable to Rosenfeld's lectures. Tough grader and doesn't curve exams even if the class average is lower than a 64%. Office hours are not helpful and are only on Zoom. Overall, don't take her class. Professor Morriss the G.O.A.T.
Claire is an amazing professor, she knows what she's teaching, and she genuinely cares about her students in and out of class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH CLAIRE!! Her lectures are not good and are boring. Her Homework problems are NOT helpful with the exams. The formulas she gives you for the exam don't help either. Her study guides are not the best and not useful; you will be on your own. I would not recommend this professor to my greatest enemy.

Taking her online master course and there are 6 items due every week and the first “quiz” took 2 hours of the 2.5 given. You have to upload work. She does not open all the modules so you can only work one week ahead. Also, her rounding rules are inconsistent, ending answer is to 4 decimal places, but the intermediate calculations vary on rounding.

Be ready for a 60 question syllabus assignment that is incredibly ambiquous. She makes it clear she wants you to fail, for example if an assignment has 50 questions and is out of 15 points, you lose half a point for every mistake. Genuinely just the type of professor that seems to enjoy being seen as annoying

Be prepared to sit in class for 75 minutes and listen to her read the slides given to you. She goes fast and gives tons of homework that is graded slowly and unfairly. There is a lot of material to study for this class and grading can sometimes be unclear. All that said she does truly care about her students and is a master of the material.
Takes off points for the most minuscule things. Do not recommend at all

No point in even going except that there's a lot of in class assignments. Also the TOUGHEST grader for NO reason. Takes off points for the most minuscule things like I have never seen in all 4 years of my college career. Also won't let you ask questions about your grade. Do not recommend at all

This class is bearable if you take the time to understand "the why". Exams are very in-depth so make sure to study. She genuinely cares, though is slow on grading/asks questions that weren't covered much in class. She will teach you a lot, but also won't hold your hand. Doing well is partially based on luck, if you remember a tiny detail from class

Professor Rosenfeld gets a lot of hate for the insane amount of content that she covers throughout the semester, which is partially justified. She throws so much information and grades the practice problems insanely hard after barely explaining the content. However, she is a person who genuinely cares about her students and loves finance.

Worst professor I've had at KU. Lecture heavy, and she is so boring I can barely stay awake. There is so much information in this course that it is impossible to study. The final is cumulative, and i'm supposed to know minor details of everything over 15-18 chapters. Extremely harsh grader, not helpful. Also, current event presentations? Really?
Do not take her course. She is very rude and will not give you any room to make a mistake. Overall, she just does not know what shes doing. Avoid her and either take Jason Anderson or William Bazley.

Takes off points for the most minuscule things like I have never seen in all 4 years of my college career. Also won't let you ask questions about your grade. Do not recommend at all.
Good professor, my biggest gripe is how long it takes here to grade exams. Didn't have the last test graded before I took my final.

Course was homework heavy with single/timed attempt on 5 items that comprised the majority of the grade. Denied any useful resources or follow-up in a timely manner. Grades were late, no follow-up on whether to continue in the course, or withdraw. Although she was nice when available to respond, would have preferred better options for instruction.

Claire is a professor who genuinely cares about her students. Her class isn't the hardest, but it definitely will require some outside work. If you do poorly in her class you honestly just didn't try hard enough and that's on you. She is very accommodating, and doesn't humiliate students in class.

Unlike some professors who seem to enjoy miserable students, she truly wants you to succeed. Great communication. Accommodating with schedules and helps out whenever a student is clearly struggling and asks for assistance. Partial credit is often given on exams. Gotta put effort into learning the material though! Her kindness wont get you an A.

I liked the content most of the time for the course and my only complaint was the final. It was cumulative, and it was tough. There's so much content in this class that it feels impossible to study for. That being said, as long as you come to class, take notes, and do the homework, you will be fine (probably).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lots of group work and half the semester was focused on the banking simulation. She takes awhile to grade things, so most likely won't get feedback on your work. Super sweet and caring though, and always willing to help. If you enjoy participating and working in groups, this is a good class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Rosenfeld is a very compassionate professor. She's one of the best professors I had during my financial studies at KU. She cares a lot about her students and she was very understanding in our class during the pandemic. I would recommend her to anybody who is thinking of taking a class associated with her.

Honestly an awful class. I took this with Claire cuz I heard she was good and now have huge regrets. She is not good. Our test was over 17/18 chapters with 30-50 slides of information each. That is a disgusting amount of information to retain and is kind of impossible. She gives NO guidance as to what to study, and I am so upset I took this class.

Rosenfeld is a good professor! Extremely organized! She posts her slides, and really wants students to do well and learn. Very nice lady as well. The practice problems are helpful review for exams, and she is very good about answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took this class in the Spring. Claire is sharp and did a ton of helping in the discussion forums . To be honest, some of us were kind of lazy. My issue, however, was the change to the syllabus midway through the class, no review of the final, and no rounding on grades, despite being required to round to 6 decimal places for homework solutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: First two exam averages were in the 60s. She didn't curve and instead made the final worth 50% of the course grade. Didn't provide any specifics for what to study. Class slides were so jammed packed with information. Also, says you can dispute grades but after you do will tell you that you need to provide written evidence backing your argument.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Claire Rosenfeld is probably the sweetest, most caring professor in the business school. You can truly tell she wants her students to learn and get something out of the class. She is always willing to help and I always felt like I could approach her with questions. Show up to class, engage with the material and put forth effort and you'll do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Was honestly awesome. Cracked jokes and gave real world examples to help explain concepts. All around a good professor.

Professor Webb is a guy's guy. You might see him at the hawk on Saturday. However, the tests are really hard. Don't really have to come to class because it felt like what was covered in class was not on the midterm and final.

Professor Webb was pretty easy. I skipped class a lot and still got a high A. The material covered in lecture can sometimes be boring, but he is a funny guy. Using R was not that difficult as the TA's clearly walk you through it. The exams are made up of the exact questions on the quizzes (2 quizzes/week). The homework was all done in groups.

Dr. Webb is a good person to know in the field of quantitative methodology. However, his quizzes and tests are very poorly worded, he's a bit disorganized with deadlines and class materials (quizzes due on Tuesday, puts up information on Monday night), and is not accessible outside of class. His classes are not high on his list of priorities.

reviews.comment: She was a good professor but there was just a lot of homework that was pretty time consuming. The homework was very easy because it was on a website and you just use the book, but it was a lot every week. We had exams but we could work on them together and it was open notes. One day in person and one day teach yourself.

This class was hybrid with one class day a week. Outside of class you would read the textbook, do a bunch of online assignments and quizzes over the chapter, then come to class where she just repeated everything. I wouldnt have shown up ever because it was pointless but you have contribution points each class that are important if you want to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She grades like she's blind. Every time I submitted a paper, I got it proof read and turned it in, and she pulls out all the stops to make sure she gives you the worst grade. I don't know what her problem is, but it's absolutely ridiculous

Get ready to read/write a lot; this class will take up a bulk of your homework load. However, the only assignments she grades hard are the analysis papers. Everything else you could complete with your eyes closed and get a 100%. She's nice, fun to talk to, and will give you interesting insights.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: There are a lot of readings, and the weekly quizzes take a few hours to complete. The two big projects involved conducting interviews, teaching a lesson to the class, and writing analysis papers (about 10-20 pages). Those were a ton of work, but it was nice to look back and see how much you accomplished. She is very nice, but does expect a lot.

reviews.comment: She is super nice and fun to talk to. You learn a lot in her class without getting stressed and feeling overwhelmed.

Not a good professor at helping you learn the material. The discussions are him talking and cutting students off when they are giving their thoughts. He won't let you make up a quiz. I tried to take a quiz I missed for a funeral, and he did not let me take it. Doesn't know how to work Canva really. Overall, not good professor.

knowledgable professor but not suited to teach. expectations not clear, too much content that he assigns but doesn't cover but appears in the weekly quizzes. weekly quizzes are completely unreasonable. for a class on discrimination and prejudice, he doesn't invite other opinions, the "discussions" are just him rambling and dumping on other views
Just go to class and you will pass. His class is fun

The content of the class is interesting if you are at all interested in human behavior. He is also a very well-read man I would suggest networking with for future connections in your career. reviews.comment: ironic that a professor teaching stereotypes and prejudice would be so unethical and unreasonable.

This was the most chaotic class I've ever had. Unorganized professor, we always had to remind him what we were doing in class for the day or the upcoming weeks. He often forgot about assignments. You will be busy in this class, BUT the lectures are interesting and the discussions are engaging if you like the topic. He has done some solid research.

reviews.comment: His teaching is very unorganized and us students have to remind him of upcoming assignments. I cannot stress how much he forgets about upcoming quizzes and papers.
