reviews.comment: very unorganized but like the course material

He was not a great teacher--I'd say average at best. Pretty condescending and was not always the nicest guy in class. I had no interactions with him outside of class so I can't personally attest to his complete character.
I agree, either read the whole book and memorize it, or don't take the class. Not a very nice guy either if you need help. Don't recommend his class.

Class was not helpful at all. Dont go to class just study straight from the book and then check his online powerpoints (he takes points from them and puts them on the quiz). I failed most of the quizzes but aced the papers and still managed to get a good grade. Take it for an easy A if youre willing to read the textbook

Would definitely not recommend this professor. Went to every lecture, went in for office hours, emailed questions, etc and none of it was helpful. READ THE BOOK (probably should just memorize the whole thing) He takes out the slightest details from the text for tests. Lecture notes didn't even help on the tests. Good luck...
While his language is sometimes a bit coarse, he's always funny and very engaging.  I'd definitely recommend sticking with him.

If you're willing to put in the work, an A is very possible. No final, just seven short quizzes (you will have to read the text to do well on them). There is also six short papers over a news magazine and a group project at the end of the semester. He will reward attendance with random extra credit too. This course was curved. Overall great teacher

This class was very annoying to attend with Crandall as the professor. If you are thinking about psyc 104, don't take the big lecture class or Crandall's class. Almost all of the test questions come from very specific details from the book and very few from lecture. The papers are really easy.

Dr. Crandall is a highly intelligent professor who knows his stuff.  If you take this course, be prepared for curse words galore, as he does not care if he offends students.  The quizzes are extremely detailed and if you desire to do well, read the textbook thoroughly.  The curve is large and there is no final.  I had a 84% and still got an A.

I loved having Crandall as a teacher. He made the classes funny and made you actually want to go to his lectures. In order to do well on the tests, YOU HAVE TO READ THE BOOK. If you have your phone out, he will call you out infront of the wole class. Overall, I loved the course. I got high B's and some A's on the tests but with the curve I got an A

He is not hilarious. he seems funny at the begining, but then it just gets annoying, especially when he cusses. Kind of a ****. Mumbles a lot. Dont use cell phones! read the textbook and pay attention in class. curve is big! try to find a different teacher if able

Crandall is very much a psychology professor in the sense that because he knows about the mind, he thinks his mind is far superior than yours. However, he's got a sharp, raw sense of humor and is a good teach. I felt accomplished after getting high grades on the quizzes. Read your book! Kind of a jerk 1 on 1, great class curve. NO CELL PHONES!

A great teacher. He is interesting, funny and doesn't really care what anyone thinks of him. In order to get a really good grade, you have to read the textbook. The papers are easy and classes are usually fun.

This guy is hilarious. Easily the most interesting professor I've ever had.  Just be ready to work hard.  The lectures are really interesting.  It's almost tough to not pay attention to the guy.  Great taste in music too.
Won't let you have cell phones, head phones, or newspapers out in class. Definitely have to read the book.

Awesome teacher; attendance isnt usually mandatory but he always gives participation points. If you are at all interested in psychology (social in particular) he's one of the best sources for info. Great class overall.

He’s a great teacher, a bit arrogant, but really knows his stuff. Hope you like politics: he requires 6 short papers written on “The Nation” (left wing political periodical). Quizzes every other week; attendance not required, but helpful in passing class/quizzes. Be sure to attend at the end of the semester, he takes random attendance for credit.
He is awesome! so much fun! you want to go to his class. There is a lot of reading from the text book the test is totally based on the book not his lecture. But i highly reccoment him!!!!!!!!

Very good teacher, my favorite so far at KU. He made me want to attend class, which is hard considering most if not all of the test material came from the book! SO READ IT-when it came to the tests I got C's-I pretty much knew the material...he makes is questions very confusing but you should be fine...read the extra articles they are easy points!

Great teacher with a great sense of humor. The 'quizes' are ridiculously hard and are worth about 80% of your grade. READ THE BOOK. All of it. Don't skim. If you do, you might as well drop. Had a great time in class.  Listen for hints about quizzes in class. Paper was a joke. A+ and I did it the night before in an hour. Good luck!
Good teacher!! I really enjoyed his class and learned something. I def. recommend him as a teacher. He was really funny, too!
Great teacher, somewhat arrogant, but deserves to be. Show up to class and you'll get a good grade. The music and jokes before each lecture was great.

The Quizzes are majorly from the book. Read, take notes on the readings, and listen in class and you will do fine. There are two papers but, they are totally easy. He also curves the class. For example, this year an 84 was an A
If he tells you that you need to know something he will really mean it unlike alot of other professor
very easy. never went to class and got a high A. he seems kind of arrogant, but also very intelligent.
lectures are interesting, but not relevant to much on the tests.
Read the book, learn it, can get an A.

be sure to read the text for detail! he'll pull the most minute facts out for the "quizzes." his arrogance is sometimes entertaining. he frequently uses profanity, but often this just makes it seem like he's trying too hard to connect with the "youngsters."

crandall may be arrogant, but he also knows what he's talking about.  i went to class, got high B's on all of my "quizzes" (tests), and received an A.  he curves quite a bit, and i really enjoyed his lectures.
Crandall is an ****. The times I actually went to class I fell asleep because he is so damn boring.
POMPOUS!!!!
He is very interesting and makes class fun.  The class is really hard but there is a very nice curve.
Great professor, funny, lectures are very interesting and entertaining, his tests can be tough, but be sure to study for them and you'll be fine. Also, DO THE READING!
His ego can hardly fit in the room! Pretty good teacher though, READ THE TEXT!!
hard, and crandell is an **** quizes are way to hard
He really has a passion for whats hes teaching. His energy really makes you intrested in what he has to say.
Complete Jerk. Nuff said.
ok
Wow...most of you are being nice. This guy is mean and NOT funny. He likes to brag that he went to Yale but he also brags about not being able to balance his check book. D- in my book.
He sucks, so mean!
He was an awesome professor!  I couldn't wait to go to class.  If you ever get the chance to study under him I would definately go for it!
Hard subject perfect Prof

Class is entertaining, the exams are not too difficult, but you definitly need to study for them and make sure you read the book because some of the questions are only from leacture and some of the questions are only from the book reading.
No Comments
No Comments
Awesome teacher, makes class fun to go to
He is a really good professor who makes class very interesting.
Good, entertaining teacher.  Very good teacher, but puts confusing questions on his tests.
Exam are very difficult and 70% of your grade

Kelvie is genuinely one of the sweetest professors I've ever met; however, that doesn't translate to her teaching. During the lecture, the materials feel very easy, and you'll seem to understand it all. When it comes to exams, that's when you have to prepare. Especially the multiple-choice questions. EVERYTHING IS TIMES HARDER ON THE EXAM.

Kelvie was a great and caring professor. I felt the class is very dense/comprehensive but she does a good job of teaching it. One piece of advice I will give is to not rely on the final grade replacement, the last exam is very difficult.

Notes are terrible, no good examples to help us for tests, she didn't make sense for one second this semester... how can you not convey your own note packet to your students and give us work that helps us succeed.  Makes my brain hurt taking this class and having to teach myself
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A wonderful person but lectures can be confusing at times. It is best to review the lectures at least twice before the test.
Great person, awful teacher.

Took her over the summer for ACCT 201 and had a great experience. She taught the class with enthusiasm each day. She seems to genuinely enjoy answering questions and engaging her class. She makes her learning expectations clear and lectures her material in an organized fashion. I would gladly take her classes again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kelvie is a great instructor for ACCT 320. It took me awhile to get back into the swing of accounting and she helped me catch up. She understood what my goal was in the class and was able to help me. She will always listen to you. This was the toughest course I have ever taken. Definitely go to class, participate and read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed Kelvie and her class. She is really enthusiastic in her lectures and you can tell. She follows the course packet really well. 320 will be difficult regardless of your professor, I highly recommend taking it with Kelvie!

Pretty easy and enjoyable class, and Kelvie is a great lecturer. Only reason I didn't get an A is because I lost so many participation points from skipping class. Tests + and final are reasonable, and not a big portion of your grade (40%). 3% of total grade available as extra credit. Posts so many study resources, such as past tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS--Would take again

reviews.comment: I love Kelvie! She gave us opportunities to see her during office hours and you should utilize them. Sometimes we just talked about accounting and life. This class is similar to 320. Do well on the first exam because the second and third exams are more difficult. Do what you did in 320 to be successful!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Kelvie is awesome. A lot of people complain that she talks fast, but it is necessary for the amount of material that needs to be covered. If you do everything you are supposed to in this class you will do fine. The group project is a huge part of the grade that takes SO much time but is not hard.  I would recommend taking this class with Kelvie!
This is a good course but can be difficult without prior exposure to accounting. It moves very quickly, with a good deal of coursework.

201 is a big class so she is actually nice to every student when they asked her questions. She gave us lots of extra credit, and the exam is not relatively so important for you final grade. Love her class

Kelvie is a great professor because she provides guided notes and bases the tests off of them! There is a semester long project so make sure your group is a solid choice, but you have to pick in the first lab.  Every monday there is a pop quiz and every wednesday there are important participation points so show up. Lab is also helpful.

Hands down one of the best professors I've  had at KU. The class is well structured and Kelvie is really passionate about what she teaches. The tests are very reasonable, if you attend class and pay attention you are bound to get an A. There is a course packet that is super helpful and there is a group long project, so chose your group wisely!

This class is clearly structured.  Kelvie uses a course packet for note taking and it makes things much easier.  Posts an older version of exams before each exam for you to study with which is helpful but not reliable.  This class has two downfalls:  it is plus/minus and there's a comprehensive group project that drags throughout the semester.

Kelvie is a good speaker. She knows the material well, and organizes it in a simple way. The course packet makes notes as easy as possible. The tests are moderately difficult, but if you use the course packet, nearly everything is covered there.

Kelvie rocks! One of the most down to earth teachers I have had at KU. I HATE accounting and by the end of the semester I looked forward to coming to class. Tons of resources to pass with a great grade.
More points added for the summer class,that makes more chance to get A

This class has been one of the hardest classes I have taken at KU.  Super nice and spunky but goes extremely fast in class.  Her tests are horrible, and are nothing like the study guides.  The comprehensive quizzes are tough too.  There are quizzes throughout the semester as well.  Some are pop quizzes but most are not.  Hard class.

Kelvie structured her class very well, and was clear in her expectations. The tests were difficult, but not impossible, and the quizzes were frequent enough to dilute the effects of the midterm and final.

Do not take ACCT 201 with Kelvie. Wait until fall to take it with a different professor. She goes way to fast in her lectures and makes the content way more confusing than it needs to be. She says she's a "visual learner" so that makes her teaching style almost impossible for those that aren't visual learners. TOUGHEST A IVE EVER RECEIVED
I like her class,it is the best class i have taken so far

The notes are already typed for you so you only have to fill in small pieces from lectures. She teaches each topic several different ways, so you have to actually learn the material instead of just going through the steps. The tests are tough and there is a semester-long group project, so pick a good team. You can learn a lot from this class.

Kelvie is an awesome teacher. She truly loves accounting and it shows in her teaching. Yes, this class is difficult, but if you go to class and truly understand the material, don't just memorize problems, you will make it through and probably with a pretty good grade!
Very fast paced lectures.  Large class size.  Very spunky and somewhat entertaining, but it can also be annoying.  Overall very necessary class for business students.  You'll get out what you put in.

Kelvie is not nearly as bad as other reviewers are leading on. Her class does make you work for your grade, but we are in college... She gives study guides and course packets which are very helpful for the exams. Also, there are tons of extra credit and project point activities to keep you in the clear. Seems like a nice lady, too.
She is of no help, gives tough assignments, and is not clear during lecture. She goes through practice problems as if we've been in accounting for years as a career. Very hard class!

I would avoid this class. I am very good at accounting and I am just trying to make it out alive. Tests are extremely difficult and the MC are next to impossible. the only reason I have a B- right now is because of projects, participation points, and extra credit. No need for this class to be so hard. Def do not take this class at KU, take at JCCC

Lectures weren't too bad, most were online, then she would work through a problem in class. As long as you read and do the out of class "optional" assignments you'll be fine. The quizzes have weird arbitrary deadlines that seemed to move around a lot during the course. She would move if things came up with work and such, so that was helpful.

Tests are 10x harder than anything you do in the study guide or in the class. Never finishes lectures, so your "discussion" turns into another lecture. The only positive is there are a lot of homework and group project points that will keep your safely in the B range if you go to class and pay attention.

Terrible teacher, lectures were all over the place. Taught the most simple example problems, then on test she expects you to know the problem in a completely new format never seen before. Didn't crack open the damn book once, and never referred to it even though you pay out the $$$ for it. Online HW never helped me learn material. SUCKS.

Kelvie makes her exams impossible. She teaches you the most basic concepts and then expects you to be able to apply them to questions that are fifteen times more difficult than anything you've ever seen. The average for the last exam was an F and she refuses to curve. She has terrible office hours and is slow to respond to emails. Not well taught.

lectures were all over the place and confusing.  I learned more from the TAs in a matter of minutes than I did in her lectures. I would say avoid if possible, but she teaches a mandatory class for B-school which baffles me.

Hybrid course, meet half the times, study the rest online.  Online videos are mediocre, sometimes grainy, some might have been better taught in person.  Online HW is easy, quizzes and group work fair, final a bit challenging.  Except for a couple of times when you present, you could travel for work and take this course.
Tough final exam. Alot of free points but tests are very difficult and requires alot of studying. They should make this class easier.

Kelvie is an okay teacher. Outside of the classroom, she's the sweetest woman ever. However, I agree that the tests are pretty hard, and I would probably be doing a lot worse if I didn't have some test files. She gives you the basic info and asks pretty difficult questions on the test.

Like all profs, Kelvie makes you work for your grade.  If you go to class, lab, & keep up-it's not too bad. Sometimes she runs out of time & rushes, but if you go to lab or open the book you'll be fine. TA Maggie Kopp is great! If you're a bschool major & can't keep up in Kelvies class, might I suggest you change your major. It only gets worse…

Kelvie is a great teacher! Some may not like her, but the only reason I can see why people wouldn't like her is because you actually have to work for your grade. Do the homework, READ the textbook,and go to class and STUDY hard and you will do well.

Kelvie is one of the BEST instructors I've had at KU. This is my second degree at KU and she deserves a lot of credit. You MUST do the homework and study! She is knowledgeable and her TA's helpful. She brings an enthusiasm to the class and this makes a huge difference. She has real world experience. Lots of work but you learn a ton! Very satisfied.
I'll cut to the chase Kelvie is the worst teacher I have ever had.

I think Kelvie is a great teacher. I can follow the course packet easily. My problem were her tests. Kelvie likes to teach you the basics and then she'll throw in other info that you haven't practiced and expect you to figure it out like common sense. Luckily, I had a great TA who reviewed possible problems she would give out.
The class material by nature is tough and boring but Kelvie Crabb helps you through it during lecture and her TAs are some of the best I've ever met

Kelvie is literally useless, she doesn't teach you anything in class and the course packs you fill out during lecture are just about worthless. By far one of the laziest professors I have ever encountered. It seriously blows my mind that somebody actually decided it was a good idea to hire her.
The material is hard, face it. Kelvie challenges students but well worth it.  You learn a lot. She's tough, but fair.

Her tests are hard but each test is only worth 7% of your grade and one test can be replaced with the final and the final is much easier than her mid term tests. Make sure to do all the homework because 25 extra credit points are build in.  Make sure to go to class to get all of the iclicker points.  It's free points if you just go to class.

Although the class is very hard, Prof. Crabb got me through it. Her office hours aren't the best, but she's flexible with your schedule. Honestly, I can't think of a better teacher to teach such a hard class as 320. Her handwriting is bad, but she explains everything very thoroughly. I would love her to teach all of my classes.

Class is boring but is easier than previous semesters. Review packets for tests are somewhat useless but TA's are willing to help. Final is near impossible, so do all the HW and get maximum points on group projects. Studied over 35 hours for the final only to get C but got an A- overall. If you can get low B's on the tests you'll be fine for an A.

I don't understand how everyone doesn't like Kelvie. She is smart, friendly, reasonable, and a good instructor. Her tests are hard but her reviews are helpful, TAs are AMAZING, she has a final replacement policy and the projects/hmwrk help pull your grade up. I think she is an incredible instructor and great person. I recommend this class for sure!
Great teacher!  I definitely recommend her for introductory accounting.  If you read the book and pay attention, you will do fine.

Gives you a packet like a second grader and you fill in the blanks. Class is boring but the packet helps with the test. As long as you study the packet the test is pretty easy. The book is ONLY used for online hw.

The class is at times overkill. There is so much material to learn in a very short amount of time. However, Kelvie is really interested in what she's teaching. Meet with her during office hours, attend class and put in effort and you'll get what you put in.
the class is hard but i really liked her. kelvie prides herself on having hard tests so at least she can admit it. she makes things really clear and easy to understand

She seems nice at first but it quickly goes downhill. At times appears unprepared, tests are more difficult than they should be, and are often too long to be completed within the given time. Last test there were 25 out of 30 students still working on it when time was up. Dumps grading off to her TA's and doesn't take blame for her mistakes.

Although the content of the class is rather mundane, she really tries to keep you interested and make sure you understand the material by using real-life examples. Go to class, and do the work, you'll get an A

Kelvie is a very good teacher and cares abt. her students understanding the material.She applies the concepts we learn to real world applications. My only complaint is that quizzes are difficult to read on the overhead. If you put the effort in you will learn a lot in this course.

Worst teacher I have ever had and I got an A in the class!  I really tried to like her, but she made the class brutal.  She does not cover any problems (and the few problems she attempted to teach she screwed up).  You will need to teach yourself how to do the problems to be successful because the tests are mostly accounting problems.

Kelvie's class is pretty boring but she tries to spice it up always talking about cookies and beer. If u show up and pay attention a tiny bit you will get at least a B. Lots of extra credit built in. Test are somewhat hard but about the same as Acct 200. Study and you will get an A

i dont know if its because of her or just the subject itself, but this class was excruciating. lectures were a bore, but you have to come because there is a quiz every day. group projects are stupid and a waste of time, same with individual ones. tests were a challenge but not horrible. oh yeah, theres homework too

She mostly teaches master level classes, so this class was close to impossible. Her lectures are boring and hard to understand and the exams are confusing some is new material that has never been covered.
Do not take he dont grade anything
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His grading was odd and unpredictable, but he was understanding. I had a rough semester and he helped me through it. The class needs you to spread out work due to heavy reading and assignments. I loved him and would take another class. He's super understanding if you communicate. Tough class for my first semester—attending is key to keeping up.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Whenever I commented I would be interrupted halfway through and he would deconstruct my incomplete answer. No grades for any paper by the last week. (But he had time to give me zeros on work that was minutes late). Attendance/grading was harsh relative to our class w/ few active participants. Nice guy, but my investment in class did not pay off.

I took English 105 and he waited til the semester was over and grades were due to grade 3 out of the 4 essays, even though we were meant to get a 2 week revision period on the first 2 essays. He never gave a single essay grade to anyone above a 92. He rambles in class about nothing important. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IT WILL DROP YOUR GPA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: My chief complaint about him is that he never graded papers when he said he would, so my class never knew how he graded exactly. He graded our first two papers during Christmas break. Keep in mind we submitted five total papers and he never graded our last three. Not cool Doug, not cool.

Never received feedback on the 3 papers we wrote before the final. Very knowledgeable and cool guy. Great insight on the readings and helpful during mandatory writing conferences. But unclear expectations and grading criteria made this class difficult. For grade-conscious students, this may be the course you avoid. Interested in his other classes!

Easily the toughest English class I have ever taken. The readings and journal entries combined were easily 6-8 hours of work per week, and I haven't even factored in the 3 papers yet. Don't let his laid back attitude fool you, he is an extremely tough grader when it comes to those papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Doug for a 500 level nonfiction class. He gave minimal feedback on my essays and non-existent feedback on the critiques I turned in for other people. He barely controls workshop in class and often only left 10 minutes for the last person. The books he had us read were the most educational part of the class.

Before taking this course, I did not have a high appreciation for poetry. Doug truly changed my opinion by the end of the semester, due to the classes being so focused and centered on discussion. He facilitated the discussions without forcing his opinions on any student. Tough grader, but I ultimately took so much away from this class. Recommended.

Mr. Crawford-Parker made poetry interesting, but I had an average of 5 hours per week in homework outside of class. The homework consists of page long journal entries that cover the reading for the night. You have to do this 3 times a week. He grades hard on the papers, but if you do the work and show up to class, you won't fail.

Dry subject matter and boring content. Takes forever to grade papers and grades them hard. Lots of reading assigned for each class. Don't take if you're looking for an easy A or just to get a credit out of the way.
Awesome class, highly recommended.

Parker only focuses on analysis; you will not write your own poetry. He's a very thorough grader. The workload compounds heavily if you don't keep up. If you want a guaranteed A, try a different professor. If you really want to develop your writing/analysis skills, Parker is probably the best prof. for that.
Smart and dry sense of humor. The people rating him really poorly are idiots. He grades tougher that most, but he will work with you to improve.

Good professor who challenges you but doesn't make it ridiculous. People complain that he doesn't answer questions clearly, but that's because he wants you to think for yourself. There's a lot of reading, especially later on in the course, but it's not much more than other English classes. Put in effort and do all the homework and you'll be fine.

I did not like him as a professor. His class was extremely boring, and we had a ridiculous amount of reading due each class period. He is a harsh grader on papers, and his expectations are often unclear. Journal entries and class participation are easy points, so make sure you do them. I also recommend doing the extra credit assignments. Good luck.

Extremely slow to grade things and get them returned. Attendance is mandatory, which sucks because class is very boring. All you really have to do is keep a journal and write papers, so make sure you stay on top of reading the books!

I took the online poetry class and his grading was really harsh. I have never gotten grades this bad in english. There is no rubric so I don't know where the missing points came from. I resubmitted an assignment with 2 forgotten paragraphs (including conclusion) after getting 98 points/130 and he gave me only 4 more points. Absurd really.

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! He returns ALL papers late and grades harshly. Until this class, I had received ONE B on a paper in my entire life...I received a B- on the first paper and had to struggle throughout the rest of the class to meet his unrealistic, unclear standards.
He was constantly late in returning papers he had to push back every paper's due date and this class was horribly boring.
*non-fiction writing* Great class!  Really helpful and encouraging toward student writing. He's fine if you turn in work late - as long as you do it in a reasonable amount of time.

This is the easiest class I have taken at KU, but expect to fall asleep every class. You just have to write a few papers, memorize three short poems and recite them to the class, and the final is three, two-paged papers.

I fell asleep in his class every time! Even when I wasn't tired at all! There was hardly ANY homework, the papers were very easy, and he graded exreamly easy. I received a much higher grade in the class than I deserved.

This teacher is pretty good.  Work load was reasonable, and he wasn't hard on people who turned stuff in late, as long as they turned it in.  In general, he was encouraging to the students and their writing.  Plus, although he is a writer, he never talked about his own writing, which was nice.
this dude is horrible

Worst and most boring class ever. Repetitive questions on homework. If you ask a question, you almost feel ridiculed. He never hands back anything hardly. It took almost 2 months to get our papers back. No idea of how you're doing in the class. VERY BORING. Stupid assignments, readings, group discussions, and in class activites. But, he grades ok.
Absolutely BORING. Too much work...made me un-interested in poetry. Not helpful unless you are a suck up. Do not take this class with this professor.
He was very unhelpful and class was horrible to get through.  Not a good teacher, he was terrible at getting the class engaged in discussion.
As one user mentioned, avoid this class! Workload is entirely too much!

AVOID! Workload is RIDICULOUS. We're writing 4 pages weekly. I like poetry but this is insane. Take Intro to fiction or take 210 from someone else b/c this guy assigns way too much writing given the material (and I'm an English major!).
No Comments
No Comments

Overall I would say that this class was helpful and enhanced my learning. We had assignments due every M,T,W,Th so you really have to stay on top of it and keep up. The late penalty is an automatic 50% off an in some cases 0%. Our TA graded pretty tough and nitpicky and often times didn't provide specific feedback and in some cases unnecessarily.
If you are not religious pick and religion and pray you do well in this class

This class is excessive, not because of the content, but because of the unnecessary workload and poor organization. She gives way too much busy work, just for the graders to doc points for small details. Quizzes often don't match videos and there are tight deadlines for no reason that also overlap with studio deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Shannon and 605 are tough. The class is time and effort consuming, and the TAs and the professor will be highly demanding. Lots of homework and projects in which detail and visual aspects are key. Weekly readings and projects with extent grading rubric. Even so, Shannon cares about his class and her students, showing interest in the class is key.

Shannon gets a bad rap for ARCH 605. Yes… it's a lot of busy work, and some of it is a waste of time, but there is some useful things that I've learned from this course. Shannon is overall a very sweet lady, if you have any questions she will help you. I don't think she warrants that bad reviews that people have gave her tbh.

If you have a medical reason to miss class and show her, good luck with her caring. You will still get points deducted. Oh also to make sure to quadruple check on projects because she will give an example and rubric to go by and when you do she will mark it all wrong since she will change her mind last minute as to how she wants things done!
she is so helpful and caring! She knows a lot about the field with decades of experience.
Shannon is a wonderful person who is always available when you need her. She gives great advice and is always willing to provide outside resources for her students to learn.

So much busy work. She makes you draw notes she puts out every week and is very picky about how its done so get ready to spend hours just trying to meet her standards. Any interest in the topics she speaks on might be gone by the time shes done talking about it.

Shannon really cares about the her students and really strives to help you develop your project. She is a little coy about the negative aspects of your project but as long as you're paying attention you will figure it out. I think Shannon is one of the best professors at KU but you'll definitely put in the work. This class is a full time job.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The workload was incredibly unrealistic for an online class during a PANDEMIC. There was no clear plan or structure for the whole semester and there is very little room for individual creativity. She grades by a very harsh rubric so If you don't do it her way you probably won't do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although she is a very nice person, Prof. Criss has the most unrealistic expectations for tasks. Everything in her class is extremely time consuming and mainly busy work. The organization of the class Is terrible, there is always so much she wants us to do with unclear direction. Respectfully, I hope I never take a class with Prof. Criss again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Shannon Criss made me change the way that I have taken notes for 13 years. We have to illustrate our notes, and when we don't have enough drawings, we are docked points. She does not respond to emails, and makes her TAs do all the work. She does not give any opportunity for creativity, if you don't do it her way exactly, you won't get the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Shannon Criss is a confusing and time consuming class. Many aspects of her class is irrelevant. Her classes waste time since she doesn't actually lecture but you waste about 45 minutes of actual class time every week. Her class is uncoordinated and unprofessional. She should not be teaching until she learns how to follow a concise plan.

Shannon is one of the two teachers that typically teaches Natural Forces, so youll likely end up with her. She doesnt deserve the hate she gets. Shes a really sweet lady but also very critical about graphic display and work output. Put in everything you got and youll be fine. I think she was a good teacher, but the class felt rushed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great amazing person. Not so great as a prof. The class felt unorganized and rushed. We spent way too much time on the research (the first HALF of the semester) and had no time to develop our ideas.

she is very nit picky and if its not done her way its not right. Also she takes forever to grade your projects so u will not get any feedback until all your assignments are in. In the labs there is a lot of work and not a lot of time to do it so its really stressful. I also scheduled meetings with her that she never even showed up for

Her projects in class are hard to understand and complete in the time available. You have to buy the book from the university and it is non refundable it said (Fall 2013 on the cover).  Read from the book she put together and take notes, then listen to her talk about the same section of the book that you just read and take notes to turn in.

suggestions are really requirements. if you do exactly what is written for an assignment (in terms of number of drawings) you will get an "average" or a C. she is helpful if you are willing to pay close attention and think really really hard about what is said. i mean like sit there for an hour thinking, doing nothing else. few A's given (2 maybe)
No Comments
She was very flexible with her projects and was always open to the students' opinions. And she cares about the environment which is a huge plus!
No Comments

Shannon was MIA half of the time we were in class and she didn't make herself available ouside of class. She blew off meetings with students all the time.  She is HORRIBLE at time management, not a very understanding teacher, and not very eager to help.
Very Spaced out all the time.  At times blew off meetings with students.I took her for her good reputation, but she seemed to be a completely different person than what she was described as.
The professor is solid, no complaints

I like Claire as a person. She is enjoyable. However, her lectures are a bit tedious, so I just do my homework during them. The class is easy. Pay attention in lab when you're looking at the hand samples and study a few hours for the lab exams and you should be fine. The group project is also extremely easy.

I took this class knowing it might be out of my comfort zone. I was shocked to discover Claire often goes on long rants that make me quite uncomfortable it's always about her personal life. I'm not the kinda person to fill one of these out but having to hear about her “awful” life when I just came to get credit really makes it hard in class.

Claire is very passionate about the chemical structures of minerals and mineralogy is an important course if your interested in geology at all, but the lectures were disorganized and would sometime devolve into her ranting or retelling stories when we were already weeks behind. Her GTAs didint communicate well with her and the 311 lab was a mess
He was not my fav professor I've had not a very fun class I paid tuition for this! :(

Dysfunctional and chaotic class. Instructions are never clear. The TA's never know how to answer questions, but somehow are able to grade the worksheets as tough as a final paper. The lecture is a study hall to do the worksheets. The amount of homework is not bad but be ready for ridiculously tough grading. Material is not covered clearly. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Unorganized and chaotic course. Classes were basically study halls to do worksheets, you are not actually taught. TAs never know the answers to questions but can oddly still grade those problems. Did not take for credit thankfully, but it was not a good class and although they are very nice and occasionally lenient, they are not a good instructor.

C is a character but a very kind person. Cares about the students and very relaxed grader/person. Very smart and knowledgeable about the subject but not the best lecturer. Content was pretty boring and hard to understand but my grade doesnt reflect that so big ups.

I really liked how Dr. Marshall did the class for the semester. I wasn't too keen on doing so many sketches for the worksheets, but at the end of the day, I got the material down. The review lectures for the exams were very helpful and made the exams much less stressful.

Dr. Marshall is very passionate about geology and breaks down complex concepts into easily digestible analogies. There is a lot of homework that comes with this course, but it all is very helpful when exams roll around. Their lectures are intriguing and chalked full of useful information for those going into natural resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Craig is a great person and very knowledgeable. This material is hard and most of it is not the most interesting.

Craig is a great guy that cares a lot about the subject. He takes time in class to really make sure you get the material as well as individual time to go over any questions. He played rugby in Australia and he came to nearly all the KU club games I invited him to. Got to chat with him a lot after games, he's a cool guy.
Go to class, weekly quizzes over material, no tests, final is over quizzes. Show up and youll get an A

Fantastic instructor- clear about expectations, makes time for students, responsive to emails, and provides .ppt files on Blackboard prior to class (in fact, most of them were uploaded within the first month of the course).  Difficult material, but he makes it fun and engaging.

Mineralogy, hard class.  I dont rag on people but this guy has a temper and is flippant about his grading.  One day he says he'll raise everone's grade, the next day he says he never said such a thing. He does allow you to write a paragrahp to ask for more points on questions,  but then gets mad if he has to regrade and may take points away.
Really nice guy, very helpful. If you study, tests are pretty easy. Helps you with what information will be on the tests. Liked the class.

Very nice & helpful teacher. Only four tests, he drops one of your lowest test grades. I had no interest in geology, but he made it interesting. You do not have to go to class, he puts his lectures on Blackboard & his tests come straight from that. Go to class the day before the test for the review session. He tells you what is on the test!

Class was fairly interesting. Everyone failed first test so he weighted it. He also let us do a 1 pg. bonus essay for a 10% boost. He is Australian and not quite with it sometimes, but he's obviously willing to help. A good guy.
No Comments

Very heavy reading before almost each lecture and the lecture is just a massive yap session which maybe slightly helps your understanding of the book. There is currently about a week left in the semester and only my first paper's grade and half of the Microsoft teams posts have been put in so I don't have a great idea of my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor didn't grade anything until after finals week and graded things extremely harshly. There is no opportunity for corrections or learning in this class due to the lack of feedback on assignments. You will not know until after it is too late whether you pass or fail. He spends most of the lecture time talking about irrelevant things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: a classically bad professor. Our first 2 papers were graded two days before the end of finals week, despite our promised 2 week revision period. Our second 2 papers were graded the night after grades were due, with the grades we already had in the class. The content was interesting, but just pick up 4 versions of Frankenstein yourself and move on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just know nothing will be graded until nearly the end of the semester. You will have to write four super detailed papers and literally will not receive feedback/grades until end of semester/after semester ended. All of our papers were finally graded in January, after the semester ended. Waste of your time and stress. Very poor communication

I took this class for a core requirement and honors credit, take for neither. All you do is read 5 books and write 4 analytical papers. He gives no rubric for papers and never gave higher than an A- as seen on canvas. My peers denoted that my papers were high quality to be given a B on each. Unless your an English major, avoid Doug at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Crawford-Parker was a soporific lecturer with a poor mind for selecting interesting texts. His grading scale seldom reflected the amount of work required for each assignment, and grades were entered at an iceberg pace. Do not, under any circumstances, take Professor Crawford-Parker unless absolutely necessary.

ENGL300 is required for English majors at KU, so I had to take this class. I dropped ENGL355 for next semester, just so I don't have him again. It's the weekend before finals, he hasn't graded a single thing all semester. He didn't respond to a single email I sent. I didn't learn or improve at all. Avoiding his classes at all costs in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his class last semester and he didn't grade anything until the day grades were due. How am I supposed to improve on papers if I don't get feedback? Definitely a professor to avoid. Also expects his students to purchase specific expensive editions of classics just so we can read one or two of the essays in the back...

I enjoyed our class discussions and interpretations, however, there are several issues here. For one, I did not receive a SINGLE grade until after the last day of class & I never got any feedback on any of my essays. Also, he says he responds to emails quickly, but I often went more than a week without a response. Must contribute a lot in class too

Its the end of April and he has not graded a single assignment. Every class is group discussions and half of them don't even make sense for what we read for that class period. Seems very nice, but doesn't actually answer questions helpfully.

Doug's pretty interesting with his teaching style (in a good way).  He'll work with you to achieve becoming a proficient reader of fiction and will take the time to help each student in the class meetings.  If you love to read and write, this class will be awesome as you get well thought-out feedback for all of your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this if you're just trying to take care of your core requirements. There's lengthy reading assignments for every class, and you also have to write about all of them. On top of that there's a Lot of papers. If that sounds like something you can handle, go for it. If it sounds challenging, better to pass ENGL 102 than fail ENGL 105.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Be ready to write and open up a little bit about your life. Doug makes everyone feel comfortable in the space he creates and is an overall chill dude. I learned a lot about others and myself in this class and it was an extremely formative experience. I would recommend it to everyone in college. Pretty easy grader as well.

He is a great teacher! He is very available during his office hours and answers questions via email promptly with great feedback. If you pay attention during lectures, it helps write the essays. The assignments are focused toward writing mechanics. I learned a lot from this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I'm sure Doug is a great guy but his class is uninspiring and forgettable. Instead of encouraging discussion he usually just talks himself. His input is not relevant nor is it interesting. He clearly has a specific political agenda and does not enjoy any challenges to his disposition. His papers & assignments are tedious and not thought provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really liked Doug, he is a great professor and very helpful if you ask for it. Sometimes he talks too much, and it made me get impatient in the end of the semester, but it's nothing you can't put up with.

Doug knows his stuff.  He's very interested in the essay and it shows.  I learned a great deal in the class but be prepared for a LOT of paperwork and reading.  That's the only negative I can think of.  It was overall a positive experience.  Also, even though it's nonfiction writing, you spend the majority of the class critiquing other writing.

Professor Crawford-Parker is amazing. He expects a lot out of his students and, since most of his classes are smaller, he can tell easily if you didn't do the reading. That being said, do the reading! The journal entries are simple and easy points. He is a tough grader but will work with you whenever you need. Amazing professor. Take from Doug!
Great teacher. Everything you want in a class. Group discussion, clear class format, and fair grading. Highly recommended.

Doug is a pretty cool professor, he is always very helpful, and he is ridiculously smart. The class itself isn't difficult, but there is a lot of busy work, like writing journal entries. No midterm or final, just 3 essays

Easy grader but when you ask him a question, he beats around the bush. NO questions were ever answered clearly. All the assignments would have been even easier if he could actually explain things in a normal, logical way!
He was slow to grade. Not very helpful or encouraging. No doubt that he knows his stuff but isn't very good at translating that knowledge to his students.

Professor Herron is literally my favorite teacher, he is so passionate and you can tell that he loves teaching and organizing the orchestra. I see a bright future for the music program under his supervision and i am excited to take his class again next semester!
just show up to class and he is so awesome
He's genius! He has a very funny and relatable metaphor for everything.

Wonderful director! Very inspirational, caring and musical. I love how he connects with us as he conducts! He is well respected by the students and treats everyone with respect. Rehearsals are funny and engaging!

The guy is super nice and he's pretty funny most of the time but he has no idea of what he is doing. His conducting is not up to any standard and his musical knowledge is circumstantial at best. People loves his attitude but he has no business working as a director at a university.
Hard for freshman! Practice lots! Great guy!
Attendance policy is rough (only 3 absences allowed before you're kicked out) but otherwise great
He's awesome. Always makes sure the class is engaging and tells fun stories.

Creston Herron is a beacon of positivity in any room he walks into. I am currently in KU Symphony Orchestra with this being his first year as our director and he is doing a fantastic job with being efficient and inspiring to his students and colleagues. He is very educated, caring, and passionate about the orchestra. Amazing person and educator.
Professor Marsh is a sweetie and is always good for a story! He is very relaxed and not strict with the course content at all; he really just wants you to gain as much as you can.
He loves to talk (not always on topic), but honestly could be way worse.
Curtis is an amazing person and teacher. He cares deeply about encouraging public speaking among ku students, and has very engaging lectures.
I loved Curtis' class. Honestly one of the best professors I have had. My favorite class I have had as well. I wish he would teach more classes, I would take them in a heartbeat.

Curtis is great, class is pretty much just conversations and participation. Each week there's a short journal due and the final was just a paper that was really easy. Easy grader and really laid-back.
The class materials are comprehensive.
Great class. The professor is friendly and helpful.
Useful and easy class.
Great professor! Clear explanation and genuinely cares about students' success.

Casper ran the class smoothly and was fair in grading all the speeches. He always explained why each student received the grade and gave clear guidance on how to improve for their presentation. He also asked for everyone's feedback on how he graded other assignments because some students might not feel confident speaking up. Very kind grader!

Mr Curry is rather "harsh" in a tough Texan kind of way. He shows "no mercy." I don't know about the kind thoughts of others. For me, he was harsh. Looks at you with some sort of "Don't you know this by now?" kind of gaze. Could be vindictive in a Texas kind of way, too. Yes, he does like to talk, but that is his ego talking, and not any kind soul.

Professor Curry is a great lab instructor. He is very clear, and he has very specific and fair expectations for everyone. If you don't follow his instructions, he will penalize you, but it doesn't take long to get used to writing lab reports his way, which is the correct way. He gives great explanations as well as fantastic stories.
Fantastic lab instructor. If you have questions about anything, he will answer them, and then some. Explains everything before the lab begins and if you need help after the lab he always has time.
He's like a Santa Claus from the South. Very clear and direct, gives good instruction, and grades fairly.  10x better than any TA I've had.
Excellent lab instructor! He always has the time to sit down and help, and he's very good at explaining.

Professor Curry is an excellent lab professor. As the director of labs, he is very knowledgeable and expects a lot out of his students. If you need help, he is more than willing to help, but he sometimes is not very clear. Make sure you use the lab manual and his infamous "yellow pages"!!!

Explains everything before the lab starts, and is really helpful. He grades pretty hard but if you totally screw up the lab he won't fail you. He also loves to talk and talk and talk. Overall he is a really good teacher and if you have him you will learn a lot from him.

Bob is the best lab instructor i've ever had. explains EVERYTHING before lab begins. will answer any questions or help you figure out any problem with equipment, procedure, etc. always willing to see you outside of lab to help with report. grades fairly. i took honors physics and had him for lab, but if you are lucky, he teaches other sections too.

Dr. Cushing split lectures with a GTA for this class because the original professor had medical issues. I always looked forward to the days he would lecture! Incredible lecturer--I wish he taught more undergrad classes!

He's a reliable professor that really knows what he's talking about. He's not one of those professor's that reads off of the slides. He takes the time to explain the concepts in depth. The summary papers are easy but a little annoying. Also, there was an incident in class where someone showed up late to class and got told off, so beware of that.

Cushing always makes his lectures interesting and very relatable. He seems like an all around good guy who cares about everyone in his class, and you can tell. There is a good amount of writing but it's nothing too bad, and the in and out-of-class quizzes are pretty easy! Would definitely recommend this class and this professor.
This is a class that everyone should take. Dr. Cushing is great lecturer and consistently keeps his lectures interesting.

Chris is a great teacher that really cares about his students. I bought the book for this and never used it once. The tests are easy if you study. The only difficult part is a synthesis paper but he's pretty lenient on it. You also get a lot of points from in and out of class quizzes so it's not difficult to get an A
Great professor who wants you to succeed. Definitely take this class with him
Very helpful, just beware of the number of papers.

Dr. Cushing was by far one of the best professors I have had at KU. His lectures are interesting, he sets clear, attainable goals for his students and makes the class enjoyable, but still packed with information. Writing is a key part of the class, but if you pay attention in lecture, and do the quizzes, it is very easy to do well in the class.
Super nice and funny guy. Thoroughly enjoyed his lecturing style. Great class.
This is one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. You should take it. He is a fantastic teacher and really wants you to pass.

Best teacher I've had. With all the quizzes it seems like it'd be difficult, but the quizzes aren't bad and they give you most the questions to the test. This is a professor that knows how to teach and isn't just educated on the topic he's teaching.
He's very knowledgeable in his field of study. Easy grade if you just  go to class and do the work. Test are like the quizzes.

In & out of class quizzes for every lecture. Summary papers & a final paper, but they're really easy. Exams were not difficult as long as you took the quizzes seriously & showed up to class.  I reviewed lecture notes & got As on all of the exams. Adds points to exams depending on the class outcome. Lectures are interesting & the class is an easy A.

Honestly, the best professor I've ever had at Oklahoma State. I took abnormal child psychology with him and he was amazing. I didn't want to leave the class, and I typically hate lecture based classes. Funny guy, but not rude funny. Very helpful, very clear in his teaching, passionate about what he does, his lectures are entertaining but you learn.
Great great teacher! Very clear with the subject material and he gives you a very good chance of getting an A with the assignments and tests he gives you. I would suggest him to anyone!
I loved Cushing. His exams are easy because he assigns in-class and out-of-class quizzes throughout the semester. He is very educated in the field of child psychology and he's a super funny guy.

I took his geography class during my first semester of freshman year. It was clear, and I did well because I always take copious notes with lots of sketches of the different things. He gave great information and I came away with a lot of knowledge. I put in the work and got the grade.
dont go to class. MEMORIZE the book.. .EVERY detail... and youll get an A... SCARY class.... but very good curves..

One of the worst professors ever.  His lectures are completely nonsensical and pointless.  If you absolutely must take his class, I'd recommend reading every word in the book and never attending class, it only makes it worse.  No matter how much I study he always seems to ask questions that are unrelated to the information I've learned.  Horrible!
terrible teacher, don't take the class if he's teaching it

He is a very funny guy, but his tests are impossible. Hes the smartest geography teacher known to man, so test questions are bizzarre. He cusses alot but it makes the lecture funny, the rest is pointless.
Horrible, don't waste your time going to class, because the lectures are unclear and pointless.

He's just a terrible teacher. He's a funny guy, but his teaching style is awful. He's a poor public speaker and his lectures don't flow very well. It's IMPERATIVE that you read the book, because you really won't get much out of attending lecture.

He's a nice guy, but sometimes he loses track of his mouth. He's said some things that could get him in trouble if he hadn't been teaching since 1972. He doesn't mean any harm by it--he just sometimes doesn't think before he speaks. But he seems like a cool guy. And he's really laid back in terms of class discipline.
he can be really funny but its true the lectures are pointless
Nice guy and easy class.

HE IS A COMPLETE JERK!!  He tells his students "he doesn't do email!"  It's ridiculous!  And if you don't like to hear bad language, don't take this class, because every other word out of his mouth is a cuss word!  His tests suck!  His lectures suck!  He doesn't teach the material!  Don't take this class if you don't have to!!

Know the information in the book, lecture are pointless, he just talks about his personal experiences. It doesnt seem like it would be hard, but the information is boring and his test questions are very difficult.  Nice guy though, very funny.  Toughest part of this class is being interested in it.

HIST150 cushmans lectures are truly fun he communicates well and easy to understand but his assignments are too heavy each assignment is basically  reading 80 pages of a book then writing about It with little to no summarizing and be ready because every week you will have to submit one of these within 4 to 7 days.he also takes grading seriously
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Cushman has good lectures. He was able to make the class a little more fun than the other 2 professors. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. Grades are off of your lab and a take home midterm and final paper. They give you questions to address for them both. Labs were a good amount of work for some but others were easy. Very cocky and opinionated. Decent
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This man has no sympathy for any of his students. He sent out an assignment (a 3000 word essay) less than 3 days before it was due and it was due on a school night. He didnt change even though most of the people complained.

Course was very disorganized between 3 professors, and don't feel like I learned much. Reading, lectures, and labs were out of order and didn't make sense. Cushman had decent lectures, but tended to ramble. He seems interesting and would like to take him in a different class, but not this one. If you take it, do the extra credit!
Interesting lectures but can go off on tangents. Really cares about the subject.
A little all over the place and full of himself. He cares about his own research more than the content of the class.
Really great teacher and a great class. Knows his stuff inside and out and is passionate enough about it to spark even the most minimal curiosity about the subject.

I love professor Cushman. He is helpful, interesting, and engaging. My class is taught by him as well as three other professors who alternate days of lecture. Although I am less interested in history of science that the other sections, I always find what he has to say interesting.
Cushman is very helpful, easy, understanding, and awesome! Why go to the movies when you could go to History 140! It is that GREEEEEAT!
This class is lowering my GPA. Cushman does not understand how to communicate clearly and the class was heavily disorganized. I would not recommend this class.

I absolutely despise this teacher. Took my paper and put it up on the projector and absolutely ripped apart my paper. He has no sense for anyone else because he thinks he is an amazing teacher. He called my class pathetic If you see that he will be your professor then i suggest leave

I took HIST 696 with Professor Cushman a few years ago.  If you want actual, honest-to-God help becoming a better writer, he is your man.  It took four years at KU to get such an honest, thorough, and helpful grader of papers.  Take his class.  You will learn something.  I learned more about writing in HIST 696 than in 30 credits of English.

Nothing like having a teacher make absurd claims with no proof.  Watched a video about ford explorers flipping in the 80's. Following the video he refused to acknowledge that the internet would have affected this disaster.  He went so far as to claim "the same internet existed in 1996." Smarmy, stuck in the 90's, rather boring, pushes liberalism.

Incredibly awful. Talks and talks and talks about things that could be exciting but in a boring way. He is enthusiastic about his subject matter but he leaves most of the class behind. If there is not enough people in class he will give you a quiz. LOTS of reading.

Incredibly excruciatingly boring. LOTS of homework and papers -approx 80 pgs reading + 1-2 pg response paper every class period. Homework is graded on completion but he reads them AND talks about your work to the class so you can't blow it off. Lectures the entire class period without stop. Very little about history, lots about ecology. Pretentious
Very knowledgeable. Very pretentious. Tries to make lectures interesting, but ultimately your grade depends entirely on your TA.

Cushman is basically a genius and he loves teaching.  He is very helpful and the class really was not that hard.  Attendance was not mandatory but I always went because I loved listening to him lecture.  The tests are take home tests.  I feel like I learned so much useful information in this class.  I really enjoyed him and his teaching style!

Dr. Cushman is very intelligent and his lectures are very interesting. You have to put in a lot of time reading and writing for this class though. If you can write good papers then take his class, that's just what the tests are.
Demands a lot, but is engaging and helpful. Do not take a class from him if your just after a piece of paper. Upbeat personality.
smartest professor at KU!
What a great professor! He's always energetic and excited about history. Sometimes it's a little hard to put everything together, but somehow it all makes sense in the end.
a GREAT teacher. he makes class very interesting and i learned a lot from him. he grades papers difficultly, but gives you easy points to make up for the low scores on papers.

taught a 100 level class like it was a 300 level class. difficult to please when it comes to writing papers.  powerpoint slides contained way too much information, and he goes through them too fast to get any information down.
No Comments
Great professor.  Very motivated.

I took his Intro to Af-Am Lit class over the summer and it was a great literature course. The reading load was very heavy but every class was essentially a short contextual overview followed by 2 hours of unpacking the novel or story as a class. Midterm and final paper, I learned the material and enjoyed the class.

I'm an engineering major who just took this for KU Core. I've always done well in English but struggled in this class. He is extremely smart and an awesome guy, and English majors should definitely try to take English classes with him because you will learn a lot and develop well as a writer. For someone like me, it was one of those hard electives.

I can't say enough good things about his 203 class. It was funny and really interesting material at the same time. Will gets really into his lectures and discussions, sometimes you just sit back and soak it in. He's a very thorough grader, but fair. It also doesn't hurt that he is easy on the eyes.

Will is a great guy, he is very engaging and really cares about his students! His classes are awesome and he makes each paper as easyfun as he can. I got a B in the class but know I deserved an A with how hard I worked and improved. I HIGHLY recommend him though, hopefully his tough grading lightens making an A more possible for average writers.

Will is a great teacher and guy. he is very understanding and help his students as much as he can. we had 3 papers and a project (compared to the 4 and a project other classes had & he made the papers more fun and not as challenging) only down fall is he is a hard grader. (i never got an A) but still possible to get an a in the class if you try.

Will is an amazing teacher. He tries very hard to make his class interesting&his papers funs. There is hardly homework except readings. &he is very engaging and accommodating to his students! He likes to get to know his students on a personal level & his class is rarely* boring! He makes you WANT to do well. I will say he is a tougher grader though

Will is a great guy, I would love to sit down and talk about something other than English. When it comes to the papers in English 102 Will is not clear at all. He has a reputation for making a project sound extremely simple and open, but then grades extremely harsh and narrow.

Will is an amazing teacher, my worst subject used to be english and now its my favorite. He makes the class interesting and relates to his students like most teachers don't do. I highly recommend taking him.
Without a doubt the greatest english teacher I've had. He's friendly, helpful, and is honest. If your paper is horrible he'll let you know, but in the nicest way possible. Overall, great teacher.

Absolutely the best teacher I have ever had hands down. Completely down to earth and you learn a massive amount without even knowing it. Recommended for first semester of college because he makes the transition to harder classes much smoother. Thank Will!

I LOVE Dr. Hunter. I went into this class really scared but was happily surprised. I highly recommend going through the prerecorded lectures on Canvas before the in-person class. The material is really difficult, but she does her best to explain. The exams are just like the groupworks.

So much extra credit is given which helps boost grades a lot! Use the group assignments as study guides for exams! Professor Hunter is amazing, do not be scared to ask her questions she loves to help.

She is underrated. She may be a little dry in her teaching, but overall the class is not bad and she goes over answers on in class assignments. there was no homework. She puts herself on the same level as her students and treats them equally. She is also randomly funny and relatable

You definitely need to study to do well on her tests, but they aren't impossible and she posts her slides, videos of her lectures, and study guides to help. Didn't love the group assignments every week, but they're pretty easy. Lots of extra credit opportunities, too! I honestly don't think she's a bad lecturer either, people are overreacting.

Although this was a tough class it is possible to do good. Make sure to get the text book!! It is very helpful to read through it before quizzes and tests. Dr. Hunter gives a lot of extra credit possibilities that helps your grade. She is always willing to help answer questions and really cares about her students.
One of the hardest classes I've taken for no reason at all. Based only exams only and I struggled with that.

She just reads off the slides and then you have to do group work for the other half of the classes. Attending was pointless as you have to teach yourself the material anyways. She does offer extra credit if you answer a question in class or respond to canvas prompts. I wish there was a different teacher for this course.

reviews.comment: Y'all are overreacting. Cynthia is a decent prof. She is not as scary as these reviews make her out to be. She cares and tries. If you show up to class, youll be ok.

Hands down the worst professor ever! She reads from jargon laden slides and is very intimidating to ask questions to. She is never available for office hours and the tests do not reflect the material covered on the slides. This college should have more than one professor teaching this class or at least someone who can simplify the material.

Dr. Hunter is very knowledgeable about the course subjects, class is structured on lectures one day a week and small group assignments the other day. The textbook is very useful and you will have to put in additional outside of class effort to learn material since there is too much to learn in one lecture. It is very possible to succeed.

I would NOT have been able to get an A  or anywhere close if it weren't for the textbook for 463. With the way she teaches, it is NOT an option. She reads directly from her slides and adds info that is not included when she posts them to canvas and they have old curriculum you are supposed to "ignore". Extra credit if you answer questions in class.

reviews.comment: Participation really matters in this class or you will fall behind. When studying for exams in this class, you have to use all the materials (textbook, lecture notes AND videos, ICAs, test feedback, etc etc) To receive a 4.0 you need a 94% or higher, which stressed me out all semester. Most of the units are hard to grasp the first, even third time!

reviews.comment: I wish there was another prof that taught this course but unfortunately she is the only one. She is awful. She teaches nothing and isn't approachable so make friends in class.

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors at KU. She stands at the front of the class and lectures right off the slides. When she tries to deviate from the slides, she speaks like she has no idea what she is talking about. Nearly all of the points in the class are from the midterm and final, but the questions cover nothing from what she teaches. Terrible.

Dr. Hunter's lectures are close to impossible to follow. The content of this class definitely is not easy, however Dr. Hunters lectures do nothing but make it more difficult to understand. Often times it sounds as though she is confused about the content herself. Tia the TA is definitely doing a better job teaching the class.

Took 120 in Spring 2021 and was my least favorite SPLH class because of Dr. Hunter. Only reason my grade survived was because of Tia and the lab portion of the class. Tia should become the professor even though she is a grad student, she would be better than Dr. Hunter. Useless class if you are going into speech pathology rather than audiology.

She doesn't explain anything and has no words in her lectures, making it very hard for you to go back and review the lessons. I feel like I teach myself more things than I learn from actually going to lecture. She never answers any questions and I feel like she doesn't know what's going on. Worst professor ever.

reviews.comment: Such long lectures and expects us to remember everything she says because her slides have no words on them. I can't review for tests with no words on my slides. Midterm and final worth 60% of total grade. This is a required class, but I require a new teacher. I wish I didn't have to take this class as I am not even going into audiology.

She is by far the worst professor in the SPLH department. There are 3 exams each 30% of your grade and barely goes over key points of what to know. She just stands at the front of the room and "teaches" by terribly elaborating on a few bullet points in a PowerPoint. I learned more from reading the book/rewatching lectures than from her.

I really enjoyed this class, however, the grading was frustrating. A 94+% is an A in this class, and each test (2) is worth 30%. To make it even more stressful, tests over *weeks* of material are 30 questions MC and T/F. All that being said if you study your butt off, watch every lecture, and understand the weekly assignments, you will do fine.
