reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had in the SPLH department. The lectures make the material very boring and she's not very accessible outside of class.
Great for a summer class. Assignments are all writing based and exams are all MC. Low maintenance class and straightforward assignments.

This was a great class, especially for summer.  Professor Steutermann was such a caring professor!  The class is really organized in Canvas and assignments are fair.  She also grades super fast!  Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If you get anything but an A in this class you're dense. There are 1-2 assignments a week that both take 10-15 minutes MAX. Quiz (exam) content is accessible and although she doesn't offer extra credit, you shouldn't need it if you just take 20 minutes out of your WEEK to do the assignments. She is very relaxed and makes her class enjoyable.
Very good instructor! Easy to communicate with and accessible for any help that is needed. This a class I'd recommend taking at KU.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very comprehensive materials, as every module has a lecture and a few YouTube videos. The assignments are easy and are mostly scenarios that you answer. The class felt worthwhile.

Just finished IST410 Project Management and I have to say I've learned so much, although the final project was hard. I'm looking forward to the new certification materials. Good professor that really made me feel like she cares!

This class is a super easy A, its like a couple hours a week at most and all of the information necessary is right in front of you and organized so well. Theres honestly no reason not to take this class because it will be an easy A as long as you do the work.
Professor gave a lot of positive feedback. I learned a lot! This was my favorite course in the business minor program!

Even though it was an online class Professor Steutermann always made sure to give me lots of personalized feedback. This is the best online class Ive ever taken! The assignments are interesting and tests are very fair. All around great class!

The class was fairly easy, if you do the assignments you should get the points. The quizzes were kind of tricky though and worth more. I took the class online and found that she wasnt very helpful when I emailed her with questions.

Dr. Steutermann is one of the best professors I have ever had. Her passion for project management made it an enjoyable experience. She truly cares about each student's success. She was always accessible anytime I had any questions/comments/concerns. She allows you to work at your own pace and is what I would consider a very lenient grader.

Really easy. 90% is an A (no +/-), 3 tests, and you can skip the third test by opting it to be the average of test 1 and 2. You can lock in an A for the class 12 weeks in, which is exactly what I did. Tests were fair,all online and to do the test all you need to do is take notes on her lectures. Book is only needed for assignments.

If you have common sense, you'll breeze through this class. Everything is readily available online, and the class itself is a cakewalk. Tests are pretty conceptual and nothing is unexpected. Extremely quick to respond to emails too. Unfortunately, you do need the book even though you only use it for a few things.

I really like Professor Steutermann's real world examples. This makes the discussions interesting and more relevant. She is very approachable and grades things very quickly. All around great professor in business minor program.
Really great professor - favorite at KU so far.  Really fast feedback and fun classes!!
Cynthia is awesome. By far the chillest professor at KU. Lectures are short and concise, workload is more than manageable, and grading is generous. Take her.

Very knowledgeable and respectful toward all students.  Grades generously on assignments and presentations but tests were a bit difficult.  But this is what you should expect for a graduate level class.  Enjoyed the class and highly recommend.
Very interesting instructor that seems to genuinely care about students.  Gives a lot of good feedback.  Tests are reasonable if you study.
Interesting class activities.  Helpful and friendly instructor!
Great instructor.  You have to keep up with the assignments but she grades fairly and provides feedback quickly.
This professor does not give lecture, she posts videos from internet and expect us to learn from it. Her exams are not related with prior homework at all. Do not take her class
Very well structured course. Lots of prompt and good feedback.  Highly recommend instructor!
She's aweome. Nice, easy but experienced in the field.

Very easy class, but super frustrating. It's split into groups of 4 and 1 group writes essays on a reading each class and presents it for discussion. Cyrus rambles a TON and some material he teaches is racist and homophobic, and he's very insensitive about it. Also gaslights students when they stand up to him. Don't take if you're a poc or lgbt!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you're interested in an easy A and not a super knowledge-filled class, take Cyrus. He's really smart, and you can tell, but this class is unbelievably easy. He's so chill- almost too chill. As long as you participate you're good. (participating can literally be dropping a '^^' in the chat and saying you agree with someone).

My favorite teacher I have had so far in college! I actually looked forward to coming to class and although it had required reading and an easy quiz everyday, it was worth it because the discussions were way better.Very fair grader. Would highly recommend him. Wish he taught other classes so that I could take more.
Pretty chill guy. As long as you read its really easy. Grades kind of hard on papers. Every class is different in the fact he is fun and doesn't take him self to seriously.

Cyrus never has any direction to his lecture he just rambles and you would think he wouldn't be too stict with grading. Well although he is very inconsistent in class is expects perfect on your papers. I have not enjoyed this class and would recommend taking it with a different teacher.

Cyrus is a pretty cool teacher, although he can sometimes get lost in thought. If you enjoy poetry and are good at writing, then this class will not be too much of a challenge for you. Cyrus is very helpful and fun in class as well. You will sometimes get a pop culture lesson.

Mr. Console was a pretty chill guy. Lectures were very consistent throughout the semester. We wrote 3 papers in the class, and while he graded somewhat hard, he also gave us plenty of chances to revise to his satisfaction. Readings are assigned every week, but I only read 2 of them the entire semester and passed with a B. Good luck!

He is a very nice guy, although sometimes not very clear.  He is kind of a push over so you can basically run the class, and if you don't understand something or have an issue, just talk to him and you can basically get your way.  He was very nice and the class wasn't too hard.

This class is honestly so easy. It would be very difficult for anyone to get lower than a B. There are discussion posts, 2 exams which you can use your technology on, discussion leading, and attendance is kind of mandatory. I am not sure she is teaching this class again but she is really nice and loves teaching.

i truly enjoyed her class and her personality. she is a talker and has a kind heart. if you need help, she is there. participate in group discussion and dont have your tech out. she did not like it at all but who would its rude because most are on social media. this class can be an easy A if you do your part

Easiest class in the whole world. You have to go to class because everything you do is in class, but takes no brain power to get things done.Shes super helpful with everything and she treats everyone like they're kindergartners.

Her only appearance is in the form of a 79 page lab manual. Really bad structure, calc 3 concepts covered. Take the regular lecture and not the engineering one, as the calc 3 concepts are apparently covered in that one.
She literally cannot teach to save her life
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: WOW! I LOVE THIS class. It's an honor to take her class. She is so inspirational, I decided to change my major to Physics.

the only thing i enjoyed about this class was that it was point-based. just a minimum of 900 points total will get you an A and the assignments she assigns are very easy. biggest complaint is the exam content. it's like AP-style questions and require you to know it at a conceptual level. don't waste ur time writing basic facts on your cheat sheet.

Don't expect an easy A. Delgado's lectures are dense, and exams are tough with no study guides. But the point-based grading is flexible—zeros don't lower your grade, they just don't add. Weekly quizzes, projects, extra credit, and chances to revise make it easier to succeed. Show effort, and she'll support you.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Entire lab structure needs an overhaul. Inconsistent and disorganized. No official rubric for final report-- it's up to TAs, so your experience will vary dramatically based on which one you get. That isn't okay. Her Excel help videos are 2x longer than necessary. Uncertainty made no sense in the book and had to teach myself.

This class was not what an 100 level class should be. Delgado was very dismissive and unhelpful. Her grading system is rough and expect to resubmit assignments multiple times. She won't answer questions and will tell you to "use google". She was late to office hours. There are no study guides or list of concepts for tests, setting you up to fail.

I don't think she does a great job at teaching astronomy always, feels like her lectures raise more questions than answer them and its hard to tell when she's giving relevant or irrelevant information

I am not sure what the purpose of the PHSX 114 Lab at KU is. ~2 hours is not enough time, there is zero overlap with lecture material, the lab procedure requires a background in statistics to even begin to understand it, the TA offers no constructive feedback, and I have left this lab every week since it began feeling like I have learned nothing.

Nothing in this class makes sense. Super long lab manual with worksheets that do nothing to explain anything going on in the class. Questions on worksheets are incredibly vague. The TAs are incredibly unhelpful and also don't seem to know what's going on. Looks like everyone is winging it. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE AT KU!

She was very helpful in class and very respectful about questions. The class was structured so that there was a 10-15 minute lecture each meeting, then we just worked on code solutions for an hour. She was knowledgeable about Python and helped me debug a lot.

Professor Delgado is an okay lecturer. Classes are pretty slow sometimes and dragged out because of the varying knowledge levels of students, but that's not her fault. The overall Kansas physics department is managed poorly. She gives daily quizzes but you can use your notes and others on them. Her grading makes it easy to get an A.

I am currently over halfway through the semester, and despite taking her lab course, I have never seen nor met Jennifer Delgado. Our labs are run completely by TA's who are clearly not qualified to teach or run a classroom. There is a headache-inducing potent gas smell in the room. The way this physics course is run at KU is truly horrible.

She seems like a funny nice person, but she spends only half the lecture teaching. She does not give enough practice problems, but when she does, she does not even show the complete steps to solving the problem. She barely gives any review to help one study for an exam. I have to rather find my own practice problems to study for an exam/test.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is unresponsive toward her emails and her canavs. Her class has a very odd grading system that is heavily based on attendance. The only time in which she responds is at the very end of the semester when grades start to get due.

Professor Delgado was very sweet. It's obvious she is smart but she does well at teaching subjects to students who don't have a background in science. Attendance isn't taken in every class. Every other Thursday you take a quiz based on material from the past week or a previous quiz. She grades on 3 things, attendance, quizzes, and mastery project.

A grading error in the lab claimed I did not have a value that was visible in the scanned submission. I emailed her a few times to fix it, but she took days to respond each time. Finally admitted the grading error, but refused to give back points because regrade deadline had passed. Even though it was her mistake from before the original deadline.

I have not even been one month into the course yet, but let me just say physics labs are the worst-run labs here at KU. The TAs are so disorganized and don't know what they are doing, each section has different criteria and grading. Our TA responded "I already answered that question" when any reasonable questions were asked when he in fact did not.
Terrible

Zero guidelines except for a 50+ page lab manual that still does not explain the course clearly. Does not answer emails or gives half-hearted attempts at answers that only lead to more confusion. TAs that run the course do not have the same grading scale and give 0s out like candy, with little chance for improvement.

Delgado doesn't even run the labs herself; she has TAs run them, and each of them set their own standards while grading the lab sheets, so you never know how you're doing or how you will get graded because each one has a different standard they grade with. She is borderline condescending and does not help even when you reach out with questions.

I didn't have her, just a TA of hers, but I disliked the way that her class was set up. There are a total of three labs and your result sheets are what you're graded on. I felt like I understood, but I kept receiving low grades. The TA wasn't very good at explaining things if I was confused. The tests themselves weren't too difficult though.

Who designs these labs? I didn't learn a single thing and the majority of my time spent in this lab was trying to figure out what to do for the data sheets. TAs and instructors always give vague answers to questions and weren't helpful in the slightest. Grading system sucks. Really easy once you get the hang of it but good luck doing so.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Every day we would go into class and she'd walk through a 3 slide powerpoint and at the end their would 5 questions on nothing that was in the powerpoint and was extremely difficult. She let us work on it but really never came up to help, and if she did, she did nothing but make things more confusing.

Physics labs at KU need to be reviewed and updated! The TAs have absolutely no idea what they are doing and are given no guidelines on grading. Each TA grades a different lab sheet, leading to overall confusion among the TAs. I go to lab every week and have my TA check my work, but when I turn it in, I get a zero from a different TA grading it.
Doesnt really explain stuff. Half the test is not on the homework. Goes on tangents about non relevant physics topics. Hard class. Really have to study. Or use chegg

They give a lot of 0s and don't give feedback as to why
She doesn't give the TAs guidelines on how to teach and they don't know what they're doing as a result
If you've taken physics before, you can do okay but most of the labs have not been covered in lecture when they start
Grading it unnecessarily harsh
Take this anywhere else, you'll learn more

reviews.comment:
worst professor in history, DO NOT TAKE
she doesn't teach, she just puts problems on the board and walks around the room and doesn't explain anything
the quizzes are super hard and combine lots of concepts such that it if you don't know the material REALLY well, you won't understand
she doesn't teach what you need to know
class organization = AWFUL
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not exactly sure why this teacher has so many negative reviews. I went into this semester expecting the worst and Delgado has absolutely been one of my favorite teachers and I rarely stress about her class. She tries to keep it up beat in lecture and absolutely everything on the exams is covered in lecture. Overall, the class was enjoyable

Regardless of what other ppl had to say, I felt like I learned something from the lab. It's structured so that you're able to fail and recover from the failure and still get an A. The approach for the lab is modeling the constraints of previously learned physics equations. You will have to work hard to understand everything, but I enjoyed it.

During my four years at KU, Delgado is the sole professor that I encountered that is absolutely terrible.  The labs have been set up in a manner that is either an all or nothing grade, so if you miss one thing expect to get a 0 for that lab assignment.  TAs are just as useless and respond aggressively to any question you have about the grading.

Labs at KU are terribly..... TERRIBLY... organized. Different GTAs grade different portions of labs, and it is an "all or nothing" approach to grading. GTAs are rarely accessible, and when you do get in contact with them, the response is to look at the rubric they give after grading (which is vague and not helpful at all).

I quiver at the thought of having to go into lab every Tuesday. Lab is horrible, disorganized and I'm frustrated that I feel like I'm not even applying any of the concepts we are learning in lecture. The lab is a JOKE. Based off of trial and error with homework and tests. Lectures aren't so bad but can't and won't receive any outside help. DONTTAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The physics labs are the worst things offered at KU. Completely unorganized and little help from Professor Delgado. None of the TA's agree on things when you ask them because she does not give them a clear way to grade things. There is nothing redeemable about physics labs at KU, if you can take them anywhere else do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A petition to have this course changed was filed and signed by over 300 students. Frankly, this course is worth transferring from KU over (No alumni donations from me). It is a waste of money and you will be behind peers who take the equivalent course at a different university. Literally everything is wrong with this course.

I have no idea how Dr. Delgado even calls herself a professor. Need help with clarification on coursework criteria? Need help with a problem? Well too bad becuase she won't help you. The only redeeming quality is the TA's who essentially run the class for her. This lab was the most unorganized, frustrating, and just downright awful class I've had.

I am a big fan of Prof. Delgado as a person. She is fun to converse with and can be somewhat helpful with class content. The course itself is an absolute joke, and a great example of how NOT to structure and grade a college course. The grading system sets students up to fail, and the class meetings are boring and un-engaging.

reviews.comment: I took this just to get my science credit and now I wish I had done anything else. She is super sweet but your entire score hinges on sections of the class. I have an A in every section except for one and now I might now pass the class. Horrible grading system.

reviews.comment: Stopped posting lecture zooms half way through an all online course. Confusing, unforgiving, and harsh.

reviews.comment: This lab was terrible. The lab concepts were okay, but became confusing because of the instructions. This resulted in several lab attempts to receive a failing grade. Your grade is mainly based on trial and error, rather than understanding the concepts. You will never hear from this professor as well and it would take days to receive a grade.

Dr. Delgado is not fit to run a lab. Her design for the lab is atrocious. The grade you receive is based on trial and error. They want you to figure out what arbitrary requirements they have (but don't tell you) to put on your lab reports so that you will get a passing grade. One of the poorest lab designs I have ever participated in.

6 days in and it's already hell on earth. No clear expectations for what to do, you have to learn EVERYTHING from a 25 page lab manual to understand what to do for certain parts of the lab, and no clear expectation of what you're trying to achieve with each lab. Waste of time and money
The PHSX labs at KU are a mess. Very unorganized with unclear expectations. Avoid taking any physics classes at KU if you can.

This class was just a mess. From the GTA to the Grading of the Lab. Lab were never grade on time so you didn't get much time to redo it for a better grade and the notes from the grading weren't any help. The GTA for the LAB barely spoke proper English and was just very hard to understand. Overall just not a good class. Need to request outside help

Only grades one 30 question test as your grade in the class, so you only have 3 chances and final to pass the class. In retrospect this sounds good, but she is very unhelpful for when you need to study for said tests.

reviews.comment: Physics 115 is such a mess right now, I've received over 5 emails just this week regarding how poorly the class is organized. Do not take

PHSX 115 Lab is so easy and the GTA's are nice and helpful enough. However, the overall Lab Instructor, Dr. Delgado, is so unhelpful and does not want the best grade for you. Do not ask Dr. Delgado for anything as she will not help you in anyway.
She does have interesting topics in class, but is pretty tough on grading

reviews.comment: While the course is straight forward she's too inflexible about grading and most of her grading doesn't make sense. Wouldn't round up my 89.7 to an A.

reviews.comment: She is strict with her syllabus and not very flexible as other people have said, but I still like her. I would take more of her courses. She gives great feedback and grading criteria is clear. The class is very informational.
