reviews.comment: The class itself is not overly difficult. For the most part - if you engage with the assigned course material, you can expect to do well enough on the assignments. However, it does seem that the professor is sometimes harsh and inconsistent in the way that they grade. One of the more inflexible professors I've had. Seems too busy for her courses.

The subject matter is very interesting but she doesnt do much to get the student interested in it. You either start the class wanting to learn or suffer thru it. Very standoffish and made it seem like it was a burden on her if we ever needed to reach out. I would recommend the course if it wasnt for the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor would grade way too hard for the subject she was teaching on, she did not offer extra credit, she refused to meet with me in person. The amount of work she required was way too much for someone taking other classes. It's as if she wants her students to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Beautiful, intelligent, and fun. Dr M. is an amazing professor who is passionate about her field, and comes from a stem background, which I feel adds to her teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: As long as you do the reading, the essays and quizzes are fair. However, some of the readings were way too long, and she requires you to reference up to 15 sources in your essays in addition to a word count. It was a lot to juggle. When she counted me off on my essays, she gave vague reasons why. You have to read a lot for a small amount of points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: There is a small essay or two due every week since it's an online class. At least one quiz every week as well. Grades essays really easy as long as it's the word count. None of the essays are too difficult. Overall easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Her readings and other assigned material did not always provide the info she required on essays. Her grades were inconsistent, and she did not allow any retakes or lenience no matter what. She took days to reply to emails. Would not recommend.

This professor will make you very frustrated. The grading makes no sense and there is constantly days were there are multiple essays due. Some of the essays she assigns require at least TEN sources. She will also disrespect your opinion on papers that she asked for it. The class is very unprofessional and all over the place.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This wasn't a bad class. The quizzes are somewhat challenging and can only be taken once (with a time limit), so make sure you are well-prepared for those. The essays weren't hard, though.  Generally only wrote one draft and got an A on them. She offered two extra credit essays. Approximately 1 quiz and 1 essay per week.  No tests or final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Essays are due weekly since it is an online class. As long as you do the assigned reading the essays will not be difficult. Make sure to use correct format in essays (grammar etc). Be sure to study for quizzes. They are timed and can only be taken once. Check the syllabus thoroughly before emailing her for questions.  Don't procrastinate on essays!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: LOTS of reading, but the quizzes, essays, and papers are not hard to do if you've just done your reading. Also, interesting videos to assist with the readings.

Extremely easy class, but I highly recommend going to the TAs instead of the professor. Their office hours were a lot more useful. Everything is in the slides and notes 90% of the time. She treats everyone differently, so you never know what you're going to get. Do not expect responses to your emails.

I don't know what all of the bad reviews are about. She was reasonable and her class was hard so of course a lot of kids are going to fail. I should have failed the first time and got a D- when I voiced my concerns. She asked me "what aren't you getting". I retook the class and got an A. One of my favorite professors at KU.

She's the only professor whom I've met who seems to treat people differently based on their background. Multiple of my peers mentioned that she has belittled them in various ways. She seems to have the mindset of "if I had it hard, so do you." Barely respects students' and others' cultural customs. Have heard other non-undergrads complain as well.

Picks Favorites and is extremely combative to students who ask questions. Regularly complained about certain students in class to me in her office hours. Tests are designed to trick you and instructions are usually unclear. One of the worst teachers I've ever had.

This class was... confusing. Lecture time was almost always wasted, and it felt like we hardly got through any material. Several times, concept disputes were met with judgment and assertions that "they only cared about their grades." It made the class environment a bit uncomfortable. Ample disconnect between the TAs and the professor.

She says that she gives you 25% of the grade for just attending class and attempting the homework. However, each test is 25% of the grade and she puts questions she's never taught in class or assigned previously. I think she is nice but the grades are unclear and there is a lack of communication between her and her TAs.

This was treated as a topics course, but I didn't really enjoy the lecture style. I liked it when she got "off-topic" and spoke tangentially the most. Otherwise, she would sometimes ask leading questions and make it obvious when a correct answer wasn't really what she was looking for. However, it was graded very nicely.

Hard class. Her lecture slides she posts are not very helpful if you don't annotate them in class because a lot of the content you need to know, she lectures about, so it's not printed directly on the slides. Get the textbook and read the corresponding chapters. Go to her office hours to make sure you know everything early, and you'll do great.

Dr. Dhar was an alright professor. She honestly cares about her students, but the course is rigorous and a weed-out class. The lectures were about 6-7 slides of the basics over a new topic, the in-class problems turned into more homework, and then the labs were so complicated they more often than not ended in tears. Take this class with caution.

By point, I should have passed this course, however, she made the final decision to fail me and 14 other students. Class is a complete joke and all in-class problems turn into hw. She canceled all help sessions at the end of the semester and left us with content filmed over covid. Also don't expect to see your final exam as she doesn't release them
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Dhar cares for her students and puts a lot of effort into teaching. It is unfortunate that her teaching is not effective. What is good though is that she gives a boatload of extra credit and the tests are very predictable and reasonable. If you do the homework and understand it, you'll do well on the tests as well as the class.

Absolutely Hilarious woman. Will tell you how it is and is ripe with sarcasm and passive comments. Love her sense of humor although some may not understand the pure genius of it. always refers to her husband in cryptic and confusing ways such as "co-caregiver" and will occasionally give you unnecessary but hilarious details about her life.

Love Dr Dhar she is incredible and cares so much about students values feedback and what students have to say about her teaching and takes it seriously if you visit her office hours she will help you with whatever you. need

Dr. Dhar cares a LOT about her students. She is sometimes inconsistent in the way she teaches material and in her notations, but she is always available for you to ask questions. Make sure you use your textbook since a lot of the test questions are very similar to the examples in it.

Wonderful professor willing to adapt to the needs of her students, She and her TA's are readily available outside class and there are plenty of worked out examples posted on BB. I highly recommend using excel to solve the problems, its good practice and much more useful later on in the course. Overall it was easy enough but some students struggle.

Dr. Dhar is an amazing professor who actually cares about her students and their grades. She provides you with worked out problems, video and live recorded lectures, and many more resources to ensure success. As long as you utilize the materials you're given, and stay on top of the material as it comes, this course should be an easy A!
Good luck with this professor, she just throws everything at you, and expect you to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Dhar is one of the best professors in ChemE department. Her TAs are also amazing. She is kind and caring for her students. Coming to her office hour to get help. Her tests are similar to the practice tests. Study the concept and know how to do it is the key. Do any ECs opportunities she provided, they might appear in your exam.

I really enjoyed Dr. Dhar's class. She really cares about her students, often asks for feedback in class if we seem lost, and values class participation. Exam and lab problem expectations were high, but were doable. She often doesn't finish problems in class, but is available for office hours and posts detailed solutions and notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She cares about her students. Come to her office hour to learn about life lesson is really good. Her exams are quite challenging but do the old exam. Her exam is twisted from the old exam and lab questions. Also, her TAs are very helpful.

Most unorganized class I have ever taken. Her tests are designed to trick you, 20% of our class failed the first exam. We would do in class problems for half of the class period which we were unable to finish in class and would not provide solutions so studying for the class was difficult. Nice but does not know how to teach this class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Dhar is a very nice and generous person. She will try very hard to get you every possible point you could get on exams. Doesn't really lecture all that much, but the online lectures are easily accessible and good for learning the concepts. Do the in class problems and you will do well on exams.
She's a sweetheart! Very easy to talk to. Always accessible (If door is open). Grades very fairly and had great knowledge of the material
great class, great teacher, a nice reprieve from some of the harder classes

Go to class, ask questions (in lecture or office hours), attend review sessions, do the homework, and you can get an A. It's pretty complicated material, but she gives you notes on all the reading and you can basically learn everything from those notes and in-class problems (which is why you need to go to class). Tests are open note open book.

Easiest class for juniors; I didn't really learn anything. The first two tests were super easy (avg > 90%) but the final was extremely difficult. It's helpful to go to class; test problems are usually class problems with different numbers (open-note tests). The two times I went to her office hours, I left more confused than when I went in.

She doesn't seem to understand the material well enough to adequtely explain it to interested students. Plays favorites in class. Wastes a ton of time doing algebra. The ONLY positive to her classes is that they're easy.

Will most likely confuse you if you pay attention in class. Takes shortcuts without explanation and makes mistakes in her notes frequently. Easy tests though, open note and book. Will help you on a test if you ask her to. Everybody should get an A in her class but probably won't learn much.
the keys in this class are to attend class, take notes, and pay attention and you will be fine.

Dr. Dhar really cares about her students. She does everything in her power to make sure her students succeed. Some students take advantage of this, but for the most part this makes for a very enjoyable class. Dr. Dhar has an open door policy which can be really helpful if something doesn't make sense. My favorite class of 1st semester junior year.
Major push over, will bend to the will of the students to seemingly no end.  Likes youtube videos.

I enjoyed taking ME 208 with this professor, which is why I'm upset I couldn't follow him at all during 508. He goes really fast during lecture and I just couldn't get my head around it. Ended up mostly self teaching by taking the textbook pages to class and reading them, while using the lectures as a vague benchmark of what to read about.

Had him my first semester at KU,  he's really nice and friendly. Tests are open book so get the ebook, it's easier to look things up. PAY ATTENTION IN THIS CLASS as you will be really lost if you don't. He's cool though. Sometimes he puts memes in his sample code.
Very funny, nice guy. He knew what he was teaching and was always willing to answer questions.
This man loves his memes. He also loves teaching coding. Perfect 5/7
He is a nice guy but the class is really a hard class. He also a tough grader. Exams are tough too. So students must spend much time otherwise they will not be happy with their grades.

He repeatedly told us to spend time between labs and HWs (and read the book if additional help is needed) and that was very helpful. Others didn't bother, and complained it was hard without even studying for the class.

This was my second class with Demarest. The only difference was there were no pop quizzes. He still works out problems on the board and always answers questions. His tests may not be the easiest but I would take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you want a professor who will show up on time everyday and won't lecture off slides. This is the man for you. He works through problems on the board and isn't afraid to make mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Demarest is THE E-Mag professor at KU hands down. He is passionate about it, and a lot of your exam grade comes from being able to “tell the story” of the content. It really helps you understand whats going on, instead of using pattern recognition to work problems. He is tough but fair, and he is great with one on one help in office hrs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Has a bad reputation but genuinely a good professor. Rambles a bit, but he's a fun guy who knows his stuff. The class is hard, but if you do the readings/homework and every practice problem in the book, you'll be set. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are random quizzes about once a week. Really great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Demarest is a great example of tough but fair professor. Althouhgh he rambles a lot in his lectures, if you pay close attention in the class, read the assigned reading, and do homework then you shoulodn't have any difficulties passing this class. He is very accessible in his office hours, and those proved to be more helpful than lectures sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Ken for 202 and 212. 202 was a great experience, and he really seemed to teach the material well with solid lectures. 212 on the other hand was a nightmare. His lectures became very rambly and hard to follow. Maybe the material is just far more difficult in 212, but his lectures just didn't seem good, unlike in 202. He's a great dude though!
Truly the best EE professor At KU , he will teach you with all the kindness and consideration you need to succeed as a EE who decided to attend KU!

I thought this class was tough, but this is not a review really on the class but rather the professor. Professor Demarest is tough but fair when it comes to grading and teaching in general. In this class or in any of his classes, I wouldn't stress to much about the HW because it does not mean much. To pass make friends, and study together.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The material is difficult but he does an adequate job teaching it. Readings and homework get to be a lot and pretty hard at points but you gotta do them to really know whats going on. The class is a lot better if you find people to work on the homework with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Demarest is a great professor. Best piece of advice is to memorize his office hours and attend them whether you feel behind or not. There is always a tip or trick he can show you that will make even a simple problem go smoother and faster. He is a tough professor but Circuits is the foundation of EE and it must be a tough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Challenging but a great professor.
He does care about students especially if he sees that they are trying however it is a very hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: I never struggled so hard in a class as much as this one. The exams are super hard and be prepared to read a lot. The worst part is that you need to have a passing grade on each criteria no matter how much it's worth even, if you have an 80% in the class, you will fail if you don't have at least, for example a 70% in quizzes which is worth only 5%.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very outdated style of teaching, a very "my way or the highway" approach even when he is wrong and he often is. If you do not ask a question that interests him during lecture he will blow it off, even if it is a genuine question about the material. You will need to read after every class as there is a random pop quiz that averages about one a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: "Once a new technology rolls over you, if you're not part of the steamroller, you're part of the road." Prof Demarest has been pavement for years and this course is in need of a new curricular and professor. It is passable, but his views are outdated, and his teaching style needs updating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
tough but he gives you the resources to succeed. eecs 212 structure is very similar to eecs 202, try to catch up quick if you fall behind.

a lot of people don't like his lectures but don't realize they follow the textbooks to a T. if you can't understand a lecture read the textbook and 80% of the time the book explains it better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are difficult to follow as his worldview is out of touch compared to the students he teaches. He is permanently rested on a high horse and would rather ridicule a question asked by a student instead of answering it. Class is passable, just needlessly difficult at parts due to the lack of materials provided by the prof (only txtbook reading
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a tough professor and most of the time lectures only make sense if you do the reading beforehand but he's very nice with grading and wants you to do well. There are also lots of pop quizzes that make attendance mandatory. I recommend you go to SI every week and make study groups with others in the class. This is what got me the A

He's a tough professor for sure, but once you learn how he runs his class, it really is not that difficult. His tests are stressful, but as long as you have the process down, he gives partial credit. This class is not an easy A, you absolutely have to put some work in. He is old fashioned, but you can't blame that for a failing grade.

Most days his "lectures" are him working through 1-3 questions on the board while explaining nothing. I would be surprised if he did any planning outside of a vague idea of what problems to do. Lots of reading and very very strict grading. He is also a Technophobe. He uses his own garbage site. Oh and the quizzes are way way harder than HW. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Demarest wants you to succeed. The class was small so you'll get to know him a bit if you go to office hours. Try to miss as little class as possible. He assigns pop quizzes that pull from the readings. I think this past semester (Fall 2022) we had about 14 or 15 quizzes. As long as you're there, you'll get points. Overall a nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a gatekeeper. Take other classes until another professor is available. He consistently fails more than half  of his students (set a record last year for % failing in circuits). He allows no notes on difficult exams, he has abysmal study resources, and he has lost touch with a student's prospective. Nobody deserves this frustration so avoid it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Puts questions you've never encountered before on exams. Spends the whole lecture solving a couple problems and it seems like half the time the answer he gets is wrong. I would avoid at all costs.

A lot of work and difficult exams. Use vague words in the lectures. Yells at students in front of everyone coming from nowhere. I never got yelled at, however, seen him yelling at students for most stupid reasons. Also, one of his classes uses his own textbook which has no merit and is less descriptive than the other ones in the market.

Tests are much harder than any of the homework problems, but they're not unreasonable if you really know the material. Reading the textbook is a must. His lectures are pretty disorganized, and he usually does the math wrong on the problems he does work in class. Overall, he's not that bad, but I wouldn't take him if I had a choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Demarest is a good person, but he is not a good teacher. He often spent entire lectures working one or two example problems -- only to get to the wrong answer and realize that he'd made an error at a very early step (notes from the lectures may lead you astray). Homework grading is a crapshoot, and test grading is unpredictable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Forced my attendance by not allowing grading while stranded in my home town 7 hrs away from campus with a non-functional car. Then proceeded to never put grades in the grade book, and it is currently mid-June. Horrible tests that are much more difficult than homework, and homework contains special problems. No other teachers for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A professor who truly enjoys his class, he makes sure you don't just know the answers, but understand the whole process. While the class is hard, it is harder content, and having him as a professor made it so much more enjoyable!

Dr. Demarest loves teaching, you can tell. He really enjoys participation, so go to his office hours if you can, get to know him. Exams are not easy -- harder than homework problems with little direction for preparation, but I wouldn't call them unfair. This is a class that you need to study for, don't expect to be handed an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He knows his stuff, ask questions, but be patient when he cuts you off midway. Lectures disorganized and hard to follow, shows favoritism towards individuals. Exam much more difficult than hw, but only exam prep advice/material is to do the hw problems. Study with classmates, get through it together. The grader was very nitpicky, so show every step
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: he deserves every bad review he has. schedules ridiculously long/complex homework assignments. beware 'special problems.' they call him a gatekeeper for a reason. he is not a good teacher or person. there's a reason he is a professor and hasn't worked in industry. lectures are vaguely related to the topics, usually just what he finds 'interesting.'

I think I can explain why the ratings for dr demarest are so polarized. After having him for 2 classes, its pretty obvious now that he gives special treatment to students who do well in his classes and is rude towards the ones who dont. Does he only respect the students who are most likely to finish the program?
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: People give Prof. Demarest a lot of crap bc they don't get to know him, but he's one of my favorite professors. He really puts in an effort to get to know the students and wants you to succeed. His lectures are a little all over the place, but he makes his class fun and loves it when you ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Absolutely terrible teacher. I'd give him a zero if there was an option to do so. His teaching style is a mess! He's extremely disorganized, rarely prepared to teach, his lectures only rarely make sense, and he's not very nice either! If you can, take this class with a different teacher!! KU desperately needs a better circuits teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Demarest is an interesting professor. I had him for three courses, over 2 semesters. All his classes are hard. EECS 221 is the hardest class I've ever taken. That being said, he has a great knowledge of the material and you will come out the class with a great understanding of the material and you'll become a better engineer because of him.
Grades assignments on an opinion by opinion base and will knit-pick all the details. You will get a question incorrect if you forget an adjective he used to define a term.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He expects you to know everything, and forgets what it's like to be a student. Dream crusher.
He tries and he knows very well the content but the hw is really hard
I do not think this professor needs any compliments. Any greatest people need no compliment to be remembered. They need nothing from people to be remembered.

Although we felt so done with Prof. Demarest acting as a comedian in class, the professor has connected Engineering with Art to form a new era of beauty. His class is full of freedom where there are no rules (except probably his mean face) but everything is organized. The best teachers are usually those who don't set rules.
211 is not bad. 212 is a little harder. 220 is probably the most difficult class in this major. very good professor you learn a lot in these classes

The most important thing is he can make the topics in class really interesting. He might be very strict but he does not humiliate his students (he is not like most teachers in China by saying China, it does not mean Taiwan, Hong Kong or Macao who think humiliation/insult/discrimination is education). He respect even the most quiet students.

His lectures seem to drag on. You are required to read every night for 220. He gives a lot of partial credit on exams, as long as you know how to approach a problem. His classes were tough, but made me into a better student.
He's a great, but tough, professor who can really teach and the textbook is so good. But there's a good amount of homework each week. The tests are gonna be pretty hard and long.
Dr. Demarest is a great professor.  His courses are challenging but you learn a lot.

Dr. Demarest has the goal of producing quality engineers from students. He wrote, and teaches from his own book because he understands the material extremely thoroughly. You will struggle in this class, because he is constantly trying to stretch and test your understanding of the material. He is a superb instructor, just try to keep up.
Quiz every day in class, MUST READ BOOK.

He's been doing this longer than I have been alive and he knows his stuff. Its hard material so buckle your seat belt. This guys loves to teach more than anyone I have ever seen. If you make it through his classes he will make you into a great engineer, and more importantly a great thinker.
Hardest professor I've ever had, but he has made me twice the engineer/thinker. He's one of my favorite professors, but you must read the textbook, ask questions, seek help, and pay attention.

Prof. Demarest is one of the best teachers I have had in grad school. He shows up to every lecture with great energy and enthusiasm, which keeps students interested. He is a very good lecturer. He asks a lot of questions and encourages discussions. He is extremely helpful outside of class. His class is solid as it should be, but not difficult.
Very hard subject but if you do the homework and ask for help Demarest will get you through it.
Ridiculous Tests! They will take you the full hour. If you want to get it done in time, you have to rush. He is very helpful. Requires professional behavior and will give you the same.

He is admittedly a really difficult teacher. But he knows his stuff and he teaches it well. I managed to get an A, but that's because it also takes a lot of work on your part too. But in a good sense. Because once you know it, you know it. Just be careful with your attitude. He demands you always be professional!

I have had Dr. Demarest now for three EECS courses 211, 212, 220. He is a wonderful professor. He makes you work hard but covers all relevant topics. The Emag textbook is just fine. Quiz questions directly from the book... Test questions are derivatives of the book problems. I %100 recommend him if you REALLY WANT to be an electrical engineer.

I got an easy A in circuits 1, my friends also got A's, some of them B's, just study for the exams solving exercises and be polite with him, he'll be nice! for me it was difficult to pay attention in class but if you do the hw and go to his office hours you'll do great!!!:)

Absolutely wonderful at what he does. His class is difficult, but appropriate for learning a concept such as circuit theory well. By far, my favorite professor that I've had at KU. He really makes a lot of time outside of class for questions, and even allocates an optional discussion for anyone who wants to come. I highly recommend him!
Avoid this professor! He has a reputation even among the staff as being hard. But if you do decide to take his classes, be prepared to answer a question or 2 on tests that he has never even covered.
No Comments
Neither course nor the professor are interesting!

Professor Demarest is tough teacher. Personally, I clashed with him, but I learned a lot about difficult subject matter. If you are serious about learning and being the best engineer that KU can produce, you should not avoid his class.

In Circuits classes, was very clear and easy to understand, and provided helpful examples in class.  Homeworks were at times long, but fair.  Emag is a different story.  Own book was pretty bad, and provided hardly any good examples.  However, his passion for the subject made the class fun.  Tough, but fair.

He may be very challenging and require alot of hard work, but he is always ready to help and tries his best to make sure that the EECS deparment produces great engineers. He gives alot of partial credits on his exams.
No Comments

he is not as bad as everyone else thinks that he is.  His class is not the best I have ever taken but if you can make it to his office hours, or call him on the phone, he is rather good at helping you out.  I agree that his E-Mag book is awful.  It is more of a manual on how to derive formulas than a textbook.

He thrives on tearing students down...GPA and confidence. It seems like his interests, other then inflicting damage upon his students, is research. Avoid his classes! Even if this means an extra semester at school. It will save you a lot of stress, frustration, and anger.
I would try to avoid this teacher at all possibly costs.

Very poor professor.  Selfish, condescending, thrives on killing GPAs, singles out students for trivialities.  Wrote the textbook for 220, and it's entirely worthless.  To pass that class you must take it from Stiles and live off the handouts.  Demarest likes to brag that he's a Christian, as if it makes up for him being the worst professor ever.
It's not so much him as it is the subject matter.
he is so dam partial.. and loves killing the students. takin a class with him is at ur risk.. ur sure to get ur GPA down.. the guy gets great pleasure is giving a F in the course.
I've had the worst exam ever in my college experience in EECS 420 Final with Demarest. As the guys said, don't panic if he fails you; that's what he does for living.

Even though he might be a hard teacher, you will learn a lot from his classes.  He is always willing to help you if you go to his office hours.  He has a genuine intrest in undergrad students unlike some prof.

THIS PROFESSOR SUCKS! God I hated this class, he was by far the most difficult professor I had in all the years I went to school. Its like he takes pleasure in failing students, if he sees that a few people didnt show up, or left early hell stop class for a pop quiz worth lots of points out of spite
The only thing worse than his book, is his lecture.

He is by far the worst teacher I've ever had.  He expects you to spend every waking hour studying his material, and even if you do that there is still no way to prepare for what will be on the test.  Hopefully you don't walk in late or have to use the restroom or you may not live to talk about it

He thinks that his class is the most important thing in the world.  You get absolutely nothing from his lectures.  Taking a class that uses his terrible book (EECS 220 and 420) makes the class 10 times worse.  Seems to play favorites and has unrealistic expectations on homework assignments.
A great professor, but don't expect something for nothing. You have to put out in his classes, but he's someone you'll remember for the rest of your life.

He was one of my favorite professors at KU.  Yes his exams are difficult, but you will learn a lot if you just listed to him.  He is one of a dying breed of 'real professors' that actually wears a tie and expects students to learn.
Never ever think of taking a class with him, unless you really have to. Very unclear and tough. Don't panic if you fail his tests, that's how everybody do in his class !

He is the worst professor ever.He loves it when no one understands anything about what he teaches. He assigns the longest and hardest homework you can imagine.His exams are like science fiction movies where no matter how long you study you won’t understan
A decent teacher for sometimes confusing and uninteresting subject matter.
Professor uses personal likes/dislikes when grading students. If he likes you, you should be ok.
He cut off our final early.

Amazing professor, super helpful in figuring out how to approach your projects, and gives very reasonable feedback. Take this class with him if you have the chance, even if you don't plan to do metals long term. There are many, many useful skills and techniques to learn here, and it's just a super fun and interesting class in general!

You can pretty much get an A as long as you make something you're passionate about and think is cool, he loves to see people be excited about metalsmithing. Ask many questions if you don't understand something, he can help! Outside of class studio work is usually a must. Not easy if you haven't done metalsmithing before, but he makes it fun! :)
Great instructor. Knows his stuff. He will help you with any outside projects that interest you. Becareful he will try to convert you to a METLs major.

had him for calc 3 and i have to say it was really fun. His lectures are really good and you can tell he really cares about what he teaches. He has a great personality, which sometimes takes away from the lecture but its worth it

I had him for Calc 3 and he is a joy. People I know who attended his office hours really liked him even more. He is a great asset to the Calc sequence. Calc 3 is hard for a lot of people, but he explains everything so well I am so impressed. I'll never forget when he played the Rocky theme song before exam 1. Structure is same as other calc classes

Dionyssios is one of the most genuine, caring individuals at KU, and he works so hard to make sure that his students succeed. The lectures he gives are well-thought-out and presented in a neat and colorful manner. He is a delight to learn from, and he always made me feel like I was capable of great things, even when I didn't believe it myself.
One of the best professors I have ever had. Genuinely cares about his students and will do all he can to help. Super accessible outside of class, utilize office hours. Super funny!

Math 500 is a tough, proofs-based class. Dr. Mantzavinos is an amazing teacher, who IMO grades a little harshly, but that made me study more and overall learn more in the class. Overall, he's an amazing teacher and his lectures are very easy to follow, and he will answer any question, no matter how 'dumb' you think it might be.
I had him for Calc 2, and although he has an accent, he is still very easy to understand and gives his lectures very clearly. Also has really cheesy humor. I would marry this man

I really enjoyed his lectures, but the class moved at a very fast pace and it is easy to fall behind if you don't go to lectures frequently. But if you miss a lecture they are usually posted on canvas.

Every single lecture was engaging, clear, and memorable. Dr Mantzavinos made this difficult subject straightfoward. He writes everything on the board so I had amazing notes to study from. Homework and exam reviews were so helpful and he was always available to help. Sincerely enjoyed lecture bc of his personality. Wish he taught all of my classes!
Great class with a great professor. Speaks clearly, writes clearly, interacts with his students in a jovial manner. Provides practice exams and his expectations are clear. Top tier.

Will tell you exactly what will be on tests and grades easy. Will happily meet with you outside of class and wants everyone to succeed. He explains concepts with a type of clarity that I have never encountered in a math professor before. His lectures are engaging and entertaining as well.

Makes sure whole class understands each topic fully before moving on, gives many examples and clear descriptions, and is very entertaining and provides real life examples on each topic. Great class and I learned a lot

He is the most clear and understandable math professor I have had so far at KU. He writes literally everything he says on the board in class and does multiple examples. He gives you a practice exam for the midterms and finals, and he has an extensive out-of-class review for exams. He cares about students and really tries to help you be successful.

Vaibhav would get more stars if I could give them. He is so caring and a wonderful professor. He will help you get the best grade you can, he is very understanding, and he helps you learn a lot in his classes. Highly recommend taking any class you can with him!

Vaibhav is genuinely the best professor I've had at KU. He is caring and always ready to go the extra mile for his students. He's extremely accommodating and puts a big emphasis on student mental health, which I really appreciated. He also gives very detailed feedback and is always available if you need help. Take any class you can with him.

He was my favorite professor ever. He is new this year and knows how to care for his students. Especially their mental health. Lectures almost every class but he makes them fun! Easy A if you attend class and get your work done. He is very understanding and easy going if you have to miss class. Such a great guy!
Diane is an amazing geologist but a substandard teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Diane. A lot of people don't like her and they bash on her because she grades harshly and knows exactly what she wants. Pay close attention to the lectures, and if you ask her questions and genuinely want to learn, she is more than willing to help. She wants people to succeed and cares a lot about her students, but people don't see that.
Great way of teaching lectures. Fair in grading, attend the class and you will be good.
Worst teacher ever. does not respond to emails and is constantly rude
Very passionate about sedimentology and a very, very good lecturer. Definitely go to class or you'll suffer a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dull, tedious and totally dogmatic. Stuck in a bunch of ideas from the Exxon School that are 20 years out of date. Not a very nice person either

Go to class - test material from class notes. Ask many questions, she'll like you more for it and will be more helpful towards you, same with office hours. Tough grader so make sure anything you dont feel good about ask in class before exam.

Absolutely horrible. Never responded to emails. Not engaging in class - monotone and boring. Her tests have a significant amount of material that she doesn't directly cover in class. The lab was painful, 1/3 of it is a guessing game because they don't teach you how to do things. Avoid if possible.
Best women teacher I have ever had.
I thought she was a great professor. I think people thought they would not have to work as hard as they needed to go get an A in the class so that gets people mad at her.

The worst geology professor I have had, have heard she is decent teaching in the field but in a classroom she lacks. Has two different grading scales for engineers and geologists. Doesn't like it very much if you ask questions about topics you don't fully understand. You can answer a test question exactly as talked about in class and still be wrong
She is not organized and off schedule all the time. She is lacking a lots of knowledge in her fields. She is not professional at all. God be with her students !

Horrible, horrible professor. She is very confusing and scatter-brained. Nearly impossible to follow in lectures. Horribly disorganized and arbitrarily grades. Test questions are completely out of the blue. Avoid at all costs, if possible.
It was not bad. she is very knowledgable, not fun at all but she is passionate and knows what she is talking about.

Excellent professor, very knowledgeable which can seem to be a problem for many of the students, but If you pay attention in class and read a little from the text she will teach you well.  Very passionate about her profession.

Wow, I love geology, but this class is taught to be much harder than it has to be. Tests are confusing. Makes it hard to study for. I'm a senior and have never had such awful test questions. Have I been lucky? I don't think so. I'm not trying to be mean, but She needs to rethink her teaching methods.
No Comments

I had her for sedimentology and it was horrible. She is zero fun, gets pissed if you talk, even to ask questions of peers ABOUT the material, and is super unhelpful if you visit her outside of class. Avoid unless class is necessary.

Her lectures are clear and to the point. She makes sure the basics are covered really well, but also dives into the tougher questions, which really gets you thinking. Her courses do involve a fair bit of math, which can be challenging. But it's not hard to get an A if you do everything she requires.

Lectures were impossible to sit through because of the language barrier. She is not suitable for classrooms in the United States. I set up multiple meetings with her to ask questions and each time I left more confused than before I went. I taught myself the entire class based on the labs and her slides. AVIOD THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS

She is very sweet, kind, and understanding and will give you amazing feedback on any questions you have. Unfortunately, her lectures were quite long and did not provide a lot of interaction. She was a little hard to understand, and I missed class every once in a while and still got the grade I got. Most assignments are out of the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Di is very kind and caring. She tries to help her students as much as possible. The materials are easy to understand. Her lecture notes are very helpful.

Don't take a class with this instructor. She is a joke! Couldn't even get through her own syllabus without falling on her face. Assigns all homework directly out of a text book so most of what you will learn will be self-taught. Just do yourself a favor and avoid this instructor at all costs.

Di Shi knows what she's talking about but her english is really hard to understand. The class is pretty easy otherwise. It says the textbook is required but I never even opened it and I got an A in the class.

I had her for both 311 and 526. For both, her lectures were rather dull and she's very shy. I can't help but feel bad for her since she doesn't seem confident in herself. She's very kind and curves exams though. In 311, she was generally informative and made it clear what we needed to know. Her 526 class was not and ended up curved significantly.

This class was my all time favorite so far. She is such a kind professor who cares about her students, and has such a fun class! The grading system this semester was based more off completion of assignments and participation, so as long as you engaged regularly with the material and participated when you could, you should be great!

Attendance is mandatory for participation points. Lotsss of homework assignments but seem to be mostly graded on completion. In class writing activities, in class (mostly group) "Exams" but were open note, and one oral exam at the end of the year. Multiple opportunities for extra credit. Overall easy but time consuming course.

Everyone seems to really like her, but to me she was a little back and forth. She graded my essays incredibly harshly and I even asked other Spanish professors and they were confused at the grade I got. She also really likes participation and you get points for participating every single class. If you miss class that's a zero, no exception.

My absolute favorite professor I think I have ever had, she cares about her students and tries to make sure that nobody fails, even if that means that she has to put extra work in. She is truly passionate about teaching spanish and is interested in connecting with each student in the classroom.

Diana was amazing. She is hilarious and keeps things relevant to whats going on in the world. She is very understanding that learning and speaking Spanish can be vulnerable and she made sure that every student felt comfortable. I never once felt pushed beyond my boundaries or embarrassed from a mistake.I took SPAN 216.

She was very specific about expectations which made the class easier to follow. However, she would sometimes be lenient if we messed up on submissions or did things a few days late, as long as we contacted her directly about it.
Pretty tough class but Capsim is really interesting. He grades pretty hard so make sure you put in the work.

DJ is an awesome teacher. The majority of the points come from two papers and the final exam, and some participation points are thrown in as well. The papers are tough and require a lot of work, but the final isn't horrible. If you went to class every day and have a general understanding of the main concepts, you will be just fine.

Cool guy, there isn't a lot to be graded on and what there is he grades a little hard...quizzes always have a few difficult questions that will drop you from an A to a B fast. Other than that the class was interesting and well structured. I had it at 8am which didn't help with my enthusiasm toward the subject.

I'm not sure what the deal is with the negative reviews on this professor (perhaps they can't comprehend that this is a graduate-level course?) Although her lectures are a bit heavy with power-points, the subject matter was always interesting and there was a lot of room for discussion. Dr. Daley (rightfully) expects quality work. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't listen to the bad reviews of Dr. Daley. She is an extremely knowledgeable, respected, and wonderful professor! Yes, she is a tough grader- but its a 600 level class- she is very clear on what she expects. She actually reads your papers and gives amazing suggestions on how to revise. Her lectures are great and she will always answer questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She knows a lot about the subject - she's so educated I feel like it makes it hard for her to teach, you'll learn A LOT. TOUGH essay grader, my worst college essay grade I've ever received was in her class - I've never been close to doing that bad. I got a C- on the essay and I'm an average A-, A essay writer.

The class was a little more on the difficult side, but she made it a seamless process and an easy learning curve. I learned a lot about both the topic of the class and writing skills in general. She gives fantastic feedback and definitely improved my skill as a writer, would recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am going to take this professor again. She is tough, but fair.

Her lectures could be quite long and difficult to sit through, and she expects a lot for the final project. However, she seems very caring when it comes to her students and is very helpful when you talk to her. Unless I'm doing a graduate course I would probably seek out other professors, but she was very sweet and tried to make things interesting.

The group project for EVRN 320 was awful, especially when transitioned to an online format. The level and quality of work she expects is that of graduate students since she also teaches graduate level courses.

This class was a frustrating time. Lectures were circular, slides weren't posted online despite the dense content on them, communication between Dr. Daley and the TAs was poor, paper assignments were ill-defined and confusing, , and grades and feedback for papers were unclear and unhelpful. I expected to enjoy this class, but really disliked it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Where do I begin? Communication between her and the class TAs was so obviously poor, no one seemed to know what was exactly going on at any point in time. Assignments took forever to be graded and any helpful comments made were too vague to properly aid in improving your work. I originally looked forward to this class, but left with a bad taste.
Communication between professor and TAs was mediocre at best. Expectations were vague and feedback was useless. Would recommend taking 320 with the professor that normally teaches it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Daley's crappy reviews here are unfair. She is a great teacher. She gives great writing feedback, because she obviously wants you to know how to be a better writer. Her expectations are clear. The class may not be easy, but she is clear on what she expects. Also, stay on top of work and she'll pre-read your paper and give comments.

She is very good at her field of environmental politics and is well known in the field for her research. Her research method skills are strong, which helps in making your project strong. Shes good, tough and will make you give your best. If you're looking for a lazy get by class, then its not with her. Shes great to work with. Excellent feedback.

This class made me freak out more than any class I've ever taken. That is a good thing though. Daley is a TOUGH grader. She expects you to write clear, concise papers and expects you to put everything into it. She is 100% there for you to talk to and get help. Do it. I am glad I took this class, but am also glad it's over, lol!
Professor Daley is terrific. I will take more classes from her!

I've studied at KU for 6 years & never ran into a professor so inept when it comes to teaching. She fails to give clear guidelines &/or examples for assignments, then proceeds to grade irrationally. Once, I was even told to "dumb down" a paper! Word to the wise: avoid her if you don't want to regress in your college career.

I have never received a grade lower than a B on a paper and in her class, I received a D because I "don't know how to write." She has very high standards for her students and is often not clear on what she expects.
Great teacher who will challenge you, but help you develop skills you will need.  Her classes are killer, but they are the best classes I've taken at university.

Her class was difficult, probably one of the most difficult I took throughout college.  However, I learned a lot & completed tasks (homework/tests) successfully when, at first, I thought were impossible.  She is a bit intimidating, but once you get to know her or put out a bit of effort, she is extremely helpful!  She was also a great resource!

I had her for Enivornmental Policy in Polics and absoultely hated the class. I was really interested in it before hand but dreaded going to this clas. Her grading is ridiculous and the subject matter is lame plus the end of the year paper is ridiculous

She has very high standards for her students, but she is willing to put in lots of extra effort and meet the student halfway.  I worked VERY hard in this class, but she helped me quite a bit and I got an A.  You can't miss any lectures or you will be lost.

She has very high standards for her students, but she is willing to put in lots of extra effort and meet the student halfway.  I worked VERY hard in this class, but she helped me quite a bit and I got an A.  You can't miss any lectures or you will be lost.
unfair

If you love sitting through 15 minutes a week of general belittlement then this class is probably for you.  If I have to sit through one more speech about how horrible we are as writers and how we should all go to the writing center, I might scream.

In POLS 431, we had hundreds of pages of reading every week, with only two quizzes, two exams, and one paper. As others have mentioned, there are only 100 points available for the course, with a maximum of 5 extra credit points. The environment does not encourage learning enough, but rather just passing the class.

Hundreds of pages of reading each week, impossible to keep up. Quizzes and exams are difficult, but they're online. Lecture heavy, little to no discussion. Very disorganized, would tell us he would open the quiz on Tuesday but it wouldn't be opened until Friday. Took many emails for him to realize he inputed my grade wrong at end of semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would avoid taking a class with Haider-Markel by all means. He puts 4 things in the gradebook for the whole semester for 100 points total. very slow at getting things done. You have to email him and remind him to do nearly anything. His tests and quizzes are quite hard despite hours of studying. This class is very likely going to ruin my 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DHM reads mostly off of the slides which can get dry at times but he is an extraordinarily knowledgable man. If you are looking for a relatively easy grade his classes can be that. He made tests available for our class online for weeks at a time.
His lectures were not that engaging but very information full, his quizzes were tough but if you barely paid attention to the lectures you could get a B+

This guy really knows his stuff. Yes, the course load is a lot, but he is clear about that at the beginning of the year. Get ready for a lot of reading, films, etc. He teaches a good class and gives thorough coverage of the subject (hence all the material). It's tough, but he makes sure you are prepared. Ask questions and he will answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I feel like his lectures would be more interesting if he opened them up for class discussion, but you just have to listen to him talk the whole time. The class is also difficult since there aren't many chances to earn points other than tests and an essay, so don't mess up. He's a bit unorganized (the class got really behind), but also pretty nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DHM expects you to read thousands of pages of dull material over the course of the semester. Does not go over those readings in class at all. Tests are difficult as you're mainly tested over those readings. Lectures and powerpoints are very unorganized. Talks in monotone. Turned an interesting subject and made it painfully boring and difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This is a great lecture class but brutal for your grade. The number of films and readings is intense and exams and "quizzes" cover small details. This class taught me a lot but was frustrating since he rarely works with students outside of class to understand difficult concepts and there aren't many assignments to cushion one bad grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Not a political science major... but this was the most interesting and applicable class I've ever taken. I recommend this class to anyone and everyone! Go to class, pay attention and take notes, and you'll be fine. I had no POLS experience (besides 110 in highschool) and got an A. Highly recommend!

Pretty tough course -- lots of readings. The guy knows his stuff, that's for sure, and does a decent job engaging with students. Most classes involved him giving a short introduction to the topic, then letting class discussion run for the remainder (a true seminar). If nothing else, I learned how to read on a graduate level in this course.

If you talk to him for five minutes you'll see that DHM knows his stuff. His research and writing are top-notch, but his teaching is little more than reading his long-winded powerpoint slides. The quizzes were easy if you studied, but the group project and research essay were huge undertakings. Interesting material, but DHM made it painfully dull.

Unorganized, but extremely easy if you simply attend class. Readings really aren't necessary when it comes to the tests.  His multiple choice tests are so random that you might as well not study, just pay attention in class.

He makes a interesting class where you think you will learn about policy as it relates to terrorism into a history of terrorism class. Its  frusturating. It is still interesting but because he is lazy and unorganized the class is not how it should be. You never know what to expect with him on tests but they turn out to be easy.Take notes in lecture

Professor Haider-Markel's public policy class is very interesting and relates closely to current events.  The lectures cover a lot of material, so consider bringing a laptop to take notes.  He takes a bipartisan stance in his lectures, which makes for a more balanced curriculum.  Be attentive at lecture, complete the readings, and you'll do fine.
His Public Policy class was soo boring. He is super dull and not energetic. He will not help you in office hours either.
I disagree that he looks down on undergrads. He knows his stuff and the midterm was just 3 questions. But we got the exact questions before. It was my first pols class besides 110 and I did fine.

Overall, he is not a big fan of teaching undergraduate students.  He looked at my class with a disdain that almost made me feel dirty for being an undergrad.  I wouldn't take him unless you feel like listening to a dry, humorless drone for 150 minutes a week.  I can't speak to what he is like as a graduate professor.

He was very intimidating at first, but as the semester went on he lightened up and even started joking with us. He is extremely knowledgeable about his subject and I think he really wants us to learn the material.  He is a hard grader, though, so be careful that you defend everything you write or he will dock points off.
Good teacher
Knows quite a bit about this material. He lectures clearly. Missing a lecture is rarely damaging. If you can competently write papers, this class isn't too difficult.
Good teacher. Wish we would have gone on a field trip.
I love this class!
He is a fantastic teacher!  He taught a ton of material and even though I had mono I still got an A because he was great!
No Comments

DRY DRY DRY DRY... nice guy.. but wow could he put me to sleep. He knows his stuff.. but isn't very engaging... even though the subject matter screams for it.  Wasn't too difficult a class, but he really didn't make me CARE about it...
The class was easy.  But, it seemed like he didn't care half of the time.
very interesting approach to teaching controversial subjects.
No Comments
I am scared about finals. I didn't take this class seriously enough. I don't blame the Professor; I blame myself. But, I am trying to make it up by cramming like a beast.

Do NOT take FIN 310 with Dieter. He moves way too fast through the material, and I feel like sometimes he forgets that this is an entry-level finance course. He overcomplicates topics, and his lectures are hard to understand/follow. I was a 4.0 student before taking this class. Save yourself and take it in the fall with the other professor.

Update, studying for exam 2, life is still ruined.

Dieter is nice and seems to like teaching but he doesnt teach great. He seems to expect us to get it right away and doesnt provide any useful materials that actually work. I feel like a course packet would be better for this class. His teaching style is simply not effective.
This class totally stresses me out. I returned early from Spring Break just to study for this class. Much more work than the typical business school class.
This is a tough class. Teacher is fair, though. I am actually learning things.
so far so good. having to spend more time for this class than I would like.
On my mom he ruined my life
he ruined my life

Literally funny how hard he makes this class. Have no clue how he is still teacher never take any of his classes everyone fails and doesn't even finish exams. This class is tough, but Dieter is fair. Take this class seriously from day one and don't fall behind. Then, it is very manageable.
The worst teacher I have ever in had in all 14 years of schooling I'm pretty sure he feeds off kids failing this guy prays on your down fall
I learned a lot and Dieter seemed to actually care.

reviews.comment:
Dieter is demanding. But, if you are genuinely interested in Finance, Dieter is The Man. Dieter is passionate about Finance; and that is a perfect fit for students who maybe interested in Finance. The best thing I like about Dieter, he will give you a ton of personal time outside of class.

If you're just a party-going B-School student, avoid him.

Honestly not as bad as others say, but I'll agree on how bad his lectures and handwriting are; It was hard to understand him and I always felt stressed out during the lectures. If you put effort into studying/learning material for the exams outside of class you'll do well enough. :)

reviews.comment: do not take finance with this professor, his handwriting is horrible along with his lectures. i never understood his lectures, i would go to his TA's review sessions for help and it barely did. more than half the class would fail the exams and the only things that helped me was the past exams question not lectures. save yourself the stress.
More work than most business classes.
This class is hard work; but it is helpful.
Be prepared to spend twice the amount of time on this class.
Dieter is passionate about finance, but is also demanding of students. Keep on top of assignments and take the class seriously and you will do fine. I actually learned a lot.

Avoid this professor if you can his handwriting is illegible and that of an elementary student. He gives us little to no study materials and tells us to just "read the slides" and dosen't even tell us how to study the slides properly. The TAs were much more easy to understand than Dieter.

reviews.comment: Dieter's style of teaching is very hard to adapt to. It's not the normal lecturing style that you're used to with other professors. The class content contains very detailed and complex concepts in finance, and it doesn't help that his handwriting is not legible. There are no study guides for exams and 65% of your grade is exams. TA's are good help.

Half of the class dropped out after the first exam. Dieter's explanations are poor and do not target the average student who is taking their first finance class ever. His teaching aids are awful. He annotates his slides every class but nobody can read his handwriting. Don't take this class.

Dieter is very energetic. He expects a lot from students. If you put in the time, the class is rewarding. If you are not willing to put in the honest time required, then you will hate this class. Dieter is very approachable.
Dieter is one of the best teachers I've had at KU. He is hard but fair and is willing to help students after class time.

Dieter is obviously a very smart guy, but he is not a very good teacher. I think students would benefit in the class if it was formatted like accounting- having a book you have to buy and fill out as you go from unit to unit. Dieter only offers annotated slides, but his handwriting is not great so they are hard to reference.
Very bad handwriting. Get this man a personal handwriting tutor. He probably paid some people to give good ratings about his class today.
I learned a lot!
excellent teacher. I learned a ton!
Dieter is tough but fare. I learned a ton. Dieter genuinely cares about his students.  Be actively engaged and you'll do fine.
Go to class and pay attention and you'll be perfectly fine
Bro isn't that bad. Just pay attention and lock in when doing homework.

thumbs down

I guess he's not fired yet because he has all the internship connections for his TAs.. worst professor in business school
hes kinda boring but chill asf
WISH I COULD GIVE A ZERO!!!! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

I am so sad this semester went online due to COVID-19. His class was my absolute favorite. I looked forward to it every day. I would 100% take this class with him, or any class!

Get ready to listen! Dieter knows how to lecture nonstop for 75 minutes. Don't interpret that poorly, he is an incredible teacher. Extremely knowledgeable and cares about his students. He is engaging and brought a lot of value to my education. I would recommend Dieter for future students!

Professor Schrader is one of my favorite professors at KU. Students complain because he isn't an "easy A", but his class is extremely value-add. If you skip class, you will not do well. reviews.comment: Very cool guy, I enjoyed his lectures but it was key to sit in front. He engages a lot with students but it's difficult to get involved if in back. Make use of office hours. drop in and he'll walk u thru questions

Get to know him. Don't let him chew gum while he is speaking and his accent isn't bad. Overall it was fairly interesting but a lot of studying made my head spin sometimes. TAs are key to passing
Cool guy, good lecturer, his tests seem easier than the notes, but aren't easy.
Dieter tried to be funny but the truth is his lecture is boring. He just like a "robot" and his accent is terrible. Just get through him.
Confusing unhelpful are terms I would use to describe this instructor. He basically reads straight from power points...AVOID IF POSSIBLE

This is not a hard class. Dieter is a great speaker. Print out the slides and pay attention in class. Dieter gives all the HW answers as he lectures. Also the TA's will give you the HW answers after you attempt once. Redo the quant HW problems to study for exams.

Overall this was a very difficult class. I received an A in micro and macro and enjoyed those classes but not this one. Pay semi attention in class and read the book chapter for the homework and you should do well on it. The tests are harder to prepare for but review all the homeworks and reread the 3-4 chapters and you should be fine.

This class is uninteresting and hard to follow. I have an A in both Macro and Micro. Probably going to receive an F from this class. Not a hands-on teacher, just reads ppt's and gives miniscule examples. I'm going to try and take it at CIMBA as another person suggested.
AVOID TAKING THIS CLASS WITH HIM!!! Take it abroad in the CIMBA program. I hated this class so much I switched majors.

I had a pretty good grasp on econ concepts going in and I think that carried me a long way, class is boring but he does a good job of trying to make it interesting, tests let you skip a few questions which helps a ton. Homework is online and if you attempt it once and take it to the TAs you'll get the answers. Nice guy and not a bad class overall.
Dieter is a cool guy but overall Managerial Economics was more difficult than I predicted. I got A's in Econ 142/144 and this class is a lot harder.  His lectures are hard to follow and very boring.

Deiter is a great teacher and very enthusiastic about the material. I'd take another class from him anyday. There are a lot of attendance quizzes so go to class. Tests are weighted in your favor and hw is online so there is no reason not to do well

Dieter is funny and intelligent (fairly young too). The course reviews some basic info so class can be boring until after the first test. The 3 tests are weighted so that your best one is worth the most (yay!). The homework is submitted online and I'd suggest doing it with a friend and getting help from the TAs as needed. All in all, a great class!

Dieter is great. His class is pretty straight forward. I did have to get coffee before class several times, but that was due to the boring nature of the subject matter, not Dieter. He has an accent which isn't too heavy, but takes a little getting used to. He's also pretty funny. Gives a lot of attendance quizzes to reward those who come to class.

So obviously you're in the business school to be taking this class, Which means you know how econ is. Either, you get it, or you don't. Either way, Dieter is very helpful and amazing at explaining economic principles. His class is NOT hard. Don't let people who don't study ruin your chance of taking a class with an amazing, talented professor.
If you go to class, listen, and fill in the blanks on the slides the homework and tests are pretty easy.  Doing the above and no more would easily get you a B.

dieter was super boring. i hate economics with a passion so i barely went to class. his quizzes are almost entirely all attendance quizzes so just give ur friends ur ku id and full name and ur set. his tests are moderately difficult. this class is a guaranteed B but if you put in more work, you could easily get an A.

Very boring teacher. I did the crossword every day in his class and when I wasn't doing that my friends and I would tally and often make bets to how many times he says, "does that make sense?" I'm not good at econ and still managed to get an A. If you do the homework and study up for the tests, you should be fine.

The class itself is really boring. Dieter is also fairly boring (but if you're lucky you'll see him go off on a random tangent). Though the material was incredibly boring, Dieter gave good examples that were similar to test problems. Also, the class was heavily curved and he gave plenty of easy quizzes/hw to get points.

I could not stand this guy. I quit going after the first test because his class did not prepare me for the test at all. I found it easier to each myself the material than listen to him. If you have the opportunity take this class with another professor. All of the BE 301 classes have the same standard so other professors will not be any more diffic

This class wasn't the easiest, but it wasn't hard to get the hang of. The long answers on the test are easy to do with practice that he provides you. Dieter is very helpful and wants you to do well. WORST TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD! Avoid having him if at all possible. He doesn't teach you anything and just points at the slides with his little laser. If you need help the TA's were awesome though

What a joke of a class,I had to teach myself the entire class because Dieter is so incredibly boring, the class is not hard, it just requires memorization of some meaningless info.  As I'm sure most students know the economics department is an absolute joke at KU and Dieter is no exception,Overall lectures are pointless and book is all that matters

The material is very boring but he is a nice guy and understands this. awful experience. did not post grades until i escalated to her department THE SEMESTER AFTER I TOOK THE CLASS. awful with communication. never responded to emails. one of the worst professors ever, and i say this as a STEM major. save ur mental health she's not worth it. get credits with a different class with different professor.

The point of taking the course was to learn how to incorporate things such as race, gender, religion, special needs, and culture into our future classrooms, and I can attest that I learned nothing. WORST PROF EVER. In class, she showed MTV Clips. For the final, we were given a list of terms to study that we had not talked about in class. She never took role but grades on attendance and participation. All in all bad experience. Do yourself a favor and take this class with someone else.

If you like reading and teaching yourself, this class is for you. The required text book was not ready till half way through the semester, and all we do is talk about the articles. We spent more time talking about race than we did any other topic. Didn't get anything out of this class. She was unorganized and made students feel inferior.

WORST CLASS. She didn't post grades until after the drop date. She splits the class up into groups which took up half of the class time due to the size of this class. The course pack required for course was not available till halfway thru the semester and was $50.00. Thought this would be interesting. . . had a bad teacher. Take elsewhere.

I was looking forward to taking this class. In lecture we spent the entire first half of the semester talking about Race and week on every other unit. She does not post grades and is the hardest teacher to get into contact with as she does not email students back or have office hours. Save yourself the stress and time and take this class elsewhere.

JMC 419: This class was brutal. Lectures had nothing to do with assignments. Grades were posted months later. Feedback didn't help. There was no need to show up to class because you wouldn't miss anything. Find a different professor.
Ward expects a lot but overall you learn so much.

Doug Ward is a fantastic professor and I absolutely loved his class. He taught me so much about different forms of research, information gathering, and general skills necessary to becoming a successful journalist. Although his expectations are sometimes unclear, he is extremely approachable and willing to help you understand content. Great mentor.

This class can be really frustrating, but there is a really simple solution: MEET WITH PROFESSOR WARD. While many complain that Ward is vague or that he doesn't say what he wants, if you go and meet with him you'll know exactly what he's looking for. I learned more from Ward than any other teacher to date, and I absolutely recommend his class.

I loved Doug Wards class. His class is designed to push students toward utilizing their creative side. This is why his assignments and readings are so open ended. He is a fabulous professor and an even better mentor. TAKE HIS CLASS! You won't regret it. You gain so many valuable skills every journalist needs.

Wanted to like this class but I am just desperate and confused now. He is completely inconsistent with material/guidelines and is one of the least approachable professors I've had. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE.
He provides absolutely no guidelines for anything. His lectures, assignments, and  overall course is very unstructured and confusing, One of the worst classes I have taken in the Journalism school.

Very confusing. Never clear on what he wants on assignments. Thought it would be easy as assignments are satisfactory/unsatisfactory, but he changes his mind on what he wants. Even if you put all the information asked for into your assignments, he won't pass you if he doesn't like it. Wouldn't take again or recommend.

One of the best classes about religion I have taken, we went over many different topics that I found very interesting, the lectures were some of the most entertaining I have every heard and in a 1 hour 20 minute class it felt very refreshing, however two things in this, the quizzes are very strange, and the final paper were very difficult.

Dr. Dolgopolski is a sweet man, however, his lectures can be hard to follow. I thought this class would be interesting since I was interested in philosophy, but this class made me hate it. worst prof and class. thought this was a law class ended up being strictly a religion class. its insanely look and hard to sit through. requires you to write a lot including a 14 page final essay. take absolutely anything else

reviews.comment: He is incredibly smart but class is tough and going would be completely pointless if attendance wasn't mandatory, as it has nothing to do with the only thing graded, the final paper. He makes this class very confusing unfortunately and therefore boring. Too much philosophy and the only graded assignment wasn't ever explained.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY
