reviews.comment: I took a JDS Justice class with Sergey at the University at Buffalo.  He is a very brilliant man, and gives inspirational lectures.  You have to show up to class and pay attention, but besides that we had one paper to do all semester.

His accent is way too hard to understand. He should not be teaching world civ when all he talks about is religion and philosophy. Not kidding he spent maybe one class talking about stuff that would be on the test. Basically theres no point to go to class just study your textbook and teach yourself. Horrible professor.

I mean...this guy is nice, I'll give him that, but his class is just downright absurd. He teaches the curriculum on a philosophical standpoint, and rambles incoherently. He has terrible clarity, and is unclear in telling his students what he's grading and on what criteria. Overall, be prepared to pay attention and study the textbook.

I thought Mr.Dolgopolski would good since hes had such high ratings but he barely teaches World Civ. He teaches about the same "microcosm, anthrocosm" bull. Then your tests in quizzes are all about the textbook. I just stopped going all together. He wasn't really meant to teach World Civ and was better off teaching Religious Studies.

The man! Such a great teacher and really cares about his students. Not only is he an expert in his field, he appears to be an expert in EVERY field. He knows so much!! He wears a yarmulke, but does not let that interfere with the way he teaches/grades by any means. He gave an open atheist in our class an A b/c he backed up his arguments with texts!

He is a very smart man, but this class is extremely boring. 67% of your grade is based on a paper that he barely gives you instructions on. Attendance is mandatory, which irritates me because I dread going to this class everyday because it is so boring and the information we learn does not matter since there are no test. Do not take this class!

He is an extremely smart man that is always addressing questions as if they would be later quoted in a research paper. Take this class if you can think outside the box, and back up your argument with text. Only major grade in the class is a paper, that you will want to meet with him once or twice about before turning it in this will help you grade!

Very, very smart guy.  Absolutely knows his stuff.  That said, he packs in a LOT of information.  I would take another course from him, but wouldn't advise anyone that isn't very interested in the material to take anything from him.

Most boring class i've ever taken. It takes a lot to drag myself to this class everyday, where I simply daydream and try anything but listen to him speak. I have learned barely anything and feel like i've wasted money. Wish i would've dropped early on, HATE this class. He is a nice man, just way too boring and unclear. Don't take this class.

Probably the most brilliant person I've ever been around.  Every day I felt sorry for him, because I can see that the general poor student body at KU doesn't deserve him.  He would be much better suited somewhere with much, much better students.

Probably the most brilliant person I've ever been around.  Every day I felt sorry for him, because I can see that the general poor student body at KU doesn't deserve him.  He would be much better suited somewhere with much, much better students.
Very hard to understand, tries to explain, but ends up just rambling. Wish I would have dropped early on.
Amazing! The reading is difficult, but very worth the effort. He is incredibly helpful and very plesant.

Slightly quiet fella but I found his lectures electrifying. They're dense, you have to show up to class and pay attention, but if you do this then you will be rewarded. He clearly finds the things he teaches fascinating and conveys this wonder very well. Class was never boring, only a little low energy at times. Very interesting and awesome dude.

Dr. McKenzie is a wonderful professor. Incredibly knowledgeable and the lectures are straightforward. The assigned readings were short but interesting. There were 6 homework assignments with flexible due dates and a final paper.

He's pretty good. Took ANTH 320 for my KU Core Goal 6, so to be fair I am not super interested in linguistics/anthropology which made lectures not particularly exciting. He is knowledgeable about his content and is a nice guy. The grade was composed of a few quizzes (open note), discussion posts, and a project that wasn't too difficult.

Passionate about his work, but his lectures are kinda lengthy and very monotonous. Decent teacher, but doesn't answer emails. Also, he expects you to easily understand difficult concepts, which is aggravating because the subject matter is extremely foreign to most people, especially if linguistics is not your major. Not awful, very eh.
Cool, funny guy with a passion for his subject. Lectures are really long and dense but he puts them all up online if you missed anything.

Overall, Dr. McKenzie is a great professor. He is very nice and helpful. His lectures are long and boring if you are not interested in the content, but he posts them all online for students' accessibility. Everyday two questions  were due, and other than that we had a few long homework assignments with plenty of time to complete.

MUS177 was easily the most fun course I've taken. Draper is such a chill guy. As long as you show up and be respectful, you'll have a great time. The projects he assigned were pretty fun and not that difficult. He's the goat.

Draper is an icon, love the guy. In MUS177 we just did a couple of group projects and a few essay's but they were so easy I literally wrote an essay over the history of Hannah Montana so take that what you will. SO FUNN

The class is a freshman Seminar, which is more relaxed than a typical class. We went on some field trips, and I learned about music scenes and the music industry. The class doesn't require much out-of-class work. We had a couple of easy assignments and group projects. THIS IS A FUN LOW STRESS CLASS.

Chill professor and interesting topics, though lectures can get boring. Essays are based on completion, and quizzes are easy. Attendance isn't required, but the final presentation must be in-person. No final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is super chill but strict about deadlines. There are only two assignments and three exams (which were super easy in my opinion). Lectures are conceptual and boring, but you can still learn by half-listening. He uses funny jokes and analogies and is open to discussing topics further.
Honestly a great person and fair instructor but the lectures can be extremely boring at times.

Professor Chen is great! He teaches networking in a fun way that is very understandable. The tests are very hard because they cover a lot of material, but if you actively participate throughout the semester, he weighs that heavily into your final grade. Definitely recommended!

His lectures are very interesting but it can be hard to take notes since he doesn't put much information on his slides. For discussion sessions just make sure to do the readings and participate because it helps a lot with writing the big papers in the class.

I loved Dr. Isenberg and his class. His lectures are very engaging. Most of his grades are papers but he is extremely willing and available outside of class! On my final paper, I went to his office hours and he explained exactly how to be successful on the paper based on the lectures. He has a great voice and Dr. Isenberg is very professional!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: LOTS of reading and long papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gave amazing lectures, you can tell he loves this content and knows so much about it. Lots of reading but its doable, the course builds on itself, but if you don't like history you will not like this class. Can be intimidating and a tough grader but he wants you to improve, ask him questions and he will have answers and a good explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Isenberg gave amazing lectures, but you need to come to class and take notes to learn the information. 4 units and 4 big essays, with mini papers every week. Friday discussions were valuable and helped with the papers, do the reading before coming to discussion and you will be fine. Improved my critical thinking and prepared me for history classes.

A brilliant, erudite, inspirational professor of history. I added a history major because of this class last semester. His coursework is difficult, but well designed. His lectures display his deep intelligence and love for the subject. A thorough recommendation for anyone even vaguely interested in U.S. history.

My favorite thus far. Super knowledgeable and I constantly talk about the content outside of class. You have to go to class, and probably wont do too well without the readings. I really appreciated Dr. Donovans feedback. There are a few writing assignments, but there are designed to aid in the acquisition of the content. Two exams, with MC and SAQ

Dr. Donovan was great and his lectures were very engaging. I would recommend him for sure.  He provided good feedback and the criteria was clear. You did have to get 940/1000 points to get an A, but I ended the semester with 980 points no problem. Just do the readings and watch the lectures and you'll be fine.

Dr. Donovan taught my honors seminar. He is a wonderful professor who truly cares about his students! he is also incredibly funny and assigns course material that is actually interesting. I do not believe that he is a tough grader- but he does read your papers and grades them fairly! I would take any of his classes!

Prof. Donovan was a very kind teacher and gave very detailed and effective feedback. Not a lot of assignments in this class, so not a lot of room for error - especially on the midterm and final, which are both difficult in my opinion. Although, it seemed other students didn't struggle, so it really depends. Overall good class, interesting topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: WARNING: If you don't like long lectures, then SOC363 is NOT for you. However, Prof. Donovan's lectures do a really good job of breaking down key concepts and making them relatable. When discussion sections occur; he's very good at giving everyone a word and responding to comments/keeping the discussion going. A very earnest and funny guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have to get 950pts/1000pts to get an A. He took 3pts off my 1st paper & 6pts off my 2nd one, never told me why he took off so many. One time I spent 30min trying to find the right answer to a question, couldn't find it, & missed the question. I have a 4.0 & am seriously concerned I won't get an A. DON'T take this class if you care about yourGPA

Brian Donovan is great for those looking to take this class for a 4.1 credit. While this online class is a lot of work, I could manage it while doing a full-time internship. Buying the additional book is a must, but the textbook is not necessary. There is an exam, writing assignment, readings, and video lectures each week. Super interesting class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Donovan is amazing. He is a great and respectable professor who is a genius in his field! I had him for SOC 104 and then proceeded to take him for 160. I also did an independent study with him and loved it. If you are interested in sociology, Dr. Donovan is your guy. His research is very intriguing. He has a lot of passion for his field.

I did enjoy Dr. Donovan's lectures overall because he always brought in relevant info that was easily relatable for students. The tests were somewhat difficult due to the reading for the books we were required to read. He did seem like a professor who was passionate about what he taught & the TAs discussions weren't intimidating at all.

Dr. Donovan is hands down one of the best professors I've had. He never showed up to lecture unenthusiastic, and was always giving great lectures. He provides you with real world examples that relate to topics, and has a really great love for what he does. Today in class, he received a great honor, the "Gene A. Budig Teaching Professorship award".

Donovan's online Social Problems and American Values course was probably the most interesting class I've taken at KU so far.  It was also the pretty effortless.   You watch a few short (5 min) lectures per week, read the book, complete a 300 word writing assignment, and take a multiple choice quiz.  Do the work & you'll have an easy A.
He made us buy a $100 textbook then afterward told us we also needed online access which cost even more. Not professional.

AMAZING CLASS. Received a high A. ALL you have to do, is actually attend lectures, take notes, and go to discussion. You will be guaranteed and A. Donovan is so sweet, and cares about you retaining the information. He applies everything to young college students- so funny. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

One of my favorite classes I've taken at KU, as well as one of the easiest. As long as you take notes and attend mandatory discussions, you'll get an easy A. Dr. Donovan is very helpful and clear with what he is presenting, as well as quirky and interesting. Overall a great class with a great professor.
Interesting material and pretty easy class.

My class was held in Budig 120 as a 900 person lecture hall. If you have questions, ask your TA. Dr. Donovan will assign readings that don't seem to match what he is lecturing in class, and you're right, but you HAVE to do the readings because exams are 50% lecture and 50% reading.

Brian, made me change my major. His powerpoints on blackboard were very convenient and helpful. Test were easy if you attended class to hear the review. Papers were great. Tophat is just easy points dont miss them
I barely studied, got an "A" on the first test. Reviewing sides help for test.

This class should be in easy A, but it is time consuming. Take immaculate notes, because half of the tests are lecture material. Second, read the assigned readings. The reading can be a little boring and long. The other half of the test are straightforward questions from the readings. Third, always attend lecture because of clicker questions.

This class was super easy. Reading the PowerPoints and the books is good enough to get an A on tests. The only bad part of this class was that Dr. Donovan's lectures were highly boring. He could make even the most interesting topic super boring. Other than that, super easy pre-req.

This class was SO easy. Brian Donovan made everything very clear and straight forward. His videos and lectures were very applicable to life in general. I enjoyed the lectures overall and would recommend attending every discussion session. If you do that, you will be golden.

This class is interesting if you like learning about people, if not you might find it boring. It is not hard at all, I have a hundred percent because I study, and I only read part of the books. The books you should probably read but they aren't hard reads. He is very nice and accommodating when you email him about a problem.
Never went to discussion, and barely went to lecture. Read the books, go over the power points, you'll be fine. Videos at beginning are interesting though!

Donovan was a great teacher. The class size is huge, but as long as you sit near the front he does a good job of making class interesting. The reading and attendance are both required, but make getting a good grade in this class very easy.
Go to class, read the books, and attend the discussions and you will get an A in this class.  I found this class very interesting but it does require that you take good notes during class.
Very boring. If you like reading you'll love this class cause thats all it is and the books suck.

Lectures are boring and personally if you get the powerpoints(online) and look the terms up you'll understand it more than in lecture aka no need to attend. Discussion is mandatory though. It's an easy C- if you try(attendance, easy online quizzes, easy papers,& super easy class assignments) so if you get 0's on all test you'll still get a C-!!
Great teacher!  Very interesting.  Dr. Donovan makes a big effort to connect his lectures with real-life events.  He wants his students to be successful and does not demand too much!

Very easy class. He provides a lot of opportunities for points. Quizzes are easy, study a little for tests (which he curves greatly) and ask for help when you write the papers and you'll get an A. You don't need to show up for class if you can get the notes but it's SUPER FUN and very interesting. Easy A, but you still learn a lot!

The class is interesting.  You need to pay attention in class & Donovan can be slightly confusing sometimes but he makes class fun with videos before & after class.  Its a great class to take to get some credit in your KU core!

I have to say that this was one of the most interesting classes I have taken. Dr. Donovan is passionate about the topic and as long as you keep up (mostly) with the readings you will have no problem getting an A.

Best professor at KU! He used really interesting topics in lectures. You do have to work to get a good grade. Attend lectures and take notes like crazy and read the books and you'll be fine. Discussion class also helps a lot.

Discussions are based on attendance.. However lecture is not.  Lecture with Donnovan is incerdibly boring. Its hard to focus with how he jumps from topic to topic. He is VERY unorganized and horrible about getting back with you if you contact via email.  Readings are mandatory to pass.. I recieved a D in the class, even though I attended lecture.
Best Professor at KU hands down - if you want to learn something take his class and talk to him in office hours.

Brian is very passionate for his topic, though it can be very hard to pay attention in class. Though he has powerpoints, it is CRUCIAL to attend lecture to understand the material. Plus, he gives answers to a lot of the test questions in lecture. Discussions are also a big part of the class, so do the assignments and show up!

He tries really hard and loves Sociology, however his lectures are pretty confusing. I think that he tries really hard to connect Sociology to things in popular culture and it doesn't always work out. IF YOU READ THE BOOKS, YOU WILL GET AN A.

If you like listening to your girlfriend blab about how her day went when none of it is relevant to you, DROP THIS CLASS, or take in fall. His lectures have nothing to do with sociology or the material on test. Talks about the most random things you can imagine. His cats, jersey shore, and real house wives......

Reading is necessary for the class. He is a pretty nice guy and will help you when you need. Try and you'll get an A. Lectures are somewhat necessary, and are hard to follow. He makes such simple topics way to complex.he thinks his lectures are hyper organized, however, his train of thought is still very scattered when he tries to explain things.

Drop out if you have him, uses textbooks for every test, unclear writing assignments in discussion, test are impossible studying does not even help, boring lecturer, thought i would like sociology but after this course, i dont.

He's a good teacher, very nice, and will help you in anyway possible when you go to get help. His lectures are somewhat disorganized but you'll get used to them. Discussion is mandatory but the lecture is not. You HAVE to read the books, pretty good chance of getting an A.

Very interesting class that keeps you interested. The only downfall is there is a butt-load of reading. Once the reading is done, the tests and hm are easy, but you'll have to get through a lot of text beforehand. Don't blow it off.

Unique lecture style but once you warm up to it it's easy to follow. He is nice and tries really hard to engage students. Overall, an interesting class, and fun for a lecture. Easy tests if you read. Discussion attendance is important.

His lectures were extemely disorganized and hard to follow.  Lecture wasn't mandatory as long as you read all of the assigned readings, the tests were a breeze.  Overall though, he was a really nice person and teacher.
i love brian. he makes these little under-the-breath comments which are hilarious. the class is really easy as long as you pay attention and read the books.  his grading scale is supernice too

I love this class. Its so easy. As long as you go to class and PAY ATTENTION you will do just fine. Grading curve is awesome. Prof Donavan uses real life/media examples to clarify. I suggest taking it!

This guy is a terrible teacher, his lectures go absolutely nowhere and for test reviews he just throws together a huge list of everything he covered and literally says "only some things from the review will be on the test, i want you to make your own reviews".  TAKE IN THE FALL

Brian was a great teacher. Going to class was not mandatory, but it helped you understand everything more. If you just read the assigned books you will do fine. He also will answer your questions in class if you e-mail him. Also, very nice grading scale!

Professor Donovans class was extremely interesting! He has a vocabulary that would make an english professor erupt into a fit of rage, and he uses it to describe key points in a way that is easy to understand. The discussion section is extremely helpful! If you get Anna Kern as your TA consider yourself extremely lucky, as she is extremely helpful!

Passionate about sociology. Doesnt use a textbook so theres no double information. Following him in lecture is very difficult becasue his slides are really bad, you have to pay super close attention. Some of the readings are good. Decently hard tests but has a curve where 86% on a test gets you an A. Make sure you read and pay attention and a easyB

Do the readings. Get Ann as your Discussion TA if you can. She is really helpfull. Pretty easy class. I did not go much cause he skips around so much in lecture. And he uses a lot of words that you have to look up in a dictionary to know what they mean. Do the Discussion assignment and study a lil for the tests and you will be just fine...
I think he is a great teacher, and pretty easy to follow.

He jumps a lot around in the lectures so it can be hard to follow, but for the most part if you're paying attention you'll definitely understand what's going on. He posts most of his slides online and the discussion section helps clarify things. As long as you understand the main ideas and do the readings before test time you should be fine.
This class overall is really interesting... The grading curve is amazing, on the first test I should have gotten an D but the curve made it a B. As long as you do the readings its easy!

His lecture's are pretty scattered and he jumps from topic to topic, but he does emphasize important details. But you have to write EVERYTHING down and do ALL the reading. The curve helps substantially if you get above a 50% or so.

He is the worst teacher i have ever had. Wikipedia is more helpful than his lectures. His curves are never made public and in most scenarious he actually takes points away from you (65% goes down to 50%, anything below 50% = 0%) He is monotone, and nothing in class really connects to each other(one minute he talks suicide, the next discrimination.)
Very helpful. Knows what he's talking about. Keeps the class interesting with video clips at the beginning of each class period.

Awesome professor and great class. He is very passionate about his work and it makes for an interesting lecture. He assigns different books - to get a good grade read them all! Most are interesting reads. Tests are difficult but read the books and lecture notes and you will get an A with the curve. Overall great class!!
read the books and your good. his tests are ridiculously hard but he has a HUGE curve so it evens out
Not a good teacher at all. Very hard to follow in lecture. Even if you study the "study Guide" you will still fail the test. The curve is pointless. Don't take this class from him.

If you can take good lecture notes (without the help of a powerpoint) and do the readings (which are a little long), you will do fine in this class.  He isnt the best teacher, but definitly not the worst.  It's real easy to get a C without trying or a B or and A with a little effort
Tests are extremely confusing.. you must read all of the readings... an extreme about of reading. The books are okay until the author talks about how it relates to sociolgy. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Readings are somewhat interesting...parts are very full with sociiological crap that is completely uninteresting. Meier was my GTA and he is bomb!!! Completely helpful. In class, it is hard to stay awake and he has a habit of talking about things but you have no idea how they relate to the words you are supposed to know for the exam. It's deccent

Donovan finds a way to make controversial subjects such as drugs, sex, and homelessness awfully boring.  His book selection may relate to the course, but they are often boring and repetitive.  Just like any class if you really try an "A" is attainable.

Donovan is very smart but quite hard to follow. You have to take pretty good notes or your screwed. Theres no specific text book but 4 different books focusing on topics from panhandlers in greenwich village to talkshows such as jerry springer. You will learn alot if you pay attention, go to class and reflect on how it affects YOU.

He seems to know a lot about sociology, but his lectures can be confusing, and are often monotonous. His tests are often material straight from the lecture, so you dont actually have to comprehend what he is saying - just memorize it. Thank God for the discussion sections.

Professor Donovan is horrible. I am taking this class on my Spring 2008 term. It is VERY EASY to get lost. The lectures are very unorganized. Discussion sections are a blessing for review. Fortunately, few of the readings are interesting.

Yes, he is a difficult teacher, but that's the point of college...to prepare you for the real world.  He is very monotone, and his lectures are just that--STRAIGHT lecturing.  But he is a very knowledgeable man, and definitely knows what he's talking about. He assigns a lot of reading, but if you actually try, you'll get a lot out of his classes.

This class is def. not for you if you just want an easy "A". He is a very knowledgable and interesting professor. He will assign you TONS, I mean TONS of reading in which you must keep up with otherwise you will fall way behind. His tests are hard but if you do some reading and ATTEND the lectures, you should get atleast a B.
the class was interesting but he's boring, tests were hard

I have no idea what everyone on here is saying...this was one of the hardest classes I have ever taken in my life!! He is so boring and monotone!! One good thing is that he will be very helpful to anyone outside of the class
so rad! best soc teacher out there. take ANY (ANY!) class he is teaching.

donovan's classes are the raddest i have taken at ku...for those of you...esp soc majors who have not taken soc of law or crime and deviance...you are truly missing out on some of the best reading and lectures ...the classes can be difficult and definately require work...but its college, and as students you deserve your moneys worth..............

Dr. Donovan is soooo awesome!!  I took his class 2 years ago, and it still ranks as one of my favorites.  As long as you attend lecture and DEFINITELY read the assigned reading, the tests are cake.  He is very knowledgable, enthusiastic about the material,and more than willing to help outside class.  I wish he was still here...
No Comments

One of the best professors ever.  This is the only big lecture size class I would recommend from my experience.  Despite the 400 other students, you can get to know him.  The class is extreamly interesting and well worth your time.  Keep up on the reading -- it doesn't take that much time and it's pretty interesting.  TAKE THIS CLASS. A++

I truly enjoyed this class.  Very interesting and Dr. Donovan is very knowledgeable.  He is a very nice guy who is always available if you need help.  Readings are interesting and are actually relevant to the content of the lectures.  Tests can be tricky. but as long as you study a bit you'll be fine.
Cool class, relevant readings. He does a great job making class interesting and fun. Reading are interesting like about crack dealers and bums. Sit in the front, it'll make you pay attention.

He is an awsome professor who knows what he is talking about.  Make sure you go to class and take good notes.  Also read the readings that he gives.  He talks a little fast at times, but is easy to understand the point he is making.  I would rec. taking a class from him to anyone interested in soc!

Class is interesting and he knows his stuff.  It is all lecture with supplemental reading.  The reading can seem like a lot at times. Tests are not difficult as long as you know names and major topics; he curves the grades too.  He has a tendency to talk fast so tape lectures to get everything.

When I have taken this course, Dr. Cousino has taught the topics properly. The course is easy because he provides short assignments and exams only. The best portion is that he drops the lowest homework grade and the lowest exam grade, so you can skip the final exam if you do well on the first 2 midterm exams. One of the best professors in KU.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Absolutely fantastic, I learned a lot and was excited to learn it! Writes his notes, so you never go through the material faster than you can take it in. Very receptive to questions and discussion. The class is very theory heavy but only tests application problems. Drops the lowest exam grade (yes you can skip the final) so getting an A is trivial.

I was retaking this class after failing it the previous semester, and Cousino was such a breath of fresh air. He made everything so much easier to understand, and his exams are only over things we talk about in class, no curveballs. Even though we went over the same content as last semester, it felt like he spent more time explaining each subject.
Prof. Denning is a witty and knowledgeable lecturer and he gives great feedback on assignments. This course called for quite a lot of reading, but I promise that it was worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Loved the class, would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great course, great lectures, professor is much more engaging and entertaining than the average. 4 major assignments make up the grade, plus attendance/participation in discussion. Read the assigned text, talk in class now and then, and write a few drafts of your papers. Relatively easy A or B
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Even though lectures aren't necessary to get an A, you'll still want to go because of how interesting and engaging Denning makes them. The entire class grade comes from your papers and participation (you'll need to do the reading to do well on these), and the grading on these is fairly tough. If you aren't a history major his class may be too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I had Prof. Denning for two classes this semester and he is now one of my favorite professors. He assigns many readings, which he goes over in Lecture, and he frames great questions about them that make you think. Participation matters, so speak up! The majority of your grade is papers, but he and the TA's were easily accessible and very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Doooope teacher. Super knowledgeable, very engaging. Loved going to lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Denning attempted to be dramatic in a sense, and come off as very intelligent by using large, complicated terms and ideas. Less history and more philosophy. He is an ok lecturer but I wish he taught like I knew nothing about the subject. Very interesting topics and I definitely wanted to go to class

Favorite professor at KU! He is really passionate about what he's teaching and it shows in his lectures. Great incorporation of media into lectures. There is a bit of reading, but nothing that is unmanageable. We had 4 papers throughout the semester; the TA was a tough grader. Visit his office hours! Super cool guy.

Andrew was a cool guy and obviously very passionate about this time and place in history (I took his class on Hitler and the Nazis). I'm not a History major and have never taken a HIST class before but he assigned a whole heck of a lot of reading. He requires participation in class but if you skim the material, even in class, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Andrew was cool enough, but the papers you have to write don't really have much to do with what he goes over in lecture. He also really likes to talk, so even if you have a good comment, he'll talk more. There is a LOT of reading for this class and you have to keep up. I don't advise taking this if you're not a history major.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Denning is my favorite professor I've had at KU! He is great with the students, easy to talk to, and excellent and presenting information. I've taken both HIST 301 and HIST 341 with him and I would definitely take another class. He offers great feedback and is always willing to help so it would be hard to fail a class with him.

Professor Denning is a great professor who genuinely wants students to succeed. His class is appropriately challenging and his lectures make the topic very interesting. My only (very small) complaint is that he gets somewhat speedy when speaking during lectures. Would definitely take another class from him.
This man is amazing. Respect him always and I promise you will enjoy your time in his class.
Easy and relaxed, always willing to talk to you about any problems you have. Just need to make sure you attend his class
No Comments

Overall pretty easy. Not a lot of work, very simple projects, good at explaining topics. However, his final was a complete 180 it was very very difficult. Also I did not personally cheat on any assignment but I've heard he will spend most of summer or winter break really checking all your work for cheating so do not cheat he will figure it out.

Professor Gill was overall a very good professor. He is incredibly smart and has a lot of cool information to share about his past experiences in his respective field. The course was graded on just several worksheets and a single final exam and a single final project. Generous, and cares about students.

Most of your grade in this class is based off of very vague worksheets that he does not really prepare you to answer. The lectures feel like he's winging it on the spot and doesn't really have a planned curriculum.

He was disrespectful. Surprised to not like his class. People only like him since he has a nice accent. I heard about him being a great teacher which was not true... Absolutely will not take a class Gill after this experience! Kind of a jerk. Grading criteria was not clear, and the homework was minimal, but left us feeling... dismayed

Dr. Gill does an excellent job of teaching by making the lectures interactive with his students. He does a good job of explaining concepts and not just how to use them, but why they would be useful. My biggest complaint would be that there is too little and too easy homework, as he grades very generously.

Dr. Gill is an amazing professor with a lot of information he loves to share with students. Lectures can be boring, but his personality and the projects he assigns are very fun. This is a class where you get out what you put in, so effort matters a lot. If you don't understand something, he'll work with you in office hours and explain it thoroughly
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy this class. Boring lectures. His exams were trivia questions from lectures. Like, the questions weren't difficult but they would be so obscure, even with attending lectures. Not to mention, he was gone on a trip the week before the final. Told us there would be a final review session and then never announced its time to the class.
Great lecturer, very knowledgeable and lenient in grading.

I don't know why there are so many people who rated so high. From my experience, he's a awful professor. Don't expect to understand his lecture well, he just don't know how to teach. Hws are easy and u'll learn nothing from hw.

Dr. A. Gill is extremely knowledgeable in the field of functional programming. He is able to explain things extremely well and is eager to help you. His lectures are interesting and his Scottish sense of humor is entertaining. He is awesome and so is this class. Oh by the way, we learnt JavaScript, Scheme and Haskell quite well in one semester.

Awesome professor. Lectures are clear and informative, although he does go fast sometimes. Tests are very easy, very few homework assignments. Attendance not required, but the lectures are very interesting and help a lot.

Amazing professor! I had taken EECS 168 with him before. Very similar format for this class too. Very easy tests & assignments. Knows his stuff, keeps the lectures interesting. Wants to help students as much as possible. Highly recommended.
Amazing professor. I had taken EECS 168 with him before, so had a great rapport with him. Tests and assignments are super easy, lectures are very clear. Extremely helpful.
Great teacher, great guy. Clear in his teaching and his expectations. Awesome accent. Tests are easy, but somewhat difficult to study for because there aren't notes to use. Highly recommend.
Best programming professor I've ever had. Extremely clear. Very easy tests, lowest grade is dropped. Very helpful and friendly. Class is easy by itself, but he makes it easier and much more fun.

totally friendly guy. he's always pushing back deadlines and trying to find ways to make the tests easier. pretty much reads from the textbook in powerpoint form, and can move fast, so plan to do the reading on your own if you want to get any actual learning done. he'll try hard to answer your questions, but doesn't always get what you're asking

Excellent professor.  Explained everything crystal clear. Has a Scottish accent but it is in no way impairing. Very nice, very kind, and mixes deep programming knowledge with humor and anecdotes that are entertaining, insightful, and helpful for learning the material.  Strongly recommend.

Professor Moorhead has been one of my favorite professors at KU. He is curious and passionate about mathematics, and it shows. He really cares about his students understanding the course material, and is very helpful in his office hours. He's also just a great person to have a conversation with about math, philosophy, or life in general.

Professor Moorhead is a very strong professor. He genuinely cares about his students and does a great job of teaching students what they need to know. He is upfront about what is on exams. He is very accessible outside of class and his office hours are so helpful. He is overall an amazing professor.
I do not like this teacher. At all.

The textbook for this course carried me through the class. I would attend lectures only because he sometimes would do the homework problems, otherwise they didn't make sense. His office hours were helpful. He was not clear about grading or the test curves at all. The class topic is interesting, but he does not do a good job explaining
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: will not cheat you out of a real experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: the worst experience I've had at ku.
Taking his class is a hellish experience
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Moorhead used to teach at Vanderbilt University and you can find more reviews of him there, which I would say are overall accurate. He has high expectations of us to develop a deep understanding of the material from the intangible examples he covers in class. The homework assignments have unwritten expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: IDK what these other ratings are on...Professor Duenas was great! An easy course if you put in the effort. Had some really interesting units, and weekly quizzes are straightforward if you do the reading. No textbook required, she provides PDFs. Would definitely take her classes again!

This is for SOC224, but just not great for low level courses. Doesn't prepare much material for class + provided material to fill gaps is sparse. Some quizzes just have vague, unspecific questions, and half the time you can't view your answers after submitting. Lectures go off topic or are just unengaging.

She was fine. Felt like I could be doing better things in her class and felt like I wanted to fall asleep a lot of the time. There was no tests and only essays and it took her forever to grade them so I had no time to improve the next one which was annoying. Also a lot of reading. No textbooks but actual books that you will have to buy on your own.
Has really strong opinions and it shows but overall she's an ok teacher she's very outgoing and helpful
So kind person don't let it fool u. IF U EVER SKIP CLASS DONT TAKE THUS CLASS PLEASE IM TELLING U

She was very sweet but only took attendance when she felt like it, showed up to class some days only to hear about her opinions and not anything about the class. Not many assignments which weren't too difficult, just some never got graded… definitely not my favorite class but it was fine.

Jenny was so good and so sweet! Defiantly go to class and be ready to take notes, but don't be scared off by her attendance policy! The course itself was so much fun. I really liked the reading notes and discussion.

She was not very great at sticking to the class lecture, and also let students ramble on about other stuff. She is very sweet, but as someone who prioritizes my grade, it was hard to keep up when I was retaining information cause she wasn't clear. The final is a joke, so much work for quite literally nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Grading not in accordance to syllabus. A's on all assignment/tests can still result in a C if she grades your participation as a greater percentage than the syllabus states & gives a very low score

Subject is very easy, but you learn more about her personal life than sociology. She yells, is afraid of devices being out in case shes recorded, etc.

Scored an A on every single assignment/test still got a C due to participation. Grading was not in accordance with her own syllabus (should've gotten a B) 

Tended to shout and get extremely worked up, was afraid of devices being out in case a student recorded her, etc.A chaotic class where I learned more about her personal life than the subject.

Jenny is awesome! She really knows what she's talking about and makes discussions very meaningful. Attendance + active participation are mandatory. 3 short essays and a handful of quizzes, this year the final was made up of old quiz questions. She's always quick to respond to emails, and is also straight up funny! I would gladly take another class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Flexible when needed, grades quickly. I always knew where I stood. She is very receptive to outside of class issues.

I liked the professor as a person and she I liked her different point of view, but it doesn't matter what you read (which is a lot; usually a chapter a week with a couple of different assigned readings outside of textbook), I could never get over a C on the tests because how much information was spewed - Relied mostly on readings

She takes so long to grade anything, the entire class was a joke and she tried to make it so much harder than it needed to be. She never specifies word count and always says you are under no matter how much you write.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Duncan is a great guy but he doesn't lecture well in larger class sizes. He tends to ramble and get sidetracked easily, so paying attention in lecture can be difficult. He offers A TON of extra credit for outside class events which is the only way I passed the class. Tests are difficult and the discussion sessions we're very useful for me.
He definitely knows what he's talking about, and for the giant class size he did well.
Great class.
Amazing professor.

Dr. Duncan is so sweet and you can tell he loves what he does. There is so much extra credit, make sure to go to discussions as there is a lot of opportunity for extra credit there. Exams are based on the reviews so study those but the final is pretty heavy, that is what dropped me to a B.

Amazing guy and professor. He really cares about his students. I enjoyed his lectures just because of his warm attitude and anecdotes. For tests, he gives a few hundred practice questions, but all the answers are in there. Lots of extra credit available.
Dr. Duncan is so sweet and caring and loves what he does.

Great guy and a decent professor. The course itself isn't difficult, but the exams feel designed to trick you. The class is very test heavy. He offers extra credit, but expect lower scores on midterms and the final. Grading takes a long time, and there is no curve. The almost entire multiple choice final feels too heavy for the coursework overall.
Very nice professor, responds to emails very timely and in a very understanding and respectful manner. Class was fairly easy, quite a few midterms (4) but overall I would take this professor again.

Dr. Duncan is an amazing professor and a warm person. The class is not difficult, and the exams are easy to prepare for if you study. The only downside is that some TAs can be hard to understand due to accents, which can make discussion sections tougher to follow. Still, attendance is important. Overall, an easy class with a great professor.

Dr. Duncan was the sweetest professor I've ever had, it is clear that he really cares about his students and wants them to do well. There are so many extra credit opportunities in this class, do them all it REALLY helps. Also, go to lecture the participation points do add up.
Lectures weren't all that useful, but he's an amazing guy and the class was pretty easy. He gives out so much extra credit you could end the class with a 120%
Great guy and an easy class if you pay attention. A lot of readings and homework but practice problems are the same that will be on the tests. He also gives a lot of extra credit.

I don't think he is an effective professor. He clicks through McGraw Hill slides without explaining the material, and everyone learns more on their own. His homework and due dates are inconsistent and unclear. Much of class is spent on irrelevant topics, including personal conversations with TAs. The course could be engaging if taught differently.

(Marketing 305) Bad. Assigns McGraw Hill smart books and tells students to study ONLY those for the exams (told my class to not read the textbook). Exams maybe have 75% questions from the smartbooks, thats 25% that he NEVER went over in class or on McGraw Hill.. which already puts you at most likely a B given you get EVERYTHING ELSE right.

Duane lets students know that lecture is non-mandatory, which is helpful for students. He is funny, witty, and laidback. Exams are straight from the book but do require a good amount of studying and memorization.
he's great, very engaging and you can tell he cares a lot about his material and his students.

Phil is the GOAT. Super clear about grading on stuff, super flexible on due dates, super helpful if/when you're struggling, super easy to talk to about the class or other stuff. I very frequently stayed after class just to talk to him about random stuff. I'm so sad I won't be in any more of his classes.

Genuinely one of my favorite profs I've had. I took his ling 106 class my first semester at KU and not only was he passionate abt teaching his subject, he was also encouraging, helpful, and understanding. I didn't expect to take a real interest in linguistics, but his class really inspired me, and I ended up picking it up as my minor!
His feedback was great and very helpful. What he required from you was straightforward and pretty easy. Highly recommend taking him for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ugh I loved this class and professor. I learned so much and had such a good time throughout the semester. I wish I had another class with him!

Phillip Duncan is the best professor. I took his Linguistics class for a core credit and he was the best. I didn't know anything about the subject but he explained everything well answers any questions and knows the content. He is kind and understanding. I can't think of a better professor than him! He always has a positive attitude!
Very student-focused

I found the subject matter boring, but Professor Duncan did a great job structuring the class. Weekly discussion section is mandatory, but they can be made up. Quizzes are open notes/book and they can be made up as well. Final Project was spaced out which I was thankful for. My grade rounded up which is why I'd say he's 10/10. Take his classes.

Great choice of a professor! He is very understanding and kind. You do a project but he structures it spaced out over the whole semester, which makes it really manageable. He offers extra credit for participating in studies. There are monthly open-everything quizzes. No tests. Lecture was boring at times, but definitely go to discussion section.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall really understanding. He will work with you if you don't understand and answers emails within a couple hours. He did quizzes and a discussion board every week as well as a HW assignment every other week. Overall a very easy, low stress class, just go to lectures and your discussion.

Singlehandedly made me fall in love with Kaqchikel, and the reason I'm taking it as a language class this year. He clearly loves what he teaches and even with units I didn't care about, his enthusiasm was infectious. Challenges you, but helps you figure things out along the way. You get a sense that he's genuinely rooting for your success.

Prof. Duncan was a really great, understanding professor. He rounded my course grade up a few percentage points at the end of the semester, which was great. He's available, helpful, and posts examples of what your final project should look like.

Professor Duncan is great - super easy to follow and understand, as well as ready to make sure everyone totally understands the material before moving on. It's not a difficult course but I'd definitely go to class, since there is a lot of material covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took him in Fall 18. Funny dude. For LING106 you gotta show up to class for the participation credit with the clicker. Only 5 homework assignments and tests werent difficult.

Just the absolute worst. He thinks he's a comedian and doesn't actually teach any of the material that we need to know. The assignments are a mess and he doesn't give a description on canvas of what to do for them. His TAs take weeks to grade and you will have several missing assignments just sitting in canvas. He yaps and flirts with his TAs.
Worst professor ever!! About 2 months into the class and I feel like everything that I have learned I have learned by teaching myself. He doesn't teach in class and just yaps.

Just not a good professor at all. Posts things to canvas with no description, constantly changing things on canvas. So unorganized and makes it hard to focus and study the material. Also plays around too much in class and rarely gets into lecture. PLEASE do not take this class with him.

Uses his classroom as his comedic stage, and he's neither funny nor a focused professor. I would avoid taking classes with him at all costs if you want to save your time and brain capacity, as all he does is drain people.
mktg 425 was like a public humiliation ritual at times. still learned a lot in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Easy class, but the structuring is terrible. Lectures are super boring and the simulations you run on McGraw Hill get repetitive. Homework is very tedious and time consuming for easy content. Duane takes forever to start class and rarely teaches you anything in his own words. The online textbook will be your only source of "learning" in this class.

This class was both beyond easy and beyond boring. I had so much extra credit that I was able to skip the final. Also, all the exams, homework, and assignments were really easy. It was just. The. Worst He'd make you redo every single SmartBook right before the exam as study material which took HOURS because there was like 100+ questions each.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at KU, extremely personable and down to earth with a good sense of humor. Does his best to encourage engagement during classes, and will get to know everyone in the room whether you want it or not. Homework assignments are extremely hard but ultimately help to flesh the content of the course out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment:
Duane "teaches" by quickly flipping through random slides, and going through an online simulation. I timed how much of the class was wasted. On average, he wasted 1/3 of class or 25 minutes talking to the football players or trying to create an assignment.

Duane Myer Quote: "Eye contact is the same as raising your hand"

Trust me, not worth it.

You will get out of this class what you put into it. Yes, you'll have to teach yourself most concepts. However, I enjoy his lectures and he is very personable. Homework isn't hard but takes a while, he offers extra credit, and the simulations are pretty fun/interesting. Exams are tricky but curved.. just study hard & ask questions and you'll be ok!

Sales Force Management with Duane was fun and engaging. He made an environment where people could speak up. The work was not too hard and it was graded easily. The group project was a lot of fun. He is a great guy once I got to know him personally and really cares for his students. He was flexible and understanding when I suffered a loss.

Professor Myer is genuinely one of the worst human beings at KU. Throughout the semester he continued to ramble on about how "some people just have to be homeless in a capitalist society" and how much he despises the lower class. If you have accommodations, you don't in this class. He will override and grade you harder for even bringing them up.
Dude is fluent in yappanese and a master in bluffing. Nothing was uploaded in Canvas. Even after 2 weeks of class, we haven't discussed anything. Absolute waste of tuition. I feel bad for the TAs

Talks about the news instead of class content in lectures. Explains nothing on canvas. Posts HW and changes deadlines at the last minute. Assigned research papers but you get zero feedback, making them worthless for learning. Assigns "wallstreet wednesday" papers that have no instructions and aren't mentioned once in the syllabus. No study guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst professor i've ever had hands down, avoid him at all costs, but if you have to take him... you can put in greatly exaggerated numbers in the simulation tracking sheets, they can't check your work, I know since they asked for a screenshot on the last homework, and you can use inspect element for that one. Use smartbooks to study for exams.

Read the textbook because he never goes over any of the material you will be tested over in class, so you basically have to teach yourself.  Attendance is mandatory and for points but every class you sit and learn nothing.  Your homework for the whole semester is to complete a simulation on how to make a backpack and it teaches you nothing.

This was one of my least favorite classes ever taken. Attendance is mandatory even though every class is an unending yap session. He teaches almost none of the material himself; you have to learn everything for the exams through tedious McGraw smartbook chapter questions outside of class. I would not recommend taking this class unless you have to.
Duane has a PhD in yapping.
Tests are a just lot of multiple-choice questions. No study guides. Class is mostly simulations. Depends heavily on the TA. Nothing is easily accessible and never posted on canvas.

This is the most pointless class I've ever taken in my life. We spent every lecture and every homework doing a 2000's online simulation that had nothing to do with the material of the class. The lectures do not set you up at all for the tests but are still mandatory to go to. Duane spends most of the class talking about unimportant current events.

Duane is a great person and is very knowledgeable but isn't the best lecturer. He does not cover exam material in class, but shows how to apply the knowledge in a simulation. He's the definition of "it'll do."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: It depends on the class, but this guy doesn't post anything on canvas. He's definitely entertaining and makes an 8am class more bearable, but you're shooting in the dark on homework assignments. Great guy and if you show up and talk with him you can succeed in his class. If you don't show up to class, it's gonna be tough.

Duane is one of my favorite teachers. I have taken MKTG 425 and 430 with him as well. The class structure is always pretty similar. HW every other week will probably take an hour or less. His tests aren't hard and have been open book. He is very reasonable and cares about his students. He tries to make the classroom fun and interactive.
lectures were boring and they have nothing to do with the exams but its still mandatory. the homework assignments have nothing to do with the exams. he does not prepare you AT ALL

This guy makes students buy a pricey online textbook along with the course work, so the class is completely "taught" using this. Not a professor in my eyes. Also, sorry to say this, but your jokes are not funny. Please stop for the sake of your students' sanity.

no tests, all quizzes and homework
good lectures 
nice guy and interactive class discussions

I liked his class you can miss a few lectures but he gives out extra credit here and there for the people that show up and took the people that showed up to starbucks one day so that was nice of him. Homework was easy but tests are lengthy but not too hard. I enjoyed his class!

Worst professor I have ever had. Makes up ridiculous reasons to deduct points. Gives clear deadlines, but then deducts points if you submit on time but "close to the deadline". Requires you to arbitrarily space out submissions and will deduct points if assignments are submitted close to each other. Your grade has nothing to do with marketing.

Myer is a stand-up guy who does care for his students a great deal. He brought a lot of energy to class and has some good jokes up his sleeve. The class taught me a lot in a simplistic way. He does not give too much work or assignments. There are two tests that barely impact your grade. Would take again and again

Duane is a good teacher. First time teaching this class so it was heavily based on the textbook and the tests were right out of the textbook. Lots of extra credit. Interesting class if you wanna learn about retail marketing and retail supply chains. Took minimal effort to get an A.

This class was an absolute joke. Took it during the COVID-19 Pandemic, but his lectures were awful before we moved online. Spent 15 minutes per chapter going through the book provided slides. Repeatedly commented, "you will want to study this concept and know what it is for the exam," but didn't provide any explanation himself. Learned nothing

Really accessible if you need help. Most of the work is case studies which can be tough because he never really taught during lecture, but he had office hours. If you study the tests are doable and he tries to make it easier because some of the content in the textbook (sales) is pretty difficult.

He teaches very little content in class, spends most of the class time showing how to complete homework assignments, goofing off or complaining about how bad the text and premade slides are. Be prepared to read an extremely boring textbook for a couple of hrs a day. He is very personable though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is very easy to get an A, but you will learn nothing from this class! The prof sometimes takes class about 10-20 minutes or just shows how to do the homework, so I don't know why I should go to the class. All you need to do is memorized the power point and ready to the exam. However, I think I just waste my time to take this class.

He's a great professor. He doesn't spend much time teaching or lecturing about the chapters (sometimes he does). We are expected to read the online book before the class and are graded on it. He has a very clear grading rubric and even offers EC. Before every test he basically tells you what material you should concentrate on for each test. Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: For tests just memorize definitions and you will be fine. Do all homework, come to class, and do all extra credit and you will get at least a B+ or an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Runs the whole class through an awful online supplement, the online book is really hard to navigate and he spends about 0% of class time talking about  marketing and instead spends the class making bad jokes.

Professor Myer is awesome. He has had a lot of experience in the business world and that translates well into what he teaches in marketing. The class is pretty easy to ace, but you have to show up and pay attention, and study for the tests which make up the bulk of the grade. Myer cares about students, so don't be afraid to ask him for help!

Lectures are required but he just stands up there and talks about anything but marketing. Days were wasted filling out march madness brackets and things of that nature. Spends a whole day going over the test questions & complains why no one gets questions he thinks are easy. As a marketing major I feel like he seriously hurt my future in the field.

Doesn't teach at all - spends the entire lecture trying to be funny and wasting your time. You have to teach yourself to pass the exams. Takes attendance every class period even though nothing is done in class. Didn't study for the final and got the same grade as the first two exams I studied hard for. Exams totally unrelated to lecture.
very  good

Class is a joke, but you have to go for participation grade. He doesn't teach anything at all, and spends the entire class trying to be funny. Tests are semi difficult. No reviews given. Teach everything to yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a great professor who cares about his students. If you have trouble understanding something he always try's to help out. Lectures can be a little bit of a snooze, but it helps that he's hot. Great eye candy.

Good guy, but a horrible lecturer.  He talks about himself and cracks jokes the entire class.  You must stay till the end of class because he takes attendance.  The tests are over 7 chapters and the smallest of details.  Be prepared to teach the entire course by yourself.  Extremely unorganized, not impressed by the ex Pepperdine professor.

Worst class I have taken at KU. Learned nothing and spent far too much time in class listening to him try and crack jokes. Take it with Clopton, because trying to learn from Myer is going to be a huge mistake.

The guy barely taught anything.  Almost all the lectures consisted of him trying to be funny.  He takes attendance throughout class so you have to stay the entire time.  No need to pay attention in class either.  Exam questions  100% definitions from textbook
I didn't get anything from taking this course. His lectures are pretty much a joke. He doesn't teach much and ends class early. You'll need to teach yourself.
A handsome and humour teacher!!
Very good
very good teacher. I like him so much. thank you for teahing
Very good teacher. Easy Class
Lectures are long and boring. Tries to crack jokes the entire time and doesn't really teach the subject so its hard to pay attention. Be prepared to teach yourself for the test.

Professor Myer is a nice guy and makes MKTG 311 a very easy class. The class is kind of disorganized and deadlines change, but he does that mostly to help students (if many people say they have multiple tests in a week, he will change the date of his test so students aren't so slammed). Tests are not cumulative and homework is pretty simple.

Funny guy that is great at engaging the class. Makes sure everyone has a say and encourages participation. Easy grader on homework and projects, but tests are hard. Each test is over seven chapters and the study guide doesn't match what is on the test. If the tests were easier, then he would be a must take. LearnSmarts can take a while as well.

Great personality and overall nice guy but not a great teacher. From the beginning of the class he had no idea what direction to take the class and overall unorganized. I did great in his class but a majority of the people in the class probably felt left out as he only taught about three of us.

He teaches at Pepperdine now but he's great. Really engages with the class and discusses marketing well. His tests are very straight forward and from the notes if you paid attention in class. Take his class if you can.
Good teacher. Light-hearted classroom environment. Also, dude has some pretty nice sideburns.

Duane is a professional and a respectable guy. The fact that he has real world experience that he often references, further proves his legitimacy. He has clear and reasonable expectations and maintains a friendly, light-hearted classroom environment.
DO NOT TAKE HIS WINTER BREAK CLASS. It's so much work it's actually insane. Despite the name - this professor is NOT your friend.
Professor Friend gives good feedback on assignments, which helped me to know what he was looking for the next assignment. The assignments, tests, and papers are a lot of work but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this class online, and unfortunately, it was a frustrating experience. Duncan's came off as passive-aggressive in emails that felt personal and uncalled. It's hard to feel supported or motivated in a class when the instructor seems uninterested in creating a respectful learning environment. I wouldn't take a class with him again.

By far the best professor I have had for an online course. He gives super quick feedback and is very helpful. I took him for POLS 390, but that wasn't an option to select. This class was harder than most online classes that I have taken in terms of courseload, but Professor Friend is a great resource.

I loved my experience in this class. Though the class was online, I felt like he was the professor that cared about my well-being and performance the most. My life fell apart at the end of the semester but he was super understanding through everything. Also, I took this class for honors and it was only 1 extra paper that was easy and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this as a 4-week course, so it was a lot more work than usual, but Dr. Friend was super helpful, gave great feedback, responded quickly, and was very understanding and willing to work with you if you needed help or an extension. Very nice teacher who cares about his students, even if they're all online!

Although I didn't really love the class itself, Professor Duncan was great. He cares about his students and is extremely flexible about due dates and grades. I realized that I wasn't very interested in linguistics, but he would a be a great resource for any student that wanted research or opportunities in the linguistics department.

professor duncan is great! i took his class to fulfill a KU34 requirement so i had no prior knowledge of linguistics. even though i learned that i am not interested in linguistics and found the class a little boring, prof duncan is a great teacher. he's very compassionate and understanding and will work with you. if you do the work, you'll be fine!
Philip is incredibly kind and knowledgeable! Easy and interesting class.
i loved him so much, he was always in such a happy and passionate mood. He was super nice to all of his students. Definitely my favorite professor at ku. he explains his content really well too.

Duncan is a passionate professor who cares about his students' well-being. I was always excited about going to this class. He is also really knowledgeable in linguistics. If you are going to take SPLH 466 take it with Professor Duncan!

Took Typology, LING 421. Really nice guy, very caring and accommodating. I think my only problem is that the course wasn't very structured so we were sort of planning as we went, which destroyed the pacing of the class. He seems like he's way too busy all the time, and he can be slow to respond to emails as a result. Loved working with him though.

This class was pretty lecture heavy but he is so nice and easy to listen to that they weren't too boring. The homework was easy and he always gave us an extra day to do it without penalty. He was always open to questions, responded quickly over email, and was happy to provide supplemental material if you needed it or missed a class.

Phil is a very caring professor. He will do everything he can to make sure everyone of his students can succeed in his classes as long as you reach out to him. I have had him for two classes now and would highly recommend him for any class he teaches.

Professor Duncan is very willing to help his students succeed in the class. He makes lectures involved and entertaining, and he is a very hands on teacher. He almost felt as involved with my research project as I was. He is hilarious, smart, and entertaining. I would definitely recommend him.

Genuinely caring professor with engaging lectures and expansive knowledge. Makes accommodations for students without hesitation. Would gladly take another class of his; loved the perspective of a linguistics professor in an SPLH class.
Didn't interact much with the prof, but when i did he was very understanding

I had Duncan for LING 320 and LING 575. As an underclassman, 320 was pretty hard because it relied on research skills I hadn't learned yet, but I think it was appropriately challenging for a 300 By the time I took 575 (Structure of K'iche'), I was much more prepared. Try to read, and show up. He has a lot to give if you put in a lil effort.

Note that this review is from an online class over winter break. Dr. Duncan is a friendly person, respects students views, and grades assignments very reasonably. My only complaint is that assignments sometimes take a long time to grade, which is especially problematic in such a short class.

If you show up to class and pay somewhat attention you will do super well on tests! Definitely go to the TA's before you turn in an assignment so you can get a 100. homework's are the best study tool. This professor makes the class super fun and exciting and genuinely cares about you. 10/10 professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved this class. I really enjoyed hearing professor Duncan lecture and it was really interesting. There are about 7 homework assignments that are a big chunk of your grade and are pretty easy. Tests are easy and are exactly like the study guide. A couple of extra credit opportunities but not many. I liked him and am taking another class with him
This is a career exploration class for the Psychology major, so it is super easy. It is a P/F course, so you have to do all of the assignments to get a P.

Dr. Duncan was a great professor, and I found most of the assignments were easy. My only problem was that he was terrible about getting things graded in a reasonable amount of time. This happened with both classes I took with him, ANTH 320 & 502. 502 was a winter class, but my grades weren't in until the end of the Spring semester.

There's nothing to say that hasn't been said already. Prepare for the most snooze-worthy lectures of your life and to teach yourself everything--he's a somewhat chill grader, though, which is just about his only redeeming quality.

Terrible awful often incoherent lecturer. A 15 minute youtube video covers more than his lectures ever do. Homework is very annoying and has questions completely unrelated to what is being covered in class, or material that would be covered the day after the homework was due. The one point in his favor is that his tests are very easy.

Every lecture I go in hoping to learn, but he is technically incompetent and always mumbling. He'll write on a digital white board instead of just showing a problem, his hand writing is not legible. He will ask a question, not even wait a full second, then ask "Hellooo???", it's not very encouraging, considering how bad campus internet can be.

I read every comment on him since 2001, and they're all still true in Dec 2020, except for him offering extra credit. This semester's class is completely online due to COVID, and he still isn't proficient at screen sharing in Zoom after 10 weeks. Incompetent at technology! No scheduled office hours, you'll be teaching yourself mostly. Retire plz!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This has to be one of the worst professors I have ever had. I'm sure he hasn't always been this way, considering he is practically 90 years old. I showed up to class every day and I don't know why. It was a waste of fifty minutes every class period, due to incoherent mumbling. Avoid him at all costs. You will save your gpa and sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This guy does not know how to teach a class. His lectures are terrible, long-winded, lack even a semblance of structure, and are sometimes nonsensical. Students often have to correct his examples and marks on homework. Stay away if you want to keep your sanity.

Worst lecturer I've had. Nice guy, but it's simply time for him to retire. Class was extremely easy. It felt like high school math. Very little calculus, no proofs. Extra credit built into all tests. If you're taking this class to prep for FM, you're out of luck. Less than half of FM syllabus is covered, and it's much easier. Take for the easy A.

Lectures are never on topic and it's usually 30+ minutes of him writing an example down wrong, rewriting it on the board, doing half of it (wrong) and then moving on. It was maddening. Homework is not at all like the tests. Tests are fair but you have to teach yourself everything. I didn't get anything out of either 627 or 630 with him. Avoid him!

His lectures are quiet and filled non sequiturs. He does not show very many examples in class, and he often does not fully finish or explain the examples he does provide. His hw schedule is inconsistent: you'll have 3 weeks of nothing and then an assignment due for 4 lectures straight. You have to dedicate yourself to read the book if you want an A

If you study the textbook you'll be fine. People tend to overlook the part of syllabus that strongly urges reading the material before the lecture, which he doesn't mention in class. Lectures only make sense if you've done the reading, if not, you might as well stay home. He usually gives a fair amount of partial credit on tests and a nice curve

This class was terrible.  I'm a 4.0 student and I ended up getting a C in the class.  I went to office hours, did the homework, studied a lot, but he was not helpful at all.  His lectures are confusing at best.

While teaching he seems absent minded. He will spend an entire class going through an example, realize he made a mistake, and say he will correct it the next class. He never follows through. He loves to call people out for answers and then will insult them if they are wrong. Please refuse taking any course from him. Katz and Duncan's wife are best.

Probably the worst math teacher there is at KU. Theres no point in going to class because you don't learn anything in class. If your taking a class with him you better be good at teaching yourself the material.
Extremely smart man and very nice but isn't the best at communicating teaching students that can't grasp much.

What a horribly, awful teacher! If you can avoid this teacher, do it! I was actually re-taking Calc 1, and I thought going into this class it would be somewhat easier, but it was WAY worse. He is smart, but can NOT teach. His wife is the co-instructor of this class and is VERY strict. Be ready to teach yourself. Very disappointed.
He is a very smart person, but he CAN'T TEACH! Beware to those who take his class, you won't be able to understand anything. Good Luck!

Will make time to talk to you outside of class, very nice and interested in his students.  He is an extremely talented mathematician.  But that's the rub.  He has a hard time instructing people who don't grasp the concepts quickly and the exams are extremely difficult. Take if looking for a challenge.
