He is a nice guy, but his teaching style is horrible. All he does is talk really abstractly and generally about what we're doing and hardly ever does pertinent examples.  On around 75% of the homework problems I had to search through the text to figure out what the questions were even asking.  You basically have to teach yourself

Don't expect to learn from the instructor in class.  If you don't read the book and just do the homework you will do bad.  Very unclear with his teaching methods.  Beware! he will not accurately prepare you for the mid-term.  Too bad he makes the Mid-term and final for all math 121 classes.  I put in (A) effort for a (B)grade.

He wastes a lot of class time going off on tangents and ridiculing students for not knowing their height in centimeters over and over again. He can take all period just working through 3 problems and still never really get to the point. His midterm and final are about 3-5 times as difficult as he lets on or prepares you for. Willing to help but...

Good guy, not so great teacher.  Will help you if you seek it out.  He is of an older school of teaching, so whilst he is a heavy researcher, he still makes a lot of time for his students.  If you don't do the work, expect to fail his class.  Really really smart guy.
Bad.
Good teacher.  To do well in his class, a student needs to be willing to read the book - minimal studying.  You can't be lazy in this class and expect to get above a C, without any prior knowledge.
Way to smart to teach low calc classes.  you will spend many class periods not knowing what is going on.  nice guy and very helpful though.  at least he speaks english
The worst instructor EVER
He is absolutely terrible. Stay away. No clear grading rubric.

Dr Dunn is great. He tries to make the lectures fun and its very evident that he cares about the course. We had 4 exams and he lets you drop one of them, although the class average on each was around 50-60% so they are on the more difficult side. He is very open to help and there is a curve. He often makes dad jokes too :)
Dr. Dunn is great. Everything about the class (schedule, grading, etc.) is crystal clear, and he makes chemistry interesting and fun.
Engaging

Dr. Dunn is an awesome guy. Material can be tough at times but he tries to keep everyone engaged during lectures and uses example and explanation to help with understanding. Jokes around little to maintain everyones attention and is a fun professor really liked him. Ask questions in class and he will becomes exponentially more helpful too.
One of the better chemistry professors at KU!

Dr. Dunn is really nice and a great professor. He does a pretty good job at explaining the information while also keeping lectures interesting. You can definitely tell he wants students to do well and pass his course. Tests are difficult though if you don't fully understand material. Lab section was a cakewalk with little to no difficulty.

Dr. Dunn is not only a hottie, he is an excellent professor. He explains things very well, and will help you out if you need it. The exams are pretty difficult, but are manageable if the material is known.  He is awesome!

Very good at explaining confusing topics by dumbing the topics down. Has a monotone voice, so don't go to class if you're tired. Very good sense of humor and tries to keep the class entertained with some sarcasm. Great guy!

Dr. Dunn was pretty awesome. I hated every single moment of chemistry, but the only reasons I pulled out the A were because of his helpfulness and his willingness to give the class a generous curve when we needed it the most. Great guy, all around.

He is the best teacher that I have ever had.  He is very energetic and encorporates demonstrations into his lectures that keep things interesting.  He is a very down to earth guy and was very helpful when I went into his office hours.  His tests were very difficult, but he adjusted his grades to fit the class average accordingly.
Fabulous  teacher.  He is so funny, and he does very cool experiments that involved sky rocketing pink foam!!!  Besides, for the women, he is wonderful to look at!
Dunn is the best chemistry professor ever. The class is fairly hard, but there is a nice curve and he is amusing, easy to talk to, and fair.
He's an awesome professor, he knows what he's talking about and is always ready to help his students out.
This guy is the best teacher that I have had in all my time in college and I'm in grad school now.  You will definitly learn something in his class.
This professor is cool as heck!
He will never answer a single email and is not away in his office when he says he would be. He is really funny tho and his exams are not to hard.

Chad is a fun guy and classes were enjoyable for the most part. I'm pretty sure he just got his PhD, and it shows. He definitely feels like he's one of us as a student. He has a good perspective. Teaching wise, he's just average. He does what he needs to but also like do dig into theory and high level applications which makes things hard to follow.
Hes so cool! I just love how he roasts us in a good way. I legitimately want to be friends with him after I am finished with this class. 10/10 would have again.
He is super chill and cool. But youll still definitely have to work for your grade. Just ask questions !!
Ken is a great teacher that connects well with his students. He is one that I would recommend to others but be warned, you either really like him or really don't.
He was little unclear and a bit confusing but I thought he looked like Zac Efron to me.

Professor Dwyer is not an effective teacher. She refuses to use blackboard and gives very vague instructions about the assignments for the class. She is often snarky and unkind when you ask for more information, and her comments on your work are rude and not constructive. I put a lot of effort into the class but did not learn or enjoy anything.

This professor isnt the best, but she definitely isnt the worst either. The best part about her is that she does respond to you by email within a day or two and her quizzes are easy as long as you listen in class. I rented the textbook, but I only read one or two chapters in total because she goes over everything from the readings in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: What's been written before pretty much sums it up. Unpredictable, clearly doesn't like teaching other than for the attention it brings in holding forth. If there's any way around this person, seek it out. Do NOT take any classes from this woman!

Stay away from this professor and anything she teaches and anything that she researcher. She'll seem friendly and nice at first, but quickly tires--unless she can use you. After she's finished, she's finished with you, too. Her courses reflect her general approach--spasms that often reflect little preparation.

Despite being a Linguistics Professor, the woman has a hard time communicating; I've tried, it failed. Multiple times, people would ask her a question and she would not understand what was being asked, and leave the subject. She also has a tendency to be all happy a cheery, until someone asked he something, then she would seem annoyed.

If you are a white male, stay away from this class--she hates you and none of your input is can possibly be valuable. She grades minority students lightly, even when they turn in substandard work (an Asian woman showed me her test, I was offended by how easily she was graded compared to me). If you are a minority student, this will be an easy A.

She was very disorganized and one of the most boring lecturers I've ever had. She stood behind her computer and refused to move around the classroom. The exams were often written incorrectly, and the majority of students failed every exam, so she always had to curve

Very easy class, very light on assignments and tests were online. She's a nice person who makes an effort to know people's names. Classroom was flipped, which I felt limited in-depth learning of topics. Primary complaint is that I feel like I didn't learn very much since tests covered vague niche concepts instead of bigger picture.

It's a flipped classroom, and the exams are online which is really nice. She's a really good professor and cares about her students. She does extra credit every week which is really nice. The exams are open book and note so there's really no reason to not pass this class. You could do the bare minimum and still  be okay.

I've had Dr. Morgan for 2 classes. She's been amazing in both of them. She is very kind, considerate, and wants the best for her students. She is superb at learning names and making students feel welcomed in her classes. Some of the material, especially 417, can be lengthy but she does her best to have high energy which keeps everyone engaged 10/10

As long as you come to class and participate on the worksheets it is very easy to get an A. The exams are formatted good and the questions are easy to understand and if you need help, you have the textbook. Her lectures slides are super awesome too to skim through before class/exams. She is such a caring person and super smart.

I took the course over the summer. Each week we had multiple lecture videos to watch, which did take a long time, but Dr. Morgan broke the lessons up into manageable sections. There were 2 exams, both open book/note, but they were timed. She was very approachable and sent out many announcements to help us stay on track.

I took Immunology with Dr. Morgan and she was always very helpful and was always nice. You can tell she cares about what she does and wants students to care as well. And even though all of our tests were online and open-note, she still offered quite a bit of extra credit which was really nice. I would definitely recommend this class.

Awful experience. Worst professor I've ever had & terrible class. Doesn't teach ANYTHING. Online only, class is just a waste of an hour. You sit & complete one 10 minute worksheet for the entire time. The teacher doesn't seem to care about helping students, just walks around aimlessly. Hated every second of the class 10/10 would never take it again
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Morgan for three classes. All of her classes were set up in a similar organized manner. Extra credit is offered throughout the semester. Grading is clear and exams are not to difficult if you stay on top of learning and understanding the material. She is a wonderful professor and I highly recommend taking any classes taught by her!

This class goes over a ton of information, in my opinion, Anki/Quizlet is necessary if you wish to get an A. Dr. Morgan is very approachable and is happy to answer questions so don't be afraid to talk to her after class. The information is cumulative so don't fall behind or you'll have a bad time.

Dr. Morgan wants all of her students to succeed. Her class for 417 was very interesting and I was never bored of the information that I was learning about in class. The lectures are the meat of the class, she states in her syllabus the lectures are what is being tested over. Very important to fill learning objectives. She is very caring!!!

The class was entirely online and you could watch lectures and do homework whenever you want during the week. This was the easiest biology course I have taken at KU, and I'm including biol 151 and 153 in that (the introductory honors bio courses). I was never concerned about my grade in this class. Very easy and I actually learned the content!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was fully online, and it was one of the easier bio classes I have taken. I thought the lectures were really interesting. There were weekly practice questions, which would sometimes show up word for word on the exams. I'd recommend this class. Dr. Morgan seems really kind and like she genuinely cares about her students
Dr. Morgan is a very understanding professor. Her Immunology course is content-heavy, but not too difficult. She makes the tests with material you already know, so that's a plus. Would recommend.

Dr. Morgan is the real deal! Amazing professor and would love to take another class taught by her again! This woman was helpful and understanding during the pandemic this year! Her online lectures were clear and she provided the right tools for us to be prepared for the exams. She also provides extra credit which was a life saver for me! LOVE HER

I had Dr. Morgan during COVID-19. Her lectures were in depth but she reviewed most of the concepts from previous classes that related to the new material. She wants students to succeed and comes up with many analogies to help students learn the material. Grade is entirely based off of tests. Answering 2/3 questions adds 3% to final course grade
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dyan is my light at the end of the tunnel on a bad day. She truly cares about her students success and makes class as easy as she can (although the material is upper level). Lectures are extremely easy to understand, and she covers everything in a way that just clicks. Exams are detail oriented and the only grade though, so make sure you study well
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Morgan is an amazing instructor and I'm so glad that I was able to take this class with her. You can tell she really cares about her students and wants us to comprehend the information she shares.

This is my KU evaluation letter. 
He started the semester by saying he rarely gives out A's, which was immediately discouraging. His canvas regarding unset due dates, rubrics, and vague questions/directions is not well established. This class has improved my reading skills, but the readings are 10-30 pages. He is passionate, but vague. 7 absent= F
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His class itself was easy it was moreso him that I didn't care for as much. I liked the writing projects and the overall structure of the class, I just felt like he wasn't always clear with what needed to be done to succeed in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is extremely difficult. If you don't want to read and are trying to slide by just for the credit, I wouldn't take this professor. However, if you are looking for a thought provoking class that challenges your understandings of society and come in open minded you will pass just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: do not take this class with this prof. he constantly gets off topic and goes on tangents about stuff that has nothing to do with the class. very vague instructions for essays and assignments. also grades tough and you lose a lot of points if you miss classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The course for Eng 102 gave you vague instructions and due dates on essays and then proceeded to lecture about topics that didn't pertain to the assignments. However, the grading on the final assignment was less harsh. Overall, I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Outstanding.

Starts the class off by saying that he hardly gives out As because this is a college level course. He doesn't have rubrics and gives you a general idea of what you should be writing. You will be graded on participation in class and it can bring your grade down heavily. He's a fun teacher but his teaching methods aren't.

Does not respond to emails, on the first day he opens the class by saying that you should not expect to get an A in the course, mandatory attendance and a 10% grade deduction when you miss class. Would never take ENGL 102 with this teacher ever again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a terrible teacher and so unclear on due dates of assignments since he gets so off topic every class. He never stays on schedule which means he then springs assignments on the class. He started off the class on the first day saying "Don't expect to get an A in this class." He doesn't care abt the students workload or that it's a gen ed class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not recommend this professor. Save yourself the time and energy and just take English 102 with someone else. Very tough grader and will not receive a good score even if it looks like you did well on the rubric. Also, he does not give you a lot of time or notice to get the essays done for his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He grades very tough and there is very few assignments in the gradebook, so one bad grade ruins  your entire grade that you worked hard for the entire semester. This class would have been better if there was more communication, when you email a question, the response is not really helpful. The readings were interesting though.

He made us purchase a textbook that we never used. There is a lot of reading that doesn't necessarily pertain to the project we are working on. He grades very tough and tends to veer off-topic quite often. I would not recommend taking English 102 with him.
Incredibly opinionated, biased, no clear points made in lectures, vague discussions, manipulated rhetoric, tries to intimidate students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's opinionated and intense about everything. He also does lots of socratic seminars in which he grades very harshly. My least favorite thing with him is that he insists that you talk a lot in the socratic seminars, but then harshly criticizes what you say in front of everyone. This just reinforces not talking. He will fail you if you don't talk
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I would suggest finding a another instructor because the course was quite difficult for a 101 level, and the instructor made us buy two books, of which only one is actually used.

He is a nice guy outside of class but in class he expects lots of work as if you are only taking his class through the whole semester. Always gets confused in his work and assigned homework problems. If you have him, find a different teacher unless you like the anxiety and a challenge.

He was my favorite teacher my first semester at KU. He's neurotic and super funny, and his lectures are easy to keep up with. Write everything--He'll explain or at least write out every problem you'll need solve; plus, he gives you time to write every word he says and that helped me stay engaged in his lectures. Study and do your homework!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a pretty nerdy guy and just reads from his notes. He doesn't teach well and makes things very difficult. I'm taking it pass fail and it is a good thing I did. Final is 30% of your grade. Lots of quizzes and homework. Two exams which are very difficult. He seems to get confused in the work, as we have to question his work at points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I think he is a good guy outside of class but inside the class he is something else. He doesn't really explain things well or good enough for us to understand. It's like a different language. Also his tests are 100x harder than his examples and homework problems. I never been to his office hours because he only has one and I have class that time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He doesn't answer questions in a way that people can understand and his tests are REALLY hard! He also doesn't give a lot of examples in class and doesn't go over anything on the test when reviewing for said tests. His office hours are also really inconvenient to most people and he doesn't help outside of his hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Much fun do take.

This course is extremely lecture heavy and attendance mandatory. She runs through the slides extremely fast so you just have to wait til she posts them the next week. Slow grader, and doesn't offer good feedback on the multiple papers you have to write. Tough grader for no reason, seems to just enjoy criticizing more than improving. Thumbs down 👎
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sarah was amazing to learn from. I went on a study abroad trip and she was one of the professors there. She had incredible insight into every work of art we looked at and knew something about everything. It was great to sit and learn from her in a classroom but even better to go to actual museums and learn there.

Sarah was one of my favorite teachers I have ever had in my entire life! She genuinely cares so much about her students and their success and makes every single lecture interesting. Before this class, I knew nothing about art history, but her class really made me fall in love with it. I learned so much and want to take another one of her classes!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ebenezer is one of the best professors I've had at KU so far, and that was during the COVID semester. There's a lot you have to read, but exams aren't that difficult if you study. In class discussions are great and very thought provoking. This was the only class where I was upset when class was called off because of weather. Highly recommended

The whole class is lecture-based and he teaches everything out of the book. He is a nice guy, but the class isn't something life changing. He has four random pop quizes that work as participation and as long as you don't miss them the class is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Obadare is among the best sociology professors at KU. He's a bit of a dissenting voice within the department due to his centrist politics, which might rub some students the wrong way. His lectures and course material cover a wide range of the spectrum. He's a deep thinker, and he'll get you to critically examine your own beliefs.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Obadare is amazing. His lectures are fun and engaging despite the material being not the most interesting. His tests are easy and open note/book. There are four pop quizzes, but he assigns so much extra credit, I missed one and was able to earn those points back for just being in class. He's an awesome guy and this class is easy.

Ebenezer is my favorite professor I've had at KU. He is passionate about what he does and he makes sure all his students understand his material and the content. His tests are SUPER easy- Open book and open note. He has four pop quizzes that are not able to be made up but if you show up to class you'll pass. He's a really good lecturer!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this professor for a graduate level course. The grading did not seem consistent and the feedback from the professor was not always clear.

Professor Obadare is by far my favorite teacher I have ever had. I had to take this class to fill a requirement and he makes the class actually fun and engaging. He is very enthusiastic and even though there is a large class, he still takes time to remember students' names.

GREAT guy. Thought this class was going to be incredibly boring on the first day of class but it is actually entertaining. This semester he has made all tests and pop quizzes open note and open book so it's pretty hard to fail. There are 4 pop quizzes so beware of those cause they are 100 points (500 total). He really wants his students to do well.

I love this man. He is an absolutely phenomenal professor who strives to foster thought provoking, intelligent conversation at all times. He has helped remind me, indirectly, what is so incredible about college in the U.S.; that young people can still gather together and have genuine, important conversations. He exemplifies what college should be.

Ebenezer is by far one of the best professors I have had, if not THE best. He cares deeply for every student and goes great lengths to help you learn & provide resources & info for the papers/projects you do in his class. He will challenge you to think about questions you would otherwise not consider. Reallyfunny, too. KU is very lucky to have him.
If have the chance to take a class from Dr. Obadare, do it.

Possibly my favorite professor of all time.  He's exceptionally intelligent & really knows his stuff.  He's a great resource for grad students who want to learn more outside the classroom.  He plays devil's advocate & really makes you think about what you are learning.  I've learned more form his classes alone than I did in my entire undergraduate.

Awesome teacher, could be my favorite at KU.  Did not have much interest in Africa before taking this class but E really gets you inspired to want to learn more.  Weekly readings, some a little heavy but no textbook to buy.  No tests just 4 written papers.  Discussions, films and lectures make this a great class.

Excellent leader of discussion, guiding the class to truths you find yourselves.  Will admire you for bold and thought out positions.  Funny, but odd sense of humor to get used to.  I would take classes from him every semester if I could.

I took E's Transnational Migration class. It was very informative through several class readings, books and a few films. His accent makes him a little hard to understand but it kind of made me pay better attention. Overall I recommend his class because of the course material. Alot of it I could not believe happened in the world. Great class overall
He is literally the best and most interesting professor I had at KU. He cares about his students and really wants them to learn. Can really not say enough great things about him and his classes.
Loved it. So easy to understand!!

E is one of my favorite professors that I have had so far at KU. At first I was apprehensive with his accent but I find myself paying MORE attention because of it and actually learning more and not having any trouble. A lot of reading, but an amazing professor with a really interesting life story.
Terrific. Inspiring. Extremely funny.

He knows his stuff and gets the students involved. Friendly classroom atmosphere. No homework other than readings which are interesting. Papers aren't bad at all and he has been known to give out the test questions early. He is becoming much more comfortable as a professor as he gets more experience, too bad I had him for only my last semester.
Perhaps the best teacher at KU due to his attitude. You must attend class but it is enjoyable and you have little to do homework wise. Emphasis on papers over tests.
he is indeed great.

Great class, hard grader, funny guy.  If you want to do well, make friends early in the class with e (I.e. speak up and state your opinions, participate, and always come to class).  You will get an A.  Oh, he also likes cupcakes too, as a last resort :)

I had African Perspectives he also teaches Migration.  Very similar course.  No tests, no homework just reading and essays.  And a group project.  Very bright, very helpful, very funny and very nice.  Nothing bad to say about him at all.  I think if you actually read and listen you will learn more from this man than from a lot of teachers

Readings are painfully easy, but no one does them anyway.E gets everyone involved at the expense of real discussion.I find myself wishing he'd just teach+not ask every idiot's thougts."social capital" gets you far in this class--so you can fail tests + still pass.Great prof with an amazing life story,but good luck getting the stories out of him...
No Comments
Very Smart guy but difficult grader.

Professor Earle teaches this class out of love for the subject. His lecture style is fantastic for a large class and he is always available to help. Tests are mostly ID questions so make sure to keep up on reading.

Earle is hilarious and he knows his stuff. He is possibly one of the smartest professors I've had, which makes his tests pretty hard. You have a 10-11 page term paper and the final is also a 10 page paper. A lot of work, but a very interesting class. If you do the readings, you're set.

Attendance is not mandatory, however it is difficult to prepare for test without the detailed notes he expects from lecture.  His lectures are interesting and easy to attend(as long as it isn't 8am). Taking notes can be difficult; no p.p slides or outline. Exams(2):ambiguous term id's and gobbits+ paper. 5 short response and 2 major resrch papers.
Best class I have taken at KU. Seriously a wonderful professor!

Took conspiracies with Earle.  He really knows the info & keeps it relevant for students of today.  His weekly reading assignments get out of control, just too many.  I think he spends too much time trying to be cool and has never finished an outline for a week's lecture.  Grading is straightforward and fair.
Class was great, lot of reading, but was usually pretty interesting and lectures were entertaining as well. Do the readings and you will do fine on the midterm and final!
very hard class....lots of reading with little of it on the test....scares students to think he will test you over all of the info you read but puts selective pieces. Very hard to get my B!

Professor Earle is hilarious and a fantastic teacher. He's easy to understand and open to helping students. I am taking his class next semester because I liked him so much. If you have the opportunity, do not pass up taking his class. The only downside is there are tons of readings and it is hard to keep up sometimes.

Professor Earle is totally wonderful. The guy cracks me up and totally knows his****. He'll make any class fun and puts tons of effort into making his material both interesting and relevant. Bonuses include being totally hilarious, super hip, and having a great taste in music. Can't wait to take another class with him.
Not a very intelligible teacher.  Very arrogant and in love with himself.  His character is questionable.

Dr. Earle is a fantastic teacher! You do not necessarily have to go to lecture, but I did anyway because he makes them very entertaining. This class is not offered next semseter which is a shame. Hopefully, in a year from now it will be back in session. There was a fair amount of reading, but it is summed up pretty well in lecture.

Amazing teacher. Very smart, funny and I'm never bored during lectures. My favorite teacher at KU by far. My only complaint is the 10 page research paper when we've already had to write 2 film response papers. I would prefer tests over a big paper but we only have ONE test and it's the final.
Great topic (History of Conspiracy Theories and Paranoia)
Great techer, very helpful. take a class with him if you have an opportunity, he is a great speaker and very interesting. great guy too.
Very interesting lectures, fun to listen to.

Excellent professor--excited, smart, hip. I really enjoyed his lectures.  My biggest complaint was that there wasn't enough time during lecture to cover expansive period (US history through civil war) so he sometimes didn't follow his own outlines. Lecture time was sacrificed for Discussion classes which were taught by grad students. oh-& a hottie.

It's an easy class to not fail, but he is a really difficult to understand teacher.  Always telling you what you don't need to know and not to write this down.  Also emphasises his political agenda on you.  He also drives a mo-ped and talks about his trips to wherever that makes him better than you.  A decent class overall.

One of the best professors I have had in my 4 years at KU, I would recommend that everyone take a class of his.  Exceptional lecturer who makes history fun and exciting.  I have found him to be extremely helpful and easily accessible through email.  He is one of the top historians in the country, take advantage of him being at KU!!!!

Dr. Earle was not meant to be a leacture teacher.  You never know what to write down because he is constantly telling you what not to write down.  He swears and is quite condescending.  When it comes to emailing him with questions, he acts like you should already know the answer.  Not a good class at all - avoid at all costs.

Nothing is graded until the mid-term. If you do not do well on in-class essays, avoid his class. Only 4 items scored: mid-term, term paper, final and participation. The only problem is, he did not explain what he expected on the mid-term. My request is professor Earle, please do not refer to a founding father as A Cutie Pie.
I didn't read any of the readings and I showed up to like 3 or 4 of the lectures and I got a C+ on the mid term and I def hate history. So its kind of a easy class.

I can not stand the way he lectures. I can never take notes because he talks so fast and it seems every other word is a cuss word. He is also extremely unhelpful when it comes to email. FYI most people taking a history 128 class are freshman, they are going to have "stupid" questions you don't have to make them feel like an idiot by being a jerk.
He stinks at giving notes. He always tells us what not to write down..the jumps around everywhere..I cannot stand it
Interesting lectures that keep you awake as much as history can.
loved it loved the man great class, very funny, p.s. keep showing "undercover brother" during lectures.
tests were hard but I loved this class. It was my favorite at KU.
Awesome Professor!!!
No Comments
I actually like getting up for this class
Energetic and lectures are ORGANIZED!
No Comments
Just a great lecturer, and a fun course!
No Comments
No Comments
Energetic, eager to teach, extraordinary professor
No Comments

Made the class fun and related it to today. She claimed to be very serious, but was actually pretty laid back. Just do the reading and participate and you'll be fine. She wants to see that you know the material. Makes the lectures funny and interesting.
As a discussion leader, she was extremely helpful in clarifying the works we were reading and kept the discussions flowing.
No Comments

On any given day, Professor Small will mention a former student who turned out to be functionally illiterate.  I don't care if that student didn't know how to breath.  He couldn't possibly be any worse a professor than Ed Small.  I wish him a happy retirement.
Small was my favorite teacher. I from Russia and he remind me of my teacher back home. He give me a D+ in basic film but I okay with grade.

Had him a decade ago. He was coasting by on his tenure and rarely came to class, and he even lost my final exam. I had to track him for 6 whole months in order for him to even give me a grade. I work for Disney Animation now and knowing what i now know, he should have been fired long ago. The epitome of lazy and pompous. An embarrassment to KU.

One of the worst professors I've ever had, arrogant and not helpful, not to mention pompous. Incredibly demanding without giving much to any support and is more concerned about pointing out how much you don't know than teaching you what you should know.

One of the worst professors I've ever had, arrogant and not helpful, not to mention pompous. Incredibly demanding without giving much to any support and is more concerned about pointing out how much you don't know than teaching you what you should know.

Very demanding and old fashioned. A lot of students get on his bad side by talking back.  His production classes emphasize classical continuity and technical proficiency with the Bell & Howell 70 16mm film camera. You have to pay close attention because he doesn't go out of his way to make things easy.
The worst professor that I have ever experienced. This guy should be fired.

Small is a trip. Honestly I could not recommend him as a professor. He is very vague and hard to understand at times, and he tests you over things you don't know. There were times when he yelled at students for absolutely no reason. He does know a lot about film, but I think it's time for him to throw in the towel.

Easily the rudest professor I ever had while attending KU.  As an alumnus I want to forewarn any future film majors to avoid taking this guy unless you absolutely have to.  Every year my peers would pray that he had retired because he's honestly that bad.  He will yell at any student who asks a question that might steer from his beliefs.
This guy is so bad that I'm debating whether or not to write a letter to Chancellor Hemingway.  As I was, I'm so sorry if you are forced to take this class because of a major requirement.

I have had his classes a few times.  His manner of lecture is completely convoluted and he injects a lot of needless personal anecdotes in them.  All his theory classes consist of two tests (50% each of your grade) which are as confusing and pointless as his lectures.  He prides himself on awarding few A's.

I wonder how the University gets away with not evaluating Ed Small. I mean, if they took one look at his bogus tests (two tests, each count for 50% of your grade) with their questions that have absolutely nothing to do with the subject matter, surely they would have someone else teach the class. Instead I have to waste my money on this old fool.

Uses his own book for the class and expects you to know it as well as he does. Nitpicks on test questions and takes pride in no student ever getting 100% on one of his exams. Although difficult, will probably curve the test scores. Book is written in academic language far above how he talks in class, go figure.
No Comments
I've never understood teachers who hate students.
No Comments

Professor Small is a very hard individual to get along with. He is almost impossible to approach or have a coherent conversation with but he is still the best teacher that I have ever had at this University.  I knew when I entered his class that it was going to be a kick in the face.  I took the basic film class and animation and I could always rely on his honesty and he was the only people that would tell me what I needed to hear to develop. He is not easy and frankly he is not supposed to be.

I had to study quite a bit before the tests to do well. I got extra credit (5 %) if I attended more than 80% of the classes so that helped out a lot. Go to review sessions and study for a few hours a few days before the tests and you'll be fine.

A lot of people complain about him, but honestly the class is incredibly easy to get an A in. All you have to do is go to class and study the night before the tests and you will get an A. He is interesting and can be funny at times. Those that complain either didn't attend class, or they just aren't the brightest crayon in the box.
that way to much worthless information
Extremely easy class. Practically the same as high school biology.

Guy was really boring. Made a simple class harder than it needed to be. He also found it necessary to make every topic related to something that happened in his life. Don't buy the book, huge waste of money.

He's a decent teacher. His biggest downfall is that he rewords everything he says. So when you're trying to understand a concept he'll rephrase it 10 times and you'll end up confused over something simple, had he just repeated what he said the first time. Other than that the class was pretty easy. I never used to book and it was a waste of money.

Students who think this class is hard, you should be counting your lucky stars. Dr. Wiley doesn't cover even half of the details that are included in the book, and THAT'S the hard stuff! This biology class is VERY basic. If you took biology in high school this class should be a breeze. I attend class and study and have no problem getting A's.

While I hear a lot of students (freshmen) complaining about the class, the material is basic fundamentals. Not that hard, especially if you study. Just study the powerpoints and you're pretty much guaranteed a B.
incredibly boring lectures...but in order to know what's exactly on the test, it's better to just go even if you feel like you want to die every 50 min period...

Nice guy to wrap up the end of the semester. He taught a bit more than biology. More like astronomy, geography, geology and such. But did his best to fill in for the class. Test was not too hard a long a you studied the material. Lecture, a little dry but he tried his best and even added some videos
very (helpful, inelegant, caring) Dr. McBride is an engineering school of one man.

Dr. McBride is the most efficient professor I have had in terms of lecturing. Does not take a whole lot of time in class, but I still felt like I was well prepared for homework assignments and tests. Homework was very reasonable, but tests took about 4-5 hours. If you have a choice, Dr. McBride may be the better one. Currently teaches at UCCS.

Now a professor at University of Colorado - Colorado Springs, and still one of the best professors out there, certainly my favorite so far in my engineering school career.  One of the few professors I have felt actually WANTS his students to succeed.  Very helpful, and a very nice guy to boot.
Best engineering professor at KU.

Great teacher.  If you go to class, somewhat pay attention, get a group to do the homework, and ask him questions before the test you will be fine.  Go to his office hours and just shoot the bull with him, become his friend outside of just class and it will help you in the long run, I did it and he was very helpful to me.  Best teacher on campus.

I had McBride for CE 201 (statics) and CE 625 (statistics). He is the best prof I have had so far. This guy knows his stuff, he is extremely helpful and always available. He is fair in grading and in the material that he puts on exams. Lectures are organized and straight forward. Oh, and he's hilarious. Thank you Dr. McBride!

Professor McBride expects students to work for their grades, but his teaching style is so fluid and involving that it's easy to keep up and in the know. He has prepared notes that require attendance and attention to complete. If you go to class you will learn, you will get a good grade, and you will love this professor.
Great professor. Knows what he is talking about

You wont find a better teacher than Dr. Mcbride, he will literally help you as much as he possibly can with any subject, ranging from calc, physics, thermodynamics and many more, u have questions; hes gonna be the one to likely have your answers.

McBride is absolutely amazing. A real straight shooter and more than happy to help anyone with any engineering subject to the best of his abilities, of which are extensive. As to the comment below, I refuse to excuse any professors lack of teaching ability because they are doing research alongside teaching the course. I pay too much money for that.
Awesome teacher, very clear and lets you know exactly want he wants. He is a very good blend of humorous and strict.  Wish I could take him for more of my classes. Highly recommend for any subject.

The greatest teacher I've ever had.  He tends to be critical of stupidity, but you can't blame him.  He teaches in a way that lets even the most dense students learn with ease, and the real world experiences he brings to the classroom are priceless.

If he is the sole reason you are still in engineering school, then maybe you should be somewhere else. If you are having problems arelady with strength of materials or thermo, you will be harmful once you get a job. He once tried to help me with my homework at the library for a class he didnt teach and he was clueless.

Took this class and didnt get much out of it. He just did different types of problems, but no indepth theory of anything. His knowledge is limited to undergrad classes. 710 should be considered an undergrad class. He very helpful to students for sure, but please, dont compare other professors with him , he doesnt do research and has a lot fre time

If you are an engineer you need to get to know this teacher, he is the most dedicated professor i have ever encountered. he is the sole reason i have made it this far in engineering. i recommend that you find out what classes he has study sessions for and go to them. also he is always there to help you with any engineering related work.
amazing

McBride is the BEST. Hands down the most helpful professor you will ever meet. Has reviews in just about every class you could take, and if he doesnt have a review he would probably sit down and explain it to you with ease. Tests follow what he teaches, unlike a lot of professors.

McBride is the sole reason I am still in engineering. He is the best teacher in the entire school, if not campus. This class is easy enough if you put the effort in-- there are no tricks, and McBride will prepare you very well.  He holds reviews for classes he doesn't teach-- I highly recommend going to them. If you can, take a class taught by him.
Best teacher ever. Period.

Hands down the best instructor I have come into contact with.  I only wish he taught all my classes.  He expects you to learn, and would probably lay in the middle of the street, if it helped you to learn.  He holds review sessions in courses he doesn't even teach, and even cracks a good joke in class occasionally.
Very good man.  All should take at least one class taught by him if possible.

McBride was one of the best teachers I ever had at KU.  He takes very difficult subjects and explains them in ways that are easy to understand.  He was a finalist for best teacher at KU.  His father was also a professor and was voted best teacher at KU.  I had McBride for Statistics and Structural Analysis and suggest you not take these classes from anyone but him because he is the best.
McBride just loves to help students no matter what class they're in.
McBride is amazing.  If you have any questions about any of your classes, he will help you with anything, because he's taught it all.

McBride is one of the best college professors around. He cares about the students' learning and that is all. His goal is to prepare students with real world topics before leaving college. Helps students with classes he isn't even currently teaching. It is to everyone's advantage to take his classes.

He is an awesome professor, will only teach suff that applies in the real world, even if that means skipping a chapter or couple of hard topics...he is really cool and spends a lot of time on students...and helps you on the homework.i would say he has an 10 out of 10 rating for motivation & teaching
Great prof; I wish there were more who cared as much as he does.  By the way, he teaches well too.

Professor Bowen is wonderful. I loved this class and def recommend it. You watch one film, read one reading, and do one little assignment each week. Bowen wants to see all his students succeed, so he is very helpful. His face literally lights up when he talks about Rome, so you can tell he loves what he teaches, which makes the class engaging.

Prof. Bowen is supportive, patient, and open to feedback. He is available to help and adapts his class to the level of his students instead of allowing us to either completely fail or be stuck learning things we already know. 100% would take again. Great prof. He's clearly passionate about teaching, super funny, and creates a great environment.
He was a good dude and is very intelligent and knows what he is talking about. I'm just salty that I tried hard and got my first ever B in his class.

I have had Prof. Bowen for most of my Italian classes at KU and I have to say he is one of my favorite Professors out there. He knows what he is doing and teaches extremely well. Participation is key, as well as reading his handouts to do well in tests and quizzes. Overall awesome classroom experience, he truly cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's just a really good Italian professor and probably my favorite teacher at KU

Professor Bowen is absolutely amazing! His classes are a bit reading intensive and he does expect you to participate, but I've never had a professor that cares more about about his students. He is truly passionate about the course topic and he comes to class not just to teach a curriculum, but also to inspire his students. I love him dearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Canda appears to be intimidating since he has over 100 publications and authored the text book. If you put in the effort and follow the directions of his assignments he is an easy grader. He puts the directions for assignments verbatim in his syllabus. His tests are generally curved and often lets you re-do them if the whole class did poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Good old Ed makes you read his book and then sit in a Korean drum circle or something at the end of class.  How he managed to swindle a university into accepting this b.s. as useful for social workers entering the field is inexplicable.  Grab the easy diversity credit and wish for more clinical classes.

Ed is like Clark Kent- a mild-mannered exterior that can fool students. Do NOT try to slip sloppy work past him. He has X-ray vision for bad writing! He's kind and really cares about students. It's well worth the effort to draw out his dry, sly sense of humor.
BORING. Not at all what I expected out of the class.

Best professor/mentor of my life.  i learned more from him than most other academic classes..can't think of another professor that was more awesome(i wasn't even a cello major, or in the music department)

if ever there were a professor where the phrase "what you put in is what you get out" applies, it would be Ed. If you don't care, he doesn't either, but if you do care, DON'T LET HIM THINK YOU DON'T.  Active learning is crucial, as is self-motivation in your practicing. He may be prone to ramble, but he also has a ton of useful info to share.
awesome
The man is brilliant.  I've learned more from him than probably anyone else in the department.
No Comments

He understands that most people in the class are not science majors. He tries to simplify complex subject matter. He is rather dry, but keeps you awake by integrating a lot of drawing with the notes. I had to buy colored pencils for the class, which is a plus. (: Hopefully you get a good TA, as they will teach part of the class.
Very smart but sometimes over my head. He is extremely nice and helpful if you ever have problems. I found 320 to be interesting, however, 660 was a little more difficult.

Prof. Auer is a very intelligent man and a great teacher.  He is also really helpful and has a nice sense of humor. Takes awhile to open up to the class, but is pretty funny once he does. I learned a lot from him.  Good class!

Very precise lectures. Lots of drawing pictures of brains and stuff. Mostly memorization and very interesting. Some people think he's monotone and dry but he makes jokes and I like dry humor like that. No homework except for occasion reading of this cool book that's a narrative about brain surgery and stuff.

One of the most challenging but rewarding classes I have taken. You have to be willing and able to dedicate lots of time and effort to the dense material or you will not do well. It's tough, but she will help you through it if you just reach out. Learned so much, with the kind of content that will stay with me for a long time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I thought she was an amazing professor. She was kind, quick at responding and gave great feedback. She is a tough grader, but as long as you read the material, or at least half read it, you will do just fine. Homework is open book, so it is quite easy. There is a lot of stuff to read though. She is very specific on what she wants in homework though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I had her for Global Environmental Literature online. I dropped after 3 weeks. It is an 8 week course, so it is designed to be hard, but she made it extremely difficult. I am a graduating senior and my 500-600 level capstone English courses were easier than this elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the best professors I have had. Will dearly miss her!

Dr. Egan shows that she cares a lot about the success of her students! Some of the content is very complex, but the exam and quiz questions are derived from the lectures-no surprises! You will need to study and memorize a lot, but it's perfectly doable. She also sent out reminders about quiz due dates. I highly recommend her for BIOL518 and 519!

BIOL519 wasn't an available option so this will have to do.
Good as it gets. Easy to understand rubrics, lots of variety in the course material, and an approachable professor.
Teacher does not give clear instructions and does not answer emails. Difficult assignments. Poor directions. Very unclear on what she expects. Extremely difficult tests.
Really good teacher.

Has notes posted on Bb but you have to go to class to fill them out. Tests are relatively easy if you study and go to class. She was very helpful during office hours too! I had no interest in the material, but I learned quite a bit from this class. Never used the textbook.
Very organised, friendly and approachable. Provides great lecture notes AND review slides prior to tests. But you still have to go to class.

Dr. Egan was useless and rude.  I went to speak to her regarding my grade and she showed no remorse and offered no real help.  TAs were nonexistent for the lecture and Egan was the main reason I despised that class.
Hard class but very useful.  Links Microbiology and Genetics.  She is very thorough and well educated.  I suggest NEVER skipping class if you want to pass! Many test questions will come from lecture.
Test are hard but they are a mix of questions that allow you to do well if you know the material.  Very friendly and explains things very clearly.

I liked Professor nutting as a person fr but as a teacher not so much I wish she had just taken the time to explain things it all felt vague and she gave bad grades when it wasn't up to her standards when she just didn't take the time to explain what she wants from you when you answer questions :/
Worst professor I have ever encountered at the University. Truly regret wasting my time in her course.
Only gives an hour for office hours. Rude, dismissive, and holier than thou. Gave boring longgg lectures and made no sense during them. Wants to hear you tell her her own thoughts, not your own.

She is nice and is friendly to students, but the material itself is very convoluted. She was tough with the content/grading but was very passionate. For an intro philosophy class things were graded very harshly. She'd maybe be better suited to a higher level course. Prepare to go to office hours, but she's willing to help you out if you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: there aren't a lot of assignments, so every grade weighs heavy. I think we wrote 10 assignments the whole semester. she's very caring, but I think it is just a hard course to understand. She does help with assignments if you go to office hours so that's good. it is not a class you can study for so she'll be your only source of help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy to not go to class and still do good in the class because nothing in the lectures was really in the assignments.

Professor Nutting was an awkward lecturer who failed to inspire any interest in her topic. She often felt out of place instructing an introductory philosophy course and would be better suited towards higher level instruction. I would not recommend taking her unless there are no other options.

This is the best professor I have ever had, and I mean that. Eileen Nutting is the ideal of what it means to be a philosopher. On a personal level, she is very kind and caring. When lecturing, she does a thorough job at breaking down philosophical concepts. She is humble, and open to any comments, criticisms, or suggestions. Take her! -David T.

I was pretty nervous about this course as your grade relies on essay grades, but it was much easier than I thought! There are a lot of opportunities to have her or your TA check over your work before turning it in, and if you take advantage of that you will do well in this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures give you the bare minimum information, but homework requires an advanced mastery of the subject. Often times her feedback leaves me more confused than when I started. And she's an excessively pedantic grader - the smallest "wrong" word choice will cost you massive points. This is an undergrad philosophy class, not a research paper review!

She is literally one of the only people in the US who know this form of logic. very clear and organized. makes the course easy.

While it's easy to coast through and get an A, you can also learn a lot in this class if you put the time in. I recommend Dr. Rauscher.

Great teacher!! Very interesting class. I learned a lot. I wasn't sure what to expect, but was very happy with the class. You have a choice to write three small papers or one long paper in addition to two tests that you are allowed to bring notes to. Highly recommend anything with this teacher.

She was a good teacher.  The class wasn't too difficult, but I learned a lot.  Most of her lecture is from a powerpoint so it isn't difficult to take notes either.  Average amount of reading.  3 small papers or 1 large one...your choice.

Worst professor in the b school. Has taken a global marketing class and turned it into a writing class and grades extremely harsh. She is more worried about writing skills than students actually learning concepts. Do not recommend.
Absolutely 1/10 professor. Needs to be removed and reprimanded. For her grading, this is not a comp class; grade understanding of concepts, not formatting.

reviews.comment: I did alternative EC assignments, receiving full points all semester until the last week of school. Don't listen to these other people. Emma rules. Great teacher.

Emma is a very bad teacher. I normally don't think teachers are bad but she truly is. She yells at her students and just laughs and yells at us when we fail or don't pass her tests. The homework assignments are super long and time consuming. Her slides were not helpful at all and she only gave us a study guide for the tests after we begged her to.

Its outstanding the school still pays her. she just regurgitates the online textbook. Assigns homework to the point its mind numbing busy work. her lectures kill brain cells there so boring and unless. she's like the KGB when it comes to the no phone, food, or drink policy. She refuses to give a study guide. She hates students.

While Emma doesn't have control over the curriculum, she does have control over her personal attitude, which, for the majority of the time, was negative. From rants about no phones every class to not giving us review material due to past classes' behavior, just overall not good.
Absolutely terrible. Is happy when students fail like it's an I told you so moment. Is really miserable to be around.

The content is not that difficult, but the lectures are not very engaging and she disrupts her own class by constantly calling out students for being on their phone. The homework consists of >50 concept SmartBooks. Most students failed the first exam, for which she only took slight blame for but did attempt to be better the rest of the semester.

reviews.comment: I did not find this to be a difficult class but Emma made it almost impossible to feel appreciated and respected as an adult and student. reviews.comment: All the other comments are right. She is horrible and not fun to be around.

Worst class I've taken at KU. I've never seen students perform so poorly on a test and then be blamed for the low average. When half the class fails, it shows it's not on the students. She seemed more focused on making an example of someone than actually helping them learn. I would not recommend this course to anyone.

She is the worst teacher I have ever had at KU. Treats her students like children and has no respect for her classes. She does not know how to teach and fails to understand what actually helps students learn.

I've never had more anxiety walking into a class. She cold calls on students to embarrass them. She also doesn't listen to any feedback from students and blames them for failing grades. Doesn't make any changes after hearing and seeing affects of exams. Crazy regarding food and phones, but the TAs (Joe) are great!

Emma is the worst teacher I have ever had in my college career. She talks down to students and finds joy in embarrassing people. The amount of tension and anxiety she is able to create in a classroom is crazy, all while all of her students are constantly failing her tests. She screams at us for anything and everything .

Emma just sucks all the energy out of the room. Starts off class with a horrible tone like she doesn't want to be teaching. The homework is just busywork and the tests absolutely blindside you. Got defensive when the class failed and said “when I was in school we just had to study”. She thinks she's generous for posting “notes” slides.

I thought that the course was not nearly as difficult as many made it out to be. With all the extra credit, I found the class to be challenging but not impossible to achieve an A. I thought she was very easy to communicate with via email and spent time with me going over my exam and ways to be successful in the course.

Horrible professor with a horrible attitude every class. Extremely bad at teaching if you look around the class 95% of students arent paying attention and no one finds what she's saying interesting in the slightest. She also finds joy in making students sad for some reason which was said from her ta.

Easily one of the worst professors I've ever had at KU. She's less focused on teaching and more on policing whether someone dared to sip anything other than water, like we're in some kind of hydration boot camp. She somehow requires two SmartBooks a week with 60+ concepts. Unless you enjoy academic suffering as a hobby, I would not recommend.

If you ever need to take a marketing class at the business school, please look somewhere else. Professor Sittenauer could not be a worse teacher. Didn't provide a study guide, students failed. Provided a "Study guide" students failed. What is the constant in that? Her teaching. Quite possibly the worst teacher I have ever had.

Can't teach at all. Out of 200 kids only 5 got a A on an exam and 60% failed. She relies on McGraw hill to teach you everything which is extremely boring. Very odd person using frog memes and says attendance is not mandatory but has pop quizzes and in class assignments. She is an embarrassment to KU and does not care for her students.

The class is not actually that hard, and she is flexible with you when problems arise. However, she cares much more about phones and kids eating in class than about making sure her students understand the information. She threatens the class with "teaching out of the textbook" instead of her slides. Her slides are the same thing plus frog memes.

Terrible. Spends more time policing phones than actually teaching the class. She is looking to fail students rather than help them learn. The class average for exam 1 was D-, with over 50% getting an F and less than 3% getting an A or A-. She blamed this on phones and people not caring about marketing, but truly, it comes down to her not teaching.

Emma really is a great person, but I cannot say the same thing in regard to her teaching. She is very disorganized and yells at the class almost every day about being on their phones or not answering her questions. If you can take the course with someone else, I highly suggest you do.

I mean she's fine, I think it's completely valid to not want students to be on their phones, she's just a bit extra in this regard. Exams are pretty ok if you just grind out the McGraw hill stuff. From a purely classwork perpspective, this class is pretty easy, people must be braindead with how much they complain about it.

This is easily the worst instructor I've had in my three years at the KU. She constantly interrupts herself to enforce small, unnecessary rules, which completely derails class. She's more focused on catching students doing something wrong than actually teaching the subject. Her obsession with control over tiny details makes class uncomfortable.
kicked someone out of the lecture for being on their phone.

Professor seems to solely focus on phones majority of lectures. She fails to teach course material that is on the exams and speaks in a constant condescending manner. Average class grades are failing and blames students for the test scores.

Professor does not care about students. She does not give any materials from class to study because she believes she works to hard on them to give them to us. Make that make sense! Along with that she only uses McGraw hill for HW.

I have never had a professor like Professor Sittenauer. Every lecture is hard to sit through as she brings up having no phones or food in class every 15 minutes. Then we rush through the last few slides because 10% of the class time is taken up by these inconveniences. The one takeaway from this class is you'll learn more from the guest speaker.

Missed 1 hw
Got B's on 2/3 exams. Final exam @ 102%
She did not give me full credit for the research credits (something didn't register) and I couldn't prove I attended them. Tried pushing for the correction of this, but she wouldn't budge.
Now had an 89% in the class for a final grade. 
Asked if she could round my grade to an A. She said no.

Controls more then tried to teach. Such a painful lecture to sit through. Will literally stop a lecture and wait in silence (in a lecture hall btw) for someone to put their phone away. Exams were nothing like what she told us to study and half the class failed before getting a curve. Formatted like a high school course save yourself the pain.

Terrible experience. She constantly calls students out in front of class and acts condescending. Says tests come from SmartBook but they don't. Everyone did poorly and she blamed us instead of helping. No study guides or structure at all. Avoid if you actually want to learn.
Terrible at her job

We had a guest speaker the other day, and while he was very engaging and interesting you couldn't even pay attention because she was climbing over seats and pacing the classroom to find who was on their phone, even crouching on the ground at one point. Overall making it extremely hard to pay attention. She needs to get her priorities straight.

Strict, treats students like kids, obsessed with phones (deducts points, complains 10+ mins each class), rude call-outs, excessive busywork, more focused on control than teaching, with a know-it-all, disconnected attitude.

Worst teacher i have ever had at my time at KU. She once asked us to raise our hands if our parents were divorced and constantly treats us like we are in highschool. She will call you out in front of huge lectures if she sees you not paying attention or on your phone. DO NOT TAKE HER. Test are also very hard and she gives you nothing to study with.

Treats you like middle schoolers, and she complains about her students in every class. Constantly yells at people to put their phones away in an intro class where half the people don't care to be here. I definitely don't recommend taking this class with her.

reviews.comment: Becomes obsessed with controlling the classroom to the point where it detracts from learning. Her grading is completely random. Lectures feel unstructured and made up along the way. Treats students like children.

Has no real sense of connection with students, gives very large amounts of busy work. Created a disconnect between the students, herself, and class material through her stale humor and "know it all" attitude and tone. Speaks to the class during lectures like we are in middle school, and overall does not make the class enjoyable in the slightest.
grading criteria is a mess take this with anyone else

Emma gets such bad feedback for no reason. She tries her best to keep her lectures engaging and relate to students. For MKTG 440, her exams are take home and there is one final project. She really is nice, understanding, and trying to better herself as a professor. Take her for yourself and you'll see she isn't even bad or mean.

She doesn't give clear outlines for the grading of the exams or projects which account for most of the grade in the class. She seems to grade differently depending on how much she likes you. She waits months to grade assignments so when you get a horrible grade there is no opportunity to make up points. I would not recommend taking her class.
I highly recommend you do anything in your power to avoid taking a course with this professor. The way she grades defies all logic and her classes are more interesting than watching paint dry.

Little to no homework, grades are dependent on take home tests and group projects. Opportunities for extra-credit in class and her lectures are easy to understand. I will say that other reviews saying Emma humiliates people are extremely exaggerated, if you say you don't know the answer she just moves on like any other professor.

Took MKTG 440 and it was one of the easiest classes I have taken. This class has no homework, two group projects, and two open-note, take-home exams. Participation is required, but showing up and not using phones obviously will earn points. No late work is accepted, but even with earning a 0 on my first midterm I got a B. Not hard to pass.

This is the worst professor I have had in the bschool. The fact that our hiring staff saw this person and decided to hire her is appalling. She is incredibly disorganized and does not know the first thing about teaching. 

I would stay away from Emma and her horribly cringy humor.

Emma was extremely disorganized and often seemed to make up lectures as she went. She tries to relate to students with awful humor. More than half of the class had an issue submitting a major assignment, but she refused to accommodate anyone, which resulted in everyone's grade dropping by a letter.

This is by far one of the worst people I have ever interacted with.This lady should never teach another class.The fact that Ku hired somebody with such little personal skills is truly disturbing to me. I have never felt more degraded than I did when interacting with this teacher. I find it hard to believe this lady has any qualifications to teach.
Horrible teacher! Created very hard exams and did not give us good things to study

She was not rude, it is distracting, and college students should not need to be treated like children and told not to talk during class. That is a review on them, not Emma.

She gave us horrible review content majority of the time, took forever to respond to emails, and took time out of class to act like a child and mock her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Going to class felt like a chore compared to my other classes. She had no respect for her students and would take long periods of time to humiliate a student for not knowing the answer or because they slightly interrupted, it took away from everyone else's learning. Take any other professor if you are able to because you'll enjoy the course more.

Emma was funny and engaging during lectures. Participation/attendance is a large part of your grade. There is little to no homework, just two tests and a couple of papers for group projects. She offers extra credit many times throughout the semester through easy in-class exercises. Truly a down-to-earth professor and person, I highly recommend her!

Terrible lecture with bad humor. Tries to humiliate students in her class when they are not paying enough attention or get a question wrong. Does not provide any clear materials for her exams, giving out a list of broad topics for a 100 question exam that every troubled to finish in time.

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed MKTG 440 with Emma. Participation is a large part of your grade; just showing up isn't enough. Her lectures are very easy to follow/understand. There are no assignments, just projects, exams, & attendance. She is inconsistent with grading, but she is bound to improve as she gains experience & a TA. Loved her class & content!

reviews.comment: I love her, one of my favorites.

She's a new professor and takes feedback well. After students requested it, she shortened the exam from 100 to 50 questions. She offers a lot of extra credit. Provides poor review materials. Lectures are straight yap and are completely not interactive. Immature and treats the class poorly. find a different teacher

reviews.comment: Worst teacher. Although she makes a lot of mistakes, is unorganized, never grades anything not even just simply putting in attendance, she still doesn't give grace on assignments or exams (tough grader). Super rude and her tone is condescending. She often calls people out, and does not care about the students success. She makes me dread the class.

This class feels impossible—like being a guinea pig in a teaching experiment. The professor is clearly figuring out how to do her job, and the students are the ones suffering. If you get this professor, drop the course and wait; it'll save you so much time and unnecessary stress.

At the beginning of semester she was by far the worst teacher I ever had in my life but at this point in November she's starting to make changes and it's getting better but by far the worse class I've taken for 300 level corses at KU.

She's a tough grader. Her exams take up to 4 hours to complete even though there are 4-5 questions. She relies heavily on participation, be prepare to speak often and if you don't.. don't worry she will call you out in front of the whole class. She's always unprepared for class and takes forever to put in grades. Do yourself a favor and avoid her.

Awful professor makes getting an A in the class harder than getting a hobo off a ham sandwich. Exams are difficult, first exam the class average was a 75% which is pretty significant for a MKTG class. The main problem is there is no structure around the exams and in a college class exams are the most important. Take a different professor.

She is a new teacher who at first seemed a little overwhelmed, but over the course of the semester, she has gotten much better. I will say she is a tough grader, and the hw assignments take a really long time. If you attend class and study for the test you will do just fine. Her lectures are good, and she seems like a nice person.
non-organized and poorly prepared for class/ test prepping. Tests are overworded and completely pointless to what is learned in the class.

I have never submitted a review here before but I honestly can't even believe this class is real. If you missed the days of elementary school you'll love this class. She stops class everyday for the most ridiculous reasons and seems to care more about student obedience than teaching. Just save yourself the trouble and take this with someone else.

She's a power hungry dictator, who will belittle and yell at people for whispering, eating food in class or any other minor indiscretion. She screwed up the first test so bad, she had us fill out a survey to grade how bad she did, and then hired more TA's and changed the test afterwards. By FAR the worst professor I've had at KU. reviews.comment: She is pretty good. Kind of a tough grader but was constructive. The hardest project so far was the statement of belief essay.
