reviews.comment: She was a great teacher, and provided great feedback on papers. She was slightly scatter-brained when she spoke to us, so sometimes the point didn't really come across. Sometimes the rubrics and projects were very vague, but she is more than happy to answer any questions you ask if you push for them.

This was my second time taking the class and it was over the summer. Te first time, I got a D. This time I got an A. Tom actually made me WANT to go to class. He has a sense of humor and was easy to get along with. He is rediculously smart, but occasionally gets confused with some simple math. He is willing to explain things until you get them.
Good grad teacher

Tom is awesome...sweater thursdays kick butt, ask him about it, he'll know.  He is very knowledgeable and you can usually talk him into extra credit for attendance.  He knows what he is talking about and is very awkward. By far the best TA teaching calc, if you have a choice choose tom...he will be awesome.

Tom Enkosky is AWESOME!  He is absolutely hilarious and makes you want to come to Calc class.  He can tell when the class is bored so he moves on which keeps lectures from getting to bogged down.  He is pretty awkward, but that just makes class more entertaining.

Tom's an extremely awkward but nice guy. He doesn't explain what he does or why he does it so don't take him unless you've had the material before. THe homework and tests are extremely easy but dont prepare you for the common midterm and final which are incredibly hard compared to the tests in Tom's class. He's a nice guy but can't explain well.
He's awkward and struggles with algebra, but he's wicked-smart with calculus and a total sweetiepie.
TOM IS AWESOME
a very helpful and sweet teacher
No Comments
Tom's lectures are confusing.. your better off reading the book and teaching yourself. But he is very helpful, i got help from him during office hours and he let us stay as long as we wanted
Tom is a really helpful guy, but his explanations and lectures are ridiclus. He is very helpful and easy, but his teaching sux

Dr. Esch is an excellent lecturer who makes all things history and culture interesting. While there can be a lot of reading at times, the reading is all easy to get through if you are ready to read at a college level. Participation in the course makes the class so much fun, and the GTAs are generally very helpful.

Easiest A I've ever gotten. She was honestly quite rude to students in lecture and very unorganized. The hardest thing you had to do in this class is write one paper. I studied for 2 hours for the final and got a 95% or something. Just go to lecture and attend the discussions. Easiest A you will ever have in your life.

she was very unorganized and frequently got off topic during class. she took pride in reprimanding students in the lecture hall for being on their computers or looking at their friends??? she was very rude and her lectures did not explain much in my opinion. the beginning of the semester had a lot of basic history, the class itself is quite simple.

This professor has no respect for you or your time. She will claim you have a test and then, in that class, claim she just said that so more people would show up, not only did this happen once it happens multiple times.she is also very unorganized.

she is so unprofessional. i needed to miss a test and i kindly emailed her to see what we can do about it as i know it is required and she reprimands me about how its required and that i shouldnt present it as a fact but as a conflict? the fact is theres a conflict. esch gets off topic and never actually teaches but stands and yells at students.
She will call you out in class for stupid things like going on ur computer and call you out in a lecture hall

reviews.comment: Dr. Esch is a fantastic professor. You can learn everything you need to know and more if you show up, listen, and read the assigned materials. Can not recommend her enough!

Professor Esch is a very nice person, but she's not a very good professor. She is very disorganized and is constantly chaning due dates and the grade breakdown which messes up plans for breaks and just makes it overall very difficult to get things done/know what you're graded on. To be fair I think problems come from the GTAs too.

She's a very intelligent, caring, and passionate professor. It's easy to tell that she cares about the well-being of her students and puts a lot of thought into their experience. Her lectures are engaging and interesting. I also know that she will do anything for a student who participates and asks for help. She's great!

Professor Esch is very nice, but also very disorganized. She does not understand how to use canvas, when turning in assignments, she loses them even though they are online. She assigns 50+ pages of historical text/speeches to read for discussion which is honestly painful. She always says that class will get over quick but then goes over the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Esch may be a nice lady, but I couldn't stand listening to her go on and on about topics that you learned in 6th Grade. Esch loves to pick on certain people in class as well. A friend of mine who finished the semester with a 99%, was constantly called out in lecture for being on his phone or computer while people near him were doing the same.

Dr. Esch was honestly a fantastic professor and I certainly hope to have more of her classes in the future! She really cares about the material and it helped me out a lot. So much so that I am now majoring in American Studies.

Her lectures aren't organized, which makes them drag on and super boring. She takes attendance 4 times randomly throughout the semester. Offers a ton of extra credit opportunities, and homework is only readings for discussion. 2 papers, midterm and final.

I am writing this many years after I have taken Elise's classes because I remember her so favorably. Elise was a kind and knowledgeable professor. She really challenged me to think outside the box and I learned a lot from her. I took many classes from her in my undergrad because I always had such a great time while learning too.
She is an awesome lecturer, highly recommend taking wgss courses with her!

Elise was such a joy to have, and I made sure to have her next semester also! The topics that she teaches about are very heavy and nuanced, but she ensures that it's all very accessible. She's an easy grader, and doesn't point out or take off any/many points for typos or grammar mistakes. You can tell everything in the class was carefully curated

I had Elise during COVID-19 & she was great before & after the transition to online learning. She's extremely understanding of people's situations and will do everything she can to help you succeed, both inside and outside of the class. She does have high expectations but gives detailed instructions. Her feedback is also constructive but nice
Professor Epp has created a very digestable learing enviroment during covid-19. one of the best professors that ive had at KU so far.
Epp is great, wish he taught more.

Epp's class was probably one of the best I have taken at KU, and made me want to minor in Public Administration. He doesn't require textbooks, but gives online articles to read before each class. In class writing assignments make up for a lot of the grade, and really helped my writing. Very helpful and incredibly knowledgeable.

Easily among the most interesting and useful courses I've taken in my time at KU. Keep in mind the Crime and Punishment course is specifically centered around racial disparities in crime and punishment, which should be a mandatory PUAD class in my opinion. Chuck is super knowledgeable and inspirational. I would take this class again and again!
If you do not take a course with this professor, you are doing yourself a disservice. This is an all around exemplary professor.

Took him for crime and punishment. Very interesting class with great lectures. Class was always finished early. Very passionate and helpful professor. I would take him again. Also, does not require purchase of a textbook!

I loved him as a teacher. You can tell he loves the subject that he teaches and knows his information thoroughly. He is extremely helpful and wants all of his students to succeed in class. He helps you understand material and assists you on papers as much as you need. Very nice man!

Dr. Epstein is definitely one of my favorite teachers I've had at KU. Econ 535 was a tough class because there was a lot of content covered. I ended up getting an A, but was very unsure about my grade the entire semester. I would definitely recommend taking his class because you learn  lot, but get ready to read and write papers often.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Epstein is knowledgeable and hilarious. He comes across snarky, but he's kind and patient. Don't be afraid to visit his office for help. The class was easy. No essays. Just two tests. Attendance is a must; it accounts for 1/3 of your grade. Just show up, take notes and his tests are easy. But if you skip class, your inevitable F is on you.
No homework except for a few papers.  Midterm and Final are blue book essays and pretty much determine your grade.
I enjoyed his lectures very much. Could drag a bit at times, but interesting for the most part. He is extremely smart and approachable. Funny and makes you study for the tests.
Fantastic professor who gives amazing lectures. Highly recommended.

reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor thrives off of throwing curveballs and failing his students. Does not appear to care if students understand the content or not, very apathetic toward learning. For a lab class, most of the grades come from a 30 minute lecture. You are not graded on skill but rather on luck. Unfair and uninteresting course. Do not take it if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was his first year teaching genetics lab, and it went okay. The labs and lab TAs were great but the once a week discussions were boring. Erik is a boring lecturer and his quizzes are super specific to the powerpoints. Its an easy A if you study the powerpoints right before each quiz and go to every lab, just be prepared for a boring lecture.

Dr. Lundquist is lovely, he guides you through the ppt and stressed on things important and filters out non important stuff on the exam. He tells you what things likes to test on, also provides practice exam. Totally recommend!

The class has no cushion. There is no homework, participation, extra credit, no curving, ONLY 5 tests. If you don't figure out a good way to study for them you'll have a hard time. They are all multiple choice but questions can be tricky. No study guides either.
Big NO. Too much material and exams are almost designed to not give you full points. Moreover, there are no drop exams and if you don't find old exams good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Lundquist is fantastic. Lectures help with understanding the material. While the subject is difficult and conceptual, his exams are extremely fair. They emphasize understanding rather than memorizing, which is very good. Exams are slide-based with multiple choice matching questions. He does provide practice exams.

Dr. Lundquist is one of the most engaging professors I ever had. He is very clear and thorough in his explanations and emanates approachability. Study his PowerPoints, making sure you understand big trends, and you will do fine!

Easy tests, just study and review old tests.  Boring as heck ppts.  I did not attend one class since test number two and test three and four were my best tests.  Study ppts, review tests, and you will do well.  Very weird test format but it's beneficially weird.
interesting class, great professor. study the practice exams!!! oh yeah, hot and spicy TA that always came to class too so that's a plus. DEFINITELY RECOMMEND!!

Nice guy in class, but a total jerk outside of class. Too busy with his worthless research to communicate with students. Delegates office hours to his dullard GTA. Weird test format; way too much information. I'd recommend avoiding him, but I doubt the alternative is much better.
I really like him. He definitely knows his stuff. The material was really interesting, but the tests were not easy. They were fair, though. I would take from him again if I had the opportunity.

He's a good guy. His slides tend to start very specific and then gives you the big picture so it's hard to understand sometimes. Definitely need to go through the notes twice at least. Study old tests to understand format because it's weird. Overall, fair, but difficult to adjust from normal test format.

Best ever... awesome power point notes that you won't even need to use the textbook. Exams are directly from his notes and very fair. his practice exams before each test are very helpful and many of the test question are directly from the practice tests. Ave is usually about 84 after each test. Class is hard thought, u HAVE TO STUDY. He is lovely,

Good instructor; seems like a nice guy; not a very interesting delivery. Covers HUGE amounts of material: 200+ PPT slides per exam.  Not an easy class just because of the shear volume of info. Format of exam questions is a little confusing.

a good teacher considering the complexity of the course. i knew this class was going to be basically genetics 2, so i'm glad that he has made the concepts seem less difficult. he takes his time explaining and repeats himself often so everyone understands. not the funniest professor i've ever had, but hey, it's developmental biology.

Great professor and great class!!  If you go to lectures and study his notes, it's not hard to get an A.  I recommend printing off his lecture slides and taking notes on them in class.  He takes test questions solely from his notes, so don't worry too much about the book.
No Comments

Unless you have last years exams, you will get a D on the exams. This class is hyperspecific, and he does nothing to help you. You are drowning and he watches you with a lifesaver, refusing to throw it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No matter how hard you study you will fail and he is fully aware of that and showed no concern when the class average was failing. His exams are hyperspecific on topics that he would brush over in class so the only way to pass is to memorize the book. no empathy for students when they had major life events occuring.

Professor uses an odd grading system for no particular reason. Although I somehow got an A in the class I averaged C's on all the exams which leads me to believe I don't actually know the info and won't be able to use it on later things. The professor doesn't care about failing test averages and a struggling majority of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The only pro to Holmstrom is that he responds quickly to emails. The exams are written like they're purposely intended for students to fail and basically no feedback is given afterwards for what you did incorrectly. So much of his class was struggling greatly and he did nothing to alter the class for the students' benefit or to provide more help.

Holmstrom is nice but a nightmare as a professor. His exams are poorly worded (he even admits it), yet every question still counts. He doesn't prepare students or give answer keys or feedback. Unless you read and memorize the whole textbook, the exam questions feel completely random. Godspeed to everyone in the future.

This professor quote on quote said that if he were to take his own exams, he would not pass them. He grades very harshly and provides little to no guidance to help students prepare for his exams. He gives alot of extra credit, but thats only to balance out the grades for his low exam averages, which are like ~60 per exam. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives little to no resources to study for the exams, and all assignments besides his tests are just there to make sure you don't fail the course. He will dock points off test questions with no explanation as to why. All in all very frustrating and generally unhelpful. I'm also pretty sure he uses AI to write his exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor does not care about students obviously struggling. Exam averages would be failing and nothing would be done.

He is generally polite & I haven't had any interpersonal issues. However, the class relies heavily on textbook memorization. The questions that get put on exams are typically complicated, specific and obscure, often leaving me wondering "When in the world did we learn this?". There's not really a good way to study in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is very test-heavy. If you want an A, you need to read the textbook.

Dr. Holmstrom seems like a pretty nice guy, but wasn't the best teacher. This class covers a lot of content, and you need to read the textbook to succeed on the exams. His lectures weren't very engaging, and generally just served as an overview for the main concepts on exams. There is quite a bit of extra credit offered, which is a life saver.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Is not very welcoming toward his students. He's known for being rude. You could tell that he cared more about being at KU for research, rather than being a professor. The exams were often very difficult... there was a lot of content to learn and he often tested on small details.

One of the most difficult courses I have taken. Four exams and one final exam, although essay grading was pretty lenient, the info tested were so detailed. Holmstrom really helps you during office hours, and you can potentially get points back from exam scores. Only got an A because of my final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Def a very tough course! We covered a lot of content, the lectures just consisted of going over slides. We had an 4 exams and a final. Exams are not easy and reading the book helps a lot. Holmstrom is super smart and definitely knows what he is talking about, but the course content is difficult on its own

Dr. Holmstrom gave lectures that aligned with the textbook and he was very clear in his explanations. Though the class is test heavy, reading the textbook helps a lot and the exams are usually straight from the textbook and lecture slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures did not teach me anything. He never explained concepts, just summarized them. When asked what would be on the test, we were told anything in the book. The tests were extremely detailed and we were completely unprepared. Only got an A because they had to curve every test. Did not teach well for the level he expected us to comprehend.

This is one of the hardest classes I have ever taken at KU. Professor Holmstrom's exams are impossible!! The class grade on the exams was 58% and he does nothing to fix that. The exams were extremely hard short answers and too detailed multiple choice. It is a 2-hours exam where you need to write more than 14 short answers and 5 long answers!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: All of his lectures were prerecorded videos that he went through pretty quickly, so it was hard to pick up on things unless you paused every 30 seconds. I feel bad for the guy as it's his first semester teaching the class and he has to do it online. A lot of stuff on tests from the textbook. Had to curve all of our tests for people to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: if its in the book, its on the test
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I love this professor! Lectures were amazing!
The in class quizzes are hard and only three questions so they bring your grade down. Its a hard class to sit through cus theres not much going on.
Super easy class with engaging guest speakers and interesting lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very easy class. Pop quizzes were not my favorite, but you should do fine on most of them. Pre work was easy and manageable, lectures were boring but not bad. The midterm project was very easy as well, and your only assignments were lecture reflections. Erin is also an extremely sweet and caring person. Overall, not a bad freshman class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the easiest classes imaginable. There would be a podcast to listen to, maybe, a very easy quiz in class, and then a lecture about very basic (but necessary) parts of getting you started in the B-school. A resource-finding class, essentially. Erin is also so, so sweet and lovely. A little boring, but helpful for clueless freshies.

Erin is such a lovey person. There was pretty easy pre work every week, a 3 question pop quiz, and a weekly reflection. The midterm project was also extremely easy. Lectures were sometimes pretty boring, though, and doing bad on a couple quizzes can tank your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Same format for every class, do the pre work, take a quiz on the pre work, lecture, lecture reflection. Fun lectures full of debates. Interesting guest speakers. Kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The business topics could have been interesting but turned into 50-minute yap sessions each time. The instructor invited guest speakers to share their careers, some were good but others just rambled. , there were too many articles, podcasts, and videos for a 1 credit class, along with lengthy assignments. The group project is also a poor design.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Erin is super nice and very passionate about the lectures that she gives. The lectures are all repeats of the prework, which is easy work but ridiculously long for a 1-credit hour class. The main portion of the grades comes from pop quizzes but she covers everything on it. Opportunities for extra credit in the class. Easy class if you go
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class covered various business topics that were not very engaging. The instructor invited guest speakers to share their career journeys. Each week, there were too many articles, podcasts, and videos for a 1-credit course, along with lengthy assignments. The group project was also poorly organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is so great in BUS 110, and BUS 120. Watch out for pop quizzes in 110, but they are very easy.

Had to take BUS 120 my senior year. Outside of class work was over an hour of videos which she would repeat in class. She was very unresponsive to emails. Pop quizzes/participation is 1/2 the grade. Group project grading was not handled well when members did not participate. Not worth the money or time.

Pop quizzes are worth 40% of your final grade. Even though the quizzes are somewhat easy, the questions are weighted heavily so if you miss a couple you are kind of out of luck. I don't care what class it is... pop quizzes should not be worth 40% of a students final grade. It sucks this class is required to graduate from KU school of business.

Makes you watch hour long videos and podcasts and then repeats everything from the videos in person. Exams have nothing to do with the study guides. Sent out an announcement acknowledging how hard it was then curved like 2 questions. I paid attention all semester, studied excessively and still got a D on the final which is not typical for me.

If you email her, she will just direct you to a TA instead of helping you. Very easy class if you put in some effort  but very unfair grader when it comes to the group project. Did the whole thing on my own and my group members still got credit for it. Got told that I wouldn't get points docked for doing it yet group members still got credit. Crazy

Erin was a wonderful professor. Her lectures and guest speakers were interesting. The only issue was the exams. The content was extremely difficult compared to everything else and ended up hurting my grade. However, the homework was rather easy to do, even if it took an hour or two to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was a extreamly harsh grader, with no explanation, and very rude in all email responses. I have completed some of the hardest classes in the Bschool with higher grades than I finished this with. He graded a lot of the assignments the day before this class ended, giving me 5 Fs and no explanation, resulting in me failing this course.

I had a hard time getting useful feedback.  I frequently failed or almost failed most discussions, even after meeting all rubric guidelines. When I emailed for clarification I only got things like "expand more" or "cite sources" when we got no guideline on word length or anything about what sources he wanted us to use. Very unclear.

He is such a tough grader, I literally failed my introduction discussion board, even though I followed all of the instructions. He automatically takes points off if you turn it in the day it is due. I am literally one week into this class and will be dropping because I have never had a professor be this disorganized. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was the worst thing I could have ever done to myself. I truly wish Eric Ruth knew how bad and mean of a teacher he is. The fact KU still pays him to teach when he is mean is really sad. I'm upset I wasted money. He truly does not care about you, and you will get a bad grade if you don't answer to a T what he is looking for. KU needs help
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He told me that my writing was poor, and found something wrong with everything that I turned in and constantly took unnecessary points off. I have never gotten below an A in my life, however I somehow ended up with a D in his class???????? BOTTOM LINE, do not take one of his classes, or you are in for a semester full of confusion and frustration.

If I had one word for Rath, it would be inconsistent. There may be a rubric, but essentially what he expects is for you to spend HOURS crafting a tiny discussion response, and even then he grades based off of what side of the bed he woke up on that day. Do not casually take this class- if you're passionate about food history the work is worth it.

Worst class that I have ever taken at KU. I have taken numerous history classes and online 8 week courses. This is the hardest 100 level course I have ever taken from a professor and I took it my second semester of senior year. He is unclear with the requirements and expectations of the course and his grading changes by the minute.

The course is asynchronous, so interaction with Prof. Rath is minimal. Following his syllabus is crucial; he grades at a college level and expects ~3 quotations every assignment. 

You'll gain valuable insights into food history. Generous extra-credit options. Affordable textbook. Canvas discussions are very shallow. Writing feedback reliant on TA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment:
I am familiar with the gastronomy and history of food, so I was hoping this was an easy class. Outside of the materials, the assignments are time-consuming for a 100 class. The grading system is egregious. Many times, I would submit a discussion post and be docked 2-3 points for failure to cite more from the materials. 

Do not take this class.

Rath is a good guy. HIST 399 discussions are the easiest things to get max points in. The essays are unnecessarily long with vague prompts. Get ready to read a whole 200-300 page book in like 1-2 weeks two times for this class. Its a LOT of work. But Rath makes himself available for office hours to get feedback on essays and discussions.

Harsh grades/Unspoken rules: He will grade harsher in 399 if you dont turn in posts before EC date, though the stated due date is later. If he wants it on WED he should state it, not play grade games with EC. I enjoy professors who create a clear standard. This professor is the furthest thing from that. Good content, horrid expectations.
To say he is a harsh grader is and understatement. His grading standards are practically random.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am a senior who has taken lots of online classes and never have I taken one so frustrating and confusing as this 100 level class. He allows many chances for extra credit, but is unclear about how to get it. It seems as if the bar moves every single week. I have never hated a class as much as I did this one. I genuinely hated it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class itself wasn't too bad, but I did feel like Professor Rath (and/or his GTA) graded papers way too harshly. The good thing is you can take the weekly quizzes as many times as you want, and if you post to the discussion board early in the week you get extra credit, so it's easy to offset your papers scores and get a great grade overall.

Half a semester Sushi class sounds easy, right? Wrong. Sure, there isn't much work, but on his papers he is looking for one answer and if you don't answer the way he wants, he won't give you an A, no matter how good the paper was. He sent out a mean email about our papers too and how they sucked and we didn't understand the prompt.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Every week is clearly laid out, the end-of-week quizzes can be taken an infinite number of times, and as long as you at bare minimum gloss through the readings and participate in discussion you'll have an A with only 3 papers to write to determine your final grade. If 3 papers in 8 weeks sounds doable to you, an easy A. If not, take care here.
Rath is not a very good professor, the class was boring and he accused students of cheating on their papers. Do not take this class, just save yourself the time and energy.

The class was not as challenging as I expected, but there are several 10 page papers and hundreds of pages of assigned readings, but I did fine without completing all the readings. If the subject interests you, definitely take it. Professor Rath is very intelligent and a compelling lecturer. You work for your grade but he is very fair.

Do not take this class.  You may think to yourself while you're still in the sun of your vacation, "I can handle it."  You can't.  He is a great lecturer, but there will be no mercy, and there will be no compromise.  You don't need a challenge.  If you want a challenge, read "War & Peace".  But do not take HIST 399.

Although lectures were interesting, this is not a class most people should take. Everyone goes in thinking that their interest in the topic will be able to overcome the much stated harness on here, but that isn't true. The 2 assignments you have to do are unrelated to the testable material, and the tests are not focused at all. Don't take this.

This class was tough. But like other classes I've taken from Dr. Rath he made it extremely interesting and was very helpful. I feel like I benefited from taking this class in several ways because of how tough this class was. I would recommend it if you're interested, but for the love of god, don't take it to fulfill a requirement.
I just hated this class. Make no mistake a 600 level class is hard and it's a complicated subject. Unless you have a tremendous interest in Tibetan Buddhism, don't take this class.
Really good lectures and interesting choice of books to read.

not as difficult as others would say just come to class and do the homework. Papers were graded harshly by the TA. Samurai class was one of the best I've ever taken and Rath obviously loves the subject and knows a lot. Don't ask about Ninjas though.

Took the Samurai with him, he is a good teacher and is clear but it is a very hard class. You can't use computers in his class he will kick you out if you have your phone out, but besides him being a hard ass the class is cool and you learn a lot.

The test material is straight off of your notes from his powerpoints; if you study those you can do well on the them even though they're hard. If you suck at writing you will probably fail the two papers. His lectures are interesting and he knows his stuff, but doesn't seem great with people. If you so much as touch your phone he will kick you out.

I liked this class a lot, it's not easy, but whats expected of you is made very clear. I loved the books we were supposed to read, but i hated that we had to take notes by hand. Anyways, cool class, not easy, but worth it.

Great teacher. He puts on the syllabus and tells you the first day exactly what he expects and tells you to drop if you can't deal with it. People that don't like him are the idiots that don't want to do the work and didn't drop after hearing his expectations. Hard class, but interesting and he clearly enjoys teaching it which makes it better!
This was a challenging class but Rath made it very clear how to do well; go to class and take notes. Going to class was not hard...he keeps it entertaining.
Slide show intensive.  Very useful information and he does a recap at the beginning of each class for a refresher.
Absolutely the worst teacher that I have every had. Enough said. He gave me nightmares because he looks like the guy off of scanners.

Teacher is somewhat strict, but fair. He runs his classroom very well, and all the information is provided in the class, and in the text. If you do the work you will get a good grade in the class. His expectations are high, but not ridiculous. You will understand what kind of teacher he is by the first day.

A lot of people complain about this class but it is really interesting.  The lectures are very good and he knows the matieral.  Yes the papers are graded hard, but you have the assignment well in advance.  Also the midterm and the final were not to difficult as long as you studied and took good notes.  Not an easy A, but really interesting

An aloof nut, grading is only difficult because his paper assignments are vaguely worded over abstract topics, but are suppose to steer you towards a conclusion he has already reached. Independent thinkers not welcome. There are good teachers that are very tough on students, Rath is not one of them.

Dr. Rath is one of the most uncooperative, difficult people I've ever dealt with.  He is extremely dismissive and evasive when addressing students' questions (even outside class hours), writes easily misunderstood assignments and harbors HUGE expectations.  Overall impatient and frustrating to deal with

He may seem like a nice guy and a cool professor the first day or two, but he is not. In class he gets annoyed when people ask questions, and tries to answer them as quickly as possible to get rid of the question. Not helpful during office hours, either. When talking about my paper, he just told me to look at the syllabus and that was it. Bad class

NOT AN EASY A!!! If you think "The Samurai" sounds like a cool  and fun class, only take it if you would also want to if it were called "A very challenging and thorough history of all of Japan that sometimes mentions the Samurai" Very strict attendance policy - if you miss 4 classes you fail. Easily offended by students' behavior, high expectations
Not an easy A! Interesting but very tough grader. If you are looking to simply fulfill requirements look somewhere else. Rath is a good teacher, but certainly not an easy class.
Very hard grader and strictly by the book.   You will learn a lot, but the material just is not that interesting.  Look elsewhere if you are trying to fulfill your non-western major requirements.

Engaging lectures and interesting reading assignments.   One of the best classes I've ever taken.  Grading was fair.  He explained all the criteria, and if you submitted your paper ahead of the deadline, he looked it over and gave advice on how to improve it.  This class is definitely not an easy A, but you will learn a lot.

This course was different then I expected but it was pretty good, i learned alot about the samurai and japan.  The ta's were okay and I felt like grading was kinda hard, but they do help if you have questions.  The lectures are okay but the people and things you learn about are easy to confuse as they all sound the same.

The course is difficult in that the essay do require you to think a little outside of the box.  He is totally approachable if you go to his office hours and ask for help, especially on rough drafts.  He is a great lecture, I have had far worst in my life.  I am looking forward to his class next semester .
The class was not what i thought it would be and required lots of memorizing of things i do not care about.

He never really seemed approchable at all. A total jerk when it came to grading papers. I am pretty sure that the class average was a C/D on the two papers. I am a senior majoring in history and I never got below an A on a history paper and I got C's. His jokes are terrible. Doesn't seem to really care about the students, just about how great he is

He is an amazing profesor, if you ever get the opportunity to take one of his classes, DO IT! He is involved, cares a lot about his students and what they think, and also quite funny. Definitly one of the best professors i've ever had.

If you have even been thinking about taking a class taught by Miguel--do it! He is hilarious, easy-going and flexible. For Fall 2022, Spanish 428 there were weekly group projects/mini-presentations; 5 TalkAbroads, one group podcast and an interview with someone who speaks Spanish. It's an engaging class that lets you be creative!

One of the best teachers in the program, I am in his 428 class and think he is super fun and definitely cares about his students and makes going to class a joy, definitely my favorite class this semster.

I love Miguel! He is always patient if you are having any issues and is willing to work with you if needed. He makes class fun and is very kind and will never make you feel embarrassed if you are not confident in your Spanish yet. As for classwork most of it is done in class and most of the outside of classwork is preparation for the next class.

Miguel is an amazing instructor! He's engaging, funny, and takes the time to make sure we understand the reading. There is, however, quite a bit of reading to do, but most of it isn't super long, just difficult to understand at times. The whole class absolutely loved this guy!

This class is made interesting and the content made easy by this professor. He is willing to extend deadlines for the whole class. His office hours are the most useful hours I have ever used. He will bend over backwards to help you finish your homework (VHDL and written) so that you have a complete understanding and full grade. An excellent Prof.
Very difficult class content wise but he makes it a lot easier to understand. Very lenient with grading. He takes attendance but it is worth it to attend.

The lectures in this class were hard to follow for a non PhD student. Should teach more in depth of less topics to get better fundamentals. HW is in Vivado which I could not stand. All of my friends in this class got less than a 50% on the first midterm. He ended up curving the other exams, but not enough. Material is too difficult.

Avoid at all costs. The lectures don't match up at all with the homework or the labs which there is almost no resources for. If you go into office hours to ask for help he will mostly ask you why you weren't paying attention in lecture. He is a stickler for weird rules, and will care more about enforcement of rules than the learning of his students

you probably always going to waste 30% of the class time hearing him complain about unrelated stuff. The Midterm is miserable, didn't give us enough guide to review and time to finish. He acts like love to communicate to students, but in fact, he just can't stop lecturing why his style is so correct so that it is all you fault if things went wrong.

Dr. El-Araby seems more concerned about course policies than teaching the material. We often spend half of the class discussing things like why he absolutely will not accept late homework assignments or how much he dislikes people emailing him stupid questions. He is not very understanding when technology causes issues, even in today's world.
Material is difficult and the lecture is boring.

Despite being a very kind and caring professor, he is not very good at communicating information effectively. He has difficulty answering questions about homework and usually just does it for you. His lectures are required but entirely pointless. He's very quick and thorough in his email responses but that's about it.

Professor El-Araby is very nice guy. He was very helpful. All you have to do is start early with the homework and go to his office hours. He will help you finish it. Tests are hard, but you get lots of extra marks.

The class seemed like it was going to be impossible at first, but ended up working out fine. Super nice guy always looking to help the students. Provided various extensions and test graders were super lenient. Homework was awful though, especially if you aren't good with VHDL. Overall happy I took 645 with him after the final average was a 96%

This is by far the worst professor I've ever had. He has no ability to communicate with his students in a way that makes them feel like actual human beings, and when someone tries to bring up a question or concern, just forget about it.

The homework in this class was awful. On several occasions we spent in excess of 10-15 hours on it. While he did grant the class every extension we asked for, this could have been solved by not assigning such big assignments. He graded tests fairly, and was always willing to help with questions. Emails back quickly.

Dr. Frykholm is very kind and patient and I liked the material we went over in this course and the way she talks about it. The only reason I would caution people is because our grade is made up of very few assignments (which mostly didn't have due dates. As an ADHD student I felt a lack of structure) and she takes a long while to grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Phil 140 was a pretty fun class. Prof Frykholm is a very intellectual professor and it shows in her lectures. 2 exams 2 essays and 1 final. Phil 671 was also a fun class. LOTS of reading tho, about 20 pages before each class. you choose between writing six 2 page essays, or one 12 page essay and that's all you're graded on.
Lectures are not mandatory, but discussions are. There are's 2 papers (400-500 words), 2 midterms, and a final worth 20%. All exams are in person and require a blue book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the intro-level course wasn't uniquely engaging or exciting, Dr. Frykholm was a solid lecturer. There were interesting and engaging course materials complimenting lectures, but discussion over them was often surface-level.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, poor curriculum. Lectures made sense and taking notes was useful for tests. The main issue was that there were only 2 exams, 2 essays and 2 quizzes the whole course and they were graded poorly. Me and my peers believed we understood topics fairly well but still got low grades despite studying and reading all course material.

Course was set up terribly. There was 6 grades put in the entire semester (2 exams, 2 essays, 2 quizzes) and they were graded very harshly. Almost all the questions on tests were short/long answer and the questions were vague/confusing. Every question was graded as though it had to be right the correct answer word for word. Class average was ~75%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As someone else said, she treats her lecture class a lot like a discussion class. Otherwise there is alot of reading assigned in this class but you can just kinda gather the information you need by listening to her and the class discuss it during class lol. You're graded on very few things but they're pretty easy as well+ she takes forever to grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very obviously knowledgeable in philosophy, but sometimes had trouble generating momentum in lectures or explaining the concepts thoroughly. However, she rewarded participation a LOT and the minimal assignments you do aren't bad if you keep up on the reading. You will have no clue what's happening in lecture if you don't, and she'll know.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Inspirational, genius, respected.

A challenging but enjoyable class. Prof. Frykholm is very smart and does a really good job of explaining topics in lecture. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory, but she doesn't post notes online. Considerably challenging for an intro class. I wouldn't recommend this class if you have trouble with critical thinking, or don't enjoy reading philosophy.

Even though this class is meant to be a lecture, Professor Frykholm treats it as a discussion. There is a reading assignment before every class and most take a while to get through. She is an engaging professor, however, the grading system is not clear at all. We only got vague comments back and a letter grade on each one. A rubric would be nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: There is a reading for every class, and some of them are difficult to understand, but she usually explains them pretty well during lecture, and the material is interesting. There are only 2 papers and 2 tests, so you don't have a lot of assignments, but those 4 things each matter a lot. Gives a big, useful study guide for the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you like to question life this is the perfect class. Overall, the class was boring and not interesting.  There's not a lot of assignments so you better study for them. Before the final there is only 5 grades in the grade book. The midterm was only worth 35 points, yet the online quiz we took was 110 points. Doesn't make too much sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The tests are all straight from lecture. I didn't do a single required reading and got an A in the class solely by attendance and paying attention/taking notes to what she said. The discussions are very helpful. She also is very engaged and makes a large class feel small. Attendance isn't mandatory so either go or do the readings, you'll be good!

Dr. Frykholm is my favorite teacher I have ever had at KU.  The class is super interesting and she has a natural gift in being able to take hard material and breaking it down step by step to where anyone who takes the time to study and pay attention will learn it.  The only complaint I have is that I don't think she knows my name in a class of 30.
Not very helpful or engaging.

Easy-ish class that doesn't require a lot of time. Don't have to read any of the assignments - but still buy the book for the papers you have to write. Go to the lectures and take notes and you will do perfectly fine!

Don't bother doing any of the reading, as long as you take good notes and go to class you will be fine on the tests. I would use a computer for notes in her class instead of a notebook because she tends to move quickly

My favorite philosophy lecturer at KU so far.  Presented difficult material on metaphysics in a clear, understandable fashion.  Caused me to have a deep interest in Kant and certain topics in metaphysics and epistemology.

Write down everything she says and keep up with the readings and you should excell on the midterm/paper/final. She presents you w/material you need, you just need to use it..and try to stay awake in class lol. Go to office hours to check review ?'s!

Overall a decent professor. I found the class a little boring, but it's impossible to teach philosophy in an exciting way so it's not her fault. MUST do the readings if you want to do well. I failed the midterm but still got an A in the class, so she is a fair grader who takes improvement into account.

Maybe we just had her in different years, but I completely disagree with the comments below. She moves quickly, but she's extremely smart and presents the material very well. The class can be demanding but it's far from unreasonable. The readings also can be interesting too, I've had a good experience with her and the class altogether.

Erin was my favorite prof. this semester. She is not feminist at all like below reviews say. You can tell she knows what she's talking about and is very clear and always has an answer to a student's question. Just like with any class, the more you skip the worse you will do. I recommend the class if you are truly interested in philosophy.

This class will not be any easy A.  However, with an honest interest in philosophy and it's history, I found this course very rewarding.  Erin clearly has a firm grasp on the subject and (despite other reviews) tries to engage the entire class with topics of discussion.  Be sure to keep up with assigned readings though; the class moves quickly.

This class is pretty tough.  The concepts are very abstract and difficult to digest.  I would not recommend this as a first philosophy class.  She sort of rambles a lot and expects that the students understand texts that were written hundreds of years ago to make perfect sense. keep up with the readings and write down everything she says, get an A

Never, not once did we have an engaging class. Which, being in Wescoe, usually all have been classes where we discuss things with each other. Not here. Very feminist as well, she had us read 100s of pages that droned on about unrelated topics merely because they were written by females. Made me stop taking philosophy classes altogether.

I liked her at the beginning of the class, but the more comfortable I got with speaking my opinion, the less I liked her.  She wants you to think what she thinks, not to form your own opinion.  7 papers are assigned, but you drop your worst grade.  And you'll need it.  She grades very tough on the papers.  Learn to play her game.

She's nice, but expected us to teach most of calc 3  to ourselves by reading from a textbook. Gave us difficult but fun group projects, but made us use LateX & provided almost no guidance how to use it. For the hw/tests almost nothing from lecture is useful. Over-the-top weekly hw I couldn't do/mostly copied from Harvard's online math powerpoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Read the other reviews and do not agree with them at all. Her exams are related to homework, study guides and examples solved in class. She knows well what she is doing. Office hours are helpful. I would retake this class!!!

Not a good teacher.  She knows her stuff but doesn't teach it well. You must teach yourself from the book. "Acts" nice in class but when you go to her office hours she is argumentative for no reason and treats you like you're an idiot when you don't get the concept immediately.  Avoid if you can, terrible teacher.

This class was a lot of work.  She taught the class in a semi-graduate style, focusing a lot on theory at the beginning, but eased up a bit near the end.  She is very fun and energetic, and although it's tough, she's very fair.

Typically, you can have conflicting reviews on a professor. I took him at HCC and let me tell you,  there is absolutely NO denying of how bad of a teacher he is. Thank God I'm somewhat good in math because you can't expect him to help. He's sarcastic, rude, and a total scatter brain. 6 or 7 students withdrew after about a month. Do not take.

I'm sure I would have enjoyed the class if he seemed to care a little more. He forgot his notes the first few days of class, and didn't really seem interested in teaching. He was very aloof, though I think he intended it to be humorous. He was also kind of scatterbrained, going off on a topic for 20 min and then asking US where he got off track.
With out a doubt the worst teacher at KU. The textbook was unhelpful as was the teacher. Please avoid this professor at all cost. Teaches the class as if it were a grad. class.

This man is without a doubt the worst professor I've ever had in college.  He is extremely disrespectful to students and assigns work far beyond the scope of the class.  His class might as well be MATH 590 the way he teaches it. Many times he will move past entire sections for no reason at all.  Stay away from this man's classes at all costs.

Not a horribly challenging class, tests are easy. But overall I would recommend taking it with someone else though. He responds sarcastically and aggressively to even the most reasonable questions, the textbook we use is unhelpful, and he cancels class too often for no reason when we could really use some more instruction on the material.
Very poor teacher. Arrogant and just truly disrespectful.

This class was overly complicated and excessive in comparison to the same class taught by other teachers. MAterial was cover broadly and at a very high pace as if it was an honnors class. He was very sarcastic and assigns 4+ hours of homework weekly. No tests except final and midterm . A make it or break it style teacher (if you can call him that).

This man does not deserve being called a teacher! He is  unhelpful,irresponsible,irresponsive.About his personality, I can't believe he has any friend.Generally,he is the worst person in the university; he does not deserve be called a teacher.Two reasons for me to not drop class: 1.I can get an A without him; 2.I need to rate him in the evaluation.

William is really just not a very helpful professor at all. He assigns 4+ hours of homework each week for a 2 credit hour class and tries to cover way more material than other professors. He is very arrogant and will answer almost any question a student asks in class sarcastically and try to make them feel stupid. Try to avoid him.
Adapts to student needs, extremely patient and persistent with questions, emphasizes concepts before drilling applications. Can't recommend highly enough.

William is a different sort of guy. First class, he went on a 50 minute tangent about Leonhard Euler. You will most likely do poorly on the first exam, but that's when you find the key to his class... seeking extra help. Once you do that he is a great teacher, and engaging though different. He can be overwhelmingly smart, but a great teacher.

He's a really good teacher that challenges you. The hard work in his class is worth it when the mid term and the final come around. The test written by the department seem simple compared to his material and trust me its a good thing. ive never gotten a C in a class and learned so much.. you earn your letter grade in this class.
If you are willing to seek out his help and attend his office hours until you understand the concepts, you'll be okay.  He seems like a jerk at first, but he is actually really funny.

I dont think he is alful, but he is not the good teacher who helps us a lot. we need to study by ourselvs and tests are hard.I just got C last semester, I feel so bad about it since i dont think im an idoit in math.
He is the worst. He makes you feel like an idiot when you ask a question and is not helpful at all.
I don't know how people get to college and still expect other people to do their work for them.  Of course you have to learn calculus yourself.  Teachers are there to assist you.
Don't take this class if you can help it. It is very difficult and he talks to students like they should be experts at math, and treats you stupid when you don't understand.
The class is already difficult, but having William as your graduate student teacher is just awful.  He is completely unapproachable.  Awful Awful Awful.  Take it with Daniel Harnett he is awesome!

He doesn't care if students succeed or not. He purposely tries to make things seem difficult and harder than they seem. If you try and ask a question he makes you feel like an idiot for not knowing the answer already. I am warning you... DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!!!!!!!!
never answers emails or shows up for office hours, pretty much a self absorbed teacher.
This guy is an absolute moron.  Being in his class is like watching him practice math, while talking outloud to himself.
horrible
He is a horrible teacher. VERY UNREASONABLE AND MADE ME CRY! I had to drop calculus because of him. He doesn't teach you anything. Basically if you take this class you have to learn it yourself.
Always in his office, and willing to help.

Professor is okay, lectures are mostly just read off slides so if you can't come in don't sweat too much but he does give extra credit just for being in class some days. Discussion posts will make or break your grade, do NOT forget them. Would've ended with an A but I missed the final and his make ups are 2000 word mininum handwritten. No thanks

It's been a year since I took this class and I still think about Prof. Rankey every day, he was my favorite even though I know nothing about oceanography nor did I have an interest in it. The labs should be taken seriously, and the textbook questions were not required. He purposely made the class set up like a 100 level for guaranteed success!!

Labs are online, and multiple tries for half of them. The textbook is helpful for some test questions, but I passed without buying the textbook. The homework takes you like 30-90 minutes per week. He's a really nice guy, funny too. Lectures are posted online but certain things aren't. You get extra credit for attendance (sometimes).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Rankey is a very good guy and you can tell he cares about his students. He tries to make the lectures entertaining. Yet the labs are hard and 35% worth your grade. There was very random questions on the exam and no guide. It is difficult to do well on exams. Would have Rankey as a professor again but would not take this class.

This class would have been a lot better and funner if it were in-person. Each week consisted of reading the chapter, and then doing the homework, quiz, lab, and discussion board. All of these online materials cost over $200, which was annoying. I never interacted with Rankey except over email a couple times. Everything was automatically graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: i have tried  a bunch of teachers for this course, and Prof. Rankey was for sure the best. Thank you Mr. Rankey!
he is awesome!

Really nice guy. Lectures were entertaining and enjoyed the class. Work on the labs together because some of the answers are hard to get right. Hard to get an A in the class for some reason but content was easy enough.

Prof Rankey is the best! He makes class enjoyable and it never usually goes full time. The tests are easy if you study right and attendance is not mandatory. Definitely take it if you're needing an easy elective. Rankey is a funny guy, so that helps too!

This was a good decision of a class. The lectures match nicely with the text book chapters, all notes are online afterwards, and the text isn't a pain to read. The lectures are funny and have lots of graphics/images rather than just bullets and paragraphs. Rankey is a cool guy. He really doesn't want you to fail and wants you to enjoy the class.

Makes students submit 5/6 questions, releases a study guide comprised of all these questions then writes a mostly different test. The lectures are helpful but it was difficult to see their usefulness as the majority of homework grades weren't entered until the very last week w/no feedback. Pushed all responsibility/blame to his TA. Toilet humor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Take this class! Coming from a 6th year senior
Tries really hard to make the lectures entertaining. Has a great personality and the more class participation, the better.

Prof. Rankey is one of my favorite professors ever! His lectures were always relevant and insightful and included just enough silly humor to make them even more engaging. All of the assignments and tests were challenging but as long as you study, they really aren't a big deal. Attendance is not mandatory, but well worth your time.

Remember to submit your homework, it is simple, a huge part of your grade, and easy to forget to do.  With only four HWs that take 5 min to complete, missing one can take a huge chunk out.  Test are the study guides, so memorize. He is one of those professors that you would want to run into while drinking at a bar.  Great stories.

GREAT guy. That being said the tests were tough and there were no assignments to earn points. Great lecture so funny however make sure you study hard for his tests because the study guides don't really help at all.
I found his tests to be difficult, but he's such an awesome teacher and gives so much extra credit that you really won't care. I hate Earth Science, but he made it bearable.

Rankey is an awesome guy, and he is really understanding and has the student in mind all the time. His lectures are fun and he understands the subject isn't always exciting so he makes use of his hilarious sense of humor (lots of NASCAR jokes). His tests are tough and require a bit of studying, but he also offers tons of extra credit.

To break up the monotony of long lectures, he puts funny things into the powerpoint to keep you engaged. There was also many extra credit opportunities that could have easily put everyone above 100% had everyone participated. Lots of info learned through the semester and overall, I very much enjoyed this class!

This is the second time I took this class however the first time I took this class it was the online option, and I would definitely choose the in class option over online any day, it was way more of an actual way to learn about oceanography and an acceptable course.

He is the man. Oceanography is such a fun class. It's tailored toward non science majors and Rankey keeps that in mind. The lectures are interesting, and he is engaging. If you need a science credit and or a 300 level class, definitely take this class. Tests can be hard but he offers lots of extra credit. Really cool and interesting guy.

He's funny and his lectures are interesting but I found his tests a little hard to study for. Maybe I should have read the book more but I always got lower scores on the tests than I thought I would just by studying my notes

He is funny and engaging. I liked the class a lot for something I wasn't interested in.  Study for the tests; they are the majority of your grade. Students make up the tests.  But also there are little assignments that are given during class - don't forget to do those. You can lose a whole grade letter if you forget those. They're really easy.

His lectures were pretty engaging and his jokes are pretty funny.  There's almost no homework, but make sure you study for the tests because they make up for the majority of your grade.  Overall, a very good professor and nice man.

Dr. Kim is very sweet, but he kind of just read the textbook off of PowerPoint slides in a very strong accent all of class. The tests were also very, very short with multi-part questions that were hard to study for. The class was weighted in a way that this wasn't a huge issue, but I did fail both exams. TA sessions were boring but chill.
I did the bare minimum in this class, had a 76% on canvas and when h checked my grade I got an A. W professor W class, light work
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor posts grades to canvas without proper weighting, giving students a false representation of their grade. I had a 94.8% throughout the whole class yet when he input the grades into the transcript I received a B+. He then sent out multiple emails explaining how he would not be changing grades. My final grade was much lower than anticipated.

Dr. Chrysikou is really knowledgeable in her field. You will learn a lot from going to lectures (attendance is taken, but lecture notes are posted online). Engaging. Study for tests from lectures, not the textbook.

She was a great Professor. The material is not easy, but she made it easy to understand and is always willing to help you understand. She answers emails very fast and will make extra appointments to help.
My all time favorite professor. She is amazing and one of the most knowledgable people I know. Also extremely helpful. Basically, she's the best.
Great professor! She gives you opportunities for extra credit, and curves her exams. You can tell that she loves what she teaches, and is very knowledgeable.

Dr. C is one of my favorites in the psych department.  A brilliant woman who pushed us to go to the studies and research articles themselves, however dense.  2 years later, I find that I am ahead in many classes I take today because of Dr. C alone.  Oh yeah, not only was she one of my all time favorites, but it was her 1st year teaching here.  :)

The class is difficult, but brain and behavior is a difficult subject. Dr. Chrysikou does the best she can to make the topic as easy as it can be to understand. She is also always available to help, responds to emails almost immediately, and is very fair when it comes to grading. She also makes class very interesting. Very nice professor :)
The material was complex, but she did her best to explain it. I found her to be extremely intelligent, if somewhat standoff-ish.

Her study guides had way more information than would ever be on her tests. Class consisted of her reading off of slides (that can be found online). Nevertheless, she is extremely helpful, provides extra credit and curves grades.

The class is hard because the material's hard.  It's Neurobiology; what do you expect?  Gives many opportunities for extra credit, tries to make the material fun, curves exams well, lenient grading policy, tries to answer everyone's questions... horrible choice in TA though; she never should've let the TA teach any of the classes, yikes

The nightmares are true. Nothing has changed since 17 years ago when the first rating for Ewing came in. This class is a joke. It seems KUAE's philosophy in teaching an increasingly large program is to teach less and expect more. You will not learn anything from Dr. Ewing, and KUAE does not care.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: huddy hut.

Ewing is a joke. His class is terribly organized, he makes things up ont he fly and gives out wrong information for projects that he only corrects the day its due (after weeks of struggling working on it). When I say you will only do well in this class if your GTA is good, I mean it. He also assigned the honors project 2 weeks before class ended.

This professor jumps between 2 textbooks and slides randomly. He's nice but treats this 3-credit class like it's 8. DO NOT take it with AE 550—your existence will be a nightmare. 4 hours of sleep a night is the norm. The material isn't hard, but you'll do group projects here on top of AE 550's group work and take-home exams. Thank god for TA Dean.

By far the WORST professor. Missed half the semester for research. Requires 2 textbooks, 1 he wrote—it's awful. If the class does well on exam 1, he makes the rest impossibly hard. Grades are a mess; most uploaded during finals. Exams lack explanations, lectures are chaotic, and handwriting is illegible. The TA determines your survival. Avoid him!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Mark Ewing is a pretty chill guy, but it's clear he may be getting a little foggy in his old age. His lectures can be hard to follow. The videos he shows the class are interesting at least. Shoutout to Dean.

Dr. Ewing is a great guy, but his class can be disorganized. The first few weeks of lecture was very good, but the middle of the class was completely disorganized. It got better again towards the end. He is a nice dude and will give you the points you deserve. Hard material and he could organize the class better, but there were some great lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ewing is a cool person but his class.. broke me. I got an A but have no idea how. Don't freak out if things seem unfair, unclear, or unorganized. Hopefully you have a good GTA who can explain things better. My TA (Skyler)'s office hours were most helpful. Just show up and try your best, everyone makes it through!

Hes not a bad guy, just kinda bad at teaching. He typically goes a million miles an hour while covering up his work because hes left handed. The best idea in his class is to find a group of people to work with outside class time at least 3 times a week because thats the only way youll learn. Pretty good on grading though and wants you to pass.

Class was very disorganized. A lot of the blame falls on the teaching assistant also, but Dr. Ewing did not do a good job of correcting deficiencies in that area. Grading criteria was very confusing. He very often contradicted himself. One day you think you are doing it right, and the next he is telling you that you are wrong.
Awful teacher, does not know how to lecture, and does not use a helpful book
Unclear grading, boring lecture, homework is difficult but doable, tests are alright I guess. Design projects are worthless.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ewing clearly has a good understanding of the subject matter, but he cannot communicate the subject matter to students. His "examples" in class are him flipping between pages rapidly and describing what he would do. No numbers, no actually working the problem out, just "I'd probably start here, obvious right?" Uh, no Mark, that's why I'm here.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is a 3 hour class that thinks that it is an 8.  I dedicated more time to this class than any of my 5 hour classes. The material is sometimes difficult to grasp, and the demand is pretty high. Dr. Ewing is a good guy that genuinely cares about his students. He's very smart, but he's sometimes forgetful. Design projects suck, tests are ok.
Really smart teacher and appears to know a lot about structures, but frankly cannot teach it AT ALL. The textbook is probably the worst book ever written. Bad  bad class.

His class is truly awful. He is a nice guy but he can't teach the subject matter in a way in which people understand. I will come out of this class with a lower understanding of structures than when I went in.

Mark is getting very senile in his old age. He is utterly obsessed with the Meridian UAV project (which isn't even his) and centers all of his assignments around it. He assumes that all students have a heavy background in structures. The fact that he is the head of the depertment is a testiment to how much the deparment needs to revamp.

He should not be a faculty member, let alone the deparment chairman. Avoid any of his classes. Save your money, invite your friends and blow your money on alcohol. That will be way more productive than spending it on one his classes.
She made me a better writer by the end of the semester. I loved her insights into Russian history. She is kind, helpful, and always available outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Don't expect to skate by with this one. Her main assignments are lengthy or technically challenging (or both) writing assignments that require you to dig deep in both of the two super dry Russian history textbooks she requires. To her credit, the lectures are fairly interesting, but the writing you have to do is way too much for a 100 level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Levin has a level of devotion to the study of Russian history that I really have never seen before with most anything. The class is difficult, make no mistake, and writing assignments can be trying, however, it is not unreasonable. She is friendly and understanding and simply put, you will learn a ton.

Before this class, I was a 4.0 student. I get almost 100% on every assignment, including this teacher's quizzes that are multiple choice. I have gotten a C or worse on every written assignment, with very little in the way of clear responses. she will often circle your answer and write "no, check the text". thanks, as if i didn't do that already!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Quizzes are easy. You are required to ask questions in class, so many ask needless questions just to get credit. You are also required to attend class and blog. As for the writing exercises, expect bad grades. She is very hard to please and doesn't give much direction. Stay away from Hist 117. Your GPA may suffer.
Just dont
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Levin is caring and brilliant, but she should not be teaching a 101-level class. The quizzes are easy and participation is a no-brainer as long as you show up, but the amount and level of reading is impossible and when it comes to papers, they are difficult and she is impossible to please.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This is one of the hardest classes i have taken in my college career. Shes very intelligent and lectures are interesting but The writing assignments are ridiculously hard and she expects to understand scholarly article and write essays on these article. expect to read a TON and write a ton,Quizzes are easy and so is participation. DO NOT TAKE CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The class is an insane amount of work. Unless your a huge history buff I would not recommend it. Mandatory attendance. The required readings can be a bit tedious and boring at times. Prof Levin has developed a bad habit of treating her students like they are still in high school.

Dr. Levin asks a lot in terms of writing, but there's no memorization required and the quizzes allow multiple chances, so you can basically look up the answers to the questions you don't know.  Good course, but mandatory attendance always sucks.

Prof. Levin is brilliant. She is helpful and kind and her lectures are interesting and entertaining. Grad students: take a Levin class; you won't be disappointed. The ratings that suggest her lectures are boring are flawed; these students must be lacking adequate brain cells.

He lectures are boring, and so is her "participation point" system. She made class somewhat interesting, but her homework assignments, mid-terms, and finals are BS. Be prepared to write essays. This class would have been better if her tests/assignments were multiple choice, but they were all essay questions and hard ones. DO NOT TAKE.
Hard to follow Dr. Levin's confusing lectures. She wanders way off topic all the time. It is difficult to follow her train of thought and guess how it will play out in an assignment.

Her participation system is seriously flawed. She teaches above a 100 level, but this is probably because she is an expert in the field. Very knowledgable, and easy to approach. The lectures are a bit boring, but she tried to make the subject interesting. I got an A in the course, but I had to put in more effort than I had expected.

Hist. of Christianity is crazy, she tells you its an easy 300 level class, but really it's not.  The online quizzes are tedious and nit picky, so even if you read the material, you won't pass them.  The take home exams are ridiculous (like a full fledged paper). And the papers are hard to write because she isn't very clear about what she wants.

Her participation is a terrible system and her grading of papers is tough to find what she wants you to write.  However, her compassion for the subject keeps you coming back and you actually learn something in the end.

Prof. Levin is very knowledgeable on the History of Christianity and had a lot of good information in lectures which are required for participation points.  All assignments, except for little quizzes are writing and she is a very hard grader on the papers you write for her.

Dr. Levin is extremely distinguished within the study of Slavic studies and is recognized internationally for it. She does straight lecture in class, attendance is counted as participation. Essays are take home, open book, but are not easy. Overall, decent class.

Professor Levin is a genius. Although she grades tough she really cares about her students and she knows her stuff. This class consisted of no tests or memorization, just online quizzes and 4 papers. Also I probably printed out about $70 worth of ink because in addition to the Chidester book you have to read lots of articles. Lots to read but great

Eve makes sure you know that she is the expert on Medieval Russian History.  Generally, you can't find a book written on the subject that doesn't cite her work or mention her in the acknowledgements.  Shes a bit long-winded, but shes the expert, so I suppose thats okay.  A very helpful lady however and a fair grader.

One of the best classes that I have taken at the University.  Professor is very knowledgeable and intersting.  She is quite funny as well.  Her personal experiances in Russia are very enlightening.  I would take a class from her again in a heartbeat.

While her classes are pretty difficult, and there is a lot of work involved, Professor Levin is very understanding, and does everything she can to make sure her students do well in her class.  She is a great teacher with an amazing knowledge of her subject.
