Professor Levin is an excellent professor, who has a superb understanding of medieval Russian history. Even though she assigns a lot of readings, and the assignments can be difficult, she is extremely helpful and very willing to make sure that her students learn and do well in her class.

Exum is one of the worst teachers I have encountered at KU. She's impossible to communicate with. If you email her, don't expect a response for at least 48 hours. When she does finally email back it's NEVER helpful and ALWAYS rude. I truly think she shouldn't be allowed to be a teacher. 0/10 rec. DON'T TAKE HER!! lots of busy work and unfair grader
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not as understanding as she portrays to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst lectures. Attendance is required but very pointless, made us play very awkward and pointless games which made 70% of the class absolute silence. The class was made out to be much more intense that it should of, 0/10 would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I was not a big fan of hers. She was not very good at communication outside of class. We only met once a week and she would not give us access to power points outside of class. The homework is lengthy because it is mostly an online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not a fan. Also, she entered the due date of our final exam wrong and said that no one completed it, when she messed up!!! Ridiculous that she is blaming us for her mistakes. She is very hard to get in touch with, never replies to emails so it is impossible to get help. Overall do not recommend unless you want to struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The worst if I'm being honest. Exum is never available when you need help, I had emailed her countless times asking for help only to finally get responses after grades had been finalized. Also if you miss one thing your grade will plummet with no hope of ever getting it back up. She doesn't do retakes or late credit, it either do it or get a 0.

Professor Exum made class material very confusing and her blackboard site was also hard to understand. Lectures were not very useful, but attendance was required. I felt that attending class was more of a distraction as we just played pointless games. Exams were pretty easy if you studied. It just seemed a little intense for an introduction course.

Prof. Exum is an amazing professor! She genuinely cares and attends to her students. Not only is she knowledgable, but she more than adequately answers questions and responds very well. She hints at material on tests during her study sessions. IF SHE ORGANIZES AN OUTSIDE OF CLASS STUDY SESSION, GO TO IT-- makes preparing for tests extremely easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: she knows what she is doing and knows the material, but grades way too hard for an introductory level class. I am undecided and considered psych as a major, but she has made me hate the subject as a whole. take psych 104 because its interesting, but take it with someone else. because its a hybrid class, it makes it harder when the teacher is rough
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fardad is one of those professors that if you answer questions in class and study for her exams…you will do just fine. She gives out extra credit to people who answer questions in class! It's free points!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Having a difficult time in this class, we are only graded on quizzes which we do not get back, and our midterms will make or break the grade. No homework does not exactly set us up for success when an exam accounts for 1/3rd of our grade and whether we will need to retake it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No graded homework so you only get to be traded on exams and quizzes, of which quizzes are not given back. Fail one exam and you're in jeopardy of failing the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: professor Fardad was ok. She doesn't have dedicated office hours, you will always need to schedule it if you want to meet with her. Her practice exams proved to be very helpful. Review your calc 3 before this class as it's heavily used there.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Do you value feedback on homework to help you learn? Too bad, she doesn't collect or grade homework. Just go to office hours then? Better schedule it 1-2 weeks out.

Exams are 90% of the grade and full of tricky wording, quizzes are 10% and you need a 70% on quizzes to pass. You also never get back quiz grades so that ads to the fun of the mystery.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought Dr. Fardad did an amazing job of keeping our class engaged throughout the entire semester. The "atmosphere" of the class was easily my favorite out of any of the electrical engineering classes I've taken so far. If you show up to class, she will absolutely do her best to help you succeed. It is obvious that she cares about her students.

EECS 221 and 312. Great professor. Show up to class and pay attention to the lectures. Nothing on exams are surprising if you review example problems and pay attention in class. She's very accessible outside of class and will answer your questions and set up officer hours for clarification. If you have the opportunity to, take a class with her.

This teacher is one of the best I've taken in the Electrical Engineering department at Ku. Great lecturer, great test resources, and her tests are fair. I wish more teachers were like her in the department.

(EECS 312 & 221): Most caring professor I ever had. Lectures are easy to understand, and she answers questions clearly. If you get lost on something and ask for help, she will genuinely map out everything step by step so you thoroughly understand. Homework is reasonable and her exams are consistent with the material taught.

Had Fardad for EECS 221 and currently taking EECS 312 with her. Either she's changed a lot over the past few semesters or the other reviews here are very biased lol. Shima is a kind and reasonable person teaching very difficult topics, and compared to some other EECS profs she's a saint. Also, as of this semester, tests are not 90% of our grade����

90 percent of grade is exams so you better do well. she gets flack, but she did the best she could given the circumstances. available literally 24 hours a day and will happily schedule a personal Zoom call to help you. lectures are sometimes long and homework is confusing, but ask questions and you will be okay. very understanding person.

Don't go to her office hours expecting her to help you make a plan to succeed in her class. She will just accuse you of not practicing enough, adamantly defend her teaching ability even if you didn't even mention her teaching, and tell you everyone in her class is doing better than you are.

Shima will blame class wide poor test performance on the students rather than herself. Grade system is funky. (Final worth 50% of class grade) Will not tell you test dates in advance. Constantly rude to students and inconsiderate of their situations outside of school. Don't show up late, she will stop the class to complain for five minutes about it

Material is explained very clearly in the slides and lectures. In-class assignments are reviewed in class, so it's free points if you put in the effort to show up to class. Lidan is a very kind and caring woman. Exams are pretty easy. Group projects can take quite a bit of time so stay on top of the milestones. I recommend joining a group for it.

One of my favorite profs; there is an in-class assignment every-class, but it's due at the end of the day. Python can be tricky but she walked us through every problem making it easier. She pushed back quizzes a few times to allow us more time to prepare! Such a great and caring professor. **group projects" can be completed alone!**

Super heavy conceptual class that gets boring really fast but is easy overall. There's almost an in-class assignment every lecture but can be turned in later. The assignments aren't that bad, and you can extra credit for attending class. You don't have to work in a group for the group project.

You'll learn the basics of Python, so it'll be hard if you aren't comfortable with logic-based programming. The professor has an in-class assignment almost every lecture, but it doesn't have to be done in-class and is due at the end of the day. She gives plenty of extra credit opportunities and is really flexible with test taking and extensions.

Get ready to read, he is not accessible outside of the class, there is no grading criteria in the syllabus and he released the grades after the deadline so if you are planning to graduate, don't take his class.
The homework is not comparable to what he taught in the class. No extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Dr. Fang is a genuinely good professor, who is passionate about the subject. He also allows extra credit for homework. However this class is EXTREMELY test heavy, and graded hard.

Spring 2023, the Final was worth 25% the grade
High was 88, Average was 48.44, Median was 44

No Curve, most of the class of ~60 failed. KU's solution was summer repeat

Amazing person and solid professor. There's also plenty of extra credit opportunities. Be forewarned, there's only 1 midterm that's 30 percent of your grade and a final that's 40 percent, so room for error is very little. If you study the groupwork and homework that he gives you, you should be fine for the exams.

Incredibly kind and positive professor. He start with a 20-30 minute lecture then transitions into working out example problems with the class and then as groups. The online homework is very time consuming, but it's a huge chunk of the grade and the extra credit can add up to a 10% boost to your overall grade if you do it all.

The class is reasonable and expectations are clear. He keeps class interesting by telling jokes. Tries to be inspirational and push students to do great things. Very nice dude and would enjoy taking more classes with him.
I love this guy. Tells a joke at the beginning of every class and truly cares about his students. My favorite class this semester, even though dynamics is a pretty tough subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Great professor that really cares about his students. Taking a course from Dr. Feng could be one of the best decisions you could make at KU.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the most inspirational professors I have ever had. Would send up little notes weekly about doing well and how he believes in us. Really wanted us to succeed, but at the same time, did not make it any easier on us. Tests are old homework, example problems, and/or group work, so that makes them a little easier. Lectures are mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the most inspirational professors I have ever had. Would send up little notes weekly about doing well and how he believes in us. Really wanted us to succeed, but at the same time, did not make it any easier on us. Tests are old homework, example problems, and/or group work, so that makes them a little easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: History 129 probably one of the worst classes to take at KU and if you can avoid it do so. I have written more papers in the last semester than I have all of college. He doesn't require attendance except for the discussion part of class and lectures are pretty boring. He doesn't give direct writing to take notes from and goes over the class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Farber is a kind, smart, and entertaining man worthy of the highest acclaim. His lectures were frequently informative, but delivered in a down-to-earth, humorous style. His deep love of American history translated into a great series of lectures that illuminated the subject. In addition, his books are of the utmost quality.

Farber was a great professor and worked well with students during a pandemic. Gave great feedback on papers and was always willing to help. He was also flexible in class and projects so you could do something that you were interested in. Made the content of the class very interesting and lectures were never boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a great guy working with great material. You can just tell how much he loves history. Besides of A LOT of reading, the class was fairly easy too. Highly recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--So many papers

reviews.comment: This guy is a real bro. He is great at lecturing and entertaining. No work in the class besides a few papers, mid term, and final. If you take his class make sure to go to his office hours because he is a chiller.
Took EECS 565 with her. Exams are terrible, and lectures are super boring. A waste of your time

The lectures are somewhat monotonous. My greatest concern though is the lack of feedback on the projects. Reports were submitted as early as February but only graded after the finals. Tests can also be challenging especially the multiple choice. Overall, a nice professor with room for improvement.

Just super boring. She reads directly from the slides the entire semester. Most people don't even come to class because they can just read the slides at home. Easy enough, and nice, but just puts you to sleep.
Difficult homework and massive take-home exams. He gave AI feedback on the term paper. Nice guy personally.

Feldman is the best professor at KU, hands down. He is a very 'anti-education system' type professor where he does not like giving tests and really dislikes the idea of grades. He grades you based off how much it seems you are putting into the class and how much you care, rather than how much you really understand. Great professor!
Overall one a genuine person and excellent professor. He assigns lots of reading and writing but gives great feedback and cares about his students a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Feldman has be one of the most interesting professors on campus. Hume has a love for physics and teaching that exemplifies teaching at it's finest. He was always willing to go the extra mile to make sure students understood the material. Plus, he is a tight old Swiss guy. Props Feldman.
Hands down the worst professor I've had in my three years attending KU. If approached with a question, Professor Feldman acts both rude and annoyed. His inability to teach the material is amazing.

Professor Feldman is a great teacher and a cool guy.  He always took time to answer my questions outside class and made every effort to help the students get a good grade.  I found his lectures very interesting and discovered a love for physics that DEFINITELY was not there before.  Highly recommended.
He was a bad teacher! I failed every test but somehow got an A... Learned nothing

Make no mistake, PHSX 521 is a tough course but if i had taken it with anyone else I would have failed the course with FLYING colours. Prof. Feldman is v.funny and explains theories very clearly. He even takes the time to give students historical background on how certain theories came about. An excellent prof. and one that I would recommend ALWAYS

Massimo is a great guy and even better professor. While I don't think the class is structured well to really learn the language, the class is at least fun and very relaxed. Full of laughs and quirky little stories about life in Italy, he inspired me to want to visit Italy but also continue learning after I have finished my 4 semesters. Do Italian.

I have taken 3 semesters of Italian, the last 2 have been with Massimo. He is a great professor with a sense of humor and is very understanding. I was unable to make it to two of our exams this year and he was very flexible with me, offering me to take them up to a week late. If you put in the work you will get a good grade. Amazing professor.

He's very laid back and very clearly cares about his students' success. He's willing to help students with their Italian outside of class at office hours. He takes time to explain difficult concepts and doesn't blame us if none of us understand. Great dude and an amazing lecturer.

I loved having Massimo. He is very helpful and understands the difficulty that comes with learning a new language. He is always there if you need help. He made learning Italian alot of fun. I wish he taught more Italian classes.

Massimo is very kind and has a very calm energy in his class. Highly recommend making friends in the class because it can get a little awkward. Also definitely write down your assignments and due dates because things come up fast.
Massimo helped me learn more Italian in one semester than I learned Spanish in 4 years of learning in high school. Hes very kind and understanding and is a very effective teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Felix leads a thoughtful and interesting course. She is personable and willing to work with you if something comes up. As long as you come to classes and are open to participation, you'll do fine.

I got an F because I missed my final presentation due to illness. I had a doctor's note and everything. She was unkind towards me and was unwilling to work with me or allow me to redo it at another time. I had an A in the class before that so she only failed me because of this. Other than that, she was a decent professor. Just patronizing at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was nice enough. Came off as a bit condescending sometimes and if you asked questions after class wasn't very personable. Make sure to do your weekly readings because she likes to get people on that, also on notes don't just write whats on the board, they're intentionally vague. Make sure to do study guides and you'll do fine on the exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Felix was nice. She is very kind and laid-back, but do not underestimate that. The class is somewhat difficult, and there are not many assignments. 6 quizzes, 3 application assignments, and 2 exams - a midterm and final, which are both pretty lengthy. Also, participation in class DOES matter toward your grade. Get ready to work! Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're serious about a career in investments, you need to take 411 with Felix. Most challenging class I've ever taken (& probably will ever take) but he focuses on teaching you how to provide actual value to companies. Takes A LOT of time outside of class (very frustrating for the first few projects) but worth it. He genuinely cares about you.

You will collaborate, learn, discover, and remember a ton with Felix and become a much better finance student. Would not recommend for students who are busy with extracurriculars or have a tough schedule (cases take 15+ hours). However, that's not to say it isn't possible as 90% of students in the class had hard schedules. Grading can be unclear.

I had the pleasure of taking a class with Felix and I was blown away by their passion for new trading strategies course. He also brought real-life examples into the discussions, and market events every class that made it interesting. The book isn't a typical textbook, its actually entertaining. Felix is a G. 100/10

Gotta read the textbook. Felix is a beast. Make sure to participate so you don't get left behind. Most insightful class I have taken but also one of the hardest. Don't let the sway you from taking his class I highly recommend his class.

FIN410 w/ Felix was hardest but also the most rewarding class I've taken. I mean I was excited to go to lectures. He seems intimidating at first, but he really does care about your understanding and progression. Just be ready to put in the work. Bottom line if you're a finance major, absolutely 10/10 I would recommend FIN410 with Felix.

Hands down the best professor I have ever had. He is challenging but the way he teaches this course is so special. Loved my time with this course - it taught me very practical skills, and I guarantee you will be very glad you took the class with him. If you want a future in finance, you absolutely have to experience FIN 410 with Felix Meschke!
An awesome and intellectual professor who had a unique way of relating complex financial theories and equations to everyday situations.

Definitely the hardest finance class I have taken at KU. Came in with little to no excel experience, which was a mistake. But thanks to my group, left the class with a strong grasp of excel. Most people fail the midterm and final, but if you show improvement, you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Very difficult course, but worth it if you're a finance major.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: A lot of group presentations, exams are hard, better hone your excel skills before taking this class.
This guy thinks a negative attitude will inspire his students to do better...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: One of the most intelligent professors I have had at KU. Course is tough but very rewarding. Expect to use excel for everything, many hard group projects and pop quizzes. Take his feedback and learn from it, you will learn a ton from this class. Wish I appreciated this course more while I took it!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Felix is great. Class is difficult, but stay focused, learn from his feedback, and you'll get through it. Enjoy it, too. I wish I could take that class again.
reviews.rating_tags: CARES ABOUT STUDENTS--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Here's the simplest way to decide if you should take a class with Felix Meschke:  Are you majoring in finance, or do you want to have a career in finance? If you said yes to the second part, take Felix's class. By far the most eye opening, insightful finance class at KU. Felix is very smart, and will work for you if you work for him.

Hardest class I've taken, but learned the most by far. Felix is an amazing professor. Expect hard group projects, reading and pop quizzes. You have to work hard in this class, but it's incredibly rewarding.

IF YOU ARE DUMB DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS HE WILL CALL YOU OUT. THIS CLASS IS NOT BS AS MANY  PEOPLE WOULD SAY, YOU ACTUALLY LEARN A LOT WITH HAND IN THE DIRT BY DOING THE GROUP PROJECTS. PAY ATTENTION IN CLASS AND REMEMBER IS NOT ALL ABOUT THE GRADE. I ENDED UP WITH AN "A" THOUGH DESPITE BARELY PASSING THE MIDTERM. FUNNIEST TEACHER EVER

very hard class, failed the first project and the midterm but still received an A. If you stay with the class and show at least improved effort you won't receive a bad grade. worth your while to take.

Felix is intimidating at first but once I got to know him and developed an understanding of his teaching style the class developed into one of my favorite and rewarding classes.  Finance at KU wasn't that challenging in a lot of aspects and it was nice to have a teacher really push and see what we were made of.  I highly recommend Felix.

Felix is by far and over the best finance professor the University of Kansas has. I learned more from him during this class than I have learned in all other finance classes combined. He is tough, but fair. Do not expect to blow this course off! If you are interested in the financial field after graduation, Felix Meschke is your best bet at success.

GO TO CLASS AND READ THE BOOK. Meschke asks a lot from his students, but you will absolutely learn more in this class than any other. Class centers around applied group projects, so set group meeting times early in the semester so you don't run into problems getting the group together later (this was a major problem for everyone in my class...).

One of the most intelligent profs the B-School has on faculty. I learned an incredible amount, and he has a great sense of humor. The problem? No consistency in grading policies. Impossible to track your progress and final grade seemed 100% subjective. Plus he missed the four weeks of classes due to a (legitimate) injury, but the sub was awful!  C-

I loved Meschke's lectures, but if no one asks questions over the material, he will not go over it in depth. That is why YOU MUST READ THE TEXTBOOK for this class. Work hard to prepare great notes (graphs, formulas, examples), because there is no partial credit on exams. Group projects kinda suck, but they are interesting and relevant.

Felix is an awesome teacher. He is not easy, & lets you know from the get-go. You will learn a lot from him, & he challenges your thinking. The cases are tailored to current events & are interesting. He relies more on his TA's if you need help who are helpful. This class is very applicable to the real world. Highly recommend taking this class.
Felix is an amazing teacher, just grades really really hard. You should expect to know your stuff after taking his class. best professor for this finance.

Felix is a very unconventional teacher however he is a good one. He understands that the material is hard and grades accordingly. Prepare to work but if you do get to know him and demonstrate that you are able and willing to learn the material he will give you the grade that you deserve.

Tough teacher, I think he's used to teaching grad students as this class is very difficult and the case studies are often vague. "You all got low grades because you only did what I told you to do" is a quote that sums up the class pretty well. I had a low C after midterms and ended up with an A- so there is definitely a curve. Very likable guy.

This class was definitely challenging, especially the group projects. He has high expectations for your case analysis so be sure to take it seriously. The formula sheet is a big help for the exams, but they are still challenging. Must read the text and spend quite a bit of outside class time on this class. Learned A LOT though.

Class is no cakewalk, and Felix knows this. Exams aren't horrible as long as you make a good formula sheet. Quizzes are online and require you to read the book with a few ones in class. The thing that makes this class such a pain is the group projects. They are EXTREMELY hard and on top of that, he grades them EXTREMELY hard. Class grade is curved.

He warns you day 1 about the workload. Its an extremely difficult class but he probably preps better for the real world than most.He grades hard on case analyses and has high expectations.  Will always clarify topics in class but defers to TAs outside of class. Lectures involve clarifying topics more than teaching so you have to read the book.

Professor Meschke's class is really great preparation for an internship or job in finance and it's not boring.  I have learned a lot from him, however, it is one of the most difficult classes I have ever taken. He grades really hard and the tests are hard.  If you are ready for a challenge, take his class and if not, go with another professor.

I took THR100 in the Spring to fulfill course requirements. I did theatre all through my childhood, but this professor has ruined everything theatre for me. If you take this class, beware that she never grades on time (I'm talking like 2 months behind), never responds to emails, and will grade based on her political affiliations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class thinking it would be an easy A. Everything we did each week was political and if your views went against hers she would grade you down. She would name call her students based on assumptions she made towards them and major projects had no rubrics. Overall very disappointed in his class.

I took this class thinking it would be an easy A and was absolutely wrong. The course-load is heavy and everything is graded extremely hard with little explanation. If you are not genuinely interested in theatre then do not take this class. I had a terrible time taking this class and do not recommend.

Weekly posts you need to post, grades very hard, you have to watch 2 musicals for this class, if you really dont like theatre, do not take this class. Thought it would be an easy A but its the hardest class I am in this semester

Timmia did a really great job of making us feel that we could succeed even if we were behind in class. She was very kind and constructive about the way that she graded our work and her lectures were very interesting! The blog/vlog/podcast didn't feel like too much work every week compared to my other classes. Overall, great prof!!

This class is my favorite class this semester. Timmia is the nicest person on the planet, she is a little strange, but what theatre professor isn't? To pass, show up, memorize one of two monologues throughout the semester, and honestly, just try. You'll be fine. There are weekly reflections, but you'll get an A if you explain your thoughts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took MATH 290 as an online summer course. Professor Feng did not post any materials that were created by him -- you basically only had the textbook to work off of. I would not reccommend taking this course in an online summer format if you would like the learn the material well. Professor Feng essentially did nothing and was completely hands-off.

He's very smart, but not that good at explaining concepts.  The homework took a while but wasn't too difficult.  The tests also weren't too difficult, but he would take a lot of points off for small things, and the tests were worth a lot of our grade.

I took MATH 290 as a summer course and all was fine throughout the first half of the semester. Professor Feng decided halfway through that he wanted to change the format of the exams to be written, while all of our previous HW and exams were online. I am taking the final today with no feedback for any of the previous written exams. Very frustrating

Took him for a summer course. He gave 0 lectures, in person or via Zoom, e-mailed out Powerpoints which were just ver-batim copied from textbook. The man is not a teacher, and doesn't deserve a paycheck. I'm lucky to be taking an easy class from him, because any class at 300+ would be impossible. The sad thing is this is par for KU Math Department

I went to his class everyday for iClicker points, but I otherwise did not learn much. I had to go to the other professor's class whenever I could to learn and understand the material. The biggest problem was that he was unprepared for lecture, and did not have the problems solved and ready, waisting time during class.

Professor Feng epitomizes all that is wrong with state university education.  What that means is that he's there only to do research. Teaching is treated as an inconvenience to him.  His teaching methods are so formal that you're better off learning from the book and skipping his lectures.
He explains many concepts geometrically. There is a significant of us do not get it easy.  Overall it was fair.

Doesn't care about the class. Doesn't seem like he even understands calculus. Gets really angry for no reason. Never prepared to teach. Doesn't understand the technology. Rude. Impatient. Doesn't care about the students' success.

on the first day, the guy said outright that it is not his job to teach. If you have a hard time getting sleep during the day, you're in luck! his monotone voice will quickly put you to sleep as you ponder the meaning of your miserable math existence.

Early on, he said that it is his belief that students should learn from the book (easier said than done, as the book doesn't explain things any better than he does), and only review in class. As such, he gives only the most cursory of explanations of material. Want to ask a question about something you don't understand? Expect a snarky response.
He's not a very good teacher, but pretty easy to pass. Homework every week, which can get hard. But you can skip class as long as you read some from the book

Feng teaches in a highly formal style that can make this subject more difficult than it needs to be.  He does not take time to explain his steps, and he tends to go immediately to the most general solution, leaving the finer details for you to figure out on your own.  Which is fine until it's not... The ability to teach yourself is crucial.

Poor instruction.  He  uses the most formal definition to explain the concepts, which means most lectures consist of him reading the book to the class.  He doesn't like to repeat himself, so good luck getting an answer to any questions you have.  His lectures assume you already know the materials and how to use them.

Jin Feng is the man. Go to lecture and ask questions when you get lost. He expects you to know your algebra so don't get upset if he gives you some snarkiness if you ask a low level question. Tests are straitforward and he is a fair mangrader. Glance the textbook before class and his lecture will be clear. Show him your effort he will warm up to u

He's a cool guy, kind of, but he will not teach you in a way you will understand.  The whole time he just kept putting problems on the board and expected us to know how to do them.  He made the class much harder than it should have been.  He skips steps often when working problems out.  Plan on a lot of work out of class to learn the material.
Horrible teacher

Awful, can't understand him. Doesn't care if you don't understand the concepts. Takes attendance points so you are forced to go to lecture and become more and more frustrated. Just pay attention in your lab section and you should pass.
It is really frustrated on guessing what he's trying to teach and talk in the class.

AVOID!I sent Feng an email about an assignment in which the material wasn't yet discussed in class. So I asked if he was planning to push the assignment back a day or 2; I only got a reply with a link to the syllabus. No words in the reply, the syllabus remained unchanged. He shows no respect for students. All previous comments about him are true.

Professor was rude and condescending.  He would come to class late and not bring the textbook and have to borrow a student's.  He made jokes and attempted to be funny but mostly just over explained things until they made no sense.  Tests were nothing like the practice tests he gave and he was just downright unpleasant.

Terrible teacher. Moves incredibly fast, no time for people to ask questions. Don't even think about asking a question about the calculus behind something. He makes fun of most of the questions asked and usually doesn't answer them. The book is awful and doesn't explain anything either. Steer clear of this prof!
Easiest Differential Equations class at KU by far.  All other friends taking diff eq with different teachers covered way more material, while we covered only the basics.

Jin is a great teacher if you go to class and pay attention.  His tests are very straight forward and many are problems he worked as examples in class with numbers in class.  With a little effort there is no reason you can't do well with him.

Not a very friendly guy...I would advise going to the lecture though as i didn't and payed the price in my grade.  He will belittle you and thinks he's a god, pretty sure he doesn't be there, and his tests were only 3 questions.  The first test involves gaussian elimination, setting up a parabola equation, and a circuit problem.  AVOID IF POSSIBLE!
Chopped, would never take class with her again.

She is just not clear whatsoever when it comes to any projects or tests. Would never recommend taking any class with her even if it was 101. I can strongly say that most people in this class are taking it for a required diversity credit not because they wanted to and she makes class feel as a waste of time.

Would suggest avoiding at all costs. Had her for two different classes and can not recommend less. Huge ego and loves praise herself about her work outside of being a professor. She makes it sound like her students are a burden to her career, and has no personality unlike most Jschool staff.

This women is the definition of tough love. At first I despised her, but towards the end of the semester the work she taught me really impacted me. Not the most tech savvy and is quirky, maybe even passive aggressive. But she wants her students to do good work.

Nice teacher! There's a reflection paper each week due pre class. There's no tests just in class writing with a prompt and they are easy. Attendence is mandatory and she has you sign a sheet. There's a book. The projects are pretty easy so this wasnt a stressful class. Presentations or only 2-4 minutes and you can just talk. NO extra credit.

She is like that evil teacher from iCarly (the ginger one), and Nevel had a baby, and then left her to be raised by Voldemort. She doesn't answer questions in class, and if you ask a question she will not only not help you, but she will look at you like you pooped your pants right in front of her. BEWARE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She lectures like she's reading it for the first time but acts like she invented the field. Ask a question? Expect a confused stare or a passive-aggressive answer that's both dismissive and wrong. The class wasn't hard, but her ego and incompetence made it unbearable. If you want a professor who cares, look elsewhere.

Extremely hard class. She is a very tough grader and gives unclear instructions when it comes to assignments. Asking questions is a no-go because she doesn't give any clarity. Be prepared to spend a lot of time doing a whole lot of nothing as assignments are intricately detailed, yet horribly structured. I took JMC 302 and would not recommend her.

Dr. Finneman is the definition of tough love. I wanted to write a review after seeing a lot of negative ones. I worked for her in the Eudora Times and although I was insanely stressed at the beginning, by the end I was nothing but grateful. She really teaches you, gives you feedback and trains you. She is a really valuable teacher at KU.

Even though attendance is not technically required, you have to go and take notes or ask a friend to succeed. The class was not structured well and needs to be rethought but it was easy and I didn't spend more than 45 minutes a week on homework. A big group project at the end of the course, its all doable just not any fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Finneman was the strictest and least understanding professor I had during my time at KU. I took JOUR 201 as a journalism elective and was surprised by the amount of work required for a 200 level class. I didn't think it was worth it.

Choose any other elective or teacher, the group projects and individual projects are busy work that waste an incredible amount of time. Ive never had to do so much project work in a class, let alone an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Incredibly hard to deal with and no wiggle room at all on any assignments. Journalism teachers are the best but avoid this one at all costs. She is a very very tough grader and is hard to talk to. The only positive comment is that she will give you a lot of feedback on assignments.

415 is by far the hardest class I've taken at KU. You won't get a lot of clear instructions for the projects, and the grading gets harsher as the semester goes on. Be prepared to throw a lot of things together last minute. It'll help to have friends in the class who can help connect you to sources and proof read your stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This prof gives a lot of outside of class work I.e mandatory field trips that are 45 minutes away from campus. Lectures are somewhat easy to follow but its super fast pace. If you take this class, just know you have to put in countless hours doing interviews with people, gathering sources, and getting constructive feedback from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved taking his class. He's an amazing professor who cares deeply about the deaf community. Quizzes are easy as long as you go to class and try. He also posts videos reviewing all the content. Amazing professor!

Larry is the sweetest professor ever. He cares deeply about the deaf community, as well as making sure that you are learning. He is kind, caring, and compassionate. His demeanor and style of teaching made me want to come to class every day and learn. I adore him, and I wish I could take more classes with him!

He teaches sign language very clearly and patiently. When asked a question, he gives a polite answer, even if he doesn't know the answer. His quizzes are pretty easy. He supplies videos each week of him doing every sign that you can look back on before each quiz. Would definitely take again.
Amazing professor who really cares. He makes learning ASL very easy and enjoyable. Highly recommend taking any classes with him!

Larry is the sweetest professor ever, I wish he could teach all of my classes!! He's nice, understanding, and very funny. No homework, but the way he teaches allows you to learn all 450 signs easily and confidently. Quizzes every 2 weeks which aren't hard and at the end we got to sign with people from the deaf community. Highly recommend him!!!

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! please take this class. He is so nice and thoughtful and will check in on how you are doing. There is no homework, yet he drills the information into your brain so well. He also does not use the textbook and uses his own material which is so much more helpful. He has so many unique ways to practice ASL in class.
I love Larry. Just stay on top of your vocabulary and you'll do great in his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love Love Love - He is great!!!!!

Cannot say enough good things about this course and Larry Finn. He is the most caring and considerate professor I've learned under. He teaches without making you feel dumb and creates the most positive environment to learn in.
Larry is the best teacher I have ever had at KU. He truly cares about his students and his class is so so fun!!
Best professor I have had at KU. Made the class very understandable and was very understanding if you needed to miss or leave early.

I would do anything for this man. He is quite literally the kindest and most caring professor I have ever had and probably ever will. The class was very interesting and the professor was very respectful when integrating deaf culture into the curriculum. No homework other than practicing what we went over in class.
Larry is great! He teaches phenomenally and is very friendly and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have never reviewed a professor before but Larry truly goes above and beyond. He has been my favorite professor so far and I could not say enough nice things about him. He is super sweet and cares about his students. I love his teaching style; there no pressure or signing in front of the class, he just wants everyone to show up and learn ASL.

I took ASL 1 with Larry. He was quite literally the best teacher I have ever had. Larry is adorable and truly wants the best for his students. If I ever had a question, he answered it clearly and promptly. I wish I could have him again for another class in the future. Trust me, you want Larry as your teacher!

Larry Finn is one of the sweetest professors and men I have ever met. The tests for this class are bi-weekly and consist of Larry giving us signs, and us writing the sign on paper. He made the class very engaging, and I think I learned a lot from him. Absolutely loved taking his class!! He is the best.

Larry is one of the best and sweetest professors I have ever had! He really cares about teaching others and loves doing so! He doesn't make class dreadful. While he isn't strict on teaching the ASL form of sentences, he always shows both ASL and CASE forms. Besides, the most important part is just being able to communicate with someone who is deaf.

I loved Larry Finn. He's a great and patient instructor. As long as you show up to class, you'll get an A no problem. He is also very good about letting students make up quizzes if they have to miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Larry is my favorite professor ever. I recommend him to everyone interested in ASL. He is so kind and cares about his students. You will have to come to class every time since that's when you learn everything and it's hard to learn on your own. If you fall behind Larry is always willing to help.

Larry was such a great professor. He knew exactly what his students needed from him. ASL I is super easy as long as you practice the signs and show up to class for new content. You'll never actually be tested on how you sign but rather on if you're able to understand what he signs and if you're able to match the sign with the correct English word.

One of the most caring teachers I have ever met. Really cares about how his students are doing. His class is super easy and an easy A (SPED 501- haven't taken 502) if you show up and do a little practice at home if you need to.  I would recommend this teacher to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very nice. Really cares about his students learning sign language. Does not put you on the spot. Answers all questions. He is very enthusiastic and it makes class fun. Does require attendance and participation(25%) of grade. You will not pass if you skip multiple classes. Since it is a visual language, you have to go to class to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very kind and caring teacher. He does well to inject his knowledge of deaf culture into his lectures and shows a documentary to supplement that. Class has a lot of practice so remembering the signs really isn't as hard as it seems. Will be taking his ASL II class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: His tests are SOOOOO easy. I know I am going to get an "A." Class was fun but I dont feel prepared to go to next class ASL III. He taught English in class and not ASL. Sweet guy but he should be following the curriculum from the textbook.
Larry is the best. He is naturally a great teacher, and is excited to teach. You do have to show up to every class, as attendance is 25% of your grade. But class is fun, so it's worth it.

Larry is an amazing teacher, and he's so sweet. He never makes you feel bad for forgetting a sign, and he is extremely positive and encouraging. He keeps an updated list of vocab online so you don't really even need the book. Class is fun, quizzes are easy, and I have really enjoyed this class. I look forward to taking ASL 2 with him next semester!

Class was easy and so were the tests. However, he does not teach ASL. He is teaching CASE. This is NOT going to help me as I progress through my other ASL classes. If he wants to teach CASE then he should teach a class called Introduction to CASE.

Finn is knowledgable in this field, and delivers the lesson to his students at a beginner's pace. It doesn't matter if the students are first-time ASL students or a little experienced since Finn treats all equally. He doesn't hesitate to help or repeat information that students need assistance on, and encourages in-class participation each class.
Great class! Larry has a passion for what he does and truly cares about his students! Very helpful and always comes prepared.
Great teacher.  He is patient, easy going, and a bit silly.  Don't bother with the textbook, he keeps an updated list of all the vocab you've learned online.  Tests are easy, class is fun.
If you like being asked rhetorical questions that you aren't really supposed to answer for 75 minutes straght you will love his lecture.

I had Professor Tzeggai for Racial and Ethnic Relations. Be prepared to read a lot and listen to him lecture for the entire 75 minutes. Throughout the semester, we had three papers and maybe 3 discussion posts. There weren't many assignments, but he graded the papers heavily. Tzeggai gives good feedback but overall makes the class a bit boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed the readings, and you learn alot from participating in the lectures. Really nice professor too. If you are having trouble, just ask him for help and he would definitely give you advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor made me rethink my major. His readings were extremely long, and his lectures rarely connected to the readings. The assignments were vague, but he was a difficult grader. I would NOT recommend it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great teacher! If you complete the assigned readings, then you will do fine in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Larry is one of my favorite professors ever. He is so sweet and always made sure that all of his students had the opportunity to succeed in this class. With him, learning ASL was actually so easy and fun, and he always made sure you had resources outside of the classroom to improve your progress.

I absolutely loved being in his ASL 1 class! Larry is very kind, he truly cares about every single one of his students and does a great job of making everyone feel welcome in the class. He is a great professor, I have learned a lot about signing and deaf culture in his class. Going to his class is always the highlight of my week!

Professor Finn is the cutest man ever and the sweetest teacher. He is not only extremely patient, but also takes time to individually encourage students throughout the semester. I cannot say enough good things about him.

If you're a quieter or more reserved student, be prepared to stand your ground. Barry has a tendency to single out students he perceives as shy, often making dismissive or belittling comments during critiques. What might seem like “tough love” to some crosses the line into subtle bullying for others.

From what I've heard from other fellow students, there seems to be mixed feelings (some love him, some don't). I do not like his classes at all. I barely learned anything. Unfortunately, if you are taking the illustration & animation program at KU, you are required to take his classes.

Had barry for 3 years now. Best prof I have ever had. He is harsh, blunt, and makes u cry. He doesn't hold your hand, but you grow and you will see it later on. He makes you career-ready, which most professors don't do. As a senior, I feel more prepared because of him. Push for feedback, ask ?, Do the work, reach new heights, and you'll succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If anyone even slightly disagrees with his feedback, it's clear he takes it personally. Barry could benefit from some self reflecting and listen when students have complaints about the projects he puts together. Yes, Barry is clearly a good illustrator, but he is not a good communicator.

I wish Barry would admit which areas of design/illustration he is not knowledgable in. I've seen him feign wisdom in certain art topics, when it's clear he doesn't really know what he is talking about. Also, he's not good at taking criticism directed at his teaching style.

Barry and his projects almost made me lose passion for illustration. Many times, his instructions were very unclear, and gets upset when we fail at tasks he never taught us. I remember back in my senior project, he humiliated me in front of class, berating me for rushing my work. I really tried to respect Barry, but he had zero respect for me.

Probably one of the best professors I've ever had. Even if you're doing something he doesn't know how to give feedback on, he will find a way to give something helpful for you to work on. Very nice and personable, show up and do the work and you're solid.
Got my money's worth, jfc. Talk to him often to succeed. He genuinely loves talking about art, and that includes the art that you make for his class.

It's a love-hate relationship with this class I will be honest. The workload will make you wanna pull your hair out, grading is tough, and critiques aren't always helpful. In the end, though Barry is such a great professor. I have grown so much in his class. Don't be afraid to speak up if you disagree and draw till your hand cramps, is my advice XD
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's very opinionated and his personal taste heavily influences his critique. In a class full of aspiring illustrators, I'd think that he'd be more openminded to different trains of thought. Disappointing. You have no choice but to take him as a professor in this major so I'd recommend avoiding the entire course.

Drawing media with Barry is one of the greatest classes I have taken thus far. He celebrates mark making and stresses thinking before you even touch the page. You'll get out of the class what you put in to the class but Barry will make you want to work hard. The way I see and interpret the world onto my sketchbook is changed for the better.

Barry is a great guy who knows a ton about illustration. Very knowledgable guy who takes time to give feedback in every critique for every student. If he can tell you care about your work he'll try to help you out as much as possible so you can make stuff to the very best of your ability.

I took Barry's sketchbook class. The man has an eye and he knows how to get stuff out of his students. Just like Dick, he expects good work. I found Barry to be very encouraging and insightful, if at times a bit wishy-washy regarding assignments and such. There's a lot to be learned from Barry, and I'm very glad I took the course from him.
No Comments
No Comments

The most depressing and unmotivating teacher I have ever had. I do not exaggerate when I say his classes are a waste of three hours. Weather your work is good or not, your grade simply depends on how much process work you do. Awful, just awful.
whatta babe...his mind will blow your mind
No Comments
No Comments

Absolutely hated this class, we had quizes everyday and the professor would always cancel class to teach via zoom. Didn't learn absolutely anything, I hope no one takes any classes with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely an amazing professor, I learned so much more in Calc II than I had ever expected, and it was a fun and engaging class. You will need to keep up with the material though - no sacrifices there.
Love the teacher, love the class, hate the material!

I took Differential Equations from Professor Bach, now Professor Flaherty, and it was a great class. it was not to hard but I feel like I learned everything I would need.  She really treats you like an adult too, not a student. She's sarcastic and funny so she keeps class entertaining.
She's quite helpful and quite spiffy
No Comments

Online class! Reading is required, recommend taking notes to really understand material. Lecture videos are somewhat short but interesting! No due dates except completing all work before each unit exam, LOVE THAT. Easy to get in contact with professor. Very accommodating!

I am in her winter break section, so this class is extremely fast paced. It is so much reading it is ridiculous. If you want to take notes a chapter can take you hours. Sometimes there is 2 chapters assigned to read over one day and then a supplemental reading. No contact with prof unless you email her. Lots of quizzes. Soooo much reading. Easy tho

Prof. Reed was a really good professor. Her criteria each week was easy, read a chapter and do vocab terms online, watch a lecture module or two each week at 15-30 min each. Module quizzes were easy, the final was easy. Just be sure to take notes on the module as the terms and ideas show on the final. Only one test and that was the final.

A lot of the classwork is online. Blackboard definitions are extremely tedious - 50 each time, often times repeating definitions. Class is not difficult, but will take some time out of your day to look over notes and work on the online homework. Sweet teacher, but do not have your phone out or be talkative during lecture or she will call you out.
I love Flo!!! She has clear guidelines and objectives that make it easy to pass.

Dr. Reed gives out extra credit and she loves being able to! Tests are fairly easy and she makes sure you are well prepared! There is a quiz at the beginning of every class so go and be on time, they are not difficult and require just about no preparation except for doing the Blackboard Definitions. Easy A and great teacher!

Class is an easy A just make sure you attend and take the quizes and do the BB defs., but be prepared to be treated like you're in middle school again. I find it particularly annoying that she continuously would stop class to tell people to put phones away when it wasn't even a distraction to anyone. Otherwise I recommend this course if needed.

This class is an easy A. I highly recommend taking a class with Flo. There are quizzes once a week no test and one paper to write. The only homework is readings from articles she discusses in class unless she sends you home with a take home quiz.

Dr. Reed is the cutest teacher ever. The course is interesting in general, and she keeps it fun and entertaining. There are quizzes every class, but she offers a lot of extra credit to make up for the hard quizzes. I would definately recommend this class. It is an easy A or B, depending on if you put some effort into it!

She was nice and always helpful outside of class but was way too hard of a grader.  Interteaching assignments were a complete waste of time and most people did horrible on them and there are 2 quizzes every week, one of them being a BB quiz that only gets you 1 point, whether it's 5 questions or 40, which is absolutely ridiculous

She changed her way of teaching this class compeletely. It's not hard and the final and midterm are only worth 20 points. You have to go to class because there are quizzes every week but you don't have to read as long as you go to class. Don't buy the book and just look up the blackboard quiz answers on google. Super easy even without trying!

Never, and Never take this course! If you have to, then good luck! The class is so hard and the stuff she talks during the class is harder! The homework are hard too! Everything is Hard, Complicated and BORING!!!!!! This is the worst course Ive ever taken! THE WORST course!!!!!!!!!!!!

She made things more difficult than they needed to be and wasn't really very helpful when questions were asked. She also changed the rules for an assignment everyday so you never knew what she actually wanted from you. Kind of unorganized.

She was so nice! Dr. Reed was very helpful outside of class too! I almost got an A in the class and didnt read at all. All you have to do is scan the book to find the answers for her inter-teach assignments. Just go to class and you will do fine!
she made things harder than what they needed to be.  I absolutly hated this class
D. Reed was probably one of the most unorganized professors. Her assignment were obnoxious and her grading was harsh. Two tests. Midterm and a Final. Overall, I didn't really learn much from her.

This professor was very warm and welcoming whenever I needed help, especially the TA (Tyler E.) too. Most of the notes would come from the lecture online instead of the book but you still needed the book for definitions. The online class had the option to take the exam online or in-person.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great class, great teacher. Would take again (but don't have to, cause it's pretty easy). Helps to have an interest in the topic! There's quite a bit of reading, but never any real homework.

Her lectures were very interesting and the book taught me a lot too. However, I only used the book for our vocabulary quizzes that we have every week. We used our iClickers everyday in class for attendance and easy quizzes. She is very lenient and helps a lot if you ask questions. She's very approachable. I loved this class.

Dr. Reed made this online class very informative with her online modules. Her powerpoints and video lectures were engaging, understandable and a great compliment to the textbook. I also enjoyed how each module was not just a powerpoint, but sometimes included video studies so it wasn't too boring. Her quizzes and tests were always fair and were ove

This is an easy class but it was frustrating at times. She gave unclear expectations for assignments and talked to students like preschoolers. There were multiple times I asked for clarification on a certain topic and she talked in circles around it.  Overall if you like being taught like you're a little kid this class is the one for you.

This class was amazing because Flo gives you a ton of opportunities for extra credit. Do the blackboard definitions, glance over them before the next class, and you'll ace the three-question quizzes at the beginning of each lecture. Tests are similar (but not identical) to the practice test. Don't text in class. Overall, easy and interesting class.

Flo is a wonderful teacher! She is engaging and easy to understand. She has clear outlines of what she expects and is ALWAYS willing to help and answer questions. Subject of both classes were interesting, Intro to Child Development and Issues in Parenting. I have recommended her to many friends.
She was really helpful and knowledgeable about the field and was willing to help students and answer questions.

I took this as a graduating senior (within the ABS major) and it was a total joke.  Biggest waste of time.  Attendance is mandatory and counts for the majority of your grade.  If this is an optional course, opt out! You will learn nothing here that you haven't already learned elsewhere (namely in ABSC 100/101).

Brian Flanagin was a great professor! Although it is a little hard to get into the hang of what he's expecting, he's very understanding and helpful. Definitely great professor that I would consider taking again!

Brian Flanagin is the worst professor that I have ever had. His lectures rarely relate to the material covered on the exams. If you aren't fluent, don't take this class. He holds all his student to the standard that would be expected of a native speaker. Do not take his class, it isn't worth the stress it causes.

Brian was awesome in preparing us to read and translate French on our own with a dictionary and he would find French articles from the various academic disciplines of the students. There was never any vocabulary on exams that were not in lectures or exercises. I learned a ton about French. Brian is easygoing and an outstanding teacher.

Brian is an awful teacher. His lectures were confusing and often pointless. Powerpoints never were in sync with the text book. Quizzes and exams were full of vocabulary terms that we did not learn in class. Brian never seemed to grasp the idea that his students were from other disciplines. Just terrible.
fair and helpful

He is such a nice guy! The course was hard, and the online homework website is frustrating, but I enjoyed the class overall. I emailed Brian several times and went to his office hours as well. He was always quick in his replies and very willing to help. He is one of my favorite teachers and I wish I could continue to learn from him in French 240!

Brian was nice when it came to asking for help and wasn't condescending. However, it was rarely clear what was being asked for in class and his tests are deceivingly hard. If you ask for help on the test he becomes extremely moody. I only took this class for my major, obviously grammar isn't that fun. I suppose he did his best with the dry material

Brian is the best TA that I have had during my four semesters in French. He really knows what he is doing and he doesn't make you feel stupid when you don't understand it! He is willing to help you out if you need it and he is great getting the class to get to know each other too. I hated learning French, but I really liked his class!

Fleissner was a fantastic professor, which in the math department is hard to come by. His teaching is easy to follow and the tests are EXACTLY like the study guide for which he provides the worked out solutions. He can go from extremely pleasant to frustrated in a matter of seconds, but it's worth it. Very easy class.
Can't say I learned much, but I did get an A. Tests are very similar to study guides.

His teaching is not understandable unless you already know what he is teaching. Everything I did in his class was based on previous knowledge or was explained by a tutor. When you go to his office he expects you to figure it out yourself and treats you like you're dumb. Also, expect no help from KU if you have problems with him or anyone.

Super awkward which makes class pretty funny. Easy homework and tests, really wants you to do well. Study guide is identical to the test. He speaks fluent english which is also a plus. SOOOO much easier than MATH 115. I had a tutor for this class and easily got over 100%!

I feel awkward for him.  I had calc 2 in high school, so the class seems super easy, but he's not helpful to those who don't understand.  Sometimes he thinks the whole class is stupid and overteaches, then other times he forgets to explain difficult concepts.  He's totally unrelatable, and very bipolar. We're 2 weeks behind other calc 2 classes.

He's kind of a dork and you can tell math is his world with all his jokes. But overall it was easy. He gives study guides before every test that are identical to the exam, except for the numbers. Really easy to get a good grade if you understand the material.

You must have a strong knowledge of exponents and logs because he loves to test on it, and get a good seat in class, because his handwriting is horrible, and attend class regularly because it will help having extra examples to study for the homework and test. He has extensive office hour though and will answer any ?'s.

Honestly, I have only been in his class for 2 weeks.  I came out of calculus I with not much understanding, and he treats me like im an idiot.  I goto his class, read the text, and every time I goto him in office hours, he treats me like im a nuisance.  He acts like im taking up his time, and is not helpful at all!  Bad teacher!

A pretty understandable teacher; doesn't stray too far from the book, and (best of all!) his tests are nearly identical to the study guides. He is a little tense, though, and tends to get frustrated with students easily.

Fleissner is a REALLY fun teacher. He ran into the wall literally ever class period---a real awkward and stumbly guy. exactly what you would expect from a math nerd. nonetheless, he's a lot of fun. I love Diff EQ with him, and i'd definitely take another class. tests are just like study guide! he's always happy to help
Sometimes his lectures are a bit scattered, but he's always happy to clarify.  Funny in a bumbly way, and tends to give in to the students' requests.  I enjoyed this class!

HAHAHAHA. And that's all I have to say about that. Okay, I'll expound. Totally wacky off-the-wall goofy scatterbrained nutjob who's happens to be a kickass math teacher. I've got him again for 220 and he's one of the reasons I'm excited to go back to school. Helpful, fair, and knows the subject matter. A++++
mm

Crazy old man that makes the class easy!  He's pretty scatter brained, and is a little confusing becuase he never says the same thing he writes, but the class is easy.  Study guide is almost identical to the test.  No final, unless you want to retake a test.  Just do the homework.
amazing professor! he is a crazy but he is really fun and makes the class interesting!

Total screw-ball, but really knows his math.  Always says off-the-wall things in the middle of lecture that make you laugh and shake your head at the same time.  Can be confusing in his lectures at times, but whenever he fully explains it he does it very well.  Nice guy to boot.
"Sex is more productive than drugs; you get more done afterwards."  I swear he said this in class one day as the moral to his life's story.  And that about sums up the class.
I love how he teach, the paradise is for few people intelligent like him.I hope in the future and mental power.

Lots of homework to do, much more than the other same classes. If you do not have enough time to finish the homework, you will lose lots of points. The in-class exams are much harder than the mid-term and final and he won't give curve.(Although I got good enough grades in mid-term and final, I still got B because of the homework.)

He is totally worthless.  He lectures as if you already know the material he's teaching, and he covers material twice as fast as the other sections do.  Also, HE DOESN'T GIVE PARTIAL CREDIT.  In a math class.  His tests are much harder than the mid-term and final.  Avoid if you want to actually learn Calc.
His exams and homework are much harder than the final or mid-term. Be prepared to really be challenged.

he was the reason i had to drop the course! spends class time talking about stuff he expects you to know already and makes you feel stupid. and doesn't give partial credit on test cause "i don't feel you deserve the points if you didn't attempt it right" AVOID!

He is the sole reason that I started skipping classes.  He is a condescending jerk.  From the few classes I attended, he went out of his way to prove everyone in the class to be wrong and stupid.  I got an A, but not because of easiness or being well-taught.

This guy really knows his stuff.  If you get in his class, you have to work hard to keep up, but it pays off.  The students who stick with it are the best in the department.  The students who don't make it blame him, but it's really their fault for not working.  Anyone who tries can make it.
Great teacher.  Students who take his class generally know more than any other class, including honors.  Anyone who takes his class should be prepared to work a lot though.
The worst TA ive ever had.
Was not clear!

Do not take his class if you have no prior knowledge of the course. I had to use my highschool notes and review sessions to get through. Handwriting is horrible, and he doesn't explain what he's doing. He is lenient on his tests though.
Does not use examples and expects you to already know everything.
If at all possible, DO NOT get Flavio Brondi as a teacher.  He's condesending and basically calls people stupid if they don't understand
No Comments

Teacher is exceptional at math, but his teaching comes off a bit skewed. Handwriting and clarity are not up to par. If you can decipher his illegibile handwriting and accent, you will be able to understand this class.
No Comments
very helpful teacher. always available for his students for explanation.

This teacher was not very clear, not very organized, and all around not very impressive.  I had even taken Calc before (did not have much trouble) and found this teaching style to be difficult.  Although only a T.A., not recommended.  AWESOME on a personal level though

least favorite professor i've ever had. can't use technology (particularly discussion boards), has ta's but doesn't let them help. responds to emails but never understands what you're asking. love the topic of the class but the way he teaches is so pretentious.

Gives incredible lectures, although sometimes has trouble finishing them before the end of class. Very entertaining to watch and listen to. Also hot in a weird way. He assigns a lot of reading but all of it is helpful to the class and pretty interesting if you're actually invested.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Its almost impossible to get an A even if you try super hard! I had asked for feedback for papers, and used the writing center and still received a very low grade. The class also requires lots of discussion so stay away if you dont like that!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funny, kind, and captivating guy. Angry White Male Studies had amazingly interesting content, and he delivered it well. Not super hard to get an A, but there is a decent amount of reading. Also extra credit opportunities! Final paper, discussion board, 3 essays for the class. Prep outlines for final paper (free points) compose most of paper's grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible communication, very confusing grading methods, and horribly confusing. Nothing was clear on what would be graded or how it would be done. I could tell by the very few emails we received that he wanted us to have a fun time, but his grading was so harsh and unclear. If you're expecting to get above a 95% on anything just forget it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of reading needs to be done to even understand lectures and discussions. Work load is manageable, but grades are determined by 2 writing assignments, final, and some minor points for participation/attendance. Lectures can be boring at times, but they help you understand readings. Overall, nice and funny guy, just be ready to put the work in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Forth loves the topic, but it's 3 straight hours of lecture, no discussion, about sometimes lofty topics. Heavy reading assignments that are rarely discussed in class; graduate requirements have twice the reading. One 12-15 page research paper due at the end of the semester, and a 6-pager (using readings) due at midterms. Time consuming, not hard.
Smart and hott. Also it dies matter who your TA is. Overall listen well take notes
I loved Forth. He peaked my interest in the books we were reading, I think he's a real interesting professor.

Do not take this class with forth, his lecture is dry, dull, and unhelpful. lecture slides consist mostly of pictures which does not help with learning the material, he tends to ramble and not clearly state what he is trying to say. wastes class time by playing movie clips that have nothing to do with the material.
Very boring class do not take it unless u have to. It used to be a requirement but no longer is at KU.

Be prepared to read an entire book every single week.  Lecture is pointless because he goes off on tangents that have nothing to do with the class.  I quit going after a month and will still pass with a good grade.  Just make sure you get a good TA and go to discussion.

Hardest class I had all semester.  You read 1 book a week, plus textbook, and weekly assignment.  2 papers, midterm, and final.  Lecture was dry and boring.  Discussion was fine but depends on your TA.  If you can, I would find a better, less boring, professor for this class.

With this class it matters more who your TA is rather than who the professor is. Make sure you like your TA b/c they grade the exams. Go to lecture, he gives extra credit typically when few people are there. The patterns book gives great summaries of the books you're supposed to read. I got by with a B just from reading Patterns and going to class.
Lecture really didn't help with exams, class was almost to big to really get personal help. A LOT of reading required. Had no interest in this class but it was required.

Dr. Forth helps make the dull topic of Western Civ somewhat interesting. He integrates art, movies, and other philosophers to give a full-story picture of what the given literature is about. He speaks in a monotonous voice, but if you pay attention through it, he is actually very interesting.

Dr. Forth doesn't get excited about the subject and speaks in a rather monotone voice, so if you have ADHD, it can be pretty hard to follow him. He gives a study guide with a list of terms and questions, which include the ones that are on the test; although, you don't know for sure which ones will be on it.
Hard voice to get used to, he gives you all the lecture notes so you dont have to go.  2 Essay tests and 2 major essays is all the class is made up of.
Smart and hot.

This is about Forth and not the TAs: he is a baller. For real, he's a cool guy, he showed clips from Monty Python and Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure. He tries to relate the subject matter in a unique and entertaining way, and is genuinely interested in what he's teaching, which helped interest me. I got stuck with a tough TA though--beware Kenagy

He has a voice that you definitely have to get used to so it doesn't put you to sleep. He is available but you can tell it throws him off if anyone asks a question in lecture despite him asking for questions (??) Class is required for lib arts majors so just make friends with your GTA (they grade EVERYTHING) and find out what they want. tests=HARD!

He gives good lectures, but if you have the outline in front of you they are really boring because he doesn't add anything to it at all. Because of this, I rarely go to class. The class is informative, but I don't personally find it interesting. The tests aren't that hard and he tells you what will be on them. I can usually get by without reading.
