Good prof, he was really interesting and could be very funny. His lectures are online so you don't have to go but I usually did because he was fun. The tests are long but not terribly hard. Good class! I would recommend him. Kinda hot in his own way too!

I hate western civ, just as a precursor to this review. Forth's lectures were not bad, but he put all his notes online. I stopped going to class cause his notes were what he lectured on. He also had a habit of turning the lights way down, and I would inevitably fall asleep. Other than being a boring subject for me, he wasnt a bad teacher.
Very intelligent man with a real passion for the subject, unfortunately, his GTAs teach the bulk of the class and your grade depends entirely on their own personal grading scale.

He is one of the most intelligent people I have ever met. He is clearly very knowledgeable on the subject, but because of that, assumes that you are as well. His lectures are informative, though slow, and rarely inspired. If you enjoy the material, he is great, and I could not recommend him more. If you find it slow though, this could be bad news.
No Comments
go to lecture. he gives a lot of pg numbers w/ quotes that help on the papers. he gives a long list of possible exam questions, so its a lot to study but is easy

Dr. Foster ROCKS. One of the most entertaining classes I've ever taken. He's a super nice guy, very motivational and really stands by his students. I loved the group project we did and had a great time throughout. Highly recommend him.

Foster's class is extremely easy. I got a 110% in his class. He is a genuine guy and a cool guy. The class is supposed to be 75 minutes and the longest we were in class was 40 minutes for a guest speaker. He is a nice guy but I didn't learn very much. Class is just how to do the assignments. He also never lectured. He has too many guest speakers!
Easy professor. Just listen to instructions and you'll receive a good grade for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such an easy class. Professor Foster is a good dude too. One hw assignment a week and thats it
Professor did not care to address concerns at any point. Is very defensive. I would not recommend.

This woman sucked. Had a surface level type of kindness but hated even the idea that she could be wrong about anything. Very narcissistic and “I'm special” type of personality. Would not recommend this to anyone. Please find a different professor to take this course with.

I loved Dr. Forbush! She cares about her students and has interesting lectures. She keeps us engaged and having fun while learning using Top Hat and a bunch of cool demos. Definitely take this class. You wont regret it!

Dr. Forbush is passionate about her work & teachings, however, I found her to be quite condescending & extremely difficult to reach outside of class. In short, my impression of her was that of someone who thinks very highly of themselves & gives little regard to thoughts or ideas from others.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: (Taking Eating Disorders with her). She is very passionate and engaging, even in a 3-hour long class it feels shorter than some of my other classes. Her tests are easy if you fill out study guide thoroughly. Very hard to get a hold of outside of class

She's awesome! Such a good instructor who really knows her stuff and wants to help. Go to lecture and get the tophat points because they are worth more than you think. Do the extra credit and you'll be fine.

She knew about the subject and you could tell she was actually interested in teaching. Funny in lecture. Participation points came from coming to the lecture and answering questions online throughout the class. Gave a good amount of extra credit opportunities which you should take since the tests are somewhat hard.

Lectures kept us involved and she made them interesting. Both her and the Tas were very approachable. The class was hard but doable if you try and do the work. It was by far my favorite class I have taken.
Jana is an amazing professor and such a nice person. If you are taking her class, take the time to get to know her. Visit her office hours or talk to her after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Jana is one of the best professors at KU! She has a passion for teaching, and she really cares about every one of her students. She brings in professionals who are willing to work with students, and I landed an internship through one of her speakers.
She's great, just don't miss any days and you'll be good!

I took her class last semester. She is a fantastic instructor with enthusiasm for teaching and real world experiences. Jana is very kind and takes active action to help her students to become future business management leaders.
Jana was one of the most fun professors I have had in a long time. Even though you have to turn your computer off and pay attention, I actually learned some stuff. Hope to see her again.
She was great
Jana is a very good professor, but this class can get difficult if you don't keep up with it. Reading and paying attention during lectures is super important. So is participating in your groups
Lots of group works and helpful guest speakers. Quizzes can be tough but its open note so just take good notes and youll be fine. Jana is a great professor overall.

She is so sweet, cares about her students, and the class is fun! Great teacher and great course. Ensure you read before each class for the quizzes, and be prepared to talk in your small group every class.
Jana cares so much about all of her students. She does a great job with making her lectures engaging. This is one of my favorite classes I have taken at KU.

Jana is one of my favorite professors at KU! She really cares about her students and wants the best for every one of them. Make sure you participate in class and do the readings outside of class so you come prepared for in class quizzes. There are great opportunities to meet guest speakers in this class and network. Jana is a must have professor!!

Jana is one of the best professors I've had at KU! Getting to know her, she cares about all of her students and makes her lectures engaging. She has tons of great advice for real world situations. Just be ready for the quizzes - need to read the chapters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jana is a wonderful professor! You can tell she cares about each of her students and their experience in her class. Although the class is fun and engaging, you have to continue your learning outside of the classroom because there is a lot of info she teaches and expects us to understand. Nonetheless, I definitely would recommend this class!

Jana is easily one of the best teachers at the business school. This class has a heavy workload and is kind of difficult but is very useful. Be prepared for quizzes each class and to work in teams. Would definitely recommend this class!

Prof Fitchett's class is fun and engaging. The quizzes can be tough if you don't prep, but using Unstuck study alongside the textbook really helps. Definitely worth taking, just stay on top of the work.

She is one of those professors that leave an impact on you. She is very caring and wise. Her selection of guest speakers is very interesting giving you an experience of multiple industries. From attendance to finals grading everything is explained well and followed until the last day of the course so there's no confusion.
Jana is a must-take for MGMT. She has the coolest connections and best guest speakers and somehow has relevant experience in every single area. One of the business school's finest.
Amazing and caring professor. 5/5

Jana is a great person that cares about her students! The activities that you do in class are super fun. The only complaint that I have is that the quizzes are purely based off of what you read in the book and sometimes have nothing to do with what you actually talk about in class. If you read and go to class you can easily at least get a B.

One of my favorite professors that I've taken a class with at KU! She cares about all her students and is able to make the class enjoyable each day. The quizzes can be tough if you don't prepare enough for them. The same case goes for the exams.

Janas class was super fun and I loved all of the guest speakers that she invited to class. Using the smartbooks will help you prepare for the quizzes/exams. The class is split up into groups of 6 and you get the opportunity to socialize/discuss often during class which was awesome. Would take again. :)
I love Jana! She cares so much!
Professor Fitchett is a great teacher who shows up to work everyday with an enthusiastic demeanor, her class is structured in way that makes getting A's and B's achievable but, requires hard work.
Go to class, prepare for quizzes, take advantage of guest speakers they are there for a reason, be ready to work in groups.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great teacher one of the best at KU
Good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was awesome and she is the coolest teacher ever but if you want a good grade in the course you have to put the work in.

Jana is a great teacher but her class is not an "easy A". Many of my classmates assumed the final would be super easy and got Cs and Ds on it since they didn't study. I studied and got a B, which I am happy with.
One of my favorite classes so far!
Great class, learned a lot about management and enjoyed hearing from guest speakers

Jana is one of my favorite professors I've had. She clearly cares about her students and makes class very engaging. The guest speakers are great and there are extra credit opportunities. The quizzes were the only thing that brought my grade down, so take good notes (you can use them on the quiz). I wish I could take all of my classes with Jana!
she is great

Jana is a fantastic professor- she is kind, energetic and has clear expectations. This course is not challenging on a conceptual level, it just requires effort and attendance (make sure to do the readings every time, the quizzes will make or break your course grade). In my opinion, it is easily manageable with harder courses.

She really cares about students and she makes sure class is a fun place to be at. One of my favorite professors at KU. She has guest speakers that come to talk about what we learned. She put us in group of 6 to have people to be friends and talk about lecture topics with.

My favorite professor so far because she really care about students and tries to make the class fun. Guest speaker reflections are easy points and quizzes are open notes. One mid term and one final but all MC. Assigned to groups of about 6 people the beginning of the semester for scenario based discussions over the chapters.
Amazing professor who really cares about her students.
Great teacher! Nothing else to say but you will enjoy this class (though there is a bit of busy work).
My favorite class I have taken at KU, provides so much more than just the fundamentals of MGMT. Jana goes out of her way to ensure the most positive classroom environment and learning experience.
She is without a doubt the best professor I have ever had. She makes learning fun and engaging. I wish she taught all my classes.

Jana is my favorite professor at KU and if you take her class you'll see why. She's built a fun and interactive culture within her class and truly cares for her students. You can tell she is very passionate about her job through her kind and energetic spirit she brings to every class. She's very approachable and easy to talk too! HIGHLY RECOMMEND

I highly recommend taking Jana for MGMT 310; she is kind, caring, and genuinely is invested in your career development and personal well being. She is an absolutely incredible professor and I am grateful to have learned so much from her!

Professor Fitchett is hands down the best Management professor at KU. She is reliable, enthusiastic, inspirational, and an incredible professor. She made me passionate about the MGMT program at KU and got me connected with great industry leaders throughout the class. She is a great asset to the school of business and hope to have her again!

Overall, I highly recommend Professor Fitchitt's class to anyone who is looking for a challenge and is motivated to learn. If you put in the work you'll come away with a deep understanding of the subject matter and a great sense of accomplishment.

Jana Fitchett rocks. If you have to take MGMT 310 take it with Jana. She's understanding of students and will work with you if you ever need help. She is funny and understands we are people not just students. She also brings in guest speakers that are actually interesting and relatable. Definitely the best professor I have had at KU so far.

Jana Fitchett is hands down the best professor I have had in college. It is so obvious how much she cares about her students and would do a nothing for the students that actually reach out and ask for help. The class is very manageable and as long as you show up you will do well. Jana is one of those professors that you want in your corner.

Professor Fitchett is simply INCREDIBLE! Her course was tough because the content was heavy at times because there is so much that should be covered, but it's a great balance! She does a great job facilitating discussions and group projects in class and it's by far the BEST professor that I have taken at KU especially in Cap Fed 1111.

Jana's class was one of my favorites I have taken from KU throughout all my time here. The guest speakers were my favorite part. Getting to hear from so many successful people and connect with them was a really special opportunity! Class was awesome and I recommend anyone who takes MGMT 310 to try and get into Jana's class.

I literally LOVED Jana. Her class was literally the reason why I switched my major from marketing to management. She literally is one of my favorite professors I've ever had at KU so if you get a chance to take her class, DO IT. The coursework was so easy and I loved every guest speaker she brought in.

She is extremely kind and genuinely cares about her students. I really enjoyed her lectures, they were very interactive and I learned a lot from her- my favorite professor at KU and I will always remember her!

Jana is a professor that truly cares about her students. She comes to class every day excited to further her students knowledge and is supportive in many aspects. She engages her students in lectures so classes are interesting and go over smoothly. Attend class and you will be just fine in this class!

I am appalled to see all the high ratings I've seen on this page. It is very clear that she doesn't actually know any of the content she teaches, as every single lecture is a copy/paste of the McGraw-Hill lectures she was given. In an ethics lecture, she bragged about going to the house of a former, pregnant employee to scream at them for quitting.

Jana is my favorite professor at KU and if you take her class you'll see why. She has built a fun and interactive culture within her class and truly cares for her students. You can tell she is very passionate about her job through her kind and energetic spirit she brings to every class. She is also very approachable and easy to talk too!
Very engaging class. Can get repetitive, but she gives it 100%. Graded "4" on difficulty because lack of participation will hurt you. Homework and tests are manageable.

Jana Fitchett is my favorite professor at KU! Her lectures are amazing, she truly cares about her students, and she knows more about her field than anyone I know. Effort and participation are necessary for her class, but if you care, you will do well.
Janalee Fitchett is an amazing professor who bring great energy to every lecture. Wish I could take her class over and over again.

Jana is an amazing professor, she cares deeply about each of her students. Her classes are the right amount of difficult without pushing you over the edge. I think she handles this fine line perfectly, she understands her students and is always wanting to help out however she can. I 10/10 recommend her as a professor.
Phenomenal professor that cares tremendously about her students!
Jana has a lot of experience in management so it helps that she can relate so personally to the material taught in class. I really enjoyed taking this class and felt like it was very engaging.
awesome teacher
Jana was such an intelligent person! If you pay attention it will be a great class for you, my favorite part was the group project at the end of the semester!
I learned a lot about entrepreneurship. Jana is a great teacher and is very passionate.
Jana is a great teacher! It will be tough if you do not show up to class! If you work hard and pay attention you will learn a lot!

The best professor and role model at KU! Professor Fitchett makes class very fun and interactive. I personally challenged with the in class quizzes, but thankfully they were open note. You should definitely take this class with her, you won't regret it!!

Professor Fitchett is very kind and wants the best for all students. In ENTR 410 you work on a big group project and she challenges and will make you redo things occasionally, but she wants you to do your best and is willing to help all the time! She is the BEST!
Super helpful cares about her students, and works make class a fun environment.

Jana is the absolute best! I've had her for 3 classes and wish I could take more. She makes class entertaining and engaging! She has so much real experience that she ties in with the lesson and truly inspires people. She's super approachable and easy to talk to and very understandable.
Jana is my FAVORITE professor here at KU and I am so thankful for every moment I get with her! If you EVER have the opportunity to take a class with her, DO IT! She is such an amazing person!

Professor Fitchett is an outstanding professor that goes above and beyond the call of duty. She did a phenomenal job of handling Covid-19 protocols by spacing each student out 6ft apart and always requiring masks to be worn. I highly recommend taking this memorable class as Professor Fitchett is one of the best professors at KU!

Really enjoyed MGMT 310 with Professor Fitchett. She is super kind, approachable, and always willing and able to help with anything you need. You can also tell she has real-world experience in management roles at big companies, making her very qualified to teach the class.

Professor Fitchett has without a doubt become one of my favorite professors. Her MGMT 310 class is fun/interactive, and she spends a lot of time going over real-world examples and personal experiences. You are expected to read the weekly chapter and will be quizzed over the material. Guest speakers were brought in almost weekly which I found great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Mrs. Fitchett is my favorite professor at KU! She is personable, caring, and she has a positive energy. She even makes an effort to talk to me individually each class, which I really appreciate. I 100% recommend taking any class she teaches. I took her BUS110 class. Her lectures were helpful, relevant, and she really kept students engaged.

Professor Fitchett is is truly renowned at KU and for good reasons. She teaches applicable lessons and expects a lot out of her students, but is always incredibly fair. She is very approachable and I highly recommend building a relationship with her. I took MGMT 310 with her and her guest speakers and lessons are fantastic!

Jana is all-around wonderful. She truly cares about providing quality education to her students. Taking her for any class is well worth your time and money. I looked forward to coming to ENTR 410 and was able to pull many valuable lessons from her lectures. As a student, you will get out of this class as much as you put into it.

Overall, I thought she was interactive and fun to be around, but it didn't feel like she respected COVID protocols. Students were spread out to social distance, but she would sit down in chairs directly next to students that were supposed to be left empty and rarely enforced restrictions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jana has become one of my favorite professors overnight. She is kind caring and goes out of her to make classes enjoyable even in the morning.

Jana was super nice this class is fairly easy there was no tests just assignments and attendance. As long as you show up and participate you can get an A in this class. She made it really interesting by still having guest speakers to com speak.

Jana is a fantastic professor. Her ENTR 410 course is by no means easy. She makes you work hard on your business plan by always providing constructive feedback! She is also not a spoon-feeder, she wants you to think critically about your business plan and encourages you to ask questions every class. Take Jana's class if you truly want to grow.
The class is heavily based on discussion with peers and is super fun when effort is put in!!

Jana is an amazing prof and one of my favorites here at KU! She makes sure you learn the material by making the class a little more difficult but everything you learn, you are going to use post graduation! I would recommend MGMT 310 to any undergrad and especially Jana who goes the extra mile each day in class to make sure youre growing!

You work with a group throughout the entire semester of about 5 people which can be strange at first, but once you get into the flow of things and get to know your group it can be one of the best classes. One of the things you do as a group is compare two competitive businesses in town with your group which I thought was a great project.

I wish Jana taught more classes. I would enroll in them all! She is phenomenal. Arguably the best teacher at the KU School of Business. Jana is funny, kind, and engaging. If you skip class, you won't perform well. I feel equipped from her class. Ready to transfer my knowledge from MGMT 310 to the real world!!

Jana is amazing. She is super understanding and cares for her students. She is willing to chat with you outside of classroom and makes sure her students are doing great. Her assignments and projects are challenging but she will help walk you through them as long as you are willing to learn. The materials are not dry and helpful for your future.

Her lectures are extremely interactive and it was truly a joy going to the class everyday. She also goes out of her way to help students. I lost my internship due to COVID-19 and the first person I contacted was Jana. She referred me to some companies and I ended up getting an internship from my connection with her! She went above and beyond!

Jana is the sweetest teacher. I respect her so much. She made me WANT to show up for class. You will do wonderfully in the class if you show up and participate. Her expectations are clear and not too burdensome. 10/10 recommend taking this class with Jana.

Jana is one of my absolute favorite teachers. She is so knowledgeable and pulls from her personal/real life experience as a professional- which is both helpful and interesting! Jana cares about her students and assigns things that are both thought provoking and applicable. I have enjoyed getting to know Jana inside and outside of class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jana is the best professor I have had at KU. She cares about her students and will work with you to ensure that you are having a great experience in her class. The guest speakers that she brings in provide great insight for future entrepreneurs. You will be challenged at times, but will walk away learning more than you could have imagined.

Amazing professor who really cares about her students. Do the work, participate, and study for tests and you'll be fine. Tests can be tough but it's made up with lots of extra credit opportunities. There are 8 pop quizzes (open-note) throughout the semester so don't skip and make sure to take notes. She is very nice/smart and wants you to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Jana is an amazing teacher who makes you work for your grade, especially because the majority of points received in the class come from a cumulative final group project. She is super enthusiastic and always willing to help. Best teacher ever!!!

I took this course for my Business Admin major since I had Jana for MGMT 310 and absolutely loved her. This course is pretty straight forward and as long as you show up and do the work, you should do well. Class is entertaining and gives lots of real world examples. She's one of my favorite professors at KU and is hilarious and caring. Great class!
shes amazing, show up and youll get an A

No negatives from me. Do the work- show up, be attentive and study the study guides for the exams and you should be fine. Jana is a great inspirational person. Make sure you show up on time. If you have any questions, just text her or go to her office hours (by appointment) and she will help you. I really got to enjoy teamwork more because of her.
I had this class at 8 am and Jana made it so interesting it wasn't even hard to get up for this class. She is an outstanding teacher.

Fitchett is fantastic. Took her MGMT 310 course. Fitchett cares about her students, brings a smile & energy to every class, & wants to students to take away valuable leadership skills. There are Pop Quizzes- & tests makes up a decent amount of your grade. YOU WONT SUCCEED IN THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T SHOW UP. But she's the best prof in Capfed

I was told to take Jana's class my a classmate of mine and was nervous because it was an 8am..I am not a morning person but Jana's teaching style made it enjoyable to show up to class. Lots of group work and participation so you need to be at class. She changed our reading quizzes halfway through to attendance after the class voted on it. Take her!
Best Teacher Ever!

Jana is awesome. There is no ambiguity in her classes, as she is very clear with expectations, and will always give feedback if you ask. ENTR 410 only had one exam this semester, but that doesn't mean its an easy class. You have to work hard on the creation of a business plan and other case studies to earn a good grade. I recommend the class.
Great teacher, really cares about her students. If you show up and put in work you will get a good grade. This class has real life application and I would highly recommend it to anyone.

Jana is an awesome teacher. She makes class worth going to and so much fun. She makes sure the content actually pertains to real life and teaches you things you can actually use in life. She is so funny and caring about her students. She does a lot to make sure every student who puts effort in the class is successful. I loved all her classes.

One of my favorite professors and she is always there to help! Part lecture, part group work. Semester long project so have to show up to work with group. Have to work hard for the project but really rewarding. Would recommend.
I believe it is actually MGMT 310, but the class was great. Jana is a great professor and you should absolutely take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jana is awesome- take her class, no questions asked. You will learn something and not have to work over the top difficult. Do IT.

Really enjoyed this class, Jana did a great job of ensuring that not only were students able to learn, but the material was not overly challenging either. A fun class where not only did we learn, but it wasn't over the top hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great Teacher

Hands down one of the best professors on campus. She's amazing and her class is too. All you need to do is attend class, do the assigned readings (really easy), write notes from those readings and you can use them on all quizzes. Final is super easy, just pay attention during her review session.

This was hands-down one of the best classes I've ever taken. It was a big time commitment, especially for our business plan. We had to do plenty of interviewing, research, and our ideas even got rejected a few times. It's a tough class, but you can do it if you attend and participate. If you're passionate about business, this class is a must!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very very hard class indeed. Why? B/c it requires more than rote memory - relies on people skills and being able to work together. She teaches what no professor nor textbook has done and that is teamwork trumps. Business THRIVES when teams win - not memorizing test answers. The greatest prof. at KU, hands down! Must take, but be prepared. Not easy

Jana is AMAZING! She is hands down the best professor I have had at KU thus far. She is super approachable and cares about every student. The class structure has a lot of group discussion, you MUST participate in class! Jana will make you work hard to get an A, but as long as you put the effort in, you will do great in her class!

Jana is an outstanding professor! She goes the extra mile and is always available to her students. That said, there is a lot of work required for her classes, but it is completely manageable. I have learned so much in both ENTR 410 and MGMT 310.

Jana is my favorite teacher at KU. I've taken three courses with her, including ENTR 410, MGMT 310, and ENTR 480. In all of these classes, it's evident that she genuinely enjoys what she does, and she makes class fun. The workload is not excessive, but Jana does make students put in the work to receive an A. I definitely recommend taking her class.

Jana is my favorite professor at KU. She's engaged and actively tries to get to know all of her students. She always has a smile on and loves to make jokes in class. She's by far the coolest teacher (I've taken shots with her at the wheel) and truly wants you to succeed. Show up and participate and you will easily get an A.

Jana Fitchett hands down no questions asked the best teacher I have ever had!!! She gets to know all of her students and is always trying to help students get the best grades possible. She is always happy and smiling, she puts the class in the best mood. BEST TEACHER EVER!

Professor Fitchett was beyond EXCELLENT. I have gained knowledge about management that I know I can and will apply towards my career. She is very accommodating to her students needs. You will never see her frown, she is always smiling so bright. If I ever get a chance to take her class again, I would, in a heart beat.
Jana is definitely one of the best professors at this University, and probably around the Nation.

Jana is a wonderful teacher and an all around great person.  But you must complete readings before each class in order to be prepared for random quizzes, and group work every day requires conscious effort, as well as several group projects.  Don't slack off or it'll be tough to get the grade you want. The material is great for the business world.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Jana is by far my favorite teacher I have had at KU!  I have taken two classes with her and have loved them both!  She keeps everyone engaged in her lectures and enjoys her job!  Overall she is a great teacher and I would highly recommend taking every class she teaches!

Jana is one of the best teachers KU has to offer. She makes it a point to get to know her students. I have found her to be inspirational, hilarious, and an amazing lecturer. I had to work for my A in her Entrepreneurship 480 class. It was not easy as she required the reading of two books, extensive studying of taxes, and more. Overall, I recommend.

Love Jana!! Honestly one of the best teachers I have had at ku. You have to do the work in the class to get an A which makes it kinda hard but she is very understanding and wants everyone to pass! You will love her

She is a great a rigorous teacher that has respect for all of the students she teach. The test are hard but if you study and go to class you should be fine. It's a great class to attend if you study the material and participate then you end with a A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Group activities are an everyday activity, while attendance is not mandatory there are 10 pop quizzes throughout the semester that are random so not coming can be detrimental if you miss the pop quizzes. Only a few projects outside of class. If you show up, pay attention and skim the book you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Jana is an awesome teacher! She is probably my favorite teacher at KU, but get ready for group projects. She is very adamant on group involvement, although the group projects are not too bad. There are quizzes, test are pretty tough, and you must read the book.

Required to attend all classes, but one of the most worthwhile, 'actually important in life' classes. Guest speakers from all different companies and backgrounds with great advice in at least half the classes (notes required, but awesome). Cool field trips to breweries and such. Tests/quizzes over book, but if you read it, you can get a good grade.

Jana is one of the best teacher I've had. She's funny, enthusiastic and hilarious. If you're shy and don't like group projects then she's not the teacher for you but even so her classroom is very "safe". She has a tendency to call on random people for participation but if you pay attention you should have no problem answering. Take this class!
LOVE Jana. Amazing teacher, even better perosn.
Great professor. Learned a lot!

If you only take one class at KU, it should be this one!!! Jana is funny, makes class interesting, doesn't lecture, and really cares about her students! You will DEFINITELY have fun in this class, but at the end you will realize that you learned more in this class then you ever have! TAKE THIS CLASS!!!
Great class if you enjoy working in groups. She really makes the group projects feel like real life scenarios. If group work and attending class is not your thing, don't take this class!

Love love LOVE! She is super nice and helpful. Very understanding to her students. Tests are easy. The whole class is a group project pretty much. If you don't like working with other people, I wouldn't take this class. You also have to show up to class. Class consists of lecture, guest speakers, and group work. THIS PROFESSOR IS GREAT
She's awsome, and really cares about students learning something new.... Take this teacher you won't regret it!
She is a great lecturer- really cares about students and their thoughts. She is super knowledgeable and I learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her lectures are rather boring but if you pay attention and do the reading, you will be fine.  If you do like I did, and couldn't afford to buy the books, there are always summaries online that will get you by.  If you get on your good side, she will bump up your grade at the end. Stick with it and you'll be great.

This is the second course I have taken with Prof. Fourny. I really enjoy her as a person and as a professor. Her classes mostly consist of lectures and discussion. If you care about the material and are engaged she's a wonderful professor. If your class doesn't like to talk then you're going to be bored, which isn't her fault imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are long and often incredibly boring. Sometimes she can be engaging but it is rare. Lots of reading, but clear paper topics. The class I took seemed to be based more on history than on literature like the course title suggests. However, I would recommend her.

I enjoyed Prof Fourny. She truly cares about your grade & will help you, if you ask for it. There is reading every night, 4 quizzes, and 3 papers: one in class that you can prepare before hand and two out of class. Class dis is crucial to your final grade. She is a tough grader in my opinion but it is all helpful. I would take her again.
I really enjoyed this class. I probably wouldn't be able to stay awake if I had taken the class longer than 1 hr. The papers are easy to comprehend.

Professor Fourny is very nice and a VERY generous grader. You get a nice portion of your grade handed to you for just showing up and talking once a week or so. She is pretty boring, but this may be the easiest A I have earned in college so far. Also, even though she may be a boring lecturer, she knows her stuff, so if you're interested, take her.
yet another "world lit" class that focuses solely on European lit. Where is the diversity in reading selections???
Every single day, we sit at a conference table and she rambles at us. So dull. She does not seem interested at all and her "dicussion" environment is just her talking and telling us why we are wrong.

Appears to lack any kind of passion for teaching. Extremely boring lectures - usually just mumbles quietly to herself. Discussion is painfully pretentious without much actual content. Our semester-long theme through which we studied the texts was "difference" - I'd expect something deeper out of a 6th grade English class. Very disappointing.

Dr. Fourny is above all a specialist in French Lit. but she is a faculty member of HWC and Peace and Conflict Studies. It is in a small French Lit. class that you really get to see her sparkle. She has a wonderful sense of humor and is extremely well-read in world literature. All French majors should take at least one class with her.
The class was fine, but the presentation always put me to sleep. It is hard to pay attention and keep attending class.
boring. monotone. impersonal.
I've never been so I-want-to-slit-my-wrists bored in my entire life.  The class is easy, and I'm sure she's a nice lady, but it takes something like seventeen espresso shots to survive her lectures.

I really enjoyed that class.  I like that I was exposed to literature that I was not aware of.  Prof. Fourny introduced a lot of french and ital lit in this class.  She made herself available when I needed extra assistance and was not afraid to call people
she is soooooooo boring...very monotone and hard to pay attention. half the stuff she lectures about you don't even get tested over. very pointless.
No Comments
She at least made western civ organized and halfway enjoyable.  Compared to some other western civ professors, I'd say she is the best.

I had Dr. Ford for THREE classes in the early 1980s. He was, as a person, a self-important, abrasive jerk. He was effective at getting his students educated, so long as they didnt suffer from nervous breakdowns.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Allen Ford is the worst professor I have ever had. Not only were his lectures unhelpful in clarifying material, trying to get help from him during office hours or his TA is useless. Ford also crossed multiple professional boundaries and I eventually withdrew from the class because of how uncomfortable he made me. TLDR; Exams are hard
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Each one of the quizzes is cumulative, so beware of that! Homework is worth no points, but you should definitely do it to be prepared for quizzes. If you participate in class, he will definitely help out borderline grades. There is one presentation, however if you do decently you will likely get full credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: If your are planning on going the tax route you MUST take this with Ford or you will be in the dark in subsequent classes. If you have no intention of pursuing the Tax track then don't take this course with Ford. It is a valuable course but will eat all of your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Allen Ford gets the worst rep from students who aren't truly ready to put in work. This was by far the hardest class I took at KU, but Ford let's you know that. He is very demanding but is very fair. Be ready to do 4-5 of HW each class. He will get the very best effort out of you and you will look back positively on it, or you will drop the class.

Great teacher. Hardest class you will take but if you put the work into it and learn as you go you can do well in the class. He expects a lot so don't take with a hard load. Ask questions teach yourself and go into office hours. Favorite professor I had all four years! You learn so much
Great person, but a horrible teacher. Expectations are absolutely ridiculous. Prepare to put forth more effort than any class in the Business school.
horrible, horrible man and professor. expectations are WAY too high and unrealistic.

The hardest class I have ever taken but I learned a ton. You cannot get behind or you will barely pass if that. If you study and learn the way he encourages you will end up doing alright and learn more than youve ever learned.
The hardest class I have ever taken, but if you are going into Tax Accounting you will definitely want to have him as a teacher.
Very difficult course. You need to know all the details of what you learn perfectly. This is easily the hardest course I took in my undergrad.

Enjoyed learning about Japanese art. She's makes things understandable, and doesn't overdo the workload. She takes interest in your interests and applies them to class. As well she integrates humor and stories into an otherwise dry subject area. Her energy is great & I learned a lot in her class. I'm great at memorization so it was very easy for me

Entire class is memorization and she asks for way too many details in her essays. She likes to tell stories about when she lived in Japan and class gets out around 5 minutes late frequently. Also, gives a list of 40+ artworks to remember and then only tests on about 10.  Also, only 3 absences are given.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is one of my favorites that I've taken at KU. Professor Fowler is such a genius and she is SO helpful. I feel like she really helped me improve myself as a student. There is a fair amount of work in the class but it was not overwhelming and I learned so much. She speaks Japanese ps.
Really nice, great teacher. Into subject, and funny.

Entire class is based on memorization. Always get the lecture notes, they are perfect to study from along with the book. If you have a really good memory class is easy, otherwise can be difficult. Tests are slide identification and essay.
memorize everything for the tests, study a couple of days ahead. Have a study buddy in this class because it is boring.
Quirky and full of dry humor but has a genuine interest in the material she teaches. Expects a good amount of memorization and participation but is not unreasonable
No Comments

Dedicated to fully answering questions and clearing up any confusion that arises (so ask!). Can elaborate extensively on topics at times - ask him if you can record his lectures if you find yourself zoning out. Homework is graded fairly; tests are intimidating but if you keep up on the readings and ask questions you'll be fine.

The information needed to know for exams is EXTREMELY nitpicky and usually the last things you would expect to need to know for an exam. The "practice exams" online could make a world of difference but I don't think he's looked at them in a long time so they almost always have nothing to do with the material being covered, thus, not useful.
This guy is a try hard and a chose

Fowle seems like a nice guy. He tries to keep the class interesting, but the actual content keeps the class from being fun. The tests are not as easy as everyone says! You have a lot of memorizing without a study guide, and the lectures are boring. You do not need the book b/c it is not used at all. He also never got back to me when I emailed him.

His tests are very easy! All you need to do is memorize old exams. If you ever have questions don't be afraid to email him and he'll address the question for the whole class. His lectures are somewhat interesting.

This was by far the easiest class I have ever taken at KU. You don't need to buy the textbook at all. To pass the class you need to study the questions that he posts on Blackboard at the end of each chapter. Memorize those and you'll do more than fine.

People, like those here, said the class was easy! But it is way more difficult than it should be. He makes us study about 80 pages of notes with no study guide for tests. The tests are basically memorizing all of those pages. All of this for a freakin' Gen Ed. Plus he co-teaches, and the other professor is just as bad. AVOID!
super easy, don't by the book or the clicker. just study all the old exams and chapter questions online before the night of the test there the exact same questions
Agreed, do not buy the book, do not go to class. I didn't read the powerpoints, only the study guides the night before the exams and ended with an A in the class. Super easy.
Don't buy the textbook or the clicker.  All you need are the powerpoint slides and semi-regular attendance.  What a waste of a class.  So boring.

AWFUL. Homework solutions are not posted and on top of that the grading is not even consistent. My friend and I would have different answers and would both get full credit. So you could be doing everything wrong up until the exam and have no clue. His lectures are god awful and boring he just goes off of the book. Good luck.

Absolutely horrific experience. Learned almost nothing from his horrible, boring lectures. Homework has an absurd amount of plots, which take FOREVER to make. He doesn't post homework solutions so you have no way to know if you're doing stuff right. No partial credit on tests. He's generally very cold/uncaring. I'd avoid taking him at all costs.

4 projects, 13 hws, boring material, boring lectures @8am so that was not attended. To study for the tests don't bother with the slides just do the HW (but he REFUSES to provide the HW solutions). The projects are terrible. Usually about 20 pages of yap. Formatting on everything is annoying. No partial credit. Passable, but don't recommend.

Lectures cover mostly things that arent on exams. Doesnt use canvas, HW solutions arent posted even after they are graded, the only feedback you get is a PDF with comment boxes that you have to click on to see. Projects have confusing instructions, and are graded solely based on formatting. Sometimes feedback on the projects is completely illegible

The material for this class is extremely boring and he doesn't make it any better. The projects don't really teach you anything. He's super weird about formatting for both HW and projects and will deduct massive points for it. Yet to take the final, but the midterm wasn't as bad as I thought it would be, but it was still pretty bad. Painful class.

He's alright. Long projects (20+ pages) and homework every week, but he'll give you the answers if you go to office hours. He showed all the solutions to hw in class one day, which was goated. A little more work than a 3-credit hour class should be and definitely not for computer science majors

lectures were WEEKS ahead of homeworks - no one knew what was going on in class. Expect to self-study the entire semester. Homeworks are tough but were great prep for tests and to make sure I knew the concepts. I learnt material but mostly thru the textbook (barely in the class). If you love being lost in class or self studying this is for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Difficult class, high expectations, content heavy, but reasonable grader. His extra-credit assignment practically makes your homework grade 100% and his exams are difficult, but doable. One problem is the professor teaches content very quickly, and I wish his speed lines up with hw. Also, solutions are not provided unless you ask him personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was the first class I've ever received a C in my whole life. Although the material itself was not difficult, I could not read 75% of the things the professor would write and he would not save the notes online in a way that was understandable. It was just incomplete bullet points. Projects got over 15+ pages sometimes. Go to office hours for hw

Idk what these other reviews are talking about Dr Frost was a fantastic teacher for this class. He makes his expectations extremely clear up front, and has a free interactive textbook for the class. The tests are literally exactly the homework problems but with different numbers and sometimes different wording He will work any problem in office hrs
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Frost's lectures aren't the most engaging, and he does not respond well to questions. Attendance is taken, yet not part of the grade. There is a lot of busywork homework assignments worth very little, and also projects that require an excessive amount of writing. The exams, however, are pretty easy as long as you've been to class.
Well, he is no Salandrino that's for sure.

Prof Frost makes too many assumptions! No doubt he understands the material really well but he assumes he has said something or that his audience already has the knowledge and invariably gloss over VERY IMPORTANT concepts. You need to figure out things yourself in his class especially if you don't have a solid background. My last class from him!!!!

The tests are easy enough if you really study. I don't mean flip through notes, I mean study hard. His lectures are boring and he is very willing to help out on homework. I wouldn't take a class from him again though

Frost is a great teacher. Class is organized, notes are fantastic, expectations are given and obtainable. He is very open to questions and will work with them till you understand. Bit heavy on homework (no posted solutions) but quizzes are generally manageable. Textbook barely touched, less homework and more solutions and he'd be perfect.
RUN AWAY......
Senior Professor
No Comments

I really enjoyed Dr. Fowler's class! She selected interesting texts, and she was super clear about grading. She met with all students to talk about our theses and excerpts we chose, which was very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I felt like I did not learn anything from her or at least very little. Her grading was unclear and confusing. She wanted the papers to be repetitive and if you didn't clearly state something, she made you rewrite it. I basically threw out everything i had learned about writing and had to start at the basics in order to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed taking this class with Dr. Fowler. She is very engaging and insightful, especially when it comes to Post-war American Literature. I've really appreciated her helpful feedback on my papers and in class. Taking this class, you get the feeling that she genuinely cares about you and hopes you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment:
Doreen bullies students. She likes to be very unhelpful except for one student. She will be nice and help only one if she likes them. She also has quizzes every class 
Good luck to you if you have her :/
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The writing part is tough, not because it's hard, but because it's too low level with no room to go outside her set of arbitrary rules. Writing essays to her is supposed to be repetitive and inane. Good luck trying to learn much, but if that doesn't bother you, she is kind and the classes can be fun as they're discussions.

Fowler is a sweet professor that engages in great class discussions about the readings. She's very understanding out missing a couple classes and simply gives you an assignment to make it up. There are numerous reading assignments but all are short stories and doable. She helps revise papers and gives good ideas to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's hard to pay attention because she speaks so slowly. The class is simplified discussion and the essay example to follow read like a middle schooler's. She'll correct/dismiss you on interpretation and nuance. She grades poorly too. I said I didn't read it on a quiz once and got an A , but a real, true answer that "wasn't worded right" got a B.

Its probably time for her to retire, respectfully. Interpretation questions are literally 8th grade level. She asked us during discussion to find examples of white supremacy in a Faulkner story about a literal LYNCHING. Hmm, I dunno, thats a tough one Doreen!!! If you HAVE to take a class with her its fine, just a little tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Fowler is not very friendly and does not have a very engaging class. She consistently calls students out for things that should be discussed in private. I was talking during a discussion and she interrupted me and called on another student to finish my point. For a level 300 course, this is a very basic course. She is too old-fashioned.

All of these poor reviews are BS. Doreen is an absolute sweetheart who appreciates one on one connection with her students. If you show up & see her as someone who will just give you a grade you are missing out on what she provides in the class. She is caring and if you are kind back she will make sure you succeed. One of my favorites so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: will not read your full email and will most likely email you back with a question answered in the first one. writing prompts for a 300 level class match those of the beginning level classes, which does make things seem easy, however, the papers are dull at that point. also a prof that says "turn your camera on so the class can see you"
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's not a terrible person, my counselor described her as "old fashioned" and I feel like that fits. She will only receive assignments by email and she won't grade it until you send it as a Microsoft Word document. She doesn't tell you why she takes off all the points on discussion posts, and I wish she had said due dates more. She is nice though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I didn't enjoy the class. Discussions weren't bad, but the class, in general, was boring. Readings for every class and usual quizzes for them. She is really smart, but I feel like most of the class didn't really like it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Fowler is a good teacher. Lectures can be boring and probably you will not have to read everything she wants you to, but if you try to enjoy the class you will. Participation matters and she hates people missing classes, so don't do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Fowler changed my life. I actually took her class the very first semester she was at KU in 1994 and she opened up a world that I never knew existed. I had a horrible English teacher in high school who completely destroyed my confidence. Dr. Fowler showed me that I was capable and if not for her, I would have probably never finished my degree.

The class is structured well and had a good balance of writing and reading. My particular section was Literature of Race in America and the literature we read was very interesting. Class discussion was fruitful and always engaging. She is always willing to help and is very knowledgeable. Highly recommend this class for anyone taking ENGL 205.

All of the literature studied was very interesting and relevant. The professor fostered class discussion and encouraged students. The papers were time consuming, but the professor offered feedback at every step of the writing process.

Amazing teacher! I took two capstones with her. She directed my senior thesis and was extremely helpful and involved throughout the whole process. I will say that if you are not a serious english student then you probably won't like her courses, because she is a serious english teacher! but if you put in the work, having her is extremely rewarding.

Dr. Fowler is very intelligent and knowledgeable but tends to disregard your opinion if it doesn't match hers. If you pick a paper topic she doesn't agree with, don't expect a fair grade. Participation is mandatory but difficult because she treats her students like small children.

I found Dr. Fowler not only dull, but completely unhelpful. While she does have good knowledge of some perspectives on Faulkner (her main academic interest), class was not interesting. I feel like I became a worse writer as a result of taking her class. She runs late for mandatory writing conferences, and I got 1 helpful suggestion all semester.

Dr. Fowler gives excellent insight on the works you read and is willing to listen to all viewpoints.  There are few actual "assignments."  Just read the required material before each class, understand it, participate in discussion, and you're golden.

Absolutely incredible class. She cares so much about each individual student and their progress. She really wants you to develop your writing in her class, and will always make time to assist you. You'll get a great grade if you simply follow her instructions, and will learn proportionally to the amount of work you put in. Incredible prof.

Dr. Fowler is the single best professor I have ever had the privilege to have.  I can't wait to take another one of her courses.  You can't sleep through her class, but you will never want to!  She is so engaging and helpful.  I miss her already.

A must take for the intellectually curious. Good amount of reading, but an interesting mix of literature and theory. In addition to class readings, two essays challenged us to engage other texts through different theoretical approaches. Class is structured as a discussion. Expected to talk and do the readings. Challenging, as college should be!

Dr. Fowler is a very intelligent woman who has a lot of knowledge that she just wants her students to know as well.  She has a passion for William Faulkner that is contagious.  It is a very reading intensive class but I found the material to be interesting.  Dr. Fowler has very clear expectations that are fair and challenging.

This was one of my hardest freshman classes simply because I was not a strong writer. That being said, Dr. Fowler is always there for her students when they need help. Reading F. Scott Fitzgerald was my favorite part.

Dr. Fowler explained complex literary theory in a clear and concise manner.  I enjoyed her reading selections and thought they fit extremely well with the theoretical texts we covered in class.  I would recommend a Dr. Fowler class to any KU English student serious about their studies.  She is incredibly helpful and knowledgeable.
She appeared pompous and opinionated. This professor has her interpretations and her rigidity in though is not conducive to n academic environment.

She was definitely not one of my favorite professors. The Faulkner books from the beginning were not particularly interesting for me, so it was difficult to read these books while trying to concentrate at the same time. Also something I noticed which some may not notice or care is that she constantly said "uh" or "umm" in every other sentence.

Her selection of readings were not at all interesting to me and I found it difficult to want to read the Faulkner books in the beginning. Also this may or may not be noticeable to some, but she constantly said "uh" or "umm" in every other sentence. This personally annoyed the hell out of me.

Loved her and the class. Lecture is an open discussion.  Reading from 30-140 pages a week. Two papers, Two test, easy daily quizzes if you have done the reading, discussion/attendance pts. She has great taste in fiction.It's mainly 20th century fiction too!  Faulkner,Morrison,F. O'Connor, and many other great short story artist. Miss it already.

Excellent teacher! Class discussions are required but you learn a lot from them. Only hard part of tests is the essays--be prepared to write extensively. We had two 5-7 page papers which were manageable because she was very helpful with forming topic sentences, peer reviews, etc. My one complaint is that she loves Faulkner, whom I cannot stand.

Dr. Fowler allows for a great deal of discussion which is helpful to understanding the works read in class. She is very willing to help you with your paper and it's quite possible to get an A if you follow her advice. Midterm and final are quite doable if you study. A very quality professor.
Very odd interpretation of literature.  Highly Freudian.

While pleasant & knowledgeable, I agree that her endless details about authors left little time for discussion of texts. Quizzes are easy if you have read the material, and often even if you havent. Was always lamenting that we must have never written a thesis/analysis/research paper before(upper level english majors)& gave me my first/last C paper
She may be knowledgeable about William Faulkner and allowed the class to have productive discussions but as a teacher she was very negative and often treated the students like children.

Teacher was alright until i said a comment about feminists and she started grading much harder. Got a B on my first paper, my second was much better, went in for help at writing center and with her and got a C-.... Lots of reading and writing, both of which i dont enjoy. Try and get Klayder.. much better teacher

Negatives: Spends far too much time reciting information about the authors covered and leaves little time for student discussion. Often appears dismissive of students' opinions that do not coincide with her own. Not effectively explanatory in one-on-one sessions. Positives: Interesting and challenging works read in her course.

Oh, Doreen.  She put too much on the syllabus and we got way behind schedule.  She was not very helpful during the mandatory one-on-one conferences before our essays were due.  She talked so much about the authors that we ended up not talking about the books.  I certainly will not be taking a class from her again.

A few of the books she chose were difficult and she knew they were but still chose them. She gives quizzes over the readings but usually gives a few questions to choose from so likely you will be able to answer one. She is very willing to help. Decently fair grader. She definitely doesn't try to make her students fail.
No Comments
She's demanding, but fair.  You must work hard, but you'll learn a lot.

She's my honors seminar professor, and she'll make you want to quit the program. She completely killed my work ethic with the endless horendous assignments. Honors is supposed to be fun and community-building, but all we do is grind through pointless assignments with zero interaction or enjoyment. No sense of community no interactions.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Friis is the goat. I was terrified at first because exams are worth 88% of your grade. But if you do the weekly homework assignments, they can be up to 10% extra credit for your overall grade. You should be doing them anyway or else you will not do well on tests. The TA for the semester I'm taking is amazing with grading feedback so that helps.

Lisa was my honors seminar and I feel like the class was so much more work than some of my three-credit hour classes. You have to write a paper and it's not very interesting. This class is a good connection for engineering students but because I'm not it wasn't helpful. Very useless. She also hasn't graded anything and doesn't understand Canvas.
The tests are heavily weighted and very hard... she does not curve it. She is a very nice professor who lectures well though. It is very difficult to achieve an A... as an all A student
The final project/paper took a lot of time, so don't wait until the last minute to do it. Other than that, the class was exactly what you'd expect from a seminar.

Dr. Friis is very caring. I found this class to be a very easy A as long as you prepare well for the exams. All homework was for extra credit, but you should absolutely still do it. Exams are worth a large majority of your grade. Lectures sometimes felt too slide-heavy.

Dr. Friis is an amazing professor to have. She really cares about the success of her students and wants them to learn the material rather than just regurgitate it. Her tests are always harder than I've expected, but they are fair and doable. She gives TONS of extra credit, I had above a 100% for a fair bit of the semester. One of my fave classes.

Well, constantly exam 1 average is a D. No curve, why? because if you work hard you get a total grade curve at the end. So if you do bad on either exam 2 or exam 3 you are penalized overall. How that makes sense I don't know? The class has tons of extra credit but not enough to account for her delusional idea that her tests shouldn't be curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Friis WANTS you to succeed. She provides all the lectures online, tons of examples, and makes homework extra credit. If you apply yourself, you will be fine in the course. The material is a bit harder to wrap your head around - so beware of that. TONS of extra credit and she will work with you to make sure you understand the material.
Worst teacher in department. i am very good student by my grades have suffered greatly in this class because she intentionally makes it impossible. take another class instead or your GPA will drop
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher. Very hard exams and very tough grader. Avoid at all costs!

Difficult exams and tough grader. You get 2 exams and they are worth the bulk of your grade so if you mess one up you probably won't pass. Also she is obsessed with chegg and and thinks everyone is cheating.

Our class average on the first exam was a 58% and Dr. Friis blamed us. She said that she'd boost our grades if we worked hard for the rest of the class. However, my friend and I asked about this at the end of the semester and she did not help us. My friend & I earn A's and B's in our other engineering classes; we ended this class with a D+ and a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The material isn't the worst, but she's tough on exams with zero tolerance for mistakes. The first exam average was 60% with no curve so don't take it lightly

Lectures are good, but also more arduous than other classes. I had to go over some lectures a few times, but it ended up alright in the end. She was caring and was available to help in office hours. Exams are tough, but everything tested is clearly laid out to you. This class is very time consuming, but not impossible

I took this as a summer class, and it was a lot of work. You will do well if you do all the reading and all the homework. The homework isn't worth any credit, but if you self-grade the homework you submit, she will give extra credit! Make sure to study for exams, and make yourself some reference sheets and you'll be good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She was very rude and uncaring throughout the semester, even in a pandemic. She did not answer questions in class even though we were supposed to watch the lectures outside of class. The material was not challenging, but she crams exams that are far too long into a limited time frame.

Worst professor ever. Extremely rude, and barely answers doubts. Bad course structure too. If you mess up any exam out of 3 you will pretty much ruin your GPA. Expects you to have an engineering degree on the first day of class. If a new professor comes in for this class, I would say just take a chance and go for that professor

The exams are hard and be ready to work hard. If you're a bad test-taker , don't even try. She does make sure that you understand the concepts and you will learn a lot from the class. However, there are 3 tests and if you mess one up, forget the A.

I wanted to leave a bad review because I felt she was rude at times but everyone is having hard times during this pandemic. The exams are challenging and you will have to learn how to study but I did learn a lot in this class. She is very knowledgeable on the material and knows how to teach it but you will have to work for a good grade.
Exam

The man is not very approachable.  Very suspicious of everything, even during colloquial conversation.   Has very high memorization demands, expect to know the chapter notes word for word front to back even for just a quiz.  He is not helpful and is quick to send you back to the notes instead.  He's a researcher, not an educator.

This class is absolutely brutal. There are 16 quizzes, 5 exams, and a cumulative final. Each exam covers three chapters; each chapter is anywhere from 21-44 pages of pure material in length.  The exam questions are incredibly specific. Be prepared to study extensively for this class. Extensively as in more than any other undergraduate class.

You will not have a life while in this class. I am only taking a few classes, granted they are difficult, but if I wasn't in this class I would love my life way more. You do not have time to do anything but memorize pages upon pages of notes. There is no book and the teacher has a very heavy accent. Take with anyone else.

Dr. Takusagawa is a really nice guy, but tough. I got an A in the class, but it was the hardest class I took at KU. For the final, I studied only biochem for 10+ hours a day for 5 days and got a low B on the test. If you can't get at least an A- in this class, you  shouldn't apply to med school, because in my experience it'll be more of the same.

This class was the worst experience I have had at KU. I got an A in biochem 636 and have a 3.97 GPA so I know how to study. But, that doesn't matter for his tests. His tests are just a random set of 25 questions. It does NOT really test if you KNOW the material. I knew some who never studied, guessed, and did better than others who studied for days

Professor Takusagawa's class is ridiculously demanding. You basically must MEMORIZE every statement, detail, and concept within his pdf lectures. He has 5 exams, each worth 25 points, and you get to drop one. The final exam is composed of 50 q's, where each section covers 10 q's altogether. Expect to study more than 3 nights in a row to earn an A.

Memorize 60-80 pages per test... word for word...  I feel like a zombie.  Test every two weeks, takes 3+days to study if you want to get an A.  Top 10-12 get As in class, almost everyone else gets a B or C.  --I advise you to not take this class teh same time as Gene Xp and Mam phys/Biochem lab like i did.

Not a fan. While I have memorized a great deal for this course, I don't feel like I've actually learned anything. The sheer volume of information makes it extremely difficult to actually understand it. I realize that biochem is a difficult subject, but I do feel there is a difference between learning and memorizing; this class is simply memorizing.

I feel almost bad for liking this class. Studying for Other class' tests is boring but his tests are so difficult you must memorize every page. It makes it extremely challenging. If you want and A, you have to really work for it.
Its an intersting subject but he made it really boring.

Dr. Takusagawa is not the greatest teacher, I'll admit, and the amount of information presented is often overwhelming. However, the class is supposed to be a weed out for med school and in that purpose it is successful. Overall, he was effective in designing exams to separate the students who simply slide through and those who memorize the minutia.
No Comments
No Comments
Probably my favorite class of undergraduate.  He gives few A's but you are almost guaranteed to get at least a B or C with the curve. I have never had a teacher be more available to students.

Taks tries damn hard at his job and knows his sh*t back to front - he is a very accomplished scientist who does devote much time and effort to teaching.  His English is not great, however, and so his communication skills are lacking.  He's not very lively

He provides excellent online resources but his lectures consist of him simply reading them out loud in mediocre English. His test format is extremely poor: 25 multiple choice questions, no partial credit given. He's a good researcher but bad teacher.
Very nice guy but his classes are impossible.  Dont bother studying since you will probably just fail like everyone else.

Do not buy the book for this class, you don't need it for any hw. I used it once for extra credit at the end of the year and the library won't buy it back from you. If you have test files and go over them and take notes in class (although it may be painfully boring), you should be able to get an A in the class and not have to take the last test.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but painfully boring to listen to. It's not his fault that the class he teaches is completely pointless, but there has to be some way to make the content at least somewhat interesting. Same monotone voice everyday. Most of the time he ends up talking about Amazon for half the class and thats all we do.

This class was so interesting to me and I genuinely enjoyed going. The lectures could definitely be a little dry, but if you sit in the front it wont be a problem. He is very kind and cares a lot about the subject. Great teacher over all.
Nice guy, not the best professor. I never talked to or got help from my TA. I would HIGHLY recommend reading the book and paying attention in lecture. The tests are pretty difficult for some reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Respectful and nice guy, but extremely boring lectures. If you want to do well I suggest paying attention in lecture, but you can get by with catching up with the slides he posts. Some of the tests are surprisingly hard considering how basic the material is, but he allows you to drop one so it ends up working out.

He is nice but discipling. He will pause if someone disrespectfully talks while he's talking. You have 4 exams and there will be one with the lowest score dropped. So study hard for the first 3 and you don't need to worry about the final one. Read the book ( the reading part he mentions on BB) because most of the questions will be in the text.

Bill is a very, very nice professor and you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. Lectures are not very entertaining though and can drag. Lots of note tacking in lectures but online modules give you a great break from going to class. You definitely have to work hard in this class and make sure you know the information taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The book is semi-needed, but do NOT buy the book for this class, it's available for free online! Just do all the virtual lectures and take notes and a B should be a cakewalk and an A is definitely doable.

Fuerst is boring. This class is boring. The homework is given with step by step instruction. Do not do the online modules, just take the quiz with it with friends and you will get 10/10. Tests are easy. Just show up to class and do other homework. Or fall asleep to this mans soothing voice. He's the joke of the B School and so is his class
Lectures were dry and boring. Tests were difficult; reading the book helps some. Beware of those pop quizzes!!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are very boring since it is a super big class. Made me not pay attention as much since I was all the way in thee back. The man was nice but very lecture heavy. Pop quizzes were thrown in at the end of classes. The test are very hard and it is important to know all the information. Reading the book helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Fuerst was one of my favorites this semester. He is genuine and wants the best for his students. He is a very interesting guy when you talk to him outside of class, even though he might not seem like it in class. Lectures are boring, but have good information if you are willing to listen. Few assignments and 4 tests. Good & easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very easy class, most boring professor I've ever had. Class is basically nap time (attendance is 20 pts, 740 total in class). Only 3/4 exams go into gradebook (200pts ea). I recommend (and what I did) is to try really hard in the beginning of this class, because you can get enough points for an A 3/4 of the semester in, and be done!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures can get long and boring but he is very nice and wants students to succeed. Basically everyone passes. You get to drop one exam (1/4). A good class.

Professor Fuerst has been ruled the most boring professor at the University. I have found watching paint dry much more enjoyable than attending and listening to his lectures. With hardly paying attention, I got a B in the class so an A is very obtainable if you have the focus skills. Plus he occasionally does online modules which is clutch.

Both the material and the way he delivers his lectures are incredibly boring. The vast majority of the material is ridiculously intuitive and takes zero effort to learn. This is not worth being a required course. Class is an easy A. The only reason this class exists is to make a former dean of the business school (Fuerst) still feel relevant.
