She cares a lot about her students and is very excited about helping students learn. You can tell she is interested in the information in the class and that helps a lot. There are no quizzes or tests, but there are papers. Attendance is mandatory but if you have a legitimate excuse she's understanding. Papers are pretty easy.

Dr. White is incredibly intelligent and really cares about Latin, Classics, and language in general. She is my favorite professor to date and she is really good at what she does. Interactive lectures, plenty of practice, and her caring nature all helped me learn Latin well.

Let me be clear the material is difficult/time consuming but thats because Latin is hard (especially for me as a Bio major) but thank god for Gina. She's one of the best professors I've ever had when it comes to explaining material & she's extremely smart-has an answer to every question even if its outside the scope of the course. Quiz every week.

I have a strong learning disability, knew this and refused to look at my final paper because it was an hour late, despite spending hours on it. Worked hard in her class, and she would belittle me and said I wrote like a child. She was a complete culture vulture, a racial fetishist, and ended up being let go from my school for saying a racial slur.

Gitti is unprofessional, and would constantly complain about the younger generation when people would leave to use the bathroom during a lecture (which is understandable considering the class was 3 hours long.) Her instructions for papers were extremely vague. Although having a detailed syllabus, it was vague in its directions for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Gitti on my senior thesis panel and originally was absolutely terrified because of some stories I had heard about her and I thought she was just on my panel because my work was about rap. But she ended up being incredibly helpful and supportive and though she wasn't very knowledgable of rap culture, she still had great things to say.

Salami is very knowledgeable and provides information few others could. She is dedicated to her work, and wants to share it. Yeah, she talks about the history and culture of the people, because those things define art! She is engaging, funny, and helpful. I'm not an art major, so maybe superficial aesthetics pass, but she offers substance.

I hope that people can dismiss some of the poor ratings. Gitti Salami is absolutely invested in her field, knowledgable and helpful to those who seek it. I would trade that kind of instruction over "spell-it-out-for-me-organization" any day. She is the type of instructor that can inform you in ways that most instructors won't.

Disorganized, Not very Clear on what we are supposed to learn, Tries to hard to connect all of Africa into one big africa art thing, Way to much info in a single lecture, Doesn't clarify much, Class was on the easy side but she changes her class formatting so much it is hard tell what to expect.
As long as you go to class and take thorough notes, her class is a breeze!  She is also very helpful if you seek her out.

This class is not easy, but Dr. Salami really knows the subject matter. Hard to follow at times, but she is willing to help you every step of the way as long as you show her respect and interest in the subject. The class was eye-opening to what Africa has to offer in regards to arts and culture. It was hard work, but it was worth it!

This class was very interesting if you are into African Art.  I really enjoyed the class but it was difficult.  However she offered lots of outside assistance to prepare for the final presentation, which consisted of a 10-15 page paper over an African artist and a powerpoint presentation.  Yes she was a bit disorganized but she is SO knowledgeable!
Very disorganized! On the day of the test I asked about it and she was like "oh was the test today? Oh well we can do it next week" She does not even follow her own syllabus!!!!! DONT TAKE

this teacher drives me crazy. completely wastes everybody's time with useless assignments. her lectures and notes are disorganized. this is supposed to be a central african art class; instead it's more like an african history class with a little art thrown in. there is no clear idea of what works of art students are supposed to know for the test.

A bit too disorganized for my liking. Lectures would repeatedly fall behind class readings which made the already foreign material all the harder to pick up on. Nevertheless, she is an expert in her field... A prior interest in Africa/African Art is highly recommended.

I think she really knows what she's talking about.  She's really opinionated, but if you ever need help, she's really available and will work with you.  She expects work out of you, but it's all work that should be expected since we're in college.

Lots of people hated this class but I liked it. It's very very interesting material. As long as you don't stress out about the class it's fine because she curves the grades at the end of the semester. It is easy to get a B but probably hard to get an A. If you go to her office hours to chat with her she will love you forever.
High expectations. Weed out class for kids looking for something easy.

This was, by far, the worst class I took at KU. She has command of the subject; however, did not know how to teach it. I didn't learn anything about Africa, except that I'd never really want to go there. DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER!

She was the undergrad advisor this past semester because the other one was gone. She gave me a lecture telling me that I couldn't take the classes that I selected because I wouldn't do well! I have a pretty decent GPA, so I was pretty mad about the whole thing. I thought that advisors are there to help you!!! Her class is disorganized too!
No Comments
really bad, disorganized, and cannot understand her.

She wants her students to succeed but if you are not good at grammar it will be a challenge She is very helpful and answers any questions during class and outside of it, including flexible office hours. The best way to do well in this class is to communicate with her outside of the class if you are struggling. The textbook was free online.

I think Professor Weatherly gets bad wrap. Initially, I did not like her class at first but I needed it. Her "harshness" is confused with her desire to get students to perfect their grammar and truly improve their French. She only became frustrated with students who clearly were not applying themselves. I truly enjoyed her class and I am thankful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was very rude and passive-aggressive in lectures when you would ask her questions. She would expect you to know things from past level classes even though not everyone has taken the other level classes offered in the school. Very insistent on not repeating things in the written work and the documents you need aren't always online.

Honestly, Prof. Weatherly was hands down the worst teacher I've had a KU. She is very rude to students, and will assume things about levels of French based on tests. Tests are not my strongest area, but take home writings are my best, but she constantly graded me down because "I must be cheating".

Mme. Weatherly is kind and funny however be warned she expects a lot from her students. This is not a class you can slide by with minimal effort. Also be prepared to participate a lot she grades hard on participation.

Madame Weatherly was fantastic. She has an adorable British accent and is very sarcastic yet kind. She's very flexible if you communicate with her. She is willing to help you if you will put in the work. Make sure to speak up, she grades hard on class participation. Loved her!
Very good teacher and really funny sometimes too. Sometimes gets frustrated with unresponsive students. Her british accent is really funny also!

Dr. Gist-Mackey is a very respected professor at KU, for good reason. You can tell she truly cares about her students and wants to help in whatever way possible. After taking this course, you will be able to add something really cool to your professional portfolio. Dr. Mack would send thoughtful emails / regularly check on her students. Recommend!

Dr. Mack gives great feedback and really wants you to do well. Really interesting lectures. Class was online because of pandemic, but Dr. Mack's lectures, directions and organization made it feel as close to in-person as was possible during these virtual times. Awesome teacher.

Took this class during the pandemic when everything was taught online, and Dr. Mack was very tech friendly. I learned every bit as much online as I would have in person. The material is interesting and I looked forward to each class. Everything ran extremely smoothly. She gives you every opportunity to do well if you put in the work.
Really cares about her students. She goes the extra mile to help you if you need it. Dr. Mack is a great professor. Take her if you can.

Your grade will reflect how much work you put in, but most of the time the work asked of you is very achievable. Her lectures allow for class participation everytime, so if you have a room that speaks up, class will zoom by.

He is one of the most thorough and talented syntacticians I've learned from. He encourages students to always ask “why” and to be brave to propose new well-motivated analyses. His teaching is clear and step-by-step—and he has a gift for telling you you're wrong without ever saying it. Take his class to see how. :)

Very clear in his explanations, always willing to clarify things when people have questions. Funny guy. You get really good feedback on homework. Uses an online textbook that's easy to navigate and covers class material thoroughly.
Dr. Gluckman is fantastic! This class is decently hard and has some complicated topics but he is more than willing to reteach or adjust the schedule to help students. He's so kind as well!

Very straightforward course - given the resources you need to succeed. You will do well if you understand the concepts, if you don't understand the concepts then ask questions / go to office hours and you will.

He's knowledgable, passionate, and experienced in the field of linguistics. His classes are insightful and engaging; the slides straightforward and have lots of examples. We had a take-home midterm and a capstone paper as our final with ~1 assignment/week. He's very willing to help and work with you with whatever you need- totally recommend him!

Dr. Gluckman is a great professor and is extremely passionate about his subject. He's a bit nervous so while teaching there is a lot of pacing and pauses, doesn't take away from the content much though. He has slides that are shared on canvas but not much info is on there. You need notes for the homework so be sure to write everything down!

Pretty great professor who is passionate about the subject. All the homework are relatively easy and if you go to his office hours he basically gives you the answers on whatever you are stuck on. Also no tests besides the midterm which is take home and open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Gluckman is a super cool dude, and it is very clear that he is passionate about his work. He makes the lectures palatable, doing a good combo of lectures and/or working over activities related to the homework. Come to class having read the chapters assigned, and you'll be fine. Also, always take advantage of office hours, he will work with you!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Gluckman wrote the textbook himself and tried to simplify those complex concepts. Worksheets and homework are not hard once you've read the textbook, which helps you get through the core. Extra credits available for those who did a presentation on a topic (of your choice), and you can skip one portion of the final. Not strict on grading. Great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Gluckman does an excellent job of teaching syntax. He wrote the textbook, and though it can be a lot of reading, it contains many useful examples for completing the homework assignments. He is always happy to meet with students one-on-one to discuss any questions they may have.

Lots of homework--but it's relevant and helpful for the concepts important to the class. For any of his classes: just do the work. None are a particularly heavy course load, but it will not go well for you if you are not engaged from the start. Just let him know when you don't understand; he'll always help!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's knowledgeable, chill, and syntax is interesting. The structure of the class needs a little work, though. Make sure to copy all the trees he draws in class, as those are the only examples to refer to when you're doing homework. Find study partners and start homework early to email your TA with questions before it's due. Still worth taking IMO

Should have dropped the class and my minor while I could. Worst class I have taken. The intro classes do not set you up for this. It's more the class than the professor, all in all, bad combo. Definitely doable when you are encouraged to collaborate on homework and the midterm. However, none of that prepared me for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Continues my belief that the linguistics department hires the best people. Great lectures, lots of examples. Don't skip class or you will fall behind and set yourself up for failure. Takes pride in teaching and teaching well. Homework was 50% of the grade, so pay attention and ask for help. Highly recommend him - also syntax is just really cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you're good about showing up to class and turning in all of your work on time this class is an easy A. For every assignment she‘ll give you back a complete or an incomplete. If you get an incomplete, you can keep redoing it until you get a complete. No exams or quizzes! Just make sure to get a complete on all of your work and no skipping class!

This is one of the most convoluted classes you could take as a biology major. If you can, do not take this elective or professor. The structure of the class is so scattered that it forces you to see her outside of class in some capacity to get a good grade. You will learn absolutely nothing from this class. You will just be left frustrated.

This is one of the most work intensive coursed I have ever taken and is taught by someone who knows nothing about the subject. Her teaching style is to give students an inane amount of assignments and send them back repeatedly for minor mistakes or things she decides she does not like that day. Never take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: AVOID THIS PROFESSOR! Class is structured horribly and she grades extremely unfairly!

No other honors seminar required so much reading and writing. The seminar was the Biology and Culture of Sleep, but this seminar was putting me to sleep. I was very disappointed by the lack of engagement of the in-person seminars. Lack of discussion, harshly graded essays, and terrible classroom environment (not set up for classroom discussions).

I AM WARNING YOU AVOID THIS PROF! So much busy work throughout the week that I did not learn from doing but oftentimes took hours to finish. At one point in the semester even the prof. could'nt keep up with grading. If I could go back, I wish I would have taken a different class. I had to spend most of my study time doing busy work for an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I have her right now for animal behavior. While Dr. Gleason is a nice person, her class is structured terribly. It is way too much work for an elective and she gives you horrible grades on hours worth of work on purpose so that you have to talk to her about it in office hours and only then she will fix it.
One of the kindest professors I have had. She really just seems to care about her students and shows a genuine interest in their life.

Her animal behavior class is a super easy A, but she does expect a decent amount of work. Exams are take home and she allows everyone a chance to fix answers on each test, and also provides a hint sheet to help answer each question for the regrade. Very adamant about getting to know classmates and discussions, kind of like a HS class. Nice lady
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Had her in the past for evolutionary bio. She's a pretty dry lecturer, but overall not a bad professor. I like that she provides lecture outlines, and I don't find her that confusing. Her section is much harder than the first, but I felt the first few tests with Hileman were very, very easy. I think that throws many people off.

I had her for BIOL412 and hated the class and her teaching style; however, in a seminar class, she is actually very approachable and receptive to discussions on topics.  She even let us pick the papers we would read for the class.  Drastic change from my experience in Evolutionary Bio.

Dr. Gleason is a good teacher.  Her exams expect you to show that you understand the material and can apply it to new situations.  If you can do that then you're set.  Tests are longggggggggggg but you are allowed to pick and choose questions that you're comfortable answering.

her lectures are absolutely boring!! her notes are incomplete and do not make sense when you look back at them (and i attend class every single day!) her exam is just horrendous...i scored an A and B on my first two exam with Lisa Hilemann who teaches the first part of the class...but with her exam i scored a D! -___-" avoid if possible.
She is a good teacher, but clearly doesn't respect students or her employees.  I think she has the idea that she is better than her students and is too good for teaching.

Gleason was an all right teacher with tests which were average when it came to difficulty.One problem with exams was that they did not correlate with the assigned homework at all, making the homework seem pointless.

Amazing professor - leaves thoughtful  feedback on every single assignment. Lots of reading, only 2 papers that are 5-6 pages each. Quizzes and reflections are about two paragraphs per question. That being said, the reading is all worthwhile and interesting. My favorite class and professor at KU. Harder than most 100 levels, take jr/sr year.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: this class was definitely busywork. Readings almost never made any sense, I had to google summaries after to make sure I understood. The amount of work I had to put in for assignments worth only 5 points was disproportionate. I cried wayyy to much over this class, def not a 100 level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is a TON of reading and writing for 5-10 point assignments and its difficult to earn full credit. She is easy to reach outside of class and is willing to help but just prepare for the workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Incredibly difficult. The grading criteria is incredibly arbitrary and hard to follow. Insane amount of feedback without actually telling you how to fix your answer. No extra credit offered, or late work accepted. Will fail the class if you don't buy the textbook. Should not be a 120 level course very misleading.

Grade mostly dictated by tests for assigned readings, but movies were often assigned as well. Gives quality feedback on ALL of your work in a timely manner, and I genuinely felt like I learned a lot from this course. Very responsive to emails and flexible with meetings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was a ridiculous amount of work for a 100 level course. There are quizzes every week along with a teamwork assignment, journals, and 2 full-length papers. Prof Giordano isn't super helpful in explaining things in simple English and a lot of her lectures didn't really make sense to me. We also had a lot of difficult and long readings
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Do NOT take her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She barely wanted to lecture you essentially have to do a lot of extra work for a 100 level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly when she said the class was going to be online, I thought she would still teach. She didn't teach one bit of this class. It was COMPLETELY all on your own reading and teaching yourself. All she does is grade your assignments and tell you that you misunderstood the reading. Maybe if you actually taught us, we would be able to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Giordano's course in Philosophy of Film was by far one of the best class I've taken at KU and has resonated with me for years. She is very knowledgable and engaging. Looking at the negative reviews, coming from entry level courses, I can't help but wonder if people were just mad she wasn't giving blow off classes with easy As.

In lecture she would make weird, patronizing comments towards the class ("you WOULD know about X if you all weren't too busy with farmville or whatever you guys play now). Her lectures were half the material you needed and half her own interests. She seemed to believe teaching this course was beneath her and the quality reflected that.

Attendance wasn't mandatory since it's a large lecture so I skipped a lot. I was still able to get an A because the midterm and final are worth a large portion of your grade, so if you ace those the other work doesn't matter as much. She gives full study guides for midterm & final, so if you go to class before the tests & study you'll be fine.
Super boring lectures. Not readily available for office hours. Cancelled class when the election happened (had her Fall 2017). Too difficult for a basic KU core class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Giordano knows a lot about philosophy and is very intelligent, but she is a terrible lecturer. Her lectures are very monotonous. For the Spring 2017 semester, we had 6 pop quizzes, two essay exams (possible prompts given prior), and an accumulative final with multiple choice, t/f, fill in the blank, and essay -- NO study guide given.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Essay exams and pop quizzes make up your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class is not easy, so do not slack off. When I took the class the midterm and final were worth 70% of your grade. Highly recommend going to the SI sessions and your discussions. The study guides are super helpful for the tests. Show up to class because the lecture notes are crucial. The readings are boring, just understand the main ideas.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Both of the tests are essay exams, she gives you a list of possible exam questions and picks 3 then says you have to pick two and write a 700-900 word response to both of them, all within the 50 minute class period, this class is awful and incredibly dry.

Overall a really good teacher. Her lectures were interesting and very helpful. All of the lectures were basically summaries of the reading, so I stopped doing the reading and just took notes off the slides in class and still got an A. She gives a full study guide for the midterm and final so you know everything that will be on the exams.

she tries to cram way to much information in one lecture. this course was overall very difficult and her lectures didn't make it any easier. if you take this course make sure you attend your discussion sessions or you will easily fall behind fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the hardest classes I have ever taken.  When she lectures its almost as if she is reading off a prewritten script that sounds like she is reading Shakespeare.  She seems to lack original ideas but rather regurgitates what the texts says.  The exams were impossible, it wasn't uncommon to find a fellow student who also agreed.  0/10

This was one of the hardest classes I have taken at the University of Kansas. Had to curve every test because the class averages were 50%. Not so introductory when Lara is teaching; does not know how to dumb it down for those of us who are only there to take it as a requirement. Never taking a philosophy class again
If you need help, she will help. Instructor is invested in her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Passionate about the content and student success.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McKeithan was super nice and her class was super easy! She laid out everything you had to do for each unit and the due dates for everything. She accepted late work and didn't even take points off for it. The only thing that I didn't like was having to do group projects in an online class, but they weren't bad!
He is the man. Take him. I hope Miami has him longer

He's a pretty easy professor for a notoriously hard class, but one thing I'll say is WOW is this guy boring. It was so hard to listen to him speak because his voice is so monotonous and I found myself sleeping through his class whenever I didn't sleep in and miss it. I was able to do well even missing 60% of his classes though, so that's a plus.
Professor Glenski was great! We studied relevant companies and related them to course material. I learned a lot and had fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is very helpful and crystal clear in explaining finance concepts.

He's a really nice guy, always willing to help students and wants to get to know them. The material is pretty tough, so it can be confusing even when he tries to explain. The online homework is a really good tool to use for studying.

I think some of these comments are unfair. Sure, physical geography is not the most exciting topic ever. But I think she does a good job of making herself and her TA's visible and available to answer questions. It's easy to fall behind in understanding stuff, but if you put in just 15 minutes a night into this class, you're going to get an A.
Pretty easy test, do the online quizzes and you will be fine.

Lectures have a lot of information, so definitely go and take notes even though attendance is not mandatory. All tests and quizzes (with the exception of the map quiz) are online, so that's super convenient. Overall, not a bad instructor but would not take another class from her. Definitely not as bad as some of the other Geog 104 instructors.

Boring. Jen does not seem to realize that most of us are taking this class because we have too, not because we are interested in it. The google earth exercises are confusing and pointless. This class is easy if you go. You don't have to pay attention or take notes because its NEVER on the test.

She means well, but can be extremely rude. The class is incredibly boring, and sometimes it seems like she doesn't even know what she is talking about. Her assignments make absolutely no sense, and are quite pointless. Only good thing is that she does exams and quizzes online and you are allowed more than 1 attempt!

She is a nice person although the class was a little bit boring, but for me it's okay. The tests and prep questions were online with 2 attempts. Extra Credit offered during class time if you go to class and do the activities. I worked hard and got an A.

Awful. She makes no sense and is constantly contradicting herself. Not helpful at all. Doesn't email back quickly. Treats students in a condescending way. Do not take GEOG 104 with her if there is a different section available.
Wow, is this class boring. She is a nice person, but is not the most interesting lecturer and is kind of monotone. The tests are online, which is kind of nice. The assignments are tedious though.

The absolute worst instructor I have ever had. Her grading system is bizarre is stacked against the students, she makes every single assignment as tedious and frustrating as possible, and she truly does not care at all. She is so robotic, unfriendly, and uninterested in seeing anyone in her class pass. Take this course with literally ANYONE else.

This is the worst, most pointless class I have ever taken.  I do not recommend taking this with Jen Glabuis.  She is the most monotone professor I have ever had.  This was offered twice a week and I couldn't even show up because she was so boring. No one would listen to her and all people did was sit on their computers. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Not the  nicest guy in the world. Very rude and always has to be "right". Class isn't particularly hard but don't miss a speech, he will be rude about it and you lose 20% of your score. Overall not the nicest

Eddie has a weird sense of humor, but he is a good professor. He gives examples for every speech and usually provides an outline example as well. You need to go to class in order to do well on the speeches. He also assigns reading assignments occasionally and will have in class short answer quizzes over the readings.
Eddie led by example in this course. Although the class wasn't easy, he made the class easy with his explanations and analogies. I would definitely recommend!
The best professor I had all semester! His lectures are interesting, he is funny and really cares that you do well. I would HIGHLY recommend him if you are taking COMS 130!

I heard a bunch of terrible things about coms 130, but Eddie actually made the class quite enjoyable. Got an A in the class without buying the textbook. Just make sure you show effort in your speeches and glance over the readings before the "quizzes" and it will be a breeze

He is a good teacher who is very clear with the information he is presenting. He is very chill and if you come in a few minutes late he doesn't mind. The main days you need to make sure to be there are speech days. When you are giving a speech don't try and get out of it.. it wont work. Just prepare for the speeches in advance and you will get a A

I did not want to take speech at all but I had to for a gen ed. But having Eddie Glenn has made it really easy, he makes the classroom really relaxed and tells you what you need to know. Speeches still suck but try and get him!
This teacher is great and makes the class interesting but not too difficult. If you take COMS 130 take it from him!
Overall good class. Pretty easy just have to put a little bit of work in to the speeches but nothing too difficult. Only used the book about 4 times and had quizes over them.

Extremely easy class to take. You seriously don't have to go to lectures, and if you decide to they never last all three hours. The lectures are posted online, all tests and quizzes are open note, all assignments are open note. The notes are all posted in a powerpoint for each unit. Follow the power point and you'll get a 100% in the class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very understanding with deadlines and allowed me to retake some of the materials from months prior to improve my grade. Responds quickly to emails even very late emails, also learned a lot about nutrition during this course.
Super easy class. He is very nice and answers emails quickly. All tests are open note, and pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Everything's online. You can attend in person, but the lectures are always at night. The PowerPoints are straight forward and are interesting and applicable to personal nutrition. The assignments and tests are also easy and open note. He did say this past semester (Spring 2023) he might make next semester more difficult, so be mindful.

Super easy class. Almost never went because of the time of the course but still passed with an A. Exams are open notes/open PowerPoint. Super easy to follow along with, and Glenn is super understanding with any circumstance. Pretty light stuff you learn, but also interesting if you enjoy it.

This class is extremely easy, you never have to show up to class and assignments are very easy to complete. This class takes me an hour each week, and you only need 90% to have an A. You can find answers on PowerPoint and Quizlet. All exams are open notes and have lots of time to complete! Would 100% recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class is the easiest class Ive taken so far. 3 homework assignments. 1 lecture a week. Test every 3 weeks. This class was on the back burner all semester. Attendance isnt mandatory. You can do the entire class online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Glenn makes this class nice and easy. It was a perfect elective credit for an easy A. All assignments are given a week before the due date. Skim over the power points and have them open for the quizzes and exams and you should pass easily.
Watch the lectures and take notes and you'll be set for the test! Homework assignments are easy. No textbook, just powerpoint slides. Nice professor!

One of my favorite classes at KU. I learned alot and was almost effortless. Take him and his class for sure. You dont even have to show up for class. Just 2 easy homework assignments and just go through the slides to prepare for the test and you will do great!

This is the easiest class I've ever taken at KU. There are two homework assignments, a few quizzes, and a few tests (all online and you can use the slides for them). I spent less than an hour a week on this class and did not go to lecture because it was optional. If you are a pre-health major or track take this class if you need an easy elective

This class was by far my easiest class this semester. Basically, you don't have to show up besides for tests if you don't want to, but his lectures are interesting if you're into nutrition. The whole class is pretty much just exams but he uploads the slides and the test questions are always somewhere on the study guide. Fun and stress-free class

Easiest class I have ever taken. All points are specifically from tests but tests are almost word for word of the study guide, so do them. He gives 15 points extra credit and it is barely any effort, so do that as well. Also, I never went to class except on test days and I was fine.

very easy yet interesting class. All points in class are from tests but if you do the very short study guides he gives and memorize/study them, you will be great I promise. the lectures are optional and everything is online.

Marty is the best. He doesn't require attendance and you really don't need to go to class to get an A. All the lecture notes are online and the the tests are exactly like the study guides. I wish I could take another class with him! One of the most caring profs I've ever had.
Marty is so sweet!!! I did horrible on my first test but studied a ton for the next 3 and got an A in the class with the help of his extra credit project.
This is the easiest class I have taken here. The tests are taken directly from the study guides. Attendance was not mandatory. No reason not to get an A

Easiest class I've ever had, just read the study guide that he provides, fill it out and memorize and you're good to go. 4 tests each worth 75 pts with 15pt xc assignment available. I don't know much about his personality because attendance is not required, but he is a very nice guy and will answer emails promptly if you have questions

Marty was the best! The class is super easy, and you'll for sure get an A if you go over the study guides thoroughly (they have the exact questions from the test). You don't have to go to class, but if you do, the lectures are put together nicely and have interesting content. Plus, you might get extra credit! It has been one of my favorite classes!
This is a very easy class. Minimal studying for an easy A. Really enjoyed the information as well. Would highly recommend this class
No textbook use, no need to show up to class. Never went to class and still received an A.

Marty is very cool and easygoing. No, you don't need to go to class, but I went to every one and really enjoyed how he incorporated short videos and other multimedia into the lectures -- it kept them engaging. The class is in the evening, so it can be hard to focus, but Marty did a great job teaching in a way that kept my attention and interest.

Marty was awesome. I only went to class once on the first day and left halfway through because I got bored, but if you do the study guides and memorize them you'll do great. He posts powerpoints to Blackboard and reads directly off of them. I had a D in the class, but got a 100% on my final (non-cumulative) and got a B. Very flexible with students.
Real easy class , you never have to go to class , not even the first day of class just do the study guides he posts on BB and you will get an A on the tests and in the class.

This class was SO easy. Do the study guides, read them over a couple times and memorize the numbers! No textbook, attendance not required (but go the first day). Although it's an easy class, don't put off studying too much. Marty was helpful and worked around your schedule if exams conflicted.

Although I got a C+ in the class, its because I didnt try lol. He makes this class easy to pass honestly. Hes super chill, doesnt make you show up to class EVER. Hes a little boring and mono toned but all around is really nice and defiantly willing to answer your questions and loves what he teaches.

So easy. Do the study guides, look over them a few times before the test, and you're golden. Memorize numbers. For example, how many carbs an average woman needs per day. These WILL be questions on the tests. He is a great guy and is always willing to help. I recommend this class to anyone who needs an A to boost a GPA!

Great teacher! He will get back to your e-mails right away and he really makes this class easy for you. Make sure you study the study guides though, going in to the test just reading them a couple times wont get you a good grade. Only went to class on test days and did good :)
Interesting class and very easy material. You never really have to go to class because all the notes and study guides are posted. Easy A!

EASY. Seriously just do the study guides and you will pass the test, you do not need to attend this class except go the first day and the exam days. That is all, easy A. Great teacher the classes I did go to he was clear and simple to the point. No busy work just the facts straight up and on the exam. Attend regularly if you really want learn!

Class is optional except for test days. Tests are very straight forward and he posts study guides online with his powerpoints. He guarantees that anything not on the study guide, will NOT be on the test. Great guy.

Never went to any classes except test days. He gives you the questions he'll ask on the test with the answers so all you have to do is memorize those questions. He is the nicest guy. Had homework once and it was super easy! Seriously easier class than high school! Loved it!

Easy class, but actually interesting. You never have to go, but do the study guides the day before the test and then study them a few hours before the test. If you need extra credit go to the last lectures for test 4 and 5 and you will get some if you stay the whole time. Nice guy.

Easy... this class is like at a high school level he is a dope as hell teacher gives you a study guide and posts his power points online. I never went to class and got an A just study like and hour or two before the test and your golden.

Marty is a really nice teacher. He provides you with powerpoint notes and wants you to succeed in his class. His tests come from his notes, he doesn't try to trick you. If you have to take nutrition, take it with him.
Easy easy easy.

This class is so easy. Marty is totally understandable and his tests are easy. Just review the study guides he provides you and you will easily get an A. He takes attendance but you can miss 3 classes, not too bad for only having to go once a week. Take this class with Marty!
Interesting fun class

Marty (he encourages you to use his first name) is a great teacher.  His Monday evening class is convenient, as well as interesting.  The 2 1/2 hour class never lasts more than 1 1/2 hours, and half the class is videos.  His notes are available online, and are directly applied to the tests.  An easy A!

Easy class. Just review the study guide and you will do really well on the tests.  He is a nice guy and grades homework really easily.  A large portion of the class depends on your attendance, so show up.

They aren't kidding when they say easy. Like... for monkeys. Never went to class (first lecture titled "why humans need food" - I never went back but for tests). Printed off lecture slides & study guides 5 hours b4 class, answered the ?s on the SG's once & never got lower than a 90% on an exam. He takes attendance now tho, so only got an 89%. Yeah.
very easy, nice...him and his wife teach the class. easy a.
VERY easy!! you never have to go and you will still easily get an A.
He team teaches with his wife and they are both very clear and the class is really easy.  An A is almost guarenteed.  Take this course from them, it is at night, but trust me, it is worth it.
He's a really great teacher that cares about what he teaches and his students. Some may consider the class to be a lot of work, but it is a great experience if you take advantage of it.

This class is a ridiculous amount of work for a 100 class, but learned a lot, nonetheless. Be in class, do all readings, and don't wait until the night before deadlines to start grant writings. Dr. White wants his students to do well. If he is not clear, just ask questions. Put in the effort and you will learn, gain confidence, and earn the grade.
I have had my disagreements with Dr. White, but have learned that he has a lot to teach.  Expectations are high and not always relayed at its best.  Overall, I would take his class over again.
He is very kind, caring and helpful.

This class is ridiculously hard for a 150 level class.  Says he wants to help his students, but during his office visits he's really not that helpful.  He's REALLY picky on what he expects, but doesn't communicate it to you until AFTER he gives you the grade.  Overall a frustrating experience.

Dr. White has been extremly helpful and understanding as my teacher and advisor. He does have a busy schedule but makes time for his students.  I recommend him and also he is a very relateable teacher.
No Comments

He doesn't communicate well and is stuck in the academic world, though he claims to be "real world" kind of guy.  He never answers questions directly and his class was an overall frustrating experience.

I took Professor Gonzalez's WGSS class this summer online and enjoyed it. I work full-time and she was accommodating when I reached out to her for help. Anyone who complains about her doesn't want do the work that comes with the class. Take her class, reach out to her, and put in the effort that comes with completing the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: im taking prof Gonzales online class right now. she's responsive to questions and comments. as long as you do the readings and the work, its an easy class. I don't know what others are talking about, she isn;t bad.
Took her for an online class summer 2025. She's quick to respond to emails. Lots of reading and weekly discussion posts. Important to follow instructions.

Her syllabus, grading style, and canvas are incredibly inconsistent. For example, she has assignments worth 125 points, but only will give 100 or 25 depending on the response without a clarity on what is what. I lost a parent and made a simple mistake on an assignment due to stress. She let me fix the mistake, but gave me a zero without explanation
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Very unstructured and all over the place. Attendance is mandatory and if you're not there it's a you problem, and she made that clear. Not very helpful at all, and can be rude if not liked or if you miss a few days. 
TA was of little to no assistance as well. Have to wait months to get grades back. Assignments created and let known last second too.

I liked this professor in the beginning. Her lectures were only via mouth, and her slides that she provided never had all of the information of them. She also refused to post the lecture notes.
Her course is very disorganized as well.  You never knew what you were walking into it seemed. I don't think she knew either.
Prof Gonzalez is easy going. Make sure to take notes in class and attend lecture. Highly recommend her so far.

im in her borderlands class and so far it's been a lot of fun. professor Gonzalez is super smart but makes her lectures and discussions relatable. we had an invited speaker this semester. she gives extra credit but make sure you do the readings and attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She's an amazing professor who is caring, understanding, and gives extra credit.

Walter is very knowledgable and passionate about sociology. That being said, his lectures can be hard to follow if you do not do do the readings. Expect to read 15-20 pages before class. If you turn things in on time, put in effort, and show up to lecture you will be fine. Interesting and engaging material, but more work than you would think.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I do think Walter cares about his students and their success, however, his class was pretty terrible. The lectures were hard to follow sometimes and the grading criteria was unclear. For a 100 level class, there was entirely too much work and it felt like a masters class at times. Don't take this course if you have a heavy workload as it is.

The worst class I've ever taken at KU. There is no structure to his class and his grading criteria is completely unclear. He is neurotic about doing things his way and expects everyone to be passionate about sociology.

Absolutely no professionalism. Long and random lectures that are sometimes wearily tied back to content. Would never take again or recommend. Not available outside of class and doesn't really answer emails. Unclear grading rubrics as well

This professor has absolutely no class structure and it is really difficult to sit through sometimes. He talks for the entirety of the lecture and fails to tie in any lessons to what was assigned outside of class. He is everywhere and extremely hard to follow. It is also hard to believe that he is not pressing a certain agenda out during lectures..
hard grader, barely answered emails, good lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Walter is a great professor and very passionate. He has a decent amount of work for the 150 level class but is understanding and helpful with everything. I would recommend this class to someone who wants to learn, but if you are someone who never goes to class this isn't the one for you. Only one test but group reading almost every week

Walter is awesome, he really knows what he's doing and it's clear he's passionate about sociology. Great at engaging with the class and his lectures were super interesting. Definitely more work than I expected for a 100 level class, but I learned a lot of cool stuff so it was okay with me. He's also just a really caring, empathetic and funny guy.

Professor Gong prepares well-thought-out lecture slides and gives all the materials well before you even need them. He is very accessible outside of the classroom and more than happy to answer any questions. Be sure to do all extra credit opportunities provided. Take his class if you get the chance!

Amazing professor, Professor Gong genuinely cares about his students and is receptive to student feedback. He is very kind and helpful, and is always willing to stay after class to thoroughly answer student questions. The lectures were always well prepared and the notes were very organized and well done. He also responded quickly to emails.

Sien is a very caring and respected professor. His notes were organized and posted for students to continually access. He never hesitated to stay after class to answer questions. He ensured there was time in class to work through difficult homework problems and checked in on his students regarding the difficulty of the homework and exams.

Sien genuinely cares about you passing his class. He always stays a little after class to answer your questions. The class does have lots of HW and weekly quizzes, but there is plenty of time to complete the HW and the quizzes are similar to the examples seen in the notes. Daily lectures (not too bad). Class averages for midterms were above 87%.

Great professor! It can take a week or two to get used to his style of teaching, but he is super kind and understanding. Take advantage of the extra credit on the assignments, and he is always available for questions before/after class.

Pamela Gordon is an exceptional professor. She deeply cares about her students and their learning experience. She cares more about understanding the content than merely remembering it. I truly respect Dr. Gordon. She is a joy to know.

She is genuinely a very kind and caring teacher. Ancient Greek, like all dead languages, is technical and hard but she really cared about what she was teaching and her students and always wanted to make sure we not only understood the material, but also were enjoying it.

This is a great class to take to fulfill KU core. You definitely have to watch the videos and read the slides every week in order to be able to do the homework, but it isn't bad at all. I took it as an 8 week course so it was just quire a but of work every week but it wasn't difficult at all. Just takes a little time. But nothing ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you do the readings and go to class it is incredibly easy to get an A. Also the quizzes allow unlimited attempts, so there's no excuse to get less than a 100% on them.

While Gordon is a rather funny and knowledgeable lady, her class was rather difficult to excel in. I had taken a year of Latin previously, but had forgotten bits over the summer months. When we started this semester, we didn't review and she only handed out review sheets and expected us to teach ourselves. Not a super hard class, but not easy.

I took the class online, assignments are fairly easy and allow multiple attempts, so you can get 100% on all. Don't procrastinate, though. She's not fast on grading but the class is easy enough you're never really worried about your grade. Easy A and prereq.
I love Dr. Gordon. She is so knowledgeable and can easily communicate that knowledge with others. She's so helpful with understanding things and giving feedback.

Really interesting class, she loves the subject, and an easy A if you attend class. You can look up the textbooks on google or sparknotes. Quizzes are online and allowed multiple attempts. She will post and overview of what you need to study before an exam; a lot you can review on the quizzes.

This is seriously one of the easiest classes you can take. It's super interesting and fun. The only way you can fail this class is if you never go to class or do any work. You can even sparknotes everything and pass the class with a "B."
Very easy class. If you go to lecture and at least skim the readings you will get an A no problem

Her enthusiasm in the subject infects the students, making class fun. The reading gets to be a bit much towards the end of class, but if you skim you'll be fine. Definitely look at the overview for every test. A very interesting and fun class, definitely take it as an elective.

This class is so easy.  Just go over the readings, take notes, and GO TO TEST REVIEW SESSIONS! She straight up tells you what you need to know for the exams. Definitely recommend if you need an elective!
Dr. Gordon is the best professor I have had at the University of Kansas.  She is dedicated, helpful, and kind.  Any class she teaches is worth taking.

Definitely take linear optimization with Bennet! His lecture style is amazing and he really cares whether students learn. One quiz and one homework per week (seem a lot for a 3-credit class but trust me the quiz helps a lot in understanding the material).
He is an amazing professor. He teaches really well and straight to the point.
This dude is awesome-end of story.

Bennet is a great graduate TA for Calc2 class. He has a great understanding of the material and knows how to dumb it down to our level of knowledge. He is more than willing to be in his office any time to help out students who request it. He makes hilarious comments while teaching that keep you engaged. He will make a great professor some day.
great teacher, was very helpful whenever I didn't understand anything. I would definitely recommend him for calc 1

Great teacher, very technical, extremely passionate (About Calculus? Yes.), super hyper and caffeinated, makes hilarious offhanded comments in the middle of his spiel, and lastly Bennet works super hard. He will have tests and quizzes graded the same day usually he is seemingly always in his office willing to help his lost students.

Im taking her immigration course, and Idk y comments down there saying things like that, but when I criticized the work she assigned to class that she likes she was totally ok. She is not a hard grader at all, and flexible towards ddl. If you are new to immigration topic def take it, but if u have had solid understanding, its gonna be a bit basic
This class was great, Andrea is a great instructor!

Students in the class became afraid to speak up because if you did not answer the way she wanted you too, she would criticize you and dismiss your point all together. The way she grades is ridiculous, if you don't say the one word she is looking for then you won't get credit. This class isn't hard or challenging, it is the teacher.

She was incredibly rude to people who did not share the same opinion as she did. I got a B on my midterm and when I went to her office hours she said that people generally do not do better then this in her class. She would assign around 40-60 pages of reading a night and was incredibly mean if someone didn't know something.

This class is interesting and Andrea is super helpful.  If you read the material, go to class and participate in lecture you will succeed.  She cares about people's success and will make appointments with you if you need help.  Do the work and you will get an A
You need to go to class or it will hurt your grade. One of the hardest teachers I have ever had. Would not take the class if you don't have to. Requirements are too much.

Professor Gomez Cervantes is one of the best professors I've ever had hands down! She is so inspirational and knowledgeable about sociology. I love her and her class! Her class is challenging but that's what makes it so great because you truly learn the information. She's a great teacher, super friendly, and dedicated to her students.
This professor was great. She is funny and she makes class easy to understand.
This professor is alright. She is really tough on grading and can be rude sometimes. She is unfair and plays favorites.
Excellent saxophone professor. He has high expectations, but is always willing to help, and is very connected to his students. Very well-liked.
Great professor of saxophone. Always engaging, kind, and helpful. He really wants each of his students to succeed.

Excellent saxophonist, excellent teacher. Takes a genuine interest in his students, not just as musicians, but also as people. Always willing to go out of his way to help you out with whatever you need, and very well-liked by everybody in the School of Music.

Great professor and great material shown in class. HIST328 was a lot of fun, and the readings / assignments were fulfilling. There were rough moments, but they paid off. Prof. Brown is very caring, but takes her job seriously. However, in my class, it seems she didn't get to the end of the intended course material(s) which was frustrating.

Took this class last year, but forgot to rate it. It was excellent and I fully plan to take more classes from MGB. I learned so much and was able to be creative and have fun with the papers. She does grade hard and there were only 3 papers so you can't mess around but if you engage with the lectures and apply what you learn you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown is an amazing professor. Lots of reading but also lots of time to digest and discuss. She is incredibly knowledgable, but isn't unapproachable for genuine questions. I have learned an insane amount, and am even inspired to look up more on my own time because of how rewarding she makes her class.

Didn't get the choice to pick if we wanted to do the take-home final we had to because she canceled class for a conference. Not much wiggle room in her class. She is a nice person and willing to help students but grades to harsh for a 300 level class. Both papers were 6-8pages too long for a 300 lvl class.

2 papers midterm and final. Offers no extra credit. Participation is 15% yet She has favorites though so it makes it hard to get picked to talk in lectures. She reads off a paper no notes on her slides digress a lot in class. Extremely tough grader and discourages you to talk about your paper for a regrade with the threat of getting a lower gr
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Brown is incredibly knowledgeable about the topics she teaches and is engaging and interesting in her lectures. She's also a very cool person. Pick the in-class final if she gives you the option!
Absolutely fantastic. Would take a class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: An amazing professor and an absolute bad ass. Be willing to put in the work that she requires, and you'll leave with an A and a better understanding of the material. One of the best professors I've ever had. Be ready to earn your grade!

MGB is an amazing professor. She is knowledgeable about her field of study and is very helpful when it comes to writing papers. She gives great advice and genuinely cares about her students. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Would take again

reviews.comment: MGB is queen
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown expects participation. If you don't talk at least once per class, you probably won't get an A. Her papers and tests aren't too hard, but you'll need to put in the work. She lets the class choose between an in-class and take-home final. Choose the in-class final. The take-home is very long and much harder. All in all, not a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Brown is extremely knowledgeable in her field, and she has taught me SO much this semester. Your participation really  matters, so don't take this class if you don't want to talk in class, but she is seriously there to help you learn and write amazing papers. You CAN get an A in her class, but you have to show her you best effort!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's very engaging but your grade is determined by two papers, participation, midterm, and a final so there's not much wiggle room.

She did a masterful job of guiding class discussions of the texts, which she integrated with bits of "lecture" to hit key points. If interested in being a professor/educator, you might want to take a class from her just to learn how it should be done. The type of professor that makes you wish you weren't a senior just to take more of her classes.

Her work ethic, work quality, overall knowledge of ceramics belongs in the fundamentals classrooms. I am terrified that she is allowed to teach an advanced course. I learned absolutely nothing from her course. Only to acknowledge that people will waste your time and there's nothing you can do about

Chaotic and exhausting class with no clear standards. Critiques are empty, grades show up weeks later with no explanation, and effort means nothing. Class time is wasted on activities that don't count. Support is nonexistent, bias is obvious, and expectations change whenever it's convenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Inflated sense of self-importance, offers no technical instruction and doesn't understand basic processes like gas kilns. Learning favors favoritism and quantity over quality. Grading is arbitrary with no rubrics or feedback. Dismissive when asked how to improve. Lacks mentorship and prioritizes her own work over students. Wastes class time ALOT
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She does not help you very much at all if you are a non-art major or even an art major that's focused on something other than ceramics. Only invested as a teacher in ceramics majors, and even then not very much. More invested in her own work than being a good professor, and sometimes prioritizes her own work over student work when it comes to kilns
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great ceramics professor, really knowledgable and gives great feedback
Gives specific students special treatment. It is unfair to others present.

Prof. Graf is very kind, although the environment can feel intimidating, she appreciates participation and effort in class. Her exams were formatted the same each time, with a mixture of different question types and not too difficult. I do recommend noting what is SAID in the lectures as well as written on slides/ at least skimming the textbook.

Graf is a good teacher in the classroom, giving solid lectures that cover the material well. The main reason why she gets a bad wrap is because she seems a bit... Stilted. It's hard to explain, but she doesn't seem entirely comfortable either in the classroom or during office hours.

Still, information is good, few assignments, and moderate tests.

Not sure why Kelly gets a bad rap. I truly enjoyed her class. She's very passionate about the content. She can be a bit condescending at times, but she means well. 4 assignments and 3 tests (noncumulative final). Overall, I learned more from her class this semester than any of my other classes combined. Everything you need is in the lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's really nice and cares, but expects a lot out of students for a second year studio. Learning about implementing structural elements was useful though.

Bryan expects a lot out of his second year students yet does not know how to work the programs he expects you to excel in ( revit and sketchup). Very contradicting and changes his mind quite often. Nice and friendly guy and I learned a good portion of structural design in his class but I think he would fit better in a third year position.

He does not know how to use Revit or Sketchup yet expects students to excel in the programs. He's incredibly closed minded and honestly disrespectful. He does not care about students ideas. Everything is about what he thinks and what he wants. It's extremely discouraging. He gives contradicting input and is always changing his mind.

Worst professor I have ever had. It is a short course, so she had to pack a lot into a short amount of time, which I understand. But she assigned a 430-page book, 2 30-page readings, an hour and a half video, and a four-page paper due all during Thanksgiving break. DO NOT take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Greene is very nice and very helpful when you reach out. However, her classes are very dull and boring. You discuss readings, and that is really it. Most assignments are just papers over the reading. I currently do not feel like I have gained anything from taking this class besides three more credit hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: From the structure of the class to the depth in which we went into the course materials, this class was a breath of fresh air for me and my interest in history. Reading multiple memoirs was a frustrating time commitment and lecture could sometimes drag but those are nitpicks; I highly recommend this course to any history enthusiast
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I had a lot of fun in this class, there is a lot of readings so come prepared to read for most of your homework.

Rather than boring textbooks, she assigns really interesting regular books and readings. I learned more in this class than any I have taken at KU. That said, there is a ton of work. A TON! More reading than any class I have ever taken and second place is not close. Be prepared to work incredibly hard. Very time consuming but very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Very good professor who is responsive to emails and willing to help you if you're struggling. She makes you read a lot, but the readings are well-chosen. Fairly tough grader, but not overly so.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I'm writing this review as I sit in this class. It is a book club. All we do is discuss readings. It's not that the topic is boring, the class is. We do readings every class and discuss them. Yes, I know it's history. But like I said, it's a glorified book club. There are seldom lectures, and you're basically instructed by the readings. Not Greene.

I was disappointed with this class. It's the classic case of an interesting topic bogged down by a dull teacher. Rather than lectures, every class was a discussion, which is the death of an interesting topic. It's annoying when you have a teacher that has dedicated her life to a subject only to leave the content open to discussion of goobers.

She assigns a lot of readings. I think we read 4 or 5 whole books during the semester, and she takes off what seem to be trivial points on papers for no apparent reason. Overall, the class was interesting, and she was a great teacher. Go to class and you can do well
Very good teacher.  Enjoyable lectures and good choices for assigned texts.  Very professional but not intimidating.  Not too hard but still challenging.  Really enjoyed the class.

I had moderate interest in learning about Mao, but this professor killed it. She tried to make a hundred person lecture into a discussion of various non-related texts which wound up moving down endless tangents. I didn't learn anything from this class, and frankly want my money back. Avoid if you dislike pop quizzes, lengthy research papers, etc.
Very interesting and knowledgeable. She was also very accessible outside of class. Her TA graded obscurely but Prof. Greene graded the important things.
Great teacher  had no idea what to think about subject but she made me think and tried to get everybody in the class to think also would definatly take a class from her again
