Often skips explanation of difficult material while proving arbitrary material. Lectures sometimes do not clearly reflect homework material. Ask a LOT of questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Horrible instruction, lectures impossible to follow, tests on material not covered in class or homework, stubborn. Avoid this class if you can, one of the absolute worst instructors Ive ever had.

Zheng's lectures were poorly structured and hard to follow. Homework was not indicative of the exams, and no other study materials were given. The tests were extraordinarily hard. The quizzes weren't much better. This was one of the hardest courses I've ever taken. If not for Zheng, it could've been a breeze. Don't take this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: TAKE AT EDWARDS CAMPUS. Avoid him if you can, he has the most bizarre niche tests possible. You have to literally memorize the slides if you want to do well. Actually knowing biochem gets you no where.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His class was hard for me, but the SI sessions really helped. The tests were more about small things and vocabulary, and yes, he counts off for spelling!! Make sure to memorize his slides word for word. The final is taken from the semester tests so make sure to study those too!

This class ended up being my favorite class that I have taken at KU so far bc it made sense, but does require you to study a lot. Exams were extremely specific, so you basically need to memorize every slide. He is a very good lecturer and outlines in class what details you need to know. Super easy clicker ?'s over lecture at the end of each class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While this was an accelerated level of biochem, there was just too much information to learn in one semester. The only way to do well is to just memorize. Don't get caught up on the concept. There was so much info on the slides that we didn't even know what he considered was "important." You are able to drop the final if you have an A in the class.

He was very boring. Class was 100% memorization of 1000 terms. All one worded answers fill in the blank. Do not recommend taking biochem with this professor. Final was 20 pages over 40 chapters. He will tell you "what to know" and then test you on opposite during the test. Averages on test were D's and one time 58%. Take at Edwards campus!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: you can't ask questions in the exams and his questions are worded poorly, the study guides rarely reflect the information that will be on the tests, attendance in mandatory, and his slides contain unnecessary information that "wont be on the test" but it still sometimes was. Take this class from another professor or avoid it all together if you can

Dr. Guzman has high expectations, and wants his students to succeed. However, if you want to do well you will need to read and study a lot on your own, and hope his study guides are an honest representation of the exam (they aren't always).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Guzman is hilarious and will keep your attention. He is a great guy, and you will see that if you take his class. With that being said his lectures can be way off topic, and the tests are very difficult. He was much better than the second teacher, Dr. Walsh. I would say take this class if guzman is teaching, but STAY AWAY FROM WALSH!!

I loved de Guzman for 639. He was funny enough in his lectures to keep you interested for exactly 50 minutes, once a week. Pay attention because he will call on people and write everything that he writes - his test is just an exact cut-out. Liked him so much that I'm taking my senior seminar with him!

Reading the textbook is essential!  His lectures are a little scatterbrained but take good notes and you should be fine.  Clicker questions everyday.  Tests are straightforward as long as you have put the time in to go over class notes and the textbook material.

De Guzman's notes end up looking like a word map. They are incoherent, but he is better than the second teacher, Gegenheimer. Do the review sheets he passes out, pay attention to what he says you should remember, and be prepared to apply what you know to questions, not just regurgitate information.
The best math teacher ever just ask question and he will answer anything he helps a lot
He really rocks. big ups Kyle, keep up the good works

I took calculus 1 from kyle and it was awesome! he is really hot and nice! he is a great teacher and explains things really well and doesn't go realllly fast. Dont be afraid to ask him questions either.

Kyle is awesome! Explains things very  easily. I never understood calculus until I took it from him. His tests are fairly easy, he doesn't make you memorize formulas, he gives them to you. If you have to take calc, be sure and take it from him. He is young and knows what it is like for undergrads. Loved him!

Worst class ever. Was so boring and she is an awful teacher. Had a ton of mistakes in the grading which i had to correct her on. Way to difficult for a gemstone class. thought it would be fun but was just dumb and hard. gives you the work and thats it, you do it with no help. tests are easy but assignments are irritating. Easy tho, but bad teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Final project is a joke. This online class expects more than a normal on campus lecture. Feedback on final project was rude, unhelpful, and borderline unprofessional. Take this class with someone else at all costs. Prof expects students to be pro's at oceanography regardless your major.

Do not recommend taking online course. 99% of lecture repeats book, but over 3 hours per week video lecture viewing required to access homework/test/next chapter. Sound quality awful for first 5 ch., bad for last 7: static, pauses, missing words. Final project must be done in person on campus with group. Homework entry confusing, feedback unhelpful
Took online class. Not very clear. Homework was not very fair. Professor not very helpful or understanding. Would recommend taking in lecture format versus online.

besides online quizzes, only a midterm and final test for grades. this is not as big of a problem after you realize the tests are nothing to worry too heavily about. i listened in class, then read over the chapters before the tests and pulled A's. she uses her laser pointer at a really sharp angle to the screen, so you can't see where she points
class wasnt what i expected.  had online quizzes that were super easy but only 2 tests were the rest of the grade.  tests were rather hard but very into it teacher that loves what she does.

lectures are pretty slide-heavy, lots of in-class discussion and partner/group work. however, you're able to "determine your own grade" as long as you turn everything in and show honest effort. i made so many mistakes and still got a good grade. can be a little boring sometimes but it was honestly really easy so i didn't mind that much.

I took SPAN 324 with Mira and they were my favorite professor of the semester! The grading policy was that you got to pick your own grade as long as you showed up and did most assignments which was super nice. Mira definitely made me feel like they wanted me to do well in the class and always tried their hardest to explain the content!
Very relaxed class and I felt like Mira helped us learn a lot not only about the language but about Latin American culture and history.

I took SPAN 324 with Mira. She does not create course content which can be confusing however she is a great instructor and is always willing to help and explain things further. She is willing to step away from the agenda to ensure the class isn't confused. She is a great instructor!
Very enthusiastic in class but there can be organization issues

While I appreciate a challenge, I didn't find professor Haydu all that helpful or approachable. I find her class a bit unorganized, which makes learning Spanish REALLY difficult. I felt as if I was just trying to survive class and was unable to actually learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Malinakova is a difficult professor. She uses lecture slides but jumps around so much that they make no sense. There are TAs that are helpful for the worksheets. That is if they come to your table which isn't often. I stayed 20 minutes after class almost everytime because we got no time to do the work sheets. Good luck, she is the only professor.

You will feel like you will know everything but then her grading is so wrong and makes you feel like you know nothing. You have to be very comfortable with learning everything by yourself if you want her as a prof.

If you prefer a teacher that's going to walk you through a problem step by step, she's not for you. I primarily had to learn from the textbook and YouTube. The textbook isn't very good and the info is hard to find sometimes. Use every resource she gives, test and homework keys especially. She uses something different from Canvas so work is weird.

Organic chemistry is hard, yes. The class is very manageable with REAL effort. Exams reflect homework and textbook problems EXACTLY as she claims, there are no surprise topics. Sure, no "traditional study guide", but the material to study is clearly there. The people NOT passing is 100% due to lack of effort and overexaggeration. Go to class.

Worst professor I've ever had. Test 30x harder than other chem 330 teachers. No multiple choice, barely partial credit. Doesn't curve exams. Had over 100 people drop the class. More people fail the exams then pass. UNBELIEVABLE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Malinakova as a person is not evil or rude or disrespectful, but her organic chemistry section will make you feel like you're taking an honors level weed-out class. The class is mostly exams, but homework takes forever, studying is entirely up to you, and she cares deeply if you answer questions the way you were taught. At least there's a curve.

She cares a lot about how things work in real life and in the lab.  She has 'homeworks', they aren't helpful except the 'study cards'. The textbook was written by her so its the exact same wording and format she uses in class. I recommend using youtube videos to fully understand the material. I would recommend still going to class.

Going to class, the lectures did not seem very useful. I studied the material on my own. The test is most of your grade. Some of the test questions were worded weirdly, which made me unsure of what to do--making me lose points. She offers 25 points of extra credit, which is enough to bring ur grade up by multiple percentages.
She is an amazing professor at knowing chemistry but she cannot teach it.

She's so sweet, and I can tell that she's passionate about the subject she teaches; however, she's not good at actually teaching it. Her lectures are based on a book she wrote (which isn't very good), and she doesn't give many practice problems.

Hearing the things previous students had to say about her class terrified me. Now, we are almost done with the semester. 
Students 1000% over exaggerate her as a professor. Anything on the tests can be practiced on the weekly HW assignments. She doesn't leave any surprises. She is nice and if you are willing to put in the work, you can succeed.

It says more about her teaching style than students' study methods when the class average is a 44% on exam 2. You would think that a scientist would make exams statistically valid. But, she doesn't curve exams or throw out invalid questions. When 60% of the class fails, look at the teacher rather than question if the students are putting in effort.

Worst lectures ive ever attended. Doesnt give study guides, practice tests. Instead wants you to do the homework assignments over and over again to study. And those are also terrible. If you cant get into benson, take honors Chem 330. Im currently on track for an A but this is after not going to her lectures and teaching myself the info. TA is odd

Just take Bensons class! Ive heard great things about his class. This teacher is passionate about the subject but not very good at teaching it. I had to watch Youtube videos and teach myself. Also the exams are worth majority of your grade so if you fail those you'll have to retake. Only thing good about her is the example problem videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (336, lab lecture) Dr. Malinakova is very sweet and one of the most understanding professors I've had. That being said, I was often very confused during her class and had to teach myself most of the material outside of class to feel like I could succeed in the class. She gave a lot of practice similar to what was on the exam, so make sure to review

The absolute hardest A I've ever had to work for. Lectures are monotonous and are almost never helpful, her explanations are difficult to follow and there are very little outside or in class resources to assist you (no TA's). I straight up just went to Benson's lectures instead and I advise you do the same. My A means nothing don't take her please.

I have to retake this class because I got a C- in her class. She has nothing in the grade book besides exams basically so if you don't do well on those you're not gonna pass. I am retaking it with benson next year because a C- is not accepted in Med/Dental/PA school so if you want to get a good grade in OCHEM run to bensons class!

Professor Malinakova knows a lot about the subject she's teaching, but she doesn't make the information easily accessible. She skims over/rushes through key topics without properly explaining them, and expects you to know/understand them with little instruction. I found her class tedious and exhausting, especially with exams worth 80% of your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is overall very knowledgeable about the topic, however, she sometimes gets off topic and can make it unclear about what we're actually supposed to know. Personally, the class was not too difficult, just need to put in the effort; paying attention in lecture and going to her weekly review sessions is the best way to get a good grade.

Overall if you want to understand organic chemistry I recommend this professor. I took her class over the summer and it was very time consuming but if you went to lecture and watched her mechanism videos you can do well in the class. Learn do not memorize the content or you will not do well in her class!

Overall, Malinakova is not a bad professor. She is very knowledgeable about the subject, just doesn't know how to teach it. I recommend attending office hours. The GTA Leander was no help so if you have her don't count on her. She never attended office hours and never responded to emails when asking for help. I still recommend taking Benson.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are applying to dental, PA, or med school do not take this class, you need to protect your gpa and this class with this professor is not the way to go. She has no mercy, my mother almost died mid-semester and I was not allowed to make up any points because I "should've got accommodations if I needed them". I had a 3.89 gpa before this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She gets a bad rep but she's a very knowledgeable and friendly professor. She is a strict grader but you will be FAR better prepared for O Chem 2 than you would with a different professor. If you're in O Chem to pass, take Benson. If you want to master the content, take her class. Also, the reason I got an A+ was due to an extra credit opportunity.

This is not an easy class regardless of the teacher. But it is harder with her. Tests are a high percentage of your grade, so don't mess up. She writes her own book/homework so if you don't know how she does something there is a good chance you will get it wrong. Her lectures are jumbled, and she speeds through content without going over it well.

Dr. Malinakova is a kind person who is knowledgeable about the subject, but she isn't the best at communicating what she knows in a clear and engaging way. Her lectures are very dry and tests make up EIGHTY percent of the grade in the course. She wrote the textbook used. A lot of this course feels like repetition of just a few concepts so far.

Book is very confusing because it doesn't explain anything. Homework and exams have many typos. I feel as though she teaches as if we took ochem before and assumes we know what she is talking about without explaining. GTA Leander is absolutely no help. Lectures sometimes doesn't match what is talked about on the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you haven't taken OChem 2 yet, I highly recommend it with her during the summer. Heads up, this class is very test heavy! To study, make notecards of all mechanisms, and watch all the videos she posts. Dont recommend taking it during a summer when you have the MCAT. Lots of work, but I'd retake this class in a heartbeat with her!

Ochem1 is really challenging, but Malinakova really does care for her students. This class will teach you that you have to take responsibility for your own grades and read through the textbook, take notes, go to help sessions, etc. (STUDY) Overall, she understands that the concepts are hard and gave us 35 points of extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Run for the hills. Do NOT take. I started asking for extra help in September and never received it. She is the type of professor that genuinely does not care about her students. CHEM 330 is supposed to be challenging, but she doesn't even help you understand other than saying to "study more." Trust the reviews- take anyone else.

I knew OCHEM was gonna be a nightmare but this was a horrible class. 80% of the grade are exams, 18% us homework, and 2% are "concept maps" so if you don't do good on test and homework you won't do good in the class. I was a straight A student until this course :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her current rating I not accurate as she reports all her recent bad ratings trust me. She exploits students and forces us to buy her online textbook which she gets a commission for she is only there for your money and that's it she really doesn't care about her students or planning lectures to be student-friendly.

Professor Malinakova is a very caring professor and always willing to help! Taking organic chemistry II in 8 weeks over the summer was not easy, but Malinakova is very accessible outside of class for assistance, and she makes every effort to work one on one with students to make sure they understand the material presented.

Very traditional lecture style teaching method. 80% of the grade was based off of exams, but you were able to drop your lowest exam score (including the final). I found this class to be graded a lot tougher than many of my other junior/senior level stem classes. The exams are exactly like the worksheet quizzes, I would use those to study the most.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have had. Her syllabus is very descriptive and straightforward. You have to pay attention in lecture and not look at your phone. Example problems in class and for homework are exactly like the test. This class takes work and dedication while learning in the classroom. Old school teaching style all paper. Nothing online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Malinakova was truly one of the best professors I have had. OCHEM is a challenging subject, so you do have to put in work to get a good grade, but Dr. Malinakova has a great teaching style and clear syllabus; the only thing that sucks is that exams are worth 400/500 points, but that is not her fault, all OCHEM classes are exam heavy

Grading is test heavy, but all homework is essentially free points. Her lectures are very thorough, but I found youtube videos more useful personally. She is a strict grader. Exams are graded by TA's and frequently have mistakes--check your exam to the exam key to make sure you get full points! This saved me several percent every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was very rude when answering emails. Take Benson to save your grade. She told us to not read the book to study for the test after I bought it. She grades extremely hard on the test so make sure u listen to every word she says and take in depth notes. Do every practice problem. Her lectures were bad. She literally scribbled on paper.

reviews.comment: I dont mind that she makes it a point to have a test average of 70% since chemistry isnt supposed to be easy. That is a big lie, dont even bother using homeworks as a study tool.

reviews.comment: Very test heavy so if you do bad on them, then you're not going to pass the class. I literally didn't learn anything this semester from this course because her lectures were horrible. I've heard Benson is better so take him if you can. The grading scale of this course is very unfair, in my opinion.

reviews.comment: Malinakova is one of the worst professors I've ever had, and I'm taking this class as a junior so I've had quite a few . 400/500 of the class points are from exams, and she makes the exam questions SO unnecessarily hard. I did fine with the practice problems then ended up failing an exam. Her lectures are pointless, she barely explains the topics.

Honestly such a great professor who really goes through lectures well. She has a syllabus that states what sections will be covered and you should read those sections before class if possible to really understand the lecture and understand the practice problems she does in class. She does a lot of practice in class, her tests are like the Pracprobs
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She does not have slides, only writes on a white sheet of paper under a projector. She made this class unnecessarily hard, making us learn mechanisms the book doesn't even cover

reviews.comment: Shes very passionate about what shes teaching, and shes a very kind woman. However, she tends to only provide practice problems during lectures instead of teaching the concepts of the problems. I had to do all of my learning from the textbook in her organic chemistry class. Shes the worst professor that Ive ever had :(

She was an absolutely terrible lecturer. She talked at us the entire class, and just wrote randomly all over a piece of paper. She didn't have slides, didn't give us problems to work on during class, or made literally any sense. She gave no extra credit, and 400 out of 465 points in the class were exams. She was very unhelpful outside of class.

Professor Malinakova is kind and willing to help after class. I was in honors ochem and I feel like I learnt more on my own than from lectures though. Personally I dont think shes the best and I feel like she could improve greatly. But its ochem so it is very possible to ace the class by studying by yourself consistently.

reviews.comment: I had Malinakova for Honors Ochem 1 and finished with a high A. You either hate Ochem or love it. Malinakova is VERY helpful after class and office hrs. Has high expectations of you  hard work. DO PRACTICE PROBLEMS!After the 1st exam, I saw a pattern in her exams and I credit that for my success in the class overall. Textbook is nice resource too!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: For those saying that those who "don't work hard in this class" are leaving bad reviews, that's not true. As someone who is an honors student, I take my schooling very seriously. I went to the lecture every time barring a doctor's appointment and I was lost. I learned more from the textbook than any of her classes. Worst teacher I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Malinakova is really passionate about what she teaches and she is always willing to help. She doesnt like to see her students fail. Most people go into ochem thinking its impossible to succeed but in reality its their flawed perception that holds back their ability to actually do well in the class!

I have mixed feeling about Malinakova because she is a nice person, but the structure of her class is very frustrating. Her tests were very detailed and overwhelming. She really likes to trick you on the test. If you do have her as a teacher be prepared to really work for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was very hard. Malinakova went over practice problems during class. I then had to go back to the book and read everything she had just taught to understand the concepts. Tests are extremely hard and she makes them harder throughout the course even if the averages are not very good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She does not post lecture slides so you HAVE to take notes in class and I HIGHLY recommend doing the reading before class. She made our 3rd exam extremely hard because she thought our class average on tests was "too high" at a 79%. I have never worked so hard for a class to do so poorly
Ochem 1 is very hard and super conceptual. It requires a lot of studying and study groups are a must. Her tests never have anything that she does not teach but they are still very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Malinakova was a decent professor! Her lectures were good and she gave a lot of hints on what problems to do for the exams, including her final exam. However, she grades tough on her exams and quizzes but overall she does make sure you prepare well enough for her exams and quizzes. Her exams do cover a lot of information.

She treats the Ochem 1 like honors Ochem. She gives a minimal amount of review materials before the exam and her notes from the lectures only cover a minimal amount of material that will show up on the exam. The majority of this class is self taught because she teaches right out of the book. I would avoid her lecture if other options are available.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: she is a cold-hearted person. don't take a class with her, i'm warning you rn.
The worst class I've taken so far. She created the tests so that the average was 70% or lower and gave no study materials. Only take her class if you want a reason to switch majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's extremely bad. I'm pretty sure reading the textbook to the class shouldn't count as a lecture, but to her, reading the textbook and expecting you to know things is normal. Be prepared for hell :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am currently taking her OChem honors course. I havent been doing too well, and asked if she graded on a curve. She got angry and told me to read the syllabus, which just says that point totals cannot be translated into percentages(?). She made me cry, and she laughed at me for being so worried about my grade. Just wish she was nicer about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Homework due each Friday, and a quiz each Friday (2 questions worth 10-15 points each). Tests are about 9 questions worth 20-30 points each. This may sound intimidating and a lot of people complain about this class but if you aren't lazy and understand the practice problems it's an easy A. She gives obvious hints on problems you need to know.

Her class was the first chemistry class I have taken at KU where I felt like I really learned a lot and retained a lot of the information. The one thing I would say is when preparing for her tests, really know the information front to back. I always found that they included the hardest aspects of everything we learned and therefor struggled.

She is very fair with her exams, and does not have any surprises. She really values the students who really show that they want to learn, and is not as responsive to those who are merely concerned with their grade. She wants to help you succeed, and expects that you put in the work to get there. I will be taking classes with her again for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Malinakova taught as if her students were experts in the organic chemistry field. Her lectures consisted of one or two examples from the textbook and then about 40 minutes of her spouting off useless information that was not helpful. The textbook was a lifesaver in here-the only reason why I am still passing the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have had at KU. Highly recommend her for Organic Chem classes. Going to class is extremely important as she teaches you tips and tricks for reaction mechanisms that are not in the book. Very clear on what she expects from you and is not afraid to call the class out on poor grades. Always willing to help her students
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: After getting a very low grade in Dr. Benson's Orgo I class, I was terrified to take Orgo II (with any professor, because I thought I just didn't understand the subject). Dr. Malinakova, however, is absolutely incredible at explaining the concepts and will help you every step of the way. TAKE HER CLASS FOR O CHEM!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very clear on what will be on exams. Go to class because she will literally tell you which types of problems and mechanisms you need to know for her exams.
