reviews.comment: So So So good! Usually teaches second semester chem 330 and then chem 335 over the summer. Worth the wait 100%! Organic is a class you have to work hard on your own regardless but she makes it very clear what we need to know and how it needs to be executed. She literally will say in lecture how questions will be worded and gives reference examples!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really liked Dr. Malinakova. The grade distribution was a little harsh for an honors class though. Make sure to actually read the book; it's the secret to doing well in OChem in general. She was a very nice person but her lectures were a little disjointed and unorganized, so I found reading the book helped clarify things.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's an alright professor. However, she doesn't give any more insight than the textbook does. I feel like she's just reiterating what the textbook is saying and reworking the textbook problems on the board. Her tests are hard and she's a harsh grader. No curves in the class.
She's great but please do not take ochem2 in the summer unless it's a retake. Also, the textbook should be your best friend. You'll be just fine if you read it.

Dr. Malinakova was excellent, didn't pass OChem 2 with Benson (terrible!) the first time around, so I took this class during the summer. She is so much more clear, and explains the material instead of only problem solving. I would've been so much better off if she had taught in the Spring!

I absolutely love her! She explains all the material, and it's a lot easier to understand than, say, just going over examples in class. The lectures are dry, but they are very helpful. I feel like I understand OChemII a lot better than I did OChemI because she actually teaches the material. I wish I had taken OchemI with her. She's a great teacher

Super helpful and very nice. Lectures are engaging. She really makes sure you understand the material and doesn't make you teach yourself. Great teacher for an inherently difficult class. Retook 335 with her because I failed the first time, and it's like I'm taking an entirely different class. I suggest you take organic from her if you can.
I love her, she's absolutely amazing and very understanding. Take her! 5/5

She is an amazing professor. She goes really slow through the material and holds extra help sessions. The class is not hard if you practice and go to PLUS sessions. The only bad thing is she is always gone on test weeks.  She is very lenient on grading  and will give partial credit.

She's is a great professor. Always available after class Mon and Wed. Homework and quizzes are what's on the exam. I think she might have changed her teaching style, because looking at older reviews, she is nothing like they describe. She's very helpful. Yeah lectures are boring, but get over it.

LOVELY WOMAN! Exams are easier then Besson's but less questions which means the less you miss the more it affects your grade. She pads your grade with free homework points as well. She's very helpful and even provided me with research experience. GREAT INSTRUCTOR!!! LOVE HER!

She was great, her accent is sometimes hard to get through but if you attend class, do the homework(honestly) and practice it again and again the quizzes and tests will almost be a breeze. She has in class tests and going to PLUS was key to my success. I got an A in her class, but its by no means an easy A. In this class practice makes perfect.

Malinakova is great!  I am retaking this class after a nightmare with Benson and I love the way she explains things in class and really makes them make sense.  She doesn't try to lord her chemistry power above all of the students either so that's great.  She responds to emails quickly and is always able to answer questions.  TAKE THIS CLASS!

Malinakova is a good lecturer as far as Chemistry, it's not an easy thing to teach. My suggestion, GO TO PLUS, it helps tremendously. Exams are very similar to homework. Book's not mandatory,, and the way she teaches/draws problems is very different. She's "out of town" every exam week so don't both asking for help. Doesn't hand back quizzes/HW.

Helena is a great teacher that is very willing to help outside of class. Her lectures may be dull, but if you pay attention and do your work the class isn't so bad. Organic chemistry is a pretty hard subject to start with, but she does a great job of teaching it. The book really helped me as well.

Easy A if you go to all the classes and do the recommended problems. Tests taken almost exactly from quizzes and homework. No surprises. Good teaching methodology and always prepared. Very nice and willing to help outside of class.

She was good at explaining things, but the book is your best bet.  She does move kinda fast, but if you have a question she'll go back over something.  I definitely say this is a study-ever-night kinda class.  The material is hard, but she keeps the formats for tests consistent even though they are tough.

The person who posted the comment below probably failed the class. She's boring but is not a bad teacher. I failed one test but still got an A in the course. Just keep up with your reading and go to PLUS if you're struggling.
two words: Run away.
Very clear about concepts that should be learn. Tests are fairly easy. Questions on tests and quizzes are taken almost verbatim from the text.

I'm sure she's a nice person, but her teaching strategy is not the best. She's confusing and doesn't go in order of the book. The book is entirely mandatory for this class cause you won't understand her. She is usually busy with research so you can't ask her for very much help.

Malinakova did a good job at getting the difficult material across. She can be dry, but going to class was worth it for me. She's good at piecing the concepts together and helping you visualize 3rd-dimensionally. I had her for both OChem I and II, and did well in both. Be sure to go over hws, practice problems, and go to reviews. She curves, too.

I liked her better than Benson. Her lectures are boring, but it's a boring subject. Her tests are written, not multiple choice, which I prefer for a class like this. The only problem was that the graders were sometimes a little hard on grading, depending on who graded your test. Don't worry if you don't get an A or B on each test, there's a curve.

she is a boring lecturer and all her lectures are very boring. Had to teach the whole class to myself through the book. I would highly suggest a tutor. She puts things on the test you have never heard about and counts off on things that arent wrong

Dr. Malinakova's lectures are extremely boring and they don't help you prepare for any of her exams.  Basically, it's pointless going to lecture (even though I've attended every lecture and still have yet to learn anything from them).  Her exams are really difficult.  At least there's HW to boost your grade.
Boring lectures.  She is not very helpful in getting the students to understand the material.
No Comments
No Comments
her lectures were a bit dull...
No Comments
Boring class.. easy tests.  I wasn't really interested in the subject material so what can I say..
Nice enough, but either overexplains or underexplains.  Boring too.
It was a course of learning by trauma... only without the learning bit...

I found her to be far more interesting than Dr. Carlson. She demands more of you in that there is weekly h.w. graded for accuracy. However, her exuberance is contagious and the smaller class size allows her to keep attention of most. Lenient on tests too.
I took UNIV176 with her, an amazing professor who provided 5+ extra credit opportunities throughout the year, was very flexible with late work, and cares about you as an individual.

I took GEOG 202 Culture and Health, Honors with Dr. Snay. Great professor! Weekly readings and annotations weren't too time-consuming. Easy A if you participate (which is required), but she's understanding if you miss class. Lectures can be tiring but insightful. Final project took time but wasn't bad. Just note an A- is 95 or below.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is very down to earth and kind. She taught course information well, but the class was very boring and the grade book consists entirely of participation and biweekly busywork assignments. Reading material was interesting and gave good insight for premed students.

This professor is super knowledgable for GEOG 202 (there was no option to pick this class). She is amazing to talk to and is great at analyzing social situations. If you're going to be a medical professional, I would definitely recommend GEOG 202. Heather is great and her class is super interesting if you participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Classwork was fine, required book was $80. My issues are with the professionalism of Heather. 
She didn't grade work from beginning of Oct. until the end of Dec. 
I sent her two emails and she never responded to either. 
Waited until the last min to grade the final, ignored my email about it, so my grade was finalized as that. Frustrating.

Professor Herlihy is clearly passionate about his work. It shows within his lectures. With this said, if you are not into long, information-filled lectures, this class is not for you. The extra credit opportunities he gives are according to his lectures, so if you aren't paying attention to the lecture, good luck! Overall, super chill guy!
He is super passionate and it shows. The one thing is that the tests can be VERY LONG, but they aren't hard. The questions can sometimes just get repetitive. Otherwise he's super fun to listen to!

Great professor. Potentially the greatest professor I have ever had the opportunity to learn from. He is very passionate and can get carried away in lectures. Honesty, if you're even half as interested as he is in giving the lectures, you'll get whole semesters worth and more out of prof. H.

Dr. Herlihy was my favorite educator I've ever had. I had him for multiple classes over a year ago but just got around to leaving a good review. His passion really sparked my own and he helped me find direction when I really needed it. If you showed up ready to learn and listen, you would be well prepared and leave hearing a lot of cool stuff.

I loved his class. I took it over a year ago and i still rave about it. he is so passionate about what he talks about and has real experience with the discussion. if you want to actually learn and enjoy it then take his class. i never liked history until i took his class!! just go to class and you'll be good. wish i kept in contact!
Herlihy is very knowledgeable on the subject of geography but that often isn't clear in his lectures as he often rambles and does not focus on things that end up on the tests.

He was a very nice guy and a good teacher. The tests are pretty long and difficult but overall he makes it really easy to get an A in my opinion. He genuinely cares about his students and is very passionate about what he teaches. I loved being in his class and would definitely take a class with him as the professor again if I could.
He's good and the class is super easy but there is a lot of work.

Class was easy and straightforward in an online format. Work load was manageable, which is a good thing since Professor Herlihy has a policy where all work must be completed by the last day of class or you will be given an incomplete in the course. He's known for getting off track in lectures, but the stories he tells are interesting nonetheless!

Peter is a great guy, but his lectures are super boring and he gets off topic really easily. Half the time he doesn't cover the material meant for the class because he is telling a story. The tests are super easy if you go to the review sessions and look at the notes online. The only thing that goes towards your final grade is 2 test scores.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: While the class was easy enough, he was often late and/or absent and it was quite hard to stay awake during his class. Attendance isnt mandatory but if you always show up itll give you extra credit.

Professor Herlihy really cares about the material he lectures on. You can tell he is passionate about what he is teaching which makes his lectures interesting. However, the exams are extremely hard, make sure you read the textbook and study the maps!
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tests are based on the maps he passes out in lecture and reading the textbook. The textbook is really the "teacher" in this course. You're really only graded on your online work and the tests. He was a really passionate guy, but more in a historical than geographical context, not really a great fit for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He tells a lot of stories and talks a long time about his experience. They would be interesting if I was different but some how each story has a similar story line. Within the hour and fifteen minutes you'll take maybe half a page of notes because he just talks and talks and talks.

I love Peter as a person, but his teaching is everywhere. Scattered in his lessons and often gets off topic. Basically only use the book for key word lists and maps. Easy to get an A though because he curves every test.

He's one of my least fav. teachers. He would get very political in class, but always add "This isn't political, but..." His notes aren't too helpful, and the key word list is an unorganized mess. The work book is a pain. It wasn't exactly difficult, but an annoying class, and an annoying professor.

Professor Peters is  a cool old man. He likes to ramble on different tangents when he is talking. However, the random tangents really help you remember the material. He is very helpful and willing to work things out with you. Highly intelligent. Make sure you do the work book and Key word list. Class can be boring at times, overall a great teacher

Really great teacher, he knows his stuff. He usually passes around a sheet of paper so attendance is required although you could probably skate through with a C if you only showed up for the tests. Tests are basically straight from the notes which he usually takes from the book. He almost always let class out early. Funny old man.
Gets off topic 95% of the time during lecture.
good teacher , however the class is boring, he is old school doesn't use e-mail nor blackbord , gives good grads study and  do the keyword list and you will be set

The best professor I've had at KU.  He is extremely nice and engaging.  Topics are very interesting and yes he goes off talking about personal experiences but that is what makes the class so engaging and fun.  He has been EVERYWHERE and his stories will make you want to travel everywhere he talks about.

Really easy class.  He rambles sometimes and gets off subject but I think it's because he's really smart and has so much information to spit out that he gets carried away.  Nice guy, gives good curves on the test.  Just study the key word list and do the maps and you should get an A.

I'll agree with the previous comment.  He's a real nice guy, but is somewhat of a scattered brains.  His lectures can get off topic real quick and you lose interest immediately.  But he is passionate about what he teaches and is actually a pretty funny dude!
He gets distracted (by himself) awfully easily, but he's a genuinely nice guy and you can tell he's passionate about his subject matter. More power to him.

Took GEOG 100 over the summer with him. Nice teacher. However, a bit unorganized. He gets off topic frequently to talk about his personal experiences, which are actually very interesting, but I wish we'd talk about it after the class material. Other than that, pretty straightforward class. Not very hard to get an A in.
Great teacher. Was a little unorganized at times, but overall loved his class.

Hes kind of all over the place and the tests are hard but he is extremely fair! Go to any test review he offers, they are very helpful. Curves the test almost 10% if not more. He is very nice as well.
I absolutely love this class. Not only is Herlihy interesting and enthusiastic hes totally hilarious.
wow how does KU hire such weird teachers...class was OK but I hate the subject matter now thanks to prof.
couldnt wait to drop this waste of a time course
Bald dude who made me fall asleep three times in lecture. I couldn't handle his stupid tests or his stuttering. Why doesn't ku ever get rid of deadwood?
very helpful and gives good lectures for notes
No Comments
Very interesting lectures, funny and brutally honest, he's not for kids that need to be spoon fed material

LOVE this guy!  Entertaining and funny...  it is thanks to him and this course that I stopped being a pre-med major... much bigger world out there!  The class isn't hard so long as you take good notes and study them - very straight forward
Stupid class. Teacher needs to organize better and spend less time making corny jokes. I agree with the reviewer about teacher´s attitude toward women. He is pathetic and silly.

Best professor I have ever had.  I took one intro level geography class and I wound up taking 27 hours of it in college because of how interesting Herlihy made it.  Take his class even if for general ed requirements, you'll enjoy it.
Bogus & boring-give this a miss unless you want to sleep. Teachar is not well prepared and his jokes are demeaning to women.
No Comments
Prof. Herlihy is very enthusiastic about his work and it is apparent in his teaching abilities.
Very easy class. All lectures are posted on Canvas, and only 3 open note exams all semester. Should be an easy A for all.

Literally don't even need to show up to class. Most of the time its just lecture (slides are provided on canvas and I would just take notes from these on my computer). You would have lab tours but attendance wasn't mandatory. Super easy class. Only have 3 exams and you can use notes and the slides that he provides on canvas. The exams are online.

Trent was a great teacher and definitely recommend him if you are looking to take a class. He is very understanding and accessible, provides many opportunities to make up for missed points including lots of extra credit. The weekly quizzes give you two tries too, so that's a bonus. Attendance is not mandatory, but sure helps for the main tests.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed taking Intro to Exercise Science with him. He gives you plenty of opportunities to get extra credit, and tests can be taken with notes. I definitely recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed learning from professor Herda. He never wastes the student's time and provides ample opportunity for students to get involved in research and get extra credit. Attendance is not mandatory, and it was easy to catch up with the chapters if the class was missed. All exams are open note/book and taken over zoom.

this class is very easy, the tests are open note, with multiple tries. the lecture materials are posted on canvas as well.  the exams are fairly easy as well and open note. dr. herda is super nice and a very relaxed professor. you dont have to attend the lectures but they are beneficial.
literally so chill. makes your life super easy and he's a great teacher :)

This class was doable because exams were online. Herda is very blunt about what will be on the exams, therefore as long as you study what he tells you you will be okay. Didn't get the textbook and was fine.

Had Mr. Herda for into to exercise science, amazing teacher, gave lots of extra credit. Honestly I went to class like every other week and still had a 98%, he actually cares about students and his job and it shows! if your looking at this class 100% TAKE HIM!

Dr. Herda was an awesome prof. Lectures were easy to follow. He gave good advice for future exercise science students. Gave insight to what the program is like. No textbook required, just his lectures and powerpoint slides! If you have a high grade at the end of the course you don't have to take the final!

Dr. Herda is great. He is very welcoming, and provides opportunities for academic achievement outside of class. He runs a research lab that is well respected, and lets undergrads get involved if they want. Stay on top of the course content and you'll do just great. One of my favorite professors yet!

Dr. Herda is so passionate about what he does and it shows in his lectures. He gives tons of extra credit and all of the quiz and exam questions are straight off of the slides. You could easily just look at the slides online and never come to class, but I recommend going because he is so nice and funny, and you learn a lot! Can't recommend enough!

I should've gotten an A but i missed it by a few points because I got kind of lazy, but this class is super easy and I went to maybe a couple actual classes. All the tests are based off the powerpoints that he posts online and that's all the classes are. If you look up quizlets for the tests they're basically the same thing. Also ec is given.

Amazing professor. Very relaxed and calm. Offers a lot of extra credit. If you show up to class he hands you what will be on the test but you can get a high grade just from studying off his power points online. Super easy class and hilarious teacher.

Trent is a great dude. He's really funny and genuinely cares about his students. Everything on the slideshows in class are exactly what's on the test. Class is frequently cancelled because of lab tours and other commitments. He wants to make the class easy for everyone, honestly don't know why you shouldn't get at LEAST a B.

If you're gonna take Intro to Ex Sci, take it with T. Herda. Knows his field well, which is evident in his lectures. Do not need textbook, all info on tests comes from his slides. Offers lots of extra credit so there's no reason not to get an A.
Very fair, not difficult to get an A

He definitely knows what he's talking about. Its a greatinteresting class, tests are online and open booknote! In class quizzes every 1-2 week for attendance. (Other quizzes too) Class is cancelled frequently due to divided class lab tours instead of lecture sometimes. Overall goodeasy class. (Spring semester is offered at 1 pm instead of 8am)

I took intro and biomechanics with Dr. Herda.  Go to class - he will cover all the slides and tell you what is important for the exam.  I wouldn't say he is necessarily a great teacher, but he definitely knows what he is talking about.  The book helps (biomechanics), but all the information you need to know is in the slides.  Overall good class.

Relatively easy. He does not make you come to class but go if you want to get an A. Especially on days when there is an assignment. A lot of these other reviews have talked about how helpful he is, but I don't necessarily agree with that. He was always annoyed with getting emails from students and getting asked stupid questions. Not welcoming.
Fantastic guy! Really wants you to do well. Knows what he is talking about. Also go to his class, he gives random 5 point quizzes and tells you exactly what to study for exams.

LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this class! Dr. Herda is HOOOOT and he is very passionate about research. He empathizes with college students! The class was 1-1:50 and we almost always got out early because he knows how much we didn't want to be there. And his class is VERY straight forward!

Great class. It's definitely hard to come at 8am, but it will be worth it. He'll tell you slides you need to absolutely study for the test and will help you out. He's a great teacher, and gives lots of free points! Easy A!

Only have to show up on days when you have an in-class assignment. text are directly off the slide show. He told us at the beginning of the semester that you could pass his class without ever coming and without buying the book...challenge accepted trent! and quite good-looking!
Easy class. Slept in the front row multiple times.
Class isn't mandatory but helps for tests. He is always there to answer questions but his tests are tough if you don't go to class. Really nice guy, take this class with him.
If I had another chance, I definitely wouldn't choose this course.

take her courses even if you find the topic intimidating or don't have much prior knowledge in the topic. at least in the 200 and 300 level courses, she will review basic concepts in the first weeks. the reverse classroom format  and the attendance policy makes it flexible.

I took FAH265 with Mostafa in Fall 2023, now I'm taking FAH325 with her. She's an excellent prof with fun lectures, interesting assignments and very fair grading. She is caring and easy to reach out to. Attend all classes and engage, its worth the experience. Prof will give hints and guides to do well. Highly recommended for everyone :)

lovely professor, one of the best at uoft! shes so sweet and clearly cares about her students, and she makes an effort to make sure that lectures are fun and understandable. i highly recommend taking at least one of her courses because she's really knowledgeable on islamic architecture and her passion is clear. truly a gem.

She is a gem of a human. Here grading scheme is the fairest I've seen so if you screw up once you have plenty of time to make it up. The lectures were well organized and incredibly interesting. Also just a fun person to be around-passionate, funny and easy going. If I could take more classes with her I would.

Professor Mostafa is clearly the leading authority on Islamic art, sprinkling her lectures with so many details and insights. Learned quite a lot about the Islamic world! However, also super easy class with an open-book midterm and no final paper or exam, just a poster. Great class, and easy A. (University of Toronto)
10/10 would reccomend!!

Heba is a wonderful lecturer. She's a fair grader and always overjoyed to help. Work hard and you'll be fine. She cares about her students and really loves teaching. She's funny and interesting. I would love to take more classes from her. No matter the subject, her course is gonna be good.
One of the best HA Professor's at KU, Heba knows her stuff and is very down to earth. She adds so much to lectures with actually providing context. TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!
I love Heba! She is so helpful and passionate and the subject seems hard at first but she manages to ease you into it. Make sure to go to class and use office hours and you will be fine!

he was a sweetie, and super funny, but not a great teacher. I had to really study the textbook and he kinda would zoom through his lectures and not give us any practice time. I do not remember any of the sign language from his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hernandez is nice but when a hearing person teaches ASL in spoken English, the content doesn't stick much in the head. He has a PowerPoint, shows the word in English, shows you the sign and moves on. Very important to get the textbook assigned or else (like me) you will miss a few signs that are on the test. Test every class.
Very easy class. Did not get much time to sign in class. The pace seemed too slow and we didnt seem to cover much.

He is one of the nicest professors I have had at KU. I enjoy going to his classes. They are easy and I m sure I m going to get an "A." I dont feel prepared to take ASL III. I did not do much signing in the class.
Michael is a great professor for beginners. I found his class to be too easy. It's an easy A, but I don't know if I'm adequately prepped for ASL 3.

Michael is a great ASL instructor, particularly for beginners.  He goes very slowly and repeats signs if you miss them.  He does not at all prepare you for the speed of ASL 3, but that's probably mostly due to the 3 prof being Deaf.  My only complaint is that he wasn't hard enough on students who talked through the entire class.

She teaches in a tone that is like youre having a conversation, and encourages in class participation. Classes make you learn the content, which she makes relevant through courses an assignments that use real world examples. It's interesting and she cares a ton for her students, but is strict when it comes to attendance, tardiness, and devices.

Professor Hind is a good teacher, but very strict. If you don't go to class you won't pass the tests or the course overall. Heavy on group projects and participation. Mainly, this class is an easy A, just a pain to take.
Pretty cool teacher, come to class, do the reading( yes its a lot), youll do fine.

Prof. Hind is easily my favorite prof I have experienced at KU! She makes a course in business law, which is not always the most engaging, very engaging and a fun discussion. She is beyond qualified, well spoken and on top she cares about every student. She comes to class with a positive attitude, smile and a genuine care for her students! A++ PROF

Windy Is a great Professor, aside from her warming personality, she is a great storyteller and can keep the class listening. I found her lectures very interesting and as long as you go to class  and review what she tells you to, you should be fine on the exams.

Super kind and easy to reach outside of class. I TA'd for her for a while and loved it. She's very helpful but I will say that she tends to be quite lecture heavy. Make sure you're attending class and actually engaging with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am unsure where all these negative reviews of Dr. Hileman are coming from. Dr. Hileman provides many opportunities to strengthen concepts, including practice problems (which will likely be used on the exam), and discussion sections. She is clear in what she expects you to know and holds office hours regularly. If you attend class, you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her lectures were very engaging, and I enjoyed listening to them and learning from her. She's available outside of class and is always willing to help students even if it means going over something she just talked about again. Just do what's expected and you will be fine.

I'm seeing a lot of negative comments about Dr. Hileman, but I do not agree. She cares a lot about her work and is always very friendly towards students. If someone doesn't understand her lectures, they probably just skipped the outside work (watching asynchronous recorded lectures before class). I love Dr. Hileman's class and I would take it again
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She was very dull to listen to. She didnt really care about the students much. The class material isnt that bad but the test are extremely difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Hileman means well but she has a hard time connecting during lectures. This class is very concept heavy and she just didn't do a good job getting her points across. Too many examples/pictures, very little explaining/material to base off of. Go to lab & get a good grade bc its 18% of your grade. The rest is basically tests. READ THE BOOK!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. does a good job simplifying complex equations and processes.  After class, if we've gone over a particularly difficult concept, she attempts to clarify through a mass e-mail.  Tests are easy if you take good notes and do a few of the optional problems she posts after each lecture.

She was a fair professor and clearly instructed her section of the course. I know a ton of people complain about the difficulty of her tests, but they are not actually difficult if you determine the main points of each lecture and know those things cold. And complaining because she tells people to stop writing after the test is ridiculous people!
Dr. Hileman's lecture are unfortunately, very boring! They tend to be dry and sometimes she can be very confusing. Didn't enjoy the class much when she taught it.

Lectures are nice but her exams are hard. I go to all lecture and pulled a D on one of her tests. Reason? Professor isn't the problem. The graders (TAs's) are the problem because when I got my exam back from a regrade, he/she still marked it wrong even though my answer meet the min. requirement. This is what happens when there's a writing test. =(

Her exams are mostly application questions: LOTS of short answers, 2-3 multiple choice, solving equations. Study lectures notes and you should be fine for the exam. I got a B and A on her exams. Compared to Gleason who taught the second half of the course I thought her lecture was more interesting and her exams was easier.

Tests are all short answer a few multiple choice here and there.  All her questions come from the notes and a few from the online book website questions.  You have to study everything from the discussion section to text book or online website of the book.  TA's are helpful if they can find the time.  Better than Gleason though.

Jill is one of the sweetest professors you will ever meet! She not only knows you professionally but makes it a priority to get to know you personally too. As a Biology major, I'll admit that I wanted to drop JMC150 after the first class. Jill played a large role in helping me speak in front of large crowds as well as figuring out my career path!

Jill is a super fun and easy going professor but could be chaotic at times. The majority of the semester was spent on a group project (she assigns groups based on feedback you provide), but at times it wasn't clear what our time should be spent on. Our final exam was very chaotic going in as we hadn't had any previous quizzes or exams.
She is very organized. Well mannered, professional, fun all in one. You would want to have Professor Hinrich as a professor!
I loved this professor. She made the 8am class fun despite having to wake up early. She's very helpful and can ask for her help on anything.

Jill is one of my favorite instructors at KU. She really cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. She was understanding on situations that arose and provided leniency while maintaining expectations she sets for her students. She provided a good feedback and allows you to revise your work based on the feedback.

She's funny and entertaining in lectures while also knowing her stuff. I had a month of just being a bum and skipping lab and she was the perfect combination of reaching out to check in and try and keep me engaged while also letting it fly as long as I was still doing the assignments. Also, Kirk Hinrich's her brother, which is pretty cool.

Jill is probably one of my favorite teachers I have ever had. She cares a lot about her students and genuinely wants to see them not only succeed in her class but in life. She wants to get to know all her students and be a mentor to them. Shes also really funny and cool.

Nice and willing to help but extremely unorganized when it comes to assignments. Due dates are constantly switched around leaving students panicking that they missed an assignment. Her lab also requires additional work on top of our assignments. She is also a very tough grader so make sure you follow the rubric closely.

I am a senior, and Jill is the best professor I had at KU. She cares about her students and their career paths. She continuously puts her students first and has real life experience to back up her teaching. Jill completely changed the course of my career and equipped me with the tools for success moving forward. Take her class.

Do not take her J560 lab, it is unorganized and requires more work than the other labs. Feedback is also very vague and guidelines for projects are unclear. Also very unprofessional offering extra credit for concert tickets and telling us how we will inevitably hook up with our coworkers. The whole class is uncomfortable, would not recommend

Jill is one of the best possible professors you could have at the University of Kansas. She truly takes great pride in helping her students and offers priceless advice with the diverse real world job experience that she has attained over the years. Jill is incredibly understanding and relaxed, but works hard to ensure her students are successful.

I was mortified when I started taking journalism courses and never thought I'd major in it. Thanks to Jill I found my passion and a life-long mentor. I am extremely thankful that she was my teacher TWICE!
Jill is amazing, She genuinely cares about her students and their success. She will call you on your BS and help you develop in the best way possible. 12/10 recommend classes with her.

You can really tell she cares about all of her students and wants them to do good. She's always energetic and makes class fun to come to! I met with her before all my speeches to go over my outline and she gave me such good feedback to make me feel confident when I had to present.

Prof. Hines is disorganized, prone to getting sidetracked, and generally vague on her standards for grading. All this compounds with the fact that she doesn't use a slideshow, making lectures hard to follow. She's nice, but I would not take a class from her again.

She made my friend cry in Torts over the summer, I just started this fall and have Civ Pro with her. She is really disorganized and never cold calls anyone except for me, and those tend to be days when I haven't read. I feel like she's out to embarrass me. Take any class you can with literally any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: IDK how/why, but they keep deleting our ratings. The nicest, most off-topic, disorganized, prof. I've ever had.

There is very little organizational structure to this class - it seems as though she makes up the class structure as she goes. Criteria is very unclear and at times seems subjective based on how she's feeling that day. She's a smart and kind woman, but very disorganized.

Professor Hines is as nice as they come, but is subpar in the teaching department. Most of the class discussion revolved around other students opinions as opposed to teaching us new 1Ls substantive tort law. Would not take again.
As long as you read the assigned material you will be fine; there really aren't any surprises in class. The class is not easy, but Hines is fair and she keeps it low-stress.

Talks so much it is not clear that she knows what she is saying sometimes.  Good teacher, but it would be much easier to learn if she spent about half the words to say the same thing.  Don't try to follow anything written on the board as it will be incomprehensible.  Very nice and happy to help.

Excellent Professor, my favorite so far in law school.  Those complaining about her teaching style are absolutely crazy.  I would rather her talk and explain the federal rules of civ pro, than listen to ILs try to explain the rules.

I had her in Civil Procedure I.  She speaks really fast, but after a few days you get used to the tempo and you end up wondering why your other professors talk so slow.  At the end of the day she came across as brilliant, interesting, and very well organized.  She can be intimidating at times. It's not an easy course, but it was well worth taking.
No Comments
worst final ever - completely scatterbrained
I love the Laura J Hines Show! She's smokin HOT. They need to have an LJH show or channel.  24 hours of LJH, All Hines, All day. . She needs to talk more and ask us less.
No Comments
Very clear, very helpful, very personable, made a potentially very boring subject interesting--a resounding 2 thumbs up
She is absolutely gorgeous and great personality.  I learned a lot in her class!
the best teacher at ku law!
No Comments
Extremely Fun Professor
drop dead gorgeous

This class and this professors teaching style are unproductive uses of your time. The materials provided are many and vague. Taking this class as a working professional makes you understand the lack of sympathy professors have for working students.

Outstanding professor that loves his material. His classes are lecture heavy but he generally provides several examples to reinforce the material. He's also quite patient with those that haven't taken a math class in a while.

The workload is much higher than the average class, but not without reason. He believes in Learn by Doing for the technical aspects and focuses lectures on practical application of theory. Great for someone truly interested in the field.

The workload in this class borders on overwhelming, but it is clear that Hillmer knows the material and is very knowledgeable. He's accessible and willing to help, and the class is structured so that if you do your homework you get full points. This class is definitely more focused on learning than earning points for a grade.

The midterm and final were very fair. Although it was an online class, I didn't get the impression that he was invested in or cared about his students. The weekly quizzes were ridiculous!!! The multiple choice questions were the perfect example of how NOT to write m/c questions. Subtle nuances in many possible answers resulted in wrong answers.

Lectures are bland and dry. The material is not always stated clearly. He is not very good at math which is kind of a prerequisite in a statistics class. He is unwilling to help most of the time and grades are based on false math.  Every assignment needed to have the grade changed. His assignment questions are not clear at all.

Semi-Hybrid course lik ACCT 701 - attend half the time / watch other lessons online.  Fairly easy, if somewhat dry topic, and Dr. Hillmer is a good teacher, but I still found it moderately time consuming. Must do each online module sequentially to open up next one. Alone its easy, but pair it with ACCT 701 or similar...that's a full course load.
Extremely easy class. He cares more about the theory than actual statistics. Gives you the chance to redo homework as well as the final. Easy "A" if you just do homework and come to class.
Very easy if you go to class and pay a little attention.  He is more interested in making sure the students understand the material.
Incredible Teacher!!!
Very nice teacher. If you pay proper attention in class and do assignments properly enough, sure to get a A.
Bring caffeine to class.  Easy.  Learned a few things, but could have learned all of it in 1 class.
Daniel is a standup and super nice guy. The fieldtrips are fun and informative. If you are going into environmental or geotechnical fields, his class is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dan is a great instructor. Be weary of the 100 level reviews as these are often skewed by freshman who don't understand the value of instruction. For 531 (Soil Physics) he provided well organized notes and through instruction. However, unless you love soils, physics, and calculus this class is quite the challenge.
The classes are boring and the tests are really hard. His tests are not open note and all of the other teachers are. It sucks.
Prof. Hirmas has a great teaching outlook. This course material is both interesting and challenging but he is more than happy to help if you see him in his office hours.
He is one of the nicest people you will ever meet! His classes are somewhat boring (just reading powerpoint slides) but the tests are all online, open book. I would definitely recommend him!
Classes are a lot of fun, Jerel is always prepared and happy to teach. Has great feedback and wants you to succeed. Take his classes if you get the chance!!!
He's the best. Totally awesome.
No Comments
great teacher...truly inspirational! One of my favorite ballet instructors. Take every class offered by Jerel!
Hilding is the King of Ballet and he knows it. This guys very cocky but don't get me wrong he's a great ballet teacher. Cocky.. but great with corrections.
Class was overall, fine? Most things are participation. Didn't feel like a lot of effort was put forth.
His lectures showed me an entirely new way to think about the living world.

His lectures are unbearably boring and uninteresting. He has no textbook for this class, so you're stuck learning from his monotonous, stale lectures (good luck!). He's awful at explaining things. One could learn more than an entire semester of his lectures by reading a single textbook chapter. One of the worst professors I've ever had.

This was a two-professor class, but Holder was pretty good at explaining a very complex topic, Biostatistics. Best tip is to READ THE BOOK, READ ALL OF IT, the tests are extremely tough but you can do it. I got a 77% but ended up with a B so they curved (no +/-). There are pop quizzes every few weeks so go to class. HW is optional for extra points.

He is a great professor! I would 110% take his class again. If you pay attention in lecture, take notes, and study (minimally) for the tests you will do very well. I never got below a 100% on any of the tests. He also gets to know his students. He knows each kid in my class by their first name.

Professor Holliday is one of my absolute favorite professors I have ever had. He is passionate about his lecture materials and welcomes all questions. He is a very fun professor. I genuinely enjoyed all of his lectures and would definitely take this class again.
He had very open communication, and wants to work with his students to help them succeed. Tests were somewhat vague as we did not get a study guide, but the material was all things we covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Holliday is THE BEST! His lectures are very engaging and his passion for linguistics makes his class very interesting and engaging. He is extremely helpful outside of class and overall a fantastic professor! If you get the chance to take one of his classes definitely do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Holliday is amazing! He is one of the best professors I have ever had at KU. He is very passionate about linguistics and his lectures are amazing! He is very accessible outside of class for help/questions. He truly is incredible. Definitely take one of his classes if you get the opportunity!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There are a few papers and projects throughout the semester that made it a little more work than some of my other classes, but he really cares about the success of his students and is very passionate about the course material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Holliday is a great educator and very passionate about linguistics! He knows his stuff and is always urging students to learn more. Decent amount of reading homework, some essays/physical homework.Very active with student participation and inclusion.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Holliday is a super nice guy, he's a great professor who is clearly passionate about the subject. He encouraged discussion and there was not much homework. Tests are pretty easy. Just pay attention to the lectures and you will be fine on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very sweet and goofy professor. He is very kind and understanding but gives clear expectations so that from the beginning you know what to expect. I loved the interactive nature of his class and even though we did not have to come to class I always wanted to. This class convinced me to add a linguistics major!
Tim is an absolute saint, he gets to know you and your classmates and crits based off of your level and things you enjoy. He makes every class an enjoyable experience!
One of the nicest teachers I have ever had. So so sweet and understanding. He also drops random lore all the time which is always fun. Take his class!!!!!!!!!!!!
Tim is one of the best teachers I have ever had, he makes sure to get to know his students and what they are interested in!
Wonderful teacher with tons of cool experience! He is very knowledgeable and understanding. Attendance is not mandatory but heavily encouraged and it counts toward some of the grade

ADS401*. The class was amazing! So many great lectures and so much thought was put into them. We had some guest speakers and that just made it even better! Participation makes the class so much more fun, especially the thought questions! I recommend taking this class even if you aren't a design student if you can. So easy to get an A!

This course is extremely easy and Tim makes this class in particular one of the best in the design department. Tim is extremely kind and caring, he recognizes students as students and not as machines built for work.
Not a hard class but I learned so much and he definitely has expertise in his field.

Tim is honestly the most considerate out of all the design department. Is very lenient to students missing classes and understands things are happening. If you just participate and do the work you are golden! attendance yes should be mandatory but if you miss a class just inform him, do the work, and you're fine. Super nice teacher!

Prof. Hossler is one of the nicest professors I have ever met. Every week we would present our assignments, and you could tell that he was always listening because he would always compliment a unique aspect of our work. He never had a bad thing to say. And then, he invited us to meet him for coffee at the end of the class! He is caring and positive
Honestly looked forward to his lectures.

TIM IS THE BEST!!! If I could take all my design studios with Tim, I definitely would. He gives good, clear feedback without making you feel bad about your work. He loves when students break design rules to make their designs different. His projects are very open so you can usually make what you want. Grades nice and is the nicest person

Tim is a great professor! He's pretty laid back and is interested in seeing how creative you can get as opposed to how well you can follow the rules; he's all about pushing boundaries and loves abstract concepts. Super good with feedback too, is always willing to help you if you show interest!

Tim is the best teacher I have had in the Design school. Being a non-graphics kid in a graphics class I was nervous at first, but he really just wants to see your creativity and lets you explore whatever ideas on a project you want. He is so kind, and class always ended early. Plus he has neat stories from his work experience.

Tim is seriously one of the better professors in the design program. He is very clear and lenient with his assignments because he wants to see your creativity rather than how well you can follow instructions. He is willing to bend the rules of the assignment a little so you can use your own ideas.

Of all the BDS teachers I highly recommend you have Tim for at least one semester. He is the most helpful and most lenient for the projects. If you are a graphics major you definitely have to be in his class.
Great teacher! Very willing to bend the assignment rules to let you think outside the box. He is helpful with giving criticism and expanding on your ideas. I recommend him!

Tim is passionate about graphic design, and teaching it! He is very helpful, thoughtful, and funny. He is laid-back about nitty gritty details, but firm where it matters: design! He is a definite asset to the visual communications department.
Professor Hudgins is obviously excellent at calculus, but also teaching.
Dr. Hudgins was great her lectures were really good and I was always happy to go to her class highly recommend she made the class super easy.

Super easy to follow lectures and explains the concepts really well. I had already taken calc, but didn't understand it until she taught it. Class participation matters, but she will tell you the I-Clicker answer before closing. She is in her office often and will help you if the math TA's can't. Really kind and answered all questions + emails.
A pretty good calc professor.

Dr. Hudgins was one of the most thorough math professors I have had in college. When I took calc 1 my freshman year I was incredibly nervous but her lectures were well thought out and she explained difficult concepts incredibly well. She is willing to answer questions that you have and was very accommodating when I had to miss a few classes.
Lectures are really useful and intuitive, tests have a lot of extra credit on them so as long as you go to class and understand you'll easily pass

By far one of the best math teachers I've had. Very easy to understand and explains things very well, making it very easy to visualize and process some of the harder topics that are covered. Walked into 125 pretty nervously and not knowing what to expect, but having Dr Hudgins made that transition just that much easier. 100% would recommend.

Professor Hudgins has done an incredible job. Her lectures are clear and to the point. She is very good at getting the conceptual understanding of some tough concepts across. I recommend her 100%; I wish she were teaching 126 in the fall.

Professor Hudgins class is taught very well. There are plenty of resources for you to succeed. Tests are cumulative and the practice tests don't cover everything you need to know. So make sure you understand the content on the worksheets each week. Responsive to emails and cares about students. 2 Midterms + Final is 65% of your grade.

Dr. Hudgins was an amazing professor. I had her for both calc 1 & calc 2 and she was amazing. Her lectures are good and here notes are easy to follow and understand. Even on days I didn't want to be in class I was able to power through because she's genuinely an amazing teacher. The only downfall is that she isn't teaching the more advanced classes

Dr. Hudgins is one of the best professors to have in the Calculus Series at KU. I had her for MATH 125 & 126 and she's very thoughtful about her lectures and responses to questions students ask in class. Her lectures can seem quick but she's very organized and thorough.

Best lecture professor I've had. She presents info clearly and concisely. She is also understanding and very professional as well as personable. Assignments can add up quickly but as long as you find a system and get help when needed you will succeed.

fantastic math teacher, I will admit I did not apply myself as much as I should have, and even with the low effort attempt I gave, I managed to pass the class slightly above average. She's a wonderful teacher, thorough, caring, and takes her job very seriously. She is the reason I managed to pass first try, highly recommend.
Dr. Hudgins is the best professor I have had. She is helpful when outside of class and wants the best for her students!

I think hudgins is a really great professor she tries to make her class interesting although math itself is boring but she really tries in explaining the material and is always happy to help outside of class. There's 2 homeworks the LGA's and the Achieve there aren't hard but just a lot. only drawside I would say is she does teach the class fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Hudgins is a very engaging and knowledgeable professor. Took Calc 1 (MATH 125), and her lectures are great. Only con is that she writes pretty fast during her lectures, but all lecture videos are posted. Office hours are useful. She also doesn't talk down or make students feel like it's not okay to not know something. Overall excellent.
Amazing. I was terrified of math Calculus before taking Math 125 but this class gave me confidence. She is great to talk to in office hours, and explains concepts very well. The GOAT.

She is a great professor who wants her students to succeed. If you have trouble with anything in the class her office hours are very helpful and she will walk you through any problems you have. She is great at explaining concepts and can answer any questions you have.

Dr. Hudgins is perhaps one of the best math professors of all time. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She goes the extra mile to make sure you have everything you need to do well in Calc.

Dr. Hudgins was a great Calc I professor. She was very easy to understand, kind, and always willing to answers questions. I strongly recommend taking course with her. The Achieve assignments had ten attempts per question and the lab worksheets were mostly participation. If you do the work and prepare well for the tests, you can get a good grade.
Great professor, genuinely cares about each student and their success. Very accessible outside of class and very clear on expectations and grading. Explains complex concepts very well.

Dr. Hudgins truly cares about each individual student and takes time to clearly explain the problems in great detail. Although my grade was lower than hoped (C instead of B), none of that had to do with Dr. Hudgins or her teaching style. A tough lesson learned by me but always ask when unsure and utilize the Supplemental Instruction!
The best professor for math 127. We got a little behind and had to cram at the end of semester, but she made a concerned effort to make sure students understood the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hudgins' lectures were engaging and organized. A lot of content was covered in the semester, which sometimes felt overwhelming, but she provides many resources for students, including individual office hours multiple days a week. She is strict and expects a lot from students, but you can tell she really cares about you. I loved having her!

I just had her in a huge lecture hall so I didn't get to experience her in a context outside of lectures. Her lectures were good and she worked through problems for the whole class. She would also walk around between iClicker questions to make sure everyone had a chance to ask questions.

She is the best professor for MATH125. Her lectures may be a little fast at times but she usually does a great job explaining and demonstrating new concepts. She not be accessible but the math helproom is. Also, don't be afraid if the first few weeks of the class seem very difficult. Transitioning to college-level math can be hard. It get's better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mr. Huber asked the class for our test taking preferences and gave us only Multiple Choice question tests. He passes times with funny stories too. You have online homeworks that prepare you for the exams, making the class very easy.

Huber made mathematics so easy for me. His humor and way of teaching made class entertaining on sleepy days. Statistics has never been more simple! He's all about letting calculators do the "hard part" of math. His stories are fun and his expectations are clear.

Mr. Huber is easily the best math teacher I have ever had. As long as you go to lecture, his class is really not hard. I took math 116 and he went above and beyond to help students understand his course. He tries to make lecture as simple as possible and his tests are not meant to trick you. He will tell you exactly what will be expected of you.

MATH 365**
Mr. Huber was the best mathematics teacher I've ever had. He made statistics so simple and easy to understand. I never dreaded his lectures or exams. His stories are interesting, and he is a fair grader who never intends to trick students.

Mr. Huber was one of the greatest mathematics professors I've ever had. His way of breaking down the equations, applying practical reasoning, and sharing real-life experiences was phenomenal. His lectures and quizzes were concise and easy to understand. He truly deserves his roses!

(For MATH365) Mr. Huber is the GOAT. His inspirational speech he made before finals week was awesome and I think about it all the time. Biggest advice: do NOT skip lecture though because the lecture is not posted.
Huber was a great lecturer that taught statistics in a fun and easy way. He made lectures enjoyable and the concepts easy to understand. If you attend lecture, it is an easy A.

I actually took him for MATH116 and he was a really phenomenal guy. Probably saved my grade (we switched professors half way through) and cares more about learning than about grades. Has a lot of funny anecdotes and can sometimes ramble. Impossible to not hear- he's got the loudest voice you'll ever meet.

MATH365: One of the best professors I've had at KU! He really sets up his students for success and works hard to build good rapport with his class. He's old-school and doesn't upload anything to canvas, but he was very sweet and easy to access if you missed a class. HW wasn't busy work and he always spent the week of the exam reviewing content.
I took MATH 105 online with Mr. Huber. If you're an Architecture major---take MATH 105 over Calc---your life will be much less stressful. This class is extremely easy, and he is super nice.

I am BAD at math but this class was easy for me. As long as you show up and take notes you will get an A. The tests are online, open note, and multiple choice. It's impossible to not get 100%. Professor Huber is very funny and will always tell you a good story. I highly recommend him!

Mr. Huber is an excellent professor. I had him for MATH 365, not 526 but he truly cares about his students and wants them to do their very best. I have never had a professor who is as kind and knowledgable as him. He really wants you to do well, but you must show up to lecture as he doesn't post notes or lectures and the exams are heavily weighted.

Mr. Huber is one of the most amazing professors I've had at KU. He is so passionate about what he is teaching and he wants you to learn. He truly cares about his students and their health, both mentally and physically. He wants you to be successful in his class and gives you the means to do so. You just have to apply yourself.
Mr. Huber really cares for his students and wants them so succeed. He is engaging, loud, and wants others to be as passionate about math as he is. You can tell he wears his heart of his sleeve.

Prof. Huber genuinely cares about his students' success. He understands that most of the kids in Math 105 are not great at math and are only there for a required credit, so he teaches this class in a way that's easy to understand and succeed in. He is one of the only math teachers I have ever been able to learn from. Take his class!!
What a fantastic man. Really cares about his students, is super clear about assignments, and loves to teach overall. Try and take him if you can!

Professor Huber is probably the most passionate professor I have ever taken a class from. MATH 105 was an interesting and easy course as long as you showed up and tried your best. Mr. Huber clearly absolutely loves what he does, and he was constantly positive, kind, and inspiring. I highly recommend MATH 105 with Mr. Huber for a math credit!

Mr. Huber is one of the best math teachers Ive ever had, and somehow he teaches to a lecture hall with 150 students in it. He makes concepts easy to grasp and its hard to not finish with an A. Even with so many students, he made it personal and tried to learn everyones name. At the end of the class everyone clapped for him. Amazing teacher.

the rest of the reviews speak for themselves! mr huber really cares about the success of his students and was entertaining every lecture. i never thought i would want to go to a math class, but 105 changed that- he's caring, funny, and turned a bland subject into something actually applicable to the real world. take a class from him if you can!

Great teacher. I enjoyed every day I went to class. Energetic and friendly, makes the effort to learn everyone's names. For a high level class, he made things simple and concise, and puts an emphasis on concepts and real life applicability, which is very much appreciated. I wish every teacher in the math department was like Prof. Huber! Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I had an incredible experience with Mr. Huber. He genuinely wants everyone to pass and makes the class easy enough that you can get an A if you just put in some effort. Really nice guy. Would definitely take another class with him.

I have never enjoyed a math class before, but this 105 class taught by Professor Huber changed that. He is a true teacher, and cares about his students more than they probably care about themselves. He will make you laugh, think, and even maybe cry. Not the easiest class, but you will want to do your best. Cannot thank him enough..

Im one of his TAs for Math 105, and theres a reason that I look forward to his class every day. His class and lectures are different, relevant, and he is an inspiration for what professors should aim to do. He has some quirks, sure; everyone does. But you will not find a more caring and engaging math professor than Mr. Huber.
Awesome class! Pure 11/10 good boi. I have never done well in math until now! He truly wants all his students to do well.

Great class. Prof Huber is an amazing person and so memorable. Genuinely wants all of us to succeed. Take notes in class, maybe take pics, he moves fast sometimes. Tests are pretty easy. Show up to class because attendance is mandatory despite being like 200+ people. Gave us a speech on the last day and made us all cry, gonna miss this dude.

Huber is perfectly nice, he cares about his students, and he loves teaching 105, but certain students may not do well with his teaching style. He speaks VERY loudly, he truly does not need a microphone, and he has certain words and phrases that he repeats a lot. Those two things can be very distracting for auditory learners.

After my experience with Huber, I never want to take another math course with a different professor. Huber was amazing. In a lecture of 170 students, he genuinely tried to get to know all of our names. He's super funny, generous, and caring. This course wasn't too difficult, but you need to go to class and study to get the best grade possible.

His teaching style is very different than other professors, so I didn't think I would like him. I grew to like Mr. Huber though. He jokes around a lot, and he really cares about his students. He does take attendance, and there is a moderate amount of homework (not too much). His tests are very easy and almost identical to the review he gives out.

Huber is the GOAT! Highly recommend taking any class offered by him! He really cares about his students and even cried on the last day of class because he "was going to miss us all so much". Huber gives me life!

He is an amazing teacher. The class is really easy, but if you are struggling he has 2 TA's at all times who are extremely helpful with a lot of office hours between the two of them. He genuinely cares about his students and welcomes them to email him personally and he never takes longer than an hour to email back.
Professor Huber is super nice and Math 105 is easy if you keep up with the homework and go to class most of the time.

Mr. Huber is my all-time favorite teacher! He is the kindest teacher and really cares about each and every one of his students. He will do anything he can to help students that are struggling and always shows up in a great mood. He has a very straightforward grading system, and it is pretty simple to end up with an A, certainly a B if you try.

I've never actually had a class with this professor but I always had class in this room after his class ended and he always seemed like he genuinely cared about his students. After class each day as students were leaving he asked them individually if they understood everything okay and if one student didnt he took time to explain right then.

Mr. Huber was one of my all-time-favorite professors at KU, and I'm not even a math major. He made the topics discussed in class very relevant to everyday life. He truly cares about his students and if they understand the material. He even tried his best to learn everyone's name (in a class of over 100).  Also super funny guy and only lecture 45min

Never really liked math, but this was easily the best math class I've ever taken and Mr. Huber is one of my favorite professors I've had.  He explains material very clearly and is enthusiastic every class period. He genuinely wants you to enjoy his class.  Lectures are entertaining, tests are reasonable, and he doesn't bombard you with homework.

Huber was one of the kindest, upbeat and inspirational teachers I have ever had. He truly cared about us, frequently told us how proud he was of us, and always cared about feedback when it came to tests. Time was taken at the beginning of each class to go over homework questions, and the lectures were particularly harmless and easy to get through.

Mr. Huber is the best teacher Ive had so far at KU. Hes very passionate about teaching, and is always accessible in class and office hours and responds quickly to emails. He's a relatively easy A. Tests will make up most of your grade, but theyre all VERY similar to the study guide, no curveballs. We didn't use the textbook at all.

Mr. Huber is an incredible professor. I've never done will in my math classes, but he has a way of really helping you understand what you are doing. He goes through and shows you exactly what you need to know. He has a few quirks which take some time to get used to, but deep down he really does care about all of his students.

Prof. Huber is hilarious, engaging, and a great person to have as a math professor. I hate math, always have, but he makes it enjoyable enough to get through. He does some irritating things like speak through his microphone while we're taking tests, but you come to appreciate his quirks rather than despise them.

Mr. Huber was the best teacher by far that I have had at KU. He is hilarious and really does care about his students. He tries to make things as easy as possible for people to understand and he wants everyone to get an A. Tests were scantron and he gives you a study guide.. the study guides were exactly like the test. Best teacher and VERY EASY A.

Professor Huber is an excellent math professor. I have struggled a lot in math before, but he takes the time to go through and explain, and re-explain things until they do make sense. reviews.comment: Lectures and quizzes every period, Final is a beast. No text book, so self-study is a challenge. Think of it as a Metaphysical Stats class. His lectures are just confusing. I tried 3 times for an appointment during office hours & struck out. Pay attention to fine print in Syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Grading: mainly quizzes a couple of homework problems (3)  and the final (30% of grade). You can accumulate enough extra credit points to have an A going into the final. All you need is a 13/20 on the Final to get a B, if you have maxed out the quizzes and homework. Very few people get a good grade in the class. Some ? on final were never covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: No text Book, Quiz every class, I only had 2 homework / lab assignments. Use TA in lab to ask questions. If you ask ?'s during class you get heightened observation during quizzes and Final. Take Stats at a JuCo.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Haug might be smart but he's a terrible lecturer. Use the TAs during the lab. Go to class, keep your quizzes to study from. He is no help during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: DSCI202 is  an ENTRY LEVEL business stats class. Haug treats it like its his PHD thesis defense. Take a JuCo class somewhere else and transfer it in. Quiz every lecture period. Lectures are off the wall material. No text Book, Hes no help during office hours. TAs are your best shot of passing. Grading comes down to Final which is really hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Ive taken two classes from this guy and he is equal parts genius and sadist. He is not a good instructor. No text book only his Power Point slides. During Lecture he will call out a name then ask a question, he'll belittle your answers, he thinks it is Socratic, it just him being a bully.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Beware this guy will accuse you of cheating . He has more than 85% of all the Academic Misconduct charges in the entire School of Business, almost all coming from DSCI202, Ask the Dean of the Business school or Andy Fost, the custodian of Public Records at KU.  Take the summer school session or Get at DSCI degree at Rockhurst
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Haug is a brilliant man, but like many brilliant people, he is hard to keep up with. If you are not well-suited for this type of non-intuitive, non-instinctual thinking that DSCI 202 entails, you'll be dead in the water. You need to understand each of his lectures before moving on to the next.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Have taken 3 classes from Mark now and have enjoyed each one more. He is a very intelligent guy and his courses are tough but if you care to learn the material you will do fine. Get to know him and utilize his office hours when you need help, he truly cares about his students! One of my favorite professors at KU.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Haug is a smart man but his teaching style is vague and INCREDIBLY hard to follow. I went into the final with a 92, came out with a C. Once it is all said and done, I do not feel like I earned a C since I do not know the material much at all. Peers who earned Ds certainly knew more than I. Buckle down and hope you have luck on your side
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mark Haug is definitely a smart man. His level of smartness is on such a higher level than the average persons that it makes it very difficult for him to teach the material. When taking his class, definitely go to lab and work problems with your TA. The tests he gives are often very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mark is a very smart person but his teaching is confusing, he often talks about things irrelevant to just learning the formulas.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mark is one smart dude, and certainly someone I can respect, but he fails to help students. The class is certainly doable, but you will have to work your ass off outside of class, be sure to attend every lecture for the quizzes, and do above avg on midterm/final to succeed. He teaches this course as if everyone had already taken statistics before

Lectures are hard to follow. No notes given online. No textbook TA's are not helpful He isn't helpful during office hours and he wouldn't make an appointment with me outside of office hours. The syllabus is unclear so make sure you read the fine print. He's not a good teacher and doesn't seem to care about his students.

Mark is one of the best professors I've had the pleasure of knowing. People say his class is hard, and yes it is a challenge, but that's because it makes you think. Don't treat this like a math class. It's a critical thinking course. If you ever have a problem with the material or are worried about the class, go see Mark. He really cares about you.

Daily pop quizzes, if you don't show up to class you will fail. Once you miss a class be prepared to fall behind very quickly. The content is hard and moves very quickly. Use your TA wisely and take use of office hours when they are available. Not that he will be very helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Haug is obviously a smart guy, but a professor is the last thing he should be. He philosophically babbles in lectures that are hard to follow and take notes to. Also, the quizzes he gives are impossible to study for and are meant to trick you. He needs to spend less time trying to inspire and more time teach the concepts of INTRODUCTORY stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I have had three classes with Haug. All of which were tough, however if you can get past the intimidating reputation shrouding Haug, you'll realize he's a pretty cool guy. He wants his students to succeed. If you're scared to take his classes, don't be. Get to know him, use the TA's and don't be afraid to ask questions. The classes will benefit you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lectures for an hour in an ambiguous abstract fashion over a simple core concept that takes minutes to explain if he ever cared to teach the concept. Don't expect to learn from lecture.  Preparing for quizzes is a guessing game.  Final was ridiculous. Really smart guy, should not be teaching.

Worst professor. I went into the final with a guaranteed C and thought I'd end up with at least a B but NOPE. I took AP Stats in high school so I came into the class with a background in the class and it helped somewhat. I studied the previous lecture beforehand for the quiz and it helped. Haug wastes his time during lecture with pointless stories.

This class is one of the most frustrating classes you will ever take.  Studied everyday to do well on the quizzes, and met the cap with 100 extra points.  Went into the final with 100% and ended with a C. If you do not go into the final with a 100% expect at least a D..  Avoid this class if you aren't a business student.

Super interesting guy. Tough class. You won't realize what you learned in the class until after the final, which is reasoning and judgement. Emphasizes professionalism and judgement a lot. Many students say he is an intimidating jerk but going to his office hours will be humbling and you get a lot out of it. The grade may not reflect what you learn

DSCI302 is not as bad as most people make it out to be. No tests, no final. All of the points come from homework and a few small quzizes. I put in a pretty minimal amount of effort and received an A. Doesn't require you to buy a textbook either, which is nice.
