AWFUL instructor. Takes a philosophical approach to teaching statistics- hardly teaches necessary formulas. A novel about being "the-best-version-of-yourself" was assigned instead of a textbook. Quizzes and final are a combination of actual statistics he never taught us and metaphysical questions. Went into the final with an 83%, came out with a D.

I liked the fact that Mr. Haug teaches you to learn the material outside of class and prepares you for your future career. However, I also want to be successful and pass his class. I worked my butt off for this class, went to SI instructions, went to his office hours( not helpful), etc, and none of it paid off, and ended up with a C.
Not good.
Need to go to lecture for quizzes and to understand how to do homework. No midterm or final this semester, not as hard as DSCI 202

Mark Haug is hands down the best professor that I've had at KU. He genuinely wants to see his students succeed. With that being said, this class is not an easy A. Mark challenges his students (something that many professors are afraid to do). His class is anything but ordinary. It completely changed my outlook on life in the best way possible.

Most people say that this is the hardest class in the business school, but it really isn't that bad. You don't have to know the material that well to get a B. Show up to class and take the quizzes after studying your notes for 5 minutes and you should be okay. His tests are insanely hard, but everyone does bad so you're in the same boat. He curves

You absolutely must attend class. If you don't like attending class, good luck taking this a second time.  START LEARNING THE MATERIAL EARLY IN THE SEMESTER. Since there's no regular homework, it's easy to slack off until you realize that the final is coming up and you understand next to nothing. Be there, and don't brush off this class.

Mark is clearly a smart man. However, he can't teach and he makes almost no attempt to. His lectures are long (1 hour 45 minutes) which he uses to mostly ramble on about nothing. This becomes a problem when he gives quizes that are actually about stats. The final, the only test, is next to impossible and covers stuff not even mentioned in class

This is the weedout class for BSchool, but Haug gives you plenty of opportunities to ask for help. Also, show up to class. There is almost always a quiz, and he calls on random people throughout lecture to give you 10 bonus points. I wish he had more tests though, because I am not prepared for the final--which is the only test of the semester.
He's lecture are so long and boring. He teaching style is abstract and inst easy to follow,

Prof. Haug deep down cares for his students and the education system but that saying DSCI 202 Statistics is the weed out course for this Business School at KU. The final exam was almost impossible and I studied for a very long time! I ended with a C in the course and had an 87% going into the final.

Terrible teacher. Not clear at all what he is teaching. Goes off topic and doesn't actually teach you what to do. Gives you a ton of case studies then expects you to understand how to actually do the problem on the final. Also you only take the final, no other tests. Not helpful at all.

Haug is a teacher that truly cares about the education system. He makes you grow as a student by challenging you to think and learn in a way you have never been taught to before. If you are looking for an easy A, take the class from another professor. Professors like Haug are what keep an education from KU a step above the rest.

Worst instructor I've ever had. The syllabus is 6 pages long consisting entirely of footnotes. If you want help he will just refer you there. Most of it is irrelevant and just him showing off his writing skills, yet he tells you that professionals should get their point across as briefly as possible. HW and practice problems almost nonexistent.

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR IF YOU CAN!!!! he is useless in class, has impossible expectations of his students, and will threaten you with academic misconduct if you ask him for help as he believes that you should not be asking him for help since you should have either read his syllabus better or learned better.

I'm a double major junior in two different schools so Ive taken classes with nearly 30 different teachers at KU. This was my second class with Haug and I can honest say he is one of the worst teachers at KU. Still as useless of teacher as he was in DSCI 301. You barely learn anything and he refuses to help you. Avoid at all costs.

His lectures are not interesting, and he will go off topic most of the time. He used to be in Law school and LOVES talking about Law; however, you must go to lecture since there is a quiz every class.  Quizzes are mostly memorizing formulas and guessing what he wants you to answer. Only good thing about this class is that there is never homework.

WORST TEACHER EVER. He gives quiz at every beginning of the class so don't be late, but even if you go to class and pay attention you will still miss most of quiz points because they are very difficult and he only teach some nonsense during the class. If you have a chance DO NOT choose this guy, save yourself.

I hated Haug when I started this class since he failed me in DSCI 301. Mid semester in this class & I've had a change of heart. Haug cares about his students, he wants them to learn and be as prepared for the real world as possible. It's an easy B if you go to class and learn the material.

Very common sense guy.  Didn't like him at first, but he definitely grew on me as the semester proceded.  Easily the brightest professor I've ever had personally.  He won't make you do anything that he himself doesn't know how to do (lengthy calculus equations etc.)  Analytical, yet philosophical.  Be ready for at least 1 quizweek.  Work hard.

Haug is a fantastic professor. People don't like his class because it is difficult to get an A in. Everyone tries harder in Stats than all their other classes and still get lower grades. He really teaches you life skills and teaches you to critically think. I loved the class, but got my first B. Haug does great for the material, you actually learn.

If you don't have to take this class, don't. If you do, I will pray for you. I did not understand a single thing taught and I attended every lecture. To pass the class, do good on quizzes, do the hw, and go to lab.

His tests contain multiple choice questions that range from A to I. That alone should tell you how the teacherclass is. I personally didn't learn anything from the lectures or the labs. Not an avoidable class either as a Business Major.

If you're someone who strives in an environment where the learning objectives are clearly outlined and organized, this is not your class. I felt like his lecture format was extremely chaotic and I never really grasped any core concepts. I really wish I would have gotten more out of this class but I just did not connect with the way Haug teaches.

Dr Haug is one of the professor who doesn't teach to the guidelines, but to what we can actually use in real life. He takes a Statistics class and uses it as avenue to teach us how to be better professionals, regardless of field. Yeah, the content's pretty dry, but given the option, I would always take him over someone else.

Stats is tough everyone knows it, just get through it.  I had Mark 3 mote times after stats for various business school classes and he is one of the best professors in the B-school.  He is one of the only professors that i feel like really cares and he is one of the smartest men I've ever met.  Just what I want in a professor.

Smart guy, awful teacher. I came into the class. He'll spend an hour making up a background story for a word problem, and then two seconds on an important powerpoint slide.The class moves at a snail's pace but then half of his test questions come out of left field.  The curve (top 10% get an A, next 40% get a B) is the only thing that will save you

I had the grade D on this class,and this is the worest grade that I have in my school life. What he called B level in the mid term turns out I got a D for my final grade. Doesn't make any sense to me. I got a lot trouble just because earned this grade D

This class is the weedout class for the Business School. Lectures are really boring and could be summed up in 50 minutes rather than 2 hours each time. I personally did not pay attention in class but still got a B. You just need to do well on the daily quizzes and you can easily get a B in the class.

Haug is a genius. It can be painful at times, the lectures can get dry, but if you persevere and pay attention 100% of the time, the guy is great. Only complaint is that the HW, quizzes, and lab problems are not on the same level as his midterm and final questions. Go to class, turn in all the HW, go to labs, take every quiz. You will get a B easy.

Worked my ASS off and didn't get a good grade. The guy is a genius, but treats everyone like they're on his level. Doesn't help you in his office hours and literally says " I don't know what to tell you " I'd rather move along and have my GPA take the hit than EVER sit through his class again. 3/10.
this teacher is a very good guy, but he is also a very mean guy. he do not mind hurt you by word. the quiz is important, the mid is important.

People's view of Haug is the most varying I've ever seen, you love him or hate him...I love him. He is brilliant. He also really cares about people. His class is rigorous and favors those who want to learn not just pass. If you show up to lecture, go to lab, study the material before class,youll do fine on quizzes. You can get a B if you study,
Intelligent professor. His lectures were very engaging. If you want at least a B in his stats class attend lab, show up for lecture, and do decent on the mid-term. Overall, recommended.

Are you bored with how easy college classes are? Think it's absurd everyone doesn't have a 3.5 GPA? I mean OBVIOUSLY they just don't work as hard as you. OH, wait, people can have memorization and not be lazy? HA. Know what, tell me why, how, or what makes a stats formula work. You can't? Right. Here: Prob (HAUGluv just how much you suck

Wants everyone to do well. If you study your notes from the previous class and pay attention it's easy to do well on the quizzes. Key to getting a good grade in the class is getting a good grade on the midterm.  The TA's are great, especially Chris Schmitz if you can get into his lab.

Honestly..its very easy to get a B in this course. If everyone took advantage of the easy quiz points and lab points, that would get you a B since you will most likely fail the midterm and final. You can miss 100 quiz points. its not that bad of a class. Haug is actually pretty nice and really cares about your learning. Just study and youll be good

Terrible. Did every homework and quiz, went to every class. Did well and what he called B level on the midterm and got a D in the class. Doesn't make sense to me. Heard this happened to a few others in the class. His grading makes no sense.

The most talented professor in School of Business, no exception. Only 5 days class meeting, 9:00am-5:00pm and 45 minutes lunch break. Really learned plenty of real world examples by using financial excel model. Average GPA for class approximately 3.75.... Take it at any expense if you want boost your GPA!! Sweet class ever!!

I went to class everyday, turned in all the homework and took ever quiz. I received a 14 out of 18 on the midterm and still got a D in the class. He doesn't post exam grades on BB, but since I got a D in the class, I obviously had to bomb it. Smart guy, but he doesn't realize not everyone is as smart as him. Try to avoid if possible.

If I were to express my true opinion of Mark Haug, my rating would be removed. I had never even received a C in a course prior to failing Haug's ridiculous class. Hurt my GPA, and am retaking it this summer  which is easy as I already know all the information, yet his tests reflect that I learned nothing. Save yourself money take it in the summer.
Brilliant man, very knowledgeable. If your goal is to learn this is your man. It is not an easy course though.

There's a lot of information and formulas to memorize and review each week. Do ALL of the homework. The textbook gives the answers, with work shown, so you shouldn't have any excuses. Study problems from the hw or previous day for the quizzes, they're usually similar. Study weeks before the midterm and final! GO TO THE TA HELP ROOM
Hardest class in Business school. So challanging. Try your  best to do it. B is not hard, however, A is nearly impossible if you do not pay 100% attention to all he had taught during class.

This is a hard class. Top 50% get a B, top 10% get an A. Haug is very helpful, visit his office hours. You need to attend class and actually do the HW to to well on the quizzes (since they are 30% of your grade). Most of your fellow students will not do well on the quizzes, so do well on them and get a B. Exams are Hard: STUDY HARD if you want an A

Do yourself a favor like i was thinking about doing and just take it in the summer like im about to. Tests are extremely hard 1-8 answers per multiple choice question so its easy to work the wrong answer and think its right.
Hardest class in Business School..But the teacher is really brilliant and nice.... It is a challenge, but thats the meaning of life. Take this coure, you will be super.

Material for this course is very difficult. Understand each homework and the quiz will be very similar. It's not too hard of a class if you keep up with the work and don't wait to learn it for the midterm or final

Really...The hardest class in business school. Try to attend every class and preview for the pop quiz. you will get a B easily....But A is nearly impossible.....I have changed my facebook head photo to Mark Haug. Pray to him, you will not fail.

Best teacher in the business school hands down; most intelligent person I know; most helpful professor. Haug will go out of his way to make you successful but you have to work equally as hard. Class is difficult if you don't attend or prepare; this is why a lot fail this class - not b/c of Haug

Points aren't given for attending lecture, but homework and quizzes are given nearly every class period, so you will not pass the class if you don't attend regularly. Points are given for attending weekly lab. The two tests are near impossible, which is why he has to give Bs to the top 50% of the class. No one I know likes Mark or this class.
Worst class ever. Bad teaching style. Basicly He taught nothing. The exam is extreamly hard. He enjoy if students fail

Awful professor. He goes on random tangents and doesnt explain anything. He seems to know a lot but cant communicate the knowledge to anyone. He's like a robot. If you can avoid taking this class with him, do it. Try online or at a different school. He just doesnt care. By far the worst class/professor I've ever had.

Contrary to popular belief, Haug is not trying to make you fail his class. However, this class is very challenging!! Class attendance is not mandatory, but it will significantly help you and your grade if you go. Also attended lab, the worksheets help when studying for the 2 exams.

Haug is the most intelligent teacher in the business school hands down. He runs a stringent class with intentions to punish the lazy and unprepared. If you don't miss class or lab you'll probably end up with a B.

Don't take this class with Haug! He is terrible and wants his students to fail. Exams are near impossible. Take it over the summer with a different professor. It is by far the worst class i have ever taken at KU!

It's a weed out class and Haug does everything he can to make the material as convoluted as possible. That being said, the textbook is your best tool. Listening to him for an hour and 45 min is like trying to learn stats from a potato. Go to class, lab, do every hw assignment, and USE THE BOOK! It's difficult but possible to pass.
hardest class in the business school...lots of homework and pop quizzes. You have to go to class.  study for the midterm and final for at least a week or you will fail.

This is the hardest class in the School of Business. However, he is an amazing professor and you will learn valuable information for the real world. Do the work, study, and go to class and you'll be fine.

I can't say enough bad things about Haug but I'll try: no tests except midterm & final - requires you to print his huge ppt as note supplement - can grade you in relation to other students but refuses to provide class avgs - "doesn't believe" in 90/80/70/60 grading system. overall, a blowhard. Take this class over the summer/from someone else.
This class is hard! class consist of final, miderm, quizzes, & homework. Attend class everyday to turn in homework and he gives pop quizzes.

Haug makes this one of the hardest classes in the business school but he is a great professor and relates almost everything to the real world. Just be sure to go to class because there are alot of easy points.

Going to class is like going to feeding time at the zoo, however, you are on the menu! You need every point you can get; every quiz, homework and lab point counts. It is possible to fail both test and still get a B. Work hard and you wont have anything to worry about.

Go to class and just do all the homeworks and at least attempt the quizzes and that way you have cushion to fall back on since the midterm and final are close to impossible. He's a very smart guy and can seem intimidating but this class is doable
Great teacher. He has a great personality and made class interesting and made it apply to our own lives. I definatly reccomend him
Definitely go to class.  That's where all your points are.  This is the hardest class in the business school.  Just show up, try your hardest, an try to get in the top 50% of the class.
Fantastic course.  Haug clearly and succinctly lays out the methods and processes for analyzing a problem that contains uncertainty and variability.

VERY HARD final!! I got an F on the final but still got a B in the class. The top half of the class automatically gets a B so shoot for that.A is almost impossible and you have to be very very smart.He is not very helpful outside of class.Fun teacher though and lecture is not too boring, but mandatory! If you can take it in the summer I would do it
Hard class that requires LOTS of studying!! VERY nice and thoughtful professor. You shouldn't get lower than a B if you try!

Great teacher. long class for only 3 credits but very good, clear, teacher. Gives good examples and at times makes stats some.what interesting. Tests were fair, study mainly from old exams and a few definitions
Extremely difficult information, but he is an interesting teacher that makes everyday worth going.

Best teacher I've ever had by a lot.  He's hysterical, yet very informative.  There are 3 ways to get an A which is nice, and there are plenty of free points.  He does an excellent job of showing you how statistics are relevant in the business world.

Amazing professor, he is probably the smartest person i've ever met and he is very good at explaining a fairly confusing subject. Books only used for homework, so share them with someone else if you can.  GO TO CLASS, just going over the powerpoint slides won't cut it. The tests are very difficult but there are 2. Half the classes points are gimmes

Haug is a really good teacher. The class is really hard but if you go everyday and do all the homework you should do decent. the tests suck but the class is actually interesting and he is a good teacher just a difficult class

Very Very hard teacher, DO NOT MISS CLASS!! try to avoid if possible, if not you will be spending lots of time outside of class to try and get a decent grade. Class is curved ONLY for people over B+ this makes no sense!!!
The best teacher I have ever had. He is a genius and a lot of fun. He'll make you think tho and the class isn't easy but keep up and go to class and lab and you'll do fine.

Professor Haug was one of the best one of the best teachers I have had at KU. The class is difficult if you don't keep up with it so its up to you how hard it is. He has interesting lectures that made it easy to go to. If you complain about the class its because you don't like working for a grade.
Impossible to do well in his class! Take it during the semester or at a different school if you want a grade that doesn't destroy your GPA.

This man is the most interesting professor I've had at KU so far. Many say the class is hard, but if you study and go to class you'll likely get a B. If you don't get the grade by points, the top 10% get and A, the top 50% get a B. Amazing individual.
It's a very very hard class, but I always enjoy going to the lecture. Prof. Haug has a way about him that is very interesting and knowledgeable.

Before taking this class, realize that you will not do well. There will be many things on the test that you will have never seen before.  The TA's are just there as a formality, they don't know how to do things either. That being said, he's not evil, he just really enjoys this stuff.
Professor Haug is a great teacher with Finance and Excel. He assigns interesting projects that can be difficult at times. Excel is used the entire semester. I recommend this class.
Terrible person who will do anything to make sure a student does not earn an A. Finals are impossible with stuff on their that he never covers. Miserable class!!
very very very bad professor, in my opinion

Very difficult class but Mark is a great teacher and makes the materials somewhat interesting. You have to go to class! Their are quizzes almost every class period and you need to get all the points possible to balance out the hard midterm and final. Good luck!

This class was entertaining, I guess...but I am still scratching my head about what exactly it was about. I really just went to hear Haug talk because he is quite entertaining and the case studies are pretty cool. I really dont think you can teach people to make good decisions, it is kind of a common sense thing. Anyways, the tests really arent har

Professor Haug is an awesome teacher. His class is really interesting (Really,no joking). He makes the class fun. But in fact, this class is hard. I think if you do the homework (go to the help room and do it, this will guarantee you get the maxim points for the HW) and go to class, you would get a B!!! You will be fine, just need to do some work^^

This class takes your time and devotion. Haug is an excellent professor and loved going to class but it was a difficult course. I spent more time focusing on this class than my other classes. The class isn't too bad and is manageable to get a good grade if you put up the time. Luckily, I received an A.

Good teacher. Every thing is in the slides and he goes over them TO CLARIFY them for you but it is a tough class. Do the homework, show up and do ok on the quizzes (almost every class has one) and do ok on midterm and final and you should have a B. People make it seem harder than it really is.

On the midterm on thought I studied and knew everything and got a C.  On the Final Exam even the TAs couldn't do 50% of the problems they told us.  Pay attention, take notes, and study your notes before EVERY class.  Good guy but difficult class.

Professor Haug is an extraordinary person and teacher. I learned a lot in his class. It is a difficult class so prepare the rest of your schedule accordingly. Getting an A is nearly impossible even though it may seem possible going into the final. The final was the hardest test I have ever taken. Sadly, the final left a bad tast in my mouth.
wonderful person and intelligent professor.
Great professor

Haug is one of the finest professors I have had at KU.  People who complain about him simply have never had to try in KU's Business School.  You have to do the homework and attend the class prepared, but you learn a lot from him.  I put more effort into this class than any other I've taken at KU, but I learned a lot about the real world from it.

Terrible instructor.  He can't teach very well.  I learned nothing from him, only from tutors.  His exams are ridiculous.  He grades by top 50% of the class will get a B.  The class average was a 62% but 50% got Bs, the rest Failed the class.
He is a really nice teacher always willing to help. Subject is hard and he moves reall fast. A lot of material is covered. He tell interesting stories about the subject. He is a nice guy

This is the truth from an A-B student: He is a good guy, everyone is right about that.  This class is VERY difficult though.  I highly suggest studying the notes before every class period so you are prepared for quizzes, which are almost every class.  Lots of the material is hard to grasp, overall it's not an easy course at all.

Tests are almost impossible. Throws a lot of information at you. Homework is difficult and you have quizzes nearly every class period. I would NOT suggest you take a class from this professor unless you want a very hard semester.

Great professor.  He comes off mean at the start, but you will soon see he is one of the best KU has and a great guy.  Prof. Haug uses real life examples to help explain the material.  If you can take DSCI with Haug, do so.

He's sharp, enthutiastic, and cares alot about his teaching. Maybe the business students are not used to studying in general and learning not so simple concepts. Come on guys, he gives easy quizzes, free voucher points, and the assignments he gives are stright forward. That's about 50 % of your grade in the class.

So far the best teacher I have had at KU.  This is my fifth year so I have had a lot!  If you need help with anything, he is always willing to make time for you and wants to see you succeed.  The people rating him poorly are those who recieved a bad grade do to their inability to understand simple logic.
Hard Midterm......Not sure on final yet.
Very knowledgable and efficient with his words and actions.

I have no idea what these other crazies are talking about.  You NEED to study for his tests.  I studied very hard for the midterm and got a 95% on it, same with the final.  DON'T bypass studying, but when studying you should mostly review a bunch of old problems and find patterns in them and be able to recognize the kind of problem you're looking a
GREAT professor! Class discussions were interesting, information was presented in a meaningful way, and it made me really think.  Test is easy if you just stay awake in class.

It's a waste of time to study for tests.  No matter how much you 'think' you understand your homework, you'll still do bad on the tests. His TA's do not know much.  Over half of KU applies to Business school and his class is why only 10% who apply get in. It's a required class so just do your best to get through it and try not to stress out!
No Comments

This class is seriously tough, probably the toughest so far.  Getting an A made me feel I accomplished something.:P  Some of the TAs aren't very helpful at all.  Prof. Haug is very smart, and seems distant from most students.

If you still have your sanity at the end of the semester after taking this class with Haug, you've really accomplished something.  He won't explain things clearly because I think it's his goal to disclose helpful info in order to set you up for failure.  Also, my TA for this class was the biggest moron ever and her last name is White.

The test are not hard. If you do all of the problems that he put on the online review you will be fine. He likes to flip the problems from the review packet though, so dont just memorize. Not that hard, but if you dont like math, you are going to hate this class and not understand it. If your a math person you will be fine. Final was easiest test.
He is unclear and unavailable in his big lecture.  He goes out of his way to weed out the non-sicophants, then he demolishes the hopes of others who give the class their all.
Very Tough
He's a challenging teacher, but it's worth it.  He's incredibly smart!  I really enjoy his teaching, he's very clear as long as you go to every class and pay attention.
Very tough class but the professor is okay.

Very difficult course!  He is a very nice man and tries to explain the info well.  Study with the TA's, they are helpful!  Do well on the homework and try to do well on the quizes, the tests are nearly impossible to do well on, especially the final - don't bother studying for it!
He is the nicest professor I've ever had.  Tests are hard but the class is extremely fair, and he loves it when people take the time to ask him questions.  He cares about his students.

This is by far the hardest class to try and pass at KU.  I failed it and am switching majors b/c his class is impossible to pass.  I found the class to be interesting and he keeps your attention.  However, his midterm and final are IMPOSSIBLE!  Quizes every day and hmk. is also due everyday!
Great Professor

Very Specific to the point... ie make sure you listen to every word... if you find yourself unable to listen to everything he says get a tape recorder... hardest class at ku if you don't study a lot. if you do and get all your homework you are almost guaranteed a B  Awesome teacher!!!SMART GUY!!

Stats is the hardest class you will take at KU.  The way he grades the class works to your advantadge, but keep up with the material, the final is suh a huge part of your grade, and its a ridiculous test

Hardest class material wise ever.You are almost garaunteed a high c or low b though if you get all your HW and quiz scores, which is easy because he gives you 100 points.One of the worst teachers I have ever had.There is no doubt he is very smart, he just cant teach.Test are IMPOSSBLE.
nice teacher..hard class..I got an 80% on midterm but I know I blew the final.
Extremely articulate, intelligent man.  The material can be overwhelming, and the class is the toughest I've taken so far, but Haug is engaging and enjoyable.
Interesting class, Haug can hold your attention pretty well, but this is one tough class. You seriously don't need to study for the final because it will not help, final is very difficult.

This class was very overwhelming at first -- the two statistical problems were almost mind-blowing. But he helped us solve them, and graded very fairly. And it felt very satisfying to finish such difficult work.
very hard class, 90% will get a C or above though so don't freak out about bad midterm/final scores, everyone does horribly
The course is freaking hard. If you need a good grade, take the sum class. If you cannot make it in sum, than be ready to sacrifice your grade. Good luck!
Hardest class so far for me at KU. Haug makes the class interesting however. He tries to get the hard material into your head the best he can.

Hardest class I have ever took.  Haug is so nice though and tries to help.  Don't worry about your midterm or final grade scores. Everyone averages about a 40% on those.  Don't study too hard for the final.  It won't help at all.
Haug has the hardest tests ever, but he keeps class interesting.  Don't try to study for the final because it won't help.  Just do homework and quizzes.  He is a good teacher, just very hard.

A very intelligent man, just has a hard time relating material to students, and in turn, helping them to understand material. This makes for a very hard time on the tests, which are already near impossible.
No Comments
Prof. Haug is nice only when he wants to be, but beware his shady lawyer tactics. he will only help you if it doesn't hurt him.

Prof. Haug is a very good teacher and keep your interest in the class. If your a business major you can't get around this class so you might as well enjoy it. The tests are near impossible becuase of all the information you have to learn.

I think she is a great teacher! I really liked the slides went over the information very well! People are saying it's too much info, yes because its anatomy and med school or such is going to be even faster paced and harder to keep up with and more in depth. Class will allow for good overview of anatomy. use the practice test and they will be easy.

I never met this professor in person, but based on the emails and her video lectures, she's a kind professor. When I needed help, she would quickly respond to my emails. She also provided many useful resources for this course that helped me prepare for the 8 exams (it's not that bad). This class requires you to be good at time management to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Every course I've taken that relies on McGraw Hill Connect has been worse for it, and this one is no exception. Material isn't too difficult, but there's a lot of information covered and the class moves fast. Tests account for 70% of your total grade and cover 3-4 chapters each. Dr. Huffman seems nice but there's very little engagement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is okay at teaching. The biggest issue is that she is not very nice and is not a very understanding person at all. She will give you zeros on assignments even if they're a minute past the due date, doesn't matter the circumstances. Class is well organized and you know what is expected on exams. She just isn't a very nice understanding person.

Though I didn't know her that well since I took the online version, she seems very nice and clearly wants students to succeed.

There are many resources to help you succeed in this course, but if you were only to do one thing, do the practice exams. For the last exam, all the studying I did was take the practice exam 10 times, and I got a 94...

Science class, so a heavier work load is expected. This class wasn't too bad if you paced yourself to stay on track. If online isn't for you, take the in person lecture. Warning: discussion posts! The due date posted is for the 2nd half so often I missed the 1st part and got a 0. Also, utilize the practice tests!! Probably the best study tool.

One of the worst classes Ive taken. Never have had a worse professor. Doesnt even teach the class just expects you to know from online homeworks. Dont take it. You will have to spend 12 hours a week studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Gives you one week to complete homework assignments, quizzes and tests. Homework takes hours only for 2 points. Too much to study for for tests . Tests are 100 points each. Only tests count for grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor's communication with her students through email is unprofessional, and ignored several emails even after following her protocol for emails. Even after studying and using the practice tests she provides, you still manage to fail the tests and final exam. The work in this class is just busy work and provides no importance.

Have to use Connect which is expensive. Proctored tests. Lots of reading. Tests were always due on Mondays. Lectures were not helpful. Discussion board posts are busy work (have to take videos/video replies). Overall not the most difficult class if you study, but be aware that the software is expensive and there's quite a few assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Expensive and intensive. Lots of reading and homework. Unforgiving when it comes to mistakes when transitioning to an asynchronous classroom. Overall, she seems lazy and my experience has been poor so far.

She teaches online only so expect the usual mediocre attempt from the instructor at teaching. Be forewarned there are a lot of technical glitches and issues with McGraw Hill Software used for homework and test. The instructor is not very tech savvy and expects you to figure things out yourself when it comes to troubleshooting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Huffman is a good person but during this online anatomy class this semester I felt like she was disconnected. Sometimes when I asked for help she responded to me like " don't you know this is an online class? I don't have to be very helpful." and taking the traditional class would be better because you might be able to form study a grou
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She was an alright professor. I had to take this class online being a commuter student. I just have to say if you struggle with online courses don't take this. She is easy to get a hold of but not easy to get a lot of help when you're concerned for your grade. The material is very interesting, but it's a lot to do in a short time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: mega chiller and the class is pretty easy

I took this class online during the Summer, so everything was very condensed. Some directions were unclear, but there are enough buffer points to feel comfortable if you don't do well on one of the many quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I have taken many online classes before and this, by far, was the best experience I've every had with an online instructor. She was very helpful and gave clear guidelines. If you do all of the assignments and tests on time, you will most likely get a good grade. I really appreciated her responsiveness. I would recommend this online class to anyone!

I took this online after hearing countless times that the in class teacher is terrible. Im so happy i did! Every week there is a HW and activity due (easy 100s) and then a short test. Tests are easy. You can find old study guidestest filesnotecards to use too that helped me tons! I got a B but only bc I missed 2 tests.(& i never used the book)

There are quizzes on random Thursdays and he doesn't tell you when, but they are super easy. The practice exam is just like the real exam and you get a cheat sheet so you should get a good grade in the class if you study properly and take good notes.

the BEST math professor I have ever had. His lectures are always so helpful to both the homework and exams. I honestly loved going to class because of how great of an instructor he was. He also gives practice exams and you're allowed a formula sheet for both midterms and the final. He's also so sweet and funny, everyone liked him.

Professor Huang is amazing. He is super nice and helpful. He is very clear on his grading if you ask him. Tests were not difficult and he had practice exams which were very similar to the actual exams. He does have an accent which can make it difficult for some. Overall, if he is an option to take for any class I would take him.

Professor Huang has a very thick accent which makes his lectures hard to understand. The exams were not too difficult, but the homework took many hours each week.  Realistically, the class was not super hard but you might have to learn a lot of the content outside of the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor has very thick accent, which make MATH 126, a hard subject already, harder. He also isn't very helpful with IClickers and goes through them quickly. Wouldn't recomend

Weizhang does additional proofs to really help you understand concepts. He's not hard to understand given his accent and really has a passion for math. He does tend to not give help on iClickers/gives short time limit to work them out, but it forces you to think and get it done. Taking him again next semester.

Prof. Huang is a nice person and a great math professor. It takes active listening skills while in his lecture, as he speaks with a heavy accent. Normally this wouldn't be a big deal, but Calc II is difficult to begin with. I have nothing but love for him, but it got rough. He also has a tendency to go off on proofs that aren't necessary to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Makes sure to prove most things in order to explain them. Cracks a few jokes here and there. Very efficient lectures.

Best film professor at the school by a mile. most film professors are more proficient in theory than they are in actual production strategy. Hurst is still working on projects to this day and understands the film making process firsthand. Breath of fresh air!
Love Professor Hurst! Great connection to have in the film school. Super easy class with valuable group projects. Gives good examples and gives good feedback. Sweet guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: I've had Bob for two film classes now, and he's a real gem. Gives great feedback, expect good results but also isn't an unnecessary hard-ass, and if you have any film questions he's easy to get a hold of outside class for help. Also a great sense of humor and really relates with students. Highly recommend!

Had him for Non-fiction production. Really good feedback and active in the class, as well as a humorous guy. His lectures were the usual, maybe a bit short which works good for a production class, and he asked for class input a lot on due dates and assignments which was really nice while also keeping us on track.

Hurst is one of the easiest graders in the department. He is a super fun guy who always cares about what he is talking about and has fun being involved in student projects. He is not overbearing (unusual here), always down to talk about good food in Lawrence, cancels class a lot, but prefers the men in classes. Still a good guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Definitely one of maybe 3 or 4 valuable professors currently working in the department. Really knowledgable, always willing to give helpful feedback, and also willing to be straightforward with you about your work instead of babying you through anything. Also willing to help secure summer internships for students. Down to earth guy, fun to talk to.

Bob provides necessary information and materials that really helped me become a better filmmaker. There were times where he was somewhat unavailable (such as going upstairs to his office while we worked on editing) but overall he was a very good professor. Very picky, which only made me better.
Professor Hurst is a fun, friendly guy to chat with and discuss film, but his lecturing style could use some work. However, he was helpful and helped me learn.
This professor was extraordinarily hard to understand and could not bring his teaching to the student's level.

Professor Hurst seems friendly enough, although he comes off as arrogant and pretentious at times.  Difficulty of exams are a mixed bag: the mid term was difficult, but the final was a joke.  The movie screenings are enjoyable, but make sure to take decent notes, as your film journals will be collected and graded.

This class has the reputation of being a joke class but I actually learned a lot from it. You will get a good grade in it if you go to class and take decent notes. Not hard, but definitely requires effort. Hurst obviously knows what he's talking about and the movies we watched we're current and good for the most part.

Robert knows alot about film, but he is too advanced to teach a 100 level class. He doesn't take into account that this class is most peoples first film class. He teaches way too advanced material without explaining the details for novices.
Hurst is the best teacher in the  film department. Unlike most, he's not a prick when he tries to help you and doesn't have an ego. Hurst wants to help you learn and has great ideas. Take his class.

Professor Hurst is great. His class is fun and he is always willing to help and give ideas. He made me love video production even more than I already do. If you want/need a film class to take, TAKE THIS ONE!
No Comments

Pretty much they only production professor that's actually worth a damn. Since he's new, he doesn't know that University protocol is to not teach you anything, and I accidentally learned a LOT in this class. He is fantastic.

One of the most highly knowledgeable professors in the department in terms of production, but challenges students to develop their ideas for their benefit. Prepare to spend about 5 hours outside of class for each assigned project, but do your best and you will do well.
She is great professor! Challenging at first, but once you get to know her, you will love her! Such a sweetheart

Dr. Seo is an amazing instructor. She provides relevant information in every class period and bends the curriculum for first year students depending on their interests, while still meeting relevant points. Every group project has clear outlines and if not, she is always available to meet and provide criticism.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--Tough Grader

reviews.comment: She is GREAT. Best campaigns teacher at KU.  You will work hard but she truly wants you to learn and pass with flying colors.  Show up to class, work well with your group, and its an A for sure.

Dr. Seo was one of my favorite professors that I had in the J-school. She is extremely helpful and always willing to help her students. She was a great campaigns teacher and I highly recommend her. As long as you work hard and put forth effort, you will get a good grade.

So sweet and helpful. She is so knowledgeable and a great professor. Very willing to help and answer any questions. Campaigns is a very demanding course but she helps you through the entire thing. I would definitely recommend her for any class.

DO NOT TAKE ANY OF HIS CLASSES!!!!Save yourself the stress and tiers.He is so disorganized and takes forever to grade and will not leave you with any explanation to justify grades.He was evaluated at our mid term because so many people complained about his bad teaching to the COMS department.Smells like smoke so badly.DON'T DO IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ian made it extremely hard to feel comfortable while presenting speeches. He amplifies the pressure to make you even more nervous. He is an extremely tough grader which adds more anxiety to not mess up. He constantly cancelled speech days, you are mentally and physically prepare to give a speech then have to wait 5 more days to give it.

Every other coms class is graded so easy but he grades so much harder than everyone else. The class has honestly giving me more anxiety when I give speeches it is just put together terribly. As well as he just talks and talks and talks about stuff that does not relate to the topic and it's painful.

Coms 322. Montgomery grades hard! Lots of other Coms 322 classes you just show up and give the speech and its an A. With Montgomery he pushes you to do almost everything exceptional and go above and beyond. Eye Contact, Voice, Movement. If you want to get a B in Coms 322 or a C take him

Surprised to see a lower-average score for Mr. Montgomery! He is a wonderful instructor. I felt that he really bonded with each student and was invested in their success. He also built a strong sense of community among the students and made class fun. If you put in the effort, it is easy to score well. I would definitely recommend this instructor!

This professor made this course much more difficult than needed, grading very harshly and making it difficult to find a speech topic. There was never a 100% given on a speech to anyone in the course and he would critique our speech right when we finished in front of everyone, which doesn't help with speech anxiety. Take this course w another prof!

He was a very tough grader and very critical of peoples speech. He made people criticize their classmates speeches directly after the speech which broke down a lot of confidence. He was very quick to strike down topics students chose and many dropped the class due to his teaching style. AVOID taking his class at all costs

He is awful, way to picky about speeches and topics for an entry level class. He will criticize you in front of the class and tell you lots of bad things about your performance and barley any good things. His quizzes are hard for no reason. He is not clear with the textbook and what you should read. He never answers his emails.

I took COMS 322 in-person and expected it to be like everyone else claimed - if you get your work done, rehearse your speeches, and show up to class you'll fine. I did all of the following and never received higher than a B on a speech, got slammed with a 50% on participation. He wasn't understanding with outlying circumstances
I've heard there are some professors that are easier, but he is very understanding when you are sick and can't give your speech! This class was probably a bit harder because it wasn't online.

We only wrote a handful of papers and gave 3 speeches during the course. It was online due to COVID but Ian made all assignments easy to understand. He was flexible with due dates and just wanted the students to take something away from the class. He was very understanding and just wanted to help when it came to the technical difficulties with zoom

Speech class, we wrote 4 speeches, a paper, and did some assignments/quizzes weekly. Ian is pretty chill. He does whatever he needs to do for you to succeed and is flexible with deadlines. I did this class online through COVID so it was a little bit less scary to public speak on Zoom. Overall fine class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: -12 Pop Quizzes 2 get dropped -Readings every week -not so much of lecture, more of discussions -1 small paper and one Term Paper  -Fun course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a great professor, he's very passionate about philosophy. He's a smart guy and he explains his lectures very thoroughly and if you still don't understand, he'll explain it again. It's a lot of material and he's tough on his grading (hit or miss), but other than that and the pop quizzes, he's a pretty good choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I have ever had the misfortune of coming in contact with in 3 years at KU. He is so disrespectful towards his students and turned what could have been an interesting class into an overall terrible experience. Each class consisted of MaDaniel talking for 50 minutes straight - he never allowed for discussion.

He grades really hard, both tests and term papers. You have to go to class and take notes on everything he says, because all of the material is used for both the tests and the term paper. He'll give you help if you ask for it, and notes when you put in the effort. Not an easy A, but pretty interesting.

Igor is a great Professor. His classes and tests are not complicated or difficult. Sometimes in class youll spend the first 20 minutes talking about current events or sports. Hes a smart dude and pretty nice and willing to help.

Professor Ristic recently moved to Oregon State University, and me being a freshman, it was nice having a professor who was just as new to the school as I was. He's super nice and always willing to help you do well. Read and pass with an easy A. Would recommend :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Study guide is good for tests. Difficult grader even when follow rubric. Attendance mandatory. Lots of note taking in class. Very responsive to emails and questions. Nice guy but grading is crazy for content on journals and papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Igor Ristic is a really chill guy and a good teacher. The class information is by no means hard, but Ristic still explains all of it very clearly and gives plenty of examples. If you go to class and take good notes (He does posts the lecture slides online as well), you should do well. Journals are easy and quizzes aren't bad.

At first I thought I wouldn't do well, ended up with an A. Write your notes with examples, email him to look over your papers before due, and just show an interest. I learned a lot and did what I was suppose to do and did very well. He is a very nice, understanding guy and he will work with you to get what you want!

Sometimes he can be a little tough to understand, but overall Prof Ristic is a very laid back professor. He is disorganized and will never respond to emails. Grades most things easily, except for your speeches. HATES VERBAL FILLERS. Don't even dream of saying "um" during a speech. Not to bad, I'd recommend him.

She disappeared two times during the semester without explanation, delaying grades and feedback for final paper prep materials without any kind of extension for the paper despite these delays. This is after saying she reserved "up to a week" to grade these, but got them back up to 3.5 weeks late. Overall extremely annoyed and frustrated.

Do not take a class with Ilana. She's rude and not at all helpful when you approach her for guidance. She won't give you specifics about how to do better on assignments yet continuously grades harshly. Her lectures are vague as are her expectations and she's generally a very poor communicator. One of my worst classes at KU.

Have sent 3 e-mails regarding course work, and have yet to receive a response. After on the syllabus she stressed the importance of email communication. I find lack of communication very unprofessional, also the issues continue unresolved.
Pretty good professor.   Fairly  thick accent but nothing that you cant get around.

Easy class if you keep up with all the busy work she assigns. 2 group projects, a testdiscussion every week, 4 papers throughout the semester, as well as a final paper at the end. She is a tough grader, doesn't hand out points easily for a 100 level course.
Relatively easy class to take online.  I found her to be a hard grader.  Directions were sometimes unclear and she was not very timely at grading, giving feedback, or returning emails.

Best GTA! She's very sweet and helpful and knows what she's talking about. SHe has an accent that's a little hard to understand at times, but it's in no way debilitating. She helps you study for tests and write your papers. Definitely sign up for her soc 104 discussion!

Ilana is great. She has a real passion for Sociology and she does a great job of encouraging her students to share in that passion. She is very open in the discussion class and invites open dialogue and a variety of ideas from her students. I enjoyed her immensely.

This instructor is terrible.  We saw her on the first day only.  The class is totally unstructured and disjointed.  The syllabus, grading policies, and assignment requirements change daily. One assignment and midterm all semester and then suddenly all these things due at the end that we didn?t find out until like two weeks left in the semester.

Absolutely terrible teacher. does not care about students and usually answers questions with "what do you think?" She switched attendance of the online lectures from optional to mandatory mid-semester and her teaching ability is lacking, to say the least. She has PhD but she no idea what shes doing.Her lack of technology understanding is apparent.

pretty bad class. pretty bad teacher. she teaches a database class thats exactly the same as another database class. both are required for what ever reason. so basically didnt learn anything that wasnt already taught. online class with terrible assignments. overall bad.

350 characters isn't enough for me to say how awful I found this class to be.  Starts off easy but homework assignments, cases, projects, and exam all pile up at the end.  The study guides for exams are absurdly long and clearly state that she's unwilling to answer any questions.  And coding SQL on paper in an exam setting is seriously ridiculous.

She is nice and encourages discussion, but she goes off on slightly related but irrelevant tangents from her personal life.  She is teaching courses about information systems, but frequently reveals her lack of knowledge/understanding and meaningful experience with technology through her comments in class.
Would be better if she didn't wait until the end of the semester to load up all of the homework.
Hello hello hello...teacher is fun and interesting but dumber than a bag of rocks

Very disrespectful teacher. She will go out of her way to make students feel stupid. Also plays favorites big time. She had too many assignments due right at the end of the semester, while we hardly had any assignments at the beginning of the semester. Often answers questions with "that's just the way it is" and won't explain any further.
No Comments

Despite her PHD, she's still very unintelligent. She refuses to work with students who are having trouble with the course. Her class structure is very boring. She doesn't try to make it interesting.  She almost never answers questions in class. She usually goes, "we'll get to that", and then, does not really answer the question of WHY.. always answ

While it was a tough class, it was a rewarding one. Indrani knows her stuff, and yes, you will have to work to know the stuff too. The tests were tough, and the weighting on one of the questions for the midterm failed me. With that being said, if you go to class, do the work, and show that you give a damn, it is possible to succeed.

If you really want to learn some economics, join this class. She is brilliant. Focus is on learning concepts and not mugging up the material. Very thorough with theory of money and international finance. She is strict but it is for the benefit of the student. Very tough grader. If you need an A, get ready to study hard. Brush up your basics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very Informative class. She's  too good. She built up the basics of IS LM and demand and supply of financial markets although this is a part of the prerequisite. Very honest grader. Only students who work really hard can get an A. Join this if you have above average intelligence. Not meant for lowly intelligent or casual students.

She's incredibly intelligent, but not a great professor. Very difficult tests, though the curve helps.  You don't know where you stand grade-wise until the end. She expects you to have a great background understanding and often fails to teach the basics. Very tough grader. Was sometimes brutally critical in class to participants. proceed w/ caution
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Manna thoroughly knows her subject. This was a difficult class, but it's rewarding if you put in the effort. Group presentations were held roughly every two weeks. Attendance and a good group are necessary if you want to succeed.

She didn't use blackboard unfortunately which made it virtually impossible to know where you stood for the duration of the class. Also, her tests were pretty difficult and she failed to provide any semblance of a study guide.

When you study for his tests, be sure to READ THE BOOK. The only reason people are not doing good on tests is because they don't read. I skimmed the book twice and I got an A on every test. Gives out extra credit for participating in class, too. Willing to write good letters of recommendation as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall, I enjoyed this class very much because the content was so interesting. Dr. Ingram is a decent professor that knows what he is teaching. The tests, however, are difficult--you will want to pay attention AND read the book. You have to work hard, but it will all pay off in the end. I did enjoy this class.

Abnormal Psychology was definitely the most interesting class I took this semester. As long as you go to class and read the book, the exams aren't too hard. There's very little filler work so the exams matter. He gave several options for extra credit. Overall a pretty alright dude.
Awesome and interesting class, tests are difficult because he takes very small details from the book so make sure to really read!

Dr. Ingram was the worst professor I've ever had. His tests were vague/unclear and were only over unimportant details. He is quite simply a mean person who mocked people, refused to help them, and did not care about his students' well-being. He did not respond to emails. When questioned he refused to be civil or respectful. Very stubborn and rude.

His class is very interesting and he is a good lecturer.  HOWEVER, his tests are extremely difficult and does not prepare you well for them. The review sessions are completely useless, the TAs just read paraphrased slides from his lectures. (He doesn't show up to them, either)

Do not take this class. The professor doesnt respond to emails. His tests are nearly impossible to pass with a good grade. Half of the questions (25 of them) come from atleast 4 chapters worth of information in the book. The reviews are pointless, he isnt even there for them. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR

I really like him as a professor. He really knows what he's talking about and makes the class enjoyable, working against the flow of many rude students in the class. His tests may be a bit difficult and rather inconsistent - he does give extra credit! - but the class itself is interesting.

DO NOT take this class with this professor! His tests are inconsistent and he does not prepare you well at all. He will ask random, irrelevant questions. When I took this course, on most tests, no one got higher than a C. Going to office hours was no help either.Also takes a very long time to respond to emails(if he responds at all).NOT recommended

This man may possibly be the worst professor I have ever had in my life. He won't answer emails (and when he does, they don't help), he is rude, and he likes to make people feel stupid. His tests are impossible. It would warm my heart if this man was fired tomorrow morning.
Great teacher! Put in the effort and you learn a lot. Not a class for slackers.
One of my favorite professors!
Best professor I ever had. Really cares about his students.

Made abnormal psychology really interesting. I really liked the way he integrated films and lectures. He's really fair and helpful and I learned a lot. Put in a little work and you will get a lot out of his classes.
always answered emails promptly and available thru office hours. Could make the most boring class interesting. Jayhawk tie is a nice touch.

Rick is a decent professor, but he never answers his e-mails.  If you have an emergency or a question about something don't expect an answer or if you get one it will be days later when it doesn't help anymore anyway.
he took an interesting class and made it hard and boring and frustrating
Abnormal psych could have been interesting if it had been taught by ANYONE else.
Ingram is a great instructor.  His classes are always super-interesting.  He's also one of the coolest guys I've ever met.
never there for review or tests...Reviews are useless
This class is very interesting but the tests are a little hard. SO study and read!

This is the worst teacher at the University of Washington. I have never had such a disorganized teacher. Changed the syllabus about 6 times throughout the quarter and never gave our writing prompts in a timely manner. I would never have my worst enemy take this class taught by her!
If you're interested in as much reading as this class requires, you might as well read the bible.  Thanks for nothing Ingra.
Suprisingly good.  Works hard to engage students.

I would not take this class at all. I took it for fun because I thought it sounded interesting and it ended up being the most stressful class I had all semester. It was not the class but the instuctor and her way of teaching. The final was over 130 questions and 29 pages long.

Do not take this class unless you have to, and if you have to, take it from a different professor.  Very confusing and boring lectures, hard tests, and long and hard final.  She is also not a friendly person.
Do not take this class unless you completley have to.  ALL of the tests are hard. The final is just as hard as the other tests.  MAKE SURE YOU READ ALL ASSIGNED READINGS!!

She ruined what could have been a interesting class, AND she hates Forrest Gump. Her tests were insane, though the final wasn't bad. I would NOT recommend that anyone that this class unless you HAVE to.
This is a very opinionated class. Participation aka showing up to class is a big part of your grade.

Professor Wadud is brilliant and extremely helpful. If you literally have any questions about anything, she will get back to you ASAP with insightful advice. Just give her your best effort, and you will get a good grade and learn something while doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is very concerned about the problems every one would have in that class. She is respectful of everybody's opinion (even those really really extreme). She is professional and her grading is pretty easy too.
Monique is the best teacher I have had at KU. She will go out of her way to help you succeed.

Monique was an excellent GTA who is very passionate about the Classics field. She was very energetic while teaching, and graded the assignments/quizzes fairly. She tried to make learning Latin as exciting and easy as possible, and I think she did a great job. Definitely recommend her!

It may be true that Monique does little annoying things (rambles, keeps you late) but you have to cut her some slack because I don't think she has taught very long & she is really passionate about what she does. By the end, I only needed a 61% on my final to get an A in the class so she can't be that terrible. She also gives alot of extra credit.
Sooa is passionate and intelligent, sweet and charming. She means well and tries hard. But yes, she can also be difficult to understand at times. Still, I would love to take her again!

Sooa Im was a wonderful teacher and helped me learn a lot throughout the spring semester. It's very important that you go to all of her classes because she takes attendance but if you take thorough notes and pay attention, you'll do well and easily get a B+ or A.

Funny and sweet, but her accent can be a little thick at times. She encourages questions and discussion. Her lecture is mostly slides of artwork with all the notes to the side, so you really don't need the textbook if you take good notes. Your grade is only based on 3 tests and an essay but you must study a lot to do well on the tests.

You're playing russian roulette here, because you will never see Peterson, only a TA. I had Monalisa Dutta- a very nice woman, but a very bad teacher. I basically taught this class to myself. Unfortunately, you need this class to pass, so if you get a bad TA you have to suffer through it. Ask for help anywhere you can get it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ingrid Peterson is rude, impatient, and does not care about her students. Ingrid Peterson is a terrible professor. She rarely teaches any of her classes as she hires incompetent TAs. She is responsible for the poorly managed KAP program and she requires everyone to buy WebAssign to do homework in the class. Take math at JCCC and skip KAP.

This class was run by a GTA not by Ingrid. Many of the GTAs were not great math teachers and rushed through class because they are on a strict schedule. The Math Help Room is available every day, so they taught me everything I needed to know. The Math Help Room is free tutoring, so definitely take advantage of it!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ingrid is not the real teacher for 101 - you get a TA for the class and how you do in the class depends on how good your TA is and how good you are at algebra. It's good to consult the Help Room for the homework as it is graded harshly. If you don't show up to class, your grade will tank. If you're required to take 101, just hope for a good TA.

I enrolled in Math 101-Data Driven. I had no idea what this course was about, but I ended up enjoying it despite the numerous word problems & math projects. However, she did teach me to understand the importance of the calculations. She accepted homework until her office hours were over & she always sent us reviews for our exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: You will never see the professor. How you do in the class depends not the TA that you get. Most of the TA's are good, but you cant garuntee that you'll get a good one. You may receive one email from the actual professor. There are several exams.

Amazing teacher and easy class as long as you are willing to put in the work to learn the material. The help room is GREAT and so are the TA's who work in it. As long as you do all of the homework and show up to class you will definitely pass.

Ingrid is an excellent professor. She cares about her students and their success and you will really stand out to her if you answer questions and participate (she will go easier on grading if she sees you making an effort). I took the data driven class and it was a very easy A.

I have never seen Ingrid in my entire life, and I took this class twice. You have a TA, so pray that they are organized. I'm not saying that my first TA was the reason I withdrew the first time, but it was definitely a contributing factor. Basically, if you don't want to stress out like I did the first time, print the notes and do the work.
This class sucks. Hope you get a TA because theres nothing better than unreliable students teaching classes!!! Avoid at all costs or prepare to suck up to your TA
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: TA's teach the class (Garrett Hages is the best TA just fyi) but there is a math help room that is available every day of the work week. Tests are not super hard, homework is easy bc of the help room. Easy A!
You don't actually have Ingrid as a teacher its a TA. So you better wish that you get a good TA because when you do you're golden.

I took Math 101 because it is required for graduation, as do most students in that class. Your grade completely depends on your TA and how much time you are willing to spend going to get extra help. I've never even seen Ingrid, I don't know what she does because she certainly doesn't tech the classes or even grade the tests/assignments.

You'll most likely get a TA for the class, and that determines how well you do. There are a lot of resources available, there is a 40-point curve in the class, and you can retake tests. I consider myself to be pretty weak at math but will be receiving a "B" in the class.
Totally luck of the draw depending on which TA you get. Mine is awesome so I have gotten a good grade in the class.

This class is pretty easy, as long as you show up to class and participate. My TA was named Jake and he was really helpful. I liked the helproom because someone would help me with the entire assignment, so I never missed a point with HW.

this class will bring your GPA down A LOT! It is always taught by a TA and usually the TA does not know how to teach or answer questions with clarity. Whenever you have a question the TA will tell you to go to the help room full of other TA's that don't know what they are doing. try to find another student that passed and ask for help. Good luck.

Do not take this course online. As a very experienced online math student, I was endlessly frustrated. You may only access textbook or assignments while online (a pain w/o home Internet) unless you pay extra for text. Access to ext. course site was DISABLED the night before the final, despite posted late hw deadline. Bad software, bad setup, bad idea. Go thru JCCC.

This class was incredibly hard. The TA's that taught it were unhelpful. My TA was an English major... Ingrid obviously doesn't seem to realize that her students have classes other than math, and in order to get a passing grade an immense amount of time and effort is required. This is the class for the people who suck at math, so why is it so hard?

It's taught by all TA's that can be helpful or suck...a lot. Hard course, put in the time and a LOT OF EFFORT and you'll get a B. Things to know there are 4 tests, a quiz every thursday and HW counts for a lot. Also you can retake 2 of your lowest scores. Maintain a 9 or 10 on quizzes and a 75 or higher on tests and GO TO CLASS, you'll get a B.

Ingrid Peterson doesn't teach the class, but it is actually taught by TAs. Depending on your TA, it can be difficult. Mine, thankfully, was a great teacher, so it wasn't too difficult. I recommend using MyMathLab Study Plan. It helps a lot in preparation for the tests. Also, use the drop-in for extra assistance.

You will most likely not get Peterson as your professor so don't base your schedule off that- you will most likely get a TA who is only a year older than you. USE THE HELP ROOM. There is never anyone in there and tutors just waiting to help people. The homework is fairly simple if you pay attention. Attend class. Attendance is usually required.

Yeah its a hard class but if you work hard its quite easy to get an A. There was a help room and offered lots of tutoring and my TA was amazing. I will be honest, if you get a crappy TA you're kind of screwed. But for the most part, Ingrid does a lot to support students

Her program sucks. You go through material way too fast, it is impossible to learn and keep up unless you are already really good at math. Skills tests are annoying and pointless. Ingrid comes across as rude and doesn't seem to care that so many kids struggle in her program. Avoid algebra at KU like it's the plague. Take it at a community college

MATH 101 is the #1 REASON why Freshmen drop out of KU! KAP sets you up for failure! I took it last semester and dropped it after the 2nd exam.  So currently I'm taking this class for the 2nd time and am failing. (Even after hiring a private tutor & attending a study group). Hopefully I won't have to take MATH 101 for the 3rd time this summer! :'(

IF YOU DO NOT END UP WITH A BRILLIANT T.A. expect to take this program over and over and over again. Ingrid doesn't even exist its just a bunch of students attempting to teach you mathematics that happen to be some of the hardest material to comprehend in your life. KU majorly fails TERRIBLY with their math program. IMPOSSIBLE. my gpa is 3.5 aswell
I didn't actually have Ingrid as a professor, but I went in for help with her weekly. She was extremely helpful and sweet, I have no idea what these bad reviews are doing on here!

TAKE FOR PASS FAIL! I struggled to get a C. I have never been good at math and the KAP progam is terrible. It didnt help me improve and made my confidence in math lower. Math help room is not helpful and the people woking in there make you feel dumb for asking for help.

Dr. Peterson was simply amazing. I was in a textbook pilot class (we were chosen to try a new textbook) and she was our personal teacher. She approached hard concepts with a soothing style and made it very easy. You have homework everynight but it really prepares you for the tests. Overall, one of the best teachers I've had in school.

I dont know what everyone else is talking about in these reviews... this class does not have an easy workload but if you put in some time and effort you can get an A easily.  There are resources everywhere someone who doesnt do well is simple just not working at it...

Her system is just terrible. You have to go in take skills tests and its just a pain. The TA hands in the homework to get graded by someone else and they take off points for no reason, just a terrible grading system. It really matters what TA you get, because some are just horrible!

Lousy program....... TA could barely answer questions.  I went to Peterson to see what I could do to improve grade and she was very annoyed that I had come to visit her.  Help room is also a total joke after asking a question in the help room to a TA the answer I received was "look in the book".  Lousy.....

Awful teacher, sets this whole thing up wrong. she relies more on the HW & projects than tests. this is college you should not have nightly HW. the idea of retakes and Help room seem good on paper but the way she sets them up is all wrong. SHE SETS THIS CLASS UP FOR YOU TO FAIL!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

This teacher just comes off as not freindly. Her system is just useless. Rather than using Ku's Blackboard, she has to use her own system. We have to go in to take online "skills" test to a computer on campus, when the practice tests are availible online and are word for word the same. Also uses TA's which are not helpful and can not answer your q

Dr. Peterson only teaches a select few of her class of 2400 students, so the TA you get is important.  If you show up, do your homework in the Help Room, and watch the online tutorials, this class is a breeze.  There are endless resources to get help from and no excuse for not making the grade you wanted.

First TA for my math 002 class did not speak english. He was fired even though Ingrid promised he was qualified. Ingrid walks in the room and makes everyone feel RETARDED. I feel like I can't go to her with any problems. It is also dumb that all tests have to be taken outside of class and they assign so much homework but only grade 10 of the proble
Crappy math program. DO NOT TAKE IT FROM KU!!!!

if you have to take 002 or 101 DO NOT TAKE IT FROM KU. ingrid is judgemental and totally not helpful. any positive ratings about her were probably writen by her puppet TAs or by Ingrid herself. if you value a good grade TAKE IT AT JCCC.  Ingrid is actually PROUD of how many ppl fail her poorly organized program
No Comments
Absolutly Horrible...enough said

though ingrid doesnt really teach all of the math sections from 101, 0r 002 for that matter,the program pretty much sets you up to fial. before you could retake every test which sounded great but now you can retake only two. all in all if you can avoid it do. take it at juco!
Worst math program ever!

She sucks.  Don't expect any help from her.  She is too good to help a student.  I would take a Calculus class or something, just make sure you don't have to deal with her.  The university won't let her teach anything above 101.  Hmm, I wonder why...
in charge of all TAs so not much contact

I have been very unimpressed with the KAP program to say the least. Skills tests are completely pointless and a huge waste of time. We go over things too fast in class and have tests way too often. Slow things down and make sure people are learning and comprehending. Stop rushing everything.
