The KAP program is the worst in the entire university. math 002 and 101 are the most failed classes at KU for a reason. the TAs are absolutely useless and don't care one way or other about you and your grade. the skills test are a complete waste of time and you have to take the exams on your own time. Ingrid doesn't care about you either

Kap sux, not only do they slap you with a TA that doesnt speak english but all the extra crap you have to do is so pointless. skills tests suck. help room is okay, you have to be incredibly specific to the tutors b/c they just want to help you as fast as possible and move on.
She is no help and the class is not set up well
Probably one of the best teachers I have ever had. Extremely helpful! I'm so thankful that I had her...I wish she taught all my math classes!!

Both times I had legitimate issues that I needed to solve they were ignored. The skills tests are a waste of time and I do not understand why we take them. There is too much crap to do outside of class. Skills tests, projects, homework, tests, plus class time. This will take up all your time. The help room is awesome.

I loved this teacher...If you go up after class or during her office hours she is willing to help you with any questions. We went over homework in class so if there was anything you don't understand you can work on it and turn it in later! i think it was definitely good having her as a teacher rather than a T.A.
No Comments
I like my T.A., Miss Katie Sanders.. but Peterson is no help & seems to pawn everything off to everyone else.
She helped, but it seemed like she really did't want to. But she did intermittently drop in to make sure her TA's were not teaching, just like their supposed to.

Not helpful, bad class go-to JCCC. Don't call people idiots for not taking this in HS.Placement is also based off of ACT scores. This math isn't offered to 8th graders. Try Jrs. Bad class, go to JCCC where it's $60/hr. instead of $138.75/hour.  At least there it's cheaper and you get a prof.
Well, personally the math program at KU sucks. Kind of funny that we pay so much money to go to a great university and we have a student 1 year older than me teaching the class. Hmm...

Ingrid Peterson was always very helpful when I needed assistance.  Concerning the pre-test,when I took the course a few years back the there was no line if you did not wait until the last 1-2 days before the regular exam.  Try taking it in the morning (8:00-10:00) or late afternoon (4:00-5:00).

I have seen this woman TWICE the entire semester! The program is horrible! Everyone says not to take math at KU, I didn't listen.  DON'T TAKE MATH AT KU! Go-to Johnson County! It's cheaper and apparently BETTER! You have to take a pre-test for everytest- wait time is about a 30-40 min.

I was lucky enough to get Ingrid instead of her TAs which I hear nothing but bad about. But she is really nice and makes sure that everyone understands the material before moving on. Best math teacher I've had thus far.

In response to the previous post, the reason that TAs teach Math 002 and 101 is the high demand for the courses.  Math needs to be taught in small classes. Most universities do not have the funding to hire full time professors to teach all sections.

This teacher does not have even the respect to teach her own classes, she instead has students teach it for her at ungodly hours of the morning. I am frustrated with her personally because she has a Junior teaching my class, and this girl knows nothing.
No Comments
No Comments
a very nice lady who will help you if you are willing to work
No Comments
He is good even if some theories are hard, sometimes i could fall asleep, i still like his lectures.
He is very kind, always ready for replying to your questions, although some theories he's introduced during the classes are very hard, i still enjoy studying and taking his class next semester again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I think the theories he introduced  during the classes are not so difficult to figure out, at least he would  like to use examples to help students to find regulations. That is great!

Gould could honestly be a good teacher if he would be more engaging as opposed to putting all of us to sleep. The discussions rarely go over what will be on the next homework which harms your grade as homework is a very large part of it.

Isidro has been my favorite Spanish professor yet. At first he may seem intimidating, but he's funny and his classes are very interesting. For the first time, I found myself wishing it was longer than 50 mins. Show up, pay attention, and talk. Not a hard class at all. Not boring. I hope to take a class with Isidro again!
Classes were very interesting. You can't be afraid to speak up and engage. No tests, just show up and participate. I enjoyed Isidro a lot and will take his classes again.

His online tests were riddled with errors. Grading of essays was subjective and didn't appear to be based on demonstrated skills and knowledge by the student. When asked for guidance (before turning in paper, and follow-up after it had been graded) was very unhelpful. Would leave cryptic notes like "awkward" with no explanation.

I enjoyed Profe Rivera's class. I took 2 courses with him. He lectures the entire class and most students are just on their laptops and listening while he's talking. He tries to be funny at times and is extremely knowledgable about what he talks about so he's honestly very interesting to listen to. If you pay attention and show up to class it good.

I hate this professor. Do not take him. Half of the class we read a book by a Spanish author, it was boring, and he made us focus on a culture that wasnt Hispanic. He is obsessed with white people from Spain. Im a native speaker, and was still graded harshly. I got an A because yes but hes an awful professor, do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Rivera is a good prof and actually cares for his students and he clearly knows what he is talking about in terms of content. A whole semester talking about print culture was a little rough and boring and made for a long hour and 15 class. He is a pretty easy grader if you try and most everything is essay/project based.

Overall Professor Rivera is a good professor and cares for his students and clearly knows what he is talking about. However, print culture in the early modern period was the worst topic to spend a whole semester talking about. He's an easy grader as long as you try and most everything is essay/project based when it comes to grades

He's honestly a nice guy, but the worst, most difficult grader. I literally speak Spanish at home and still got C's on the papers. Everything in the class is fine until he gets to grading papers and it all goes downhill. He's so harsh and for what. Also yelled at my friend for asking if a paper was our final. The books he makes you read are SUCK
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I think he deserves a higher rating than he has. I was very attentive and I participated a lot in class and he gave me a lot of grace on assignments. If you're trying then he will like you.

Prof. Rivera is a closed minded professor. He does not give all of his students the same respect/ opportunities and he doesn't provide good feedback on his assignments. If you go to his office hours you will hear a lot about all of the books that he has edited, but not a lot about help on assignments. Also, his handwriting is totally unreadable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I've enjoyed pretty much all of my professors at the University of Kansas, but definitely not Professor Rivera. I went to his office hours to ask for help on some grammar problems and asked for things I could do better. He told me there really wasn't anything I could do, but struggle and hope for a C. Least helpful professor I have ever had.

I have taken many classes with Isidro. I understand the negative comments, I thought about dropping my Spanish Major, and his class at one point. Throughout the semester I went into his office hours before & after every paper & it helped my grade and my knowledge. He is now my mentor for my graduate studies. Really great guy, you just have to try!

This class is a great example of the actual difficulty of the later Spanish major courses.  I highly recommend this class to people considering the Spanish major.  If you think this class is too hard and you can't pass it - don't major in Spanish because you're not going to do any better with any other professor.  I loved the class and the subject.

Avoid taking Professor Rivera if at all possible!!! He is by far the WORST teacher I have ever had. His expectations of students are completely ridiculous and he is extremely demeaning and rude. He has made me hate being a Spanish major!

If you want a good grade in this class, you're going to have to work your tail off.  His grading is harsh, though this is a literature class - he takes off unbelievable amounts for grammar errors.  Overall, just unneedingly high expectations and not very good instruction.  Don't expect to sail through this class.  Get someone else.

Isidro Rivera does not give grades on merit, he grades on if your are an attractive girl or not. You do not use a textbook you use documents by him or other people at KU. I am honestly astonished that he has a good comment at all, that person must of been one of his select favorites. Only a matter of time before he gets in trouble for harassment

Although the material isn't difficult, he has made this the hardest class I have ever taken. He is an extremely hard grader, unless you are lucky enough to be his favorite. Please avoid this class. I don't want anyone else to have to go through what me and my classmates have gone through. Please do whatever you can to get a different teacher.
Great teacher, so it surprises me to see so many bad comments. I went to his office frequently and he helped me out with everything - you just have to ask.
DO NOT take this class. incredibly rude, makes his students feel inadequate, and an incredibly hard grader. i will NEVER take another class from him. stay away!!!!!

By far the worst teacher I have ever had. His criteria for grading is absolutely ridicolous; he expects way too much out of native English speakers. I would avoid taking him at all possible costs. Never again wilI I ever take a class with him. He makes me not want to be a Spanish major anymore.

Where do I begin with Isidro? My classmates and I are completely dumbfounded that this guy still has a job. He's rude, makes students cry when they come to talk to him, and is COMPLETELY impossible when grading essays. Good luck if you take one of his sections...you'll need it.
RUN. Do not take this class. If you are not his favorite, you will not pass or receive your desired grade. He will even go to other teachers in the Spanish department and bad mouth you.

As people have said, all of his writing assignments are graded very subjectively. He definitely plays favorites, and if he doesn't like you he will grade your assignments harder. The course content was interesting enough, but he makes it seem more difficult by speaking in needlessly abstract terms. If you're a suck-up, go for it. If not, avoid.
He's very helpful and not nearly as difficult as people seem to think. He actually teaches instead of just asking questions. I learned a great deal from him and enjoyed the class very much.

Subjective, subjective, subjective. Better hope this guy likes you. Not a good teacher. Very arrogant, even though his area of study is needlessly esoteric (Medieval Spanish Literature? Really?). His insights are useless at best and his "help" he gives during office hours is always condescending and frequently uselessly brutal.

I am surprised by two thing: 1.) That this teacher doesn't have a frowny face by his name and 2.) That he is still employed by the University. The people who have given him positive ratings are incorrect. He is not helpful even if you do your work and going in to see him will not get you a better grade unless he likes you. DONT TAKE HIS CLASS!

This is without a doubt the worst teacher I have ever had. He frequently talks in vague generalities and then expects students to deduce specific insight. He does not make his expectations clear and grades terrifyingly subjectively. For those seeking to understand their evaluation and truly learn Spanish, beware.
Do NOT take this professor. The class difficulty would not be hard if he didn't make it that way. Very subjective grading, and in class he plays favorites. I hated every minute of this class.

Unquestionably the worst professor I have ever encountered. The grading is incredibly subjective, and he plays favorites. Show up at his office hours all the time and BE one of those lucky few. The class itself is not difficult, but the teacher is impossible. Stay away at all costs! I will NEVER take another class from him EVER.

The grading on your compositions are pretty brutal. You learn a lot, but it is easy get on his bad side, especially if you miss a class or come in late. He is a very good speaker and often funny and entertaining. Be prepared to work hard in his class.

He is very difficult. His classes usually go by quickly, though, because he is a good speaker. His office hours are VERY helpful. Get to know him. I am still in the class, and it is very tough, but challenging in a good way.
Go to his office hours! He'll help you!

i have never learned so much in a class. If you apply yourself you will get so much out of his class. He is extremely helpful and is more than willing to help you during office hours. I was probably in his office every other day to get help on papers.

LOTS of work. And he doesn't always agree with the professor for your section so make sure you know who is grading! I've been given the chance to take another class from him, and I'm not if I can avoid it.
No Comments
He is one of the best teachers I've had so far. He is very good at what he does! It was a pleasure to have him as a teacher.
great
very interesting class:)

Professor Six is incredible. She's devoted to her students and wants to help you succeed. I had both a month-long battle with an illness and a family crisis one semester, and she was so kind and understanding, allowing me to submit assignments well after they were supposed to be due. She's so knowledgeable and entertaining. I highly recommend her.

Irina is a wonderful, interesting, and knowledgeable teacher. You can tell she really cares about each of her students and the material she is teaching. She is very flexible and open to student input for which artists/musicians to study. Overall a fantastic teacher and individual. I wish I had her for another class!
Dr. Six is a really sweet woman and a great teacher.
Irina is amazing. Very knowledgeable, enthusiastic, helpful.
This is a very difficult class but she will do everything she can to make sure you learn everything. She really cares if you learn the material.

Irina is very sweet. You read a few books, and she posts all the discussion questions prior to the discussion day. The papers are easy. She gives you all the powerpoints. Come up with weird ways to remember the art section of the test. I had the book but only read on things I needed more info on for the tests. Take it to get the history credit!
Great professor, tests are easy if you prepare, as she gives you the exact questions beforehand. The films and selected literature are interesting. Great option for a history credit.
entertaining and helpful.
She is an excellent teacher if you get help outside of class. She really tries to help you understand with this really difficult class.
she does not come to class prepared and blames the class when discussion is not moving along

WOW. i was completely blown away by the work load when i entered this class! its a 100 level course and its out of control! 2 page paper due every class and she picks them up randomly, so i spend two and a half hours completing one only to have it not graded! TALK in this class, otherwise you'll be bored as crap! but she has a good sense of humor
This will be your biggest regret if you take this class with this teacher. The workload is unreasonable. She's on a power trip. It's harder than 300 level courses i've taken.

DO NOT TAKE this class with her. This is a 100 level class and most all people take it as an easy A. She is absolutely nuts. You have to have a 2 page research paper due at the beginning of each class and it's not just complete/incomplete.. she grades it.. not to mention she may or may not collect it, it's all random.
I loved Iris. She is so approachable and so sweet. I went to her office hours many times and she explained things so well. She is hands down the best spanish professor I have had at KU so far.

She is one of my favorite teachers so far. I don't think she was that tough when she graded my papers. She really cares that you learn and wants to help you if you need help. She is very nice and approachable as well. Just make sure you participate in class.

She is such a caring and nice lady. She really wants you to succeed. The class has homework pretty much every day, but it isn't too hard and it's all online. No tests or quizzes. Great class to take if you are willing to put some effort in.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: I think she's a great teacher, interactive with you and takes offense if you drop her class because she cares.

Best teacher I have had so far. She really cares about everyone succeeding so she will definitely help anyone needing help. She makes sure you understand everything. She is so caring and nice! I wish she taught the other levels I would take her class again.

I am horrible at spanish and was very worried because she is the spanish coordinator. The class is not hard as long as you put in effort and try. She knows not everyone is comfortable speaking spanish and may not know exactly what to say. She is willing to talk to students and is very warm and engaging. Participation in this class is key.

Depending on how well you know Spanish will determine whether you will do well in this class. If you know a little Spanish then some things will be difficult. Just participate in class a lot. She can be hard to understand sometimes and she isn't very helpful if someone doesn't know what they are trying to say.
You would lose your job in a law firm if you do your work like Prof. Russel teaches her class: disorganized, confusing, redundant, scattering, and beating around the bush when answering questions.
Prof. Russell is nice and courteous. But her class is mumble-jumbling.

Likes responding to questions with a question.  Provides no clarity on the subject matter.  Very nice and tries to help, but her teaching style would be better suited to a class on philosophy than contract law.
Extremely fair and helpful. Much better than my Contracts I "professor". Apparently, if you aren't a pompous burnout, my classmates will gripe about you.

She has been very helpful and quick to respond to any questions that I ask her.  Her office door is always open and she's a very friendly lady.  The only thing I didn't like about the class was her participation policy, your grade is 25% participation which is different than other law school classes.

Professor Russell is a nice person but her circuitous speaking style and inability to communicate complete thoughts make it impossible to learn from her.  I had to rely on a horn book and lots of prep time outside of class to get through the U.C.C.  You will not learn anything in this class-- it is amazingly bad.

Iris has an incredibly intelligent mind. Yes, she is strict. Yes, she is a tough grader but this is college and her coursework reflects that. She's helpful and insightful. If you actually want to learn something, take a course with Iris.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Though she is a tough grader and speaks in a 'dry' manner, she is a great professor. If you want to learn and are ready to put in the effort you will enjoy her class. Don't expect an energetic lecture, but know that she is passionate and her passion is expressed in reserved but intelligent ways.
She is extremely unfair when it comes to grading and if you don't think like she does, you're wrong. I recommend staying far away from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a very nice teacher but as the following reviews state, she is a very tough grader and expects you to make very complicated connections within the readings. You definitely have to ask questions before you submit your papers to her. Be careful with your interpretations, she grades based on her own perspective.

I didn't like the class at all. She didn't like to hear different interpretations of the text than what she wanted and her assignments were pretty vague. Difficult to stay awake with her voice and style of lecturing. Definitely would not recommend.

She is incredibly dry and boring to listen to. Her voice screams "naptime" alert. She has a very clear idea of what she believes to be "right" or "wrong" interpretations of the texts and is not welcoming to other opinions. She creates a class environment that discourages discussion rather than promotes it. She isn't especially nice either. Avoid.

Iris was not respectable towards her students. She belittled them and was unclear of assignments. With papers it's her way or the highway and you don't know until after the fact. You never know what short answer questions over readings she will give out. Do NOT eat/drink/go to the bathroom or she will call you out. Good luck!

Took this class for req. FML I didn't check RMP before I enrolled with her. I hated every day I had to go to this class. She goes on and on asking for input until she gets the EXACT answer she wants. Grades hard, etc...

Prof. Fischer is very smart and knows her stuff. However, she is vague when she assigns things and grades really harshly when it comes to papers. Read the readings, go to class, prep for the essay tests and do everything in your power to write a good paper, or you won't get a good grade.

I love English, it is my major and why I transferred to this university. If you're looking for a teacher who values your creativity and style as a writer this is not the professor for you. She wants your writing kept a certain way. HER way. And she won't provide you with any examples on how to achieve an A on anything.

Professor Fischer is rude and unhelpful. Beware if you have any struggles with writing, she acts put out if you ask for help. We were also told we could not use the bathroom during class time!?  If you have to take English 308 DO NOT take it with her.  Wait until someone else teaches it, or you will regret it.

Moody and difficult to please, she ruined the subject for me. Even though she knows a lot about what she is talking about, she is full of herself, not responsive to new ideas and creativity, and not pleasant to have discussions with. She talks down to her students. Plus side, interesting reading and class concept.
Quizzes are given over readings, so keep up. She is a fairly tough grader when it comes to papers. Overall, she is interesting to listen to and knows a lot about theatre.

Possibly the worst professor I ever had. She is extremely boring, full of herself and rude to students. She ruined a subject I found thoroughly interesting. Mandatory attendance, she treats you like children. She also has no ability to deal with creative, intelligent students. Her class is a painful waste of time, particularly for honors students.
This teacher is ridiculous.  She has a very high attendance and participation policy.  Which she can't keep up with.  She likes to take points off for any and everything.  Good Luck!

Prof. Fischer is a nice lady with good intentions, but sometimes her lectures are dry.  If you're not an English major, you might be struggling to make yourself care about the lectures.  Overall an ok class.

This was a horrible class. She has a ridiculous participation policy, which she does not document, but attempts to grade people down for. She claims to have recorded attendance after class, but it could not have been accurate since she did not know my name until after Spring Break. She plays favorites and values quantity over quality/intelligence.
She did an awesome job of getting the class into discussions about the plays.  She has a great command of her subject and loves it!  Great class!
She is a great teacher with an excellent attitude, strong command of her subject and an awesome writer herself.
Prof. Fischer is a very sweet lady.  She knows hr stuff and really loves talking about weird theater.

She is literally the worst French teacher I have ever had. Don't take her class. Even if it's the only time you can take. She doesn't know how to teach properly and acts like we are supposed to already know what she is trying to tell us. She doesn't give back quizzes unless you keep asking her and she won't even explain more about the topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Madame Cauley doesn't teach at all. It is very obvious she does not care about what she is teaching. No one in my class is doing well because we have not learned a single thing. She does not teach. She cancels class all the time for no reason. I wasted money this semester with her being my teacher. Im taking my French class again with someone else.

Prof. Cauley gives good comments back on writting assignments but she doesn't clearly explain some of the fundeamentals of French. She expects you to learn by reading the textbook, which isn't the best way to learn a language. While I found this class was easy, I do not feel that it helped me learn the french language.

Prof Cauley is a very straightforward and sometimes tough. It made me learn more and participate. She is extremely good about explaining fuzzy sides of French.  She is also one of the hottest and smartest professors whose class I have ever attended. She has a genius respect for students' opinions but try not to bs her.

She's a pretty good professor, but she gets noticeably irritated if you make lots of rookie mistakes, especially with pronunciation, which is understandable. The work load is pretty light. Those online homework assignments take like 15 minutes.

She was nice for the most part, but was always pretty vague about assignments and requirements for projects. She was never exactly clear on some things either, sometimes she would just skim over important topics. Wasn't too difficult of a class, but not an 'easy' A.

Absolutely fantastic teacher! She makes the material relevant and fun to learn about. Anyone is extremely lucky to have her as a teacher. She has a hard grading system but she sets you up to succeed, so just try.

Try to get an early start with the essays. If you bring a draft to a meeting, she is really helpful. She is quite positive and seems to be having fun. I feel like she grades the essays well but it is really tough to get an A on most of the essays.
very helpful and friendly
Knows what she is teaching. very helpful and prepared with her lectures.
Very clear in her teaching, grades kind of hard but if you take notes on all of her examples and attend class regularly you will be fine.
Whoah.

Worst professorclass I've had at KU yet. He rambles for the entire class period without asking for student discussion of texts. Reading assignments are demanding and you get almost no deeper interpretation of literature. He's a cool guy, extremely knowledgeable, and I'd love to hang out and chat with him some time, but he's a terrible teacher.

I took this class when the topic was Kerouac and Ginsberg, and I was really excited about the class going into it. What could have been a really cool class was made unbearable by the professor. He is a really interesting guy, but he's the sort of person that I'd want to grab a drink with, not be taught by. He rambles endlessly.

Irby is incredibly intelligent and thought provoking if you pay attention. He rambles, yes, but if you're truly interested in poetry you'll notice him talking is an art of sorts. Yes he rambles and connects thoughts to biographical facts or personal stories, he is a different kind of professor and an admirable respectable human being. Loved him.

Clearly a genius, but a terrible teacher. He's very nice and an easy grader for essays, but his quizzes are ridiculous. More about about biographical-historical information and hardly about the literature. The lectures are torture and he doesn't discuss anything that's relevant to the literature. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
Brutal. Not much work but lectures are unbearable. Crazy Quiz everyday. Avoid at all costs
You learn more about the poets than anything else, he's pretty easy going but EXTREMELY boring.

Most BORING lecturer ever, Also don't be surprised when this "literature" class is more of a history class with more importance given to dates and people than literature themes.There is a quiz most every class but they only amount to 10% total grade so don't worry if you bomb. Easy class, but don't expect to be engaged in the material.

This professor is clearly a very smart man; however, his lectures are awful.  They are irrelevant, and just plain boring.  Don't get me wrong-- he is a very nice man, and very helpful as well. He understands that some people in his class are there because a 200+ level course is required. His quizzes are very difficult as well.

*The* most boring lecturer on the planet, and there was absolutely no engagement from the class. We were assigned a substantial amount of reading, and I barely did any of it. Two papers and a final. Passed with flying colors. Take this guy for a SUPER easy class.

Irby's class is worse than torture, but this man knows his stuff, seriously. He's like a machine that gathers information and never loses it, and during his class he spews it at everyone. A woman filled in for him one day and told us that there are people that write their dissertations on his poetry. I read >half of what was assigned, got an A.

I honestly tried to give the man an chance, but he failed, miserably. He's a genius, of that I am sure, but he cannot teach. I learned nothing in his class, and neither did everyone who sat in the front row with their crosswords and sketchbooks. All Irby does is mumble and talk of his drug use. He favors students who he can relate with.

I'm sure he's a great teacher for undergrads-- he really doesn't care what you do, he will not ask you a single question or get you to engage with the material at all, he doesn't talk about relevant material at all, no one speaks but him and it's a really easy class. For a graduate students these are all of the reasons that this was an awful class.

Easy, easy class.  Attendance not mandatory.  Read the material, ask yourself tons of questions and boom, you have an A.  Two papers (your choice of topics), one takehome midterm, and a final.  He also tells awesome stories.

Prof. Irby is awesome. He is incredibly knowledgeable, genuinely loves poetry and poets, and very interesting to listen to. He tells great, funny tangential stories about his life and other poets he has known. Treats students like mature adults. Take any of his classes if you get a chance!

Prof. Irby really knows his stuff and cares about it. He brings a wealth of personal experience to the classroom. Pay attention, read the texts, take the daily quizzes-they're not hard if you pay attention to the bio info that precedes the texts. Good stuff.

Do you want to get an A for writing two papers and taking a midterm and a final without actually going to class? Then Irby is for you! I quit going once I realized that he just kind of rambles and you won't be tested on anything in lecture. Just read the texts and write the papers, it's all fairly simple. Just depends on what you want.
Wonderful person with so much to life to share.  you will learn so much about life and yourself in his courses.

Great teacher, made Shakespeare very accessible. Lots of quizzes so you have to do the reading. Papers can be hard because you have to choose your own topic, but I really liked this class. Great story teller.
good nice guy

He is all about poetry, so his survey classes become almost completely poetry. He is an incredibly nice and caring man, and is very willing to help his students. Unfortunately his lectures seem to largely tend towards biography of poets, and his quizzes obsess over minute details of introductions to the text. Take creative writing classes from him.

Teaches Modern American Poetry- should have been called Minor Biographical Details of Ezra Pound or Irby's Drug Reminscences. Well-known poet- awful teacher. No class discussion. Fond of playing endless recordings- once spent 3 1.5 hour sessions sitting and doing nothing but listening to recording about Duncan. Avoid.
this man knew everyone that mattered in poetry
Ken Irby is a national treasure amongst a fading ilk of men. Take any of his classes while you have the chance!

The grading in a poetry class can be pretty subjective, and he didn't seem to give out anything but "A"s the semester I took it, even though I thought some of the students were writing low-level stuff, but the in-class feedback and his teaching style really did encourage me to write, revise, and read poetry. I like this guy!
Crazy guy.  Difficult to understand what is expected, therefore difficult to achieve decent grade.  Entertaining, but not helpful.

Best Spanish teacher I have had at KU so far. She is kind, patient, understanding, and beyond helpful. She truly wants her students to improve, and if you put in the effort, she will help you succeed. I highly recommend her class and having her as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She is the most down-to-earth teacher I have had. Incredibly helpful, super energetic, always brings out the best of the students in our class. In a class such as Spanish, participation is key, and she makes students excited to participate and interact with works of Spanish literature. TAKE HER CLASS
She was great!! Made me want to major in Spanish- she is extremely helpful and is willing to help you with assignments if you're struggling and proof-reads essays.

One of the best spanish professors I've had.  Really animated in all of her lectures and would definitely recommend students take her for Spanish 216217.  Learned so much from her and when I did not understand a concept she's always willing to help.  Great teacher.

This was a four week class with tons of reading. THIS IS NOT AN ART HISTORY COURSE. It is an anthropology course through and through. You get three days (including the weekend) to read literally hundreds of pages on the ANTHROPOLOGY of Prehistoric art. It is difficult to stay interested in this class with no professor present.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I had to take her for three classes. All were awful. There are several, overly long readings, lectures really do not prepare you for quizzes - she even said herself that you can't rely on her lectures for studying for quizzes, and her grading is weirdly harsh considering we have no idea what to actually study and focus on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I This class was NOT an art history class but rather a sociology class/anthropology. I would have never taken this if I knew it was going to be this much reading every single week for homework. The final paper is 12 pages long and the first week of class before you have even learned anything on the topic of prehistory, you chose a final paper topic
I took 3 courses with her because I loved her so much. Each class was well-thought out, and informative. She is a wonderful and passionate person who wants to see her students succeed.

Do you love reading scholarly articles about a dead culture that is boring as hell? Well, this is the class/teacher for you. Don't speak your mind, because if you start bad mouthing prehistoric art, she'll grade you accordingly. Doesn't seem to respect the opinions of others- even when you do all the readings. Oh and by the way, there are a ton!!!!

A lot of reading and the tests are super hard but she's fair and does give partial credit a lot of the time and will give you help when you ask for it. She's really smart and funny, just take her class seriously because its no easy A.
Ivana is very knowledgeable and helpful.  She expects students to complete assigned readings; if you do the class is easy!

The test study guides are ridiculous. Way to much information to actually learn, then the tests have 3 questions over the copious amount of info you tried to memorize. The class is interesting and she was funny, but I would not recommend taking the class unless you really enjoy the subject.

Ivana is kind of crazy...but definitely in a good way. She makes class fun and is pretty funny even when she doesn't mean to be. She's really smart and obviously has a lot of experience. LOTS of reading.

Having just declared my anthropology major, I was excited about this class, and by far it is my favorite. Ivana is an amazing teacher, and if you do what she asks of you, pay attention, accept she has an accent and don't knock her for it, you are going to have a great time. I'd recommend her to anyone. You'll learn a lot by being in her company.

Her classes can be difficult- (Pre-history of europe) but she is very smart and very egar to share her knowledge!Be prepared to do the reading and  the studying( she does give study guides- and they are usually worse than the test themselves). she does require a paper,but it is done step by step. Just do what she ask and you will do fine.

She is funny & I have heard good things before registering for this course. It is still early in the semester but so far I am not impressed! Make note: the quizes are not open note, even if she tells you they are-I found that out the hard way. It is kind of hard to understand her with her strong accent & she does ramble A Lot! Overall, she's ok.

She is great.  Show up for class and read the material...and you will be fine.  Amazing archeologist, she isn't an "armchair academic".  She has lots of fieldwork experience.  Great source of information!

wow get over it some people in this world get accents. and as a personal friend of this professor i can say with confidence that she has read more books (in english, serbian, french) than you will read in your entire life times ten. so keep those essays coming, because i'm sure that someone with a doctoral degree can understand them.
I took this course over the summer and it was very easy. If you pay attention to the images from lecture you should be able to pass this class with no problems.
Was supposed to be lithic technology, but we really learned nothing. The syllabus meant nothing - the class didn't follow any structure at all. It was a waste of time.

Once you get past her accent, she is a relatively entertaining lecturer and makes a lot of jokes, some at her own expense. Her quizzes were  more than fair and she gives lots of EC. For our term papers, she let us choose a topic rather than assigning one. My only complaint is that  test study guides were huge, too much memorization of dates, etc.
Lectures are relatively painless, plenty of extra credit opportunities, interesting subject matter, very little homework/outside of class time required.
Very easy, a little hard to understand.

Dr. Rad is Rad!  She is smart, hilarious, and VERY easy on grading.  In this class (mortuary archaeology), if our work was on time, we got extra credit!!  She would say "last call for turning in papers..after the deadline, no extra points!" It took awhile to get around her accent, but its fun after awhile.  Went down to the wheel on the last day of class, too! Good times.
Cool class--wonderful presentations. prof. Ivana helped me to consider archaeology as a career. Thanks!

This subject could have been so cool. Instead, this teacher thought that Americans dont work hard enough and she doesn't entertain questions.  Plus, I could hardly understand her.  However, the class wasn't too hard and she doesn't give essays because she can't read English too well.

I thought Ivana was a wonderful teacher.  She has a great sense of humor and she's extremely passionate about her research and teaching others about prehistoric art.  Her quizzes were multiple choice, t/f, and some short answer.  Overall...great class.
It was difficult for me to know what information was necessary for the tests, and what information was extra.  her accent does not help either.

This Japanese guy is a condescending jerk, he spends first 15 minutes of every class criticizing this and that and this and that, and never show due respect to students. If you ask him a question right after the class, his most polite response is "Actually I have to go."
He is an expert on finance and economics. You want to learn the stuff, take his class.

Absolutely the worst English speaker I have ever encountered in college.  You'd think he would spend some of his big bucks for a English language tutor.  Stay away unless you want all math equations in the blackboard and choppy garbled sound blurbs to explain it.
He is great teacher but his accent is hard study well for the test listen carefully for every thing he may mention in the class and you will learn lot of interesting information and knowledge

If you want to challenge yourself, receive a world class education, and really learn something useful, take his class.. He knows what he talks about.. He's an expert! Otherwise, dont take any class with him...
The worst professor in my life! department should invest some money in english language classes for him
Straight A's in 4 years except for this one... Nightmare... Pain... Torture... Defeat... Nothing learned... I want to kill myself in his class... Avoid at all costs...
Sometimes as a student you seem helpless, when shigeru is your professor you feel helpless all the time.  Shigeru please go away.
Arrogant, Can't understand, seems to enjoy ridiculing students.  Avoid him if possible.
The new G.O.A.T of EECS. Prof. Gibbons eat your heart out

Schoonover is hands-down most experienced and engaging professor in EECS so far. Class is much more difficult than other EECS courses, especially as freshman. Lectures are super detailed. Quizzes every Thursday that are open note and open class, mostly to see that you understand. Discusses deep topics succinctly, and office hours are very useful.

This is for last semester, but he did an amazing job teaching 645 to us all. The structure was pretty similar to 388 outside of an extra exam (since there was no lab) but he did a good job teaching the content.

Great professor, clear class expectations and if you read the posted lecture slides you will succeed. Weekly quizzes on Fridays which you are required to be in person for, with assigned Homework every 3 weeks or so. Generous grader and gives partial credit for most questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Amazing guy! I love his exams. They really get you thinking and aren't the same as the homework. His exams are really well made. The content is tough, but he's a good teacher and cares a lot. He even recorded the lectures just for me because I was hospitalized for a month and made time for makeup quizzes for me.

Jacob is the sweetest pookie bear i love him with all my heart i hope for him the best fairytale life with endless love and happiness.. i have a deep desire to kiss him every lecture.. but alas i can only daydream. He is the Jesus to the devil who goes by prof. Saiedian. That dude can EAT ROCKS
Honestly the topic is a little hard, but genuinely caring professor you can tell he cares if you understand the material or not. I would take him again.
Class is difficulty because material is difficult, but he does a good job, and exams are open note. Labs are very TA dependent

Very supporting and caring professor. Your lab experience fully depends on the TA you get, so don't be afraid to change your TA if you don't like how they teach. Exams were open note and he always uploaded lecture slides to the canvas. Quizes and homeworks should be manageable as long as you know what you're doing. If not, go to his office hours.

Amazing individual. You will learn so much and nothing felt unfair. Labs were interesting, homework and quizzes were helpful, and exams were open note. He truly wants you to understand the topics, and is incredibly accessible. This is a no brainer choice if you need to take 388
Great professor for computer architecture! The material was a bit confusing but it he was able to teach it through. Exams are open note and has end of weekly quizzes! Totally recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Always saw him in labs explaining issues and helping. Some problems on the exams are complex, but he gives a practice test, practice homework, and allows notes. You can tell he cares and wants his students to understand and succeed. So much different than how EECS330 is.
When I worked at Garmin...

I took this class last semester but still felt it necessary to give a review. He is one of the best EECS teachers at ku, he provides lots of extra credit, in the midterm, final, all of the labs, and even some of the homework. he has a completely open note policy and has weekly quizzes that are simple 5 question on lecture.  Great teacher overall.
dudes nice and class is fine but the tests are extremely hard probably since its open note other than that everything else was fine, and he grades generously

JACOB IS THEEE MAN!!!
He is so nice and really cares about his students!

The lectures can get a little boring but I think that I am just not the biggest embedded systems fan and that is a me problem. 

If you have an option between lecturers take this guy!
Tests are open note.

Super kind professor who genuinely cares about his students. Willing to help outside of class if you need it and explains labs and other general confusion in lecture. Labs are a but confusing but my TA helped explain it. This class has weekly quizzes but they're short and help review. Quizzes & exams are open note. Cant wait to have him again!

Great professor! Very chill and you can tell he really cares about students understanding the content rather than giving us tons of work to do. Two exams and weekly quiz both open notes. Gives good applications of the content in the real world. Labs are tough but that really depends on your TA. Really recommend him!

Great Professor! It's his first year teaching at KU, and I enjoyed him immensely! The lectures were good, and you could tell he had a deep knowledge of what he was talking about. Eager to answer questions, especially if they're interesting ones! Very willing to help with career stuff and resume reviews outside of class.
I could have learned more from a toothbrush.

Another year of film, another year of censorship on projects. There was always something that his classes lacked for me. The best part of both FMS100 and FMS375 was the friends you could make in your film groups.

Regurgitates your ideas back to you, doesn't know the equipment he assigns, preaches religious beliefs. No grades until the last week and graded assignments he never gave us. I had to withdraw and file a Title IX case against him after he rudely dismissed my health.

His lectures lacked nuance. He hardly ever responds to emails, if he does, you'll most likely see "Get Outlook for Android." Each activity lacked depth. I HAD MORE ENGAGING WORK IN BEGINNER FMS 275! He also graded all my work on Thursday of finals week! This class felt like an improvised online community college course. he is a loathsome teacher.

I have never had a professor so condescending and incompetent. He treated us like children and set expectations for my 300 level class like we were middle schoolers and not grown adults. He would also send us out with equipment that he didn't know how to use and be surprised when we didn't know how to use it either. Would not recommend.

A lot of the negative reviews surprised me although I was in a entry-level film class he still seemed like a very normal, of course I can't speak on the higher classes in which he has more negative reviews but he does seem to care and means well. The class was easy as long as you did the work and show up. Overall an average teacher who means well.
Awful coursework distribution, almost fell asleep in his class multiple times.  Harsh grading, especially on late assignments.

Stone would often ignore me, patronize me, or plagiarize my ideas during critiques. He is one of the most disrespectful and condescending instructors I have ever had. Stone also makes students work on 2 films simultaneously. This is near impossible, given that most students have several other classes, and makes finals week feel like a nightmare.

Can this guy teach us anything new? I'm paying thousands of dollars just so he can pretend that he's introducing new concepts, when in reality, we all had to learn these skills to enroll in this class.

Stone is a solid Professor. I found his FMS 100 class to be very interesting. He lectures on relevant topics. His tests are fair and he gives great study guides. He sometimes took a long time to grade. The movies he chose were applicable to the assignment. He is easy to approach. Just be sure to sit in the front of the class he is very quiet.
accidentally clicked 2 instead of 1 .
good lord get this guy off the stage tomato tomato boooooo
Reread elements of my film's pitch to me as if they were his own new ideas.

Makes his personal beliefs/experiences unnecessarily clear. Lengthy lectures that cover information that you should have already learned in Basic Production. Assigns pointless extra work to accompany pitches. Extremely long list of prohibited subject matters, which essentially forces you to make a fantasy film.

She doesn't grade well AT ALL, she literally wrote in the rubric, no more than 350 words. And then proceeded to give me point off because I didn't have 350 words! So obviously she doesn't know what up to 350 words means!

Took Literature of Human Rights online, asynchronous. Class was weekly discussion boards, weekly assignment (page long writing thing, not too hard), and a final paper (plus its presentation). Enjoyable class, good selected content (movies, books, graphic novels, and articles). Grading is reasonable and not harsh. Good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Janzen is a great teacher! She makes class so much fun and is really respectful to her students. She is a teacher I would take a again in a heart beat!

Class discussions are good, I feel like a really got to know the material and its importance well. She gives quizzes almost every other day; they aren't hard, but you have to actually do the reading she assigns. Most texts are pretty good, but there were a few rough ones. Overall, I enjoyed the class. Kind of a tough grader.

Overall a very informative class. Janzen provided many different perspective about the concepts of peace and war through required readings. There were 10 in class quizzes and the tests included two short essays. Participation in discussion in important.

This class was pretty easy, and enjoyable at times. There is a lot of discussion and you get daily points for participation. The tests are extremely easy, and she isn't really a difficult grader on papers/essays.

Marike cultivates one of the best discussions of any professor that I have ever seen. However, if your beliefs do not sync up with her own, you may have trouble making the grade. Therefore, it is imperative to note what she likes and dislikes about each text, and note those items in your writing. Semi-hard grader, very nice person.

Marike is very encouraging in her classroom, and the discussion that she cultivates is rich and deep. However, if you do not give answers her way, or if you don't sync up with her beliefs, you will have a rough time in her class. Semi-tough grader.

Class was much different than I expected and alot of work. But Professor Janzen cares about her students and wants people to succeed. She works hard on powerpoints and is big on discussion. Doing the readings and coming to class is essential. Overall, it was a positive experience and I really enjoyed her as a professor.

Marike is overall a good teacher. She works hard on her presentations and is great at encouraging all students to participate. She is sort of a questionable grader, but is willing to listen to problems students have with her.  Overall, her class was a positive experience.
Every answer has to be her way or the highway. She's a pretty fun teacher, but only HER answers are the right ones.

Do not take this class if you don't specifically need it. I had to take it for my major and it made me reconsider my decision. Extremely tough grader for literally no reason. Doesn't give good instructions for assignments and then leaves comments on your assignment stating the things you did wrong.

Awful class and teacher. I hope he sees this and changes how he structures that class. Nothing about it was enjoyable, and it could've been such an interesting class, but it wasn't. Jacob, if you're reading this, chill out. It's an LDST 200 class, we aren't trying to figure out quantum physics. Such an awful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Wow. I expected this class to be enjoyable and interesting, but Jacob just takes that and ruins it with how he teaches and structures the class. Right off the bat, you're writing an essay and have 5+ things to turn in. Each week is worse than the other and I was constantly on my computer trying to finish all of the busy work he gives out. Dont take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I received an A in this course, but getting this grade brought me to the gates of hell. Stutzman is the most difficult teacher and LDST200 is the hardest course I've ever taken in my life. Get ready to spend 15+ hours a week on his assignments and have them graded insanely tough. Schedule office hours and get ready to grind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. If you wanna feel like you're in middle school again prepare to take this class. Teacher speaks in riddles and quizzes are impossible. Nothing is ever good enough and is hard to talk to. Also, who does minus and pluses since high school? He does. rate 0/10

A LOT of work for this class!! The weekly journals and quizzes are pointless, but easy points. And for finals week you have a large project, a final paper, and an exam--only given 6 days to do it all. His expectations are extremely high. If you need this class, prepare to spend all of your time completely the assignments, readings, and videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: There aren't kind words for this man. The amount of work required is ridiculous. The weekly journals were pointless. The weekly quizzes were OK. The weekly projects were complicated & the directions were difficult to understand. The ethics discussion was all about promoting hate. It seems his PHD went to his head & forgot how to be nice or human.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I didn't like him at first but if you actually listen to the feedback he gives, you will understand the things he's saying. You have to be willing to work for a good grade, hence why I got a B-. I just didn't really work. But the feedback he gave me seemed stupid at first but then really got me thinking.

This professor may be the worst teacher I have ever encountered in all of my schoolings. This is a required course and this man takes this class too seriously and makes it nearly impossible to get 100% on anything. Way harder than any major course I have at the moment. Seems to me that this professor needs to have some more happiness in his life

There is a tremendous amount of work for this class, none of which is easy. For example, for finals week we have a large project, a final paper, and an exam--only given 6 days to do it all. His expectations are extremely high, and it's impossible to earn full points on any assignment. DO NOT TAKE. This 200 level elective ruined my 4.0.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took this class as an easy elective to fulfill my credits. Safe to say it is 10000x more work and more stressful than any of my major courses. Zero explanations for anythingfeedback consists of questions rather than tips or reasoning behind the grade. Exams are unnecessarily difficult & worth A LOT of your grade. Weekly journal prompts are vague.

DO NOT TAKE. He is the worst teacher I have EVER dealt with. He assigns journals with prompts that make no sense (not even grammatically correct either). So much busy work, and no matter how hard you try in this class, he will never give you an A on any assignment. He is terrible. Do not recommend. My easy A turned into the worst class ever.

Jacob is an extremely hard grader. He gives prompts to each assignment but they are unclear and there is no rubric given just "tips for success". His feedback is just asking us more questions on what was written and he doesn't explain why we got the grade we did. Very homework heavy. Was give a test, quiz, paper, and journal in one week DON'T TAKE!

This class was probably one of the worst classes I've ever taken. He grades each journal and paper so difficult, that my quiz and test grades hardly even bring up the average. Besides that, there are some weeks where there's close to two hours in lecture, a paper, discussion posts, and a journal, and some with nothing. Literally do not take it.

Inconsistent work flow, it will not match up with the syllabus, very little explanation given for work assignments as well, a clear lack of clarifications and explanations. Teacher is lazy at the expense of the students, you will have to make up for his lack of initiative if you take this course.

Took this class for a certification and mini-mester, Failed me on an assignment I did 4 times because he did not agree with me. Gave me no help as to what I needed to do and gave me zero credit. Failed the class and was not able to graduate on time after asking him in advance if he could give me a heads up on my grade and he was rude. The WORST!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You have to apply yourself from the beginning. A's are so difficult to earn. The two tests make up 30% of your grade (50 questions in an hour very hard)and the final essay (which is so hard) is 32.5% of your grade. There is a lot of reading (memorizing) and journals. He doesn't really give feedback, so you have to advocate for yourself. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lack of details to what he wants us to do and expects us to understand how to score well on assignments without giving us any information to go off of.
He grades hard for no reason and rarely leaves comments for how to improve. Took this for core and got a B? Im a 4.0 student for O-chem major. Got a B in a stupid leadership class. Dont take.

Horrible oroginization. The class didnt even have a syllabus on blackboard. Jacob is a horrible teacher who grades unecessarily hard for the lack of details he gives. The exams had no relation to the study guide and often brought up questions never taught to you. I took this class as a fun elective and ended up hating everything about the class.

Took this class as a filler to receive full financial aid and thought I would get something out of it. Ever since I took his horrible class I started using Rate My Professor before I sign up for classes now.
Straight to the point but never boring. If you like communications you will enjoy his teaching, guaranteed.

TERRIBLE!!!!  don't take this class with him!! Did a speech and won the best speech which was voted by classmates online and he had the nerve to give me low C. Lots of work and nothing is good enough for him. Also a very annoying sense of humor, gets old in about 5 minutes your first day.
He's kind of arrogant, not flexible. Can be funny, but isn't very clear about what he wants from you. Not a favorite. The class is kind of tough.

He seems a bit arrogant at times. Also, he tried to make the material interesting, but most of it wasn't. I'd highly recommend not taking the honors version of this course unless you're really into speaking.

Jacob is a aweful grader and has horrible questions on his mid-term and finals. I just don't think he knows how to teach at all. A ton of work for a low grade. For example the avg. on the mid-term was around 50%. SOOOOOO boring, because all we did was listen to eachother give speeches in a 300 level class. Decent lecturer, but few lectures.
No Comments

Not very helpful makes you create your own study guide for the midterm and uses none of the questions you submit. Plays favorites and he's not very understanding about speech anxiety (even when it's covered in the class)
Extremely hard teacher. Helpful if u like to hear how bad of a speaker you are. Not interesting. Do not take him unless you want to do a lot of work for a C or D grade. Not a good speech teacher.
Very hard teacher; makes coms 130 a very tedious class but is very nice and gives great tips for improvement

The worst 75 min lecture to sit through. Extremely boring and really just covers the reading so you don't have to actually read. Engagement is graded but it's not hard to add commentary as long as you have a general understanding of the material. Tough grader too and doesn't give much feedback as to why he gives certain grades. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great class, interesting lectures/discussions. Grades are determined by a few quizzes and papers. Attendance isn't mandatory but encouraged. Overall pretty fun course although it can be boring at times. Can be challenging, but good introductory course into higher levels of philosophy

Jenkins is a great introductory philosophy professor. In PHIL 140, goes through a variety of profound topics. Textbook Elements of Philosophy required physically. Two papers and multiple quizzes, and engaging lectures. Some people here called them boring, he's not, you just need to try and engage.  Frequent health-induced class cancelations.

For a 100 level class Phil 141 was far too difficult, especially as someone who is not majoring in Philosophy. I found that Dr. Jenkins expected you to understand the material right off the bat and then build off of it in lectures. I would have expected a 100 level class to put more emphasis on the basics before introducing the important content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Jenkins is a very entertaining professor and I greatly enjoyed his class. It has an immense amount of reading but that is to be expected with the course. He is very knowledgeable and easy to work with. Easily accessible through email if need be.
Good at leading discussions, very nice dude. Took a 100 level class, so not sure what he's like for higher-level classes but definitely recommend him in general.

I took Prof Jenkins for PHIL 570 and it was honestly one of my favorite classes taken at KU so far. The class is solely based on Nietzsche's own works and you have 3 papers for the entire semester. The prompts are thought provoking and the lectures are very engaging. Would definitely recommend!

His lectures can be very boring but I respect him. Before writing the papers I would always conference with him to clarify my ideas about the readings and I always got As on the paper. I couldn't make it to his office hours but he always made extra time for me. He also responds very quickly to emails. If you take the class serious you'll do fine

His comments on my graded papers were off-kilter and vague. For example, in one of my papers he said that "my criticisms of X were underdeveloped," which is funny considering the fact that the thesis of my paper was largely in support of X. I seriously doubt that he took the time to read my work. Terrible professor.

Very competent and reliable. Solid background at Stanford and Princeton. That is evident in his coherent organization and consistent performance. He's really very good as a scholar. Isn't the most engaging as a lecturer as others have noted, but does drop a subject related joke occasionally, completely unexpected, that completely redeems him.

It was really easy. 2 papers only 3-4 pages each and two test: midterm and final. The test are multiple choice with one essay at the end. Easy class if take notes. His notes are power point slide show. You really dont have to read because his notes summarize so well. but I had to read some of the book b/c my discussion leader was fairly strict

Mostly?  He is just not very engaging.  In fact, he is incredibly boring.  But he seems like a very nice guy.  He explains all the readings in lecture, but I think you might be better off reading the book because you might be bored into stupidity in class.  Omg.

great teacher with solid TA's.  Does a good job of explaining and makes sense of philosophy for first time philosophy students.  doesn't put up with people messing around on phones or computers in class and will call you out in front of the entire lecture so don't do it

When I started this class everyone kept whispering "I hear he never gives out A's. I heard he's really hard."  At the end of the semester the 6 people who sat in my area were all laughing at that: 3 of us got As. He is easy if you try, and asking that you try is more than fair. He's a good teacher if you aren't a total idiot and you try.

You don't have to do all the reading, so it's not very time-consuming outside of class. It's impossible to get an A on a paper--he doesn't grade with a rubric, just tags papers with the grade he thinks they deserve.  CONFUSING lecture, hard to take notes on it.  Only one person got an A, but hardly anyone got a C, also.

Hands down the best professor I've had at KU. Incredible command of his subject, down to earth, well organized in both class and lecture style, gives no busy work or tests yet still demands your best work and respect. All that and you still wanna have a beer with him.
It's a little nerve-racking to have your entire grade based on 2 papers and attendance, but once you realize that you only really have to read two of the books, it's not too difficult to keep up.
He's pretty cool and laid-back. Maybe not the most engaging of lecturers, but not outright bad. And I thought his grading on my papers has been pretty fair thus far. Good, subtle sense of humor.
Seriously listen when people say not to take this class. It will make you crazy for no reward.
DON'T TAKE!!! YOU WILL BE A MISERABLE PERSON!
He didn't give out any As last semester, good luck!

In a class centering on the theme of free thought and varying perspectives this professor diverged little from his own thought process.  He was immensely unreceptive to questions in the class; he just changed the subject.  He gave only two As during the class on papers. My suggestion, avoid this class at all costs.

He explains philosophy well and has a good sense of humor. Only complaint is that it's difficult to get an A on his papers, but it's an easy B if you try. The subject of Philosophy is not for everyone so if you're not the philosophical type definitely don't take this class, but the teacher is good. Keep up with the readings!
One of the best professors I've had, makes content fun and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Jennifer is very sweet and cares about her students. If you are taking BLAW, I highly recommend her. However, there is a lot of information to memorize in the class, and the tests are extremely difficult. If you study and participate in class, you should be fine.

If you're wanting to do law, take Jennifer's class. she is a good professor. however, if you're a business student needing to take blaw, take another professor. jennifer's exams are extremely difficult compared to the other professors and you need a higher % to get an A (doesn't round) with the other professors, you need a lower % to get an A.

Her lectures are engaging but she was not nice or understanding. She is nice to students in BLP. Even with valid excuses, she was unwilling to accommodate. I took two classes with her, but the lack of care and respect has put me off taking any more. She was sometimes outright mean to me despite being an engaged and hardworking student.
She's amazing and cares so much about her students. Also went to Harvard Law which is pretty cool!

Best ever. No complaints. Take any class with her you can.

Teaches like you're having a conversation with her which makes it so easy and fun to learn. Definitely intelligent and expects that you try in her class but doesn't make it impossible by any means to do well in her class. Genuinely enjoyed her class.

Gives Great Feedback.
Passionate about the subject.
Answers questions thoughtfully.
Gives practical examples to bring the law into context.
Very Clear (and strict) Grading Criteria.

Jen is a very knowledgable professor and she really loves the material. The class is based off mostly tests. All the tests are cumulative so by the time you get to the the 3rd exam, there is over 250 terms that are fair game for the exam. She is a little picky on what she looks for on the essay responses on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: By far the best class at KU. She truly cares about the students. I would definitely recommend to take BLAW 301 with her! Don't buy the book and make sure you attend class

Extremely knowledgeable and approachable professor. Probably the best one I have had at the University of Kansas. She also loves what she is teaching which makes everything all the more interesting for the student.

My favorite professor, made a class I was dreading my favorite class of all college. She really cares about her students and lets you dive into topics you are interested in. Very supportive and makes lectures engaging and memorable making the tests much simpler. TAKE THIS CLASS

Jen is not only a great teacher, but a very caring individual. This class really did make me want to go to law school, she taught every topic in such a dynamic and interesting way. Early lectures are hard, no matter how amazing the class - remember to bring coffee. The content and material is hard and there is a lot to memorize.

Jen was really sincere about her teaching. She is passionate! Business Law is not my major, and she made the introductory class really informative yet challenging. Tests are all cumulative, which helps you for the final in the long run. Don't buy or read the book. Lecture is all you need.

Fantastic teacher. Made learning so easy and enjoyable. Her class made me want to go to law school! She truly cares about the success of her students. Tests are pretty easy. She's also a Harvard Law grad who practiced for 20 years, so she knows what she's talking about. The best professor I've had since I've attended KU.

Best teacher I've had at KU. She really cares about her students and makes what she's talking about interesting. This class is also a pretty easy A if you just show up and study the slides before the tests. Would definitely take another class with her.

Jenn is the nicest, most caring professor I've encountered at KU. She is truly there to help students and makes a rather boring topic really interesting. You have to go to class for participation, but there is no need to read the book (it costs over $200 so just don't buy it). She posts slides online and gives study guides for the tests.

Best class I have ever taken at KU. Jen is the best professor and I actually learned a lot from this class. Would highly recommend if need BLAW credit. Plus she's a Harvard grad so she knows what she's talking about.

Easy to follow her slides in class- she gives really good examples and it makes it that much easier to understand the material! Participation on Tuesday's and quizzes every Thursday. Not too hard tho!  Overall, I really enjoyed this class and her as a professor. She's so inspiring and I actually considered switching my major to law at one point!

The class has been described as uninteresting and boring. Jennifer makes this class engaging, intriguing, and she's the best thing to happen to business law at KU ever. She's a new lecturer this year after practicing law, in class she gives engaging examples and her passion for law and business is contagious.

Caring and funny teacher who uses a lot of creativity to make hypotheticals in class. Before the test, she gives you a study guide with all the relevant terms, so as long as you study that, then the tests should be easy. She also offers students a lot of food. :)

First time professor, was a lawyer for 20 years, and went to Harvard Law school. She makes class interesting by telling funny stories and inventing entertaining scenarios to illustrate the concepts. Her lectures are concise and easy to follow. Her tests are all short answer but never too difficult. If you do the reading, you'll succeed in her class
Bro can not hold attention for more than 5 minutes, lowk just a hard class to do good in without a lot of outside research. Lectures confusing.
Yeah, this is the class that broke me this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: McNaughton is an ok professor with practice exams nearly identical to the real ones, and he's generous with credit. But exams aren't most of the grade, watch out for the in-class problems and homework. Lectures are VERY hard to follow despite his effort, so be prepared to reteach yourself with youtube. The labs are HELL and all depends on your TA
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McNaughton is a decent guy with an incredible amount of knowledge, but unfortunately not good lecturer. He is decent if you go one-on-one to talk to him about subjects, but he does not teach the lecture in a super intelligible way, especially when you get near the end to topics like FSM. Don't recommend as lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: drink an energy drink before this class because he will ramble you to sleep in a terrifyingly david lynch-esque voice

the homework is overkill and graded harshly. study guides were 80% accurate to the exam questions. I'd say 90% of my learning in EECS 140 came from outside resources in addition to the slides and the SI.I mostly felt like I would come back home having to restudy all of the lecture slides from scratch! the grading was very harsh and exam heavy.

Jims a great guy. Always ready to talk about the class or other things during office hours and decently funny during lectures. He can be a bit confusing at times, but the content isn't super hard or difficult to understand as long as you study a little.

This man is on his last leg and he is nearing the end of his teaching career. He easily gets confused while teaching his own content. Because of this, much time is spent watching YouTube videos online. The grading system is good and you get a cheat sheet on the test. Class is set up well, I learned a lot, just not from Jim.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great dude, but definitely nearing the end of his teaching career here. Homework can be unnecessarily hard, but preps you well for exams. Labs aren't too difficult, and he is kind and patient during office hours.
Easy class just don't slack on the homework or in-class problems. Helps if you have friends that have previously taken the class.

Pretty lecture heavy and the homework is a bit overkill on the difficulty at times; however, the tests are pretty tame as long as you brush up on study guide content. Show up to the discussions even though they are optional as homework questions are discussed. Do the homework on time. Be ready for Thursday in-class problems based on the lectures.

Very nice guy but I would not recommend taking EECS140 with him, the homework often feels unnecessarily difficult and is not usually covered in class. The tests aren't super hard and you get a cheat sheet, but other professors do not give tests at all and are said to be much easier.
Very organized and structured. His lectures are very easy to follow and helpful, and he also provides a lot of outside resources if needed.

All in all a pretty good teacher, just gets a little confused at his own work sometimes. To do good in the class, you HAVE to pay attention in the lectures. Don't sit on your phone during the lecture portion of this.

Prof. Lee obviously knows what she is lecturing. She makes a pretty interactive class environment and its easy to learn without taking notes. Would recommend, especially for Mind and Brain Certificate needs. She checks attendance but regularly told us ahead of time if she was checking it that day. You can drop one exam, final is online open access.

She is a great professor! Other reviews say she moves fast but personally it was a perfect pace for me. The content is easy, and honestly you don't need to do the readings since they are talked about in class. Group project is annoying if you get bad partners but not too hard to do. So much extra credit I ended with 106% overall. Highly recommend!

This professor is truly one of the worst. She does not provide any help, she goes so fast in lecture that you don't have time to comprehend anything, and she takes attendance. She does not understand how extra credit works. She changed the syllabus near the end of the semester and refused to honor what was on it originally. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was a great professor. The lectures are pretty easy and understandable, but she often goes fast as there are not much time. The tests are pretty easy as it was all in the lecture. The quizzes might be hard but if you do good on the test it should not affect your grade too much. Overall a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things
