reviews.comment: She is super nice and the class isn't too difficult. Not much homework and the tests are pretty easy. Quizzes are hard but barely affect your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The tests do not align with the unit homework whatsoever and occasionally the test will be so unbalanced that most of the questions are over a topic that was covered once. On the topic of tests, each unit test is multiple choice, which sounds fine, right? No. There is zero possibility for partial credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally was ok with Changstrom as a professor. To fully comprehend the lectures, I had to read the textbook. There are usually two quizzes per CA that are mostly multiple choice with little partial credit, but if you do decently on both, you shouldn't have to do the final. Honestly, if you do the homework and take notes, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams have no partial credit so some exams during the year had averages below 50%.

He is a great person but definitely not a good teacher. It is nice that whatever you got on the final is going to replace all the midterms with lower grade but getting there is a nightmare. I didn't understand a thing he taught and friends and hours of trying to figure out the homework is the only reason I survived. Be prepared and good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is sometimes doesn't explain things very clearly when going through problems and the grading system needs to be reconsidered, however he can explain things well during office hours and it seems like he cares about the success of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class isn't hard if you read the textbook and do practice problems before class. The course is out of 1000 points—tests and final are 800, participation is 200. The final superscores earlier tests, so a 100 on it guarantees at least an 80%. The instructor isn't great, and lectures just go over problems, not the reading. Uses 12 point grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worse professor I've ever had at KU she was never clear about exams constantly changed the way the class was run. It felt like I was being lectured by a brick wall the entire semester the class was incredibly boring and she expected us to basically learn everything by ourselves by reading the textbook which makes no sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The tests are so difficult and don't relate to the in-class examples or the homework at all. Expectations for tests are unclear.

The tests are 11 questions long: 10 base questions and then 1 extra credit question. The test is fully multiple choice and DOESN'T contain any partial credit. It does have questions where you need to get the one prior correct to solve the one you're on correctly. There is limited support, and the textbook is used lightly at best and often ignored.
She is given a bad curriculum from the physics department and does her best with it. Overall if you pay attention and do the work then an A is easily reachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures cover basically no content, and the majority of class time is left to boring and simple Iclicker questions that teach nothing. Textbook sucks, homework assignments often have wrong answers in the key, and grading system shouldn't take 10 minutes to explain how it works.

I think he is a good professor but I think the curriculum is just shi. They did a "test" semester to change things but I feel like more changes are needed. He did give extra credit and the last month he allowed us to do retakes for 2 quizzes which really helped. There are no big tests only quizzes he grades them based on your average on 2 of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I honestly think she's a good professor, the class is questionable but overall ok. The reversed-classroom format is definitely hard to those unfamiliar though. Do all the lectures and homework early so you can not do them later. You shouldn't need a paragraph to explain how the class will be graded. Use the formula sheet and you'll be fine though.

Changstrom is a chill person, but not a great professor. Physics is hard to teach, I understand, but she was not  helping us to succeed in the 24 quizzes. Free-response, no partial credit quizzes. Lectures were doing the practice problems which had the answers posted after class, anyway, so I stopped attending lectures and studied on my own instead

Jessy Changstrom is the worst professor ever. The 24 quizzes had no partial credit, and the lectures were a joke, only going through 2-3 problems they got incorrect even with a key. Multiple weekly quizzes demanded 4/5 correct answers for an A. Even perfect answers lost points if they disliked your work. Avoid them if you value your sanity and GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Changstrom was perfectly nice; the course was the issue. EPHX 210 is set up in a manner that does not promote student success. If possible, take an equivalent course somewhere else. Changstrom did not create the curriculum under which the class was taught, and she was always respectful and willing to help those who reached out.

Jessy Changstrom oh what a sight
Her lectures go on with a freight
With equations and theories writes on the board
But her students are yawning feeling quite bored
Her tests are like puzzles impossible to solve
Her assignments a riddle they can't quite resolve
With a cackle she says, It's all quite clear
But to her students there's nothing but fear
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is continually a disappointment. Both the curriculum and teaching quality is consistently awful. Changstrom regularly gets her own example problems wrong and is corrected by her students, exhibiting either minimal effort or knowledge of the subject. The grading system is appalling - assessments have only 5 problems and no partial credit.

Changstrom tries, but the class is awful. She wants you to succeed but the class is organized horribly, her teaching is mediocre, the grading is inconsistent, there is so much homework and its way harder than anything else. You can succeed in this class, but be prepared for misery and frustration.
It is not the professor's fault for the department's problems. They sometimes got questions wrong in class and were corrected by students but the real issue was the grading system and curriculum.

The problem is her curriculum. She demands a complete mastery of all topics which takes 15+ hours a week. The problem is that the last quiz of one section is on a Friday and the first quiz of the next section is the following Monday. That gives students the weekend to master the entire section of material. She claims it is a 3 credit-hour class.

She is the worst professor I have ever had in my entire schooling life. She was corrected by students daily in lectures because she did almost every problem wrong. One of the worst things about that is she changed a part of the syllabus MIDWAY THROUGH THE SEMESTER saying she would grade our work and she did not mention it in lecturer. 0/10

The most excruciating class I have ever taken. I was miserable all semester long. Never had any problems preparing for classes with much more difficult material. However, the whole class feels like it is set up to make as many kids fail as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures are almost impossible to stay engaged in as she constantly jumps back and forth between different steps. The quizzes are impossible to prepare for unless you go back and do every single homework problem again.

The worst class I have taken at any level. It's impossible to prepare for the quizzes as the study material given feels like a trap because they have nothing to do with the actual quizzes. The whole class feels like you are being set up to fail. Just take physics at a community college over this.

Professor Changstrom is the worst professor I have encountered while at KU. She messes up problems in lectures and then expects us to know how to do the problems. She does a terrible job explaining where she gets equations/answers. On top of this, there are 2 quizzes per week with 5 questions on them and there is no partial credit. Take it online.

Honestly, this class makes no sense. You have two tests a week with no chance of partial credit. You can literally walk into a test knowing the final formula and do better than someone who knows all the content but forgot to make something a negative. This class is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible Lecture,though grade

This class is miserable. There are 2 tests per week, which have no partial credit because "engineers should be able to get stuff right the first time", right because trial and error doesn't exist inside her head, which I'm convinced is full of rocks. The test answers and examples are oftentimes wrong, so you can't even trust the study material.

I would rather file my teeth down to the root than listen to another changstrom lecture. She is the epitome of incompetence and insecurity. Her lectures are 50 minutes of her bumbling around getting her own practice problems wrong. Then she expects you take 4 question no partial credit quizzes with the content that you werent able to learn from her

Jessy Changstrom never taught anything. The class was flipped, but the videos never explained anything and were not helpful at all. There were in-person quizzes outside of class every week that had no partial credit or cheat sheet. The whole class was basically just trying to memorize every single problem and hope for the best on the quizzes.

Truly horrendous that a course like this can exist at KU. A laughing stock among furious students across campus, Jessy Changstrom cannot and will not teach you physics. It is appauling how an introduction class to physics has so many unfair 4 question quizzes with no partial credit that you are just doomed to fail. do not take this course.

I'd rather take a razor scooter to the ankle every day for the rest of my life than step foot in that class room. I'd rather have little red riding hood try to teach me kinematics rather than her. Each and everyday I woke up loving my life, then I remember this gurl will attempt to "teach" me energy and my day will go to complete and utter shiii

This professor does not teach. She assigns videos to watch before class and then does one question and an iClicker in class.Her teaching is just a bunch of droning, and at least once a class she messes up a question and has to restart. Tests have no partial credit, so either you are right, or you get a zero. I will drop this class and go to JCCC.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: At least one problem is not correct per lecture. Does not fully grasp or understand the content. You can tell she is not enthusiastic about being there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gets her own lecture problems wrong, doesn't really teach, just tries to get through class.
If you can take physics somewhere else, I recommend you do.

Avoid this class at all costs. Besides this professor not teaching anything at all during lectures (but needing to go to secure participation points) the quizzes are all but impossible to do well on unless you memorize every practice and HW problem. There is no partial credit whatsoever, so if you mess up even slightly your grade tanks.

Prepare to teach yourself all the material. Professor will make mistakes, have typos, and not explain everything thoroughly. No quiz partial credit, to do well in the class you need to do well on every quiz, given weekly. Study guides don't always have what you need for the quizzes, making it a pain to know what to study. This is beyond "weed-out."

The quizzes/tests that she gives out do not have any partial credit. In the past, she's utilized multiple-choice answers (so you could compare and see if your answer matches one of the given choices), and allowed students to have a reference "cheat-sheet" in exams. However, this semester, she decided to remove all of those altogether.

A quiz OUTSIDE of class every week with only 5 questions and no partial credit so if you mess up once slightly you get a 0 for that question. Learned nothing in lectures had to learn all myself. homework was impossible because it never told you what to round to and she never fixed the issue.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
WARNING:Avoid at all costs
You will not learn anything in this class. On top of that, the quizzes do have not partial credit, so you WILL fail if you don't take advantage of every single quiz retake. Changstrom supports this structure completely, so you will have no wiggle room with her.

Terrible at teaching. The class structure seems designed to get people to fail, and Dr. Changstrom refuses to take accountability when there is an error in a quiz or homework problem; if you miss because of it, even if you got the correct answer, there is nothing she will do about it. Take Physics I anywhere other than KU if you care about your GPA

The grading used in this course is not fair. Each quiz has only five questions, answered with a number rounded to two decimal places, with no change for partial credit. Missing one question on any quiz by a simple rounding error, or forgotten unit means that the MAXIMUM grade possible on the quiz is 80%. The quizzes compose most of the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Dr.Changstrom's PHSX 114 course in Spring 2023. I was very enjoy her class because she did one of the example of the problem and explained it carefully that helped me understand what to expect when solving problem. What you need to do is to stay focus during class and practice problems on Powerpoint slide after class. I'm sure you get an A.

It is a reverse class setup where the lectures are online, however the videos were clearly created in a different decade, reused throughout the years in canvas. The lectures themselves weren't even worth going to as there was no new info, and we usually spent the whole 50 minutes on the same problem with no progress nor help from the professor.

She is new to the University. She reuses Rush's Canvas page (which kinda sucks). The quizzes are exactly the homework problems though... it's the only think that kept me afloat. she does absolutely not lecture during lectures... youre kinda just stuck confused with the same practice problem the whole hour. very good during office hours though
Great professor!
Pretty laid back. Try and you'll get a good grade.

reviews.comment: Loved this class. Great teacher who cares.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: For an intro English class, Logan is an alright professors. His lectures are somewhat boring, but do truly help your writing as you go on. Daily assignments for attendance, and a few classes a month skipped for 1-on-1 meetings with him. He responds to emails, and questions rather quickly as well. Decent class overall, just gotta get through it.

To start, Logan is a decent guy. His lectures are pretty boring, and he loves to sit in silence when asking pretty difficult questions to students. You're graded weekly by chiming into lectures, and daily writing prompts that take 15-20 min. He's a very hard grader on essays, but gives pretty decent feedback in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My writing improved drastically over the course of this semester. He grades hard, but all of the feedback makes sense. Would take again.

Might be the most stressful teacher I've ever had! In class, almost the entire time is him asking the most complex question possible that only he knows the answer to, followed by almost 5 minutes of him just staring at us. Is also the harshest grader I've ever seen. Do not expect an A to be possible, you will have to fight him hard for a B.

This class was discussion heavy but the discussions were led poorly. It was very awkward to sit in silence during discussions and not much learning happened in the lecture time. You will read a lot outside of class and do a few assignments but he does give good feedback on turned in assignments. Go to lecture and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher!!! 100% you should take his class!! I learned a lot and had a fun time this semester!!
I will admit he is a tough grader, but all of his feedback makes sense. My writing definitely improved over the semester with his teaching

Very tough grader and was no helpful when it came to feedback on projects. I could spend days on projects and I did not score higher than an 85. He once told my classmate they needed to start showing up to class when they were there everyday. Sometimes was rude

I took this professor for a level one fiction writing class and let me tell you, nothing you will do in the class will please this man. You could write the best story out of the whole class, and he won't ever give you an A. He only gives out B's and lower. You have to participate every single class or he will give you a zero. Do not take him!

reviews.comment: Does not explain things well. Does not give A's, way too picky when grading for a 102 class. Do not take his class if you want an A.

He is very picky about sticking to the prompt, but he also chooses terrible, uninteresting, and thoughtless prompts. He decided to teach us all about "how to write summaries" as if we have not been learning to do this since elementary school. Prepare for condescending lectures about common sense writing. KU core nonprofessionalism at its finest.
Felt like a lot of homework, but was very understanding.

I didn't enjoy this class

reviews.comment: He is genuinely a great teacher and an even better human. Enjoyed all of his lectures and was super nice to the whole class. He cared about us a lot and would always give extensions if needed. My guy for real!

reviews.comment: Korbin is enthusiastic, kind, understanding and intelligent. He granted extensions when needed, and always made class interesting. His sense of humor engaged the class and made it more entertaining. The assignments were well explained and he always responded to emails quickly and provided helpful feedback.

He is the funniest teacher and I loved my class this semester. You do small activities outside of class and class attendance isn't mandatory at all. You just need to figure out what he wants when he grades essays and you're gucci for getting an A. My favorite class this semester by far.

He is a tough grader and kinda thinks highly of himself too much, but he is really relaxed and is very understanding when it comes to mental health. Introduces the class by saying you won't get an A on you papers tho unless they really blow him away

I took this class with online lectures and in-person discussions. It was a lot of reading, but it was doable. Most of the content was interesting, but I got tired of reading. Dr. Morris is nice and gives good feedback.

I personally never met Dr. Morris because I was in the discussion class with a GTA, but let me prepare you by saying: GET READY TO READ!! As long as you are up to date on reading and attend discussions, you'll be fine and pass with an A.

reviews.comment: Never met the professor, only the GTA who led the discussion. Very very textbook heavy, but still enjoyable. As long as you do the weekly readings and participate in discussion, you will get an A.

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most difficult courses I've taken for just being Geography 100. Attendance is graded in such a weird way. She likes to grade really hard. All I say is good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There are mini-lectures, readings up to 100 pages, and an essay due each week. Grading is fairly easy if you put in the work; you have to pay close attention to the readings to do well on the exams. It's not hard work, but it is very time-consuming. Aside from that, very fascinating content, if you'll put in the work you'll really like this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was over all very interesting. However, It was a LOT of reading and writing. Every week there was chapters of a book to read and then an essay to write. The prompts weren't difficult, but the work was just a lot to do. My main complaint is that if an assignment is turned in even a minute late you get a 0, no questions asked.

Her lectures were pre-recorded videos from the pandemic that didn't line up with what we were learning. You have to write a 5 paragraph essay every week. The GTA(at least the one I had) is the one grading your stuff. The GTA I had would dock me points on my writing style,   and align with our even though that wasn't in the rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: There's a lot to read, and I mean A LOT! There's also a lot to write. Not the most difficult class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Teaches Calc 3 in a way that makes it easier to understand. Jila will teach the geometry behind the problems to make them intuitive. Very accessible and wants to help you succeed. If you took calc 2 somewhere else, this class assumes you know about vectors which most calc 2 classes don't teach, making for a steep but manageable hurdle at the start
Amazing instructor

Jila is the nicest and most accessible professor I have had at ku. She cares about her students doing well and offers above and beyond in terms of help. The lectures can he hard to follow, but it is mostly due to the sheer amount of course material she needs to go through. Go to her office hours and the help room if you really want to do well!

Jila is one of the best professors at KU. Everything she does is amazing, and every professor should try to emulate her. She explains everything really well and gives lots of extra credit and study guides are very similar to the tests. Take Jila if you can!

I loved this class, easiest calc class at ku and if you put in the work for homework/studying then you will get a good grade. You do have to teach yourself a little bit but its simple work compared to what I have to do for other classes. Jila is super personable and you can reach her outside of class and she tries to learn everyones names.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Niknejad does much more than she gets paid to do.  She spends so much time making sure students succeed.  Would 100% take her classes again.  The helproom and Jila's office hours are your best friend nya~!  But seriously she's underappreciated for all the work she does to keep the calculus courses running.  KU will miss her if she leaves.

Jila is great at listening to students and caring about how they feel. She inspired a lot of us who weren't math majors, but liked math. Sometimes she goes through lectures a little fast, but the resources she makes are good. Class is taught in a standard way, so it's easy to get extra help. It's a shame she makes less than her male predecessor.

I love Jila. She puts in effort to get to know each and every student and you can tell she genuinely wants you to succeed. Her lectures are very fast paced and sometimes her handwriting is hard to read, but it's really easy to ask questions or get her attention during class if you need clarification. She also cracks jokes all the time!

Jila is probably one of the kindest professors I've had.  However, her lectures were sometimes hard to follow, and she seemed to encourage memorization over actual understanding.  The tests were very easy with very similar study guides and LOTS of extra credit.

Jila Niknejad is the best math professor that you can get. She is very kind and respectful to her students. Her grading is lenient as long as you show that you know what needs to be done per assignment. GO TO THE HELP ROOM. Not only does she want help but she gives out food to students if you go talk to her. She is the best calc teacher, period.

SUPER SUPER NICE LADY. She is so accessible, math help room is extremely helpful and she is always in Snow offering help. Tests are fair, class structure is fair, only downside is the lectures are a little confusing to follow sometimes. 

ALSO RYAN FRIER IS THE GREATEST MATH TA OF ALL TIME.

Jila is such a kind person. She is very accessible outside of class and wants the best for all of her students. The material is difficult. She cares about students and tries her best to explain material, however some explanations are confusing and difficult to follow. The math help room is a lifesaver and she's willing to elaborate on any subject.

Jila's great at explaining concepts. The class itself was somewhat difficult, but not too bad as long as you put in the work. There is a lot of work, but as long as you pace yourself you should be good.

This woman is a literal blessing from God. She's the queen of math department at KU no competition. It sucked that she was just the coordinator of the course because her explanations were top notch. Please protect her at all costs she's a blessing for anyone in mathematics.

Though I sometimes found her lectures a bit disorganized, I found that she explained things much better during her office hours. She cares so much about the success of her students and always tries her best to help us during the iClickers. Love her!

Jila wants you to succeed, and gives you many opportunities with extra credit on exams and open office hours. The only downside is that she is very very difficult to understand, and so were quite a few of the lab TAs. I took AP Calc AB and BC and the class was easy, I didnt even have to pay attention.

I had Jila for Precalc, Calc I, and Calc III. She is the most caring professor I have ever had. She will make sure you succeed. She is quick to respond, making her very easy to reach. She is so sweet and I all around love her. I would for sure recommend doing all the previous exams for study tools!
Calc 3 sucks in general
Jila is an absolute queen. Cares about our understanding of the material and really takes our feedback. Wants everyone to get the best grade possible. Lecture heavy class for sure though.

Dr. Jila Niknejad is the best professor I have had at KU. I had her for MATH125 and made sure I had her as my professor again when I found out she was teaching MATH127. I 110% recommend her as a professor to everyone I can. She genuinely cares about each and everyone of her students!

Jila is hands down a wonderful professor. I have had her for calc 1 and 3 and she is a fair teacher who genuinely cares about her student's success. No to mention, her open-door policy is amazing as she goes above and beyond to help her students perform well and understand the material.

Jila is the only reason I am still at KU. She is the best professor on this entire campus. If it wasn't for Jila's absolute passion for the content and her accessibility outside of class Calc 3 would be an impossible course. She is pleasant to students and truly understands what we are going through. Jila makes the content approachable.

The most wonderful professor you'll find. She is truly caring towards every single student. She wants to help you in any way she can, super supportive, and caring. If I had to take a math class from anyone, it would be from her! Definitely a top-notch professor and super caring human-being. Jila is amazing. Anyone who complained, didn't try.

Jila has been my favorite professor while attending The University of Kansas. (I took Precalc, Calc 1, and Calc 3 with her)She cares about EVERY single student and memorizes so many individuals names. She is always willing to meet outside of class. She provides previous exams for all the midterms which makes studying a breeze.

very nice lady, but not a good lecturer. she doesn't teach the same content that we do in the labs, so we have to teach ourselves. does NOT do a good job teaching concepts b/c she picks a problem and does it without explaining how to do it and it leaves us all confused.

I love the structure of all of the calculus classes at KU it is very easy to follow and I really enjoyed having jila for all three calculus classes love her a genuinely good person and tries her best to get everyone in her class to understand lots of homework and worksheets but very good for practice and directly reflect the exams
She is genuinely so lovely and willing to provide help. Sometimes her lecturing can get a bit off track, but it's 90% clear and easy to understand!

One of the best math professors at KU. Incredibly caring and understandable, she wants you to succeed and that means a lot. Lectures are sometimes a bit hard to follow, but the homework solutions and office hour availability do wonders. Don't be afraid to ask questions when something is tough and you'll do fine.

Jila is so great! She's one of the nicest most caring people I know and she has a passion for teaching. She goes above and beyond to teach any student willing to learn. She great at explaining things and really wants to help everyone succeed.
The lectures do not make much sense and she is hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor cares about students and teaching. She delivers the material and organized the course well. Plentiful resources are given and students are given many opportunities to succeed.

She was one of my favorite math teachers at KU (especially when our math department isn't great). She cares so much about how you do, and will go the extra mile to remember who you are out of her 200+ people in her lectures. If you ask her questions, she will try to explain to you until you understand, and wants you to know the material. Love her!!

She is really hard to follow in lecture. If you get lost in her lectures sign up for tutoring. If you actually do the homework and take okay notes this class is not hard. Print out the slides before class and take notes on it.

She is very nice and cares about her students. She really wants you to understand and have good grades. Her lectures aren't very organized, but they are good overall. You can learn a lot with her, would take the class again. You will need the Webassign code more than the book and attendance counts for iClickers.

She can get flustered at times causing lectures to seem disorganized. She also has an accent that takes some time to get used to. HOWEVER, Dr. Niknejads genuine care for her students was outstanding. I know caring isnt everything, but having a prof that not only wishes for your success but is also proud when you do succeed makes the difference.

Dr. Niknejad is the sweetest professor I have ever had. She really cares about her students and makes sure to break the lessons down without being condescending. Her class is difficult but you can to get an A if you goto the practice exams, do the homework, and study every night for about an hour. She also gives extra credit at the end of the year.

This is a professor that truly cares that her students succeed. She made an effort to learn the names of people in her 200 student lecture section. She tried hard to give us opportunities to raise our grades when needed, and at the same time she worked to ensure we are prepared for future Calculus classes.

Jila is very smart and caring (not too bad looking either lol). She's a little hard to understand but not bad. The only thing I didn't like was that she is very messy. She constantly changes due dates and her lectures are disorganized. If you get lost, her online notes are actually VERY clear and helpful! Don't skip, you may have random group work.

Jila is one of my favorite professors. She gives engaging lectures, is available for office hours as well as her 2 TA's, and is extremely supportive of all her students. She can make mistakes in class and sometimes not write the topic, but as someone who needs a large amount of organization in class, it was not difficult to follow. Take her class!

The class content is easy, but she is to disorganized and her lectures are messy. She doesn't follow a schedule and makes a lot of mistakes in class. Personally I hated the class because I had to study everything outside class. However, she is one of the nicest person and truly cares about you.

Jila is such an amazing professor. The content for this class is pretty easy and straightforward so it made the semester a whole lot better. She gave so many opportunities for extra credit which was pretty nice. The tests are based very heavily on the examples in class and the homework assignments so pay attention to those.

Very helpful professor and very fair. She gave multiple extra credit opportunities to help people bring their grade up. Lectures are pretty quick, but the content on the exams is pretty straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Jila is one of the sweetest, kindest, and most caring professors I've had at KU. Although her lectures can sometimes be a bit scattered and flustered, she is always accessible through email and office hours, and will go out of her way to help every student possible. Overall a great professor.

Amazing teacher who really cares about her students. She knew the names of everyone in our 70 student lecture. Pay close attention to the feedback that she gives on homework and ask questions. If you go into the tests with a good understanding of the material you will do fine.

Jila is absolutely the nicest professor on campus, and genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. My only complaint is, with rowdy students, she doesn't have the capability to shut them up, and I felt like it hindered the rest of the student's learning. Besides that, she posts slides online which help with homework and quizzes

Jila is a very caring professor who will 100% go out of her way to make sure you understand concepts. Jila does sometimes get flusterd at herself due to going to fast or trying to talk and write at the same time.

She is honestly the best instructor I've met since I've been here! She went out of her way to make sure everyone that at least tries to succeed do so. She is also super funny and will poke fun in class.

She is the absolute best teacher I've had in the math department. She really does care about every student (she knew every name in our 100 person lecture). She won't do the course for you but if you show her that you care she'll take time out of her day to help you out. She teaches well; I feel like I know the material well enough to teach it!

Absolutely the best teacher I have ever had at KU. There might be better, but I didn't face them yet. I took two classes with her up till now. Because of her clear notes and  guide, I am ready to be a teacher at those two classes. She is very clear on what to expect on exams unlike other teachers who keep confusing students all the time. LOVE HER.

Dr. Niknejad is the best math teacher I have ever had. As a freshman in DiffEq, I was worried about how hard the material would be coming right out of highschool. She was very helpful during office hours and her notes were consistent and precise to the homework. This class made me study but I achieved a good grade and learned a lot from it. Loveher
She is a very good teacher that will help you whenever you ask for it. She wont do everything for you but if you put in the effort you will do well.

She is a really good professor. She knows what she does. Loves teaching and her study guides are really helpful. Review sessions is a MUST GO if you wanna get an easy A on the test. I wish she could teach all Math courses.

She's amazing, easily the best professor I've had at KU. Pay attention to the feedback on what she hands back and if you ever need help, go to her office hours. Nicest and most helpful professor out there, I've never met one who cared more about their students.

By far the best professor I've ever had. She is always willing to help students and really cares about how each student is doing in her class. Very engaging teaching style and always makes sure to stay on track with material. Absolutely loved her class, wish I could have her for a professor every semester.

She is one of the best professors I've had in my two years at KU.  She assigns a few of the easier problems for homework each class and has group reviews in class before tests.  All of her material is easy, with practice tests just like the real thing.  She's very kind and her utmost priority is you learning as much as possible without headaches.

Amazing teacher. If you learn the review she gives out before each exam, you will do well. She is very willing to help and offers opportunities to earn credit back. Sometimes a concept isn't entirely clear at first, but it seems to come together before the exam. She is very enthusiastic. One of my favorites!

One of the best teachers I've had.  She makes it clear what is on the test.  Go to her office hours for help.  She really helped me out this semester.  I became very ill(in the hospital) and missed a test and she told me to email her as soon as I felt better.  It's a breath of fresh air having a teacher care so much about educating her students.

SO VERY HELPFUL. Would not move on until you understood what she was teaching. I strongly recommend going to office hours. She'll let you work on homework if you need to. AMAZING MATH TEACHER!!! One of the few good ones at KU.

Recommend this teacher for ANY math class she teaches. She gives out review guides for her tests that explain EVERYTHING and is extremely helpful during office hours. Believe the hype, take her class. She is the nicest professor I've met and will actually teach you while still giving you the best chance at an A.

She's an amazing prof and very passionate about teaching and making her students succeed. Her reviews let you concentrate on what will be on the exams and a nice chunk of your final grade is simply from hw, attendance and in-class group work. Definitely take advantage of her office hrs if you feel confused about a topic, you won't regret it.

Easily the 2nd best math teacher at KU besides Jeff Lang. If you can take a course from her DO IT! She's very helpful in her office hours and truly wants you to succeed. Bottom line, she cares about YOU. Great teacher. Her study guides are extremely helpful. Keep up on homework, go to her office hours if you need help, and you'll do great!

She is fantastic, go to her office hours, she helps a lot and is also interested in your life. She is clear in class and her material is straight forward, and her exams are straight forward as long as you look at the study guide. As an instructor, she is fantastic, very clear, helps a LOT.

She is the best professor I've ever had. I loved the way she taught, and her tests were SUPER SUPER easy. On top of that, you can get back half of missed points and get extra credit easily. I didnt miss a single point in her entire course. I WOULD DEFINITELY RECOMMEND HER!!!!
Took the online class. Always willing to help if you seek it and show that you attempted to understand the problem

She is very helpful and willing to meet with students, she is also friendly. The thing about her that I think makes her a good teacher is she lets you know what to expect on tests then puts that on the test.
Great teacher! Has fun with her students and enjoys her job. Lenient, fair grading policy. Keep up on homework and quizes and you'll do fine.
Great teacher. Has fun with her class and enjoys her job. Keep up on the homework and quizes and you'll do fine. Fair grader and generally really fun person.
I took her class during summer. It was fairly easy. Book is extremely useful.

There was no clear grading scale or expectations for any assignments. Weekly homework assignments took hours and were only worth 5 points, half of those points being deducted for the smallest mistakes. Every time I would reach out for assistance, I would be referred to hours of lecture videos instead of any form of guidance. Very frustrating class.

The course it self should not have been challenging. She grades very strict and when I asked what I was doing wrong she just told me to figure it out. The entire class was online and she goes through each video at lightning speed. Nothing about this class should have been hard but her grading system is unclear.

I get this is an accelerated online course, but this was the least helpful professor & the hardest grader at the same time. Assignments open daily 7 days a week, from 5am-9pm, you can't work ahead on assignments. Lockdown browsers are used but points are still taken off even if work & answer matches hers, literally no reason. Bad reflection of KU.

Please avoid this professor if you can. She makes a simple class (that isn't a major specific requirement) incredibly difficult for no reason. She uses McGraw-Hill, and the smartbooks are graded based on accuracy instead of completion. Exams are timed with many questions that require showing work. Please pick someone else.
Very unhelpful. Lazy teaching style, wouldn't recommend to anyone
This is the least understanding professor I have ever had. A terribly teacher if that title is even deserved. Should take a course in empathy or find a different field.

Tough grader. Homework takes hours, and even if you watch the lectures, she'll say you didn't. The class feels like a waste of time. It's extremely time-consuming, and you lose points for the smallest things, which is very frustrating. I recommend taking a different class if you can.

3 homework assignments per week. 2 Smartbooks and 1 HW (generally). Smartbooks are about 40 concepts which equates to about 80 questions (if you get every answer correct). These are graded for accuracy and the HW is too. She claims the SBs are "practice", but it's hard to practice when you are penalized greatly for incorrect answers.

Terrible setup-absurd time investments to achieve her expected perfection, and inflexibility in the scheduling of assignments and texts.   Most other classes let you take a test up to 4-5 days early depending on your schedule, especially since this is an asynchronous class, but no, you get one day from 5am-9pm.  Just avoid at all costs.  Nightmare.
Please avoid this professor at any cost
Lots of homework. Insanely tough grader. Homework will be worth five points and take you two hours but she will take off points for very small things. I would recommend you take anybody else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall great professor and quick responses. 4 exams total and the short answers have to be written in a specific format because there are no partial points at all for questions. Typical online class where you get out of it what you put into the class. Lengthy McGraw Hill hw.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Where do I even begin with Ms Chappel? She has no tolerance for late work at all, even in light of technical issues, and assignments are due at 9:00. She grades Smartbook quizzes for accuracy, and overall, her lectures are a waste of time.. She's a nice lady, but is still a terrible teacher, and has no business teaching a class at KU.
It was a full semester course within a 4 week period, so assignments were due almost everyday. Putting aside that this was a heavy workload class, the material covered was presented well.

For each chapter, has 6-8 lecture videos, including Smartbook assignments, homework assignments and quizzes with essay questions that take 5-10 minutes each with a 60-minute time limit. She grades SmartBook assignments, and if you go to her Zoom asking for help, she tells you that you "clearly" didn't watch the lecture video. Don't take this class!

This is probably one of the best teachers that I have had in college. To begin, she will respond to every email and wants all of her students to get an A. In addition, Professor Chappel is one of the easiest Professors to work with because she cares so much about her students. Amazing teacher would definitely take her classes again.

She isn't a bad teacher by any means but there are areas she can improve in. Most of the homework was simple, online and due at 9pm (Rather she do 11:59pm). Checked for accuracy when it came to Smartbook assignments. Exams weren't crazy but her "essay" show your work problems are unnecessary and you almost always run out of time trying to do them.

Professor Chappel genuinely did not do anything helpful this semester, the class is run completely through McGraw-Hill where you will do assignments with as many as 170+ questions that are graded on accuracy. The only learning comes from the book or extremely long lecture videos, I ended up using youtube to teach myself the entire semester's work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was one of the worst classes I have taken at KU. It requires an absurd amount of videos to be watched throughout the course as well as following her make a model. She grades very tough and it always seems like you put in way more work than what you are credited for. Look elsewhere for a finance elective.

I had a great experience taking FIN 410 with Professor Chappel. Her grading was strict however if you reached out to her she would be more than happy to walk you through any questions. Homework was abundant, but this was a semester-long course squeezed into a month. I recommend this class to anyone looking to lighten their load next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Insanely hard workload. 6-8 recorded lectures per day, 1-2 textbook chapters to read, 1-3 hour long accuracy graded "smartbook" assignments, and then 100 point homework assignments in the same day, and then 150 point exams every weekend. I do not know if she actually thought people could spend 12 hours on this course per day but she must have.

I was looking forward to taking Finance but after taking it felt like I learned nothing useful. The entire course was more based on grades than learning the content. Exams were too difficult with little time. Homework doesn't help prepare you for the exams. Lectures are boring and unrelated to exams. Overall I'm disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She doesn't really teach anything just reads off power point slides. All she does is make you do endless HW assignments and 1 quiz per week so you are basically teaching yourself. The material isn't very hard though so you can still get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Had a 92 percent in the class. Got a 92 on first test. 94 on second test. 100 percent in all homework. Went out of her way to give me a 33 on the final project to drop me to 76 overall. Then wouldnt talk/meet/email me about what was wrong. Do not take any classes, even if you know the information she doesnt want students to succeed.

Professor Chappel is a very good online professor who truly cares about her students. She wants her students to succeed and she makes sure her students will succeed as long as they work hard. Her powerpoints were very resourceful and her guidelines are clear. Take this professor if you want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Yikes, please don't ever take her. She gives an assignment before the semester even starts and doesn't even tell you about it. She puts zero effort into this class and has no interaction with students. Julia needs to change her ways because she has no care in the world. I have zero clue why she's being paid to be like this.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good class, you just have to put in a little extra to be successful. This isn't a bad thing of course, it's important for courses to be challenging. Quick email responses, very encouraging, but tough grading.
Fair grader and expects students to try. Don't shy away from the work because you'll learn a lot as a result

Julia is a very hard teacher that will not just hand you the grade. While I struggled in her class and with all of the excel, she was great about providing additional help outside of class and making sure I understood the concepts. Touch up on your excel skills before you take this class because the class is based on developing a model in excel.

Julia's class is extremely difficult. 60% of your final grade is based on these quizzes that are basically in place of tests. They are extremely difficult, where you are required to memorize a lot of formulas. Multiple times there have been things on the quizzes that were not in lecture. All the class is is her reading off the powerpoint slides.

Great teacher. Not a hard class, clear grading criteria. Barely went, never studied, still got a B (didn't deserve it). Excel Assignments take forever, but make you knowledgeable in Excel. Class is FIN310 on steroids. Good lecturer, cares about her students. Not a Finance major, but if I was, I would try to take classes with her whenever I could.

Julia is a really good professor. The class is basically just 7 quizzes (you can drop one) and some excel assignments that match up with each chapter that are really helpful. It's a lot of work, but if you put in the work you will learn a lot. She talks really fast at times, but is always available to answer questions over the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Really good class. Expect to work hard but you definitely learn the material. Would definitely take again, very nice professor.

She's awesome! Take this class, you'll learn a lot. I wish she taught more classes, I'd definitely take another from her. She is very knowledgable and knows how to transfer that knowledge to students. Great class, great professor.

Professor Chappel is the best professor I've had at KU. She really cares about her students and is always there to help, plus she's funny so class is entertaining. This class really wasn't very hard, as long as you do the work you'll be fine. No tests, only quizzes that cover a chapter or two so it makes studying much easier. A+ teacher
Tough class but fair.  It requires you to put in the time and study the material.  If you take it seriously, you'll learn a lot.

Extremely difficult class. She expects you to know all of the formulas, none are given on tests. Tests are hard, and then graded hard. If you don't know excel, you sure will after taking this class. Doesn't teach much, have to go in knowing excel already.

This class has a reputation among MBA students as being a filter for people who aren't serious about graduate school. If you put in the work, this class is doable. Anything less, you will not survive.  That said, she's a great professor, and I learned as much in this class as I have in any other in my MBA.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This will be one of the harder classes you will take in your core MBA curriculum. The good news? You'll actually learn a lot.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken. She's not easy and her "quizzes" are tests. You have to kill yourself to pass them and even then there's a good chance you won't pass. Don't take this class unless you absolutely have to.

The book required in the class has the McGraw-Hill connect program to it BUT SHE DOESNT USE IT. the assignments are tough and you can only email her a question, which is not helpful since its math. Her availability is scarce, its scarce for all teachers at this school. Powerpoints she gives out are not same as ones given.

Terrible class and terrible, lots of homework and she goes everything a way fast than you expected. what she marked on your homework is not understandable. Don't take this class unless you are an excel master

Great teacher, hardest class I've taken. Struggled but somehow managed to pull off a B. "quizzes" every class are more like exams. Takes a lot of commitment and studying to make it through this class alive. Teacher delivers prompt grading as promised. I respect her a lot. Attend and do all the HW to study if you want to pass.

One of the most difficult classes I have ever taken.  Julia is a nice lady, but very by the books.  If you do the homework at the end of the chapters you will have a good shot at half of the quiz problems, the other half is fair game from the lecture and reading.  She was always there for office hours to help.

Mrs. Chappel is very nice. This class is difficult. There is no test only 7 quizzes and the questions are usually complex. You have to memorize every formula. She does allow one open note quiz. The lectures can be boring because she reads the slides word for word. The final is a project and it is no joke. It will take you days to finish.

No-note quizzes favor the copious note-takers & algebraic savvy & are most of your grade. Travel and make-up quizzes possible but brutal.  Time consuming take home final cases from text and extra credit is to summarize a long book.  The honest are disheartened by a web full of “help” for both. ~1.5-2 x the effort of ACCT 701. You do learn a lot.
Wonderful lady.  Took financial modeling with her. Very kind, always there to help.

Boring class.  She literally recites the slides provided by the textbook publisher and nothing more. Almost no discussion. Quizzes are an exercise in pump and dump memorization, no actual thought required.  Basically, this was a far cry from an MBA course.  FIN 201 for grad students.

Difficult class, but not impossible. You'd be well served to do all the questions available at the end of each chapter. Quizzes every week, and she likes to test your critical thinking -- seems that one question a week was way out of left field.

Brutal. She goes over slides at break neck speeds. Quiz's come from absolutely any material she has access to... book, slides, lectures. She just expects you memorize everything whether she mentions it or not. Very frustrating as a student because its a complete crap shot if you are studying the right material.

Hard teacher.  All the homework comes out of the book.  Will not give you a formulas sheet, she thinks you should just know how to do everything.  Took it in the summer and she covered way to many chapters to comprehend in one month.

midterm and final are nearly impossible. tests are short answer and multiple choice. many people in my class failed the mid-term, and she doesn't curve the tests. She quickly goes through slides. honestly good luck if you have to take this class. It did NOT seem like an intro to finance class. Prepare for a lot of memorizing formulas. It's awful.

This is a difficult class.In order to pass you need to really study each chapter and even then there is no guarantee that you'll pass the quizzes & most of your grade is from Midterm and Final. I don?t know anyone in the class that has above an 80%. She is nice but has a strong accent and will mix up numbers & jump to the next topic in mid sentence
I will be winning any "I had the worst TA" arguments.
Went to his office hours he said I show "attitude" in my program because I had spelling errors in my comments. Also didn't make eye contact with me ONCE the whole time.
One of the meanest TAs I have ever encountered. Would often remark that he did this in elementary. Would leave comments on assignments making fun of students submissions.

He didn't answer all of my questions. I kept asking about what he had just explained, and I still didn't understand it. He didn't seem to care about the students. He was supposed to let us know what we needed for the first day, but he didn't do anything. He didn't look friendly, and the way he answered my questions felt like he was judging me

If you have Junyi's lab section, for your own sanity switch out of it. Labs are a free for all. There are few questions he will answer and if he does, the answer will not make sense in the slightest. I've never seen someone ask him a question and not look more confused than before after. Also grades extremely harshly. Could list issues for hours.

Worst TA ever. Only follows posted rubrics and refused to give me 100 even if I worked so hard on my assignment while other lectures give me free points based on the same reason. Have zero leniency for late work and claimed that he “only follows Canvas timestamp” even if it's just a minute late.

Brutally harsh grader. We did one of the homework problems in the lecture with the actual professor and he counted it wrong for everyone in the class. It feels like he strives to take points off all your assignments.
just switch out save yourself its not worth it

Junyi Zhao is my arch-nemesis. I think he may secretly be a demon. His presence gives off pure evil. If you get him as a TA, switch off as soon as you can. He goes out of his way to make sure you never get a 100% on any assignment. He literally had to be told by our professor to stop grading so harshly, but that still doesn't stop him.
Best Math Teacher Ever!!! She explains the problems clearly and thoroughly. Plus, she has funny jokes. I would definitely recommend her.

very nice and wants to help but tests are tough and material needs to be well known. she expects you to know the basics, as well as the hardest problems on the homework. good teacher but you have to pay attention.

She is a very hard teacher. Her tests are tricky, especially the first one. She told us she wanted to show us that Math 115 was "no cakewalk." She is nice and is willing to help you, however she requests that you come visit her during her limited office hours. Her accent is hard at first,  but you get used to it. I wouldnt retake a class from her.
Very, very hard. I got a 98 in Calc 115 but am on track to fail 116 with her. If at all possible, in any way, do not take this class from her. Quizzes and tests are very hard and tricky..

How do YOU feel about proofs that make no sense!? About 150 pt tests with some problems NEVER taught in class before?! Or your professor having no idea what he's talking about? Well you're in luck! This would be the class for YOU! Personally, I'm never taking an HNRs Math class again, but HEY! If you want to hate your life, go for it!

This is my warning. I used to love math, not so much now. He speaks really quiet, talks to the board, and you can't see what he writes in the moment because he is blocking it. Wingspan can't help. The only way I understood anything was by watching Professor Leonard on Youtube! Any other advice on here about EC or doing homework, listen to it!

Half the issue with Prof Katz is is poor TAs. Mine did not show up to most lectures after the first two weeks of class, yet was the one doing the daily updates for our lessons and running our labs. Katz doesn't provide a lot of examples, most of them come from the homework. Quiz problems come directly from the homework, but exams are concept heavy.
he was lowkey fine just don't panic when you don't understand things right away when you learn them just make sure to do the homework. videos and chatgpt also helped me to understand concepts

Homework is optional, but no answer keys to check your work. Weekly quizzes were questions from the homework, but you didn't know if your answers were right. Tests required you to memorize multiple theorem definitions and provide a proof. A poor summary of notes is uploaded after class, so good luck if you're absent. Difficult bonus problems for EC
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
**REVIEW IS FOR MATH 590** 
Dr. Katz is an awesome professor especially for linear algebra. He has clear explanations and is super available and responsive outside of class. Weekly homework quizzes in lieu of homework can be tedious and he can be dry however, if you get to know him he is a fantastic person. His numerous teaching awards shows.

Professor Katz is very organized and clear in his teaching. There are so many opportunities to increase your grade (especially towards the end). The first exam can be tough, but once you understand the format, the rest become more manageable. This class made me grow an appreciation for math, and It is one of my favorite classes I have taken at KU.

I loved the way this class was taught! Lectures were clear and interesting, and very proof-based which I enjoyed. Katz will make a lot of arithmetic mistakes when teaching, but this is usually fine. Exams are very difficult and not curved, but lots of extra credit is provided to make up for this, and partial points are usually generous.

Didn't go to many lectures and taught myself most of the material. However, Professor Katz was always accessible outside of lectures and more than willing to help and accommodate you if an issue arises. There are a lot of opportunities to make up points through extra credit or through his grading policy (drops lowest scores).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He knew the material very well, but explained all concepts with higher level math language. If you haven't done many proofs, this is not the class for you. He had a hard time doing basic algebra sometimes, but it wasn't a huge deal  mostly funny. He was organized and had a schedule that he stuck to all semester.

Dr. Katz is a great lecturer and tough professor. At worst, his lectures are somewhat dry. However, he skips no proofs and does his best to make sure that you understand the content. You will get out of the class what you put in.

His online homework was easy, but I felt like I had to teach myself a lot of the course material. He let us have a full 8x11 "cheat sheet" for the final exam, so it was incredibly easy. He wasn't the best professor, but his grading system was lenient, and he would bump your grade up a little if you actually show up to the class (most don't show up)

Lectures were boring and useless. Didn't know how to use the technology for clicker questions. I learned more from my lab TA in a day than I did from a semester of lectures. However, if you ask him questions, he'll help you out with what you don't get. Unfortunately, there are over 100 other students in the class who don't get anything either.
Hardest class I've had at KU but one of my favorite lectures

Started teaching 105 again - very organized for the first week or two. Lectures are dull and attendance isn't mandatory but you get bonus points for going. I have put almost no effort into this class and will get a B. An A is definitely attainable if you put in the effort.

Easy class. Extra points if you keep up attendance.  On the last day of class he made announcements that made getting a good grade in the class pretty easy: if your hw grade hurt you he didn't include it in the grade, final replaces your lowest scoreetc.  Material wasn't all completely useless like most Math classes are though lectures were boring

This class was easy but it's EXTREMELY BORING!!! The class is so easy, it's almost hard to get an A. I wouldn't particularly recommend taking this class from this professor, but if you end up in it, you'll do fine!
He is so awesome! Best teacher I have ever had! He got applauded as he was leaving the class for student evaluations!
if you go to class, you get extra credit. VERY easy for someone who doesn't like or do well in math. Pay attention, and it is a breeze

I don't know what these other people are talking about. Maybe in his lower level classes he is easier, but 558 was almost impossible. He was really good about the final grade, the only reason I got a C was because he made the C range from 60-75%. He is one of the most boring teachers I have ever had and spent about half an hour talking about Arthur

Here's the truth, He is very into math, so it is hard for him to relate to his students. He tries to make jokes, but he's really dry. Its an easy class mainly because its simple math but he doesn't explain it well to his students. Luckily he does a lot to keep the class average grade high (like throwing out grades). He does teaches both semesters.

What a waste of my time.  Make sure that you take this Math 105 during first semester because he only teaches during second semester.  Dr. Katz was dull and taught me nothing.  He seemed bored and about ready to retire.  Good luck to all
The class was somewhat a joke.  He knows that no one takes this class unless they have to, so he doesnt expect to much.  It's an easy class.

Incredibly easy...take this class if you want an easy A. There are 4 tests (including the final) and HW every week.  At the end of the semester, he threw the HW out if it hurt your grade and let your grade on the final replace up to 2 previous tests...wow.  Also, you get 30 extra credit pts for perfect attendence and class NEVER took a full 50 min
Great entry level math course!  He is funny and makes a lot of alcohol references to make the class more fun.  Oh yeah, and he has an example problem about grama being run over by a bus!

Bad teacher, I had to teach it to myself. Gave a couple of test that were way too long for a 50 minute period and could not answer some questions which lowered the test grade by20-30% even though I knew how to do them. Not very understanding and very arrogant when I talked to him in his office.
He is hysterical if you can get him talking about drugs, otherwise it's a good nap.  To get a good grade you really do have to do the homework, which means you have to go to class everyday.

One of my most memorable professors, but I'm not sure why.  I remember getting an A in the class, and thinking that I was stuck in 1985 the entire time, but not much else.  Certainly don't remember whatever it is I purportedly learned at the time...If you want to enjoy college, take this guy.

If you dislike math, TAKE THIS CLASS! You will learn nothing, and recieve an A. It fulfills the required math class, and helps your GPA as well. He's a little random and bizarre, but the class is interesting.
He is hilarious b/c he obviously doesn't want to be teaching the class.  He sounds like the "dry eyes" guy but is amusing.  This class is SUPER EASY!
ah Dan Katz.  God bless him, he tried.  reminded me of Ross Gellar.  easy class, dull lecture.  but I'm still confused as to whether or not Grandma has wheels. ???
This class is a breeze! He wants to give away as many A's as possible as long as you show up and do the work.

I don't know what the other reviewers are talking about. Sure his tests are multiple choice but his lectures suck! He has a monotone voice and entirely too fast with his overheads that are impossible to read. Good luck trying to take notes! I can't wait until it is over!!!!!!!

I thought it would be intimidating being in a big lecture, but really you wouldn't notice!  He is a great teacher and gives interesting and good examples.  The homework is easy, the tests are 20 questions MULTIPLE CHOICE!  Go to class though, you get extra credit for going!
This class is NOT hard, people just need to learn how to pay attention and go to class. He's a fun guy, and he looks like Jeff Goldblum! Easy material, not much homework. Take the class, do it.
No Comments
Easy, but a really good teacher, too.  He taught so that everybody would be able to get it.  And, of course, totally hot.
No Comments

(ACCT 2102 @ UGA) I think Kara did a good job teaching managerial accounting. Cool dude, and he was easily accessible outside of class. Lectures were still long and boring. Consisted of online homework, three exams, and an optional final that would replace your lowest exam. The exams were very challenging, but definitely doable.

(ACCT 2102 at UGA) Y'all he was AWESOME. He's at UGA now but seriously the best. This accounting class is very standardized so yea you have attendance questions and all the homework but thats gonna be with every professor. His lectures were really engaging and easy to follow. Made this course really easy. Super great teacher, absolutely recommend!

He's at UGA now but I can't find his page there so I'm rating him here. He's actually the goat, take him!!!! Accounting 2 is tricky but he made it so much easier than Accounting 1. He's always happy to help out, lenient on tests (he goes through them the week before and eliminates ones he finds unreasonably challenging.) Uses Top Hat for attendance

Charismatic and energetic lecturer which made it easy to pay attention in class.  The exam were open note but were challenging due to the time constraints.   I finished all of the exam within a few minutes remaining which created stress.   Go to class and be present, study 30-60min once a week and you should be fine to get an A!

Mehmet was a great professor! You should probably attend class cause he doesn't post the slides. Only graded on 10 quizzes and 3 exams. Judy Wu is so sweet! She truly enjoys the topic of physics and is there to help you understand as well! She has multiple exams, but they are 10 questions each, multiple choice. They are challenging, but not terrible!

She is a very good teacher. She really cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed so she is very accomodating. If you ask she will provide extra credit on the homework and tests. Dr. Wu is such a sweetheart! If you're scared to take physics, take it with Dr. Wu! She is so helpful and answers her email all the time! hard class only good thing is that the class is curved so that an 85 is an A

Her accent is noticeable but it never affected her teaching ability or my learning ability. She is very helpful if you have questions on the homework. Go to class, do the homework: easy A.
Interesting class. If you do the study guides and go to class then you'll be fine. The tests are pretty easy too and similar to the study guides. Don't bother buying the textbook, never opened mine.

She's really nice and really helpful. But kind of hard to understand, english isn't her first language. She's really intelligent but can't always spell words and i guess, it may just be my own fault, but hard for me to understand.
i think shes cool and teaches the material well.  she is pretty flexible and works well with students
The teacher was very helpful, and very knowledgeable of the subject. I have learned a lot in that class.
she was very helpful and the topic was interesting.
Worst class so far at KU.  Avoid at all costs.
She is a great teacher who makes the class really easy, especially for 212 and 216. I highly advise taking this course with her. And yes, she is really hot too.

I had Mascha for the conversational German class.  Even though I thought it was easy I was still constantly entertained.  She really tried to work with the students so they were happy. She has a great command of the German Language, particularly for a non-native speaker.  Plus, she's smoking.....

Pretty easy, as far as German goes.  It took some getting used to the Russian accent, but after that everything went smoothly.  Her hotness was slightly distracting though, not that that's a bad thing.

Mascha was the best German teacher I've had.  She uses many handouts and visuals to drive in important details, which helps a LOT! She is very understanding and allows most to turn in homework late.  Because of all this, my grade improved dramatically in her class.  If you have a choice - choose her.
Excellent teacher.  Very sweet, very helpful, very easy, very understanding.  Definitely take her for German if you get the chance.  Very little outside work, very fun class, definitely worthwhile.
Damn
No Comments

She's really sweet, and really quiet, seems pretty private too. She's knowledgable, and gives out so many little handouts and slips of paper with exercises, I thought my book was going to split apart! I think she did a good job. She's a cutie too!

Masha rocks! She even helped me understand english better.  Who knew there was a differnce between 'who' and 'whom?'  Plus she is really laid back about late homework, completely understanding.  I wish she taught german 3 and 4.
Kesh is a bad teacher because he doesn't he hides behind a mask of friendliness while hating everything.

AE550 is a difficult class, and my friend you must be prepared to study! However Dr. Keshmiri is the best and most caring professor I have had during my time at KU. Come to class prepared and do not be afraid to ask questions. Do not panic if things are not going well at first, the material builds in a way that is helpful in learning.

My friend, if you do not attend class you will fail. Keshmiri is probably the best lecturer I've had so far. He's clearly very passionate about what he teaches. Very derivation heavy work, prepare do do a lot of writing. Long homework assignments and take home exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: 550 is a tough class, do not underestimate it. He holds you to very high standards and will ask you questions about the material during class. If you can't answer, he will call you out for not studying. He cares a lot and even chose to stay late and finish an example problem when he had a flight he could have missed because of it. Official GOAT.

Dr. Keshmiri cares about his students more than any professor I've ever met. When I was struggling with anxiety and the pressures of the very intense junior year course load, he was very encouraging and helpful. Go to him with ANYTHING you could possibly need. He is a very busy man, but always finds time for you. Put in effort and you'll be fine.

Good: He really cares about his students' success and always answers your questions, even if he shames you for not studying first. Bad: Lectures are often unclear and unorganized. The info is presented strictly on whiteboard and explanations can be meandering. Worse, the content is not the same as the text. You have to learn to speak Keshmiri.

Dr. Keshmiri is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is really hard on his students, but actually shows that he cares in their long-term success. His whole lecture is based on derivations, so students know the background behind everything. The material is very complex, but with a lot of studying and office hours, anyone can pass.
Fantastic professor, but will make you work very hard for the class.

I adored this class and while we worked heavily with out GTAs we were lucky to have Hady, Daksh, and Arno. They all cared about us and between them and Dr. Keshmirir it was one of the best classes I have ever taken.

AE 245 was a fun class especially the lab section because you get to build an actual aircraft. The course was mainly handled by the TAs. There will be quizzes at the beginning of every lecture and a homework assignment every week. Overall a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Mullinix is one of the best professors out there. He genuinely cares about his students' mental health and success, and you can tell he loves what he teaches. His passion makes learning fun, and he's hilarious, supportive, and engaging. You'll actually look forward to class—take him if you can!

Mullinix truly wants all his students to succeed. Put in the effort to do well, and he will do the same for you. Attendance was taken, but his lectures were engaging and enjoyable. Attend office hours, ask questions, and participate in class—he's approachable and helpful when you reach out. Because of Mullinix, I second-guessed transferring out.
Professor was very well-versed in Poli Sci and kept the class engaging. One of the best professors I've had yet.

Although the material wasn't hard and I got A's on every single assignment, I still had a very low A throughout the whole semester because I missed a total of two lectures. Each one Brought my grade down 2%. Also uses + and - scale which messes up GPA. Don't take this class, prof is super high on himself and talks about his own research too much.
Attendance questions for every lecture and discussion. Engages with class but very opinionated and annoying when giving lectures
Professor Mullinix is incredibly good at explaining political science topics in a way that's easy to understand. A great introductory class. My GTA was also great, which made the class smooth for me.
Dr. Mullinix was a great professor and gives good feedback for all your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mullinix is very knowledgeable and hilarious when teaching. The topics we learned were so interesting and I learned so much. The tests were very easy if you read the textbook and took notes during lecture. I highly recommend taking him if you get the chance.
Prof. Mullinix is amazing! If you have the opportunity to take a course with him, do! He is very understanding of student circumstances and wants all of his students to succeed (but learn something).
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Mullinix is the best political science professor at KU, and most people do whatever they can to get into his classes. Very nice guy, funny, but also does a great job teaching his classes. Go to class, take good notes, ask questions and you will do very well.

One of my favorite classes ever. He knows so much about the subject and loves to facilitate discussions which make the class SO interesting. He also adds in side comments sometimes which would make us laugh. There isn't a ton of homework except for a book analysis, so just start that early and you'll be good. Amazing way to start off in Poli Sci!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best prof ever! if you ever have the ability to take a class with this prof please take it. His lectures were so good that they actually made you want to go to class. He was always available for help if needed, Be warned though he does not post any lecture material so if you miss class just have a friend that will give you notes.
