Prof. Mullinix is the best professor I've every had. He is hilarious and he had great lectures. He is the best teacher and makes lectures so interesting. He is also very understanding and helpful. Responds to emails fast and answers questions clearly and is very helpful. Only missed class when I was sick, cause I looked forward to it.
I got a C because im lazy. If you go to class and do the work you'll do fine.

Great prof; great person! Between his enthusiasm and jokes, his lectures are never boring. He always communicates what the most important points are and will warn you about specific test questions. Friendly and approachable if you need any help. Always read and show up because he won't post the notes and you're graded on pop quizzes/participation.

Mullinix is easily one of the most charismatic profs I've ever had. I don't know what the class would feel like for someone who didn't already have an interest in this, but he did a good job making it interesting. I never minded the >1hr-long classes, and they were the high points of my day. I decided to take POLS626 and POLS 512 because of him.

I was excited to take Professor Ward's class this Spring, especially after all the positive reviews I read. However, he may be a good BUS 150 professor, but in terms of MGMT courses, he is a nightmare. Make sure you do the hours and hours worth of readings for his pop quizzes, and show up EVERY DAY to class, or you will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be prepared for lots of pre work and online discussion breakout sessions. But besides that, Ward is great at what he does. He is able to keep the entire class engaged and focused throughout his entire lecture. He is very motivated and very helpful if in need! Always be prepared to ponder.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall easy class and good guy, but the biggest thing to know about this guy is he isn't he afraid to play devils advocate

Lots of out of out-of-class prep work. In class, you are expected to participate and be in a group. The AI breakouts also require pre-readings. The professor did not reply to emails super promptly, but just go to his office. He is great and genuinely passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Teacher with lots of enthusiasm who cares. Class requires lots of videos and reading outside of class with in-class quizzes every day. You only need effort to get a good grade in this class. Overall, a good class that will challenge your thinking.

I really liked him. There is a lot of group work and there's pre work (lectures and videos) each class, but it's pretty easy and usually fairly interesting. He cares a ton about the subjects and will be super awesome to you if you engage in class and talk to him outside of class. Exams are extremely easy; I got 100s on all of them.

This course is meant to teach you how to come to class with knowledge and prepare to discuss it. It's designed to teach underclassmen time management and academic responsibility while learning new topics. Review your materials and engage in the discussions, and you will do just fine. He is very engaging and passionate about his work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ken is so passionate about what he does. The homework can get a bit extensive (especially for a 100 level class) but he makes lectures engaging. You get out of it what you put in. The assignments are mostly completion based and he is great about referencing them in class. Funny guy, class is better if you participate.

You will learn everything in pre-lecture work before class. The lectures are pointless for learning, the only reason to show up is because of in-class assignments. This professor is an on the spectrum know it all who asks pointless rhetorical questions like "what is meaning" and "what is scarcity" while waving his fingers in the air.

Dr. Ward is kind, very knowledgable and approachable. He will meet with you to discuss not only academic material, but also your future plans. I always enjoyed being in his class because of his positivity & industry knowledge. I recommend his classes all the way. If you are a curious mind, his class is a perfect place for discussion.

The professor himself doesn't teach you anything, you're supposed to learn through reading long articles, YouTube videos and University recorded lectures. You will be tested on the readings/videos and asked to present at random. It's not his fault, the class is designed that way no matter what professor you take. However, he makes more difficult.
Tough class but very worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Ken is honestly on of the best professors I have encountered in the business school. You can tell he genuinely cares about his job and his students. Be ready to do a lot of readings, but that is basically it. I would 100% recommend him for any class, he's super funny, and makes his lectures actually fun.

This class offered a ton of thought-provoking material that will help any student in the real world. Professor Ward does a great job with the structure of his class and the added information he brings. Most work is done in groups besides the essays and quizzes. Would definitely recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A well put together course that I felt like I learned a lot of real-world stuff in. Not necessarily an easy class, but very manageable if you attend and submit assignments.

Great professor who makes lessons engaging. A large portion of the class is participation, so attendance is 100% mandatory. I have not missed a class, so not sure if there is much flexibility. If you attend class, participate, and do all your assignments well, there is no reason why you cannot get A or a B. Read all the required readings!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Ward was one of my favorite professors I've ever had at KU. He not only cares about the students, but you retain much of the information you learn and he teaches with clear examples that help you understand the material more.

Laura is, if not the best, professor at KU. She is always there to help with whatever you need and is so flexible with whatever life throws at you. She is very respected through the theatre/film studies program and has lots of experience in the outside world, which makes her knowledge on the matters even better. I love Laura Kirk!!
Laura is an absolute joy to learn from. Her experience, pleasant attitude, and knowledge of the business supply students with endless learning opportunities when working with her.

Laura is possibly the best professor I've ever had. You will want to go to each and every class to learn from her because she will not let you down. She's caring, professional, inspirational, and will work with you every class to help you succeed. Couldn't recommend professor Kirk higher!
Honestly the best professor I ever had while in school. Super inspiring and up lifting. There is no other professor who teaches you more about the real world of the entertainment industry.

Laura is the best. I've taken a few classes with her and I highly recommend her to all theatre & film students. She really cares about your personal career goals and will help you tailor class assignments to be useful to you. Since COVID she's been really chill about due dates as long as you communicate with her. She's a really cool person!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and passionate about the course. Recommend 100%!
He's the best professor, if you have to take CURRIC --> YOU HAVE TO TAKE HIM!!!!

Though he assigns a lot of reading, all of it is useful and not a waste of time. He puts a great amount of effort into planning classes and he genuinely cares about all of his students. He's been one of my favorite professors at KU because he really goes the extra mile. Every assignment is given paragraphs of helpful feedback to show he truly cares
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor is very hard to follow in lecture, oftentimes getting off topic in a confusing manner. The homework is difficult and poorly explained (every assignment really) as well as the class being graded on very few assignments making it hard to get your grade up. I would not take this professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor knows what he's talking about and is passionate about sociology. However, he's not very nice.

I graduated from Kansas in 2010 and took SOC 510 from ChangHwan Kim and still refer to him in 2022, one of the best professors at KU. His teachings are to real world applications that can be used in macro and micro business applications. He encouraged class room discussions with an open mind to topics in current, past and future analysis.
Very hard to follow in lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kim was really invested in current events or whatever interested him and sometimes this derailed the lecture. Also when he posed questions to our class, it was really nerve-wracking to answer because hed never admit whether or not you got the answer right. His grading is fair though and you can tell he cares. Hes a solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I would never take a class from Dr. Kim again. We had no homework. Our only grades consisted of three exams and three papers. He does not care much about his students and makes that very evident. He's too smart and worried about his own research to be teaching classes at an undergraduate level.

Took EEE 554 at ASU. Professor Kim is one of the kindest people you would ever meet. His lectures are clear, he shares notes, and is always open to questions. Very fair grader, took best 2 out of 3 exams for final grade. I wouldn't recommend this course for Data Science students, as lot of the content focuses on probability for Electrical Engineers
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely love Dr. Kim, he's so smart and cute. I got so much out of his class which has been a huge benefit in all my other courses. He really cares about our success and will accommodate individual students when necessary.

Prof Kim will help you outside of class and is very available. Make sure and know the concepts and theory. His style of test writing and homework writing is all theory and variables, very little number crunching.

He is the worst teacher I have had yet. He doesn't teach he just speaks the notes his supervisor gives him. He doesn't assign homework so if you want to learn the material for the midterms you have to do that on your own. He has open note quizzes but since there's no hw to learn from they are hard unless you prepare well.
Prof. Kim is so funny. He likes to help students and Knows that 360 is heavy and so tries his best to explain everything more than once. Great resource outside class too.

I was worried about taking a research and statistics focused class at the start of the semester, but Professor Kissan does an excellent job of making the subject digestible and relating subjects back to the real world as the semester goes on.

Really nice guy, terrible communicator and unclear instructions on almost everything. Canvas page not up to date so if you miss class you will have no idea what he decided to say or do about the assignment or if he moved the dates for them. Class is about 500 points, 200 of those being exams,grades very hard, perform bad once it tanks your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kissan is a very good person. His lectures are a little boring, but can be funny at times. Don't get the textbook, everything you need is in the packets.

Kissan is a great guy, but not a great BUS150 teacher. It's frustrating because friends have taken his marketing classes and say they're fantastic, but lectures for this class are rough. His student grader (he doesn't grade essays) is too proud of himself, nobody in the class has gotten higher than 86% on the essays unless they meet with the TA.

Prof Joseph is a very good teacher. You can tell he is invested in the things he teaches. He does grade a little difficulty, but he does make up for it with a big curve. I really enjoyed his class and plan to take another with him next semester. Extremely nice and if you show up to class, you should do well. You don't need the book for HW.
You can tell Prof Joseph enjoys teaching about Sales Force Management; he tries to bring in real-world examples to enhance to learning environment. I recommend taking this class.
Only have to go to about half of the classes and the tests are fine if you study his slides. Doesn't require too much homework or studying and he's a nice guy.
this teacher is absolutely terrible

Interesting material, no text book. Weekly case study consisting of a two page review to an article. Impossible to get a 55. No matter how well you know and understand the material, if you don't write what he wants you to write on the test he will take off points. To compensate he gives a 20 point curve (80-100A, 60-80B, etc.). Very frustrating.
an example of how vague his exams are is that he has given 20 points curve on every exam he has given. He grades brutally
He was an awesome guy and a great professor.

Interesting class/ subject but Prof. slides are vague and his 2 exams are very specific which is a bad combination. Have to make lots of little notes in lecture to make the slides he prints make sense. Case studies are interesting but when discussed in class, he focuses on specifics way too much that are not important to the class. I give him a C.

Kissan is one of the best professors in the Business School. He doesn't use a book at all, but instead discusses harvard business cases. You need to go to class to understand the material. He makes concepts that would seem unimportant very interesting and applies it in a way that will actually be useful.

Kelly is a good teacher and he really cares about Finance and what he teaches. I was in his Honors class and I wasn't sure if I would like being called on in class all the time, but it kept me attentive and not distracted in case I got called on. The exams are pretty similar to the practice exams. There is an attendance quiz like everyday though.

Go to lecture for attendance points and do the extra credit. Use the sample exam questions under each module to help prepare for exams, as well as using the practice exam of course. Kelly is a nice guy and his class is not difficult if you put in a decent amount of effort. I suck at math and ended with an A. If I can do it, you can too. Good luck!

Kelly's class kept me attentive. He's a stand-up guy and a solid teacher. All you need to know is this: Go to lecture and pay attention. He gives out FREE quizzes every other(ish) class. Study every chapter's multiple choice on Canvas, big portion of the exams. Go to review sessions, for your own sake. They help a lot AND you get extra credit.

His class isn't super easy, but it just takes effort. If you want an A just study the practice exam questions in each module, study the official practice exams he gives out, and go to class. The cold calling is intimidating at first but the questions he asks are relatively simple.

Screwed myself by not making up the attendance points with excused absences, I believe that his policy on excused absences are stupid (you have to hand write 9 pages per class missed), also MCQs are a large portion of exams, but TBH if you should take online over the summer, because both of the Fin 310 teachers suck, but he's the better one.

Kelly is one of the best professors! He is such an inspirational professor, and truly wants you to learn nd succeed! I recommend him as a professor 100%!! He is the best and is so amazing at helping you learn and is very funny! He is a very kind person and fun to get to know!

Kelly tends to ramble sometimes but is overall a good lecturer. He also "cold calls", but it's extremely low pressure. The exams are somewhat difficult, but predictable: do practice problems at the end of each chapter because he pulls MCQs directly from them. For 311, the exams are the same but we have calculation quizzes which aren't that hard.

Not engaging at all, rambles. While he does give practice exams but when the MCQ are worth more than the actual formula problems its hard to take the class seriously when learning the formulas aren't the most important piece. Good guy, so so teacher. Make sure to go to TA help hours, had to self teach a lot which wasn't hard just annoying.

I learned a lot in Kelly's class, but it is definitely tough. Similar structure to ACCT 200/201, lecture heavy with homework assignments and difficult exams. Go to the TA extra help sessions for extra credit and test prep. If you don't love Finance it'll be tough but very manageable class all in all
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This dude is horrible. Lectures are incredibly dense and impossible to take notes on rambles about random stuff. Exams 1 and 2 are similar to the sample exams. The final is incredibly hard. Smart dude bad teacher.

Kelly is a nice guy and he knows his stuff. I am not a math person by any means but I managed this class very easily. Do the practice exams and use the "sample exam questions" at the end of each chapter on canvas to study for multiple choice questions.

Not engaging at all, unless he calls on you. Slides are filled with information, however the way he drones on makes it hard to learn and is so forgettable. While he does give practice exams, he might very well change a 15–20-point question to be phrased in an entirely different way when taking the actual exam.
Worst professor ever

This class takes more effort than other business reqs. On par with acct 200/201. Lectures are done by cold calling on people, everyone will get called once. Once you get used to it it's somewhat entertaining though. He is knowledgeable about finance and always explains concepts in depth. Tests are extremely similar to the mock exams.

Kelly Welch is a great professor. His style is a bit different as he is talking one-on-one with someone throughout the class and teaches through conversation. Look at the EXAMS ON CANVAS. Almost no complaints, except no grades on Canvas. He went to Oxford and UChicago. I wish I could say more, please take his class. There is a textbook I didn't use

Go to class, your attendance is these little quizzes that he tells you the answer to. As for difficulty, I have mixed feelings. I did pretty bad on the final, but for the other two, the TA sessions prepared you very well for them. Maybe ask more questions on what's on the final? Also, make a quizlet of all the homeworks, trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kelly calls on every student in the class, and the lectures can get boring. He is a caring professor. However, he taught the content quickly and poorly. The supplemental instruction sessions are extremely helpful, and the practice exams can help, too. Overall a nice professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He did not explain basic finance principles and his PowerPoints were often unclear, making the class difficult without any background knowledge. However, if you utilize the practice exams and attend the extra credit review sessions, you will get an A. He cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

He wasn't the best at explaining concepts in my experience, partly due to the large class size. However, he's a caring professor with impressive credentials (University of Chicago). It's not too hard to get an A if you review the practice tests and complete all the assignments.  I hate to leave partly negative reviews but I have to be honest.

The professor teaches like you're supposed to already know the content. There's a lot of vocabulary that isn't defined, and he likes to go off-topic often. The assignments aren't too bad but take a lot of time. I learned most of the material from the textbook, which didn't help anyway. Professor seems like a good guy but not the best teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Kelly is clearly very knowledgable and wants his students to do well. He offers extra credit by attending the TA review sessions which are helpful. The tests are predictable by studying the practice exams, but the lectures do not always align with the exam, making it difficult.
He will call on every single person. The lecture can be dry at times, but he is incredibly knowledgeable. Makes the concepts easy to learn.

Kelly is a great professor who knows what he's talking about. The exams don't always align with his lectures but they are very predictable. He teaches through conversation (unique style, but I didn't hate it) so it's important to stay alert during class. Very entertaining.

The way this course was structured was essentially a flipped classroom. You have to watch his video of him doing the slides with equations before class, and then be immediately quizzed on that material which his video does not explain well. He spent over half of every class droning on about whatever article he found that was neat and did not teach
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Welch is a brilliant man, however his lectures are not conducive to success for the average student. Be willing to do a little extra work outside of class to do the textbook readings. I enjoyed his kindness and insights, and I generally recommend him. Though he calls on people, he isn't scary at all. 5/5 person, 3/5 lecturer.
Kelly is a nice guy, but a poor lecturer. The class was formatted poorly.

Sweet and smart guy, but has no idea how to lecture. His lectures were so ineffective at least 80% of the class would be doing homework or playing video games, people only showed up since he gave random pop quizzes. Doesn't give some formulas for exams, so type them in your calculator with PRGM, he says he'll wipe your calculator but he doesn't.

This will be tougher than most classes. That being said this class should be easy if some effort is put in. Do not skip class, sometimes it is directly mentioned what will be on the test. do the sample exam questions and it will be easy peasy.
Great professor! Would definetly reccomend if your taking FIN 310. Homework is hard but tests are easy as long as you study all of the practice tests. In my opinion a "Must Take" professor!

Can tell he's very knowledgable on the subject and is a caring and good teacher. With that being said he isn't that great at actually teaching this subject. Exams are very hard, I got D's and C's on all of them despite getting an average of 95%+ on the homework, in-class quizzes, and projects. No true way of studying for the exams effectively.

This class was one of the most challenging classes I have taken as a Business Administration major. With that being said I am glad that Prof. Welch was the instructor. He knows so much about the world of finance and is very good at explaining it. He is a very caring professor and easy to talk to. Would recommend him as a professor to anyone.

Professor Welch was one of the most insightful professors I've had. The test grades will basically make your grade but he gives you enough resources to get a high score. Make sure you study the sample exam questions for the exam! The projects and homework are easy points as long as you try. Would definitely recommend this professor.

A fairly easy course. Review the exam question examples (both multiple and free response). These appear on the exams almost verbatim. 

Even without paying attention during class, the supplemental resources make the exams and quizzes easy. 

I recommend getting the TA's help with Projects to get 100%s.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is quite difficult. Lectures are mandatory however you won't learn much by attending them. The tests are very hard unless you basically memorize the previous exam questions he gives you. It feels like a class for finance majors and definitely doesn't feel like a 300 class. I really haven't learned much.

Prof. Welch is a great teacher, sometimes he can go on random rants and gets lost in the lectures. His tests are difficult but he tells you exactly how to study for them and sets you up well to do good. He is clearly very well educated in this area and that shows through in his lectures.

I have not met one person this semester that did not get below a 60% on both of the exams. Paying attention in class won't help either because he uses business terms that you should know already and doesn't teach the material very well. You basically have to teach yourself the material because you won't understand him one bit. Take it at JCCC.

The class is taught like a 400+ level class. He makes the exams hard on purpose and does not curve at all. On both of the mid-terms, my friends and I got below 50%. He does not care about students. He expects you to know the information out of the gate and simplify the content down at all. Don't take FIN310 from him if you can help it. Take @ JCCC

Prof Welch is very knowledgable about FIN 310, and you can tell he loves what he does. Exams are pretty short, but make sure you study the previous exam questions he gives you. Most questions come from those. make sure you attend the study sessions for extra credit. He's super easy to talk to and truly cares about your success!

He believes that having a trend of low average test scores is sufficient and lacks the ability to understand the needs of his students by structuring the content around two exams and one final. By doing so, he prevents students the ability to truly absorb the information he 'teaches' and makes it about memorization rather than about learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly I didn't like him. He calls students out in front of the entire class. So prepare for constant anxiety. I hate going to class and he acts like you should know everything about Finance already and that everyone is just Finance majors.

Professor Welch is a very nice guy and does seem genuinely interested in what he teaches. For me personally, I just didnt like his style of teaching. He would call on a student and practically have a conversation with them and teach that way. Overall, solid professor, just wasnt my style of learning.

One of the nicest professors I have had. Lectures can sometimes be difficult to follow, however, the previous exam questions that he posts with each chapter are very useful for the weekly quizzes and homework. With covid, I think quizzes were weighted more heavily this semester so definitely try to do well on those.

One of the nicest and most caring professors I've had at KU. Tests are very reasonable and if you go to class you will easily be able to get at least a B on them. I thought sometimes the quizzes were hard but they don't have a big impact on your grade. Cares a lot about students learning, overall great teacher and person.

Unique lecture style where he talks with individual students for 5 mins in class. Ties to the theories discussed in class to contemporary business subjects. Great TAs that held review sessions each week helped me to master the subject. Final questions are taken from the first 2 exams. Take the exams seriously, they're worth 2/3rds of your grade.

Not that difficult of a class at all. You have to show up so you dont miss the quizzes, and he literally tells you what problems are on the test. Kelly is a super nice guy and way easier than the other Fin 310 teacher. He also gives you your tests back so you can study for the final and the same problems show up on the final.

Class lecture is terrible, imo. Calls on one student and directly lectures to them for 5-10 minutes, then goes to a different student. Maybe 10 people out of 300 paid attention in lectures, most just went in case there were quizzes. DO NOT SKIP TA REVIEWS, ALL PROBLEMS ARE FROM THEM. SAVE THEM ALL FOR THE FINAL. If you do this you will pass easily

I was in the FIN 311 course. Professor Welch obviously knows the material that he is teaching very well. He has a great passion for teaching and always challenges his students. One recommendation: make the class more interactive. Sometimes having the same format of lecture everyday can be tiresome. Add a few videos or class activities.
Best professor at KU if you care about learning

This class overall is a tough class no matter who you take it with. I am glad however that I took it with Kelly. There are HWs for every chapter which are much harder than the tests, but doable. Projects were annoying but not too difficult. Study the old exams he posts, understand the material and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Kelly Welch is one of my favorite professors at KU. He loves what he does which makes learning possibly dry material somewhat interesting . The way he calls on random students in class creates an engaged learning atmosphere. He clearly lays out what is expected and what you need to do to get an A. I'd take more classes from him but I took them all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kelly is a decent teacher, the material is very difficult and hard to sit through especially if you are not a finance major. Be prepared to be called on randomly during lecture to answer questions. The homework wasn't bad just time-consuming. Tests are difficult so study the his old test files and you'll be fine.

Professor Welch's class was extremely organized and there were no surprises. The exams were difficult, but the material is difficult.. He does a great job of making class matters relate to things going on in the real world and is good about making sure you know what's going to be on exam. Go to all review sessions!! Would definitely take again
Really nice guy, go to class and he gives the answer to the pop quizzes. The tests require a lot of studying but he provides a lot of useful study resources.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Kelly loves what he does and tries to be enthusiastic but his lectures are so so boring. He'll call on you at random to make sure you're paying attention. Gives out easy quiz points but get ready for a ton of formulas that are worthless after this class... have fun. Good luck staying awake.

Kelly Welch is a solid professor. He is enthusiastic about teaching and it shows. Unfortunately the lectures are incredibly boring and he does call on people throughout each class. Make sure to study for the final though. I did well enough that I just needed a 70 on the final to end with an A- in the class and I got a 66 and ended with a B+. Study!

Kelly really wants his students to succeed, and gives you all the tools needed to succeed. Hard to an A but decently easy to get a B or C. Go to his extra credit review sessions, and make it through his lectures. They are pretty boring, but it's important you go.

This class was easy..I stopped paying attention in lecture but still managed to do perfectly fine. All of the blackboard homework is on google somewhere. The projects are a little hard to understand but they're loosely graded. The tests are all based on the practice questions he posts so as long as you know those you'll be fine.

Similar class structure to FIN 310, he provides the old test files which helps with studying. Attendance is necessary. Textbook workbook will be required as homework assignments are due approximately every other week. Homework assignments are long but not hard. Overall, pretty easy A. The course material is genuinely interesting also.
The first 2 tests were super easy. so expected the final to be the same way- absolutely not the case. Final was extremely difficult with problems that were never taught in class.

Kelly is a great professor. He's very nice and wants his students to succeed. If you do the homework, his tests are very easy. If you are in his honors class, expect to be called on frequently to answer questions. You will learn a lot. I would take this class again.   The textbook is not necessary. I never opened it and received an A in the class

Really straight forward and i found his lectures to be interesting but i also enjoy finance so it may vary by your interest. As long as you put forth effort and go the the weekly reviews with your TA you will get an A. When it comes to the exams just study the previous exams and you will do great.

The lectures are boring but of no fault of him. he really does a good job to make it engaging, just finance sucks. YOU MUST go through every practice test when preparing for a test. I didn't for the first 2 (just studied 1) and did very poorly. I got a 62% on the first test. on the final I got an A. questions are the same on practice tests as real.

Kelly is a great guy. He will help you if you reach out. However, his lectures are long and he reads off powerpoint slides the whole time. There is a quiz almost every other class. 3 tests,  multiple choice,  calculations for each one. Projects are a piece of cake. You can do it!

Lectures are the most boring thing you'll ever experience. Did really bad on the first test, but quickly realized he uses the same questions from previous tests(which he post on blackboard). If you want to do well in this class, study the OLD test, go to every class (for quiz grade), do all the homework. If I made it through, you can too.

Kelly has an interesting teaching style (utilizes the socratic method to an extent), but his class is still hard to sit through.  Getting a good grade is fairly simple if you take the time to do all of the online homework, projects, and study the provided test files for the exams. I can imagine that as a teacher he thrives in a smaller setting.
Good teacher and very smart. Be prepared to get called on in class. But do not look into his eyes, he looks straight into your soal by how intense his eye contact is
Class is super boring and hard! I wouldn't recommend Kelly at all! Study test files as much as possible!

Kelly makes fin 310 about as easy as possible.  If you can't handle this class, then finance/math is not your strong point.  Having him in higher level finance classes opens you up to his real personality and his expertise.  Highly recommend taking portfolio strategy from him for finance majors.  Kelly might be the best finance professor at KU
Easily the worst teacher! glosses over the material and his exams are extremely tough. Stay away if you can.

Kelly is a great teacher, but if Finance doesn't really make sense to you, you'll be lost. He assumes you have prior understanding to most topics and glosses over, if he even mentions, the why you do what you do. If the class was less calculation and more conceptual and application, it would make more sense.

Kelly is the best finance instructor at KU if you are looking to learn the material and not just get an easy grade.  Hard class but do-able if you are willing to put in the time and effort.  Go to the TA's review sessions and work the homework problems over and over to prepare for exams.  Overall great instructor and great class

Only used the textbook for homework. DO the hw and projects. Tests are pretty hard. I wish I would of gotten a tutor.. His method of taking notes is horrible a bunch of circling and underlining. Class is VERY boring.

His lectures are very engaging, and he calls on students throughout the lecture to answer questions, which gives the class a more discussion-like structure, and ensures active participation in the lecture. As others have indicated, his exams are not easy, but he usually curves at the end. One of the best professors at KU. Highly recommended!

Kelly is a classic example of a good teacher who has a hard class. You will learn a lot. side note: Felix Mensche is not on this site, but I want to warn all that he is the worst teacher at KU. He teaches nothing during class, then expects you to do projects that you haven't learned the material for each weekend. How he has not been fired? No Idea.

he is the most boring teacher ever.  If you plan on taking finance 310 from him be ready to teach the material to yourself because you WILL fall asleep in class.  His tests are pretty tough, but do-able, similar to accounting tests if you have had Shafel or Crabb.  His class is a lot of work, most of which is pretty useless, stay away if possible.

I am a finance major and this professor is terrible. His HW, projects and quizzes are easy but are only 40% of the grade. His exams are impossible and are a major part. He does not curve this class but he does other classes. The TA's are terrible and cannot grade and are harsh. Check your exams b/c they take off excessive points.

Super nice guy! Draws on his power point slides while lecturing which some might find to be distracting, but he does it to highlight key points. Tells you exactly what to study for the tests repeatedly during class. He gives attendance quizzes that are always super easy as a reward for those who come to class. That being said, it is a hard class.
GREATEST Professor at KU. Material is somewhat difficult in nature, but after the curve getting a grade you wish is definitely attainable. Kelly is great, all there is to it.

Greatest Teacher at KU. Material is somewhat difficulut at times, but he makes it easy to understand. Tests are straightforward and homework is all from the textbook with the answers in the back that you can copy if you wish. Easy to get an A if you attend class.

Really a great professor. The material is difficult but you really learn a lot and he is more than willing to help you with anything you need. He designs the class to benefit the students as best as he can and will be as accommodating as possible. Be ready to work but definately take at least one class with him.
Awesome teacher but it he is not easy.  Hard tests but he curves the class at the end.

Very challenging class and Kelly is aware of this. Test scores are typically in the mid to lower D range.  However, at the end of the semester he will curve the class so that the average GPA is approximately a 3.2. Overall, very effective teacher but if you are only here to fulfill a requirement you should re-think taking this class from Kelly.
seriously take this professor, one of the best i have ever had.  Hard, but it will make up for it once you know literally everything going on in the world

Very knowledgeable teacher but extremely hard homework and tests.  Curves tests and final class grades.  Don't fall behind in material.  Lectures really don't help with the homework, he wants you to have to "think" really hard to figure anything out.  Calls on people a lot in class.  If you  truly like investments you will like his class.

Awesome teacher.  His classes are very difficult, but the amount you learn more than makes up for this.  The course packet will remain a valuable reference throughout your MBA and your career.  Can't recommend highly enough.
He's the best teacher in the MBA program
Without a doubt the best teacher at KU, includes professional school
No Comments
He was fine for 448 since it's a pretty on your own class. However, the grading was extremely delayed so we had no idea how we were doing on our projects.

The past few reviews of Paul I found awfully harsh. His tests do tend to be somewhat long but he always puts out a pretty accurate study guide of what will be on the test (Yes I know. A study guide. It's true). Also he's very willing to give more information after class if your stuck on something. Overall all one of the better proffessors I've had.

His tests are incredibly long and his grading of them is unforgiving. He rarely brings energy or enthusiasm to class and he honestly doesn't seem to want students to succeed at all. The only thing I learned from this class was from the readings.

Paul comes off as a pretty chill instructor, but don't be fooled. His exams are ridiculously difficult and to say that his grading is harsh would be a terrible understatement. You can get every answer on an exam correct but if you fail to provide the supplemental information that he specifically wants, you can kiss your grade goodbye.
Interesting class but she goes on tangents a lot on things that didn't really pertain to the topic

Class is interesting but she talks about Theatre too much (I understand it's a theatre class too) but it never related to the class. She goes on tangents a lot about herself or other topics, very hard to stay focused.

I absolutely loved her. She had daily quizzes which were all just EXTRA CREDIT for the tests! She is animated and fun and took the time to give extra input in my papers and point me toward future research I might be interested in. I took her for Children and Media. I'd take all her classes if I were a Theater major!

She's neat and her Children & Drama class playing with kids is fantastic, but she's not cut out for a regular classroom. Her teaching style involves clicking through hundreds of slides and literally shouting "memorize this!" Constantly interrupts student presentations and makes little attempt to listen & understand students. Often keeps class late.
No Comments
Expects you to work hard, but is there to help if you need it - learned ALOT!

Worst class I have ever had.  Her tests are very hard and focus on tiny details not discussed in class.  The grading system and attendance policy need major revision.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FROM HER.
helpful

Tests are really hard.  She has "Multiple Choice" questions that are choose the best answers (can choose more than one) out of 20 options.  Everything in class revolves around the feminist approach with little room for other views.  Would NOT reccomend this class to anyone.
No Comments
She is an AMAZING teacher!! Such a great class!! Highly recommended!! I had a BLAST and learned a ton!!! She is totally cool and fun!!!
Best SOC teacher at KU.

Her Armed Forces and Society class has been the best Sociology course I have taken, and I'm done with my Sociology major this semester, so that says a lot. The Sociology department is great in general, but she's exceptional. Lively commentary. Personal experience helps her make the class more human and less lecture--we actually discuss and learn.
Probably the best choice for a soc major to take stats.
She is hot and can teach
She was an awesome teacher.  She was always willing to help those that seek help.  She does not act like some prof. that has been there and done that eventhough she has.
Energetic teacher.  She has plenty of time to answer questions during office hours.  Some might not like her because she actually asks you questions and expects some sort of answer.

She knows the material and is capable of keeping an intrest going.  Would req. and have from more students about this teacher than any other.  She does help those who want to be helped and does not make time for those who LOA for half a sem.

This professor will NOT help you in any way. She gets annoyed easily and only likes students who major in Soc. If you're not majoring in Soc, she expects you to know how to work with all the data and basically have no instruction. If you miss a class or have something during her office hours, too bad. Kleykamp will NOT do any more than she has to.
He was not clear on how he wanted the paper to be written and was a very hard grader. The class was pointless and I learned very little.
Mr. Kmak is one of the best teachers you can be under their teaching during your college life. He is very clear, and such a good person. He is very understandable.
Grades really hard and doesn't exactly say what he wants you to write about.
Great person and is willing to help out alot. Never had a teacher that cared as much as him. You will enjoy his class
This guy is great! I never had an English teacher who cared so much.

This class was so fun. You do have to write but its creative writing like what would you do as a vampire. The lectures were interesting and engaging. You watch vampire movies and read vampire books and short stories like Dracula and go over them. Class is not mandatory but still recommend going. Overall fun class.
Her lectures were really interesting and she has a really cool way of connecting vampires with large intellectual topics. Its a big class, but I felt she cared about students.

The first half of the content was kind of boring but I really enjoyed the second half of the semester. Could not have been an easier class and Kokobobo makes lectures at least some what interesting. The TAs grade very easy and are very helpful and nice. Super chill and easy option if you're looking for something a little different.
Topic was not my thing but she made it at least somewhat interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Taking this as a KU core was a great idea. Being a business major I rarely get to take exciting classes like this. The material is super fascinating, and contains lots of movies to watch. TA's grade very easy and I got A's on all papers.
Easy class, I took and it was really fun. If you need a philosophy credit, take this class.

This course was really fun and interesting. Theres a little bit reading and a film to watch every week, but every lecture she goes over everything and can help out if you don't have access to prime video. The 2 position papers were fairly easy, mid term and final are similarly structured but also pretty easy since they go off of the power points.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Kokobobo is awesome!  Really fun class.  She brings a lot of knowledge to the class, but is also very open to how students react to Russian lit.

Great prof, passionate about the subject, cares about student opinions, and really gets you thinking. There is a lot of reading, but that's just Russian literature for you. Actually, by the end, there were times I found myself wanting to read more.

Interesting and very intelligent prof. However, she assigned a massive amount of reading, and there really wasn't enough meaningful engagement with the material to warrant the quantity. She listened well, but there were a number of obstacles, including the fact that a lot of historical knowledge is needed to understand her points.
Mary is one of the most amazing people I have ever met. I looked forward to her class every week and learned a lot about myself throughout this course.
the best! respected for a reason! Loves all her students and is an easy grader!

Dr. Klayder is an engaging professor who cares about her students. The class has a good amount of reading, but the discussions are rewarding. Unstuck study helped with study prep. Definitely take this course if you can.
Mary Klayder is a legend and lived up to the hype

Despite being a STEM major Dr. Klayder is one of my most favorite professors. She is truly caring about her students and wants them to succeed. There was a lot of reading but the class itself was very engaging. Take your English classes with her if you have a chance. She also hosts a house party for the students at the end of the semester. 10/10

Klayder is a great professor. She cares about her students. Honestly easy class, just submit stuff on time. Don't be afraid to email her if you need an extra day or two on an assignment. She likes when you contribute to class conversation. Definitely go to her house for the end of the year presentation, it was pretty cool.

Dr. Klayder is awesome. She's really chill and caring. I took her "So you want to be a writer" seminar, and if you're an honors freshman and it's available to you then I would totally recommend it. She cares about what we do and is very likable. Dr. Klayder is great, take her if you have the chance! :)

Dr. Klayder's Ways of Seeing class is a great course--she teaches through connections and spends more time just talking with you than giving "lectures." Taking a class with Dr. Klayder will enhance your writing and analytical skills. She is an incredible professor.

Dr.Klayder cares more about her students than any professor I have ever met. She again and again goes the extra mile for them, and it very kind and accommodating. One of my favorite professors at KU, and I highly recommend any of her courses.

Professor Klayder is so kind! I was worried to take the class because I did not want to drop my 4.0, but she grades everyone very high. I have gotten full points on every assignment so far. She also lets people redo the first two out of three essays in the class and have them regraded. I'm so happy that I was able to be in her class!

Dr. Klayder is a legend! Attendance is mandatory. There are three papers and a few in-class writings. First few readings are shorter, but the next will be around one book in a week. Plan accordingly; show up; and it'll be great!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you aren't a fast reader this class can be time consuming, and the papers can take a while to do. That said Klayder is possibly one of the best professors I've had at KU. She made me really utilize and develop my reading and writing skills, and the stories really made me re-evaluate my outlook on life. If you can take a class with Klayder, do it
I absolutely love Professor Klayder. She's easy to contact and always willing to help if you have questions with papers. This class has a lot of reading involved, so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Incredibly kind. Dr. Klayder truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. If you ask for help, she won't hesitate to give it. She really values students' insights and their individual opinions. She encourages class discussions which are very helpful for sharing your ideas and coming to a deeper understanding of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Show up to class and complete essays on time. Very caring and led great seminars in class.

Dr. Klayder must be the nicest Professor I will ever have in KU. She is a wonderful person and really wants everyone to have a voice in her class. She is very open to making appointments for helping her students with the papers. She loves different perspectives, so it is not like other English classes where you feel there is only one way to write.

She understands that all her students want A's so she is very willing to meet with students outside of class. She's super flexible if you simply talk to her. If you put in the effort you will get an A. Treat Mary Klayder well. She is so special.

If you have a change to study abroad with Mary, GO! I have never met such an encouraging, amazing, knowledgeable woman. She is an inspiration to every student who knows of her at KU. Her classes are engaging, and she listens to you on both an academic and personal level. Everyone jumps at the chance to get into her classes; don't miss it.

Mary is like a mythical creature who rose from the ashes of destruction to bring about peace for the people. Shes like a unicorn, rare for a professor like a unicorn is rare amongst horses. She cares about us like were family and genuinely wants to hear our opinions.

Dr. Klayder allows you to share your ideas and really learn different perspectives on life, social issues, etc. Speak up and really try to meet with her outside of class, she is always there to help her students. She really cares and will let you revise your paper! She is really understanding.

I loved learning from Dr. Klayder. She allowed revisions for all the essay papers, so it was possible to receive an A. She really tries to help you earn an A and is very respected on campus. I would recommend taking ENGL 105 for sure!
One of my favorite professors at KU. She will improve your writing and prepare you for the future. Very respected around campus and willing to help you in any way she can.

Dr. Klayder is so wonderful. Take this class. You will have a great time with the reading, the discussions, and the projects. She does not make the class terribly challenging. Dr. Klayder really truly cares about her students and wants them to walk out of class seeing the world in diverse and authentic ways. LOVE her! Have fun and speak up!!

Absolutely one of my favorite professors. I was ready for this class to be a typical English class, but it definitely was different. She really cares about her students and challenges you to look deep inside yourself and your way of thinking. Go to office hours, even if it is just to chat. Highly recommend having her as a professor!
One of the coolest teachers at KU. Ask her about meeting Kanye. She's a great person, doesn't usually forget a face, and really cares about her students. Highly recommend.

Mary is absolutely one of the best professors I have had! She is very much about having fun while learning and prioritizing the process over the grade (You never really have to worry about your grade). She is also the perfect professor for someone who may not be the biggest fan of English classes as well as those who love English! She's the best!
I love this woman to pieces. She opened so many doors for me, and this is as of my first semester freshman year! If you have the opportunity to take any class or study abroad trip with her--DO IT.

I love her so much. She makes ENGL 105 accessible to everyone and focuses on the thinking and appraisal of culture rather than the fine details of it. I personally hate English but I'm really glad I took this requirement with her. Put in some honest effort and you'll get a great grade. Visit her office hours too, even if it's not class-related!

Mary Klayder is the best! She's really funny, cares about her students, and genuinely loves what she does. This honors english course is a pretty easy class, but you still get a lot out of it. There's not a lot of work--it's mainly reading and discussion. I didn't read a single book and got by just fine with sparknotes. 10/10 would recommend.
The 2017 London Review was one of the best classes I've taken at KU. Mary is wise, witty, and inspirational  in so many ways. I can't wait to travel with her more!
She is so motivational and really caring and an amazing professor / woman.

She was a really great teacher, and I loved her English 105 class! I really like English, but even my classmates who don't like the subject as much thought she was a great teacher. She's very understanding, and she really wants all of her students to succeed.

I am not a huge fan of writing papers and never have been, but in Mrs. Klayder's class, she made it kind of fun. She was very open to any kind of perspective you wanted to take on your papers. If you have a specific style of writing, she'll understand and  help you develop it. Also, class discussions were always interesting and funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She lives up to the hype, even for English-haters like myself.
I went on the London Review with Mary and had possibly the best time of my life. In terms of class, she's super helpful and easy-going. It's always clear that she cares about her students.

Mary is one of the best teachers I've ever had. She's exceptionally kind and inspirational, and is overall WONDERFULLY AMAZING. The class is not stressful. Enjoy her class and be yourself, I know I felt sad at the end of the semester when I left my classmates. Don't forget to read!

Mary is one of the most wonderful professors I have encountered at KU. She's so caring and helpful. She genuinely wants her students to succeed. As long as you put in your share of the work, she will make sure that you can do well. She's the kind of professor that you can talk to about more than just class, and she cares about what you think.

Dr. Klayder is very helpful. If you don't receive an A your first time, she'll let you turn in papers until you get the A. She has a final and its very easy as long as you read the material. Awesome professor. If you don't get an A, that's your fault.

I loved Dr. Klayder! I am an engineering major and not a huge English class fan, but I really liked her class. She was very helpful and you can tell she genuinely enjoys teaching and interacting with students. She does assign a lot of books and you are expected to participate in class but she is very helpful and understanding.
Mary Klayder is an outstanding professor. I've taken two classes with her at Ku as well as studied abroad on the British Summer Institute. She's spectacular! Would recommend ANY course by her!
Mary is exceptional. I'm not an English major, but her classes have been some of my favorites. You learn so much more than how to write well - you grow as a person.

Professor Klayder is the best english professor I have ever had. She is truly passionate about her subject, and as long as you participate in class and are engaged, this class will be so easy and interesting.
I LOVE THE LONDON REVIEW AND MARY KLAYDER. GO TO LONDON WITH HER. YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT. :)

Mary is one of the best professor's I've ever had at university. She engages every student and brings so much enthusiasm to every class. Her intellectual fervor for literature, teaching, and advising is both phenomenal and admirable.

One of those teachers you should have at least once before you leave KU. Engaging class, offers lots of opportunities to be creative, very helpful, allows revisions to papers, really gets to know her students.

Mary is one of the best, if not the best freshman professors on KU's campus. She's very flexible with creativity, compassionate, and willing to develop a personal, caring relationship with her students. She's reminded me why I love writing.

Best professor ever. Yeah, the material is a bit hard, but she explains it so well and makes it so interesting. And her final was, dare I say it, actually fun. Go to her office hours and develop a relationship with her. She'll even answer random advising/KU questions if you ask nicely. Take a class with her! You won't regret it!

Professor Klayder is the only person you really need to know in the English department. She is an amazing instructor and really gets you to think about life. I went on her 2011 London Review trip and is was amazing! I highly recommend Mary to anybody!
She is one of the best teachers at KU for sure. As long as you do the readings her class is manageable. She's a fair grader and overall an amazing teacher that is very understanding!

I can't say that I was caught up in the wonder that most people observe with M.K. That being said, Mary is great at understanding that you have other things to do and hers is not your only class so she is flexible with due dates (due a reasonable extent).  In class she is above average and out of it she is very helpful but nothing to cry home about

She is kind of crazy, but fully amazing. The "ways of seeing" theme of the class was really interesting, and although it was not always pronounced, it was present in every work we read. I suggest keeping up with the readings and thinking outside the box for your essays. She has office hours, like, alllll the time too! Go talk to her!!

Had Dr. Klayder for 105 and 205. The coolest woman on the face of the planet! Endless energy and boundless spunk! Loves her job, cares about her students and makes her students use their heads. Relatively easy class, keep up with the readings and think about your essays. Fair grader. Wears lots of scarves :D

Professor Klayder is just about the nicest person you'll ever meet. As a teacher in class, she is not the most engaging lecturer, but that is only because she loves students to share their opinion and really wants to hear what they think. Talk to her and make friends with her and you will go far! Such a truly wonderful person.

I studied abroad with Mary and I have to say she is one of the best, nicest, most amazing people I know. She wants her students to learn and have fun. YOu will not regret taking any class from her!!!!!

The best English professor on campus. She engages with her students and makes her classes extremely enjoyable. Sometimes, the book choices were a bit strange, but she has experience and knows how to develop interest in her students.

One of the best teachers I have ever had up until now. Very social and helpful. The class is relatively very easy for an honor's course. You learn a lot about novels and the meanings behind them without feeling too overwhelmed.

This class was the highlight of my first semester. Klayder makes the reading interesting and exciting by encouraging discussion. As long as you put in some effort on your essays, you'll do fine. Also, keep up with the reading it will help so much. She wants to see you grow through your writing, and is always reachable for help!
Absolutely love Professor Klayder! She really cares about her students and her lectures are interesting and mostly student-led.
Pretty easy class even though it is an honors course. I got an A without reading a few of the novels. She is a fun person.

She edits your major papers and gives you a chance to revise. She will let you turn in a paper late if you let her know about it before hand. She does not grade very tough. She doesn't pick apart every little mistake in your papers. She cares almost soley about content. Do not use maybe or I think in your papers. She wants you to be assertive. ****

Mary was extremely helpful in all aspects -- in English, in school, IN LIFE! English 105 is not a particularly hard class, but Mary expects her students to be engaged and hard-working. Take this class not only for the readings, but to find a good friend in Mary.

Mary is by far the best professor at KU. She has gone out of her way multiple times to help me succeed, as well as for her other students who truly want it and work for it. I see her as a friend now and she has been a great teacher. TAKE THIS CLASS
Absolutely amazing professor and person.

I have taken 10 hours with Mary, and I wish I could go back in time and take them again just to be in her class more.  She fixed my writing, taught me to love classic lit, and instilled a love of scarves in me that will never die.  Mary Klayder=my hero
She is amazing!
Book choices are terrible and although she is nice I found her a terrible teacher

Lots of material reading to keep up with.  Class is incredibily interesting.  Mary Klayder wins lots of teaching awards, and deserves every single one of them.  She will touch your lives and you will never forget her.
Mary Klayder is a teacher that you will remember for the rest of your life.  I loved her class.

She's basically the most amazing professor in the entire world. She wants you to pass her class, but more than that, she wants you to want to pass her class, and all of the rest of your classes. There have been many times that Mary & I have just sat in her office talking for an hour about school, and life in general.

Mary Klayder is a professor you need to get to know. She is extremely enthusiasic about her job, loves teaching, and will do anything in her power to make you love English as much as she does. She has office hours almost constantly, Use them! A year after I had her as a teacher, I still go to her office hours. She's my go-to lady

I love her, love her, love her.  She is the type of person that makes you love yourself too.  She is a fabulous professor and completely kind hearted individual.  She snaps her fingers and things get done. The books are amazing and always my first choice on my homework list.  SHE WANTS YOU TO GET AN A, so put in the effort and she will help get you
really a fabulous professor.  wants to help all.  very helpful with advising even if you aren't an english major.  totally enjoyable class
I took her honors tutorial. It was amazing.

Loved this class! She LOVES classroom discussion, so everyone gets the opportunity to voice their opinion. Wants to help the students pass, so if you have a paper and you want her to edit it for you, she would be very happy to do so! Great teacher!

Mary encourages everyone to have something to say, and she will affirm anything that's thoughtful.  You won't know her opinion, though.  Your growth is her goal.  I took 205 from her too, no time to talk about every book.  Complexity increased in 205 drastically.  My writing improved because of Mary; she's been very supportive of me all the way.
Amazing.  She definitely made my first semester of crappy classes bearable.
No Comments
great!

Mary Klayder is kind & thoughtful. She has lots of office hours and is really open and willing to get to know all her students. But I heard from several other students that purposely slacked on papers and still got A's or B's. Some books we barely discussed. I think she's very sweet but a little too easy & that's why lots of people like her.

Klayder, in one word, is phenomenal. Her ability to connect with the students is impeccable, and she really makes herself your peer and not her teacher. Take complete advantage of her office hours and get to know Mary outside of the classroom; it not only helps you understand one another, but makes writing papers easier and more relaxed. MaryRULES!
Totally the best english teacher ever...I'm definitelly taking her 205 class next semester

I took my honors tutorial, eng 205, and the london review with Mary Klayder. She is an outstanding professor and woman. In addition to her teaching skills, she's a combination of a mom, career counselor, and resident Yoda. I ranked the English 205 class as a 2 in difficulty because she gives you ideas for paper topics but she actually makes you think and create something. It's harder than most paper assignments, but a lot more satisfying.  #1 influence on my life at KU - & i'm not an english major!
No Comments

Took my freshman honors course with her and thoroughly LOVED all topics. She appreciates anything a student has to say, even if she doesn't agree with the point. So long as your papers are well-written, supported and viable, you will get awesome grades. She's so nice, too, and loves to help!

I took my honors tutorial class from Prof. Klayder, and she is also my honors advisor. She is always really helpful and she is willing to let me decide on my own which classes are best for me, while answering any questions I may have.
She made me want to be a better student and writer.
Best teacher in the world.
Very interesting and entertaining. Loved class. Watch out- she grades hard on first paper. Is engaging and wonderful and willing to help outside of classroom.
The nicest professor at KU.

I usually despise English classes, but Mary Klayder made my freshman English class an enjoyable experience.  She is sooo nice and willing to meet with you any time about anything.  I would recommend her class to everyone!
Not only is she helpful, she is also one of the nicest people on campus.
Delusional; patronizing; she can't take challenges by mature, smart students; will be teaching lower level by choice forever.

She's incredibly intelligent and has a passion for your subject. Her door is always open and will NOT forget your name. She's the only teacher so far that has actually gotten me out of bed in the morning looking forward to her class.
an awesome experience will awesome reading list. I am taking her 205 class next!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Her class is very memorable unlike the other first semester english classes

Professor Kohnle does a great job preparing you for every test and the in-class activities always keep you engaged. If you utilize the learning aid properly for the exams you will be more than ok! Would definitely take another class with Professor Kohnle

Professor Kohnle does a great job at preparing you for exams. She keeps the class engaged and makes her lectures interesting. The work load was not too intense and she grades fairly. This is a good class to take if you need to fulfill a core.

Kendall is such a great professor and I really enjoyed being in her class. She really does a great job in her lectures and helps us better understand the content. It's a hybrid class so there is good amount of work that you have to do online but it is not too difficult and Kendall will work with you and help you fully master it.

Professor Khonle was a good teacher this semester. We only met for a little over an hour, once per week but she made the most out of that time . The lectures were helpful and clear and she did a good job preparing us for class.

I recommend taking psyc 104 with Kendall! She's very friendly and enthusiastic which makes the class fun to go to. She also really cares about her students and their grades and gives all the materials needed to do well on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ms. Kohnle prepares the entire class for each exam and you will feel confident going into each one. Her class is easy to participate in and I enjoyed being in it even though I am not majoring in psychology.

She is a wonderful teacher. She makes the class very interactive which is very helpful for learning the material for the tests. She is a fair grader and understanding if something unexpected pops up. I really enjoyed her class.

I highly recommend taking Pysch 104 with Kendall. She is very understanding and will prepare you for tests very well. You need to show up to class for contribution points but the course is pretty easy as long as you stay engaged. There are 2 papers but you are given plenty of time to complete and revise them.

Ms. Kohnle is very helpful when preparing for test. She gives interesting lectures that won't bore you to death. The class is test heavy, but that is for the entire PSYC104 class, but Ms. Kohnle does a great job at making sure you are prepared.

Took the PSYC 104 hybrid course and would highly recommend it. A couple papers here and there but lectures are engaging and she's a great instructor. She's a bit on the younger side, which means that she hasn't lost her passion for the subject matter she teaches. Just keep up on your assignments and put effort into studying for exams. No big deal!

Paul is a nice guy but teaches the class poorly. Koch's EXTREMELY boring lectures and cryptic notes make it difficult to learn. He doesn't go over the projects in class so you have no clue what to do. Most of the class failed the midterm and final. I ended with a 55% in the class and got a C-. If you have to have a 15%, your class is too hard.
If you are interested in derivatives, this class is the best choice for you at the undergrad level and Koch explains abstract concepts really well.

If you're very interested in the topic, he's a great teacher.   If you're just filling a requirement and tend to skip class or tune out for lecture, you can expect to be completely lost real quick -- as the topics he teaches are complex, and he doesn't shy away from mathematics.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! Finance 425 with Koch was the worst class I have taken. Aside from it also being an extremely tough class, koch's style of teaching is awful. I'm sure he is a nice guy, but as a teacher he is one of the worst I've had a KU. This is coming from a student who had a 3.6 GPA before taking this class and I ended up with a D.
Worst teacher I've ever had. Monotone... hard to stay awake... and yet his quizzes are hard af. Don't take him no matter what.

Good teacher, makes everything easy to learn and appears to be sincere about learning students strengths/weaknesses and names. Very helpful and his quizzes aren't bad they really do intend to keep you in line with material.  Best finance prof. I've had at KU

excellent professor, very clear in his teaching, uses very good examples, very calm and always approachable, his grading is on one midterm, a final, weekly quizzes and 3 or 4 one page projects (which can be time consuming if you do not know what you're doing). His exams are challenging but I learned a lot from him and I think he is one of the best!

excellent professor,very clear in his teaching,gives very good examples, makes the class sooo very interesting, but is challenging on his exams.I think he is one of the best finance professors that the KU School of Business has. Very calm man and always approachable for further understanding as well.....his grading is on exams, projects and quizzes

very good in teaching, only bad thing is that he gives one mid term and then the final.....there aren't any point for attendance, homework, extra credit etc. so all your points are dependent on that one mid term and the final (which is not comprehensive).....50% of questions on each exam comes from his sample exam and homework questions

He is an amazing teacher! He is smart and helps students who show real effort. Participate in class, go to office hours (DO IT), and study with groups. There are only 4 grades in the class. Go to lecture, he curves your grade at the end if you showed up on random attendance days. He is my favorite teacher in the SPLH dept.

Easiest class ever. Honestly he teaches it so slowly, especially the "math" part which are very self explanatory equations. He reuses old midterms, finals, and quizzes almost word for word for the most part so that's beneficial if you can find an old test file. I skipped so many times and still had a 98% at the end. No textbook, no homework ever.

I absolutely loved having him as a professor! The class was challenging for me but I went and saw him before every test/quiz and he was always very helpful and willing to meet with me whenever. The tests/quizzes are a little tricky so that he can really test your knowledge of the material but as long as you review over the notes they aren't too bad

Kostas is a mad man I tell you. Every morning he drives 3 hours (5am to it make 8am) to class every week. He takes time in lecture, has great one on one conversations at office hrs, and gives you everything you need to know for tests. You have to put in the effort for this class. He takes notice who shows up and will reflect it on your grade.

Definitely had to take plenty of time to prepare for this class, but that's expected at this level. There are only 2 quizzes and 2 tests, so be sure to study. He can be a bit intimidating in class, but if you take the time to ask for help outside of class he's Extremely helpful & makes sure you understand the material. I'll kind of miss this class.

Seriously, don't make a single peep in his class. Today, someone's watch beeped and he kept us late. A watch for god's sake. It wasn't even a phone. And if you ask the person next to you a question he stops lecturing and just sits and stares at you until you stop talking. Even if you're quiet and it pertains to class.

Doesn't waste time telling you stuff you don't need to know. Quizzes sometimes have trick questions but are open-note. Go to class and take good notes. Don't need a textbook for any of his classes. He comes off harsh but is very helpful. Great professor.

He is not very helpful in class and takes criticism harshly. Don't talk in class unless you want to be patronized the rest of the semester--just a tip from what I observed of students who did talk. Study the notes very well to do well on the tests and you will be fine.
Hard material, but Dr. Kokkinakis is very helpful and available.

While the syllabus says to contact the ta for any questions, I had an issue with a submission that the ta disregarded. I turned in a blank sheet by accident and provided proof it was done on time with time stamps. Contacting the professor saved my grade, she was very understanding and cares about this course

One of the best instructors I've experienced at KU or Columbia. Helpful! If you need help Request assistance in understanding syllabus. Overall classmates exclaim an diffiecult, yes is work, but Dr. Knuckolls made the class far more barable than the crappy platforms KU uses. A great instructor of EVRN!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: She didn't really do anything. We would walk through the assignments by ourselves while she just did her own thing on her computer. If you ever did get her to help you when you were stuck she usually didn't know how to solve your problem. She also didn't grade anything until the last few weeks of the semester so you had no feedback, but grades easy

Class was boring. Buy the online book with access code, to complete the online modules. The modules really help cushion your grade. The tests are more difficult, but she provides all lecture notes online to review and even puts up a practice test before the final.

Not a bad class. Read through the chapters for the tests AND especially her notes on BB and you should do well. The homework isn't really homework- you get infinite tries until you receive 100%. Attendance isn't really needed at all.

She is a very kind and likely person. I loved her class this year and plan on taking another one very soon. She is on the easy side, but with that said I have learned a lot more than I have from my harder courses. She is very smart and the only reason that people would not like her is because they don't like outgoing people.
She is a little on the odd side but it was a good class. I enjoyed it and I thought she did a good job.

Do not take this class with her!! If it is a requirement spare yourself attending the lectures because you will want to puke your brains out, she teaches the class as if the students are first graders, absolutely annoying

Pete was a good teacher at first. He is funny and mostly nice. The problem is he grades harder than he should. If you aren't a grammar whiz, you should NOT take his class. Discussion is fine in this class but lectures are a bit boring and repetitive. I would recommend taking this class from someone else if you can.
Simply awesome. very good teacher. Pete is one of the instructors you want to hangout with after class.

Pete was soooo sooo hot and funny and made me care about business even though before I had watched Fight Club 50 times and wanted to take down the man. Well I met the man, and it's Pete. Now I'm synergizing outside the box and reshifting my paradigm toward expediating positive emphasis in my business life.
