You either like or dislike Chad. I personally like him. By far the most knowledgeable 3rd-year professor when it comes to materials, tectonics, and building systems. The work-life balance for this studio is extremely difficult, though. Chad expects a lot, but ultimately it's worth it and stands out over the other studios' 3rd-year work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kraus cotaught this course with Professor Trefry and I was hesitant to take the course due to the negative student comments.  The course had a decent amount of work and participation was expected, but this quickly became one of my favorite courses.  As an introvert, I had to push to engage in discussions, but I enjoyed the content a ton.

Was really great the first few weeks but he's seriously out of touch with reality and listening to him lecture is basically torture. You have to develop some thick skin in his classes, his feedback is almost always negative and given rudely. He has a style and sticks to it - won't give your project/concept the time of day if it's not his taste.
If Chad asks your class to take an elective class to finish your studio's project, run. Don't do it, the elective class will be basically another studio.

Chad does not have a reasonable idea of work-life balance. He also will expect things to be accomplished in a short period of time that he does not personally know how to do. He only kind of knows Revit and SketchUp, but will expect things to be completed in both programs in only a day or two.

Not bad, not great. His teaching style is very philosophical, which to some this comes off as pretentious. I think he comes by this honestly, but it can get frustrating when you just need answers.  We had a really unique and interesting design build project, but overall it was a lot of work. Some students contributed way more than others.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chad is a good professor for Design-Build. He makes sure that people are either working to their strengths or are trying to build on weaknesses, and if you are doing the latter, he'll walk you through it. If you take him, be prepared to take matters into your own hands. He wants you to be independent and won't always rush to answer your questions.
Has very little experience and expects more out of his students than what he is willing to give.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He expects more from you than any other teacher, and has exacting standards... but you should too... if you care about what you are doing and want to do well in this world. Do not take this class if you want the easy way out, take the class if you want to learn how to be an excellent architect and can push yourself to achieve. Great Teacher.

Still trying to establish himself as an intellectual, rather than having any passion for students. Will give you a useless Mumford quote when you need real advice. Coldly robotic, very quiet introvert, which would be fine--if his job did not require having enough social skills to help others--which he does not.  Textbook definition of pretentious.

If you aren't the same style of design he is, he does not like your work and will give you an average grade. He hovers over you wanting daily progress but is useless in giving good direction. It doesn't matter how much effort is put forth he will not care and it does not show in your grade. He's a new teacher and is possibly not meant to be one.

Hes a great professor. He tells a joke halfway thru class. asks students if theyre following alright. He also hosts optional discussion sessions if you have questions to ask him. My only complaint is that his grading scale is skewed where a 93-100 is the scale for an A. I feel like that is unnecessary because the course is already so difficult.

Nothing ever made sense in the class. No clue how I got a B. Some students would get +10 points on a question while others lost points WITH THE SAME ANSWERS. Grading was never clear. I spent 6 days on an assignment meticulously checking everything & got 5/10 points, next day I wrote random equations & numbers and mixed up the pages and got 10/10.

CHEM510 is definitely a tough class, but Prof Kuczera was super understanding, helpful, and reasonable. He's willing to meet outside of class to provide extra guidance and discussion sections but make sure you come prepared with questions. Best way to study is to review the in-class worksheets and sample exam problems and ask questions!

Not horrible, but not great. Lectures consisted of watching him do problems and examples. We had 6 take home exams which were very fair and 6 group projects. The projects were definitely harder than anything we did in lecture or anything that was on exams.

Kuczera is a great professor. He is really laid back and always tells a joke about half-way through the lecture. The class itself was really easy--especially if you have any background knowledge on chem
What a guy
Good jokes. Great accent.

His lectures were straight forward, a little dull, but informative. He writes literally the easiest tests imaginable. Drops lowest test score and those with A's didn't have to take the final (3/4 of  the class had an A before the final). Rounds up grades without being asked and really wants you to succeed. Very kind with silly jokes/

Kuczera was a good chem professor, if you study and pay attention. He was also hilarious. He tells a dad joke half way through every lecture to break up the monotony. He narrows down what you need to know in the study guides he posts which is helpful, and the tests are all multiple choice which can be good and bad.

Good guy. Kind of quiet during lectures, so try to sit up front. He tries to crack a joke  every class, and once you get used to his light accent, he's super helpful. If you have any background in chemistry, the class is very easy, especially by doing the practice problems from the book.  If not, you'll still succeed with some studying!
he was a good professor, a little hard to understand at the beginning of the class due to his eastern European accent but over the course of the class it is a good into chemistry class

He's hilarious. He seems like a really cool guy. Kind of unapproachable and intimidating and asking questions in class is tough because it takes him a bit to process what you're asking and he often answers a question you didn't ask, but one-on-one questions usually go smoothly. I studied the wrong way for the first exam, use his practice exams.

Kuczera's class was one of the easiest I have taken in my whole life. He makes chemistry so easy to understand and he loves it. He is very sweet and wants his students to do well. Offers extra credit on exams and takes a break during class to tell a joke everyday. Take his class. He's awesome!

I love him so much! He is the nicest guy I have ever met! He is so helpful and really funny! He is willing to help anyone! I took CHEM 640 with him and I am retaking CHEM 188 strictly to take it with him! TAKE HIM!
tough!

Dr. Kuczera really cares about his students, and is very passionate about physical chemistry. He tells at least one joke per class period, and they're usually pretty good. He wants you to succeed, and even though the topic is notoriously difficult, he will do his best to help you get the grade you deserve.

This class was not easy, and not because of the professor just the content. He is one of the better professors at KU. He is very intelligent and the class is not just test-based, there is hw and quizzes as well. If you put the effort in it will show. He wants to help you succeed, all you have to do is ASK!! It was hard but my work paid off.

I took this class over the summer with Kuczera, he was really nice and laid back. He would take a break during the class to tell a joke so bad that it was actually funny. I had a good time in this class, and learned more than I would have if I had taken it during a regular fall or spring semester.

This class is hard. the topic is diffcult for most people. the professor is not very helpful. he thinks that everyone is smart and understands the material as he speaks. the discussion session is helpful but also humilating if you ask the question.

This class is difficult and Professor Kuczera is not helpful. He requires groups to present problems each week then proceeds to bark orders at them while the attempt to solve them! Unless you are an expert in Physical Chemistry and Calculus you will probably hate this class.

Lectures are presented in an uninteresting way and are too fast, lacking thorough explanations. The lecture notes appear unorganized, are unhelpful, and are unclear. He takes an unacceptable amount of time to reply to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The hw is important: do all of it, as much as you can including the suggested problems in his lecture notes. 210 covers a ton of topics. You want to do so many practice problems that, come final time, each problem type feels like riding a bike again. If you don't do enough problems, you'll try to hop on a unicycle. Always questions in discussion.

The material he teaches is just difficult. But I had him for 210 and 560 and I would still probably prefer him over anyone else. Definitely better than taking anything with Kinnersly. The labs tie in directly to the lectures. Some labs are hard, some are pretty easy. If you don't study for his tests extremely thoroughly, you probably won't pass

Good teacher, has a bit of an accent but still easy to understand. The material is definitely challenging but the tests are easy, mostly based on homework. 2 midterms, 1 final and 6 homework assignments, that's all! Loved this class.

Has an accent, not thick enough to really hurt communication. Only ~8 homework assignments, 2 in class tests and a final. Homework solutions can be found online often. Requires a lot of studying before tests: proofs proofs proofs

Overall a very good professor. If you don't understand something he will always explain it in further detail to you.  Always available in his office hours and won't leave until he has helped everyone there.  His classes and tests can be tough but if you go to class every day and ask questions you should be fine.  Took 560 (A) and 660 (B) from him.

Not a great professor. Nice guy; hilarious accent. Teaches the material well; it's just a boring subject. The tests will crush you. Out of eight questions on the final, I answered six before time ran out. He only covered four of them in class; rest were "intuition". It seems like he focused on things, we studied them; then tested over other things.

The materials are not that hard and exam problems are all from the notes. The problem is he has a strange grading method and I never knew what he wanted to see. I thought I could get 90/100 in an exam but ended up with 60s because "the proofs are not clear". I am a graduate student with 4.0 GPA so I don't think I'm that stupid. I regret I took his.

The professor was very good at explaining stuff. I enjoyed the class and learnt a lot. The course was only hard for me at beginning cause I had no prior experience in C++ and Linux environment. after that it was not hard. ( lots of work, but not hard)
Decent.

His lecture notes can be hard to understand, the pseudocode especially.  He'll explain if you ask, but when you're up late working on a project it would be nice to understand the notes.  Tests are straighforward but the class is lots of work--programming and written HW.  The textbook is useless as well.  His accent is funny but easy to understand.

I got an A and hardly ever went to class. When I did go to class, Kong was hilarious and it was actually not bad at all being there for 50 minutes. His accent is awesome and he explains thing very well.
Kong is the best. Everyone in the Engineering LOVES him.
One of the worst teachers I've ever had. Anyone that puts him as anything above awful is lying. Everyone at KU hates him.
He's a good teacher that explains the subject well.

Kong is a pretty good teacher. His notes are clear as well as his explanations as long as you can understand him. His tests def arent easy, but if you study and know the material you will be good to go.

I've taken both 268 and 210 from him. Managed to do well on the homework and projects but his exams will screw you over EVERY time. His idea of "easy" is not up  to par. He always feels generous by saying one chart will be on the exam. Whoopeedo. I'm looking forward to another semester with him, I will squash him!

Kong is a good lecturer. His notes are clear and so are his explanations of what's going to be on the exams. His exams aren't easy, but if you've studied his notes, you should be OK. His review sheets are excellent.
I also sense that he wants you to fail.
He's a great professor with a good sense of humor. He always answers questions to clarify things. He's also responsive to his students.
No Comments

This class sucks, but I think its just because of the material.  Kong is hillarious and usually is as good as anyone can be at explaining this stuff.  His accent is more hillarious than hard to understand, e.g. "chitting" for "cheating."  My one complaint is I think he WANTS you to fail, and that just sucks.

Took this class a couple of years ago and don't understand the hate. Kong has a great sense of humor and does a good job communicating the material for the most part. His accent is a barrier at first but you should be able to get used to that - if not, take Kinnersley.

Avoid Man Kong at all cost.  I much prefer Professor Kinnersly to Kong even though I got a D in EECS 210 when taking it from Kinnersly and a B from Kong.  It may just have been a personality clash between Kong and I, but I have taken several other classes with Kinnersly and have learned much more from her and enjoyed them to boot.

His class is extremely hard, but I think he wants people to do well. You have to really pay attention and work hard if you want a good grade. He's really not that hard to understand but he does pronounce some words incorrectly. He is a pretty funny guy and is more than willing to help outside class.

Very fast paced and very hard.  The class is more of a theoretical mathmatical weed-out class.  Way too much material to truely understand what you are doing.  If you ask a question he will respond by telling you when he already told you the answer before answering your question.  :(

Extremely smart and funny. Jokingly refers to himself as "Mean" Kong and says he makes the class hard so he can have job security. He is fast paced. You will get out of it what you put into it. Accent isn't too bad after awhile. Most important translation is "Wallify" means "Verify."
He is a pretty good professor.  If you have to take this class (EECS 210) take it while he is teaching.  He is MUCH better than the other instructor.
One of my favorite professors.  Lucky enough to have him for two classes.  Always willing to answer questions in class or in his office any time.  Also one of the smartest and kindest people I know.
Another professor who thinks he's king of the world
Translation Guide: anti ti = integer type, compina = compiler, He loves to ask about things in exams that he didn't explain in lecture.

Hands down the worst professor I've ever had. Doesn't actually teach physics she just throws equations and concepts at you with no context and then drowns you in homework assignments. Nobody in the class knows what's going on we all just plug and chug.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a nightmare of a class to endure. There were multiple mistakes per lecture it was a flipped classroom. The professor should theoretically help with assignments in class. Whenever questions would be asked, the professor regarded them as if they were ridiculous or illogical questions to be asked. She also would never clarify questions.

Homework very annoying to do, since its on Canvas and randomized. Its supposed to teach how to do the problem algebraically, but some of the answers are wrong and plugging in all the numbers takes so long that you might as well do the entire problem again. In general, this teacher has no common sense.

Sarah is a great professor if you ask lots of questions. Try to catch her during office hours and go over any tough problems or concepts. She is really available and helpful but you do have to try to get to that point.
She was genuinely the worst professor I have ev
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is probably the worst professor you will ever have during your college experience. Maybe the worst professor in the midwest. Does terrible job teaching the content of the class. Your grade is determined from the weekly quizzes you have to take. They frequently make mistakes on the quizzes that harm you and they don't own up to their mistakes

I've had her for both PHSX 211 and 212. 211 was spending hour-long class periods reviewing 2 practice problems. She's much better in 212 (she actually lectures) but still not amazing. Homework is insanely hard. Take advantage of her office hours and ask her questions; she's very nice and is willing to help. No partial credit though :(

I didn't think Rush was that bad. She explained everything pretty well and answered questions thoroughly. The problem is the class itself and how she chose to run it. Get ready for 1 or 2 quizzes every single Wednesday. The "lectures" are videos in canvas you have to watch on your own. There's 3 of those and 3 homeworks every week. It's a lot.

You are expected to watch lectures before class and in class you go through 2 problems the entire time...then expected to do 10 problems in the same time period for a test. There's 18 multiple choice tests and sometimes the answer isn't even one of the choices. One time the answer key was printed on the test. She should not be a teacher

Horrible. If you can, take this class online/over the summer. The reverse teaching system that's supposedly backed by research is awful, especially for a class that covers as much content as this one does.

Rush uses a geometric grading system. To put simply, instead of the average of your assignments being the grade you receive, your unit grades get multiplied and then taken to the nth root. There is no partial credit on anything, and it is all based on quiz grades which can be up to 2 a week in a 50 minute class period.

This class is awful. When the professors mess up, they just make excuses instead of taking responsibility. This class is easy to fail if you have a couple of bad days on quizzes. It makes no sense why a class is set up to not learn anything.

There were errors in one of the exam keys that we brought to her attention, but she told us we were wrong and refused to fix it. We even checked with another physics professor to verify the error. Extremely unhelpful during office hours, got offended when I asked for help on a lecture concept claiming she had taught it sufficiently in the lecture.

Be ready to teach yourself physics. She will teach you absolutely nothing. The "lectures" are just her giving you problems to solve on your own. You have to read the lessons outside of class, and the homework has 3 more layers of complexity than the example problems. There are weekly quizzes that make up your entire grade, and they often have typos
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rush was actually fine as a professor, her class was just set up weirdly. All of the grades depend on the quizzes, and there's no partial credit offered.  The homeworks weren't too difficult.

Rush started in the math department at KU which she will state at least a few times through the semester. In short, she can explain the math part of physics fine, but is very ill suited at explaining the concepts behind the problems. The class just ends up being how to plug numbers into a formula sheet, but the quizzes require knowing the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the physics department here is horrible and you'll find out why. lectures are always empty except on quiz days because they don't help in the slightest. you're expected to do the majority of learning on your own if you can even figure out what's going on. either take this class somewhere else or switch majors. they need to get their act together.

Physics at KU is one of the worst classes I will ever have the displeasure of experiencing. Grading criteria is unclear and unnecessarily complicated. Told the class that there are "errors" on the formula sheet so how do you expect us to use the formula sheet? Lectures get you nowhere and quizzes are all in person. Don't take this at KU. Please.

Sarah doesn't understand not knowing things. Most people don't go to lectures because they accomplish nothing but being confused. The lectures do no help. Weekly quizzes make up most of your grade. You can redo them at least but they get harder as you go.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if i could redo it i would take physics over the summer
Didn't learn

Her class is set up so that she has to do no actual lecturing or grading. Test are online and have 5 questions with no partial credit; if you miss 2 questions off minor mistakes, that's a 60%. It's easy to cheat and get an A, but if you actually want to learn the material, avoid her class at all costs. Take at JCCC or another community college.

Professor Rush is not very good at teaching. Her style is horrendous and (in my opinion) doesn't contribute to a very good learning environment. Although attendance is optional, the big idea is to do all of your classwork at home. This class is a gross version of an introduction-to-physics course because of how unthorough her teaching is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Bad
Avoid at all costs

The classwork wasn't too difficult, but you still don't learn much.  There are a total of 12 quizzes that make up your whole grade, and there is no partial credit.  There is a minimal amount of reading (also free) and there are many practice problems to help you though.

All content for PHSX210 is online but you can go to the lecture to ask questions if you want. Textbooks, weekly quizzes, and homework are all on Canvas. Final was optional. I talked to her maybe once the entire school year- it's entirely possible to get an A by treating this class as an online course. If you're decent at math/physics you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She gets a bad wrap but that's because she has a class of like 300 people so she can't slow the lectures down much. She posts herself solving most of the hw problems and has office hours like 5 times a week which can be used to solve the hw. It is very easy to get an A in the class, you just have to work a little.

I couldn't tell you much about Rush because attendance was not mandatory. But what I can say is that her class is near impossible to pass. The only grades you receive in the class are from weekly quizzes which are only 5 questions and they are usually extremely difficult.
Tough class but she makes it easy and possible to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: TAKE AT COMMUNITY COLLEGE AND TRANSFER THE CREDIT. Weekly quizzes: 5 complex questions, each 20% of the grade. There is no partial credit. Lectures do not cover concepts used on homework, just walkthroughs of vaguely similar physics problems. I should have listened to my brother and all my friends. You will regret taking this class. Be warned.

My experience with Professor Rush was awful, and it felt painfully obvious she was not interested in actually teaching. The only lectures we have access to are ones she recorded multiple years ago, that don't account for changes in curriculum and are never reflected in the homework assignments or quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: overall the structure of the physics classes at KU do not work, I learned nothing and I do not like her tone when she speaks to students.

This class was a complete waste of time, there was absolutely no instruction. In every email sent by the professor, she said to email with questions but never gave any valuable feedback. Your grade depends on 6 tests each worth 10 points and there is no partial credit, your answer has to match hers exactly or else it is wrong. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Rush was fine, lectures were step-by-step, and a worksheet at the end of class for participation (which didn't have to be finished or correct). There's a lab with the class that's a bit tougher but if you get a good TA you'll be good. Got a lower grade because I turned the wrong paper in and they wouldn't take another submission.

She is one of the best professors Ive ever had my whole engineering career. I dont know what happened with everyone else but I loved her! She actually cares about you and wants you to succeed. She will do everything in her power to make sure you succeed. Even outside of class if you have issues she will try to help you. Love her! 10/10 recommend.

This course is the worst course I have taken at KU. There were no recorded/zoom lectures that covered concepts. You will never hear from this professor. The amount of homework assignments and readings was overwhelming. The grading system was very confusing. Worst of all, I had no idea what my grade was until the end of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I got an A in this class because I'm pretty good with math and I took AP Physics in high school so this just seemed like a repeat of that class but I know some people struggled. Homework isn't hard to do online as long as you find a schedule that works for you. Tests were about covered material but still left room for your brain to think.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I did not enjoy this class at all. It is a flipped classroom, but it is in this awkward middle phase and not effective. I feel I learned nothing in this class because I was overloaded with too many things to learn and the tests were very specific and unfair. Almost every engineer hated this class and wanted a better teacher. Do NOT recommend it.

Never been a huge fan of physics, and this class didn't help. The flipped classroom led to every class being a mediocre/brief lecture with 1-2 examples and then group work (for attendance points) where no one knew what was going on. The grading system was very fair and easy so an A is not hard, but I didn't feel like I really learned much.
The participation is not required, but directly affects your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. LeGresley is so nice & actually made me like physics (which is something I never thought I would say). As long as you do the homework, study hard for the tests, go to lecture, pay attention &take good notes, this class is not that difficult. She gives a lot of extra credit & if you go to majority of the classes, you don't have to take the final

I loved Le Gresley!! I thought she was a clear and effective lecturer. I really liked all of the example problems she went through with us, and the group problems we did, too. I think it's fair that she makes class mandatory, basically. If you don't miss too many lectures you can opt out of the final which is great. Her tests were pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Get ready to read the textbook word-for-word and learn everything on your own (that's what she requires you to do)... What's the point of paying thousands of dollars just to do this? Tragic waste of time, money, and what could have been a really interesting course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher. Would definitely recommend.

This class is a joke already, and she conducted every class by discussing something she thought was interesting that had nothing to do with the class material. Tests are copied and pasted from the textbook. She thinks group work is effective in a 100 person lecture and we fill out a silly worksheet every class. Easy A, but you don't learn anything.

She strongly believes in having the students teach themselves and then reviewing in class. First of all, a 300 student lecture is not set up for this style of teaching. Second of all, this course is not something you can easily learn on your own. The tests are easier than the assignments and I do like the points for attendance.

Tries to do flipped format and makes class 100% group work, only it's physics so no one knows what is going so you'll HAVE TO Chegg the answers after class. However, her exams are literally just the homework/in-class problems with different numbers and they're multiple choice so the test are easy if you can memorize what happens on Chegg.

Terrible lecturer, clearly tries to do as little actual teaching as possible. If you don't read every word of the textbook, you will not pass because you won't learn anything from her. Assigns a handful of problems each class, she will walk around and complain about people not working but will not offer any help when you ask questions. Just bad.

She was one of the worst lecturers I have ever had. Made me dislike physics more than I thought possible. Tries to do the flipped classroom style and utilize group work in a 300 person lecture with apathetic TAs. 0/10 would not take again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Timmons is a great, highly engaging teacher! She would often have games and group works set up to get better participation from the class. Additionally, her tests are very similar to the practice material handed out so as long as you study you should have easy success!

Dr. Timmons explains everything you need to know for the course in her new pre-lecture videos! There's no homework, and if you study beforehand, the exams are relatively straightforward with a VERY generous amount of extra credit. Don't let the bad reviews scare you; as long as you memorize a reasonable amount of material, you'll be good!

Although this class was not extreamly difficult content wise, I often found myself confused with her lecture style. Most of the learning is done outside of class through her lecture videos, but then when you come to class you will be confused by what she is teaching. Her exams are not hard as long as you have a general understanding.
A beast of a class with some amazing materials that are helpful. Knowledgeable prof with a sense of humor. Videos were super helpful. Class was dope and I had fun.

Not a great experience with this professor. Quite often, some of the materials were posted the night before the class that covers it at around 7-9 PM. Lectures themselves felt more like a high school improv class rather than a biology lecture, as lesson plans appeared to be made the night before. My advice? Take 150 instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was a good class. Topics followed the textbook and class.  Exams were fair -- with lots of points for signing your name! Easy A if you study.

Ignore the 5 star reviews, she doesn't teach that well and her exams are literally the same from the practice exams. If you want to learn biology, don't take it with her. She isn't understanding and is honestly really rude. Worst class I have taken here by far. Take 150 if you can, the honors credit isn't worth it on this one.

When I signed up for this class, reading these comments gave concern, but everything was fine.  Be sure to go over practice problems and read ahead.  Dr. T will help you with anything you don't understand.  It's a good class and makes you think.

Most influential prof in my 4 years at KU. My BIO151 notes were useful in other classes and the MCAT. She helped me through a rough time my 1st year and always had a kind word when I ran into her.  I'm sure her recommendation got me into med school and I appreciate her encouragement more than she will ever know.
thank god i made it out alive.

I had to learn everything myself since the professor isn't great at lecturing and goes off-topic. Her tests aren't hard if you know what to study, but she doesn't cover the right material, and some questions are too random to prepare for. Tests make up over 80% of the grade, and while extra credit exists, it only boosts scores by a percent or two.

Timmons is a bitter old woman who doesn't know how to teach and has no respect for anyone. If you have accommodations/disabilities, beware: She WON'T be easy to deal with, and you will need to strongly advocate for yourself and more than likely report her multiple times. Be prepared to teach yourself and come to class only for the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: While she does understand the material, she does not know how to teach it. Professor Timmons was condescending towards students and would not answer their questions fully or make them feel heard. She would waste class time with drawn out lectures and assignments that were unhelpful. I would not recommend.

She gave lots of pointless assignments that did not apply to what we were learning. Her lectures were long, confusing, and did not relate to what was tested over. She was rude to students in an expected way. She made me dread coming to class and would switch how she taught often. I do not feel I truly learned anything from this class.

Dr. Timmons changed her lectures multiple times throughout the semester, and it was difficult to know what to study. Textbook material was unrelated to most test questions, but lectures were hard to follow and included a lot of unnecessary information. She was passive aggressive, and did not create a positive learning environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Timmons seems to care about her students. However, her lectures are often incomprehensible - not due to the difficulty of the content, but rather her teaching style. With a strong biology background I found myself having to teach myself nearly all content in the class. Prof. Timmons doesn't make much sense, and it's hard to place why.

She has no idea how to teach, although she knows the material. She doesn't know how to use technology and she frequently gets frustrated if you correct her. It is extremely difficult to pay attention to her lectures, she is very boring and condescending. You have to learn on your own because she will not teach you. I do not recommend her classes.

On 200 pt tests your name is worth 100 pts and people still often get 75 or below. When asked questions she either wont answer or goes on a rant that will still not answer the question. All her test questions come from the practice exams. But often the questions are worded so weirdly that the only thing you can do is memorize the answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I am not fond of her teaching style. I did better in AP biology with no gen bio background than I did in her class. Take 150 instead of 151 if you need bio. She is very knowledgeable but has NO teaching skills. She also makes sketchy comments during class that border on offensive. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She lectures over course content and goes into detail but often gets a bit behind, so make sure you know the content well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Timmons cares about her students and she makes that very clear, however the content covered in class is often different from what is assigned for homework/ reading, and different from the what we are tested over. It is very difficult to grasp onto the information we need to know and the lectures are not the most engaging.

She is overall okay, and a genuine person. Dr. Timmons does want you to succeed but the tests are simply nonsensical. There is not a strong correlation between the lectures, the tests, and the homework. This class shouldn't be too hard, but if you're taking this class for anything other than getting a credit out of the way, don't.

She knows her stuff, but doesn't know how to teach it well. She focuses on the insignificant topics, and her tests don't really test your knowledge, just how well you can memorize her practice questions. I wouldn't recommend anyone to take this class, because her tests, lectures, and homework don't match up. Just memorize practice questions.

Professor Timmons is very smart, but her lectures are a drag. She reviews what you read in the textbook the day before. Just put on a good podcast and act like you're listening. 
Practice problems are almost identical to the tests. There are so many points in the grade book that the class should be an easy A.

Professor Timmons cares a lot about her students, but her lectures are unclear and somewhat disorganized. She expects that you already know the material before going to class so that she can build on your basic understanding of the material. Her exams aren't that bad because she provides a lot of study material to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is not the easiest person to talk to and constantly seems like she is speaking down to people. She also does not help at all during group work or on any other assignment where you ask her for assistance.

Will often not answer questions, instead looking at the student as if they should already know the answer and then moves on. Lectures rarely follow assigned readings, often jumping from topic to topic. She posts PDFs of questions from past exams, I'd recommend to run through them to study, since she often just copies or modifies the same questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad lectures but easy tests

Dr. Timmons knows a lot about what she talks about, but conveys the information in a very boring way. I could often be found sleeping during lectures and wishing I was somewhere else. Your grade in this class will almost solely be determined by your exam scores, so study up! Do the practice exams, her actual exams are very similar.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zoom office hours are a big plus. Tests are hard but w a good amount of bonus. Personally wasnt able to access her online textbook w notes which is frustrating but oh well. Super nice and helpful if you seek help. Study study study dont fall behind and pay attention even if you might be bored. Reading ahead will let u understand lecture better

This woman literally made fun of students in her class. Horrible at answering questions. At one point, a student asked a question and she responded, and I quote, "Blah, blah, blah, anyway..." and continued teaching. The reading, lectures, and tests had nothing in common. She gives you practice questions she uses for tests to memorize.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is entirely lectures that are difficult to follow and never gets through all of the planned material. Is condescending when people ask questions and berates people for asking said questions. Gives 25+ page chapter reviews for each chapter (5 per test) and no other review. Reading the textbook is the only way to learn. Class is confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst class I've taken at KU so far. Extremely lecture dependent and oddly specific to very niche topics that do not contribute to overall learning. Lectures are not structured or well paced and extremely, extremely confusing. I learned nearly nothing in this class. Most exams pull from the practice exams, however.
This class sucked all the joy out of what used to be my favorite subject. Dr Timmons literally bored me so much I changed my major.
Professor Timmons was the worst teacher I had at KU. The lectures are very confusing and often are not related to what is on the exams.

A few exams make up almost all of your grade, however there is lots of extra credit. The practice exams are extremely similar to her exams. However, her lectures are extremely confusing and hard to follow. I often left class more confused than when I came. I never really knew what my grade was in the class until the end-Canvas was not accurate.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Seems bothered when people ask questions about her lectures. Her pacing is all over the place. No consistent test format. The amount of effort you have to put in to get a half decent grade is atrocious. Super unhelpful when you ask questions. Attending lectures makes things more confusing but she makes still attendance mandatory.

Terrible experience for an upper level class. 90% of your grade was determined by 3 exams. Extremely unorganized, never uploaded lectures, and showed up late to our final. I stopped showing up to class because it confused me. I found it easier to figure out the material on my own.

Very disorganized, emails back extremely late (if at all), doesnt seem to care about students success or failure. Honestly just doesnt seem like they want to be teaching. Least they could do is check their email, but nope. Also waited until night before class started to even upload any info about the course. Just an overall terrible experience.

Dr. Timmons is an amazing prof who cares about her work as well as the people in her class. I took Biol 350 the summer between my sophomore and junior year of high school, and even without most of the background knowledge needed for the course, I got a high B - that's how well she explains the material. Because of her, I decided to come to KU.
Practice Exams are awesome!

Great class.  Powerpoints are provided before class.  In class problems and breaks help with the long classroom hours.  Timmons is a kind and intelligent professor who provides thorough explanations along with interesting  real world examples and career opportunities related to topics.  REALLY helpful with office hours ?s. Practice Exams a must-do.

This is not the typical pre-packaged, class-in-a-box that you normally find at KU. She obviously put thought and effort into organizing materials that will help you understand the function of your cells & genes, which is great because the text is waaay too dense.  Loooooved the class and I learned A LOT!  Great preparation for grad school.
Treats students like we are a bunch of dumb-asses.  She actually chuckled once when I asked her a question.

She is an awesome teacher who loves to help her students. She is super easy. Just make sure to study her practice exam packets because those are SUPER HELPFUL!! If you do that, you will definitely get an A in the class.

Very poor lecturer. Powerpoint slides are useless. I felt like I had to try incredibly hard just to learn simple facts and concepts because her rambling lectures about experiments just confused me. You learn in this class from the practice tests because that's the only time you can get even half coherent information from her.

She treated us like real scientists who want to understand how knowledge is acquired.  Most exam questions come from practice exams, so it's impossible to fail.  Exam questions are actually informative.  I learned a lot in this class.

One of the most useless classes I have taken a KU, and there are quite a few of those. Timmons drones on and on about random experiments that turned out to be wrong - not actually teaching anything useful. Get to the point. Get to the biology. Get to learning how to teach.

Doesn't know how to teach. She teaches techniques - not actual biology. What she fails to realize is that not everyone is going to grad school, so the techniques become useless. My suggestion is to teach the biology - the techniques can be learned by doing, in an actual laboratory, not in a classroom. Also, stop jumping around topics so much.

Timmons is a nice lady, but an awful lecturer. She just starts rambling about techniques and procedures without any introductions or transitions. Her powerpoints are all pictures and useless for reviewing. She'll spend an hour on something and it won't even be on the test. Exams are out of 25 points even if they're 6 pages long. Awful class.
Dr. Timmons is my favorite professor in biology.  I changed my major because of this class.

Dr Timmons is the nicest professor! She wants everyone to get an A. Generous with her time, explains things well & tries to make class enjoyable with stories, music & videos. Complex material that requires work. Keep up & you'll do fine. Focus on the PPTs, practice exam & other problems.  I used the reserved text & found reading material online.

Excellent A#1 class. Prof Timmons was extremely helpful and patient, in and out of class.  Practice exams helpful and essential.  Textbook useful but not entirely necessary.  This is the best Genetics class around--if you can keep up in the summer 'cause Genetics is not easy,  The focus on recent technology was awesome!  I would take it again.
the class was recommended to me and I would recommend it to others.  helped me get into med school! expect to put in some effort at times.  good mix of topics--last 2 weeks rocked!

I specifically created an account on here to inform other students about this instructor. Timmons DOES NOT CARE about her students. As many have said, her tests are very poorly worded, she gave bad lectures (and I thought Ward/Hallberg were bad when I previously took it!)  READ THE BOOK, don't bother paying attention! Altogether terrible.

This was one of the worst teachers I have ever encountered at KU.  Her lectures are dry and boring and she constantly says one thing and then goes back and says another.  Her tests were fine but worrded poorly. What bothered me the most is she seemed uncompassionate and didn't care about her students at all. Take this from someone else.

I enjoyed this teacher. She really seems like she wants to the students to learn. If you go to class and do the homework you'll be fine. Definitely study the practice tests for a few easy points. All in all I think she's a good teacher. Stupid kids asked dumb questions just to make her look bad. She knows what she's talking about.

her lectures are extremely boring and very jumpy. i often sat in her class bored and confused. thus i relied on my textbook. attendance is mandatory. homework is guaranteed perfect score. her exams aren't extremely hard. study off old exams and do the readings. took this course summer 08 and got a B.
don't take her class if you want to learn anything

Seems bright, but lacks communication skills. PP slides often as unintelligible as the lectures.Skips around the book a TON. If you can't learn from a book, this class WILL be hard because she does not convey concepts well. Exam questions are HORRIBLY worded and misleading--makes tests harder than the the material should dictate. Wouldn't recommend

** seating chart put me near the One we?re all avoiding! Easy class for my superior intellect but some work required. Has a desire for students to learn. Answers tons of questions which is annoying. She?s the real deal & truly helpful but ruined my summer. She made it interesting, just not the fun I?m looking for.  Solid class, so it's a thumbs-up.

lectures are very confusing because she jumps around a lot and talks about irrevelant stuff. her word choice on exams is terrible. the exam material itself isn't difficult, its just the way she words it. so good luck if you take this class.

Horrible teacher. Confusing, lectures and homework do not coincide at all. Jumps around from section to section instead of teaching a book. Tries to make it easy to follow, but ends up confusing most students.
i highly recommend this class.  timmons will walk you thru each step whether you need it or not.  one of the easiest and most interesting bio class i've taken. and one of my favorites.

Powerpoints and homeworks available weeks in advance.  Exams are very fair.  Unlike other classes at KU,You know what to expect from this class from the beginning.  I would highly recommend this class.  but you'll have to work for an A.

worked mybut off but learnd a lot.  youll have to keep up to get a good grade. lectures are important because some of the stuff is not covered in the text. VERY knowledgable prof and also helpful. really wants students to learn ALL the stuff. beware, theres a lot of it.

I would recommend this class.  Prof tries hard to make the material interesting,explains well,and helpful outside class.Tons of work tho--work all the practice exam problems and youll do ok.  Exams emphasize material in lecture so go to class.
tough lady!
She reads from a script, flyes over material and actually tries to explain things by saying "blah blah blah" change in transcription? What the hell lady? One of the worst teachers in biology.
Good prof.  Reasonable.  Don't expect a cake walk though.

very helpful after class, even after the semester was over. Gave helpful pointers that helped me keep on track. in-class demos and experiments were great, although I would havel liked more. Exam questions came from lecture material, homework problems and practice exams. She IS the queen!

Most difficult class I've ever taken!  thankfuly, prof was organized.  I loved having the lecture slides and homework one week in advance. And after slopping all over campus this fall to pick out my exams from piles off of the floor, i appreciated having my papers handed back to me face down in biol350. prof also nice and rediculously intelligent.
summer course rocks she shortens the info and makes stuff really easy!!!
If u wanna get an easy A in this course i recommend taking her class. Her exams are really easy and contains 30% from the sample exams. Also the HWs are 100% mark in her class.

She assigned seats for us. The confusing lecture is not helpful and she does not check if the homework materials are covered in the lecture (they were covered the next day sometimes). She does not care what you ask (answered "do the problems" and told a long story when asked about the format of the exam). Yes she wants to be the QUEEN!
No Comments
Lectures are confusing.  Test are confusing.  She is very inteligent, maybe too much for an introductory genetics class.
She is very knowledgeable, but not the most articulate professor.  She's not a pushover, but seems a bit inflexible at times.  She can probably be a great teacher, however, if given the chance.

She's a new teacher (2003), although very knowledgeable she's still DISCOVERING how to teach. Lectures are incoherent and don't answer "why",tests are phrased dubiously. She tries however, but not a good teacher yet. Reliance on book is NECESSAR

Dr. Lindsey is a great professor. The assignments aren't "due" until the end of the entire course and he doesn't dock late points but there are various assignments that are more time consuming. He's very knowledgable on what he teaches and the course work wasn't difficult as it mostly was reading/watching something and taking a quiz on it after.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring since it's online and he's just mainly talking really slowly. Read his syllabus, it's the best way to succeed in this course. He's good at responding back to emails. Just stay consistent with the course material and you'll do fine. The textbook is recommended but he mainly covers enough in the lectures for the quizzes.

Very knowledgeable, lectures are either super interesting or super boring, no in-between. Attendance is taken, but you can still miss several classes, and he won't care. As long as you show up regularly and show some effort in the tests/assignments, he seems to give you an A regardless of your actual score in the class. (I should have gotten a B-).

Professor Lindsey is probably my favorite from this semester. He clearly cares about his subjects and really genuinely seems to care about what his students have to say during discussions. Most people in my class agree he's adorable because he gets very excited and passionate over little things. Show up and turn stuff in, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: All homework is extra credit, but do all of them because it's really easy and helps prepare you for the tests! You could fail an entire exam (there are 3) and still get over a A by doing the extra credit assignments. He's very knowledgable and his tests were easy if you read the textbook as you go along in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The lectures were long and drawling, he is very very passionate about his subject and expects students to know what he knows and feel what he feels.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Lindsey truly knows his stuff. He's very passionate about his studies and if you truly listen his lectures are pretty interesting. Class is super easy with no homework at all. His tests are structured weirdly but you'll get used to it. Overall, he's super sweet

This class was a breeze. While a bit dull at times, Professor Lindsey makes his expectations really clear from the start. The only grades came from exams, which were in 3 parts. He gives you tons of choices on them so you can choose what you're good at and write about that. Really nice guy, pretty relaxed grading. Easy A as long as you show up.

Professor Lindsey is a nice guy and he is really understanding and cares for his students. His lectures are sometimes a bit boring but you are willing to listen, you will learn a lot of interesting things. Tests are okay, it will be easy if you read the book or listen carefully in class, study the images and keywords are the most important things.

Going to class never feels like a chore. Makes the syllabus with you in class. I occasionally skip class on the reg but as long as you show up most of the time he either doesn't notice or gives you a pass. He hated taking tests as a kid so his tests are made for you to succeed. Literally just show up and let him ramble at youA+ every semester.
Lectures are boring, sometimes interesting. He really knows his stuff though. Overall the class was okay. Easy because of extra credit

A very good professor. His lecture is a bit boring but if u listen him carefully, u will find some stories he tells are very interesting. I never took  notes from the lecture but just enjoy listening the stories. The tests are OK, strange format but acceptable. Spend 6 hours on reviewing key words and PPT, u will easily pass the class and get an A.

His exams have a weird format, but he's very helpful and the class is easy if you study the lecture notes he puts online and do all of his extra credit. One of the easiest humanities classes at KU and you will learn something new.

If you go to lecture and take decent notes, this class is fairly easy. Dr. Lindsey is slightly confusing at times, but he is super nice. You need to actually study for the tests. They are a bit difficult, but 20 or more of the points on the test count as extra credit.

He is very sweet, passionate, and really knows his stuff! I loved the way he took confusing foreign concepts and compared them to American ways to help the class  understand them. Tests are a bit difficult, but he has review sessions that are very helpful!

He's a very nice man. His class is difficult but if you show up and take notes you will be fine. You will struggle if you dont come to class because the tests are pretty difficult. He uses an odd format for exams but all of the questions are straight from lecture. Honestly, just talk to him he's very nice.

Awful.  I'm taking his class now and I'm completely lost and I don't even care.  He doesn't follow any kind of intelligent format for the class, like a time line.  I haven't taken an exam yet, but if they weren't take home, I would have dropped this class weeks ago.  It's so worthless, I'm learning nothing.  Don't take Religions in Japan!

This class is really easy if you show up and pay attention during lectures. Grades are based on 3 tests, but there is a lot of extra credit, so it's not bad. He gets really nervous at times causing him to stutter, shake, and turn really red. The course material is interesting, but he's not the best at carrying it into his lectures. Easy GenEd.

He is so boring. And his tests are IMPOSSIBLE! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! His tests are the hardest thing ever, literally the hardest test I've ever taken in my life.. The format is matching, short essay, multiple choice with two answers for each, fill in the blank, and identifying images and pictures. I repeat, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

Worst religion teacher I have ever had. Unclear on expectations, and doesn't usually go over all material on tests. Mumbles and goes on tangents when lecturing making it hard to keep track of what he wants you to know. Seating charts and attendance are mandatory.Don't bother sending email questions about test the TA won't give you a straight answer

Worst religion teacher I have had. He tends to divert from lecture and drones on about irrelevant things. Unclear about what he expects you to know. He will dock points from a test if the class does "too well" in his opinion, so don't be surprised if he takes off 15-20 points just because he feels like it.He somehow managed to make religion boring!

go to class and pay attention and you'll get an A. he almost always lectures with either his eyes closed or while looking at his shoes. if you have a question don't bother to raise you're hand because he won't look at you. he is very helpful and nice outside of class. he seems bitter/jaded towards his field of study, but he's quite knowledgeable.

Took him for East Religions. He makes his own notes for the lectures. The textbook just goes into further detail about the lecture but their version won't be on the test. You have to read the excerpts/passages. He goes over them and explains in class but you write your own notes over them. Exerpts/passages are a big part of the test.

He is really a nice guy, warm heart and happy to help you. However, multiple choice has 2 answers need to circle, short answers are from the notes.The first section confused most people, but the second and third part will be easier. He does give curve at times.  I dropped after taking the first exam, now I'm regretted. My advice: talk with him!

Impressive teaching style and very helpful with student questions. Many test questions come from the lectures, and address concepts, not just memorization, so web-surfing in his class and internet outline banks are not helpful.  Attendance and note-taking are critical to doing well. Overall -- kind professor, respects students, excellent class.

He is very into what he teaches. Must go to class (assigned seating and attendance). His tests are difficult and notes can be confusing. He does put up studyguides on a certain website but students have to buy them! :(
REALLY nice guy, great teacher, and really knows his stuff. Tests are difficult, but if you take notes, and study you'll do fine! Definitely recommend him for a teacher.
REALLY nice guy, great teacher, and really knows his stuff. Tests are difficult, but if you take notes, and study you'll do fine! Definitely recommend him for a teacher.
Class is enjoyable and interesting. Professor Lindsey is very nice and is enthusiastic about the subject. Attendance is mandatory and is taken daily. Tests are easy if good notes are taken in class.
very informative

The Grading Scale for this class is tough.  An 'A' is a 93-100% and a 'B' is a 92-83%.  He claims this was his high school grading scale, and he decided to use it because he didn't think it was fair that a student could recieve an 89.5% and it would round up to an 'A'.  The tests and quizes are not hard as long as you go to class and take notes.
This class is over super interesting material! Take this if you want a better understanding of Japanese religious thought in a historical context. The prof. is really nice and interesting and smart.
Wastes a lot of time.  Doesn't clearly explain  things.
Sweetest guy! Always willing to help. listens to student's needs, fair, personable, honest, overall great prof! Talks to you not at you.

I loved her 200 class! Just be prepared for a lot of work outside of class time. Don't take the class if you're not actually passionate about photography; because she is, and she expects you to be as well. Prepare to have your work discussed and analyzed in many class critiques. They can be harsh, but so valuable if you truly care.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Lilly is super cool! I really want to take more classes with her. Her feedback and discussions are super helpful and positive. Just make sure to participate.

The project briefs can be confusing, so ask questions if you don't understand something. Some assignments have a very short turnaround and require outside materials, so be ready to be crafty.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Just a ridiculous amount of work for a 101 class. Gave an entire project to work on during spring break. Because thats exactly what I want to be doing while on vacation! Your assignments! I wonder if Lily is doing much work over break, my guess is no given the fact she is 3 weeks behind on grading.

Extremely woke. Will be forced into group work and presenting even though it has absolutely nothing to do with photography. I dread showing up to this class because its complete nonsense. She acts like you have insane amounts of free time to be wondering around snapping pictures but in reality I have other classes that actually are important.
Lilly was a good professor, sometimes would wonder off into a yapping session often but no big deal. Critical of people's work and she will tell you how it is. Would take her class again
She was super validating and made everyone in the class feel proud of their work. Most work was in class. She did a great job of including photography skills mixed with photography history.

I did not love the class but I loved Lilly. She was a very personable teacher and very vocal on behalf of her students when we had an issue with the way an assignment was presented to us or expected to be done. It seemed like she was kept out of the loop sometimes from Kent and Mark but she was very lovely to have as a studio professor.
She is an amazing professor, was definitely understanding with situations that came up and I loved her personality!!
Really nice, doesn't really make you pay attention or require attendance which is good because the content is pretty boring. Easy grading since art is so subjective. Would take again if available.

was a wonderful, kind, and understanding teacher who made the material fun. had clear grading (beware of pdf and jpg names) and always outlined the assignments clearly. was also very relatable and not super strict

Personally not my favorite. Easy class overall but really boring and not a lot of participation opportunities. You present projects in front of my class usually against your will but overall not terrible.

Took photo for a core goal when im a pre med major and LOVED it. you have to have a camera but it was a fun class. She was an easy grader bc everything you turn in can be artistic in a way basically an easy A. She was really caring and thoughtful about missing class/ late assignments. 110% Recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor became somebody I ended up talking to and meeting with outside of class time just because she was caring and wanted to help me succeed. Would 100% recommend

One of if not the best professor I've had at KU. Her class is very engaging and applicable to the real world. If you ever need help she is very willing to meet outside class. I would take another one of her classes!

Lisa is a caring professor that is very fun and keeps the class lively. I always enjoy attending Lisa's class and would suggest this class to anyone wanting to learn more about entrepreneurship. She is always very helpful when it comes to understanding assignments and is accommodating to students needs!

Lisa is a very caring and understanding professor. She understands if you need to take a day off or if you are struggling with your classes. She is one of the best professors and is always there for you.

Lisa is my favorite professor I have taken at the University of Kansas. She genuinely cares about her students and makes herself very available for extra help. Students are always in her office as everyone loves her. Show up and do your work and you will get an A in this class.

Lisa is my tutor and she is OUTSTANDING. She genuinely cares about her students and wants you to do well in their classes. I have never met a professor that cares about their students as much as she does. She is always willing to go the extra mile to make sure her students are prepared for tests, quizzes, and homework.

- Takes attendance manually at the beginning of class. - doesn't really pay attention to the people in her class. - Rambles and goes off topic frequently. - incisistent due dates - Graded assignments twice, once in the middle and once at the end of the semester. - Does half the work for you, then changes her mind and decides it's wrong, lost pnts
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: No tests. However, lengthy case study projects every week that you will never discuss in class. Gives long lectures, doesn't try to engage with students during lectures. There's better electives to take if you want to learn modeling and finance.

Lisa is one of my favorite teachers I have taken at Edwards Campus.  She gives 0 tests, 0 quizzes, all you have to do is buy a 50 dollar course pack of articles and read them throughout the semester and do a few homework assignments, one big group project at the end but it is easy!  Take her you will be happy you did!

I love Lisa. She is super down to earth and very helpful. She is also very easy going. Her ENTR 302 class does not have any tests. Although she takes attendance, she gives you 3 freebies to miss class because she understands things come up. I would recommend taking her class.
I don't know how Lisa can have so many low scores. She's hilarious, knowledgeable and will bend over backwards to help you.

I have never made a review, but Lisa is one of the best professors at KU! Along from being incredibly smart she is down to Earth and kind! She lays out the semester in the beginning to go at your own speed, but she still teaches you along the way and she is ALWAYS there for you to help. She is extremely fair so you will get the grade you deserve!
Lisa is awesome! Gives lots of extra credit for those who care about their grade. Showing up is a must if you want extra credit. I ended up with 40+ points at the end bumping me from a B to an A

GO TO CLASS! She likes to reward students for coming to class and at least once a week there was extra credit or a quiz, which consisted of writing your name on the paper. Exams are difficult and you will need to study, but there's no reason you can't get at least a B in the class.

I loved Lisa as a professor. She is very helpful. I did go to office hours for almost every homework assignment and the TA's were helpful as well. She wants to see her students do well, as long as she knows your trying you'll be fine. Gives out lots of extra credit too!
She makes it so boring and impossible to pay attention during class. The work is pretty straight forward but taking this class from her is just not fun and I dreaded going to class every time.

No textbook but there's a slide packet you need to purchase. There will be a total of 12 assignments for in-class quizzes and homework and if you don't get up to that much she just gives you 100s on the rest. No +/-. 3 exams that if you are happy with you don't have to take the final (cumulative). If you study you can get an A

I took her class in the summer. I hate finance, but she kept the class interesting and understandable. She's really funny and easy-going, and she also helps as much as she can if anyone is lost in the material. It's an easy class if you show up everyday and just do the homework.

Seriously one of my favorite professors at KU! I don't understand why people are saying that she isn't helpful cause shes always there for help. Very nice lady and is very laid back. Pretty simple material and you'll actually use it in the real world. Highly recommended!

Probably one of the least helpful professors. She used to teach the basic finance class, a very good reason she doesn't. Very incoherent but will blabber on all through the lecture, hardly taking questions and rarely answering them well. Avoid her if you can.

I took this class for my business minor. Lisa is a great teacher, and an A is really easy to attain (I got 99%) as long as you go to class every day, complete the homework, and study for exams. She also gives out a lot of extra credit just for going to class.

Lisa was pretty easy going, very laid back, very nice. I did see in a previous comment about the amount (or whether at all) of help one would receive was paralleled by the brand that they wore, and I completely agree. Overall, her TA's were pretty laid back, but a couple of them were a little arrogant.

The best advice I can give is to take this course during the summer!She is very easy-going and so are the TA's.Memorize the slides and know the concepts for the first test,attend class because there are in-class quizzes and answers to extra credit on exams.

I was a little hesitant taking Finance from Lisa but she makes it very possible to get an A. She offers extra credit for almost everything including just showing up to class. Just make sure to show up, take notes, and get help if you need it and you can easily pass the class.

This class wasn't easy, but Lisa makes it very possible for everyone to get an A. GO TO CLASS. I went everyday and almost had 40 extra credit points at the end, which is about half of a letter grade added on. The tests were a bit long but she tells you what each question is worth, so start at the ones worth the most and work your way down.

she is an intelligent person and seems to want the best for her students. i would be lying though if i said the help i received was not do some degree impacted by the brand of shirt i wore. midwestern prep days, great help and very encouraging. if not, good luck getting her attention over the frat party that was her syllabus listed office hours.

She's just a bad person. She's unbearable, unorganized, incomprehensible, and should be fired. She's teaches a relatively simple class but makes it difficult because you have to deal with her. I would avoid her if you could.

She is the reason, symbolically speaking, why the business school has lost its prestige. She does not know how to teach at all, she just talks without ever putting across the concepts clearly, and their are always trick questions on the test that are never presented beforehand. Her idea of teaching is just saying in so many words "do algebra". Badd
This INTRODUCTORY class is ridiculous. There material is not that hard to grasp if you really look at it but the way she explains it and word it on the exams makes this extremely difficult.

I once enjoyed finance and looked forward to my upcoming internship for the summer regarding the subject.  This has all changed after taking this class. GOOD LUCK. The manner in which she teaches the class is uncalled for and uncontrolled.  She's an immature person and is not level headed or fair at all.  First B I've gotten in school.

Lisa made her class harder this year to avoid getting canned, and congrats, Lisa, you did it -- grades are lower than ever. Why? Because she won't answer questions on her new projects, uses lecture to tell her life story (Zack/Hallmark), and subtracts bogus points. Like what, u ask? I lost 10% on HW for not underlining my last name. Total B!a+Ch.

This class is only hard because of the way Lisa runs the class. The material itself is not very difficult.  The grading is absolutely ridiculous. Lisa just looks for reasons to take away points.  Your grade in this class will probably not reflect your knowledge of the subject, but how well you can read her mind.

Lisa is very knowledgeable about the finance field. She simply doesn't know how to teach. Her TA's also don't understand that it is a basic business course; grading like a major capstone course. Overall, this is the worst class/teacher/TA's I've ever had!

By far and a way the worst business teacher in the school of business. Not only does she have no idea how to teach the material but she is paranoid but thinks she is GOD. On the tests the TA's grade them like its a Graduate thesis, taking off for not boxing your answers or writing $ signs and also have no idea how to help at all. Good Luck

For the course level she's teaching, she's not that great of a teacher. For what's suppose to be a junior level course, her class covers really basic concepts regarding finance. This would be nice but she's really hard to understand, nor is she or her TA's very approachable after class.

Lisa is an intelligent person but teaching isn't for her. She doesn't really explain anything well and the lecture notes you're required to purchase are quite useless. She's also extremely strict on grading, if you don't do things exactly as she taught it in class then you won't get full points.

Felt as if I was better off teaching myself. Her class isn't difficult, she makes it that way because she's difficult. Half your grade is just learning how to deal with her. Her exams especially, she puts word limits on free response questions, counting off if you go over. She's completely inflexible and anal about everything.
If you understand and can work out the problems in the homework you will be fine. Might use outside study materials, does not teach some stuff well. Talk about halmark and Todd Reising, Alot.

Overall, Lisa is a pretty good teacher. If you take the time to learn the slides in the the book that she provides, you will do just fine on the tests. However, you have to be extremely careful with your work on the tests because often times she is beyond unreasonable with the grading of her work problems.

Anyone who speaks positively of Lisa's teaching skills should lose all credibility and be banned from posting on this site. Her "book" is the worst I have used in college, just slides with facts and equations. No explanation of WHY it is important or HOW it is used. How you do in this course has little to do with what you learned about Finance.

Take it in the summer!!! Shes very  laid back, even brought us donuts! Dont miss a single class...and after class talk to her if you dont understand something! Tests are hard...and the textbook sucks... so make sure you write down everything she says, and then some!

If you go to class, pay attention, and take notes you're going to be fine. The more she says it out loud the more likely it's going to be on the test. The text book is a pre-made note packet so write MORE then just filling in the blank to pass the tests. Just ignore her constant bragging and the class is easy.

My complaint is that we spend a lot of time on simple foundational problems, but then are tested on more difficult versions of these problems on the tests. What good does it do to prepare us with easy problems if you're going to test us on one's we've barely covered? Do the HW, go to class, and don't get tricked on the test, because she will try.

It's not hard if you go to class. Random quizzes are given so you should attend class. She sometimes explains the simple things into too much detail and not enough on the more difficult problems. Go to class. Get the book. She's hot. It's easy.

Simply terrible. I think the only people that make positive comments on her are former TA's. She only talks with them anyway. I took the class and Todd Reesing is not a TA but she still talks about him a bunch. She is not a good educator. She won't let anyone leave the class through the front doors because she is afraid someone will attack her.

I actually had to take Lisa's class twice, because the first time I took it I just couldn't ever keep up, not to mention, Todd Reesing was our TA and Kerry Meier & Jake Sharp were in our class, so she talked about them ALL THE TIME. Todd was my TA both times, he's a nice guy, but she is obsessed with him.  It's absurd.

Lisa was a horrible teacher. She refused to personally talk to her students and only permitted them to talk to her TAs. Her power point book made it very difficult to learn the material as well. And yes, she talks more about Todd Reesing and her kids than she does finance.

Lisa was great the entire semester. From what I heard she has gotten more difficult as the semesters have progressed but it wasn't unbearable. You have to go to class because she has random quiz's (that have also gotten more difficult). I didn't have to take the final but most people do because there isn't much room for error in her class.

She is hot, but her class is not. No textbook use and all you have is stupid power point slides bundled up in a package. Class is so big that you cannot even ask questions. I would definitely recommend KU to have more FIN 310 classes available. You will see how her class enrollment will drop. I would definitely NOT recommend this teacher, but this

Despite the other comments, I found this class pretty tough. Lisa is not that great of a teacher. She repeats herself way too much. Also, since Todd Reesing is a TA for this class, she will NOT stop talking about him. It got really annoying.

really easy class. i am not sure if its because of her or because the material is so damn basic. i do know is that every exam i took, she took points off even though i was correct. i argued back to her and she gave me my points. it sucks that i had to do that.
