This class is so easy.  FIN 310 is definately one of the easiest business classes at KU. The lectures are ridiculous and pointless but as long as you go and half-way pay attention to the problems she does in-class you will be ok. A lot of inclass E.C. Easy class, Easy A, if you do the work.

I enjoyed this class and Lisa's teaching style. The fact that there is no textbook to purchase, or need for one is a bonus. All the notes you need are purchased in a packet. She gives lots of examples - if you pay attention and learn these you will do fine on the exams since the questions are the same style. Would not recommend missing class.

You WILL pass this class if you go to every lecture and pay attention, it can be extremely boring at times but FIN 305 is not very difficult and she gives out lots of EC for just showing up to class. I got a 50% on the second test, met with her in her office hours and got a 96% the next test, her and her TAs can be very helpful outside of class.
Lisa is the worst teacher i have ever had.

Class was ridiculous. She lectured fast so that she didn't have to be there the entire time, which didn't help much on exam day. She isn't very approachable for questions with her 20 million TAs.  Fact or Crap and Name that Tune took up more time than the actual lectures. No text required and the notes she provided were sloppy/worthless.

Lisa is an awful teacher, and if you go to her for help will only insult you for it.  Her book is filled with inconsistencies which makes most easy work extremely difficult. Lisa should not be a teacher and probably only does this because she is a failure in all of her previous employments. Do not take her class if at all possible.

A sweet lady but don't know how to teach. Spent a lot of time doing name that tune or fact or crap for so called extra credit. She talks about Hallmark all the time because she used to work there. She doesn't use any text book which makes it impossible to catch up, confusing and way to fast lecture. Avoid this teacher if you can!

It's true that Lisa does not use  the text book but she does prepare notes for her classes. I don't see why people whining about this fact. This class is easy. The material that you will learn is basic stuff for finance  (basic stuff is supposed to be boring, isn't it!!!). Lisa is helpful teacher and she's almost at her office everyday for students

I did not like her teaching style. She used no book but when given examples in class, you could barely read her handwriting. I wish there was a textbook to follow up on and clearly explain the material. She does offer some EC but overall this class is not too bad, just pay attention (which is hard to do).

Professor Bergeron's teaching style is very unique. There is not a textbook so students are required to learn from lectures and ppt slide handouts. Once I adjusted to this I found success in the class. I enjoyed the class material but not necessarily the lectures which were hard to follow. I recommend the class. Take advantage of EC opportunities!

Pretty easy class.  Lectures are boring as she just reads from the slides and underlines everything she wrote.  If I have to hear about Hallmark one more time, I swear....  Doesn't seem too approachable after class because whe likes to hang out with her TAs.  Didn't learn anything retainbable, but easy nontheless.
Decent examples, class can be dry at times. Pop quizzes and homework turn in are random so come to class. Take advantage of extra credit opportunities. Getting an A shouldn't be too tough.
No Comments
This woman is very weird. She's awful at lecturing but is helpful outside of class. She talks about a lot of things like Hallmark and her kids.
The fairest instructor I've ever known. Tests are doable if you've studied and attended almost every class session.

Lisa is great at explaining the materials and relating it to the real corporate environment.  Is very helpful to those who need it and will meet individually if the student desires.  She keeps class fun, and strives to make the students in the class as successful as possible.

She is a pretty good teacher who brings a great attitude to class almost every day.  She does try to help you out and seems to care about what's going on.  She is a fun person and the class wasn't too bad itself.

This woman is great! She really cares that her students do well and she is there to help with whatever you need. She is great to keep in contact with if you are a finance major because she will help you get the in on good/bad classes to take! The class topic isn't the greatest but she makes the class fun to go to! Do the HW and study for the tests!
Speaks very fast and her class flow is quite jerky! Overall not a very effective teacher.
She explains things really well and will meet one-on-one every week if necessary.  Her handwriting is hard to read.
Very nice and helpful.  The class itself is so boring unless you're a Finance nerd, but she tries to make it interesting.  Take FIN 310 and any other class offerred from her if you can!

She is a wonderful teacher!  Tells you what you'll need to know in the real world and doesn't teach you stuff you don't need.  It is an easy class as long as you take notes during class and do the homework.  Test questions are taken from the notes.  Great class!

Very nice woman, a good prof as she lets you know what the real world is like and what is necessary and what isnt.  HW is annoying, but necessary, take it serious and you dont have to do that great on the tests.
Homework is tedious and she even admits its not a good representation of the real world. She offers tons of extra credit and the final is optional!
Really nice prof. Do well on the tests and won't have to take the final. She's pretty cool. Do all the EC you can, helps if you have to take the final.

This class and professor get more flak than necessary. The class is hard, but upper-level classes only get harder. You have to be willing to put in the work to get a good grade. If you do the homework, the class is designed to force you to understand solidworks well. Go to office hours! Prof is genuinely willing to help the more he sees you trying.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is definitely designed to be a clear introduction to how hard mechanical engineering will be. But it is not necessary to be as hard as this professor makes it. Do not get graded by him unless he's in a good mood. Also you might be screwed if your group doesn't wanna do the work. Most odd grading of all time. A 100% is an 80% like what.

Grading is entirely based upon the grader (TA or him).
The prof is generally a snob to be around.
Our exams were unreasonably intense and worth 40% of our grade in the class.
Expect to not cover a substantial part of material in lecture or lab just to be blindsided by it in the final.
Must get lucky on group members to receive a good grade.

Class is based on luck. You have to get lucky with who is your grader and the type of project you have since projects are 40% of your grade. Got lower grades despite having better results than multiple groups who had TAs grading. He's a tough grader and genuinely a tough guy to be around. Had no respect for me until he knew I had an internship.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, he does not deserve the hate. BUT. Some of it is deserved based on him as a person. When it comes to teaching, he knows so much, and you will know exactly what is required of you to become an engineer. Disregard getting to know him and just do the work. He is a hard grader but will do what he can to teach you and can always get 100%.

Great professor. He understands that this class is a hands on, and facilitates it accordingly. If you really try on the homework, you will learn CAD rapidly. His assignments are hard, but reasonable. Honestly wish he was the one that ran the dept because he is a good educator and knows how to teach a class. Laid back, strict but reasonable.
Very unfair grading sometimes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You better have time for his class. Though you will spend many hours on his assignments, you will master what you learn. If you dont have good groupmates/arent strict with them, you wont succeed. But he is always in lab when not in class and he will absolutely help you with problems; though you will have to figure things out yourself a lot of times
if you have no prior knowledge of CAD, then youre screwed and he made me switch my major
very awful professor. I had to leave this class because of him

Lots of work but he plans out his lectures and tells you exactly what he expects from you in class. Classes are formatted where you read beforehand, he gives a short lecture and you do a group problem. Only thing is it's very test-heavy but you will remember everything from this class because of the way teaches statics. Also willing to help on HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Maletsky is a good guy. His class is difficult and uses a structure where mastery is required to get an A in the class. He provides lots of resources outside of class where you can succeed and learn the material. He offers extra help to understand this class conceptually. Overall I learned a lot and enjoyed the class.

His class is hard, but he offers a ton of help outside of class time. His office hours are literally any time he's not teaching, and he's never too busy to have a conversation with a student. You can tell he genuinely wants his students to succeed, which I've noticed is rare in professors. Go to office hours regularly and ask questions.
In my 19 years of living ive never felt this way about a teacher. He is one of the worst teachers ive ever had. He aslo is very stingy for giving people a few extra points for their grade to go up

He learned my pronouns quickly, actually helps you when you ask politely, and honestly seems like he wants students to learn. He's not a monster that people claim he is, he just seems like he's under some stress at home. He's chill, cracks jokes, but also isn't afraid to tell you you totally screwed up your homework. He's blunt, sure, but not cruel
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I understand that many people have had problems with this teacher. I personally found him to be helpful and caring. The graphics work wasn't too bad and you had infinite attempts every week to get a 100%. The group projects felt insane at first but they're broken up into smaller pieces. I've found him to grade fairly and give helpful feedback
very creepy. someone should definitely look into this guy.

Unfortunately, the professor has not been helpful and does not even help with the projects and explains verbally . There should be a quick action taken before our midterms because honestly I don't have any experience and if it goes like this , I could even fail his class . I request to please take this issue seriously .
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Maletsky is a classic example of a male engineer. He bragged about his Title IX and court cases to the class. Really creepy guy. If you're a gender minority, don't take his class unless you want to become a statistic.
i won't take his class again.

This class was mid even before Maletsky. With Maletsky it was unbearable. Grading is entirely subjective and nonlogical. He had big marital problems this semester and struck a war path with his students' GPAs to deal with it. He was unprofessional, saying "quit ya b----ing" and having "f----t" on his slides. Please don't take.

Awful professor. Will fail seniors and have no regrets. Worst grading scheme ever. This course was supposed to teach important topics but failed to do so in every capacity especially statistical tolerancing. Avoid this tech elective at all costs... you can teach yourself everything better than he will anyway.
His class is a catch 22... good luck

Everything about this class is truly awful, but the worst part is the group assignments. Partners are randomly assigned and they will make or break your grade as projects are worth 40% of the total grade. If you do something wrong on the homework, he will tell you, but he won't tell you what is wrong so you cannot fix it (his feedback is useless).

He was alright at the start of the semester, but once he started doing his job and grading assignments on the last day of the semester, my grade started slipping because he grades solely based on how far the stick is up his butt that day. He will dock points because "you didn't explain well enough" on a question he didn't ask for explanation on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have four years of CAD experience and I despise this class. For this being a freshman class, the expectations are crazy. He has a very poor understanding of what beginners are capable of and asks a lot of passive aggressive questions during one-on-one grading sessions. Be ready to spend 12 hours a week on homework.

The thing that makes this class difficult is the group projects. The teammates you have will determine how difficult the class is. Your grade for the project depends on who your assigned grader is (a TA or him), and he typically grades based on how he is feeling at the moment. Not a good experience. You have to put way too much work in to get an A.
BEWARE OF A-'s. They count as a 3.7 to your GPA and he's the only professor who hurts your GPA for having a 92.5% in his course.

Lorin is genuinely caring, but he can be a tough grader and the group projects can be a nightmare. Exams are fairly easy and he curves exams and projects. It can be very time consuming though. I spent many hours in the lab, and received full credit on homework, but the group projects bombed my grade.

Lorin's grading system is complete bs and he threw my drawing book at me and told me to get the f out. His class goes off his mood (which is typically bad) and the TA's are useless as a mf. Hand drawings have to be spot on otherwise he will dock an incredible amount of points ruining your grade. He's disrespectful asf so good luck.

This guy is the most passive aggressive person I know. Everything depends on his mood for the day. He hardly teaches and most of the time just reads of slides. I had to teach myself everything in this class. His grading system is a joke and this class has a ton of work. KU should get rid of this man.

This is exactly how a class should be setup. I am learning while also testing on my skills frequently. Come to class and you will be fine. Put in the work and you will see the results pay off. There is a discussion section that I highly encourage to get more aid on the homework if you are struggling.
The grading system in this class is beyond horrible. Besides exams, your grades on projects are completely dependent on whether your TA/Maletsky is having a good day or not.

I don't know why he is still in the teaching community. grades are important essence for any student and if you conduct points, you need to give feedback for why it's wrong on details, not doing it for enjoyment.

This guys actually sucks. Gives no guidance at all and expects you to know way too much. NOT a beginner class, although there is no pre reqs. This professor will give you no help and does not give a shit about his students. He sucks KU please do something about this
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Maletsky is the best teacher I have had at KU so far. Statics is challenging, but his style really helps. He will do everything he can to help you pass and if you want a grade higher than that it just depends on how you do on the tests and how much you are willing to study.  Redoing the class worksheets is what I found most helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Maletsky is very clear with how the class is graded and is always an email away if you need help. I also had him for ME 228, and even in that class the standard was the same.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Actually one of the better engineering professors in terms of teaching, but sadly he's apparently one of the worst as a person (that is, if the allegations are true, look up the KC star article). Not sure if I would take a small class with him. But being in a large class with him currently, I would say he is fairly good at communicating concepts.

This is my second class with Maletsky, and he is a genuinely amazing professor. His lectures and videos are entertaining, and he does a good job of explaining concepts. He genuinely cares about how you are doing in the class and will do everything he can to help you succeed. He has a lot of poor reviews on here, but he's definitely a 5/5.
Bad advisor, discouraging.

from what ive heard, youve done a terrible thing. i personally hope you get fired and blacklisted in the teaching community. when a person comes to you for help, you help them, especially since youre in a position of authority where u can actually do something. not helping people who need help is the reason y many are afraid to come out for help

God I hate this man so much. He's a nice guy but good lord is he awful to take a class with. Lots of assignments with a group project that spans through out the semester, and if you have bad teammates than it's going to be pretty rough.

Office hour availability is great and can hop on a zoom meeting almost anytime. Lectures are really good in that its all important material, but are kept generally short. He can be a bit of a tough grader, but he always explains why things are graded the way they are, which is really helpful. I also think his reviews on here are too harsh

I don't understand everyone's bad reviews. He's always fair and understanding. His lectures and videos are great and he's funny. He shows the class averages and discusses what people should be doing to improve. He is caring and always is willing to spend his time to help people.
He did not ever do a full problem in class and did not care if everyone fail or not. To him it does not matter what they class average was
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Before taking this class, I was very excited to have dr. Maletsky as my prof. As he seemed to be a good teacher and knew what he was doing, I was extremely mistaken. I have never had a worse teacher. Statics is almost entirely a problem solving course and he NEVER once solved one whole problem in class, hes a horrible grader and I hated his class

Tough and challenging. All the effort and time you spend is nothing compare to him. He assumes that you are already engineer and knows every thing and not suppose to make mistakes. He wants every thing you did to be perfect. He is a hard grader takes off a lot of points in the exams for simple mistakes. He doesn't care about the class average.

Good Teacher, however, he is a bad person. I respect him but I don't like him. He has no problem whether students succeed or fail. He didn't tell what is the average of class the whole semester. He has no problem if the average is( F). Try to avoid him as much as possible.
Simply has no problem whether students succeed or fail. Too much talk less actions
He's a cool guy.

You need to work hard in order to survive his class. But his teaching method is very great for this subject. The assignments take lot of time to do, but they help you a lot in gaining knowledge. In the end, it is an awesome class and nice  grading criteria. Spend some dedicated time on this course throughout the semester and you will get A grade.
useless

Maletsky lectures well and clarifies a lot with the weekly homework assignments. The only negative is that you sign up for a 10 minute grading block where him or the TA's grade the work in front of you. There are also 2 semester projects which are very time consuming. Find a good group to work with. Lab is optional except for the midterm and final

Projects are very hard and time consuming and are the largest portion of your grade. However, if you do well on them and do all the graphics assignments it's a pretty easy A. The final is only 10% so it doesn't really affect your grade if you've done all the homework and done well on the projects.

He makes short, 5-15 minute videos over each of the new subjects. His method of teaching is to have us watch the videos and read the chapters and then fully understand. Be prepared to teach yourself most of the time because his office hours are usually crowded and can be less than helpful.
Great Intro Class.  It was fun and pretty easy, if you applied yourself.
This class was tough in the sense it was a lot of work. Individually, the assignments weren't that difficult. He curves the class somewhat so an 85 is usually an A.

Completely wastes your time. There is a project involving building a race car with certain constraints. I guess he thought that one race car wasn't enough, as it had been before he took over this class, and has made us build 4 versions of a car. He has no respect for a student's time constraints. Prepare to give 200% to get an A.

Assignments are very time consuming and often useless. The group assignments tend to cost more money than I would like to invest in a class. He seems to act as though his class is the only one you are taking at the time.
He is a nice guy will will help you.  Lectures are usually boring but sometimes important.  Lab is mostly on your own but still pretty easy as long as your not retarded.

Lorin has designed this class so that he doesn't have to work at all. This semester, he canceled half of the classes and outsourced the writing of lectures quizzes to the students. His assignments are useless and take up too much time. In a word, it's all FLUFF.

More work than any other class I have ever been in.  Attempts to break you when he grades papers.  Grading is extremely subjective.  He often contridicts himself.  Count how many times he says "incidentally" and "consequentially" in a lecture for fun.

tough class...but he does teach it,and is very good at it, tests are difficult and don't expect an easy answer when you go in and ask him a question during office hours...he'll still make you think and work for it...homework load is pretty heavy...while  working 30 hours a week i found this class incredibly time demanding

Dr.Rocha is very sweet, he class could have been more productive. It had its good and boring moments. There is a lot of discussion incorporated into lecture, which I enjoyed. Lots of guest speakers - some I really valued and some not at all. Decent amount of homework, but she is lenient if you communicate. not a bad class, just wasn't for me.

Lonna was a super sweet lady! She understands that we have other classes and was willing to hear our input on due dates and how certain assignments were done. Class participation is mandatory, but if you have a good excuse she will not penalize you.
Lonna Rocha was my favorite professor this semester. She made class super fun and really cared about her students.
She is super caring to all students with that being said the course is definitely catered towards elementary education and sometimes expectations were not very clear.

She is a very kind professor! Her lectures are interesting and have a lot of variety in them that help people stay engaged with her class. Though, I felt kind of weird about them since the lectures were very much oriented towards elementary education majors. She's very receptive of feedback though! One of the best professors I've had at KU so far.
Super nice professor, she was always super understanding and i loved being in her class! I will say be ready to write at the end of the year there is lots of writing but overall still a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lonna is a great professor. She actually cares about her students and accommodates for them very well.
She was very timid, and a bit of a pushover.
Lonna Rocha is an extremely empathetic and charismatic professor. She is honest and humble and being in her class is always a delight.

Professor is very kind, and truly wants students to succeed. Class was pretty easy for the most part, almost made me switch my major to education lol. But I definitely recommend this class and professor. She understands how hard college can be on your mental health and is very accommodating

Lisa is by far my favorite professor. She genuinely cares about you and is very knowledgeable about advertising. Show up to class, ask questions, and have her look over your projects before you submit. I would recommend everyone to take a class with her. You will learn lots of real-world applications.

She actually helps and wants you to succeed. Would suggest to anyone taking 560 to take her class. Her labs are very laid back. She does grade hard, but if you show her your work in class she will tell you what to fix and you'll get a good grade.
She is awesome. She genuinely wants to see you succeed and gives really great feedback.

Taking Lisa for J560 was my best decision of junior year. SO PRACTICAL. SO LAIDBACK. She cares about teaching you so you can get a job, not so you can learn bs that you will never use. Can't recommend her enough honestly. Such a nice person too. Best feedback too!!!

Hands down one of my favorite teachers in the J-school. She is one of the only J304 teachers who actually prepares you for the upper level courses - she really knows what she's talking about and each assignment has a purpose. The class is structured where assignments overlap which can be confusing but they were never extremely hard at least.

Professor Loewen is a great teacher! There are no tests and she makes sure the assignments have clear directions and expectations. She really wants to help you learn so she gives great feedback and helps you to improve your writing. Would take her class again.

Lisa is one of my favorite teachers I've ever had at KU. She's incredibly personable and loves her students. However, she's also pretty rough on the grading, but that's just tough love. I still run into her quite often, and we have conversations in the halls that leave me laughing. In a way, she's like a mom in the J-School.

Lisa was an awesome professor. The class was pretty easy overall, but she taught a lot of the basics to media writing. No exams in the class. Couple small group projects, but nothing that would take more than a few hours to do.

Lisa is the best professor I have ever had in my entire life. She is so cool and funny and so helpful. She understands that we have other stuff to do in our lives and is so easy to work with. She is such a good teacher and if you have the chance to have her, get her.

Lisa saved my life in this class. She is now one of my favorite journalism teachers at KU. Would highly recommend to anyone and everyone. She sympathises with students and is always willing to help out. Lecture for 560 is dull but if you get Lisa for a lab instructor youll be just fine

Lisa Loewen IS my favorite teacher in the journalism school. She teaches with a high level of passion and is incredibly down to earth. She has very reasonable expectations and I would highly recommend her to anyone.

Lisa has been one of my favorite teachers I have had in the Journalism School so far. She is VERY understanding and extends deadlines, let's you work on individual projects with partners, and is always there to help you when you need it. She isn't a hard grader and she allows re-do's for almost every project, get her if you can!!
Great professor. She's helpful and understanding about extending deadlines. She makes message development much easier to handle. She knows her stuff.

Lisa was one of my favorite teachers in the J-School. She was always really nice and willing to help at any time, including if you were stressed and needed to use class time to study or if you needed a little extension if something goes wrong for an assignment. She is great! High recommendation!

Very kind, passionate about class material. Always willing to answer questions even if they feel silly. Extremely approachable professor who is happy to work with you, and very neurodivergent-friendly.

I used to be a straight A student. After asking for clarification before submitting, a single homework assignment nearly brought me down a letter grade. Working every example multiple times is not enough to succeed in her class, based on my post-midterm grade. No extra credit. She is nice, but I feel tricked and can't learn from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor of EECS
One of the best professors I have ever had. She's very clear and organized when she lectures and it's obvious she actually cares about what she's teaching and about her students in general.

Fantastic Professor. One of the best professors the EECS department offers. Take any and all classes with her if possible. She will work with you to ensure that everything is understandable, grading is clear, and she genuinely wants you to succeed, a rarity in this department.
Great professor. The material was tough but she is great at helping us understand. Two exams with similarities to the homework and a final project!

She has great lectures for theory of computing. I would recommend going to lectures as they provide more insight than her notes. The entire semester consisted of 6 homeworks, 2 exams, and a final project. She is very helpful and led a surprisingly lively class given that I took her 8 am section. I would recommend taking any of her courses.
Class is good but the TA be tripping in office hours. Be looking like I stole his snickers bar when I ask him a question

Good professor and I enjoyed the class. Really intelligent and has experience in both academia and industry making her a well rounded. Materials were difficult but she made it easier to understand and she's available in office hours and outside the classroom as well. Only criticism is the time being at 8:00am, wish it was after 9
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the best professors in the department. Her lectures are very clear and understandable, and although some of the material can be challenging, she cares a lot about helping us. The homework assignments are very similar to the exams, so she makes it easy to study for them and succeed. Amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Lohefener is a joy to have as a professor. Although I found the concepts challenging, she would take the time to answer any questions. I really enjoyed office hours as well. There were six assignments, only due by the end of the semester, and no final. The tests were almost the same as the homework. Highly reccomend!

One of the best professors, up there with Gibbons! She's super nice and very lenient with grading. There were only six homeworks for the entire semester and they didn't have a deadline. Easiest class I've ever taken.

EECS 662 is easy because Dr. Lohoefener expects us to work on projects and discussions that are simple and helpful for the quizzes. She is funny, caring, and superb. The best part is that there is no final exam in her course, but she expects us to do the final group project. I highly recommend you to take her courses in the future.

Dr. Lohoefener is one of the nicest and best professors in KU. Her projects and quizzes are balanced and simple if you attend her lectures and read the online textbook and notes. She is always helpful and gives good feedback. The final group project is not too difficult, so I highly recommend you to take her courses. Best professor in KU.

Really welcoming atmosphere in lectures that promotes learning. Homework assignments aren't too difficult and while quizzes are weighted highly in the grade, they are not too challenging if you study and understand the material. She is so caring and understanding/lenient for student hardships. Great person and professor.

Jenny is one of the best professors in the EECS department. Programming Languages (662) was a fairly laidback experience with only a handful of assignments: 4 projects, 4 discussion posts, 5 quizzes, and a final group project. I never felt overwhelmed and it was easy to stay caught up on material with the course textbook and online notes.

Amazing professor, with wonderful engaging lectures. Its a tough topic but she teaches it beautifully, and everyone has an opportunity to learn and do well. Absolutely recommend her for anything she teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took ENGL 102 and I never rate my professors, but the frustration this professor caused me was insane. There was no clear grading rubric for any paper or project actually there was no rubric. She was very opinionated when grading which made it seem unfair and biased. Do yourself a favor and take anyone else for English 102!
Cassidy is the best teacher I have ever had. She always made class fun, and my writing really improved.

i love this teacher!! she is very reasonable, and if you needan extension she is very understanding. I 100% recommend. She posts the schedules for the week before class so you know what you will be doing.

She was by far my favorite professor I have ever had. She is so welcoming and it was only her first semester teaching. She always made sure her students were taken care of and that mental health came first. I found myself joining her zooms a few minutes early just to chat with her!! Absolutely 100% recommend and I chose to take her another semester

Good person, lots of stories. PORT is heavily discussion based, read/watch then talk it through the next day and repeat, not too bad unless no one in your class likes to talk. Some of the movies and books are a bit outdated, but always given a free link. Once a week 1 page reflection. I would take again, easy credit class + watched avatar
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I absolutely love Professor Tosta. You go on lots of fun field trips on and off campus. Not much homework besides a weekly assignment, a final paper, and some readings and films to watch throughout the term. Although there was no clear grading criteria, he is a pretty easy grader. He is also very responsive to emails and is an overall fun person.

Tosta really cares about students and what they take away from his class! He is an extremely insightful professor who is very passionate about what he teaches. However, the expectations set for the class (assignments, due dates, rubric details, etc.) are often unclear or non-existent which caused a lot of stress and confusion.

Professor Tosta is a very knowledgeable and respected professor that is passionate about what he teaches. He is not the greatest at running the class, often would change assignments and readings with little notice. The syllabus does not reflect what is actually expected in class and often I found myself guessing what expectations were.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved having this guy as my professor. He is wildly educated and it is so clear that he loves teaching students. I took a freshman class with him so it was relatively easy, but he always tried really hard to get us to participate bc so many people just wouldn't show up. I loved him and I'm going to look into take more classes w him.
He is a very caring teacher that will ask how you are doing. Very little instruction for projects but critiques heavily.

Art 105 is pretty much fully based on attendance. I had health issues through out the semester and it was very hard to reach him through email. I talked to him about this in class too due to my worries. I emailed him multiple times and he never once responded. I still gave him a 2/5 because he is quite a nice caring guy, just not the best teacher.

Luke is a pretty nice guy, the class itself felt very disorganized for a prof who has been in the scene for so long, he's an avid canvas hater don't expect to know your grades til end of sem. He talks and goes off topic a lot, sometimes disvalues what other students say, also is not hands on and you'll be getting advice from YT vids for projects
Very vague on what he wants but once you share your work he critiques it heavily.
If youre ready to be slammed with incredibly vague instructions to each project, Luke is your dude. Hes pretty flexible though with due dates which is nice.

Luke is such a chill dude. The class I took was a discussion class and that is definitely where he shines. He is an understanding professor, and would often be lenient with the class on work (maybe a little TOO lenient). Getting off topic was pretty common, but as the class was mainly discussion it wasn't exactly detrimental to the experience.

Luke is very off topic and isn't clear in what he wants. Quiet a few times all we did was watch music videos, which is fine until you realize you are paying over $1000 for this. He can be rude and judgemental about your work and he doesn't really have room to talk because all the photos in his art show were off his iPhone. He talks way too much.

Luke is a great professor. He is very personable and seems to really care for his students. Not to mention, Luke is very knowledgeable, especially on the topic of photography (what our class was focused on). I always found class with with Luke fascinating and always learned something new. This was my favorite class this semester.

He is the best and so laid back. The class itself had no set syllabus or path set in place for it. As our class came up with new ideas we would create fun and interesting projects from them. This class is totally worth it to take, our class met for breakfast several times off-campus which was semi-optional and a big plus. 100% would recommend.
Luke is a great teacher and makes class interesting. He can be frustrating because he talks a lot and gets off subject; but, I definitely recommend taking a class of his.
Luke is amazing! Inspirational, but gets off track easily.

Luke is awesome! He made my whole semester 100x better and you really learn about the fundamentals of photography. Best know about Detroit because it comes up every class. He lets you do your style of photography and helps you improve it. He gets off topic a bit which can be nice in a 3 hour long class. Meet for breakfast & take photos are Mass St.

I was really frustrated by this class. Luke picked up our assignments, but never gave us back a single grade or formal assessment until we saw our final grade on the transcript. He's a nice person, but would benefit from studying teaching. I paid to learn about photography, not to talk about the mens basketball and what we did last weekend.
fell asleep everyday, he just talks to talk. required expensive materials we never touched. i did not learn a single thing about how to use or operate a camera. very frustrating and a waste of time.

Very nice and friendly. Talks a lot, just about anything, even during lectures he somehow manages to get off track. You will like his class in conventional photography more than digital. Doesn't do well in emails. It's a pretty relaxing class.

awsome guy. entertaining, never a dull moment in class. talks forever, if given the chance :) but always helpful, and very nice guy. One of the most enjoyable classes! Easy to do well if you just try.

its an awesome class that has very little structure so you have lots of freedom to explore the techniques and tools you like. luke is a great guy, hes crazy in a good way. once you can get past his sarcasm and if you do you work class should be a breeze.
luke is honestly one of the nicest teachers ever. very sarcastic, but that's exactly what i loved about him. if you like photo, you'll love this class. period.
He's the best teacher I've ever had. Hands down.
He's a bit sarcastic, and his lectures are loooong, but you'll get a B if you try, and an A if you are good at photography.

I've taken Luxi for Digital Marketing and Marketing Strategy and can't recommend her enough! While there are times I wish she gave clearer instructions on the grading criteria, if you work with her and show that you're trying, you will succeed in the class. She has hilarious commentary and doesn't take herself too seriously which I love.
She is very, very caring and truly wants you to learn about marketing. Her clarity on grading is somewhat difficult and hard to understand, but she is a very good professor and a very nice person.

I took a class with her, and my experience was very disappointing. Her lectures often felt like long ramblings, making it hard to focus and learn.

She also penalized entire groups for some members not participating. This felt unfair to those who were contributing and affected our ability to work together as well as our grades.

Absolutely my favorite professor at KU who cares a lot about her students if you get to know her by interacting in class. The majority of the grade is made up of group projects which allows you to learn the content of the class through real world examples and situations.

Such a fun and entertaining professor. Once you get to know her, she genuinely cares about her students and just wants them to get better. If a student gets a bad grade, it is probably because they did not follow directions or pay attention in class. If you don't understand something or need help, just ask! She genuinely wants you to do well.
Worst experience of my life, intentionally embarrassed students

Projects with no details on how its executed then gets mad when everyone does it differently then she wants, cold calls students then tries to embarrass them. Hates when people question her when we don't understand. She raises her voice and talks in a condescending tone towards students.Coursework is not hard. No attendance points if you're late.

Professor Chai is knowledgeable and passionate about marketing. If you attend class (which you should because attendance is graded), you'll leave with a deeper understanding of what marketing actually is. 
Note: This class was graded with a 93% cutoff for an A, with 90% being an A-.

I was unimpressed by horrible communication and derision when students asked clarifying questions. Her schedule was always changing, she did not put in assignments / due dates in canvas, but was upset when no one knew what was due. I attended 95% of classes and received a good grade overall but I can't say I would choose her section again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class, 200 pt class with about 50 pts of ec. Mainly group projects with presentations. Most work doesn't matter as long as you do extra credit. Most of the class finished with over 100%.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very easy yet engaging course.

Lots of homework, but nothing unbearable, and three lowest get dropped. Lab is insanely easy and tests aren't too bad, and half of it is with your team. I had a bad team, but still really appreciated the way this class was taught. Definitely do not take it with anyone else. Also, offers tons of EC so definitely take advantage of that
Love Luchies, great class setup, a little homework heavy but worth it and lowest ones get dropped. tons of EC, exams are partially group. Great class dont take it with anyone else

Luchies gives a lot of content for each lecture(lecture videos, slides, group work, and two hw problems). If you stay on top of this every lecture, this class is a breeze. There is also a ton of EC and he drops the lowest exam grade. The final is also optional if you have a B or higher.

ME455. If you resist to be a flatterer, you won't get the grade that you want. I got 89.7% which he gave me a B compared to my friend who didn't put any effort, and got 80%. No difference in the final grade. He's moody and don't fulfill his promises via email. You have to consistently be fake happy in front of his face or white to get good grades.

Luchies seems like an alright guy, but assigns constant homework, puts you in random groups, and explains concepts poorly. The tests are way harder than the things covered in class. The "flipped classroom" isn't really flipped since he still lectures (wasting everyone's time). Lots of extra credit though, which made this class kind of a joke.

Dr. Luchies is a nice guy and I feel like the content for this course isn't difficult if you're comfortable with Matlab. The majority of the difficulty comes from the sheer number of assignments that you're expected to finish by the end of the semester, and that's not even including a group project and an exam on top of that.

Dr. Luchies is awesome. If you go to every class and work with your group you can understand the material. He also gives a ton of extra credit work, boosting my grade from a 78 to an 85. He also bases the class average on what letter grade you get. So 85 was at the cut off point for an A and 70 was the B cut off point.

Dr. Luchies doesnt lecture. He uses team based learning (aka the blind leading the blind). If the class does badly on an exam, he takes no responsibility. The exams are harder than what you learn. You will be in class for an hour doing IClickers and group problems. You literally have to teach yourself. And no partial credit on the exams. 0/5.
Dr. Luchies is super helpful but the tests have no partial credit so take them very seriously.
Got into trouble for threatening Turmp supporters in class. Made extreamly innaporopriate comments often and loved to share his left wing agenda from the front of the class.
Love how passion he is about class and he definitely stands up for what is right! I honestly full heartedly agree with him.
Terrible comments made in class
Doesn't teach, just complains about his opinions.
Horrible professor
Worse teacher
Not good in fact he was disappointing
His class was extremely easy and all of the assignments could be done remotely however he made class very uncomfortable sometimes with making sexual jokes even when it wasn't related to the topic

Phils lectures were very good and the material covered directly relates to things you need to know outside of the classroom. I feel like Ive grown in areas from what we learned from the lectures. There are weekly prompts for writing that are very easy in addition to weekly assignments. Attendance isnt mandatory but he gives out extra credit.
Phil is a great guy who loves his job! Always has a smile on his face and his lectures are interesting and valuable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Took as a gen ed requirement and wasnt really sure what to think at first. Phil is a great guy, who tries his best (and succeeds) to make the lessons interesting. Do all of the homework assignments and study the notes before a test, and youll do fine.
One of the best professors I've ever had. Phil makes his lectures fun and keeps you entertained. he is also very understanding and will help you with accommodations if needed

Dr. Phil is one of the greatest and most understanding professors I have encountered at KU. His end goal is to help you finish at your highest level. Everything is straight forward and easy to understand!! However he does do random assignment checks so make sure you don't oversleep.

Phil is the man. He explains all the material in a well-organized matter and gives great feedback to students with questions. He incorporates funny and real-life examples with whatever topic may be discussed. If you have to take HSES260, pick Phil!!

Phil Lowcock, otherwise known as Dr. Phil is an amazing teacher, and I had so much fun in his lectures. Not only is he a very good teacher, he cares about every student and wants everyone to succeed. His importance lies in attendance. He wants the students to learn, because he knows some students struggle with tests. 10/10 recommend this teacher.
Phil is the man. If you go to class and pay attention I am confident you will do fine. He is funny and engaging, he makes what can be a dull topic pretty interesting.

The homework is literally just surveying about yourself. Attendance is taken a few times throughout the semester. The class is all notes every lecture so can get boring a bit. He is a good teacher though overall and an easy A.

Very lecture-intensive, but he tells you explicitly what will be on the test (along with descriptive study guides). He only takes attendance when he feels like it, so it just depends on when you show up and he happens to take it. He doesn't use the textbook, which is great, but the online assignments are definitely worth doing.
Just show up, do the online surveys, and pay the smallest amount of attention to pass. This is an "athletes" easy A course.
Great professor who cares about his students

Phil really cares about your success, and does not try to trick anyone on assignments or tests. He is fair, funny, and as long as you show up and study the powerpoints well you will do well. He does 10 attendance checks for 100 points so make sure you are going to class consistently even though the lecture slides are posted on blackboard.
One of the easiest class I have ever taken. Don't go to class unless you want to learn more than needed for the exams. Just do the study guides and review the slides you'll do fine.

He's a great professor. He makes the lectures quite interesting. Just pay some attention and look through the slides and you'll do just fine on the exams and such. He'll have random attendance days for points so go to class

He is a wonderful teacher and is completely willing to work with students if you miss, He is really pationate about sports and honestly is an all around nice guy. He really knows what is happening and how to teach this class.

While these are usually in a medium sized lecture hall, he will still take attendance! It's worth an entire test grade and takes it randomly 10 times during the semester. Awesome class to take though and very interesting. Take it in the spring though if you want a smaller class size. Dr. Phil was an excellent professor.
Super cool guy.  Awesome teacher.  Takes random attendance.   Didn't buy book but had to buy access code.
Attend class and pay attention. Easy A.

Attendance is not mandatory but he does 10 random attendance days throughout the semester worth 10pts each which can greatly help your grade.  Homework is completion points and is done online. I got B's on all 4 tests but still got an A in the class due to all the attendance and homework points so make sure to show up and do the homework!
He's an easy grader and is willing to work with you if you are struggling. He takes attendance randomly and gives you 10 points every time you are there when he does. Very easy class to pass.
This professor is amazing!!! He is very concerned with helping you understand and he loves his job it is obvious.  I would definitely take this teacher again.

LOVE this class. The material is presented well and very interesting! He definitely wants his students to succeed (other prof. should take notes) Tests are easy enough and if you study you can get an A! Attendance is taken every now and then but I enjoyed going just because the class was always funintriguing. HIGHLY recommend course.
Attendance is "mandatory" but he only takes attendance 15 times a semester but its 15% of your grade. Makes jokes through out lectures. I would take more of his classes
He is a really fun teacher that only takes attendance like 10-15 times a semester! Just make sure you study for the exams, even if they sound easy!!

My FAVORITE teacher! Phil is so funny and a GREAT teacher! He presents all the information like he's just talking to you or having a conversation. He takes attendance once every two weeks, homework and lecture slides are online, and tests are easy! Great class!

Great guy, attendance is "mandatory" he takes attendance only ten times per semester, and it is random. Super easy assignments, everything was online. Test are super easy as well, mostly common sense stuff.

This class was very easy. The teacher was very easy to understand. He puts all of his notes on blackboard so that you will have them. He also gives you a detailed description of the test. He tells you exactly what is on it. He does take attendance points so make sure you attend the lecture. Very compassionate teacher who is very easy to learn from.
Great teacher. Definitely top 3 since Ive been at KU. Although theres alot of people in class, he still cares about everyone. His door is always open and he's willing to help you no matter what.

Best professor Ive come in contact with. His classes are very, very easy as long as you attend class regularly. Also he cares ALOT about his students. His office door is always open and he's always welcome to hear whatever you have to say. Great teacher, definitely going to take another class with him.

He really cares about his students and that they leave the class understanding what he has been teaching.  He was genuinely interested in what he was teaching and was interesting and easy to understand.
Dr. Phil really cares about the student. He gives a very detailed test review and posts all his notes a week prior to the test.  Pay attention and you can get an A.

Dr. Phil was awesome. Class was optional and all notes were posted online before the test. If you went to class the day before the test he would tell you what exactly was on the test. Tests were somewhat difficult, but manageable.

Loved this class! Dr. Phil really knows his stuff and as long as you went to the review session before each exam and studied that material, tests are no biggie. He knows the material very well and lectured well.
He's great! Yes an easy A, but you actually learn a lot from the class, if you do decide to go. He's really a great person and overall good and clear teacher. Knows his stuff.
he is an awesome professor. He's been working in athletics for a long time and really knows his health facts. it's really interesting and everyone should take this class. it's an easy A too.
Great teacher! Go the the review sessions before tests and do the Connect assignments and you will have no problems.

Took this class in hopes that it would help boost my GPA and to get another 3 credits out of the way. It worked perfect.  Just cram for the test the night before from his powerpoints and the test is an easy A/B. Take the "post-test" questions on his online section and a bunch of questions come straight from there too.  Easy points.
EASY A!.....Go to the review session the class before the test and you will do fine.  May be an early class but EEEAASSYY!  Many athletes take this class!

Going to class is really a waste of time. He puts the powerpoints up on blackboard and the tests come straight off the powerpoint. You don't really need a book. Just study the powerpoints and you will be fine.
Dr. Phil is a lot of fun. His class is very easy as long as you show up and take the notes. Make sure to show up to the class before tests to get the review!!

Don't buy a book. Go to class. Easy A. Tons of athletes so the class is a gimme. Only covered "history and foundations" for the last section. Most of the class was based in Sports Psych. Pretty full of himself. Study guides are helpful. Just take notes and you can cram in the morning.

Don't buy the book, you won't need it.  Tests are over lectures, but he's pretty interesting when he talks even though the class is boring in general (history and foundations of PE....seriously).  he makes it bearable.  I didn't think the tests were that bad, final isn't cumulative.

Caroline's passion for classics makes the class so enjoyable. The packet issue was overblown—it only happened once, and we worked in groups to finish it quickly. If you keep up with the reading and pay attention, you'll be fine. She's so Gen Z and explains things in a way we get. She's also more flexible with late work than it says in the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She really likes to guilt the class if we don't act like we're having fun, but then gives us the most confusing projects. She also gets upset when we don't talk in our groups after assigning us huge packets that we all are working on seperaly anyway

She never seems to fully know what is going on. There are 3 separate schedules put up, but none of them are even correct. For a 100-level class, the work she is asking for is ridiculous. While she says she is happy to talk about things, every conversation has left me thinking she thinks I'm stupid and doesn't want to talk with me.

If you're looking for an easy elective, this is NOT it. HOWEVER, Professor Lunt is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about Classics! She's a touch grader, but she gives a lot of good feedback. There are a lot of essays to write and lots of books to buy. She's very caring and wants you to actually gain the life skill of critical thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very well put together class and a great instructor, but there is a LOT of work (readings, discussion posts, assignments) due everyday at midnight. She is supportive though and a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Everything posted on Canvas was hard to access and confusing to understand. I did more work in this ONLINE ENGLISH class than I have ever done in any other class. Seriously, in all my years it was ridiculous. Overall, she gotta changed the entire curriculum and figure out how to use Canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took Professor Benda for Professional Communications and it was great! It is a short class so there is a decent amount of assignments and projects in just a few weeks, but it is definitely manageable. She gives a lot of freedom in terms of creativity with projects and gives both positive and constructive feedback. Highly recommend!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class but going to class is very important and it was interesting

This class wasn't super hard but it also ain't a walk in the park. The tests are hard and they make up a majority of your grade. The study guides aren't very helpful. Going to lecture is worth it because he gives extra credit activities in class which are very helpful. He is a cool guy but is a little too politically bias at times in my opinion.

The exams are not hard at all if you study (crazy thought), and the material is easy to learn. Yes, an hour and fifteen minutes of straight lecture twice a week is sometimes boring, but he does his best to create an engaging environment, given that it is so early in the morning. Molina does a great job at keeping the lectures fun and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Boring lectures where he sits and reads off slides but slightly changes up the words like a high schooler. Exams are hard with 50 questions per exam 1 point each, which are hard to study for because of terrible study guides that just give terms to know, not how to apply them. Class averages are always pretty low compared to other PSYC courses.

His lectures are very long and he will typically skip to the next slide before you can have half of it written down. There are not many homework assignments so your overall grade is based off of exams which are not easy. The study guides are pretty broad and last test, majority of the class got a C or lower.

Makes everything political and not enough psyc or social issues. We all know how he votes and encourages students to talk poorly about the other party. I don't disagree with his views, but cmon this class is supposed to be educational, not a rant/yap fest. Also graded by 2 exams, 2 assignments, and attendance/participation.

Assignments are graded generously and are interesting. Tests are difficult, but talking to TAs and Professor Molina during office hours can help tremendously as they will explain every question of the exam. You will have 3 exams and a final, the lowest of the four will be dropped. Lectures are enjoyable, but reading is equally important for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Molina is a nice guy but his grading criteria is hard. You are graded on very few things. The tests are impossible to study for. When I was in this class the average grade on a test didn't get over 75% and he was happy about that. Overall, content was interesting just a very hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is only made up of 250 points, 150 of which come from three exams. The rest of the points come from online homework and two papers. His tests are extremely difficult and are computer generated. His ego is huge and he was happy with an average score of 76% on exams rather than changing his style for student success.

I have had a horrible experience in this class. There is no good way to study for exams, and he will not help you study. Class average was a D on exams. There are 3 exams that make up the ENTIRE grade plus two small assignments. I am a good student and have struggled in this class. I will not take a class with him again.

Covers really interesting articles & topics. Class discussion-based so come prepared to participate, but he makes it engaging. Created an environment where it's safe to ask questions & talk about big ideas. I think a lot of folks kind of blew off the class which was a bummer because it's one of the better ones I've taken at KU.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super engaging lectures! Delivery is entertaining (often humorous) with fascinating content. Barely any homework  a couple easy projects/papers and you technically don't have to do the readings, but they make the exams (open-note) easy As. Clear grading criteria.
Very easy class to pass if you pay attention and turn in assignments. He is clear about the requirements for assignments, if you follow them, you will get a good grade.

Attendance isn't mandatory but highly recommended. All questions from exams and papers are discussed during lectures. He is very easy going and straight forward. Clear expectations for assignments. His focus is for students to learn and be interested in his class. Exams and writings aren't created to be tricky, everything is in textbook or lectures

Ludwin was a great orator, his lectures were very engaging. if you want to excel read the text book. as long as you make sure you pay attention in lecture and skim the book and study a few days before the exams you should be fine. and go to the lab they take attendance there and those are easy points and participate!

Lectures are not mandatory but his tests are very hard. You would think its common sense but you have to be able to apply the terms and concepts and the test questions can be confusing. There are also only 190 points for the whole semester.

Really enjoyed this class! I thought it was easy. Didn't read the book at all, almost everything on the tests comes from lecture and discussion. Make sure you go to discussion section! They tend to be really fun too.

Lectures are interesting and engaging. He is intelligent and his powerpoints hold all the information you need. The textbook is also very helpful. I would suggest showing up to lecture but it's not mandatory.
Don't need to go to class, puts all ppts online. As long as you know the information on the study guide you will do fine on the test

I showed up to the first three lectures, then after that only showed up on exam days, didn't once look at a textbook, and still managed to get a B+. Attending discussion is essential, and trying on the film reports is important, but other than that, the class is mostly common sense combined with review from previous psych classes. Very easy.

I didn't go to a single class after the first exam and ended up with an A in the class. Don't miss discussion because that is half of the class points. Go to discussion, try on the film reports, study the lecture slides and book, and you'll be fine. Just use the study guide for tests you can get an A

Dr. Molina is awesome! I was bummed that a lot of my classmates found his class boring, I thought it was super interesting. He makes social psych easy to understand and I got a lot out of his class this semester. He's super into social justice and film if that's your niche too. I wish he taught more classes!
Great teacher I would recommend him for anyone. His lectures are good and understanding them is a breeze. Just make sure you participate in the discussion because that will save you grade.

Great teacher. Gives a ton of examples that are very interesting. He never will email you back but you get paired with a TA for discussion and they are super helpful. You write 2 short papers and take 3 exams and the final is optional. I loved this class and my professor and I would recommend it to anyone!

Molina is a great lecturer. He knows his stuff and throws out plenty of good examples. Not the greatest at emailing back, though. Lecture attendance not mandatory; discussions are. Tests are multiple choice, but can be tricky.

"I would suggest" and "I would argue" are his favorite phrases. You'll hear them over and again. Class was interesting enough, but not necessary to attend. Notes are online and read chapter for tests. You must attend discussions. Only 150 pt for the entire semester. Don't have a bad week or a life, if you do this easy class will kill your GPA.

Molina is a nice guy, pretty funny, but the class overall is a joke. It's pretty easy, and you can tell he definitely knows what he is talking about and loves it, the class is just kinda "eh" though. An easy enough grade.
Professor Molina is an average professor. He really enjoys showing video clips and having students watch films. The class isn't difficult if you attend discussions and lectures.
He's very funny and will get you interested in the course. Very fun class to take, and he tries to keep textbook costs very minimal.

no text book.  journal articles make up the course content (which he posts for you)interesting and timely lectures. excellent and passionate teacher.  uses multimedia.  encourages real discussion. respectful of diverse opinions. challenges you to think.
Allows actual discussion, respects students ideas and values them.

i took social psychology. he's so funny, VERY passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches, and his tests are pretty easy. if you study, you can def get an A because he doesn't write trick questions on the exams. they're all straight-forward and his lecture are very interesting and can be applied to real life! :)

Syllabus: "Homework every day. Plan on 3 hours of outside work each day."
Hw usually 2-3 questions. Tests are the same as the hw but you are only given 50 minutes. Professor claims tests show mastery over concepts but expects perfection from rushing students 3x faster than normal...
Rome wasn't built in a day.
Very Intelligent engineer/politician/professor guy! You will love his class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very good at explaining the content
He was great and you get a lot of extra credit. He is great.

Its true that he is a hard professor, but he knows his stuff and his lectures are well structured. Exams make or break your grade which can be a challenge to some. I personally loved his rigid class structure. My ADHD brain was able to focus on the content which I appreciated. I'd take his classes again.

he is one of the most unfair profs at the university of Kansas. The lec are long and sometimes irrelevant. the exams are hard and worth 75% of your grade and the homework grading is confusing and unfair. there's no extra credit opportunity and he does not care if you understand the content or fail the class or if you are going through a hard time.

Bob Lyon is the franklin the turtle of professors. He believes fully that you life should revolve around statics and dynamics. On top of this the lecture is 50 minutes five days of the week with homework due the next day. The homework does not match any example done in class. Tests are worth 75% of the grade with the homework grading sabotaged.

Amazing professor, he is very kind, respectful, and understanding towards students. His lectures were always very engaging and fun. I learned a lot in his honors seminar, and the content was genuinely very interesting. Additionally, there was little to no homework outside of class.
Lyles is a goat

Ward is compassionate about the success of his students. The focus of the class was about personal emotions and bias when working as a planner, and understanding how to spot bias and holes in data and research. Ward provided real life examples and discussion to ground the importance of compassion in planning. Would take a class with Ward again.
If I had 3 wishes, one of them would be to go back in time and choose NOT to take a class with Prof. Ward Lyles. It was an undoubtable waste of time. Clown.
Absolutely loved this course taught by Lyles. Hes an incredible professor and I would take another class with him in an instant.
Lydia is very kind and inspiring to have as a professor. The class became close to her and she made sure we were on top of our readings. She's a powerhouse.

Took this course years ago but I maintain that this is the least I have ever seen an instructor care about a class. She would show up late, end class early and generally make it clear that she did not want to be there. 

The SW 220 course is about as easy as it gets but I would be wary when taking a 600+ level course with her.

Lydia prefers to be called Lydia, not Professor. She's really great, and I really don't understand the poor reviews. If you do the work, as with any teacher, and put forth effort, you will do well. This was my easiest class this semester and I really enjoyed it. I'm looking forward to taking 353, Macro SW Practice, with her next semester.
She's a very sweet person and definitely accessible outside of class but the lectures are pretty dry. It's an easy A but not the class to take if you really want to learn and be challenged.
No. No, no, no. 0/10 do NOT take lydias classes. She doesnt even read the papers she assigns
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lydia is a complete dunce. She needs to get her life together before she tries to be in charge of students grades and education
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I love Lydia! She gives class time to discuss current events. Lectures are exciting and fun. She is very knowledgeable about the profession and brings to the table her own experiences. I took the two classes I could with her and would do it again in a heartbeat! She is a very caring person and genuinely cares about you as a student! Take her class

I adore Lydia! She engages students in a variety of ways with a ton of opportunities for hands on work. She is a practicing social worker and extremely knowledgeable about the field. Lydia makes the classroom and safe and enjoyable space for all students.

Lydia is an amazing social worker, and a good person to learn from. She doesn't believe in the basic style of learning, which I respect, and she doesn't want to waste our time. Her lectures are really interesting, even though we get off topic sometimes. Show up, participate, and do the work, and you should get an A.

I love this class. It's not finished yet for this semester but wanted to let you know who need it for the SW program that she's a rock star in all ways. Caring, thoughtful, respectful, wants you to succeed. I'm taking her class next sem too! She's also very personable and  talks about her practice which I think is a great quality in a professor.

Lydia is a practicing clinical social worker and her experience in the field certainly shows in the classroom. She is extremely warm and empathetic with a strong passion for social justice. Very respectful of her students. I wouldn't change a thing!

Lectures are insanely boring, if it was not for her doing attendance points I would never show up because the weekly quizzes are all straight from the book/her ppts that she posts. Everything she does is group work, so if you get a bad group you are screwed. Not understanding whatsoever and just overall bad at teaching (loses her train of thought)

Doesn't show that she knows what she is talking about. She will lose her train of thought multiples times during lecture and can not explain things well. Quizzes and tests are fairly easy. You can skip class and not miss anything.

I'd taken this back in 2008. After seeing some of the comments, I wanted to stick up for her a bit. She's not "easy", but if you put in the effort, you'll do fine. She is very willing to help, even outside of regular hours. Just ask. And put in the effort.
sucks! she shouldnt be teaching. Shes rude, and horrible, i cant believe the higher ups havent done anything about her yet
Worst teacher ever, shes a T.A. but she doesnt know how to teach, selfish and doesnt know the topic.  I dont even know how she's even going to get her degree, she doesnt do anything

40% of grade was attendance.  You will need to keep up by reading 1-2hrs per night.  As long as you read, you will be fine.  Lectures are boring and all over the place, which makes it impossible to keep good notes. Make sure to turn everything in on time.  Teacher seems to want opinions, and can somehow grade them.  Clarity is bad.

Worst teacher i have ever had,  i was having trouble understanding a concept once and went to ask her.  She told me to go look at the notes, but she talks to fast to keep track of the notes in class so what am i supposed to do guess.   And she makes her tests nearly impossible and writes them based on how much coffee she has the night before....

Lectures are very boring and really come straight from the book, but it is worth going to. Lectures off of a powerpoint that just has pictures on it, so you have to listen real well to get the information. She gives out a study guide before the test, which is very helpful. Not really that hard of a class.

TERRIBLE!!  No need to attend lecture because all power points come directly out of the book.  If you have a question, don't bother because usually she doesn't answer it.  Doesn't care if you have a legitimate illness or reason for needing to take a test early, forget about it.  Seems like an ok person, but shouldn't be teaching this course.

For summer version, his pre recorded lecture videos, supplementary videos and other resources help you a lot. Exams constitute most of your grade but He is very generous with partial credit. He cares more about you understanding the concept rather than just cram equations and then plugging in the numbers. One of the best engineering professors FR.

The professor was good but i just don't like how the class is set up. 75% is exams and the exams are 3 questions so the majority of your grade is 15 questions. you have homework every day and can take up to 2 hours to do. even if you do well on the homework then it doesn't matter because your homewrok grade can only be 10% higher than your exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lyon is the best lecturer I have had at KU. It was easy to pay attention and listen to him. Doing group example problems in class was very helpful, and the hibbeler example problems were practically essential for preparing for the exams. It's tough to get an A but the class is set up so you really learn the material.
Robert is a great teacher but makes his class really test-dependent, which was a problem for me and some of my classmates.  I learned a lot in this class though, and he's great at explaining things.

he's a good teacher. not very personable, i feel like it's hard to talk to him because he's "all business". daily homework that takes ~2 hours to do. new unit is taught every day with an exam every 10 units. working together on homework is frowned upon by him. we already know everybody does it. very rigorous class. you will need to work for an A.
Amazing professor! Always wanting to help and make sure you thoroughly understand the subject, made a typically hard class much easier!
Professor Lyon is a great teacher, tells you what he expects from his class and helps you achieve it.

Bob is a good professor. He does a good job explaining the material and makes studying fair as he uploads videos and has plenty of extra problems to practice. His class was very difficult for me, however. You will have homework every day and he will not take any excuses for missed assignments. You will do fine if you try.
Good professor, the class is lots of work but doable.

Prof. Lyon is a pretty good teacher. There is HW every day that you need to upload, it is a good way to test your understanding of the class. The bad thing about him is that he is test heavy. Usually, 60% of the class is just the exam; but when I took it he said there wasn't enough time for the group project and added that 15% to the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is easy to get a B in, but hard to get an A--if you study hard for ALL the exams, you should get an A. It's nice because he doesn't make you buy a textbook and gives you a printed out version of everything you need to know for the whole semester. No curves, and doesn't tell you the class averages on exams...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework every night, good lecturer and tests are fair. Work hard and you'll get an A.

Took CE 301 online over summer. Horrible experience. Lyon was inconsiderate of student's struggles and believes he does no wrong in his teaching/grading. TA that held office hours did not know the material well and graded unfairly. Homeworks were made by students while they were taking the course. Posted solutions were often wrong. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Lyon is extremely knowledgable on the subject and his lectures are purposeful. He expects a lot from his students (homework every night, very strict formatting, etc) but it is helpful come exam time.
