Attending class is essential, especially because there is homework due every day. His exams are fair and are easier than the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class every single day, HW every single day, and at least 2 hours outside of class per day. If you want to do well, you must show up to class and pay attention, and complete the HW's. It also helps to work the "Fundamental Problems" in the textbook for extra practice. Amazing professor though. Clear, concise, and truly cares about his students.

Homework everynight. Test are tough. Final is not partial credit and very hard. Instead of helping students in class he sits up from and makes the TAs help. Not a good teacher and not very helpful. Final will kill your grade. Dont expect anything from him.

Professor Lyon has been one of my favorite instructor during my time at KU.  His lectures are purposeful and I found that I learned a great deal in them.  His tests can be a bit hard, but I always found them to be very fair.  All of the problems are solvable; some are harder than others, but nothing was unrealistic about them.
he's not helpful

VERY knowledgeable of course material. Comes off very arrogant; everyone either loves him or hates him.   Homework EVERY SINGLE night, tests about every 2 weeks, lots of group work, & 1-2 heavily weighted group projects. Fundamental Probs from book are VERY helpful.  You cant slack in this class, it will seriously hurt you. DON'T MISS CLASS!

Material is well-organized and presented concisely in short videos prior to lecture. HW every night due AT the beginning of class, no exceptions. Tests problems are fundamental, not tricky, but cover lots of material. Course grade too dependent on assigned group members, with challenging in-class group assignments to be completed in 20 min.
One of the worst teachers I've had in Ku Engineering. He is extremely nit picky with homework. Do not even udder the word "cheat" in his class or he will implode. Wouldn't recommend.

He works out problems in class and posts the lecture notes online. He explains everything very clearly. He didn't really tell you what to expect for the exams, which was hard to study for because so much material was covered yet only 4-5 questions were asked. Homework every single day.

Was a structural engineer before KU so teaching statics & dynamics is easy for him. My only bad thing to say about this course was he changed the the format of testing for the final from the Given: Find: Plan: Diagram: Solution: with points being awarded for work to multiple choice with no credit for work  shown but had to show work to get credit.
not the best

Demanding course. Homework/class everyday. He teaches off of slides, but will usually work a problem or two out pretty regularly. He does not produce a study guide for his tests, which would be extremely helpful considering the vast amount of material covered between tests. Overall, a pretty good teacher.

Lyon is very clear and goes over material well in class, but rarely actually does problems. The only reason I'm surviving his class now is because of his amazing TA Stephanie. He also takes a letter grade off your test if you ask a question during the test. That just seems crazy.

Bob Lyon is the most engaging lecturer I have had at KU. He is very knowledgeable, but also very demanding. You can't be average and get an A in his class - probably a sore point of some poor reviews. He gives out a lot of work and expects you to go beyond the assignment prompts and really learn the material.

This Assistant professor is not helpful. He just reads his compilations of slides and gives you a ton of homework to go complete and the next day reads the slides. No examples worked out by him in class. He expects you to produce everything on your own. Horrible teacher. I regret taking this class especially in the summer.Not worth it.
One of the worst professors EVER !!! He doesn't help much, he gives tons of homework and he is very strict

I am an "A" student. This professor is so weird that I still do not understand his behave. I am taking this course in the summer, and he is horrible. Everyday 1-5 homework problems. He doesn't explain them after due date, all he do is posting the solution manual. If you ask him a question during the exam, he won't answer.I don't recommend his class

He is a good teacher, but the daily homework is a little taxing. Also, he's very strict about getting to class on time. He would frequently deny people the ability to turn in their work if they were more than a minute or two late. I hated his attitude the whole time I took the course but I can't deny his teaching ability.

Lyon is a great professor. He has an exciting, intelligent lecture style. He gave us a reasonable amount of homework, and was fair about what was expected on tests and projects. Everything was very straight-forward. We are lucky to have him here at KU.

Remarkable Professor, I learned an extremely large amount of information in very usable ways in chunks that I could understand and keep straight. The quintessential excellent engineering professor. Go Lyon!
Very nice and helpful. I took this class during the summer and absolutely enjoyed it with Dr. Lyon.

She is very relatable and easy to talk to. Sometimes her accent is hard to understand and speaks fairly fast but overall I have never minded going to class. She is slow about responding to emails though.

My favorite French instructor. Mary is always willing to work with students. She is patient and explains difficult concepts in a way students can understand. Not only this, but she's incredibly friendly. I high recommend taking French with her, especially if you are just beginning intermediate courses.

I am so glad that Mary received an award for teaching this class because she did an amazing job. She is clear, very knowledgeable and very approachable. I will take any other class she teaches and I highly recommend her to any student. She is awesome!

This is a conversation class and Mary made it worth the while since we are supposed to just speak French and scared me stiff. She varied the activities and both inside and outside the class that made it easy to speak French. At the end, I became more confident and my study abroad experience was a breeze. Thanks a lot Mary.

Our Instructor for this class died and Mary had to step in. She turned out to be the best that could possibly happen to us in this class. She is very smart, intelligent, helpful, and very cheerful. This is the best class I have ever taken. ay golden Mary.

Where do I begin? Mary is simply a great teacher, nice, understanding, always available, clear. She does all the activities in the book and posted her lesson power point online so you could go back and review. The class was intense, but Mary's attitude made it all seem easy. Lots of homework though, but this is intensive grammar. I recommend her!!!

Fren 300 is an intensive grammar class so most grammatical structures are covered. I failed this class the first time I took it and had to take it with Ms. Mba on recommendation. Her class was already full but she accepted me. She worked with me one on one and followed up with me even outside of class because I needed the class to graduate.

Her accent was hard to understand most times and the homework load was nonstop. The first test we took was the hardest French test I've ever taken in my 6 years of the language. She doesn't completely have her act together when teaching the class but is nice on her own.

Mary is Awesome! I was her student because some other students told me that she is good. I think that that is an understatement because Mary is fantastic. She is extremely helpful, very cheerful and always cheers the students up. Her class is so much fun to be in and I learned so much. I recommend Mary's class to any and everyone.

I love Mary! She's one of the nicest professors you can get. She does talk in French a lot, but if you don't understand, she will explain it for you. Very helpful. Does a lot of partner work in class. If you have a problem or need some accommodation, she's very willing to work with you. I highly recommend taking a class with her.

Fantastic teacher. Super nice and caring. Really wants every student to do well and get a good grade. Grades very easy and is very helpful. Will let you make up missed work and doesn't take off many participation points for missing class.
Dr. Hartley was awesome. She gives lots of iClickers in class and does handwritten notes in class that are both very beneficial.

Dr. Hartley was a great professor!  She does a great job of simplifying concepts and making the subject really easy to understand. She was super nice and made the expectations for the class crystal clear.  The problems on tests were almost exactly like the practice problems we did in class and the practice tests we got to do.

Dr. Hartley is an awesome professor that truly cares for her students. She is always approachable and available to students. The class is pretty test-heavy, but her tests have a built-in curve that helps make it more manageable. She provides lots of practice problems for the exams, and there isn't too much homework overall. Highly recommend!

If you enjoy an environment where criticism is disguised as “teaching” and favoritism is basically a personality trait, then you'll love him. He hides his bullying behind whatever excuse is convenient that day. Good luck getting basic respect.

Had him two years ago and just the other day a freshman was talking about how bad their comms teacher was. I immediately guessed Dan Merwin and I was right. If that tells you anything, it is that his reputation still speaks for itself. One of the most frustrating and unprofessional teachers I have ever had.

He constantly used humor to mask his insecurities and mean spirited attitude. His grading was completely subjective and based on personal opinion. Feedback was rarely constructive, just sarcastic and condescending comments that felt more like personal attacks. One of the worst teaching experiences I have ever had.

Dan is an interesting guy who makes class fun. He is very clear with his gradings which makes the speeches easier and helps you have all the resources you need. He is also very responsive with emails and professional in the class.
He is a really good professor, he kinda grades toughly but at the end of the day, he wants you to do good and learn public speaking and if you focus and work hard, this class is easy.
Phenomenal instructor. Take in as much as you can while he lectures and no doubt you will get an A. Take him if you are a hard worker and want to actually get better at public speaking.

Don't get me wrong, Professor Merwin is a cool guy. However, he is so picky about answers after he asks a question. Be aware that if he asks a question and you are at all questioning your answer, he will get annoyed that you don't 100% know the answer. He often acts like he can't be bothered by questions you ask, or that he is above you.

Extremely nice and you can tell he is experienced at what he does. Even as someone who doesn't enjoy public speaking, this class was fun for me and I felt I learned a lot. Dan is great and will always offer you helpful feedback after every speech/exercise. I genuinely enjoyed being in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dan is very nice and enthusiastic, making this class very fun even as a required course. He's always open to helping you individually through email or office hours so I would recommend taking advantage of that! Overall, it's an easy course that you will learn a lot from regardless of your major.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Was nervous about taking a speech class but he made it so relaxed and easy. He is very laid back and easy to talk to for help. I have gotten all A's on speeches surprisingly and there are only 2 tests you take (easy 100%). Participation matter and will make or break your grade. Overall great teacher. TAKE HIM
He is so awesome! Work hard and you will get an A.

Dr. Tara is ok for an intro to bio class. She reads off the slides and her exams are easy (and I don't think they change). You have to go if you want participation points. Sometimes I'd just sit outside the classroom because I didn't need someone to read the slides that day but I needed clickers!
Dr. Marriage is very kind and accessible. Semi-Mandatory Lectures. Posts slides from class, and tests are very straightforward. Good professor to introduce biology at KU.

Great woman, always interactive with the class, TAs were cool. I was never great at Biology but she made me want to try just a little bit harder. Homework amount was always reasonable, and everything was mainly done through McGraw-Hill SmartBooks and textbooks. Ended the semester with a B, and she still rounded me up to an A!
LOVE her. Got both BIOL 150 & BIOL 370 from her. She is the best. But she is not answering your emails. Just go to office hours.
This class is easy, the test is not hard if you use her slides to study along with the study guides and the groupwork assignments.

One of the easiest classes at KU. Do the assignments, go to lectures, take the exams, and go to review sessions and you'll be golden. She will literally drop the final too (or lowest exam grade), drop your lowest graded assignment, and will give extra credit. Lectures are posted online and there are tons of opportunities for practice in class.

As long as you do the Smartbooks and Connect quizzes, you'll be fine. She has opportunities for extra credit on every test. There are review sessions before every test and going to them helped with refreshing on each topic.

Dr. Marriage was great. She made boring subjects not-so-boring and made me excited for the class along with making me feel like I am where I belong and I can do well. I've taken a lot of science classes and these tests are not hard. Study the material and the resources she gives you. Take notes during lectures and put in what you want out of it.

Dr. Marriage has a way with words when she is teaching. She loved teaching and you can tell. She will answer any question you have with a smile on her face. The PLUS sessions are a lifesaver and help prepare you well for the tests. The grading is also extremely balanced and one bad test score will not tank your grade. If you can take this class do!
She is so funny and has such a great way of explaining the concepts.
Dr. Marriage is a great professor. She knows the material she's teaching and tries to get to know her students. She is mainly a lecturer, but she's enthusiastic and engaging.
I barely studied for the exams and continued to get above 95% on almost all of them. She does a great job with the lectures.

she is a very nice and caring professor. her lectures are easy and exams are pretty straightforward. use the homework to help study for exams, because they are very similar. take advantage of group work and take good notes!

I took this class online during the summer, and it was great. Homework is assigned every week and isn't too bad, just WS and online lab(lab can take a min to figure out). You have a group project that you work on throughout the course, annoying but to hard. Tests are open note and can get points back on them. The teacher seems super nice and chill.

This was my first science class at KU, and I was worried, but Dr. Marriage made it very easy to learn. Her lectures are clear, and the homework helps a lot with the exams. We had five exams, could drop one, and got 5 points EC on each. The exams were very straightforward and all MCQ. To study for the exams, look over lectures and do SmartBook HW.

Taking Dr. Marriage's course has helped me learn to love science and gain confidence. She has clearly outlined expectations and her exams are straightforward. Lectures are engaging and it is clear that she loves the content she is discussing...also provides tons of resources for those struggling. She takes a complex subject and makes it enjoyable.
I LOVE THIS WOMEN PLEASE TAKE HER CLASS
She is so kind and will help you at any time. She will sit and talk to you because she cares about every student. She is cool

Dr. T is a kind & friendly professor, she clearly outlines expectations and is efficient. She gives excellent advice on studying if you ask her and overall her class is designed to promote student growth. The most challenging aspect of the class is that some tests are way harder than others. She also has a great sense of humor and is very sweet!
Loved Dr. Marriage and this class

Dr. Marriage is definitely one of the best biology professors. You do have a lot of exams and things kind of go quick. You get a lot of dropped assignments and one dropped exam (can be the final). Five total exams and there is always 5 points of extra credit for each one. Her lectures are really fun and she really cares about her students.

Dr. Marriage was a fine teacher she gave extra credit for tests and study guides which did make those easier. I do have to say I had the flu during one of her test and she would not let me take it at a different time even though I gave her a Dr.'s note. You do get to drop one test but she didn't try to work with me which is against KU policy.
I liked her, there was just a lot of notes. We covered a chapter a lecture so it was rough. Just make sure to actually study and you'll do fine.
Dr. Marriage is the best bio professor that I think I've ever had. She is so funny too and i don't think she even knows it.
I love her

I LOVE Dr. Marriage! Her lectures are so engaging, and it's clear how passionate she is about her field of study. The class schedule makes sense and was easy to follow. She is also very encouraging when questions are asked. Just be careful and study up for the tests, as they're worth a hefty portion of the overall grade. (Go to PLUS sessions!)
Dr. Marriage is an excellent professor and I was truly inspired by her ability to teach and re-energize me. Highly recommend her!

Dr. Marriage is an absolute gem. She is such a kind person and genuinely cares about her students. She is the type of professor that does not take pride in students failing. She drops grades and offers extra credit. Clear outline for tests and posts study guides. My favorite professor, literally amazing.
Honestly I loved Ms.Mapes so much she was such a kind and caring teacher and I had such a fun time gaining confidence in my public speaking skills in her class. :)

Dr. Mapes is one of my favorite professors. She is very understanding and always willing to talk about anything you need. Her priority is very clearly learning not grades. Just a wonderful woman and makes the class so much bigger than giving speeches. She equips you with information on bias, research, and understanding audiences as a whole.
Top 5 funniest professor of all time

One of the best professors I've had! Definitely not a public speaking person but she made this class fun and made sure everyone was really prepared. One of the most caring and relatable professors I've met. Would absolutely take one of her classes again.

You can tell Dr. Mapes cares about students and makes class interesting. You have four speeches to give throughout the semester, but if you prepare, they're nothing to worry about. I never did the textbook readings listed on the course schedule and she never asked about them in class. However, the book is very useful for the open note quizzes.

Dr. Mapes is incredibly caring and understanding of the difficulties of class during a pandemic. Its not an easy class by any means but if you do your work she is more than willing to help you improve your grades.

Great professor, obviously cares about her students. Provides meaningful and descriptive feedback that is helpful for improving your communication skills. One note - she's one of "those" professors who doesn't give out perfect grades on speeches (on papers she does). However, an A is very attainable as long as you put forth the effort and time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Mapes is a great professor and gives helpful feedback on speeches. That being said, she is very hard to please and is not an easier grader. She will always find something on every section of the rubric to mark points off of. I had her read through a paper before I turned it in and she said it looked great and I still got points off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She teaches this class for honors and non-honors students. I took the non-honors version; however, she grades it like it is a honors course. She is a very picky grader when she grades the speeches. This class is way harder than it needs to be for a 100 level course. I struggled more in this class than I did in my honors biology class.

Dr. Mapes definitely pushes you to do your best, but she's there to help you along the way. Not an easy-A class. Tough grader, but gives good feedback and is eager to help if you ask. Very engaging and relatable. Didn't read textbook in class, but used pages out of it and needed some info for the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's a tough grader, but is more focused on progress rather than ability going into the class. She's understanding and provides good advice/feedback. Can be pretty funny.
Super easy class: first 5 weeks for resume building before career fair. Attendance taken, occasional presenters, few class cancellations. 1–2 short assignments weekly (~30 mins total)
bus 210 easy A

Although the class can be boring and sometimes repetitive, it is fairly easy. She is very caring and flexible when you reach out to her about something. Don't be afraid to ask for help on your resume, she gives clear and honest feedback that will help you and your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super great teacher and is an easy class. Gives lots of extra credit and helps you when you need it.

She was very helpful in providing feedback on assignments, such as my resume. She teaches well and thorough in her zoom calls and always remains professional in the workplace. Material in the lectures was always conveyed very clearly and showed interest in her students during the calls. Maria is also very accessible outside of class.
He is a very passionate professor who wants you to have fun and succeed. Just make sure you participate and come prepared otherwise he will get pretty upset.

He isn't bad, he just crashed out a lot. Like he will freak out and storm out of the class. I failed his class because I never went, it was just so painfully boring and he's a tough grader when it comes to papers and will catch you if you use AI. The most boring class I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A great teacher that has high expectations for his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McDonald is an awesome professor, and really engages with his students. It's clear he cares about as well as enjoys his job, which contributes to the environment in the classroom. I would take his class again.

He means well and likes to have good class discussions but the lectures can be heavy and a lot of the time you can get lost in them. I will warn you, there's a 10-page end-of-semester paper that is only worth 60 points. (It sucks and should be worth more) There are no quizzes or exams, but he's kinda picky and critical about writing assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor was stressful and gave me bad grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worked very hard in the class,  but still gave bad grades.

This is my favorite class I've taken at KU. Professor McDonald's lectures are incredibly thought provoking, and he is very accessible outside of class to answer questions and help with homework. He truly cares about his students and wants them to be their best. The class was difficult, but so worth it.

I had Professor McDonald for COMS177 last year. I always looked forward to attending class because of its thought-provoking and engaging atmosphere. The coursework is manageable, as long as you communicate, he will give you extensions (within reason). His lectures left me with something to think about and I genuinely enjoyed my time in this class.

Attendance is not mandatory but I only missed one class because of how much I enjoyed it. The lectures are engaging and he introduced very interesting concepts that were well explained. His feedback was very complementary and if you want to bounce an idea for a paper around with him he is open for office hours.

Best grader, will not screw you over as long as you meet the criteria. Classes are easier than most but he puts all the effort in to make it fun for students. His in class lectures are great, if you have ideas, always present them. He's always listening.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The lectures for this class are amazing. The professor is really great with extensions, absences, and other things as long as you communicate. I wish I could take this class again! The stuff you learn in this class is so cool and thought-provoking for anyone. He makes the lectures exciting and you get to talk about your favorite movies and shows.
This guy is a horrible teacher. If you have the opportunity to take this class pass because its awful and its taught by an awful dude

I found McDonald to give the best feedback of almost any professor I have taken. He is an amazing teacher and gives really good input on his lectures. He has given my favorite lecture at KU hands down and always grades fair. I find that he is very easy to talk to and always willing to help students improve their skills. A true scholar.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Taking COMS 235 with Dr. McDonald was not the easiest but I enjoyed it and if you really want to succeed in this class you must work for it. Dr. McDonald is caring about all his students and pretty good at lecturing. Ultimately, I would say this class helped me in my development of writing more than anything and for that I am extremely grateful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really did not enjoy this class. Although it's not too hard, the professor grades way too tough for what we are doing. Very specific on what he wants and doesn't conform to others' ideas. Most people will be fine in this class if they participate and do everything the way he wants it, but otherwise I wouldn't take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great teacher! Very easy going and not much homework besides the reading, which you can skip as long as you listen in classes. Besides that, just the speeches and two tests which he tells you exactly what you need. Engaging and fun, I really enjoyed this class!
Very fun and engaging. Lays out exactly what he expects from speeches and what will be on the tests. Tough grader on speeches but gives plenty of other assignments to make up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I cannot stand this guy. First, I have no clue what he's about. Half the time he dresses up business casual, the other half he wears soccer jerseys and star trek uniforms. He's also a really tough grader and gives a completely whack participation grade at the end of the semester. Definitely get a different lecturer if you want a reasonable grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ma laoshi believes in all of his students and has a very vast and deep knowledge of China as well as many other cultures. He wants the best for his students and while the class can appear difficult, with time and practice it benefits you in the long run. Stick with it! I know you can do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a harsh grader, but that just means you're expected to know the material inside and out. The material isn't conceptually difficult, you just have to read carefully and often reread. Due to this, I learned a lot and feel like I can actually retain what I've learned.

In his classes, he expects you to be very prepared each day as he will call on you. He is also a very harsh grader. His classes are very book heavy as well. He is very knowledgeable in his studies, and his lectures are very interesting but difficult. Overall, his classes were the hardest and worst grades I ever received in college.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I thought that his knowledge and personal experiences involving the topics in his class made it all really interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He gave good lectures and was fairly nice, but the course was extremely difficult and time consuming for a 100 level. He was a harsh grader too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He covers each lesson's material well and efficiently every class period. Not too much homework, though he is a bit of a tough grader.
The guy really knows his stuff. He is a leader in his field. Sexual politic, opium wars, and an excellent Chinese teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: McMahon's class was one of my favorite in the whole department. He is incredibly well spoken and cultured, and his knowledge base is vast and built on years of experience in China. He is quite funny during lecture as well. He is a tough grader when it comes to papers, but the feedback is good as well. Don't miss the chance to take his class.

Incredible man, if you ever are given the opportunity to take his classes, do so! He is the smartest in his field as has an extremely specific knowledge base, witch includes homosexuality in China, Opium Smoking and female rulers. Do ask questions, this man will not disappoint

He is an excellent professorshuman beings. You'll regret not having taken one of his courses if you are at all interested in anything "China." He knows his stuff backwards and forwards, but is not arrogant in any way. If he doesn't know something, he'll tell you. He enjoys good discussions, so speak up and follow along! You'll love him- for sure.

Professor McMahon is an awesome teacher! The way he explains things in class is very clear and very well. He will help you whenever you have any problems/questions. I really enjoy taking his class and I wish all teachers were just as nice as him!

Professor McMahon is a great teacher. He's also a very interesting and funny person. I've had more than 1 class with him and they're all pretty fun. His classes aren't easy but they're not hard either. Just be prepared for class and you'll get a good grade.

His Sexual Politics class is extremely interesting. I like his lecturing style as well. My problem is with the paper assignments and essay tests which seem to ask the same questions over and over, and he's a hard grader. He is a really friendly professor though with a great sense of humor and a vast knowledge of the subject he is teaching.

He only expected us to know what he provided us. He's a stickler for details but he's not unreasonable. He has the patience of a saint and and really cared about our success. I found myself caring about learning what he had to teach more than my grade & stopped taking notes, which consequently improved my grade.

I really liked Professor McMahon as a person.  That being said, he was not the most organized lecturer I've ever had.  As the previous poster said, he is a hard grader.  He will rip you apart on your writing style for the papers.  An A seemed unobtainable, and most of my class settled for C's.  The class is interesting but difficult.

He's a good guy, but his lectures are very disorganized.  He asks very specific, yet ambiguous, essays and open ended questions. (no multiple choice). I would never recommend him.  A lot of good students in my  class had to settle for Cs.
Great professor would take again

She is an extremely hard grader. Rarely gives extension even if you email. Have to do all work as a group and are graded by the group and not an individual grade. Asked her a question once about a project we had and she gave a rude response saying she wouldn't answer it until after class and walked away from me.

She was yapping the entire time about her being lonely and our team member had a really bad problem with one of the students in class and went to tell her because she felt unsafe and the woman didn't do anything about the issue.

She picked and chose who she likes and if doesn't like you, she makes it known. She's very passive aggressive. My teammate was dealing with a very serious issue and instead of fixing it she would favor the people who were harassing her. Do not recommend her.

I had a terrible experience in her class and asked for her help dealing with a serious in-class issue and she did nothing about it. She knew that I was in a dangerous situation and she flirted with the student that was harassing me. Terrible teacher.

She is actually awful. All of the information is taught online yet lectures are still mandatory. In lecture you will only learn about her personal life. She puts you in randomly assigned groups with a heavy amount of group work. There is about ten assignments due on Monday of every week. Her GTAs also grade really hard. Take a different professor!

Very centered around group work with a group you are assigned to for the whole semester, I personally was not compatible with mine at all. She makes a lot of self-deprecating comments and can tend to be offensive, also talks about herself a lot, you can tell she is lonely. Attendance is mandatory, also a pretty heavy amount of homework.
Good teacher with fun lectures. Lots of work outside of class.
She is not nice at all. Do not take her class

Dr. McCartney did not have clear grading criteria, provided inconsistent feedback for grades, was snarky at times, unresponsive to emails, dismissive of feedback or questions, and had obvious favoritism. The best way to succeed in this class is to make friends in the class, since she assigns many long assignments and will provide little guidance.
Light-hearted

Dr. McCartney's class was hard, but the lectures were helpful. However, she does not grade anything symmetrically. My friends and I would compare answers, sometimes we would have the same thing and she would take off points for one but the other would have 100%. She very obviously has favorites, and can be snarky when she is challenged.
Good

Class is mostly self taught with no lectures in class. Lots of wasted time in class and most assignments are group assignments. Tests/quizzes relate to nothing being learned in that section and the entire class mostly consists of Clicker questions. Good if you already know the material or want to teach the class to yourself.

Dr. McCartney makes this class your only priority. Most projects are group projects. Attendance is mandatory, but there is a lot of wasted time in class. The tests have questions that don't relate to class. The grading system isn't clear and is a coefficient based on several factors. You won't really know what your grade is until after finals.

I took 200 and 500 with Dr. McCartney and I love her! She is a tough grader and there is lots of group work in both courses, but you're able to dock your partners credit if they aren't contributing. She is super understanding and gave me tips just about navigating the higher education system. Very funny and always keeping it real!

Not only does Dr. McCartney assign on average 3-10 hours of homework (a 16 question short answer writing assignment every week), but she does not even give a lecture. Lectures are to be watched online, while class time is used for group work and its all self taught. Structure is confusing & simply too much for a 3-credit, 200 level class. DONT TAKE

This class was overall the most difficult compared to 500-600 level PSYC classes. The amount of work assigned was unnecessary especially since she could not get them graded on time. Her lectures were pointless and the group project was a waste of time. She did not respond to emails since she was so overwhelmed with the work that needed grading.

Groupwork is big in this class, but she does good to match you with people you're compatible with. She really cares about her students and tries to connect even in bigger classes. I think she's really funny and relatable, on top of that she values your mental health and if you're struggling she will extend deadlines or whatever you need.

McCartney and TA's were unclear about how we were being graded. Brought this up in class and was told she doesn't want to spend time on this and become disrespectful towards me. Doesn't provide rubrics for all assignments and the class was basically all group work with the same group all semester. Lack of instructions. Would not recommend.

SO MUCH GROUP WORK. do not take this class with this professor. Nothing was ever explained and we were just expected to figure eveerything out on our own. all material was essentially self-taught, and dr. mccartney or the TA's provided little to no help.
She makes absolutely no sense

Her grading criteria makes ABSOLUTELY no sense. For example, she offered an extra credit assignment; however, counted it as an actual assignment. (I was given a 10/10  just like regular assignment, NOT a 10/0  what an extra credit assignment should be). Thats just one example, her logic  NONSENSICAL.

She does not explain any of the assignments she gives, and she also doesn't tell you about assignments but then doesn't accept late work. It is very easy to get a low grade in class because of her idiotic lack of communication.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class involved a lot of busy work, and revolved around a group project. Even though the material was useful, the work that we did was not (especially considering most of it was done with the same group all semester). Dr. McCartney was unapproachable and did not want to be bothered. Take this course online if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Doesnt give adequate examples or Rubrics for projects and expects students to know advanced statistics. Fails to answer emails & cancels office hours frequently. TAs give out advice contradicting hers. The whole class is her summarizing the textbook and expecting students to understand without elaborating and mocks students for asking.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The content was easy to understand, but she made the class much more difficult than it needed to be. There were a lot of unnecessary, time-consuming assignments. Your entire grade, except for tests, is group work. The set up of the class is confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: My group could complain about how she taught us all day. She would give us wrong information and give us the right information a day before our project was due. Grading was tough and the TA's did not seem interested in this course, they did not know much and they looked uncomfortable. Tests are long but online.

100% group projects where you are reliant on others to actually contribute. Says she hates kids and doesn't want to be a parent. Piles on group projects the same week as her tests. Thinks she's clear in her requirements but isn't clear. Tons and Tons and Tons of quickly quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: While Dr. McCartney runs a tight shift, she knows what she is doing and genuinely cares. She is confident and smart, so sometimes it is hard to connect with her, especially since she is sarcastic. Yet, both times I have been in her class, I have felt well prepared and leave at the end of the semester knowing more than my fair share on her topic.

Honestly, not my favorite. Be prepared to work in groups because that is pretty much all you do. In class activities are typically easy, but the TA's will grade and will take many points off and won't tell you why. Tests are online which are super helpful. Lots of work outside of class.
very lazy, reads powerpoints, discussion is awful because it relies on others in the class, grading criteria is random, don't expect to get helpful information, instructions, or feedback.

I think that Dr. McCartney is a wonderful teacher. She is very supportive and always makes sure that everyone has the chance to participate. She cares a great deal about her students and it is very nice to see.

Dr. McCartney is the professor that forgets that students take other classes. She believes she has clear directions and grading criteria but most of it is unclear. She encourages students to ask her questions, but then doesn't answer kindly or tells us to figure it out. Exam averages were typically low Ds or Fs. Gives +/- "at her discretion."
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. McCartney is GREAT! She's really approachable and tries to add humor into her class. It is a very challenging course and you do have to read and study for the tests and actually try, but this should be typical for a 300 level course. I had to work really hard, but feel like I learned so much and my grade reflected it.

This class was unnecessarily difficult. She doesn't lecture during class, but makes the tests super hard. When you go into the class you are under the impression that in-class activity points are contribution points (easy 100%), but then very rarely do you get 100 on them. Don't ask questions because she will get defensive, and become condescending
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Tests are way harder than they should be for the set up of the class, classwork does NOT talk about the textbook in depth enough to make all of the questions straight from the book. Averages were rarely above a 60%,she did very little to try and raise them. Made many inappropriate comments in class and does not seem to actually care about students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Tests are very difficult. She doesn't use the study guides that you complete through LaunchPad. The lectures aren't lectures. If the material is discussed, it's very brief and she doesn't go in depth. Most of this class, you learn on your own, and the class isn't easy in general. She does lots of group work, but not actual teaching and explaining.

This was the by far the worst class I have taken because the teacher was not only unhelpful but made it very difficult to get a good grade. There is lots of in-class activities that are hard to score 100% on and there is not much feedback given for what was wrong. Also studied hours for the tests and the averages ended up getting worse each time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Actually, it is so unreasonable, won't give clear instructions, you will have 3 group projects at the same time, and he does not understand students, is not flexible, or reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very unorganized. Assignment guidelines are vague and grading is harsh. If there is another professor available, I beg of you to go with that choice. His class structure is stressful and overall a massive headache.
have fun finding out what you are supposed to do in the class he doesn't even tell you that.

Gives no guidelines, won't answer questions, and expects you to read his mind. So many group presentations and he will grill you with ridiculous questions. Grading is unfair. Participation is based on quality not quantity, so you get no participation points if what you said wasn't "good enough" which is subjective. Worst teacher I've ever had.

Provides very loose guidelines for assignments and is not helpful/incredibly dismissive when asked for details, but will take points off for very specific things he never mentioned. Gave feedback like "do better." Literally. He also tries to have a discussion-centric class but cuts everyone off constantly.
Professor was difficult to work with when it came to group projects and providing feedback.

Very difficult to communicate with, every time I spoke with him (both in class and outside of class), I felt disrespected. It constantly feels like he's trying to prove you wrong rather than help you. I've asked for help on multiple occasions and was told to figure it out. Awful teacher, he seems very knowledgeable but fails deeply at teaching.
Instructions for assignments and projects are very unclear. Hardest grader I have encountered at KU

Sanjay is fantastic - the lectures are student led and finally applied everything I learned in college to this class. Attendance & participation are large portions, however group projects are the largest - no exams. Dont choose teammates that wont work or youll severely struggle. Very complex but rewarding projects. Amazing guest speakers!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is tough due to Sanjays high expectations and the work load but it is very rewarding and you learn a lot! The only things I didnt like were the unclear instructions in some assignments and the amount of group work. Pro tip: pick good teammates if you want a good grade because this class has so many group presentations/group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: He loads this class with group projects and only one test. The test was 4 questions and had close to no information he provided in his lecture slides or on blackboard. The projects wouldn't be bad but he provides no framework for the work allowing you the student to fill the void. Its helpful and hurtful at the same time. Participation is HUGE.

Took two semesters with this professor. If you're looking for an easy A, probably not your class. But if you put in the work and effort, it's definitely worth it. Learned lots, a few presentations, and a lot of critical thinking and number sense. Direction on assignments can be somewhat vague, but you're an adult, you can figure it out. Go ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sanjay is a very knowledgeable professor. Go to class - He makes it worth your while and participation matters. Group projects, reading assignments, and presentations are expected. If you put the work in, you'll do great. Highly recommend I actually learned a lot from Sanjay and he challenges you!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was both valuable and engaging. I truly enjoyed collaborating with my peers throughout the course.

This introduction to the dance major course is designed so that Michelle can help guide students in this department. She will provide resources and helpful conversations for questions and concerns. She is very sweet, understanding, and ready to talk through your questions.

Michelle is caring and adaptable to fit the needs of her students. We explore body movement and choreography in class and present studies of work. Her lectures and feedback are insightful. She is a great teacher and this is a great class to develop movement vocabulary for your own dance and setting work on others.
Danc 150 Michelle is a helpful teacher, she is willing to discuss your progress. Lectures are designed to really push your dance ability. And enjoyable.

Laura is a fun and witty teacher who cares about her students and their needs. There's a decent amount of reading you'll have to do in this class, which is necessary if you really want to improve your writing.

Professor Moriarty cares about her students. She is always available to chat, review your work, or help you out in any way possible. She goes out of her way to get to know her students and pushes them to be their best and do their best work. Would recommend Moriarty to anyone who wants a professor who will really help them develop their writing.

Prof Moriarty's ENGL205 class was my favorite class that I've taken. Very engaging, I never even thought about skipping. There's a lot of reading and some creative writing involved, and each class is centered around class discussions. An easy and enjoyable class as long as you do the work and make sure to communicate with her when you need help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Moriarty is the best teacher I've ever had. She's very kind and really wants to help her student improve. I went into 551 not having much confidence, but she pushed me to keep going and helped me become a better writer. Highly recommended for any English major
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Moriarty was probably my favorite professor at KU. She is kind and compassionate while still offering valid and constructive critiques. She is amazingly humble for being so successful, and very down to earth. She gave me a lot of confidence as a writer and I could not recommend her enough.

She was very inspirational. She is one of those professors that can inspire to try something new, and make you like it. For example, I wrote my first creative work ever in her class and I found out I loved it! She's helpful, but don't expect her to cater to you. She'll always help as much as she can but you have to put in a lot of effort.

This is one of your professors who turns out to be a big deal as she is an active author. She has a different teaching style and comes up with prompts for papers that keep students thinking creatively. In general, you'll just want to comes to class because she makes English interesting through discussions about author's writing choices.

Really interested in what she was teaching and genuinely interested in students' opinions. Great discussion. Graded papers pretty fairly, gave good comments and advice. I enjoyed the reading material and going to class

Professor Moriarty is great, and not just because she shares the name of a Sherlock villain and wrote the book chosen as KU's '14 common book. She's very reasonable and gives a lot of points for participation. Book choices were diverse and interesting. 2 papers+1 creative nonfiction piece. Pretty easy class but she's very particular with the papers

Im certain all those reviews telling you to disregard the previous ones are from himself. He's lukewarm when it comes to actually teaching, basically just reads off slides. The quizzes have little to do with the slides themselves. You're better off just reading the textbook and watching the author's own videos on youtube. He never answers emails.

Good professor, interesting teaching style. I think he is alright, nothing good nothing bad I would say the reviews before the exams are helpful, class is made harder than it needs to be. The topic is very interesting, he can tweak some things and be greater.

Fav EECS prof. Always greeted me with a smile when I had questions after class. Super clear lecturing & always asks if we have questions (doesn't make you feel dumb at all). Sends out announcements/reminders for quizzes. He very clearly wants everyone to do well. 3 exams - 20%, 20%, 25%. iClicker attendance - but not graded for it.
Not sure about the red reviews, but he gives great lectures and homework with quizzes for understanding. If you study, you should do fine

I don't understand those bad review. This is a wonderful professor who is cared support students' success. He made communication networks become very interesting. If you go to class and do homework then you will be fine. Plus, the WireShark labs are very interesting and helpful for understanding the concept of this class

Be prepared to learn the material independently, as this professor shows little concern for their students. While the course material is interesting, the professor approach is disappointing. He doesn't even take the time to prepare a proper syllabus. It's unfortunate that this is a mandatory course and that he is the only professor teaching it.

I don't understand all these bad reviews! He's respectful to all his students and his lectures are clear. Go to class, only about 20% of students actually show up & I bet those are the people leaving reviews
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Previous ratings of this professor are outdated. The lectures are extremely engaging. The homeworks provide good background knowledge on the material learned in class. The tests and quizzes are more than fair. One of the top courses I have taken so far at KU.

This professor provides very interesting and engaging lectures, there are weekly homework and quizzes, however they are not too difficult. Some of the homework asks you to learn new content on your own that he has not and will not cover in class.  Overall and easy going professor.
Attendance is expected, but be ready to learn everything by yourself. Homeworks are regular. Aweful teacher but content is interesting.

I am glad to see others had a similar experience with Dr. Hashemi. He was quite unpleasant and made me less interested in the material, although I enjoyed the content. Take this course if there is another professor, but if it is only Hashemi, I would recommend waiting or learning the material on your own.

The most difficult and uncaring professor I have had at KU. He has NO interest in the wellbeing of students and whether or not they are learning, rather he is simply condescending and tries to impose his knowledge on you at any moment he can. Extremely, extremely tough grader. I would not take a course by him, ever again.
I don't think he really cares about the students. The test and homework questions are ambiguous. It was hard to know what he actually wants.

Professor Hashemi will not force you to come to class, but will call you out if he even thinks you aren't paying attention. He maintains a distinct lack of ability to lecture, and teaches this class to only let him research at KU. He cannot write test questions, homework questions, or effectively receive student feedback. The worst professor I had.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. The average and median on the first exam was a very low D, though a curve was not considered for that exam and the professor even went so far as to say the exam was actually "easy." Lectures and homework questions are often unclear and ambiguous.
Always goes out of his way to help students. Super kind and knowledgeable!

I really appreciate we do the Hands on (Homeworks) in class, he is patient and very thorough with his explanations and lectures, and he even posts videos after class so that you can still complete it and earn points if you couldn't make it. Respect for Mohammad! Also responds to mails.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very engaging professor. One of his biggest strengths is his passion for the course content. SQL and Excel assignments were very useful. Always responsive to email.

Best class I have ever had. I have learned a lot of things. If you attend class every day you will learn a lot. He is very passionate. Hands-on are top-notch. The class has quizzes which help me to do well in the exam.

He is one of the most supportive professors. He always tries to help students. Clear grading criteria. His class is organized. He always gives clear instructions. He has clear guidelines for hands-on and also gives videos for the hand-on, which is really helpful. I really recommend this professor for learning. He is the best fit for this course.
Bad grading, complex assignments, lecture-heavy, and bad instruction.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The GOAT!!!!! Dresses for success and is the best.
Great professor. Has great passion for what he does also a very nice guy in general.

Mohammad was a very inspiring teacher and cared a lot about his content. I was in his honors class so it was easier to ask questions and learn at a good pace. The assignments you basically do in class with him and then just submit it at the end of class. His slides do have a lot of information though which can be a lot sometimes. Good teacher.

His lecture is amazing. He is very passionate about his class. It really helps me understand the topic clearly. I learn a lot of new things from his in-class assignments as well. I would highly recommend taking his class and attending every class. It's very helpful, and he is also very cooperative. His lecture and course is very organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Something graded every class. In class assignments and in class quizzes. Neither were particularly difficult. Lectures were boring, but needed to be in class to get the quiz code. For in-class assignments, you just had to follow along with his walkthrough or the posted video.
the nicest professor ever at KU,i highly recommend taking his class,Lectures can be boring but he makes them fun ,Overall amazing professor

He is such a nice guy. My computer got knocked over during an exam and he let me finish the rest of it on his computer. Exams are very straight forward and easy if you take thorough notes. I would highly recommend his class.

I learned a lot from this class. I must say his hands-on approach is straightforward and top-notch. It really helps me learn Excel easily. If you face any problem, he always helps. His class is very organized. I would really recommend him to anyone who wants to learn. His mock exams are also helpful for doing well in the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My experience wasn't great but I can tell he cares a lot about what he's teaching. I showed up for every lecture and took plenty of notes but don't feel like I ever learned anything because of how quick the turnover was for subjects. There was only two big tests (midterm and final) but both were open note and open book which was my saving grace.

Great professor you can tell he really cares and is knowledgeable about the subject. Very good at communicating and answering questions. I voted him for most outstanding professor at the KU Business school. Highly recommend

He is one of the skilled professors in the  department. His in-class assignments are beneficial, and I learned a lot. He gives videos for the assignments, which are useful. The course includes two exams that closely resemble the quizzes. The date for the quizzes and in-class assignments is outlined in the syllabus, ensuring you won't miss anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor is very helpful. He was accessible outside the class. Very understanding and I learned a lot of things.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very nice guy. The class is a little slow, but he is very helpful and accommodating. Would recommend.

I just don't believe we were a good match for each other. There is very little variety in the practice done before exams…usually we would do one problem in class and maybe two on the homework. I believe my semester with him was his first, which makes sense, as our study material and exam help improved through the semester. He is so sweet, though.

You can tell that he really cares about what he does and wants to help students learn. He does a good job of relating class information to the real world. There isn't too much homework and the in-class quizzes are not bad if you pay attention. Overall, I have learned a lot in this course and the professor makes the lectures very enjoyable.

He is very passionate about teaching. His marks distribution is very clear. His classes are well-structured, and he assists with homework in class, which helped me finish them successfully. I learned  a lot about SQL.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He provided really clear and helpful material for the test. He is a really effective teacher. His lecture was enjoyable. Highly advised for this course.
Before this course, I had never used Excel. I was taught how to do calculations in Excel by the professor.  The best person ever for this course is him. He was quite helpful with his mock exam.

He is incredibly helpful and friendly to the students.  He was always quick to respond when I had any questions. He responds to emails promptly. For the test, his study guide is really beneficial.
I heartily recommend this instructor who genuinely wants to learn and perform well on tests

The course isn't difficult if you read the material, as homework and exams are straightforward. However, the professor's teaching lacks impact, and the content feels forgettable. Classes don't align with homework, and numerous assignments and projects add confusion. Without structural changes, students must rely on themselves to succeed.

This professor is highly suitable for this course. Anyone who attends class regularly and practices at home will find it to be one of the easiest classes. He is always available to help students, and his lectures are very informative. He genuinely wants his students to learn, which is truly commendable. I have learned a lot from this course.

He is one of those professors who always strives to assist students in every situation. When I had difficulty logging in to complete my assignments, he patiently guided me through each step. He is always willing to answer students' questions and demonstrates a high level of skill in the course.

Very knowledgeable about this course and helpful with SQL assignments. He is also very cooperative during office hours and is one of the caring professors with clear guidelines. There are also some in-class assignments that are helpful.

I took the professor for BSAN310. He is very skilled at understanding students' needs and is helpful in explaining the material. His instructions are clear, and  even assists with homework assignments. Additionally, he is very responsive via email. Overall, he is an excellent instructor for this course and teaches it very effectively.

He is one of the best professors. He is accessible outside of class and always cares about his students. I wasn't very good at Excel, but now I understand how to perform calculations using it. A calculator can also be used in exams. His lectures are easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You cannot understand him in class. BUT the course is easy to succeed in. Attendance is mandatory due to the quizzes, but they are not difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The best TA for Math 125 by far. If you have the opportunity to take him, please do! He's very knowledgeable and can explain things well, which made the class a lot easier.

He is the best! He had a unique style of teaching which required us to go to the board and present our work to the class, which helped a lot with my learning and was something that I had never experienced before. I will genuinely miss him and miss being in his class.

He was the GTA but I wish he had taught the course. The few times he covered lectures for the professor were some of the best classes I had this semester. Always encouraged us to do group work and answered questions with respect and clarity. Could be a little tough on grading but otherwise a great TA.

He was super helpful and created an environment where I was encouraged to ask all my questions. Excellent with breaking things down and going at students pace. I thoroughly enjoyed learning math in his class.
Great with explaining concepts with interesting examples

First professor Ive ever felt motivated to review because he was the goat. Class is easy enough if you care about that, short readings and 3 short papers with easy grading. But his feedback and lectures are the best I've ever got, better than some 500-level courses. 🐐🐐

Had three essays to write, one which was a group project. He is easily accessible over email and during office hours, and has great ideas to get the writing process started. Very kind and loves to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved him, very philosophical discussions about the readings and about life

The guidelines on all the writing were easy, clear, and graded fairly. He was always willing to help advise writing. There were readings for every class, but to be expected. You can tell the professor really cares about the pieces. Discussions were a bit awkward, but that's because the class didn't really engage much.

Taking ENGL with Kevin was one of the best experiences of my life in terms of english classes. He makes the class feel nothing like a English class and everything is very collaborative. He is a joy to be around and is very easy to talk to about random things. He appreciates particpation but he doesnt cold call or anything ever. 10/10 reccomend!

I have 12 years of music background, and this is the hardest class I've ever taken; the course material is not introductory at all, more like expert. It is advertised as a class you can do at your own pace, but really, you have to wait for every assignment to get graded before moving on, and that can take days. Don't take this class.

I have 12 years of music background, and this class is one of the hardest classes I've taken at KU so far. The material is Expert level. It's advertised as an introduction to music and a class you can do at your own pace, but you have to wait for each assignment to be graded in order to move on to the next.

he overestimates how good the students skills are. I have terrible ear training and this class kicked my bum so hard I failed every single dictation, but at least they were curved. he talks in the most insane  musical terminology, so instructions often make 0 sense. but he is kinda funny and i like him as a person

comments on assignments are prettttttty much irrelevant since there is NOOOO opportunity to correct. class averages on assignments is HORRIBLE. don't be surprised if you get a 45% on an assignment. This is not worth it to me. run run run!

Lectures in class do not match the level of difficulty of the assignments. It is difficult to take notes for the class because most of the lectures are conceptual. Three weeks of lectures could be condensed into one day of class. Many people have cried because of this class. Don't recommend unless it's absolutely required. His singing is bad.

Probably the worst course I've ever taken. Supposed to be for students of all musical skill levels, but he requires intermediate skills to be read day one. For a class that claims to teach "how to make music", this class involves hardly any creativity at all, instead just being exercises in "correct form" for music creation. Absolute waste of time
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! This class is extremely difficult, and it appears that he has quite literally made up the course material. He has his own website, and someone with a MUSIC DEGREE from KU has not been able to figure out anything he has been talking about. None of it makes sense. Not for beginners. EXTREMELY difficult and time consuming.

This is the worst class I have ever taken in my life. He claims that his class is for "beginners" but proves to be intermediate. He assigns three online assignments each week, and each of them takes about an hour and a half to complete. If you ask him for help, don't expect to improve as he expects his students to understand advanced material.

Probably the most brilliant person you will ever meet. If you're looking for an easy A, take someone else, but if you want to learn music theory, take his class. Read the material before class and you will get more out of it. Murphy is a genius and an incredible teacher/person. He is very caring about his students and always willing to help you out

Scott is not a good teacher. This is an introductory course but he makes the material much more convoluted than it needs to be. He isnt very responsive to emails and his feedback on assignments is bare and not very helpful. If youre looking for a music class to enjoy avoid this teacher.

Dr. Murphy is the greatest professor on this planet. He comes up with new, brilliant ways of thinking about and analyzing music, and he WILL teach you music theory. Go to every class and do your work; it is difficult and you will need to fight for an A but in the end, you will possess great critical thinking skills in addition to musical knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr Murphy is a genius. His lectures are fascinating and he's really passionate about what he does. This class moved really quickly. We had homework due most classes and if you got behind you were going to be lost for the rest of the semester. The material was complex but he encouraged us to ask for help and clarification. Very responsive to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The fact that everyone is saying his class is a difficulty 4 or 5 and still rating him a 4 or 5 is all you need as proof. Proof to know Dr. Murphy is one of the greatest professors you could ever have. You will learn more than you thought possible, some how not completely hate your life, and at the end be thankful for how far he pushed you.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Murphy is the most brilliant person I have ever met in my entire life. Not only this but he is super understanding, caring and not at all condescending in any way at all. He genuinely loves music theory and it really shows in his teaching. Learning from him has been such a pleasure and if you have the chance to take his class, DO IT!
One of the smartest professors that I have ever met. He is literally a genius and even though I don't love theory, his love was contagious. If you ever have the chance to take a class of his, do it.

Let me say this first. Music is not easy. Dr. Murphy is extremely fair in his grading and is crystal clear about what he expects out of you. He is the best instructor I've ever had at this university and every music major in Lawrence should take from him at some point. Music is hard, but he will make it easy for you after studying with him.

By far the hardest class I have ever taken. He will push you to do things you didn't think were possible, but he has a million and a half resources to help you succeed and was always willing to meet with me to go over anything I needed help on. Literally the best teacher I have ever had.
Prof. Murphy is incredibly smart and a good but tough teacher. He gives lots of handouts which help make things easier. He is a very picky grader and expects you to be prepared at every class period.

Fantastic professor. He is very funny, heavily invested in his students, and loves what he does. Every single person that comes out of his class loves him. It isn't an easy course, and he expects you to work at it, but it has been one of the best experience s of my college career, and I will miss having him as a professor.

He's an awesome teacher, but he'll definitely kick your butt. So be ready. But you'll do much better in Theory IV if you take from him. Sit in the front row. It'll make you pay attention, because he will walk up right in front of you. Smartest professor I have ever had. He's a great guy, and an amazing teacher
Excellent class, excellent teacher.
One of the smartest profs I have had but his theory classes are not easy.
Easily the smartest man I've ever met

I've taken both Theory III and Form & Analysis with Prof Murphy. They are the two hardest classes I've taken at KU, and by far the most rewarding. He is an absolute genius and he expects his students to do their absolute best.

If you're looking at this to decide whether to take Scott Murphy's class (ANY class, not just Form & Analysis), TAKE IT TAKE IT TAKE IT. It'll be tough but so worth it. He has brilliant mind, he is an excellent teacher, he is incredibly passionate about what he does, and he loves seeing his students understand the material more than anything else.

No doubt in my mind, Scott Murphy is the best teacher I've ever had.  Theory III beat me down, and I had something to work on for theory most every night of the semester, but I can't wait until I finish Theory IV so I can take another course with Dr. Murphy.

Theory III: Murphy's theory classes are the hardest classes you'll ever take as a music major, but they are the most rewarding. I've never been proud of a 'B' before, but I worked my tail off for it and it was well worth it. If you want to learn, take his class. He's passionate about music which makes the difficulty level seem much less stressful.

He and Paul Stevens are film music knowledge rock stars. I honestly learned more in this class than probably any class I've taken at KU. Granted, it was all about the history of film music, but still! Also, I can now tell the difference between an oboe and an English horn!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

If you want an honest review, here it is. Professor Mure's Ochem course is tough, like anywhere. She's not the strongest lecturer, but shines in office hours. She's kind and wants students to succeed, but you have to show you're motivated. Show up to office hours, and you'll excel.

Prof. Mure was an incredible teacher for me. Some people might say that her class was too hard or that she did not teach it well, however I would say she is one of the best professors I'v had during my time at KU. She is very caring and wants her students to succeed. To be successful in her class, you just need to show up, pay attention, and care.

Very rude and does not respond to emails in a timely manner, email responses are very unprofessional. Read off of slides without actually teaching the material. Doesn't further explain nor provide good explanation, you essentially teach yourself. Is not understanding AT ALL. Her tests are not structured well and are super confusing.

She barely even teaches, all her lectures are just her reading off a power point slide. When doing the Clicker questions, she doesn't care to explain the correct answer and just continues. You have to teach everything to yourself outside of class and the tests are significantly harder than the practice problems that she claims are "identical".

The material in ochem is generally difficult and you HAVE to practice the content outside of class or you should not expect to pass. That being said she makes the exams very straight forward and tells you exactly what you should be practicing. A large majority of the exams are from the practice problems so if you put in the work you will succeed.

She gets bad reviews, but she genuinely care and wants to help. Ochem is a difficult course, she may not be the best lecturer and her tests are difficult, but attend class cause she gives hints and help to those who consistently show up, do the practice problems, and go to her office hours and you'll be fine.
She is so sweet and funny! Put in the work and do the problems that are given to you and you will get a good grade.

OCHEM is in general a tougher class and you have to put in the work to see results. Her tests are exactly the SkillBuilder questions and she gives so many hints to what is on the tests. I don't see how you can get a bad grade as she gives you all the resources you need. Don't blame a professor if you're not willing to put in the time and effort.

Honestly, she's fine. I'm convinced that others have not taken OCHEM with other professors, because they'd realize how easy she makes the course. She literally offers you an entire paper for a cheat sheet and takes 80%+ of her questions from the Textbook and her assigned problems. It's near impossible to fail if you actually try outside of class.

Expect to teach yourself!! She reads off the pp slides and doesn't thoroughly explain the material for a difficult class. Told us partial credit is awarded on tests and gave none. asked for partial credit answer was no. Grade is based off exams, final is worth 20%! It's possible to do well, but I'm emphasizing teaching yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mure is very passive aggressive and is horrible at lecturing. Had to find an outside tutor to learn material. Long story short, don't take o chem with her!!!

I took Ochem1 with her in the spring, and now I'm paying for it in Ochem 2. She skipped 2 of the biggest most essential chapters in Ochem, so anyone who took her for Ochem 1 is suffering now trying to play catch-up. Also, her structure is very confusing and frustrating; it's inconsistent and has changed multiple times throughout the semester.

Do not take her, she is not accomodating to her students at all and is not helpful either. Does not respond to ANY email
Lectures are all over the place and doesnt explain the material clearly.

I took this class in Spring 2024, and it was a mess. The professor was very disorganized and not consistent at all. She changed the syllabus many times during the semester and was hard to communicate with. She wasn't consistently at her office hours, making it hard to succeed in the class.

I took Mure SP24 (reference other reviews from that semester). Do not recommend her. grading was super unclear, she changed the syllabus 4 times, each exam was formatted differently, and she didn't tell us how our grades would be calculated until after the final--she also refused to answer questions about grades and told us not to ask her about it
