The professor was very inconsistent and it was hard to understand her expectations. She was discouraging and never took accountability.

Extremely disorganized, passive aggressive, read slides given by the textbook, NEVER demonstrated solving a problem in class, bad at teaching. She'd be a cool friend as she is very caring + funny, but she's a bad teacher. For example she never once drew a chair conformation in class, just read the slides. I went to a tutor to learn it.

Waited until after the final exam was taken to change how course grading would work, refused to answer emails and made it vocal especially if it was an email concerning your grade, & was very discouraging to students. Study guides and tools were often messed up or had incorrect answers which she wouldn't take accountability for. Passive aggressive.

Halfway through the semester, changed the entire syllabus. Made attendance mandatory; heavily weighing iClickers, and if you were to miss a day it would drastically drop your grade. Extra credit & the make up quiz couldn't account for nearly as many lost points. Very disorganized in teaching, unproffessional, and impossible to contact or reach.
hard to follow along with during lecture. disorganized, and very discouraging to her students.

Sweet person, but poor professor. Her lectures were rereading the PowerPoint notes that were posted online. She didn't teach, she just read off the slides which I took notes on later. The exams were a mess (read other comments from spring24). The final was changed to in-person, but we were given 2 full pages, front & back, which was really helpful.
Very unorganized and changed her syllabus throughout the semester

Made multiple major changes to the syllabus, was super disorganized, and did not tell us how her class would be graded until after we'd already taken the final. The lectures weren't really helpful and she skipped 4 chapters' worth of content (that we've been told will be in ochem 2) because of how disorganized and chaotic her class format was.

She made some big changes to the syllabus in the middle of the semester, which led to a lot of disorganization. She barely provided any review sheets and the stuff she did provide, sometimes gave the wrong answer/no answer, and always have no explanation. She was also VERY hard to get a hold of and was very passive aggressive in emails.
Doesn't communicate well and is very harsh.

Originally this class had online exams. An incident happened with cheating so she changed the syllabus and made the rest of the exams in-person. I emailed her in august and still haven't received feedback. Theres no reason to email her because she never answers any of them. This class was so unorganized. also iclickers weight HEAVY on your grade.

This class no longer offers online exams- all in person and not open note. Attendance is now mandatory as iClicker is heavily weighted. This all changed in the middle of my semester. Incredibly disorganized; she can't solve the problems herself, answer keys always wrong, and impossible to reach. Overall not a great a professor. Don't recommend.

She reads from the slides super quickly and then asks if we have any questions after lecturing us for 50 minutes about a lot of difficult information. She claims she provides useful review slides for us to use yet it doesn't include actual examples. She does not show how anything is solved or answered and expects us to do it from the textbook.

Read the text book and get a tutor. Professor Mure is very sweet and caring, however she is not a great teacher, she's very smart and doesn't know what it is like to struggle with the course matter. During lecture she only reads off of slides, there are no practice problems in class and she doesn't go into much depth on the topic.

OCHEM I in itself is hard, but Dr. Mure does really care about her students and wants them to do well. She has plenty of practice material, but in turn does move really fast in lecture. Come prepared to take notes and do a lot of practice outside of class.

I originally made a positive review on Dr. Mure, but as the year has gone on, I must take it back. She is an absolute sweetheart, but is extremely passive aggressive, disorganized and is extremely difficult to access outside of class. If you are a working student or have other extenuating circumstances, avoid.

She is incredibly sweet, and says the funniest things during lecture. Attendance is not mandatory (as in it does not impact your grade), but she gives out EC for attendance. I will say, her lectures are primarily regurgitations of the textbook content, so reading the textbook will get you through the class. Also, exams are open note.

She is super understanding and easygoing. She gives plenty of opportunities to get an A, especially with her test corrections. I highly recommend her, she had great stories to tell! But, it was much more difficult to grasp the content during the 2nd half of the semester. In the end, she rounded by 85% up to an A!!!!

Organic chem is not easy, but Dr. Mure tries to help as much as possible. She makes lots of extra study guides and videos to explain things and encourages students to ask questions. She's very caring and supportive.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Mure keeps a structured format for her in-person classes and does take the time to meet with you outside of class if any concepts are unclear (pertaining to lecture or lab). The class is pretty test heavy with 90 points dedicated to homework. The exams online were harder than the in person ones, but if you work hard the results will show.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She the worst teacher ever. She doesn't know how to answer questions unless it directly deals with her research. If it doesn't, outside resources would be your best bet. She's rude and manipulative.

Minae is nice, but extremely disorganized.  Memorize the info she gives you re: what will be on the test and you'll get a good grade.  However, she doesn't really teach you how to figure out chemistry on your own.  She says she's willing to meet for office hours, but I never managed to get her to keep an appointment.  Overall, I do not recommend.

She tries to make sure everyone in the class gets a good grade.  She even tells you the test questions in advance, just be sure to attend.  The Lab TA's were awful though; they graded hard and did not care about their students.
She was good. Pretty easy exams and she literally walks through each and every type of question she's going to ask on the exams in the review sessions. If you can get her, you should.

she was alright her self. TA's varied thu which made my life hell. Run away from Lucas. he gave 50 and 60% on reports just because they didnt follow his guidelines. even though they followed the prof's guidelines. so that made our section the worst section.

Mini is a caring teacher with an unorganized teaching style. She really cares about how her students are doing and if you take the time to go to her lectures you will get a number-by-number detail of what to expect on her tests. Practice problems are given for every quiz, and tests are based on those. Overall, this class was easy!

professor is nice and she is helpful, however the class was extremely unorganized and answer keys had wrong answers all the time, it's confusing when you have to go back and keep regrading your tests, quizes, and practice problems. she blew me off when i tried to go to her office hours too.. try e-mailing her instead.

The best professor in the chem department, possibly one of the best at KU.  Minae Mure, or "Mini" as she told us to call her, really wants you to understand this material, and does everything she can to make sure you do.  She's a really fun professor, and makes class interesting.  I took her class after dropping Hansen's; I learned so much more.

minae mure is a great teacher; it IS nice to have a teacher that you feel is working with you instead of against you. if the class was having trouble with a subject, she would go over it more times and added extra materials like study guides to make things more clear. i also really liked the way she explained things without overcomplicating

Dr. Mure is a nice break from the norm at the KU Chem department. She is actually a teacher who wants all of her students to succeed, and will go out of her way to help them get the grade they deserve. Unlike other organic teachers she follows the text and does not throw out curveballs when it comes to exam time. Overall the best teacher I have had

Minae is the best chem teacher I've ever had. She actually cares about what grade you receive, unlike Paul Hanson, and wants everyone to succeed. The weekly homework assignments are easy points. She is willing to help outside office hours. Her class is much smaller than Hanson's. If you need to take organic, take it from her! Minae is wonderful!

Almost all of her tests were things she covered in lectures and she gives a lot of hints about tests during lectures, so I'd suggest going. And definitely talk to her sometime before each test because she basically tells you the whole test when you're in there! She's great!

We had three exams in class that made 90% of our grade. This professor did not give us the study guide for our final (with over 100 questions) until three days before the final. She's a lovely woman but very inconsiderate of our time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Muehlenhard is an incredibly kind woman. Her presence is calming, she is easy to talk to, and she genuinely cares. As a professor, she can be unprofessional. Her exams can be poorly put together, as she admittedly does not make the test until the week of. She did not give us our final study guide until three days before the final.

so so so severely unorganized. the syllabus and assignments are a jumbled train wreck. the tests are easy as long as you read and go over the lecture slides yourself, as she isn't easy to follow in class.
Literally showed up to our final with out the test, left the building to get more, took over 20 minutes away from our test time. She is very difficult to follow in lecture

This class does not have much to do with psychology or women despite it being psychology of women. Speaking in class is mandatory 15 times a semester. She has a very hard time facilitating discussion because she often comically misinterprets people's words. She is also regularly late including being 20 minutes late for an exam.

She doesn't respond quickly to emails, can be kind of boring at times, and overall I was expecting to take away more from her class. I think she could do a better job at being engaging and could be more professional by responding in a timely manner. Although, this class was okay. If you have to take it it's bearable.

Probably one of the worst professors that I've had at KU. Her lectures are based off of PowerPoints that she goes through so quickly that you won't even get an opportunity to write down the material, so be ready to read the information rather than absorb it in class. Her lectures felt like she was trying to hit a word count.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Where can I start with this lady... 1. She was constantly late for class, very disorganized, and seemed like she barely knew her own content half the time. 2. She read directly from powerpoints every single day and is quite frankly, a poor lecturer. 3. Grade based on 3 assignments, 3 tests, and a few extra credit points. 4. Class was pointless
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very disorganized and not a great lecturer. She reads word for word on her PowerPoints, so going to class seems pointless, BUT you need participation. Sometimes all of class is students talking which doesn't help on exams Q's. Often late. Study guides are not helpful and lectures barely help with exam questions. I just wish class was more useful.
Was horrible at teaching. Super disorganized and her study guides and syllabus were hard to understand. Had an open-note test, looked up all the answers and still got a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Women and Violence with her, and overall I enjoyed the class. 80% of your grade comes from 4 tests, so you have to make sure to really study for them. There are 3 short papers which are pretty easy. Participation is important, you have to write what you said on a slip of paper, and it affects your grade. She was often a bit late to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Oral participation is worth 10% of your overall grade which means people just spit out uninformed opinions because they're scared of missing out on points. She's super disorganized and gives zero direction for writing assignments. Get ready to teach yourself. DO NOT TAKE AS GRAD STUDENT.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Grade is based upon 4 exams and you must speak up during every lecture or you won't get points. Exams are very hard and the study guides don't help a ton either.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: WONDERFUL teacher and person! She listens to each student and tries her best to help in any way she can (whether it's class related or not- she actually ended up helping me with a personal issue and was caring and professional). I recommend her class to people who want to challenge their own beliefs and grow as a person. Love her!

A great teacher in small settings… more than 10 students though, and she begins to lose track of her thoughts and repeat herself a lot. Plenty of discussion. Tests are multiple choice (straight from lecture and readings), with excellent study notes posted. Attendance was based on participation… had to participate in at least 15 classes.

Charlene was a great teacher. Her classes are discussion based and there is a lot of articles she wants you to read. DON'T GET BEHIND. Her tests are based solely on facts from the readings, so don't let yourself wait until the last minute. She is very helpful and is willing to change things around or clarify anything to help her students. Love her.

Charlene strives to have an environment that fosters discussion.  If you are in class and read the assigned pages from the texts you will do well on the tests.  She even puts all notes up on blackboard.  She is an overall nice person and wants to see all her students do well.  She gives many opportunities for extra credit.

Her tests are hard, first of all. She provides study guides, but they're very loosely related to what's on the exam. And she does hand them out ONE BY ONE in huge lectures. She drones on, and things that seem like tangents turn out to be material she's testing you on. Overall not bad, but she's not a great professor.

As the semester went on, she annoyed me more and more. She doesn't know how to teach, she stutters her way through every lecture. She doesn't use powerpoint slides, she just sits at the front of the class and talks. She hands out tests ONE BY ONE in a 250 person class. She's so set on her ways and can be so rude. Don't like her AT ALL.

A little eccentric but extremely helpful with a good sense of humor. Passionate about her work and students, and her lectures are really interesting. Lots of extra opportunities make it easy to get a good grade. One of the best people in the Psych department.

She is overly helpful with things sometimes, which leads to long, sometimes monotonous discussions. I never read the material until the test study guide. TESTS ARE HARD in this class, because her multiple choice includes up to option i and are VERY specific to the readings. Overall I am ok with her

Professor is easy. Lectures and readings are boring and she talks really quietly. However, tests are made up of lecture notes that she writes on the board and key concepts over the reading. If you think she is hard, you are dumb. I am not a brain surgeon.

I thought this class was fairly easy.  Make sure to do all of the readings (pay close attention to any studies mentioned and their results).  She kind of blabs on and on about the same thing during class, so lecture material should stick with you.  Just show up, pay attention and read the books, then you will get an A! Overall, decent class.

not the easiest unless you've taken similar classes but Charlene is absolutely a great professor &extremely helpful. she's very tricky w/ test but there is no reason u should have less than a B or C+ in the classgo to her office hours!! she had her gta send me copies of notes after every class TAKE HER!!! I give the subject/ a C her a A!

This was independent study and I took it two semesters in a row.  Charlene really encourages students to get involved with the research project and take ownership.  She is very helpful and just wonderful!

This is the second course I took from Charlene.  It involved lots of reading but was informative and interesting.  Charlene has a way of assisting in broadening your mind without bogging you down with her own beliefs.
Charlene is tough but she is very fair, knowledgeable and does the best job of all professors I had in college, at giving unbiased information.  This was the first class I took from her.
Love this woman!! She's like Bette off the L word...knows her stuff...make sure to do the readings...and pay attention if she shows you a video...and don't forget to enjoy the view!!
Classes covered nothing on exams. Exams come from readings. Not too bad of a class.
charlene was a fantastic teacher and was had very interesting information to share.  the exams were fair and not too hard

She seemed to love teaching the women's studies class and did not just stand up there and talk all the time it was a true discussion.  The readings assigned in the class were real long and sometimes boring with lots of stats but over all the class was awesome and so was the prof.
challenging class but very informative
Charlene is brilliant!!!!

Charlene is a WONDERFUL woman and is truly interested in what she does, however, she fails to be a truly effective teacher.  I took 3 of her classes and was disappointed each time with her teaching techniques.

Charlene's classes are very interesting, challenging, and life changing. You WILL work for your grade, but she'll make it enjoyable along the way. She also offers a lot of extra credit. Just be prepared for some reading.
Her class change my life totally. Very informative and fair. She is nice even sometimes she is kind of forgetful, but it is ok!! Her class has a lot of extra credits, great job Charlene!
GREAT teacher who has an OPEN MIND and an OPEN HEART!
I learned so much in my first course from Muehlenhard I took a second course from her.  She's an excellent teacher and will take the time to help you one-on-one if you need it.
She was very fair, very friendly, and very informative.  One of the best professors I've had at KU.
No Comments
Prof. Muehlenhard is completely qualified-- she REALLY knows her stuff. Good class with good texts.  I learned a lot from her. She's very pleasant, too.

Attendance was not taken for a grade and not many actually attended the course. Lectures were all over the place and were not always helpful with what was going to be on the exam. Exams were online and the assignments were simple and easy.

Anyone thinking about or planning on going into any kind of healthcare should take this class. As a neurodivergent student, I found the design of the class makes the material easier to comprehend than others. The layout is consistent and flexible. The workload was just hard enough to exercise my research skills. Be prepared for lots of projects! :)

This class was challenging. You had to listen to lectures and take notes on every small thing and the same with the textbook. The assignments were easy, and the lectures weren't boring because she was funny, but the exams were decently hard. You have to study a lot, but the one drop exam grade makes it much easier.
Very smart professor, great at lecturing and positive attitude. Her class is not difficult but I still learned a lot, so I would recommend attendance.

Not the best professor, but she is very kind. She would often times explain things, state she didn't explain it well, then continue on. Her discussions were often times very hard to follow when it came to the thought process. As someone who is a bit scatterbrained, this class was hard to follow due to its added layer of confusion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the hardest class ive ever taken. She is hard to get a hold of, just reads off the lecture slides, and doesnt really elaborate on the information. she gives us no idea what is going to be on the tests, tests are often, and they are incredibly difficult. you have to memorize all information otherwise you dont stand a chance.

It seems that COVID made this class a bit more manageable. We did not have any exams, only weekly quizzes. We did have a final that was technically mandatory, but it could only help our grade by replacing our quizzes. There were no late penalties and several opportunities for extra credit. In-person lecture was once a week; everything else online.

She was a great person, funny and helpful if you had questions. But the class is very hard. Tests are based on book and lecture, with no clear study guide, and even after studying for hours before a test I still felt unprepared when taking it. Make sure you go through the textbook as some questions will come from it.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's a nice professor, offers help, and has interesting lectures. She isn't great at using blackboard but she does offer extra credit if you go to class and participate. Tests are a mix of book and lecture, final is optional. She was very nice and passionate about what she taught! Her TA, Ilana for fall '19 was great too!

I love Dr. Hamilton. She's nice, funny, and is good about being accessible after classes. HOWEVER, she teaches behavioral neuroscience the same way she teaches another class that I take that is taught by her as well. She reads off the slides, tests seem very different and almost more specific/detailed then what she teaches in class.

Dr. Hamilton is a funny, engaging professor. Plenty of time to ask qs in class. Biggest complaint: no study guides. To study, you have to spend hours going through your own notes and essentially memorizing everything. There is extra credit, and you can drop one of the 5 tests (potentially the final). Hard class, but interesting content.

Very interesting class, but it is biology heavy, so it helps to have a decent grasp before taking the class. She is a good lecturer and interesting, but her powerpoint slides can be unorganized at times. Chances for extra credit throughout the class and the final is option because you get to drop the lowest test.

I took Nancy's psyc370 class. Neuroscience is not my favorite but the material we covered really interesting and I liked the class more than I thought I would. Blackboard was a mess, assignments were not always under the right category, calculate your own grade. Test were rough, no study guide so I never knew what exactly to cover to be prepared.

Such a nice woman! She is very helpful and willing to set up a meeting to discuss class work and elaborate on topics that arent clear. Lectures are very interesting and engaging. All around a very interesting teacher.

Terrible teacher. Says "I don't know" when asked questions. Reads directly off the power point slides that are very unorganized. Doesn't understand how to use Blackboard. Class topic is very interesting but she makes it very hard to learn anything from this class unless you sit down and look at every power point on your own. Would not recommend.

A few opportunities for extra credit, but if you don't understand the material because it is so dang abstract, you're SOL in this class. Tests are ridiculously hard and she doesn't give any indication of what you need to study for them, very vague. Her lecture slides do not make sense out of context of lecture, even after sitting through every one

A few opportunities for extra credit, but if you don't understand the material because it is so dang abstract, you're SOL in this class. Tests are ridiculously hard and she doesn't give any indication of what you need to study for them, very vague. Her lecture slides do not make sense out of context of lecture, even after sitting through every one.

Powerpoints are EXTREMELY unorganized. She makes no sense and the material is scattered. The powerpoints are online so you can skip class. Majority of test is 'which of the following are NOT' questions, which makes it even worse. Do NOT take this class. Some extra credit but not enough. Also gives you two days to write two essays before each exam.

She is a great professor who makes sure you understand the material. She encourages class participation and even gives extra credit for it. You will have a paper to write but it's not too terribly difficult. Easy points with quizzes but exams are kind of tough. 50 multiple choice, short answer, and 2 essay questions. But get to drop lowest exam.

She is an amazing teacher who encourages class participation in order to keep the class interesting. She also gives extra credit for participation. She has quizzes but you can do them over and over until you get a 100%. Easy points and tests are multiple choice. You get to drop your lowest test score as well.

She makes it sound like this class is extremely hard; it isn't if you know how to study. I went to class for the first four weeks, and I didn't find the lectures to be particularly helpful, so I only showed up on test days after that. Earned a solid A.

Loved her as a person, but her thoughts were often disorganized. Does not give a study guide, often had the wrong slides - as most of her tests were based off of lecture concepts and a deeper explanation of material on slides, tests were impossible. Very interesting class, but very difficult to do well, even if you really study and come to class.

Very unorganized. Had another professor lecture during the "hardest part of the course" (quotes by her). By the end of the year was highly annoyed with the class...and her voice. However, if you are needed to take BIOL 408, 646 or other physiology courses or courses in neurobiology there is much overlap from this class.

I enjoyed this class A LOT...very informative and had a lot of material that I will carry with me after graduation. Easy to understand and engaging teacher...she is also really funny & down to earth. However, you do need to be ready to put in work! Reading the chapters is important and understanding main concepts! Take her class!

Dr. Hamilton is a nice lady and really wants her students to do well. Reading the assigned text before class helped me to understand what she was talking about. When you ask questions, she often doesn't know the answer if it does not directly pertain to what the lesson is over unless it is about her favorite topic: sleep. This class is challenging.

I didn't like the written assignment that involved peer to peer grading it seemed like every assignment had an issue with the system. Her lectures aren't bad and her tests seemed fair, plus shes pretty hot as a teacher.
this class isnt easy, you will have to put work in order to achieve a good grade, I never used the textbook I just read the blackboard notes and I achieved an A- in the class.
Good teacher, definitely hard, but she tries a lot to help with extra credit, explanations multiple times, and reviews
I felt that lectures were a bit dull... Tests were difficult.  Don't get behind it will kick your butt in the end...

Her lectures were great; however the tests could prove difficult. The last section was exceptionally difficult at it dealt more with the medical aspect of things. Very nice and thorough professor, but be prepared to put in some honest effort

This class is interesting but she makes the exams difficult and has weekly quizzes to test on the reading.  It is a good class to take if you are looking into a healthcare career... but expect to work hard.
I thought she was a wonderful instructor, but the exams were very difficult and tricky. I read the book, attended class, and took notes, but I still had a more difficult time in this class than most.
interesting class, but the tests can be tricky. she looks like michelle pfeifer.

Even though it is about health-related issues in which I have previously learned, it is still a hard class!  I studied so much for the exams and yet, I still didn't get a decent grade! It's a hard class..
I would highly recommend this class to anyone. It is difficult, but interesting. She is a difficult teacher, but youwill learn. She is also very open to helping students in any way possible.

Nate Miekle was the best professor i've ever had at KU. He is truly a legend and he cares so much about his students. The only thing to watch out for is the exams are surprisingly difficult but DO NOT let that stop you from taking this class, just study a bit. No homework like ever besides a journal entry and some podcast. Again, best teacher ever!

Professor Meikle is one of the best professors I have ever had. He teaches a lot of material that are useful in the real world and tries to teach very applicable life lessons. This was an online course for me, and he was very understanding of the fact that lots of his students work full-time jobs in addition to his class. Loved his class!

Nate is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. He's accessible to his students, he teaches clearly and concisely, and it's clear that he cares about both his students and the material he teaches to them. Would definitely take this class again, if only to have Nate again.

Professor Meikle is easily one of the best teachers I have had at KU and his classes are always interesting. He uses his own stories and engaging activities instead of just lecturing from the book. You can tell he cares about his students, always being accessible. Most of the grade comes from attendance so if you show up to class you can get an A.

my friends and i loved this class. literally as long as you go to lectures and take notes you will get an a. the papers are directly from what she talks about in lecture, and are further cemented in the discussions. discussions were fine, a little redundant, but great if you miss a lecture. would take again with snow!

She's great - Dr. Snow is funny and engaging, and takes what can be difficulty subject areas/coursework and makes it easy for any student to learn. She really makes you want to come to class and engage with the topic.

People say she's funny but she's just an old woman who talks about sex too often. Her class was boring and too difficult to be an intro w/ unclear expectations for exams that were 3 hand-written essays each. The class was only graded off of three exams and she is making the class harder bc of RMP reviews. Discussions are mandatory. Don't take!

Lectures were boring and the concepts were hard to follow. She would cold call the class a lot which sucked. I barely did the readings and was fine. I heavily relied on my TA Cole who was amazing and put in the work to help me succeed. There was also 6 assignments graded 3 being essays/tests. Definitely not the easiest class but was required for me
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite teacher in the philosophy department! She's absolutely wonderful and very charismatic. She makes lectures easy to follow yet entertaining. Her classes can be content heavy but as long as you go to class and engage you'll be fine. Attendance is for sure vital to your success in her class.

Dr. Snow was amazing. She makes philosophy interesting, personal, and fun! 3 exams worth 75% of your grade, 2 ethical analysis papers, and discussion grade participation is all. The TAs grade your exams - Cole is SUPER hard, Mohammad is easy, and the other one I am not sure about. Either way, go to class, pay attention, and you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Snow keeps lectures very engaging by just being herself, she will say whatever comes to mind and it is always a surprise every day. Lectures are recorded and she doesn't take attendance so you could skip, but it is nice to be in person. You are only graded on basically five papers throughout the semester, but review and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An amazing professor; she makes lectures personal which also allows for a better understanding of the material. Only 3 written essay exams + two essays written in class that make up the entire grade. GTA will be grading all of your work; mine had average exam scores of C-'s, so don't be afraid to ask Nancy about your grade. Advocate for yourself!

Such a sweet woman who carries her personality into lecture. She knows the content well and encourages questions. You're able to pass very easily without doing readings. Labs are helpful for tricker analyses.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 2 papers, 3 exams-only grades. Nancy is an incredible professor, she introduced a passion for philosophy to me. Very good at keeping attention, interesting, and clear about standards for good answers on exams. If I were to stay at KU I'd change my minor to philosophy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Snow's lectures were engaging at their worst and unforgettable at their best. Review could be a little lackluster and sometimes lecture banter could get a bit grating, but I definitely recommend Dr. Snow and her courses.

This class is super fun, she makes philosophy very entertaining. Along with this if you don't feel comfortable participating in the lecture there are weekly discussion sections where it is much easier to ask questions. She is responsive to emails. The only thing is there are very few assignments, so study before the exams!!

If you are taking PHIL 160, take it with Professor Snow! Her lectures are extremely entertaining, fun, and thought provoking. If you do the readings and participate, you should do well in the class. Highly recommend taking one of her classes.

If you have the chance to take a class with Dr. Snow, do it! Going to the lectures is super important to get a good grade, but she will make them entertaining and fun to attend. She even learned students' names in a decent-sized lecture which shows she cares about and engages with her students.

Nancy Milner is AMAZING! By far one of the nicest professors I have had at KU so far, and I have learned a lot in ASL 1. She teaches in a very clear way making it easy to learn as long as you also practice outside of class.

Nancy is great but not a good teacher for our University. She has some good material but there wasn't an appropriate layout for what we were learning and never posted anything to our blackboard page. I love learning ASL and was very excited, but after this, I have less faith in the higher ASL professors and their ability to teach appropriately.

Unorganized, me and other students in the class often times had no idea when things were do, what the requirements were for assignments, had trouble reaching out and getting a response outside of class. Teacher is very sweet and clearly cares a lot but the stress just isn't worth it.

Professor Peters was the best professor I had during my 1L year. She cares a lot about her students and their success. Exams are closed book. She does not cold call and uses the panel system. This panel may be difficult at times, it's hit or miss. However, the final my year was not really reflective of the material covered in class.

My favorite professor of my 1L year!! She makes her class fun and engaging and responds very well to class feedback. I reorganized my entire schedule next year to take more of her classes. She provides good feedback and opportunities to improve but you have to go out of your way to take advantage of them. She uses assigned panels for cold calls.

Weird office hour system, not usually drop-in. Not super eager to help later in the semester, probably because she's really busy, but that's why I didn't rate a 5. Actually one of my favorite profs because she's funny and has good vibes. Does do her job and give opportunities to access her and get help. Take advantage of that sooner, not later.

The best prof I had this semester. She cares about her students and is passionate about privacy law. The fact that she doesn't take BS from students and expects good work doesn't make her a bad professor -- you simply get what you give in her class.

nicest 1L professor- every time someone from my section complained abt something she did (that other professors did as well but no one mentioned them), it always had racist undertones: aggressive (speaks loud & clear), rude (helps you answer it yourself), etc etc. take bad reviews with a grain of salt bc there's def internalized anti-blackness

All you have to do is show up and show effort and you will do well in the class. He is very understanding and the assignments are all very easy. He will also make sure he makes time to meet if you ever have questions.

Nate is the reason I actually started to consider audit as a career path. I seriously enjoyed the coursework. The homework was very hands on, but didn't always clearly correspond with the exams. Studying with the slides prior to the exams is absolutely necessary, but the content is clear and easy to get through. Loved him and the class.
He puts things into context well. If you put in a grain of effort you will do fine in the class

Nate is far more into research than helping students learn. He reads off PowerPoint slides that he got from the book for lectures and then proceeds to test on topics he doesnt cover. The class is also case heavy but the lectures do not prepare you to do the simulated audit work which is required so you must self teach and receive no feedback.

This is the worst professor I have taken at KU, which is sad because I liked every other professor. He is a horrible lecturer and just reads off of the book provided slides. The exams are poorly written and he never provides enough lecture to feel like you can study well. The class feels thrown together and rushed. Worst KU major class I've had.

Alex was very engaging during lecture & made our Criminology class interesting by incorporating various texts/ films. He made concepts within the course easy to understand, and I enjoyed class discussions which provided different perspectives to learn from. Alex is incredibly kind, funny & willing to help-I'd highly recommend any of his classes!
This professor doesn't grade fairly. Most of the students got really bad grade.
Try to avoid this professor as much as you can.

Alex is one of the friendliest TAs I've ever had. He's really helpful and gets really excited about the books we read for class. Lecture isnt always totally clear but Alex helps a lot. Great instructor.

She is quite hard to understand, but if you follow along in class it's not that bad. Homeworks and projects are another story. I would not have passed without going to the TA office hours at least twice a week. Thankfully there were many TAs with a variety of hours to go to. Her teaching style assumes everyone is following along at all times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She followed the syllabus almost exactly, and gave the entire class a passing grade on an exam that she realized was too difficult for us. She's very fair. The homework was almost always exactly like the in-class examples, with a few exceptions. Exam material was fairly predictable, and she interrupts the exams to give explanations on problems.
She is great if you try and go to class.
Hard to understand, odd way of teaching, rambling lectures
She is incredibly difficult to understand. When you fall behind a little bit it is impossible to catch back up to be on pace with the class.

The ethnic ambiguity really bothers me. Also, she's kind of the worst teacher I've ever had piled on top of just being rude to students who ask questions or don't understand something due to her poor teaching

Absolutly no help what so ever.  If you ask for help she will get mad at you for not knowing the material.  Youtube  will become your best freind because  her lectures are just her writing code and not explaining why,  which is especially bad since this class is  for people who have never written code before.

The whole grading system for this class is an absolute joke. The exams are worth 200 points each but the homework  is at most 3 point,. Labs are only worth 7 points. easy until you get to coding. Her grading rubric is horrible for tests too and she will get mad at your for not knowing the material even though shes not clear.
She is just bad.
Lectures are pointless. She can't teach. All the lecture slides online will help you through each assignment to easily get an A.

She fails to explain the VBA language, but rather types seemingly random code during lecture. Also tells you laptops "distract her" and can't be used in class. Provides the entire code for every assignment at first, then stops providing it abruptly.  TA's help, but the class is difficult as the language is not explained in any way.

Garth is an amazing teacher.  Out of 4 years of college, he is definitely the best professor I have had.  His class is difficult, but if you keep up with the work you will do fine.  If you have a chance to take his class go for it.  Also, get to know him outside of class by going to his office. He will really appreciate it and will return the favor
Extremely helpful and encouraging.  If you have a problem, go to him and he'll help you figure out how to study, etc.
Garth is fantastic.  That's all there is to it.

Garth is fantastic.  His classes are tough, but he keeps you really engaged and interested, so it isn't "difficult".  He's organized, very up-to-date, and goes above and beyond, especially if students do the same.
Enjoyed the class.  The teacher seemed to really enjoy teaching.  Really nice guy and knew what he was talking about.
really cool guy. very interested and knowledgeable on his topics. tests are tough and he is a hard grader. class is about 100% lecture and he writes down little. i give him a B+
Easy easy easy. Such a nice and helpful man.
Knowledgable and spirited.  Hot to boot!
makes the class fun for all. does a good job explaining things and relates them to all.
Excellent teacher, boring topic.

Dr. N was absolutely amazing. I technically took her for SOC 480, not 500. She is such an engaging lecturer! Don't be scared off by her technology policy. It is surprisingly helpful to write by hand. Make sure to ask questions if you have them, but she is so thorough you won't need it! Get ready to write and be thorough for the tests!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Najafizadeh puts so much effort into making theory make sense. I went into this course extremely nervous about how I'd understand theory, but this class ended up being one of my absolute favorites. Professor Najafizadeh is one of the best professors I've ever had the privilege of learning from, I could not recommend her course enough.

She is AMAZING. The lectures are material heavy but if you pay attention the class is very easy. She will spend extra time with you if you ask. She truly cares about her students. I would recommend rewriting your notes before quizzes/exams. I didn't read text book and got 90% or above on every quiz or exam. I wish I could take this class again.

Dr. N is truly one of the most compassionate and understanding professors I have ever had. She is also extremely passionate about her field of study and because of this, her heavy lectures are very easy to understand. She taught me 1on1 how to effectively study and take notes and I started to perform much better in class. Love her and recommend!!!

Nicest and kindest professor out there. You could not ask for a better professor, trust me. When I was having trouble with the course, she came and spoke to me to ask what the problems were and helped me to get back on track. You have to take notes to do well on quizzes and exams, but she structures the notes so easily it's not a huge chore.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Actual most caring prof i have had.. if you pay attention and take your notes you will get a good grade. notes are clear and doesnt have you write down things you dont need to actually know.. sets you up perfectly for exams and explains content in interesting way!! Wish all my professors were as organized and diligent as her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class expectations were fair & earning an A was attainable w thorough preparation. I was disappointed she was not more considerate/clear when Pres Obama came. Sent out an email a few days before he came stating class attendance was required. So the maj. of students showed up for class only to learn other students were excused to see the President.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This is the best professor I have ever had. I work 40 hours a week to help pay for my schooling and didnt have time to study for a test we had. She noticed my score and set up a meeting with me to give me tips and help for the next test. I reviewed at 95 on the next one. She is incredibly kind and just wants her students to be/do the best.

Professor Najafizadeh is the kindest professor I've had at KU. She goes the extra mile to make sure all of her students succeed. Her lectures, quizzes, and exams are clear and straightforward. She makes material that could be difficult if taught by other instructors easy and fun to learn. I would recommend this class to everyone!

Passionate, open office hours, nice, great smile, caring, great teacher, knowledgeable, very smart, most professional teacher you will find at KU, which is why she was head of the department for Sociology.

One of the best teachers I have ever had in my entire life!! If you have to take this class, take it with her!! She called one of the students in my class just because his dog died and she wanted to offer her condolences! Amazing and kind woman!

This teacher is by far the best teacher I have had in college. She is so enthusiastic and passionate about theory. It isn't the easiest class, but theory isn't really easy for anyone. I'd take another class with her in a heartbeat. Loved her!
She writes everything on the board. No powerpoints, no visuals. Just white board. The class is not outrageously hard, however, you will start counting down the minutes until class is over.

I have taken two classes with Prof. Najafizedeh now, and I don't think I'll ever have a better teacher. She is remarkable at lecturing, always helpful with questions, encourages class participation, and on top of all that she is a sweet lady. Please, take either 130 or 500 with her!
I loved this professor so much!!! She is such a great teacher!  She writes all of her notes on the board so you can copy them down.  As long as you study for her tests you will do great!

This is a very easy class-attendence is essentially required but if you attend then you don't need to do any of the readings for the test. Since test make up the entire grade and she pretty much says what is on the test, this is a very easy A. That said, the class is occasionally interesting but often so watered down that it is often not.

If you like discussion, this is not the class for you. That being said, she is very honest about what she expects and the tests have no surprises. Be forewarned, if you miss class you have to ask another student for notes. Overall I liked her and I would recommend her, but her class is not very interesting.

She is very understanding of her students when it comes to conflicts. She makes sure that everyone understands the material and goes at a VERY good pace. If you go to class, you would do very well. Class and lecture are pretty interesting. She is by far one of my favorite professors. I definitely recommend taking one of her classes! She is great.

Absolutely one of the best teachers I have ever had! She really tries to help students do well and will repeat things until everyone understands. She's very laid-back about following due dates on the syllabus and will reschedule tests as needed.  Theory was so interesting with her amazing teaching style! She is very knowledgeable and kind.

This class is really easy and interesting enough. Take notes during class and skim the reading, and you can easily get an A.  There are 3 exams and 6 quizzes. She tells you exactly what to expect on them, and if you need help she is very approachable and helpful.

Incredibly smart woman. While lecturing, she never used notes and was incredibly thorough. She would even tell us how to position our notebooks to make a table/chart/etc. Quizzes and exams are really easy. Very pleasant to be around!

Avoid this professor! She thinks extremely highly of herself and assumes you do too. She didn't even come close to making it through her own outline for what we'd cover in class and it was a big waste of time, I didn't lean anything relevant

This class is very straightforward: take notes during lecture, read the book, and study for quizzes and tests. There are no surprises, so you're in complete control of the grade you get. She offers a lot of help for anyone who needs it out of class. Exactly what I would expect from a 100-level course.

Prof. N. is not at all an effective teacher.  Her notes/lectures are frightfully   meaningless.  Not to sound bitter, but she definitely plays favorites in the class.  Also, her very large ego is quite unprofessional and immature and got in the way of my learning in her class.  I strongly suggest avoiding her as a teacher.

Great teacher! All tests are essays, and she is difficult with grading. Although, the tests are hard she explains everything thoroughly and writes everything on the board. She is always available to help and is very nice!!!! Wants all students to succeed and is good about writing letters of recommendation for grad school.

Definitely has a firm grasp of the course material. Incredibly sweet and caring towards students; willing to make small talk at 9am and keeps door open an extra 5 min to account for the early time/weather conditions. Incredibly enthusiastic about the subject and responsive to all questions posed. Contributes firsthand experience in Eastern Europe.
The best teacher I have ever had. Great attitude and remarkable person. I graduated in 2001 and took 3 classes that she taught.
Very good at relaying complex information. She definitely knows her stuff inside and out.  She also gets the class involved, which is nice.
She KNOWS her stuff. She was a good teacher and is ALWAYS willing to help out or go the extra step for a student. The info in the class is kind of dull so hard to pay attention.
No Comments
No Comments
She is extremely willing to help you, but she is so clear and to the point in her class, you probably won't need her help!
No Comments

ARCH 752 - Ethics and Leadership. Despite my efforts,the grading has been overly restrictive.Although the instructor initially stated that class participation would not affect the grade, I noticed that it was included in final grades. after discussing a task with her,I observed that my grade for that task was reduced. the grading was not supportive

ARCH 752 Fall 2024-Ethics and Leadership
Despite all my efforts any opportunity to reduce my grade, she will take it.She did mention the on-class would not affect my grade, but it was mentioned in my grade. once she graded I spoke to her about a subject, she reduced my graded task. it's very restricted grading.Unfortunately, she is not supportive.
Makes students lives very difficult. Doest like everyone. Would not recommend this assistant professor.

I loved SPAN 340 with Ninel, she made the class super engaging, and we got to take a few field trips to museums and libraries, which was a great change of pace and learning environment. Ninel ensures that we all understand class concepts and have opportunities to connect with the content and work with classmates!
Ninel is an amazing spanish teacher. She taught us so much but also kept us engaged all year long and we had fun class discussions. Homework was reasonable and never took me longer than 30 minutes.

Ninel is one of my favorite Spanish professors I've had! Everyone loved her class and it's clear she knows a lot about the historical topics in SPAN 346. Great balance between lecturing and engagement, reasonable amount of homework, not a tough grader but gave good feedback, and requirements for assignments were very clear!

This is a research class so most of the grade is participation. She is the overseer of the lab but you will likely only meet with her during weekly lab meetings. If you intend to go to graduate school, this is VERY important. She is a fantastic teacher who is always ready to share her knowledge. She will turn you into a strong researcher!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pam was a fun professor and made class enjoyable. She loves answering questions and is super passionate about what she teaches. She has a tendency to ramble and didn't always make grading criteria super clear which was frustrating.

She's really passionate about the material she teachers. She is extremely clear, and her slides make the material even easier to understand. She gives lots of examples, is clear about what is needed to know on tests, and posts the slides online so your hand won't fall off in class! She assigns papers, but understands this is not an English class :)

Being on Dr. Neidert's research team was very helpful. She explains everything very well, the projects we worked on were interesting, I learned a lot of skills I will continue to use in the field, and she was very helpful in writing recommendations and helping me prepare for future jobs, grad school, etc.

Pam is an excellent professor. She has very clear expectations of her students, and this class is insanely easy, due to the amount of extra credit given on the tests. All it takes to get an A is showing up, and completing the semester project, which is also easy to finish. She also cares about her students, and wants them to succeed.

Pam really cares about how you do. I didn't take her in a regular lecture (though I've heard she's great at that too from many people) and she urged me to do things to improve my resume, step out of my comfort zone, and gain more experience. She doesn't just want you to do well in school she wants you to do well in the field and jobgrad school.
Pam was really helpful and her classes were interesting
Not helpful

Pam made it very motivating to attend class because many points were earned toward final grades during class time. She was clear about her expectations, and gave as much proactive information about tests and assigments as possible. She was also willing to work with students on a 1:1 basis as necessary.

I took ENGL 205 Honors Proseminar: Imagining a Better World on utopias and Dr. Neill was great! This class influenced me to switch to and English major. I really appreciated the diverse pieces of literature/media we looked at in this class! She also really cares about her students and helping you succeed (as long as you read and put in the work).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really knowledgeable about the course material. Grades fairly and offers a lot of opportunities for feedback. Awesome at directing class discussions!

Professor Neill is personable and intelligent. You can tell she's passionate about the subject. She's a bit of a hard grader, though, and her feedback isn't always the most helpful and can sometimes be confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is really a phenomenal professor! She is very interesting to listen to and her discussions are thought provoking. I thoroughly enjoyed taking this course and would definitely love to work with her again in the future.

She's a great teacher!! She really helps in discussion and loves to teach. I sucked at explaining, but she always helped clarify what I wanted to say. There are readings and discussions every day. No tests, but 4 papers that basically compare books' ideas. She gives good feedback on papers and even let's you redo them.

I think professor Niell is absolutely wonderful. She is a joy and cares about her work. Whoever said she had an annoying New Zealand accent was very rude; I found it endearing. Be willing to work and she'll be fair.
Her uncle is Sam Neill!

For ENGL 105, every single paper could be revised as many times as you wanted. Her comments on how to revise are very helpful and if you put in the work an A in the class isn't difficult. The discussions were often slow to start and hard to maintain, but that's more on the students than the professor.

Not as great as these comments suggest. I'm convinced she has a wealth of knowledge of literature but one of the key assets as a teacher is to be able to CONVEY that knowledge to the students. For some, it clicked. Others, not so much. This is coming from a student that specializes in understanding her teachers. Taking this class is risky.
Tough but incredibly helpful. Fun and encouraging.

A great techer, however the grade consists mainly of four papers and she grades very difficult. Attendance and participation are 20% of the grade which helps. She assigns a lot of reading which is very time consuming and difficult to actually complete. She is very helpful when you go in and talk to her, though.

This class was one of the more difficult I have taken at KU, but was totally worth my time; I took a lot away from the course. Her lectures were always thought provoking, and she always demanded the best out of her students; and this helps you grow as a writer and with critical and analytical thinking. Demanding a lot from students is good, right?

She is a good teacher but she expects entirely to much for a 300 level class. She grades hard and has very high expectations of her class. She is very willing to help outside of class but it is next to impossible to get an A in her class.
No Comments
No Comments

Anna has a terribly annoying New Zealand accent, but when you get past it you see she really likes her job, cares about the material, and assigns reasonable readings and papers. She is also great about helping outside of class.

Madame Lord was very engaging in lecture, gave great examples, used relevant references in her teaching, and was very clear about expectations. Only a few pop quizzes (even though we were warned one class ahead of time) over the semester. She grades based on your effort, which is very fair in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I would not suggest taking this class
She's a very nice teacher. Pretty laid back, but lets you know what she expects. Class attendanceparticipation matters. Do the homework, its usually pretty simple. Tests are kind of hard, so study!
Christina is an awesome teacher. I didn't know any french that much but if you go to her office hours she will help you! She is also pretty so that's a plus.

My favorite professor in the program. Yes hes sarcastic, yes he can talk a lot, but he's a good teacher. He explained to us that he doesn't necessarily want to ramble on about architecture, but naturally teach you as it comes up in your own work. Is very kind and lenient if things don't work out for you and you need more time. Good desk crits!
Called me a "twit" when I went in for help. He likes to listen to himself...I could learn just as much from his slides w/o him speaking...it's just his aesthetic opinion anyways.

Would spend the entire 12 hours of studio time every week talking... talking... talking... stroking his own ego. Did not TEACH architecture as much as he tried to display his own narrow-minded "intellect." This class was a great example of everything that is wrong with architecture education in the United States. Not recommended.

Barry Newton has a great sense of humor.  Everything he says seems funny coming from a British accent.  I didn't get a very good grade because of the sketchbook.  There is some drawing required in the class even though the catalog says there isn't.

He was actually a reallyyyy funny guy. His British accent is very entertaining, and almost everything he said made me laugh. The class isn't TOO demanding...just memorize the TA notes for the test---literally!!! any little detail could show up. he's not going to like your sketch book, so just try your hardest and hope for the best!

Everything he says is hilarious.  Especially because of his English accent.  He has high expectations for your sketch book, however the TA's grade them.  I loved waking up for an 8 o' clock class everyday just to fall asleep and print the notes later.
Going to class at 8am only to fall asleep. It is a rare day when things are interesting. Tests are hard but all the notes are online.

Do those red glasses get on anyone else's nerves?  The humor is funny at first, but after a semester, you will be absolutely sick of it.  Doesn't really like to try new methods.  It's just pin ups.  No desk crits.  A big fan of drawing, not so much of models.  He has a pretty cool house, but he didn't design it.  Rockhill did.
A little sarcasm goes a long way...not a fan
Interesting class.  Grading pretty easy and all the notes were online with everything on the tests taken directly from them.
He is an **** if you go talk to him during office hours. His big head is hard to contain in one lecture hall; he has good taste though.

He does have a very good sense of humor, and he always has the deadline for a project like a week before the jury, so you have plenty of time to finish.  But thatcan be bad also because you don{t feel as motivated to finish.

He's hilarious! i crack up in that class all the time. he's funnier because of his english accent.  he knows a lot about architecture and you can tell he loves it, but he makes jokes and gets off subject sometimes, but it's always funny as hell
Hope you have good drawing skills...the sketchbook is all about the pictures.  Notes get put online so class isnt mandatory.
No Comments
barry's gruff demeanor can be off-putting at first, but he's a great teacher with a lot of knowledge and passion for architecture.

Intimidating at first in a small studio setting (especially after taking his intro to arch class) but an amazing studio professor once you get to know him.  Go into his studio willing to listen and learn and you will not regret it.  His great sense of humor is an added bonus.
He does not read the sketch book so work hard on the pictures, and BS on the text. Fore the test, memorize the notes! Hell, you dont even have to go to class most of the time.
No Comments
No Comments
I think he was an ass most of the time, giving his opionion and talking bad about the guests he had come to the class.
Crazy english accent and he loves to cuss.  Funny as hell, and don't ever read a news paper in his class, he'll get pissed.
No Comments

Terrible class setup due to him using Petr's method of lecturing. Amazing professor in the sense that he adjusts based on what works and how well his students do. Very reasonable with regrades too! Dry lecturer though, but I can't tell if it's him, or if it's the way the lectures are set up. Great professor overall!

Most of the issues I had with the class were because it was Petr's 461 setup, which isn't his fault at all. He changed exams to be a lot more fair, and he is just generally a super great and helpful guy. You could see his progression as a professor throughout the year, and I believe he is going to be incredible in other classes
The absolute goat

Prof. Nguyen cares about the students, and he is reasonable about stuff when you talk to him. For this class to be good though, he has to change Prof. Petr class structure because it's just bad, not engaging and I don't think anyone benefits from mindlessly writing down notes. If he changes that, I think he has the potential to be a great professor

Professor Ngoh was the best English teacher I've had. She improved my writing skills, and her class was always a joy. She based our class on rap music and it made me interested in English class because we weren't talking about old books we were talking about rap songs. She also did a rap for the class which was a highlight. Wonderful teacher.
She genuinely cares about her students and it shows. Although some content is tough, she will always work with you on deadlines and care about your mental wellbeing first.

She's awesome. Really worked with us to give us a good semester. Content was challenging and she's a tough grader, but she's happy to sit down and help you learn what you did wrong. She cancelled class on Halloween "just cuz". If I were taking another english class, I'd look for her name on the class description. You won't be disappointed!
She is amazing.
As English is my second language it was a bit difficult for me initially but she explained it really well to me and as semester proceeded the projects got easier

If you have this teacher for ENGL 102, switch to another professor. She grades essays much harder than all other ENGL 102 professors and her class was boring and filled with pointless busy-work. Do all homework (easy) and show up to all classes to get 20% of your grade. No final but 4 large essays (hard to get A on essays from straight-A student)

This class was very easy, we only had 4 papers but they get easier throughout the semester. This class is engaging and the material learned is helpful to getting a good grade. Sarah cares about her students and is very easy to get in touch with or meet. She brings in food towards the end of the semester! Would recommended taking a class with her.

Sara Ngoh is such an amazing professor and human in general! she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She helped me with anything I ever needed and was very accessible and approachable! she made me actually want to come to class because she made a class i dont normally enjoy fun and fresh

Sarah Ngoh is fantastic, by far my favorite course and professor last semester. She does have expectations, but she makes sure you are able to exceed these expectations and grow as an individual. She is relatable and isn't afraid to take a few minutes in class to chat and connect with everyone which I greatly appreciated. Much love and respect.
Sarah was great this semester, she's really funny. For 101, she didn't have us buy any of the textbooks listed for the course. Really cool and smart, made a typically boring class interesting
She is amazing. Highly recommend this class be taken

She def cares for her students past their educational needs, she's approachable, encouraging, and passionate about the subject matter. Creates a space of comfort and tremendous mutual respect and often randomly brings in candy- which is always a plus. I absolutely recommend taking a course from Sarah Ngoh at any given opportunity!
The best, best, best, best, best instructor I ever had. Definitely take her class if u have a chance, u wont regret it.
Really cares about students, is open and respectful. Lots of reading, class is fun. No lectures just student discussion. Eye-opening

I took this class (pop lit) over the summer. I've never gotten below a B on any papers before her, but she let me rewrite them and I appreciate that she made me actually work for my grade. She makes you read a lot, but the books were really, really good reads! Participation in class is a must or you wont do well.
She was an incredible teacher. She really cared about my well being and how I was doing in class. The best teach I have had a KU.
She's really a great teacher. She cares about her students. You can tell. She says the  'F' word a lot, but that's why I like her. She keeps it real.

Sarah Is the awesome teacher, she respects everyone, different cultures. Her assignments seem hard but it is easy, she is always helpful. She helps the students whenever they need help via email and office hours and even not during the office hours. She is the bright and positive. Very creative and fun and warm teacher!
Great teacher!

Ms. Ngoh was by far the best English teacher I've ever had. She makes the topic actually interesting, as well as making her expectations clear. Put in a little bit of effort and you're guaranteed an A

She is super helpful and she really cares about her students.  She is high energy and tries to make writing fun even for people who hate it.  I think she is just a really good person and an awesome teacher.

She is a very helpfull teacher, sometimes she doesnt explain exactly what she wants from her class. If you do bad in a paper she may let you rewrite it, overall good teacher, made english 101 a somewhat stress-free class.
Seriously awesome teacher.
BEST teacher i have ever had. Makes class so fun :-)

My favorite Calc 2/3 TA. He gets to know everyone on a first-name basis and is very helpful on top of it. Get his lab section if you can and go to the help room when he's there. A great guy all around

Cuong was an awesome teacher! I took MATH116 and I had class every morning and it was one of the only classes I didn't dread going to. He is a ver sweet and caring teacher and you can tell he genuinely cares about his student's success. I would definitely advise to go to his office hours. Not only will it help you, but he will respect you more.
I'm terrible at calc and Cuong didn't make it any easier, almost didnt pass. He's funny and helpful, but his lectures are long and confusing.  Make a point to go and see him in office hours.
Awesome teacher. Definitely the best TA for MATH 121
GREAT teacher! You can tell that he really cares about his students! I would HIGHLY recommend taking a class from Cuong. Super helpful.

I took it as an accelerated course online. Quizzes + Exams are open book, exams are timed but not too bad. Three big Assignments make up a lot of your grade. They are pretty difficult only because you have to be very thorough. Start them early, go to her office hours to ask questions, and you will be fine. She is very helpful.

This class was a full 3 credit hour course online in 8 weeks but it really didn't feel that way. Lectures were easy to keep up with, questions on weekly quizzes were similar to the questions on tests. There were 3 big assignments but they weren't very hard. The professor was very easy to contact and is very good at answering questions.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Norman's very enthusiastic about the class & is always available to talk to students. She also understood that we had other classes so she gave us extensions if we asked for them. We could miss 5 classes without losing points. We only had one group project but it was worth 30% of our grade. We had two tests worth 9% each and both were easy.

Buy PDF book-much cheaper and you really do not need it. Lots of lessons and info. Gives a ton of extra credit worth a lot if you need it. Interesting class. The workload was okay. Quizzes, discussions, 3 assignments, timed midterm and final. The midterm and final were fairly long for the amount of time but not to bad. Good online course to take.
Neal is a really easy guy to respect. He's funny, down to earth, and laid-back. His tests were frequent, but simple and had no curveballs.  I'd gladly take him again for an ECON class.
Becker is a really good teacher and made things interesting. As long as you make some effort and prepare for the half hour exams you should do fine.
Awesome professor. Funny and engaging, even in big classes.

If you have an interestaptitude in economics, Dr. Becker is perfect for you. While he "suggests" looking at his online resources, you definitely should, as they're basically the answers to the free response question on each exam. Easy if you read the book and watch his online instructional videos.

Overall he's a really good lecturer. He makes what could be an extremely boring topic very interesting. You MUST read the book or you will fail the multiple choice section of the tests. The short answer part (50%) is by far the easiest. Attendance isn't technically mandatory, but your missing out if you skip. Highly recommend. (Honors section)

Dr. Becker is a nice guy, really obsessed with Game of Thrones. lectures were usually pretty interesting. not a lot of math involved for an econ class.  the final really caught me off guard, though. until the final I had a 90% in the class without ever picking up the book. the final knocked me down to a B, most of it must have been from the text
Dr. Becker is a great instructor and makes economics an engaging subject. The class is easy if you stay on top of the readings, do all of the homework, and use his online resources.

I didn't like him so much. The hw is long and the online quizzes are pretty easy. if you put time towards these, it will be good. You have to read the chapter pretty well to get the multiple choice correct. I wouldnt take him again.
Study the book closely, do all of the homework, don't miss his group projects, and study his online screencasts as closely as the book. It's an easy class if you just follow that advice.

If you are a bad test taker, stay away from this guy. You can only miss the equivalent of ONE question per test to receive an A. Almost impossible to do so. I had a B the entire semester and the final bumped me down to a C+. No need to go to class every other day when there is no group project as he just rambles. He is willing to help, though.
I had a rocky start with this class missing a lot of the first half of hw and projects, but the first three exams I took were all A's. If you read the chapters and do the homework it's not that hard.
his syllabus is cryptic at best. He makes you do excessive homework

Dr. Becker is an extremely knowledgeable and engaging professor. Many think his tests are difficult, but if you just read the book and use his online resources then you'll find that his class is easy. He's also a really funny guy.

He's a good professor and he's infinitely knowledgable about his subject. What he says in lecture isn't necessarily what will be on the test, so you'll have to read the book and attend the discussion sessions to do well. Grades are also updated very quickly on Blackboard, which is always useful.
Awesome professor. I just finished Econ 582. Best class ever. Interesting research that empowers students to make their own decisions about economic policy.

Tends to get off topic, but explains things well. Online homework comes from the book, but what you discuss in class does not. Tests every two weeks, but they're not bad. Olympic scores everything (Drop highest and lowest grade), and curves the honors class using the same curve as the regular class.

He does get off topic…but it's interesting at least. If you go talk to him, you're going to get help. He does give challenging test and doesn't curve them. BUT he curves the entire class at the info of the semester...I heard that it could be over a letter grade.

Do not take this class, what he says during class has nothing to do with what homework that you will have online.  There homework or quizzes due every Friday, and Sunday night, so plan on not having anything to do then, because everything is extremely hard. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM.

Review your notes. Go to his office hours if you have questions. He relates material to funny stories to make it easy to remember. You will have a take home test after every in class test. the take home tests are hard and will take critical thinking. he is willing to help you as long as you given him specific questions.
n/a

This is one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. He assigns quizzes and homework that are due every Friday and Sunday night so be prepared for not having a life. He often "challenges" his students on exams with material we hadn't seen before just to see if we can figure it out. SO frustrating. Please find someone better.

Neal Becker is a decent teacher. I can see how others don't do well in the class. If you're good at Econ and have prior experience in the class than you'll do just fine. Class isn't mandatory. Be sure to read textbook. Homework is easy.
One of the better teachers of econ at KU. Lectures are very informational. Does get off topic a lot though.

While you should read the textbook, I learned the most through the online homework. The hw really helps with the exams, especially graphing questions. At times Becker gets off topic, and wastes time at the start of class, but overall he is a good teacher and great guy who likes all of his students and will answer any questions easily.
Pretty good for a relatively big lecture class.  He plays music at the beginning of class and tries to keep it interesting.  He's a nice guy, I'd recommend taking a class with him.

Dude wears awesome shirts, and on top of that he is really interesting and easy to get along with. Keeps your attention in the class which is really nice. Stays true to the course material and wants everyone to get an A
I really enjoyed taking this class, professor becker does a great job teaching and making economics interesting. I highly recommend taking a class with him if you are considering an econ course.
The short answer questions on his exams are very hard and worth over half your grade. I hate this class so much.

basically it was like this. first exam gave 3 days of studying, got an F, understandable. second exam studied a week in advance, got a D. ok... third exam studied 3 weeks in advance and walked into class knowing the whole material, got a C... basically he teaches the class well but his exams are never what he goes over in class. he screws us over.

if you like economics you will like neal. i guess the class isn't that easy but what science course is? he is more than happy to help and often in his office. wouldn't say he's the best teacher i've had (how can he be a babying prof in a huge lecture class) but he is my favorite i've ever had.
