Good teacher who does a good job explaining things in class.  He doesn't make it easy (he plays to the highest common denominator not the lowest), but that's something I like.  And he doesn't act as if he is above the students.  All and all, an excellent professor.

Very interesting teacher and very smart. I feel like he knows the material very well and teaches at an appropriate rate. While attendance isn't required, if you don't go you will miss him explain how he wants that question answered on the test. Highly recommend this teacher although a lot of time is required.

Prof. Becker understands the subject so well and sees the math in economics so clearly that sometimes I think he forgets that students not studying econ don't really get all of it. The class is very mathematically and graphically oriented. Be prepared to study and practice making graphs and interpreting them a lot. Tough, but a manageable class.
A GREAT PROFESSOR!
He was a decent teacher. Class was difficult, test were very challenging and Aplia was sooooooo annoying. Be prepared to study hard for this class and put in lots of hours.

Far from the best prof as the other said. My experience in this class was terrible. Neal knows what he is talking about but teaches it horribly. He is very non engaging so there is zero class participation. I'm a decent student and micro econ made me pull my hair out. Boring, unclear lectures. Worst class I've ever had. He's an imbecile.

Class was easy enough.  The grading on the tests seemed to not be on any sort of clear rubric.  The essay questions can be vague, make sure you know what he expects.  At the end of the semester, my grade was figured incorrectly.  I ended up .05% (85.95% when an 86% was needed) away from an A.  He wouldn't round up.  Took forever to get tests back.
Seemed to know the subject well.. The class was rather boring though.

Best Class I've taken at KU due in large part to Professor Becker.  Frequently available after and outside of class.  Loves what he teaches.  If you apply yourself, he'll give you the benefit of the doubt.
The best professor I had in my whole life.

A very unclear and vague teacher. In a field that is very technical and requires essential fundamentals, he does not provide very well. His lectures have some information, but not much. Most of the information one needs can be gotten only from homework and reading. Discussions are not that helpful either.
i hated this class, you have to put a lot of effort into it, the homework is hard. the tests are very hard you have to study ALOT at the end i think there is a big curve

Avoid at all costs, this guy is the most unorganized teacher ever. TA's grade tests unfairly, you have to go see becker for a chance to get back points you earned. Becker's TA's have no idea whats going on becasue of his lack of organization. Dates  are different depending on who you talk to and the sylabus. Doesnt respond to e-mails either. AVOID!

I learned  lot from this class but you must apply yourself. attending lecture is a must to understand all of his graphs and there are  a LOT. tests are hard but grading system is extremely fair. hard at the time but looking back, i learned a lot about economics that i can apply to lots of different situations in the future
Makes everything really difficult but can't teach at all!

Much better than most of the econ teachers and tries to keep class as entertaining as possible. Very clear with his examples and you shouldn't have a problem with understanding it. Offers a ton of extra credit(5% of total grade) but tests are pretty difficult for a general ed class.
Just good.

Horrible teacher, very confusing class. He thinks his tests are easy but they are impossible. The graders can make up reasons to not give you full points. His TA's dont care, and dont help. Avoid Becker!
Class can be boring at times, but he always tries to make things clear.
He knows his content well, and is an outstanding professor. I would recommend him for anyone...
worst Econ prof ever! Definitely Avoid him!
Weird tests,which convers most concepts different from textbook

An average teacher (at least for 142), don't really expect a "full effort" from Becker, although he could teach better, he doesnt since its only an intro course. Sometimes wastes time on youtube videos/daily news and overdraws certain graphs as well as sells future econ courses, but a decent teacher. Go once a week and you'll get a B with some work

The best professor at KU. Have had him for several classes, and I find myself remembering things 3-4 semesters later. On a side not, I always used to laugh at the kids with the four different colored pens and mini-rulers in class...until I took Becker's class. You will learn to love graphs!

Prof. Becker is a good teacher, but he's kind of full of himself.  I have had him for both ECON 142 and ECON 522, and I like his style (a lot better than other alternatives), but he's not the most clear or most helpful.  However, he's a safe bet cuz you know exactly what you're getting.  And when it comes to ECON at KU, that's pretty good.
Class seems like it would be difficult if you never read the book.  Helpful to take calculus before the class although it is not a pre-req. Lots of EC opportunities.
Very confusing lectures, and incredibly tricky and confusing test questions.  Try to find a different professor for this class.
His lectures are impossible to understand or follow along with. Discussions are the only way to pass ECON 144.
The class itself is pretty good, but sometimes professor uses vague examples to teach and the tests are pretty challenging as well, but if you put in the work an A is very attainable.
funny guy, good teacher, tests are pretty tough
Becker is a funny guy. Likes to draw graphs alot. Read the book. Weekly homework is online and it sucks especially when you wait an hour before its due. I didn't really try and I managed a B.
Neal tries hard to make it fun, but it's not.  You don't need to go to lecture, just read the book.  The TA's suck, you can't understand them
maybe its just this semesters, but all the TAs are either really mean or really hard to understand. The class is interesting, but I learn a lot more from the book than the lecture or the discussions.

Superlatively good teacher.  All of his classes are graphically intensive, and you get to draw lots of pretty pictures.  Makes the subject extremely interesting, and you get wonderful applied economics at the start of class.  However, looking back over class notes, they are not always clear enough for study (and he teaches off the book, A LOT).
No Comments
I really enjoyed this class and his TAs were helpful, but hoped they could speak better english!
Interesting, but I wish his TAs would speak better English.
Brings life to what is usually considered boring to most.
Decent Professor, doesn't explain concepts very well, learn more in the review sessions than I did in class.  Hard to get an A, a B is attainable.

Attend your discussions and you'll be fine. Try to get Dieter Schrader for a TA; he's awesome! Class takes a good effort to get an A in, but if you do an average amount of studying you should at least get a B. Short answers on the tests are hard, but long answers are worth a lot and are easy.

Knows his stuff and teaches clearly. He tries to make the material entertaining by telling jokes and having haiku contests. Don't listen to everyone else. Tests are easy if you study a bit and don't come to the exam ****. But what can you expect from these liberal arts majors. ;)
Great techer but his box questions on the exams can be tricky so watch out.

His tests are hard and ANYTHING he's mentioned can be on there. The graphs are a huge part of the class/tests. He's really annoying though, so fight the urge to skip all the time, you need to go to get a good grade. He's known for wasting a whole class.
Good teacher, but leave class when he starts surfing the internet. Tests are not easy, study everything he has ever mentioned in class.
His tests are hard, so do lots of studying.  It is a hard class, but he is a fun teacher to have.
No Comments
His tests are difficult and confusing (read: hard) but he does a good job of teaching...I liked him but it is NOT an easy class.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
It was just impossible to succeed in this class because she tests over things we didn't even cover in class.

Fresh PhD graduate becomes teacher riding her high horse. 101 intro class that felt like a 500 Geology major class. Incredibly rude and unsympathetic towards any situations. Worksheets every single class along with iClickers you couldn't miss. We were expected to research things on our own and then they would explain answers later. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Disorganization and unclear instructions made the class unnecessarily challenging. Coursework was extremely unhelpful. We were given paper worksheets every class and asked to search for answers, only to have the correct answers provided later on. The exam questions were consistently unclear, always necessitating clarifications.

Dr. Bartlow is a very rude professor who acts as if she is better than everyone in her class. She is unhelpful, not to mention rude in email responses as well as when she rarely helps out in class. She expects you to be at every class with illness or anything else as no excuse. I would avoid taking a class from her at all costs.

I figured a 101 class would be easy, and the content was easy. There was just too much busy work. Every question required a large detailed diagram drawn to scale. We also spent 2 hours looking at a sandwich to explain that rocks stack on each other. I am still not sure how that was news to anyone, or how a sandwich made the idea and more clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Drops 3 labs, very kind professor, teaching assistants are generally good quality. Uses A- but not A+ grading scale. While class isn't mandatory I-clicker is a part of the grade, so attendance is recommended and can hurt your grade

Professor is insufferable and awful at lecturing. This class is the hardest class I have ever taken. I spend more time doing work in this class than in any of my project-based classes. It would have an ounce of potential if it was a traditional lecture with notes/guided notes, but instead we do worksheet after worksheet. Do not take this class.
i hate this class
Refuses to help students who cannot come to his office hours and made a creepy joke about his "center bulge" during class.

Noah McLean is friendly and passionate about his work. That being said, he moves too quickly for you to have time to read and answer the questions that make up most of your grade. Additionally, these questions are on iClicker, which is an added, unnecessary cost. Expect heavy group work. Lastly, there is assigned seating, even though it's college.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a good professor, a good person, he's nice and knows his job and the content well. The problem is that this is a 101 class, literally an entry class, I am a senior at KU and I have taken 700 level classes easier Than this. The professors require way too much, please avoid this class if you're looking for a science/lab credit.

I love him so much!!! Such a sweet man whos clearly passionate about his field and will also inspire you to be! Hes super helpful and so nice and will always make you feel better about urself, and you will genuinely want to switch your major to geology. Would give him a kiss! best professor ever!!
Literally the best professor. He is always extremely helpful and passionate about geology. I literally changed my major to geology its also a really easy class.

Dr McLean is a very nice person and loves his field. He always seems excited about giving his lecture, which by the way over half of the time is working on worksheets with your group and it is pretty good .Other great thing is that he is always willing to help you in his office hours or by appoiment with lots of enthusiasm. Take him.

I'm in a major that is unrelated to geology but I loved this class. I would recommend it as your core science credit. He is a lot of fun and obviously very passionate about the subject matter. Expect group projects and make friends quickly because you need to work with someone to understand concepts. Go to SI sessions. It's tough work, but fun.

Him and is TA's are always willing to help and are the key to getting an A. The tests are important but the quizzes and miniprojects add up to more over time. I would always go to a TA with questions over the miniprojects and I never got below a 92 on them because of it. The final was scary but him and his TA's helped so much it was relatively easy

Even though it's a lecture class, only 10 minutes of lecture then the rest is group work. Plus the class also has graduate students and a few other professionals in the field of geology to help out. He reassured me geology is the path i want to go. OH and he's an adorable nerd with TONS of puns. What's not to love?

Engaging lecturer, clearly outlined all material that would be on the exams. Highly recommend taking one of her classes even if you're just passively interested in Art History, she is enthusiastic about the content and helped me gain so much appreciation for the topic. She is very knowledgable, super empathetic and willing to answer any questions.
She cares about her students.
Loves to lecture but does her best to make every single one interesting! I love how passionate and excited she is!
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you take this course online it is such an easy A. The workload is very minimal and easy, plus the tests are all online. She is very specific with her grading criteria and is a little bit of a hard grader, but if you just check the rubric and meet all the requirements you'll do fine. She clearly cares a lot about the topic and is very passionate.

Took the class online, not necessarily a hard class, but extremely unclear directions at times, and things were listed all over the place, not easily accessible. Kathleen is not understanding of problems you may have encountered and sticks to her "rules" that are quite opinionated. I've never had to rate a professor until now. If possible, avoid.

Kr. Nuckolls was not very helpul in her class. She would never respond to emails, it was an online class. I had the worst time trying to figure out my grade as it would never be graded. Thank God I passed this class, but unless I MUST take a class from her again i will I do. I do not recommend taking her unless its a required course.

Dr. Nuckolls is a very organized professor who is very knowledgeable about the natural world. Her class discussions and homework are very helpful in learning many aspects of the natural world. The textbook that is required for this class is very interactive, intriguing, and enjoyable. If you stay engaged in the course, you will easily pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is way too hard for a 100 level course. The discussion board posts require too much effort especially when responding to comments which no one really wants to do. The one written assignment is a 3-4 page single spaced paper which also felt too hard and pointless. Taken online you rely on the textbook and really have to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is HARD. Be ready to spend all your time devoted to arcGIS because it consumes your life. I even dreamt about making maps. Kathleen honestly does what she can do be able to teach this class through online. You must read the textbook and set aside hours to work in GIS. I recommend attending office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took toxicology seminar with her and it was a very interesting class. We read two books and wrote responses for the assigned reading. Also did a lot of group work. Overall I enjoyed this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved taking Dr. Nuckolls' First Year Seminar called Toxicology, Toys, and Tator Tots. Her class is very easy to understand if you enjoy discussing toxicology with small groups. We read two small books and were required to write a response to each chapter, but honestly, if you just skim the chapter, you'll be fine. Would take again!
This professor is way too quiet for lecturing purposes so she makes a whole bunch of in-class assignments to go with the textbook readings. Not hard, just tedious overall.

She loves to be a professor, but she doesn't know how to teach. The whole class period is just group discussion and no lecture at all. All you can learn from is the online textbook. I don't see the different between this class and to take the online class.  DO NOT enroll in her class if you like to learn from the lecture.

The online section deals mainly with a textbook that quizzes you as you go. Don't wait to complete the chapter quizzes - if you do, you'll miss out on points unnecessarily. Tests were always easier than I expected, but I hated having to go in to take them. Very little interaction with professor. DO participate in online discussions.
Basically, this class killed my GPA. The study guides she puts online are basically the entire chapters so study up.

This class was freakin impossible online. I have a very good GPA and do well in school, but her tests made no sense and there was no clarity concerning what to study. Pretty much says "study everything" and hopes you make it. Honestly, I studied so hard and yet did so poorly for how much work I put into it. Avoid online if possible. Not easy.

Her toxicology class is awesome! The work load is low. She is friendly, funny, and laid back. We talked about current day relevant topics. I attended about half the lectures and still got an A. Minimal homework also!

She is a really HELPFUL and Nice person. If you do bad in your first exam, no worries, go and ask for help. She would be very nice.  One paper due final, but seems that she grades the paper not strictly. Anyway, the class is not a  very easy one.

She gets pretty excited over a lot of EVRN stuff for some reason, but she at least knows what she it talking about. this is basically a combo of BIO 100 and GEOG 104 so if you have taken those you should be good. her tests are impossible to understand and online quizzes are pointless...

She is kind f a crazy person, but she does love what she does and you can tell.  She is a big nerd, but I learn learn a lot about basic environmental components that helped me in future classes in the field.  It is interesting, tests are kind of oddly set up but over all not that bad of a class.

Good professor. VERY passionate about the subject and very willing to lend a helping hand. Tests are hard but manageable and ALL notes are provided. Attending discussion section is a MUST. EVRN 148 setup: 3 tests, final is test 3 and cumulative, online chapter quizzes, easy labs.

Tests made no sense. She calls the questions multiple guess and that is was they are! You just guess on all of the quiz and test questions because they are very confusing. She is very organized and give good class notes attending class helps but is not mandatory

She used a program that involved her really not having to do much work. She did not have the assignments on canvas and there were about 40 a week. It was way too complicated and unhelpful and just busy work and she graded so strictly especially if we used words we have not been taught which is wild because some spanish words are quite common
It was a good class and she's a good teacher.

Lots of REQUIRED participation. No test or quizzes, except for a group test at the end of each unit. She is very understanding and helpful. You will have to pay for some subscription to a website(I think I paid 80) for homework and stuff like that. Very little ec but it's an easy class as long as you stay on top of it. HW everyday.

Took class half semester, heavy reading, lots of hw. Fast paced. Didn't interact with her too much, doesn't allow grade changes (talks about it in syllabus). No exams. Do the discussion posts (1x week) bc they're worth 45% of your grade and will significantly change your grade if you miss one.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures can be really long & difficult to stay interested in but she is a great professor who clearly loves social psychology. The more you participate the more you'll get out of class & material. Tests are mostly multiple choice with 5-6 essay questions each & you can choose to skip the final. 4 writing assignments & 4 discussion posts. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is not difficult at all if you show up to class and pay attention. I never read the textbook and got A's on all of the exams. The class is incredibly boring though and 3 hour lectures are just as horrible as they sound so keep that in mind.

Although helpful, clear, and easy, I think there should be another category added to this rating, as this doesn't reveal how boring the class is. The three hour lectures didn't help anything, but Nyla is not a very engaging speaker, and she's quite awkward as well. The text (co-authored by her) is very dry, I only used it for my papers

I had this class once a week for 3 hours, now and then, she'll let class out early. Two writing assignments that were kind of fun and easy to write. Four exams, but you get to drop one. Final is cumulative (and is included in the four exams). Read the book and notes, know the examplesstudies, and it's an easy A. Branscombe was also very helpful.

I learned a lot in this course, and Dr. Branscombe is a great professor. She grades fair, but she also expects a lot out of her students, ultimately helping them to succeed. A couple of writing assignments were required over the semester, and the tests were m/c, short answer, ans essay. As long as you study and write well, an A is achievable.

this professor is the most unfeeling professor I have ever come across in the field of psychology. She is a social psychologist but WOW her social skills are greatly lacking. She would rather ostracize students than teach them! I thought professors were supposed to teach not criticize without listening or teaching!
nyla is cool. topics alwways interesting. i liked the videos and her lecturing style is great
course is pretty great. Content is controversial and interesting. She keeps it rolling along and I forget it's 3 hours. Nyla is amazingly knowledgeable about psychology.

Nyla is really a sweetheart...she is fun, likes to joke around a lot, and even bought candy/pizza for the class...She puts all of her lectures on powerpoint, and her tests and assignments are extremely easy, but you still come away from the class learning the information.
gets us involved and is fun
Very helpful and tests are clear. she lectures well and keeps your interest with good things in the powerpoint you can download
in the class now and she's great. don't know how her tests are yet
fun lecturer, never boring even for 3 hour class
No Comments
She really got everyone involved. VERY effective teacher.

I have never had a more caring or understanding professor. The class I took was not easy, but Dr. Obrien is an amazing teacher that will go out of her way to help you. Her courses may not help your GPA, but will definitely be worth your time!

Extremely disorganized. Added a Final Exam worth 40% of our grade to the syllabus in October. Lectures were random fodder about globalization with a few movies thrown in and large books which we spent little time discussing. Her one saving grace is that she's not too bad, and actually pretty helpful, one-on-one.
Her class is very tough. However, she is a extremely nice teacher who always likes to help her students.  You also learn a lot new and interesting stuff in her class.
She obviously taught from notes going back ages. Her lectures were hazy, dissembling things. Lost interest in the subject fairly soon (class was International Law).
Very difficult class, but fun.  It helps a lot if you go to class and do the readings.
the material is hard, but she is a great teacher
Tough Class, but the teacher is excellent and very helpful.
Very, very difficult class. But it is rewarding, if you stick it out.  Teacher is excellent, extremely well-informed, extremely helpful, and just a nice woman in general.

Kind person but class was confusing & disorganized. Lectures are repetitive and tangential. Not consistent in uploading slides on Canvas, did not upload the syllabus until October. Unpredictable whether class will follow the syllabus or not. No/incorrect dates on syllabus. Minimal assignments, graded harshly. Harsh criticism on writings especially.

He's super passionate and knowledgeable about his subject which makes the lectures entertaining, but sometimes he goes on tangents that seem irrelevant. He is very receptive to feedback and values students perspectives. Slightly disorganized on canvas and in lectures and takes a while to grade. However, he is understanding and willing to change.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice and caring guy. He has a lot of knowledge about the subject and loves sharing it, I definitely learned a lot of interesting things. That being said, it is hard to take the class seriously when he doesn't. Very frustrating.

Do not take a class with him. He did not have a correct syllabus until halfway through the year and did not grade any assignments on time. Most were returned after the end of the semester, even those where feedback was necessary to complete the others. His contact information was incorrect and he did not respond to emails or texts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was by far the worst experience I had with a professor teaching any class! He didn't grade any assignment until the end of the year such as a paper that we had turned in on October 7th we did not receive a grade until the last day of the semester. Please do not take any classes with this professor as it will cause unnecessary stress and angry.

Do NOT take a course by this professor. No clear outline for lectures, no clear dates for assignments, and no clear guidance or information for assignments, tests, or quizzes.  Hard to get a hold of and does not return grades for assignments and tests within a reasonable time. Not worth your time or money. Be prepared to teach yourself

Do NOT take a course by this professor. No clear lecture, no clear guidance on assignments, tests, or quizzes. Hard to reach if you have questions and does not return grades in a timely manner. Not worth your time or money

I want to begin by being positive, Hannington is a good person, and I have no personal issues with him.

that being said, he is a terrible professor. Despite giving his personal contact info in the syllabus, he doesn't reply to emails or texts. He doesn't post online assignments online, and his assignments are focused on meaningless details, avoid

Didn't get the syllabus until November Grades were arbitrary and all given on the last day to submit Made us submit drafts but graded them after final papers were due Both lectures and readings managed to be irrelevant Made us get 5 books (used 2) Didn't respond to emails/texts (gave us his #) Confusing/unclear expectations Nice guy though, easy A

I would absolutely not recommend. Doesn't respond to emails, shifted course from BB to canvas 2 weeks in, and didn't give credit unless you moved your assignments over. The syllabus was inaccurate, he didn't start grading until 6 weeks into the 8-week course, and the course is very reading-heavy and discussion-heavy. Overall was very disappointed.

The prof is very nice but there is no communication and little organization. I emailed him multiple times trying to ask questions about assignments and received no response. Grades always took forever to get out (even when we needed the feedback for assignments). I'm disappointed because my friends met him out of class and highly recommended him.

He's very organized and updates students regularly about what is due when. He's incredibly knowledgeable in his field too. He will reach out to students, but good luck hearing back from him. He does not grade most assignments (if any) and just uploads the content. The TA grades. I had to buy all textbooks/books out of pocket too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ochwada is an interesting character but not a great professor. He is impossible to get a hold of outside of class. He is very forgiving if you can get a hold of him. His lectures are interesting but often have nothing to do with what is tested on. He forgot to assign 3 important quizzes and often missed class.

Doesn't generally give reason to his grades on your written work, so it feels arbitrary. His instruction and ESPECIALLY his tests are hard to understand because they're not written clearly, so I was forced to guess what he meant most of the time. Also a lot of emails with no purpose and rambling video lectures. My worst class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Taking his class wasnt bad. He realized we werent on track with the syllabus and then he never updated it. So basically we didnt know when the papers were actually due. So he would come in class like oh yeah. Your reaction paper is due next class. Hes a great prof, very engaging. Also, taking notes is pointless, itll end up confusing later.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Ochwada cares about his students and provides an African perspective on the history he teaches. However, I don't recommend him for several reasons: 1. He is disorganized. He canceled a book discussion the day we were supposed to discuss it--when I had already bought and read part of the book! 2. I often got no response to my emails to him.

Literally I couldn't even pick one of the RateMyProfessor tags because I don't know how to describe Hannington. He is the strangest professor with unclear expectations. He refuses to be contacted by email and I feel like I have more questions coming out of his class than I had going in. Don't take his class if you don't have to!

Very knowledgeable about what he teaches. Lectures would sometimes go off on tangents, but they were always very interesting and relevant. A majority of your grade will be essays and attendance/participation. So be prepared to put a lot of work into your writing and show up to class with knowledge of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is super nice and funny! He will work with you on due dates and any assignment if you just ask. PARTICIPATION is key in his class it is a large part of your grade and he wants you to put in your input.

(AAAS 105/HIST 104) Hannington was very clear from the beginning about what he wanted, show up, participate and pass. He REALLY looks for you to provide feedback, participation matters, don't expect to just show up. If you talk to him he is willing to help, but be ready to do the work. Amazing professor.

I found the course to be poorly organized and lacking in clear instructions. Lectures often felt disjointed, and key concepts were not explained in a way that made them easy to understand. I would recommend seeking out a different professor if possible. Gyat diggly dooon what was this dooooozy of a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: To be honest, unless you're already smart/have a solid foundation for the concepts in this class, an A is gonna be very difficult to get. His class is structured in a way that the only resource you got to study for the med school level tests are the dog water lectures (the smartbooks are useless). My A means nothing don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He should not be teaching undergraduates. His exam questions are so specific, making it incredibly difficult to study. There are almost no preparation materials apart from sample questions that often do not appear on the exam anyway. If you want a professor that is difficult to listen to because he is so monotone, take this class.

Pretty much your whole grade depends on solely exam grades, apart from 51 points extra credit. However, the exams do not have many questions on them and are over very specific details out of incredibly lengthy slides. The slides contain more random diagrams than words. Each exam question is weighed very heavily.
Usually I am a very good student. Whole class bases on a guessing game of what will be on the 4 exams (only assignments btw). Already enrolled in the summer section if that says anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 4 exams, 51 extra credit, over half get below 70 on each exam with lots under 50. Lectures long, boring, and mostly irrelevant. Hard to study because slides have random, useless diagrams, and "150+ practice problems" come 2 days before the exam, most not even covered. One tutor for the whole class. Guessing what will actually be tested Doesnt care

paraphrased: "Final will be comprehensive. I won't provide additional practice questions for previous material covered. Theres already 150 practice questions available. They should cover the material well enough to help u test how well u have learned the material. Some questions will come from the midterms. The majority, however, will be new."
bruh

reviews.comment: HIS SLIDES SUCK! he never puts the information you'll actually need, all his slides are pictures. he starts explaining things that aren't on the slides and always goes on tangents and there is no study guide! HE ALSO DOES NOT RECORD LECTURES! his class is also 100% exam based!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Man does not care about anything except aspergillus nidulans. Lectures are straight nonsense, pretty much him just flexing his extensive knowledge of useless info. Graded on 4 exams, which on the first, more students received below a 50 than above a 90. Walked out of the first exam and thought I was gonna have to switch to business.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I mean it's pretty obvious he only cares about research. In midterm1, only 5/104 students got a 90-96. We are mostly 2nd year premeds with GPAs to maintain, and probably only ~15% of the class will get an A because his exams have concepts not found in lecture OR the textbook. We are tested over +300 pgs of textbook content--he expects WAY too much!
Easy A. Interesting if you want to learn about screenwriting and have no prior experience. He is very friendly and funny at times. I've enjoyed the class. Not very demanding.
If you are a serious writer, he can be a severe critic, if you are just learning, he can be humorous and warm

I had David for screenwriting. I took the class because I heard it was easy. It ended up being super boring but you can just bring your computer to class and work on other things. Pretty painless. He's a nice guy, really quiet though.

I loved Ohle & the fact that he wasn't one of those professors who thought that his class should be YOUR LIFE for that entire semester. He has a great outlook on things and realizes that everyone is at a different level when it comes to writing. I would definitely recommend anyone take his fiction classes.
Ohle is a great guy with and interesting sense of humor. I feel I learned a lot from his class. Being introduced his books was also a major plus. Ask him about Einstein's brain.

This is quite possibly the easiest class I ever took at KU.  All you have to do is complete two short screenplays and you are basically guaranteed a B.  If they are any good, you get an A.  About 1/3 of the classes are cancelled because he realizes that th

very nice guy, funny, helpful, not too hard, just about everything you want in a teacher.  if i could take a class of his again, i would.  he pushes students to do good work, and the text book is actually interesting. likes to have class discussions.

He's a good guy, that is very helpful. The class gets boring at times, but when there is nothing to do, he'll let you out early. The papers aren't bad, and he'll tell you how to improve them.  He is very humorous at times, when he is trying not to be, very easy guy to talk to. Get him for 101

His dry humor is funny. If you are at the beginning of the alphabet, be prepared to answer all the questions on the readings. He helps you with papers, and they aren't too bad. Lectures get boring. Ask him about the novels he's written...
Good teacher, also teaches screenwriting...sometimes quite dull but good guy

PETER IS THE MAN, THE MYTH, AND THE LEGEND! I have never had so much fun in a class while constantly learning new things. This professor is clear about who he is and how his class will be. He cares DEEPLY about his students and his studies, and will be there for you to help you pass the class. Show up, PARTICIPATE in class, and have fun!
If I had to say one sentence I would say he is terrible at communicating and I didn't know my grade until a week before finals.

Extremely knowledgeable, excellent teaching methods, considerate, VERY enjoyable class!! He really cares and knows what works. In order to keep up with all the new words, follow his instructions and method. Lots of great reading, new vocabulary & there is written homework about reading matter & news. Tons learnt in this class. Highly recommend!!!
I feel like the class would be more enjoyable and easier to comprehend if we went over things that were going to be on the quiz rather then just skimming. hard grader. Homework readings every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mwalimu Ojiambo is basically the GOAT. I don't go to KU, but I took Swahili 210 with him over the summer (5 hours a day, everyday). The class was without a doubt the most enjoyable course I've ever taken. He's definitely an mgonjwa, but he is very knowledgable and deeply passionate about education. (Also, the textbook < $10)

I've taken Kiswahili courses and African studies courses (AAAS 417) from Mwalimu Ojiambo. He's an amazing professor who cares deeply about all of his students. He'll do anything to help you if you're struggling. He's also the nicest person ever and is extremely passionate about what he teaches. He's the reason I chose to minor in African Studies!
I'm taking forensic science in high school and she is one of the best teachers I've had she makes me actually want to come to school

I'm taking her class in high school, and while the assignments are tough and it's one of the hardest courses I've taken, she's a good teacher. She's passionate about her field, clearly cares about improving, and I respect that.

My reviews keep getting deleted so I'll keep it short and simple. This is the worst professor I've ever had. Brittney is rude to her students, and consistently expected us to know things we had never gone over. I have never felt more worthless than when I was in Brittney's class. I'm a good student and I dreaded going to her class, it was horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is tough, but you'll learn a lot. She shares a lot of tips for writing and research, and just skills needed to be professional. If you read the book, which is awesome and not like a textbook at all and the resources online you'll do just fine. It does take some time, but instead of spending 3hrs/day in a classroom, you just put that to reading.
OMG!!! I love Dr. Olcott, she changed my view of the world of science and also was hilarious her kids are adorable wish I could take this again!

Dr. Olcott-Marshall has worked to make this class digestible for non-science majors while remaining very useful for any STEM student, especially as an intro class. If you come to class prepared and ready to learn and participate, you'll enjoy the unconventional group assignments that actually do prepare you for the essay exams. Two thumbs up!

This class seems really easy on the surface, because when you show up and complete the in-class activities you'll get hella participation points. She basically teaches the class like we are all in seventh grade. However, she grades extremely hard on tests (which are not real tests they are take-home essay questions that you turn in via SafeAssign).

Alison knows what she's talking about but she covers too much information for one lecture. All the in class assignments and exams are short answer. If you can at least understand the main idea and explain yourself, she'll give you the points.

This class is pretty easy and if you are interested about the subject itll be pretty enjoyable for you. You can tell Alison is really into this stuff which makes it easier to pay attention in class. If you show up and do the work youll get an A no problem.
She is nice, but her class is nearly impossible. She covers way too much information for one exam. Don't buy the textbook.

No book. You don't have to go to class, because she doesn't take attendance, & all she does is read her power points out loud which you can print off online. its kind of ridiculous. She will curve because everyone does awful on her tests.
Really easy. I got a 71% in the class and ended up coming out with a B. Just study the slide and thats it.
Dont bother buying the book, you won't use it one time. She has a lot of lectures but tests aren't too bad if you go to everyclass. she is VERY helpful in office hours.
Very nice teacher, tests are nearly impossible. If you learned everything she splurges out in lectures you could write your own book on geology.

Course is not easy. Alison is a sweetheart and is willing to help but she goes through enough information in just one lecture for an entire exam's worth. She will curve because everyone does awful on her tests.

Christine is without a doubt one of my favorite professors in the art department at KU. She is incredibly caring about her students and tries her best to inspire them with artist recommendations, good critiques, and an overall positive attitude that contributes to a great class dynamic. Highly recommend taking one of her classes.

Christine truly cares about her students. The amount of effort she puts into making sure your drawing improves and that you're making something you love is astounding. I truly hope I can have her as a professor again and recommend anyone who wants true feedback and learning to take her classes.
Very interesting person! She has a very unique perspective on everything, and she is extremely passionate about teaching and drawing. Always willing to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Excellent!
Dr. Wallo is always prepared. Her lectures and classes are perfectly structured. She balances workload and timely feedback. If you take a class with her, you will learn a lot.

Dr. Wallo is passionate, knowledgeable, and diplomatic. The course load is reasonable; when a certain topic proves particularly challenging, she will allow more time to ensure full understanding of the concept (you must try, of course). An engaging language teacher (a crucial factor) who is good at what she does.

Oleksandra is a fantastic professor and really knows what she is talking about. She assigns A LOT of reading, but if you like Ukrainian history and you do the work your grade will be good. The overall workload is not too bad and it makes this class very worth the time.
She is a nice person and a good professor. She cares. Some of her classes were boring but others were fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She's pretty supportive of everyone's stories in class, no matter how bad they are, so it's tough to tell what she thinks. However, she marks up your story too and gives tons of helpful comments. Really excellent and friendly and good.
i learned more in this course than i did with all other profs combined.  she is incredible
best creative writing prof at KU.  TOTALLY, TOTALLY brilliant.  reads your stories very carefully.  take as many courses w/ her that you can.

Deb is the smartest teacher I've had, and one of the best.  I don’t know anyone else who knows or cares so much about experimental fiction.  Her intelligence would be intimidating if she wasn't so friendly--she's one of the most approachable teachers around.  Only the most untalented students dislike her.
The hottest profesor you will ever have. Not very smart.
unbelievably hott.  disappointing instructor.

All of Anne's tests are fill in the blank with no word bank and short-answer questions. She is a very tough grader, no one gets 100% on her tests. There are 5 quizzes and 5 discussions and that's it for the points besides the 2 tests and final and participation. GO TO CLASS! She does not post her notes on BB and if you don't go you will be lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a  tough professor! I think she is annoying but many people seem to like her teaching style. To each your own I guess!

Annie was a pretty good professor. Her class was not easy, she really makes you work for it. Attendance isn't mandatory, but because she does oral-based lectures, if you miss a class, you will be SO far behind. Test questions came directly from notes. Tests were difficult, but manageable, just be prepared to study heavily before them.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Annie does oral base lectures-no PP slides. Was very interesting topic and had great in class work. Quizzes and tests were a stretch because she would up her wording/specificity 10x more than what the lecture goes over. She let us earn back credit from a bad exam, but really made us work for it. I respect her work, but she is far reaching.

She's real strict.She NEVER allows you to be late for the class,and we had to buy the reading materials,which costs 20 bucks,in addition to text books. If you become her favorite student,your opinions would most likely be accepted. But if not, it might be better to say nothing.this class requires TONS of readings and presentations,so be aware.

The class is very time consuming but if you are enrolled in this type of class you should already know that you would have to spend a lot of time on it. Naima is very helpful and wants all of her students to succeed.
Unbelievably difficult, not very helpful, and a genuinly unpleasant disposition.
No Comments

Plays favorites with her students.  Says she wants to hear her students opinions but really only wants to hear opinions that agree with hers.  Lots & lots of reading.  Long papers to write.  Class was very time-consuming.

Dr. Omelicheva is great! I loved her lectures. Made my first semester at KU so much better. I took International Human Rights, and don't regret it at all! Semester was a midterm, opinion editorial, and a huge research paper. Small assignments throughout but not many. Would definitely take her again!

I had Mariya for IR Theory.  It was my first graduate course at KU.  If this had been my second year as a graduate student at KU, then my experience might have been better.  I found her to be at times rude and created a very cold and uncomfortable class atmosphere.  However, she knows her stuff and she really does develop her students.

The key to Omelicheva's class is time management. You will have a lot of work and have to spread it out or it will overwhelm you but if you do the basics (ATTEND CLASS, get key concepts from reading, turn hw in on time) you're good because, as hard and evil as the class is at times, she wants to give you an A and will try to do so.

While it appears that Omelicheva has a reputation for being rather easy as a teacher for the intro classes, it seems to change for the upper level courses. She is a very fair teacher and outlines what she wants, but do the reading for class each day and make sure to go over the presentations. If she senses that the class has slacked off, watch out.
Easiest class I've taken at KU by far.
I love Prof. Omelicheva. She is kind to students and will help you if needed. As a non-POLS major, I really enjoyed this class.

Easy, fairly interesting class. Her lectures are very boring, and she says the lecture material is different than the book but its not, you dont have to go. Class consists of online final/midterm, and 2 portfolio(3 page reports). She is very nice and helpful but certianly not a class you must attend in order to get an A. Textbook does wonders.

I had very little interest in the international side of politics before i entered this class, so that probably skews my views of the class, but I thought the class was fairly easy. The midterm and final were both online which makes them easier. She is very personable and cares about her students, but I was somewhat easily bored by the lectures.

This class was easy to a fault. During lecture, she interacted with the class, but her questions were too simple, often able to be answered with a "duh!" The lectures were not very thought provoking and lacked depth because the material was dumbed down so much. After a few lectures, I quickly lost interest in the subject. At least it's an easy A.

Great teacher, knows her stuff. Quick to answer questions via email or before/after class. Very personable. Cares about student success as long as you put forth effort. Would gladly take another class with her.
She's really helpful! She listens to what the students have to say about the class! She WILL work with you, and make concepts clearer!
No Comments

Dr Kazeem is one of the most kind and compassionate professors that I have come across at KU. Took MATH 220 with him and He made sure we understood the topics well. Homework was average but the best thing about his class was that we could take make-up exams if we didn't perform well in the first ones. Learned a lot from him. Way to go Prof Kazeem!!

He was very kind. He does expect a lot of class participation and his lectures drag on a bit. But he really just wants his students to do well and he even let me retake my exams. A little disorganized but much more empathetic than most of the other professors Ive had.
He was su

I love this man and would say he's my favorite teacher/professor of all time. The complaints about him making mistakes or not being clear are inaccurate. He is the most compassionate teacher I have ever met. He has let multiple people turn in homework late, and he allowed everyone who wanted to retake the exam. Even let me retake a retake. 100/10

I took MATH 116 with Dr. Okosun, and I would highly recommend not taking this with him. He is HIGHLY disorganized, does not respond to emails, makes mistakes during lectures and on his solutions. He will give important information shorty in class and fail to send it out in an email or announcement. He does not seem to care about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Okosun is a funny guy. His accent is cool. He's willing to answer questions and is lenient when it comes to grades. There's a quiz or homework almost every week but they are short and easy. His exams are also really short. The only bad thing is that he makes mistakes in his work sometimes. I would take another class from him if I could.

He does not know the material he teaches. He'll start an example, get lost, look to the class for help, we wont know how to do it because he hasnt taught us, and then literally give up and leave the example unfinished. He barely explains anything and mostly just copies straight from his notes which were copied from the textbook. He also gaslights!

Professor Okosun was a great teacher. He cared a lot about the success of his students. Although this class was really easy, whenever you had questions, he was always ready and willing to answer them. Overall, he was a great person, really funny, and a great teacher for college math.
My favorite teacher at KU so far. So helpful and very caring about the success of his students.

This class was very easy. During class, he goes over practice problems, and you have quizzes every Friday. There's some opportunities for extra credit as well. The syllabus says attendance is taken, but it doesn't actually count for points, and I honestly stopped going to zoom lectures halfway through the semester.

The hardest class I've had don't take unless you want to fail. Please don't waste your money on this class choose a different professor. Lectures every other day and quizzes every Friday worth 50 points( too much for no reason) Midterm and final. Two books required. If you take this class god be with you seriously.
taking his history class now.  never knew history could be so relevant.  he's way down to earth. knows his stuff.  and kind heart.  highly recommend!!!
He's currently my history tutor.  Very smart and super helpful.  I would recommend taking him as a teacher!
Mark is an as.shole. He is a mother fu.cker with no life.

Maybe a little reading and participation now and then would improve your grade in his class.  If you find the readings boring, then you've never were curious about why we believe in what we do as Americans.  I don't think you need to favor him or not, but if you didn't learn a lot in his class, then you cheated yourself.  This is YOUR education!
I love him! he's very opinionated but he encourages debates. He's very sexy

Mark is a pretty cool guy. I mean for a teacher, way down to earth and not all high on intellect. The books we are going to cover are probably not that great. Margret Thatcher naked on a cold day. Anyway next semester he has said to change things up a bit. if you are thinkin about taking this class do it. you can only walk away with ensight.
I am in this class right now and it is actually my favorite this semester.  We will see how good it goes the rest of the semester, but at least this class gives me something good to get up for.
Yes he is very liberal, but so is everyone in Lawrence. He is super helpful and he is a real nice guy.

I leave every class depressed... The class is called 'Understanding American' but it should probably be called 'Understanding How America Sucks.'  However, the class is pretty easy... a lot of reading and he doesn't give too many quizes but I wouldn't take him again...

He is a very liberal teacher. He is stuck on his own opinoins and speaks very highly of himself. There is alot of reading that is not nessecary and very boring. I would reccommend finding a different teacher for this class.

The discussions for the class appeared simple. I involved myself (as did most other kids in the class) and it came around to "journals." The fact is he grades very strict on both journals and essays, especially for a 100 course. Majority of the class got D's on the major paper. LOTS OF READING to do each night. And he brags a lot about communism.

Marilyn Ortega was probably the worst professor that I have had at KU. She often did not talk very respectful to students and did not make the class material very enjoyable. If your opinion did not match with hers, it was obvious that she was offended and it would reflect on your grades. Would not recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was one of the most frustrating classes I've taken. Guidelines for projects and papers were very vague, and there wasn't as much class discussion as I was told to expect (mainly lecturing). While Ortega did have some interesting insights on some topics, the teaching style was somewhat all over the place and the quality depended on the day.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this professor! She was brutally honest and was very responsive! You do have to read a lot for her class, but it's simple homework assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Marilyn teaches the hardest AMS 100 class that KU has to offer. While AMS 100 is normally a very easy A, this class is nearly impossible to get an A in, especially if your opinions do not coincide with Marilyn's.

As an introductory course, this professor has shown far more expectations, especially when most students feel like this class should be considered on the easier side. If you want to take this course, please do not take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you don't want to take a class where the teacher will disrespect you because of your opinions, I would not recommend this class. If you and Marilyn don't agree, be prepared to work your ass off for a good grade. She didn't upgrade grades often and when you asked her about it she would say "don't worry, you have a good grade".
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Ms. Ortega proved to be inconsistent in her expectations, structure, and grading criteria for readings and projects. Class was centered around discussion of readings. Readings and discussions were very insightful, interesting, and inspirational. However, it felt as though one must already be well-read in fem and queer theory to understand anything.
He is really nice I like him

His lectures are amazing. Make sure to note what he says, not just what's on the slides, and you'll do fine. You'll need to be able to create and defend your own opinions. My GTA was also great and most of the stuff is graded by them from my understanding, which is part of the reason I liked the class so much.

Professor Saint Onge is fantastic! Interesting lectures and discussions and he's super accessible for meetings outside of class. SOC424 is a great class for anyone interested in American healthcare. The exam questions are pretty specific, but they come straight from the slides so as long as you take good notes you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The lecture is super interesting and the tests really aren't hard if you pay attention and do the readings. Do the readings! They get brought up on the tests, but test are open note which is nice. My discussion leader was also great, I see that as a complaint on here a lot, but Saint Onge himself is awesome to learn from and talk to.
his lectures are thorough and enjoyable; good personality

Even if you dont care for sociology, he really makes the class content very relatable to the current world in an interesting way that not many other professors can. Its easy to get lost in what hes saying since he tackles very large issues, but make sure to take notes and read all thats required of you because itll all show up on exams

I dropped out of a previous sociology class because I disliked the professor and topic. I was prepared to tolerate an average class, but after the first day I was very engaged and interested in the topic. Great lectures that are applicable to life, and a very great professor. Very well spoken. Must attend lectures and pay attention to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I took SOC 160 and the class was interesting. The professor was good and the TA's are easily accessible and ready to answer all your questions. He does a good job of keeping the lectures interesting with videos and evidence.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Favorite professor at KU. His class is by far my favorite class I have taken and the material is very interesting. He's a really good lecturer and I loved going to his class. He is a very caring and understanding professor. If you have the chance to take one of his classes I would. Class was made up of papers, tests and attendance. Not hard though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Saint Onge was AMAZING! The course itself was very interesting, but he took it to another level. He was always enthusiastic, ready to answer questions (in or out of class), and of course, well-versed in all things sociology. He cared about the well-being of his students too. The discussion sections were hit or miss (TA wise).
He was one of my professors all throughout college! He is very neutral politically which was super nice. Very easy to listen to in lectures. If you do the readings and listen in class its easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's got mad skillz
Hearing from Dr. Saint Onge really gave me so much appreciated for the field of sociology. He made me want to learn and his topics were very interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor that makes lecture funny and easy to learn. There are articles and a few small books to read, but it's not bad at all. Exams are based on lectures and articles that we read and the papers we write are two pages MAX. If you put in an average amount of effort into the class theres no reason to get below a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took this class to fulfill a KU core, would I take it again? No. He talks a lot and goes off slides, but sometimes I find him vague. You also need to pay attention and go to discussions or else you won't pass. You might also have to ask questions if you don't understand something. I will not be taking a SOC class again for personal reasons.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: I love professor Saint Onge, he is by far the best professor I've had at KU. He is kind, respectful, and willing to work with any student. More than anything he is very passionate about healthcare and inequalities in society. He makes you think and encourages conversation at all times. I would encourage everyone to take a class from him.

The lectures were actually really interesting. You do have to answer questions online during class, but if you just get a friend to text you the daily code and you keep your laptop open during class time and put random responses when questions come up, then you don't have to go to class.

The largest part of this class is the two readings assigned every week. If you read those early on and take good notes, then the class isn't that difficult. For the lectures, pay attention, stave off distractions, because you will regret missing notes. And *all* the test questions are directly from the lecture material and the readings. Fair class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Jarron Saint Onge is great! He sincerely cares for his students and is so passionate about the topic he is teaching. He was organized and used very relevant articles and resources in his lectures and reading selections. This class did not use a textbook so careful note taking was required, but lectures were interesting. Happy I took this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great guy in general and cares about his teaching. Lot of reading to do if you truly want to know everything that could come up on a test. The TA you get may make or break your experience.

Saint-Onge is a great guy. He seems very passionate about his lectures and the material is pretty interesting. The biggest downfall is that he says he just wants us to understand the "big picture" or "overall trend," and yet his test questions are ridiculously specific. The TAs make the exams and do all of the grading. They're VERY tough graders.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor was great but the gta ruined my experience. Discussion was a complete waste of time and no grades were entered until almost April. Class was interesting, but there was a lot of information to take in. Having a better GTA and useful discussion would have been beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Saint Onge is by far one of the best professors I've had at KU. He has a lot of respect for his students and it shows. He's funny and witty and knows a lot about the subject of medicine. Discussions in class are where you'll learn the most. Overall, an awesome professor. Semi-easy tests if you participate! Definitely recommend his classes.

Professor Saint Onge was one of the most dynamic teachers I have ever had. He made the lectures so interesting and made me love the class. It is hard but use the study guides to study for the test and it will be easier

Great likable respected professor. Lots of papers. Makes you read 3 sociological books. No textbook  must attend every class. Write detailed notes, not just PowerPoint. Will curve. You'll learn a lot.

Thought this class would be easy, yeah no. Good topics, but doesn't put power points online which make it hard sometimes if your confused and want to double check. Alexander Myer is a bad TA so don't get him. Tests can be difficult, study the jeopardy, read books, know articles, anything is fair game. Go to class they take attendance.

Dr. Saint Onge is hands down my favorite professor at KU. I had him first semester of my freshman year and his social problems and american values class had a huge impact on the career path I am taking. Very inspiring.
I heart this professor.  Funny.  Friendly.  Excited about the material.  Consistent.  One of the best I've had.

Saint Onge is one of the best at KU! Very engaging and interested in Sociology. Class consists of a lot of discussion and was very interesting. He made going to class enjoyable. Work load wasn't too hard, and tests were mainly from the lectures and class discussion. Super helpful if you meet with him outside class and always willing to help

Saint Onge is an Awesome professor! I loved both SOC160 and SOC 624 which I took from him. He is very helpful and clear in his lectures! He really loves sociology and it reflects in his teaching. The tests are mostly from the lecture so while class isnt mandatory, going to class will really benefit you!He makes and effort to learn everyones names!

Dr. Orive taught Genetics with Dr. Holder and did the math & statistics side. She went so fast on the math and offered few examples. The tests she wrote were the hardest of the class. She is a nice lady and really smart but is just not good at teaching the material.
Dr. Orive talks way too fast. She does not explain material in a way that is able to be understood. If possible take Dr. Holder.

Dr. Orive's lecture style is very directly fact oriented, which can make things difficult for students that learn more through analogies. She does teach rather quickly, but she is very helpful during her office hours.
She talks a mile a minute.  I could never keep up.  She tries to be nice and help out, but she tries too hard.
Lectures can go a little fast, but she's very helpful and explains things well outside of class.
High standards for herself and for us. Passionate about her subject, very articulate speaker. Come prepared and you will do well. If you want to slack, look elsewhere. Bring your A game!

The thing about Orive is that she is just doesn't know how to explain things. She's brilliant, but cannot present the information in a way that is truly comprehensible. A VERY picky grader, and the tests are not easy. The TAs will end up being more helpful than she will be.

Talks way too fast and test this year covered almost 2X as much as the previous year, given old tests, questions for them were very easier which is ridiculous when everyones GPA is looked at by graduate schools, etc. just the same.
nice and willing to help.

Dr. Orive was a great teacher! The class was defintely tough and a lot of studying was required to do well, but she was very easy to follow and seemed extremely excited to be teaching. It was a hard class, but I loved it!
Dr. Orive definitely forces you to study to do well.  She separates the ambitious from the lazy. I think those unable to handle the material may have be better off in the nursing program.

Dr. Orive is a genius. She teaches fast and expects students to study(go figure). There was excessive whining from some of my classmates, but that is probably due to their laziness, not her quality of teaching.
No Comments
No Comments
Totally unavailable - she must be doing research or something.  Incredibly smart person.  I feel she would be happier doing field work or research rather than teach.
I would disagree with the other rating 100%.  This was a terrible class and she was a terrible teacher to boot. It's not tough at all, but just annoying. Why is genetics so terrible @ KU?
What can I say?  This is a TOUGH class.  People whine too much, because they want to be doctors and not work at it.  But I learned a lot.

Dr. Ordner was clearly passionate about sociology and liked teaching a small class, which kept the class engaging. He let class out early 90% of the time and the quizzes were mostly just definitions. It's an easy a, making it a good option if you just want the KU core credit. But it's nothing you can't learn from reading the news every so often.

Dr. Ordner took what seems like a difficult subject and broke it up into easier concepts to understand. Class is an hour and 15 minutes yet we usually get out about 30-45 minutes early. No homework, just weekly quizzes. Quizzes are easy if you attend lecture (answers come straight from notes). You get one free absence, other than that you MUST come
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: James is an awesome professor. Doesn't believe in tests so you take quizzes every week instead. The quizzes were super easy and never really had to do the reading to pass the quizzes because he sent out study guides for every quiz. Hardly every lectures. We did group work 99% of the time. He's passionate and the course material was interesting

James doesn't believe in formal or cumulative exams, instead you take a quiz almost every week to go over what you have learned. He will send out a study guide of what will be on the test so you know exactaly what to study! He does not try to trick you and will help you with anything you need! Over all, was a great class and an amazing professor!
I wouldn't call her an "easy" grader, but you can get a decent grade if you take the class seriously. She's great at leading interesting discussions.

Ashley was one of the best English teacher's I have had thus far and best teacher I've had at KU thus far. To explain how fun she kept class, she came in one day with pink hair. She rarely used the textbook and does not grade on grammer but content. Def take her.
She is. Really nice and an easy grader. She doesn't grade work based on grimmer but on content and keeps class interesting. If your looking for a great teacher go for Ashley.

Dr. Osborn is INCREDIBLY rude and dissmissive of his students. His class is easy, but only because the material is simple to comprehend. I feel sorry for everyone that has to take it. He explains the subject as convoluted as possible while also answering 0 questions clearly. Any other prof could do his job better with less of an attitude problem

Super chill guy with a lot of knowledge in his field. The group projects are really tough but there are only a few. If you show up to class and do the work you will succeed, but that's easier said than done when the class is at 8 am. Follow the master schedule! Lock in! You got this!

Osborn's teachings are less classically focused. However, it is still a serious class. The projects are very difficult which is something to keep in mind. You get ONE WEEK to write, record, produce, and make a music video for a song with 4 other people. He is very understanding if you help as long as you put good effort into the class.

Brad's a cool person but maybe not as good a teacher. He doesn't bother to learn names, even though there were only 40 of us in his class. He gave three quizzes and assigned three papers plus a final project. The quizzes are easy if you show up to class & can identify the music he plays in class. The rest of the grading was incredibly subjective.

He's a very nice guy, and the lectures were immersive and entertaining. Unfortunately, I learned the hard way that he is TERRIBLE at checking emails and communicating, which caused major issues down the line. He is unstructured, as others have said, and took a very long time to grade important assignments.

The grade I recieved was a fair representation of my final work however he is very unstructured. We had one essay within the first 3 mo. and then another 2 crammed within the mo. of finals. Lectures are entertaining; he is very passionate about the literature. Ultimately I feel I didn't have any opportunity to grow or get the grade I wanted.

Professor Outka is laid back but expects serious work. He'll work with you outside of class but you need to be your own advocate. For fall 2023, we had weekly reading responses and one 20 page final paper. Like others have mentioned, you need strong time management and self-direction for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This man was SO unstructured. We had 1 essay during the first 3 months of semester and that was it. Out of the blue he gives us 2 essays and tells us there will be a final right before finals week. You will write difficult essays. If you don't do well without an organized environment I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Paul Outka is the best professor I've ever had, and the only good one I've taken thus far in the English department. Well-read, erudite, and hilarious, Professor Outka gives thoughtful, engaging lectures on very interesting, difficult topics. He's the best -- take him every chance you can!

one of the best professors I have had, he is very emotional when talking about Dickinson and Whitman. He really cares about your views and opinions about the poems. if you come to his office hours he will help you with understanding the material. you will probably write long essays. he is funny, sometimes gets too excited over literature.

Really nice guy. Was always available outside of class and answered emails quickly. You need to talk in class if you want to get a good grade. For papers, if you go to him before you start writing, he'll basically tell you what to write to get an A. Gets off topic pretty easily but encourages healthy and interesting conversation on most topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: It was a lot of reading, participation heavy, with the grade resting on two essays and a final exam, which was essay based as well. Overall, a really interesting experience if you put in the work, like poetry, and do well on written essays and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the very definition of an kind, eccentric genius - emphasis on the genius. i found myself just writing random quotes down that he said because i didn't want to forget them, he was that wise about his subject and life. he wants you to do well, and definitely makes you want to do well for yourself in turn. one of my favorite professors of all time.

Paul Outka is one of the most fantastic teachers I have ever had in my life. His classes are generally all centered around discussion if you read, participate, and engage, you will get exponentially more out of the class. He is a quirky, hilarious, absolutely brilliant mess of a man and I recommend every class he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Sweet, weird guy. Grading system is nebulous. If you are a good writer & can analyze text w/o doing the readings, you can get away with minimal effort. Don't half-ass papers; he will help you outline them in office hours. Did not realize that a white dude in my class was recycling my points in discussion immediately after I said them EVERY DAY :(
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Extremely passionate and knowledgeable about his subject. His lectures are all incredibly interesting and informative. Spends a ton of time outside class helping students with their papers and writing detailed feedback. Theres a ton of reading and he expects a lot from papers but its worth it.
one of the best teachers i've ever had.

He's a funny guy and pretty receptive to opinions that differ from his own, often playing devil's advocate. He knows when you didn't do the reading, though. It's somehow more embarrassing that you have to participate and if you didn't read you still have to contribute. Basically, read or skim the reading and it's all easy going.

Dr. Outka is a quirky dude teaching a quirky class. The class is generally fun but is also incredibly challenging. If you don't have a deep interest in poetry, don't take his class. If you enjoy it however, you're in for a real treat.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: While he is very passionate about the subject matter, class consists mostly of him talking. He rarely asks questions/engages the class. Paper topics are vague and the readings often seem pointless. Very rarely responds to e-mails, regardless of their importance.
Almost all his classes are just discussion, however it's important to show up because these discussions will help you write essays later on. He's very engaging and makes the class go by fast.

Dr. Outka's class on poetry changed my life. He is always there to help you better understand the material, and once you feel a connection to these poets, it is difficult not to enjoy the course. Homework is bearable but the essays will consume your life until you finish them, but you'll enjoy the pain. Best class I've taken yet.
