Mr. Naderi is the real deal!  He is super passionate and smart (we barely used the textbook).  I'm really going to miss his class.

Great teacher, discussions were easy to follow, but also really interesting. Lectures were never dry, and tests are very doable as long as you come to class everyday and take notes on the power points. I recommend this class and teacher!!
Makes class interesting and seems like he knows what he's talking about.
Was a discussion leader for David Smith. Did great, and even if he was a complete idiot, its ok by me. He is simply gorgeous!

Professor Pultz is definitely enthusiastic about Art and it shows in class, this Covid-19 online semester we only had 3 test and two papers which made my grades fluctuate a lot. Over all the TA's and Professor Pultz were all accessible outside of class and they give good feedback, I would take again if it was not all online like this semester was.
Gives incredible lectures and makes great connections

Pultz is amazing. I see everyone complaining about his teaching style, but I wish all were like him! He gives the most informative and engaging lectures. He asks you think and participate with his lecture, making each class really unique to the students' feedback. Titles to works ARE included on the sheets he hands out in the beginning of class.
really loves his subject, wants students to learn

Professor Pultz may not be the best at giving a lecture but he loves his job and is willing to admit when he is wrong and give extensions on papers and even tests. His main goal is to help you get the best grade possible even if it means giving you two options for taking your final or giving extensions on papers.

Pultz is a good instructor who knows his stuff. His teaching style is different than most and took me a bit of time to get used to. You can tell he really cares about what he is teaching as he can get behind on lectures when talking about an intriguing work of art.

Pultz is engaging, intelligent, and an extremely eloquent speaker. He provides you with all the information you need for tests in lectures. He is my favorite professor in this dept and I can't wait to take another class from him. His class prompted me to major in art history.

Love Pultz. He does tend to be a bit frenetic at times and go off on tangents, but they still feel relevant, or are at least humorous. His style of teaching is interactive, engaging, and really makes you work to learn the material. Don't buy the main textbook.

Pultz seems cool, but I hate his style of teaching.  He doesn't give titles of work which makes it hard to follow in notes unless you have the preposted list (past few times they haven't been posted). Maybe I'm not great with the subject, but I just do not follow what he says.

Awful. Outdated way of lecturing, didn't know anything about the subject (he even admitted that at the beginning of the semester), gets off on useless tangents, and puts way too much information in his lectures. It's impossible to take notes. My GTA (Jarryd Page) was 100 times better at teaching than Pultz is. He needs to retire, seriously.
Talks fast. crams a lot into one lecture

During lectures he often closes his eyes and tenses his forehead to think outloud. You can tell he is very passionate about the subject, and keeps it interesting. Doing the readings and attending class will make the papers and tests a breeze. There are 2 tests (75% essay 25% slide ID) and 2 papers. I would recommend this class to any HA student.
He was really interesting and funny. He had a lot of energy. He doesn't grade over memorization, he grades on essays to see if you get the overall picture of what you're studying.
quirky, passionate professor who is interested in helping his students and teaching courses they want covered. Not afraid to cover controversial topics.
I hear one more word about phallic symbols or his wife's breat-feeding practices, I'm gonna puke.  His knowledge of photography is excellent, but he shares way too much about his personal obsessions.
He is very monotone and often the material is very hard to understand since he doesn't do the best at explaining.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Boring lectures and pointless homework activities. Doesn't know how to put grades on Blackboard, so I've been in the dark about my grade the entire semester. Talks above our heads and expects us to do ridiculous assignments. Don't take this course.

Prof Pye was very knowledgable.  My only complaint was that he would sometimes talk above my linguistic level, but he was never that hard to understand.  If you have questions he is always available through e-mail or office hours.

Pye may be knowledgeable about semantics, but he can't teach it. He favors a "throw the baby into the pool and see if it swims" style of teaching, and his lectures are unhelpful. Also, he drastically changed the syllabus and how grades were determined halfway through the semester.

While definitely knowledgeable about the subject matter, his ability to communicate the material in any meaningful way is pretty much non-existent.  Semantics is already dry, but Pye is some soporific.
No Comments

If you can avoid taking this guys class, do it. Purna had two guest lecturers this semester and honestly I think I learned more from them than I had himself the entire semester. I stopped going to lecture because I sincerely could not understand a word he was saying AND on top of that he would yell at the class because when we didn't know an answer

Dr. Purna was super compassionate when it came to extensions. While teaching he would always pause to make sure everything was understood. He's one of the best professors I've ever had at KU. The homework, quizzes, and exams are all online on Webassign. Would take again!

He is probably one of the best professors I've ever had at the University of Kansas. He is so funny and so genuine about his teaching. He cares a lot about his students and everything is online. if you want a good laugh during lecture definitely take his class.

Dr. Purna was one of the nicest professors that I have ever had. He was always telling jokes and making sure that we understood the material. He gave lots of advice throughout the semester. His tests and homework assignments are online and correspond to each other. He is one of the funniest professors I have ever had! Would definitely take again!

Unorganized and inconsiderate. Went through three periods' of content in one class (reads off slides to teach math which isn't great for note-taking), yet when asked to slow down, blatantly said no. Pushes deadlines after the previous deadline already passed of his own volition, then pretends it's because we complained. Unhelpful syllabus/lecture.

Most disorganized class I've ever taken, he yelled at us a lot which was pretty funny but exhausting after a while. Changed his mind a lot on exams and homework and I never knew my grade in the class. He seems to value working together with the class on theorems/problems to give a thorough understanding, but it was just never executed well at all.

Your course will essentially just be online. He makes you use WebAssign for all homework and exams... Despite this, first two class exam averages were still 50's/60's. You'll learn linear algebra pretty okay from Webassign but nothing from lectures. Will ask a room of engineers to prove random stuff. WebAssign is good tho even if it's $$

Purna is not the best prof. He changes his mind frequently about the exams and homework and nothing is clear. He told us our final would be take-home then during finals week he changed his mind and gave us a 2 day heads up. All the HW/exams/quizzes are on WebAssign and if you enter the answers wrong formatting-wise, you won't get points back.
Unorganized and not helpful. Never kept grades in a visible gradebook and only gave limited information regarding homework and the final.

Professor Purna is a very friendly and seems to want his students to do well. He does lecture straight out of the book, but in my opinion keeps the class interesting. The class is unorganized at times, including pacing, test dates, and homework due dates. Although I really enjoyed him as a professor and would recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Purna is not a good teacher. While his lectures are identical to what is in the book, the book is wordy and hard to comprehend. He is also a poor lecturer and his voice tends to get louder and louder as it becomes more obvious the class does not know what is happening. Also aggravating that friends with other teachers learned nothing similar
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Purna is just not a good teacher. I believe he probably has a meaningful contribution to the university in the area of research. He refused to release test averages because he was too embarrassed to be associated with them. The most aggravating part was that other students got better grades in the same class because they had easier professors.

Purna is an funny and caring guy. His lectures are just copied word-for-word out of the book, with some of his odd humor thrown in. He loathes technology, so aside from personal emails, he will not communicate any class info online. I.e., you must attend every single lecture to get the homework assignments and know what material is being covered.

He literally just copies everything that's in the book for his lecture. He only assigns homework in class at the very end of class, which caused me to be late to my class after. He goes through material VERY slow. The other classes were 2 full chapters ahead of us by the end of the year. Somehow ended up with a B despite failing a test.

I liked his teaching style. Instead of just lecturing us, he would usually write the theorem on the board and then guide us as the class tried to prove it. He has a funny sense of humor and made the class interesting. Test problems weren't hard, but he grades pretty harshly. Also, he's pretty disorganized with test dates and the pace fluctuated.

He is really a terrible teacher. He pretty much reads his lessons directly from the book so his class is pretty much pointless except that he doesn't post the homework online so you have to get it in class. His homework is unnecessarily tedious and the tests don't match up with the material very well. Overall he is lazy and uncaring.

Purna is a show to see (very entertaining). He isn't the most clear teacher and often focuses on proofs which students aren't used to. The homeworks can be long and often contain a proof, but it's only due once a week. Overall a pretty easy class, plus the tests and final were a joke and he can easily be talked into postponing them.

Purnaprajna (called Purna) is a pretty good teacher. He's a very, very funny guy, and enjoys getting to know his students. His homework is difficult, though, and is often very long. He is the only math teacher that I have ever encountered (as an engineering major) that puts proofs on his homework and tests. Tests were difficult, final was easy.

Not helpful. Hard to understand. Gives tons of homework problems and grade 2 or 3, so if you struggle on one you can fail the whole assignment. Leaves lectures frequently to make personal calls and expects you to stay through them
very difficult to understand therefore very easy to get lost, a math teacher that doesnt know english as a first language is pointless
Applied a great deal of pressure on students in-class answers

Overall, he's a great professor. He's willing to work with his students and to answer questions. He does believe in meditation ("go home and meditate" on the theorem of the day) and class participation. He's also crazy in a fun way. Whenever the class kind of dozed off, he'd always wish for swings in class so that we could grab them and swing.
He did not teach very well. Going to class was not necessary. I did not like him overall, I learned absolutely nothing from this class but still got an A.
ABSOLUTLY HALARIOUS! make sure everyone understands everything, really tries to help us out and make us smile. An over all AWESOME teacher and person
No Comments

I had her for ECON 526 and 522 (econometrics and macro) and she was above average for your typical ECON teacher. She is very understanding, always emails back timely, and can always meet with you outside class. I would recommend going to class because she does print out notes where you fill in the blanks which helps with tests. Her tests are tough.
Awesome teacher

Great teacher but her class is TOUGH! Explains the concepts well but it will take lots of studying outside of class. Tests are very long because she expects you to know the material well enough to give an answer without having to sit and think about it. You learn alot in her class but its NOT an easy "A"...very helpful during office hrs.

Taught to the material. Go to class, take notes, do practice tests and go to office hours (if you dont get the material) and you will do fine.  Pretty easy and her practice tests do a great job of prepping you for the big tests as the questions on the test are similar.  The students in this class are like zombies though..why even go? ps- she is HOT

Class wasn't that bad if you go and take notes. Do the homework, and make sure you look at the practice exams, they are the exact same as the real exams. You don't need the book if you come to class, which isn't bad either because she is super hot.

This class is pretty hard. The concepts are so broad and Pym doesn't do the greatest job explaining them. She does, however, definitely boost your grade if you go see her in office hours and she's a completely different teacher one-on-one, that's really the only way of making it through this class. There are 4 difficult tests and some homework.

She is such an awful teacher. Please take my advice and don't take her class. You can tell she's smart, but she can't explain the concepts well at all.  Going to class puts you to sleep, especially because she doesn't like to answer questions. I think she's a nice person, but she needs to choose a different profession. Avoid her class.

Fine professor. Her presence is uplifting, and it seems she's always willing to help students - more than most. My experience is Historian's Craft, so perhaps she was more gentle on the students; overall it seems like she cared a lot. Lectures, however, can be jumbled, and class organisation can begin to make little sense as the semester goes on.
Loves her students and only gave out like 5 assignments all semester. Take for an easy elective.

No tests, 3 total assignments that are essentially completion this is probably the easiest class at KU. There's weekly readings but there's no quizzes over them so... Full attendance points if you attend 80% of classes. Rachel makes the lectures interesting and is definitely entertaining to listen to.
Great choice for US culture class. Super easy and very little work. Attendance is graded, but you can miss a couple. No exams and two easy papers. Highly recommend.

Professor Schwaller is the GOAT, and anyone who says otherwise is clearly not confronting something within themselves. Class is super easy; almost everything is based on completion. Saying something like "I had to take this class for credit" would be a disservice, as I had the opportunity and privilege to take this class with a fantastic professor.

I took this class to fulfill my U.S culture credit. The professor has clear instructions and is not strict in the slightest. There were no exams besides the final, and no homework besides a once-a-month discussion board response. However, attendance is mandatory because you don't get a grade otherwise. Great professor either way!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Schwaller is a teacher who you can tell cares about her students. While attendance is mandatory, she allows a few misses and it very lenient on attendance. It's a lot of talking and reading, but nothing too crazy, definitely an easy A.

She is an amazing professor who cares about her students. She makes it very clear that it is ok to miss class if you are sick or need a mental health day. There are readings and discussions each week but these are not graded. There are not many assignments and it is a very laid-back class. She is good at introducing and explaining topics.

The work is primarily student-led as you choose a topic related to the course and present your work to others as speeches which you are graded on. Dr. Schwaller was one of my favorite professors and was genuinely excited in whatever topic a student was working on and supported them even if they shifted ideas last second.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's very clearly passionate about what she does. She wants people to participate and is very engaging and supportive of those that do.

Best professor I've ever had. You can tell they care about their work and their students. The lectures were entertaining and impactful. Made a 'boring' subject interesting. Very funny, connected to students. The best.

Professor Schwaller is very understanding, flexible, and respectful of her students. It is very easy to understand the assignments and what is expected of you. If you go to class and participate in discussions, assignments and papers are light work with large impacts. Get ready to look at the world in a new way

Very understanding and works with her students. Truly my favorite teacher I've ever had at KU. Her lectures are exciting and were literally the highlight of my day. Not too many assignments either, so when scheduled one, she makes sure to provide you with all the tools necessary for an A.

She was absolutely wonderful, easy to contact, and very kind. She gave extensions when needed and didn't have much busy work. The lectures were very interesting and more discussion based than just lectures. The grading criteria were very fair and well explained. Meeting with her once per project was required but very helpful and informational.

Definitely one of the best classes to take on campus. Schwaller is super caring and works well with her students regarding deadlines, homework, and attendance. Attendance is not mandatory and homework is next to nothing. I would recommend taking this class if you want a stress-free course but also engaging.

Professor Schwaller is one of the most caring and intelligent professors I have ever taken a course with. She is very understanding and cares about each of her students. Lectures are always very informative and engaging but not mandatory to attend. There is about 1 reading every 4 weeks and are never hard to understand or dissect.
gives great, engaging lectures that keep you entertained but you also learn a ton. Super easy to work with on accommodations and easy to get ahold of.

Dr. Schwaller is really passionate about what she teachers and that's very easy to see from her lectures. For this course, there was one day a week of lecture and the other day was spent discussing reading. Graded by a few assignments throughout the semester, this was an easy course and I'll be taking more with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Schwaller did not disappoint -- This was my second class with her. She was very understanding during the pandemic and promised that no one would fail the class. The class was easygoing but she also made a strong effort to keep it engaging, which it was. Easy yet informative class and a fantastic teacher. Don't hesitate to take a class with her!

I LOVE THIS PROFESSOR! She is very understanding and will make sure students are provided with feedback. She responds within a decent amount of time and is respectful to her students. She sends out weekly reminders and announces what's due at the end of the week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Schwaller is SO understanding and flexible, especially during the pandemic. Her lectures are engaging and she's very knowledgeable in the field.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: WHAT A LOVELY PROFESSOR! She was so kind during COVID, and still managed to make the class interesting and accessible for all students. It was an interesting class, and her lectures are wonderful

In this class I expected to be learning about the different types of religion in America, as it was a Religion in America class. However, this was not the case. It was more of a history class, something I am not a fan of. Her lectures were boring to me. A lot of readings, but you can get away without reading them. Only 6 grades total, all essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class and professor was amazing! Very engaging lectures and readings. Rachel really loves what she's teaching, which is what makes her such a great teacher.

For my first semester of college, I wanted to try out a course outside of my major. Dr. Schwaller was fantastic. She is clearly passionate about what she teaches and made the class interesting. The course material was sometimes difficult to comprehend but she would review concepts and made sure people understood. Very glad I took this class.

This has probably been one of the most challenging but amazing and inspirational classes I've taken so far at KU. Rachel's lectures are so fascinating and really help you open up your eyes to different perspectives. Beware, there are a lot of readings, but she walks you through each one, that really helps you hone your critical thinking skills!!!!

WONDERFUL TEACHER, very inspirational and it's obvious that she is very passionate about what she teaches. Very interesting topics. Readings may sometimes be slightly difficult and or moderately long, but she gives solid analyses (although make sure that you pay attention during class b/c active learning is very important). Couldn't recommend more!

Professor Schwaller is the best professor I've had at KU. Her PCS 120 class makes you question a lot of your assumptions about peace and social movements. There is some reading, but she always explains it and it's never more than 15 pages. There's also not a textbook. Super funny and engaging! Take her class if you get the chance!

Made an account on this literally only because she is 1 of the best profs Ive ever had. Gonna second what most of the positive reviews say, SUPER ENGAGING. There is a decent bit of reading BUT for PCS120 a text book was  NOT required & none of the weekly readings went over 60 pages. Very caring and is willing 2 offer extra credit if u talk 2 her!!

Rachel's Lectures are so good that you won't mind dragging yourself to an early morning class to hear them. Grade consisted of two big papers using what we had learned- and participation.  She is hilarious, brilliant, and genuinely cares about every student. I would take her class again in a heartbeat.

Rachel is super cool, and a great teacher. She cares about her work and her teaching, and will help you whenever needed. Lots of reading in this class though, but if you read and participate you will get a good grade.

Professor Schwaller approaches a classroom with a fresh and engaging attitude, she respects and cares about her students and the topics, and is willing to show her own humanity. The classroom is reversed, so be prepared for lots of reading outside of class. It's definitely worth it though! Pllus she included Key & Peele in her lecture once!

Very intelligent and friendly professor. Class is pretty easy overall. There's a decent amount of reading, but you don't even have to do most of it. Got A's on all papers and exams wout reading 90% of the time. However, she has very high standards for participation, so make sure you attend and be ready to participate often.
Engaging lectures. Very helpful. Adorably cute.
Rachel is an excellent teacher, but if you miss two of the worksheets or journals your grade will suffer. Just make sure to do your readings and journals and you're all set!
Professor Schwaller is a very engaging instructor who really wants her students to succeed. If you get a chance, take a class with her.

Dr. Taghavi is an amazing professor, and even better person. His knowledge is vast and his experience in the aerospace industry is unmatched. His lectures are hilarious, he is a laid back and genuinely cares about his students. Make sure to ask him lots of questions and pay attention to the stories he tells you can learn a lot from him.

“Easy 'A' Ray” is no more. AE445 was disorganized and frustrating—not due to the material, but poor instruction. Lectures were repeated and irrelevant to exams, homework never posted, and a surprise quiz outweighed exams. Taghavi seemed confused and didn't coordinate with TAs at all. Avoid if possible. HWs never graded in time for exams either.

Homework after every class. Nicest professor ever. Lectures are good and easy to understand. The biggest problem is lectures feel repeated most times. A monday lecture will basically be regurgitated for 30 minutes on wednesday before new material is covered.

It's not Taghavi that I really have an issue with, it's the TAs. Takes a literal month to grade things. It's 50/50 on whether or not you'll get a response. I understand they have other things going on, but it's pretty annoying since it happens so often. Taghavi is nice but lectures could be better since he's pretty much reading out of the textbook.

Lectures run a little long/are a bit drawn out, but the class is still good and enjoyable. There is homework after each class which is 3 times per week, but the homework usually does not take too long so it is not a horrible time commitment. Overall, he is a really nice and considerate professor that cares about his students.

This is a professor who wants you to succeed, and if you put in the time and effort, you will. I received a poor grade in the course, but that was due to me not putting in the amount of time I should have. He makes the content clear with plenty of examples and helps guide you through problems if you have them. I highly respect this professor.

Dr. Taghavi is one of the professors I respect the most at KU. No matter when you see him, he is always positive and willing to help. I did not put as much time or effort into his course as I should have, but I still feel like I learned a lot, and would gladly take a course from him again.
Love taghavi. This man is a legend. The only good professor in the AE department-cherish this man.

Best professor I have had. I don't go to KU but I took this class over summer to transfer back to my school and I loved him. I have never gotten above a B+ in an aero course until this class. He is so nice and so patient and helpful. I wish he taught at my school. It was less than a month long course but I learned so much. Take him if you can.
Amazing!

Dr Ray is my most favorite professor till now. His lectures are super easy, interesting and he even cracks jokes! He understands the students too well, will inspire you even you are doing really bad and will give really good suggestions. He is my professor and advisor, so trust me, I am talking from first hand experience.

Dr. Taghavi is one of the most well respected, and well liked, professors at KU. He goes over all information a number of times, so there is little chance that anyone will get left behind knowledge-wise. Exams and homework are clear cut and easy to do good on as long as you pay attention in class.

This man is a gift from God himself. His class was always very interesting and he makes you want to care about the material. Went from 0 understanding on how rocketry works, to coding an entire analysis on a Rocket engine and understanding every single part of it. Challenging class, but extremely fulfilling.

Ray is a genuinely nice guy. He cares about his teaching and his students. AE345 was a very easy class IMO, made hard only by the fact that to avoid getting an A- you need a 95%+. The tests were very easy considering the content. You should get away with at least an A- if you do all your home works and work hard to understand what you are doing.
Trys to make a difficult subject comprehensive. Accommodating. Hands-on experience. Pay attention during lecture and youll do fine on the quizzes and tests.
If you show up to every lecture and do the homework, youll be fine.

By FAR one of the best profs I've had! He makes everything completely understandable & is very patient with slow learners. He made a 4-week, 3 hours a day, everyday class enjoyable! He gives announced "pop" quizzes and there's always hw, but its totally doable! Test problems are from the hw. Gives lots of EC, too.. There's no way to not get an A.

Taghavi is easily the best professor in the department. He actually cares about his students, has a lot of personality, and he doesn't make his tests or homework god awful and difficult like his workers enjoy doing. Just pay attention to what he says in lectures, and you'll do fine on the tests. The project is very fun, but it can be time consuming

Dr. Taghavi is hands down the best engineering professor I've had thus far. Tests, quizzes, and homework are all fair and doable, the stress level is manageable, and his lectures are funny and engaging.

Dr. Taghavi is hands down the best teacher that I have ever had at KU. His lectures are fun, and engaging, and his homework is appropriately challenging, as well as the test. He is a really funny guy, and you'll be disappinted if you miss a lecture just because he is so entertaining. His tests aren't very difficult. I would highly recommend him.

Took fluid mechanics during the summer and expected the worst. On the contrary, Dr. Taghavi is a fantastic instructor and makes the material extremely easy with clear explanations. The textbook was mandatory-but-not-really, in most cases he handed out copies of the problems. Definitely would recommend the AE section of fluids.
Taghavi is just awesome! I thoroughly enjoyed this class as well as 345, 445, and 5711
Great Professor! Conveys both academic and industry application importance of concepts in a meaningful way!

Great professor. Tries his very best to ensure you understand. Go to him whenever you have questions cuz he is more than eager to help you and will definitely explain things to you. Shouldn't be too difficult to ace his class.
Very Very good teacher. Loved his class. Tests are all basically from the homework. Very highly recommended.
Awesome man.  I took this class in the summer to meet an ME requirement, and didn't miss a single session.  This guy knows his stuff, and knows how to teach it.  Very fair grader as well.  Must take!

Explainations are always clear, he knows how to teach, and classes were never boring. He is an extremely good adviser too, he will never say he is busy if u want to talk about class or school, even if he actually is.
Good teacher, always helps with hw, interesting class
I loved her, she is so nice.

Professor Reiff made what could be a very dry and boring subject into a fun class that I wanted to attend. The discussions were thoughtful and inspiring. It was easy to get lost if the readings werent done before class, so those are crucial. She gave amazing feedback on papers and she made her office hours fun. Again, shes an amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's super helpful and passionate about what she teaches. We only had 4 papers over the whole semester which are spaced out well. She gives TONS of helpful feedback and also offers revisions for better grades on papers. Attendance is pretty important because we have daily class activities for points. I'd take another class with her!
Dr Reiff is an amazing and respectful teacher who makes her students to find their own interests and write about it. She is supportive and generous.

Dr. Reiff is big on group work and in class activities so class attendance is a must if you want a good participation grade (15% of the course). She is very clear in what she expects and is always there for you. Always do revisions and participate in group revisions and you will easily pass. Also, meeting with her helps if there is confusion.
Amazing professor!! She was always ready to help when we had questions, and her lectures were very engaging and I felt as though I learned a lot from her.

Professor Whelan has engaging lectures with fun demos almost every week. There are usually weekly quizzes on Fridays to ensure you're attending the lectures and following what's happening in class. She also holds weekly discussions, and I highly recommend attending these if you want to do your best.

I really enjoyed professor Whelan's class (Chem 175), as she was very accessible outside of class in order to ask questions about homework assignments, or go over previous quiz questions, as well as the demonstrations that she would do in class to show what we had learned.

Dr. Whelan was a great professor she really cared about her students she has quizzes every Friday but they are short and mostly comprehensive. Has review nights before a tests which helped a lot, her lectures were very helpful and clear.

This professor was amazing!!!! She did everything to help you pass especially outside of the classroom. Really kept the tests to the point with no curveball answers. She was so nice and caring and loved helping students.

Dr. Whelan is very kind and clearly cares about her students and their success. I really enjoyed her class. The only drawback was short quizzes every Friday. If you read the textbook and attend lectures, you will do well in this class.

Professor Whelan was a great first professor to have for college chemistry. Lectures are done really well, and individual/group work is straightforward and really helps your grade. Tests aren't too hard and are easy to finish in time, and cheat sheets are allowed. She also posts lots of resources to Canvas and is always willing to give extra help.

Only points in this class come from in-class quizzes as well as four midterm exams, and one final. Very difficult if you aren't a good test taker. I like Dan and Jen's lectures quite a bit. However, in our brief direct communication, Dan has been surprisingly callous.

Genuinely one of the worse classes I have taken. It's structured horribly, you have to master all the textbook individually, while the professor adds on pounds of content you also have to master. Extremely content and MATH HEAVY. It is near impossible to consume everything for the tests. There are only tests no homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a very nice guy and his lectures are good if you can get past his monotone. Beware though, tests are often very challenging!

He goes over the topics very in depth to the point where it is so boring you cant pay attention. He gives you practice problems for the test which most of the test questions are directly from the practice but he grades the short answer and essay questions really hard. He also test over material from the book not covered in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Reuman taught this class with Dr. Foster when I took it. Both were great&very knowledgeable about the topics. The class was focused on online homework assignments, class participation, two midterms, & a final (COVID era). They both were very eager to help us in any way and did a great job of adapting the class due to coronavirus. Lecture heavy!
Very similar class setup to her BSAN 415, but you will be using python instead of R. Harsh grader but will always work through problems you have and help you if you are stuck anywhere.
Tough grading professor but she is willing to work with you through any problems you may have, and her lectures are pretty fun at times.

The professor uses Python to do analytics, where she's very hands-on and explains all the concepts. It gets really math-y sometimes, but she explains for the class to easily comprehend it. The assignments are time intensive and sometimes the instructions feel vague, but her rubrics are straightforward and show you what she's grading on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The content is dense, so missing class would be a mistake. You'll learn R and statistics, so the content is pretty difficult, but the professor is competent and clear in her teaching. She bases office hours on the students' schedules. She has a reputation for being a hard grader. If you ever get confused, just ask her and she'll clear anything up.

Jason is an architect who loves teaching. Engaged in projects, he regularly checks progress through desk visits and presentations. He sets clear guidelines and deadlines, and is always available online for questions. Skilled in Sketch Up, he encourages using all available technology.
He's really good at giving specific feedback and guide you toward a path. He'll be honest too if what you're doing is just bad or confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jason is a skilled architect, but his role as a Studio professor did not meet expectations. The guidelines were unclear, and deadlines often felt unrealistic. The feedback I received during critiques didn't align with my grades. Additionally, I didn't receive evaluations for 2/3 projects, making it difficult to learn from my mistakes this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely love taking Jason's studio. He is incredibly involved in each student's project and really cares to see everyone succeed. He works countless hours in and out of the studio to ensure everyone progresses quickly. He takes time to understand each student's workflow and how he can individually push everyone to be the best they can be!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Jason is an amazing teacher, he's a tough grader, but a fair one that grades relatively quickly. There's a very small amount of points per design project. Very intense working hours and sometimes he  doesn't set extremely clear expectations for development, so you have to work more then originally anticipated the day/days before due.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class has a lot of homework but her grading is very lenient. It is a very easy A just a lot of busywork.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Rhine gives a lot of busy work, but she is an easy grader who gives 90 extra credit points. The essays are only 250 words. But the topics are really interesting. Please keep up with the work and submissions, this class is an easy A as long as you are submitting anything it does not have to even average.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You have to do hours of homework and it is just a core class. It. is busy work. Almost 2 hours of reading each week plus 2 lecture videos and two long assignments plus a 90 minute. test some weeks. It is ridiculous because. this class is. not even for anyones major and she takes. it way too seriously. Also the test was unnecessarily hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was accelerated so it was only 9 weeks rather than the full semester; the number of assignments each week, around 10, could easily get overwhelming if you have other obligations. Some assignments were short and easy, and others involved hours of reading. Overall, the class was graded easily and is manageable if you devote time to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: TA graded most of assignments. Like others have said: this class has lots and lots of reading/homework and is not a "light" elective. Took this as an online course so Idk what it's like in-person. Do your work and know what you're siging up for. Get ready to read and write!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Believe the professor often forgets that the modules take time and students have other classes. A lot of reading, quizzes are often. Sometimes quiz questions have nothing todo with the current module. 
If you have knowledge of culture or health outside of the North America, then its a boring/ annoying class.

Between awful and ok.

Lots of reading, lots of writing, and lots of videos and note-taking. From my experience, Dr. Rhine underestimates how long the modules take. The class was extremely time-consuming, but it did pay off in the end. The final is optional and there are lots of extra credit opportunities if you need it. The material is very interesting to learn about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took this class completely online and enjoyed it. She spent lots of time studying abroad so she was ver knowledgeable. Lots of reading but honestly if you have chegg you could skip reading & use that for tests. Decent amount of work but it wasnt hard at all. Took this for a core goal randomly and would recommend to others bc i actually enjoyed it.

This teacher was absolutely terrible. I have never had such an awful person "teach" a more boring class. I spoke with my advisor about how bad this class was and she mentioned the class has had more complaints than ever with professor Rhine. Kathryn Rhine comments on the papers you create and has no real experience actually grading anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would take a whole semester of her classes alone. Great professor.

The content of the class is very interesting, and the books were enjoyable. Lectures have lots of videos so you could skip them. As long as you go to the discussions you should be fine because they tell you what happens in the books. Exams were super easy so you don't need to study. She's a really nice professor, so I would recommend. Easy A.

Lectures are pretty boring and she posts the slides on blackboard, so unless there is a quiz, lecture is basically useless. Lots of reading but easy A. Grades easy and exams are a confusing format but pretty easy.

With the class grade revolving around your knowledge on vocab and the few required books, the lectures arent anything you really have to go to, but Dr. Rhines passion for the topics makes for a very interesting and insightful listen if you care about other cultures and progressive values. If not, this class might wear you out with the readings

Lectures were pretty boring, some of the books were okay though. Lots of reading, but you could probably get away with reading summaries. Offered 7% added on to your total grade of extra credit so GO TO THESE! You might not even need them at the end of the semester but the final and midterm and fairly hard so just do the extra credit just in case.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: No textbook, but we had to read 5 nonfiction books. We had "pop quizzes" over every book but they were given on the day the last chapter of the book was due. Tests were interpreting quotes, so make sure you know the terms on the study guide & you'll be ok; don't worry about learning the quotes on it. Lectures are boring but posts the slides online

Lectures were pretty boring but the information covered was interesting. There are a lot of books assigned to read and quizzes over each book of about ten questions, but you can just skim the book and read summaries online and do well. Exam formats were kind of odd but pretty easy, and they matched the study guides. Definitely recommend!

Gives A TON of extra credit but the exams were all about interpretation which means if you interpreted it wrong you got the question wrong. Most questions had more than one correct answer. Don't take this class unless you have to, it is not an easy A and it's not a fun class. Lectures were boring and she moved way too fast through the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was an elective class based on her book about how society creates health. If you understand entry level concepts about inequality and bias then youll already get most of the material. Assignments hold your hand so you dont really need to read the material. Lots of videos and movies watched in lecture, which most students left during.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Rhine is a very thorough professor, and very interesting to say the least. She has a big personality which is fine, and I felt like she was a living meme. She was very clear in her syllabus about homework, readings, papers, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super nice, gives tons of extra credit opportunities. Go to discussion.
Not a bad professor but not great if your just trying to get credits. But did give a ton of extra credit chances.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great teacher and TA's. I did not use my text book that much. Weekly online quizzes.  Weekly discussions. Big end of the semester group project - very easy points to earn.

Great teacher, really great to talk to if you go to her office hours. She's a hard grader and expects a lot out of her students but if you are interested in anthropology at all, she will get you hooked.

Not a fan. Lectures are mostly just reiterating book material instead of delving deeper. Discussion section is required but really feels like a waste of time. A group project with outside of class work is required and a huge portion of the final grade. Would not recommend if anthropology is not a major/minor.

Rhine hardly taught. She would often have us read long papers outside of class, that weren't helpful. I never used the book, just quizlet and memorized terminology for the midterm and final. The "mini" ethnography was a nightmare even with my solid group. It was a lot of research in a short time for an 100 level which she never officially graded.

Rhine talked to us like we were children. The ending project took more time and work than assignments from my 200+ level classes, and this is a 100 level class. Would not reccomend, would not take again.

The class was pretty interesting, but it required a lot more work that I was expecting for a 100 level class. A mini ethnographic project that is very tedious, and requires a lot of time. You have a TA and discussion, and it requires a lot of reading.

Oftentimes Rhine just let her TA's speak, she did very little lecturing herself. The only problem that I have with the class is the ending group project. We had to form groups with two people we had never met and then conduct a mini-ethnography outside of class-time. It was a ton of unnecessary work that involved research beyond a level 100 class.
Loved this class. She is sometimes hard to understand, but she is very intelligent and you can tell she loves the subject. Would definitely take another class from her!
Probably the best Professor I've ever had. Highly Recommend taking her class - you will learn so much more than just Arabic.

Very energetic - she loves her subject! Class is hard for Arabic newbies, easier for students w/ some familiarity. Flipped classroom style, meaning you need to do your hw every night. Attend class, you get graded for it. Go to her for help - class is fast paced and little time to ask questions. Keep up and you'll learn a ton!

Nadia is one of the nicest people I have ever met. She is very friendly and very enthusiastic about arabic but this class is very hard. Her lectures are fun and engaging but she expects you to learn all the material at home & does not allow you to take notes in class. The course moves too fast & you will have 1-3 hours of homework per night.

She is best professorteacher of any sort that I have ever had. Always comes into a class with a smile on her face, never misses a day, and is willing to work with you to boost your grade. The course IS intensive, and she rarely offers extra credit, but it's definitely worth taking the course.
Best language teacher I've ever had! Highly recommend this course. You'll be amazed how much Arabic you'll come away with.

She was a great teacher, really engaging, really sweet/understanding/helpful. If you are interested in learning Arabic and willing to put forth the effort then she is a great teacher to take from. I will say that homework factors HEAVILY in this class and it takes a long time to do. If you get behind it is very hard to catch up.

he was super nice and you could tell he really cared about his students, there was some content in the class that did seem a little too advanced and complicated for an intro class which also made the discussion  sections difficult

Great teacher and I loved how much he involved the GTAs. Some quiz questions can be weirdly phrased, so be careful and read closely. If you know basic psychology information, this class should be a breeze.

Participation matters in that you have to go to lecture and discussion. Lecture was always interesting and you had to go to lecture in order to know what parts of the chapters was actually what he wanted us to learn. I wish there was a little more preparation for the final but most of the class is easy if you try a little.

Lectures & class work is super repetitive, yet he will get frustrated when the amount of student that show up tapers off throughout the semester. The coursework itself was easy & he offered extra credit opportunities, but the final was stupid difficult compared to the rest of the semester. Plus, he will NOT round up grades after the final.

here's the thing..this prof is a human behavior prof so he set up the class intentionally to make sure students didn't work the system & knew exactly how to make it so that we had to come to class to get certain points/answers lol which was kinda annoying ngl, but class was pretty easy and not too bad for an intro class, just annoying at times ;;
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor was fantastic. He clearly cares about the subject he teaches and gladly answers any questions. I found his class so exciting I added ABSC as a double major. The class has a textbook that is very helpful to read, but the homework directly linked to it can be found online and it is participation. Attending class = easy A. 10/10 teach.

I thought Dr. Reed was great. He was really engaging and throughly explained the subject matter. Lots of guest lecturers. Attendance is mandatory and there are quizzes due at the end of the day each class day. Outside of reading quizzes, lecture quizzes, and Thursday activities there are few assignments. Each week had pretty much the same set up.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super funny and very understanding!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was a really simple class. There are no tests except for a final at the end. I spent a maximum of two hours outside of lecture working on stuff for this class. He has interesting lectures and uses clickers to make sure people come to class. The material is not too difficult especially if you read and listen in lecture.

I took ABSC 100 for the online winter break course. Dr. Reed was very clear with what he expected from us and made the class reasonably simple in the short period of the course. Grades in this term are mostly based on quizzes and tests, so make sure you watch video lectures if you take the online course. Dr. Reed was good - I would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Reed is perhaps one of the greatest instructors that I have had the opportunity to learn from. He manages to make monotonous materials into interesting and applicable lectures. Tests are fair, and homework is certainly manageable.

This class is an easy A but you just have to work the system. Click into the class with your clicker when it starts then go sit out on wescoe beach until the class starts to come out then run back in and answer the clicker question. You can also work your way around the quizzes by copying and pasting them each time the searching back through them

First of all, do not waste your money on the textbook. I have never once opened it and I have a 101% in the class. Lesson quizzes and vocabulary quizzes are very easy, but time consuming. However, if you do them to 100%, you are exempt from the final. He is a great teacher; it was a very fun and easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: The textbook helps but it was not necessary. Use quizlet and show up to class with your clicker & you're good to go! He's really nice but the content can get tiring. Sometimes I would read/do homework for other classes when I was there.

Awesome class and awesome professor. Make sure you work hard at the lesson  quizzes so you don't have to take the final.  He even offers extra credit. If you pay attention the in class quizzes are easy, and he drops the two lowest grades. I found this class enjoyable, interesting, and stress free.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: His lectures are great, when he does them. Most of the time its GTA's doing it.

This class felt like a waste of time, and was treated like a 400-level class not an intro. Get ready cause you have to spend a lot of extra time outside of class working on their repetitive 'lesson-quizzes'.  Book is ridiculously expensive and I never once opened it. Class only consists of lesson quizzes and the final exam, which you can opt out of
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: As long as you go to ABSC 100 and participate it is really easy. The Lesson Quizzes may take awhile but the class is really easy. Just do what you are supposed to and you can get over a 100%.

I took this first year seminar class because I thought it would be interesting. Although the class wasn't what I was expecting I really enjoyed having Derek as my professor. The class was really easy and a lot of fun. I recommend taking this class just to have the opportunity of having him as a professor.

You take in class quizzes everytime so you have to attend class and the guest lectures. Interesting material. Laid out in a really easy format. If you complete all the lesson quizzes with a 100% you don't have to take the final. Really great professor and great TA's
Great class. They give and explain really good information, but the class is super easy. Just do the basic work and you're good.

Honestly, best, most interesting, and easiest class I have ever taken. I learned so much. Attended almost all the lectures (you get 2 free misses), did the extra credit, got 100% on the lesson quiz (you can take them as many times as you want, if you get 100% on them then you don't have to take the final) and ended up with a 103% in the class.

This was by far my favorite class my freshman year. As long as you show up for class and do decent on the easy in-class quizzes then you'll pass. The final for the class is optional as long as you get a 100% on your Online quizzes and he also drops your two lowest in-class and AC4P quiz scores, which is really nice.

It's solely a lecture class, so it gets a bit boring at times, but he is so clear with his material. There are weekly lesson quizzes that if you get 100% on all of them you're exempt from the final so that's pretty convenient! Most of the students in his class are there for a gen ed requirement and he seems to be aware, making the class easier.
Seriously one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. As long as you show up. Easy A.

Very easy class as long as you do the work. Study a little for the lesson quizzes every week and you'll get an A. Dr. Reed explains things very well and is VERY passionate about behavior science. Really cool guy. Final is optional, no tests, and he drops your 2 lowest lesson and in-class quizzes at the end of the semester!!! TAKE THIS CLASS!
Interesting class. Study and do well on weekly lesson quizzes and you dont have to take the final. ACTUALLY READ the book for the lesson quizs!

Fun class and excellent professor. Lab proctoring, readings and discussion, semester projects, and mock syllabus are required work. Be reliable, attend class, participate in discussions, complete assignments, and you will get an A.
However much effort you put in , he will too.
Very Helpful. If you put forth effort so will he.
Dr.Reed is amazing! 509 is a very difficult class but with extra credit as well as available office hours....he really helps you succeed!
Dr. Reed is a nice guy and a good professor. Read assignments and be in class. Daily in-class quizzes and weekly lab quizzes required.  Easy A, if you put forth the effort.

Dr. Reed teaches all of his classes with a great sense of direction and guides his students through the required materials with a high understanding and knowledge for the subject. He is reasonable and often offers extra credit for simply speaking in class. Great professor, and he is easy on the eyes as well! ;)
The quizzes were very difficult

If you do not like group work do not take this class because all assignments in this class are a group effort. There are quizzes every Monday and he only lectures on Fridays. He gives out a ton of extra credit so it is easy to get an A in this class. There is also a mandatory 2 page single spaced paper you have to write.

This is a easy A class! Show up to class read the chapters take notes during class because at the end of class there is a open note open book quiz. Make sure you have a little extra free time because you take test outside of class time in dole computer lab but they are easy.

Easiest class on the planet!  daily quizzes in class for attendance, no wrong answers!  weekly quizzes over chapters, short chapters, read before quiz & can do it 3 times, so you just look at the answers & retake quiz. Biggest hassle was having to go to testing lab for the quizzes, but get 18/20 on 15 quizzes an NO FINAL.. that is whole grade!
Very kind, generous professor. Takes a very humanitarian approach behavior analysis. You'd be hard-pressed to find a better teacher for this course.
Amazing class and amazing Professor.  Dr. Reed is great and makes the class so simple. I'm not sure how people don't get at the very least a "B" in this class.

I loved this class. His lectures are very clear and he gives many oppertunities to earn points. His classes are not difficult if you attend regularly and apply yourself. The class is set up to follow the basic principles of ABSC (reinforcements/punishments) which makes it all the more interesting. He is well organized, friendly, and knowledgable.

Awesome teacher. Everything is SO clear, and easy to understand. It's like the perfect class. You get points for showing up, and you take a mini quiz on the computer for every lesson, so there are no big tests or midterms. And if you average an A on these, you don't have to take the final! I feel like I am learning a lot. LOVE this class.

I can't complain about Dr. Reed. However, this is the most frustrating class I have ever taken. The quizzes you take outside of class are not only time consuming but frustrating. They're fill in the blank with answers that are often very vague. If he taught the class differently I may have been intrigued, but honestly, I hated the class.

Easy class. It is what a 100 level should be. Derek is great teacher and very person-able. Highly recommended. Also, if you get As on the majority of "lesson quizzes" you don't have to take the final.
As long as you get a C on every test and are at every discussion, and do every inquisitive, you will pass the class
He was fine, only thing i wish was put the slide show notes on canvas. not sure why would wouldn't do that.

I have only high praise for Dr. Ringenberg. I had the pleasure of taking three of his courses. Each lecture was engaging, interactive, and overall very informative. He is quick to provide clear and constructive feedback on exams and project, and he does a great job at making himself available during office hours. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I am surprised Dr Ringenberg has good feedback.. He is an extremely tough grader and is not clear on assignment expectations. He gives very few A's. maybe 2 out of 30 students. He never hands back tests, or quizzes. You have to speak to him in person to see that so it's hard to see what points you missed. He also assigns very expensive textbooks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tom is a great instructor overall, but his class has very few assignments. I would recommend taking his class, but keep in mind that your grade will depend mainly on a few exams. Be ready to study hard for those, as there aren't many other ways to earn points. Attending lectures is important, or you'll have to rely solely on the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would absolutely recommend taking a class with this guy. He is very clear with his expectations and is very consistent with grading. He also is very knowledgable about Congress which made the class a lot easier. Participation during class activities and attendance matters though. Overall, if you have a chance to take a class with him, do it!

Ringenberg is a great professor who truly cares about students and knows a lot about his field. In this class, there are two exams - multiple choice and essay which are quite easy. and then a few small assignments like 1 page papers. He is a very fair grader and as long as you do the work, you'll get an A! Also he has great lectures so go to class!
Dr Richard is an amazing professor, I've never met a man so dedicated to his craft like him, you won't ever find a teacher out in the open. HE MAKES PHYSICS SO EASY.

I could tell he was really caring and all, but he just wasn't the best online class teacher. It usually took around a week to get an email back from him, and months to put grades in blackboard. The majority of the class is lots of busywork assignments that are easy, but tedious. Much of the homework is repetitive. The class was overall an easy A.

Dr. Richard is absolutely the kindest and most dedicated professor Ive had at any university. He really puts in the time to work with you and get you to understand the material. Dr. Richard is nowhere near condescending, e.g: dumb questions that are asked and he never makes you feel that way. Hes always available for office hours and patient!

This professor believes in the "flipped classroom" setting in which you are put into groups of your peers and expected to teach yourself. Going to class is essentially useless as he offers little help and expects you to learn from other students who also don't know what they're doing. You're best off reading the textbook and teaching yourself.

If you're taking engineering physics 1 at KU, this is the guy to get it from. The class structure is not great, but GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS. He'll help you with almost anything physics related and is extremely patient. He's also very lax about giving points back on tests if you make simple mistakes since they're stressful. TAKE HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Richard is hands down the best professor I have had thus far at KU. Throughout the semester, he has been especially focused on his students as people first and learners second; he encourages students to come to him for anything. Extremely available- has office hours 3 or 4 days a week. Would DEFINITELY recommend!

Nice guy, but definitely an awful class structure. Not saying that flipped classroom settings don't work, but with 300 people and an awful textbook its definitely not effective. Lectures don't help at all when doing the homework, and the tests can be relatively easy but harshly graded. Discussion sections are a waste of time so 210>211

He always encourages students to come into his office hours for help and he really knows what he is talking about! He explains the topics in a way that makes them very easy to understand, and is very understanding and sweet. I have an incomplete in the course due to personal reasons in the semester, and he is still working amazingly with me!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes taken at KU. Ric is extremely passionate about his work and this class. His lectures are engaging and make understanding the material so much easier. He keeps the class engaged. Tests are handwritten, but he gives possible test questions in the slideshows throughout the unit. It is a little bit of work, but go to class!

One of the best professors I have had at KU. His content is really engaging and culturally relevant, you will actually use the information you learn in this class. He is very helpful and can be a tough grader at times but wants you to succeed.

Professor Steele is f*cking awesome. He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is very engaging during class time and is accessible outside of class. Professor Steele is very knowledgeable, humble, and helpful. You have to be willing to put in the work for the class but it's work it. I would trust this man with my life

Ric is one of the best professors I've ever had at KU. His lectures were so entertaining and educational. There wasn't a lot of homework. Just readings for each class and summarizing an article once a week. Also two papers, but he was always happy to meet with me outside of class to discuss them. If you have the chance, take a class with him!
Great guy, great teacher! Has had lots of experience in his field so can talk about just about anything.

Dr. Steele was one of the best profs I have ever had. Clear, to the point lectures that are interesting, which made class actually fun. His lectures follow very closely to the book, but would suggest reading in addition.

Dr. Steele was one of the best profs I have ever had. Clear, to the point lectures that are interesting, which made class actually fun. His lectures follow very closely to the book, but would suggest reading in addition.

I really loved taking this class. It is the best class that I have taken at the university because the information was interesting and relevant to everyday life. Prof. Steele is fun and understanding of the fact that we are students with other classes. Easy, but enjoyable!

Child Psychology was wonderful!  Steele may be one of the best lectures at KU, and a really nice guy.  He gets you involved in the lectures. which have very insightful and useful info.  They are not out of the book or really on the tests, just aimed at teaching you relevant psychology as child, parent, etc.  Great Class and Great Teacher!!!

Dr. Steele is one of the best teachers I have ever had! He is very knowledgable in his field and if you do the work and are willing to go talk to him if you have questions he is a wonderful resource. He is very approachable and the class is fantastic!!
only two grades for the whole semester besides the quizzes...which many fail....Read the material two or three times to understand what lecture is about

Ric's a knowledgable guy and the information is cutting edge and relevent. However, the workload is way too heavy. Does not take into consideration that people have other classes to work on as well. Highly recommended for people taking only one or possibly two classes during the semester, otherwise, avoid this one. It will ruin your GPA.

Where do I start, this was the worst class of my life.  It was the longest 3 weeks, of 2 hours a day of hell!  He was rude, uneducated, and talked from his soap box constantly. I learned nothing from this course other than to never take a class taught by him ever again!!!

he was very passionate and tried to include and relate to the students. sometimes a little too passionate and advanced for a class of students that are all taken this class as a gen ed, so i felt bad he was teaching this low of a class

Trevor loves what he does. No tests. Online quizzes each week- very easy. Is a textbook but DONT BUY IT its not necessary at all. Attendance is graded through iclicker but you get skips and points through iclicker are ONLY for attendance nothing more. if you have to take a science credit take BIO 100 its the easiest out of all offered.

Show up and do the work and you will get an A. He knows most students are just trying to get the science credit, but still gives fun and engaging lessons. He really is a good teacher and should probably teach more advance classes to students who are more excited about science as a lot of his lessons were interesting. Overall a really good teacher.
Easiest class I've ever taken. Literally just sat there listening to music and on my phone the entire time lol. No tests, just easy weekly assignments and you can use chatgpt for all of it

Solid professor but the class is just boring. It's a basic High school-level Biology class with 1.5-hour-long lectures. It's just a long class. The class has over 500 students so you don't have any relationship with him. He is far too knowledgeable to be teaching a 100-level class. His personal experience makes his lectures more interesting. Easy!
He's an ok professor and BIOL100 was super easy. Did not like the user of iClicker and mandatory attendance though. Also, being stuck in budig with all the seats filled up is not fun.
Really nice and genuine guy, if you just do your work and attend the classes you will get an A. People who dont have an A in the class and complain likely just dont do their work.
This class was super easy and the instructor is always available for help when you need and actually responds to your emails

This class is probably the easiest class I ever took. As long as you don't miss more than 6 classes and complete the assignments, your grade will be perfectly fine. He's a super nice guy and lovesssss answering questions.
Prof. Rivers is a great professor and makes biology interesting for non-biology majors. The lectures can be pretty long but I found them to be interesting.

He is aware that for most of us this class is required, and makes it as engaging and interactive as he can. No exams in BIOL100, just participation, in-class group work, and an online quiz every class. He is passionate about biology, which leads to interesting and engaging lectures, where even though you don't NEED to pay attention, you'll want to.

I loved his class. he understood that many of his students were being required to take the class, so he made it fun and took the class lightly. No test, just quizzes every class meeting. Attendance = points, that's the only reason I received the grade I did.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed biology with professor Rivers. His lectures were straight to the point, and the class was easy to follow. Attendance is partially mandatory, with some built-in excused absences. However, class time can be used to complete every assignment in the class for that week so I rarely spent time on the class outside of it.

Very easy class! He is very knowledgeable. No exams and no finals. Class quizzes and weekly assignments, but fairly easy. Clicker questions in class don't affect your grade if you get it right/wrong, mostly for attendance. Take attendance in a blue book and you get points for answering the questions. He allows for 2 weeks of absences (4 classes).

This class is as easy as it gets in college. No tests or final exam. There are weekly quizzes and assignments but they aren't too bad. Prof clearly cares about what he's teaching. There are clicker questions + you have to sign into your assigned groups book so that you can get participation/attendance points but it's a easy class if you try a lil;;

I thought he was really cool for a professor. So much extra credit. It was really easy to get a good grade in the class and wasn't a class to stress over in my opinion. A little fast paced but he records the lectures I'm pretty sure so you can always go back and rewatch.
I liked him a lot. His lectures could sometimes be pretty boring to listen to though, but overall he was a good teacher.

Dr. Rivers and Dr. Hotze both teach the same course, however break it up 50/50 in terms of the material. Dr. Rivers does a great job with going through the material and is keen to answer any questions that are asked in lecture. There are plenty of office hours and he holds some as well. Oh, and he’s a Jiu-Jitsu instructor.
Dr Rivers is a King. He teaches jiu jitsu which is cool. Also makes biology interesting which is a near impossible task. Highly recommend

His lectures were pretty good overall and he was a pretty personable guy. Online homework questions were kinda useless and didn't really focus on most of the content from the exams, but I think the group work we did in class was pretty helpful for preparing for exams. Exams were mostly multiple choice, so if you study well you should be fine.
He goes at a solid pace and his lectures, though advanced, are easy to follow if you read the textbook beforehand. Use the textbook! He's very easygoing and approachable for help.

While I enjoyed Dr. Rivers as a person... his teaching style, assignments, and tests made the class insufferable. The tests went into specifics without going over the broad knowledge of chapter, i.e. the chapter over cell division asking more questions about prokaryotic division rather than eukaryotic. While group work was worded wrong mult. times

Dr. Rivers is great at teaching and explaining the material, is very approachable, wants to help you succeed, and is willing to admit when he is wrong. I took the asynchronous class which was the best decision! He curves, posts addendum quizzes, provides extra credit, and drops lowest test grades to help with your grade since it is a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you can take the asynchronous BIOL 150 do it. There are a lot of quizes about the lectures but you can always rewatch the lectures until you know the answer. The weekly modules are easy enough to get through and then just study hard for the tests. Trev dawg hitting me up with a bunch of curviture or something because my grades looking nice.

BIOL150 is a pretty tough class, but his lectures gave all the information needed to do well on the tests. Learning what to study and what not to study helped a lot. He's a pretty approachable guy too, which I appreciated

Almost all of the class was taught by TA's or pre- made videos. Definitely not hard, but Rivers is not an understanding person when it comes to personal issues at all and is extremely strict about quizzes and exams, refusing to make accommodations for students in need when most of his classes consists of first semester freshmen in a pandemic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a fine professor I just had a bad experience with him. My grandma had passed very suddenly and I had to leave campus and go home. With that, I couldn't take an exam so I emailed him and he told me I either had to withdraw from the class or fail out. and there were no other options to take it during office hours or anything.

I don't like the way he teaches, his lectures are all over the place. The tests have a lot of material not covered in class. It's hard to know what to study for. He told me once that "sometimes the book has too much info, and sometimes not enough."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He may not go over everything but he is really good in explaining everything.
Lectures are a bit messy online. Would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture videos are very nonspecific and messy. The lectures do not prepare you for the homework assignments whatsoever so you are better off just reading the textbook and not bothering with watching the lectures. His handwriting in the lecture videos is also next to impossible to decipher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Rivers is a great professor who really cares about his students. If you have him for a huge lecture, you don't get to know him personally. Nonetheless, he will happily answer any question and demonstrates great respect for every student's point of view.

Trevor Rivers is a great professor. He is very entertaining to listen to ( if you are actually interested in the topic). His lectures are easy to follow, and he likes to crack some jokes in between topics. Do the readings before class as well as the guidelines and you will do just fine.
read and youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: None
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You'll need to basically teach yourself because he will teach what he is interested in and then give a test over material he didn't lecture and that you were supposed to read and teach yourself. Better BIOL100 professor than Mort but I wouldn't take either again. Tries to hard to engage in a 300+ class where no one is interested and it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Rivers knows what he's talking about. He will tell you what you need to know and will call on every group at some point so make sure you know what's going on. The best way to do this is to read the textbook before class and take notes. You should also do the guidelines so you have them as a reference when you go to study for exams.

He was the professor that led an online Biology Major seminar. There was some reading and some videos to watch, then you would take online quizzes that were open.
