The quizzes literally had the link to the answers written in the questions. You had to get a 100% to pass the class. Only took a couple hours to get through all the material for an easyA
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Labs aren't easy, but I have always managed to work hard and pass. TA was useless, would get annoyed & shut off when asked questions. Lab directions and report rubrics were vague. This slowed my progression and prevented learning and made labs dangerous. I would spend hours on reports & was told that requirements weren't met due to poor directions.

If you spend hours on the lab reports then the class is do-able but very time consuming. The reports are graded by a different rubric than the one given at the start of the lab. If you want a good grade, make sure to not only answer the questions on the rubric but explain your answer further. Go to the extra credit lab. It'll help save your grade

It feels like they try to make Chem 331 as hard as they can, without any help for students. The feedback forms for lab reports are very vague as to what you messed up on, and the process to get help on lab reports is also ridiculous. Don't take the lab if you have to!! Even though it's said to have gotten easier over the years, it's still very hard
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: When confronted with concern from students and other professors alike over the lack of feedback forms being returned to students for lab reports (i.e. the forms that help us improve our report writing skills and overall grades) her response was "students should have been more proactive". Reports are graded with a separate rubric from the one given.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super easy class, but I skipped lecture a couple times--don't do that... this class is half attendance, so just go to class do the easy HW and you'll get an A. The only thing is that he does NOT read emails, so if you need to reach him, go to his office hours. Don't even bother with email...
Honestly, I liked Sorem. He was very interested in the subject he taught, and it showed.

For the love of god do not take this class. It is a capstone class that takes up your entire senior year allowing you to have a terrible final year with no time for friends. You will hate your life. The teacher only grades if the capstone car works and does not account for learning and progression. If you want a life don't take this!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: won't even grade half of your assignments. he just gets a gist of who you are, looks at your test scores, and assigns a letter grade. hasn't graded the very time consuming group projects in years
So many exams and homework and group project. A lot of work. Boring lectures. Most students come out of this course knowing nothing more.
6 exams... doesn't ever respond to emails. Very unavailable to students.

Great person who really cares about his students. The class is pretty straightforward, and there are a lot of resources to ensure you do well. Although I wouldn't recommend taking 628 and 661 in the same semester...learned this the hard way. If you can't avoid it, start bracing yourself for an ungodly amount of work.

Dr. Sorem is one of my favorite professors in the ME Department. He makes the lectures easy to read and highlights the main points. The exams are VERY doable, however, do expect a lot of homework. These homeworks are super beneficial in your learning and help prepare you for the exam. Outside of the class, he's just a really awesome and caring dude

Sorem is very understanding and caring. He really just wants to help everyone learn. I really liked the lectures and the project was set up well. There is a very large amount of homework but its not hard and if you do it you will be well prepared for the exams. Don't be afraid to ask questions, he is really nice and funny.

Honestly, this class was harder than Thermo. This class is A LOT of work and the lectures are long. But Dr. Sorem does care greatly for his students and wants you to succeed. He's very understanding, so if you're struggling, talk to him! The exams are HARD but as long as you know how to use his equations sheet, they're not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He expects to discuss every detail before any action is performed, but he only gives negative feedback in return and makes every interaction a miserable experience. He expects you to treat him like a boss instead of like a professor. This leads to a toxic learning environment that stifles creativity for students who want to try new designs.

Lectures are incoherent speeding rambles. Weekly homework and lab reports make this class an unbearable amount of work. Exams have questions that were unsolvable. Didn't have a clue if anything I was turning in was correct because over 80% (not exaggerating) of the grade wasn't graded till finals week and after. Didn't learn a thing.

No professor has to make a 3 credit hour course into a 9 credit hour course. He purposely overloads students, his lectures are extremely rushed, and does the majority of grading after finals. In the mix of confusing and ridiculously long homework assignments and weekly lab reports, there is a project that will teach you nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: I've gotten to know Dr. Sorem pretty well. He is more caring and involved than you'll ever know. Everything he expects of you is fair, but rushed. He takes on 3cr courses that should be divided into 9cr, so he HAS to rush you. It's not your fault OR his, he just wants you to overcome it. He is sharper than he lets on and he knows you cheated.

This professor is notorious for his long lectures. At one point we were over 100 slides for the duration of class. The best way to take notes during class is to print out his slides, however many you need per page to see the content, and take notes as he goes along over what he says. You should notice a difference when you do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class should be split into two semesters with the amount of information this professor wants to cover in this class. Didn't understand anything I learned. The amount of work he gives is more equivalent to a 9 credit hour class than a 3.

7 big exams (most given under extreme time pressure), 5-10 hours of homework every week (including all the weeks you have exams), and a group project with vague expectations. In this class you can't learn anything due to the extreme overload in useless work. Be prepared to get fast at copying chegg!

Dr Sorem glides through slides in one class session so I suggest to be present to grasp an understanding of what is going on. There's lots of homework bc this class covers 6 new topics that he'll test you over every other week. This method is great since once you learn it, you'll be tested, and then its over with. Don't be afraid to ask questions!!

He's tough at first, but you find he really cares about his students' learning. He often asks the class for suggestions. He presents the material in a way that makes sense. There is a lot of homework but it's usually not overly difficult and it's always relevant. The class IS hard, but you can't say he's unfair. You def. get out what you put in.

Homework isn't very difficult but is very time consuming. If you get solutions ahead of time he purposely makes mistakes to catch cheaters. Everything seems pretty clear but he goes very fast through lectures and wants questions answered during lecture. Answers any questions you have and usually quick to help students if they need it.
A professor that really works for the students
A great professor. Would recommend.

Dr. Sorem definitely knows his stuff and is pretty okay at teaching it, but has the worst format for a class I've ever seen. The first half is lecture, the 2nd is an in-class problem. Problem is, he races through the lecture so fast you can't take notes, then he collects the ICP for a grade, so you leave the class with no notes and no examples.

Very interesting class, but you need to learn everything by yourself. In the first half year, he just give some comments about the formula car. You need to do more research from previous car. Well, he looks like advisor in this class. BTW,you only need to draw solidwork model in first half year.
he is the dean of engineering but was the most disorganized and least prepared teacher ive had.  Made up assignments as he went along.  15 minutes on google could have done what he did in a semester
just as bad as southard

He was very unclear about what his assignments were and he never stopped to see if anyone understood what he was saying. He assumed we all knew what he was talking about. All I got out of this class is that he worked for Slumber J as a Mechanical Engineer.
Teacher was super easy if you know what I mean.

Not a fan of this class. The biggest problem (among several other small things) was that it took her forever to grade. One week before finals, 5/15 of our assignments were graded; nobody knew where they stood. The final paper had an interesting topic but I could tell she rushed grading because there were no comments and a perfect grade on mine.

Ruth is AMAZING. She truly cares about her students and what they have going on in their life. This is my second class with her, and I adore her. This class had a lot of reading with corresponding responses, but the readings were interesting. As long as you do the work and go to class, you'll get an A. No exams!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Ruth was a very considerate professor, and was very cooperative and helpful if you just communicated. She gave a lot of readings, but they were interesting and the assignments and work were pretty easy. I feel like she was a pretty easy grader as well, but she appreciates people who put in an effort. If you messed up, just talk with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Ruth was a great instructor, one of my favorites ever at KU!  The feedback she gives is so helpful, and she is always trying to make sure her students have all the tools they need to succeed.
If you have a chance to take a class with Dr. Ruis, do it! He's kind and caring, and the material is super fun. No matter your major, you'll be able to use what you learn.

One of the funniest, most caring teachers I've ever had. Genuinely cares about each and every one his students and truly wishes to make them more confident and better actors. His stories are fantastic, and he's fun to listen to.

David made Theater a fun and inviting experience for everyone in the class, wether or not theater was an interest to them previously. Coming to class everyday was a joy and gave me something to look forward to during the busy school day.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Favorite prof I've ever had!!!!! Take him if you can!!!!! you won't be disappointed, I promise. Not a theatre major, but still enjoyed every minute of it.
David was the best. All our speeches were freeformed, letting us talk about things we're passionate about. So long as you do the incredibly easy assignments, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: She is extremely disrespectful. Once I asked her why I was docked points and she told me, "I was just feeling like a b!t#h that day". Extremely disrespectful. She grades so much harder than any of the other TA's for this course. She is not considerate or nice at all. If you get her as a TA switch immediately.

Does not know how to teach in a way that college kids can understand and her ego complex definitely shows through. I suggest any other TA than her. She is blatantly mean and doesn't really explain the lectures, just expects you to know what you're talking about. She is a harsh grader as well. I have never been miserable in a class at KU until hers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You have to be investing in caring about what philosophical topic that we are talking about. If you did that, easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Won't give feedback until 2 days before paper is due. Her feedback is the vaguest I've ever received for all the assignments. Arbitrary grading, assignments everyday for an online class, tricky questions for the readings, not very accessible through email. All in all one of the worst classes and professors I've taken at KU and I'm a senior.
Shannon is very good at her job. Great amount of reading, very good. 10/10 super ninja professor

Shannon is so cool! She showed that she cared a lot about the things that were going on in her students lives. The readings were interesting and the weekly quizzes were simple. I was always entertained during this class and would totally take a class with Shannon again.
Expects wayyyyy too much out of students taking online classes. If it were an in person class, the work load would be fine, but it is honestly way too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ryan was an amazing professor and I am so glad that I took his English125 class. He makes it very clear where you stand in terms of grades and it is completely up to you to determine how well you do in his class (if you do put in a little bit of effort, you will get an A). If you are looking for an English125 professor, choose Ryan!!

I feel so lucky to take Ryan's course during my first semester at University of Michigan. He helped me a lot and provided me with lots of sources I wasn't aware of. It requires hard work to be sucessful in his class, but I did improve a lot. And he is definitely a good choice for international students.

I am taking his course in winter 2020 at Umich. He is so nice and really cares about students. His class really teaches how to write instead of writing for earning credits. The grading depends on what you have improved. He is an excellent teacher and can also be a really good friend in your life.

I was in Ryan's first class at the University of Michigan, and I am so glad I had him as a teacher. He will take the time to sit down and talk to you about things not only related to class, but just life in general. He's a really great guy, and I felt really lucky to have him as my English professor! If at all possible, take a class with this guy!
No Comments

Good teacher, if you need help, he will do everything he can to help you.  Emails you back immediately.  really into what he's doing, and does everything he can to get you to have a good grade.  Not very clear in class, but if you toss him an email, he'll explain it very well, and help a lot.
Eh.  If you work with him you can probably figure out how to do well.  He's into what he's doing and wants you to be too.
Long lectures with a lot of rambling and random Greek and Latin thrown in.  Pretty hard to pay attention let alone participate.

Interesting class, but not what I was expecting. Most of the reading is of a philosophical nature. It wasn't until later in the semester that I began to see the point of the course. A good experience overall.
Good guy, rambles a bit. Really nice and willing to explain things to you.

Good teacher. Attending class is important for passing tests. (essay tests) But attending class will help get good grades. Really very nice guy and understanding. Attendance is not required but highly recommended. Easy to get on his "good" side. I loved him!
contribute to online discussion and prepare for class - participation is a big part of the grade
Entertaining subject matter, straightforward lecture, very good looking professor
He is absolutely wonderful to look at, an easy grader, and fun in class!!!
Great teacher!  Funny and interesting to learn from!  If you'll be attending Charleston next year (s) take a class from him!

Awesome guy and very helpful if you don't understand the assignment. Multiple speeches are required, but if you start ahead of time and ask for help, it shouldn't be a problem. Class isn't mandatory, but he gives random extra credit points for showing up on certain days, which really helps in the long run.
Unfair grader. If you can, take class with a different TA.

When grading papers takes off points for no reason.  Can do revisions but his critiques do not help you figure out where you lost points.  Impossible to get a good grade unless you can read his mind on what he wants.
Best class I have ever taken at KU, he is a great teacher and he is very interestd in the topics discussed in class.

He is a very good teacher and makes class very enjoyable.  He makes the class feel like a bunch of friends which helps when giving your speeches.  I thought I was going to hate this class but it turned out to be my favorite class this semester!
Great teacher, more concerned with reflection than terms and definitions
Ryan is an awesome teacher. He has a good sense of humor and realizes that people don't think his classes are their world. He is VERY fair an down to earth.
he is no longer at kansas but wherever he is teaching is lucky to have him. Likes teaching, interesting man, fun to talk to etc. best teacher I've had in college.

He's awesome! Take his class!! He really cares about the material, and makes it interesting. He loves to talk, so if you can talk to him outside of class, you're golden!! Just show up, do the readings and participate and you will not only do well, but actually learn something!

One of the best general studies instructors I've had a KU. He is extremely intelligent and very enthusiastic about the material. He loves to get into discussion and will open your eyes to a new way of thinking about Western Civ. KU needs more instructors like Ryan.

Made class enjoyable to go to. Was enthusiastic about the material and wanted to make it relevant to today's world. Always willing to hear student opinions out and was very available for extra help. He's not going to hand you an A, but he'll give you the help you need and there are even opportunities for extra credit.

There are mandatory questions for each discussion.He claims they're the test questions; they're not.Discussions don't touch upon topics he tests you on.He spends a vast amount of time talking about how awesome he is and how much stuff he does.The final was unbelievable as he asked a vague question that made you wonder what he wanted.Better than mos

He's a smart guy, and he really does know his stuff.  Unfortunately, he's pretty full of himself, and tends to make a lot of jokes that he finds pretty hillarious, but are irrelevant.  It's not a terrible class, but listening to his cockiness does get old. Over all gives off kind of an **** vibe.

Great teacher!  Loves and knows his stuff.  Made some dry material very relevant.  Also, he's pretty lenient which really helps.  It's still not an easy A class though.  Highly recommend him if you're actually interested in learning about the civilization we live in.  Very enthusiastic guy and two thumbs up.

The grading rubric on notebooks needs work. I saw a comment here warning about this a few years ago, so here's the warning returning; when answering questions on the rubric, answer the question, AND the consequence if you do the opposite of the question, else you lose points. This will make sense when you take the class. God speed.
Run away. Tough class, structured for failure instead of success. Professor does not care.

He was not good at communicating topics in multiple manners. Honestly felt nervous to even ask questions because half the time he would respond in an annoyed or upset manner. Prelab lecture attendance wasnt super important until it came to prep for the single exam which was very difficult. TAs run the labs so grading varies depending on who you get

Dr. Rubin is a great guy, but as an undergrad OChem professor, he's very inaccessible. Optional lectures were dense with information; only a few of us regularly attended them. Lab notebooks are most of the grade, so make sure to understand each experiment. Dr. Rubin expects a lot, but often does a bit too little to help his students achieve that.
Run Away
I liked Rubin as a professor, this class is just set up for some serious failure.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: So I particularly liked how Rubin had helped students with review sessions before Chemistry Lab Exams in order to better succeed on the exams. Also I liked the idea of having powerpoints put up on Top Hat for students to view to do the Top Hat quizzes due on Sunday each week. It was helpful to have the lablecture prior to Chemistry labs.

Lectures are haphazard and inaccessible, even to those experienced in science and chemistry. Assignment expectations are not given; you're expected to learn by trial and error. He makes wild, unsubstantiated accusations of plagiarism whilst ignoring conflicting evidence. He has no respect for his students, nor for the university. Avoid him if able.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is very hard to understand because of his thick accent and talks quietly. Makes you take quizzes after every lecture that have nothing to do with what he just taught. He gives 2 very difficult tests but he curved the second by 18%. Lab reports saved my grade. He does call people out for plagiarizing even if they didn't. Weird way of determining.

With respect, Ochem lab does not need a separate lecture. 95% of what I leaned in this class was from experiments and my lab GTA. Calculating your own grade was unnecessarily difficult. Be sure to reserve at LEAST 5-10 hours a week for writing lab reports. There are 8 of them and they have to be pretty solid if you want a good grade on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: For many, this class was a coin flip. Some fo the smartest and hardworking individuals are rejected for reasons that should not occur. The GTA's were my problem. You can come in with a blatant problem with grading and they will give 100% effort... to make sure you don't get your points back. The lecture material is far too difficult for many too.

He is probably the worst professor I have had. I know he accused at least 15 people of plagiarism and was extremely rude to them, then eventually reviewed the papers and realized they were not plagiarized. The TAs were a great help, however a few were quite rude as well. Lab reports make up the majority of the grade. Exams are very diffuclt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Rubin is very intelligent and holds students to high standards. The class was challenging but manageable. Expect to spend a lot of time writing lab reports according to very specific but secret criteria. Tests are okay if you study the old ones and pay attention. He is very helpful in answering any questions during and after lab lecture.

Rubin is a bad to mediocre teacher. He doesn't explain reactions well, nor does he use or provide lecture notes. Your best bet is to just read the textbook and research reactions on your own using the internet. The only thing Rubin taught me was to write lab reports based off his grading rubric. Fortunately, there is a heavy curve. 68% ---> B

Issue isn't so much with Rubin, although he isn't a great prof, it's primarily with the course itself. Almost all of the grading is based on the lab reports, which take multiple hours at least and that's likely for C/B work. It felt like every report I turned in I had no idea what grade I was going to get. Class is curved though
Chem 336 was really enjoyable experience. The professor is extremely smart and he is willing to help, especially outside the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof. Rubin will challenge you, and you will have to learn a lot if you want an A. But you still will not fail the class even if you do not follow, C is pretty much guaranteed if you do all the assigned labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed this professor. His tests are super difficult, best way to pass is to know every single thing he teaches front/back. 336 is much harder than 331 but far more enjoyable, in my opinion. Really neat guy who really loves chemistry and has a cool sense of humor. Hard to get flat A in class.

To pass the exams you have to really know the material inside and out but if you do well in everything but the exams you can still pass. My friend literally got an F and a C+ on the two exams and her lab grades and TopHat scores brought her up to a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class, it was an eye-opening experience. Prof. Rubin teaches you how to learn, not just sitting through the lectures. I wish I studied this way in all my classes in the past. I would be much better prepared for medical school.
Cool class, engaging professor. Will make you work for your grade, which haters do not like, but you will know the material really well.
Great lectures, very helpful office hours. Sample tests makes preparation easy.

Probably the most boring class I have taken at KU. 8 AM is too early to have to go to a class like this. Reports often require random detailed information about very specific reagents you've never used before, and there is no readily information available to answer any of these questions. Overall, it is an easy class made difficult by poor teaching

Lectures were slow and full of pauses, making it near impossible to pay attention. Replaced clickers with a very expensive online system for participation/text book that is difficult to use. Bulk of the grade comes from lab reports, which are graded by TAs and are very subjective. Exams are horribly difficult and very specific. Hated this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great class!  It is hard to keep everyone satisfied, but Rubin did the best job to deliver the material to the class.  Would love to take his classes again.
Really enjoyed this class.

Prof. Rubin will not leave you indifferent.  Students either love his teaching style or hate it.  Frankly speaking, the haters should not be in the class to begin with.   If you want to get an easy A for just attending the class, this is not for you.  But you will know a lot by the end of the semester if you work the way he instructs you.

I love his teaching style.  He gives you clear understanding how to proceed and teaches you how to succeed in the class.  Everything is straight to the point.  Videos makes preparation very easy.  To succeed you have to work all through semester, but the load is manageable.

Rubin makes a difficult class even more challenging. It is very hard to focus while in lab lecture and there really isn't much room to make mistakes in this course. Overall, would not recommend him as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Rubin's lectures are very boring. He is hard to understand. I believe if you listen to his lecture they can be helpful, but it is hard to pay attention. Overall, lab lecture is not necessary, but clicker points are needed for class. I usually did other work while in lecture.

Difficult class, but doable as long as you do well in your lab section and you attend every 8 AM lecture weekly. Clicker points, pre-lab quizzes, weekly lab reports, online hw and a midterm/final make up your grade. Rubin's lecturing wasn't very structured or helpful in my opinion, so be sure to stay on top of the material and self-study a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ochem lecture (CHEM 330) is straight-forward and requires work, but is a fairly graded course. Don't expect that with CHEM331 with Rubin. His lectures are hard to understand and the in-class quizzes are impossible. You have quizzes in lab, in lecture, pre-lab homework, lab reports and online homework. Makes a difficult class nearly impossible.
I really like his style.  He does not use countless power point slides, which makes his lectures very focused and specific.  Videos describing experiments help a lot.

I like his lectures very much, they are well organized and really help to succeed in the labs.  His sample tests help a lot for the test preparation.  Prof. Rubin is very approachable and always ready to help.
Go to lab lecture once a week and the only thing I take away from it is self defense techniques. Not good at explaining material. Basically have to teach yourself everything.
Lecture is DEFINITELY not organized; very strong accent; Very bad at explanation;
His jokes are better than his lecture. Which is sad because I'd rather sit in a boring lecture and actually learn something than laughing at his jokes but walk out learning nothing.

I really enjoyed this class.  Lectures are cell organized and videotaped.  Multiple on-line quizzes keep you well prepared for the tests.  Dr. Rubin's approach to teaching spectroscopy is very engaging, he made even hard stuff crystal clear.  I also liked his "self-defense" practices )))))
Very helpful and very engaging instructor.  Great lectures, very funny jokes ))) Loved this class!
fantastic teacher!
Great class with very well organized material, a lot of practice tests that really help to get ready for examination.  In-class quizzes are helpful as well.
great prof - he made me understand organic chemistry!
Materials are very well organized, lectures are useful and very inspirational.  Dr. Rubin was very helpful during office hours too.  I enjoyed this class.
He is very smart and very funny, I love his jokes ))) Excellent teacher who made organic chemistry fun.
Very helpful, his lectures are well organized, practice tests teach you how to deal best with real tests.  He may be the best chemistry teachers at KU!

Dr. Rubin gave very clear and well organized lectures. He's very funny and loves to make jokes! Practice questions are provided that are similar to quizzes and exams, but of course expect the real thing to be harder.  Make sure to go to the review sessions. Dr. Rubin and Rubina are always available to help and communicate with students effectively.
Wow!  This was incredible semester!  Hard material, but he made it very clear and understandable.
innovative teacher, tough material but he's incredibly helpful and tries to keep us interested.  work hard you will do well.

This is the worst professor I have ever had. He always scratches the chalkboard with his fingernails just to freak us out and during his labs he would often make us deal with dangerous chemicals! Avoid at all costs and run as fast as you can

Material is very well organized, and he teaches very clearly, explaining all the details of lab procedures.  He makes very complex concepts clear.  Very helpful at office hours, and always available.  The class is not easy, but If you attend the lectures you have to be dumb to get poor grade.

Worst teacher I have had in my college career thus far.  He did not teach me anything.  There is a significant curve in the class which is good considering the class average on the midterm was a 53%.  The lab itself is only difficult because of lab reports but they are curved as well.

I've never felt the need in a year and a half at KU to rate a professor until now. Rubin is hands down the worst professor at the university. Doesn't teach anything, expects you to know a ridiculous amount. 53 average on the midterm.

The worst professor at KU, by far. He teaches the class as if we're graduate students and expects us to understand everything he says, though his thick Russian accent doesn't help. Average on the midterm was an F and he does little besides 10 extra credit points and a curve.

Lectures have nothing to do with quiz questions or the content of the midterm/final.  Midterm/final are not based to the book.  Study every aspect of the test reviews bc tests are very similar.  Rely on help from your GTAs. I suggest Luke - he's the best.

I love his accent! I really don't think he's that hard to understand if you're actually listening. Yes, lecture is boring, yes the tests are hard, but the curve is awesome! The quizzes are online now so there's no reason why you shouldn't get 100% on all of them. Go to the class and lab and you should be fine.

Great teacher!! Difficult class but he makes it easy to understand. In the end he curves the final grades so much that as long as you score above the average you will probably have an A!  The website is extremely helpful!
If you work just a little bit - you will get an "A".  Wonder what losers gave him bad ranking?
With how large of a curve he applies to this class, you don't even have to bother studying for exams... when a 60% on a midterm is curved to an A, just good test taking skills become suffecient.

I thought that his teaching style was very hard to understand. You have to read the book thoroughly and do well in the lab. His midterm and final are cracked up to be a lot harder than they actually are. Study weekly and you can get an A.

You must teach yourself in this class. Rubin does not act like a professor. Mid-term average: 50%. The final was identical to the review. Aim to get 25/25 on each lab report. You can fail both the mid-term and the final and still get an A, since your grade is based upon how you score compared to your classmates. Class avg is a B.
He is quite rude and his thick accent makes him hard to understand at times.

Worst class ever... not only are his lectures boring as hell, but its almost impossible to understand what he'ssaying.  His midterms are probibally the hardest midterms you'll ever take... i would definatelly not recommend his class, but unfortunatelly, he's the only 625 teacher... so we dont have a choice

I took 625 from him last fall and hated him, but he has done a 180 in his teaching style.I took this class over the summer but never felt overwhelmed. He held multiple discussions before exams which helped alot. Exams are tough, but managable if you study. Plus, he is still a fan of the curve. Very likeable guy, you'll even fall for his accent!

Dr. Rubin has made an effort this semester to improve his class. He really does try to be funny and make the material interesting and understandable.  However, he is still confusing and the tests are extremely hard.  Final test average was an F.  However, he curves the class a lot so students will be okay in the end.

He thinks that the world owes him something. He is very hard to understand. His test are random; really just educated guesses. Do well in the Lab component to make up for the F's you will get on his test. And yes you will get F's on his test. You also have a quiz in class every time you go. However, he has improved from the last time I took him.

By far the worst class I have taken at KU.  He is a horrible teacher and i only went to class to get quiz points.  I always needed help understanding what he was saying and what was going on so I constantly went to my lab TA for help.  They will all help you out a ton.

This professor was horrible, lectures were of no help. He was very hard to understand and did not know how to teach at the level where students can understand. Tests were very hard and did not relate to lecture. Even TAs were not happy with the way he was teaching. He should not be teaching this course anymore

Wow.  I have never in my life been so bored in a class.  The only reason I went to class was so I could attempt to get some points on the quiz.  Ridiculous tests--everyone fails.  No point in studying.  He did curve, but he acted like he wasn't going to.  Hope he stops teaching soon, since he's the only one who teaches this class.

Worst professor ever.  Tests over material that is not emphasized or covered in class rather than material that is emphasized in lab.  Class avg for midterm and final were failing.  Even the grad student TA's said how they didn't know how to do some of the problems on our tests.  Hopefully he gets denied tenure and has to go work somewhere else.

I have never had any trouble in prior chemistry courses, even o-chem.  But this class is ridiculous even if you study what he gives you and previous tests you are probably still going to fail.  A 25 question comprehensive final, multiple choice... ridiculous.
Eastern European, incomprehensible speaker, uncooperative teacher, rude lecturer

This class was ridiculous. The lectures were very difficult not only to understand but to pay attention to.  The quizzes at the end of class we were allowed to work together on but still no one knew the answer, and the average on the midterm was failing.

He has a very thick Russian accent, so unless you know a lot of Russians, it's impossible to understand him. His lectures make no sense and the quizzes every time are really random and don't have much to do with the actual lectures. Reading material from the O Chem lectures helped me understand what he's talking about in lab...also Wikipedia haha

He can't even finish a sentence in English. This class is useless, but you have to go to take the quizzes which contain none of the material he covered. He's not nice, either. He'll scream at you if you have the wrong colored scantron. It's boring and pointless.
Awesome professor! He was kind and willing to work with you if you had a hard schedule. He was also easy to keep up with and understand what is happening in class. Very nice guy too.

Super chill professor who does a great job applying otherwise boring statistics concepts to real-world examples. He knows the class is a “get it out of the way” requirement but makes it worthwhile and approachable. The grading is very exam- and project-heavy, so staying on top of work matters.

He's literally the best ever. The class is mostly discussion based, and sometimes it can seem like he's getting off topic, but he always relates his stories to what we were learning at the time. He cares about his students and will do whatever is in his power to help you succeed if you ask!

The definition of a king. He's funny, engaging, and an experienced, versatile professor. He encourages discussion and creates an environment that you want to participate in. Highly respected in the SOE, he will help you with literally anything- advising, professional opportunities, etc. Definitely in my top 3 best profs at KU!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was his first semester teaching ethics in class, and he did a great job. He used his own experiences and real life cases to explain topics to us, so every day in lecture was interesting. He is lenient, but loves class engagement (especially laughing at his jokes). I never read really, but was still able to engage in class and homework.

ISP 567 felt like a community as much as it did a class. It felt like everyone in the class genuinely wanted to engage with and learn from the course materials. There's plenty of reading to do every week, but the discussions make it all worth it. The essays were fulfilling and very doable.

what a wonderful human being. just excellent all around and this class goes beyond any type of specific syllabus or outline, we talked about what genuinely mattered in today's world. she gave us opportunities to speak our minds freely and have important conversations, definitely one of the most meaningful classes I've ever taken.

Professor Deer was an amazing professor who made it clear how much she cared about the topics she was teaching and their effect on her students. There were plenty of opportunities for extra credit and to achieve a high grade. I could not recommend her enough!!

Everyone at KU should take WGSS 101 with Professor Deer. Not only does she teach about very important topics, but she does so in a very accessible way. She genuinely cares about her students and I've never felt more comfortable in a classroom. The coursework was very easy yet informative, and there were lots of extra credit opportunities.
I loved her so much! Definitely cares about all her students, even in a large lecture class.

I loved this class. She picked out great reading materials and her lectures were very interesting and engaging. Not assignment heavy, mostly discussion based. Prompts for projects were really interesting to write about, and she allowed creative alternatives to papers. So much extra credit and lots of opportunities. Rly lovely learning environment.

She spends half her lectures looking for input from the class. I got nothing from this class and it was a waste of money. If you're looking for an easy class go for it, but if you're looking to get anything out of it it's not worth your time. She can also be pretty rude sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easy to follow and understand class, lectures are engaging!

Deer is an amazing professor! It's very obvious how knowledgeable she is on the content which makes the lecture more enjoyable. Participation matters more in discussion sessions than during lectures, however. I would take her again in a heartbeat!

I loved taking WGSS! It was really interesting and educational, while not being a massive workload. Although attendance wasn't mandatory, there was pop-up attendance throughout the semester. All quizzes could be taken twice with answers after the first attempt and 3-unit projects through the entire semester. Fantastic class, just participate!
Excellent professor, very passionate about the subjects being discussed and made lectures very easy to understand.

I can not say enough good things about Professor Deer. She makes class lectures super easy to understand and she makes expectations for assignments very clear. The only time participation matters is in the discussion and even then as long as you actually go to class you'll get most of the points.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Deer was an excellent teacher. She is a very understanding and kind person and you can tell she actually cares about what she teaches. She is flexible with deadlines if you are sick and gives several extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Overall, I enjoyed taking her class!
Professor Deer was awesome, caring, and you could tell she cared about the content
Prof. Deer was a wonderful lecturer and a very kind person. She loves to have participation in her lectures, and she made the class feel like an incredibly safe and welcoming space.

Prof. Deer is one of those great professors that really care for their students. If you struggle in her class for whatever reason, she will make an effort to accommodate you. I'd rate her as a 6 if I could!

Prof. Deer is an amazing professor. Her expectations of you are clear, just do the work on time and you'll do fine. I would recommend anyone to take one of her classes. She also offers tons of outside of class extra credit opportunities that are usually really easy, so if you fall behind it's easy to get caught up.
Great Professor, she tells you a lot about her experience as a lawyer and with tribal law. She is laid back, but she expects you to participate. Do the homework! Was a very easy class for me.

I am having a GREAT time in her class. I just switched my major to Law and Society and I like how she makes me think outside the box. She knows how to make class fun and interesting. I am excited to have her for another class!

Prof. Deer is hands-down one of the best professors at KU. She's kind, energetic, and full of wonderful life experience. Without even trying to, she singlehandedly convinced my entire WGSS102 class to either major or minor in WGSS. She's just a really awesome person all-around and I try to take one of her classes every semester.

She is outstanding! This is her first Law & Society course at KU and I'm so glad I took this class! I've learned so much from her & she is focused on making the most of your time. She has many different avenues of teaching that stick with you. Also, as long as you do your work & come to class, receiving a good grade is very easy. Highly recommend!

This professor is very passionate about this course. As a result of such, he requires a lot of work done and expects students to show up. Doesn't cancel class on break weeks either. Expect a lot of work.  There's a group project worth a lot of your grade that lasts for near the entire second half of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: So passionate about what he teaches, really a great professor. whatever you put into the class, he reciprocates
Guy assigned a stupid amount of work for an aviation history gen ed class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of excessive work, incredibly time consuming.

Professor Seyer is very rude and impatient with his students. If you even make a simple mistake in his or take a moment too long to respond to him, he gets angry. I would never take Professor Seyer again, nor would I reccomend any student take his classes. He also grades incredibly harshly, and brags about the class average being C on his exams.
There are multiple readings every week and nearly every assignment is writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: tough grader, yet doesn't explain why you're given poor grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is one of the most knowledgeable professors here. This is a super interesting class that He teaches with passion. Attendance is mandatory and He deliberately DOES NOT put the lecture slides on canvas so students cant afford to miss any class, which IMO is a great tactic as in the end, it benefits you. Exams are easy and he is a very fair grader.

Dr. Seyer is a great professor. He is a great person but will stick straight to the rubric, with very little flexibility on grading. His lectures can get a little boring sometimes but the topics covered in the class are very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My experience with Dr. Steyer was an excellent HIST 101 class with many readings that covered a variety of topics from human prehistory up to the modern day. The readings were always relevant to discussions, lectures, and tests. He was quick to respond to emails, always informed us on changes to the syllabus/schedule, and clarified information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite courses that I've taken at KU. Dr. Seyer did an excellent job teaching the course. Lectures, assignments, and discussions were all thought-provoking. Definitely a 400 level course load, but well worth it if you participate and have a willingness to learn the material.

Taking a class with Seyer is entering a contract. It's signing up for a heavy workload-- to put in significant time, effort, and thought in order to succeed. In return, the class is an extremely intellectually stimulating experience and genuinely enjoyable. 

You get out what you put in, so don't take this class if you're not up for the work.

Let me preface this review by saying that Dr. Seyer's classes are for people who want to learn. Many people have left bad reviews and I can not see why. His classes are interesting and there is never a class where you leave without learning or questioning something new. If you are interested to learn Dr. Seyer's classes are for you.

Dr. Seyer gives great explanations on difficult topics, and clearly lays out what is due and when it is due. He also makes a lot of extra effort to make sure that students are reminded about assignments that they may have forgotten.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Seyer gives clear expectations from day one of class. He cares about students' opinions and wants them to succeed. He is honest when he says that there is a lot of reading and writing, but the amount of work required is to be expected for an upper-level class. He is inclusive and presents his subject from all perspectives.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 10 + hours of reading per week, extremely hard tests, hard grader. hard hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is the worst prof. I have ever had. He will tell you that you have a deep understanding of course material and then give you a 60% on papers with no explanation as to why. He is the worst ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I have taken multiple classes with Dr. Seyer. The theme of his classes seems to be making everything harder than it needs to. Be prepared to write a reflection of a reflection. He is a super punctual grader and replies to emails quickly. Many times an assignment has to be above and beyond to earn a 100%.

With the COVID-19 pandemic we were forced online. Dr. Seyer showed little care about student wellness and actually started assigning more work than usual. The final was assigned a little over a week in advanced which was an 8 page paper while also assigning another paper on stop day. All during finals week. DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASSES WITH HIM!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have ever had in my entire collegiate career. Class was taken during COVID-19; professor was not accessible, showed an utter lack of care/complete disregard for students and their well-being. Only cares publications and departmental reputation. Little to no feedback on assignments; horrible experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It is a hard class, he requires a lot of assignments and doesn't grade "easy", but he grades fairly, he gives all the information you could possibly need to do well so if you put in the work you will do fine. He is also extremely timely and puts comments on any written assignment, & also gives pointers for how to build on it for future assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Apparently Dr Seyer has seen some of the critiques here and adjusted his style accordingly. This class was very well structured, with ample discussion time, and every assignment had a clearly defined grading rubric. Cheap books wise, and he worked with the libraries to get excerpts so we wouldn't need to purchase an abundance of literature.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Not a useful class in any way. Takes off points for using the verb "to be" in any form and can't explain why. Felt like a middle school English class with the grading of a 300 level college course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Non compassionate at all. Participation grades are not specified and quiz grades are never clarified. Choose a different professor unless you want to receive unfair grades. The class is a 100 level class but treated like graduate level grading. I would never take this class again even if it depended on my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It doesn't matter if you fully participate the best you can, there are days when the professor just won't hand out 100% on participation points. It's nice having no exams and only papers, except when the papers are graded harder than papers in any composition class. Even the best writers barely get A's on papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Do not be fooled by the 110 level. This course is lecture, note, and paper heavy. You have to buy at least a dozen of useless books and have to write papers over them that he grades harshly. If you are looking for a class that is an easy A and will satisfy a Humanities credit, do not pick this class because it is my hardest class. Should've dropped
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This was not a 110 level course. This is the only class I have taken that I've never skipped a class and still felt like he expected more out of us all. Do not take if you are looking for an easy course. At the end of every discussion (after writing an hour worth of notes) he makes you answer discussion questions and doesn't allow enough time. NO

The class lectures are incredibly long and Dr. Seyer leaves no time for questions or discussion about the material.  He does not encourage class discussion and instead requires students to take notes for the whole class period. The class requires many interesting and classic sci-fi novels, but unfortunately the course does not do them justice.

He was extremely detailed in his lectures, to the point where there was little time for explanation of concepts. He began grading harshly while trying to fulfill the writing component of the course requirements. His relation of superheros & robots to history was interesting, but the amount of books we had to relate was too difficult to keep up with

To start off, his grading IS not straightforward and it IS not clear what he wants from your papers.  Do not be fooled by the 110 level, it IS more like a 300 level course.  I'm assuming because he IS a new professor he feels the need to prove himself to his dept.  I would not take this course if you are looking for an easy A.
Super kind and makes sure he knows how to make a student feel welcomed.
I loved having Sergio! He gave amazing feedback and really cared about his students. One of my favorites!
Acting 1 was definitely an interesting class.
Didn't overcomplicate this entry-level class. You can tell he cares about making a comfortable class environment, one that's encouraging for people who aren't normally public speakers.

We had a total of 5 formal speeches. The speeches were only 3-5 minutes long, and they were easy. The speeches were graded on participation. This class was easier and more fun than the other KU Core 2.2 class (COMS 130).

Really cool and chill TA. Genuinely cares about creating a safe and comfortable space to deliver speeches. Grade comes just from completion and not speech quality. Class environment motivates you to try and give a good speech.

Love this class and think Sellet is awesome (cool accent too). The rumors are true--there is a 8-10 pg research paper due at the end of the semester which is pretty rough. Downside of this class is that you HAVE to attend class or you will not do well on exams b/c the powerpoints are hard to understand and the textbook is no help (do not buy it).
Dr. Sellet isn't the best lecturer, but he knows what he's talking about and understands that it's a lot of information. If you take good notes and actually study, you'll be just fine.

Sellet has his moments where he is an amazing, engaging professor. However, the study guides and courseload are a lot to manage and oftentimes don't give the best assistance on your exams. Very helpful if you have questions but isn't easily accessible through email, I would recommend going to the TAs first, they are super friendly and helpful!

Generally an extremely easy course. That said, 20% of your grade is a 10-12 page research paper. You will be graded harshly if your research is subpar. You have to do the work on this one. If you hate papers, take a different course. If you don't, lectures are a lot of fun!

GTA had to email all students TWO WEEKS BEFORE DUE DATE that if their final paper had less than 10 pages long, they would be required to take points off. The guidelines provided for the paper IN THE BEGINNING OF THE YEAR stated 8-12 pages. GTAs did not know about this.
Class is pretty light on workload; tests make up majority of grade and they can be semi-difficult. Discussions are easy.

For this to be a 150 class it is way too hard. There is so much information you have to remember. The lectures are long and boring and it is hard to understand him with his accent. Definitely my hardest class and will mess up my GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE HIM UNLESS ABSOLUTELY MANDATORY.

His lectures are very long and hard to follow, but he knows what he is talking about and just wants to share. I really enjoyed his class and found him humorous at times, he knows that his lectures aren't amazing. The TA's do most of the grading and are the most helpful. Take his class, but be prepared to work and read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He goes through the slides very quickly but if you attend lectures and pay attention, the class is not hard. The tests are based on lecture materials and are very short. During discussion, the TA goes over everything that will be on the exam. A 100 point paper is due at the end of the semester, but you get to choose the topic and he grades easy.

During his lectures, he goes incredibly fast through the material so it is hard to get all the notes down. His tests aren't hard, but are short and extremely selective about what material is covered, so studying for them is a must if you want to pass! The tests are 90% of your grade & are entirely lecture based. He "curves" test grades when need be
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Sellet's lectures are the longest, most boring and confusing lectures I've ever heard. My notes are always an absolute mess because his powerpoints are so unorganized. The average test grade is a 65. Do not take this class. There is no way to get anything above a C. & If you're one who skips class, don't take this. Attendance is for points.

Dr. Sellet knows what he is talking about, and enjoys sharing it.  I took this course as an elective and thoroughly enjoyed it.  The tests are multiple choice with a few definitions.  Study guides are given prior to each test.  These are essential.  Fill them out based on notes (he goes fast so be prepared)  and the book, and instant A.

The lectures are interesting, but the TESTS ARE NEVER OVER MATERIAL THAT YOU LEARNED IN CLASS OR THROUGH THE READING. I'm an Honors student and I never take a B, but I have a C in this class. It's ridiculous. I'm disappointed with this course.
The class really isn't that difficult if you attend review sessions and take detailed notes during lectures. Getting an A isn't too difficult if you're good at memorizing details about sites.

He is a respected archaeologist; however, his teaching skills are subpar. His tests were very difficult, his lectures were confusing, and his feedback was sarcastic and unhelpful. Worst of all, he didn't teach key parts of archaeology. His class was more like a history of archaeology sites with some lithic information thrown in. I slaved for my B.

If I could go back in time and untake this class, I would! He didn't learn any of our names although there were only ~12 of us. His slides were practically all pictures--btwn not knowing anything about the subject (INTRO course!) and his accent, it was difficult to take notes. He voices strong opinions, especially about religion, in insulting ways.

Teaching and students are not a priority. The concept of him being wrong about anything is unfathomable to him. His default state is talking down to others, so when he "turns on" sincerity, it is clearly fake and with an ask at the end. Class is mostly busy work, and he misses a lot. His priority is travel and whatever else he has going on.

KU should be ashamed of having this guy on the faculty. There is no way KU SPED is actually the best in the country if Smith is one of the main professors.

Smith is mean, condescending, and prone to emotional outbursts. He has no anger management or social skills. His students end up teaching themselves while doing his research for him.

I've never met a professor so intent upon making themselves appear intelligent while simultaneously maintaining such a staggering amount of both disorganization and disdain for students.

He didn't grade anything until the last two weeks, gave everyone identical feedback, and outright mocked every  answer given in class. 
Expect frustration at best

Sean should not be a professor, he is disrespectful and his assignments make absolutely no sense. He doesn't provide a rubric and always asks for more detail, but never provides actual feedback that's helpful.
An absolutely horrible human being.

I had Sean last year and honestly just wanted to come back to warn everyone. Truly the worst professor in the ed department. Personal life is too closely related to the curriculum so every innocent mistake is treated like a personal attack. Just the worst environment for any classroom. If there's another professor for this class get them. Trust me.

I've never met a man obsessed with making his students do all the work for him.
His forms are 10 years old, his assigned videos are basically unwatchable (240P max, no subtitles), and he has absolutely stuck us with 18 hours of work as a final. I've never met a more "holier than thou" man than Sean Smith.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
He doesn't count you in class if you use virtual.
He has literally given everybody the same feedback on their finals project. Everybody got the same. Feedback. Word for word.
He will make you learn the subject matter yourself, present it to the class, and call it "teaching".
Be prepared to have no grades in the book until big breaks.

Dr. Smith was so egotistical and unaccommodating. He constantly was asking us questions and calling on us randomly but then cut us off while we gave our answers. Who does that? lmao. Such a weird and hostile guy. Would not recommend this class and certainly would not recommend Dr. Smith.

Do not take Professor Smith for this SPED course. He isn't accommodating or understanding and will grade harshly despite circumstances. If you get a bad partner for the group project, you're screwed even if you contact him and explain the situation. You will be the one doing all the work if you want a good grade. He also provides poor feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Never met a teacher with such a big god complex. Thinks his class is the only one that matters. Also calls you out on personal stuff in front of the whole class. Doesn't care about anything you say if it's not what he wants to hear. Scary to think he's been teaching here as long as he has.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I would rather change my major entirely than take this class again. Dr. Smith reminded me how cruel teachers can be when they don't care about their students. Such a mean person. Ruined the class completely. If you have him as a professor do whatever you can to get out of it. Seriously. This is your warning.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I hate Sean Smith. I was so excited for this class and he completely ruined it. He "teaches" his students to be inclusive, kind, and empathetic yet he incorporates none of those traits in his teaching styles. Always interrupts students and has the messiest blackboard site. Also sends 30+ emails a day (like actually 30 or more that's no joke).

Sean Smith is the worst professor I've ever had at KU. Not even that, he's the most disrespectful, condescending, passive-aggressive teacher I've ever had in my LIFE. He embarrasses/bullies his students when they're wrong/confused about anything. Just a terrible excuse for a human being who should NOT be teaching anymore. Hope to see him fired.

Dr. Smith may be the most condescending professor I have met at this school yet. He treats students like they are in middle school, frequently interrupts students, disregards their ideas and opinions, and does not accommodate students' needs well. Worse is the fact that I literally have not learned a single thing in his class.

One of the most genuine, caring professors i've ever had. He's extremely knowledgeable about the content (having personal ties to it), and his lectures are super engaging. He really cares about us as students & future teachers, and wants to see us succeed. He gives consistently good feedback, and if you just put a bit of effort in, you'll get an A!
Interesting course material, engaging lectures, would happily take another class with Dr. Smith

Dr. Smith may not be the greatest professor, but he definitely means well. He's not a hard grader, many of the assignments are easy to understand, and he is always accessible if you have questions. I don't understand why there are so many negative reviews for him, his class was interesting, and having a son with a disability, he knows the topic.

He is quite good at asking simple questions and making them sound ridiculously complex so that you have no idea how to answer it.  He talks to the class like we are five year olds.  My biggest problem is that he is telling us how to teach and how to modify plans for students, but he does NOT model what he teaches at all.

Sean is possibly the most egotistical person I have ever met.  Class discussions are essential a game of "What the hell am I thinking of now?"  Very frustrating and he makes students feel very small.  He also has a habit of asking questions rapidly and then moving on the next person after 2 seconds without waiting for an answer. Very frustrating.

The entire class was on blackboard which I found seriously annoying. When I went to class I didn't feel like I was learning anything. Then he would give us ridiculous online assignments. I felt like the class was a waste of my time.

Other reviews spot on. Absolutely by far the most needlessly difficult class I've ever taken. She is fine as a lecturer, but exams and homework are graded extremely harshly in my opinion, while already being unreasonably difficult.

Would often go over concepts in little detail, failed to emphasize important stuff, which was tested in quiz/HWs. HWs, quiz, exams were way tougher than whatever we had studied in class. Overall the grading is a bit unfair, expectations are not clear from the on-set, but as a teacher she is okay, seemed reasonable enough, listened to feedback

Adds artificial difficulty to every concept, assignment, quiz, and exam. Lectures are unintelligible. Grading is draconian. I took 560 one semester later with a different prof and got a strong A. Her awful class caused me to graduate a semester late and lose my scholarships. Incomprehensible that KU allows someone so terrible at teaching to teach.

IMO, Dr. Shontz does not deserve such a low score. I had her in 560, and her lecture was honestly my favorite that semester (labs were hard). My biggest tip: FOLLOW ALONG AND ANNOTATE SLIDES DURING LECTURE (w iPad or printed slides). Study them WELL and you will be just fine on exams. Did this and scored ~20 pts over the average on each exam.

Dr. Shontz doesn't know mathemtical concepts well, and she gives assignments that are not helpful for quizzes and exams. The worst thing is that she grades harshly, and she doesn't admit that her teaching methods are not helping us. She blames the students and says that the students' learning process has changed after COVID. Worst Math Course.
Horrible.
The worst academic experience of my life

Tests were worth 20% per midterm (2) and final worth 30%. Labs take 10-20 hours and are only worth a small portion of your grade. All tests are graded very harshly: 44/96 people failed the first midterm. Be ready to put in 20-30 hours weekly for this class, and avoid Shontz at all costs. Doesn't take student feedback or criticism at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely learned a lot. Dr. Shontz is not an easy professor. The labs will take you a while, but are graded easily and do not make up a huge part of your grade. Tests not cumulative (including final) which is nice. Also you have to be at class to be able to see her do examples that will 100% be on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty difficult class for just data structures. Felt like EECS 268 on steroids. I did learn a lot in this class, which a lot of other reviewers won't mention a lot of the content was helpful. Labs were long and tough but felt practical. Lecture slides easy to review, and many data structures I now know. Exams are very tough. Exam 1 avg 63.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst educational experience I ever had. Simple topics are made needlessly excruciating and convoluted. So are the labs. Grading is extremely harsh. Lectures are very poor. Just awful all around. If you must take one of her classes, all I can say is prepare for the worst. And good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: awful. just awful. enough to make you want to drop out of college. fairly simple content is made excruciatingly complex. one of if not the poorest taught courses at ku

Class is made complicated for no reason. The concepts are best learned through youtube videos rather than the in - class lectures or labs. Tests are very unfair. Need to avoid this professor at all costs.

The homework assignments and exams have a lot of unwritten expectations, and the labs have a lot of completely artificial difficulty to them that make them far more cumbersome and unnecessarily time-consuming than they should be, and far less educational than they should be. Avoid at all costs.

1. I don't know why we have to attend labs that we have access to the instructions. Students who are confident about some type of data structure shouldn't have to go. Though, It is very helpful, if you don't know much about some structure.
2. Homework and class examples don't match. Have to show *all work for simple calculations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was shocked by the negative reviews but I'm just sitting in on the class (will take later) and I've been very impressed with the lectures. I'm also reading the material in the suggested textbook and the lectures are much more clear and enjoyable. Seems the harsh reviews are because of the exams, not the teaching.

I have never taken a class that was so needlessly difficult and just flat out awful. Quizzes are every week but you will never know exactly what in the world your gonna be quizzed on. Her concept of grading is beyond me she practically gives you no partial credit refusing to show solutions to practice tests. And the project is impossible. Stay away

This was the most needlessly difficult class I've ever taken. There are incredibly few opportunities to actually learn the material. She'll very briefly go over a topic in lecture and expect you to somehow have it mastered for hw/quiz/exams. Extremely stressful and she has unrealistic expectations of her students. Midterm 20%, final 35% of grade
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Shontz likes to make things unnecessarily complicated. She adds extra steps and pieces to data structures, then insists everyone follows her arbitrary conventions on the homework and exams or you'll miss points. The homework and exams are extremely tedious - manually drawing 20+ copies of trees doing operations that we wrote code for in lab.
The worst teacher probly
She tries to avoid giving solutions to questions people have during class. She will do a lot of things before going out of her way to help students

She talks down to her students every chance she gets. Seems like she doesn't care about the students at all and is not understanding at all. She is the worst teacher I have ever had as she thinks of herself as a God that has all the answers and is right all the time.
Does not accommodate differing learning styles whatsoever. As others have said, it's as though information is purposefully obfuscated. You will have points taken away from nowhere.

She doesnt seem like she wants to help students pass the class. She hands out practice exams, but wont give solutions for them. She thinks she is right just because she has a PhD. Talks down onto students. Grades insanely harsh (because she has a PhD and knows everything ofc). Take anyone else if you can
Really terrible. Really Really terrible

Talks down to students who do not understand the material well enough to ask coherent questions. Expects you to have a thorough knowledge of all the material, even stuff she didn't teach. Her "practice exams" are nothing like the actual exams and grades with unwritten rules that drop your grade significantly for tiny mistakes. Not a good professor.

She teaches better than most professors, lectures are worth attending. She was a bit rude over email, but acted fine in class. She doesn't understand what "tentative" means, so don't go off her class schedule (she thinks it's tentative even if the date listed for an assignment is impossible to happen on the calendar - lol). Otherwise, she's alright

Even if you know the material, you will be counted off for arbitrary grading rules she didn't mention. Teaches one thing and expects another on the hw or tests. Problems are *redundantly* large and you need to show every step. She just reads off slides which aren't her own and has trouble explaining them. She has good intentions but still...

Antonio cares about his students, but the class itself was very disorganized. The grading criteria was not clear and he did not grade anything from the semester until finals week. I also do not feel that this class improved my Spanish conversation skills at all. Participation is required, but every class felt very unproductive.

Antonio was very unorganized throughout the semester, and it got worse as we progressed. Instead of creating assignments, he uses discussion boards to turn in homework, which does not appear on the 'Task for Canvas' Google extension. This made it hard to prep for upcoming classes. 48 hours to research and create a presentation isn't enough time.

Prof Simoes is very kind and understanding and he is willing to work with you if you need extra support. However he is possibly the most disorganized professor I have had at KU. There were no lecture slides and it felt like he talked about the same thing every day which made it very hard to know what we were supposed to be doing or learning.

I wouldn't recommend this professor. His class is mostly videos and student presentations, with minimal guidance. Sociolinguistics was taught in a boring and stressful way, and there was little preparation. While lenient when I got sick, you'll mostly be teaching yourself the material. Not well-organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's probably been 15 years since I took his Spanish phonetics course but it's still useful. It probably only took a few sessions to learn his main points. But they're lessons I still apply every time I speak Spanish. People always complement my accent, ask where my parents are from. I'm American!  But thanks to his class, I sound way more native
I never knew what was going on. Homework required work was unclear and there were lots of presentations with little feedback and criteria.

He clearly knows his stuff when it comes to linguistics and the content is not hard. However, this was this most disorganized class I have ever been apart of. He likes to randomly changes the homework calendar and not say it was update or say things in class that don't reflect online instructions. Its also December and I still don't know my grade.

A little unorganized, but I don't think he was supposed to teach this because I was originally signed up with Sean Gullickson. He changed the syllabus weekly, and your grade consists of 2 papers, 2 exams, a presentation, your final, and participation/attendance. He's extremely brilliant, and you can tell how much he loves linguistics vs. history
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The title of this course was "Transatlantic Hispanic Cultures", however Professor Simoes spent a lot of time talking about linguistics, which is another course he teaches. Instructions for projects and assignments were very unclear and his grading style was very confusing. It might be better in person, however online was very confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Kind & not arrogant or unnecessarily political in class like some of the other professors in the department. Fair abt participation. The subject was difficult, not many students had a background in linguistics, but he taught so that progress and good grades were attainable. One critique would be more thorough feedback on the presentations & papers.

I really enjoyed this class. At the beginning of the semester, I felt lost (phonetics is a weird thing), but he explains things really well. The tests aren't too hard, and he grades generously. He's also hilarious, and I enjoyed going to this class more than any other I've taken. He really knows what he's talking about and makes it fun.

I don't think anyone in my class knew what was going on even half the time in class.  It was so disorganized and the material was never really explained in class.  If you hate reading the textbook, you will never be able to pass this class.  He's really cool and a great human being, but it was really difficult to keep up.
He has great command of the language and makes the class interesting. Study hard for the tests and be ready for a lot of group projects.

Prof. Simoes is a great teacher- he's interesting and engaging and knows an incredible amount about his subject. He is the kind of person usually reserved for graduate classes. Strongly recommend him.
He's an okay teacher. Kind of flaky, but a nice guy.
