He's a great guy!  Very nice but his lectures are boring and all over the place.  I think they're hard to follow and confuse me a little.  I don't like the readings but the tests aren't very hard if you just study the review.  I'm not crazy about true-false tests but the review helps so much.

A ridiculously inept and inane lecturer.  Will harp and rehash certain points for about thirty minutes, only to slip in a comment off-handedly that will be on one of his ridiculous, ridiculous 50 question true/false tests.  Takes a long time to get tests back to you as well, even though they are scantrons.
One of the most brilliant minds on the KU campus. A delight in every way.
Brilliant as all get out.
Dr. Smith is a very smart man. He knows so much about sociology, and his lectures are interesting. I loved this class!
i went to class 6 times and got a B. all the test questions are on the internet. just find the answers in the readings and you are set

I thought he was a cute old man.  And yes, he is very boring and the comment about "belaboring" is 100% correct, but I found him endearing.  Tests are easy as hell, so if you can stay awake and if you find charm in old men then go for it.

BORING as can be but easy as can be

He goes off on tirades which pertain to nothing.  He often says  Not to..belabor this point  & then goes over that same point for 20 more minutes. He speaks in monotone. He puts notes on the board that aren't visible. He gives test ?'s ahead of time,
Scatter brained and one of the worst teachers I have ever encountered. Completely unequipped to be teaching students.

reviews.comment: She can't teach and her lectures are completely worthless. She is very unorganized and not helpful. Stay Away!

reviews.comment: Southard could talk for hours and not say anything. She spends so much of her lectures talking about why econ is important that she does not teach us how to do problems. Her online videos are a waste of internet capacity. Her notes are useless. Never thought I'd have to say that a 2-credit econ course would be the hardest class in chem-engineering.

Dr. Southard is seriously unequipped to teach this class. It is clear when the majority of the class receives failing test grades that there is something wrong with the teaching. She should not be allowed to teach this class because neither myself nor any of the many people I have spoken to feel like we have learned a single thing in this class.
Bad. You will be so bored throughout every lecture, that you will stop listening. This will in turn make it so that you don't know what is going on.
Terrible professor for a terrible class. Doesn't know how to teach but the class is mandatory so just study for the tests and watch the videos for the homework and you'll be okay.

Dr. Southard was clearly unable or unwilling to do the necessary work to teach this class. Grades have still not been submitted for a project that was turned in three months ago. I will give her the benefit of the doubt regarding her substantial lack of knowledge over the material because she has not taught this class in many years, if ever. AWFUL.

I felt like I didn't learn anything but still got an A (even though I miserably failed one of the tests). The class had online videos you were supposed to watch before and then she did examples covering the same topics in class-did not like this set-up. I didn't think the videos, book, or in-class examples were helpful. You either "got it" or not.

Posts notes hours or days later than she says she will, sometimes posts notes right before class, says she knows we have more important classes but still gives pop quizes that most people fail, lost one of my hw's and refuesed to respond to any of my emails about it, responded to most others though so I know she got them,

Like many of the comments state, scattered brain, don't plan on getting any sort of response by email. If she says she will get something back to you by blank expect a to add a few more days. One of the worst CPE teachers I've had.
r u kiddng?  u r on ur own in this class.
Great teacher.  Cares a lot and spends lots of time with students helping them understand
Very helpful one on one and the text was useful.

I can't really say it was a hard class because I got an A, but Southard is NOT a good teacher.  She is really scatter-brained, and doesn't do a good job in getting her point across.  She can be helpful if you go see her, but there's a good chance she will give you the completely wrong answer (like she did to me on the final).
one of the worst
shows favortisim, changes grading rules at end of semester

She lost all of our finals, after we took them!  Very disorganized, poor handwriting.  Take Nordhedan, Ostermann, or Green.  One third of the class failed, and 14 students were taking it a second or third time!

Tough grader, sometimes did not reply to emails which made it difficult to communicate because it was an online class. I understand it isn't easy for a professor to reply to every email as soon as possible, but it got somewhat frustrating. Tough grader despite learning how to write speeches as a beginner. The Professor graded very specific. Awful.
Tough grader

Difficult grader for a class for people who are new/trying to learn to give speeches. 
Felt like no matter how hard I tried I was set up to get a low score despite pouring hours and days into a piece. 
As a half-sem online class its fast, which is acceptable. However, as an introductory class to speeches, this class was extremely discouraging.

Spencer is legitimately one of the main motivators in me continuing my degree. When I felt exhausted and disheartened, he kept me engaged and interested in my education. The class is not easy, but I learned a ton and absolutely loved it. He encouraged me a lot in my semester and I wish him nothing but the best
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Spencer is a wonderful TA- I would happily take another class from them! Spencer truly cares about students and explains concepts extremely well. They are a pretty easy grader and will usually give you full marks if you do the work and participate.

Spencer is excellent at what he does and did a fantastic job reinforcing the concepts in the lectures into simulations and discussions. He is an understanding individual and gives clear instructions. He made this class enjoyable and easy to understand when I was confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love Spencer! He taught the discussion portion of my international politics class and was amazing. He is truly a good person who cares about his students, and hes incredibly smart (without being pretentious). He always knows what hes talking about and answers questions clearly and easily. Keep up with the textbook if you want to impress him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: My class didnt want to participate and he some how got use to. I think Spencer cares a lot about his students and he met with me multiple times this semester to help me on papers and understanding readings. The best part of the class was he gave tips on how to write and made me a better writer. There were three papers. Nice and funny.

Smart and funny. He likes to make you learn through filling in the blanks during discussion. Mixed it up with in class debate and had good meetings outside class. He also teaches how to look at things instead of telling you how he feels.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The absolute GOAT. Julien is very laid back and takes a vested interest in the fact that you understand the course and the material. If you put in even the slightest effort I promise he'll give you an A. Just an incredible professor.

This professor was so helpful and the material was readily accessible. He was also available outside of class. I emailed him a question and he called me! I was so shocked by happy he cared that much about my question. I would absolutely recommend taking classes caught by Julien Sperling.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's a super nice and understanding professor. Doesn't make class too difficult and really cares if you understand the topics or not. Highly recommend taking a class with him.

Great professor! I went into COMS dreading the course but he made it super fun. He did a good job at getting the class to know one another so we all became really good friends which made giving speeches so much easier. He is really understanding and wants you to succeed in the course.
Awful

Attendance is mandatory with little consideration for any outstanding circumstances. The majority of lecture time she spends explaining concepts of mindfulness, rather than the class topic. I was expecting and hoping for a lot from this course, but do not feel like I have learned anything from her actual lectures. All learning is from reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is an excellent. Be prepared to learn and work for it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dan is an awesome professor. He's one of the few professors I've had at KU that truly wants to see his students succeed. If you do the reading and take notes, then he lets you use them on the test. Although this is a lot of reading every single night, it definitely helps come final time. Overall great guy, gave extra credit for showing up to class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Such a cute professor.  He truly cares about his students.  His homework each night is a little excessive but you get to use the notes on the exams.  The exams are essay questions.  Work in the same group everyday, it is crucial to get a good group, attend class, and participate.  Class was boring but loved him.

Gives extra credit if you aren't tardy or miss any classes which really helps final grade. Tests are easy if you prepared the notes. Exams graded on reading every exam then assigning grade based on how well you did compared to class (basically just have to beat the class scores). If you get put in a bad team good luck. Overall I enjoyed this class.

I would not recommend taking this. It's not a "hard" class but there's plenty of busy work and he's not helpful at all. He basically gives you a syllabus, has you evaluate yourself each class in a 2 pg single space paper, then grades it harshly, and has you lead discussions about it.

yah the notes suck, but it atleast takes some of the weight off of the exams (good thing). If you go to class, participate,  and take good notes the night before you should get nothing lower than a B in this class. Exams are very difficult but as long as you do everything else right you will still have a shot at an A.  Notes will make or break you.
He is inconsiderate and wouldn't bump me up the points he took away for a tardy when it never even happened. The homework is very extensive and he is basically not easy to work with.

For summer section, this class will be your worst nightmare -.- !!!! Each night, you have to read about 40-50 pages and take NOTE (I and my teammate spend at least 4 hrs to make one note each night). I also have no idea what the test would be like before I take the test. I don't think his way of teaching is effective (but apparently he thinks so !)

There is A LOT of work in this class. The test is just essay questions which is are alright but there is so much information  you could write but only have a few lines to express your ideas. Hopefully you write down what he was looking for. The HW in this class is insane (single spaced,8 font, front and back notes, each night)
No Comments
Very easy grader

If you are a male student, DO NOT TAKE ANY OF HER CLASSES. She is the biggest feminist I have ever met. Also, get ready to read 20 pages of articles twice a week. Hope you like group projects, because your grade will depend on it.
Very engaged and passionate professor. If you don't slack you'll get along great with her as she appreciates effort. Very good for intro to research.

She is annoying.. Doesn't give clear instructions at all and thinks she is always right. Quizzes were easy but I hated this class. She is a hard grader and I didn't understand how to do the projects even after asking for help. I learned nothing and this class was a total waste of my time!!!

Extremely intelligent and passionate about teaching. Very happy to help outside of class as long as you put forth some effort. The course is somewhat challenging but you learn so much; a good teacher should push you. I wish I could take another class from her, she's a wonderful role model for anyone who wants to be a successful professional!

Prof. Sprague is an engaging woman provided the student is willing to engage with her.  She provided useful commentary to the texts and encouraged student exploration of the material.  The final paper was difficult, but it taught me so much!  Great class!
She actually made it fun sometimes
She is a bit egotistic domineering, and conceited if you have an idea of your own.  She seems to think she knows all.

I think that she tried her best to help out the students.  She gave us several opportunities to do well on the exams.  There is a great emphasis on the final assignment, but not clear explanation.  Overall, good class and professor.

This class was not very difficult.  She gave many test re-take opportunities and homework re-dos.  Professor Sprague was not very clear in a lot of her explanations and then wondered why most did bad on the tests.  She tries to come off as frinedly and helpful, but I found her to be neither.
Very confusing, comes off as being fair but isn't, can be interesting but is VERY liberal and doesn't like anyone that is not.

This teacher is a crazy feminist and obviously has a problem with male students (particularly with Crime and Delinquency Students). She categorizes (stereotypes) all of the male C&D students and assumes that we are a bunch of Bush loving conservatives. For someone who is against oppression, she sure tries to oppress the male students in her class.
Amazing and kind professor.

Karthik is maybe the best teacher I've had in the B school. The content is tough, but he will slow down if you need further clarification on concepts. He is very accessible outside class and offers plenty of opportunities to improve your grade if you show that you care. Pop quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Respected--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You'll learn database structures and Oracle SQL. The professor is passionate and caring, though sometimes hard to follow. Office hours helped clarify things. He's a clear communicator about grading and expectations. My group project was difficult due to poor communication, but the professor was understanding and gave me different options for work.

Genuinely wants you to learn in his class! Lectures can be long, but I learned alot about SQL and data relations. Weekly online quizzes, and 4 major assignments throughout course. Offered xtra credit, and let us resubmit assignments to get points back. The big part of your grade is the group project, get started ASAP.
The professor is really helpful and focuses on learning things.
No complaints. He does hound on participation but very straightforward exams and feedback. You can approach him with any grading questions.
He is a nice professor and walks you through a lot of SQL. You will enjoy this course.

Karthik has been my favorite BSAN professor that I have had at KU. He wants students to understand what he's teaching and works with them however he can. I got a low grade on a exam & he allowed me to get back my points by completing modules on Data Camp. Not only did it flip my grade around, but it gave me a understanding on what I struggled with.

Professor Karthik was very helpful and understanding. If you do all your assignments and attend classes, you will be fine. There are in-class quizzes that include submissions of the work done in class. There are 2 exams, pretty easy in my opinion but if you have trouble understanding anything, professor Karthik uploads his lectures to canvas.

Very enthusiastic about teaching and his students. He's a super nice guy and he is very lenient with grading. His lectures can get dry, but everything he teaches is practical and easy to learn. There is a lot of group work, and these are your best study materials for exams.
She's very nice and easy to learn with.
she is so kind and and is so smart, there really is no one better to be a GTA then her
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I didnt have Sungmin for any of my classes but she was always in the math help room and is, by far, the best GTA in there. Shes extremely intelligent, always cheerful, and genuinly wants to help. If I could have attended her lab instead of mine, I wouldve. If youre reading this Sungmin, thank you for all the help over the semester! Youre the best!

Sungmin is so kind, and always took extra time to help me, even outside of class.  She will never make you feel dumb about asking a question, and can explain concepts in many ways.  I loved how hands-on her lab sections were, where everyone could work problems out on the boards.  If I could take another course from her, I would!

The class itself was good and the professor clearly knows the subject well, but grading can be nit-picky. I earned strong grades but still lost points for being “too thorough” and for going slightly over the page length on a rationale. Follow the instructions and page limits exactly. More detail is not always rewarded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I LOVE this professor; she is so nice and super sweet! I had her for CRIM 300 online, and she made everything clear. Now, she did assign a lot of homework, but it was expected because it was an 8-week course. She quickly responds to emails or texts and always reminds the class when work is due. I'm a psych major, and I enjoyed this class. TAKE IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a great professor and KIND person. She replied to my messages right away and even lets her students text her. She cares about her students. Her homework is a bit different than other professors', but not in a bad way. Grades things in a timely matter. I definitely recommend her.
An amazing professor, would 100% take this class again. Any issues I had she would answer my email right away or the next morning.
Lectures are not helpful because she just goes through the slides and adds nothing. I skipped every class after the midterm and learned it all on my own right before the final and did fine.

She is late to class, or cancels it, more often than she is on time.  No textbook, only slides that are very wordy and often confusing.  She will talk circles around a concept, without ever getting to the point.  No homework, only graded on exams and labs.  She seems like a nice person, but I'm having a hard time learning anything in her class.

Easy, Very boring, learned nothing (like other graduate data science classes). Would give us 10 mins for a 30 sec problem. Over-explained simple things. 
She also doesn't allow people to use the bathroom during (1 hour long) exams, and if you do leave she deducts 20 minutes off your time. 
She is often late to class and takes longer to set up.

I took SLAV 320 with her and it is my favorite english class I have ever taken, I love the format in which it is taught and think I learned way more than I would have in a traditional class, I would highly reccomend.

Wonderful professor, but the course is very challenging. Get ready to read... Even with thorough reading, the content is extremely dense and heavy. She is very particular about grading and what she wants but doesn't explain it well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very nice and helpful. Class consisted of reading graphic novels, doing some discussion boards, journal entries, and writing two 3-4 page papers. She grades extremely easy. I got 100% on every single assignment (except the intro quiz) and I was only giving half of my usual effort by the end of the semester. I learned a lot in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Be prepared to learn and work!

Was the teacher that had my back during a really rough semester. He saw how I liked to work and worked with me on it while still challenging me to step outside my comfort zone. He was passionate about his work, caring, and a little bit of oldie, but nothing that got in the way of teaching.

He's the best professor I've met in KU so far, the course he gave is inspirational that make you think in the way you haven't been in. He doesn't give any homework basically, the only work needs to be done outside of the class if the mid&final project, and it's simple to finish. If you are interested/major in art, don't hesitate to take his class.

Jon Swindell has incredible knowledge about rendering figure and form which translates well when he gives feedback about work. Unfortunately, Swindell tends to be often condescending towards younger generations and quick to publicly belittle students. Because of this, I found his attitude to be insufferable and devoid of academic value.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: 3-d design in 1995. Saying he was inspirational; understatement. He challenged and encouraged my creativity and my passion for art even-especially-when I thought I was out of my element. 22 years later I'm not a designer, I'm a commercial photographer and my work has taken me throughout the world and I've been published globally. Thanks, JS.

HE'S AWESOME. He really is. As long as you show improvement and genuinely want to learn from him (because he's the best), you will pass with flying colors. Really listen to what he has to say because he is a master of drawing. Ask him to show you his drawings from HS and then judge him, bc you will understand his love of art and why he critiques u.

He's been teaching forever so he really knows what he's doing. Learn the anatomy. He won't sugar coat his comments but his main concern is seeing everyone develop so he'll tailor his critique to your skill level.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Out of 15 or so students I was one of three to get an A. I only got an A- because I skipped a few classes.  You really have to work for it. He can tell if you're actively trying or just going with the wind and your grade will show for it. He's a quirky guy who likes to rant sometimes.  Upside - no homework except the final portfolio.

Amazing. I constantly improve as his student. Some students don't want to break from their comfort zone or put in the effort. THEIR problem. Yes, drawing is hard, but I see EVERYONE in his class develop and take away something. If your mind is open to self-improvement, you will see growth too. He grades on growth, not on a mastery of the subject.

He's knowledgable and you learn a lot. But the class extremely difficult, and he expects more than possible from students who give it their all, some how their very best is still not enough. I don't recommend unless you are the next da vinci.

Jon (not JOHN) Swindell is one of the best teachers i've ever had. He's been teaching for 40 years, and it shows. He's only attentive if you are trying. He will not hesitate to tell you what you are doing wrong, and he won't coddle your ego. I got a huge scholarship because of the drawings i did in his class.

I thought he was okay.  I felt like he picked favorites in the class, and I never really got any one-on-one help.  He was definitely passionate about art though, and I thought that was nice.  I just really felt like he wanted us all to be exactly like him in the way we draw, and I'm not a fan of that.
Jon changed my life and opened my eyes to the influence of design, color, and symbolism. Without Jon's kind and stern guidance I doubt I would have found the success I have in my career.

He was an amazing professor who will push you and give you honest criticism, but will also help you figure out what direction you want to take in the design process. If you want to be inspired and pushed toward being a stronger, more introspective artist and designer, he is the one you  want.

If you like to be creatively challenged, John's class will do that. You will learn about not just art, but about life in general.  John totally changed my perspective and led me to follow my passions and dreams. Don't go into this class if you can't handle criticism.  In fact you probably should not go into art or design at all if you can't take it

Had him for design 2 and I hated every sec I was in his class room! He made you feel stupid and made sure the whole class knew when you screwed up. If you don't think like him you're screwed. He made my life hell and I never want to do design again because of him. DO NOT have him as a teacher!!!!
He is a really hard teacher, but you will learn so much that its worth it!  Its one of my favorite classes I've EVER taken.
No Comments
fabulous! you learn so much!
He may seem a little crazy, but he just wants you to get out of the box.  His grading is incredibly easy.

Don't take this class unless you can handle it. John can be intense and hard to understand at times, but he knows what he is doing and this class will change your propsective. This man earned tenure for a reason and he should be respected. He can also be a huge help to you once you leave his class as well.
No Comments
No Comments
I hated this class and thought John was, regardless of design intellect, ignorant and a jerk. But somehow, even though my projects sucked I got a B in the class. So there is hope.
most people in my class didn't enjoy this course...maybe it was because this professor was so negative.
you love him or hate him, but he is really passionate about his ideas. It's a good class if you want to get really involved in art and think outside the box.
No Comments

With Swindell you have to be able to think outside the box. He likes it when people break the rules and "go crazy" in terms of projects. He is a teacher who expects creativity and he values process over final product. Some people didn't like his class because they thought the projects were too ambiguous, but if you work hard you can get an A.

Professsor Marshall is such an amazing professor and really cares about her students. She wants you to succeed and will work with you outside of class. This class was easy with our final being a final project, and Professor Marshall gave extra credit opportunities as well. I am looking forward to taking another psych class with her!

I loved having Dr. Marshall! She is an absolute delight, and really cares for her students. Her lectures are always entertaining and she takes student feedback seriously so as to improve her classes even more. Lovely person, would recommend taking a class from her!

Super fun class, kind of overwhelming at first but once you start doing the work you get into a groove. There was a lot of reading but not wayyy more than other class. Super fun lectures, hopefully I get a class with her again.
Dr. Marshall is awesome!! She is always understanding of people's time and priorities. She is a very fair grader and truly cares about her students.
She created a great learning environment! She includes lots of real life examples in her engaging lectures and communicates well.
Dr. Marshall was a great professor with very interesting lectures (and interactive). There were only 3-5 assignments per week and it only met 2/3 days a week!

Good professor. For this class just attend and participate and you'll be fine. I was sick and had a lot going on throughout this past semester, however, if I just put in a little bit more effort I would've gotten an A. Loved the class and was taught well. A lot of weekly assignments(~7). Met once a week not twice. Overall amazing class and prof.
very nice and will work with you. you can tell she's a psych teacher bc she actually cares. we had one group project and she helped make sure every group had all members participating equally

She is very good, and offers a lot of support in the class. It consists of a HIP project, but it is simplistic. The class has a lot of homework, but it is not hard. The exams are taken on respondus lockdown browser now.
I enjoyed Dr. Marshall as a professor and her class was easy enough. She was very readily available for questions in and out of class.

She is a great professor; she is nice and understanding and gives you a fairly good amount of extra credit for the class. The class is pretty easy if you come to the lecture and the tests are not that hard.
I've taken multiple classes with this professor and she's amazing every time. Her lectures are always interesting and interactive and she offers lots of late work opportunities to get a better grade.

Go to class, turn in your three weekly assignments, submit discussions on time and its an EASY A. Open note tests and quizzes. Easy assignments. Gives "late work credit" that you can either use on assignments or if you don't use it it bumps your end grade up 1%. Funny, understanding, and interesting. Take this class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Marshall is a fun professor that likes to use a lot of demonstrations and activities to teach concepts in an interesting way. Most of your grade is completion-based, so as long as you put in the work you will get a good grade. She is super friendly and helpful in person and truly wants you to succeed.
I loved the class and the content, I will say though the exams are comprehensive and application based on the material she teaches.
amazing

Class is pretty easy. The grades are distributed reasonably and there are lots of opportunities for extra credit. There is a good amount of reading involved, but you can get away with reading it last minute. You technically don't have to go to every lecture, but she is looking to make attendance mandatory in the future. She's very helpful and nice!

She was a really great professor with interesting lectures and easy to get in contact with/flexible. All the test are online they are somewhat difficult. There are a couple homework assignments each week that are not very time consuming. I would take a class with her again for sure.

Dr. Marshall is literally an angel. She is by far the best professor I have had at KU so far. She actually cares about her students, and truly wants everyone to succeed! The classwork isn't too hard as long as you go to class and participate. Please please please take any class with her, I promise you will enjoy it and have a great time!

Shes a great professor. A lot of her grades are literally participation for coming to class and busy work. It isn't hard what so ever and she is willing to help you if you are struggling. She is not much of a stickler about attendance, she doesn't expect an excused note if you miss class as long as you let her know. She's great.
Dr. Marshal is super nice, and her lectures are super fun. She gives many extra credit opportunities as long as you come to class and pay attention. Please take any class with her.

Great at giving feedback and responding to emails and questions. Professor Marshall cares about her students and understands that college is difficult and is willing to work with you for deadlines and for extra help. Lectures really clarify the Pre-Work for every chapter. Unit tests aren't difficult if you do the Pre-Work and attend lectures.
Such an amazing professor! You can tell how much she cares about her students and the material she teaches!
Great professor, cares about material and students, 10/10 would take her again.

Professor Marshall was amazing! She ACTUALLY cares about each of her students and made PSYC 105 very enjoyable. This class has a lot of work, but none of it is that hard. As long as you stay on top of it, the class is very manageable and interesting. Definitely take advantage of professor Marshall's help and support, teachers like her are rare.
I'd take this lady again, she actually gives a crap about ya!
This teacher was really nice. I have respect for her and honestly do wish her the best.

Super personable and upbeat which makes lecture all the more interesting, which is very important to show up to for both a grade and content. Lots of extra credit opportunities but also a decently-sized workload so be sure to stay on top of all assignments. Exams can be hard if you dont prepare, even if you think youre set, so make sure to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Love her! Took 210 with her as well. Shes very nice and funny and gives great lectures. There is lots of homework for the class, but for most of it you get credit just for doing it. Participation is also important as well. She lets you bring a sheet of notes to each exam which is very helpful. As long as you do the work, you should be fine.

Very understanding of life events (we got lots of snow the day before the final, so she made it optional :')) Her lectures were easy to understand and aside from some technical difficulties, thorough explanation of cognitive psychology. The examples she gives in class are memorable for exams. 10/10

Dr. Marshall is the best professor I have ever had! Her lectures are engaging, she offers contribution for attendance, and has a point of extra credit on all exams. She's very accessible if you need help for office hours. I also had her for PSYC210 (stats) & she was amazing. She really cares about her students and learning the material. She's great

Dr. Marshall was probably one of the best teachers I've had so far, she makes the class interesting and even better you mostly likely will end up an A afterward. She even cancels classes very few weeks on Fridays. 10/10 teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Marshall is the best teacher I have ever had. One of the most caring and intelligent people ever. Class wasnt too hard, but I put that on Dr. Marshalls incredible ability to help you understand the material.

I was nervous about taking a math related class but Professor Marshall made the topic a lot more manageable. Reading the book I was often confused, but her lectures made things easier. For the tests, made sure to focus on the concept questions too, Theres a group project worth 20% of your grade, which is pretty stressful. Use her office hours!
Dr. Marshall is such a great professor and a great person. She is so knowledgable and was always willing to help. Go to class and make a bomb cheat sheet for every test and you'll easily get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Marshall is the best professor I've had in college. Her class is an easy A, just because she cares more about her students learning the material rather than focusing on a grade. She cares about her students and is always available to help. Her lectures are engaging and assignments are easy and help to understand content.

Dr. Marshall was an amazing professor. It is a hybrid class and there is quite a bit of online homework which was time-consuming, but it was all the same as the regular version. She was not a particularly hard grader on essays and made the class very engaging. Definitely take the class, easy A especially in an honors version!!

Dr. Marshall was such a great professor. I took this instead of normal stats because it seemed more interesting and applied. The class was easy as long as you show up and do the homework. Tests weren't too bad and no final, just a group project that was presented during finals week. Great class overall and highly recommend Dr. Marshall.

Such a competent & fun person. Psyc 105 was incredibly easy--all you have to do is show up & do the hybrid assignments on time. Group projects were painless & replaced an essay and a traditional final. Take her classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--Would take again

reviews.comment: I loved having Susan as my Psyc 104 teacher. She was very helpful and flexible. The material was somewhat difficult and the tests are HARD. I took the hybrid version and the class only met once a week. If you skipped, it wasn't the end of the world. Most of the material you learned is in the book and all powerpoints are put online.
Very hard class.  Not sure if it was because it was online, but it took hours and hours or reading material to make since of the book.

The material in this class is fairly dense at times, but Dr. Marshall makes it understandable. The course is structured the same way as her online course, therefore I stopped going to lectures after the midterm and still made an A. Lots of quizes and writing assignments. Midterm and final are kind of difficult.

The most helpful thing I did to do well on the online exams was to save all of the quizzes. Many of the questions are exactly the same. Be sure to save them right after you take them because the quizzes do disappear. I took screen shots and printed them.

Susan is an interesting lecturer and enjoys the material she teaches. Expect 9 assignments, 10 quizzes, and 4 exams. Be in class, take good notes, read the text, and you should do well. My only complaint were the exams. They are online, 60 questions in 45 minutes. I focused more on the time limit than the material. It was a bit frustrating.

Cognitive psyc is her speciality, and she knows it thoroughly! She's also very good at explaining info so it's easily understandable. Tests are difficult, not because of content but because of the extremely unreasonable time limit and format: tests are online, 60 questions in 45 min, one question at a time that must be answered to advance and you are unable to go back! I would have a much better grade if I could read the test questions faster but the test times out and locks you out. Frustrating

If you attend class, easy A and no reason to buy the textbook. I didn't use it more than once. 4 tests, multiple choice w/ essay, non-cum.  One easy homework assignment.    She sometimes gives easy points for going to class.  Grades curved at end of semester.  Also, she lets class out 15 to 20 minutes early almost every time.

Her powerpoints are great and she posts them all on blackboard. Attend and pay attention to all the lectures and read the chapter in the textbook every week like you're supposed to and you'll definitely get an A!

Easy class.  She flows really well with her powerpoints.  if you go and listen and just study the powerpoints you can get a good grade.  I recommend taking this class because it is interesting and she is smokin ;)

Best teacher that I have had in college so far. Very organized, and ensures that students understand concepts before moving on to new material; also, integrates great examples into her lectures. I especially liked that she repeated questions that were asked before answering them.

Great teacher. All power point slides, posts them online. No attendance requirement, though the information can be confusing if you just look at the slides and don't go to class. She puts the test grades up same day. Real straight forward. Definitely take if looking for a psyc 300+ class.

The class wasn't very well organized, but the professor was nice. The lectures were quite boring as well, and there is no in-class engagement at all. The slides were pretty detailed, and it was enough to do well on the exams. It was a great course for the summer, very manageable.

A great prof for summer genetics. His explanations were thorough, he was approachable, clearly defined what would come up on exams, and the discussion and homework problems were similar to his exams. The tests were very fair. He's funny and very understanding, some lectures can be fairly heavy but he posts everything to Canvas. Memorization heavy.
He seems like a great guy but his teaching style is inferior. No in-class engagement, just him talking through basic slides with the expectation that we remember everything for each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Swanson is an absolute delight to have as a professor. Truthfully, I sucked at the laws of phonetics, but she never made me feel stupid and only saw my room for improvement.

Dr. Swanson is a very caring teacher who wants you to succeed. She is super fun in lectures and only gives homework that is meant to help you succeed. This isn't an easy course, however, she tries to give you all of the resources you will need to be able to perform your best. I highly recommend taking her course.

I cannot say enough good things about Prof. Swanson! She has been my favorite professor, and 310 has been one of my favorite classes! She really works with you to improve your French in a way that is constructive, and I saw my fluency improve so much after her class. She is amazing and seems to genuinely care for each of her students!

Professor Swanson is by far the best professor I have had at KU. She cares deeply for us as people, as well as if we understand the subject matter. She's super sweet, I definitely recommend FREN 310, Phonetics!! She also plays Cold Play in class, so extra points there too. Be sure to participate in class, though.

Professor Swanson is great. She is really passionate about phonetics which makes the class even better. She is always there to explain concepts that you don't understand. If you study and improve, you will get a good grade. I definitely recommend Prof Swanson!!
Very nice, open and friendly with students. Felt comfortable asking questions in class. Explains things well. Homework is near-constant but not overly time-consuming and prepares you well for tests.
She is extremely helpful and the class never feels boring despite it being every day. If you study for the tests and do the homework you should get an A or a B, easily.

Micheal is who we really can call teacher. He's always there to help you, and also, his lectures are really helpful and funny. He always comes prepared and with a dose of motivation. Totally approved!
Michael is an awesome teacher!! He is always available to help outside class. He is a brilliant teacher.

Micheal wasn't just my teacher , he was more than brother , he helped me and my class mates in everything we need. We used to deal with him as a best friend  or old brother. He helped us  to get high scores in the proficiency exam by teaching and giving us some important tips. Hope to see him again.
He is very good teacher. I like to have another class with him. He is awesom.

It was the best class and teacher that I've already taken. The teacher is really amazing, he always came prepared to the class, and brought useful. Also, his class was hilarious, he teaches very well and clearly. As well, he always invited us to eat in his house,  and gave us several extra classes that was crucial for us in the proficiency test.

Michael became a true friend. He always helped us with everything we could, in and out of class. He did everything to make fun and interesting class. I'll miss him! He was my best teacher and it was my best class, for sure!
He is an outstanding teacher. He is SOOO much clearer than the book, and makes the class way easier.

Great professor. Tests and homework were fair. lectures didn't drag on. He had a little bit of humor. Frequently would ask if we had questions in the middle of his lecture. All around a great guy. You didn't have to read the textbook, but the hw was there.
Take any classes taught by him is a good choice, you will understand almost everything he mention on class, very clear. Exams are based on HWs, and HW are based on Class notes.

This is a class that COMPUTER SCIENCE students take, and yet nothing is posted online. He doesn't even have lecture slides, he just handwrites on a chalk board like we're in 1960. But he tells you pretty much what's going to be on a test but if you don't have all the handouts, you're screwed. He gives all handouts and HW in class on paper
Clear and concise lecturer. excellent professor
He is a very easy grader and teacher in general. Wants the students to focus on learning than the grades.

His lectures are very easy to understand, and he is very approachable with a good sense of humor. He cares very much about the students and waits until everyone understands the material before moving on. He also gives several examples for each new subject. I would highly recommend taking his class.

Extremely easy class. Informative lectures, easy to do assignments. Labs were a breeze. Final exam was take-home. In the review discusses pretty much everything that's on the test. I'd recommend his class to everyone!

tries to make everything as simple as possible. seems to actually care about his students & is very open during office hours for extra help. basically all the material was covered in lecture. outside reading (like in textbook) was unnecessary. not much homework. class very straightforward, but a bit slow & easy; not much material was covered really

Amazing professor. He was very good at teaching all the concepts. Attendance is not mandatory, but I took it more seriously than any other class that semester. He is also a nice and very helpful guy. I strongly suggest anyone to take his class.

He is a great teacher. Compared to all other teacher who teach 140, Dr. Chakrabarti is extremely clear and very helpful. All you have to do is SHOW UP to class. His lectures are easy to understand, he gives a review before the test which pretty much states almost the same problems on the test. He will go over it and if you pay attention, its easy.
He is a fantastic teacher who is very approachable for a first semester Freshman. I hope I can take another one of his class while at KU.

Chakrabarti is a fantastic teacher. His class was a breeze so long as you went to class and weren't asleep...which would be hard anyway because his classes are so engaging. I got an A in his class hardly touching the book, except merely for reference of a few things I was foggy on during the homework assignments.
He really knows his stuff and is even better at explaining it in a clear concise way.  Should be a spokesperson for sprite.

I love this guy, especially after grading for him. He knows how to lecture, how to create homework assignments and tests, and how to clearly explain complicated concepts. Plus, he has some of the funniest tendencies I've ever seen.

Great teacher. Textbook is required for the homework assignments, unless you have a friend you can share textbooks with. Take notes on paper - a laptop won't work here. Too many drawings. Lecture attendance is not "mandatory", but its the most important thing you can do to get an A in the class.

the best professor ever! he makes a quick review at the begining of each lecture so u can remind past material! he is helpful in his office hours and he does not move on until making sure u understand the lesson!!

Very good teacher and has a good sense of humor. You cannot skip class or you will get behind. Very good at laying at notes and as long as you pay attention you should do just fine in the course. Slight accent but it is more funny than a problem in understanding anything.

"The exam is designed so that assuming that you do not take a nap, you will be able to finish it in an hour and a half.  You should not need the full two and a half hours.  If you do, you will have to buy me a doughnut or something."
He tries to make certain that his students understand the material.  He has an accent, but it is not a problem.  He's also funny.
Very good teacher, very clear, enthusiastic and humorous. Who say? Your text book say.
Lectures and notes are key for this class.  He is very helpful and practically begs for students to come by his office for help.  He's a funny guy.
Very good/helpful Professor. If you take notes during class, then you will breeze through his course. He uses lots of examples, and makes sure that you understand the material before moving on.

He is so great!  The guy is very good at explaining things and the class is taught in a straightforward manner. You KNOW that everything you take notes on will be on the next test.  He's also pretty funny in an adorable old man way.

A great teacher. Always willing to help. Speaks very clear English and always goes over difficult points of previous lectures in latter lectures. Use his office hours, he wants to help as long as you will put the work in. A high B/A is easily attainable if you don't miss class/use your time wisely. Reading the book is not necessary.
Interesting class, funny and helpful teacher. I really liked attending his classes.
A very good teacher.  Boring subject but he explains a lot and backs up to repeat things that aren't clear.
Good teacher, but don't plan to bring a notebook computer to class.

Good teacher.  Has an accent but not too difficult to understand.  Usually makes sure the class understands what he's doing before he goes on (doesn't like to go back to previous topics so he makes sure you understand the first time.)  Good at explaining things though, and material not too difficult.  Can get a little boring sometimes though.
teaches everything you want to know
just a perfect teacher..
perfect
Terrific Teacher. Explains everything very clearly.
He begins each lecture with what he ended the previous one with, so it really reinforces the points. His exams aren't too hard, if you've paid attention in class and/or taken good notes.
HE IS THE BEST
Easy and cool.
cool guy
No Comments
No Comments

Rob would take a lecture that could easily be finished within 20-30 minutes but is determined to fill up the remaining 45 minutes by getting off topic, publicly humiliating students in front of their peers, and makes jokes that nobody laughs that but him. I highly suggest to not take his class unless it is the absolute last resort.

This dude sucks. He gives lectures nonsense and then says "if you aren't getting 10 out of 10 on the quizzes it's probably your fault" Like how am I supposed to learn when you talk and rant about the most random stuff ever? It is so unprofessional to get political and will make fun of you for asking a question so do not bother asking any questions.

Bruh just talked about the most random things the entire time, he really did not care that much and was more self centered. The way he got students to "learn" was just laughing at the way they did an assignment or asked a question. Seems like a cool dude, but horrible teacher

He is an awful professor that does not care about his students. He laughs when they ask questions and never answers the questions. I would not recommend him to anyone, He does not answer emails and does not look to have his students succeed. He spends most of the class talking about porn and the bible and makes his students uncomfortable.

Don't take his class if there's any chance to. How this man is a teacher still has me puzzled almost a year after taking his class. All he does is go in front of his classes and talk poorly on other staff members as well as goes on a tangent for his entire class period about completely irrelevant talking. He makes the word, teacher, a joke.
He teaches everything but the syllabus and keeps bullshitting about other topics that are not related to the course. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS, he is not a good professor.

THE WORST PROFESSOR EVER! Be ready to teach yourself everything! This guy laughs at his own jokes the whole class and basically calls you stupid for getting a question wrong. Does not respond to emails and is an extremely unfair grader. SO RUDE and unhelpful on feedback. Loves hearing himself talk and he told me to get over my dog dying.
Best English prof at KU. Equally interesting discussing works you love and ones you don't. Very insightful critic, and really educates well.

I took Dr. Swann's Elizabeth class and LOVED IT. She instilled in me a passion for a subject I never thought I could love. She is difficult but only because she demands a lot of effort; she's extremely clear about that at the start. Don't just go to class, BE EARLY AND PREPARED. Ask questions. Go to office hours. Be INTERESTED. She notices.

I had a traumatic semester in my personal life, and she was always there and more than understanding.  Be prepared to be taught by one of the best KU has to offer. She made me fall in love with the most boring doorstop of a book, and I will always appreciate it.

She has pedigree from the luminous colleges that she has taught at. She is difficult and seemingly immerses herself in her subject matter, so much that she can lose touch with reality and alienate her students. Tons of feedback on your papers, and frankly she is one of the easiest graders that I have ever had. She thinks everyone is a cheater.

One of the most challenging and rewarding classes I've ever taken.  I produced a paper that I'm still very proud of because of her pushing me.  Also, she was very understanding and willing to work with students.

If you want to work really hard and be graded like you are a doctoral candidate, then she is the professor for you. It will also help you enjoy her if you have feminist leanings. I strongly suspect that the diverse reactions to her in her ratings may fall across gender lines. If those things do not dissuade you, then you will learn a lot from her.
Swann has an infections enthusiasm for her subjects.  She will do anything for an interested student.  Be prepared to work.

Very intelligent professor. Helpful and always pleasant IF you are pleasant to her. Just go to class, read your assignments, adhere to her critiques and you'll do fine. She demands effort from you because she puts effort into teaching you.

One of the few english teachers with a good method of teaching, and who is really objective in her grading.  Just do the reading (or read clif notes, except for the papers) and go see her at least once for each paper, and you should get an A

She laughs loudly. She went to Oxford. She's EXTREMELY smart. She's a hard grader (I did some quality work and got B's on both papers). Tough, but fair. Her criticisms were valid. She is willing to offer advise on papers before you turn them in. TAKE ADVANTAGE! Also, show up to class. There are pop-quizes every day and your notes will be priceless.

When someone prides herself on being the most difficult grader in the University, then believe it.  It also means that she is not at always compassionate to students with any real life challenge outside of the classroom.
Interesting lecture, too much reading. She appreciates an effort, which is cool. She is kind of icey, though. You get the feeling that if you slip up, you'll be put on some kind of list.
No Comments

Swann is a genius...  But when she laughs, I wanted to throw myself out a window.  She's really funny though, tells it how it is, and expects a lot out of her students.  She teaches a fun class though, and although the reading was a little steep, I enjoyed myself.  She's fabulous!

I had her for two classes. One of the best teachers ever. I took a second class from her because I liked her shakespeare class so much. However, GO TO CLASS. I didn't and paid for it. She's very tough, but she's very interesting and VERY knowledgable. GOOOO TOOO CLAAASSSSSS. If you really actually LIKE english, take her. if not,don't.

She's excited about her studies, as her LOUD laugh indicates. Swann pats her own back for being reknowned through the department as the "hardest grader" of essays. This is very very true. While she's smart (regularly points out her fellowship at Oxford and time spent teaching at Princeton) and nice enough, it's not worth it. Find someone else.
Amazing teacher.  Endlessly helpful and knowledgable. Be sure to go to class.
She does have the loudest laugh I have ever heard.  This class is easy, I read spark notes the entire time, but she was very rude to me about attending a funeral.
Prof. Swann is very dedicated, hard-working.  She really cares about her students.
kind and generous.  excellent teacher
angry and unpleasant
One of the most amazing professors I've ever had--she was very challenging but I learned a lot

Accused me and about 100 of my other peers of cheating on the midterm exam for using a definition that he gave us in class. I didn't even use his exact words just summarized it on my own and was still accused of cheating. Said we should be grateful that he didn't report us to the academic board. I love him up until this point but was disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Some people are naturally good at teaching, and Dr. Syrett is obviously one of them. He expects academic performance from his students, and makes it clear he views us as actual intellectuals. Dr. Syrett manages the perfect balance of a well organized class, while still coming off as approachable, funny, and kind. His classes are truly gems.

Class isn't mandatory but if you want to do well on tests, show up and put in the effort. The lectures are amazing and Prof. Syrett is funny and is also very passionate about WGSS. One of the best courses I've taken at KU.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures were very engaging and interesting. All the material was easy to follow and I enjoyed the subject. However, TAs grade everything and I felt that grading wasnt always consistent. Be sure to attend lecture and take good notes and this will be an interesting and enjoyable class without too much work outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I liked him but his TA's grade the papers and there is only a few assignments. Take notes because he doesn't upload slides. I would have really enjoyed this class if I had a good TA.
I loved taking his class. Even though there was 150 students he still made it feel welcoming and engaging.

Very knowledgeable & funny professor, lectures are long but contain good information & are very clear. Very willing to answer questions & clarify info/assignments for you. T.A.'s grade papers, so grading will vary depending. Papers are pretty easy & personal. Tests are do-able if you take notes & do the readings.
His lectures are engaging and the material is overall interesting. I would take a class from him again.

Dr. Tappan is a wonderful professor. Super nice and funny, and very understanding. He clearly puts a lot of effort into his lectures. Tests were not hard if you pay attention, a lot of questions are straight from the slides which he posts on Canvas.

Taylor Tappan is truly enthusiastic about his work, I personally enjoyed learning from him! Yes, he does talk A LOT, I recommend using class time to take notes and highlight the most important parts that he talks about on slides/in the textbook as all midterms and finals are online with open notes. Plenty of extra credit & understanding on late HW
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice guy, the midterms are tough but were taken online. Lots of homework and reading assigned, but extra credit opportunities almost every class period. Lectures often were long winded and hard to keep up with, but if you show up, you should get a good grade.

Tappan is very kind and helpful if you approach him with questions, with that being said the amount of homework in the course is kind of ridiculous and the tests are quite difficult. Attendance is not mandatory but if you want a decent grade you need to go.

I like him as a person and he is very nice, but his grading criteria is very inconsistent and unclear. I received 0 feedback on assignments, so I had no way of knowing what I was doing wrong. His tests are also pretty difficult but you have time to prepare. He is very passionate though and there are lots of extra credit opportunities available.

This Professor creates assignments that are just frankly terrible attendance is not mandatory but if you want an A in the class you should definitely go. I'm not sure who grades the assignments but they do not do a great job they are very inconsistent and need a refresher course on how to grade!
Nice guy, not a single lecture actually related to the COPIOUS amount of homework we received.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: I found him to be needlessly long winded in lectures that had little actual content. He had many assignments that were not actually needed nor enhanced my learning. His scheduling of 2 separate midterms was horrible, not only for students, but also his GTA's as they were given hard and quick deadlines to have grades in.

Really great professor, although the course content can be difficult or dense at times, he is a really charismatic guy that explains stuff well and engages with questions well. Even though tests were weighted pretty heavily, they were half open note and half in-group so if you show up to class you should be okay! Good guy, I liked him a lot.
Awful. save yourself and find a different professor for the class. worst teacher i have ever had and if you aren't a favorite you are done for. go take tom or matt's class instead!

Linda is a caring and knowledgeable teacher. She gave me decent feedback often; however, she has a hard time controlling students who speak over her as she is soft-spoken. BDS 101 is a very difficult class due to the large workload and the quality expected, but Linda seems to be a kinder grader than other professors who teach the same class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Linda's a decent professor and has a lot of experience with type and stuff, but is really minimalist with feedback. It's hard to figure out what direction your project is supposed to take when you're not sure what you're working with. She's usually kind with the grades though.
I enjoyed this class a lot, unlike many. If you attended class and tried to do each project, it went well. I wish she gave more feedback, I wasn't always sure what she thought of my projects.

I have had Linda multiple times she is great, if you get your work done and aren't lazy you will do well. She can sense excuses from a mile away so just do what you are supposed to and you will be fine. If you are lazy design isn't for you anyway.
Helpful when you ask.  Unclear and not so up to date on what to do in class. Chooses favorites, so get on her good side. You'll learn a lot from her, but if you can, try another teacher.
Very nice professor, though a bit unorganized.  Wading through a new curriculum didn't help (FA10) but certainly wouldn't advise against her.
Linda is my favorite, I love her and she is so nice and helpful!  Highly recommend her!
I LOVED LINDA. She was great. take the class

Very easy teacher.  strict on craftsmanship, but does indeed play favorites.  i as defineltey one of her favorites, so her class was easy for me.  laid back!  just finish projects by due date, and you're fine
Linda is a great teacher and very caring.  Sometimes scatterbrained, but DEFINITELY worth taking.

I thought she was fun, interesting class.  occasionally takes off points for the hell of it.  very strict on your craftsmanship...but overall...very laid back class, with plenty of freedom.  just get your projects done

I'm not going to lie, she is terrifying at first. But as the  class has progressed, she has become much more understanding and much more helpful. Definetly not as weiner-y as the rest of the Deisng teachers...Minus Professor Swindell...
No Comments

I HAVE NEVER EVER SEEN A TEACHER PLAY FAVORITES LIKE LINDA BEFORE. She may be quite wonderful to you if you were someone she liked, if not... OFF WITH YOUR HEAD. Class is tough, but that's not her, all the design classes have the same projects.

Terrible!!  We had a project due on a monday afternoon.  Linda failed to tell us that we didn't have class, by not e-mailing us or contacting us in any other form.  Whole class was up all nite working on assignment for a total waste.  Very unclear instructions and not helpful.  Steer clear.
She's very demanding but if you're willing to work, you'll learn a lot from her.

Linda is a nice teacher.  she will really go out of her way to help people individually and the class as whole.  people in my class complained that she wasn't good at explaining projects but i didn't see that as a problem.
Super sweet, super helpful. I don't care what you may have heard, Linda is an AWESOME art teacher. She is so understanding too! Definitely take a class from her.

In this class there are no assignments outside of class everything is completed during class time. However the majority, if not all, of your grade is based on exams.The instructor does not clearly outline what will be on the exams.... on the plus side, he occasionally offers random extra credit opportunities during lectures for those present.

Anything you might see on an exam is something he might mention two or three times, sometimes in passing. for the stuff later in the course he poorly went over how it worked and talked more about stuff that wasn't even in the exam rather then extensively explaining it or even reviewing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I learned so much from this class through the online lectures and the TA. Maz was very helpful. He is extremely smart and respectful. I liked how everything was clear from course material to grading criteria. 9 reasoning challenges and 3 exams, lots of group activities. This was by far the best and the most useful class I have ever taken at KU.

The discussions were in person but the lectures were online. Professor symons ' lectures were ok and informative. The GTA- Maz is nice, caring and knowledgeable. This class is not easy but totally manageable if you study 20 pages each week. I loved the concepts in the course and Maz gave many examples and explanations.

This was a hybrid course with discussion in person, and he told us he would come to the class, but we never saw John in person the entire semester. He seemed to trust in the GTA a little too much because we could have used some help from the professor. This class was very difficult considering it is a 100-level course not required for majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this class for my core goal and I loved his teaching techniques. I feel that if you participate enough and showcase your progress, it's really an easy A. Focus is mainly on exams and lots of extra credits during discussions. Textbook is there for reference however going to lectures would suffice. This was the best class I took last fall!
I really loved this class, Prof Symons, and the TA Cole Bruening. This has been my favorite course I've taken at KU thus far. I highly recommend this course and John!

I didn't take intro with him, but he was a guest lecturer when I took PHIL 500 (philosophy abroad in Paris). He wrestled a French homeless man who had been harassing two young women on the metro at 1am on the way back from the Eiffel Tower. You really just had to be there.
John is the only professor who would wrestle hobos for students. Honestly he is very caring and wants the best for his students, work hard and he will reward you with a good grade.

Probably the greatest philosophy professor I have had. Fantastic discussions and lectures. He is really, genuinely engaging. He is a brilliant thinker and knows how to grapple with the topics extremely well. The papers left a lot unsaid about grading, though he graded fairly. Highly recommend if you're serious about learning philosophy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Due to Covid, I was taught this class through the TA for the spring semester. The rubrics for all papers/videos don't matter because the TA graded everything very arbitrarily, never giving feedback for missed points. The lectures very unclear and did not match up with the textbook content, not helpful for weekly quizzes that make up your grade.

If you show up to class every once in a while you should be fine. The TA's are super helpful. Symons is super funny and a little cocky and at times a little confusing. The tests are not bad because it is open textbook. Really easy A.

This class was fully online (COVID 19) and it was okay. I went to this class maybe a total of 5 times during the semester. Professor Symons can be rude to students if he doesnt like their answers, and made me nervous to speak up. He is also very pretentious at times. The tests are not difficult, and I enjoyed reading the textbook.

I took PHIL 148 as a 4 week course and it was brutal. Lots of homework. I genuinely thought I was going to end up with a C in the class. I would recommend taking this class as a regular 14 week class. It's too hard online and it's hard to grasp all of the concepts he teaches in 4 weeks.
He's honestly pretty stuck up but can be interesting. The class is a lot tougher than I expected.

I took his online class over winter break. The syllabus made it look really hard but he's an easy grader from what I've seen as long as you know what you're talking about not to mention that he gives out bonus points on almost every assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures were entertaining at the beginning of the semester but he spends way too much time on truth tables which are easy to understand. Things in the class are not worth a lot of points so if you miss points it will hit your grade hard. Not an easy A elective. Don't buy the book he puts it on Blackbpard
Take 148 in person. It's too hard online. I dropped the class online in summer got an a in the fall.

Took the 4-week online winter section for this course. Definitely should believe the more recent reviews than the earlier ones. Class material at the beginning is easy, however the material at the end is worth a lot and is extremely difficult to understand. The lectures were not helpful and the professor was not either. NOT AN EASY ELECTIVE.

Awful Teacher. The online winter class was just videos of him lecturing for hours and he didn't explain ANYTHING. The homework and tests were near impossible because they did not relate at all to his video lectures. Worst class I've ever taken. I have a 3.7 GPA, so I'm not stupid. Got a D+, but luckily took it credit/no credit. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

This was the hardest class I have ever taken. He just reads the slides and doesn't explain any of the material that he expects us to be able to do. His lectures were terrible he got off topic a lot especially at the beginning of the semester and he would talk about something unrelated for most of the class period.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The class is fairly straight forward. Symons makes the class very enjoyable and adds real world applications. He is funny, but also manages to teach the lesson well. There are 4 "problem sets". Weekly quizzes that are fairly simple.  There are 4 tests. I would take more classes with him if I could.  Easy class and excellent professor.

This class was painfully easy. However, I still attended every lecture with the hope that Symons would quit showing us truth tables again and again and give us some wisdom. I recommend experiencing Symons, but I can't recommend PHIL 148. Started off interesting, but the logic stuff that took two months could've been done in three weeks. Good man.

I loved Professor Symons. He makes coming to class enjoyable with his humor and interaction with students rather than lecturing at them. Overall, if you pay attention in class and try to understand the material, you will. It is important to attend discussions.

PHIL 148 was the biggest waste of time. Never went to lecture, only went to discussion, and got a high A. Prof Symons spends way too much time talking about topics that the class already understands and all assignments are online. No textbook needed

2 midterms worth 15% each, 20% final and a group project worth about 40%. Content is interesting and the lectures are not too bad. Exams are more conceptual and he is generous with partial credit. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I did not have Dr. Hoque in undergrad but I wish I had. His teaching style is engaging and even though I am someone who never loved my hardware courses, I feel like more classes with Dr. Hoque would change my mind. Workload was pretty light, but all assignments had value, and I felt that I learned a lot from them and lecture without undue stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I was able to do well in Tamziduls course, although the lectures aren't the most engaging. If you prefer studying the lecture slides on your own time, I would recommend taking his class

Hoque is a good guy that cares about his students. I thought the class was a little too light. I feel finessed cause I paid for this class and I had to put in very little effort. Sometimes I wish his classes were a little harder. If you actually care about computer architecture material take it with another professor because you won't learn much.

This class was difficult but Professor Hoque is very nice. Both the midterm and final were open note and similar to lectures and review sheets. The lab wasn't too bad and can be difficult to interpret. Good class and professor!

Good professor, not sure why but his lectures were easier to understand than other classes. Easy to get a good grade if you put the work in. Midterm and final are both open note. There's a series of cybersecurity lectures that are very confusing (taught by a TA), other than that, good course. Your lab grade will depend on your TA though.
I had him for 388 and 645. Big chiller. Only thing I hated was them busted ahh RC cars for the final project in 388. 388 was honestly harder than 645. 645 was ridiculously light.

Prof Hoque is a nice guy who gives fair tests, homework and extra credit. The tests are all open note and the questions are pretty close to homework problems/review material. The lectures are a little dense/boring and the lab isn't run the best (old equipment/bad lesson plans), but overall 388 was a solid class.

The content of this course was difficult to understand and the lectures dragged a bit but Professor Hoque is a sweet person and he cares about his students. Exams are open note and almost exact copies of the homework/practice problems. My favorite professor!

I actually don't even know why she didn't like me. She just chose to not like me because I was white. Other than that, her class isn't like super hard but she is hard to read on when she likes you and your assignment.

WGSS 101 was a great class for me when I was a freshman. There are readings, small assignments (ex: discussion boards, reading responses), and a couple papers. Do not confuse her quietness or reserved nature for a lack of experience, she is extremely knowledgeable. Always considerate about accommodations/absences. We even had free days sometimes.

Proceeded to give me a shockingly bad grade on an essay while having a surplus of grammar errors/ incosistencies in her comments on my paper. Essay expectations were unclear and grading style was unreasonably harsh and confusing. Do not reccomend.

No, no and no. Grading criteria was never clear, missing class will tank your grade. Not to mention she is not good at lecturing, always very awkward and non-confident in what she is “teaching.” She grades and teaches like you have a degree in women's studies, avoid taking this class.

The weekly assignments pose biased questions. The instructor also does not plan presentations well, assigning more students to present per day than the class has time to allow. Assignment guidelines are not clear. The instructor does not create a great learning environment for a discussion-based class.

The professor's professional ability could use some work. Their teaching style and ability to convey the material clearly could use a lot of work. She definitely needs to explain the material clearly, could lose the amount you have to read, needs to grade within an appropriate amount of time, and could stand to make instructions clearer.

She is a great professor and made this class very organized. Each week is structured the same with assignments and she will give you great feedback on your work. Just do the assignments and this class will be easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Takikiawa was really caring and easy to get in touch with, she offered easy-to-achieve extra credit and made the class more about understanding the material and student feedback than earning good grades on tests. Would definitely recommend it to anyone needing to fill in their schedule with an interesting elective credit.
, so rude and unaccommodating.

One of the most challenging classes in the LASC school, but he is an outstanding professor, especially if you enjoy philosophy and deep thought through logic. However, if you aren't a philosophy enthusiast, then you should avoid the class, as he will certainly test your skills.

He is a good guy with good intentions but one of the hardest professors I have ever had. If you don't mind reading old texts then this guy is for you. Taking notes is very important with his class, if you write down EVERYTHING he says in class, then you will do fine on all the tests and papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dave Tell is an excellent educator. He is extremely knowledgeable in his field. Professor Tell continues to advance initiatives such as the Emit Till Project which you will learn about. My suggestion? Read! Occasionally it can feel like a lot of reading. However, the readings are some of the most engaging I have ever interacted with!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I received a 4.0 at KU. This class was close to ruining that. Tell's class was an experience. I definitely grew and it gave me the chance to improve as a student. I don't regret taking his class. He is a good teacher and if you want a challenge you should take this class.

Dave's seminar on Memory Studies was my favorite hour each week this semester.
