The material is engaging and intellectually stimulating, and you won't get bored as long as you keep up with readings each week. Absolutely loved this class and would recommend it to anyone who likes to think critically think about history.
He goes on about ancient philosophy and rhetoric that is entirely irrelevant. Tries to come off as a smart intellectual, but just regurgitates old philosophers and doesn't add any original thought.

He is best described as a wannabe. He wants to come off as an intellectual and a serious professor, but he's not. His grading system is based on whether he likes you or not. He'll like you if you talk a lot, even if you have no idea what you're talking about. Didn't learn anything. Pretty easy though.

I could write a short paper on why you should take his class. As long as you're prepared, you'll be just fine. He comes across as cocky sometimes, but just take it in stride. The guy knows his stuff and he just wants you to get as excited about the material as he is. You will learn alot so get ready or else you'l be left behind.

I took 2 of Professor Tell's classes as an undergrad over 3 years ago.  He is one of the 3 professors I remember and I wasn't even a COMS major.  He is an EXCELLENT teacher. Yes, he's a little arrogant,and he values his own opinion a little more than oxygen. Yes, you have to DO THE READING!!!  If you think he's tough, wait until you have a boss...

Make sure you do the readings before class.  His tests are very hard because he will give options of 4 authors of the text mixed with 4 text so you have 16 choices on some of the multiple choice questions.  Learn the key terms and you should be okay.  Also, he is a tough grader on the paper.  But, he tries to make sure everything is clear in class.

I thought this class would be interesting but it gets boring pretty quickly and it's not long before you dread going. Lots of bland reading, and there is a quiz or paper every class so attendance is pretty much mandatory. Dave thinks he knows everything and will make you feel dumb if you say something that he doesn't 100% completely agree with.
The class can be somewhat interesting but Tell has a level of arrogance that can become just annoying.  Pretty much be ready to read A LOT.

Terrible. If I had wanted to take Western Civ 3 with a prick for a professor then this class would be fine. However, I was under the impression that it was a communications course where I would learn something applicable. Guess I was wrong.

Dave Tell is a really good professor because he is very passionate about the topic of rhetoric, and knows his stuff. He makes class fun and makes rhetoric interesting. There 's a 1 page paper due once a week, 2 tests, 1 paper, and a cumulative final. He is a fair grader but really does not like it when you are late to class.
Great professor. Not there to be your friend. You have to come to learn and plan on doing the work required. If you don't you will fail miserably.

AWFUL!!!! No study guides. You have to show up for class- and he WILL call on everyone! You have to read, and its so difficult to understand the info. The tests are hard, but he made it seem like it would be worse- still hard! I would never take this class again if I had to! I will NOT take another class with him!

One of the best profs I've had at KU. Very tough about attendance and readings (quizzes that make you come prepared), but lays it all out at the beginning. No surprises. If you are a good student you will love him, I learned a lot in his class. Interesting lectures, no memorizing dates!
do the readings, show up to class. . . not terribly hard

I have never hated a class as much as I hated Dave Tell's class. He forces questions on you, and your opinion means NOTHING. If it's different than his, it's wrong, and he strives to make it known you are wrong. Find another professor or another class. Grading is inconsistent. As a 3.75 gpa student, trust me - Dave tell is truly awful. Truly awful.

Extremely engaging lectures where simplifies very difficult topics. There are 4 Homeworks, 2 Midterms and a Final. 90% of course grade is based upon exams. These exams are tough, but they are based entirely off of the Homeworks and he tells you that. Attendance is not mandatory, but you will likely be lost without going. Spring Semester only.

Professor Juhl is one of the best lecturers in the business school. He is a great person too, as I regularly attend his office hours and he was always happy to help. His class is difficult, but he makes himself available to help students when needed. 90% of your grade will come from exams, but if you study the homework you will be fine.

Probably the best teacher I've had at KU at least while being in the business school. He moves fast so if you have questions you have to be vocal about it or else he won't stop. Really easy to get a hold of outside of class you just have to apply your self.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Ted wants you to succeed and works really hard to make sure everyone understands the material. He somehow keeps lectures about math fun and interesting and I honestly looked forward to going to class.

Fantastic. I had an 8am but was happy to get up and go to this class. He is very clear and funny. Just show up to class, take the notes and you will be fine. 4 HW assignments and 2 midterms plus the final. That is all. Take him if you have the chance.
Best professor I've had at KU.  Super smart but is very thorough in his explanations.

He is the best economics professor at KU. I was in his 522 class last summer. The coursework was not easy but he can explain everything extremely clearly even for an international student like me. When I found he would teach ECON526 in this summer, I dropped my spring 526 class immediately and enrolled his class.
Was the good for a professor. For to meet outside class wuz easy. Ted's Plasma Tv Warehouse is a example that he likes.  Great helpfulness in the explanations of class for the material to be good.

During the class he seems very useful and helpful, but whenever you try to see him and ask him advise, he becomes just opposite. I can say he is so selfish. He does not even invite you at his office even though he is graduate adviser. He just answers your question in front of his office's door.

Great professor, great sense of humor. Helps to show up to class. I took this over the summer, so things might change. Offers mandatory homework, the grading on tests is VERY generous. The guy is crystal clear on explanations, cant stress that enough. The content itself isn't terribly easy, but with a professor like this, it isn't so bad.
Extremely clear explanations, perhaps to a fault.  Doesn't add as much fun outside information as, say Becker, but his notes are unbelievably clear.  Really nice guy, too and willing to help.

Hes SO BORING, but its an easy A. Didnt show up to class for two months, but I was fine because the lectures hardly had anything to do with the actual assignments. Just do the assignments and youll pass. I skipped for a solid month and literally ended with a 97.65

Truly the worst professor ever. He is very intelligent he just does not know how to teach. Not engaging and rambles on with scientific jargon that no one understands. His lectures do not relate to labs and doesnt explain anything well.
Dr. Loecke's lectures were great. The professors and GTAs are super welcoming and compassionate. It was a fun and engaging class with a very manageable workload.
Dr. Loecke is literally one of the least engaging professors I've had. He really tries though. Just make sure you pay attention in lab sections for EVRN 140/2 since it reinforces lecture material.
Was a very nice professor. Took for 142 and his labs and material were much better. I would try to get in with working for him, I wish i was able too. Show up to class
Nice guy. Very down to earth. Lectures were boring but he tried to make them fun. His material seemed to be much harder than the other professors. Also, his labs were way more difficult to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Thompson was a great teacher for my class. His lectures were pretty interactive and he provides good feedback and help. The exams are pretty easy if you understand the iclickers well. He conducts quizzes every Friday but they're pretty light.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Thompson was a really good teacher to have for my intro class. His lectures are really interactive with iClickers that help you learn. However, do attend class, since he doesn't post slides or lectures online. His class is also a little fast paced, but ask questions and you'll be okay.

Professor Thompson was always easy to find and sets flexible office hours for students to attend. Also there are weekly quizzes every friday, but all content is strictly what you learn in lecture and in iclickers! Chem labs are also pretty easy! Thompson had also helped me find research opportunities! He wants his students to pass so ask questions!

Dr. Thompson comes off as fairly strict at first but his lectures are interactive and understandable. The way he teaches chemistry has changed my perception of the subject. Having struggled with it before, I was nervous for this class. If you study and attend lecture, there is nothing to worry about. A wonderful professor for my intro to chem!
Took 170 with Dr. Thompson, one of the best professors I've had at KU!! Truly cares about his students and was very engaging during lectures.

Professor Thompson was a great professor, but this class was difficult. There are usually weekly quizzes on Fridays to ensure you're attending the lectures and following what's happening in class. He also holds weekly discussions, and I highly recommend attending these if you want to do your best.

(I took chem 170 but it's not an option) Intimidating course at first, but with time and consistency it becomes a stimulating and enjoyable class. Office hours help a lot and so does attending lectures. This professor wants you to succeed and is understanding.

I had Prof Thompson for Chem 170 (Gen Chem) and this guy was amazing! At first he seems intimidating, but he is so helpful in office hours. He is great at explaining things, lots of partial credit on exams. He knows what he's talking about and the TA's are the same! Would recommend, don't be intimidated, there is so much help. Only one HW a week!

I took Chem 170 with Prof Thompson and he's an amazing lecturer. In class Iclicker questions and 1 ALEKS assignment a week made material very easy to understand. Thompson wants his students to succeed and gives all the information students need to excel on tests in his lectures. Grading is kind and gives many participation points.

Thompson's 170 class was tough for a first year chem course because of the background knowledge he expects you to have beforehand. He posts no content from in class lectures so attendance is mandatory for a good grade. However, he is extremely intelligent and willing to help if you put in effort. Tons of partial credit so grading isn't too harsh.

Dr. Thompson is a dedicated and intelligent lecturer. If you attend the lecture, he expects you to engage and participate without getting distracted. Weekly tasks include an ALEKS homework (~1 hr) and a Friday quiz. His pace suited me, but it felt fast for some. He stays on topic, offers discussions and office hours, and is approachable and funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He can be funny and chill, but very hard to reach outside of class and his lectures hardly follow the book so be ready to be confused. Also be prepared for subs because this dude will not skip a class ever, even if he has to.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His tests were so hard! even if you study the whole book! if you miss class you miss so much material ! Take with any other teacher !
Much harder than expected for a level 100 class. Class is easy in the beginning and gets much more difficult, as does his clarity when teaching. Would not take again.

Professor Thompson gives lectures that are easy to understand, but aren't very interesting. Attendance is mandatory for a good grade and the tests are extremely difficult. Homework assignments are not turned in for credit, but are a necessary to do well on the exams. Office hours and study sessions are very helpful.

Took this class because I thought it would be an easier option for chemistry. Definitely a lot tougher than I expected. Dr. Thompson is a very intelligent man and sets clear expectations. He is strict about phones and expect to have quizzes every week. He  provides discussions every week which were useful and helped to break down confusing concepts
Dr. Thompson really is a gifted educator. One of the best, and most intelligent, professors I've ever had.

This is a tough class.  He knows the material and teaches it well.  He does not tolerate excuses or distractions, and does not want to be you "friend".  Go to lecture, do the homework, handle your business, and you will do well and learn a lot.
Very enthusiastic professor. Used plenty of demonstrations to keep class enjoyable.

Ward Thompson is, simply put, an extremely intelligent man that expects the same level of comprehension from his students.  He absolutley covers everything you need to know to have success in his class, either in lecture or homework.  This class is absolutley an engineering weed-out class, so you'll quickly find out if you've got the stuff, or not.
Good teacher. The students who are poorly rating him are frankly dumb as rocks and don't belong in college. He just shows them. Put in the work and this class isn't bad.

Tests require thorough understanding of material presented in class. The labs can also be difficult to grasp but if you understand the labs you'll probably do well on the tests. He does provide ample opportunities for help but I'd  go to the TA's office hours. He can be impatient towards struggling students.

Tries to make Chemistry for Engineers more complicated than it needs to be. He seems to take pride in students having a hard time with the material. He makes sure you know when office hours are and when discussions are. When taking this class make sure you do the homework to do well on the exams.

Ward was very down to earth and obviously knowledgeable and enthusiastic about his class.  He has a dry wit that gets you through the lectures and is methodical in his teaching. Tests are punishing but fair, with a healthy curve.  Me and all my friends loved this man to death.
responded rude to any email i sent and never acknowledged me when i greeted him outside of class

Not quite the freshman-level course I was expecting, but by no means impossible. Lectures are often difficult to understand because he moves quickly, but he offers lots of very helpful office hours and discussions. Tests are very difficult unless you've put in many hours of studying.

One of the hardest classes I've ever taken.  He tried to cover way too much material in one semester and ending up just barely glancing over most of it.  Tests were extremely hard, class average was around 52% on all three of them.

Lots of students, particularly freshman, just simply hate Ward Thompson without much reasoning behind it. You have to put in work to get an engineering degree. He teaches the material very well, and is extremely helpful. Dr. Thompson is a genius, and you have to work hard to learn the stuff.

He wants to teach his 350-student-lecture-hall ALL of chemistry in this one semester. He isn't mean at all, he just demands A LOT OF WORK. Chem for Engineers is supposed to be a 5 hour freshmen level class. It has turned into a 15 hour Junior level or more class. Go to his and the TA's office hours as much as possible. He also uses lots of books.
Great teacher, he really loves the material and has a very clear understanding of the topic. It is a hard class and you have to put time into it but the teacher is fair.

Extremely hard class, and the tests are pretty brutal.  The class average ends up really low (in my class it was about 61-63), so getting an A isn't impossible.  Be prepared to study A LOT for exams and know your algebra/calculus.

Nice guy. Very understanding. Typically it's lectures on tuesdays and group work on thursdays so don't miss a thursday. All assignments were very easy. TA graded all assignments and she was an easy grader and was so sweet. There is reading and videos to watch every week but it's not too bad. Super easy A if you do every assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: (took UBPL 200, can't add a course) Prof Thom Allen is the best! Funny, really cares about his students and is passionate about what he lectures on. Great discussions. This class is like a breath of fresh air between challenging major specific courses. If you have a chance to take a class with him, DO!!!

I took his UBPL 200 course (not ARCH109). Work was light and well-structured. He is an awesome guy who is very passionate about what he teaches. He remembers faces even in large rooms and still says hi when he sees me on campus. I hope I get the opportunity to take him again in the future. Long live Thom

I took him for spring semester studio and he is one of the best professors I've come by. He is very understanding and tries to work with students based on their needs and talents. It's a more free-flow studio class, but if you need more feedback or pretty much anything, he'll help you out.

I took him for Theory of Urban Design and enjoyed his class. You could tell he enjoyed what he was teaching and wanted to ensure students understood the assignment criteria. He is also a really good resource, even if you don't take his classes, he is helpful in general.
Thom is one of the best professors in Architecture. He truly cares for his students, and is excited about what he teaches.

You never find somebody like Thom more than once in your college career. Although I didn't take his architecture course, the energy he radiates whenever lecturing or discussing with us is evident. He genuinely cares about his students and the work he does. Very down-to-earth, and one of the most respectable teachers I've ever met. Amazing guy.

Such a sweet guy. He's easy to talk to, and passionate about his subjects. Very knowledgeable. He will help you with anything. Great teacher to have for this seminar. The work we did was actually fun- I never minded doing the work in there because I learned SO much. He's honestly just such a cool professor- don't pass him up!

Interesting lecture topics and speakers, assigned insightful reading and projects, and a generally enjoyable and valuable class! Was great about answering questions at the end of lectures. Unfortunately he assigned like four major final projects that I couldn't balance with studio and tanked my grade at the last minute. Gave me an actual ulcer :(

Thom is one of the best professors I've ever had. He clearly knows what he's talking about and is great at balancing between giving good feedback and directing you while also letting you do your own thing. Be prepared to spend a lot of time on his class though and practice good time management.

What a fantastic professor. In a field that devalues students, Thom actually cares. I have had multiple occasions where we told him an assignment was stressing us out or was too much, and he actually treated us like adults and listened. Both times he revised the assignment after hearing us out. One of these was studio. Take him if you get a chance!

I took Thom's 'Building the Future of Cities' course. This was a fun and easygoing class. I really enjoyed getting to use Minecraft as part of a college course! Thom is fun and made the class open-ended, so it wasn't too rigorous. This was my second lecture class with Thom and would definitely consider taking him for a studio class in the future!

Thom really cares about students learning and appreciates architecture and urban design. If you show up, stay attentive, and ask questions you should have no problem in this class. He makes sure the class stays up to date and exciting.
Thom was a great professor. He knew the subject my matter (urban design) and was accessible so I could be successful in his class. I would highly recommend taking any courses he teaches.

Thom is a great Professor, extremely friendly and down to earth. Theory of Urban Design was very organized and clearly understood, had many guest lectures which kept the class really interesting, and had very interesting subject matter that was relevant to current issues. Really enjoyed the class and disappointed we couldnt finish in person class!

Thom was the first teacher of ARCH 620 and I liked him. He made strong efforts to bring in engaging guest lecturers to educate us about urban design and how cities are developed and structured. Assignments were generally interesting and never felt like a burden. Thom was also fantastic about communication and responding to concerns. Good teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Thom is the man! He was excellent at recognizing you for the effort you put into the class and encouraging you with personalized feedback. Thom left some room for your own interpretation on projects and really let you make them your own. Would definitely recommend.

Thom, whatta gem. A teacher who really wants to see his students succeed. I really enjoyed taking his course and learned a lot of interesting things. The homework/quizzes he assigned were always reasonable and would normally include a podcast which I thought made learning easy. If you have the opportunity to take one of his classes DO IT!

I loved Thom #ThomTime. He's clearly passionate about architecture, and kindles that same passion in his students. He devotes quality attention to each of his students. He set clear expectations well within reason and the projects were appropriately challenging for first-year students. He pushes students to strive to the best of their abilities.

Thom has become one of my most trusted professors. He gives good feedback, and has a set program for the class, but is willing to let the students drive the bus. Take the initiative and pursue something that interests you in his class, and you will generally find Thom pushing you to go further down the rabbit hole. Wish he taught all my studios.

One of my favorite teachers Ive had. Very clear with what is expected and really wants to see his students succeed. Teaches with purpose and does not just give out random assignments but things that will actually help students learn.

I absolutely love Thom! He was very open to suggestions and allowed us to mold the projects into something more interesting. There were critiques almost every class, which I thought was so helpful because by the time the final was due you knew your project was the best it could be. He expects a lot- be prepared to make +/- 12 study models/project

Exams were very difficult and were worth 80% of the grade, and it was often left to the student to teach themselves using the book. Nothing felt unfair, but it took every ounce of my time and sanity. One of the worst lecturers in the physics department and not very helpful, but was generally considerate towards students during class.
homework and exam problems are not always thought out or clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There were multiple times in Dr. Cravens lectures he would just say "read the book over this topic" and then it would show up on the test. He did not try very hard to teach us what we needed to know to succeed. I felt like he put no effort into helping us actually learn throughout the whole semester. Take this class with a different prof if you can
No further comments:)

Dr. Cravens likes to ramble about off-topic things during class. He's very hard to follow and makes the tests too long for the amount of time given. He has a very good understanding of physics, but is not excellent at sharing his knowledge.

He's very vague in his lectures. He doesn't understand some of the concepts he's teaching. You're given equations and that's about all there is to it. He's there to help, but the book was the only thing that saved me in this class. His class consists of quizzes & exams, w 3% participation via clicker. Learn the system and you'll be fine

By far the worst class I've taken at KU. I got an A and learned nothing all semester -- concepts are taught be equations, solutions are typed in one line and hard to follow, very  boring. He does not change his tests year to year (one plus) and you get clicker participation. A vert poor reflection of the realm of physics and the art of teaching.

The lectures are incredibly worthless, but there are daily attendance points and a quiz every Friday. Homework was assigned, but not collected, instead a couple of the homework problems were used as the quiz. I didn't learn much from the class. The tests weren't too bad, but the final was brutal, got a D on it, but still managed an A- in the class.
He does not teach. Lectures are just him rambling about things that don't matter to the homework or exams. Be prepared to teach yourself everything in this course.

He can be horribly unorganized and scatterbrained, but he really cares about his students doing well and learning the material. Lectures can be confusing, but his office hours are great. He keeps tests and homework relatively easy compared to how hard thermodynamics can be. If you don't mind teaching yourself the material sometimes, I recommend.

He probably shouldn't be teaching. I have had him in the past and he is just an overall bad teacher. You will have to rely heavily on books and self teaching if you want to make it in this class. He will ramble and not get to important content in the course.
Tenpas is an incredibly smart man that is a little bit goofy. The class in itself is hard, but Tenpas does an outstanding job explaining the difficult topics.

TenPas is the only professor who teaches this. Very disorganized. Lectures are 75 minutes full of tangents and a waste of time at 8am. Gives 0 partial credit on exams, even if you did the process right. If you go to his office hours, youll be there for 1 hour listening to stories. No coordination with the TAs at all but they are great help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor whenever possible. Lectures are clearly unplanned and nonsensical. The textbook, homework, and even the exams have typos everywhere. The only way you'll learn in this course is through the TAs, textbook, and occasionally whatever documents are buried in Blackboard. Difficult because of the professor, not the content.

Lecture are incoherent and unrelated to course content. HW and Exams have so many typos you don't even know what the questions are asking. He has no organizations skills and due dates are never clear. He usually just lets a bunch of people pass at the end but I promise you wont learn what you need to for future classes.

I have never been so furious at a teacher before in my life. He has the worst grading system I have ever seen. He never replies to emails, makes no sense in lectures, gives out 8+ hours of homework a week then sends emails saying it should only take an hour. He also has the worst scheduling for due dates possible. Lastyl his tests make 0 sence. RUN

ME 508 is unavoidable with tenpas since he is the only one that teaches it. My biggest advice would be to read the book and do the practice problems to study for exams and so that you have better understanding of how to do lab assignments. If Michael is your GTA, you're going to probably rely on him the most to teach you the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Good person and decent class but concepts are difficult

TenPas does not teach a single thing in lecture. He only rambles about irrelevant problems. I read my textbook instead of listening after a few weeks of class because it was the only way to learn anything. Deadlines mean nothing to him. He canceled our final for anyone with a passing grade so that we would not disturb his research any more. (s)pain
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: I have never been more frustrated with a professor in my entire life. He just genuinely seems like he has no care for his job. Textbook is riddled with typos, lectures are incomprehensible, homework along with group projects are unclear and time consuming. Having no feedback on assignments either makes this a very stressful class to say the least.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I've taken 3 classes with Tenpas but not out of choice. He's a very intelligent person but can't teach at all. He only goes over the theory in lecture that isn't in the homework. He's VERY disorganized with unclear due dates and what he wants for homework. You work in groups and if the final is optional, TAKE IT! ->Likely to jump up a letter grade
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He really gives the impression that he just doesnt care about his job.

TenPas is a professor who truly does care about his students. However, he is not there to hand out easy A's. You have to work for your grade, which is understandable. He has an open door policy for office hours so he is very easy to reach if you have any questions. He provides previous exams for studying purposes which is SUPER beneficial.

His lectures are nonsensical. I am taking his numerical analysis class so far he has been late to nearly every class. He has also ranted at us more about Powell doctrine and the trilateral convention than anything else. I wouldn't expect to learn global politics in my numerical analysis class.

Lectures are completely incomprehensible. The few things that are comprehensible make you question why he's even allowed to be a professor. He blanketly says incorrect things about the subject, assigns homework that take more time to understand what he's asking than actually doing it, and makes tests and quizzes that are incredibly time sensitive.
How he is still a professor is beyond me. Doesn't teach at all during lectures just goes on tangents and assigns homework that only he understands.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Overall this wasn't a fun experience. Part of it is probably the fact that its the COVID semester, but there was virtually no feedback on submitted assignments. Lectures are very unclear, but the online videos he posts for some things are very helpful and clear. Overall it seems he wants students to succeed, but isn't really organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: The absolute worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life. Majority of the class is ending with a "D", and he doesn't believe that it's a reflection of his teaching abilities. He's extremely unorganized, nobody knows what's going on ever, he walk-in circles during class and talks about random things that come to mind, then expects you to know.
Speaking non-sense on lecture, and exams have a lot to cover with small amount of time.

Doesn't even show up to our discussion sections sometimes. No warning or explanation. I'm on my third class with him and honestly, if you can take any of his classes with someone else, you'll have a better time. There's not much organization. Homework and exam dates are changed without warning. Good luck following his lectures/examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: TenPas is very much a full person with goods/faults and learning to work with him will mature you as a person. He's scatterbrained, doesn't prepare much for lecture (prob cuz hes old+bored), and communicates poorly. But he gives great resources to improve, cares and helps his students especially during office hours, and is funny and charismatic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Tough but fair most of the time
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: i've got literally no idea what's happening in this class, ever. his lecture style makes so little sense, and exams are way too many questions with very little time. would deeply appreciate it if he put up the homework answers earlier than the night before the exam, bc i dont understand the homework and have very little to study from.

His lectures are so disorganized even when I focus super hard in what he's saying I can't learn anything. Not enough time for quizzes or tests with minimal curve to compensate. He lectures beyond the 50 minute period about 90% of the time. Homework will test you over things he will never teach. This class wouldn't be hard if it wasn't for him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Unorganized, scatter brained, but very intelligent. Doesn't convey material well in lectures, but provides a lot of material online. However, the material is as unorganized as his lectures - looks like a picasso painting. He likes to talk about related subject matters, but leaves little time for explaining course material well. Try to avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Tenpas is a good teacher and he seems to care but is terribly unorganized and his lecture are all over the place. The class has a quiz every week and if you do not read the chapters before lecture you will terribly confused. This class requires an insane amount of out of class work but if you put in enough time you can enjoy it.

I like and respect him a lot. He deserves respect because he cares about his students. He cares about science too. He wants his students to think logically and learn not just copy and memorize equations. Yes, he does not teach as he should be in the class but he gives a lot of sources to help students prepare very well for exams.

Weekly group homework, group quizzes, group case studies, and Tophat questions for participation. For this class, he drops the lowest exam score, and if you opt out of the final, the average of the best 2 exams and all quizzes becomes the final exam score. Start off strong and you won't fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr TenPas is a great professor! If you have trouble to keep with the class pace, he is always there for you when you talk to him during his office hours. Also the review sessions he offer will help you do well in the course. He cares more about what students learn in the class than their course grade.
Amazing professor! He is always there for you when you are having trouble understanding concepts!

The first couple days of class are intimidating but once you start to understand the topics, it gets a lot better. make sure to stay on top of homework assignments. at the beginning of the semester, MAKE SURE TO GET IN A GOOD GROUP (that can make or break your grade). try not to take the final if you don't have to.

Dr. TenPas is unequivocally the best professor I have had in the mechanical engineering department. He is a scatterbrained genius who goes off tangents every now and then. The problems he gives you are extremely realistic  and will prepare you for tests. The best thing about his class  is the amount of resources he provides for tests and quizzes.

Peter is the best. Beginning of the semester, I didn't like him. But he turned out to be my fav professor. He is a squirrel in class and the tests are very hard. But it is going to be okay. I got a 40% on the first test and got an A. Thermo is a hard subject but Peter is the best to take it from. Get with him 1 on 1 and you'll see why. 10/10.

Professor Tenpas is a genius, but extremely scatterbrained. Lectures can take odd tangents. The homework is rough, but tests mirror the homework pretty closely. If you attend office hours, be prepared to go off topic. Take it with him over the summer if you can, as he seems more focused with smaller class sizes.

He puts you in a group at the beginning of the semester which is nice if you know people but if you get a random group it could make you or break you. Homework and quizzes are in groups but if a group member doesn't show up or do their work then you're both screwed even if you did yours. Overall, lecture is messy and his grading could be better.
He is a great teacher!!!!
Peter is the man! XD
He is a very good professor. His lectures help the students to think like engineers. He is a genius and also has good working experience in this field. Would definitely take another class with him.

He isn't as bad as everyone makes him out to be. I was scared  to take this thermo section, but it wasnt all that bad. Go in with the mindset that you will work really really hard and you will succeed. His tests are fair and very similar to his homework. The homework is super hard, but you learn well. Overall not as bad as I thought.

TenPas wasn't all that bad. The class itself is tough and he really does a great job on the content he teaches. Can come off as rude in lecture to questions and is best approached outside of lecture. If you put forth the effort you're going to pass even if you don't have the greatest grasp on the material. Load up the equation sheet with examples.

Take this class in the summer. This man is very brilliant, but his charisma and genius is best experienced in a smaller setting. He uses real life examples, and teaches with a mix of his vast experience and textbook notation. His equation sheet has the answers to the questions. He always provides and explains how to read them too.  Do not be afraid

I have above a 3.3 gpa and am a good student. I never miss class and study hard but his lack of organization and clarity is so terrible that I am going to do everything in my power to never take a class with him again.
very confusing. tends to be frantic in class. wouldn't suggest taking a course from him.
Professor Tenpas is ok when it comes to physical problems but avoid any class of his that is theoretical.

Brilliant, but hard to follow sometimes. Come to class expecting to sprint through the notes everyday, and you'll do fine. Come to class expecting to LEARN. It doesn't help that most students have him for Thermo-1, which is the first truly hard course in any engineering curriculum.  Also, keep the Moran/Shapiro book, it is invaluable.

good professor. sometimes confusing in class but he does his best to help you during offices hours. Give you a lot of chance to earn points during the semester. you just need to study. first day of class a lot of people drop, but now that the time went by i realized that this class is way easier that it really looks like on the first day.
he is way too smart to teach n he is a nice person at strip clubs however in the class he is awfully rude, he post loads of stuff online which i found it overwhelming.
awfully rude, doesn't care to help you if you're struggling. shouldn't be teaching undergrads.

Dr. TenPas provides you with all the necessary tools to succeed in his class. The handouts complements the book very well. People complain about him all the time, but these are students that are not putting forth the effort. Read the book and pay attention in class. His overall grade breakdown is easy; had my A guaranteed by mid-semester.

Worst prof u could ask for. This guy has no idea how to teach. Lessons were messy, all over the board, incoherent and u couldn't ask questions without being humiliated in front of the class. Homework was extremely difficult and nothing like what we learned in class. Same goes for exams, each was curved at least 15%. KU, why is this guy teaching??

Worst instructor ever, very disorganized and he would get stucked on derivations all the time. It is clear that he does not prepare for class at all. Why is this guy still teaching? i want my money back.

Thermo is a tough subject in general.  If you want to do well in his class go to office hours, do the extra credit, and make sure he knows that you are trying.  If he knows that then he will be sure to help you out when it comes time for the final grade.  Oh and there is a course curve as well as individual tests/quiz curves

Quite hard and he expects a lot from his students but he knows his stuff.  For a 3 credit hour class, you actually have to put in at LEAST 6 hours of studying and doing homework a week.  Don't drop it though cause he gives you a lot of opportunities to do good.

Ten Pas works very hard putting together handouts and assignments.  Be prepared to read the book because his lectures are confusing and unorganized.  You will learn something if you try however.  Go to his office hours.  He'll be plenty willing to help but do NOT, whatever you do, ask questions in class.  Bad idea.  He will treat you like an idiot.

I have had Dr. TenPas for ME 312, 412, 510, 612, and 508 so I've probably had more expedience with him than anyone else here.  Yes, his classes are some of the harder ones, and yes he can be unorganized, but all you have to do is go to his office and he is more than willing to explain anything you may have missed.  He's not that bad.

I do not understand what people complain about.  He is a very good professor.. yes, he can be confusing at times but if you put effort and attend review sessions that Daniel does, you should have no problem in the class.  He does not overwhelm you with work.  He just expects you to study for tests.

People tend to complain about Dr. TenPas without reason.  They blame their own stupidity and inability to pay attention on him.  He teaches EXACTLY what is on the homework, but when students don't do well, it is mysteriously his fault.  He is a little sharp with students who have questions in class, but he is always extremely helpful in his office.

Peter TenPas runs the most unorganized lectures I have ever encountered. He will start something, but branch off on a tangent, returning to the original subject minutes later. Definitely ADD.  He is really smart, and if you are VERY hard working you could gain alot by paying close attn.  But for the rest of us, impossible.

Although he is hard, and quite incomprehensible at alot of times, I still kinda liked him as a teacher. He is by far the most challenging teacher I've had and without McBrides help, I would have probably failed. He is by no means dumb.
Need priscription for adderall, constantly trip over things, mildly amusing, and lacking any capability of being organized.

Thermo was hell for me last semester. I put in a lot of effort, not all of which was directed the right way. Lillianna the ta is very good at explaining things and is extremely organized when working problems. I only wish I had gone to her sessions from the start. The one thing I can say about Tenpas is his grading style is fair. Good final policy.

If anything, I feel like I LOST knowledge from taking a class of his. Watching him in lecture can be compared to watching a dog run around the yard - pointless, yet mildly entertaining. Examples in class have nothing to do with homework or tests. Save yourself the hassle and just go to the review sessions or avoid this professor all together.

Where to start... Prof. TenPas knows his stuff, but doesn't understand that we're 40 years behind him. Liliana, the TA, relays the material in a much more helpful manner. Help sessions are how I survive. He is often very condescending, and refuses to slow down if you miss a step of his spastic work on the board. comb his beard for extra credit!

Putting it bluntly, you'll barely learn anything from TenPas.  He'll give you a ridiculous amount of handouts, then talk about completely unrelated matters, and work some practically useless example problems.  Avoid him at all costs.
I think he's A.D.D.. His mouth cannot keep up with his brain.

TenPas starts every lecture of by going  on a rant about some arbitrary subject, not necessarily thermodynamics related. 15 minutes later, everyone wonders what exactly we are even learning about. He is highly unapproachable and seems to challenge students who ask questions in class. Without Professor McBride's help, we would all fail.

Tenpas is not a good man. At all. His lectures are hard to follow and he seems to hate teaching because he sucks so bad. Get help from professor McBride if you want a good grade. p.s. he wears sandals with business casual clothes. goof.
Horrible. Don't ever take any classes from him. Ever.                                   Ever.                                        Like really, never.
Really bad teacher!!!

Took Thermo and Fluids - learned nothing from him. Had to learn everything myself just to barely get by. Clarity and simple, concept based examples are non-existent. Feels that because he knows it, everyone else obviously knows it too. Horrible. I don't have enough room here to describe how bad he is at teaching.

Tenpas = tough. HMWK: get a solu. manual, go to Liliana & McBride's (CE prof) reviews.  TESTS: you MUST undrstnd how stuff works together; study his chp reviews off blackboard, know what the symbols mean, know what situations call for what eqns, b/c his tests revolve around THEORY. On tests first write basic eqns for each prob then come back to it

Tenpas has the unhealthy knack of completely degrading and humiliating students who dare ask questions. He believes that since he understands it, everyone in his class should automatically understand it. He gives examples, but these are all too often so quick and unhelpful that after about a week, even the most studious of students stop paying attn
i was only in this class for a couple of weeks, i dropped because i didnt think the way he taught was very good - TOO FAST, that and i thought he was rather rude toward the class
TenPas is a great teacher, and i believe that he has the difficult job of teaching us thermo.  He is very smart, and holds an interactive type of class.  A lot of homework.
He knows the subjects well. He is a genius, just doesn't know how to teach. He thinks that everyone is at his same level of understanding.

TenPas does a good job of presenting material which is very difficult for many people to understand.  He is charged with presenting too much knowledge in too short of a time, but he grades fairly, so if you work hard you shouldn't have a problem.
too fast of a pace in class, hard to follow.  has good intentions, nice guy, but tough to understand
He talks quietly and jumps around too much.  It is hard to follow what he is saying.  The class is interesting, but you'll need to learn most of it from the book.
No Comments
No Comments

I just finished PHIL605: Plato last semester. Professor Tuozzo does not mince words, and he does not let students take over lectures with extended ramblings. He is a fair grader, but the workload exceeds other philosophy classes. Professor Tuozzo is a must take professor for any philosophy major that takes their education seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class gives a bland history of ancient philosophy and then asks you to memorize it. Tuozzo is unorganized and scatterbrained, though gives decent lectures and is nice enough. The study guide is deceivingly bad at preparing you for the exams, of which there are three and they make up almost all of your grade (and are very poorly administered).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a pretty tough class, but Tuozzo does a good job with it. Sometimes the lectures can drag a bit but that's not unexpected for an hour long philosophy lecture. But Tuozzo is engaging and kind. Definitely a professor to keep on your schedule if you find yourself in his class. Show up, do the reading, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Tuozzo was an excellent professor. I took him for Ancient Philosophy, and greatly enjoyed his lectures. He gave me excellent feedback and made his expectations clear. Pay attention, read, and make half an effort to understand the material and you'll do fine. Communicate with him and he will work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Grading is a bit confusing, but hes kind and willing to help. Most work is participation based so as long as you do the readings and answer the questions/responses you should be fine... YOU MUST DO THE READING THOUGH, this class is impossible without an understanding of the books.

This guy is literally terrible.. Rude in class, no concept of what he teaches, and completely disrespectful to students in class. I took PHIL 384 for my minor and no joke I know more about this class than he does. His grading is absolutely ridiculously random and has no logic behind it. I cannot stress this enough, BAD BAD BAD BAD BAD professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Love him, would take again 100%. just make sure you come to class and read. Super nice and funny guy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I think that I learned a lot about the Ancient Philosophers this semester. His knowledge about the topic has a very large breadth and depth. Going into his office hours was beneficial and he is a very nice guy. Solid choice for a class - I took it as a requirement for my Philosophy major.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Tuozzo is clearly very passionate about philosophy, and he knows his stuff. He generally does an excellent job of explaining the complexities of whatever philosopher we happened to be reading. If you're a philosophy major this class should be relatively easy, as long as you do the reading and attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Subject matter is very interesting, however the lectures are very hard to follow long with and the tests are 100% written response and almost impossible to receive the grade you feel you deserve.
Thomas Tuozzo is an excellent professor and he knows absolutely everything about ancient philosophy, especially Plato!
Very hard tests  and is looking for specific things in each answer.  Not an easy class, do not take unless you really have to, and would recommend a different professor.  Not easy.

I'm liking him ok so far but can see how he can rub people the wrong way. He seems really reasonable and cares about the subject matter. HOWEVER, the grader must be picked straight from hell itself. It's like the grader is out to prove wrong everything you have learned without logical reasoning. It's a shame one pr*ck can ruin an interesting class.

I am a senior at KU and thought I had already experienced the worst professors here; I was wrong.  Tom Tuozzo is hands down the worst professor I have encountered.  I suggest you run from this class and don't look back.  He is rude, condescending, and does not care about his students.  He should not be allowed to teach.

Dr. Tuozzo rambles a bit sometimes but he clearly knows what he's talking about and is good at explaining it. He's always happy to help you during office hours or meet at another time. He's a great professor and I'd recommend his Ancient Philosophy course.
Always Go Tuozzo. He is a great Professor. Just pay attention and you'll learn a lot.

Tuozzo is nice enough, if incredibly scattered and his class is interesting at first but it wears on you.  It takes an huge amount of effort every week and you are excepted to understand a great deal of the material before the class but you have to in order to pass the incredibly hard tests.  If the class was not 3 hours in one day it could be ok.

This class is alright if you've taken a philosophy class before, it is not easy by far tho. Tuozzo is helpful, but he's not the one grading your tests and papers. The grader he used for my class was a prick. HE is the one to watch out for. Tuozzo straight up told me he would've given my paper at least 1-3 more points, which is huge! Be very carful!
Prof. Tuozzo is a badass. I'm a philosophy major so im biased, but i really enjoyed the class. I got an A, but not easily. If you just go to class you should get at least a B.
So boring it takes a huge effort to make it to class. However, he is helpful if you go in and meet with him in office hours. If you choose to take this course/have to take this course, good luck!

Make sure you've taken a philosophy class before this one because Dr. Tuozzo assumes you know exactly what he's talking about at all times. Two tests and two papers and weekly in class writing assignments (in groups). Make sure you spend time on the papers!!!! Tough grader. Must memorize quotes for tests and short essays. He's very smart but tough.

His tests have short answer and essays, sometimes quote ID. Short answer isn't too bad, but the essays seem to require knowing exactly what he's thinking. He gives you possible essay topics before the tests. All I can tell you to help is to make sure you know what he thinks about each question by attending lecture.

The most boring experience of my life, hands down. Lectures were boring and repetitive, and although he repeated the same things, the deeper he went into them the more confusing they became. Boring + Repetitive + Overcomplication = Bad.

tuozzo doesn't teach 288 like an entry level course.  i took phil 140 and got an easy a, but this class is much much more difficult.  you'll learn a lot but to do so you'll have to attend every class. unless you're majoring in philosophy don't take.  if you're just interested look elsewhere

You have to go to class every day and copy down almost everything he says.  In other words, you have to work and pay attention.  I don't think it's too much to ask.  He gives you all the information you need for the tests. Requires a lot of study, but it is clear what he expects of you.  You don't need to read, just attend lecture.

he teaches this class like its a graduate level philosophy class, i think because he is the chair of the philosophy department. he is obviously very knowledgeable in his field but absolutely cannot bring it down to the student's level. don't take it if you don't want to work really hard

Great professor.  Goes above and beyond to provide all the resources you need to know the content.  He posts all the slides, records class, provides a free pdf of his text book, and his own version of an outline for his class.  He's also both funny but manages class time very well. 11/10 would recommend.

One of the best professors at KU Law. Lectures and exams are straightforward--maybe a little boring, yes, but he tells you what you need to know. Incredibly generous of him to take the time to give you feedback on practice exam answers during the semester. Gives amazing feedback, is super accessible. Smart, funny, and genuinely loves teaching.
One of the smartest greatest down to earth guys ever. seems intimidating at first but a totally nice and brilliant guy.

Very smart man, although equally lacking in charisma (lectures tend to drag, especially if technology doesn't co-operate with him). Hardly a bad prof, but would take Con Law from someone else if I had it to do over.

Brilliant teacher who asked novel and compelling impromptu questions.  Led class discussions with genuine interest and welcomed every student's involvement. This class is what graduate education should be like.
It's all about the gun show!  Very easy class though.

Good professor and gives you a great outline to follow.  The test is so easy that everyone does well.  You will think you aced it and then get a lesser grade.  This happens every year.  Good professor though!

BUS 150 is an easy class and all professors have the same curriculum, homework, and activities. Charlotte gave the lectures very well and always explained the activities well. Just go to class and participate and you'll do great.

Lots of busy work but the topics are interesting. MUST GO TO CLASS. I could have gotten a better grade if I would have gone to more of the classes. Although time consuming take detailed notes because quiz questions are oddly specific. Will spend a lot of time watching videos.

The class isn't hard per se but if you get behind in any way its a major hit to your grade. Easily 2+ hours of homework a night all for 5 points and if you didn't do the assignment exactly how she wants you'll get a zero. this class could've been said in an email but annoyingly if you want an A, make this class a priority, don't get behind.

Tritch is a great person but a below average professor. Classes are engaging and fun but she makes you read/watch an OBSCENE amount of content to do 5 point assignments. miss class one day, you miss an insane amount of points. The quizzes are extremely specific and hard to remember little details of a 2 hr video. Good content, terribly executed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really liked this class and Charlotte. She cares for her students and you can tell she's passionate about the content. Our class is pretty quiet and she does a good job at drawing people out. Make sure you read the pre-class material before the lecture and be ready for quizzes weekly. This class is very manageable if you stay on top of your work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She doesn't teach, she makes us watch videos and read 30 page books to learn what she should be teaching us. Then we discuss in class but, she doesn't further explain what we should be learning.
She was probably my favorite professor at KU. She is very understanding when it comes to personal things and gives you the respect and sympathy you need.

Charlotte Tritch is an absolute gem. She is my school mom and you can tell she genuinely cares for all of her students. She was my favorite prof this semester and if you have the chance to take a class with her, do it. Her class was a lot of busy work but I'd rather do the busy work with her than any other professor.

Charlotte is one of my all time favorite teachers. She is caring and gets to know you on a personal level, and is always wanting the best for you. Super easy class, didn't need to study one time and the group projects are cake. She's such an easy grader and will basically hand you an A. Only thing is there is an attendance grade.
Take bus150 with any other professor.

Charlotte is one of my favorite professors I've had at KU. She is VERY intelligent and she always keeps classes interesting. I am already looking for more of her classes I can sign up for next semester.
Charlotte is one of my favorite teachers at KU. She is extremely helpful both in the class and for your future career.

Of all of my 5yrs & 3 majors at KU, Tritch is my all time FAVORITE professor, enough for me to write this. Not only is she a great teacher with extensive knowledge & experience while encouraging class discussion, but she actually cares about you & your learning experience. She cares, shes smart, understanding, and always available to help. The Best

A wonderful professor, if you have the opportunity to take him absolutely do. He is such a caring and insightful professor and you will come out of the semester feeling as if you have made good friends.
Super laid back and his teaching style works great.
Amazing person, great class
John Trefry is the absolute GOAT. He provides a great introduction into the department of architecture.

Trefry is an amazing first studio professor. He made me feel comfortable coming to a completely new place. He will give good design feedback throughout the design process, but he is not very critical of the final project... some of the other ARCH 108 professors will be more critical. In architecture, you want to be criticized (even 1st year).

Really great professor - you 100% have to take extra initiative in his class to get good feedback but he's such an easy going & genuinely interesting professor that it's easy to do. Teaches outside the box - great for people that are struggling with finding their creative flow during first year.

Trefry is a great professor. He gives good feedback, is understanding with both missing classes and grading assignments. You don't have to be good at drawing, as long as he can tell that you're putting in the work. He is also a friendly and nice guy. Laid back & fun to talk to. Also doesn't make you stay for the full 4 hours if you don't need to.
If you can be self-critical, Trefry is a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Trefry's classes are very interesting and makes you think outside the box. His methods are a bit different than other professors, but that's what makes his class so interesting and an amazing learning experience.

Trefry really cares about his students and is overall pretty laid back. He is an easy person to talk to and if more time is needed on a project, he will most likely allow it. Trefry is not very judgemental which can be a drawback for architecture students but he is very respectful and easy to learn from. I did find I wanted to be criticized more.
He's by far the best.  He may seem hipster-like, and super artsy, but he is very helpful and contributes a lot of feedback to your work. I would definitely take another class by him.
Trefry for chair!

Allocate time for homework. A lot of papers to read. They are optional. Exams were open book. Getting the grades you want is not that difficult if you allocate time for your assignments and projects. Exam are similar to homework and class problems.
Overall, I enjoyed the class.

No constructive feedback, no grading criteria, no structured plan/path, goals or deliverables, which caused me +2 years of additional efforts working with a new advisor. I was lost all the time, and did not help me in achieving my research goals. It was all random. I will definitely not take this course again.

I took this course in a hope to learn new information about construction equipment. Unfortunately, it was just the exact same information he taught across his other course such as CMGT 500/700, CMGT 707. There was not a grading rubric or a structured curriculum, and all class examples were unrelated to construction!

Dr. Tran was a great professor. Lectures were pretty dry and a tad, but he covered the information you needed for homework and exams. Sitting through 3 hours of lectures was honestly the worst part. He is really nice and is always willing to help!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dan has 3 hours to teach you once a week, and hell use most of it going over generic slides with no in-depth information and few examples. Pay attention, he remembers every persons name. All 80 of you.
Class is needlessly complex. He easily takes an hour and a half to explain 1-2 example problems. Slides and notes are disorganized, and overall he is just very very bad at conveying information
Kind of tough with grading

I should start off by saying that I was only able to experience a third of the semester with Dan because he was out for two thirds of it with a hernia. When he was there, his lectures dragged on, and he was an extremely inconsistent grader (deducting different points for the same mistakes). Easy class, but you have to go to every lecture .

Fantastic professor. Best chemistry professor I've ever had. Exams are difficult, but Prof. Jackson acknowledges this and adjusts grades accordingly, focusing on your ability to demonstrate improvement and understanding of material in many other ways. Groupwork formatted to prevent lazy ones from dragging others down (75% grade individual contribu)

I had Professor Jackson for Chem 195. One of the best science teachers I have ever had. He inspires a greater understanding of chemistry in his students and is great at relating the concepts learned in class to the real world. For anyone leaning between chem 135 and 195, I would highly recommend 195 with Jackson.

Dr. Jackson is probably the best professor I've had so far. His lectures are engaging and he clearly goes above and beyond in preparing them. The material is pretty difficult but the curve really reflects that.

This class was extremely difficult because he wanted to prepare us for the difficulty of future classes, but he acknowledged the class was for freshmen, so the class was curved a lot. I definitely still had to work for my grade. Entertaining lectures, good environment, interesting projects, etc.
Very helpful in office hours and through email; cares about your future goals and will try to help you achieve them; treats you with respect and like someone with a life outside of school

Dr. Jackson is seriously a fantastic professor. Even if you don't like chemistry, you'll enjoy his class. You can tell he cares about his students, not to mention he's a great lecturer. Also, he brings treats for his students on exam days. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, do it!

Dr. Jackson is by far the best professor at this school. I had some severe medical issues during the semester. He was extremely kind and helpful in helping me get everything done during the semester. Not only this, his lectures are fantastic and he helps you to truly learn through a structure of quizzes, reviews, and exams.

Dr. Jackson is one of the best professors I have ever had. I am terrible at chemistry, and his class was very challenging, but I learned more in CHEM190 than in any other class. He is an amazing lecturer and explains the content so well. He's truly the one who taught me how to learn. He knows honors is hard, so he curves based on the average.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great prof overall for my honors intro chem. Experienced in teaching freshmen, and great at keeping the material to our level while keeping it challenging. Not hilarious, but has his moments - he comes across as a master of his craft that genuinely enjoys educating others.
the best
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Jackson is awesome. In addition to this class, I have him for my honors adviser. He writes on the chalk board during lecture with a small amount of reading off the slides. He is one of the most genuine people I have ever met.

Awesome at what he does & I hope he teaches honors orgo next year so I can take a class with him again. If you don't have a natural affinity for chem, it may be hard, but his discussion sections & office hours are always helpful. He's so sweet; he brings treats during exams :D

Professor Jackson really makes sure students understand the challenging materials. He goes beyond the bare minimum of teaching and answers the question "why and how?" in regards to the concepts. Class is challenging but definitely worth taking.

Dr. Jackson is what stopped me from dropping out of college. He is a shining beacon of light, and his knowledge of chemistry is greater than GN Lewis'. He is extremely helpful with his students, and he truly cares for the people he teaches.

While the course is difficult, Professor Jackson does a fantastic job of explaining the complicated material. He is a fair grader and says he does not wish to punish you with a lower grade than you would get in regular chem because you are taking an honors course. All in all, a very good professor. If you need help, he provides many opportunities.

Professor Jackson was absolutely my favorite professor! He is not only a wonderful teacher but a really great person. He is always willing to help you if you need added clarity. His tests are tough but he grades fairly and takes care of you in the end. If you have the opportunity you have to take his class!!

Dr. Jackson is a wonderful professor! I have had him for two semesters now, and he is by far my favorite teacher! He is very fair with grading and gives the class a huge curve because he knows his tests are hard. His lessons are always very clear and well thought-out, and he is really flexible about meeting with you outside of class. Great guy!

Prof. Jackson is an amazing professor. He is also an amazing human being. He is one of the kindest, funniest, most intelligent and fair teachers I have ever had. I thought I was insane to take two semesters of honors chemistry, but the professor is the reason I did it, and he made it worth it. I also laugh way more than I should at his jokes.

Before I took his class, I hated chemistry! Now I'm probably going to get a double major in biochem because of him. He is super helpful and works with you to make sure you understand. He always takes the time to meet with you even if you can't make his office hours. The course is challenging, but if you use him as a resource you will do well.

Professor Jackson is great! He makes even the hardest material easy to understand, and will work with you both in and out of class on anything you don't understand. His tests, however, are pretty challenging, but if you put in the effort, you should do fine in the class.

Dr. Jackson is an incredibly intelligent man with impeccably planned out lectures and engaging class demonstrations. CHEM 185/189 is quite hard and required significantly more time than my other 12 credit hours combined, but he is a fair grader and is always available if you need help. Listen for his subtly sassy humor and nuggets of wisdom!

One of the best science teachers you'll ever have. Second semester was harder than first semester, but that may have been because of the subject matter. One of the tests this semester had a low average, but Dr. Jackson specifically made the next test easier to help. He sincerely cares about every student and doesn't believe in D's or F's on tests.

Take Jackson's class if you get the chance! I took 185 & 189 with him. It was challenging, but I learned a ton! He explains things very well, grades fairly, and is just a really nice guy. I was always excited to go to class and I felt like I actually learned things in the lectures.

Wonderful teacher. I thoroughly enjoyed the class. It was difficult, but I feel as though I have a decent grasp on Chemistry concepts and that I've learned a lot of new information this semester. Going to take another class with this Dr. Jackson this semester.

Great professor! Teaches difficult information in an easy-to-understand way. The class requires a lot of time if you want to do well, but it is very possible. Dr. Jackson really cares about his students doing well, and is easily available for help.

Excellent professor. Best chemistry teacher I've ever had.  Lecture was clear and interesting.  Jackson made the class enjoyable and extremely rewarding.  Class requires a significant time commitment and is much harder than 184, but worth it in my opinion.

Perfect professor for chemistry. Down to earth and always ready with an answer and an explanation (or two or three if need be). He throws in his flair here and there and its always a treat. I am flabbergasted how much I WANT to go to his class in the mornings. Great intro to what a good class in college is.
Great teacher that works hard to help students.  Total hottie.  Like pie. Not pecan.  If you come to class and read, you'll do well.  Don't take this if you enjoy free time. P.S. He's hott.

Dr. Jackson is one of the best teachers I've had. He teaches clearly, cares about the students, and patiently helps students whether the questions seem dumb or not. Occasional spurts of humor and surprise demos add to the class. Most of the test material is covered in lecture, the quizzes are mostly easy, but the HW can mess with your grade a bit.
Great professor! Had him for Hnrs Foundations of Chem I and II.  The material is tough but he is very helpful and available if you have questions.

Professor Treaster is so awesome! I had Lisa for 560 and was really upset about how I wasn't able to have her again this semester. However, he quickly proved me wrong. He is so dedicated to his students! He did work outside of class that would benefit our group work. Multiple times he read a book for us and took notes and to us on his own time!

Had Alex for Visual Storytelling, Agency and currently Creative Concepting. One of the best teachers I've ever had! Shows genuine passion for what he does, is always willing to lend a helping hand and always uses fun examples in class. He breaks down things very simply and overall is just an amazing person. Couldn't recommend him enough!

I found him to be disrespectful, passive aggressive, and honestly petty. This class should be an online lecture class because it's very dull and no one participates. This class should be free, none of the information provided was worth money and it made me question a lot. Take this earlier than later so you can switch if necessary.

He is a great professor. Attendance is not mandatory but he chooses random days to give extra credit which really helped my grade. There are two exams and both are open note. There are not many assignments in the class which is why the extra credit was super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Treaster is a great professor whose classes are a breath of fresh air from your regular coursework. He provides the class with a multitude of group and individual exercises that further your grasp on the material whilst being entertaining. Do the readings, take loose notes, and ask questions and you'll succeed in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would recommend.

Dr. Tripathi was a great instructor for BSAN 440. He took the time in class to help us troubleshoot any problems and was very generous for testing parameters. You can tell he is genuine and cares about his students. Not sure why there are low ratings on here?

I took the honors version, and it was a disaster. There was no introduction to R or SQL, and the professor expected us to already know the concepts. Despite the class expressing confusion, he kept moving fast. Grading was inconsistent, with similar code receiving different grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most difficult class I've taken and it was an honors course. Grading is subjective and seems to pick & choose grades. Same answers to assignments as multiple people and all received different grades. The class was almost over and 90% of students could not code at all. Can't explain in 350 characters why not take his class. Please Save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This honors class is not structured like any other at KU. It failed to foster discussion and deliver what is expected. Grading was all over the place and no meaningful rubric was ever provided. The grading structure was heavily dependent on a few things and was very unclear. Would not recommend it to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: watch the videos and you'll be good. very easy to follow and keep up with. never met the guy in person but his voice isn't annoying and he seems nice. clear and good grading and easy to follow
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although the class was online, I really enjoyed having him as a professor. He was always so kind in his emails and very encouraging. Classwork was very simple with a video, discussion, and quiz each week with an occasional exam. I loved the consistency in this class and would 100 percent take another class with him in the future.
Williams is very nice and encouraging. He is very helpful and wants his students to do well.

Rehearsals frequently run past scheduled class times. Leadership and travel opportunities are disproportionately given to those in the Music School or Basketball Band. If you aren't in those specific groups, expect to be sidelined regardless of your audition performance. Not a merit-based environment for non-music majors.

The definition of what a band director should be. Cares so, so much about every single person in the band and is amazing at organizing and working with her students. I hope she knows the positive impact she's made on everyone here.

This is my last year being a part of the Marching Jayhawks, but the first year Toulouse became the director of the KUMJ. She has always been such an amazing teacher and person in general. If you looked her up to see if you should do band or not, do it! She's a drum major alumni and worked with the US army band so she knows her stuff. She is great!!

Dr. Lapierre is so amazing. She grades well, her videos are so helpful, and she works hard to make sure you understand what she is explaining. She grades really thoroughly on quizzes so you won't make the same mistakes on tests, and if you prepare and do the work, you will do well in this class.

She is understanding, didn't double penalize on grading but did a poor job of explaining ideas. It seemed like she didn't understand the curriculum herself - legitimately could not answer when I asked a question concerning two similar terms. You don't need the textbook you can learn everything with the packets she hands out.
A lot of reading, the quizzes are difficult. This class is not for everyone and I will not take more classes with this professor.

Very fun and bubbly person to be around 24/7! 4 major writing assignments but she is very supportive the whole way and is very lenient in how you approach these papers and cares about the effort you put in. Accepting of all ideas and creative thoughts, she's encouraging and motivating as you progress through the semester. Very personal too.

I have never really enjoyed English but Ms. Toay made it actually enjoyable. She is very understanding of things coming up and truly wants the best for each of her students. Homework and essays are given lots of time to complete and she is very aware we have lives and other classes on top of hers. MS. TOAY IS AWESOME!!

Ms. Toay has been my favorite English teacher I've had so far. She genuinely cares about your success inside and outside the classroom. She is a great communicator and teaches the subject in a learn-friendly way.
