SHE IS AMAZING! Literally one of the best English teachers here. She's very easy to work with and if you can't make it to class, she'll make sure you're caught up! Ms. Toay actually cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. I highly recommend her for English 101 and 102! She's also a young teacher so she understands we have lives.

Professor Tucker is very sweet, and there is an option to zoom into class instead of attending which is very helpful, but I think also hurts the discussion as people quit attending and don't talk online. She clearly has a passion for the subject, and if the students actually participate in class it can be very meaningful.

Got an A+ on every assignment besides one because I blanked on the due date. She refused to let me submit it late for any points. Told me if I get a 10/10 on final journal (I got 10/10 on first two) I would finish with an A-. She gave me a 9.8/10 and I ended with a B+. 

She immediately removed her course from my canvas after. 

Didn't miss class.

I took this class taught by Dr. Sherrie Tucker during the pandemic, and it is clearly different from the usual in-person classes. Wednesdays had an option for synchronous (Zoom) or asynchronous (Blackboard). The synchronous discussions were always engaging even though a majority of the class would choose asynchronous. Material is also interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Sherrie is one of the nicest professors Ive had at KU. Gives feedback on papers before you turn them in. Do the readings for the papers, follow her instructions, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Sherrie is the nicest person you will ever meet!!!!!! I turned in a paper over a week late and she let me revise it for credit.   Participate and enjoy the discussion. She has a laid back class with little in the way of busy work. Cannot recommend the class enough - ALSO DO THE READINGS
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor wasn't great. Communication was bad, and they were quite judgmental towards the whole class. The classes were repetitive, focusing on the same small topics over and over again. Plus, the grading was extremely tough, much more than what was reasonable for the level of the course.

He is an awful grader, doesn't have a clear grading rubric to determine what grade you'll receive for how much work you put in. Personally I went to the writing centers on campus and even after that it's hard to get an A or B on his essays. Participation points count a lot in his class. You also do ALOT of writing assignments,. Don't get him.
What can I say, it was a writing course. We did a lot of writing, like, a lot. It was difficult, but the instructor was nice. And helpful. Always ask for help.
very hard grader
Tough grader. Uses the book a lot. Knows what he's talking about, even if it's boring. You'll probably do really bad in his class if you're not at least trying.

Sometimes some classes go better than others, but it is generally a pretty easy going time. He is a hard grader and he expects a lot from his students, but he is also more than willing to help out and work with you, which I should have did more.
He is the easiest most helpful teacher out there!

Lance is really willing to help you with the papers and your grade. I went in to get help on a paper and it really paid off. He is a good teacher, however is a hard grader and uses the textbook often. Pretty much an easy class.

Lectures done at super fast speed and you can't record. Also doesn't provide the lectures to you if you miss/want to go back. Has no assignments so you have no way to do practice questions. No study guide, so again no way to practice for exams. Exam averages are between 60-70%. Does have a grade curve which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is very caring and knowledgeable!!

Amazing professor. Grading scale was curved and outlined clearly in the syllabus. His lectures were interesting and extremely relevent to the content covered on quizzes and exams. Exams and quizzes were difficult but extremely fair. The quizzes were group quizzes, learn to collaborate well! I would highly recommend this class for a challenge.

If you're going to take ochem, take it with Dr. Tunge // honors section

It's going to be hard regardless, so take advantage of smaller class sizes & make a connection. His lectures are personal and engaging. Test heavy but graded based on class average -- very doable. Always willing to go the extra mile. Highly recommend any classes with Dr. Tunge
Loved Dr. Tunge. One of the best teachers I've had. He assigned no homework, had a quiz every Friday, and the tests are hard, but he grades based on the class average, so it ends up being very fair.

Dr. Tunge is very intelligent, but his lecturers are fast paced and it is easy to fall behind. 

He is accessible for office hours but not much help. 

Not an understanding or accommodating professor for Title IX incidents.

Dr. Tunge is the best chemistry professor I have ever had. This is a hard class and you will definitely have to study a lot to get all of the concepts, but Tunge does an amazing job explaining the material in a way that connects all concepts. Most of the grade comes from 4 hard exams, but the final score is determined from the class average.

Dr. Tunge is a great guy, but I didn't learn from him. 
- Lectures/slides aren't on Canvas
- Recording is prohibited
- Graded only on weekly quizzes + 4 exams
- No assignments
- Textbook isn't always reliable for accurate information
- Khan Academy, practice problems in the textbook, and The Organic Chemistry Tutor on Youtube are your best friends
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great teacher, but beware premeds, memorizing your way through his class will be awful. Study the overarching reasons, and do some practice. DON'T just try to memorize methods and relations.
A god amongst men.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hes really cool I think. I hated the class at first, thought it was too hard for no reason. Moving on I saw the benefits, as youre graded off the class average instead of some arbitrary cut off. Tests were very fair. Nobody really knew where their grade was all semester though, but as we got closer ot the final it made more sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tunge is one of the smartest and best prof. I have had at KU. I suck at organic chemistry, but still managed 2A's. He doesn't punish you for taking honors. Hardest and most stressful class I have ever had, but wouldn't give up Tunge for any other prof. Just be prepared for bad grades, he curves at the end based on the average
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Tunge is one of the best professors I have had. Organic chemistry is a very difficult subject, but if you develop good study habits and attend the lectures, you'll really enjoy it. Highly recommend taking his classes.
Loved Dr. Tunges class. The class was very challenging, but since organic chemistry is tough either way you should take it from him.
He is a good teacher and very helpful. I would retake that class if I could. I think you should take the class it is hard but worth it!

This is an incredible professor that will teach you ochem in a way that you will never forget. Incredibly difficult until you get the hang of the way to think about the subject, but he is extremely willing to help you. Hands down one of the best teachers I've had at KU.

Phenomenal teacher. Always willing to accommodate students. Has tough quizzes, but studying them will prep you for the exams. Doing exercises throughout the chapter of the book and problems at the end of the book is incredibly helpful as well. Tunge is a brilliant researcher and professor, and is incredibly jovial and enthusiastic about the course.

The class was a blast. It was super cheesy chemistry humor. He lectured the entire class but ALWAYS stopped to answer questions (even if he was mid-sentence). You can tell he not only loves the material, he loves teaching it (he's won numerous teaching awards). That being said, the class isn't easy. Lots of studying is required, but it's worth it.
A great teacher!!!

Had Tunge for 625/627. Extremely difficult mainly due to the TA's. Tunge seems very arrogant when teaching, almost like it is a chore to be teaching you. He is extremely intelligent though. The midterm and final are impossible, but there is a massive curve at the end of the semester. Attend all labs and study for the quizzes and you will do fine.

Teaches from powerpoints and fails to get the information to the students effectively.  Mid-term and final are insanely difficult (class averages in the low D range), and the curve is minimal at best. If you have another option, go with it.

I've heard graduate students within the Chem Dept remark that Tunge is a genious and they are not far from the truth.  Though the course is a considerable challenge I would DEFINITELY recommend 628/630 over non-hnrs. No waiting in line outside the professor's office to ask questions and the curve is very generous.  I think no grade below a B.

Extremely difficult but very rewarding. Hard enough to destroy your will to live, but at the end you'll know organic 1 and 2 backwards and forwards. Great emphasis on actually learning concepts instead of rote memorization. Took honors section- there was a MASSIVE curve. Rewards hard work and improvement. Funny guy- great personality.

THE BEST TEACHER EVER! He's funny and interesting, and the best teacher ever! It is easy to pay attention, and makes his class fun, the tests are challenging, but they are like puzzles. He's easy to ask questions to, and will never make you feel dumb...TAKE HIM. It's more about how molecules work than bland memorization. KThxBYE.

Good teacher.  He explains organic chemistry very well.  Take this class if you really want to learn something about organic chemistry.  Don't take the class if you expect it to be easy. He is also pretty funny!

He's very knowledgeable, but tends towards verbal abuse with passive aggressive humor to make it "better" but no one ever does anything about it. He is challenging musically, and gets results, instead of using vocabulary, just yells and makes you do it again. He often says things about how stupid we are or how we don't deserve to be in his classes.
He is great! Super nice and friendly, wants to help in any way he can!

Dr Tucker drove the arts institute chorus harder than any conductor I've seen.  He was phenomenally picky about every single detail of every piece we performed and it payed off entirely. His methods are fairly unconventional, but they work.  He doesn't tolerate slacking off and he is incredibly dedicated to his students.

Dr. Tucker was our Choral Conductor at the Oklahoma Arts Institute. Never have I musically connected so quickly or strongly with any clinician before. He renewed my love for choral singing and my passion for music. To get the chance to watch him teach is magical.

I've never heard a choir master the sound that Tucker can get out of almost any group he conducts. He is one of my heroes and he absolutely knows what's up. The only students who ever complain about him happen to be the same students who are lazy and uncooperative. He's an incredible musician all around, and a phenomenal teacher.

Dr Tucker is fun, but a little egomaniacal.  His attendance policy is WAY too harsh, and much of the class is geared towards music ed majors.  He's a great guy, and very fun in class, but there are better choir directors out there, and I don't understand why people idolize him so much.

He rehearsed the orchestra for a production of Elijah. 1. He is clueless when it comes to string playing and bowings and everything along those lines. 2. He doesn't take his work seriously...he goofed off and didn't get the music down before the performance. 3. He can't cue and so the performance was a mess because none of us knew when to come in .
LOVED THIS PROFESSOR! He loves music and knows how to make the subject matter interesting. Pretty good looking too. ;)
Knows more about music than anyone since Brahms (cause he killed him).
Made music and singing fun for me again. The man is hilarious and the music selections are excellent. I learned more about vocal techniques in one semester than I had previously learned in my life.
Tucker Rocks!!! All guys come be in men's glee. He's a great teacher, his selections are awesome, and he is just flat out hilarious.
Tucker is a fabulous teacher! i am looking forward to the my next semester with him as my choir director!

He doesn't respond to e-mails that quickly but he is accommodating. He was willing to extend a due date when I explained the textbook I ordered would arrive later than expected. I do think the homework assignments were made by a previous professor, which is neither good nor bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The textbook was not listed in the syllabus as required, but we needed to purchase it anyway. This was especially confusing because he provided the readings for the first two assignments, without saying that he wouldn't provide after that. He can take several days to respond to emails as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I had him for Introductory Meteorology. He's pretty down to earth and a recent grad of Arizona State (he mentions this and I've seen him at the bars). Class is stupid easy if you show up. Not to mention he's easy to the eyes

Hilarious guy, interesting lectures, and fun class. This was one of my favorite classes. My only complaints were that his TA who graded almost everything wasn't as awesome as Tsutsui and you really don't need to read his book about Godzilla. Take this class if you have the chance.

Love, love, loved this class.  He's passionate about Japan and if you're slightly interested, it's great.  Easy grader, attendance not mandatory, and the reading material is pretty decent. One paper, midterm and the final.  He's super funny and his laugh is the greatest. Best class I've taken at Ku.

He is fun, creative, and very good at teaching.  Its been a year since I took his class and I remember nearly everything.  You learn a lot yet the class seems really easy.  I will remember his laugh until the day I die!

One of the best professors at KU hands down. He knows his stuff better then just about anyone able to teach this subject. Class is a lot of fun and is pretty easy if you just attend. He just asks that you understand the material, not memorize it all. Take it if you can!

Amazing teacher. Is truley interested in your learning, not the standard reciting of information, but that you understand what you are learning. Makes everything interesting and even mentions before hand when something might be a bit dry. Very helpful, teaches to the students who care and really want to learn. MUST TAKE CLASS!

One of the better professors I have ever taken classes from.  There is alot you can learn from him, including the little nuances about Japanese society that you would have never thought of before.  He is our local Godzilla expert, so be prepared for an abundance of unneccesary Godzilla knowlege that you will obtain from this class.

Awesome Class, he is a fun and interesting professor that makes you interested whether you want to be or not.  I highly recommend taking Prof. Tutsui if you have to take a Japanese History course, it is well worth it. Not to mention deserving of the hot pepper he requested we put next to his name.
No Comments
Probably the easiest Non-western class you can take. And he's extraordinarily enthusiastic.
EASY CLASS!! tests are easy, papers are easy! take it if you need an easy A..u still gotta do the work, but if u just take notes and study a little..ull be ok. no need to buy the book

I absolutely loved May. She is great to talk to and goes out of her way to help you with projects. 
She appreciates bold choices if you do it right — make sure you can explain your thought process. Take a lot of documentation photos, ask for help if you need, and you will be fine.

Took INDD 200. Get ready to have unclear instruction and little help outside of class. Use your TA's. Guard your work so May doesn't throw it across the room and destroy it. May's ok, just wasn't the right fit for the class and doesn't bring a great attitude.

Excuses don't make the difference to her on not putting in the effort on a project. Having small classes (8 people) doesn't leave room for it. Expects you to buy a lot of materials & not having the money for it isn't a valid excuse either. A lot of work outside of her class is necessary since she spends most of them talking and destroying models.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: May comes across kind of harsh when you first meet her, but she truly values the work of her students and wants to help them get better and achieve their goals. I loved her class and would gladly take classes with her again in the future.

Not structured like a typical classroom really. She really pushes you to try many options, but you have to be firm about your project directions. She seems to show interest in student projects and will often go out of her way to help if you ask. Would recommend.

Skipped class all the time and left us with a TA that didn't know what to do, gave unclear directions, and didn't give us back a single grade the entire year. Seemed like a nice lady sometimes, but not a good teacher.

No matter the constraints, ignore them and make something design-y.  Always late, and crits are worthless.  Will often push you in a direction, and then crit your work based on your following her advice.  Not a horrible person, just not truly an industrial designer.

Professor doesn't even use his own lecture videos but makes you pay to take proctored exams online. Never have I ever had to pay to take an exam in an online class. I might not have minded if the class itself was actually taught by the professor, but it feels lazily thrown together.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT BUY THE BOOK IF TAKEN FOR WINTER SESSION WASTE OF $100 Other than that, this was an easy course. I once missed points on a quiz question that I felt was confusing, I just emailed and explained my rationale to him and he gave me points back. Easy course, I finished with over 100%

Do whatever EC opportunities they offer (there will be a lot) and do the work online till you get 100% & you will get the A! I recommend studying for exams because those could really throw me off, even though I understood the content well. Use quizlet. I absolutely recommend reading the book... everything will make much more sense. Lots of work!

This class is mostly online but meets once a month to do a group activity for easy points. There are weekly online quizzes, the main lectures of tests are online and then definitely read your book. The tests are in person and are kind of hard. Tyler is sweet and easy on the eyes, but not a very good communicator. Offers a lot of extra credit.

He is a great professor and knows the content super well. For this class, you have to put in the effort though if you want a good grade out of it. Go to all the in person lectures. Nothing is posted on canvas except homework. He explains what you should know clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best professor in the entire KU econ department. 10/10 cannot recommend enough. You need to go to class and take notes but if you go to class you will get an A.

I have taken both of his undergrad econ courses and WOW I wish I could take more. He doesn't use canvas or slides, he handwrites on the whiteboard. Follow along with his whiteboard notes and you will do well on the exams. If you are an econ major take his courses if you want to actually learn econ and not hate your life. ALSO he curves at the end!

Dr. Tsvetanov is truly the best economics professor at KU. Every lecture is enjoyable and the exams are on what is covered in class. He really wants every student to understand the material, so he breaks down everything to the perfect level. TAKE HIS CLASSES THEY ARE AMAZING!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tsvetan is a great guy. He has an accent but you can still understand clearly if you pay attention. Show up to class, do the homework and participate occasionally and you will do fine in this class. Expectations and grading criteria are crystal clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Tsvetanov was a fantastic professor. His expectations were crystal clear and the class was extremely manageable as long as you did one thing: show up. There is a textbook, but it isn't needed if you attend class, as all the homework problems are based on his lectures and his exams are based on the homework. TLDR: Show up and you'll pass.

Super easy class. All homework and exams are online and not lengthy. Lectures help but are not necessary. Discussion section attendance wasn't required, but attendance could correlate to extra credit at the end of the semester. Such an easy class, and the professor did a great job. Take this class with him if it's a part of your degree requirement!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class is super great, and the professor was very nice. I thought that the class was very very easy and that it was not difficult. I showed up to every class, but do not think it is necessary. The labs are not mandatory and in my personal opinion are a waste of time, but other than that it is super easy.

One of the easiest classes I have ever taken. Every homework assignment and exam is online. You get a homework assignment once a week that is 10 questions and 3 exams that are all 20 questions. He is a very nice professor and attendance is not mandatory I would 100% recommend this professor and class.
A very black and white professor exhibiting extreme professionalism.

Overall, good professor. The class was all online (including the exams) which made it fairly easy to get an A. The lecture notes and lecture videos are very helpful and the exams/homework come from the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Tsvetanov is one of the best professors that I've had at KU. He is very clear with the class criteria and is a great lecturer. You do not need a book to succeed in his class, as showing up to each lecture and taking organized notes will get you an A. He does not try to trick you on the homework, nor the tests. Highly recommend.

Everyday is a lecture, if I was to take the class again I wouldn't buy the book, you don't need the access code because he posts it on blackboard, one quiz a week and there are 4 exams he will drop your lowest one. Make sure you study because every test matters. Its either an A B C or D grading scale. He does not give extra credit. Show up
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't the most interesting or fun, but he explains things very well and goes over all the relevant exam material. Homework is light; there are only five short assignments throughout the semester. Skipping class will be dangerous as there are pop quizzes at least once per week.
I really enjoyed having Tsvetan for Econ 142. He is really easy going and he goes through the material at a good pace. He tells you what to study for the exams and the quizzes were open note.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: read the all of the chapters that are required for tests the night before and you will probably do well. I went months without understanding anything in class, and then learning all the material on my own the night before. Tsvetan is cool/chill and all the tests are multiple choice but they are not necessarily easy.

Super nice professor. Straight to the point and gives good examples in lecture. There is no homework, only 4 exams, and 15 quizzes. He drops the lowest exam and 5 quizzes. Overall, I enjoyed this class and would take again.
Go to class and you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: What a man. Besides his saucy sweater vest game, he's a great professor, excellent lecturer, very helpful (especially if you go into his office hours). Tests are straightforward and he reviews the class before every midterm. As long as you pay attention in class and take good notes, you will pass.

Textbook isn't mandatory if you go to every class and take good notes, but if you miss a class or didn't do a great job on notes it really helps to have it. There's nothing in the lectures that isn't covered in the textbook, but he makes an effort to explain things and keep it interesting. No homework, just quizzes and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tsvetan is a very interactive lecturer. I attended his office hour a day ago to discuss the econ major and he was more than welcoming. If you show up to class, sit in the front section, and interact as needed, he will notice you and your grade will reflect that.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tsvetan Tsvetanov, the Profesor with two first names. He's been the best teacher I've had throughout my time at KU, always helpful and respectful, available to talk outside of class. If you participate during class, he'll notice you and respect you. DO THE HOMEWORK! There's only like 5 easy assignments throughout the semester, but you HAVE to do em

Very intelligent and a great teacher in general. Lectures are optional, you can learn all necessary material through textbook if desired. Material is somewhat interesting, though most concepts you've learned in previous macro classes. He's incredibly helpful in office hours if you have questions. Would certainly take another class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tsvetan is very passionate about his job and is always willing to help students outside of class when they need extra help.  His lectures are interesting and tests and homework reflect what he goes over in class.  Definitely would take another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fun class, good informationhistorical narrative, but his guidelines on assignments are vague

A good professor. He's not very clear on directions, so talk to him if you have questions. Attendance is important and the reading load gets heavier as the semester goes on. He also requires a reading response the night before class. Stay on top of the assignments and you'll be fine.

Not a good teacher at all. He never tells you want he wants and then grades you harshly. He gives you a ton of reading but doesn't explain any of it. He will make you write short papers but not explain what he wants you to do with them. He has been by far one of the worst teachers that I have ever had at KU and I would never recommend this class.

Professor Uchiyama is very passionate and knowledgeable about Japanese history, but he often lacks clear expectations for his assignments. The class material is interesting and his lectures are engaging, but the reading load can be huge. Keep track of the syllabus - he doesn't post it online. Attendance is also a pretty big part of the grade.

Expect class discussions and tons of weekly reading Professor Uchiyama is a fun and charismatic guy who truly cares about and understands history. He expects a lot from you and makes you a better student for it. Gives awesome readings his classes always make me laugh, inspires you to work hard and does his best to help you, best professor at KU.

He does not know how to teach. He spent classes reading from a piece of paper, showing pictures on powerpoint, and had trouble giving thought provoking questions for class discussion. When students did ask questions, he had a habit of interrupting them, giving vague responses, and showing little appreciation for their interest in the topic.

Professor Uchiyama is new to teaching, but really knows his subject. His grading expectations were not always clear, but if you go to class and make an attempt at doing the  readings you will pass his class.

New Japanese History Professor.  I really enjoyed the class.  It was a lot of material to cover, but the readings he selected were informative and fun to read.  I feel like I got a lot more than "just the facts" out of this class. Uchiyama is really nice and personable.  I would recommend his classes!
Lectures do not help....go to his office hours and he will show you MAGIC!!!
he is too old to teach

This man is the definition of badass.  He's 83, and been teaching since 1950.  He broke his arm last summer by FALLING OUT OF A TREE, and he just keeps going.  Bob Umholtz invented engineering, and has actually developed technologies that are now industry standards.  He's the only ME teacher whose primary job is teaching, and he loves his job.

He has been at KU since the '40s. So yes he is a bit old. This makes it REALLY hard to hear (and thus follow) him in class. At first I really didn't like him, but I started going to his office and found out that he is UBER helpful and nice. His classes are fine you just have to try and take the time to talk to him.

Mumbles a lot, and not particularly helpful even when you can hear him. Lectures hop around with students left in the dust. He will help you if you go to office hours, but if you ask anything but a cookie-cutter question, you're not going to get a proper answer. TAs are much more helpful than he is.

Passing Umholtz's classes are like a right of passage.  Lectures are HORRIBLE, full of his assumption that the students know exactly what he is doing each step of the way.  However-he is very  helpful when you ask for help in his office.

I am glad to see it was not just me who thought this professor completely unhelpful and useless. Impressive CV, no doubt a smart guy, but he should not be teaching. He should locked be in a room somewhere churning out numbers and equations. I have only ever met one teacher in my life who has contempt for his students-this one. Unforgivable.

Imagine a place;you don't know where you are or what you are doing here.There is a passage out, a flimsy staircase made of the mumblings of an old man.You scream out, but he can't hear you with his face pressed directly into a whiteboard.You inevitably fall, and your mind is treated like a girlish man in prison by the material. You get a B, max.
When a 75 is an A and a 23 passes a test, odds are it's not the students' faults.  Just saying.  The material isn't really that bad, he just doesn't teach it. Also: so old!
I must say just one thing: Our test AVERAGE was 53. That explains enough. SO OLD!

This class has been the single worst college experience of my life. We are currently five weeks in and I learned more from the 30min guest lecture today than the 5 weeks prior. I would rather eat a spider than finish this course. Umholtz = terrible

Dude hasn't changed his handout sheets since the stone age. His textbook is absolutely useless other then an expensive paper weight. Attendance of his class is mandatory if you feel like having a chance of passing, but bring binoculars because his handwritting is smaller then his "units"size if you get the picture. All i have to say is tenure blows

Umholtz is really old school. He doesn't even use a computer. However, he has teaching down to a science! He taught Faddis and Faddis is about to retire. That's how old Umholtz is. His tests are difficult, but fair. Study hard to get an A.
Worst professor in the ME department hands down. Only faculty to not have a PhD too...
kind of hard to follow, but overall a good teacher
No Comments
Ugh. my worst class ever ever ever. a nightmare teacher. avoid at almost any cost
Freeze this guy's DNA!!  But lose the outdated vax compiler!
This professor was amazing and I loved the class, I have been able to apply the concepts in my every day life. The environment was so healthy and fun take this class!!

I highly enjoyed this first-year lecture and its content. Professor Velasquez made the class very enjoyable and engaging, and took time at the beginning of classes to connect with the students. Not a lot of homework at all, but it was important to do the readings ahead of class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Velasquez always answered any questions that students would have in class -- you just have to show up. Attendance -- although it wasn't worth a grade -- is necessary to pass this class. His lectures, which cover the readings, and the opportunity to engage in class discourse will help you pass this class. Always ask questions and attend class!

I learned so much from Dr. Velasquez. He is there to help you if you simply ask questions and let him know you are struggling. When I took COMS 207 with Dr. Velasquez, he would pause lectures and provide plenty of time for students to voice their concerns. His grades are test heavy, but if you show up to class discussion, you will be fine :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Treats an elective as a Graduate Level class. In his own words, "this course was as hard as classes you'll take in Graduate school". Wouldn't recommend if you have other options.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This professor wants you to fail based upon how he grades. The class has a D avergae, and he is unclear about expectations.

Professor Velasquez was absolutely horrible. His grading techniques were unorganized and he is never clear about expectations of assignments. Don't take his classes unless you want to get a 59.9% in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Velasquez is pretty accessible outside of class.I had no problems reaching out to him after class or through email.His tests are heavily based on lecture and the readings. He posts the slides and tells you what you need to know about the readings during class.He also allows you to ask questions about the tests and what  content you need.

Professor Velasquez gave me little to no help when I emailed him with questions. He is one of the worst professors I've had at KU and strongly advise everyone not to take a course from him. He goes into little detail of what is expected for group projects/exams and gives no valuable feedback.
He is absolutely horrible. Does not go into detail about anything and contradicts himself constantly. Do not take you will not pass this class, the whole class has a 60% average.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: An intro-level class where you really learn nothing new or that you can't get better in a different class, it's not a great class to take. Quizzes and tests are just regurgitating the textbook with very little thought. The lectures also regurgitate the textbook but do so right after you take a start of class quiz where you just did the same thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Twarog is a tough grader. HW is due at the beginning of each class; it consists of 4-6 long-answer problems, worth 10 points each. Thorough explanations are required, this takes loads of time. Be prepared for a B or C if you don't want to hate your life. Tests are curved. He knows his stuff though, and he's kinda funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Twarog is super engaging and I loved his lectures.  The recitation sessions were really helpful and I learned a ton in the class.

Unlike many of those who've left a rating, I found Professor Twarog to be a great teacher. I had absolutely no background in astronomy or physics, or any science for that matter, but so long as I kept up with the reading material and went to his small group help sessions, I was able to get an A in his class without even having to take the Final.

Bruce is hilarious and crazy. I loved having him as  ateacher. You HAVE to pay attention in class or you will look dumb when he calls on you. This was one of my favorite classes so far at KU. To be honest, I never read the book. I studied the questions and my notes a few nights before the tests and got an A on every one. Beware. The tests are hard.

This is not an entry level class!!!!!!! Harder than most of the 500 level classes i've taken. He zooms through material and randomly calls on you and asks you questions that you most likely don't know the answer to. He suddenly stomps on the ground or pounds on a table like a lunatic. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS unless you have background in physics

I had to switch out of this class 1/3 through the semester to make sure I didn't fail a gen ed requirement before graduating! I'm a senior, and up until this class I never got anything below a B. I'm pretty sure I would have failed his course, because he seriously moves at the speed of light through the material. Far too fast for an intro course.
Extremely hard. it is by far the hardest class i have ever taken and if you have no physics background, it will be very very difficult to pass his astronomy class

Warning: Bruce is the most incomprehensible, scatter-brained professor I have ever come across. He knows the material, yes, but it is impossible to follow him! This is a terribly hard class, and if you are a bad test taker, beware. I would steer away from any of his classes if at all possible.

FROM STUDENT TO STUDENT any comment you have read is from a kid who ended up loving this guy because they are prob. obsessed with astronomy. if you are anywhere near normal do not attempt this class. VERY VERY VERY VERY VERY hard.

Knows the material very well and is very helpful to those who ask questions.  His lectures, however, are often difficult to follow because he goes so fast. He is also somewhat of a "gotcha" grader on the homework, he expects you to know the answers to things that have not been discussed in class.  Tests are killer also. Ask questions in class!
Bruce is one of the best teachers in the department and his dedication to the topic shows through. He is available to all of his students and his classes are always a pleasure.
Answer specific questions directly, makes every attempt to explain and clarify.  Laid back personality, but quality professor.  Very open to office drop-ins.  Highly recommend!
This class was fantastic.  If you have any interest in Astronomy, take this class.  The fundamentals that help you understand the cosmos is awe inspiring.

This class is hard, and yes you actually have to read the material and study intensely for the tests. It takes a while to get used to his test questions and the way he lectures, but you eventually get the hang of it and it grows on you. Out of all of my classes this semester, I learned the most from this class. He is very animated!

This class is hard, and yes you actually have to read the material and study intensely for the tests. It takes a while to get used to his test questions and the way he lectures, but you eventually get the hang of it and it grows on you. Out of all of my classes this semester, I learned the most from this class. He is very animated!

If you want any kind of life in college, do not take this class! To receive a decent grade you will have to live and breathe this course. The teacher doesn't make it any easier. He'll throw in pop quizzes the first class after an exam! The tests are purposely tricky to throw you off. Not for people with average work ethic, must be very dedicated.

GREAT teacher!I love the way he lectures, he's really animated and hilarious, lots of spontaneous yelling and jumping around, really makes it easy to pay attention. He also explains difficult concepts in a way that all can understand.His class was hard, but as long as you do the optional homeworks and listen in class you can get a good grade.I did.
One of the hardest teachers yet, BUT if you work AND show up for class you'll love it. The "why" can and is always answered

This guy knows what he is talking about! Make sure to do all of the problem sets before the tests! If you can do those you are in good shape! Be sure to do the reading to because that is where the quiz ?'s come from. I learned more in this class than I have in any other! I wish he taught more classes relavent to my major!!!

I am bad at science; so if I can get an A in this class, it's possible for anyone. But you do have to actually do the work. Do ALL of the problem sets before the test, take notes, and go to his office hours and recitation sessions! He's really open to questions, you just have to make the time to ask them. It was tough, but I loved this class.

His class is not easy.  That being said, he is a wonderful teacher.  I missed a week of classes because of an injury and he still worked with me.  Read the text book and do the problem sets.  I would take another course from this guy.  If you can get through the first month of classes, you will be allright.  Read the text book.  Class is easy.

I know some people will tell you the class is a little hard, but Prof Tuarog does well in explaining the material, which by the way is very interesting. His eccentric lectures keeps you alert! Go to class and pay attention, you'll be fine.

He's very nice teacher and teaches the subject matter well. But you HAVE to read the chapters, do the test review, do the RQs, and you have to goto class. The random quizes can really make or break your grade. They are very easy if you have done the reading the night before. I learned more in this class than any other class I've taken at KU.
No Comments

For an intro course this class is WAY TO HARD!! His tests are total crap... I spend 95% of my free-time trying to figure out what is going on and I still get D's on my test.. Unless you want a big challenge stay away. I talked to a graduation advisor today and she said that she see's more F's and D's on Arts forms form this class than any other...

The guy is this crazy mad scientist type, but I totally thought that was hot. The class is really hard, and the only way to get an A is read every word in the text book, do all the problems in the problem sets, go ask questions during office hours and during study sessions. I worked my ass off because I was really interested in learning that crap, and pulled an A. Drop the class if you don't want to do tons of work for it.
This guy can do a lot with a limited amount of time.  I took one of his hour long courses and he moves fast and talks fast, but he knows the topic thoroughly.
No Comments

God, this class was so difficult. I took this to fulfill a requirement, and regretted every minute of it. Somehow I managed to get a B, but I don't really know how it happened. If you're not a physics or astronomy major, get out of this class quickly! Eith
Good but not helpful

This class is really interesting. It is totally worth taking (if you have a basic knowledge of physics). It is not impossible if you do the readings and problems sets, which Twarog says uprfont is the only way to get an A. It's true. Just do the work and you will get the grade. It's a good class.

I am a History major.  My husband talked me into taking the class to fulfill a requirement.  He's lucky I didn't divorce him!  VERY difficult class.  However, I went in to his office nearly every day.  He sat with me and helped me.  I got a C.

I'll admit I filled this out because I disagreed with what some of my classmates said.  Yes, the class is not a piece of cake, but it's not impossible if you do what he says, either.  I can honestly say I learned something new everyday in class.
This guy is unbelievably hard.  Tests are just plain insane.  The odd gyrations and odd facial expressions don't help, either.

Took this class to satisfy a physical science credit.  EVIL, EVIL man!  I missed 1 lecture all semester for my best friend's funeral, went to every recitation session, read the book and studied for hours and still got a D.  He actually called me stupid!!!
His tests are insane and impossible to pass with a decent grade.  If you're not an astronomy or physics major, I would not take this course.

Don't take her for Span 443 study abroad ruins the experience & the most passive aggressive teacher. She isn't a native speaker; her Spanish is bad & hard to understand from a native speaker. She makes up words and adds Spanish accents to them, pretending its Spanish. Would get mad when you were gone from class if sick, even with a doctor's note.

Very kind woman! Participation matters 100%. There is an assignment due twice a week before class, but you could write a few lame sentences and she would give you full points. She gives you a grade based on your overall performance; attending class, participating, and your Spanish improvement. She will call you out if you have not been speaking.

She is a SWEETHEART, such a generous and caring person. She is very aware that her class is easy, but wants her students to actually get something out of the class. She is not a hard grader, but go to class.

I think she is one of my favorite Spanish professors so far. She is very knowledgable, wants students to succeed, and facilitated an open and fun classroom environment. The course covers such a huge timespan and she was able to make learning it easy and enjoyable. I had a great experience with this class.
She can be rude to her students and it is obvious she is not a native speaker of Spanish. Average teacher.

Margot was a great teacher- she was very understanding, always well prepared and had interesting things to say. All of her assignments were interesting and pretty fun to complete (as far as essay writing can be fun). Her tests were in line with what one might expect for a spanish lit course and the reading and discussions were sufficient prep
She is good.

I also had Margot for SPAN 340, and both classes benefitted my ability to write Spanish. Margot offered a lot of help outside of class to improve my writing and answer any questions I had about a Spanish major. Occasionally, both classes got mundane with the same lessons each day, but my overall experience with Margot was great.
Simple class. Follow instructions
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Public speaking is a difficult subject for most but, Professor Vellinga makes you feel comfortable and is always offering help. Attendance was not mandatory but I loved the environment she created where I always showed up. I definitely recommend Professor Haley, you won't regret it!

Most enjoyable class I have taken which is saying a lot considering it was public speaking. She is great at making the classroom a comfortable environment and we were always laughing during her lectures. She really cares about her students and goes out of her way to help you. Plus she cancels class a lot which is always nice! Super easy A.

I loved her class! She made the speaking part of the class easier and less nerve wracking. Her lectures are amazing and the tests are a breeze. She gives many opportunities for extra credit and is always accessible.

COMS 342 is a class with a lot of group work. The lectures are okay. Haley gets off topic a lot, so sometimes it is enjoyable but it is hard to follow especially for someone who likes things to be more in order. I wouldn't recommend this class if you want straight forward lectures and assignments, but would if you like to have fun in class.

Haley was one of the best professors I've ever had. She makes class fun and enjoyable and makes a point to know each of her students. I hate group work and projects but this class actually wasn't too bad. I would suggest taking this class with Haley as the professor, she's amazing.
Awesome!

I typically dislike working in groups, but this class makes it bearable. Haley's lectures were typically topical, however occasionally got off topic. She's very energetic and feels strongly about what she teaches, which is always nice. While the class was relatively easy, having to set up a fundraiser with people you don't know is a challenge.

She's a good violinist, but she travels a lot. I got tired of subs. It's hard to improve without a consistent studio teacher. Responds to email. Knowledgeable, but unclear when explaining technique. Not encouraging. Submits semester grades on last possible day. Few students get to perform regularly. Doesn't give grade updates during semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Veronique is a wonderful violinist who clearly enjoys performing more than teaching. She treats students as clients, with no effort in trying to build a good environment for the studio. I was never encouraged to play meaningfully. She often makes me hate my instrument. Realizing your teacher couldnt care less about you really hurts. Dont be fooled,

Veronique makes you work hard and become a better musician. She focuses on technique, which is important for me right now. It's rare to get feedback from her, especially nice comments. In lessons she takes things seriously, is energetic, and makes sure everything is clear.

Does not require attendance, but says that if you attend 80% of the classes, then you can get up to 25 points of extra credit at the end of the semester. Fair tests, tough papers. Grade based on just tests and papers. VERY boring lectures. Puts all of the information in his slides, yet you still need to come to class for EC. Overall, fine teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Vernberg would benefit hugely from a public speaking class. He is not very clear and not a confident lecturer which makes it hard to pay attention to him.  Reads off the slides without adding anything interesting like having a relatable story, etc. He is a good guy though.

4 tests & 4 papers. Optional paper 5 & test 5 to replace a low score. Up to 25 extra credit points for good attendance/participation. Vernberg made lecture feel like FOREVER!! He just reads off the powerpoint slides. Tests are SO HARD compared to lectures. I was excited to take this class, but it became the class I looked forward to going to LEAST.

Easy class. He posts slides online and will just read them to you in class. Lectures become redundant. Harps on one subject for too long, which makes class hard to attend or pay attention in. Gives extra credit for attending 80% of classes. Drops lowest test and paper so no mandatory final. Tests are MC, T/F, short answer, and 2 essays.

Vernberg is a good guy (a Miami guy).  Though, he does say a lot of words to get across a minute point.  If you read the chapters and study... you'll do well.  75% of the info is in them.  The rest comes from his slides.  Tests consists of multiple choice, true false, fill in blank, and essay.  If you read and go to class you'll get an A!
Difficult to understand.

Professor Vinjimoor is very receptive to feedback... if you feel there was an issue with an assignment or quiz and let her know she will take your feedback into consideration and often make changes because of it. The lectures are pretty boring but the homework isn't bad. You must go to class.

Shanthy does her best, but the classes are 99% lecturing which she makes extremely boring. I actually have to drink coffee before class or else I will fall asleep. Be prepared to use SQL developer and start coding your heart out. If you skip you will fall behind and is hard to catch up. The HW is pretty difficult too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Shanthy is arguably the least fun professor I've ever had. If you're ready to be insulted for asking questions, shes your gal!
This was her first semester teaching this course at KU. Be prepared to use SQL everyday and ask any questions that you may have because if you fall behind it will be very hard to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
Only take this class if you want to constantly feel like you are writing while running out time. She doesn't know an appropriate amount of work. There is a week were you will have a 3 page essay due on Sunday, a 13 page essay due on Tuesday, a discussion post due on Friday and another 3 page essay due on Sunday. 
Save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was truly remarkable and her enthusiasm for her work is strong! Her lectures are not only captivating but also informative.

This class was atrocious, to say the least. Granted it was an 8-week course, but it was just awful. I took WGSS 320: From Witches to Goddesses, and somehow she made this subject not fun, as well as being lazy. She does not know what is an appropriate amount of work to assign to students. For your sanity, do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I love Professor Vicente. This is my second time taking one of her classes, & while her classes are on the more difficult side and can be very writing intensive, she is such a great professor that I do not mind. She cares so much about her students & truly wants them to succeed. She tries to celebrate everyone's bday too and she's also hilarious.

This class was alot. Very writing intensive, had a paper due like every week and you have to read a lot. can't believe I got an A but because of how repetitive it was, you knew what to expect each week so you could get into the routine of it then it isn't so bad. it was online so idk the prof that well but she seemed kind + cares about students ;;
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took "Intro to Queer Theory". Heavy amount of reading, but good content - can get away with skipping some readings. Easy 1-2 question quizzes online. Online & in class discussion. 8-10pg research paper at end of semester, lots of your grade goes into easily-scored preparation for paper. Intelligent & assists with your work. Easy-going class/prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is a very funny person and is very open. Her tests and quizzes include all short answer, it is very easy if you understand and read the material/lectures. Her lectures are kinda boring and she rambles a lot, however, she is very caring and extremely friendly.
AN ABSOLUTE DREAM PROFESSOR

She keeps her class interesting just by being her. There is a LOT of reading (4 books and textbook). A paper on each paper, and quiz over the reading each week, so you have to read. Only 3 test (midterm and final) both are essay format but she gives a list of essay questions she will choose from so its easy. Also, attending class is a must!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Vicente is so sweet and very funny. She's a great historian who knows what she's talking about and grades fairly. She does get off topic a lot which can be fun but time-consuming. The structure of the class could have also been better and the assignments were pretty redundant. Keep in mind that this was a thesis class.

Dr. Vicente is incredibly nice. She's approachable, always willing to meet outside of class to discuss your progress, and happy to give feedback on your work. She comes across as flighty and distracted, but don't let that fool you. She's an excellent historian with a lot of knowledge. Take her advice seriously, and you'll do great. A great prof.
Dr. Vicente is a great professor. I have taken two of her classes and I would take another if I weren't graduating.
Dr. Vicente is awesome. I have taken two classes taught by her and I would take a third if I weren't graduating. She is fabulous!

Prof. Vicente is thrilling and insightful. Truly dedicated to her students and pushes them to fulfill course requirements, but expects rigor and no sloppy scholarship.One must work in her courses, but the result is most definitely worth it.

I loved Marta as a Women Studies teacher. This class was extremely easy and also very interesting. She gets a bit off topic and loses her concentration, but that was always hilarious to me. She has a wonderful personality and she has such a good sense of humor which made the semester ten times better!

Large class setting, but if you sit in front you will get to know her pretty well and if you enjoy fading into the background you can do that too. Very fun class, she is a really funny women and great teacher. She really cares.
This professor is both fierce and fabulous! She really cares about the class and the students and really helps you develop your research interests.

Not an awful class, but it's difficult to understand her. She is well educated on the subject matter but often got off topic that I wondered what it had to do with the class, and I eventually lost interest.  Papers are over 4 books you read and tests are essay form, so you can pass but effort is needed for an A.

LOVE HER!! My favorite professor. I go out of my way to take her classes if possible. Everyone should have her in class at least once during their college time at KU. SHE IS THE BEST! Need to do the readings and pay attention in class but with her it isnt difficult to do :)

Prof. Vicente is great!Class discussion were always very engaging.She was always interested to hear what everyone had to say and made sure that everyone in class got the chance to state their opinion.She is patient, funny, and amazingly fashionable.Not only was she one of the best professors I've had, she also was one of the best dressed!

I really enjoyed this class and the professor is great. She really interacts with everyone and the tests were essay, but pretty fair for the amount of reading and class time, and four papers with the readings. It wasn't bad at all!
Prof. Vicente is great! I would definitely recommend of her classes.
I loved Marta!  I didn't get the grade I wanted, but I still love her.  I worked my butt off and I think that's why I got as good a grade I did.  She was extremely helpful and an absolute pleasure!

I didn't put easy at a 5 because you have to work, but that isn't a bad thing.  If someone takes her and fails it is their fault because she does nothing but help.  She is hilarious, and kind, and made very abstract theoretical notions very, VERY, uderstandable.  One of my favorite professors ever!
marta was great, okay english may not be her first language (you may have to actually pay attention)but at least she is intelligent and has a sense of humor.
No Comments
UGH.  Marta.  What a buzz-kill.  Her classes are excrucating.  If you can figure out what the hell she's talking about, you might be able to stay awake.

I had a 4.0 before this class. Artman is very lazy he makes no study guid or notes or videos or anything to help you study. All you get is a massive book and you are somehow expected to know all the questions from that. You also only one min per question. He 's nice just not a very good teacher. Have an A in every class I took exept his.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Artman was wildly inconsistent in his assignments and grading. He went from giving us four fairly easy questions on weekly quizzes to anywhere from twenty to thirty. He also makes you participate in online discussions, and my posts went from 100% to around 85% with no change in the quality or quantity of what I posted. Wouldn't recommend.

This guy is hilarious and incredibly intelligent. His knowledge spans multiple fields in the humanities and he finds interesting ways to incorporate all of them into his lectures. One of my favorite professors from freshman year. All quizzes are online, midterm is super easy, and he's generous with curves/dropping low grades. Great guy, fun class.

His lectures are very long, but very clear and directly correspond to the tests. The bookwork counts for most of the grade, and he grades hardly on that, so take your time on those. He can be VERY rude at times, and thinks very highly of himself. Suck up, sit in front row, and don't use your phone. Study the review guide and you'll ace the tests.

His lectures are very long, but very clear and directly correspond to the tests. The bookwork counts for most of the grade, and he grades hardly on that, so take your time on those. He can be VERY rude at times, and thinks very highly of himself. The review (class before test) is very helpful. Study the review guide and you'll ace the tests.

It should be noted I took an online asynchronous course, but it is still evident he simply assigned very dense readings to understand entirely on our own and never actually made it clear what we should be learning. It was hard to complete assignments successfully for a good grade and was frustrating to experience. His grading criteria also varied.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This course has been a struggle for me. It is completely asynchronous (no meetings), so I have never heard the professor's voice. the assignments are specific and require a deep understanding of the  reading and video recourses provided. Given that I have never talked to vitevitch, I can't speak on his character.

This class is easy because there is so little work but you can tell he put 0 work into the courses. you have to teach yourself everything with the worst resources possible. Also, he has deadlines but does not post any so you have no idea when to turn stuff in on canvas unless you continually refer to the syllabus.

If you're just looking to pass the class for a requirement or an easy A, you can learn everything that you need from the book. If you're interested in psychology, his lectures will give you a lot of interesting tidbits, but aren't at all necessary to pass the class. Can be entertaining at times, and his enthusiasm is infectious.

One of the most animated teachers I have ever had. Vitevitch is so entertaining throughout his lectures. He keeps the content informative, fascinating, and even interactive. I took the class because I thought Psychology would be cool to learn. I drastically underestimated with those expectations... With Dr. Vitevitch, Psych 105 was AWESOME.

Easy class. Only 3 assignments + 1 required event and they were essentially graded on completion, so as long as you turned in all 3 things you are guaranteed an A. Class usually ended early and he cancelled 3-4 of them.
To put it short: EASY class. Meh professor.

The psyc dept seems to want to make this class better, but that seems to have fallen short. A three day a week lecture with "flipped classroom" style teaching did not do much. We learned all material from an online book outside of class and showed up a few days a week to hear Vitevich tell us some additional info. Class time was not necessary.

This class may as well have been online. Didn't talk about much in lecture,; he showed us a few videos and shared a couple stories. I didn't have a problem with Vitevitch; seemed nice and tried to joke around sometimes. Only had a final. If you do well on the online homework (easy) and study for the final, you'll get an A.

Professor Vitevitch may have been one of the worst professors I have had during my time at KU. His lectures were uninteresting and useless. The online homework seemed more of a way to trick students rather than actually help us learn psychology. Furthermore, Professor Vitevitch was not polite or respectful of students opinions and views.

Dr. Vitevitch is a good professor who knows a lot about the field of psychology.  I disliked the online textbook format of the class, but in-class Dr. Vitevitch offered lots of discussion which I appreciated.  He was very clear when explaining what needed to be done to be successful on individual assignments.  Interesting class!

I took the Honors version of psych, and it has hands down been the easiest class I have taken here at KU. you basically have an hour worth of online homework a week, and assuming you complete it all, you will get an A in the class.
He's a pretty swell guy.
Vitevitch is a really nice guy. Awkward, but nice. Class was a little disorganized at times, but easy to follow.

Dr. Vitevitch is an incredibly rude and annoying human being, but he is an ok professor. Lectures can be kind of boring, but he is funny at times. His tests are fair, and he is willing to meet with students.

Professor Vitevitch knows a lot about the material. If you read the textbook and study for tests, you will do very well! Lecture can get a little boring, but overall it is pretty easy for being an honors class.

Prof. Vitevitch was very engaging with the students and cares that they do well. Even if you don't know/care much about Psychology (I didn't) take his class or seminar, he will make it interesting for you.

Prof. V was really helpful and engaging. He truly cares about his students, and does what he can to give them the best experience. Some of the topics we discussed didn't always interest me, but he still made class fun. He's a good guy, flexible, and willing to work with the students.

I took the honors section of the 104 class, and as far as I can tell it wasn't any harder (but was a class of 30 instead of hundreds). Professor Vitevitch is a really good lecturer - engaging and gives plenty of examples to help you understand the complex ideas. You'll have to study a lot for the tests, but if you put in the work you'll be fine.

Class was always very interesting, Dr. V definitely is passionate about psychology. If you go to class, you don't need to buy the book.  Tests are extremely easy if you go to class, you can drop the final if you do well enough on the first four tests

I think he may have recently changed his teaching style or curriculum because the past comments are completely false. This class was incredibly boring, I had a hard time staying awake every day. He takes pride in making his test harder than what they should be and he's almost impossible to get a hold of unless you get him right after class.

OK. He is clearly a very nice guy, he cares a lot, but sitting through this class is a terribly boring experience. I dread going to class. The stuff is insteresting but he has terrible humor and its such a drain to sit through his lectures. He should be teaching a lecture in budig or something, but in front of a small class its just awkward. Nicegu

GREAT professor! His lectures are very interesting and he gives great, memorable examples. If you pay attention and do a little bit of studying, you'll do fine on the tests. Also, no homework, which is definitely a plus. And don't bother buying the textbook. You won't need it.
He was a really good teacher. His message is clear and his tests are over what he covers only. I havent opened the book yet and I have an A.

i was really nervous for this class because im absolutely horrible at math but he made it really easy and you get a cheat sheet for every test...front and back...if you have to take this class definately get him as a teacher
A lot better than I expected.
Vitevitch is nice guy and is very (a little overly) animated.  Print the notes out, and you'll be fine.  Class isn't a must, but it helps.  Don't even bother to buy a book.
No Comments
Dr. Vitevitch is a great professor. He made stats pretty easy!
He is a great psych teacher
Humor is a bit on the cheesey side, but overall this guy is a good prof. Go to class and pay attention and tests should be easy.
Great teacher who knows what he is talking about and makes class interesting.
Very good teacher!!
vitevitch is the man. i think i may change my major to psych cuz he made it sound so interesting
An outstanding professor...very helpful and genuinely interested in teaching...
She is the worst!
She is an awesome instructor. Simplifies complicated subjects helps me a lot to learn stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great instructor who will go above and beyond to help her students succeed!  I tried this course in another department.  This one was much more understandable because of the instructor!
The subject matter can be tough, but she is an excellent instructor.
Vicki is an amazing stats instructor.  Everyone hates stats, yet she explains everything so clearly.  A superb teacher.  I'd definitely recommend having any of her stats courses.
Great professor!  She really helps you understand what you need to know about statistics to REALLY get it!
No Comments
The best stats. Prof in School of Education. She  definitely knows her subject matter and conveys the material in a clear and often humorous way.

Erik is so passionate about his work and eager to share further learning resources. He's also really nice with grading and helpful during office hours. You should do the homework beforehand so you can ask him questions about it in class and he typically went over them if he finished lecture early, which happened often. Overall a very nice person.
Very nice and genuine, and is enthusiastic about the content. There wasn't much solid structure in this course, but I genuinely did learn a lot and he's very flexible and encouraging.

Differential Equations. Awful, useless lectures. Had to learn everything on my own online. Textbook used was unnecessarily confusing and worthless for learning. Entire class was just applying the right formulas to the right equations. I feel like I understand nothing. Terrible, terrible class.
Diffeq was hard, but I didn't really learn anything in class. I had to teach myself before class. Most of his lectures we pointless to go to. But we did work on homework after he was done lecturing.

Van Vleck is a decent lecturer. Real friendly guy. He throws in a few jokes and you can tell he knows his stuff. Sometimes the lectures are a bit hard to follow but it could be because he's following slideshows that were prepared by the other professor.

This teacher is by far the worst teacher I have ever had. he does not explain anything, he just states the answers... with no explanation!! and dont bother asking him for an explanation because he wont give one! Stay away from him unless you want to fail!
Made the class as interesting as a math class can be. He's pretty funny and did use curves. Used matlab as part of the grade.

Proofs Proofs Proofs. Thats what we did in class. out of class Matlab Matlab Matlab. Did very few examples in class, and Matlab will not be helpful to you on a test. You will have a really good idea about what will be on the test but not a degree of dificulty. He is an okay teacher who is very funny. class will not be too boring at least.

This was the worst experience I've ever had with any class. I had always done really well in math before, but Van Vleck was indecipherable to me. He only teaches using examples and does a very very poor job explaining why he's doing things, just expects you to know. I recommend you either drop the class or prepare to ask a ton of questions.

If you already know Calculus he is probably good for you. If you have no previous experience and want to learn from his course, you might as well get a tutor, sit in on other classes, or get used to the help room. Doesn't explain the basic concepts very well, just sort of skips into examples and doesn't say how or why he is doing the  problem.
Terrible teacher. He's knows what he's talking about but no one else does. Everyone failed the first test so bad that he made a curve with F=C
No Comments

He was pretty frickin sweet.  Hilarious too.  Very friendly guy as well.  Still waves hello to me around Snow.  It was hard, but he's really clear about what he wants, and does a great job explaining the material.  I love analysis now.
He was the only reason why I passed 500.  Really really helpful.  Most math professors require a certain level of RTFM before one steps to them.  This guy is no different.

okay so it's obvious van vleck doesnt like teaching intro calc classes because, well, id hate teaching intro calc classes. but otherwise he's great! i had him for 500 and he explained things really well and made jokes that were actually funny and i ended up with an A!
really smart guy, effective teacher
expects a student to understand material.  There is more to education than memorizing.  Because of his teaching method I can still remember everything about the course
SEEMED OUT OF IT EVERY CLASS! VERY UNCLEAR! I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS TEACHER!
Totally unclear .. appeared dazed at times.  Arrogant when asked for help.
Terrible teacher. Can't understand anything and he just rambles on reading his notes. Exams are hard and completely different from homework and other material.
Very disorganized course material. Lectures seems more like he is talking at you rather than to you. Overall doesnt seem to care much. Study hard and just try to make it through.

I learned absolutely nothing from him. His lectures were just him going over his notes which are online anyway so get ready to teach yourself everything. The third test and final are an absolute nightmare and he's a hard grader but if you talk to him he might give you points back. Homework and projects aren't bad but they can take a while.

Dr. Vossoughi is an awful lecturer. The only reason anyone goes to class is because they are afraid of failing. When he lectures he is really intense. He dislikes talking to his students. He is never in his office and has a slippery personality. He will only answer questions if he feels cornered. If you have to take one of his classes, good luck.

I will be honest he will listen to your concerns. His tests are the hardest tests I have ever taken in college. He allows you to drop one exam. The third exam and the final exam are very tough. You can not fail both of them. If you have test files exam one and two are easy. Projects are huge and tough. Homework assignments relatively easy.
As long as you complete the quizzes and keep up with the readings and videos, you'll be fine. The exams are not very hard. He is also really good at responding back quickly!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Tom does his best with a very difficult subject. With any other teacher this class would be unbearable, but Tom tries to liven things up and bring some humor into lecture, which is nice. He really does care and will work with you if you work with him. GO TO CLASS, take good notes and you'll be fine

Don't buy the book, go to every class to get notes because that's all you'll need for the tests. 3 tests and 1 paper, follow directions and know cases for the tests. Dates are not important at all, and neither are names. If you go and take notes and study them for a few hours before each exam you'll get a B or A in the class.

Required course. Three tests (90%) and 1 short paper (10%).  I skipped more than 10 classes and still got an A. He doesn't really know how to deal with someone who stays up to date on current events and already knowledgeable about the Constitution, Bill of Rights, etc. Gets annoyed if you raise your hand too much, likes to call on the dumb ones.

A little bit tough and intimidating, but a really great lecturer. If you're a grad. student and planning on taking this class, beware: Volek assigns an additional 30 page paper for grad. students. I've heard other professors who teach this course only assign an additional 5 page paper.

The class is graduate level. Study for the tests from the book and make sure you can decipher between what is an example and what is real. The book is arranged differently from the class outline so go to class. You can't skip.
Volek is the best!! Really truly cares about his students and will bend over backwards to help you. Great person and great professor.

Volek is not funny.Stretches lecture out with long winded, once again-Not funny- descriptions and weak pop culture references. Includes his class lecture "language" in his tests. Knows very little about much of the course content except his "area of expertise" libel law. You need to go to class for test preparation.
He is hilarious! Great guy all around. He is very helpful and makes sense of what he is teaching! He is always there to help out!

Hilarious, get to know him. His lectures are fun, but if you ask a tough question he's likely to say "its a mystery" so watch out for that. His tests are multiple choice and true/false.  One easy paper.  Doesn't post lecture slides online, so go to class and take notes.
No Comments
Volek is a great prof with some great teaching techniques. I loved how he started every class with "howdy campers!"
No Comments
Volek should have been a standup comic for the intellectual.
No Comments

I think he's funny sometimes, and so cheesy its funny at other times. His class is really interesting and he tries to get students involved when he knows we're getting tired. You really do have to read and take notes to do well in the class, but if you do that, you'll get an all right grade.
Utterly unfunny.  He tries way too hard.  He does this phony DJ voice...  ::shudder::  Maybe he works better in smaller classes, but I seriously cannot recommend him after taking this course.
He's funny and made the class very interesting.  If you want a good grade, you have to go to class and take good notes, then study and you'll do fine.  Grade is mainly comprised of just three exams.

I don't know why people are complaining about the amount of reading required. I thought the point of education is to learn, which actually requires some work. I had Vo****a for Western Civ. II and he was my favorite teacher at KU because he cared about the issues and involved the class in thought-provoking discussions.

He definately assigns a lot of writing for the semester, and too many points are weighted on two papers.  The tests were easy.  As a lecturer, he does fine, but in discussion he loves to hear his own opinion and tends to monopolize the conversation.  Grading on papers seemed random, as did the selection of paper topics.
He didn't follow his own grade outlines in the syllabus and he wore the same shirt and jeans every day
