Best teacher for western civ. Incredibly insightful. Demanding but fair and entertaining in class. Also, gives good study guides and good review sessions. Since everybody has to take HWC at KU, Vodicka is your best bet to get the most out of it!
He is tough! There are 4 tests, 2 huge papers, and a whole bunch of reading responses!! not an easy class
No Comments

He expects a lot of you.  If you want an easy professor look somewhere else.  If you want to learn and expand your thinking then he's your man.  He is somewhat elitist about his ideas and it's sort of like he's too smart for his own good.
Expects a lot out of her students, but is caring and will work with you, actually cares about your overall wellbeing.
Great Class. Great teacher!!! If you need an A+ take her class
Great teacher overall! I recommend taking classes with her.
She is very hot
She is amazingly hot.
AWESOME TEACHER. I loved her teaching style. She is really nice and you can tell she cares about her students. She is usually in the help room if you have questions and is always willing to help!
Extremely confusing to follow and not helpful in class or outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Use the 4 questions he gives you to case brief instead of other methods. You can also diagram with the boxes like he does in class for each case when you're prepping for class (you'll understand after the first few classes). Participation does matter. He will cold call if no one raises their hand, targets people who don't talk often.

Professor Ware is an excellent professor. His classes demand students read closely, as principles are taught through class discussions of problems related to the readings. So long as students participate, the class often does not utilize the Socratic method. This approach allowed me to gain confidence in my legal skills and be a better law student.

Volunteer early & often, he saves harder questions for students who don't volunteer. He'll also call on you when you aren't paying attention. I enjoyed reviewing the big picture in class often & the speakers he had talk to us about the practice. Overall, I believe he really cares about his students & his teaching style is one of the best at KU Law.
does not really tell you what he wants as an answer and it always feels like he speaks in riddles

Goes the extra mile for his students-always available for questions after class. He uses a pure Socratic method so its intimidating at first, but super effective. I just passed the bar exam and was surprised in my bar prep how well I remembered contracts & secured. He also trains you to speak like a lawyer, which matters out here in the real world.

most of what's written here already is true - especially want to +1 "mean for no reason." dismissive of questions and generally deflects answering them, and will make you feel stupid for asking them as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had him for Secured Transactions and Bankruptcy. Flat out mean in class for no reason. Weird 'guess what I'm thinking crap' like 'I'm thinking of a word from this chapter that begins with R.' Thankfully we were all 2 and 3Ls and knew how little class meant. Straightforward test and textbook. Can sleep through class as long as you show up.

This is the type of professor you were afraid of when you started law school, but that's not a bad thing. Ware is 100% traditional lightning bolt method, and you won't want to admit this, but it does help you learn. Make it a goal to raise your hand every day, as early as possible in class. Final was kinda terrible. Study hard and just embrace it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: nice prof.
Clear, logical, good diagrams.
Decent professor for contracts. I thought the material covered in class was clear and the exam was very straightforward.

Very knowledgeable on Secured Transactions.  His tests are horrible, it's basically three long fact patterns followed by "discuss" with no questions.  Very interactive in class.  Likes to call on people with hard to pronounce names to prove he can say them well.

had him for secured transactions. just get a good outline, come to class prepared. lightning strike method, likes to call on people who arent prepared. but doesnt take down notes so participation doesnt count for the final grade.
No Comments

Honestly, this teacher is such a good teacher, she's so nice and very reasonable. The only thing I have an issue with is she makes us stay after class and do our worksheets and doesn't just end class. I would leave during this time, and she would give points off my attendance grade. Otherwise, she really is a great teacher.

Loved the way this class was structured. Participation definitely matters. If you miss a day you definitely can get behind quickly. The material is so easily understood and so easy to reach out if you need support.

biggest regret was missing a few classes thinking I could easily catch up. She is very much about making you succeed and is good at explaining things, but understand if you miss class if you do not make an effort you will be lost. The math help room is your key to success to catch up and studying as there's not much guided studying done in class
One of my favorite math instructors ever. She cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. Always helpful and answers questions. It's an amazing class and she's an amazing instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Love Lindsey! She is such a great instructor, and teaches at a pace that is comfortable for everyone.
very good at explaining and wants you to succeed. there are frequent quizzes but you get to use your practice problems in your notes on them which have basically the same questions so its an easy A.
One of the best math teachers I have had for a while! Very understanding, lets you ask various amounts of questions. can tell she really wants you to learn. very much recommend.

She was so nice and always wanted to try to make sure you understand her class is super easy. Just make sure to do the video notes, those count for a grade, and make sure to do the worksheets. Their optional but she lets you use them on quizzes and they help a lot.
She's pretty chill and very understanding
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: BEST GTA EVER!! Made sure that everyone understood each topic. Class is basically everything you learned in high school algebra. Will meet with you after class if you need help. Lots of extra credit given. Make sure you do all of the WebAssign hw and do the study guides. The study guides actually help. Taking this everyday was also a big help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was in-person for me. I found it easy. Truth be told, I attended this class maybe 5 times. It was every Tuesday and Thursday for a whole semester. I came in basically if I was confused and to take exams. The lectures go over what you read/did homework over in the book. Scott also did his best to set everyone up for success.

Taking ACCT 205 online made the class easier. Book reading and assignments for almost every chapter. Zoom lectures just went over what was read, no exams or quizzes, just a solo project (financial statement analysis) for the final. TA's and Professor were easy to communicate with and responded to emails quickly. Just do the work and you'll be fine!

I was really hesitant to take his class because of the reviews. I'm pretty sure he was different before COVID-19, but online he was a really good caring professor and gave all his students opportunities to succeed. However, this class is good for accounting or business minors, but not majors because I felt like I was teaching myself accounting.

Im not sure about some of these reviews. Professor Whisenant gives many opportunities to redo homeworks even if they are submitted late. Bulk of the class was a very easy group project and he and the TAs were very accessible! Good class for business minors being introduced into accounting
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a wonderful teacher who is very understanding and good at explaining things. He is very helpful and understanding. I have had a great experience with him and would recommend him for anyone. This comments are disappointing for me to read. He is a great professor.
Do not take this class. He is a terrible professor.

Do not take his class. He will not help you even if you go into his office hours. He does not care about his students whatsoever. If you email him you'll just get a random email back that doesn't even answer your question. Even the TA's don't like him.
Coronavirus personified. Hopefully that will help you see how bad he is.

Simply horrible. I am literally at a loss for words when it comes to how bad of a teacher he is. He DOES NOT care about his students and will let you know it too. Save yourself from this disastrous excuse of a teacher.

Dr. Whisenant clearly does not know how to teach. Accounting isn't a subject you should be teaching yourself, and yet, I had to learn it all on my own. Also, I tried to introduce myself the first week and he told me "Doesn't matter, I won't learn your name anyways". Like how hard is it to teach? It's literally your job...
Pretty certain that my dog could teach better than him. Take care of yourself and do not take his class.
If you have to take a class with this man just change your major. I'd rather get coronavirus than ever have another class with him.
If I could give a zero I would. Absolutely the worst professor at KU. Have fun learning nothing about accounting and having to take tests over things he never taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I'd rather change my minor than ever have another class with him. Do yourself a favor and stay away from his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS! He doesn't actually teach anything useful. A simple google search will teach you more about accounting than him. One of the worst professors at KU by far. A waste of my time and money. If you email him for help he'll respond with literal nonsense and not even address your question; the same goes for if you ask him in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures are just a combination of him rambling about Tesla and taking roll for 45 minutes. His homework and projects make no sense. Given the class is an introductory course you'd expect him to make the class easy, but he doesn't. I can say with 100% confidence that Professor Whisenant is the worst teacher I've ever had. Do not take his class.
I loved Scott. Accounting in general is hard for business minors, but he definitely made the class feel more fun and interesting.

Lectures were pretty pointless because he just talked about different companies, but the homework was pretty easy and he went over everything before the exams. As long as you average a B on exams you should be able to get an A in the class due to homework and project grades. Projects are easy A's if you do the work.

He only taught grad students before they brought him on to teach a class that only business minors can take. Insane. He never taught us anything useful, everyone was always confused, and I know I could have easily gotten a better grade in this class if it wasn't for him. It was easier to skip class and teach myself accounting.

Scott is a great guy. Really smart, knows US GAAP well. His codification research class really  helps studying the FAR section of the exam. Full disclosure: He also wrote me a letter of rec for grad school. Didn't meet 1/2 class periods, other "class" was used for 1-on-1 professor time if needed. Super great guy. Best ACCT prof @ KU

I took the tax version of her class and loved it. There are a lot of sources where she has you learn from, but it really does help you prepare for the CPA.

We had extra group projects that normal 545 kids did not. I learned so much about preparing returns and it put me at ease for industry. 

Just do the work, and save yourself time later.

Horrible Lecturer. She has you study from 100 different sources. Just compile all of the information into one packet and only test over THAT packet. It's not about the amount of content, but more so to do with how disorganized she is. She is also super lazy. Everything is online and her explanations are inadequate at best. STAY AWAY!
Great teacher!
He has no desire to help students and the class is so difficult. He is rude to people who ask questions.

Exams are timed but all open note. Don't have to go to class but he gives extra credit occasionally in class. He doesn't deserve the bad reviews that he gets. He is very smart and funny. Also curves most exams

Him and his wife are a JOKE! He yelled at me in office hours so bad another professor apologized to me about the way I was spoken to. He told another student if she was his daughter he'd be disappointed in her! HOLY UNPROFESSIONAL, & disgusting. I have no clue how either of them have jobs at KU let alone a job. disgusting people, & bad professors
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Neuromuscular Exercise Physiology with Dr. Weir this semester. All of the lectures were posted online along with the slides. I live 20 min from campus each way and still drove every Tue Thurs to this class because I enjoyed the content and his lectures that much. Very witty, down to earth guy with quite a lot of sarcasm. Would def take again.

Took 310 and 375 with him. All the lectures and slides are posted. 310 exams were open note but timed, 375 exams were in person. Questions were pretty straightforward and he curves exams. Very genuine guy and also funny so long lectures aren't boring. Would recommend taking classes with him.
He is unprofessional and not helpful with any questions you may have about homework.
Awful class, difficult assignments with little to no help on what to do. Graded incredibly hard, -1 point for every cell incorrect (out of 10 possible) absolutely avoid taking this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hopefully, this is my last class with this man. This is my 2nd class with this man and he's awful. He gives no grace, unless he thinks you deserve it.  310 should not be as hard of a class as it is. I love that it's online and I don't have to see him in person, but having a 5 pm deadline with difficult assignments is definitely not the moves.

Professor Weir does not care about his students and shows no compassion or empathy towards anyone having issues with his class. He always has to be right and will never show any grace. Probably the worst teacher I've ever had and would strongly recommend a different teacher then him if you have to take this class.

Lectures are long and his voice is monotone. Not a horrible class if you do the homework and review over notes for the exam. Exams are open note and open textbook, but he gives 35 minutes for a 30 question exam.
Just do the homework only problem is if you mess up on a few he does not care you cannot turn it in late.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Weir isn't much help and you will end up having to attempt to teach yourself the material. Hundreds of slides worth of material.

Joseph Weir simply does not care about students at all. All of the quizzes and exams are timed and it's nearly impossible to get every question done in the time given. I was very disappointed in both of the classes I took with him. The material he teaches seems way harder than it probably should be.

Professor Weir is a rude teacher who has no feelings and does not care whatsoever. Gives minimal extra credit and is not empathetic at all. If you miss a due date, tough luck, he does not care and will not give a do over. Tests are very hard and barely any of the material is covered in lecture. Like reading a foreign language.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Joseph is many things but a good teacher is not one of them. - provides very poor feedback when grading - is a VERY tough graded - is not consistent with his grading he will mark some people off and not mark off other people for the exact same thing - will not round up your grade even if you are 1 point away - VERY monotone boring lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had to work hard for my grade. A majority of my class failed at least 2 of the 5 exams. He offers some extra credit but not enough to make a significant change in your overall grade. Highly recommend going to his office hours and finding a study group. Many people I know had negative interactions over email, so try talking to him in person!

This class is challenging, you really have to put in time outside of class to study for exams. 3 exams and weekly quizzes are what your grade is based on. Lectures every class period, taking good notes is critical. Weir is very knowledgeable and is there to help if you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class if you can avoid it. His lectures are confusing to understand not to mention his voice is so monotoned, it's hard to focus. Emailed him a few times with homework questions that he never answered. Was worried about failing the class and he really couldn't care less. Save your mental sanity and don't take this class.

I had some medical issues this semester and Dr. Weir was very helpful and caring throughout that whole process. He was by far the most supportive professor I had this semester and I think that says a lot about him as a person and professor. He seems like a hard-ass but he really just wants you to put in effort and show that you care.

You need to take notes and pay attention to detail because he is a conceptual professor. This is best done if you watch his lecture videos or go to class. If you reach out to him, he really values that. The study guide is accurate exam material, but make sure you ask if you don't know bc it gets confusing since the material is very dense.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yes, HSES 375 is a hard class. But if you put in the work, it's manageable. Weir is the most caring professor and if you go to office hours, he is more than willing to help out!! Go in and ask questions and I promise you'll do better on the exams. Weir gets a lot of shade but he genuinely is such a good profess who cares a lot about his students!

Professor Weir had very information-heavy lectures that were not explained well. The exams make up most of your grade and are extremely difficult. Most of the questions arent in the notes and the ones that are, are worded in a way to confuse you. Very stressful class.

This class was not hard. You literally just have to complete homework, watch the lectures and get an A. The only "hard" part was some of the math but if you go to Weir's office hours he will help you out. He's a genuinely great guy and professor! 10/10
Very hard class, especially because its online. Definitely one of, if not the, hardest class ive ever taken.

Horrifying class! He is very monotone. The stuff he puts on the study guides are not what show up on the exam. You really have to understand the concepts because his test questions require you to think which is difficult because he can't teach. There are only 3 exams and your grade is based off of that alone. Completely ruined my grade

This is the first semester this class exists.. Dr. Weir definitely does not explain very well and class is extremely boring.  The material is tough and I always read the chapters in the book.  He follows the book very closely and sometimes that is where test questions are pulled from rather than solely the slides.  He also curves a lot.

Not a good professor. Just got hired as departmental chair for the HSES department. Does not care about anyone, just statistics. Unwilling to help when asked a question. Tells you to "look it up in the book." Doesn't teach just reads slides and doesn't actually show you how to do problems . Worst teacher I've ever experienced.

by far the worst experience i have ever had with anyone. she does not respect students disability accommodations whatsoever and will not communicate properly with students she doesn't like. on top of that, she does not wear her mask properly and will spew terf/transphobic and colonizer rhetoric. i wouldn't recommend her class to my worst enemy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Loren was my teacher at KCAI. Honestly, one of the best professors there. Take advantage of everything she has to give (AKA pay attention!!) , she is very enthusiastic and knowledgeable. Her classes are super dynamic, entertaining, and full of amazing content. I do not have enough words to describe how amazing she is in every level. Truly a gem.
Exactly what the first person said. Very helpful, knowledgable, enthusiastic, prepared. Awesome teacher! Really has excellent command on the subject matter. Take her!

Loren was an amazing teacher.  Extremely enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the subject, very well prepared to teach, makes every effort to be available for students.  Uses technology very effectively and assignments and course materials are promptly posted to Blackboard.

Prof. White is the best prof. I have had, she is super caring and has a real passion for what she teaches. She has a team based learning approach, which I was nervous about because of social anxiety, but she created such a warm environment that I genuinely enjoyed coming to her class every day. I highly recommend taking her class.

Professor Stacey is an amazing instructor. The class structure and her personality make her classes phenomenal. She is someone that can make you truly interested in Urban Planning and is always willing to help. The class is not tough, but it's good to always show up to team assignments, as those are the bulk of your grade.
Big fan of Prof. White, I love the way she lectures and organizes the course.

She's a great professor and really cares for her students. Stacey wants everyone to do their best and succeed. I personally did not like all the readings we had ( there was a quiz each week over them). I enjoyed our group projects were we got to interact with other students.

I LOVED prof White. She is so kind and caring about her students. We worked in teams for the semester, which worked well, and she is constantly checking in on us to see how things are going w online school. The content is super interesting and its clear that she cares a lot about it. She is an awesome teacher and you're lucky to be in her class.

Professor White is such a kind professor! She is so sweet and provides a very positive learning environment. We worked in groups (teams) for most of the semester, and the set-up worked surprisingly well. It is a pretty easy class, but you still learn a lot! (Attendance is sort of mandatory, but she will also let you make up things if you're absent)

He is a very interesting lecturer and I like what he had to say when it comes to law and ethics in journalism, but he grades insanely harshly. After midterms he did a grade check in the class and showed the top and bottom 5 grades, showing that only TWO people had As in the class.

Dr. Wolgast is kind, knowledgeable, and cares about his students. The class isn't too too hard if you attend and work on the Friday group projects, but the quizzes and exams are tough and often very specific, so good notes are essential. He also calls on students at random, so be prepared, and he's always stylish in his suits.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wolgast sets up this class with very little room for error. Miss one point and you lose your A. Quizzes were confusing with wording (sometimes would make us select more than one option, which defeats the purpose of Scantron). He didn't show up for a single Friday class, yet we had to be there. Groups were random. Don't recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were boring, but he was trying. Class is 100 points so there is 0 room for error. 1st quiz/exam were online, 2nd quiz/exam were on paper. 2nd quiz he said if the question had "which" there was more than 1 answer + to select all, but there were questions that didn't say "which" that had multiple answers. Refused to curve due to his error.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wolgast is a very nice professor, but the class only has 100 points and leaves no room for error. I think he could be more understanding of that since the exams and quizzes are short and cover little material. He can be boring but is an organized professor and does what he can to help you succeed. Just needs more extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Wolgast was awesome! He clearly cares about students. The only thing that was rough was the quizzes. They weren't necessarily hard if you paid attention, but only being 5 questions doesn't help your score if you miss even one. Overall though, kind professor and fun class!
Take her class !! She is a good professor and loves her students! she will help you understand anything if your confused. she will find time to meet with you if you want to meet one on one.

The amount of fear-mongering around plagiarism is absolutely insane- she parades her involvement on the policy student board as if she can't wait to turn in another student for accidentally citing something incorrectly. I don't trust individuals who act this way in terms of learning. Don't take this course, she won't make it worth your while.

Loved the topics discussed in class but the content learned and depth of it didn't match up to the tests, which made the tests harder. Dr Alesia was awesome at getting back to you and welcoming you into her office hours, but she was strict when it came to Skill Reports. Overall great class, that I would take again with some things fixed!

Took over the summer, was a women's leadership class. Got to meet and interact with women from all around the world, very interesting and a great experience. Several in class activities that are very interactive and fun. Minor homework given throughout the week,easy. Final-cumulative project that you have plenty of time to work on before presenting

Hybrid class met once a week in class for lecture, discussion on Friday and had online assignments released once a week(not hard at all). The lectures were engaging & interesting, random quizzes (not hard) & in class points so be sure to show up. Discussion had several class activities, journal every week, and quiz before every class. Recommended
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She was a great professor of communication theory. I came in with a journalism background, not having been in college for about 30 years. Her lectures were clear, she actively engages students, and made herself accessible during office hours. She NEVER, not once, created the impression that I should doubt my abilities in 844 seminar.

she was great! you have a few easy papers that are like a page or 2 long.  Once a week there is an online book reading thing to complete. it takes an hour and it's actually really helpful.  Fill out the study guide &go over it a few times and you'll do great. go to class-- random participation pts and tests are over lecture AND book

This class isn't easy, but it isn't hard either. If you pay attention in class and take good notes, then you should do pretty well on the tests. The writing assignments were pretty easy topics to write about. She takes random attendance, so you should always go to the class. You can't use your phone, though, or you lose attendance points.

Her lectures are very boring and less than half the class would show up. We took numerous notes every day and only a few things from them would be on the test. Her grading scale sucks. The total points for the whole semester was 280. 50 for 3 tests and the rest were worksheets and quizzes. These were not very hard but were not helpful for the tests

I took this class with her this spring and just finished. Her teaching could definitely improve as the classes I did go to were very boring. She also makes you take a ton of notes, however only some of these were even used on the tests. I would only recommend taking this class if you already enjoy interpersonal communications, not for an easy A.

I thought this class would be super interesting, but Alesia made that impossible. Worst COMS teacher I have had so far at KU, she should not be a teacher. Her lectures are just her reading word for word off of her slides, and her tests are insanely specific. She does not care if her students do well, so do yourself a favor and avoid her class

This class is great if you like to be read everything word for word from power points that she'll eventually post on Bb... I can't stress enough how BS this class is, she expects you to remember 6-7 chapters of material for Exams and there's only 3 of them! No room for error. If you want to succeed in this class, remember everything she says.

Run from this woman and any class she teaches. Horribly boring lectures, harsh grading, and low points for test and papers make it that much more difficult to receive high grades. She basically just reads from slides and clearly has a difficult time involving the class.Requires A TON of information for each exam, difficult to see what is important

Professor Wong was my favorite professor.  She was tough and demanded excellence but I learned so much and felt that my grade was really deserved rather than rubber stamped.   I've had several instructors that made me stretch but she was the best.

Jane Wong was the single most difficult teacher I have ever had.  Difficult meaning she does not explain herself and gets upset very easily. Multiple times she would make corrections to my plans with her own markings and then critique them later saying it is incorrect. Definitely not a fun course!
no patients

One of the kindest most gracious human beings I have ever met. Very honest with grading and if you take initiative the course work it will pay off. This course is designed to make you think about the content and analyze it. This class will enrich your understanding of many world cultures and their music. Open to all KU students! Take this class.

MUSC771. Incredibly racist and unprofessional. She marks down students who speak out against the racism present in the readings. Coursework is a joke, she often assigns sensationalistic documentaries that have nothing to do with music. I would VERY strongly warn you to reconsider taking her class, this was the worst mistake of my graduate career.

She repeatedly uses problematic language to refer to groups of people, the pictures on the exam are difficult to see. The study guides are not helpful and what you think is important will not be on the test. This could easily be an online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She has homework and quizzes every week as busy work, and sometimes, the information we are supposed to know in the homework or quiz was not in the lecture or the lab. She talks so quietly that it is hard to hear, and her slide shows are sometimes hard to see or understand due to the color of the text and background, or the lack of text.

I was confused in this class even though I rarely missed class. I also have always been a straight A student but this class has dropped my gpa by a lot. During a project we were threatened with needing to write a term paper in a single week if our project did not meet her standards by the next day though we had already been working on it for days.

After giving her the date I wanted to present my final presentation, she "forgot" to write me down and moved me to the very first day about two days before the presentations started. She told me if I didn't present that day then I would fail the class. Completely unfair :)

the audio in her power points don't ever really work, the assignments are a bit confusing, and some of the information that's needed she doesn't provide. I def would never retake her class. I now understand why she has such a low score on rate my professor.

Do not take any of K Wong's courses. In just the first two weeks they are the most disorganized and rude. The material is difficult to follow and they never posted a syllabus but continuously said refer to the syllabus when students would reach out. Marked things as late that were not submitted late. AWFUL.

Not too horrible, I took this class online, it could be a bit much at times. There is a lot of homework, and a $200 textbook you're supposed to purchase (I never did). If you do the assignments you will be fine, but not a particularly interesting class.

Honestly, she is hard to understand sometimes because her english is not perfect but overall she is very interesting and makes the class fun. Just read the book (even though you dont really have to) and the class is a breeze.

You can get away with not reading the text book and getting As on the quizzes. When you discuss with her your research paper topic, she acts overly enthused with everyone's topic and not just your own. She is hard to understand and her power points don't match up from the class power points to the online ones. It's a nap hour.

Ketty had great potential but she just seemed to read off of her power points. And although her english is very clear, she sometimes didn't get what I was saying in a paper because it referred to an American reference, and she counted me off for it. Over all boring class. I learned almost nothing from it.

Absolutely useless.  She doesn't understand how to communicate with students, and it's not just the language barrier.  There are some professors who just know what makes student's tick.  She's not one of them.   You can answer a question in class, then several other people will give answers, then she gives her answer, which is exactly the same!

Terrible professor with too high of expectations for a 300 level class. I have never taken a music class before so I am totally lost and the fact that she spells instruments differently than the book really throws me off. I would not recommend her.

Absolutely a worthless professor and a worthless class.  I am an honor roll student and normally do not feel this way about classes, but I am learning NOTHING.  She says the word "ummm ehhh" more than actual information.  Stay away from her class at all costs.  Her class isnt too hard, but if you want an intellectual experience look elsewhere.

It was hard to understand her in class. Her spelling and the book spelling of instruments and other important words for the course often didn't match up, creating more communication problems. Outside of class, she was very helpful in office hours in terms of helping with the steps of a research paper and topic ideas.
I loved Ketty. She was a great teacher! She shared so much information with us. I learned a lot in her class. She is also very approachable and nice.

Absolutely the worst professor I've ever had. Her English is terrible, often to a point that she completely miscommunicates information. She has no ability to put information into context. It's the equivalent to a teacher of psychology reading case studies to students without explaining any processes, outcomes or relevance.

Ketty is not only hard to understand, but she has unreasonably high expectations for her class. My group met with her before a presentation, and she said unless we spent several more hours doing research, she wouldn't let us present to the class. It's too hard for something that most people aren't even interested in!

She doesn't know what she is talking about, her lectures are useless as the tests are from the textbook, her English is...ie: the first day of class she kept mixing up the words "question" and "answer." She makes everyone buy the anthology because she is to lazy to bring a boombox to class since she can't use the speakers & the overhead simutanilou

Terrible, terrible, terrible. She actually freaked out on our class and started screaming at us for no reason. Unfortunately there isn't anyone else to take this class from, so you're pretty much screwed. Read the book and go to labs or expect to understand nothing.
I agree that she is a very nice lady, but she is also a terrible teacher. I learned nothing in this class.

Dr. Woodburn curates positive discussions on overwhelming topics that have big impacts on the world. If you are serious about your education and the future of our water, take this class. I selected "4" for the difficulty as you can make the class as challenging as you want. You have the support needed to excel from both classmates and Dr. Woodburn.

Dont worry about the capstone. Terri and staff are very caring and understanding. Pick a topic you like and that will not take a ton of effort to find. Create an outreach thing so you can submit a paper with heavy research and then sections over what you did based on the research. Makes life much easier and gets it done in a semester. Online pres
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was a good class. Wish we would have been able to do the field work portion of class. I bought the text book for the midterm and then returned it for the money. Terri is a caring and kind teacher that is great at conveying difficult concepts. You learn so much from her-take all of her classes. Do not do any class without her that u can. Great!

Find the book as a free PDF. One of the best class I have taken at KU. Terri is an outstanding teacher and cares more about you learning than busy work. This class is absolutely worth taking so take it. I wish I would have taken every single class with terri I could. I would recommend doing that. All about rivers and how they work and basic info.

Great teacher and great class. Discussions, one short quiz, paper (for grad students only), CTW worksheets, and a powerpoint project. Missed only 2 points the whole year. Very caring and nice teacher. Workload was the perfect amount and you learn so much. Wish there were more classes like this. Just take it you will not regret it.

This class is easy to pass if you show up and do the numerous readings. My only problems are that the lectures are dull (usually just a projected word document) and I am put off by the belittling, grade school-style of address she uses in class.

Claire is a great teacher, but this class is not easy. It has a lot of reading and she gives 4 pop quizzes throughout the semester, along with a midterm, final and two papers. If you do the readings and take detailed notes on her lectures, you will do fine. However, she talks really fast which can be hard sometimes. She is very helpful though.
Very helpful on understanding the concept and well organized notes. I recommend taking her class, you'll learn more.
Claire is so sweet. She is a tough grader and she expects a lot out of you, but she is very organized and she always makes sure you understand the readings

Shane is so different compared to the english teachers I have had in the past. He really tries to make his assignments mean something and he wants you to have fun while doing them. I would say, if you miss class or show up late a few times you most likely won't get a grade higher than an A. Just keep that in mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Teach is by far one of the best professors I have had throughout college. He genuinely cares about his students and wants you to succeed.  He can be a tough grader on papers, but as long and you go to office hours and talk to him about them, you will do great! (PS you will low key fall in love with him)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: The teacher could have been more lienant on absences and online homework that could bump your whole letter grade down. Hard grader, but genuine guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Teach is the goat. Simple as that.  insert goat emoji here
Shane is a very original character, cares a bunch about his students and wants to make sure you get the most out of his classes. He's willing to meet out of class and help you any way possible.

Shane is one of the best professors I've ever had. His passion for not only teaching but learning from his student is made clear in every class. He is a very fun guy who wants to get to know his students and wants his students to know him.   P.S. Girls: he's hot AF

Professor Wood (AKA Teach) is one of the best instructors I've had all through school. I've had some tough professors this semester, but he is one of my favorites. I've always loved English, but he challenges me to be a better writer with very unique & interesting assignments. I've learned a lot and he truly CARES about his students! Thanks Teach!!
Shane wood is super hot and I love him so much.... Much hot such love.... A+++ fast shipping and good quality -skyler

Shane A. Wood is the best GTA EVER! He was very helpful and understanding. He would help his class better understand rhetorical writing. I enjoyed his class very much. Before I stepped my foot in that class, I hated English and now I love it! Show up, do the online discussions, and write well written papers and you will do just fine in his class.
Teach is the freakin man! He's an all around good guy and a great professor! I highly suggest anybody taking this class to try their hardest to get Prof Wood!

duh! huge emphasis on class participation and communication so if ya don't like talking... thats okay because there are discussion boards for you to eXpReSs yourself freely. shane is very open to helping and clearly cares about his students. though he doesnt believe in grades he still holds high expectations for his students. nice guy real human!

"Teach" is a great English professor. Finally, a professor that succeeds in improving students writing. Instead of finding all red marks on papers, he explains why it is marked and what can be improved. I felt I left this class with a greater understanding of rhetorical writing. Teach helps remind students how easy it can be to love writing.

It's interesting to come to his class!! Professor Wood or "Teach" as we know him comes into class with smile on his face and imparts his own love of English to his students. He takes into consideration what is going on in the university, being aware of upcoming exam schedules and often tailoring the projects to take stress off of the student.
She seems to be busy with many other things other than teaching.

Sometimes stuck in a world of "what was" or "what could be". Overall, I like her, but she could stand to open herself to constructive critiques without taking it personal. She should also be more open to what the student wants and not what she wants for the student.
Meh.

The College Student is a great class for learning how college students develop while we have them on campus.  Lots of reading & writing, but assignments are fair and help students understand the theories.
No Comments
No Comments
Great!
Dr. Wright is easily one of the best professors I've ever had, so kind and genuinely pulling for you to become an educator. Down to earth and so sweet.

Dr. Wright is a great professor, she really cares about the students in class. What she teaches is relevant to the class and important for education majors also. Attendance is required but if you email her or absent every once and awhile it's okay! The books were required but we hardly used them. Overall, a great and easy class.
Dr. Wright is the most wholesome person to ever roam the earth. Wouold strongly recommend taking her class- learned a lot despite it being a lighter load.

Dr. Wright is such a sweet and caring professor. She truly cares about her students and their overall well being as well as their academics. She did an amazing job making multicultural education accessible and applicable to everyone. I would highly recommend taking her C&T 235 course, even if you aren't an ed major.
Dr. Wright is a very sweet person and her lectures are very moving. The coursework was fine as long as you addressed all the necessary criteria.
Kindest Professor who teaches things that really make a difference

Dr. Wright was a very caring professor who wants you to do well in her class, it is easy to succeed if you come to class and complete the few assignments on time. She has a lot of experience with education and has great stories if you take the time to listen. The biggest assignments were an essay about ourselves and a project with a presentation.

She is such a gem. She is so knowledgeable and has been through so much that it is so inspiring, especially for those who are taking the class because they want to be educators. Truly a dream professor and so kind. Class was very easy too but I actually enjoyed learning in this class and she was very understanding if we weren't able to come ;;
This class was super easy for me and not heavy at all. Dr. Wright is a very compassionate woman who has experienced a lot in her life and her resilience is extremely inspiring.

Dr. Wright is truly an inspiration to students. She emulates the idea of coming to class for development rather than sticking to a textbook and quizzes. She makes education fun and new after being in it for so many years. I HIGHLY recommend requesting her for classes.

Cheryl Wright is an excellent educator, and is so kind and sweet it almost hurts. She is a great source of stories and information about diversity and she knows plenty about what she teaches. The class itself isn't hard at all, she just wants to see a bit of effort and participation. I pray I get to have her again.

One of the nicest profs I've ever had, super kind, and the class itself is super interesting. As long as you do the bare minimum you will get a good grade, but putting in the work is definitely worth it for this class!

Cheryl Wright is an amazing professor who makes her students feel comfortable in her classroom. She does a lot of group activities that are fun and I actually have made a really good friend from her class because of this. She is a wonderful educator and I think every future teacher could learn a lot from her.
Dr. Wright is so sweet and caring. Her lectures are interactive and insightful. There is a light workload and I learned so much about diversity and equity. Love this class.

This class was the worst. It didn't help that I could care less about Chinese Sculptures, but she does not present the material in an engaging way AT ALL. Drones on while your hand furiously attempts to keep up. Take someone else and don't buy the textbook if for some reason you take her course.
No textbook, and her notes are incredibly specific. She's hard to keep up with.

She is quick to go through slides, but will answer questions if you have them. She does not tell you exactly what will be on the exam, but as long as you attend both the lecture and the discussion, you will do fine! I liked her a lot

250 total points + 10 EC. 50 pts/exam, 4 exams in total. 10 pts/quiz, 6 in total(drop one). The average grade for exam was always around 78%, not a easy class. Not recommend his class if PSYC is required class for you. Difficult for international students

would NOT recommend this teacher. He is a bad lecturer and goes on and on. His tests are mostly based on the book and barely any on his lecture. he doesn't take attendance so there's no point in going to class except for his random in class quizes. He grades hard on assignments then when he gets lazy he gives everyone all the points.

He is probably my least favorite teacher that I have had.  His standards are extremely high, the tests are VERY difficult. I managed to receive a B.  There is no final.  Attendence is not mandatory, though he will randomly check some.  I would recommend taking this class with a different teacher.

It is very interesting material, class is enjoyable BUT I find the tests very difficult.  There is a total of 4 tests, drop the lowest and no final.  There are other assignment through the semester also.
The best dissertation advisor anyone could hope for.
had to watch boring vidoes that had to watch to full up time.  have to do the review in order to do well in the course.

My honors thesis advisor - extremely helpful and full of good advice. I also took several of his classes, and learned a great deal about his area of study (forensic psych). Great professor and very nice
Man, you're one of the best Teachers I ever had.  I miss having you as a teacher.

Great teacher who has the experience and knowledge to back up his work. He expects the best, but knows it cannot be achieved overnight and works with students to get to their goals. One downfall is sometimes his lack to understand the woes of a student who works, and goes to school, and their lack of time.
Jack is a wonderful source of information

The difference between Acting I and Acting II is that in Acting I the grad students really don't teach that much. in Acting II, your actually learning something.  It may seem the same, but when Jack helps you with a scene, he teaches you techniques to act better, not just how to say a line better.
A great teacher with lots to say!

Jack is the most inspirational teacher I've had in the department. Be prepared to learn, because you will. I feel like a much better actor after taking his class; he's honest with you and really wants to help.

Jack is a nice guy, but I think he is past in prime as far as teaching goes.  He was not the inspirational teacher I thought he was going in to the class.  In fact, the class is basically just a rehash of acting 1 - which is boring!
No Comments
Jack is an amazing teacher and a wonderful person.  He is honest with you and helps you become the best that you can be.

Not a tough class.  Dr. Wright is interesting in lectures and doesn't give a cumulative final which is great.  Two presentations, one paper, and three tests all worth 15%.  10% for showing up and participating.  Lots of assigned reading, but you can circumvent most of it by using the wiki to read abridged versions of most cases.

She's great. Take the class. Read + show up = do well. No powerpoint, no outlines. She just talks-so pay attention and take notes. No final exam. No papers. Discussion readings are real snoozers and LONG. Get used to it. But, the class is easy, she's a great, great lady, and you should sign up.
This teacher is amazing!!!!

Dr. Wright is nice and grades easily. She makes you give 3 presentations in this class, so it's student run. If you don't like to get up in front of the class, don't take this. We also had a midterm and a paper. The only thing that was bad about the class was that she let some students preach almost daily on abortion....that was annoying.

Sherry is absolutely my favorite teacher.  She facilitates great class discussions and always helps students clearly see both sides of an argument.  Taking this class will greatly enhance your appreciation for the complexity of issues of religious freedom.

If you can take a class with Wuthrich, please do it. He is literally the GOAT. He makes it seem like the exams will be extremely hard, but literally just show up and study the DETAILED STUDY GUIDE and you will get 100%. People want to make it seem like this class is hard but I am convinced it's personal error. also epic girl dad lol he is the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Literally one of the coolest professors I've ever had. He wants to see students succeed

Professor Wuthrich is very nice and you can tell he cares about his students. He knows a lot of names including people who don't talk. Lectures are generally helpful but can get extremely boring when he starts talking about random things. The final was difficult but curved extremely generously.
The nicest professor of all time. Has gone above and beyond to improve my college experience as a whole, not even just in his class. Very kind person, and the class was great.

This was the second class I have taken with him. His lectures are great. He's funny, super knowledgeable, and loves to answer questions from students. I would definitely suggest taking at least one class from him. Grade composed of 2 reading quizzes/week that can sometimes be tricky, group project, and 2 exams (potential to opt out of final exam).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I actually took POLS 564 with this professor but couldn't add the course code. Professor Wuthrich was great. He provides all the readings on which there was 2 weekly quizzes. His lectures are interesting and he was always willing to stay and talk with me after about any questions I had. His grading criteria was clear and fair.
The course work isn't too bad and if you show up, pay attention, and take notes on the lectures you should be fine. It's pretty hard to fail this class, just don't slack on studying for exams.
Midterm was very unique and one fo the better tests I have taken
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Wuthrich is a great professor. His class is reading heavy, but if you do the work, it's an easy A. His lectures just mainly rehash the reading, and he doesn't take attendance, so it's fine to skip, but he puts some lecture-only info on the tests so don't always skip. He's fair, nice, and cares about his students. Will take another class from him!

A lot of the overall grade depends on quizzes. This was the only homework, and the problem with these quizzes is they are only five questions, but each question is worth fifty points. Another problem is you do the reading and take the quiz over the reading before the lecture. The lectures felt pointless since the material was already tested over
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: really nice guy! lectures kinda boring, and two reading quizzes every week. honestly all the answers are online and those same quiz questions are on the test. if you read and show up to some lectures you should be getting a B or an A!
lectures are kinda dull but class is easy and he's nice (and occasionally funny). he knows your name even if you don't talk. HUGE Turkey guy (the country).

If you have the chance to take a course from Dr. Wuthrich, do it... best professor I have had at the University of Kansas. Fair, open-minded, and supportive of his students. Awesome guy and inspirational professor.
This class was the easiest class I have taken at KU. The lectures were pretty boring but it was an easy A. Also, Dr. Wuthrich is just an overall great guy.
Nice dude. Funny.
Shes pretty hard to reach outside of class and her grading criteria is rarely clear.

Professor Wuehle was okay at best. Gives great feedback on papers and really makes you feel like you got the grade you deserved. So vague when introducing new assignments, it takes forever to realize what she wants. Felt like an underclassmen high school class, super boring most of the time but she's good at applying lessons to current events.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: not an english major but she made this class interesting. obviously cares about her students and gives a lot of feedback.

Unclear grading criteria. Does not round an 89.9 to an A. Boring class. Not very qualified to be teaching in college. Does not teach much in class but grades like it's a 400 level course. Irrelevant projects such as speeches and presentation of an annotated bibliography.
This was a required class, but she made it interesting. Had to work for the grades but she gave a lot of feedback.
The class is only out of 100 points, and you have to work for them. Toughest grader I have ever experienced. Seems impossible to get an A.
She is hard to communicate with. Not personable at all. Blunt. Unhelpful. Seems uninterested. Doesn't respond to emails.
You cannot understand anything she says. Incredibly uninteresting to follow. Over-explains easy math. Take with Hauge or Walden.
The class is an easy A if you can bring yourself to sit through it. She is by for the least interesting teacher I have ever had.
Just follow her study guide, exams will be eazy. Attend all the classes to make sure you don't miss any quiz points(quiz are eazy). Eaziest course in Business School.

Prof Wu is a nice and knowledgeable person but the course material can be dull if your not into logistics.  However, she gives plenty of extra credit opportunities. There are only two tests, no make-up for the quizzes (which are generally doable if you've been in class), and be sure to check your homework with the TAs(they are life savers!)

Easy A class. Wu is a very kind person, she is always ready to help the students. Her class explains everything clearly, maybe long and dull at times. Lots of EC opportunities, notes is enought for class and textbook is only helpful for homework.
Provides plenty of opportunity for points, including EC. Overall good quality, class can be dull at times, however.
Great teacher, explain everything clearly.

The material she tests you on is easy but she is nearly impossible to understand. Don't even bother buying the book, she doesn't ever teach out of it. Her slides are a joke, poorly laid out and give you very little information on how to actually work the math related problems. If you miss a single day you're behind, she rarely posts ppt solutions.

Diana is a good teacher, but if you are an SCM major, you will need to join the SCM club to find something that excites you about the subject. You'll learn all the math you need to know, but the exciting stories about supply chain and the theories behind everything(the interesting stuff)is saved for the later classes. Class may be boring.

Professor Wu is a good teacher. She makes sure everyone is understanding what is going on. All of the quizzes (10, 8 count toward grade) are very easy; same with the homeworks (6, 5 count). First exam is pretty easy. Second exam is take-home. I would recommend this class.
Horrible class.  Confusing teacher.  Does not have much in the way of help for working students.

Says 'OK' and Right' way too much. I tallied one day...266 OK, 187 Right...it is ridiculous. She is terrible at explaining things that are confusing and over explains simple algebra. Poor, poor teacher
One of the easiest classes I have taken at KU...
No Comments

His lectures are not overly complex - lots of examples so you know what to do on homework and tests, but pretty boring. Very knowledgable and cares about teaching. You get a cheat sheet for exams (copy the example problems from the textbook). The class was easy but also I don't know that I learned a lot. Definitely has an accent, but not too bad.

290 in general covers stuff that most math or engineers are already familiar with. But Dr. Wu is smart and you're pretty much guaranteed an A as long as you do the homework and study a bit. He gives concrete examples and explains them well but sometimes it seems very slow. As long as you study efficiently, attendance isn't mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Reasonable amount of homework and reasonable tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Gives great notes and examples in lecture

Dr. Wu is one of the best math professors I have ever had. He gives great examples that are detailed and useful. He makes himself very available during office hours and is very helpful and patient as well. His accent is moderate but he tries very hard to communicate clearly and efficiently with amazing notes and examples in class.

Professor Wu's teaching method basically consists of writing tons of examples and solutions on the whiteboard.  Honestly, if you just attend class and take good notes then getting a good grade shouldn't be a problem.  The fact that a one page cheat sheet can be used on exams is icing on the cake.
Wei knows her stuff, but she's just a little hard to follow. She does help out a lot with her slides, but many times things didn't click for me during lecture.

Her lectures are well organized, and the course is homework based with a final project. No tests. She is very approachable and will further explain course material during office hours, if needed. I've taken two of her courses, and I'd recommend her to anyone. KU is lucky to have her.

Wei is a great professor; she is extremely approachable, answers e-mails promptly, sits down with students one-on-one if they need help with course material, and explains material fairly well. She can be hard to understand sometimes due to her thick accent, but once you adjust to it, you'll do fine. An A is attainable if you do well on homework.
Challenging but very well structured class.  This class had the right blend of lecture, lab work, and homework.  Very good feedback provided on homework and other course work.

It will be difficult to understand her at first, but you will get used to it. She definitely goes above and beyond helping the class as a whole when it comes to things like curving the test. Work hard and you'll be rewarded with a good grade. An A is very possible even if stats isn't your strongest point. Overall, she is a great teacher.

It takes a few class periods to get used to the way that Wei speaks, so give her a chance.  She does a great job explaining things, and is more than willing to help with whatever you need.  You can't slack off in this class, but you'll be rewarded if you put forth the effort.

Wu is patient, accessible, and responsible to students. A living example to students, she is ambitious as an individual, and encouraging to others. Had she been my first math teach in college, I would have achieved much more than now.

She is a terrific teacher in class. She has made a difference in my life after taking her course. Outside class, once you get to know her, you would love her pleasant personality and positive outlook.

She has very high standard for her students and assumes her students are smart. After you get used to her teaching style, you would love her class. Wu tries to bring out the best part of your potential and boost your confidence to pursuit your dreams by doing well in academic as a springboard. Besides, she is understanding and approachable.

Being a patient and nice teacher, she  treats her students very well.  Also, she is encouraging and very passionate. You get more than math from her class. It is a most valued class I have had so far.

Her English needs MAJOR improvement. Very difficult to understand, and has trouble communicating the lessons to students, who can hardly understand her. I would highly suggest taking this class with someone who can actually explain the material well. Unless you can pass with just reading the examples she writes on the board, do not take her class!!

Make sure you have the textbook as many tables/formulas/properties are needed to solve the homework and exams. This man is a BEAST when its comes to grading the exams (next day, grades are in) and answering homework questions in a timely manner. Every test comes with 2 pts extra credit if you turn in your own equation sheet. He wants you to succeed

Dr Xianglin cares alot about his students. He grades homeworks, projects etc. in a reasonable way and in the exams, he just wants to make sure that the students have learned the course materials. I highly recommend taking his courses.
Overall good teacher. Has handouts for his lectures which helps a bunch. Homework every week that is a pain.
Lazy POS who makes all his students pay 70$ for worthless grading software so he doesn't have to do anything. Let me pirate my books not a 70$ subscription to view my homework.

One of the best engineering professors I've had so far. His lectures are great, he explains different concepts rather than just reading off of a slide. As long as you pay attention in lecture and make sure you understand the homework you'll do well.

Professor Yang is by far the best professor I've had so far. He lectures kinda fast, but he makes sure to iron out any confusion with the material and explains his example problems very well. Go to class, focus, and you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Yang really cares about his students and their learning. He was always helpful and interesting during lectures, and very approachable for help with homework and studying.
Yang is the GOAT. Not a difficult class if you pay attention and study hard.
Not a difficult class. However, you have to pay attention during lectures. Office hours really help. Very interesting professor.

Took this the same semester as thermodynamics so I put little to no effort into this class hence the grade received. His lectures are hard to follow and if you don't go to lecture you will miss out on daily clicker questions and notes as they are not posted. However,you will easily pass if you get "online hw help" and prepare for exams efficiently.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Oh, dear. Lectures are not easy to keep up with, and I have barely any idea what's going on in them. I've been keeping up with the material mainly by just reading the textbook/working on my homework in class. Print out the powerpoint slides and bring them to class, it'll help on the clicker questions.

The homework is worth a quarter of the grade so do not blow it off. He is not a good teacher so if you take him you will be very stressed. The material is not that complex, but he will not be able to help you understand.

Dr. Yang is a very smart man meant for research, not teaching. He is completely unfit to be teaching any class and especially not this one. He's very condescending especially when you go into his office hours for help. In class and in office hours when you ask him a question he'll laugh at you and tell you "it's easy" or "it's simple."
Easy class

Chen, despite the manageable asian accent, is a very good teacher. Lectures were always well structured and he gives good examples of a wide variety of problems. I had never done any programming before taking this class and I got an A. His tests are fair and the work load is reasonable. STUDY THE SAMPLE TESTS!

pretty good class overall. Sometimes the lectures are boring. Prof. Chen is full speed ahead at all times. Not sure how important going to class is. I went to almost every one and still usually ended up having to refer to the book. lab tests are fair

Excellent professor.  Lectures are extremely organized.  Note taking is nonstop (LOTS of material covered).  Chen's test are fair.  Study example problems in text b/c test questions are very similar. You will have to write a full program on his test that will take up about 40 lines of code.  Go to class if you no previous exposure to programming.

Good professor. He's a serious guy and you will never hear him make a joke. His class test scores were higher than his colleagues, and they were just as comprehensive. I felt I learned a lot from his class and put in minimal effort. He comes to class well prepared. He does have an accent, but it's manageable. He wants his students to do well.

Very helpful although he can be difficult to understand at times. In-class tests aren't too difficult, although the midterm and final were tough. Attendance isn't mandatory but he did give extra points to those who attended regularly.

Basically Calc I, if you took AP Calc in high school this class will mostly be a review. In-class exams are easy. Midterm and final were very difficult. Homework wasn't overwhelming and he goes over many of the problems in class. Going to class is extremely helpful, but if you keep up with the concepts and hw, not necessary. He's a nice guy!

This course is hard because calculus is, by virtue, hard. He isn't American but his English isn't terrible. He will have a hard time understanding questions sometimes though. Will almost always answer all questions before starting class. If you have taken calculus before, even in high school, this class won't be that bad.

She was so nice, but a terrible instructor. Only read off the slides and used notation irrelevant to the slides or book. Honestly, I don't feel like I actually learned anything. You'd be better off not going to class and teaching yourself.

Lectures were directly out of the book with little alteration. Assignments were some of the most difficult things I have ever done in academia. The content was super interesting, but I don't think the structure of the class helped the content at all. I had to re-read the book in-depth in order to try to get a grasp on the content for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just not a good lecturer. Teaches directly from the book. Makes no effort to ease into concepts, or check-in with students when lecturing. To finish the homework every week, I had to teach myself the material-- from the book and from online videos of other lecturers. Somewhat merciful grader, but that's it. Make a point to avoid her when possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She will just go straight from the book without any deviation at all. If there is an exercise in the book that is left to the reader, she actually leaves it to us. It is like you're showing up to a live audiobook reading or something. Would be so much better with any sort of originality.
She was amazing 10/10 would take again. If you're ever confused definitely attend office hours. So helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Claims to be a mental health advocate and then gives us 6 assignments due DURING finals week. Also will make several passive aggressive about how she deserves more respect but then does not show us any. On top of that more than 3 abstinences and she will drop your letter grade. Lectures also extremely boring, confusing, and mostly irrelevant.

A very nice person, but gives inconsistent feedback. I would go up for feedback, and would be told that it was good, minor adjustments etc. Without fail, I'd get a C on each project. I think she's nice and a good person, but not a great professor.

Very caring Professor and will tell you how much you have grown. The only reason not giving a 5 is due to the fact that she does not give out the rubric so you never know what to expect until you receive the grade. Sometimes does not always reply especially last-minute feedback. Overall great teacher, helps you grow, and recognizes hard work!

Sam is fantastic! very easy to approach and never immediately shuts down your idea, but helps you to improve it or will straight up tell you you need to find something else. Cares very much about mental wellbeing and knows how it can affect her students' work. Love her so much, if you need anything she is the person to go to! Communication is key!
Very disorganized and (whether intentional or unintentional) can be condescending to students at times too. Best to avoid taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: While the class wasn't great, he's very kind and approachable. He definitely wants his students to succeed, and he's very passionate about the course topics.
Not an easy class and he can be very confusing. That being said, I learned so much and I can confidently say that the takeaways from this course will impact my life profoundly.
Neither helpful or clear. Do not recommend this professor.

Do the readings, and participate in discussion. And try and go see him for help. Sometimes his feedback is confusing, but I think he's more than willing to work with students who come to him for help. As hard as this class is, you will probably still walk away with some valuable knowledge and insight that you didn't have before.
Discussion is an important part of your overall grade and you will not be able to discuss if you have not done the reading. DO THE READING. It is a lot but it is important.
Difficult to understand, makes attendance 20% of your grade, will call you out in class to read powerpoint or do problems on the board.

He only grades on if he likes you or not. Spends the entire class talking about vodka and how it "deals with supply and demand". If I asked for the answers of the test we just took to see how I missed something, "he lost the papers" The worst professor I have ever dealt with. You can never understand him and you will fail if he doesn't like you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is one of my best econ teacher. He gave me the passion of Economics. I was considering to minor in Economics, but after taking is Principles of Micro, I fall in love with Economics. He always real life example during is lectures. If you are lazy, you should avoid to take his class because his teaching style makes students to participate in class

He is good teacher.  The class was difficult but, he managed to make it easy by providing study guide.  He also curved every single exam.  I got A because he dropped my worst exam. I definitely encourage you to take his class.

This was his first semester teaching so he wasn't super organized but he made sure our grades didn't suffer for it.  He curved every test and attendance points are easy.  The book wasn't very helpful.  The tests included vocab and math/econ problems.  Should be easy if you show up an prepare.  And after a few classes you get used to his accent.

Horrible professor! I dropped the class due to his rudeness towards students, and lack of clarity. Would not recommend him, maybe if he taught a different economic course it would be different, but that I even doubt.

By far the worst professor I have ever had. I have never felt so clueless about a class. He doesn't answer your questions and just yells that the answer is in your notes. He is all over the place and does not go over how to do the difficult math, he expects you to know the equations already. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS.
Hard to understand. Avoid him if you can. I would never take a class of his again, nor would I recommend taking any class he instructs.
Very hard to understand and is all over that place
He is a good guy and helpful for the text. He always makes some jokes in order to work up people.

He was a good teacher, I did not take calculus before but I did well. Hes a quiet guy but you can tell he cares a lot about teaching and the class. Going to class is a must in order to learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Yenisey really cares about teaching, but the lectures arent nearly enough to pass. He is quite helpful on a one to one basis, but when lecturing that kinda goes away. Overall, if you want to pass Khan Academy is the way to go after the lectures.

I enjoyed his class very much. I had already taken calculus in high school so that probably helped, but I didn't think it was too difficult. All notes are posted online. Easy quizzes every friday. Not that much homework, one due on friday and online homework due on monday. He is Russian but easy to understand. Overall I liked this class
Great lecturer, has a passion for everything math.
Dr. Yeager is an awesome professor -- hands down! I would highly recommend Dr. Yeager as a professor to anyone.

This was the best class I've taken at KU so far! She picks great material and topics for discussion and makes it easy to participate. There's usually a reading for every class period, but nothing too long. There are two 2-page comparative papers due each 9 weeks (4 total for the class) and a final presentation. This is a class I enjoyed attending.

One of the best classes I have taken here.  She gets the class really involved and the material she picks is really fun!  Just go to class and do the readings and you should be fine.  She's super cool and really nice!

A very interesting class. The course load is much more than a typical 100 level class. If you can manage to keep up with all the readings, the class is a lot of fun. The midtern and final are on BB and are 100 questions of T/F. Very tough. Average score was a "C". Uses a +/- scale unfortunately. Papers are easy and she is really helpful with them.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. She gets the class involved in daily discussions and is more than willing to meet with you to talk about your papers. The material she picked out for the class is also very interesting. I would definitely recommend this class and professor to anyone.

Dr. Chen was an amazing and understanding professor. She has taught this course for years and knows how to help her students succeed. She might get on you about being on your phone but don't get on it while she's teaching. She brought so much fun to this class and always knew how to make us laugh! She was always willing to help with coursework.

Took 420 Dr. Chen is rude and will make you feel awful about your work and who you are as a person. Will yell at you for being on your laptop and phone in front of the whole class and if were paying for the class we should be able to be on our devices if thats what we choose. It was so hard going to her classes because I didn't enjoy being bullied.
Said we shouldnt waste our time becoming a lawyer because theyre unethical. As a pre-law student this struck a nerve with me and I dont think its acceptable classroom conversation.
If you don't find brutal honesty refreshing, don't take her class. No final just one large project broken up into chunks throughout the semester.

Chen is super helpful and compassionate. You learn a lot in the class but she expects a lot and is a tough grader. Her comments are very helpful and she takes time out of her day to make sure you understand the material.

Doctor Chen calls herself the "GPA Killer".
