She is a very tough grader, her lectures are actually entertaining, lots of group work (you are put in a group for the whole semester), lots of assignments that take a very long time to do. Get ready to work. However, if you work hard you should receive a fair grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Chen was awesome! She is one of the best professors in the journalism school. Her class is challenging, but she wants to push her students to compete with students at top universities, which not enough professors in the journalism school do. She gives a lot of constructive feedback, and she is always willing to work with her students.

There is definitely a LOT of work in this class. It is mostly group work, but can still be very overwhelming. Chen allows for drafts to be turned in for feedback, and I highly recommend doing so. The tests are pretty difficult.
Awesome professor, never regret having his class during undergrad. Very caring and inspirational, love to talk outside of classroom.

Yi is an amazing instructor! He is extremely knowledgeable in East Asian art, ready to answer your question at any time. He is always passionate about his materials in class. His lecture is highly engaging, also he knows how to explain complicated stuff in a simple and clear way.
Seemingly endless amounts of assignments everyday, however I enjoyed the class and learned a lot despite it being online only!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Joey is amazing! He was a TA in my first advanced art history class, and then I had him this past spring for a more introductory online course. He really knows a LOT about East Asian art, and does a good job of making his students laugh with dorky jokes. We even got to go on an optional field trip to a museum for the class!
The class was literally on 300%... easiest A ever. Also, his lecture notes were mildly hilarious.
Easiest A ever! 10/10 would recommend.

Despite being an introductory level class, Kachi spends most of the boring lectures rigorously defining and proving even the most obvious of math concepts. Attendance is 20% of the grade with absolutely no valid excuses to miss an exam. The homework is ridiculously tedious while the exams are trivial in difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: That class was a trip. The material wasn't very difficult to begin with and he would just straight up give you the answers to the tests. I think he may have had some crisis going on because he always seemed stressed and behind schedule. Very easy A, but I'm not sure how much of that information I retained. Real nice and goofy guy though.
Really nice guy and homework and tests were literally the study guide
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Made a difficult course not so bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Truly a paradox. Attendance is 20% of grade. Homeworks (40% of grade) often took us hours to do (due to length, not difficulty). He graded hw harshly. Strangely enough, it was an easy A. His midterm was his practice test verbatim. His final was extremely similar to the practice final. I learned nothing because he is an awful teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 10/10 rating

I see people saying that his class is easy but the reality is he teaches what is actually necessary and not unnecessary things. While the coursework was easy, his knowledge and approach to things are amazing. As an applied maths(or engineering) person, I thoroughly enjoyed his class. It's an easy A and fun class.

The lectures are boring and while no one wanted to go, attendance was 15% of our grade. The tests were almost exactly like his notes that he posts, never once used the book, the material wasn't even challenging and was pretty much a joke for a 500 level class. If actually interested in learning, steer clear. If you want an easy A, just go to class.

Pretty boring lecturer but if you pay attention, he covers all the material and tests aren't hard. Just have to show up and get through the lectures without getting distracted.  He's obsessed with Taylor Swift which is a bit odd.

He has an obsession with T Swift but also has an assistant Bunny that he calls Kitty he uses to teach class when everyone is lost. He does go through the notes page by page which is boring and not the most effective way to teach. He is understanding if you miss class. Not a bad teacher.

He is understanding about missing class, however this class is in Budig 120 and attendance is mandatory and there are assigned seats. All of his quizzes and homework answers are not hard if you pay any attention in class and just review the notes he posts online. He's not afraid to call out students in class if you're not paying attention.

He has an obsession with Taylor Swift, which is pretty hilarious. Super easy and very straight forward. He has in class and take home quizzes, attendance points, and tests. Just study the example exams online for the tests and you'll get an A. For the quizzes you need to either go to class or just look at his online notes to get A's on the quizzes.
One of my favorite professors from KU

If teachers were rated only on their niceness, he would be amazing. But as a teacher he is horrible. Don't take this class if you want to learn math. He has no idea how to teach. The tests have nothing to do with class work, and require memorizing the study guide. He doesn't show his work or tell you your grade during the semester. easy class tho

I could not tell you a single thing about calc 2 but I got an A in this class.  His HW consist of copying down his hints.  His tests are fill in the blank straight from the reviews so you just have to memorize the reviews. His quizzes were kind of hard but with all the extra credit it really didn't matter.

Math class was what others below have said. He posts answers and solutions for most homework problems. Tons of quizzes (some are hard) TONS of Extra Credit. Tests are replicas of the reviews he posts. Easy class! Nice professor too. ATTENDANCE IS MANDATORY!!

So easy. Just go to class because attendance is required. Homework is so easy and so are take home "quizzes" and "exams" because he posts "hints" online which are basically just the answers. You would have be a stupid if you don't get an A.

Worst teacher ever! Only teaches something he's interested in! He looks like a good guy, but if you did something against his will, he is evil! He would do whatever he can to put you into the hell! Whoever said he's a nice guy here, you are lucky because you haven't done anything wrong according to his will.
If you get anything below an A in this course you should sincerely re-evaluate your decision to attend college

Easiest math class ever. You don't really learn anything. Kachi types up his lectures word for word on a PDF and reads directly from them during class. Doesn't do sample problems in class. He gives "hints" for his HW & quizes/tests that basically give you all the answers. Copious amounts of easy EC will easily push you over 100%.

I can't believe that half his Math 660/661 classes were composed of immature students for such a level. Kachi is a great professor. (not a "teacher", read the syllabus). If you just want an A, then go to class, do the assignments, don't complain about how easy they are, and grow up.

Whoever says his Math 660/661 is terrible needs to grow up; you're in college now, and such slander is grounds for ridicule. Anyway, he's a great professor, and always more than willing to help me, no matter how trivial my problem seemed to be.
Don't, ever, take, his, class.  Worst, teacher, ever.

His motto is study hard/party hard! Kachi is easy to understand. Not hard to u I got an A... you can too by 1. Doing all the HW 2. Doing the Extra credit assignments 3. Reviewing for quizzes and tests. Class is very easy and although some effort is required it takes very little time if you have the right resources.
easiest math class at KU! if you don't need more math classes (b-majors), you should take it!

If it is the last math class you are ever going to take, I highly recommend it! You learn almost nothing, but it is the easiest class I have ever taken. The textbook is unnecessary because he puts all the problems on his webpage along with the work. There is A LOT of extra credit. And finally he is absolutely hilarious!

Need to knock out Calc II and don't really care if you learn anything?  This is the professor to take. Attendance is mandatory but if you have nearly perfect attendance you can get away with murder.  Homework is easy but somewhat time-consuming, quizzes become self-grade half way through the class and exams aren't too bad. Fairly easy A.

Kachi is a professor of "pure mathematics" so his specialty is classes that use math to learn more math. So if you take a class from him, make sure it's theory-based. (aka. math 791,790,290,) (not 121, 116, 122) in the latter, he will cover material that is too difficult for the average student to understand. Pick your prof wisely.

Yes, Kachi doesn't quite follow the ciricculum (spelling) for the class. No, he's not a stupid teacher. He just has an assumption that 90% of his students love math. If you actually read his notes, you WILL learn something I promise. Otherwise, you're pretty much given an A for his (relitivly) easy tests, so quit complaining!

Mr. Kachi's class maybe the easiest Math 116 class at KU.The textbook is even unnecessary. The exam is fill in the blank, and the notes is enough. But he almost don't explain how the formulas was proved, he just tell you to remember it. You can take his class and get A, but you won't learn any knowledge of math.

If you want to be a mindless drone, not learn anything, but get a good grade, take him (still lots of work). He spent a whole 2 days of the semester on the actual course material, then covered useless theoretical math he interested in. It was somewhat interesting, but not the class I payed for. He's a social nut, and makes for a good laugh...

Odd man, but very easy and willing to help you get a good grade. Not socially compatible with anybody, which makes for many funny moments during class. That said, I HIGHLY recommend him. He made hard math very learnable and helped me whenever I asked. Great teacher.

By far the easiest professor at KU. Quizzes are self-grade, test are fill in the blank and are exactly like the study guides. If you show up to class, you are pretty much guaranteed an a. He didnt have time to give our class 3 mid-terms so he is giving our whole class 100 percent on the test. Dont expect to learn anything though... cause you wont
KACHI IS THE BEST MATH TEACHER I HAVE EVER HAD!!!!! He made math make sense. If you have a choice between Kachi and anyone else, always always always pick Kachi!

Easily the worst professor I have ever had. Did not cover anything pertaining to the course and rebuffed anyone questioning his choice of topic. However, show up to class and you will get an A. Just don't expect to learn anything.

Kachi is an odd character to say the least. He did not stick to the curriculum at all. At the end of the semester I looked through our book that we never used and we had never covered a single topic in there. He taught us about his research which was interesting but did not pertain to the class.

Kachi is a very interesting man. Asian but speaks good english he is just socially not there.  Very nice and wants all his students to do well.  Take home quiz's weekly are identical to test and test are fill in the blank so fairly easy. Material gets harder after first test and he warns you many times. No study guide for final so that stinks.

Kachi was a badass! I would recommend him to everyone! The quizzes were take home and he posts study guides for tests online. The questions for the tests come off of the study guides! Great guy! 10 out of 10!
I got a D in 115,and then had Kachi for 116 and got an A. super easy nice guy, but he a stickler for attendance.
Kachi was the****! I loved him as a teacher for my 116 class this last summer...maybe you guys just suck at math

I think his quizzes are pretty easy. I just had to study the study guides that he's posted and get quite good results! However, his notes are messy for those who miss his class because he always uses his notes. At first, I thought I would not get an A but I got A!

His quizzes are pretty hard but he gives them out at the end of class.As long as a few people need more time he'll make them take-home quizzes, so you can look at your notes.I've gotten a "Perfect" on every one so far.His tests come directly from the quizzes so study those.Don't waste time studying the textbook, he never uses it on tests/quizzes.

He seems to have improved since he taught Math 121, since his Elements of Linear Algebra, Math 290, is a breeze. He writes out all of the lecture notes so you never have to take notes, he has every lecture, quiz, exam study guide and answers to every quiz and exam online well before class starts. The quizzes are easy but useful in forcing you to le
Teaches worthless information & teaches things that are supposed to be taught in upper level calc.  Writes quizes and homework very poorly.  You can never understand what is being asked.

he teaches concepts that you do not need to know until calculus 2 and higher. His quizes are impossible to get a good grade unless you have already had, and aced calc (but then again, why would you be in calc1?). The majority (15/18 people) have F's. DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!!

It's essential you attend Dr. Miao's lectures. I would also recommend supplementing his lectures with the Biochemistry textbook to cover areas you didn't understand. If you put the effort in, and study for every exam, you will do well in this class. Dr. Miao does an excellent job in outlining what to expect on the exam - he's a good professor.

Dr Miao was the worst professor Ive ever had. I actually think an orangutan clashing cymbals in front of the lecture hall for an hour and fifteen minutes would have been more informative on biochemistry then him. All jokes aside, this class was borderline impossible. So much content in too little time. Dont take this class with him.

Dr. Miao is a GOAT! This man changed my life and didnt even know it. I went into this class in severe depression, but seeing this man every day cheered me up so much. It is difficult but he gives you all the opportunities that you need to succeed. He is also incredibly understanding in terms of grading. One of the greatest people Ive ever met!!

Being a non-bio major made this class a little challenging. But after the first test, I recognized that understanding and fully comprehending the lectures was the best way to be successful in the class. You must read and digest the content. Dr. Miao is a kind and considerate person, and he truly wants to help his students achieve.

It's a tough class, but Dr. Miao makes every effort to make this class manageable for his students. He sets up very clear guidelines on how to succeed in his class and if you're willing to put in the work, then you'll get a good grade. Dr. Miao provides many opportunities to master the course content and even takes time to review with us. Top tier.
When I took Professor Miaos online biochemistry class it was very clear and to the point. As long as you study for the exams it is easy to pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is a really nice professor. Accessible outside the class. Helped me many times clear my doubts. He is very encouraging and has helped me greatly with my med school application.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was definitely taught from the point of view of chemists, so good luck if you are a biology major. Lectures are super boring and detailed but you basically need to memorize every slide to do good on the exams. If you read the book (its optional) that will help a lot. Neither Dr. Miao or Dr. Siebold were very forgiving on exams.

He was very boring. Lectures were not fun. Class was 100% memorization of 10000 terms. All one worded fill in the blank answers. Do not recommend taking biochem with this professor. Class was made way too difficult for what it should have been. Final was like 20 pages all fill in the blank over 40 chapters.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is nearly impossible to understand, gets confused by his own notes and is not helpful at office hours. His notes contain fifteen pieces on a slide, without any additional information given, textbook needed to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Rearrange your schedule to get Yi Yan as your TA. The best around KU by far! Made calc 2 so easy and fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This teacher is quite honestly THE BEST math teacher I have ever had. I was extremely nervous to take calc 2, but with his class you really understand what you are learning.. He is super nice, and he is really understanding of your circumstances. Only bad thing is lots of quizzes, but my lowest test score was a 96%, so they aren't bad at all!
If you need to take Calc 2 (Math 116) at KU, do whatever it takes to take it with Professor Yan.
Absolutely loved Miranda! She was a very fun, exciting and very accommodating professor. She gave amazing feedback and critiques for group assignments and projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She was a great lecturer. Exams and projects are clear cut and really follows pace of the textbook as well as the lectures. She wants you to succeed in the course and as long as you put in effort, you should do well.

I have never written a review for a teacher before but felt the need to here. She is HORRIBLE. How is it that I pay thousands and thousands of dollars a year and end up with a teacher that reads off a power point slide word for word, hardly speaks english, and makes her quizzes ridiculously hard.  Do NOT recommend. Avoid if you can.

I took her ENG 352 class (Poetry Writing I) during a fall semester and it was my favorite class I've been in. She helped foster a community feeling in the class, assigned productive and reasonable work, and was understanding and kind to every student. She's now the faculty advisor for SNAPS, KU's poetry club, and everyone in the club loves her.
Gives a ridiculous amount of work. Gives assignments out of spite when some students dont do the readings. Gave an entire project to work on over spring break, due the day we get back.

This is for English 351, poetry writing 1, but I can't find that one in the course tag. This is the best course I've taken at KU. Dr. Y created an environment that encouraged experimentation and growth, and she created a community of poets I plan on continuing friendships with. Great course and great professor.

Overall, I enjoyed the course content and thought it was easy/interesting. As far as the professor, she barely grades and didn't give any feedback on our writing. If you need to take this class for credit, definitely take it. If you want to grow as a writer, find a different professor.

Ms. Youngdahl really cares about her students and is willing to work with them to be lenient. Show up to class and it's not very difficult. Also, there are 4 writing projects throughout the semester which isn't asking too much at all. 10/10 recommend her and this class.

Meagen was a good teacher. The class was relatively easy - our grade was only based on reading response exercises, three unit projects, peer review exercises for these projects and leading a discussion. Everything in the class was fairly elementary and the only reason one shouldn't get an A is if they forget to submit something or don't show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Young is an amazing professor! He was always understanding, and super flexible when I needed a few extra days to complete an assignment. Lectures were relaxed, and he made learning ArcGIS Pro fun!
One of the most efficient instructors the department has. Very clear and concise. Also a genuinely nice guy.

Dr. Young was one of my favorite professors so far in engineering. He was extremely helpful and I went to office hours before almost every homework assignment and he would help me. Also he made it clear what would be on tests and would reply to emails within a few hours.
Great guy. He was helpful but sometimes his lectures got boring. Hopefully he continues to do the videos

he is extremely helpful! i was going to his office almost every day and ask him questions ! and he was more than happy to help me !! he really cares about his students ! and he always trying to find the best way for student to learn !! explain the hw in short Youtube videos ! Dr.Young is the best i have ever had !

Extremely helpful, i was going to his office everyday and ask him for questions !! and he was more than happy to help me out !! he really cares about his students ! Dr.Young is the best teacher i have ever had !

This class is great, and he is an excellent professor. He started putting the the lessons on short youtube videos prior to class, so you could easily use class time to do the homework. Really an interesting class!

Half of your grade is homework and the other half is projects, one from AutoCAD and ArcGIS, which are pretty interesting programs so the class is pretty interesting as well. Great teacher though. Explains everything very thoroughly.
Awesome professor and great man. Very helpful, intelligent, and easygoing. He was also my Honors advisor and he is extremely helpful. Highly recommend.
Excellent teacher, KU needs more professors like Dr. Young.
Was really helpful and a great teacher.
Great and inspirational professor! She truly cares about her students and gives great feedback
She is really great, cares about the class and wants students to understand the material. SHE IS AMAZING!
THE BEST. ever. ever. everrrrrrr. ever. you're a fool if you disagree. She gives great demos. And she's very approachable. And helpful. And smart. And nice. And funny. Oh, and good at litho.

Great at explaining all of the childhood mental health disorders and including interesting personal experiences/examples. Exams took some time to study for (I used a full day usually) but they were pretty straightforward and easy to get A's on with some studying.

Yo is awesome and hilarious, she could make any subject interesting. You won't do well in this class if you skip class and don't read, but she makes class interesting and the subject matter is fascinating anyway. Take her for this class if you can, you won't regret it!! She offers extra credit as well.

UNFAIR!! Yeah she's funny at first--but it's the same jokes--same voices--same stories. Although interesting class and teacher--don't expect her to give you an inch--ohh and she also makes you feel like you're wasting her time if you go to office hours...so don't even bother. But if you get stuck with her..memorize your notes for sure. Good luck!

Child Psych, after taking this class, I enrolled in her other class developmental psych because Yo's just hilarious. If she ever wanted to pursue stand-up comedy, she would succeed. Her experiences working with abused children provide several of her in-class examples. I learned so much from this class and highly recommend it!

Devlopmental Psychopathology-- Yo is an excellent teacher. Very experienced. Well-versed on the current issues and very entertaining. The tests have some funky wording sometimes but she usually cuts the class a break if too many people miss one. This class is very relevant for all education majors and highly recommended.

No tests but don't be fooled. Instead of tests there are a number of essays. You must know the material well to do well on the essays. Dr. Yoon definitely cares about her students and will help if you ask her. Just do the readings and you will enjoy the class and learn a lot.

Dr. Yoon is a very good professor. She is knowledgeable about comparative politics, and is very good at getting students to explore areas of comparative politics they like. I would definitely take one of her classes again.
lecture is easy to understand. topics are interesting. she always bring her own handouts other than textbook. she changes deadlines of paper and exams often.

no use textbooks only her handouts. changes paper deadlines. she is nice to you in person but is merciless in email and grading. overall, her teaching skills stays at discussion level like any other TA. she is a professor just because she herself receive good education in political science doesn't mean she can teach well.
Most boring class I've taken in my life.

Dr. Yoon makes it a point to establish a connection with all of her students. Although her assignments may not always be perfectly clear at first, she is always willing to help and is not a tough grader. After taking this class, I hope to have her again in the future. Highly recommended!
This was an awesome class! It's easy enough if you do your work and follow her rules. She is VERY reasonable and tells you exactly what's needed to succeed in her class. Highly recommended!

Horrible professor.  Required you address her as Doctor Yoon as directed in first day of class, put in pretty rudely too.  Class is all lecture, over provided readings.  No point or goal of class, talks about everything under the sun.  Very dismissive and rude to students and their ideas and questions.  Cannot teach to save her life.  AVOID!!

She's the goat. Lots of homework, almost-daily quizzes, but it's a 5-credit-hour language class, so that's expected. In my other JPN classes I struggled to maintain an 85; in Naito-sensei's I am maintaining a 95 easily and learning all the content. Love her
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Every lecture she shows up with a nice smiling face and when teaching, will only move to the next topic if she is sure we all understand everything well. She is obviously very passionate about teaching and is willing to help any student. She also has lots of good tools like the quizlets she makes for each unit. And her fits are always amazing.
guided me to a new world.

Let me preface this I did fail Naito-Sensei's class but that was my own fault for not showing up to class. While trying to catch up Naito sensei went out of her way to make sure I had help. She is one of the best professors ive ever had I cannot wait to retake her class because of how wonderful of a teacher she is.

Naito-sensei is a wonderful professor. You will have daily vocab quizzes, but they aren't too bad to prepare for. Speeches are required after each chapter, but you get to use a script. Naito is a very kind, caring person, and her classes are great. You'll learn a lot with her!
Naito-sensei is an excellent teacher. She always took time to answer questions and clearly cared about about educating her students.

Naito-sensei is very kind and willing to help you succeed if you will work with her. It's because of her class at Washburn that I transferred to KU and became a Japanese major. If you want to learn, this is definitely a professor you will enjoy.

I had her at Washburn University in Topeka. This was my first Japanese class, and my first foreign language class. She was lenient and easy going. (kind of a pushover). but she is really nice and cares about whether or not you succeed.
Fair, easy going, and a native speaker. Her enthusiasm and willing to work outside of class shines through the tedium of learning Japanese.

Dr. Younger is probably the best professor at KU. He has well rounded knowledge and cannot be outdone on Greek history. Go to lecture and get some of his awesome stories from living in Greece during the 60's-70's (during the military Junta). Can't recommend him enough. Great guy and professor.

He's an extremely knowledgeable guy, but his guidelines for projects were not very clear. However, he's also a fair grader and won't dock you for doing an assignment differently than he imagined. No final if you show up to lecture!

One of the best teachers I have had a KU! He is very passionate about what he teaches and really cares about his students and their learning of the material. Very interesting to listen to in class! Even though attendance was mandatory, I wanted to go to class every day.

I took Intro. to Archaeology with Younger, and it was a pretty fun class. He has an interesting sense of humor, and his lectures are usually pretty interesting. Go to class and do well on the mid-term, because if you are happy with your grade, you can opt out of the final. Attendance is mandatory, but it's a pretty cool class.

Dr. Younger really knows his stuff. His lectures are engaging and even his tangents are extremely relevant to the material.  As long as you are in class and take notes, you will have no problem on the tests, so don't bother with the text book. Dr. Younger is very liberal and intelligent, one of my favorite professors at KU!

Dr. Younger was by far one of the greatest professors i have ever had. His class was EASY!!! Dont buy the text book you dont need it. He gives you the midterm and final before you take it, and if your in class you dont have to take the final if your happy with your grade!!

Prof. Younger was a great teacher. I enjoyed the way he held his lectures and he didn't just read off his powerpoint slides like what most professors do. This was the first Budig lecture I had my freshmen year and it was a good pick. To have a good grade you do have to read all the books and including the text.
Class was so easy.  Never really had to study for the tests.  Go to lecture and he makes it easy on you.  Beware the GTA's.  Some suck.

dr. younger is very funny and sarcastic, but i got a 68 on my first exam. you have to know quotes from like 12 diff books and who said them which was hard. otherwise great class, but i hated the discussion class.

Dr. Younger was an awesome teacher. His exams were pretty simple and you were well-prepared if you did the study guide. He has a good sense of humor and tells a lot of interesting life stories that really illustrate the class. I highly recommend this teacher.

Younger is the MAN.  By far the best teacher I've ever had at KU.  He's hilarious and his tests aren't hard.  Review sheet for midterm/final cover ALL material.  If you don't love John Younger, you have no sense of humor, because his sarcasm is amazing, and he made an interesting subject even more interesting with his commentary. CLSX 148 = Younger
No Comments
No Comments
He talked loudly to a couple of the TA's during our entire final exam! I could not concentrate!
His lectures do not seem to go with the books - I agree with everyone else - you get all the info from the TAs.  He also talks about sex way too much.  Comes across as arrogant.

Overall not a difficult class. The midterm and finals both have a study guide with every possible question on them. The lecture itself seemed very extraneous. The readings/discussion were more important and your grade definitely depends on the TA.

Never really have to go to lecture. I would learn everything need in Disc. Puts important note on the web. Midterm and Final are fine if you study, which isn't hard. The rest just depends of the TA you get...
Good teacher, makes the class interesting. The study guide helps alot. Overall great class and he helps out when needed.
I went of the KU Classics Dept. Study Abroad tour of Greece in 2002 with Dr. Younger.  If any of you have a chance to go, DO IT!!
No Comments
Great guy, insists on making things fair and straightforward because he knows most people aren't running to take Western Civ. :D
No Comments

Professor Younger is the sh*t.  His lectures are interesting and make class worth going to.  The best part is, he puts his notes on line.  He makes a study guide for the midterm and the final that he takes the test out of.  He is a great teacher and really knows and enjoys what he is talking about.

Professor Younger is an amazing man. One of the best professors the U has to offer. Wonderful teacher, will do all he can to help out his students. He knows his stuff. Very intimidating at first, but nothing to be afraid of.
EXCELLENT. Tells great stories. Will expect a lot from you, but you will learn a ton. Great to go in and talk to in office hours, and gives great advice. Expert in his field.
Very entertaining, and very smart.  Might expect a lot from you, but sometimes makes the final optional

We are halfway through the semester, she is about to submit midterm grades yet we have yet to receive any feedbacks/grades for 7 assignments dating back to Mid September. Four of which are written papers. Very unprofessional.

The assignment guidelines were clear and self-explanatory. Professor Yuchen was always available after class to explain anything that wasn't clear. The assignments weren't necessarily an easy A, but you will do great in her class if you put in the effort. Lastly, you will work a lot with a group throughout the semester. Overall, great class.

AWFUL. Completely unclear expectations, inconsistent feedback (Received two sets of feedback on an assignment that were completely contradictory). Ignored questions in class often. Does not explain guidelines well and does not provide necessary tools to do well until after submission. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Professor Liu is always super responsive to emails and really wants you to succeed in the course. I especially liked that she gives such specific criteria for the assignments. You always know what is expected of you which makes it easier. Its an upper-level course so of course the work can be a little intensive but its manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I don't know why, but I honestly love him and his lectures. He keeps things light. Midterm was easy if you studied his exam review and the scheduler/policy problems are fun. Way better than 678 the previous semester. One negative: he doesn't post the lecture slides until AFTER each section quiz, so take good notes and read the textbook.

The lectures are confusing, and he expects us to know everything even though the topics are not easy. The labs and the projects are not related to the course topics, and the midterm and final exams are hard. So, I don't recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The course is just slides which Yun reads from, and his feedback is short and not extremely helpful. Most of the learning I did for this course came from outside materials and other resources, and the majority of the course was based off lab grades and exam grades.

The mandatory lectures consist of boring PowerPoint recitations that add very little value over just reading the slides yourself. The grade almost entirely comes from two tests and the lab section, which is not strongly related to the lecture.

Definitely teaches outside the box, draws on real-life experiences to get you to engage. She also challenges you to apply rules and concepts learned in one area of law to atypical situations to test your understanding. Doesn't spoon-feed, just do all the readings & participate in groups, she will have your back. Don't bother asking about grades.

She uses many different types of assignments to show off a wide variety of methods to other faculty members. The assignments are not well thought out and aren't used by any other professors at this school. She has a hard time posting things online and following through with her end of the assignments, including grading as promised and on time.

I appreciate Prof Yuille's good intentions and her experience/knowledge. However, Biz Orgs was torture. Her pedagogical methods waste so much time. So much busy work. The material isn't difficult, but this class sucked the life out of me emotionally. I will begrudgingly admit that it is a good foundational class though. But take it with Harper Ho!

She often wasn't in her office for her office hours and didn't respond to emails sent to clarify many mistakes in her assignments on Blackboard, used for most of her weekly assignments. She wastes a lot of class time telling personal stories, showing off what she's read recently, attempting to justify her teaching methods, and critiquing students.

The assignments and expectations were very straightfoward and she was one of my most understanding professors in regards to adapting to technology and COVID. Her lectures felt like they dragged on though and were very repititive. The capstone didn't feel like it matched the class and felt very out of place.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Last semester was the first time she taught this class, and even though we had to go online halfway through, Dr. Zahn continued to amaze me as a professor. She is very interested in what she does, and makes the lessons fun and interesting. I was never bored in this class. Expectations are clear, so if you just pay attention, you'll do fine.

She lets her political beliefs reflect in her lectures/ grading. I didn't do well on my first exam and couldn't get my grade up even though I received an A on everything else. Didn't get clear feedback on what I missed either. She didn't provide true facts in lectures, and included a lot of her opinions which made the homework/ test difficult.

Dr. Zahn is really good at what she does. She's very clear and knowledgable about the material. Not always the most engaging but you will definitely learn a lot. Definitely makes you work for it though. If you slack off you will crash and burn. But she's always available for clarification. She's nice, challenging, and intellectually stimulating.

Professor Zahn is amazing. She cares about what she is teaching and she is more than willing to answer any questions. She expects her students to do college level work. If you do the homework and the readings you will do well, but don't expect to slide through without doing the readings. I have taken a few of her classes.

Tests are graded pretty harsh but if you study with her study guide you should get a decent grade. Doesn't require too much outside work and her powerpoints are all online so you don't need to take notes during  class.

Fairly easy class, if you study a lot. She makes sure every little detail you discussed in class is on the test, and grades them rather harshly. Just be prepared to study and you will get a decent grade!

This class was one of the worst i have ever taken. The material, tedious and uninteresting, was extremely hard to comprehend. Furthermore, the grading on the tests was asinine. I would not recommend this class for someone "looking for an easy A". However, if you are a fan of religion you will enjoy this class.
The material is really interesting but no matter how much you pay attention just be prepared to study a lot. By studying for a week instead of a couple days I raised my test grade by almost 20%

SOOOO HARD!! you have to read a lot of material in order to do well in this class. but the material you have to read sucks. takes a lot of time out of your day. do not take this class unless you absolutely need to.

Good teacher, pretty easy class. You only have to read some of the material for the assignments, and the rest of the time you just have to be in class. She gives you thorough study guides that you can fill out from your notes and her online lectures, and if you do this and study it, the tests are cake. Medium time commitment, fairly easy.

Easiest class I have ever taken. Go to class and take notes, fill out the study guide, and study it! Every question on the exam is already given to you prior to the exam. It takes a bit of effort but she couldn't make it easier. I got a 98 99 and 99 on the exams..Take the class!
BE PREPARED TO READ!! So much reading. Such a confusing class. She does not teach clearly to help the student understand. Not my favorite teacher!

I had her for Living Religions of the West and it was extremely hard for me. All of her tests were 10 fill in the blank, around 5-8 short answer, and 2-3 essay questions. I failed the class but I know a couple people who got B's. Its not impossible, just HARD. Just be prepared to study for 5 days or more leading up to the test.

Zac is an amazing professor and really breaks down difficult material. He gives helpful practice problems and the course notes were great. Don't get me wrong, it's a hard class but he makes it as simple as it can be. If you put in effort you can get an A. Grades on a curve too. Material can get boring but Zac does his best to make it interesting.
The best professor I have had thus far in my undergrad. His exams are difficult but his accessibility and knowledge of the class makes the class enjoyable and rewarding.

Dr. Wiebe is probably the best professor I've ever had. You leave class feeling more confident and with a better understanding of the material. It's a very difficult class, but Zac structures the class in a way that is easy to stay up with and follow along.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Zac went beast mode all semester. Coming into this class I was a 4.0 student and thought if I made a B the world was going to end. I made a B but I'm not mad because Zac is a homie.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very difficult material but Zac really breaks it down with course notes and practice problems. There are pop quizzes so come to class but they are only 5 points so it wont kill you. When Zac sasys study 4 hours, atleast put the effort in to study atleast 30 minutes beause not studying is going to fail you.

Zac Wiebe is my favorite accounting professor I have had so far. Intermediate 1 is historically a very difficult class but he is a very strong professor overall. Though he is new to teaching, he is very energetic and wants you to do well. If you show up prepared how he suggests that you do, and put forth effort you will be fine.

Zac is awesome. Everyone talks about how hard ACCT320 is but he made it easy because he was great at explaining everything. I never even opened my book because the notes he gave were so thorough. He's always willing to meet outside class to help. I hate accounting but enjoyed his class. Put in minimal effort and you should come out with an A/B.

Zac, while somewhat new to teaching, isn't the greatest at explaining his thoughts and the concepts that underlie this class. However, he is the most available and willing to help professor I've had at KU. That alone will take him a long way in his career... his in-class teaching skills will improve over time obviously. Tough class overall.

Zac is probably one of the best professors I've had. He took a notoriously hard class--Intro to Tax--compressed into a month and made it not only reasonable to learn but almost fun. He was always available if I had trouble with something and was really easygoing in class. Not to mention he didn't mess around, but taught to the CPA exam. Very cool.

Zac is a PhD student that taught some of the summer Acct 201 under Kelvie Crabb. He is a young and energetic guy that uplifted the class on a daily basis. The class was somewhat difficult but Zac explained things that were so clear. One of the best TA's I've ever encountered at KU. Helpful before and after class. Zac  has a bright future.
Super approachable professor and knows exactly what he is doing. Do NOT make fun of Wisconsin (where he is from) or he will body bag you instantly. Show up engage in class and ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Zach is a laid back dude who is easy to get along with. He gave a ton of extra credit opportunities so make sure to take advantage of those if at all possible. He loves to include guest speakers, and expects people to be on their best behavior for the guests, but not for himself. He is straightforward and makes objectives extremely clear and fair.

Great professor. Young and knows his stuff in Sports Management. Lots of background in the field and a very nice guy. Taking another class with him this spring because of how great he was. Go to class on "in class assignment" days, guest speaker days, and review days. and you'll do great.

Dr. Zeedan is an amazing teacher. He's always so positive, and that makes a difference in the class. The material was interesting, and he explained everything really well. If you participate in class, the experience will be even better. personally, he's one of the best teachers I've had.

I enjoyed Dr. Zeedan's class. Dr. Zeedan himself was phenomenal. He gives great feed back, has a lot of positive energy, and shows benevolence when it comes missed deadlines. He is also quick with grading. The course involves a lot of reading and critical thinking, but I would not say it is very difficult. It is paced very well.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Mr. Zeedan is my favorite professor here! He is such a caring individual, prioritizing understanding the context and material in his courses. His role as an Israeli Druze gives him great perspective especially concerning Israel and Palestine. He is very respectful of student's personal lives and gives great feedback when grading your work.
Really great professor, makes his lectures very interactive and never has a bad attitude when in class. Very helpful and assigns fun projects, not test heavy.

Professor Zeedan is extremely knowledgeable about the topic and has a very unique personal perspective that adds to the class content.  If you keep up with all of the work and attend regularly, you will be set up for success.  He is also extremely understanding and willing to give you opportunities to improve your grade with hard work.

Professor Zeedan was a fantastic teacher and a great person. I took his class, Israel: From Idea to State and it was one of my favorite classes of the year because of him. He was very understanding and helpful when it came to assignments and feedback, and his personal connection with the subject matter made the class very enriching.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such an incredibly kind person. He noticed I was struggling in the class due to personal reasons, and made sure that I was taken care of. It was obvious that he cared more about his students being successful than anything else. I cannot recommend him enough, his kind heart helped me through such a difficult time in my life. Really cool class too!

This prof is very genuine and listens to the feedback you give him! There were a lot of assignments each week, so prepare yourself for a lot of writing, but that's to be expected in a short semester course. There's a lot of reading but you can get away with skimming or relying on the lectures.
Pest professor ever. Incredibly intelligent, flexible, and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Topics class, was crosslisted with JWSH and RELG. Class was informative but abnormal in its schedule, one class per week for 2 1/2 hrs. Lecture can drag as a result. But, the assignments: there aren't a ton, especially for a 500+ course, and his rubrics are very clear and he is a very lenient grader. Easy A if you do the readings and go to lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Teacher wants to believe he's still 20, very immature and lets his emotions get the better of him. Long-winded critiques in which he says nothing important. Seems nice  but is a very strange grader

Extremely helpful professor. All the papers have rough drafts that get you completion points AND he will help you in correcting the rough draft. Just contribute to discussion and you'll be on his good side which may be helpful in grading. Definitely a good professor and a nice guy.

I hate English, and this class was a breeze. You write 3 papers total and everything else is for completion. He's a really cool guy and practically begs you to let him help you. Just show up to class and turn in everything on time and you'll get an A. One of the easiest classes I had this semester!!!!

AMAZING PROFESSOR! I took MATH 220 with him and it was such a great experience. DEQ is an otherwise difficult course, but he makes it so manageable. Attendance matters, at the end of class each day there are open note quizzes that are simple given the subject. He is super caring of his students and you get a cheat sheet on the exams.

This professor cares about his students, but his lectures could've been more organized and accessible. He didn't post detailed notes online, so attendance was important. There were also open-note quizzes after every class. When lecturing, he would write the notes in tiny handwriting; I sat in the 2nd row and had a hard time reading the board.

Great teacher, really understands the material. Has an accent, but easy to understand. Easy to relate to and great with students. Quiz almost every day (free points if you pay attention). The tests are tough, but you get a cheat sheet. Posts all material he uses on canvas. Would recommend taking Linear Algebra first.
Quiz everyday. Don't miss a class.

One of the best professors I have ever had. His method of teaching allows students to fully grasp the ideas, which are fairly tough to understand, and succeed if they put in the effort. Quizzes were every lecture, but you can choose from a couple of different short problems. Exams were pretty hard, but very reasonable for the given material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Got a B+ but probably could have gotten an A if I spent more time. Quizzes were tough but you will get most of the points. Literally got a 30% on the 2nd midterm, and was 0.2% off from an A- in the class. If you avg. over 66% on exams, do okay on all pop-quizzes, and get all the easy HW points, you will probably get an A. Beautiful notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This was the hardest class I have ever taken. The grade cutoffs reflected that: a 77% was an A. He is a nice guy, but could teach prob/stats in a much better way. There's a quiz everyday over the stuff he just taught. The exams are open note/book, but crazy hard nonetheless. He was nice and caring, but had a hard time explaining difficult concepts.

This class was def one of the hardest ones I've taken at KU, however he was very reasonable with grade expectations. Very easy to get a hold of and he provided a lot of helpful feedback if you asked him any questions! Really nice guy and I would recommend if you have to take this course

Professor Liu is definitely one of the better math professors I've had. He really does care about you and he is very receptive to student feedback. While the material is difficult, Professor Liu makes it a lot easier. If you have a chance to have him as your professor, take his class!

I've never rated a professor before but I had to for this guy. TAKE HIS CLASS. He is the sweetest guy and actually cares about how you're doing. He takes student feedback so well and changes his class so that his students can succeed. I bombed my first exam and still got an A- that how awesome this guy is. Can't recommend this guy more

Professor Liu is great! He adapted to the online class structure very well. The material isn't easy, but he cares about his students and wants you to do well. He listens to student feedback. There is usually a quiz after every lecture, but they are not a problem if you keep up in class. His grading system was very fair.

Take his class! The material itself is difficult but Professor Liu makes it easy to understand and genuinely wants his students to do well. His grading scale is very good and sets you up to get a good grade in the class. Kind of a bummer that I bombed the final because his exams aren't too difficult. Quizzes every class but they help your grade.

The material covered in this course is not easy by any means. But Professor Liu recognizes that. He is an extremely fair grader. Expect nearly daily quizzes, but they shouldn't be an issue if you paid attention during that class.

Highly recommend. Short 1 problem 15 minute quiz at the end of most lectures. Homework once a week. Listens to student feedback. Difficult course but fair and worth taking with him as the professor. Managed the technological challenges that naturally happen with online courses excellently.

Professor Liu was an awesome professor. It is very important to attend the lectures as you will most likely be lost without them and there are daily quizzes worth points. Another incentive for showing up to class is that extra credit was offered for being there the whole lecture and not for just the quiz. Overall I would recommend Liu.

Zhipeng is great! Quizzes every lecture, but they are easy. Exams are very fair, and homeworks are not bad. Highly recommend studying the textbook - he is a very nice man but lectures can be hard to follow at times. He also provides very organized lecture notes, which are extremely helpful. Very smart! He knows his stuff!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The class moves very fast and, for the first half of the semester, there was a quiz at the end of every class over the material covered in that class. That was gradually changed to quizzes that covered new and old topics and only required you to answer one question. A little bit of a mess, but he's helpful and genuinely wants you to do well.

The lectures are super boring and make the subject material seem awful. When studying for exams however, the material itself was actually pretty interesting. Although his class is very boring, he is very fair and wants everyone to do well in the class. The class itself is not too hard if you study adequately for the exams-they're worth a lot.

Dr. Zhao is very knowledgeable about Physics and he does a pretty good job at explaining it as well. While his lectures are very fast paced and boring at times, he and his TA are very accessible outside of class for questions and his exam policy is very favorable. He tries his best for every student to get an A as long as you put in the work.

Dr. Zhao was a very good instructor that clearly is passionate about physics. He taught the concepts very well and there were plenty of example problems. His policy for the final was that it would replace every test grade lower than it, which really helped me. The class was difficult but he did his best to help every student got an A.

God-tier exam policy with 1 page filled front and back with whatever notes you want for each exam and the final exam you get 4 full pages of notes, plus final exam is a replacement for any exam you scored lower on. Lectures could be a little slow sometimes but Zhao is funny, nice, and very helpful whenever you need help. Very tough but fair class!
I am convinced he is the best professor at KU, he is hilarious and teaches things incredibly well. His test policy is very generous and is fair. You really won't regret it!
One of the most caring professors at the University, I highly recommend taking a class with him. His tests are incredibly fair and his final policy is absolutely amazing. You won't regret having him!

Dr Zhao is a great professor. He's super funny and teaches Physics III very well. If you get him, don't worry, you're in a good place. Exams aren't hard, but mistakes do result in large point deductions. He allowed us a full sheet of notes, front and back, for each exam (3x), and allowed for three full sheets of notes for the final.
Great professor. Teach efficiently with applicable examples. Exam is very related to the topic.

Attendance10% of grade, minus 1% if they take roll and you're gone. Hw was mastering physics, and Chegg helped out a lot. Tests were hard, some questions pulled straight from hw, and he reuses old test questions. Can be hard to follow in lecture sometimes. Nice teacher, likes helping students.

Clicker quizzes in class make attendance mandatory. Tests suck. BUT, the final will make or break your grade. Your final exam grade becomes the lowest grade you can get in the class and if the grade is higher than any other average (tests, quizzes, HW) it is replaced by your final score. So Ace the final and nothing else matters.
Very tough grader (zero partial credit,) and expects all students to be calculus experts.

Dr. Zhao is funny and personable. He balances making the concepts tangible with covering a lot material. Lots of assigned reading, discussion and problem solving in class, hard online homework, relatively easy tests. He warned this would be one of our hardest classes, but as a ChemE this class was not at all anxiety inducing.
Keep up with the class. I like physics a lot but because the tests are only 10 questions its very easy to get a B.

His lectures weren't bad, but my one complaint ruins the class. The exams only have 10 m/c qs and are worth 30% of the grade. Each question is worth 3% of the overall grade w no partial credit. The questions are easy to mess up even if you know the material and with a 8.5x11 cheat sheet. I recommend taking PHSX at JCCC.

He was kind of difficult to understand at times and the tests were terribly difficult. He also totally cancelled a test after a snow day, which seems awesome, except that that decision was probably detrimental to a lot of grades, mine included.

Really cares about students. He makes things interesting by using some fun real life examples and throwing in funny jokes. Very helpful answering questions in class and via email. One of my favorite professors at ku. Some tests are tricky but he gives a nice curve, mastering physics is also helpful. Easy to do well if you put forth the effort.

In general, the physics professors at KU are TERRIBLE lecturers.  They assign pointless amounts of homework, and deliberately make tests as hard as they can.  Dr. Zhao is the ONLY good professor in this department.  His lectures are well organized and well prepared, he assigns reasonable HW, and his tests are very similar to the homework

Good teacher. Made good/funny analogies, tried to keep the class interested. Accent needs slight improvement.  He taught half the semester of 212. I hardly ever attended--online lecture slides are from the book. Class averaged a 60 on tests, I got an 80 and got an A. Study the book hard and do its problems, forget HW and lectures. I give him an A.

spent most of the class preaching religion and a need to find God. A walking religious discrimination case waiting to happen. She brought in a speaker to talk about his godly use of prison labor and exploitation of villagers in South America and was quick to anger against student who spoke out. Also learned absolutely nothing from this capstone.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Spent 3 weeks in a row indoctrinating us with her views that believing in God is the only way to be an effective manager. Not exaggerating.

Oh sweet, sweet Jane Zhao. The woman has the biggest heart in the world but is tough professor. Lectures are dry; show up to class for participation points. Group projects the whole semester. Changes her own syllabus constantly and doesn't follow what she says. Never answers questions directly. Excess amount of work. Classic JZ. A real whirlwind.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her real name is Zheng Zhou. But DO NOT take her class!! Extreme amount of useless busy work that teaches you absolutely nothing. She is extremely rude during class. The class consists of 8 group modules and then a final report of all the modules combined. The final report is over 30 pages. Jane just expects way to much effort for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: THE WORST professor I have had at KU. DO NOT take MGMT 498 with her. While my friends were sitting back and relaxing in their 498 classes, I'm doing a different group project every week. Her lectures are painful & she is terrible at explaining concepts. Way too much work for what should be an easy A class. I got nothing useful from this class.
just freaking terrible.

Taking this class with her was a waste of time and a bigger waste of money. This is a required class but if it's offered a different semester with a diff prof, then do that. It's TORTUROUS to sit thru that class. So much work over NOTHING. Idk how she has time to make all these detailed modules. She's such a detailed grader. Just awful.

was a lot of work, but could see that the professor was interested in more than just teaching the raw material. She spends a lot of time trying to show students the significance of the material and how it applies. Good transition from academia to the working world
Way too much work for an useless class, avoid her if you can

Jane is the worst teacher I've had at KU.  It's a shame because this is a capstone course. She does not even follow her own syllabus, and often adds extra work throughout the semester. Just an awful experience. Hardly learned anything.

A waste.  Lectures straight out of textbook. Lectures are drier than sandpaper.  Has her TA grades the homework.  Despite the homework being mainly subjective in nature, the TA subtracts points for anything possible.  My favorite:  the TA (unless its the prof herself) loses homework.  Multiple people in my class reported losss/missing h/w.  A joke.
Worse teacher I've had at KU! Don't take her class! Unnecessary work, always changing directions, SUCKS! Save yourself now!
Excessive amount of work for a class that should be a Victory Lap.

It's very helpful that there were two ways to get a grade so that whether you're stronger student in homework or tests, you could succeed. The lectures were boring, not really his fault though. I'm sure some people are enthralled by phonology but I certainly am not. They record all of them so if you miss class you still get access to the material.

One of the worst professors I have ever had at KU. He stands at the front of the classroom and reads off a sheet of paper. No PowerPoint or visual to look at. Lectures are so boring I can't even keep my eyes open. HW assignments are impossible and have nothing to do with what is talked about in lecture. I never skip class and am really struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhang is good at explaining phonological concepts and motivating why they are useful to learn. He is able to effectively handle the mix of undergraduate, graduate, in-person, and online students all at the same time. He even took the time to teach the in-person undergraduate discussion section himself. Homework is weekly, but not too bad.

Knowledgeable and kind. Lectures aren't the most engaging but he does a lot to support students: he gives lecture outlines for each class, quick and detailed feedback after each homework, and many chances to go to office hours before each assignment. Good guy and a manageable class, just try not to do the homework at the last second

Absolute jerk! Only cared about the graduate students, lectures were boring at best, and some of word sets made no sense for the languages he wanted to exemplify. If this class wasn't a required course, I would have dropped it on day two!! I never rate teachers but couldn't help myself this time. Cannot say enough bad things about this man.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is a good teacher. His class can get pretty boring at times. But he is very knowledgeable and if you are struggling in the class he wants to help. Just make sure you take good notes and read the readings before lectures and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I had a hard time focusing in lectures because they weren't very compelling. That said, Jie is very knowledgeable and is willing to help if you need it. Go to office hours. If you can do well on the homeworks (they're 50% of your grade) and understand them, you'll be fine. You don't need the book - that goes for all KU Linguistics classes, honestly
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There were 12 homework assignments, but the lowest two were dropped (thank goodness because I got As on all of them but one really, really bad one). Those were 50% of your grade. I got 100% on both midterms - 25% of grade. The final was really hard for me, but I still got an A. He gave extra credit (3%!) due to people doing bad on the first midterm
No phonology pro in this school, only Jie Zheng. If I got another choice. I might choose another Pro. Damn phonology
Very informative. Very good prof. Requires a lot of you, but helps you through it all.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: his course is really boring. He got 6 homeworks, and if you want to get good grade, you need to read lots of things. Consider WELL you really want to take his class, otherwise, just choose a better one.

the subject is a bit dry but  Zhang made it interesting enough that I always felt like i was on my 4th coffee.This said both my joy and stress about in class. He is a great teacher,very knowlegable in his field. He would help you when you give a headsup before standing up on him without notice.He likes to throw inner jokes about phonology in class

Interesting subject, but class gets boring pretty quickly because he lectures with a PowerPoint every single class.  The class was very easy in the beginning, then got more difficult toward the end, and I felt there were some areas that lacked adequate explanations.  Overall a pretty decent class though, and he's a nice and pretty funny guy.

Zhang is a quirky and silly man and a genius when it comes to linguistics. One of two professors I have actively searched to take classes with.Phonology requires a LOT of time and patience but if you go to every class, do the reading and have an open mind, you will have a blast in his class and learn an extraordinary amount about the subject.

I had to drop this class because it took so much of my time. YOU HAVE TO READ AND ATTEND ALL CLASSES.  Missing one class will leave you so far behind that you're screwed.  It's also really hard to schedule a time with him outside of his office hours and he makes you feel like the biggest idiot ever.  I would leave office hours or class crying.
guy's amazing. one of the best in the linguistics department. knowledgeable AND knows how to teach. hard class, but you'll come out knowing you've achieved something. amazing class and person.

Phonology was an interesting and stimulating class. It had enough challenge to keep things interesting, and you could tell that Jie was really into the topic. I though he did a good job explaining the material and engaging students in the lectures.

While the material in Phonology is definitely challenging, professor Zhang is good at making sure one understands, though not without effort on the students part.  He has high expectations for his students, and you will NOT get an easy A in the class or on homeworks, so when you do actually get an A on a homework or test you actually feel like you'

Dr. Zhang is not helpful at all. His class is extremely difficult and going to him for help or assistance on homework only makes you feel stupid. It's unfortunate when his class is required for a major, and he can't even be approached by a student for help without being made to feel like an idiot.
Dr. Zhang, besides being smokin' hot, is clear, fair, and approachable.

He is an amazing teacher.  Very intelligent and explains things well.  His expectations are clear and really makes you DO phonology.  It can be pretty difficult and homeworks take some time, but it is worth it :)
He really made me work hard in the class, and I think I'm a better Linguist for it. Very specific about what he expects. He made me love Phonology. Sort of.
No Comments
Tests were hard for a religion class. Boring lectures. Super nice guy, just was bored with the class.

I really like this professor and have a lot of time for him and his classes. Admittedly he can ramble a little but its endearing and he is so interested in what he's teaching. He wants you to participate, he seems genuinely interested in his students and because of that it has been a pleasure to be taught by him.
I liked him a lot. He's really nice and pretty funny at times. He's a little old fashion but I enjoyed his lectures for most of the time.

I haven't learned anything in his class at all. His class is discussion based but he is so argumentative that it seems the only right view to have is his. It may just be this class, but either way, I regret taking it.

uses an overhead for all of his notes which can get pretty boring, but overall provide really good information. if you go to class and at least skim over your notes before the tests, you'll do just fine. textbook is not necessary for this course

Incredibly helpful. He is always willing to meet with students to help with anything.  He is very intelligent and is willing to admit when he doesn't know something. His teaching style is not for everyone, but he teaches in a way that I learn the most because students are forced to pay attention and take notes. A great prof!
I love this professor! He is one of the nicest people I have ever met, and he is truly willing to listen to your point of view and help you in any way he can. One of the best.
STULTIFYINGLY boring. Additionally, he will keep lecturing after the bell is rung, until everybody finally gets up and leaves.

Class grades are based on daily participation, and papers. Normally Im not a fan of participation points, but it is actually very simple in a smaller class size like this where all you have to do is simply make a comment about the class for the day. She is very helpful and I found to be very fair with paper grades. Gives you a few skip days.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She was very good in class.  No tests, all writing assignments, but I felt very prepared for all of them.  Overall I really enjoyed her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class was nothing about what I thought it would be about. I learned nothing and wasted a whole semester dreading every Monday/Wednesday at 12:00. If you didn't go to class or discussion you lose 10 points. Very unfair with grading criteria and everything was through her TA. All she did was read slides in lecture. Her outfits were fabulous tho.

I came into the class thinking it would be a clear cut course learning about all the religions with no bias. Everything she taught was related back to Buddhism. There are no right answers in this class, merely your opinion. Tests are all essays and final was essay. Work hard and go to class and you'll pass
I took the class with an interest in global religions, and I came out with more knowledge on Buddhism than I wanted. She barely covers any other religion.
Avoid at all cost. TA does all the grading and is extremely unfair. I had a genuine interest in religion and this killed it all.

This class was a lot of reading, but it wasn't difficult. GO TO CLASS. You have to get all the participation points possible. The lectures can be boring but with interesting subject matter (if that makes sense). She's not very lively but if you go and pay attention, you'll be fine. And no tests! Only papers.

TA takes forever to grade your papers, about a month. I don't like having to wait that long to know how I did and what my current grade is. But other than that, fairly easy, covers all the introductory religious bases.
Class is pretty straightforward, show up. All the grading is done by a TA. The textbook readings are not necessary for success, although you must have the book for reference.

She is a very nice (and eccentric!) lady. The class was fairly easy and had some interesting moments. For the majority, though, it was kind of boring. Her grading is very fair and I would take the class again.

She made some anti-Christian remarks, which set the tone for the class early. Some of her lectures were good, but many were unorganized and she rambles. May be better to take her in a small class size.

Fair grader, actually grades pretty easy, IMHO. Go to class to get attendance credit (you'll need it), and take notes! She gives you the answers/themes you'll need to do well on the papers.  She likes humor and is not the hard-ass she comes off as at the beginning of the semester! I'm hoping to get her again for 205 if that says anything!

STAY AWAY! Got high A's on all tests and papers but a low B in the class for attendance, which is rediculous in a huge lecture. She actually announced the first day of class that she is a ****, so judge for yourself.

Hey, do you want to take the "Dreaded Western Civ" (in her own words)? Then take it from her, because I promise you will come out of it pretty much hating humanity and everything you read (which I'm pretty sure is the opposite effect they are going for at the University). She is awful.
Lectures vary from interesting to down right strange. This was not an Intro class. The guy sitting next to me guessed tenure was the only thing keeping her around. Avoid if possible.

Attendence is required to get an A, assigned seats for no reason, and after she got done telling us how guessing authors to quotes didn't help students learn, guess what was on the final. Got tired of hearing about her bird.

She made the Book of Job seem interesting, and that was only the beginning.  Not the easiest western civ class, but not the hardest either and very informative.  If you have any interest in history, you can learn a lot from her class.
For a Intro to religion class it was very in depth and and had to stay on top of things. I graduated from a catholic high school and still had to try really hard in this class. DONT TAKE IT WITH HER
a seating assignment in a 100 person lecture, are you kidding me, this class started as a job and never stopped being one

Definatly must attend class to keep up. Reading is only partially necessary. Take online quizzes as a group. Tests aren't too bad. A little hard so you need to study. She is kind of interesting to listen too. Her vests are hilarious. You always wondered what she'd come in wearing next. A good teacher I would say.
Keep up with reading and study for test.

Love her.Best teacher I've ever had.She's interesting, VERY well read. If you have a problem with tough teachers then go back to highschool or drop out. Zimdars is awesome. She's tough, I won't lie, and you don't want to say anything dumb, but how could you hold that against HER? She's a very cool lady.  Love her.

She is one of the best teachers on campus.  If you cannot keep up it is because you are inept & don't pay attention.  She will donate any free time she has to assist you in any way, shape or form.  Yes, she assigns stringent hw assingments, but she is

I thought this class was kinda boring most of the time and I have a very strong interest in religion.  I don't even know that I know more about religion after taking it, I got much more use out of other religion classes.

Class should be buddhism class- that's all she rambles on about.  She is a very very boring teacher and her exams are hard!  The only thing I learned in this religion class was about buddhism.  Attendance is required!

she is a very fair teacher and grader. I'm not gonna lie you have to come to class, and you will be taking notes the entire time and getting hand cramps, but its all very straight forward. If you do the reading, study the notes and come to class you will be fine.

She is over controlling, pretentious and just plain mean. She responded to a question of mine with the most rude email. The class isnt what you expect it to be, but you learn alot. Online quizzes are easy (take in a group!) and essay q's are given before test. Attendence is key

I was very interested in the subject, yet I despised the class. NOT an intro to various religions, more like a lot of Native American stuff and some existentialism and buddhism. I thought she was pompous and arrogant. TA's grade all your stuff though.

Class isn't too hard, you do have to work though. Get a good grade on her first test and your in like flint. If you screw up your likely to keep the same grade the rest of the semester. Simply put, if you can study, you can do well in the class. She keeps you honest.
Won't let you get away with anything.  If you dare to speak, think about it first.  Man, I wish I had...

This class is what it is--if you don't mind classes where you have to show up all the time, read some books, and take and study notes, then this class is for you.  If not, don't take it.  If you take/study notes, the tests aren't very hard.
Hard class, but very usful for study habits.  She is a very inconsistant grader and seems like she hates some people for no reason, i was scared of her.
I  hated this class. Professor has anger management issues and acts like she hates college students --especially the men.
Great class and teacher
She's not a bad teacher but her grading is inconsistent and she is very random in her lectures.  I did enjoy this class though.
not that bad of a teacher but definatly not easy
Avoid!  TERRIBLE professor!
Very unclear, and very strange when it comes to covering topics. Grading on test is odd at best. Class is extremely boring. I do not recommend taking this class under her if at all possible.
Horrible teacher, goes off on tangents in discussion and fails to relate it back to class discussions.
She is an excellent teacher, well-organized, engaging

Rob is an amazing teacher! He made the class fun, enjoyable, and a pleasure to attend. Rob goes through tons of examples, answers questions on homework, and gives practice tests almost identical to the actual test. If you have the option to take a class from Rob, do it, you will not regret it!

Rob is a wonderful teacher! He is very interested in the topics he teaches and is always there to help you if you have a question. I took MATH 115 Enhanced with him which was a very easy class to get an A in. I would strongly recommend Rob and his class!
